source.name: obdex
source.note: Independently written descriptions; not SAE J2012 text.

B0001.d: The restraint control module tests the firing loop of the first inflator stage in the driver airbag, which sits in the steering wheel hub and is fed through the clock spring. B0001 is stored when that loop is open, shorted or outside its resistance window; the fault byte added to the code names the exact type. Mercedes-Benz logs B000113 for an open stage 1 squib, Honda used B0001-13 on the 2013 Civic, Mitsubishi files it under the driver airbag module, FCA under squib 1, and GM on its 2020-21 full-size trucks, where B0001-1B came from rust particles at the airbag connector raising the resistance (bulletin 21-NA-005). Stage 1 is the charge used in every deployment, so a fault here can cost the driver frontal protection. The airbag warning lamp stays lit.
c: Corroded or poorly seated connector between steering wheel harness and airbag module
Broken or worn conductor in the clock spring
Internal fault in the driver airbag module (stage 1 squib)
Chafed lead in the steering wheel or column harness
s: Airbag warning lamp or service airbag message stays on
Driver frontal airbag may not deploy in a crash
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0002.d: Dual-stage driver airbags hold a second charge that the restraint module fires only in severe crashes or after a short delay, so the cushion fills harder or for longer; a Nissan patent bases that choice on the change in vehicle speed and belt use. B0002 flags a fault in the firing loop of this second stage. Land Rover documents B0002-13 as an open stage 2 circuit on the Evoque, which also appeared after a module replacement had loaded older software (SSM 74577). Mercedes-Benz, Mitsubishi and FCA list it as the driver squib or module 2, GM as stage 2 of the steering wheel module. Because both stages share connector and clock spring, B0002 often comes together with B0001; alone it points to the stage 2 lead or squib. Adaptive inflation is lost and the airbag lamp is on.
c: Open stage 2 squib lead at the airbag module connector
Stage 2 track in the clock spring broken
Replacement restraint module loaded with unsuitable software (Land Rover SSM 74577)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver airbag loses its second, high-severity stage
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0003.d: Some driver airbag modules carry a third pyrotechnic element in addition to the two inflator stages, and B0003 covers its firing loop. FCA lists the code as driver frontal squib 3; its STAR case S2108000180 found B0003-2B (wires shorted together) next to B0001 and B0002 when connector locks behind the steering wheel were not engaged. Mercedes-Benz uses B000313 for the squib of the vent valve inside the driver airbag, which lets gas escape so the cushion becomes softer. An FCA patent describes such an active vent that the airbag electronics opens or keeps closed using data from occupant classification. With this loop faulted, the bag loses its third stage or adaptive venting, while the two inflator stages may still work. The airbag lamp lights up.
c: Connector position assurance lock at the airbag module not engaged
Third squib or vent valve squib in the airbag module faulty
Damaged clock spring conductor for the third circuit
s: Airbag warning lamp on, often together with B0001 or B0002
Adaptive venting or third deployment stage unavailable
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0004.d: A knee airbag, also called an active knee bolster, sits in the lower dash below the steering column. It fills the space in front of the driver's knees and holds the lower body back in a frontal crash, mainly for unbelted occupants. B0004 reports a fault in its firing loop. Mercedes-Benz stores B000413 for an open squib of the driver kneebag. Ford lists B0004:1A with the passenger knee code B0013 on the 2024 Ranger and traces it to certain airbag connectors, recognisable by a number moulded into the connector lock (TSB 24-2444). In an IIHS study of more than 400 crash tests, knee airbags brought only a small benefit for belted dummies. Still, the restraint module counts the loop as part of the system, and the airbag lamp stays on until the circuit is repaired.
c: Faulty or loose knee airbag connector under the dash (Ford TSB 24-2444)
Harness pinched or damaged during work below the steering column
Internal fault in the knee airbag module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver knee airbag may not deploy in a frontal crash
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0005.d: Some steering columns can change how much energy they soak up while collapsing in a frontal crash. In a Delphi/Nexteer patent a controller fires pyrotechnic actuators that force an absorber strap into a tighter path or couple in extra absorbers, matching the column to driver size and crash severity. B0005 is the restraint module code for the firing loop of such an actuator. Land Rover documents B0005-56, an invalid or incompatible configuration, on the Evoque from 2018 when a replacement restraints control module had received older software than the factory level; a manual patch of the diagnostic equipment fixes it (SSM 74577). FMVSS 204 caps rearward column travel at 127 mm when the car hits a barrier at 48 km/h. With the loop faulted, the column keeps its fixed default behaviour and the airbag lamp is on.
c: Restraint module configuration or software does not match the vehicle (Land Rover SSM 74577)
Open or shorted lead to the pyrotechnic column actuator
Faulty actuator in the steering column
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Adaptive energy absorption of the column unavailable, no effect on normal steering
Safety note: the column actuator is pyrotechnic; leave tests and connector work to a workshop with the battery disconnected

B0006.t: Driver Frontal Deployment Loop Short to Ground
B0006.d: B0006 is missing from the public J2012 code lists, which go straight from B0005 to B0010. The only documented use found has nothing to do with airbags: on the 2025 Ram 1500 the body control module stores B0006-11 for a short to ground in the latch control of the left RamBox stowage lid, fixed by a module update (flash 08-204-24). The title describes a driver airbag firing loop shorted to ground. Current restraint modules report that as a fault byte on the stage code instead, for example GM B0012 02 on the 2011 Saab 9-4X, set after two seconds of ground short. A ground short in a squib circuit can stop the stage from firing, so the scan tool must first show which module stored B0006 before anyone works on the airbag.
c: On Ram 1500 2025 the code belongs to the left stowage lid latch circuit of the body module, not the airbag
Driver airbag squib lead chafed against metal (ground short)
Insulation damage inside the clock spring
s: Airbag warning lamp on when stored by the restraint module
On Ram 1500 2025 stowage lid will not open electrically, alarm may sound
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0007.t: Driver Frontal Deployment Loop Short to Battery
B0007.d: Like B0006, this number is absent from the public J2012 lists. FCA uses B0007-11 on the 2025 Ram 1500 for the latch control of the right RamBox stowage lid, again a short to ground in the body control module and cured by the same flash 08-204-24; an airbag meaning is not documented anywhere. The title names a driver airbag loop shorted to battery voltage. Restraint modules treat that as a fault type of the stage code: GM sets B0012 01 or B0013 01 on the Saab 9-4X when the steering wheel airbag loop sits at supply voltage for two seconds. A short to positive is the more dangerous case because a further fault could energise the squib, so modules usually disable the affected stage and light the lamp. Confirm the storing module before any repair.
c: On Ram 1500 2025 the code belongs to the right stowage lid latch circuit of the body module
Squib lead touching a powered wire in the column or steering wheel harness
Moisture bridging pins in a connector of the airbag circuit
s: Airbag warning lamp on, affected stage disabled by the module
On Ram 1500 2025 right stowage lid inoperative
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0010.d: The front passenger airbag in the dashboard is normally dual-stage like the driver bag, but it also depends on occupant detection: FMVSS 208 allows it to be suppressed for small occupants and requires a readiness indicator that monitors the system. B0010 reports a fault in the firing loop of its first stage. Mercedes-Benz stores B001013 when the stage 1 squib of the passenger bag is open; Mitsubishi files B0010 under the passenger (assist) airbag module with several fault bytes. A suppressed airbag is not a fault and does not set this code; B0010 means the wiring or squib of stage 1 is electrically out of range. Typical spots are the connector behind the dash panel and harness routed past the glovebox. The passenger bag may not deploy and the airbag lamp stays lit.
c: Loose, corroded or unlocked connector at the passenger airbag module
Harness damaged during dashboard or glovebox work
Internal fault in the passenger airbag module (stage 1 squib)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Front passenger airbag may not deploy in a crash
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0011.d: B0011 is the passenger counterpart of B0002: it concerns the second inflator stage of the dashboard airbag, which the module adds in severe crashes or fires with a delay. Mercedes-Benz logs B001113 for an open stage 2 squib of the front passenger airbag, and Mitsubishi lists B0011 as passenger airbag module 2. Stage 1 of the same bag has its own code B0010, a third element B0012. Since both stages leave the module through one connector, a code for stage 2 alone usually means a fault in the stage 2 pins, lead or squib rather than a general connector problem. Older GM modules (Saab 9-3 up to 2011) put passenger stage 2 faults under B0012 to B0014 instead. The airbag lamp is on and adaptive inflation for the passenger is lost.
c: Poor contact on the stage 2 pins or open stage 2 lead
Stage 2 squib in the passenger airbag module faulty
Output stage in the restraint control module faulty
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag loses its second stage for severe crashes
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0012.d: In the J2012 order B0012 is the third element of the front passenger airbag. Mercedes-Benz uses B001213 for the squib of the vent valve in that airbag, and Mitsubishi lists B0012 as passenger airbag module 3. GM gives the number a different meaning. Its later sensing and diagnostic modules assign B0012 to stage 1 of the steering wheel airbag; the Saab 9-4X 2011 manual trips it after two seconds of contact with supply or ground, an open, more than 4.4 ohms or less than 1.7 ohms; GM bulletins link it to chafed coil wires on the 2009 Cobalt and to weak terminal tension at the coil connector on the 2015 CTS. Older Saab 9-3 modules used B0012 for low resistance in the passenger stage 2 loop. Read the code with the maker's tool before choosing which airbag to check.
c: On GM vehicles weak terminal tension or chafed wires at the steering wheel airbag coil
Open or shorted third squib (vent valve) in the passenger airbag (J2012 meaning)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on maker, passenger airbag venting or GM driver airbag stage 1 affected
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0013.d: B0013 belongs to the knee airbag on the passenger side, which deploys from the lower glovebox area and keeps the passenger's knees and thighs from sliding under the dash. Mercedes-Benz logs B001313 for an open squib of the front passenger kneebag. Ford pairs B0013:1A with the driver knee code B0004 on the 2024 Ranger; the TSB has all four airbag connectors checked, the passenger knee airbag being C2433, and swaps those with the wrong moulding number. GM uses the same number differently: in its later modules B0013 is stage 2 of the driver steering wheel airbag, with the same fault bytes as B0012 (Saab 9-4X 2011, GM 2009 Cobalt coil coverage). So a GM vehicle needs a check at the steering wheel, other makers at the passenger knee airbag. The airbag lamp is on.
c: Faulty connector at the passenger knee airbag (Ford TSB 24-2444)
On GM vehicles fault in the driver airbag stage 2 loop or clock spring
Internal fault in the passenger knee airbag
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger knee airbag (or on GM driver airbag stage 2) may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0014.d: B0014 is not in the public J2012 code lists; there the driver knee airbag has B0004 and the passenger knee airbag B0013. The number is documented only at General Motors, and with another meaning. GM modules from about 2010 use B0014 for the side airbag in the driver seat; the Saab 9-4X 2011 manual adds a fault byte for each failure, from a shorted or open loop to a high reading (0D, over 4.2 ohms) or a low one (0E, under 1.4 ohms). GM bulletins blame chafed or loose seat harness connectors and high connector resistance on Silverado and Tahoe 2014-15, Equinox, Traverse and the Bolt EV. Older Saab 9-3 modules used B0014 for a short in the passenger frontal stage 2 loop. A knee airbag meaning for this code is not publicly documented.
c: On GM vehicles loose or high-resistance side airbag connector under or in the driver seat
Seat harness chafed by seat frame, motor or foam
Internal fault in the airbag module served by this loop
s: Airbag warning lamp or service airbag message, often intermittent
Affected airbag may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0015.d: B0015 does not appear in the public J2012 code lists, which assign the passenger knee airbag to B0013. Only General Motors documents the number, as the firing loop of the belt pretensioner built into the driver's retractor. In the Saab 9-4X 2011 manual this pretensioner shares one diagnostic page with B001A, the anchor pretensioner, and both trip when their loop stays outside the allowed resistance band or touches supply or ground for two seconds. On the 2009-11 Impala GM notes that B0015 points to the retractor pretensioner while a second pretensioner sits at the belt anchor (PIC5396A). On an Equinox, a wire under the power seat rubbing on the seat motor set B0014 and B0015 and blew the seat fuse (PIT4898C). A passenger knee airbag under this number is not publicly documented. The airbag lamp is on.
c: On GM vehicles loose or corroded connector at the driver belt pretensioner
Harness under the power seat rubbing on frame or seat motor (GM PIT4898C)
Internal fault in the pretensioner or airbag served by this loop
s: Airbag warning lamp on, sometimes intermittent
On GM, belt pretensioner may not fire; power seat may fail if the harness is shorted
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0016.t: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Deployment Loop Short to Ground
B0016.d: The public J2012 code lists skip B0016. General Motors used it in two generations with different meanings. In older modules, documented for the Saab 9-5 2006 and the Saab 9-3 up to 2011, B0016 means low resistance in the passenger frontal stage 1 loop: the reading drops under about 1.5 ohms, tolerance 0.2, for two seconds. That is close to the title, since a short to ground or between the leads also pulls the measured resistance down. In later GM modules (Saab 9-4X 2011) B0016 is the left roof rail airbag loop, with its own bytes for short to ground (02) and low resistance below 1.4 ohms (0E). GM bulletin 08-09-41-002H lists B0016 among codes caused by unseated connector locks on many 2005-14 GM models. The airbag lamp is on in every case.
c: Squib leads shorted together or to ground in the passenger frontal loop (older GM)
Connector position assurance lock not seated (GM 08-09-41-002H)
On later GM vehicles fault in the left roof rail airbag loop
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger frontal airbag stage 1 (older GM) or left head airbag (later GM) may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0017.t: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Deployment Loop Short to Battery
B0017.d: None of the public J2012 lists contains B0017 either. In older GM modules (Saab 9-5 2006, Saab 9-3 up to 2011) it marks an open passenger frontal stage 1 loop, set once the loop reads more than roughly 4.5 ohms for two seconds, so the component matches the title but the fault type does not. Later GM vehicles use B0017 with GM's usual fault bytes, where 01 stands for short to battery. On the 2020-22 Acadia, XT4 and related models GM traced B0017 01, together with B0024 01 and B001E 01, to faulty SDM software rather than wiring: the code is cleared and the module reprogrammed (PIT5827, 21-NA-176). The parts named there are the knee airbag and the driver seat inboard side airbag. The airbag lamp is lit.
c: On GM 2020-22 models faulty SDM software, cured by reprogramming (21-NA-176)
Open passenger frontal stage 1 loop (older GM meaning)
Squib lead in contact with a powered wire
s: Airbag warning lamp on or an OnStar SIR notification without lamp
Affected airbag stage may be disabled
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0018.d: In the J2012 order of seating positions (driver, passenger, center, then second and third row) B0018 covers stage 1 of a frontal airbag for the middle seat of the first row. FMVSS 208 demands frontal airbags only for the outboard front seats, so such a bag is rare, and no carmaker publicly documents B0018 with this meaning. It is not the GM front center airbag of 2013, which deploys from the inner flank of the driver seat in side impacts (SAE 2013-01-1156). GM did use B0018 itself in older modules: on the Saab 9-5 2006 it reports a voltage out of range in the passenger frontal stage 1 circuit, above 4.1 V or below 1.0 V at module pin 44 for two seconds, and on the Saab 9-3 a short to battery or ground in that loop. Check which module stored the code.
c: Open or shorted stage 1 loop of a first-row center frontal airbag (J2012 meaning)
On older GM/Saab passenger frontal stage 1 loop shorted to battery or ground
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Affected frontal airbag stage may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0019.d: B0019 is the stage 2 member of the first-row center frontal series B0018 to B001A, meant for the second inflator charge of a middle-seat frontal airbag. No carmaker publicly documents the code with this meaning. General Motors uses B0019 widely, but for stage 1 of the passenger airbag in the instrument panel: on the Saab 9-4X 2011 sub-codes 01 and 02 mark shorts, 04 an open, 0D a loop reading that stays high and 0E one that stays low, while stage 2 of that bag is B0020. On the 2009-10 Chevrolet HHR, fretting corrosion in the in-line connector between body and dash harness raised loop resistance and set B0019 0D or 04 (PI0117B and a customer satisfaction program). On GM vehicles the passenger airbag therefore needs checking first. The airbag lamp is on.
c: On GM vehicles fretting corrosion in the passenger airbag in-line connector (HHR PI0117B)
Fault in the stage 2 loop of a first-row center frontal airbag (J2012 meaning)
Internal fault in the airbag module on this loop
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM the passenger frontal airbag stage 1 may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B001A.d: B001A closes the first-row center frontal series and stands for a third stage of a middle-seat frontal airbag, matching B0003 for the driver and B0012 for the passenger. No carmaker documents it publicly in this sense. At General Motors the number belongs to the anchor-mounted belt pretensioner on the driver side, a second pretensioner at the belt end fitting that works next to the retractor unit coded B0015. Its limits match the other GM squib loops: a pretensioner loop reading beyond 4.2 ohms or beneath 1.4 ohms for two seconds sets the code, as do shorts and opens. GM bulletins report it on the 2009-11 Impala with a pinched or misrouted pretensioner harness (PIC5396A, 15-NA-074) and on Equinox and Traverse 2018 (PIE0438). On GM vehicles look at the lower belt anchor first. The airbag lamp is on.
c: On GM vehicles pinched, misrouted or corroded anchor pretensioner harness
Fault in the third stage loop of a first-row center frontal airbag (J2012 meaning)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM the driver anchor pretensioner may not fire
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0020.d: B0020 covers the firing loop of the left front side airbag, the thorax bag usually built into the outer flank of the driver seat backrest. Toyota names B002011 and B002012 as short to ground and short to battery on the 2022 Tundra, where the wireless phone charger caused false entries that new SRS software cures (TSB005722). FCA reads B0020-13 as an open left seat squib on the 2014-17 Cherokee and the 2015-17 Chrysler 200 and fits new jumper harnesses in the seats (10-001-20). Honda collected parts from Accord, CR-V and TLX with the same byte 13, and Mitsubishi confirms each fault after 2 seconds. GM modules of about 2007-14 used B0020 for passenger frontal stage 2 instead, so check which bag the scan tool names. The airbag lamp is on.
c: Poor contact or corrosion at the side airbag connector or jumper harness under or in the seat
Internal fault in the left seat side airbag module
Pinched or chafed side airbag lead in the seat frame
Restraint module software reacting to interference, e.g. Toyota Tundra 2022 with wireless charger
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left front side airbag may not deploy in a side impact
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0021.d: In the J2012 order B0021 is the first firing loop of the left curtain airbag, the bag that drops from the roof rail over the side windows. Mitsubishi files it under the left curtain module and stores byte 11, 12, 13 or a short to another circuit once the condition has lasted 2 seconds. Mercedes-Benz reads B002113 as an open squib of the left window bag on the A-Class, CLA and GLB, where raised contact resistance at the restraint unit plug was the cause (LI54.21-P-070658). Curtain 1 is the only or front curtain inflator; B0022 is the second one. GM Global A modules use B0021 for the passenger seat side airbag instead, with bulletins on seat harness contact (PI1469, 23-NA-030). Airbag lamp on; the left curtain may not fire.
c: Raised contact resistance at the curtain airbag or restraint module connector
Damaged lead along the A-, B- or C-pillar or the roof rail
Internal fault in the left curtain airbag module
Fault or unsuitable software in the restraint control module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left curtain airbag may not deploy in a side impact or rollover
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0022.d: B0022 belongs to a second firing loop for the left curtain airbag. Mercedes-Benz shows what that means in practice: on the A-Class, CLA and GLB, B002213 is an open squib in the left rear window bag, the curtain section for the rear seats, while B0021 serves the front one (LI54.21-P-070658, version 1 of 2019 and version 4 of 2020). Cars with a single curtain inflator never set it. General Motors has older meanings for the number: the 2006 Saab 9-5 used it for driver frontal stage 1 resistance below 2.0 ohms, and Global A modules for the passenger belt retractor pretensioner, as on the 2009-11 Impala (PIC5396A) or the Saab 9-4X. The module and descriptor shown by the scan tool decide which part is meant. Airbag lamp on.
c: Raised contact resistance at the restraint module connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Damaged lead to the rear curtain section at the C-pillar or roof rail
Internal fault in the rear left curtain airbag module
Fault or unsuitable software in the restraint control module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Head protection for the left rear seat may be missing
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0023.t: Left Side Deployment Stage 1 Loop Short to Ground
B0023.d: B0023 does not appear in the J2012 code lists, which jump from B0022 to B0028, and no carmaker documents it as a ground short of a left side airbag stage. It is documented at General Motors with another meaning: in the Saab 9-4X 2011 manual B0023 is the right roof rail (curtain) airbag loop, with bytes for short to battery (01), short to ground (02), open (04) and resistance above 4.2 or below 1.4 ohms (0D, 0E), each confirmed after 2 seconds. GM bulletin 08-09-41-002H lists B0023 among codes caused by unseated connector position locks on many 2005-14 models. A real ground short in a squib loop can stop deployment, so first read which module and descriptor the scan tool reports. Airbag lamp on.
c: Connector position assurance not engaged, so shorting bars bridge the loop (GM 08-09-41-002H)
Internal fault in the affected airbag module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
The airbag on the affected loop may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0024.d: B0024 is missing from the public J2012 lists; there the right front side airbag is B0028. General Motors used the number twice. Older modules, such as those of the 2006 Saab 9-5 and the Saab 9-3, assign it to driver frontal stage 1: on the 9-5 the voltage at the module pin leaves the 1.0 to 4.1 volt window for 2 seconds, on the 9-3 the loop is shorted to ground or battery. In 2021 GM listed B0024 01 beside B0017 01 and B001E 01 on Cadillac XT4 to XT6, Blazer, Camaro, Malibu and Acadia as a software fault of the sensing module, pointing to the knee bag and the inboard side bag of the driver seat; new SDM software fixes it (PIT5827, 21-NA-176). A right side airbag meaning is not publicly documented. Airbag lamp on.
c: Restraint module software fault on 2021 GM models (PIT5827, 21-NA-176)
Short to ground or battery in the driver frontal stage 1 loop (older GM/Saab)
Worn clock spring in the driver airbag loop (older GM/Saab)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on the vehicle, the driver airbag or a seat side airbag may be affected
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0025.d: No public J2012 code list contains B0025, and no manufacturer publicly describes a second stage of a left side airbag under this number. The only trace is at General Motors: the Saab 9-4X 2011 manual groups B0025 with the roof rail airbag codes B0016 and B0023 but gives no descriptor for it. Two-stage side airbags are rare in any case. A Ford patent notes that thorax, pelvis and head bags usually have a single inflation setting because of their small size, and the dual-chamber side airbag described by Autoliv divides one cushion into chest and pelvis zones rather than firing twice. If B0025 appears, the descriptor and module name on the scan tool decide what is meant. Airbag lamp on; the affected bag may not deploy.
c: Open, shorted or high-resistance squib loop of the airbag the module assigns to this code
Connector or its position lock not fully engaged
Fault or unsuitable software in the restraint control module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side or curtain protection may be reduced on the affected side
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0026.t: Left Side Deployment Stage 2 Loop Open
B0026.d: B0026 is missing from the public J2012 lists. General Motors documents it in older restraint modules with a meaning other than the title: on the 2006 Saab 9-5, B0026 is an open circuit in driver frontal stage 1, set when the measured resistance stays above 4.5 ohms, tolerance 0.2, for 2 seconds; the Saab 9-3 manuals add bytes for an open loop and too high resistance in the same driver circuit. GM bulletin 08-09-41-002H blames loose connector position locks for B0026 on 2005-14 models such as the Cobalt, Pontiac G5 and GMC Envoy. An open second stage of a left side airbag is not publicly documented under this code. If the driver loop is open, the steering wheel airbag may not fire. Airbag lamp on.
c: Airbag connector or its position lock not fully seated (GM 08-09-41-002H)
Broken track in the clock spring (driver loop on older GM/Saab)
Open squib inside the airbag module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on the vehicle, the driver airbag may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0028.d: B0028 is the right-hand twin of B0020: the firing loop of the right front side airbag, normally in the outer flank of the passenger seat. Honda asked for parts from 2018-20 Accord and CR-V and from the 2015 TLX that stored B0028-13, an open or raised resistance in the passenger side airbag inflator. FCA traces B0028-13 on the Cherokee and Chrysler 200 to the jumper harness in the seat, and Toyota's 2022 Tundra stored B002811 or B002812 because the wireless phone charger disturbed the module. Mitsubishi confirms a short to ground after 2 seconds. The older GM numbering differs: the 2006 Saab 9-5 and the 9-3 used B0028 for low resistance in the passenger side bag loop, under 1.5 ohms. Airbag lamp on.
c: Poor contact or corrosion at the side airbag connector or jumper harness under or in the seat
Internal fault in the right seat side airbag inflator
Lead pinched or stretched by seat adjustment
Restraint module software reacting to interference (Toyota Tundra 2022)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right front side airbag may not deploy in a side impact
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0029.d: B0029 stands for the first firing loop of the right curtain airbag. FCA's STAR case S2010000001 for the 2019 Ram heavy-duty pickup reads B0029-11 as a ground short in right curtain squib 1 and sends the technician to the wiring at the C-pillar trim fixings. Mitsubishi lists the right curtain module under B0029 and sets the ground short after 2 seconds. On the A-Class, CLA and GLB Mercedes-Benz stores B002913 for an open squib of the right window bag. Older GM modules used the number for the passenger side airbag: the 2006 Saab 9-5 sets it when resistance stays above 4.5 ohms for 2 seconds. B002A is the second right curtain loop. Airbag lamp on; the curtain may not deploy in a side impact or rollover.
c: Lead pinched or chafed at pillar trim fixings (FCA S2010000001)
Raised contact resistance at the curtain or restraint module connector
Internal fault in the right curtain airbag module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right curtain airbag may not deploy in a side impact or rollover
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B002A.d: B002A is the second firing loop of the right curtain airbag, needed only where the right side has two curtain inflators or a separate curtain section for the rear seats. Mercedes-Benz uses it that way on the A-Class, CLA and GLB: B002A13 marks an open squib in the right rear window bag, while the front part reports B0029; a known trigger was poor contact at the control unit plug (LI54.21-P-070658). A TRW and Ford patent describes front-row and rear-row curtains that inflate separately and may be tethered together at the B-pillar. Where curtains also deploy in a rollover, FMVSS 226 requires a readiness indicator the driver can see. Airbag lamp on; head protection for the right rear seat may be missing.
c: Raised contact resistance at the restraint module connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Damaged lead to the rear curtain section at the C-pillar or roof rail
Internal fault in the rear right curtain airbag module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Head protection for the right rear seat may be missing
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0030.t: Second Row Left Side Airbag Deployment Control
B0030.d: In J2012 the B003x block covers the second seat row, and B0030 is the left rear side airbag, mounted in the rear door or the outer backrest. Mitsubishi files B0030 under the rear side airbag module LH and sets a short to another circuit after 2 seconds. Mercedes-Benz reads B003013 as an open squib in the left rear sidebag on the A-Class, CLA and GLB, often caused by higher contact resistance at the restraint unit connector (LI54.21-P-070658). The older GM numbering differs: on the 2006 Saab 9-5, B0030 is a passenger side airbag loop whose pin voltage is above 4.1 or below 1.0 volts for 2 seconds, and the Saab 9-3 reads it as a passenger side bag short. The right-hand rear twin is B0038. Airbag lamp on.
c: Raised contact resistance at the restraint module or rear side airbag connector
Damaged lead in the rear door transition or rear seat backrest
Internal fault in the rear left side airbag module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Rear left side airbag may not deploy in a side impact
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0031.t: Second Row Left Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control
B0031.d: B0031 points to the first firing stage of a frontal airbag that protects the left rear passenger, so it can only be stored where such a bag exists. The known production case is Mercedes-Benz's S-Class of 2020: an optional rear airbag (standard on the Maybach) unfolds from the back of the front seat for the two outer rear seats, built as a gas-filled tube frame that draws ambient air into its cushion. No carmaker publishes B0031 with this meaning. GM used the number differently: the Saab 9-4X 2011 manual groups B0031 with its front seat side airbag codes. Stage 2 and 3 of the same bag follow as B0032 and B0033. The airbag lamp lights and the rear bag may not fire in a frontal crash.
c: Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Internal fault in the rear-seat airbag module in the front seatback
Lead stretched or pinched by the seat track or folding mechanism
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left rear passenger may lose frontal airbag protection in a crash
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0032.t: Second Row Left Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control
B0032.d: B0032 concerns a second igniter for the rear-seat frontal airbag on the left. A second stage lets the module add gas later or skip it, depending on crash severity and on who sits behind the seat; a Mercedes-Benz filing for a backrest-mounted rear airbag allows separate deployment devices for its chambers so they can fire in sequence. In that car the rear bag's tube frame is filled with compressed gas while its centre takes in outside air. No published DTC table assigns B0032 to this use. GM's Global A modules give the number to the left rear belt pretensioner: the Saab 9-4X 2011 sets it after 2 seconds of a short, an open, above 4.2 ohms or below 1.4 ohms. Airbag lamp on.
c: Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Open or short only in the stage 2 pair of wires to the rear airbag
Faulty second igniter inside the rear-seat airbag module
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Rear-seat airbag may inflate with less force or not at all
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0033.t: Second Row Left Frontal Stage 3 Deployment Control
B0033.d: B0033 is the third deployment element of a frontal airbag for the left second-row seat. A third igniter can be a further gas chamber; a Breed patent describes an inflator with one igniter per chamber whose firing order and 0 to 25 ms delays the controller chooses. Mercedes-Benz fills the stage 3 slot of its front bags with the vent valve squib (B000313, B001213), a model for what stage 3 may mean behind a seat. No carmaker documents B0033 for a rear bag. GM bulletin 08-09-41-002H names B0033 with bytes 04, 0D and 0E in its CPA retainer bulletin for numerous GM cars and trucks of 2005 to 2014, where the number belongs to another GM loop. Airbag lamp on.
c: Connector position assurance lock missing or not seated, so the plug works loose
Damaged stage 3 lead or igniter in the rear airbag
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Adaptive inflation of the left rear airbag is lost
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0034.d: B0034 is absent from the J2012 lists, which skip from B0033 to B0038 in the second-row block, and no carmaker or bulletin documents it publicly; the code cannot be traced to a real vehicle. The title describes a second firing stage for the right side airbag. Such bags are rare: Ford's far-side impact patent treats thorax, pelvis and head bags as single-setting because of their size, while Autoliv covers chest and pelvis with a two-chamber bag, not with two firing stages. Right front side airbags carry the J2012 code B0028; Mitsubishi, for example, checks that loop for 2 seconds before storing a fault. If B0034 is read, the module and text shown by the scan tool are what count. Airbag lamp on.
c: Poor contact or corrosion at the side airbag connector or jumper harness under or in the seat
Fault in the squib loop the module assigns to this code
Fault or unsuitable software in the restraint control module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side airbag protection may be reduced
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0036.t: Right Side Deployment Stage 2 Loop Short to Ground
B0036.d: B0036 appears neither in the public J2012 lists nor in any accessible manufacturer document, so the code is not publicly verifiable. Its title describes a short to ground in a second stage of the right side airbag. How restraint modules handle such a fault is known from other codes: Mitsubishi stores B0028-11 when the right front side airbag circuit has been grounded for 2 seconds, and the GM manual for the Saab 9-4X sets byte 02 on the passenger seat side airbag code B0021 after a ground short of the same length. GM adds that a badly seated connector lock can let the shorting bars bridge both firing leads, so connectors are checked first with byte 02. Two-stage side airbags are uncommon. Airbag lamp on; the bag may not deploy.
c: Chafed side airbag lead touching the seat frame or body
Connector lock not engaged, shorting bars bridge the loop
Internal short in the side airbag module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side airbag may not deploy in a side impact
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0038.t: Second Row Right Side Airbag Deployment Control
B0038.d: B0038 watches the firing loop of the side airbag for the right-hand second-row seat, fitted in the rear door trim or in the outer bolster of the rear backrest. Mitsubishi lists it as rear side airbag module RH with exactly this J2012 wording and logs B0038-12 when the circuit has been shorted to supply for 2 seconds. On Mercedes-Benz compact models (A-Class, CLA, GLB) B003813 is an open squib in the right rear sidebag. A GM patent family keeps rear-row side bags on their own gas generators, separate from the front-row system. GM's Saab 9-4X 2011 manual lists B0038 in the same procedure as its front seat side bags. Left twin: B0030. The airbag lamp is lit.
c: Poor contact at the rear side airbag connector in the door or rear seat
Internal fault in the right rear side airbag module
Lead chafed against a powered wire, e.g. at the rear seat fold or B-pillar
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear passenger may lack side airbag protection
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0039.t: Second Row Right Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control
B0039.d: B0039 belongs to the right-hand rear-seat frontal airbag, stage 1, which is the primary charge that the module fires in any frontal crash severe enough to need the bag. The bag sits in the back of the passenger seat ahead; Mercedes-Benz offers this layout as an S-Class option and fits it as standard to the Maybach, where it is meant to ease head and neck loads on belted outer rear passengers. An older Daimler application already described a bag at the rear of a front seat that spreads a channel frame and fills with ambient air. No public DTC table pairs B0039 with this bag. GM Global A modules use B0039 for the right rear belt pretensioner instead (Saab 9-4X 2011). Airbag lamp on.
c: Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Internal fault in the right rear-seat airbag module
Lead stretched or pinched by the seat track or folding mechanism
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear passenger may lose frontal airbag protection
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B003A.t: Second Row Right Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control
B003A.d: B003A covers stage 2 of the right rear-seat frontal airbag. The second charge allows the module to soften or strengthen inflation; for a rear bag this matters because the person behind the front seat may be an adult, a child or a child seat facing either way, a point Mercedes-Benz stressed when it introduced the S-Class rear airbag in 2020. The Mercedes filing for a bag on a sliding front backrest provides separate deployment devices so its chambers can fire one after the other. No vehicle maker documents B003A, and no bulletin with it is on record at NHTSA. A stage 2 code alone suggests the stage 2 wires or igniter rather than the whole bag. Airbag lamp on.
c: Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Open or short only in the stage 2 pair of wires
Faulty second igniter in the right rear-seat airbag
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Rear airbag may not adapt its inflation to the occupant
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B003B.t: Second Row Right Frontal Stage 3 Deployment Control
B003B.d: B003B is the third firing element of the right rear-seat frontal airbag. In front airbags Mercedes-Benz uses this third position for the squib that opens a vent valve and lets gas escape (B000313 driver, B001213 passenger); a patent from Breed shows the other option, a third gas chamber with its own igniter that the controller can fire later, for example in a second impact. Which of these a rear bag would use is not published, and no carmaker documents B003B. If it is stored, the module has found the third element out of range in resistance or voltage. Stage 1 and 2 of the same bag report as B0039 and B003A. The airbag lamp stays on.
c: Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Damaged stage 3 lead or vent squib in the right rear airbag
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear airbag may deploy without its adaptive third stage
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0040.t: Third Row Left Side Airbag Deployment Control
B0040.d: B0040 is reserved for a side airbag at the left seat of a third row, as found in some seven-seat SUVs and vans; most of them protect that row only with an extended curtain. A Joyson (TK Holdings) patent states its seatback side module may serve any row, third included, and a GM application gives rear-row side bags their own gas generators and allows the rear row to be the third. No maker documents B0040 with this meaning. Earlier GM modules assign it elsewhere: Saab manuals for the 9-5 of 2006 and the 9-3 treat B0040 as low resistance in the driver side airbag loop, under 1.5 ohms with 0.2 tolerance for 2 seconds; bulletin 08-09-41-002H also names it for loose CPA retainers. Airbag lamp on.
c: Poor contact at the side airbag connector of the third-row seat or rear quarter trim
Lead strained by folding or removing the third-row seat
Internal fault in the third-row side airbag
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left third-row occupant may lack side airbag protection
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0041.t: Third Row Left Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control
B0041.d: B0041 would report the first stage of a frontal airbag for the left third-row seat, which would have to deploy from the back of the second-row seat in front of it. Such bags are described in patents, for instance a Daimler application for an airbag at the rear of a front seat and a Mercedes-Benz filing that compensates for a sliding seat with stacked chambers, but no production vehicle with third-row frontal airbags is known; the S-Class rear airbag serves the second row only. No maker documents B0041. GM's old numbering is unrelated: for the Saab 9-5 of 2006 B0041 means an open driver side airbag loop, read as more than 4.5 ohms over 2 seconds. Airbag lamp on.
c: Loose connector of the airbag lead in the second-row seatback
Lead strained when the second-row seat is folded or slid
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal airbag for the left third-row seat may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0042.t: Third Row Left Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control
B0042.d: B0042 stands for the second stage of a frontal airbag aimed at the left third-row passenger. A second stage only makes sense with an inflator that has two independently fired charges, as in Breed's multi-chamber design where the controller picks which chamber fires first and the gap between them. No carmaker documents B0042 for the third row, and no series car with such a bag is known. The older GM meaning is clear-cut: Saab's 9-5 (2006) and 9-3 manuals define B0042 as driver frontal stage 2 loop resistance below 1.5 ohms lasting 2 seconds, and the GM CPA retainer bulletin 08-09-41-002H covers it too. Airbag lamp on.
c: Open or short only in the stage 2 wiring
Connector lock not engaged at the airbag plug
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Adaptive two-stage inflation for this seat is unavailable
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0043.t: Third Row Left Frontal Stage 3 Deployment Control
B0043.d: B0043 completes the left third-row frontal group as its stage 3 element. By analogy with front airbags this can be a vent valve squib, as Mercedes-Benz uses for B000313 and B001213, or a further gas chamber like the third chamber in Breed's patent that is kept for a second collision. No public source ties B0043 to a third-row bag. GM gives the number a separate, documented meaning in its older modules: the Saab 9-5 of 2006 stores B0043 if the driver stage 2 terminal sits above 4.1 V or under 1.0 V for 2 seconds, and the 9-3 splits it into shorts to supply, to ground or to another firing loop. Check which airbag the scan tool names. Airbag lamp on.
c: Short between two firing loops in a shared harness
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Third deployment element of this airbag is disabled
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0046.d: B0046 appears in none of the accessible J2012 code lists, which jump from B0043 to B0048, and no carmaker or bulletin uses it publicly, so the code cannot be traced to a vehicle. Its title describes an open firing loop of the left curtain airbag that drops from the roof rail. J2012 normally encodes that fault as B0021 with failure type 13: Mitsubishi stores B0021-13 when the left curtain circuit has been open for 2 seconds, and Mercedes-Benz reads B002113 as an open left windowbag squib. GM's Global A modules report the same fault as B0016 04 for the left roof rail airbag. If B0046 is read, trust the text the scan tool shows. Airbag lamp on.
c: Unplugged or loose curtain airbag connector at the pillar or roof rail
Broken lead in the roof rail harness, e.g. after headliner work
Open igniter inside the left curtain airbag
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left curtain airbag may not deploy in a side impact or rollover
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0047.t: Left Curtain Deployment Loop Short to Ground
B0047.d: B0047 is missing from the accessible J2012 lists as well, and no vehicle maker or NHTSA bulletin documents it, so it is not publicly traceable. The title names a grounded left curtain airbag loop; this inflatable curtain covers the side windows in side impacts and rollovers. Under J2012 this fault is normally stored as B0021 with byte 11: Mitsubishi sets B0021-11 once the left curtain circuit has been grounded for 2 seconds. GM Global A uses B0016 02 for a grounded left roof rail airbag loop, also after 2 seconds. A grounded lead often sits where the roof harness passes sharp body edges or trim clips. Airbag lamp on.
c: Insulation of the curtain lead chafed through against the body
Lead pinched by a pillar trim or headliner clip
Internal short to housing in the left curtain airbag
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left curtain airbag deployment may be blocked
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0048.t: Third Row Right Side Airbag Deployment Control
B0048.d: B0048 is the right-hand counterpart of B0040: the deployment loop of a side airbag for the right seat in a third row. Few vehicles have one, because the third row usually relies on a curtain that reaches back to the D-pillar. Patent literature covers the hardware: Joyson's seatback side module is described for any seating row including the third, and GM's application treats each rear row as a separate system with its own generator that may stay idle when another fires. No manufacturer documents B0048, and NHTSA holds no bulletin with it. For a second-row right side bag, Mitsubishi shows the usual logic under B0038, a fault confirmed after 2 seconds. Airbag lamp on.
c: Poor contact at the third-row right side airbag connector
Lead damaged by folding, sliding or removing the third-row seat
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right third-row occupant may lack side airbag protection
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0049.t: Third Row Right Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control
B0049.d: B0049 marks the stage 1 charge of a right third-row frontal bag, the main charge of a bag that would have to come out of the second-row seatback ahead of it. Daimler's application for a bag mounted behind a front seat and Mercedes-Benz's later design with chambers that bridge a changing seat gap show how such a bag can be built; in series, Mercedes offers rear frontal airbags only for the outer second-row seats of its S-Class and Maybach models. No carmaker documents B0049 and no bulletin cites it. A third-row frontal code on a vehicle without that equipment points to a module set up for the wrong variant. Airbag lamp on.
c: Loose connector of the airbag lead in the second-row seatback
Lead strained when the second-row seat is folded or slid
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal airbag for the right third-row seat may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B004A.t: Third Row Right Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control
B004A.d: B004A is the second-stage loop of the right third-row frontal airbag. Stage 2 is a separately ignited charge: Breed's patent shows an inflator whose chambers each carry their own igniter, fired alone, together or with a delay chosen by the controller, and Mercedes-Benz's rear airbag filing allows one deployment device per chamber for sequential filling. No published DTC table, vehicle maker or bulletin connects B004A to a real vehicle. If it appears, the stage 2 circuit of that bag is out of range while stage 1 (B0049) may still be fine; the left-hand equivalent is B0042. Airbag lamp on.
c: Open or short only in the stage 2 wiring
Loose connector in the second-row seatback
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Two-stage inflation for the right third-row seat is lost
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B004B.t: Third Row Right Frontal Stage 3 Deployment Control
B004B.d: B004B is the last code of the third-row frontal block: stage 3 of the right-hand bag. What a third element does is up to the maker. Mercedes-Benz shows one answer in its front airbags, where the third slot is a vent valve squib (B000313, B001213); Breed's patent shows another, a third chamber held back for a later second impact. Mercedes-Benz's rear airbag filing also links an extra chamber to the first through valves or throttles. No vehicle maker documents B004B and no NHTSA bulletin contains it. A fault here leaves the bag without its third element; stage 1 and 2 are B0049 and B004A. Airbag lamp on.
c: Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
Loose connector in the second-row seatback
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right third-row airbag may deploy without its third element
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed

B0050.d: B0050 monitors the switch in the driver's belt buckle that tells the restraint module whether the belt is latched; the module uses it for the belt reminder and for choosing the airbag and pretensioner response. Usually a two-wire Hall sensor whose current changes when the steel tongue enters the buckle. FCA documents B0050 with this wording: its 2016-17 parts notes for the Dart, Cherokee and Chrysler 200 list B0050-13 as an open circuit of the driver belt sensor, and TSB 10-001-23 for the 2015-22 Renegade and Fiat 500X lists B0050-13 and B0050-1D (out of range), traced to terminal corrosion at the inline buckle connector under the seat. Mitsubishi uses B0052 for the passenger buckle. The airbag lamp lights.
c: Corroded terminals at the inline connector between buckle and seat harness
Faulty Hall sensor or switch inside the driver buckle
Buckle lead pinched or stretched by the seat track
Foreign object or debris in the buckle confusing the sensor
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Belt reminder for the driver may warn wrongly or stay silent
Restraint module may treat the driver as unbelted and adapt airbag and pretensioner firing
Safety note: the buckle connector sits under the seat next to the side airbag and pretensioner plugs; disconnect the battery and observe the wait time before unplugging anything

B0051.t: First Row Center Seat Belt Sensor
B0051.d: B0051 belongs to the buckle sensor of a middle seat in the front row, found in pickups and vans with a front bench for three. FMVSS 208 requires a belt warning only for the outboard front seats, so a centre buckle sensor is extra equipment that feeds the restraint module and, where fitted, a reminder for that place. Typical hardware is a non-contacting Hall buckle switch as offered by CTS and described by Allegro. No carmaker documents B0051 with this meaning; Mitsubishi uses the same J2012 pattern for the passenger buckle, B0052, with an open or invalid signal for 2 seconds. Older GM modules (Saab 9-5 2006, 9-3) store B0051 as Deployment Commanded, a crash record. Airbag lamp on.
c: Loose or corroded connector of the centre buckle under the bench seat
Faulty Hall switch in the centre buckle
Lead strained by a fold-down centre seat or console
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Centre seat belt reminder may be wrong or missing
Safety note: the buckle connector sits under the seat next to the side airbag and pretensioner plugs; disconnect the battery and observe the wait time before unplugging anything

B0052.d: B0052 concerns the front passenger's buckle sensor, reporting to the airbag module whether the tongue is latched. That signal feeds the passenger belt reminder that FMVSS 208 requires at the front outboard seats and helps the module decide how the passenger airbag and pretensioner fire. Mitsubishi uses the code in exactly this sense: its SRS manual stores B0052 with byte 11, 12, 13, 29 or 2B for a grounded line, short to supply, open circuit, invalid signal or short to another line, each after 2 seconds with the ignition on. FCA parts guidance for its restraint controller in the Dart, Cherokee and Chrysler 200 calls B0052-13 an open passenger belt sensor. GM, by contrast, logs a deployment under B0052 in its 2011 Global A modules. Airbag lamp on.
c: Loose or corroded buckle connector under the passenger seat
Faulty Hall sensor inside the passenger buckle
Buckle lead pinched or torn by the seat rails or a mat fixing
Input fault inside the airbag control module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger belt reminder warns although the belt is fastened, or stays silent
Passenger airbag and pretensioner strategy may assume an unbelted occupant
Safety note: the buckle plug sits under the seat next to airbag and pretensioner plugs; only unplug it with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0053.t: Second Row Left Seat Belt Sensor
B0053.d: B0053 is the J2012 slot for the buckle sensor at the second row's left seat. Rear buckle sensors drive the rear belt reminder: for vehicles built from September 2028, FMVSS 208 S7.5(c) demands a start-up display of which rear belts are fastened or open and a warning when one is unlatched while driving. No carmaker documents B0053 with this meaning publicly; the closest documented case is Mitsubishi's passenger code B0052, set for an open, shorted or invalid buckle signal lasting 2 seconds. Older GM airbag modules give the number another meaning: the Saab 9-3 and the 2006 Saab 9-5 store B0053 when a deployment was commanded while a firing loop fault was present, a code that cannot be erased after a front airbag deployment.
c: Loose or corroded buckle connector under the left rear seat
Faulty switch or Hall sensor in the left rear buckle
Lead damaged by folding or sliding the second-row seat
Older GM/Saab module: deployment record with a loop fault, module replacement needed
s: Airbag or rear belt warning lamp on
Rear belt display shows the left seat wrongly as fastened or unfastened
Safety note: the buckle plug sits under the seat near pretensioner and side airbag plugs; only unplug it with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0054.t: Second Row Center Seat Belt Sensor
B0054.d: B0054 is reserved for the buckle sensor of the middle seat in the second row. That position often has its buckle in a split bench or under a fold-down armrest, so the lead runs through moving seat parts. The rear warning required by FMVSS 208 S7.5(c) for vehicles made from September 2028 covers every rear designated seat, the middle one included. Ford's patent for rear belt monitoring counts latched belts once the car passes 3 mph with the doors shut and warns only when that count drops, so a passenger who changes seats is not flagged. The sensor itself is usually a Hall switch that detects the steel tongue in the buckle. No carmaker documents B0054 publicly; Mitsubishi's passenger code B0052 shows how such a buckle fault is set.
c: Lead of the centre buckle strained at the split bench or armrest hinge
Loose or corroded connector of the centre buckle
Faulty Hall switch in the centre buckle
s: Airbag or rear belt warning lamp on
Middle rear seat shown wrongly in the belt status display
Safety note: buckle plugs under the rear bench lie close to pretensioner wiring; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0055.t: Second Row Right Seat Belt Sensor
B0055.d: B0055 stands for the buckle sensor of the right seat in the second row, behind the front passenger and in vans often beside the sliding door. Where that seat is a removable captain's chair, a disconnect in the buckle lead is unavoidable; IEE points out in a patent that a wireless buckle sensor alone cannot tell the module whether the seat is fitted, so a missing signal may mean a fault or simply an empty floor. A seat refitted with its plug left open is therefore a common trigger. CTS supplies non-contact Hall buckle switches for such uses. The rear belt warning of FMVSS 208, section S7.5(c), applies to this seat for vehicles made after 1 September 2028. No carmaker documents B0055 publicly; the Mitsubishi passenger code B0052 is the nearest documented model.
c: Seat connector not engaged after the removable seat was refitted
Corroded buckle connector, e.g. from wet floor near the sliding door
Faulty sensor in the right rear buckle
s: Airbag or rear belt warning lamp on
Right rear seat shown wrongly or missing in the belt status display
Safety note: seat and buckle plugs under the seat lie near pretensioner and side airbag lines; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0056.t: Third Row Left Seat Belt Sensor
B0056.d: B0056 belongs to the left third-row seat's buckle sensor, found in larger SUVs, minivans and seven-seat estates. Third-row seats usually fold flat into the floor, so the buckle lead has to pass through the folding mechanism and is flexed every time the cargo area is extended. In Ford's patent for rear belt monitoring the third-row bench is the hard-wired part of the system, while only the removable second row needs a wireless link. FMVSS 208 S7.5(c) extends the rear belt warning to all rear rows for vehicles built from September 2028. A Hall switch that senses the latched tongue is the usual hardware. No carmaker documents B0056 with this wording publicly, nor does any service bulletin mention it; Mitsubishi's B0052 is the documented model for this fault type.
c: Buckle lead broken or chafed in the fold-flat mechanism of the third row
Loose or corroded connector at the third-row seat
Faulty sensor in the left third-row buckle
s: Airbag or rear belt warning lamp on
Fault may appear only with the third-row seat folded or raised
Safety note: third-row buckle plugs can sit near pretensioner wiring; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0057.t: Third Row Center Seat Belt Sensor
B0057.d: In J2012, B0057 is the buckle sensor for the third row's centre seat, a position found only in eight-seat vans and SUVs. FMVSS 208 S7.5(c) will require a belt warning there from September 2028. No carmaker documents B0057 publicly with this meaning. Older GM airbag modules give the number a different job: the 2006 Saab 9-5 and the Saab 9-3 store B0057 when the passenger pretensioner loop resistance stays under 1.5 ± 0.2 ohms for 2 seconds. GM bulletin 14609 lists B0057 with B0058, B0059 and B0064 to B0066 on 2004-09 Colorado and Canyon extended cabs, whose rear door harness can suffer fatigue breaks and can disable the front pretensioners; GM extended coverage to 10 years. On older GM vehicles, check the pretensioner loop first.
c: Faulty buckle sensor or lead at the middle third-row seat
Older GM trucks: broken wire in the rear door harness to the pretensioner (bulletin 14609)
Older GM/Saab module: shorted passenger pretensioner squib or connector
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on the module: wrong belt status for the middle third-row seat, or passenger pretensioner possibly inactive
Safety note: buckle and pretensioner plugs carry firing circuits nearby; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0058.t: Third Row Right Seat Belt Sensor
B0058.d: B0058 is the J2012 code for the buckle sensor at the right seat of the third row. The sensor reports a latched or free belt to the module that runs the rear belt display, which FMVSS 208 S7.5(c) makes mandatory for every rear seat from September 2028. Fold-flat third rows and access from the right-hand sliding door put the lead under strain. No carmaker documents B0058 publicly with this meaning. Older GM modules again differ: on the 2006 Saab 9-5 B0058 means an open passenger pretensioner loop, with more than 4.5 ± 0.2 ohms for 2 seconds, while the Saab 9-3 also knows a high-resistance variant. GM bulletin 14609 for 2004-09 Colorado and Canyon extended cabs covers B0058 among the pretensioner codes caused by broken rear door wires.
c: Buckle lead of the right third-row seat damaged by folding or loading
Older GM/Saab module: open passenger pretensioner loop, e.g. broken rear door wire
Faulty sensor in the right third-row buckle
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on the module: right third-row seat shown wrongly, or passenger pretensioner may not fire
Safety note: buckle and pretensioner plugs carry firing circuits nearby; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0060.d: B0060 refers to a belt tension sensor in the driver's belt, a force gauge usually bolted to the lower anchor with the webbing running through it. In Delphi's design a spring-loaded slider moves against the belt pull and a Hall element between two magnets turns the travel into a voltage; the springs give way at roughly 5 to 15 lb. CTS, which calls itself the market leader, builds such sensors in several mounting styles. A second Delphi patent has the sensor report its value in 3-lb steps over a two-wire line and flag readings outside the valid band as a high or low fault. Tension sensing serves mainly the passenger seat; a driver-side unit is rare. No carmaker documents B0060 publicly; Saab's older airbag modules do not list it. Airbag lamp on.
c: Loose or corroded connector at the anchor-mounted tension sensor
Tension sensor output stuck or out of range, e.g. jammed slider
Sensor lead pinched under the seat or at the sill trim
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Restraint module may fall back to a default firing strategy for the driver
Safety note: the sensor plug sits beside the seat near pretensioner and side airbag plugs; only unplug it with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0061.d: B0061 covers the belt tension sensor of the front passenger seat, a key input for passenger occupant classification. FMVSS 208 lets carmakers meet the child-seat rules for advanced airbags by fitting a system that automatically switches the passenger airbag off for small occupants. A child seat strapped in tightly presses into the cushion and can look as heavy as an adult on the weight sensor; the tension sensor exposes that. Delphi's patent lets the occupant module subtract belt load from seat weight and suppress the airbag above a calibrated pull of about 30 lb, and the sensor reports out-of-range values as faults. No carmaker documents B0061 publicly with this meaning. Saab 9-3 modules use it for a low driver curtain loop resistance.
c: Loose or corroded plug at the passenger belt tension sensor
Tension sensor reading out of range or stuck
Input fault in the occupant classification or airbag module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag status indicator may show an unexpected on or off state
A tightly fastened child seat may not be recognised reliably
Safety note: the sensor plug sits beside the passenger seat near airbag and pretensioner plugs; only unplug it with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0062.t: Knee Airbag Deployment Loop Short to Ground
B0062.d: None of the publicly available J2012 code lists contain B0062; they jump from B0061 to B0070, and no carmaker describes it with the knee airbag meaning shown in the title. J2012 files knee airbag loops under B0004 for the driver and B0013 for the passenger, with the fault type in the added byte; Mercedes-Benz logs kneebag squib faults as B000413 and B001313, and in that scheme a grounded loop would carry byte 11 instead. The only public use of B0062 is at Saab: 9-3 airbag modules (manuals of 2003 and 2007) store it for the driver-side curtain or rollover bar loop, with byte 04 for open and 0E for resistance too high. Knee airbags sit in the lower dash; an IIHS study of 414 crash tests found little overall benefit for belted drivers.
c: Knee airbag lead chafed against a dash bracket or steering column part
Damaged knee airbag connector after work under the dashboard
Saab 9-3: fault in the driver-side curtain or rollover bar loop instead
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Knee airbag may stay inactive in a frontal crash
Safety note: knee airbag plugs sit under the dashboard; do not probe the circuit and only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0064.t: Driver Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Loop Resistance Low
B0064.d: No publicly available J2012 code list includes B0064; there, B0060 names the driver belt tension sensor. Older airbag modules from General Motors do use it: on the 2006 Saab 9-5, B0064 is set when the resistance of the driver pretensioner loop stays below 1.5 ohms, with a 0.2-ohm tolerance, for 2 seconds; B0065 marks an interrupted loop and B0066 a voltage at pin 34 outside 1.0 to 4.1 V. Saab 9-3 manuals of 2003 and 2007 describe the same fault as too little resistance at the driver's belt tensioner. The module still attempts to fire the pretensioner in a crash. GM bulletin 14609 names B0064 among the codes caused by fatigue breaks in the rear door harness of Colorado and Canyon extended cab trucks, model years 2004 to 2009. Airbag lamp on.
c: Pretensioner leads shorted together, e.g. squashed harness at the B-pillar
Colorado/Canyon extended cab: fatigued wires in the rear door harness (bulletin 14609)
Internal fault of the driver pretensioner squib
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver belt pretensioner may not work properly in a crash
Safety note: pretensioner plugs sit at the B-pillar or under the seat; do not probe the loop and only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed

B0070.t: Driver Seat Belt Pretensioner A Deployment Control
B0070.d: B0070 covers the firing loop of the driver's first (A) belt pretensioner, the squib the airbag module ignites to take slack out of the belt in a crash. A short or open in that loop lets the module no longer count on the device, so it lights the airbag lamp. Toyota names the code in exactly this sense: its Tundra bulletin T-SB-0057-22 (model year 2022) lists B007011 (short to ground) and B007012 (short to battery), there triggered by the wireless Qi charger and cured by reprogramming the SRS ECU. J2012 does not fix which device is A; GM notes that a front seat may carry a retractor, buckle or anchor pretensioner, or more than one. Mitsubishi logs its front retractor units under its own codes B1029/B102A. Saab 9-3 airbag modules use B0070 for the passenger curtain loop instead.
c: Loose or corroded plug at the driver pretensioner (B-pillar base or seat side)
Firing lead chafed by seat rails or trim clips
Interference from added electronics, e.g. a wireless charger (Toyota Tundra 2022, ECU update)
Internal fault in the pretensioner squib
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver belt is not tightened in a crash; airbags themselves are usually unaffected
Safety note: the pretensioner is a pyrotechnic part; work on it only with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed, ideally at a specialist workshop

B0071.t: First Row Center Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control
B0071.d: B0071 is reserved for a pretensioner at the middle seat of the first row, which exists only where a three-person front bench is fitted. The airbag module would watch this squib like any other firing loop and flag an open, a short or a resistance outside its window. No carmaker publishes B0071 with this meaning. Mercedes-Benz does show that such a device can be present: its information LI54.21-P-070658 (A-, CLA-, GLB-Class) lists an open circuit at the emergency tensioning retractor in the centre of the first seat row, but files it under its own code B1B36. GM places buckle pretensioners at the inner flank of a front seat. In the airbag modules of the Saab 9-3 (2003, 2007), B0071 stands for a short in the passenger curtain or rollover-bar circuit, a different part altogether.
c: Plug under the front bench centre seat loose or corroded
Harness damaged when the centre seat or console is folded or removed
Airbag module configured for a centre pretensioner the vehicle does not have
Internal fault of the centre pretensioner
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Middle front occupant gets no belt pretensioning in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic component; disconnect the battery, wait the specified time and leave the work to a specialist workshop

B0072.t: Passenger Seat Belt Pretensioner A Deployment Control
B0072.d: B0072 reports a fault in the deployment loop of the front passenger's A-stage belt pretensioner. While that loop is faulty the device cannot be relied on to fire, so the airbag module lights its lamp and keeps the code. Toyota uses the number this way: T-SB-0057-22 for the 2022 Tundra and Tundra Hybrid lists B007212, a short to battery, among the codes the wireless charger can provoke, and the remedy is an SRS ECU reprogramming. The passenger seat often carries further devices; Mercedes logs the passenger's belt end fitting tensioner and retractor as B007A and B007F, and FCA ties B007F to the passenger retractor at the B-pillar. NHTSA's 2013 evaluation explains how buckle and retractor pretensioners remove slack. Whatever the hardware, a stored B0072 means passenger pretensioning is not assured.
c: Passenger pretensioner plug not latched or corroded
Lead pinched at the passenger seat base or B-pillar trim
Interference from added electronics such as a wireless charger
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Front passenger belt may stay slack in a crash
Safety note: the pretensioner is pyrotechnic; only handle it de-energised (battery off, wait time) and have it serviced at a specialist workshop

B0073.t: Second Row Left Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control
B0073.d: B0073 concerns the pretensioner at the left outer seat of the second row, normally built into the rear retractor. Mitsubishi documents it under exactly this name: with the ignition on, its airbag sensor unit stores B0073 with byte 11, 12, 13, 1A or 1B for a short to ground, a short to power, an open, lines shorted to each other or excessive resistance, and with byte 55 when the stored configuration does not match the vehicle; each fault must last 2 seconds. Toyota's Tundra bulletin T-SB-0057-22 lists B007311 and B007312. IIHS frontal tests with a dummy in the left rear seat show why such units are now spreading to the back row. GM uses the number differently: bulletin 22-NA-170 for the Equinox and Terrain links B0073 to water in the right front seat harness connector X320.
c: Plug at the left rear retractor loose or damaged after trim or seat removal
Harness to the left rear pretensioner shorted to ground or power
Airbag module configuration does not match the fitted rear pretensioners (Mitsubishi byte 55)
Internal fault of the left rear pretensioner or of the airbag module
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left rear occupant gets no belt pretensioning in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic part in the rear retractor; work only with the system de-energised and preferably at a specialist workshop

B0074.t: Second Row Center Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control
B0074.d: B0074 would flag the firing loop of a pretensioner at the second row's middle seat. Rear centre belts with their own pretensioner are rare; IIHS rear-seat tests concentrate on the outboard positions, and no carmaker publishes B0074 with the J2012 meaning.
