The code is common in GM vehicles, but with an older meaning: the 2011 Saab 9-4X sets B0074 00/04 when the passenger presence module loses its seat sensor mat, GM's Impala bulletin PIE0485A (2015–2018) covers B0074-0D, and campaign N182188910 for the 2017 Buick Verano ties B0074 0D/0E to a pinched presence sensor wire that suppresses the passenger airbag. In a GM vehicle, B0074 therefore points to the front passenger seat sensing, not a rear belt. Where the code does mean a rear centre pretensioner, the airbag lamp is on and that unit is inactive.
c: On GM vehicles, fault in the passenger presence sensor mat or its pinched wire (older GM meaning)
Plug of the rear centre pretensioner disturbed when the bench is folded or removed
Open or short in the harness to the rear centre seat
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM vehicles also passenger airbag status shows OFF with an adult seated
Safety note: restraint parts may be pyrotechnic or part of the airbag control; disconnect the battery, observe the wait time and use a specialist workshop

B0075.t: Second Row Right Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control
B0075.d: B0075 is the right-hand counterpart of B0073: the pretensioner at the second row's right outer seat. Mitsubishi lists it as PRE-TEN REAR RH with the J2012 title and tests the circuit whenever the ignition is on; byte 11 stands for a short to ground and 13 for an open circuit, while further bytes cover shorts to power, crossed wires, high resistance or a configuration mismatch, each after 2 seconds. Toyota names B007512, a short to battery, in its 2022 Tundra bulletin about the Qi charger. Rear retractor wiring passes through seat and trim areas that are opened during interior work, which makes a disturbed plug the usual suspect. With the code active, the airbag lamp is on and the right rear passenger may not be pulled back into the seat in a crash.
c: Plug at the right rear retractor not fully latched after interior work
Chafed lead to the right rear pretensioner (short to ground or power)
Interference from added electronics, fixed by an ECU update (Toyota Tundra 2022)
Internal fault of the right rear pretensioner
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear occupant without belt pretensioning in a crash
Safety note: the rear retractor contains a pyrotechnic charge; work on it only de-energised and leave it to a specialist workshop

B0076.t: Third Row Left Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control
B0076.d: B0076 belongs to the pretensioner at the left seat of the third row, a position found only in vehicles with a third seat row. No carmaker publishes B0076 with this meaning. Mercedes shows how third-row units are logged in practice: its LI54.21-P-070658 names open-circuit faults of the emergency tensioning retractors at the left and right of the third seat row as B00E7 and B00E6, the C-stage slots, so a B0076 is not to be expected on those models. The circuit itself is a pyrotechnic squib that the airbag module checks for opens, shorts and resistance drift, as with the front retractor and buckle units GM and NHTSA describe. If B0076 is stored, the airbag lamp is on and the third-row left occupant may not get any pretensioning.
c: Plug at the third-row left belt disturbed by folding or removing the seat
Harness damaged by luggage or trim work in the cargo area
Airbag module coded for a third-row pretensioner that is not fitted
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Third-row left occupant without pretensioning in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic belt component; disconnect the battery and wait before touching it, repair at a specialist workshop

B0077.t: Third Row Center Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control
B0077.d: B0077 stands for the pretensioner at the middle seat of the third row. Hardly any vehicle fits one, and no manufacturer documents B0077 with this J2012 meaning; Mercedes, which equips some models with third-row tensioning retractors, lists only a left and a right unit (B00E7/B00E6). The number is met more often in older GM-built Saabs. The 2006 Saab 9-5 stores B0077 when the airbag module cannot communicate with the driver-side side-impact sensor because of an open or a short, and Saab 9-3 modules of 2003 and 2007 use it for the driver-side B-pillar sensor. On such cars the fault lies in the door or pillar sensor, not in a rear belt. For a genuine third-row centre pretensioner, a stored code means a lit airbag lamp and a disabled unit.
c: On older Saab 9-3/9-5, fault at the driver-side side-impact or B-pillar sensor (older GM meaning)
Plug of the third-row centre pretensioner disturbed during seat folding or removal
Airbag module coded for a centre pretensioner that is not installed
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On Saab, side airbag deployment on the driver side may be impaired
Safety note: airbag sensors and pretensioners belong to the pyrotechnic restraint system; work only de-energised and at a specialist workshop

B0078.t: Third Row Right Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control
B0078.d: B0078 refers to the right seat of the third row and its belt pretensioner. No carmaker publishes B0078 in this J2012 sense, and Mercedes models with third-row tensioning retractors log the right-hand unit as B00E6 instead. Like B0077, the number has a sensor meaning in GM's older Saab modules: the 2006 Saab 9-5 sets B0078 for an open or short in the communication with the passenger-side side-impact sensor, and the 9-3 airbag module (2003, 2007) uses it for the passenger-side B-pillar sensor, with bytes for faulty communication, a short to battery or ground, or a wrong sensor fitted. Where the code really concerns the right pretensioner of the third row, the airbag lamp is on and that seat loses its pretensioning until the loop is repaired.
c: On older Saab 9-3/9-5, fault at the passenger-side side-impact or B-pillar sensor (older GM meaning)
Plug at the third-row right belt loosened when the seat was folded or removed
Internal fault of the third-row right pretensioner
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Third-row right occupant without pretensioning, or on Saab impaired side-impact detection on the passenger side
Safety note: pyrotechnic restraint parts; only work on them with the battery disconnected, after the wait time, at a specialist workshop

B0079.t: Driver Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control
B0079.d: B0079 marks the driver's second (B) pretensioner. Mercedes-Benz uses the code in exactly this way: in LI54.21-P-070658, valid for A-Class, CLA and GLB, B007913 is an open circuit in the squib of the belt end fitting tensioner on the driver's side, while the retractor of the same seat appears as B007E. An end fitting or anchor pretensioner pulls on the lower belt anchor next to the door side of the seat and so tightens the lap section; GM's restraint guide and a Hyundai-Kia patent describe this layout. Older Saab models give the number another meaning: the 2006 Saab 9-5 stores B0079 when an incorrect driver-side side-impact sensor is installed. A stored B0079 lights the airbag lamp and means the driver's lap tensioner may not fire.
c: Plug at the driver's belt end fitting tensioner beside the seat loose or corroded
Lead to the end fitting tensioner pinched by the seat rail
On a 2006 Saab 9-5, wrong side-impact sensor fitted (older GM meaning)
Internal fault of the end fitting tensioner squib
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver's lap belt section not tightened in a crash
Safety note: the end fitting tensioner is pyrotechnic; never probe it live – battery off, wait time, specialist workshop

B007A.t: Passenger Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control
B007A.d: B007A is the passenger-side twin of B0079 and covers the second pretensioner on the front passenger seat. Mercedes lists B007A13 for an open in the squib of the passenger's belt end fitting tensioner on the A-, CLA- and GLB-Class and keeps the passenger retractor apart as B007F. A lap or anchor pretensioner of this kind fires together with the retractor unit, as Joyson explains for its lap pretensioner, and draws the lap belt down onto the pelvis to cut the risk of sliding under it. Mitsubishi files comparable lap pretensioners under its own codes B1001 and B1002 rather than in J2012 slots, so B007A is not expected there. Once B007A is set, the airbag lamp comes on and the module records that the passenger's lap tensioning is unavailable.
c: Plug at the passenger end fitting tensioner disturbed, e.g. after seat removal
Lead to the lap tensioner pinched under the passenger seat
Internal fault of the passenger lap tensioner
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger's lap belt not tightened in a crash, higher risk of sliding under it
Safety note: pyrotechnic tensioner next to the seat; disconnect the battery, observe the wait time, have a specialist workshop do the repair

B007B.t: Second Row Left Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control
B007B.d: B007B would cover a second pretensioner on the outboard left seat in row two, for example a lap tensioner in addition to the retractor unit. No manufacturer publishes B007B. The documented rear cases use other slots: Mitsubishi files its left rear retractor pretensioner under B0073, and Mercedes logs the left rear emergency tensioning retractor as B00E3, the C-stage code. Joyson's lap pretensioner shows the kind of hardware a B stage could stand for, since it is meant to fire alongside a retractor pretensioner. In IIHS crash tests that placed a dummy behind the driver, submarining showed up in some vehicles with rear pretensioners, which is the risk such a lap device addresses. A stored B007B keeps the airbag lamp lit and leaves that stage inactive.
c: Plug of the left rear lap or anchor tensioner disturbed when the bench was removed
Airbag module coded for a rear B-stage tensioner that is not fitted
Floor harness to the left rear seat damaged
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left rear lap belt not tightened in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic part at the rear seat; work only de-energised (battery off, wait) and at a specialist workshop

B007C.t: Second Row Right Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control
B007C.d: B007C is the second-row right counterpart of B007B: an additional pretensioner stage at the right outer rear seat. No manufacturer publishes this code. On that seat Mitsubishi uses B0075 for its retractor pretensioner and Mercedes uses B00E4 for the right rear emergency tensioning retractor, so neither leaves a role for B007C. A B stage would typically be a buckle or anchor unit acting on the lap belt; NHTSA's 2013 evaluation explains how a buckle pretensioner pulls the buckle down by a cable and piston, while Joyson describes lap tensioners working with the retractor. Rear lap units are far less common than front ones, so this code is unusual. When it does appear, the airbag lamp stays on and that stage cannot be counted on.
c: Plug of the right rear buckle or anchor tensioner loosened during seat work
Airbag module configuration lists a stage that is not installed
Internal fault of the right rear B-stage tensioner
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear lap belt not pretensioned in a crash
Safety note: the tensioner contains a pyrotechnic charge; only work on it with the battery disconnected and at a specialist workshop

B007D.t: Second Row Center Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control
B007D.d: B007D names a second pretensioner at the middle seat of the second row. No carmaker documents it, and since even one pretensioner at the rear centre seat is uncommon, a second stage there is rarer still. Where such hardware is fitted, the B stage would act on the buckle or anchor side, comparable to the Autoliv pulley-and-cable buckle tensioner of patent US7360795B2 or the buckle units GM shows at the inner flank of front seats. Wiring to a rear centre position runs through the seat base or floor and can be disturbed when a split bench is folded or taken out. The firing loop is monitored like every other squib circuit. A stored B007D lights the airbag lamp, and the module treats that stage as unavailable.
c: Plug at the rear centre buckle or anchor tensioner loosened by folding the bench
Airbag module coded for a rear centre B stage that is not present
Harness under the rear bench chafed or pinched
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Rear centre occupant without the second pretensioning stage
Safety note: pyrotechnic belt hardware; de-energise the system (battery off, wait time) and have a specialist workshop do the work

B007E.t: Driver Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control
B007E.d: B007E is the driver's third (C) pretensioner circuit. Mercedes-Benz fills this slot with the retractor: in LI54.21-P-070658 for the A-, CLA- and GLB-Class, B007E13 is an open circuit at the squib of the driver's emergency tensioning retractor, with B0079 for the belt end fitting tensioner and B0080 for the driver's belt force limiter. The retractor unit is housed either inside the B-pillar or within the seat and winds the spool back to remove slack from the shoulder belt, as GM and Joyson explain. The same Mercedes list puts the rear retractors on the C codes B00E3, B00E4, B00E6 and B00E7, so there the C stage consistently means the retractor. A stored B007E means the airbag lamp is on and the driver's shoulder belt will not be pretensioned.
c: Retractor plug at the lower driver-side B-pillar loose or terminals spread
Harness pinched by B-pillar or sill trim
Internal fault of the driver retractor pretensioner
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver's shoulder belt is not tightened in a crash
Safety note: the retractor holds a pyrotechnic charge; disconnect the battery, wait, and leave the work to a specialist workshop

B007F.t: Passenger Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control
B007F.d: B007F covers the passenger's third (C) pretensioner and is the best-documented code of this series. Mercedes lists B007F13 as an open in the squib of the front passenger's emergency tensioning retractor (A-, CLA- and GLB-Class). FCA uses the same slot for the same part: STAR case S2008000193 for the 2020–2021 Ram 1500 links B007F-2B to a loose or spread plug of the retractor down at the passenger-side B-pillar, repaired with kit 68148100AA, and case S2008000137 for the 2020 Jeep Grand Cherokee reports B007F-11, a short to ground, from a body harness pinched by B-pillar trim. The retractor is a pyrotechnic unit that rewinds the webbing in a crash. With B007F set, the airbag lamp is on and the passenger's shoulder belt lacks pretensioning.
c: Retractor plug at the lower passenger-side B-pillar loose or with spread terminals (FCA S2008000193)
Body harness pinched between B-pillar trim retainer and body (FCA S2008000137)
Internal fault of the passenger retractor pretensioner
s: Airbag warning lamp on, often after recent interior or body repair
Passenger shoulder belt not tightened in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic retractor in the B-pillar; work on it only de-energised (battery off, wait time) and at a specialist workshop

B0080.t: Driver Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control
B0080.d: B0080 reports a fault in the firing loop that switches the driver's belt force limiter. In adaptive retractors a small squib, fired by the airbag module, changes the level at which the webbing is paid out, so the chest load suits crash severity and occupant. Mercedes-Benz uses the code exactly so: topic LI54.21-P-070658 (cars of the 177, 118 and 247 series) gives B008013 for an interrupted igniter of the driver's belt force limiter, traced to raised resistance at the airbag module plug. Ford names B0080 among the restraint module codes cured by reprogramming on 2017–2018 Fusion/MKZ, without giving its meaning. Older GM-built Saabs (9-3, 9-5) use B0080 for an internal fault of the driver-side B-pillar or side impact sensor instead. With the code set, the airbag lamp is lit.
c: Raised contact resistance at the airbag module connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Chafed or disconnected lead to the driver's retractor at the B-pillar
Restraint module software needing an update (Ford Fusion/MKZ)
Internal fault of the load limiter squib in the retractor
s: Airbag warning lamp on, sometimes with an SRS message in the cluster
Driver's belt keeps only its basic force limiting level in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic part in the driver's retractor; work only de-energised (battery off, wait time) at a specialist workshop

B0081.t: First Row Center Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control
B0081.d: B0081 is assigned to a squib-switched limiter for the centre place of a three-across front bench. No carmaker publishes the code with this meaning. Mercedes-Benz files a first-row centre tensioning retractor under its own code B1B36, and NHTSA's 2013 study notes that load limiters became universal only at the two outer front seats. In practice the number almost always carries a GM meaning: on Global A cars such as the Saab 9-4X it means a passenger presence module fault (00) or a wrong module fitted (3A), with the passenger airbag disabled; GM special coverage N182188910 (2017 Buick Verano) and bulletin PIE0407B (Impala) deal with it. Saab 9-3 and 9-5 airbag modules use B0081 for a wrong passenger-side B-pillar or side sensor. Check the make before suspecting a belt.
c: On GM vehicles, fault or mismatch of the passenger presence module in the seat (different meaning)
Wiring to a centre front seat retractor damaged in the seat base
Internal fault of the centre seat load limiter squib
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM vehicles the passenger airbag status shows OFF although an adult is seated
Safety note: airbag system with pyrotechnic parts; diagnose and repair only de-energised at a specialist workshop

B0082.t: Passenger Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control
B0082.d: B0082 covers the firing loop of the front passenger's switchable belt force limiter. Two manufacturers document this meaning. In the Mercedes A-Class, CLA and GLB, B008213 marks an interrupted igniter of the passenger-side belt force limiter. Ford special service message 51998 covers 2023 Escape, Corsair, Bronco Sport and Maverick that store B0082:1A because of the passenger belt retractor at connector C303B; where a connection fault is found, the retractor and pretensioner assembly is replaced before any wiring repair. Autoliv patents show why retractor and limiter belong together: the pretensioner's own gas can select the higher limiting level. On GM Global A cars (Saab 9-4X) B0082 means the seat belt reminder sensor in the passenger cushion instead. The airbag lamp stays on.
c: Poor connection at the passenger retractor plug (Ford C303B, SSM 51998)
Raised resistance at the airbag module connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Internal fault of the passenger retractor and limiter assembly
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger belt cannot switch its force limiting level in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic retractor at the passenger B-pillar; work only de-energised (battery off, wait time) at a specialist workshop

B0083.t: Second Row Left Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control
B0083.d: B0083 is intended for a switchable force limiter on the left rear seat. No manufacturer publishes it with this J2012 meaning. Rear load limiters do exist: in an IIHS rear-seat test series presented in 2020, ten vehicles had both pretensioner and limiter at the back and one had a limiter alone. Much more often B0083 is a GM code for another part. On Global A models (2011 Saab 9-4X) it means the left front impact sensor, with symptom bytes for shorts, opens, low current, internal failure, wrong part and bad serial data; an open is flagged when the sensor stays silent longer than 375 ms. GM bulletin PI1480 (2015 Colorado/Canyon) traces stored B0083/B0084 with byte 05 to a corroded sensor or an unlatched connector lock. Saab 9-3 and 9-5 use it for the passenger seat position sensor.
c: On GM vehicles, corroded left front impact sensor or unlatched connector lock (PI1480, different meaning)
Wiring to the left rear retractor damaged under trim or seat
Internal fault of the rear load limiter squib
s: Airbag warning lamp on, possibly only intermittently
Left rear belt keeps a fixed limiting level in a crash
Safety note: restraint system with pyrotechnic parts; work only de-energised at a specialist workshop

B0084.t: Second Row Center Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control
B0084.d: B0084 names a squib-switched force limiter for the middle rear seat. Neither a carmaker nor a bulletin shows it with that meaning, and the hardware is rare: NHTSA's 2013 evaluation reports load limiters as standard only at the outer front seats, and the rear centre belt is often a plain retractor. A Delphi patent for rear seats without airbags instead chooses between roughly 4–6 kN and 2–3 kN purely mechanically, with no firing loop at all. Owners usually meet B0084 through GM. The 2011 Saab 9-4X, a Global A design, stores it for the right front impact sensor, set after ten seconds of a short, open or bad data; PI1480 covers it on the 2015 Colorado/Canyon. Saab 9-3 and 9-5 modules use it for the driver seat position sensor and then disable the driver airbag's second stage.
c: On GM vehicles, fault at the right front impact sensor or its plug (different meaning)
On Saab 9-3/9-5, open or short in the driver seat position sensor circuit (different meaning)
Damaged lead to a centre rear limiter where one is fitted
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On Saab 9-3/9-5 the second stage of the driver airbag is disabled
Safety note: airbag system with pyrotechnic parts; diagnose only de-energised at a specialist workshop

B0085.t: Second Row Right Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control
B0085.d: B0085 points to the igniter circuit that would change the force level of the right rear belt. No maker documents it with that meaning. Joyson offers dual-stage limiters with degressive or adaptive behaviour, and an Autoliv patent switches from the stiff to the soft torsion section when the controller fires a squib once cabin deceleration crosses a threshold; in a rear seat such a loop would be watched like any other squib. IIHS rear-seat work found the right rear position tested less often than the left (16 against 27 runs). In practice, B0085 on a GM Global A car (Saab 9-4X 2011) is the left front side impact sensor, reported for shorts, opens, current above 23 mA, internal failure, a wrong part or invalid serial data. Only the make tells which part is meant.
c: On GM vehicles, left front side impact sensor or its door wiring faulty (different meaning)
Lead to the right rear retractor pinched by seat or trim
Internal fault of the right rear limiter squib
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM vehicles the code clears from history only after 100 fault-free ignition cycles
Safety note: pyrotechnic restraint parts; work only de-energised at a specialist workshop

B0086.t: Third Row Left Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control
B0086.d: B0086 is reserved for a switchable force limiter at the left third-row seat. No manufacturer documents it, and an electrically fired limiter that far back is unusual. Delphi's rear-seat patent explains why: without airbags or weight sensing in rear rows, it picks the level from the length of webbing drawn out, about 4–6 kN for a large occupant or a child seat and 2–3 kN for a small occupant. NHTSA's 2013 study likewise counts load limiters as standard only at the front outer seats. On GM Global A cars (2011 Saab 9-4X) B0086 stands for the right front side impact sensor, watched for shorts and opens, too little current, internal errors, an incorrect part and corrupt messages, each needing ten seconds to set. Where a third-row limiter loop does exist, a fault lights the airbag lamp.
c: On GM vehicles, right front side impact sensor or wiring faulty (different meaning)
Third-row harness stressed by folding or removing the seat
Internal fault of the third-row limiter squib
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left third-row belt limits force only at a fixed level
Safety note: restraint system with pyrotechnic parts; work only de-energised at a specialist workshop

B0087.t: Third Row Center Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control
B0087.d: B0087 would flag the igniter circuit of an adaptive belt force limiter on the centre position of row three. That combination is close to theoretical: no carmaker documents the code, and NHTSA's 2013 study dates universal fitment of load limiters (by model year 2007) only for the front outboard seats. Joyson describes how such a unit works, with linear limiters tuned to a vehicle's crash pulse and dual-stage versions for adaptive or degressive force. On GM Global A vehicles (2011 Saab 9-4X) B0087 means the left rear side impact sensor. GM sets it after ten seconds of a fault, or when the module hears nothing from the sensor for over 375 ms. A history code there clears after 100 fault-free ignition cycles. Check the make first.
c: On GM vehicles, left rear side impact sensor or its connector faulty (different meaning)
Damaged lead to a third-row centre limiter where fitted
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM vehicles the AIR BAG indicator is lit by the cluster at the module's request
Safety note: airbag system with pyrotechnic parts; diagnose only de-energised at a specialist workshop

B0088.t: Third Row Right Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control
B0088.d: B0088 closes the load limiter series with the right third-row seat. No manufacturer documents it with this meaning. If such a squib-switched limiter is fitted, the module tests its loop for opens, shorts and out-of-window resistance like any igniter; an Autoliv patent shows the principle, where gas from a squib releases a blocking ring so the softer torsion section takes over. Some designs avoid the extra loop altogether, such as the Delphi rear-seat retractor that switches mechanically. On GM Global A models (2011 Saab 9-4X) B0088 instead flags the right rear side impact sensor, using the same symptom bytes as its siblings: shorts, open or high resistance, low current, internal failure, wrong part fitted and invalid serial data. A stored code lights the airbag lamp.
c: On GM vehicles, right rear side impact sensor or wiring faulty (different meaning)
Harness to the right third-row seat strained by seat folding
Internal fault of the right third-row limiter squib
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right third-row belt cannot change its limiting level
Safety note: pyrotechnic restraint parts; work only de-energised at a specialist workshop

B0090.d: B0090 concerns the left frontal crash sensor, a satellite accelerometer in the front crumple zone that tells the airbag module early how hard the front end is being hit. Bosch notes such upfront units sharpen frontal crash detection beside the central sensors. Several makers use the code exactly so. Acura bulletin 18-016 (2017 ILX) describes B0090-87, a missing signal of the left frontal impact sensor, caused by water entering the connector through a wire size variance; sensor and engine bay harness are replaced. For the Ram 1500, FCA reports B0090-49, internal electronic failure of the left frontal acceleration sensor: after sensor replacement the part number must match the restraint controller (STAR S2408000050), and TSB 08-150-26 (2025 Ram 1500) reflashes the controller. The airbag lamp comes on.
c: Water in the left front sensor connector damaging the harness (Acura 18-016)
Replacement sensor part number not matching the restraint controller (FCA S2408000050)
Restraint controller software needing a reflash (FCA TSB 08-150-26)
Sensor damaged by a front-end impact or poor refitting after body repair
s: Airbag warning lamp on, often after front-end repair or water exposure
Frontal crash detection relies on the module's internal sensor only
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and observe the wait time before touching sensors or wiring, work at a specialist workshop

B0091.d: B0091 covers the first left-side crash sensor, which Mitsubishi places in the front door and lists as DOOR SATEL SENS LH with the J2012 title in brackets. The airbag unit checks it with the ignition on and stores a subtype after a two-second delay: -11 for a short to ground, -55 when the configuration held in the unit does not fit the vehicle, -81 for a communication fault, plus further bytes. Door satellites of this kind are usually pressure sensors: Bosch explains that the sealed door cavity acts as the sensing volume, so a crush raises pressure and the module can decide within about 5 ms. Continental sells a pressure satellite for the same task. With B0091 set, the airbag lamp lights and left side impact sensing may be weakened.
c: Short or poor contact in the door harness or connector to the sensor
Internal fault of the front door satellite sensor
Airbag unit configuration not matching the vehicle (Mitsubishi subtype -55)
Internal fault of the airbag diagnosis unit
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side and curtain airbags on the left may deploy late or not in a side impact
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before door work, then have it checked at a specialist workshop

B0092.d: B0092 belongs to the second crash sensor on the left side. Mitsubishi fits it at the left B-pillar and lists it as B-PILLAR SAT SEN LH, adding the J2012 title Left Side Restraints Sensor 2; its index shows only subtype -55, set two seconds after the unit finds that its stored configuration does not fit the vehicle. A pillar position suits an acceleration satellite: Bosch mounts these on stiff members such as sills, seat cross members or B- and C-pillars, and its SMA773 chip measures two axes up to 60 g and talks to the module over a two-wire PSI5 link. GM-built Saabs use the number differently: the 2006 9-5 and the 9-3 store B0092 for a general fault of the passenger presence system, with the airbag system then rated out of order. The airbag lamp is on.
c: Airbag unit configuration not matching the fitted sensors (Mitsubishi subtype -55)
Loose or corroded plug at the B-pillar sensor after trim or body work
On GM-built Saabs, passenger presence system fault (different meaning)
Internal fault of the B-pillar satellite sensor
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side impact detection rests on the remaining sensors only
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before removing pillar trim, work at a specialist workshop

B0093.d: B0093 is the third left-side crash sensor. Mitsubishi mounts it at the left C-pillar, names it C-PILLAR SAT SEN LH and gives the J2012 wording Left Side Restraints Sensor 3. Unlike the B-pillar unit, it carries the full set of subtypes: -11 when the sensor line is shorted to ground, -55 for a configuration mismatch, -81 when communication with the sensor fails, and others, each confirmed after two seconds with the ignition on. A sensor that far back can give the module an early view of impacts behind the front door. Bosch lists C-pillars among the mounting points for its acceleration satellites, and Continental's gSAT measures acceleration in rigid structure for the same purpose. The airbag lamp lights while B0093 is stored.
c: Sensor line shorted to ground or poor contact at the C-pillar plug (subtypes -11/-81)
Internal fault of the C-pillar satellite sensor
Airbag unit configuration not matching the vehicle (subtype -55)
Internal fault of the airbag diagnosis unit
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side impact sensing behind the front door is degraded
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work at the rear pillar, specialist workshop only

B0094.d: B0094 refers to a single crash sensor placed in the middle of the vehicle front, used where a car has one central frontal satellite rather than a left and right pair. Mitsubishi's airbag unit shows it as CRASH ZONE SENS and adds the J2012 name Center Frontal Restraints Sensor. Its index lists nine subtypes, logged once a fault has persisted for two seconds at ignition on: -11 and -12 for shorts to ground or supply, -88 for an open line, -81 for lost communication, -25 for a failed self-diagnosis, -28 for an offset error, -93 for a reset fault, -55 for a configuration mismatch and -86 when sensor and unit are not the specified parts. That index has no B0090 or B0095, so the centre unit is the only frontal satellite there. Bosch notes that crumple-zone acceleration sensors improve frontal crash detection. The airbag lamp lights.
c: Open, short or corroded contact in the harness to the centre front sensor (subtypes -11/-12/-88)
Internal fault of the crash zone sensor, e.g. offset or self-diagnosis error (subtypes -25/-28)
Sensor or airbag unit not the specified part, or unit configuration wrong (subtypes -86/-55)
Sensor or bracket bent by a front-end impact or refitted poorly after body work
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal crash detection falls back on the sensors inside the airbag unit
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work at the front sensor, specialist workshop only

B0095.d: B0095 is the right-hand partner of B0090: an acceleration satellite in the right front crumple zone that lets the airbag module judge early how severe a frontal hit is. Honda's Fit and HR-V of model years 2016–2017 use the code this way, B0095-87 meaning the right front impact sensor sends nothing; in request AER17060A Honda asked dealers to report such cars before any repair. On the Ram 1500, FCA stores B0095-49 for an internal electronic failure of the right frontal acceleration sensor. STAR case S2408000050 traces repeat faults to a replacement sensor whose part number does not suit the restraint controller, and TSB 08-150-26 reprograms the controller on 2025 trucks. Mitsubishi once recalled Lancers because salty water could corrode the front impact sensors. With B0095 set, the airbag lamp is lit.
c: Replacement sensor part number not matching the restraint controller (FCA S2408000050)
Water or road salt in the sensor housing or plug at the right front
Restraint controller software needing a reflash (FCA TSB 08-150-26)
Internal failure of the right front acceleration sensor
s: Airbag warning lamp on, often after front-end repair
Frontal impacts on the right are judged later or less precisely
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before touching the sensor, specialist workshop only

B0096.d: B0096 concerns the first crash sensor on the right side, mirror image of B0091. Mitsubishi puts it in the right front door, calls it DOOR SATEL SENS RH and prints the J2012 title beside it; its airbag unit checks the sensor with the ignition on and, after two seconds, stores -11 for a ground short, -81 when data from the sensor stop and -55 for a configuration that does not fit the car, among nine subtypes in total. Honda logs B0096-87 when the first right side impact sensor of a 2016 or 2017 Fit or HR-V goes silent. A door position suits a pressure sensor: Bosch describes how a dent in the door changes the air pressure inside it, turning the whole door into the sensing element. Saab 9-3 and 9-5 models give B0096 to the passenger belt buckle switch circuit instead. The airbag lamp comes on.
c: Chafed wire or poor contact in the door harness between body and right front door
Internal fault of the right front door satellite sensor
Airbag unit configuration not matching the vehicle (Mitsubishi subtype -55)
On Saab 9-3/9-5, passenger belt buckle switch circuit fault (different meaning)
s: Airbag warning lamp on, sometimes only after the right front door has been opened or worked on
Side and curtain airbags on the right may fire late in a side impact
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before removing the door trim, specialist workshop only

B0097.d: B0097 is the second right-side crash sensor. Mitsubishi fixes it at the right B-pillar, lists it as B-PILLAR SAT SEN RH and gives Right Side Restraints Sensor 2 as the J2012 name. Only subtype -55 appears there: the unit flags, after two seconds with the ignition on, that the stored configuration does not match the fitted sensors. Honda's request AER17060A confirms the numbering with B0097-87, meaning the second right side impact sensor has gone quiet on 2016–2017 Fit and HR-V cars. On a pillar an acceleration satellite is the usual choice; Bosch fits such units to B- and C-pillars, sills or seat cross members. Not every maker uses this code: FCA reports its right B-pillar acceleration sensor on the 2025 Ram 1500 as B2764, and Saab 9-3/9-5 use B0097 for the driver belt buckle switch circuit. While stored, the airbag lamp stays on.
c: Airbag unit configuration not matching the fitted sensors, e.g. after unit replacement (Mitsubishi subtype -55)
Plug at the right B-pillar sensor loose or damaged after trim or seat belt work
Right B-pillar sensor sending no signal (Honda subtype -87)
On Saab 9-3/9-5, driver belt buckle switch circuit fault (different meaning)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side impacts near the B-pillar are detected only by the remaining sensors
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before removing pillar trim, specialist workshop only

B0098.d: B0098 belongs to the third right-side crash sensor. In Mitsubishi's airbag index it is the C-PILLAR SAT SEN RH, given with the J2012 wording Right Side Restraints Sensor 3. The full set of nine subtypes applies, each set two seconds after detection with the ignition on; beside the usual short to ground (-11), configuration mismatch (-55) and lost communication (-81), the list covers a short to supply (-12), an open line (-88), an offset error (-28) and a reset fault (-93). A sensor this far back sees impacts on the rear door and rear seat area early. Continental's gSAT reports acceleration from rigid structure for such tasks. FCA uses its own code B2765 for the right C-pillar sensor of the Ram 1500, while the Saab 9-3 airbag module uses B0098 to flag that its passenger presence system has failed in general. The airbag lamp lights.
c: Open or shorted line or poor contact at the right C-pillar plug (subtypes -11/-12/-88/-81)
Internal fault of the right C-pillar sensor, e.g. offset or reset error (subtypes -28/-93)
Airbag unit configuration not matching the vehicle (subtype -55)
On the Saab 9-3, passenger presence system fault (different meaning)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side impact sensing at the rear door is degraded
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work at the rear pillar, specialist workshop only

B0099.d: B0099 reports a fault in the rollover sensing that decides whether curtain airbags and pretensioners fire when a vehicle tips. Bosch integrates rollover sensors in its base airbag control unit, so the sensor is often part of the module. A Delphi patent shows the principle: roll rate and low-g vertical acceleration give roll angle and rate, which are compared with deploy and no-deploy curves, while a high-g lateral accelerometer acts as a separate arming check. FMVSS 226 requires a monitored readiness indicator where ejection mitigation deploys in a rollover; Karma recalled the 2018 Revero because its rollover sensing was not enabled. FCA uses the code: recall Y79 (2021 Grand Cherokee, 2022 Wagoneer) has technicians check for B0099-96 before reflashing the restraint controller, without defining it. The airbag lamp lights.
c: Internal fault of the rollover sensor built into the airbag control unit (module replacement)
Airbag unit loose, mounted at an angle or after a crash no longer within its fitting tolerance
Wiring or plug fault where a separate rollover sensor is fitted
Restraint controller software or configuration not matching the vehicle
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Curtain airbags and pretensioners may not fire in a rollover
Safety note: airbag control unit with rollover sensing; work only de-energised (battery off, wait time) at a specialist workshop

B009A.d: B009A extends the left-side sensor row past the three positions most cars use. No carmaker documents this code publicly. Mitsubishi's airbag index ends the left row at B0093 (C-pillar), and FCA numbers its pillar satellites in its own B276x range, so neither fills the fourth slot. A fourth left sensor makes sense on long bodies or extra seat rows: Bosch says its acceleration satellites can sit on sills, seat cross members, B- and C-pillars and also in the rear, while pressure sensors watch a door cavity. If a vehicle sets B009A, the airbag module has lost a plausible signal from that added satellite or found it shorted, open or wrongly configured; the matching subtype and location must be taken from the maker's own airbag documentation. The airbag lamp comes on.
c: Damaged line or plug to the fourth left sensor, often after seat or trim removal
Internal fault of the fourth left crash satellite
Airbag module coded for a sensor layout the vehicle does not have
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side impact detection in the area of the missing sensor is weaker
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before any work on sensors or wiring, specialist workshop only

B009B.d: B009B names a fifth crash sensor on the left side. No carmaker documents this code publicly, and the reviewed bulletins and airbag indexes stop well before it. Why vehicles carry several side satellites at all follows from FMVSS 214: cars must protect occupants in a moving barrier crash and in a vehicle-to-pole test, and a narrow pole can strike anywhere along the side. Continental offers two kinds of satellites for this: the gSAT reports acceleration from rigid structure, the pSAT reacts to the pressure rise of a crushed door. A fifth left unit would most likely monitor a rear door or an extra seat row. When B009B is stored, the module has rejected that sensor's signal or circuit, and side or curtain airbags may react later on that side. The airbag lamp is lit.
c: Line or connector fault on the way to the fifth left sensor
Internal fault of the fifth left satellite (pressure or acceleration type)
Replacement sensor of the wrong part number after a body repair
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side and curtain airbags on the left may deploy later in a side impact
Safety note: airbag system; switch off, disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work, specialist workshop only

B009C.d: B009C is the sixth and last left-side slot in the J2012 sensor block. No carmaker documents this code publicly. Real vehicles show how many side satellites are usual: FCA's 2019 Jeep Cherokee recall 19V-449 lists two engine bay sensors and four for B- or C-pillar positions, three per side at most, and FCA files those pillar units as B2761 to B2765 rather than in the B009x block. A sixth left sensor would therefore suit only long vans, buses or vehicles with several rear rows, where Bosch's option of satellites in the rear body also fits. If B009C appears, check first which sensor the maker assigns to it; a scan tool reading on a car with fewer sensors may point to a wrong module configuration. The airbag lamp lights.
c: Airbag module configured for more side sensors than are fitted
Damaged rear body harness or plug to the sixth left sensor
Internal fault of the sixth left satellite
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side impact sensing at the rear left is reduced
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time, then have it diagnosed at a specialist workshop

B009D.d: B009D opens the second half of the right-side sensor row, after B0096 to B0098. No carmaker documents this code publicly; Mitsubishi stops its right row at the C-pillar sensor B0098, and Honda's Fit and HR-V use only two side sensors per side. What a failing side satellite means in practice is shown by FCA recall 19V-449: on 2019 Jeep Cherokees the restraint controller could lose contact with acceleration sensors, which lit the airbag lamp and risked late or no deployment, so the sensors were replaced. Bosch's PSI5-linked SMA773 is an example of such a satellite, measuring two axes up to 60 g. A stored B009D therefore means the module has lost or rejected a fourth right sensor; its location comes from the maker's documentation. The airbag warning lamp stays lit.
c: Communication with the fourth right sensor lost through wiring, plug or sensor fault
Internal fault of the fourth right crash satellite
Airbag module coded for a sensor layout the vehicle does not have
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side impact detection in the area of that sensor is weaker
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work on sensors, specialist workshop only

B009E.d: B009E stands for a fifth crash sensor on the vehicle's right flank. No carmaker documents this code publicly: Mitsubishi's airbag index ends its right row with the C-pillar unit B0098, and the NHTSA bulletin index shows no entry for B009E at all. A fifth right-hand sensor would mostly make sense on long bodies, vans with sliding doors or vehicles with extra seat rows. Two sensing principles are on offer: Bosch's peripheral pressure sensor sits in a door cavity and reacts when the crushed door raises the air pressure, while satellites such as Continental's gSAT pick up the shock in stiff structure. FMVSS 214 shows why several are needed, because a pole can hit the flank at many points. With B009E stored the airbag lamp is on and deployment near that sensor may come late.
c: Open, shorted or corroded line or plug to the fifth right sensor, often after door or trim work
Internal fault of the fifth right crash sensor (pressure or acceleration type)
Airbag control unit coded for a sensor that the vehicle does not have
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side and curtain airbags on the right may react later in the area of that sensor
Safety note: airbag system; unplug sensors only with the ignition off, battery disconnected and wait time observed; after replacement have the configuration checked, specialist workshop only

B009F.d: B009F would be the sixth and last right-hand restraints sensor in the J2012 block. No carmaker documents it publicly with this meaning. The number does appear at GM, but for another part: on 2008–2013 two-mode hybrid Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra trucks, bulletin PIT4614C ties a no-crank condition with B009F stored in the SDGM gateway to water passing the seal of the HVCID crash sensor for the high-voltage circuit, mounted on the lower radiator support; the sensor and terminals are inspected and replaced. That is a crash switch for isolating the hybrid battery, not an airbag satellite. A genuine sixth right satellite would be an acceleration unit, for example a PSI5-linked Bosch SMA773 sensor on a rear pillar or sill. Its failure lights the airbag lamp.
c: Damaged rear body harness or plug to the sixth right sensor
Internal fault of the sixth right acceleration satellite
On GM two-mode hybrids, water or corrosion at the high-voltage impact detection sensor (different meaning, PIT4614C)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM two-mode hybrids, no crank or a Service Hybrid message instead
Safety note: airbag and, on hybrids, high-voltage system; disconnect plugs only de-energised; after a sensor change have it checked or initialised, specialist workshop only

B00A0.d: B00A0 is the catch-all code for occupant classification, the function that judges at the front passenger place whether the passenger airbag may fire and with what force, as FMVSS 208 demands for advanced airbags. Mitsubishi lists it as OCCUPANT SENS UNIT with ten subtypes, among them sensor faults (-02/-09), low supply or unfinished zero-point reset (-22, battery at 9 V or less), lost communication (-83/-86/-87/-88) and a reset error (-93); most are set after 2 s with the ignition on, -88 after 5 s and -87 after 10 s. Mazda traced B00A0:09 on the CX-3 and CX-5 to a sensor too quick to react to low voltage while cranking and replaces the cushion (08-002/23). Nissan reprograms the OCS unit when zero reset fails (NTB19-071D). The airbag lamp lights.
c: Poor contact or open circuit in the passenger seat harness or plug, often after seat removal
Low battery voltage or voltage dip while cranking (Mitsubishi -22, Mazda B00A0:09)
Zero-point reset not done or not possible after seat work (Nissan reprograms the unit)
Internal fault of the classification sensor or control unit, often replaced with the seat cushion
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag status lamp shows the wrong state or the passenger airbag stays switched off
Fault may appear only after cold starts with a weak battery
Safety note: airbag system; unplug seat and sensor connectors only de-energised; after replacing seat sensors or the unit, the zero-point reset/calibration must be done, specialist workshop only

B00A1.d: B00A1 covers the occupant position system, which watches where a person sits rather than how heavy they are, so that an airbag can be held back when someone is too close to it. FMVSS 208 accepts this as dynamic automatic suppression (DASS): the bag must be switched off before the occupant's head, neck or upper body reach a zone beside the cover that the maker defines. No carmaker publishes B00A1 itself. Honda's OPDS shows the idea: sensors in the passenger backrest report height and lean, the side airbag is switched off while a Side Airbag Off lamp is lit, and the system needs initialising after seat-back parts or the unit are changed. Patents describe other ways, such as ultrasonic beams from the headliner or a sensor at the airbag door. A fault lights the airbag lamp.
c: System not initialised after seat cover, seat-back sensor or control unit replacement
Damaged seat harness or loose plug under the seat
Faulty position sensor or position control unit
Damp seat, accessory seat covers or objects disturbing the sensors
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Airbag off indicator stays on although the occupant sits upright
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect seat and sensor plugs only de-energised; after a sensor or unit change initialise/calibrate the system, specialist workshop only

B00B0.t: Driver Seat Occupant Classification Sensor A
B00B0.d: B00B0 is the first of five classification inputs on the driver seat. No carmaker publishes this code, and J2012 leaves it to the maker which sensor the letter A means. Classification normally sits in the passenger seat; a Bosch patent notes that it can be omitted on the driver side, on the assumption that drivers are adults, or fitted there as well. One sensor type that could fill such a slot is a switch mat under the cushion: Autoliv patented a mat with 28 dome switches grouped in five zones, chosen from a 2,016-cell test mat loaded with FMVSS 208 dummies and child seats at several back angles. If B00B0 is stored, the restraint module no longer trusts that input, so adaptive driver airbag staging may be lost, and the airbag lamp is on.
c: Open or poor contact in the driver seat harness or plug to input A
Cushion sensor mat creased or damaged, e.g. after seat cover work
Sensor or seat replaced without the required zero-point calibration
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver airbag may deploy with a fixed instead of an adapted stage
Safety note: airbag system; unplug seat and sensor connectors only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate the sensor after replacement, specialist workshop only

B00B1.t: Driver Seat Occupant Classification Sensor B
B00B1.d: B00B1 marks the second of the five driver seat classification sensors. No carmaker documents it publicly, and the letter is not tied to a fixed spot. Seat weight systems often measure at the corners: a CTS patent puts one thick-film strain gauge sensor at each corner between seat pan and slide rail, so the occupant's whole weight passes through four bridges whose leads meet in one junction box before the airbag controller. In such a layout every corner could carry its own letter, which would explain a series from A onward, yet no public source confirms that order. A stored B00B1 therefore means one load input is open, out of range or implausible; seat bolts fitted with the wrong torque and harness strain after seat removal are typical suspects. The airbag lamp lights.
c: Seat refitted with wrong bolt torque or distorted mounting, loading the sensor unevenly
Strained or chafed lead to load input B under the seat
Internal fault of the strain gauge sensor
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Weight-based adjustment of the driver airbag unavailable
Safety note: airbag system; work on seat and sensor plugs only de-energised; calibrate the seat sensors after replacement or seat refitting, specialist workshop only

B00B2.t: Driver Seat Occupant Classification Sensor C
B00B2.d: B00B2 is the third driver seat classification sensor in the J2012 list. No carmaker documents the code publicly. A widely used sensor type is Bosch's iBolt: the four bolts that anchor the seat frame are swapped for sensor bolts, a magnet and Hall element register how far a bending beam deflects, and the unit derives weight and how it is spread, separating an empty seat, a one-year-old, children of three and six, a 5th percentile woman and a 50th percentile man. A Bosch patent adds an accelerometer in the seat back that freezes the classification while jolts would distort the bolts' readings. Which bolt the letter C would denote is not published. With B00B2 stored, the airbag lamp is on and adaptive deployment cannot rely on that input.
c: Internal fault of the Hall-type sensor bolt at seat anchor C
Sensor bolt overloaded or seat frame bent, e.g. after a crash or wrong torque
Open or poor contact in the lead to input C
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver airbag cannot be matched to occupant size
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect seat and sensor plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate weight sensors after replacement, specialist workshop only

B00B3.t: Driver Seat Occupant Classification Sensor D
B00B3.d: B00B3 refers to the fourth of five driver seat classification inputs. No carmaker publishes it, and the mapping of letters to sensors is undocumented. A fourth input can rest on a different principle: Delphi patented a silicone-filled bladder between cushion foam and seat frame, carrying a pressure sensor and capacitive films whose spacing shrinks under load, so that weight and its spread over the cushion are estimated and cross-checked. Honda's job aid for its passenger seat weight sensors shows the service side: the sensors sit in the seat base or frame, need recalibration after a sensor or unit is replaced, and a binding sensor may be freed by loosening, shaking and retorquing the seat. Worn seat harnesses can also set such codes. A stored B00B3 lights the airbag lamp.
c: Seat harness worn by seat movement, open or intermittent contact to input D
Sensor binding or preloaded in the seat structure
Recalibration not done after sensor or unit replacement
Internal fault of the sensor, e.g. leaking bladder or failed pressure cell
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Classification of the driver unavailable for airbag staging
Safety note: airbag system; unplug seat and sensor connectors only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); recalibrate after any sensor change, specialist workshop only

B00B4.t: Driver Seat Occupant Classification Sensor E
B00B4.d: B00B4 is the fifth and last driver seat classification sensor. No carmaker documents the code publicly. A fifth input need not weigh anything: IEE's BodySense uses capacitive sensing in the seat surface, placed over the heater mat, under the cover and on top of the foam, and tells a child restraint from a seated person whatever the belt tension, posture, weight or height; IEE says the vehicle maker does not have to calibrate it and that it serves the FMVSS 208 advanced airbag rules. Other designs add a belt tension sensor so that a tightly cinched child seat is not taken for a heavy adult. Whether E stands for such a field sensor, a mat or another load cell is the maker's decision. When B00B4 is stored, the airbag lamp is lit and that input is ignored.
c: Open or poor contact in the seat harness or plug to input E
Damaged seat heater or trim where the capacitive electrode shares its layer
Internal fault of the fifth classification sensor or its electronics
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Possible related faults of the seat heater on the same seat
Safety note: airbag system; work on seat and sensor plugs only de-energised; after replacing a sensor or trim follow the maker's calibration, specialist workshop only

B00B5.t: Driver Seat Track Position Restraints Sensor
B00B5.d: B00B5 reports a fault of the driver seat track position sensor, which tells the airbag module whether the seat is pushed far forward toward the steering wheel. FCA uses it with exactly this meaning: GPOP tech tips for the Dodge Dart (PF), Jeep Cherokee (KL) and Chrysler 200 (UF) name B00B5-13, an open circuit, among codes to clear with engineering before replacing the restraint controller, and a 2024 tip for the Pacifica and Voyager (RU) asks for wiring, plug and low voltage checks first. Allegro describes the usual hardware, a two-wire Hall switch that the steel track shields from a magnet as it passes, giving zones. Honda lowers driver airbag force in the forward zone. Saab 9-3/9-5 file this sensor as B0084 and then disable the second airbag stage. The airbag lamp lights.
c: Open circuit or bent/corroded pins in the seat harness to the track sensor (FCA subtype -13)
Sensor loose or wrongly positioned on the seat track, so the Hall switch no longer sees the track edge
Low system voltage (FCA asks to check this before replacing the controller)
Internal fault of the Hall-effect seat track sensor
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver airbag may fire without seat position adjustment (e.g. second stage locked out)
Safety note: airbag system; unplug the seat and sensor connectors only de-energised; after replacing the sensor check its position output/calibration, specialist workshop only

B00B6.t: Driver Seat Recline Position Restraints Sensor
B00B6.d: B00B6 concerns a sensor that tells the restraint system how far the backrest of the driver seat is reclined. No carmaker documents this code publicly, and the NHTSA bulletin index has no entry for it. Patents show why the angle matters: an ATI patent lets the controller suppress or depower the airbag from seat position, back angle and belt spool-out alone, without looking at the occupant, and a Bosch application derives the tilt from a three-axis accelerometer in the seat back, uses a 45 degree limit to decide which airbags fire and feeds the angle into occupant classification. Autoliv even calibrated its classification mat at several back angles. If B00B6 is stored the module loses that input; the airbag lamp stays on until the sensor or its circuit is repaired.
c: Lead pinched or broken at the seat back hinge, where it flexes with every adjustment
Internal fault or loose mounting of the recline sensor
Sensor or seat back replaced without the required zero setting
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Airbag adaptation to a reclined seating position unavailable
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect seat and sensor plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate the sensor after replacement, specialist workshop only

B00B7.t: Driver Seat Occupant Position Sensor A
B00B7.d: B00B7 is the first of five occupant position sensors for the driver seat. No carmaker publishes the code, and J2012 does not say which sensor the letter A means. Position sensing serves the DASS route of FMVSS 208, which also exists for the driver: the driver bag must already be suppressed when a test dummy's head, neck or chest moves into a zone next to the cover that the maker defines. Ultrasound is one way to watch that zone; an Automotive Systems Laboratory patent crosses beams from transmitters in the headliner about eight inches in front of the airbag door, asks for an update within 10 ms and treats any undiagnosed fault as a reason to disable the bag. A stored B00B7 therefore means the module has lost this view and the airbag lamp is on.
c: Open or poor contact in the lead to position sensor A (e.g. headliner or trim harness)
Sensor face covered, dirty or misaligned after trim work
Internal fault of position sensor A
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Out-of-position suppression of the driver airbag unavailable

Safety note: airbag system; disconnect sensor and seat plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate/initialise position sensors after replacement, specialist workshop only

B00B8.t: Driver Seat Occupant Position Sensor B
B00B8.d: B00B8 names the second occupant position sensor at the driver seat. The code is not published by any carmaker, and the letter assignment is the maker's choice. Instead of looking down from the roof, a position sensor can sit at the airbag cover itself: a patent first filed in 1998 by Automotive Systems Laboratory, now held by Joyson, puts an active infrared, ultrasonic or electric field sensor in or near the inflator door, keeps the bag disabled while a large body part is in the at-risk zone and cites NHTSA findings that injuries drop if the bag stays off for occupants roughly 4 to 10 inches from the door. FMVSS 208 accepts such dynamic suppression for the driver bag. A stored B00B8 means this input has failed; the airbag lamp lights.
c: Fault in the lead to a sensor at the steering wheel or cover, e.g. via the clockspring
Sensor window covered by stickers, covers or dirt
Internal fault of position sensor B
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Airbag cannot be suppressed if the driver is very close to the cover
Safety note: airbag system; work at steering wheel, cover or sensor plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate the sensor after replacement, specialist workshop only

B00B9.t: Driver Seat Occupant Position Sensor C
B00B9.d: B00B9 is the third occupant position sensor of the driver seat. No carmaker publishes it. A third input could judge posture from the seat back: a patent now held by Joyson places two electric field electrodes under the seat-back cover, one across the upper middle and inboard side and one along the outboard edge, and combines them with seat weight to block the side airbag when a small occupant leans into its path. Honda applied the same idea on the passenger side with OPDS sensors in the seat-back, which must be initialised after the cover or sensor is replaced and can be upset by a damp seat. Whether a driver seat uses the letter C for such an electrode is not documented. A stored B00B9 brings on the airbag lamp.
c: Seat-back cover or sensor replaced without initialisation
Damaged seat-back harness or plug under the seat
Damp seat or accessory seat cover disturbing the electric field
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side airbag suppression for leaning occupants unavailable
Safety note: airbag system with seat side airbag; disconnect seat plugs only de-energised; initialise/calibrate after sensor or cover replacement, specialist workshop only

B00BA.t: Driver Seat Occupant Position Sensor D
B00BA.d: B00BA covers position input D, the fourth of the driver seat sensors. Its use by a carmaker is not documented publicly. Early out-of-position concepts mixed several sensor kinds: a 1989 Automotive Systems Laboratory patent uses a pyroelectric detector for presence, ultrasound for the distance to wheel and dashboard and a pressure transducer under the occupant for weight, recommends redundant sensors of each kind against false readings, warns the occupant with a lamp and fires a multi-cartridge driver inflator step by step to match size and position. A fourth slot thus suits a redundant sensor or one working on another principle, but no maker confirms what D stands for. B00BA indicates a fault in that input; the warning lamp for the airbags lights and position-based staging is limited.
c: Open or shorted lead to position sensor D
Signal disagreeing with the other position inputs, e.g. sensor dirty or misaligned
Internal fault of position sensor D
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Staged driver airbag deployment based on position restricted
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect sensor and seat plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate position sensors after replacement, specialist workshop only

B00BB.t: Driver Seat Occupant Position Sensor E
B00BB.d: B00BB is the fifth and last driver seat occupant position sensor in the J2012 block. No carmaker publishes this code. Position need not be measured on the body itself: an ATI patent family dating back to 1992 infers it from the seat, using a potentiometer or other track sensor, a recline angle sensor and belt spool-out from a shaft encoder in the retractor, and may suppress or depower the bag when the seat is fully forward. FMVSS 208 leaves both the suppression zone and the choice of sensors to the maker. Because J2012 already has separate codes for the indirect seat data, B00B5 for the track and B00B6 for the recline, the letter E probably denotes a further direct sensor, though no source confirms it. When B00BB is stored, the airbag lamp is lit.
c: Open, shorted or loose lead to position sensor E
Restraint module configured for a fifth position sensor that is not fitted
Internal fault of position sensor E
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Position-based adjustment of the driver airbag partly unavailable
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect sensor and seat plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate the sensor after replacement, specialist workshop only

B00C0.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Classification Sensor A
B00C0.d: B00C0 flags the first of up to five classification inputs in the front passenger seat. Their job comes from FMVSS 208: the passenger bag must stay off when a 12-month dummy sits in a listed child restraint or a newborn dummy lies in a car bed, yet it must be live for a 5th percentile woman, and a yellow PASSENGER AIR BAG OFF lamp reports the suppressed state. Honda's 2013 Fit shows a typical weight solution: sensors in the seat switch the bag off at 29 kg or less, the off lamp may flicker when the load sits near that limit, and bags hanging from the seat back or a rear passenger pushing on it can upset the reading. No carmaker publishes B00C0, and which sensor the letter A names is left open. The airbag lamp lights and classification falls back to a safe default.
c: Loose plug or chafed wire to input A under the passenger seat, often after the seat was removed
Classification sensor A itself delivers no or an implausible signal
Objects under the seat, items hanging on the seat back or pressure from the rear disturbing the measurement
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag off lamp shows a state that does not match the occupant
Safety note: passenger airbag may be wrongly enabled or disabled; seat and sensor plugs only de-energised, recalibrate the classification after repairs, specialist workshop only

B00C1.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Classification Sensor B
B00C1.d: B00C1 belongs to input B of the passenger seat classification. It is unpublished as such, but Toyota shows why a seat can carry several such sensors: on 2012–2013 Camry, Prius c and Yaris and 2013 Avalon, a left and a right weight detector sit between seat frame and rails. Their readings decide whether the passenger bag is armed, and they also serve as collision sensing. In campaign F0B (about 753,200 US cars) Toyota found that some seating habits or rough roads were taken for a rear impact, lighting the airbag lamp and AIR BAG OFF; dealers fitted new sensors, torqued them to 30 N·m, zeroed the system and verified its sensitivity. Whether B stands for such a right-hand cell is not documented. With B00C1 the airbag lamp is on.
c: Load cell B damaged or drifting, for example after the seat was forced or dropped
Seat pan or sensor bolts fitted under tension or with the wrong torque, preloading the cell
Zero-point calibration not done after sensor or seat work
Poor contact at the plug of sensor B
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag off lamp lit although an adult is seated
Safety note: passenger airbag status may be wrong; disconnect seat sensors only de-energised, keep tightening torques and run the zero-point calibration with the scan tool, specialist workshop only

B00C2.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Classification Sensor C
B00C2.d: B00C2 names the third classification input of the passenger seat. No carmaker documents it, and nobody has tied the letter to a known part. Another common sensor type besides load cells is a mat in the cushion. Hyundai extended the cover of the OCS mat in 2006–2011 Accent cars to 15 years with unlimited mileage: the mat should spot child seats and small occupants, and a faulty one could let the bag fire for a child; the lamp then lights with Hyundai's own codes B1447/B1448. Subaru tells technicians for 2014–2016 Forester that spilled drinks, rain through an open window or high humidity reaching the mat can set its occupant detection codes B1760 and B1650. Should C be such a mat, moisture and wear would be the prime suspects. A stored B00C2 lights the airbag lamp.
c: Liquid, rain or condensation soaked into the seat cushion and sensor
Sensor mat cracked or worn from years of getting in and out
Damaged lead or plug between mat and classification unit
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Fault may come and go with weather or after cleaning the seat
Safety note: a child on the passenger seat may not be detected; replace mats only as the maker's kit with the seat de-energised, then recalibrate, specialist workshop only

B00C3.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Classification Sensor D
B00C3.d: B00C3 is the fourth passenger seat classification input. No carmaker documents it under this number. Some classification signals are not a weight at all but a frequency, which makes them prone to electrical noise. Tesla reported for 2017–2019 Model 3 cars that the OCS frequency could leave its valid range because of interference on the passenger seat harness, so the airbag symbol appeared on the touchscreen. The first fix added a harness extension with a ferrite filter at the OCS module, which sits under the front of the seat; a later bulletin used a dedicated filter module, each about 0.15 h of labour. Whether a maker files such a signal as D is not known. A stored B00C3 means this input is missing or out of range, and the airbag lamp stays on until the cause is found.
c: Electrical interference coupled into the seat harness (seat heating, motors, routing near other leads)
Harness under tension or plug loose at the classification module when the seat moves
Internal fault of sensor D or the classification module
s: Airbag warning lamp or airbag symbol on the display
Fault may depend on seat position or on other electrical loads being switched on
Safety note: occupant classification unreliable; work on seat wiring only de-energised (12 V off, wait time), use the maker's filter or rework kit where one exists, specialist workshop only

B00C4.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Classification Sensor E
B00C4.d: B00C4 stands for the fifth and last passenger seat classification input; no public carmaker source uses it. Two field cases show what goes wrong besides wiring. Mazda found on 2016–2019 models that a phone, tablet or laptop lying on an empty passenger seat could make the system see a person: the passenger belt warning came on while PASS AIRBAG OFF stayed dark, and the advice was simply to keep devices off the seat. Land Rover quarantined 2025 Range Rover Sport SV cars because the OCS modules had been calibrated with the wrong weight, so the bag might not be switched off for a child seat as FMVSS 208 demands; new modules took 1.1 h. Calibration and plausibility therefore matter as much as the sensor. With B00C4 stored, the airbag lamp is lit and E is not trusted.
c: Classification module calibrated wrongly or not at all after replacement
Open or high-resistance contact on the lead to input E
Electronic devices or other objects on the seat confusing the sensing
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger belt warning or airbag status lamp does not match who or what is on the seat
Safety note: passenger airbag may stay enabled for a child seat; disconnect only de-energised, calibrate with the maker's procedure after any module change, specialist workshop only

B00C5.t: Passenger Seat Track Position Restraints Sensor
B00C5.d: B00C5 reports a fault of the sensor that tells the restraint controller where the passenger seat sits on its rails. FCA uses the code with exactly this name. A 2022 STAR case for the 2021 Dodge Durango treats B00C5-13, circuit open, with the airbag lamp on: check the yellow 30-way plug I6634A under the passenger seat and make sure the seat track position return wire R730 is seated in cavity B11, using a pull-push-pull test. GPOP tips 68264880A and 9003579 for Dart, Cherokee and Chrysler 200 list B00C5-13 among codes to raise with engineering before an ORC is replaced, and ask for pins that are bent, corroded or opened up to be checked. Such sensors are usually two-wire Hall switches that change state when the rail passes.
c: Terminal pushed back or loose in the under-seat connector (FCA Durango, R730 return wire)
Lead to the track sensor pinched or torn by the moving seat
Track position sensor faulty or its gap to the rail wrong after seat work
Restraint controller internal fault, only after wiring and sensor are ruled out
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag deployment can no longer be adapted to the seat position

Safety note: airbag system; disconnect under-seat plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), do not replace the restraint controller before checking pins, specialist workshop only

B00C6.t: Passenger Seat Recline Position Restraints Sensor
B00C6.d: B00C6 concerns the sensor that reports how far the passenger seat back is reclined. It appears neither in any public carmaker list nor in NHTSA bulletins. On the passenger side the angle matters mainly for classification, because a reclined back carries part of the occupant's weight. A patent filed in 1997 gives numbers: a cushion sensor read 42, 39 and 27 lb for a 60 lb child at three recline settings and 74, 64 and 49 lb for a 120 lb adult, so a recline sensor feeds a lookup table; there, below about 95 lb the bag is suppressed. A 2010 Delphi patent corrects bladder pressure with a backrest angle from an accelerometer or potentiometer. Without this input a small adult may be taken for a child. B00C6 lights the airbag lamp.
c: Lead to the recline sensor stretched or broken at the seat back hinge
Recline potentiometer or inclination sensor worn or faulty
Angle reference not learned after replacing the seat back or the sensor
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag off lamp may light for an adult sitting with the seat back reclined
Safety note: airbag system; work on seat back and sensor only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), relearn or calibrate afterwards, specialist workshop only

B00C7.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Position Sensor A
B00C7.d: B00C7 opens the row of five passenger seat position sensors, a code absent from all public carmaker documents. The passenger seat is where position sensing reached series cars: Honda's OPDS puts sensors in the passenger seat back that judge sitting height and whether a child leans toward the door, and then blocks the seat-mounted side airbag and lights a side airbag off indicator. Honda's 1998 patent describes the principle: band electrodes in the back cover are fed with a high-frequency signal, and a nearby body raises the current, so shoulders, head and a door-side lean can be told apart; the unit also diagnoses its own faults. Honda asks for the system to be initialised after seat-back parts are changed. Whether a maker maps such a sensor to A is not documented. B00C7 lights the airbag lamp.
c: Position system not initialised after seat cover, seat back sensor or control unit replacement
Electrode or lead in the seat back damaged, for instance by a non-original seat cover or repairs
Damp seat back or objects pressed against it
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side airbag off indicator lit although the passenger sits upright
Safety note: side airbag may be wrongly enabled or blocked; work on the seat back only de-energised and initialise the system afterwards, specialist workshop only

B00C8.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Position Sensor B
B00C8.d: B00C8 marks the second occupant position sensor of the passenger seat. No carmaker publishes it. A position input does not have to look at the person; it can come from how the load spreads over the seat. In a Honda application filed in 2002, a weight unit under each side of the seat carries four strain gauges in a bridge; comparing the front and rear gauge pairs shows whether the occupant sits on the front edge, and comparing the two sides shows a lean to left or right. FMVSS 208 accepts dynamic suppression for the passenger: the bag must already be suppressed when a 3- or 6-year-old dummy moves its head, neck or torso into a zone in front of the cover, a zone each maker defines for itself. Whether B means such a load-based signal is not documented. B00C8 brings on the airbag lamp.
c: Plug or lead to sensor B damaged when the seat was moved or removed
Strain gauge bridge or position sensor B faulty, drifting with temperature
Seat frame mounted under tension, so the load split looks implausible
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag may be suppressed or released without regard to sitting position
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect seat sensors only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), recalibrate after work on the seat, specialist workshop only

B00C9.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Position Sensor C
B00C9.d: B00C9 names position sensor C of the passenger seat, and no carmaker lists it publicly. One concept for a third input watches the gap between torso and seat back: a patent first filed by Automotive Systems Laboratory in 1998, now with Joyson, pairs an electric field sensor in the cushion with a capacitive or radar proximity sensor in the back, aimed at the band about 10 to 18 inches above the cushion. While the torso rests within about 2 inches of the back the bag may fire; if it has been away by more than that for over 50 ms, the bag is disabled. If the back sensor keeps seeing someone the cushion sensor misses, the patent treats that as a fault. FMVSS 208 leaves the choice of such sensors to the maker. B00C9 lights the airbag lamp.
c: Lead to the seat back sensor broken at the hinge or after trim work
Proximity sensor C faulty or its signal disagrees with the cushion sensor
Thick accessory covers or a wet seat back weakening the field signal
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Airbag status lamp may change while the passenger leans forward
Safety note: airbag system; seat back and sensor only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), no third-party seat covers over sensors, specialist workshop only

B00CA.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Position Sensor D
B00CA.d: B00CA is position input D, the fourth for the passenger seat. Its use is not documented by any carmaker. Optical sensing is one way to fill such a slot: a patent family of Automotive Technologies International, going back to 1995, places imagers with infrared lighting at the A-pillar, in the headliner or on top of the dashboard, two arrays spaced apart for depth, and calls an occupant out of position once head or chest come within about 5 inches of the airbag door. Pattern recognition separates a rear-facing child seat from a person, and the authors judge ultrasound with roughly 10 ms per update as too slow for tracking during a crash.
