For the passenger, FMVSS 208 permits dynamic suppression and prescribes no method. With B00CA stored, that view is lost and the airbag warning shows.
c: Lead to sensor D damaged at the pillar, headliner or dashboard after trim or glass work
Sensor view blocked or lens dirty, for example by stickers or accessories
Internal fault of position sensor D
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Out-of-position suppression for the passenger no longer available
Safety note: airbag system; work at pillar, headliner or dashboard only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), recheck sensor alignment afterwards, specialist workshop only

B00CB.t: Passenger Seat Occupant Position Sensor E
B00CB.d: B00CB is the fifth and last passenger seat occupant position sensor. No carmaker publishes it. Position alone is not always enough; an early patent of Automotive Technologies International, first filed in 1992, also wants the speed at which the occupant approaches the bag. It uses ultrasound bursts near 50 kHz, taking distance from the echo time and speed from the Doppler shift, or modulated infrared and radar, mounted in the headliner, on the mirror or on the airbag cover. In a 30 mph barrier crash it allows only about 8 ms of sensing for someone 9 inches away but 57 ms at 24 inches. FMVSS 208 lets the maker define the suppression zone that such sensors watch. Whether E denotes a velocity or a further distance sensor is not documented. B00CB lights the airbag lamp.
c: Open or shorted lead to sensor E in the headliner, mirror base or dashboard
Transducer of sensor E faulty or covered
Restraint module coded for a sensor the vehicle does not carry
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag deploys without position-based suppression or staging
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect sensors only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), check configuration after replacement, specialist workshop only

B00D0.d: B00D0 reports a fault in the driver's seat belt warning, meaning the lamp, its circuit or the output or message that drives it, not the buckle switch. No carmaker documents it publicly. The warning itself is mandatory: FMVSS 208 S7.3 asks at ignition-on for a 4 to 8 s chime plus a lamp for at least 60 s while the driver is unbelted, or a 4 to 8 s lamp with the chime tied to the unfastened belt; from September 2028 S7.5 keeps the lamp on as long as the belt is open and adds a second chime phase above 10 km/h. FMVSS 101 forbids cancelling the telltale early. UN R16 asks for a first visual stage of at least 4 s and a second, audible one of 30 s or more, starting by 25 km/h, 500 m or 60 s. With B00D0 the driver may get no reminder at all.
c: Open or shorted lamp circuit or connector between restraint module and cluster
Warning lamp or LED in the instrument cluster failed
Belt warning message not received by the cluster, for example after a cluster change without configuration
s: Driver belt warning lamp stays dark or stays on regardless of the belt
Airbag or restraint warning lamp may be on
Safety note: legally required warning missing; buckle up regardless, cluster and restraint wiring only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop

B00D1.d: B00D1 covers the passenger seat belt warning. Unlike the driver warning, it only makes sense if the car knows the seat is occupied, so it leans on occupant sensing. No carmaker documents the code. Ford's 2014 F-150 uses the passenger sensing system to decide who gets Belt-Minder reminders: above 6 mph and after 1 to 2 minutes, lamp and chime come on for six seconds every 25 seconds for about five minutes. Honda's 2013 Fit lights the passenger warning about 6 s after ignition-on but not for a child or slight adult whom the weight sensors miss. Mazda saw the passenger warning come on for an empty seat holding a laptop or phone. FMVSS 208 S7.5 requires a passenger warning visible to the driver from September 2028. B00D1 points to the lamp side, not the buckle.
c: Open or shorted circuit to the passenger belt lamp or its display segment
Lamp, LED or display unit for the passenger warning failed
Occupancy information missing or wrong, so the warning logic cannot run
s: No passenger belt reminder, or a reminder for an empty seat
Airbag or restraint warning lamp may be on
Safety note: passenger may ride unbelted without warning; wiring work only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop

B00D2.d: B00D2 means the restraint module has found a fault in the circuit of its primary warning lamp, the airbag or SRS light. FMVSS 208 S4.5.2 requires such a readiness indicator, watching its own readiness and within the driver's view, and FMVSS 101 lets it push other messages out of a shared display. No carmaker publishes B00D2. Saab shows what the check looks like under its own older numbers: on the 1998 9-3, B1227 is set when the lamp output reads above 5 V for 1.25 s, a short to positive that keeps the lamp from its 3 to 4 s bulb check, and B1228 when it reads below 1 V or above 10 kOhm while off, an open or short to ground that turns on the central warning lamp instead. Until fixed, the driver may not see further airbag faults.
c: Bulb or LED of the airbag warning lamp failed
Lamp lead open, shorted to ground or to battery voltage, or loose cluster connector
Internal fault in the instrument cluster circuit board
s: Airbag lamp does not come on for the bulb check at ignition-on, or stays on
A substitute warning such as a central warning lamp or a tone may appear
Safety note: airbag faults may go unnoticed; work on cluster and restraint wiring only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop only

B00D3.d: B00D3 refers to a second restraint malfunction indicator. No carmaker documents which lamp that is, so its meaning has to be inferred. One reading is a backup for the main lamp: the 1995 Saab 900 calls its SRS light warning lamp 1 and switches the central warning lamp on for good if that circuit fails. Saturn patented a similar fallback in 1991, using the seat belt lamp as second SIR indicator once a voltage check or photocell shows the airbag lamp is dead, flashing ten times and then glowing for ten minutes, or flashing constantly. Another reading is a separate telltale, since FMVSS 101 names a side air bag malfunction lamp besides the main airbag lamp. In either case B00D3 reports a fault in that second display circuit, not in the airbags themselves.
c: Open or shorted circuit to the second restraint indicator
Second indicator lamp or LED failed
Restraint module or cluster configured for an indicator the vehicle does not have
s: Airbag lamp on, second indicator dark or not doing its bulb check
Backup warning missing if the main airbag lamp also fails
Safety note: restraint warnings incomplete; work on cluster and wiring only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop only

B00D4.d: B00D4 concerns the audible restraint warning, the tone that stands in when a fault cannot be shown by the lamp. Ford's 2014 F-150 manual describes it: system readiness is signalled by the warning light, or by a backup tone if the light is out, and a problem announces itself as five beeps in a row, repeated until the fault and the lamp are put right. Audi's 1986 patent explains why such a fallback exists: a blown fuse could kill both the airbag module and its lamp, so the driver would believe the system was fine; it mentions an audible alarm as an alternative signal. No carmaker publishes B00D4. A stored code means the restraint module sees a fault in its chime or speaker path, so a later lamp failure could go wholly unannounced.
c: Open or shorted lead to the chime or speaker used for restraint warnings
Chime module or cluster speaker failed
Tone request from the restraint module not received by the sounding unit
s: No warning tone where one would be expected, other warning chimes may also be silent
Airbag warning lamp on
Safety note: fallback warning missing; work on cluster and restraint wiring only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop

B00D5.d: B00D5 concerns the lamp that tells the front occupants the passenger airbag is off. FMVSS 208 wants it yellow, worded PASSENGER AIR BAG OFF (short form PASS AIR BAG OFF) and separate from the readiness lamp; Ford's 2014 F-150 places it by the radio and lights it briefly at start as a self-test. Mitsubishi defines the code in its 2022 airbag index as PASS A/B INDICATOR: subtype -11 for a short to ground, -12 for a short to power and -13 for an open circuit, each checked with the ignition on and set after 2 s; harness, the indicator itself or the airbag control unit are listed as causes. Ford logged B00D5:01 in the restraint module of 2021 Edge and Nautilus among network faults, cured by updating the gateway module. Occupants may be misled about the airbag.
c: Indicator lead shorted to ground, shorted to power or open (Mitsubishi -11/-12/-13)
Passenger airbag off indicator itself failed
Network or gateway software fault, as on 2021 Ford Edge/Nautilus (SSM 50127)
Internal fault of the airbag control unit output
s: Passenger airbag off lamp stays dark during the start check or shows the wrong state
Airbag warning lamp on
Safety note: occupants cannot see whether the passenger airbag is off; do not fit a rear-facing child seat until repaired, wiring only de-energised, specialist workshop

B00DF.d: B00DF is set for the key switch that lets the passenger airbag be turned off by hand. FMVSS 208 S4.5.4 allowed it on vehicles built before September 2012 with no forward rear seats or a short rear row; it must take the key, stay apart from the ignition and keep the bag off until switched back, and 49 CFR 595.5 governs retrofits under an NHTSA letter. Two makers use the code. FCA describes B00DF-95, incorrect assembly, on 2018–2021 Jeep Wrangler built without the on/off switch option CGZ: unused dash harness circuits R167/R168 should be checked and isolated at the ORC. Ford reports B00DF:4A after self-tests on 2024 Nautilus, from an internal counter fixed over the air, and on 2026–2027 Transit, cleared with FDRS. A real fault lights the airbag lamp.
c: Switch circuits present in the harness of a vehicle without the switch, damaged or picking up faults (FCA B00DF-95)
Key switch worn or its lead open or shorted
Restraint module software counter or configuration error (Ford B00DF:4A)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag does not follow the switch position, or the off lamp disagrees with it
Safety note: passenger airbag state uncertain; no rear-facing child seat on that seat until checked, wiring and switch only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop

B00E0.t: Third Row Left Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control
B00E0.d: B00E0 points to a second pretensioner stage (B) on the left seat of the third row. Such a stage would be an extra device next to the retractor, typically a lap or anchor tensioner that pulls on the lower belt end. No carmaker publishes B00E0. Mercedes-Benz, which does fit third-row tensioners (the 2017 GLS manual lists them for every third-row belt), logs the left third-row retractor under B00E7 in topic LI54.21-P-070658, i.e. on the C slot, and never names a B stage back there. GM describes anchor units only for front seats, and Joyson pairs its lap pretensioner with a retractor unit against submarining. A stored code lights the airbag lamp; the stage is treated as not available.
c: Plug of the lap or anchor tensioner at the left third-row seat loose, unlatched or corroded
Lead strained or chafed by folding and stowing the third-row seat
Airbag module coded for a B stage the vehicle does not have (after module or seat replacement)
Internal open or short in the tensioner squib
s: Airbag warning lamp lit
Lap belt at the left third-row seat may not be pulled tight in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic part – work only with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed, preferably at a specialist workshop

B00E1.t: Third Row Right Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control
B00E1.d: On the right seat of the third row, B00E1 stands for a B-stage tensioner whose firing loop shows an open, a short or an out-of-window resistance. In no public service document does a manufacturer use B00E1. Where Mercedes-Benz fits a right third-row tensioner, it is the retractor, and the airbag unit reports it as B00E6 (LI54.21-P-070658, versions of March and June 2020). A B stage there would be a buckle or anchor device; NHTSA's 2013 study of pretensioners explains how a buckle unit drags the buckle down by a cable when its charge fires, and GM lists buckle, retractor and anchor units as the three possible types. Expect a lit airbag lamp and no tensioning from this stage until the loop is repaired.
c: Connector of the right third-row buckle or anchor tensioner not fully seated
Wiring under the cargo floor or side trim pinched or damaged by loads
Raised contact resistance at the airbag module plug
s: Airbag lamp on in the instrument cluster
Occupant at the right of the third row gets no B-stage tensioning
Safety note: the tensioner contains a pyrotechnic charge; only work on it de-energised (battery off, wait time) and leave it to a specialist workshop

B00E2.t: Third Row Center Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control
B00E2.d: B00E2 would report the firing circuit of a B-stage tensioner at the centre seat of the third row. This is about the rarest slot in the pretensioner table: a centre seat in row three is uncommon, and a second tensioner stage on it even more so. No manufacturer documents the code. For comparison, the third-row tensioners in Mercedes vehicles are listed only as left and right retractor loops (B00E7/B00E6 in LI54.21-P-070658), and the GLS manual of 2017 likewise speaks of retractor tensioners. A B stage would act on the lap section, as Joyson's lap pretensioner does in combination with a retractor. If the code appears, check first whether the module's equipment coding matches the seats actually fitted.
c: Module variant coding expects a centre B stage that is not installed
Plug under the third-row centre seat disconnected after seat removal
Squib of the centre lap tensioner open or shorted internally
s: Airbag indicator stays on after the self-test
Centre occupant of the third row may lack lap-belt tensioning in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic restraint component – disconnect the battery, wait the specified time and have the work done by a specialist

B00E3.t: Second Row Left Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control
B00E3.d: B00E3 is the C-stage tensioner of the left outer rear seat, and two makers document it codegenau. Stellantis case S2408000089 (Jeep Wrangler 2023) has the occupant restraint controller store B00E3-13, named there for the retractor tensioner at the left of row two, after a service visit; the fix was to secure connector D3244A with a push-pull-push check, no parts. Mercedes-Benz topic LI54.21-P-070658 (A-Class, CLA, later GLB) reads B00E313 as an open squib in the tensioning retractor behind the left rear passenger, usually caused by high contact resistance at the airbag unit plug; reconnecting comes first, a new control unit only if the fault returns. So C here means the retractor, as Joyson's pyrotechnic retractor describes. Airbag lamp on.
c: Retractor pretensioner plug not latched after trim or seat work (Jeep Wrangler 2023, connector D3244A)
High contact resistance at the airbag control unit connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Lead to the left rear retractor chafed at the C-pillar or seat frame
Faulty squib in the retractor pretensioner
s: Airbag warning lamp or SRS message in the cluster
Left rear shoulder belt is not retracted in a crash
Safety note: the retractor pretensioner is pyrotechnic; work only with the system de-energised (battery off, wait time) and preferably at a specialist workshop

B00E4.t: Second Row Right Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control
B00E4.d: B00E4 belongs to the outboard seat on the right in the back and its C-stage tensioner. Mercedes-Benz uses it in that sense: every version of LI54.21-P-070658 seen here (December 2019 to June 2020) lists B00E413 as an open in the squib of the tensioning retractor at the rear right. The topic blames higher resistance at the SRS unit connector rather than the tensioner and tells technicians to trace the wire, reseat the plugs and replace the unit only on recurrence. The retractor sits behind the rear trim or in the seat and winds the webbing back when fired, as GM's rescue guide and Joyson explain. No public bulletin from another maker cites B00E4. While the code is stored, the airbag lamp or SRS message stays on.
c: Poor contact at the SRS control unit plug (Mercedes A-Class/CLA/GLB)
Plug at the right rear retractor loose after trim removal
Airbag control unit itself faulty (fault returns after reconnecting)
Squib in the right rear retractor open
s: SRS message or airbag lamp permanently displayed
Right rear passenger loses shoulder-belt tensioning
Safety note: pyrotechnic tensioner – only work on it with the battery disconnected and after the wait time, ideally at a specialist workshop

B00E5.t: Second Row Center Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control
B00E5.d: B00E5 covers a C-stage tensioner at the middle seat of row two. No manufacturer publishes it. Rear centre tensioners are scarce: Mercedes' 2017 GLS manual names tensioners only for the outer second-row belts, and the Mercedes bulletin that assigns B00E3 and B00E4 to the outer rear retractors has no centre entry. IIHS research on rear occupants (2020) states that belt countermeasures for the rear are available yet rarely fitted, so such slots often stay empty. If a vehicle does carry a centre retractor or buckle tensioner, the airbag module watches its squib like any other and sets B00E5 for an open, a short or a resistance drift; the warning lamp then comes on and that seat loses its tensioning.
c: Centre-seat tensioner plug under the rear bench not engaged
Module coded for a centre tensioner that the vehicle lacks
Lead damaged where it passes the split or folding rear bench hinge
s: Airbag lamp on
Rear centre passenger may not be held back early in a frontal crash
Safety note: the tensioner holds a pyrotechnic charge – battery off, wait time observed, repair at a specialist workshop

B00E6.t: Third Row Right Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control
B00E6.d: Note the order in this block: B00E6 is the right seat of the third row, while B00E7 is the left. Mercedes-Benz fills B00E6 with the retractor tensioner on that seat: LI54.21-P-070658 (first issued December 2019 for A-Class and CLA, extended to GLB in version 4) reads B00E613 as an interrupted igniter in the tensioning retractor on the right of row three. The stated cause is again contact resistance at the airbag unit plug. Mercedes' GLS manual of 2017 confirms that the brand gives third-row belts their own tensioners and force limiters. No other maker publishes the code. With B00E6 stored, the airbag lamp is on and the right third-row belt will not be tightened.
c: Contact resistance at the airbag unit connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Plug of the right third-row retractor behind the cargo trim loose
Wiring in the rear wheel arch area pinched by trim or cargo
Squib of the right third-row retractor defective
s: SRS message or airbag warning lamp
Right third-row belt stays slack in a crash
Safety note: work on this pyrotechnic retractor only de-energised (battery disconnected, wait time) and preferably by a specialist

B00E7.t: Third Row Left Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control
B00E7.d: B00E7 marks the C-stage tensioner of the third row's left seat, listed after its right-hand twin B00E6. Mercedes-Benz documents it: LI54.21-P-070658 uses B00E713 when the firing pill of the left third-row tensioning retractor shows an open, in the same list as the rear and driver retractors. In that topic the remedy does not start with the tensioner but with fault-tracing the wire and reconnecting the restraint unit plugs; only a recurring fault calls for a new control unit of at least level Q4. Joyson describes this kind of pyrotechnic retractor, which can sit in the body or the seat structure. No other maker publishes B00E7. Airbag lamp on; the left third-row occupant is not tensioned.
c: Raised resistance at the restraint unit plug
Left third-row retractor connector disturbed during trim or seat work
Control unit below the required level, fault keeps returning
s: Airbag lamp or fixed SRS message
No pretensioning for the left third-row seat
Safety note: pyrotechnic device – disconnect the battery and wait before touching it; have it serviced at a specialist workshop

B00E8.t: Third Row Center Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control
B00E8.d: B00E8 closes the C row of the table with the centre seat of the third row. No manufacturer publishes it, and the one public list that uses this block, Mercedes-Benz LI54.21-P-070658, stops at a left and a right third-row retractor (B00E7, B00E6). A centre tensioner in row three would mostly appear in large vans or SUVs with a three-seat rear bench. Joyson's retractor pretensioner is compact enough to go into a seat frame, which is where a centre unit would have to live. IIHS frontal tests of 2019 compared rear dummies in vehicles with standard belts and with tensioners plus load limiters, and noted such rear countermeasures are not yet widespread. If B00E8 is set, the airbag lamp is on and the centre belt is not tightened.
c: Connector of the seat-mounted centre retractor unplugged after removing the rear bench
Restraint module coded for a three-seat third row on a two-seat vehicle
Squib of the centre retractor faulty
s: Airbag warning lamp illuminated
Centre seat of the third row without belt tensioning
Safety note: contains a pyrotechnic charge – no work without disconnecting the battery and waiting; leave it to a specialist workshop

B00F0.t: Driver Inflatable Seat Belt Deployment Control
B00F0.d: B00F0 is the firing circuit for an inflatable belt at the driver's seat: a section of webbing that a gas source fills in a crash so the load spreads over a wider area of the chest. The production inflatable belts known from Ford and Mercedes-Benz sit only at rear outer seats; no carmaker documents B00F0. The idea for front seats is old and well described in patents, for example a Daimler design of 2010 with the gas generator at the lower anchor beside the B-pillar and folded webbing held by tear threads, and an Autoliv design with inflators mounted on the seat back. Joyson also lists a belt-attached restraint supplement among its airbag innovations. If the code is set, the airbag lamp comes on.
c: Airbag module variant expects a driver inflatable belt that is not fitted
Plug of the belt gas generator at the lower anchor or seat loose or corroded
Lead to the inflator chafed by seat adjustment
Igniter of the belt inflator faulty
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver belt would not inflate in a crash
Safety note: the belt contains a pyrotechnic gas generator; work only de-energised (battery off, wait time) and at a specialist workshop

B00F1.t: Passenger Inflatable Seat Belt Deployment Control
B00F1.d: B00F1 is the front passenger counterpart of B00F0, reserved for an inflatable belt at that seat. No manufacturer documents it, and no series vehicle is publicly known to have a passenger inflatable belt; Mercedes' S-Class manual offers the beltbag only for the outer rear belts. A passenger version would still face the same engineering choices as the patents show: Allied Chemical patented as early as 1972 a buckle that routes gas from a floor-mounted inflator through tongue and buckle into lap and shoulder belt, so the belt itself needs no wires, while Autoliv's 2002 design mounts separate inflators on the seat back. The airbag module would watch the igniter loop and set B00F1 for an open, a short or bad resistance.
c: Module coded for a passenger inflatable belt that the car does not have
Connector at the buckle-side inflator under the passenger seat loose
Seat wiring damaged by objects under the seat or by seat movement
s: Airbag lamp lit in the cluster
Passenger belt cannot inflate in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic belt inflator – disconnect the battery, respect the wait time and have repairs done by a specialist workshop

B00F2.t: Second Row Left Inflatable Seat Belt Deployment Control
B00F2.d: B00F2 covers the inflatable belt at the left outer seat of row two, the position where such belts actually reached production. Ford offered them from the 2011 Explorer; its 2018 owner's manual puts the bag into the shoulder part of the belts at both outer seats in row two, filled with cooled gas at lower pressure, deployed in frontal, side and rollover crashes and monitored by the same module and lamp as the front belts. Ford itself logs faults under its own codes B141B/B141C: programme 21B11 (Explorer 2014–2016) traces them to damaged seat harness wires at the rear inflatable belt connector. Mercedes-Benz fits its beltbag to the outer rear seats of the S-Class. Neither publishes B00F2. Airbag lamp on when set.
c: Internal wire damage in the second-row seat harness at the belt connector (Ford programme 21B11)
Plug of the inflator under the left rear seat loose after folding or removing the seat
Fault in the belt inflator igniter
s: Airbag warning light on
Left rear inflatable belt may not deploy in a crash
Safety note: the belt holds a stored-gas or pyrotechnic inflator – battery off, wait time, work only at a specialist workshop

B00F3.t: Second Row Center Inflatable Seat Belt Deployment Control
B00F3.d: B00F3 refers to an inflatable belt at the centre seat of the second row. No manufacturer documents the code, and the known systems leave this seat out: Ford's 2018 Explorer manual limits its inflatable belts to the outermost second-row positions, and Mercedes fits its beltbag to the outer rear belts (S-Class manual 2017); the E-Class manual of the same year lists the belt air bag as a frontal-impact device. A centre version would be harder to package because the gas usually enters at the buckle or lower anchor; NHTSA's belt tensile study notes that the 2011 Explorer belt needed a retractor in the lap loop because its inflator was attached to the buckle. If set, the airbag lamp is lit.
c: Restraint module configured for a centre inflatable belt not present in the vehicle
Connector at the centre buckle inflator under the bench disconnected
Igniter of the centre belt inflator open or shorted
s: Airbag indicator remains on
Rear centre belt would not inflate in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic or stored-gas inflator – only work with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed, at a specialist workshop

B00F4.t: Second Row Right Inflatable Seat Belt Deployment Control
B00F4.d: B00F4 covers the inflatable belt on the outboard right seat of row two. The hardware exists in series cars, but the code is not documented by any maker. Ford's Explorer (2014–2016) logs belt faults as B141B and/or B141C; supplement 2 of programme 21B11 (June 2022) stresses checking those codes first and allows a separate labour time when both are present, then repositioning or replacing the seat harness pigtail. Mercedes-Benz offers the beltbag on rear belts of the E-Class; its manual warns against routing a child seat through a belt carrying the BELTBAG label. Daimler's 2010 patent places the gas generator at the lower belt anchor and folds the webbing with tear threads. With B00F4 set, the airbag lamp is on.
c: Worn or broken wires in the right second-row seat pigtail (Ford Explorer 2014–2016)
Inflator plug at the lower belt anchor or under the seat not latched
s: Airbag lamp illuminated
Right rear inflatable belt not ready to deploy
Safety note: do not open or probe the belt or its inflator; battery off, wait time, and leave the job to a specialist workshop

B00F5.t: Third Row Left Inflatable Seat Belt Deployment Control
B00F5.d: B00F5 opens the third-row part of the inflatable-belt block with the left seat; B00F6 (centre) and B00F7 (right) follow. No manufacturer documents B00F5, and the known systems stop at row two: Ford's Explorer has its inflatable belts only at the second-row outer seats, even though it has a third row, and Mercedes offers the beltbag for rear belts of S- and E-Class (outer seats in the S-Class). The inflatable belt in NHTSA's 2021 test series was likewise a second-row belt. Technically a third-row unit would work like the others, with a bag in the shoulder webbing and an inflator near buckle or anchor, as the Autoliv patent outlines. If the code is stored, the airbag lamp is on and that belt will not inflate.
c: Airbag module coded with a third-row inflatable belt that is not installed
Plug at the left third-row belt inflator disturbed when folding the seat
Defective igniter in the third-row belt inflator
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left third-row inflatable belt not available in a crash
Safety note: inflator with explosive igniter – disconnect the battery, wait, and have it handled by a specialist workshop

B00F6.t: Third Row Center Inflatable Seat Belt Deployment Control
B00F6.d: B00F6 names the deployment circuit for an inflatable belt at the middle seat of row three. That seat is the least likely place for such a belt: the series systems on record sit at outboard rear seats, Ford's Explorer only in row two and Mercedes' beltbag on the outer rear belts. The 2017 Mercedes GLS manual, for a three-row SUV, lists pyrotechnic tensioners and force limiters for its third-row belts, but no beltbag there. NHTSA's belt test series likewise used the inflatable Explorer belt from a second-row seat. Joyson's belt-attached restraint study for new interior layouts shows where such bags might spread. No maker publishes B00F6; if set, the airbag lamp is on and that belt would not inflate.
c: Airbag module coded for a centre third-row inflatable belt the vehicle does not have
Inflator plug of the centre belt loosened when the third-row seat was folded or removed
Igniter in the centre belt inflator out of its resistance window
s: Airbag warning lamp lit
Centre third-row inflatable belt would not inflate in a crash
Safety note: igniter-equipped part – battery off, observe waiting time, work only in a specialist workshop

B00F7.t: Third Row Right Inflatable Seat Belt Deployment Control
B00F7.d: B00F7 closes the inflatable-belt block with the right seat of row three. No manufacturer documents it. The nearest real case is one row further forward: on the 2014–2016 Ford Explorer, the dealer bulletin for programme 21B11 names B141C as the right and B141B as the left second-row harness code and has technicians re-route or repair the seat pigtail when either appears. Ford's 2018 owner manual puts the rear inflatable belts in the shoulder webbing of the outboard second-row seats only; on the right of row three there are child-seat anchors but no bag. Mercedes lists beltbags for the outer rear belts of the S-Class, and Autoliv's 2002 patent shows one inflator feeding belts through a gas guide. With B00F7 present, the airbag lamp stays on.
c: Chafed wires in the right rear seat harness, as seen one row forward on the Explorer (B141C)
Restraint module variant coding expects a right third-row inflatable belt
Open or shorted igniter in the right third-row belt inflator
s: Airbag lamp stays on after start-up check
Right third-row inflatable belt not armed
Safety note: never probe the inflator circuit with a test lamp; disconnect battery, wait, leave it to a specialist

B0100.t: Sensor Cleaning Air Blower Actuator A
B0100.d: B0100 is the general fault for air blower A in a sensor cleaning system, i.e. the fan or motor unit itself rather than its wiring or relay (those are B0102 and B0104). Such blowers keep camera lenses and lidar windows clear of droplets, dust and insects. Ford's patent US12115948B2 mounts a blower on the sensor bracket; it pulls outside air through an intake duct and pushes it out across a cylindrical lidar window and a camera lens. In Ford's roof-mounted sensor tiara for its self-driving test fleet, slots release an air curtain that deflects most bugs, and air also dries a lens after washing. Which blower is A is up to the maker. No vehicle manufacturer documents B0100 publicly. A dead blower lets dirt build up until the sensor reports itself blocked.
c: Blower A motor worn, seized or with an open winding
Impeller blocked by ice, leaves or debris in the intake duct
Corroded or loose plug directly at blower A
s: Sensor blocked or cleaning fault message
Driver assistance or automated driving functions limited or switched off
No airflow audible or felt at the sensor outlets

B0101.t: Sensor Cleaning Air Blower Actuator B
B0101.d: B0101 reports a fault of the second cleaning air source, blower B. A second unit makes sense where sensors are spread over the body: a roof pod and a bumper or corner sensor need separate air supplies. Not every design uses a fan; Uber's 2016 patent (now Aurora) feeds lidar and camera air knives from a compressor and accumulator held at about 140–160 psi, with one solenoid valve per outlet and a pressure sensor that raises a warning on a leak. AUMOVIO's lidar nozzles use compressed air to strip water droplets and to clear dust without washer fluid, and Kautex's Allegro systems combine water and air for camera and lidar. The split between A and B is not published by any carmaker, nor is B0101 itself.
c: Blower or compressor B worn out or drawing too much current
Leaking or split air hose so blower B cannot build pressure
Water or salt ingress into blower B at an exposed mounting point
s: Cleaning fault shown for the sensor group served by blower B
Water droplets or dust remain on lidar or camera window
Assistance functions reduced when the affected sensor goes blind

B0102.t: Sensor Cleaning Air Blower Actuator A Control
B0102.d: B0102 narrows the blower A problem down to its control path: the controlling module sees a wrong voltage or current on the line that commands blower A, typically an open circuit, a short to ground or a short to supply. In Ford's lidar cleaning patent US10569746B2 a computer opens airflow from a blower or compressor by driving an electric solenoid valve and may modulate it; when window opacity exceeds about 30 %, air runs first and autonomous mode may be dropped. Ford's later patent US12115948B2 places the blower beside the sensor on its bracket, so its feed runs into an exposed pod. Valeo notes that an obstructed lens can end automated operation. No carmaker publishes B0102. Unlike B0100, the blower itself may be fine here.
c: Broken control wire or pin between module and blower A
Control line of blower A shorted to ground or to battery voltage
Output stage in the cleaning or maintenance module defective
s: Blower A never starts although cleaning is requested
Blower A runs constantly when the line is shorted to supply
Sensor blocked message and limited assistance features

B0103.t: Sensor Cleaning Air Blower Actuator B Control
B0103.d: With B0103 the module flags the command line of blower B, not the blower: open wire, short or a driver that cannot switch. In compressed-air layouts the controlled element is often a valve bank. Uber's patent lets the controller fire individual solenoids for set times, for example one valve for three seconds, so a single faulty drive line leaves only part of the lidar or one camera without air. Ford’s test-car tiara blows an air curtain through slots beside each lens to keep insects off, so a dead control line on the B side lets dirt settle where air should flow. Kautex says its software prioritises cleaning points by coordinating actuators. Which outlets belong to B is unpublished, and no carmaker documents B0103; its partner on the A side is B0102.
c: Damaged harness or connector in the control path of blower B
Solenoid coil of the B air valve open or shorted, where air is valve-switched
Failed driver for blower B in the controlling module
s: Lens streaks or droplets remain after a wash cycle
Cleaning warning for sensors on the B circuit only
Assistance features temporarily unavailable in rain or dust

B0104.t: Sensor Cleaning Air Blower Actuator A Control Relay
B0104.d: B0104 points at the relay that switches power to blower A. A fan motor draws more current than a module output can carry, so a relay is a natural choice: the module energises the coil (terminals 85/86 in HELLA's scheme) and the contact (30/87) feeds the motor. HELLA's relay brochure explains that coils may carry a diode or resistor against switch-off spikes and that relays are checked for coil resistance and contact voltage drop. Faults here are an open or shorted coil, welded or burnt contacts, or a missing feed. Ford's US12115948B2 places the blower on the sensor bracket, and the Ford tiara uses that air to shield lenses from insects, as eeNews reports. No carmaker publishes B0104; the B-side relay is B0105.
c: Burnt or welded contacts in the blower A relay
Relay coil open or its control wire interrupted
Blown fuse or loose socket on the relay supply side
s: Blower A dead, or running without command if contacts are welded
No relay click when cleaning is requested
Sensor cleaning warning with possible loss of assistance functions

B0105.t: Sensor Cleaning Air Blower Actuator B Control Relay
B0105.d: B0105 is the relay fault on the B side of the sensor-cleaning air supply. If B is a compressor rather than a small fan, as in Uber's patent where a compressor charges an accumulator and recharges once pressure drops to roughly 130–140 psi, the relay carries a sizable inrush current, and pitted contacts become the usual weak point. HELLA lists change-over and make relays for motors such as fans and names the checks: dropout voltage, contact drop, coil resistance. AUMOVIO stresses that air keeps a lidar usable in bad weather by blowing off droplets, so a stuck relay shows up first in rain. No carmaker has published B0105 or what B supplies.
c: Contacts of relay B pitted by high motor or compressor inrush current
Relay B coil or its suppression diode failed
Corroded relay socket or wrong relay type fitted
s: Blower or compressor B does not start, or will not switch off
Droplets stay on sensor windows in rain
Assistance functions drop out when a sensor is reported blocked

B0106.d: B0106 opens a row of four lidar washer actuators (A to D). The actuator is whatever delivers fluid to a lidar window: a washer pump or an electromagnetic valve. In Ford's patent US10569746B2 a computer triggers a wash pump for the spray nozzle of a roof lidar, after an air nozzle has run for about 5 s and the window is still more than about 20 % opaque; a wiper follows only if needed. Solero builds 2/2- and 3/2-way valves that send washer fluid to individual nozzles, including lidar. AUMOVIO's lidar nozzles clean the dome with pressurised liquid using the Coanda effect. Which lidar or nozzle the maker calls A is not published, and no carmaker documents B0106. When the wash fails, the lidar may report a blocked view.
c: Washer pump or valve A for the lidar nozzle seized or electrically open
Wiring or plug fault at actuator A
Frozen washer fluid blocking pump A
s: No spray reaches lidar A during a cleaning cycle
Lidar blocked message and reduced automated driving availability

B0107.d: B0107 is the second lidar washer actuator. Why a car would need several becomes clear in Uber's 2016 patent: its roof lidar is washed by three separate nozzle units, each with its own pump and check valve, fed from one reservoir, and the controller normally sprays fluid first and then dries with air. A fault on one pump leaves only that segment of the window dirty. ARaymond's cleaning brochure shows multi-outlet lidar nozzles and integrated electromagnetic valves as an alternative to one pump per nozzle. Kautex supplies complete reservoir, pump and nozzle sets for camera and lidar cleaning. B0107 has no published meaning at any vehicle maker, and whether B is a second lidar or a second nozzle on the same one is not stated anywhere.
c: Washer pump B worn or its motor open
Check valve or line to nozzle B blocked, pump runs against closed path
s: One section of the lidar window stays dirty after washing
Repeated cleaning requests and lidar degraded warning

B0108.d: B0108 covers lidar washer actuator C. Robotaxis with several lidars, for example on roof and corners, are where a third circuit would fit. Valeo lists a heated telescopic lidar nozzle, a 2021 PACE award finalist, and says it supplies cleaning systems with ECU and software for private cars and robotaxis; a telescopic nozzle adds a moving part that can stick in frost. Solero's 4/3-way valve distributes fluid centrally so fewer DC pumps are needed, meaning actuator C may be a valve position rather than a pump. Jalopnik noted in 2018 that Waymo cleaned its lidar domes with small wipers and that Cruise was building its own cleaning hardware. No manufacturer assigns C publicly or documents B0108.
c: Telescopic nozzle C stuck by ice or dirt, actuator overloaded
Distribution valve position C not switching
Nozzle heater or shared connector on circuit C faulty
s: Lidar C not cleaned, especially in frost or snow
Automated driving refuses to engage or hands back control

B0109.d: B0109 ends the lidar washer group with actuator D; the next codes, B010A onward, move on to camera washers. Four lidar circuits match fleets built for driverless service: Kautex fits two complete Allegro cleaning and clearing systems to every Zoox robotaxi, combining water and air for cameras and lidars. On Ford’s self-driving test cars, nozzles next to each lens spray washer fluid on demand, and the roof tiara that carries cameras and lidar adds an air curtain. In Ford's US10569746B2 the computer can even leave autonomous mode while a lidar window is too opaque. Nothing public tells which unit is D, and no carmaker documents B0109. A failed actuator D usually shows as one lidar staying dirty while the others clean normally.
c: Pump or valve D for the fourth lidar nozzle defective
Hose to lidar D kinked or pulled off, so the actuator runs dry or overloaded
Open or shorted wire to actuator D
s: One lidar remains dirty while the other sensors are cleaned
Vehicle limits or ends automated driving

B010A.d: B010A opens a row of eighteen camera washer actuators, lettered A to S with I left out. The actuator is the electrically driven part that sends fluid to one camera lens: a pump of its own or a valve on a shared line. Continental's patent US11673532B2 (filed 2019) shows the layout such a row implies: front, side and rear cameras, each with its own nozzle and valve, fed by one or more pumps and switched by a controller that washes when the picture looks blocked and always cleans the rear lens in reverse. Solero sells electromagnetic valves in 2/2- and 3/2-way form for this job, and Valeo builds complete camera cleaning systems including the control unit. Makers keep the camera behind letter A to themselves; B010A appears in no public manufacturer document. The camera keeps working; only its wash is lost.
c: Valve coil or pump motor of actuator A open or shorted
Corroded or loose plug at actuator A, which sits in the splash zone near the camera
Driver stage in the controlling module defective
s: The camera assigned to actuator A is no longer washed, neither on request nor automatically
Camera view stays dirty in rain, mud or road salt; a camera blocked message may appear

B010B.d: B010B covers actuator B. A common way to reach a reversing camera is a branch off the rear-window washer line with an electric switching valve. Asmo's application US20120266926A1 (2011) describes a solenoid spool valve: unpowered it feeds the rear-screen nozzle, energised it diverts fluid to the camera nozzle. The coil is powered once reverse is engaged, and the washer switch then sprays the camera, for about two seconds in one example. Land Rover's bulletin JLRTB02100NAS1 for the 2022 Range Rover shows the plumbing side: a loose rear washer connector stopped both rear-window and camera wash, and hoses swapped at that connector made the rear-window switch wash the camera instead. Whether B is a rear camera is not published; no maker documents B010B.
c: Coil of the rear-window/camera switching valve open or shorted
Broken wire in the tailgate or boot-lid harness passage to the valve
Reverse-gear signal that enables the camera wash not reaching the module
s: In reverse the washer switch no longer sprays the reversing camera
Rear window may be washed instead of the camera, or neither

B010C.d: B010C names actuator C. Front cameras sit in the grille and get a jet of their own. Ford's TSB 20-2267 (2020) covers 2015–2020 F-150 (not Raptor), 2017–2020 Super Duty and 2018–2020 Expedition fitted with a front camera wash: the jet dripped fluid when idle because of its internal rubber seal, and the cure is a new jet, with the grille removed and the 360-degree camera aligned afterwards. Asmo's application US20110292212A1 explains why such jets carry a check valve: it opens only under pump pressure, so fluid neither runs onto the lens nor lets air into the line. A leaking seal sets no electrical code by itself; B010C points to the actuator or its circuit. The camera tied to C is unpublished, as is any maker use of the code.
c: Damaged wiring or plug at the front end, exposed to stone chips, water and salt
Pump or valve C seized or electrically defective
Plug left disconnected after grille or bumper work
s: Front camera lens is not sprayed when the wash is requested
Front or 360-degree camera image stays dirty in winter or after off-road driving

B010D.d: B010D covers actuator D. Audi's TSB 2059228/2 (2022) for the 2019–2022 e-tron and 2020–2022 e-tron Sportback shows what a missing check valve does to a rear camera wash: the line empties while driving or when the tailgate opens, the system stops after four activations to save fluid, and four tries are not enough to refill and pressurise it, so the lens stays dirty until the ignition (terminal 15) is switched off and on. The fix adds an inline valve, part 4N0 955 481 A. ARaymond fits such a non-return valve directly into a slim rear camera nozzle in a tailgate handle. Here the driver sees no spray but no fault code; B010D itself points to an electrical fault at actuator D, whose camera assignment is not published by any maker.
c: Pump or valve D open, shorted or drawing abnormal current
Wire break where the harness flexes into the tailgate
Pump damaged by repeatedly running dry on an empty line
s: Camera wash request must be repeated several times before fluid arrives, or nothing arrives
Reversing camera stays smeared after the wash function has been used

B010E.d: B010E names actuator E, which may be a dedicated pump rather than a valve. Audi's TSB 2073568/1 (2024) for e-tron, e-tron S and Q8/SQ8 e-tron models reports rear camera washer pressure too low to clean the lens: the mono pump could not build enough pressure, and production moved to a dual pump (1K6 955 651) whose spare outlet is plugged. Before swapping it, technicians rule out low fluid, a clogged pump filter, low supply voltage and kinked lines. AUMOVIO lists its washer pumps with one or two outlets for 2.0 to 4.0 bar. A pump drawing no current or too much is the kind of fault a module can flag; whether any maker calls that pump E is not published, and no manufacturer documents B010E.
c: Camera washer pump motor E worn, seized or open
Low supply voltage or poor ground at the pump
Clogged inlet filter making the pump labour and draw high current
s: Camera nozzle only dribbles; the spray does not reach across the lens
Pump hum without spray, or no pump sound at all when the wash is requested

B010F.d: B010F covers actuator F. On 2021 Chevrolet Tahoe and Suburban and GMC Yukon with the rear camera mirror (RPO DRZ), GM service update N202311260 found the hose feeding the rear camera nozzle kinked behind the tailgate trim in about 630 vehicles; technicians test the wash, shorten the hose to 127 mm at most and slide an 85 mm split sleeve over it. A kink starves the nozzle without any electrical fault, so it would not explain B010F; the code points to the actuator circuit. The camera itself falls under FMVSS 111, which demands a rearview image within 2.0 s of selecting reverse and tests external camera parts for corrosion and humidity, yet sets no rule for a washer. Which camera F means is not published; no maker documents B010F.
c: Open or shorted circuit to valve or pump F
Wiring pinched or unplugged during tailgate trim removal
s: Camera mirror or reversing image stays dirty because the rear camera wash does not work
Rearview image itself is still shown when reversing

B0110.d: B0110 names actuator G. Not every washed camera sees visible light. Bentley's product information 2051045 (2023) concerns the infrared night-vision camera in the front bumper of Bentayga, Continental GT/GTC and Flying Spur: fluid dripping from its washer jet is cured by a new non-return valve, and the camera needs recalibrating only if it is replaced itself. An earlier note (2021) replaced the short link hose between that jet and its supply connector instead. Valeo's cleaning range likewise lists infrared cameras next to visible cameras and lidar. Whether G stands for a night-vision camera is not published, and no manufacturer documents B0110. If set, the night-vision image may blur in rain or slush.
c: Valve or pump G for the camera jet electrically open or shorted
Harness damage in the lower bumper area after a parking knock or repair
Output stage of the controlling module defective
s: Night-vision or front camera image stays smeared; the camera jet does not spray
Assistance functions relying on that camera may report limited availability

B0111.d: B0111 is the J2012 code for camera washer actuator H, but the number has an older second life. Toyota's bulletin T-SB-0069-12 (revision 2, 2014) for the 2004–2009 Sienna lists B0111 together with B0116 as an open side-airbag squib circuit with the SRS lamp lit, repaired in the floor harness. On that van the code has nothing to do with washing, and a scan tool showing the generic title would mislead. In the generic sense, actuator H is one of the pumps or valves that suppliers such as Kautex offer for ADAS cleaning, next to heated nozzles, heated hoses, connectors and level sensors. No manufacturer publishes which camera H means or documents B0111 as a washer code.
c: Pump or valve H open, shorted or seized
Water ingress or corrosion in the plug of actuator H
s: Camera served by actuator H is not washed
No washer fluid leaves the nozzle served by actuator H when the wash is requested

B0112.d: B0112 covers actuator J; the letter I is skipped in this row, so J is the ninth. Large systems wash many cameras from one fluid network. Stellantis TSB 23-028-23 (2023) for the 2022 Grand Wagoneer and Wagoneer built up to 28 February 2022 names rear backup camera washer, surround-view cameras, night vision and the digital rearview mirror as the equipment involved; when cameras front or rear stop spraying, or fluid leaks behind the fascia, in the headliner or at the liftgate, quick connectors had come apart and are checked push-pull-push. A 2024 reissue repeats the procedure. ARaymond supplies such quick connectors for cleaning circuits. A loose coupling is not electrical; B0112 points to actuator J or its wiring.
c: Valve or pump J electrically open or shorted
Washer fluid from a loose coupling running into the actuator plug and corroding it
Chafed wire on the route to actuator J
s: One camera of a multi-camera system is not sprayed while others are
Damp trim or puddles of washer fluid inside the vehicle if a coupling has also come loose

B0113.d: B0113 names actuator K. Even a working actuator is useless if the jet misses the lens. Stellantis TSB 23-049-22 Rev. A for 2022–2023 Jeep Grand Cherokee (WL) built between 13 April and 15 September 2022 found the liftgate nozzle of the digital rearview mirror camera pointing the wrong way; it is unclipped, turned 180 degrees and refitted, after which the mirror is reset by holding its plus and minus buttons for about 15 s. Bowles' application US20140060582A1 explains the geometry: a nozzle offset roughly 10 to 30 mm beside the lens, aimed within about 1 to 20 degrees of its surface and kept out of the field of view. A misaimed jet sets no code; B0113 concerns the actuator circuit, for a camera that is not published.
c: Open or short in the circuit of valve or pump K
Wire fatigue in the liftgate hinge area
Plug not reconnected after the camera or nozzle was removed
s: Camera wash does not run for the camera served by actuator K
Digital mirror or reversing picture stays dirty after the wash is requested

B0114.d: B0114 covers actuator L. Stellantis STAR case S2123000051 (2021, Jeep Grand Cherokee) describes a front camera washer pump that stopped spraying when the reservoir ran low although the cluster showed no low-fluid warning; a new pump, reservoir or level sensor did not help, and engineering was still investigating. Ford's German application DE102018109892A1 shows a quite different actuator: a magnet that squeezes a flexible chamber next to the camera, with one-way valves at inlet and outlet, triggered at ignition on, in reverse or by the wiper lever, plus an optional float reporting a low level. Washer level codes form their own row from B011C. Which camera L serves is not published; no maker documents B0114.
c: Pump or actuator L damaged after running with a nearly empty reservoir
Open or shorted wiring to actuator L
Level sensor not warning in time, so the actuator runs without fluid
s: Camera wash stops working while the reservoir is low, without a low-fluid warning
Front camera view remains dirty after a wash request

B0115.d: B0115 names actuator M. Where several cameras share one pump, the actuator is often a distribution valve. Solero's SCV43 is a 4/3-way valve switched by voltage, with one inlet and three independently switched outlets, so a single pump can serve up to three nozzles and fewer DC pumps are needed in the reservoir. Kautex's Allegro systems clean several camera points and lidar with water and air, and their software decides which point is served first. With a shared valve block, one failed coil can stop washing at one camera while the others still spray, and that is how a single-letter code like B0115 would show. No manufacturer publishes B0115 or the camera behind M.
c: Coil for outlet M in a shared valve block open or shorted
Valve M stuck by deposits or frozen fluid, drawing abnormal current
Wiring or plug fault on the line to valve M
s: One camera stays unwashed while other cameras on the same pump are sprayed
Camera blocked message for that camera in bad weather

B0116.d: B0116 covers actuator N. Like B0111 it also turns up on the 2004–2009 Toyota Sienna, where bulletin T-SB-0069-12 uses it for an open side-airbag squib circuit, not a washer. In the generic sense, cold is a typical burden for camera washers. Denso's patent US9180840B2 mixes air from a pump with fluid admitted by an electromagnetic valve and adapts to the weather: at or below a threshold such as 2 °C it lowers the pump voltage so that larger droplets form, which freeze less readily on the lens, and it lengthens spray and blow times. Kautex offers heated nozzles and heated hoses against the same problem. Frozen fluid can stall a pump or valve and make it draw abnormal current. Which camera N serves is not published.
c: Washer fluid without enough antifreeze frozen in pump or valve N
Actuator N electrically open or shorted
s: Camera wash fails mainly in frost and recovers after the car has warmed up
Ice or salt film stays on the lens of the camera served by actuator N

B0117.d: B0117 names actuator O; unlike I, the letter O is used in this row. Not every silent washer is faulty. Continental's patent US11673532B2 (granted 2023, now held by Aumovio) lets the controller hold back the camera valves on purpose: in an off-road mode only selected cameras are washed, and with four-wheel drive engaged below about 20 km/h all valves stay shut so mud does not use up the fluid; a timed mode washes at most once per interval, two or five minutes in the examples. AUMOVIO also clears dust with air alone to save fluid. A deliberately inhibited actuator should set no code; B0117 indicates a fault in actuator O itself. Which camera O means is not published, and no manufacturer documents B0117.
c: Valve or pump O open, shorted or seized
Wiring to a low-mounted camera actuator damaged by mud, water or off-road use
Module software or configuration fault in actuator O control; update per maker
s: Camera stays unwashed also in normal road mode, not only when washing is intentionally paused
Camera blocked message in mud or rain

B0118.d: B0118 covers actuator P. Equipment can disappear in the middle of a model year. Ford's SSM 51564 notes that the 2023 Lincoln Aviator and the 2022–2023 Explorer and Police Interceptor Utility built from mid-July or August 2022 lost washing of the rear parking camera; the jet may still be fitted without a hose, which is normal and needs no repair. Should a module be configured for an actuator the car no longer carries, a missing-load code of this kind could follow. Asmo's US20110292212A1 shows the options designers pick from: a T-piece off the rear-window hose, a separate pump for each nozzle, or a diversion valve. No manufacturer documents B0118 or the camera behind P.
c: Module coded for a camera washer actuator the vehicle is not built with
Actuator P or its feed open circuit
Replacement module fitted with the wrong variant data
s: Fault stored although the camera has no working wash, or only a dummy jet without a hose
Camera image and parking aid otherwise work normally

B0119.d: B0119 names actuator Q. Land Rover's SSM76076 (2023) for the Defender (L663) from model year 2020 traces dripping headlamp washer jets and a dripping rear camera washer jet to a one-way valve in the feed pipe that no longer seals; the dealer tool runs a guided leak test and may call for a new rear camera washer hose with the valve. Headlamp and camera washing thus often share fluid and parts. ARaymond's cleaning brochure lists non-return valves, quick connectors and heated nozzles as building blocks of such circuits. A leaking valve is a hydraulic fault, not an electrical one; B0119 itself points to actuator Q or its wiring. Which camera Q serves is not published, and no maker documents the code.
c: Pump or valve Q electrically open or shorted
Fluid dripping from a leaking jet or valve corroding the nearby actuator plug
Chafed wire between module and actuator Q
s: Camera wash for the camera served by actuator Q does not respond
Washer fluid level drops faster than usual if a valve is also leaking

B011A.d: B011A covers actuator R. Some camera cleaners use air as well as fluid, so the actuator may be a blower as much as a pump. Thunder Power's patent US9539988B2 places a water nozzle and an air nozzle at a reversing camera: air blasts first, then unheated fluid, and below about 0 °C heated fluid, while an infrared drop sensor behind the lens decides when cleaning is needed. Denso's US9180840B2 opens its fluid valve only after the air has started and keeps it open for 0.1 to 0.5 s; in its tests at least about 70 % of salty mud had to come off for a usable picture. Air blowers for sensors have their own codes from B0100. Which camera R serves is not published; no manufacturer documents B011A.
c: Pump, valve or air blower R electrically open or shorted
Heater element in the camera wash circuit defective, affecting cold-weather operation
s: Camera served by actuator R is neither blown nor sprayed clean
Drops or mud remain on the lens; assistance functions may warn of a blocked camera

B011B.d: B011B closes the row with actuator S. Electrically, each actuator in the row is a coil or motor switched by a module or a relay. HELLA's relay guide explains the switching side: a control coil on terminals 85 and 86 pulls in the armature and moves the contact from 87a over to 87, and some types carry a resistor or diode across the coil to tame the spike at switch-off. Asmo's US20120266926A1 energises its camera wash valve through a relay fed from the reversing-lamp circuit, so a fault there can disable the wash as well. An open coil, a sticking relay or a broken feed on this last actuator is what B011B points to. No public source ties S to a particular camera or reports B011B from a real vehicle.
c: Coil or motor of actuator S open or shorted
Relay feeding actuator S sticking or with a burnt contact
Blown fuse or broken supply wire to the relay or actuator
s: Camera wash for the camera served by actuator S does nothing
Wash may run continuously or not stop if a relay contact has welded

B011C.d: B011C is the first of six fluid reservoir level sensors, A to F. J2012 does not say which reservoir each letter belongs to; the neighbouring codes deal with washing windows, cameras and other sensors, so washer tanks are the obvious candidates. The classic design pairs a magnet-bearing float with a reed switch: falling fluid lowers the float, and the contact flips. The application US20040200278A1 shows such a unit pushed through a rubber grommet in the tank side wall. FCA parts tip 9003109 adds a practical failure: a float that has turned out of its anti-rotation guides keeps reporting low fluid in a full bottle. No maker documents B011C publicly; the effect is a wrong or missing low-fluid warning.
c: Float jammed, rotated out of its guide or soaked with fluid
Reed contact inside the sensor broken or welded
Leaking grommet letting fluid reach the plug, corroded terminals
s: Low-fluid warning stays on although the reservoir is full
No warning at all when the reservoir runs empty

B011D.d: B011D concerns level sensor B. Not every washer tank relies on a float. Volkswagen's bulletin 2037322 (2015) describes its washer level sensor G33 as a part whose reading depends on the fluid itself: the wrong mix or additives coat the sensor, cut its sensitivity and leave the lamp lit with a full tank; the remedy is draining, cleaning the sensor and refilling with approved fluid. Sensors moulded into the reservoir cannot be replaced on their own. A non-contact alternative is the capacitive single-point detector of patent US5017909A, fixed on the outside wall at the minimum level, where the liquid shifts the measured capacitance. Which principle sits behind letter B is not published, and no maker lists B011D publicly.
c: Deposits from unsuitable washer fluid or additives on the sensing surface
Open or short in the sensor wiring
s: Warning lamp lit with a full reservoir, often after a change of washer fluid
Level warning appears late or not at all

B011E.d: B011E covers level sensor C. Vehicles that steer by camera and lidar need their own cleaning supply, and there the level reading becomes an operating condition. Uber's application US20180015907A1 shows a sensor-cleaning reservoir with a dedicated liquid level sensor reporting to the vehicle computer; below a threshold the computer lights an indicator or tells a remote operator to refill. The related patent US10220817B2 adds a compressor and solenoid valves and handles pressure and fluid readings beyond their limits in the same way. Whether reservoir C is such a cleaning tank is stated nowhere, and B011E appears in no public manufacturer document. A fault leaves the system unsure whether it can still clean its sensors.
c: Level sensor C defective or signal implausible
Damaged wiring or connector between sensor and computing module
Dirt or ice in the reservoir disturbing the measurement
s: Refill request or cleaning-system warning without obvious reason
Sensor cleaning may be withheld, and assistance functions may restrict themselves when sensors get dirty

B011F.d: B011F reports level sensor D. A recurring weakness of float switches in washer bottles is motion: fluid slopping around in corners or under braking lifts and drops the float and can set it spinning. Continental's patent US9003878B2 answers with a float guided in an angled carrier, ribs that stop it turning and an optional slosh guard, so one design suits side or bottom mounting. The other weak point is the wiring: FCA parts tip 68225064A tells technicians who face a false low-fluid message to check circuits W1 and W11 at a 48-way connector before condemning the float sensor. Which tank letter D refers to is left open by the makers, and nobody documents B011F publicly. Expect flickering or false level messages.
c: Loose or corroded pins at an intermediate harness connector
Float moving freely with sloshing fluid, guide or slosh guard broken
s: Level warning switching on and off while driving, especially in bends
False low-level message with a full reservoir

B0120.d: B0120 relates to level sensor E. Ford's application US20190265715A1 describes a container for sensor cleaning whose level sensor measures conductance at a fixed height: air gives a resistance above roughly 1000 ohms, the slightly conductive fluid one below it. Because the fluid moves with the car, the computer filters the signal with acceleration and yaw rate, then estimates the remaining volume from pump activity, and it suspects a leak if the level falls while no washing is requested, in which case the vehicle may be routed to a service centre. Ford's patent US10569746B2 puts such a container on the roof beside the lidar. Letter E is not tied publicly to any tank, and no manufacturer documents B0120. Without the signal, remaining fluid can only be guessed.
c: Electrodes fouled or fluid with unsuitable conductivity (e.g. plain distilled water)
Open or short in the sensor circuit
Leaking reservoir or hose making the level drop unexpectedly
s: Refill warning too early, too late or constantly on
Cleaning of exterior sensors may be restricted

B0121.d: B0121 closes the row with level sensor F. Small local reservoirs are one reason a vehicle might carry six level sensors: Ford's application DE102018109892A1 describes a camera washer with its own container close to the lens, fitted with a buoyant level sensor that signals when the fluid has fallen to a set low point and the container needs topping up. How the result reaches the driver is a separate design question; Mannesmann VDO's patent US6588270B1 even moved the washer level display next to the fuel filler neck so that it is noticed while refuelling. No manufacturer publishes which reservoir F stands for or documents B0121. Driving is not affected, but the washer it watches may run dry unnoticed.
c: Float of sensor F stuck by deposits or ice
Wiring to the small reservoir chafed or connector corroded
s: Missing or permanent refill message for the affected reservoir
Washer served by this reservoir runs dry without warning

B0122.d: B0122 flags pedestrian alert speaker A. Hybrid and electric vehicles are almost silent at walking pace, so they have to make an artificial sound. In the US, FMVSS 141 covers such vehicles up to 4,536 kg GVWR and sets minimum sound levels when stationary with propulsion active, in reverse and up to 30 km/h. GM's preliminary information PIC6478 for the 2023 Cadillac Lyriq shows a typical front speaker behind the bumper: it plays from standstill to about 25 mph, can be silenced for diagnosis by pulling fuse F46UA, and its bracket may buzz against the bumper beam. Which speaker is A is not published, and no maker documents B0122. With the speaker dead the car loses its mandatory warning sound but drives normally.
c: Speaker A failed from water, salt or stone impact at the front end
Open or short in the speaker wiring, often after bumper repairs
Output stage of the sound generator module or its fuse faulty
s: No artificial driving sound at low speed from the affected side
Warning message about the pedestrian alert system in the cluster, depending on make
Vehicle no longer meets the legal minimum sound; repair promptly

B0123.d: B0123 is the same check for pedestrian alert speaker B, which implies a second sounder. Ford's special service message 48451 for 2020 hybrids and plug-ins describes speakers at the front and the rear that sound in forward and reverse between 0 and 30 km/h. In the EU, Regulation 540/2014 made an acoustic vehicle alerting system compulsory on all new hybrid and electric vehicles from July 2021, sounding from start-up to about 20 km/h and when reversing. Stellantis records internal faults of its quiet vehicle pedestrian module as B2779-04, a maker-specific code rather than this one. No manufacturer links B0123 to a particular speaker in public; with B silent, one direction loses its warning and the legal sound requirement is no longer met.
c: Speaker B defective, for example from moisture in the rear bumper or wheel arch area
Loose or corroded connector at speaker B or a rattling internal connector at the module
Fault in the sound generator module or its software
s: Artificial sound missing at the front or rear, e.g. only audible when moving off forwards
Possible warning message about the pedestrian alert system
Legally required warning sound incomplete; have it repaired soon

B0124.d: B0124 points at the night vision camera, usually a far-infrared thermal sensor behind the grille or in the bumper; Teledyne FLIR says it has supplied more than a million automotive thermal sensors. Its exposed position causes most faults. GM's PIC6352A for Cadillac CT6, XT5 and XT6 traces failed camera learn procedures to loose or corroded LVDS connectors between camera B276 and its control module, often after water entered a damaged camera. Bentley's 2055858/1 for the Bentayga describes stone chips letting water in and corroding the camera cable, and Stellantis case S2408000119 warns that a cracked lens distorts the picture. None of these bulletins quotes B0124 itself. Night vision stops working; normal driving is unaffected.
c: Water ingress through a stone-chipped or cracked camera window
Loose or corroded LVDS video connector between camera and control module
Camera replaced but not learned or calibrated
s: Night vision image missing, distorted or pixelated
Message such as night vision unavailable, service required

B0125.d: B0125 concerns the night vision control module, which processes the camera image and passes it to the display. Stellantis uses this code: on the 2023 Jeep Grand Cherokee the cluster stores B0125-02, Night Vision Control Module general signal failure, alongside U02BD (lost communication) in the BCM. Case S2208000163 blames misaligned or not fully seated terminals at connector D3944A of the processing module; case S2408000119 adds B14FB-31 (no video signal) in that module and names a cracked camera lens as one cause. GM's PIT5785 for Cadillac XT5 and XT6 shows the same link from the cluster end: an unplugged black LVDS connector there leaves a green pixelated picture. Night vision is lost; driving is not affected.
c: Misaligned, bent or not fully seated terminals at the module connector
Video link (LVDS) to the cluster loose or damaged
Camera delivers no usable image, e.g. cracked lens
s: Night vision unavailable message in the cluster
No, frozen or pixelated night vision image

B0126.d: B0126 belongs to the driver monitoring camera, an infrared camera aimed at the driver that tracks gaze and head position for hands-free and attention functions. GM uses the code: preliminary information PIC6556 (versions B to H, 2024–2025) for Super Cruise models from Cadillac Lyriq to Silverado EV lists B0126 symptom 82, stored by the module that processes camera images and often paired with B1DD0; the steps are a 30-minute disconnect, a check of the LVDS cable and finally a new camera. PIT6229 reports Super Cruise dropping out because software wrongly judged the driver's gaze to be off the road. In the EU, Delegated Regulation 2023/2590 requires distraction warnings above 20 km/h and a failure warning when the sensor is faulty or blocked. Hands-free driving is unavailable while the fault is active.
c: LVDS cable to the image processing module damaged or poorly connected
Software fault, or camera view blocked by objects or mounting problems
s: Hands-free assistance such as Super Cruise unavailable or disengaging
Driver attention or distraction warning inactive, failure message shown

B0127.t: DC/AC Converter A High Voltage Power Outlet "A" Circuit/Open
B0127.d: B0127 reports an open circuit to power outlet A of DC/AC converter A, one of the household-voltage sockets the converter supplies. Ford's patent US11043801B2, behind Pro Power Onboard, gives every socket its own conductor, on/off switch and ground-fault interrupter, fed by an inverter that draws on the traction battery, the motor-generator or both; sensors ahead of and behind each switch let the controller check the path. GM's program N222385490 shows how directly the outlets hang on the converter: 2023 Silverado and Sierra 1500 built without a working inverter had dead dash and bed outlets until it was retrofitted. The makers keep the position of socket A to themselves; B0127 appears in no public document. Outlet A stays dead; driving is unaffected.
c: Wire or terminal in the feed to outlet A broken or pushed out
Socket insert or its built-in protection defective
Output switch or relay for outlet A inside the converter faulty
s: Outlet A supplies no power while other outlets may still work
Message that onboard power or the outlet is unavailable
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised

B0128.t: DC/AC Converter A High Voltage Power Outlet "B" Circuit/Open
B0128.d: B0128 is the open-circuit fault for outlet B. Such a fault has to be told apart from a tripped protective device. In Ford's patent US11043801B2 each socket has a ground-fault interrupter whose breaker opens on a current imbalance and normally needs a manual reset; Ford adds an actuator so it can also be reset from a distance, plus test switches for the interrupters. Ford's SSM 49709 for the 2021 F-150 hybrid shows the everyday side: after the built-in Pro Power test the screen reports a ground fault until the reset button is pressed, which is normal behaviour. So rule out a tripped interrupter before chasing wiring. Where outlet B sits is not published, and no manufacturer documents B0128. Until repaired, socket B gives no power.
c: Feed to outlet B interrupted at a connector or in the harness
Ground-fault interrupter of outlet B defective or its reset actuator stuck
Moisture or dirt in socket B
s: Socket B dead, ground-fault or outlet message on the screen
Reset does not restore power to socket B
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised

B0129.t: DC/AC Converter A High Voltage Power Outlet "C" Circuit/Open
B0129.d: B0129 covers outlet C. Apart from wiring faults, the converter also cuts sockets on purpose when the load is too high. Ford's patent US11043801B2 gives limits of 20 A for the 120 V sockets and 30 A for the 240 V socket, and when total power exceeds the ceiling it de-energises sockets by priority, the lowest first. Ford's SSM 51498 for the 2023 Super Duty describes the resulting Pro Power Onboard Turned Off message after wattage thresholds were exceeded, which could only be cleared once the load was unplugged. A shutdown like that is not an open circuit: B0129 means the converter finds no intact path to socket C. Which socket that is, and any maker using B0129, is not public.
c: Terminal at outlet C overheated or burnt from heavy loads, contact lost
Switching element for outlet C inside the converter defective
s: Socket C stays dead even with no load connected
Outlet message that cannot be cleared by unplugging and resetting
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised

B012A.t: DC/AC Converter A High Voltage Power Outlet "D" Circuit/Open
B012A.d: B012A concerns outlet D. Sockets in a pickup bed live in a harsher place than those in the cab: dust, rain, washing and cords left plugged in. Ford's customer satisfaction program 21B52 shows how tightly bed outlets are tied into the vehicle: on certain 2021 F-150 Raptor trucks with Pro Power Onboard, a bed outlet cover standing open more than about 17 degrees kept the truck from shifting out of Park until the PCM was reprogrammed. In Ford's patent US11043801B2 the bed outlet carries several sockets, each with its own switch and protection, and a second outlet sits in the cab. Whether D is a bed socket is not published, and no manufacturer documents B012A. Moisture in the socket or its connector is a likely cause.
c: Water or corrosion in socket D or its connector, typical for exterior or bed outlets
Harness to outlet D chafed or crushed in the body or bed
s: Socket D without power, other sockets may work
Message that onboard power or an outlet is unavailable
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised

B012B.t: DC/AC Converter A High Voltage Power Outlet "E" Circuit/Open
B012B.d: B012B is the last outlet circuit code, for outlet E. Many trucks combine bed sockets with one in the cabin. Ford's SSM 49562 for the 2021 F-150 with the 7.2 kW system notes that a message about a tripped bed-panel breaker could really come from the breaker above the 120 V outlet in the instrument panel, or from that outlet's connector not being fully plugged in; an over-the-air update corrected the wording. Ford's patent US11043801B2 also lets each socket be switched on its own from the screen or a button. Which outlet E is remains unpublished, and B012B appears in no manufacturer document. Before blaming the converter, check breaker, connector and socket of the outlet concerned.
c: Connector at outlet E not fully engaged, e.g. after dash work
Circuit breaker of outlet E tripped or defective
Wiring between converter and outlet E open
s: Socket E dead, possibly with a misleading breaker message for another outlet
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised

B012C.t: DC/AC Converter A High Voltage Power Outlet Control Module "A"
B012C.d: B012C names power outlet control module A of converter A without a fault type, so the module itself is under suspicion rather than one socket. Ford calls its unit DCACA; on the F-150 with the 2.0 kW system it sits in the cab under the left rear seat. Ford's SSM 50167 traced a loud fan on early 2021 builds to DCACA software, and SSM 52213 for 2022–2023 F-150 and 2023 Super Duty a dealer-service message with P0A93:96 stored in the DCACA; both were cured by reprogramming. Neither bulletin mentions B012C, and no manufacturer documents the code; it is open whether module A means the inverter itself or a separate outlet controller. Usually all outlets of the converter are unavailable.
c: Outdated or corrupted module software; reprogramming per maker bulletin
Power, ground or network connection of module A faulty
Module A internally defective, e.g. cooling fan or power stage
s: Onboard power unavailable or service message in the centre display
Unusual fan noise from the module's location
Module handles 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised

B012D.t: DC/AC Converter A High Voltage Power Outlet Control Module "B"
B012D.d: B012D addresses outlet control module B. A converter for household sockets interacts with the rest of the vehicle both electrically and by radio.
