c: Open or shorted supply wire to the right front sensor
Sensor shorted internally and pulling the supply down
Sensor supply output of the ABS module faulty
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS, traction and stability control disabled
No speed signal from the right front wheel

C0036.d: Covers the left rear tone wheel (reluctor or encoder ring) read by the left rear wheel speed sensor, the rear-axle counterpart of C0030 and C0033. It is a signal-plausibility code set when the module sees an erratic, noisy or intermittent rear speed signal consistent with a damaged, contaminated or loose tone ring rather than a sensor circuit failure. Ford documents C0036 with C0037 and C003A on 2021 Bronco and Ranger vehicles with an illuminated ABS warning. A fault disables ABS, traction and stability control and lights the ABS warning lamp while base braking remains; on vehicles that use the rear sensors for electronic brake-force distribution that function is affected too.
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
Grinding noise from wheel hub

C0037.d: Covers the left rear wheel speed sensor and its circuit, the rear-axle counterpart of C0031 and C0034. The active sensor reports rear wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution. The module monitors the circuit for opens, shorts to power or ground, a signal outside the valid range and a missing signal while moving. Ford documents C0037 on 2020-2022 F-53 motorhome and F-59 commercial chassis, frequently caused by a bent or damaged sensor, and lists it with C003A/C0036 on 2021 Bronco and Ranger. A fault disables ABS, traction and stability control and lights the ABS warning lamp while base braking remains.
c: Wheel speed sensor bent or failed
Open, shorted or chafed sensor wiring
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
Speedometer may read erratically

C0038.t: Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Supply
C0038.d: Covers the supply circuit that powers the left rear active wheel speed sensor, the rear-axle counterpart of C0032. Active sensors need a regulated voltage from the ABS/ESC module; this code is set when that supply is open, shorted to ground or to another voltage, or outside the regulated range so the sensor cannot produce a valid signal. Ford lists C0038 with C0037 on 2020-2022 F-53 and F-59 chassis where a bent or damaged sensor and its circuit set an ABS light. A fault disables ABS, traction and stability control for that corner and lights the ABS warning lamp while base braking remains; it is distinct from the sensor-signal code C0037 in that the feed itself is faulty.
c: Open or shorted sensor supply wire
Corroded connector on the supply side
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
No wheel speed signal from this corner

C0039.d: Covers the right rear tone wheel (reluctor or encoder ring) read by the right rear wheel speed sensor, completing the four-corner tone-wheel set with C0030, C0033 and C0036. It is a signal-plausibility code set when the module sees an erratic, noisy or intermittent rear speed signal consistent with a damaged, contaminated or loose tone ring rather than a sensor circuit failure. Ford documents the right rear sensor group including this corner on 2021 Bronco and Ranger vehicles with an illuminated ABS warning. A fault disables ABS, traction and stability control and lights the ABS warning lamp while base braking remains; electronic brake-force distribution is affected where it uses the rear sensors.
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
Grinding noise from wheel hub

C003A.d: Covers the right rear wheel speed sensor and its circuit, completing the four-corner sensor set with C0031, C0034 and C0037. The active sensor reports rear wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution. The module monitors the circuit for opens, shorts to power or ground, a signal outside the valid range and a missing signal while moving. Ford documents C003A with C0036 and C0037 on 2021 Bronco and Ranger vehicles built in a specific window, with an illuminated ABS warning. A fault disables ABS, traction and stability control and lights the ABS warning lamp while base braking remains available.
c: Wheel speed sensor bent or failed
Open, shorted or chafed sensor wiring
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
Speedometer may read erratically

C003B.t: Right Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Supply
C003B.d: Covers the supply circuit that powers the right rear active wheel speed sensor, completing the supply set with C0032 and C0038. Active sensors need a regulated voltage from the ABS/ESC module; this code is set when that supply is open, shorted to ground or to another voltage, or outside the regulated range so the sensor cannot produce a valid signal. It is distinct from the sensor-signal code C003A in that the fault is on the feed rather than in the sensor element. A fault disables ABS, traction and stability control for that corner and lights the ABS warning lamp while base braking remains. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; NHTSA lists C003B as right rear supply in the J2012 table of its EPS safety report.
c: Open or shorted sensor supply wire
Corroded connector on the supply side
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
No wheel speed signal from this corner

C003C.d: Covers a single rear tone wheel (reluctor or encoder ring) on vehicles that use one combined rear wheel speed signal, for example from a differential or rear axle sensor, rather than separate left and right rear rings. It is a signal-plausibility code set when the module sees an erratic, noisy or intermittent rear speed signal consistent with a damaged, contaminated or loose tone ring rather than a sensor circuit failure. A fault disables ABS, traction and stability control and lights the ABS warning lamp while base braking remains; on such vehicles rear-based functions like electronic brake-force distribution are affected. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; NHTSA's EPS safety report lists the rear tone wheel code C003C among the J2012 wheel speed codes.
c: Loose or displaced bearing or axle ring
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
Intermittent rear speed signal

C003D.d: Covers a single rear wheel speed sensor on vehicles that use one combined rear speed signal, for example a rear axle or differential-mounted sensor, instead of separate left and right rear sensors. It reports rear rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution. The module monitors the circuit for opens, shorts to power or ground, a signal outside the valid range and a missing signal while moving. A fault disables ABS, traction and stability control and lights the ABS warning lamp while base braking remains. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; NHTSA's EPS safety report carries C003D as the rear wheel speed sensor in its J2012 table.
c: Open, shorted or chafed sensor wiring
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
Speedometer may read erratically

C003E.d: Covers the supply circuit that powers a single rear active wheel speed sensor on vehicles with one combined rear speed signal. Active sensors need a regulated voltage from the ABS/ESC module; this code is set when that supply is open, shorted to ground or another voltage, or outside the regulated range so the sensor cannot produce a valid signal. It is distinct from the sensor-signal code C003D in that the fault is on the feed rather than the sensor element. A fault disables ABS, traction and stability control and lights the ABS warning lamp while base braking remains. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the J2012 table in NHTSA's EPS safety report lists C003E as the rear sensor supply.
c: Open or shorted sensor supply wire
Corroded connector on the supply side
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
No rear wheel speed signal

C003F.t: Wheel Speed Sensors Rotation Direction Correlation
C003F.d: A correlation code set when the directional information from the wheel speed sensors does not agree across wheels or with other motion inputs. Directional (bidirectional) wheel speed sensors tell the ABS/ESC module whether a wheel turns forward or backward, which the module uses for hill-hold, rollback detection and stability functions. The code stores when one wheel reports a rotation direction that is implausible against the others, the selected gear or the yaw and acceleration sensors. It points to a faulty directional sensor, its wiring or the tone ring. Affected functions are disabled and the ABS warning lamp is set while base braking remains. Direction-capable sensor ICs such as Allegro's A19302 send speed plus direction over PW or AK protocol. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Damaged tone ring giving false direction
s: ABS warning lamp on
Hill-hold or stability functions disabled
Incorrect rollback or direction detection

C0040.d: C0040 reports a fault on brake pedal switch A, the first of two switch signals that tell the brake, engine and transmission modules the pedal is pressed. Mazda defines C0040:24 as a circuit malfunction of brake switch signal no. 1; on the 2024 CX-90 it appears with P0504 and a push button start warning, and service alert SA-062-23 cures it by moving the switch one adjustment notch. Ford sees C0040 with P0504 on 2020-2022 F-Super Duty trucks that cannot be moved out of park, pointing to corrosion inside the battery junction box or a damaged shift-interlock circuit. Typical effects are stop lamps that stay lit (Ford TSB 22-2044), a start system warning and a shift interlock that will not release. Older GM vehicles use C0040 for a wheel speed sensor circuit in their own scheme.
c: Brake switch out of adjustment (Mazda SA-062-23)
Water or corrosion in the battery junction box (Ford TSB 22-2044)
s: Stop lamps stay on or do not light
Vehicle will not shift out of park
Push button start malfunction warning (Mazda)

C0041.d: Covers brake pedal switch B, the redundant second brake switch used to cross-check brake pedal switch A. The two switches change state in a defined pattern as the pedal is applied; the module compares them and sets this code when switch B is stuck, open, shorted or disagrees with switch A. The redundant signal supports driver-assist features that must reliably know whether the driver is braking. Honda documents DTC C0041-14 as a brake switch fault that, together with resting a foot on the pedal, can falsely trigger the adaptive-cruise, collision-mitigation and lane-/road-departure warning indicators. A fault can disable those assist functions and illuminate warning lamps; stop lamps may be affected depending on wiring.
s: Driver-assist features disabled or false triggers
Cruise or adaptive cruise will not set
Warning lamp or driver message

C0042.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor Circuit A
C0042.d: Covers circuit A of the brake pedal position sensor, which reports how far the pedal is pressed rather than just on/off like a switch. The brake or stability module uses this analog signal for brake-by-wire assist, regenerative braking blending and precise stop-lamp and cruise control. The module sets the code for a signal outside the valid voltage range, an open or short, or a value that disagrees with the pedal switch or a second sensor channel. Chrysler documents C0042 on 2015-2017 Durango and Grand Cherokee alongside P0572, with the brake lamps remaining lit or cruise control failing to engage, and prescribes checking and relearning the pedal rest position. A fault can disable assist and cruise functions and set a warning lamp.
c: Pedal position sensor out of range
s: Brake lights stay on
Cruise control will not set
ABS or brake warning lamp on

C0043.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor Circuit B
C0043.d: Covers circuit B of the brake pedal position sensor, the redundant second channel that the module cross-checks against channel A (C0042). Dual-channel pedal position sensors provide two independent voltage signals, often with opposite slopes, so the module can detect a single-channel fault by correlation. This code is set when channel B is out of range, open, shorted or does not track channel A within tolerance. It supports brake-by-wire assist, regenerative braking blending and precise stop-lamp and cruise control. A fault can disable assist and cruise functions and set a warning lamp while base braking remains. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; NHTSA's EPS report lists C0043 in its J2012 table, and its brake study explains how the module uses the pedal sensor to read driver intent.
c: Pedal position sensor channel B out of range
Channel A/B signals do not correlate
s: Brake lights stay on or behave oddly
Cruise control will not set
ABS or brake warning lamp on

C0044.d: Covers brake pressure sensor A (sensor 1) in the ABS/ESC hydraulic unit, which measures master-cylinder or circuit brake pressure. The stability and brake modules use this reading to know how hard the driver is braking and to control traction, stability, brake assist and hill-hold. The module sets the code for a signal outside the valid range, an open or short, or a value that disagrees with pedal demand or a second pressure sensor. RAM assigns code C0044-01 to a general electrical failure of brake pressure sensor 1 on the 2024 2500; because the transducer sits inside the hydraulic control unit, the published repair replaces the whole integrated brake unit. A fault disables stability and assist functions and sets the ABS or brake warning lamp.
c: Pressure sensor failed or out of range
Fault internal to the integrated brake unit
s: ABS or brake warning lamp on
Stability and assist functions disabled
Changed brake assist behaviour

C0045.d: C0045 covers brake pressure sensor B, the second pressure transducer in the ABS/ESC hydraulic unit next to sensor A (C0044). Two sensors let the module watch both brake circuits or check one reading against the other for stability control, brake assist and brake-by-wire functions. The code sets for a signal out of range, an open or short, or a value that disagrees with sensor A or the pedal demand. Where the sensor sits inside an integrated brake unit, repair usually means replacing the whole unit. NHTSA's EPS safety report lists C0045 with this J2012 meaning. Older GM vehicles use C0045 for the left rear wheel speed sensor circuit instead (GM PIE0456, 16-NA-248), so the make decides what a stored C0045 means.
c: Pressure sensor failed or out of range
Fault internal to the integrated brake unit
Signal does not correlate with sensor A
s: ABS or brake warning lamp on
Stability and assist functions disabled
Changed brake assist behaviour

C0046.d: A correlation code for the pair of brake pressure sensors A and B, set when their readings do not agree within the expected tolerance. Where C0044 and C0045 flag a single-sensor electrical fault, this code is a plausibility fault: at the same instant both sensors should report consistent pressure (allowing for their known relationship), and a persistent mismatch indicates one sensor has drifted, a hydraulic fault separates the circuits, or a signal is corrupted. The stability and brake modules rely on agreement to trust the pressure reading for stability, brake assist and brake-by-wire control. A fault disables those functions and sets the ABS or brake warning lamp while base braking remains. NHTSA lists C0046 in the J2012 table of its EPS report. No manufacturer documents it publicly.
c: One pressure sensor drifted or biased
s: ABS or brake warning lamp on
Stability and assist functions disabled
Changed brake assist behaviour

C0047.d: Covers the pressure sensor in the power brake booster or brake actuation unit, which measures boost or assist pressure so the module can regulate assist and detect loss of boost. The module monitors the sensor for a signal outside the valid range, an open or short and values that disagree with pedal demand or master-cylinder pressure. Ford documents C0047:64 on 2020 Explorer and Lincoln Aviator, where it is stored in the ABS module with a noticeable loss of power brake assist or a soft, long brake pedal just after start-up. A fault reduces or disables controlled assist and sets the brake or ABS warning lamp; the driver may feel a harder, longer pedal until assist is restored.
c: Booster pressure sensor out of range
s: Lack of power brake assist
Soft or extended pedal at start-up
ABS or brake warning lamp on

C0048.d: Covers the travel (position) sensor of the power brake booster or brake actuation unit, which reports how far the booster input rod or piston has moved so the module can match assist to driver demand. The module monitors the sensor for a signal outside the valid range, an open or short and a position that is implausible against pedal position or boost pressure. It complements the booster pressure sensor C0047: travel gives displacement while pressure gives force, and together they let the module close the assist loop in electronic and brake-by-wire boosters. A fault reduces or disables controlled assist, changes pedal feel and sets the brake or ABS warning lamp while base braking remains. Patents describe an electrical travel sensor that tracks the moving wall inside a vacuum booster. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Travel sensor out of range or failed
s: Changed brake pedal feel
Reduced or inconsistent brake assist
ABS or brake warning lamp on

C0049.d: Covers the brake fluid level input to the brake or stability module, used to warn the driver and to disable functions that must not run with low fluid. A float switch or sensor in the master-cylinder reservoir signals when fluid drops below a safe level; the module sets this code and lights the red brake warning indicator. A genuine low level usually means worn brake pads that have drawn fluid into the calipers or a leak in the hydraulic system, but Ford documents cases on 2021-2025 Bronco and 2024 Mustang where a false low-level message with C0049 (sub-types :01, :0A) was caused by the reservoir or its sensor and resolved by replacing the reservoir. Low fluid can disable ABS and stability control; the condition should always be inspected because it can indicate a leak.
c: Low fluid from worn pads or a leak
Faulty reservoir level sensor or float
s: Red brake warning indicator on
Low brake fluid message
ABS and stability control may be disabled

C004A.d: Covers the brake lining (pad) wear sensor circuit, which warns the driver when friction material is worn to its limit. Electronic wear sensors use a loop embedded in the pad that the disc contacts and opens, or a wear-indicator circuit, as the lining wears down; the module reports pad wear and may store this code for an open, shorted or implausible sensor circuit as well as for a genuine worn-pad signal. It is an advisory function rather than a safety-critical control loss: braking and ABS continue, but the driver is told to inspect or replace the pads. The code can appear after pad replacement if the sensor was not renewed or reconnected. Delphi describes both the single loop and two-stage sensors with two resistor circuits. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Brake pads worn to the sensor limit
Open or shorted wear sensor circuit
Sensor not renewed after pad change
s: Brake pad wear warning message
Warning lamp on
Possible squeal from a mechanical indicator

C004B.d: Covers an electrical fault, specifically an open or out-of-range circuit, in the brake fluid level sensor or switch, as opposed to C0049 which reports an actual low-level condition. The float switch or level sensor in the reservoir provides a defined signal to the brake or stability module; this code is set when that circuit is open, shorted or gives an implausible value so the module can no longer trust the level reading. Because the level warning is a safety function, the module may illuminate the red brake warning indicator and treat the level as unknown. A fault is usually a broken wire, a corroded connector or a failed switch rather than low fluid itself. Patents show the usual float magnet acting on a reed or Hall switch. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Red brake warning indicator on
Brake fluid level reads as unknown
Intermittent low-fluid warnings

C004C.t: Brake Booster Motor A Position Sensor Exceeded Learning Limit
C004C.d: Set in an electric or electro-hydraulic brake booster when the position sensor of booster motor A reports a learned reference value outside the allowed adaptation range. The brake control unit learns the rest and travel positions of the motor-driven actuator so it can meter assist precisely; if the learned value drifts beyond the calibrated window the module can no longer trust the actuator position and stores this code. It points to a worn or shifted sensor, mechanical wear in the actuator or a learning routine that ran under wrong conditions rather than a hard electrical fault. Controlled brake assist is reduced or disabled and the brake or ABS warning lamp is set; conventional braking remains. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and electro-hydraulic brake actuator design.
c: Mechanical wear in the booster actuator
Learning routine ran under wrong conditions
s: Reduced or inconsistent brake assist
Changed brake pedal feel
ABS or brake warning lamp on

C004D.d: A performance code set when the brake system builds or changes hydraulic pressure more slowly than the control unit commands during an assisted or automated braking event. In electronically controlled brake systems the module commands a target pressure and watches the pressure sensor; if the measured pressure lags the demand beyond a calibrated time or rate it concludes the pump, motor, valves or hydraulic path cannot respond quickly enough. It is a plausibility and timing fault rather than a single electrical defect, and can be caused by air in the system, a weak pump, a sticking valve or a restriction. Automated braking and stability functions are limited and the brake or ABS warning lamp is set. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and electro-hydraulic brake control design.
c: Air in the hydraulic system or low fluid
s: Longer pedal travel or delayed assist
Automated braking functions limited
ABS or brake warning lamp on

C004E.t: Brake System Pressure Control Valve Actuator Stuck
C004E.d: Set when the actuator of a brake system pressure control valve does not move as commanded and appears mechanically stuck. In electronically controlled brake and stability systems a pressure control valve regulates how much hydraulic pressure reaches the wheel circuits; the module commands the valve and checks the resulting pressure against the demand. When the pressure does not change although the valve was commanded, or the valve position feedback does not follow, the module concludes the actuator is stuck by contamination, corrosion or a mechanical fault. Pressure modulation for ABS, traction and stability is lost on the affected circuit and the brake or ABS warning lamp is set while base braking remains.
c: Valve actuator stuck by contamination or wear
Corrosion or debris in the valve bore
s: ABS, traction and stability control disabled
Abnormal brake behaviour on one circuit
ABS or brake warning lamp on

C004F.d: Set when the ABS/ESC control module or its integrated pump motor reaches a temperature above the safe operating limit. Repeated or prolonged pressure modulation, for example during long downhill ABS use, frequent stability interventions or an electrical fault that keeps the pump running, heats the hydraulic unit and its motor; the module monitors an internal temperature model or sensor and stores this code to protect the hardware. It temporarily disables ABS, traction and stability control until the unit cools, then restores them. A persistent over-temperature points to a seized pump, a stuck valve causing continuous pumping or a control fault. Base braking remains and the ABS warning lamp is set while the function is suspended. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and ABS hydraulic unit thermal protection.
c: Stuck valve causing continuous pump run
Pump motor seizing or high friction
s: ABS and stability control temporarily disabled
Function returns after cooling
ABS warning lamp on during the event

C0050.t: Right Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
C0050.d: A general circuit-malfunction code for the right rear wheel speed sensor, covering an electrical fault not resolved to a more specific sub-type: open circuit, short to power or ground, or a signal that drops out or becomes implausible while driving. The active sensor reports rear wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution; a chafed or broken harness, a failed sensor element or a corroded connector interrupts it, often intermittently. ABS, traction and stability control are disabled and the ABS warning lamp is set while base braking remains. Bosch active wheel speed sensors use a Hall element reading a magnetic encoder and need an intact two-wire circuit. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Broken or chafed sensor harness wiring
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
Speedometer may read erratically

C0051.d: Covers the steering wheel position (steering angle) sensor and its circuit. The sensor reports absolute steering-wheel angle and rate to the ESC module, which combines it with yaw rate, lateral acceleration and wheel speeds to decide when the car is understeering or oversteering. The module sets this code for an out-of-range signal, an open or short, or a neutral/centre position that is not learned or is implausible. Honda documents DTC C0051-54, set when the steering-angle centre position has not finished its learn routine, which can occur after a battery disconnect and usually self-clears after a short straight drive; Mazda logs C0051:62 when the learned steering-angle value differs too far from the initial value. A fault disables stability control and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains.
c: Neutral position not learned after service
s: Stability control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Sets after battery disconnect

C0052.t: Steering Wheel Position Sensor Signal A
C0052.d: Covers signal A of the steering wheel position sensor. Multi-track steering-angle sensors output several phase-shifted signals (A, B, C, D) so the ESC module can reconstruct absolute angle and detect a single bad channel by cross-checking. This code is set when channel A is out of range, open, shorted or does not agree with the other channels. Ford documents C0052 together with C0053, C0054 and C0055 on 2020-2021 Police Interceptor Utility vehicles, where the codes store in the steering module if the police-package steering-wheel accessory outputs are left unwired. A fault disables stability control and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and multi-track steering-angle sensor design.
c: Steering angle sensor channel A failed
s: Stability control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Implausible steering angle reading

C0053.t: Steering Wheel Position Sensor Signal B
C0053.d: Covers signal B of the steering wheel position sensor, the second of the multi-track channels the ESC module cross-checks against signals A, C and D to reconstruct absolute steering angle. This code is set when channel B is out of range, open, shorted or inconsistent with the other channels. Ford documents C0053 together with C0052, C0054 and C0055 on 2020-2021 Police Interceptor Utility vehicles, where the codes store in the steering module if the police-package steering-wheel accessory outputs are left unwired. A fault disables stability control and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and multi-track steering-angle sensor design, where a single faulty track makes the reconstructed angle untrustworthy.
c: Steering angle sensor channel B failed
s: Stability control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Implausible steering angle reading

C0054.t: Steering Wheel Position Sensor Signal C
C0054.d: Covers signal C of the steering wheel position sensor, the third multi-track channel the ESC module uses with signals A, B and D to reconstruct absolute steering angle and detect a bad channel by cross-checking. This code is set when channel C is out of range, open, shorted or inconsistent with the others. Ford documents C0054 together with C0052, C0053 and C0055 on 2020-2021 Police Interceptor Utility vehicles, where the codes store in the steering module if the police-package steering-wheel accessory outputs are left unwired. A fault disables stability control and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and multi-track steering-angle sensor design, in which redundant tracks guard against a single wrong angle.
c: Steering angle sensor channel C failed
s: Stability control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Implausible steering angle reading

C0055.t: Steering Wheel Position Sensor Signal D
C0055.d: Covers signal D of the steering wheel position sensor, the fourth multi-track channel that completes the set with signals A, B and C. The ESC module reconstructs absolute steering angle from all channels and uses their agreement to detect a single faulty track; this code is set when channel D is out of range, open, shorted or inconsistent with the others. Ford documents C0055 together with C0052, C0053 and C0054 on 2020-2021 Police Interceptor Utility vehicles, where the codes store in the steering module if the police-package steering-wheel accessory outputs are left unwired. A fault disables stability control and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and multi-track steering-angle sensor design.
c: Steering angle sensor channel D failed
s: Stability control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Implausible steering angle reading

C0056.t: Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
C0056.d: Covers an intermittent fault in the left rear wheel speed sensor circuit, where the signal is lost or corrupted only part of the time rather than permanently. The ABS/ESC module expects a clean pulse train proportional to wheel speed; a chafed wire that opens over bumps, a loose or corroded connector, a cracked sensor or a contaminated encoder ring can make the signal drop out briefly. Because the fault is sporadic it may set and self-clear, and ABS, traction and stability control drop out only during the glitches. The ABS warning lamp is set and base braking remains. Bosch active wheel speed sensors depend on a stable two-wire supply and a clean air gap to the encoder. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
s: Intermittent ABS warning lamp
ABS/ESC drops out briefly
Speedometer flickers

C0060.t: Right Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
C0060.d: Covers a general fault in the right rear wheel speed sensor circuit. The active sensor feeds rear wheel rotation to the ABS/ESC module for anti-lock, traction and stability control and electronic brake-force distribution; the module monitors the two-wire circuit for opens, shorts to power or ground, out-of-range current and a missing signal while the vehicle moves. A broken or chafed harness, a failed sensor or a corroded connector sets the code and disables ABS, traction and stability control while base braking remains. It overlaps with the right rear circuit-malfunction code C0050 and the intermittent code C0066, differing in the exact fault qualifier the module assigns. Bosch active sensors read a magnetic encoder through a Hall element and need an intact supply. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Broken or chafed sensor harness wiring
s: ABS warning lamp on
ABS and stability control disabled
Speedometer may read erratically

C0061.d: C0061 flags the lateral acceleration signal, which the stability module compares with the value expected from steering angle, yaw rate and speed. The code sets when the signal is out of range, frozen, noisy or implausible against the other inertial channels. FCA uses it on the 2022 Jeep Compass as C0061-29, signal invalid, together with C0062-29 and C0063-29; customers see the MIL plus ESC and parking brake warnings, and bulletin 08-007-23 reflashes the ABS module. FCA also lists C0061 in a PCM update for the 2016 Jeep Renegade 2.4 l. Mazda uses the same number in the headlight auto-leveling module: on the 2018 CX-3, C0061:54 means the acceleration sensor's initial position was not learned, typically after transport on a trailer (bulletin 09-012/18).
c: Headlight leveling sensor position not learned after transport (Mazda)
Lateral accelerometer failed or out of range
Sensor cluster loose or shifted on its mount
s: Stability control disabled, ESC warning lamp on
MIL on together with ESC and parking brake warnings (FCA)
Headlight leveling warning flashes (Mazda)

C0062.d: C0062 flags the longitudinal acceleration signal, the fore-aft reading used for hill hold, grade detection, all-wheel-drive torque split and brake distribution. The module checks it against the change in wheel speed, braking and throttle and against the other inertial channels, and stores the code for a value out of range, frozen, noisy or implausible. FCA documents C0062-29, invalid signal, on the 2022 Jeep Compass with C0061-29 and C0063-29, lighting the MIL and the ESC and parking brake warnings until the ABS module receives new software (08-007-23). On the 2019 RAM 1500, FCA lists C0062 among the codes a PCM software update addresses (18-058-20). Stability and hill hold are switched off while the fault is present; normal braking remains.
c: Sensor cluster loose or shifted on its mount
s: Stability and hill-hold functions disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
AWD behaviour may change

C0063.d: C0063 flags the yaw rate signal, the rotation about the vertical axis that stability control compares with a reference built from steering angle, lateral acceleration and speed. A lasting gap means understeer or oversteer, so a corrupt signal would trigger wrong interventions; the module therefore stores the code and stops ESC when the value is out of range, frozen, noisy or implausible. FCA documents two variants on the Jeep Compass: C0063-29, invalid signal, with C0061-29 and C0062-29 on 2022 models, cured by ABS software (08-007-23), and C0063-9A, component or system operating conditions, on 2024 models, where the MIL is on and the driver assistance module is reprogrammed (08-128-24). Normal braking stays available throughout.
c: ABS or driver assistance module software (FCA 08-007-23, 08-128-24)
Yaw rate gyro failed or out of range
Sensor cluster loose or shifted on its mount
s: Stability control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Unexpected or absent stability intervention

C0064.d: C0064 covers the roll rate sensor, a gyroscope that measures rotation about the vehicle's longitudinal axis. NHTSA's brake safety study names roll rate among the vehicle dynamics inputs of the ABS/ESC module, and roll stability control uses it, mainly on tall vehicles, to spot the onset of a rollover and counter it with braking and torque reduction. The module checks the roll signal against lateral acceleration and the other inertial channels and sets C0064 when it is out of range, stuck, noisy or implausible. In current six-axis inertial units such as Bosch's IMU the roll gyro shares one housing with pitch and yaw gyros and three accelerometers. Roll stability control switches off and the ESC lamp lights; base braking remains. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Roll rate gyro failed or out of range
Loose or shifted sensor cluster mounting
s: Roll stability control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Rollover mitigation unavailable

C0065.d: C0065 covers the vertical acceleration sensor, which measures up-and-down acceleration of the body. Bosch's inertial measurement unit shows where it lives today: one housing measures the rates of yaw, pitch and roll plus vertical, longitudinal and lateral acceleration and serves several control systems at once. The vertical channel supports rough-road and wheel-lift detection, rollover recognition and, with adaptive damping, the suspension control. The module checks the vertical reading against the other channels and stores C0065 when it is out of range, stuck, noisy or implausible. Depending on the vehicle, stability or suspension functions are reduced and the ESC or suspension lamp lights, while normal braking is unaffected. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Loose or shifted sensor cluster mounting
s: Stability or suspension functions disabled
ABS/ESC or suspension warning lamp on
Degraded rough-road handling control

C0066.d: Public SAE J2012 code lists still mark C0066 as ISO/SAE reserved, and no manufacturer documents the code in a retrievable bulletin or service text. One current code table assigns it to the pitch rate sensor, which fits its place between roll rate (C0064), vertical acceleration (C0065) and the yaw/longitudinal pair (C0069); the title follows that use. Such a sensor tracks rotation about the vehicle's lateral axis, as when the body dives under braking or squats under acceleration. Bosch's six-axis inertial unit reports pitch rate next to yaw and roll rate, and a GM patent compares the measured pitch rate with a virtual value built from suspension heights, wheel speeds and accelerations, flags a fault from the difference and rebuilds the signal. Where fitted, a fault limits rollover and stability functions and lights the ESC lamp.
c: Pitch rate gyro failed, drifting or out of range
Sensor cluster loose or tilted on its mount
Harness or connector fault at the sensor cluster
s: ESC or stability warning lamp on
Rollover and stability functions reduced

C0069.d: C0069 is a plausibility code for the yaw rate and longitudinal acceleration sensors taken together. When the vehicle brakes in a bend, yaw, longitudinal and lateral motion must stay in a physical relationship; if the two signals keep contradicting each other or the rest of the inertial set, one channel has drifted, both share a fault, or the cluster has shifted on its mount. NHTSA's brake safety study lists yaw rate and longitudinal acceleration as inputs of the stability module and notes that several vehicle dynamics sensors are often combined in one unit, which is what makes such cross-checks possible. The module stores C0069, switches off stability and related functions and lights the ESC lamp; base braking remains. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: One inertial channel drifted or biased
Sensor cluster shifted on its mount
s: Stability control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Inertial signals implausible together

C006A.d: C006A covers a combined multi-axis sensor that delivers several motion axes from one device, the integrated form of the separate lateral, longitudinal, vertical, yaw and roll sensors; NHTSA's brake study and Bosch's six-axis IMU describe such units. The module treats the device as a whole and sets C006A for an internal fault, a failed self-test, lost communication or values that disagree across the axes. FCA documents C006A-49, internal electronic failure, on 2019-2020 RAM 2500 to 5500 trucks: the MIL comes on and bulletin 08-061-20 cures it with new ABS software; a RAM 2500 case report lists it as an active code in the ABS module. Stability, roll and related functions stay off while the fault is present; normal braking remains.
c: Internal sensor fault or failed self-test
s: Stability and roll control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Multiple inertial faults at once

C006B.d: Set when the stability or traction control system has been intervening continuously for longer than the calibrated maximum. ESC and traction control are meant to act in short bursts; if the controller keeps modulating brakes or reducing torque beyond a time limit it concludes something is wrong, for example a persistently spinning wheel on ice, a dragging brake, a mismatched tyre or a sensor feeding a wrong signal, and stores this code while backing the intervention off to protect the hardware and avoid masking a real fault. The ABS/ESC warning lamp is set and base braking remains. Traction-control patents describe the controller overriding the driver's torque request only transiently to bring slip to target. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Wheel spinning or slipping for a long time
Wrong sensor input driving the intervention
s: Stability/traction control cuts out
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Prolonged intervention before fault

C006C.d: A general stability-system fault code covering the electronic stability control function as a whole rather than one named sensor or actuator. The ESC module sets it when an internal self-check fails, when the stability function cannot run because required inputs are missing or inconsistent, or when a system-level plausibility check is violated and no more specific code applies. It usually appears with companion codes that name the actual faulty sensor, valve or communication link. Stability control is disabled and the ABS/ESC warning lamp is set while base braking remains. Integrated-control sensor clusters and supervisory logic described in ESC patents coordinate yaw, lateral, steering and wheel-speed inputs; a break anywhere in that chain can set a system-level code. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
s: Stability control disabled
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Appears with companion DTCs

C0070.d: Covers the vehicle speed sensor circuit, the source of the overall road-speed signal used by the ABS/ESC module and shared with the speedometer, transmission and other systems. On many vehicles road speed is derived from the wheel speed sensors or a transmission output sensor; this code is set when that speed signal is open, shorted, out of range or implausible against the individual wheel speeds. A fault can disable stability and speed-dependent functions, disturb the speedometer and affect shift scheduling, and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. Active wheel speed sensors, which typically feed this signal, read a magnetic encoder through a Hall element and need an intact circuit. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Open or shorted speed signal wiring
Failed wheel or output speed sensor
s: Speedometer inaccurate or dead
Stability and speed functions disabled
Erratic transmission shifting

C0071.d: Covers the input that tells the ABS/ESC module whether the vehicle is in two- or four-wheel-drive mode. Because four-wheel drive links the axles and changes how wheel speeds relate, the stability and ABS strategy must know the current drive mode; this signal comes from the transfer-case switch, the drive-mode selector or a message from the drivetrain controller. The code is set when that status is missing, implausible or inconsistent with observed wheel behaviour. Subaru documents DTC C0071 in the vehicle dynamics control system with revised troubleshooting. A fault can make the module default to a safe strategy, disable some functions and set the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and all-wheel-drive mode-signalling design.
c: Missing drive-mode message on the bus
s: Stability or ABS strategy limited
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Drive-mode display incorrect

C0072.d: Set when the brake or stability module estimates that brake temperature has risen above a safe threshold. Few vehicles measure rotor temperature directly; most run a thermal model that integrates braking force, speed and time to estimate how hot the brakes are, and warn or adapt control when overheating is likely, for example on a long descent. The code is stored when the modelled or measured temperature exceeds the limit, prompting a driver warning and sometimes reduced regenerative blending or electronic brake-force changes. It is advisory and protective rather than a wiring fault; braking and ABS continue. Persistent setting can indicate a dragging brake or an implausible model input. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and electronic brake-system thermal modelling.
c: Brakes overheated on a long descent
Implausible input to the thermal model
s: Brake temperature warning to driver
Reduced regenerative braking blend
Brake fade on long descents

C0073.d: Covers the delivered-driving-torque signal that the engine or powertrain controller reports to the ABS/ESC module during traction and stability control. To limit wheel spin the stability controller asks the powertrain to reduce torque; it then needs confirmation of how much torque was actually delivered to close the loop. This code is set when the delivered-torque value is missing, out of range or does not match the request, for example because of a communication fault or a powertrain controller problem. Traction-control patents describe the request/deliver handshake between the stability and engine controllers for torque reduction. A fault limits traction and stability control and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
s: Traction and stability control limited
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Appears with powertrain DTCs

C0074.d: Covers the requested-driving-torque signal that the ABS/ESC module sends to the powertrain controller during traction and stability control, the counterpart to the delivered-torque signal C0073. When a driven wheel spins the stability controller computes a torque-reduction request and transmits it; this code is set when that request path is faulty, the value is out of range, or the request and the powertrain's response are inconsistent. Traction-control patents describe how the controller overrides the driver's torque demand transiently to bring slip to target by cutting spark, fuel or throttle. A fault limits traction and stability control and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains; it usually appears together with powertrain or communication codes. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Fault on the torque request path
s: Traction and stability control limited
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Appears with powertrain DTCs

C0075.d: A performance code for the brake pedal position input, set when the signal is present but behaves implausibly, for example it does not change as expected, lags, or disagrees with brake pressure and the switch. The stability and brake modules use pedal position to blend regenerative and friction braking and to arm or cancel driver-assist functions. Manufacturers map this code to the input their system uses: Subaru documents C0075 as a concern with the wheel-cylinder pressure-sensor signal in the EyeSight dynamics-control hydraulic module, while some European systems tie it to the brake-light switch feeding the ESP unit. A fault degrades regenerative blending and assist functions and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Pedal or switch out of adjustment
s: Degraded regenerative braking blend
Driver-assist functions limited
ABS/ESC warning lamp on

C0076.d: Covers the pulse-width-modulated signal used within the traction control interface, for example a PWM torque-request or status line exchanged between the stability and powertrain controllers or driving a traction-related actuator. The module monitors the PWM signal's duty cycle, frequency and presence and sets this code when it is missing, out of range or implausible. Traction-control patents describe the controller commanding torque reduction and actuators through defined signal interfaces; a corrupted PWM link breaks that chain. A fault limits traction control and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains, usually alongside the torque request/deliver codes. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and traction-control signalling design.
c: PWM signal missing or out of range
s: Traction control limited
ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Appears with torque request DTCs

C0077.d: Covers a low-tire-pressure indication reaching the ABS/ESC or body module, typically from an indirect tyre-pressure monitoring system that infers pressure from wheel behaviour rather than from in-tyre sensors. An under-inflated tyre has a smaller rolling radius and turns faster, and its vibration spectrum shifts; the system detects this from the ABS wheel speed signals and raises a low-pressure warning. Honda documents VSA code C0077-78, which refines the warning threshold for low tyre pressure, where the indicator stays on although the tyres are correctly inflated, calling for a TPMS software update; Volvo documents BCM-C007768 on indirect-TPMS vehicles. A set code warns the driver and may require a reset after correct inflation. Indirect TPMS patents describe the wheel-speed and resonance methods used.
s: Low tire pressure indicator on
Warning despite correct pressure
Requires reset after inflation

C0078.d: Covers a tyre-diameter fault or mismatch detected by the ABS/ESC or indirect-TPMS logic. The system learns the rolling diameter of each tyre from wheel speeds at known vehicle speed; a tyre that is a different size, badly worn, or a mismatched spare makes one wheel turn at a different rate, which the module flags as a diameter problem. The code is set when a learned or compared diameter falls outside the allowed range or the learn routine cannot complete. Indirect-TPMS patents rely on exactly this rolling-radius comparison to infer low pressure, so a true size mismatch can disturb TPMS and stability logic. A fault can affect TPMS and stability functions and sets the warning lamp; correcting tyre sizes and relearning clears it. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Badly worn tyre changing rolling radius
Diameter not relearned after tyre change
s: TPMS or stability warning lamp on
Inaccurate speed or TPMS readings
Learn routine will not complete

C0079.d: Covers the variable-effort (speed-sensitive) power steering function, where steering assist is high at low speed for easy parking and reduced at high speed for stability. The ABS/ESC or steering module uses vehicle speed to command the assist level through a solenoid-controlled hydraulic valve or an electric power-steering actuator. This code is set when the variable-effort actuator circuit is faulty, the commanded assist cannot be achieved, or the speed input it relies on is missing. A fault typically defaults steering to a fixed assist level and sets a warning; braking and ABS are unaffected. Because the function depends on a valid speed signal it can appear with wheel-speed or speed-signal codes. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and speed-sensitive power-steering design.
c: Missing or wrong vehicle speed input
s: Steering effort fixed or abnormal
Steering warning lamp or message
Heavy steering at low speed

C0080.d: Set when the two front wheel speed signals disagree by more than the allowed amount under conditions where they should match, pointing to a wheel-speed or tyre problem rather than a single open circuit. The ABS/ESC module continuously compares left and right front speeds; a persistent mismatch on a straight road can mean a failing sensor, a damaged tone ring, a mismatched or badly worn tyre or uneven inflation. Indirect-TPMS logic uses the same front-axle comparison to infer pressure loss, so this code and a low-pressure warning can share a root cause. ABS, traction and stability control may be limited and the ABS warning lamp is set while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and wheel-speed comparison diagnostics.
c: Mismatched, worn or unevenly inflated tyres
Failing sensor or damaged tone ring
s: ABS warning lamp on
Traction or stability control limited
Possible false low-pressure warning

C0081.d: Covers the ABS malfunction indicator (warning lamp) itself as driven or monitored by the ABS/ESC module. The module commands the ABS lamp on for a fault and off when healthy, and monitors the output circuit; this code is set when the lamp circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or the commanded and observed states disagree, for example a bulb-check failure or a bus message not reaching the cluster. It is about the indicator path rather than the ABS hydraulics, so braking and ABS themselves may still work while the driver loses the warning. The related rear-axle mismatch and wheel-speed codes describe the faults the lamp would normally announce. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and warning-lamp output monitoring.
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster
s: ABS warning lamp stuck on or off
Failed lamp self-check
Driver loses ABS warning

C0082.d: Covers the brake system malfunction indicator (red brake warning lamp) as driven or monitored by the brake/stability module. The module commands this lamp for serious brake faults such as low fluid, pressure problems or a control fault, and monitors the output; this code is set when the lamp circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or commanded and observed states disagree. It concerns the indicator path rather than the hydraulics, so the underlying brake function may still work while the driver loses an important warning, or the lamp stays on without a brake fault. Electronic brake-system designs route many warnings through this lamp, so it often appears with the brake fault it was meant to announce. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster
s: Red brake lamp stuck on or off
Failed lamp self-check
Driver loses brake warning

C0083.d: Covers the tyre-pressure-monitor indicator (TPMS lamp) as driven or monitored by the responsible module. Regulations distinguish a steady low-pressure warning from a flashing TPMS-malfunction indication; this code concerns the indicator path, set when the TPMS lamp circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or the commanded and observed states disagree. A system that cannot monitor pressure, for example an indirect system that has lost its wheel-speed reference or a direct system missing sensor data, requests the malfunction indication, and a fault in that path sets this code. Indirect-TPMS patents describe deriving pressure from ABS wheel-speed signals, so a loss of that data can drive both a TPMS fault and this indicator code. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: TPMS cannot monitor, requests fault lamp
s: TPMS indicator stuck on or flashing
Failed lamp self-check
Loss of tyre pressure warning

C0084.d: Covers the traction-active indicator, the lamp that flashes to tell the driver traction control is currently intervening, as driven or monitored by the ABS/ESC module. The module flashes this lamp during a traction event and monitors the output circuit; this code is set when the indicator circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or commanded and observed states disagree. It concerns the indicator path, not the traction function itself, so traction control may still operate while the driver loses its activity feedback. Traction-control patents describe the controller cutting torque and modulating brakes during intervention, which this lamp signals. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and warning-lamp output monitoring.
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster
s: Traction indicator stuck on or off
No feedback during traction events
Failed lamp self-check

C0085.d: Covers the traction-disable indicator, the lamp that shows traction control has been switched off by the driver or by the system, as driven or monitored by the ABS/ESC module. The module lights this lamp when traction control is disabled and monitors the output; this code is set when the indicator circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or commanded and observed states disagree. It concerns the indicator path, not the traction function; the driver may lose the on/off feedback while control itself behaves normally. It is closely tied to the traction-disable switch and the active-indicator lamp. Traction-control patents describe the driver being able to disable intervention, which this lamp announces. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster
s: Traction-off indicator stuck on or off
No feedback when toggling traction control
Failed lamp self-check

C0086.d: Covers the vehicle-dynamics indicator, the lamp that signals the status of the electronic stability / vehicle-dynamics control to the driver, as driven or monitored by the ESC module. The module lights or flashes this lamp for stability status and faults and monitors the output; this code is set when the indicator circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or commanded and observed states disagree. Ford documents C0086 in this indicator context. It concerns the indicator path rather than the control function, so stability control may still operate while the driver loses status feedback, or the lamp stays on without a dynamics fault. No further code-specific detail was confirmed beyond the Ford bulletin; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and warning-lamp output monitoring.
c: Lamp request not reaching the cluster
s: Dynamics indicator stuck on or off
Loss of stability status feedback
Failed lamp self-check

C0089.d: Covers the driver switch that turns traction (or stability) control off, and its circuit to the ABS/ESC module. Pressing the switch tells the module to disable intervention and light the traction-off indicator; this code is set when the switch signal is stuck, implausible, or the circuit is open or shorted, for example a switch that reads permanently pressed or a broken wire. A stuck-on switch could keep traction control disabled, which is a safety concern, so the module may ignore the switch and default to control enabled. Traction-control patents describe driver-selectable disabling of the intervention. A fault affects the on/off function and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Switch stuck or reads permanently pressed
s: Traction control cannot be toggled
Traction-off indicator wrong
ABS/ESC warning lamp on

C008A.d: Covers the traction-control mode selector and its input to the ABS/ESC module, used where the driver can choose among traction/terrain modes such as snow, sand, mud or sport that change the slip targets and intervention strategy. This code is set when the mode signal is stuck, implausible, out of range or the circuit is faulty, so the module cannot tell which mode is selected. The module then defaults to a safe mode and may disable mode selection. It differs from the simple on/off disable switch C0089 in that it carries a multi-position mode rather than a single state. Traction-control patents describe mode-dependent slip targets and torque strategies. A fault limits mode selection and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains.
c: Mode selector signal stuck or implausible
s: Terrain/traction mode cannot be selected
System defaults to a safe mode
ABS/ESC warning lamp on

C0090.d: Covers the actuator that engages or modulates the power transfer unit (transfer case / front coupling) in a four- or all-wheel-drive system. On demand the controller drives this actuator, typically an electric motor or an electromagnetic/electro-hydraulic clutch operator, to send torque to the secondary axle. This code is set when the actuator circuit is open, shorted, out of range or the actuator does not respond to the command. AWD coupling patents describe electronically controlled clutches actuated by a motor-driven ball-ramp or a gerotor pump to vary torque split between two- and four-wheel-drive modes. A fault can lock the system in one mode or default to two-wheel drive and sets the AWD/4WD warning lamp; braking and ABS are unaffected. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: PTU actuator motor or coil failed
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp on
Stuck in one drive mode or 2WD default
Reduced traction on loose surfaces

C0091.t: 4WD/AWD Power Transfer Unit Position Sensor A
C0091.d: Covers position sensor A of the power transfer unit actuator, which reports how far the transfer-case or coupling actuator has moved so the controller can close the loop on torque split or mode. The controller commands the actuator and reads this sensor to confirm the achieved position; this code is set when the sensor signal is out of range, open, shorted or implausible against the commanded or expected position. AWD coupling patents describe electronically controlled couplings whose controller relies on actuator position feedback to meter clutch engagement force. A fault makes the controller unable to trust the actuator position, so it may default to a safe torque split or two-wheel drive and set the AWD/4WD warning lamp; braking and ABS are unaffected.
c: Position sensor A failed or out of range
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp on
Default torque split or 2WD mode
Inconsistent AWD engagement

C0092.t: 4WD/AWD Power Transfer Unit Position Sensor B
C0092.d: Covers position sensor B of the power transfer unit actuator, the redundant or second-channel position feedback the controller cross-checks against sensor A (C0091). Dual position sensors let the controller detect a single faulty channel and keep metering the AWD coupling safely. This code is set when sensor B is out of range, open, shorted or does not track sensor A within tolerance. AWD coupling patents describe closed-loop control of the clutch actuator using position feedback, where losing a channel degrades control. A fault makes the position feedback untrustworthy, so the controller may default to a safe torque split or two-wheel drive and set the AWD/4WD warning lamp; braking and ABS are unaffected. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and dual-channel actuator position sensing.
c: Position sensor B failed or out of range
Sensor A/B signals do not correlate
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp on
Default torque split or 2WD mode
Inconsistent AWD engagement

C0093.d: Covers the temperature sensor of the power transfer unit, which lets the controller protect the AWD clutch from overheating. Sustained torque transfer, for example prolonged slip or towing, heats the clutch pack and its fluid; the controller reads this sensor and reduces or opens the coupling when temperature climbs too high. This code is set when the sensor signal is out of range, open, shorted or implausible. AWD coupling patents describe electronically controlled clutches whose controller monitors operating conditions, including temperature, to protect the hardware. A fault removes thermal protection and can force a safe default such as reduced engagement, and sets the AWD/4WD warning lamp; braking and ABS are unaffected. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and AWD coupling thermal management.
c: Temperature sensor out of range or failed
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp on
Reduced AWD engagement for protection
No thermal protection of the coupling

C0094.d: Covers the temperature sensor of the rear differential unit in an all-wheel-drive system, used to protect the rear drive module and its electronically controlled coupling from overheating. Prolonged torque transfer to the rear axle heats the clutch and fluid; the controller reads this sensor and limits engagement when it gets too hot. This code is set when the sensor signal is out of range, open, shorted or implausible. FCA documents C0094-4B on the Jeep Compass in the rear drive/AWD context. A fault removes thermal protection for the rear unit and can force reduced engagement, setting the AWD/4WD warning lamp; braking and ABS are unaffected. It is the rear-axle counterpart of the power-transfer-unit temperature sensor C0093. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Temperature sensor out of range or failed
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp on
Reduced rear-axle engagement for protection
No thermal protection of the rear unit

C0095.d: Covers actuator A of the rear differential unit, which engages or modulates the electronically controlled rear coupling or locking differential in an all-wheel-drive system. The controller drives this actuator, typically a motor-operated clutch operator or an electromagnetic coil, to send or lock torque at the rear axle on demand. This code is set when the actuator circuit is open, shorted, out of range or the actuator does not respond. Ford documents C0095:99 in the rear drive unit context. AWD coupling patents describe motor-driven ball-ramp or gerotor clutch operators that vary rear torque. A fault can lock the rear unit in one state or default to open, reducing traction, and sets the AWD/4WD warning lamp; braking and ABS are unaffected. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp on
Rear axle stuck engaged or open
Reduced traction on loose surfaces

C0096.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator A Data
C0096.d: Covers the data or feedback associated with rear differential actuator A (C0095), as opposed to a plain circuit fault. Where C0095 flags the drive circuit, this code is set when the actuator's reported data, its position, current or status feedback, is missing, out of range or implausible against the command, so the controller cannot confirm what the actuator is doing. Ford documents the rear drive actuator A context on this family. AWD coupling patents describe closed-loop control that relies on actuator feedback to meter clutch engagement; losing that feedback degrades control even if the drive circuit is intact. A fault makes the rear engagement untrustworthy, so the controller may default to a safe state and set the AWD/4WD warning lamp; braking and ABS are unaffected. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
c: Actuator feedback data missing or implausible
Communication fault with the rear module
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp on
Rear engagement unconfirmed
Default safe AWD state

C0097.d: Covers actuator B of the rear differential unit, the second actuator used on rear drive modules that control two functions, for example torque transfer and a limited-slip or locking element, or that use two coils for redundancy. The controller drives this actuator to engage or modulate the rear coupling; this code is set when the actuator B circuit is open, shorted, out of range or the actuator does not respond. AWD coupling patents describe drive axles with more than one hydraulically or electromagnetically controlled coupling, one for front-to-rear torque transfer and one for side-to-side limited slip. A fault can lock the affected function or default it to open, reducing traction or torque vectoring, and sets the AWD/4WD warning lamp; braking and ABS are unaffected. It is the counterpart to actuator A (C0095).
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp on
Limited-slip or lock function lost
Reduced traction or torque vectoring

C0098.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator B Data
C0098.d: Covers the data or feedback associated with rear differential actuator B (C0097), as opposed to a plain circuit fault. Where C0097 flags the drive circuit, this code is set when actuator B's reported data, its position, current or status feedback, is missing, out of range or implausible against the command, so the controller cannot confirm what the actuator is doing. AWD coupling patents describe closed-loop control that relies on actuator feedback to meter clutch engagement; losing that feedback degrades control even when the drive circuit is intact. A fault makes the affected rear function untrustworthy, so the controller may default to a safe state and set the AWD/4WD warning lamp; braking and ABS are unaffected. It is the data counterpart to actuator B (C0097) and parallels C0096 for actuator A.
c: Actuator feedback data missing or implausible
Communication fault with the rear module
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp on
Rear function engagement unconfirmed
Default safe AWD state

C0099.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator A Position Sensor A
C0099.d: The title gives actuator A of the rear differential unit three position channels, A to C. That layout matches the way brushless actuator motors track their rotor: three Hall elements on the stator read a magnet on the rotor, and their combined states step the motor through six commutation phases. C0099 concerns channel A alone. It is logged when that signal drops out, sticks or leaves its voltage window, typically from an open wire, a short to ground or a dead Hall element. Schaeffler patents a sensor carrier of this kind for a clutch actuator motor, TI documents Hall-based commutation, and BorgWarner drives its current AWD coupling with a brushless motor. No manufacturer publishes a C0099 case. Losing one channel usually means the rear clutch is released and an AWD warning appears.
c: Open or grounded signal wire of channel A between actuator and module
Corroded or loose connector at the rear drive unit
Failed Hall element A inside the actuator motor
Missing sensor supply or ground from the module
s: AWD/4WD warning lamp or message in the cluster
Rear axle no longer driven, front-wheel drive only
Reduced traction on slippery surfaces

C009A.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator A Position Sensor B
C009A.d: Channel B is the second of the three position signals that actuator A of the rear differential unit reports to its control module. This code points at that one line or element, while channels A and C still deliver plausible edges. A Hyundai Kefico patent explains how a controller singles out such a channel: while one healthy Hall signal keeps toggling, a channel that never changes is marked faulty and a code is stored; all three reading low hints at an open supply, all three high at a short. The same document lets the motor continue in an emergency mode by estimating rotor angle from the remaining edges. BorgWarner equips its electro-hydraulic AWD coupling with a brushless actuator whose control electronics are built in. A public C009A case from a carmaker was not found. Expect an AWD warning and a released rear clutch.
c: Damaged or chafed signal wire of channel B
Loose or spread terminal for channel B in the actuator connector
Hall element B in the actuator motor defective
s: AWD warning with the vehicle driving on the front axle only
Fault may come and go with temperature or vibration

C009B.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator A Position Sensor C
C009B.d: C009B covers the third position channel, C, of actuator A in the rear differential unit. With A and B intact the module can still see motion, so a fault on C is caught by comparing edges: a Woodward patent identifies the failed sensor as the one whose output stays constant between two invalid state combinations, roughly one electrical revolution apart, and then keeps the motor running on two sensors with a synthesised third signal at reduced torque. Whether an AWD module uses such a fallback is not published; most simply release the clutch. Schaeffler's clutch actuator patent places the Hall carrier on the stator so it can be swapped separately, though in many rear units the sensors sit inside the motor housing. No carmaker documents C009B publicly. Unlike C009C, this code blames one channel, not their combination.
c: Open circuit or short on the channel C signal line
Hall element C inside the actuator motor failed
Moisture in the actuator connector at the rear axle
s: AWD/4WD fault message
All-wheel drive switched off for the rest of the trip

C009C.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator A Position Sensor Correlation
C009C.d: Each of the three position channels of actuator A may look electrically fine, yet together they make no sense: a combination that cannot occur, a sequence that skips states or runs against the commanded direction. With 120-degree spacing the patterns 000 and 111 are invalid, as a Woodward patent notes. Ford is the only maker with a public case: SSM 50188 reports C009C in the AWD module of 2021 Bronco Sport vehicles alongside cluster messages: Service AdvanceTrac, unavailable Hill Start Assist or Pre-Collision Assist, a 4WD Malfunction notice and Reduced Power. Ford blames connector C413 being only partly engaged or having loose terminals, which should be ruled out before a new rear drive unit is fitted; otherwise the workshop manual section 307-07A applies. Hyundai Kefico separates open from shorted lines via all-low or all-high readings.
c: Rear drive unit connector not fully seated or loose pins (Ford C413)
Poor shared sensor ground or supply corrupting all three channels
Internal sensor or magnet fault in the rear drive unit motor
s: 4WD Malfunction message and AWD switched off
Service AdvanceTrac, hill start assist or pre-collision assist unavailable (Ford)
Reduced Power message

C009D.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator B Position Sensor A
C009D.d: Actuator B exists only on rear units with a second controlled element, for instance twin-clutch modules that apply torque to each rear wheel on its own, or a rear axle with an extra disconnect. GKN describes a separate actuator controller managing such twin-clutch actuation, adapting to clutch temperature and wear. C009D flags the first of the three position channels of this second actuator: its signal is absent, stuck or outside the permitted range. The sensing principle is the same as for actuator A, a set of Hall elements reading a rotor magnet, as Schaeffler's actuator patent and TI's commutation note show. No carmaker has published a C009D case. Because only one side or one function is affected, the module often shuts down left-right torque control first, then AWD altogether.
c: Wiring fault on channel A of actuator B
Poor contact in the actuator B connector
Hall element A in actuator B failed
s: AWD warning, torque vectoring or locking function unavailable
Vehicle may push wide in corners where it normally rotates

C009E.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator B Position Sensor B
C009E.d: Middle channel B of the second rear-unit actuator is reported here. It belongs to designs with two independently controlled elements; GKN's Twinster, used on the Focus RS rear drive module, can send torque to either rear wheel separately through two wet clutches. A fault in channel B of actuator B is typically an interrupted, grounded or frozen signal while channels A and C still switch. The detection logic in a Hyundai Kefico patent fits this case: it takes a healthy channel as reference, and a partner that never changes while the reference toggles is stored as defective. That patent also lets the motor run on in an emergency mode from the remaining edges. No public manufacturer document names C009E. The usual result is that the controller stops using the affected side and shows an AWD warning.
c: Channel B signal of actuator B interrupted or grounded
Harness chafed near the rear axle or exhaust heat shield
Internal sensor failure in actuator B
s: AWD fault message, one rear wheel no longer driven actively
Drift or sport drive modes unavailable

C009F.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator B Position Sensor C
C009F.d: Third position channel C of actuator B in the rear differential unit is the subject of this code. Its absence is noticed because the remaining channels A and B still produce transitions that C should follow. Woodward's patent shows the method: after an invalid combination the controller waits for the next one, and the sensor whose output did not move in between is the failed one; the motor can then be driven with a substitute third signal. In a rear unit such as BorgWarner's electro-hydraulic coupling, whose brushless actuator motor carries its own electronics, this monitoring sits next to the motor, so the fault may be reported over the bus by an integrated controller. No manufacturer bulletin mentions C009F. Repairs usually mean wiring checks first, then a new actuator motor.
c: Open or high-resistance channel C line of actuator B
Hall element C of actuator B defective
Fault in electronics integrated in the actuator motor
s: AWD warning lamp
Rear torque split or locking function deactivated

C00A0.t: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator B Position Sensor Correlation
C00A0.d: C00A0 is the plausibility check across all three position channels of actuator B. Each line may be intact, but the pattern they form is impossible, out of sequence or contradicts the commanded movement, so the controller can no longer trust where the second actuator stands. Woodward lists 000 and 111 as illegal states for 120-degree spacing and 101 or 010 for 60-degree spacing. A Hyundai Kefico patent uses all-zero and all-one readings to tell an open line from a short. Common roots are a shared ground or supply problem, a connector that is not latched, or a magnet that has shifted. Ford reports the sister code C009C for actuator A on the Bronco Sport, but no manufacturer publishes a C00A0 case. GKN notes that its actuator controllers include self-diagnostics.
c: Shared sensor ground or supply of actuator B faulty
Actuator B connector not fully latched
Rotor magnet or sensor carrier shifted inside actuator B
s: AWD fault message with rear torque control switched off
Possible loss of related assist functions shown in the cluster

C00A1.d: This umbrella code concerns the driveline control module itself, often called AWD or 4WD module, not one of its outputs or sensors. It covers internal faults such as memory or processor errors, a missing or poor supply and ground, or software and configuration problems that stop the module from controlling clutches, transfer case or disconnects. GKN describes such controllers as layered software, from operating system through actuator drivers up to vehicle functions; BorgWarner builds the electronics straight into the brushless actuator of its coupling. Ford gives a code-specific example: SSM 51659 covers 2023 F-Super Duty trucks built up to 9 May 2023 that store C00A1 in their AWD module or lose four-wheel drive, and asks to check that ground G239, under the right-hand front sill trim close to the BCM, is tightened to 8 Nm.
c: Loose or corroded module ground (Ford G239 on 2023 Super Duty)
Low battery voltage or poor supply to the module
Module software or configuration fault, update or reprogramming needed
Internal failure of the driveline control module
s: Four-wheel drive inoperative
4WD/AWD warning or service message
Further driveline codes or lost communication with the module

C00A2.t: Driveline Control Module Power Transfer Unit Control Circuit Driver
C00A2.d: The power transfer unit sits at the front transaxle of a front-based AWD car and, on disconnecting systems, can uncouple the propshaft.
