P0230.d: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0230 concerns the primary side. GM's output driver compares the commanded with the actual state of the relay control circuit and sets the code at 8 of 10 mismatches, after two trips; Ford checks for open or short circuits for 2–5 s. With a failed relay control the pump stays off and the engine will not start or dies; a short to voltage keeps the pump running and drains the battery. On Ford systems with a pump control module the code means its power relay circuit; on the Subaru-based Saab 9-2X it is the pump module's collective fault report.
c: Fuel pump relay faulty (coil open or shorted)
Control wire from module to relay open or shorted to ground or voltage
Relay supply, ground or fuse missing
With a pump control module: its supply, ground or the module itself
s: Engine cranks but does not start
Engine stalls while driving
Check engine light on
No pump prime noise at ignition on; with a short to voltage the pump runs on and drains the battery

P0231.d: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0231 means the secondary side reads low, and the meaning differs by system. Ford's relay systems read the voltage in the pump power circuit through a monitor wire: if it is missing with the pump commanded on – relay contact not closing, fuse missing, wire open or shorted to ground – the code sets after 2–5 s. GM pumps with their own power module report a short to ground as overcurrent at 18 A or more, setting the warning light in the first trip and switching the output off. The pump gets no voltage, so the engine will not start or stalls.
c: Power wire from relay or module to pump shorted to ground (chafing at tank or underbody)
Relay contact not closing, fuse or battery feed to the relay missing
Pump motor jammed or shorted (high current)
Connector at the tank flange corroded or burnt
s: Engine cranks but does not start
Engine stalls while driving
Check engine light on
Blown fuel pump fuse

P0232.d: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0232 means there is voltage in the pump power circuit although the pump should be off – a welded relay contact or a power wire shorted to another supply. GM pump modules check this after switch-off or in the off phase of the PWM cycle; above about 4 V the code sets once per trip, with the warning light after two trips. Ford's relay systems see it through the pump monitor wire. Driving is usually unaffected, but the pump may keep running with the ignition off and drain the battery – and an emergency shutdown would not work.
c: Pump power wire shorted to another supply
Pump control module output stage shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector causing leakage current
s: Fuel pump keeps running after switch-off
Battery drained overnight
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Often nothing noticeable while driving

P0233.d: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0233 reports brief, recurring dropouts in the pump power circuit that count neither as steadily low nor high. The secondary circuit is the power side of the same pump, not a second pump. No manufacturer using this code was found – GM counts intermittent faults within P0231/P0232/P023F, Ford's relay systems only use P0230–P0232; the description follows CARB's output monitoring requirement and Ford's description of the power circuit. Symptoms are occasional stumbling, stalling or starting problems.
c: Loose contact at pump connector, tank flange or relay socket
Harness chafing at underbody or tank with intermittent contact
Pump motor with commutator or brush dropouts
s: Occasional stumbling or jerking
Engine stalls now and then
Occasional starting problems
Check engine light on

P0234.d: P0234 is a function code, not a sensor fault: the engine module compares target and actual boost, and actual boost stays above target although the control is already lowering it (wastegate opened, variable vanes opened). GM petrol engines set it at 20–35 kPa over target with the warning light in the first trip; GM diesels with variable vanes at 7–10 kPa, after two trips; Ford EcoBoost at about 28 kPa (4 psi) over 5 s while the wastegate is already commanded fully open. Ford diesels instead use P0234 for exhaust back pressure above 4.0–4.5 bar. The engine limits boost or enters limp mode. Typical causes are a wastegate stuck closed, sooted variable vanes or a faulty control valve; Audi traced cases on the Q7 TDI to cracked exhaust parts jamming the turbo vanes. Check the boost sensor against barometric pressure first.
c: Wastegate stuck closed, actuator or linkage sticking, control hose off or blocked
Variable turbine vanes sooted or stuck closed (diesel)
Boost control valve or electric actuator faulty
Boost or manifold sensor reading too high (drift)
s: Check engine light on
Limp mode with clear loss of power
Boost overshoots on acceleration, then power drops
Knocking under full load (petrol) or smoke (diesel)

P0235.d: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure. P0235 is the general fault of sensor A's circuit or signal, for modules that do not split low, high and range. GM, Ford and Saab do not use it; Audi documents it on the Q7 TDI together with over- and underboost, so there it also marks an implausible boost value, for example from a charge air leak or jammed turbo vanes. No manufacturer threshold for this code was found. With a sensor fault boost control is switched off and only the base boost of the wastegate spring remains, with a clear loss of power.
c: Connector at the boost sensor corroded or loose, broken wire
Boost sensor faulty, often oily from crankcase ventilation
Charge air leak or jammed turbo vanes causing an implausible value
5 V reference shorted by another sensor
s: Check engine light on
Clear loss of power, only base boost
Boost reading implausible in a scan tool

P0236.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0236.d: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure. P0236 is the plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but wrong. After a stop of at least 10 s boost, manifold and barometric pressure must match (Ford within about 7–9 kPa); while running, GM compares the sensor with models from airflow, manifold pressure and throttle and flags deviations such as more than 30 kPa from manifold pressure – with the warning light in the first trip. A charge air leak often triggers it too, because the model comparison drifts apart. VW traced a Tiguan case to contact resistance in a harness connector. With a sensor fault boost control is switched off and only the base boost of the wastegate spring remains, with a clear loss of power.
c: Charge air leak (hose, clamp, cooler) between turbo and throttle
Boost sensor dirty, oily or drifting
Contact resistance in connector or harness
Manifold or barometric sensor faulty (correlation partner)
Ice or condensate in the charge air cooler in cold weather
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power, only base boost
Hissing or whistling with a leak

P0237.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Low
P0237.d: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure. P0237 means the signal voltage is below its lower limit: GM below 14.4 % of 5 V (about 50 kPa) for roughly 4 s with the warning light in the first trip, Ford below 0.19 V for 5 s, Saab's V6 below 0.30 V for 1 s. Causes are a signal wire shorted to ground, an open 5 V reference or a failed sensor. Saab's 1.6 turbo only lights a service lamp for this code. With a sensor fault boost control is switched off and only the base boost of the wastegate spring remains, with a clear loss of power.
c: Signal or 5 V reference wire open or shorted to ground
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor
s: Check engine light on
Clear loss of power, only base boost
Boost reading implausible in a scan tool

P0238.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit High
P0238.d: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure. P0238 means the signal voltage is above its upper limit: GM above 86 % of 5 V (about 372 kPa) for roughly 4 s with the warning light in the first trip, Ford above 4.88 V for 5 s, Saab's 1.6 turbo above 4.8 V. Causes are a signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V, an open sensor ground or – on GM modules with a pull-up input – an open signal wire. If several high codes appear at once, check the shared ground. With a sensor fault boost control is switched off and only the base boost of the wastegate spring remains, with a clear loss of power.
c: Sensor ground open, or signal wire open on a pulled-up input
Signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V
Connector corrosion or moisture at the ground
s: Check engine light on
Clear loss of power, only base boost
Boost reading implausible in a scan tool

P0239.d: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P0239 is the general circuit fault of sensor B, the counterpart of P0235, without telling low, high or range apart. As with sensor A, boost control would be switched off, with loss of power.
c: Connector or wire to sensor B open or corroded
Shared 5 V reference or ground disturbed
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power, limp mode
Uneven boost build-up on twin turbos

P023A.t: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P023A.d: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023A means GM's driver diagnosis has found an open circuit (more than 200 kΩ between output and ground with the low-side driver off). Bundled conditions: main relay at least 11 V, ignition above 5 V; 50 of 63 samples set the code with the warning light in the first trip on 2018–2019 engines, older modules need two trips. Without the pump the charge air gets hot and boost is limited.
c: Wire or connector at the pump open (front area, corrosion)
Fuse, pump relay or supply missing
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power under load or in heat (boost limited)
Follow-up code P026A possible

P023B.t: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Low
P023B.d: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023B means GM's driver diagnosis has found a short to ground (0.5 Ω or less between output and ground with the driver off). Bundled conditions: main relay at least 11 V, ignition above 5 V; 50 of 63 samples set the code with the warning light in the first trip on 2018–2019 engines, older modules need two trips. Without the pump the charge air gets hot and boost is limited.
c: Control wire to the pump shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power under load or in heat (boost limited)
Follow-up code P026A possible

P023C.t: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit High
P023C.d: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023C means GM's driver diagnosis has found a short to voltage (0.5 Ω or less between output and battery voltage with the driver on). Bundled conditions: main relay at least 11 V, ignition above 5 V; 50 of 63 samples set the code with the warning light in the first trip on 2018–2019 engines, older modules need two trips. Without the pump the charge air gets hot and boost is limited.
c: Control wire to the pump shorted to voltage
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power under load or in heat (boost limited)
Follow-up code P026A possible

P023D.t: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Correlation
P023D.d: P023D compares the manifold pressure sensor (after the throttle) with boost sensor A (before the throttle): with the engine stopped both must read the same ambient pressure. Saab's 2.8 V6 checks this once per trip with the ignition on before starting and sets the code at a difference of more than 12 kPa, with the warning light and limp mode limited to 170 Nm. The code does not say which sensor is wrong – barometric pressure as a third value decides. Electrical faults of either sensor (P0107/P0108, P0237/P0238) block the test and must be fixed first. GM and Ford run the same comparison but report it as P0236, P0106 or P2227.
c: Manifold or boost sensor drifting or dirty
Contact resistance at connector or ground of one sensor
Pressure port or hose of one sensor blocked (oil sludge, ice)
s: Check engine light on
Limp mode, limited power
Otherwise often unremarkable

P023E.t: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Correlation
P023E.d: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P023E is the counterpart of P023D: manifold pressure is compared with boost sensor B, and with the engine stopped both must read ambient pressure. Saab sets the sensor A version at a difference of more than 12 kPa; a deviation beyond the manufacturer's limit sets this code.
c: Boost sensor B or manifold sensor drifting
Contact resistance at sensor B's connector or wire
s: Check engine light on
Possibly limited power
Otherwise unremarkable

P023F.d: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P023F means the power circuit to the pump is open. GM pumps with their own power module, whose speed is controlled by rail pressure, measure the pump current: if it stays below 1 A (older modules 0.5 A) although the pump is commanded, the code sets with the warning light in the first trip, and fuel pressure diagnostics are suspended. The cause lies in the wire from module to pump or its return, the pump connector or the pump motor itself. The pump stops, so the engine will not start or dies – there is no limp mode.
c: Pump connector at tank flange or pump module open or corroded
Wire from module to pump or return wire open
s: Engine does not start, no pump noise
Engine stalls while driving
Check engine light on

P0240.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0240.d: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P0240 is the plausibility fault of sensor B with an electrically valid signal – as with sensor A, compared with barometric and manifold pressure after a stop and with a model while running. A charge air leak on the side or stage of turbo B is a likely cause.
c: Charge air leak on the side or stage of turbo B
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power
Uneven boost between the turbos

P0241.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit Low
P0241.d: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P0241 means the signal of sensor B is below its lower limit – for sensor A, GM uses 14.4 % of 5 V and Ford 0.19 V for 5 s. Causes are a short to ground, an open 5 V reference or a failed sensor.
c: Signal or 5 V reference wire open or shorted to ground
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power, limp mode
Boost B reads very low in a scan tool

P0242.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit High
P0242.d: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P0242 means the signal of sensor B is above its upper limit – for sensor A, GM uses 86 % of 5 V and Ford 4.88 V for 5 s. Causes are a short to voltage, an open ground or, on a pulled-up input, an open signal wire.
c: Sensor ground open, or signal wire open on a pulled-up input
Signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power, limp mode
Boost B shows its maximum value

P0243.d: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0243 is the general circuit fault of actuator A. GM uses it for an open circuit: with the driver off, more than 200 kΩ between output and ground in 10 of 20 samples sets it with the warning light in the first trip (older modules: two trips). Ford uses P0243 on its electric wastegates as the collective code for open and short circuits (0.4 s), together with P2ABD for driver overcurrent or overheating. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.
c: Connector at the wastegate valve or actuator loose, corroded or with spread contacts
Valve coil or electric actuator winding open
Supply voltage to the valve missing (ignition, relay, fuse)
Broken control wire between module and valve
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Clearly less power, boost only at base level
Sluggish acceleration, turbo lag
Reduced engine power message possible

P0244.d: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0244 means the actuator does not respond as commanded although its circuit is electrically sound, and manufacturers implement it differently. Subaru engines (Saab 9-2X) set it when manifold pressure exceeds an altitude-dependent limit – about 220 kPa absolute at sea level – for over 2 s, with the warning light at once. Stellantis documented it with a wastegate rod that had come off for want of a retaining clip. Older GM modules (Saab LDK, LLU) however use P0244 for an open solenoid circuit; newer GM and Ford systems do not use it and monitor function under P0234/P0299 or P25B3/P25B4.
c: Wastegate rod unhooked, retaining clip missing or linkage worn
Control hose to the wastegate can leaking, off or swapped; diaphragm torn
Position sensor of the electric actuator not learned correctly
s: Check engine light on
Lack of power or surging, too high boost
Limp mode with reduced power
Rattle or whistle at the turbo possible

P0245.d: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0245 means the control circuit of actuator A reads low – typically the ground-switched control wire shorted to ground, so the valve would be permanently energised. GM checks with the driver off for less than 0.5 Ω to ground, 10 of 20 samples, warning light in the first trip; Ford's driver chip reports it after 2–5 s, and on pneumatic wastegates Ford also includes the open circuit here. A shorted supply shared with the bypass valve can set it together with P0033/P0034. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.
c: Control wire to the wastegate valve chafed through to ground
Shared supply shorted (e.g. by the bypass valve)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Clearly less power, boost only at base level
Sluggish acceleration, turbo lag
Reduced engine power message possible

P0246.d: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0246 means the control circuit of actuator A reads high – the control wire is shorted to voltage, so the driver cannot switch the valve to ground. GM checks with the driver on for less than 0.5 Ω to battery voltage, 10 of 20 samples, warning light in the first trip; Ford's driver chip reports it after 2–5 s, and Ford's functional check of the wastegate control pressure (P1015/P1016) only runs when P0245/P0246 are clear. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.
c: Control wire touching voltage (damaged harness, neighbouring wire)
Solenoid shorted internally (very low resistance, driver overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Clearly less power, boost only at base level
Sluggish acceleration, turbo lag
Reduced engine power message possible

P0247.d: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two. P0247 is the general circuit fault of actuator B, the counterpart of P0243. On GM's 3.0 litre twin-turbo V6 (LGW) it means an open circuit of more than 200 kΩ with the driver off, 10 of 20 samples, warning light in the first trip. Ford uses it on twin-turbo V6 engines with electric wastegates as the collective code for open and short circuits (0.4 s), together with P2ABE. Boost control on that side is switched off, costing power.
c: Connector at wastegate valve or actuator B loose or corroded
Coil or motor winding of actuator B open
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Clearly less power, boost only at base level
Uneven boost between the turbos
Reduced engine power message possible

P0248.d: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two. P0248 is the counterpart of P0244: actuator B does not reach the commanded position, or boost does not respond as expected, although the circuit is electrically sound. Stellantis documents it on the 2025 Ram 1500 with the 3.0 litre Hurricane twin-turbo, often with P2B94 (position sensor B learning limit): incorrectly fitted retaining clips on the wastegate rod caused missing turbo boost. Thresholds are not published; GM and Ford do not use the code, Ford monitors actuator B position under P25B5/P25B6.
c: Retaining clip of the wastegate rod missing or fitted wrongly, rod unhooked
Wastegate flap B coked or sticking
Position sensor learned value outside limits (e.g. not relearned after turbo replacement)
Pneumatic wastegate: control hose or can B leaking
s: Check engine light on
Missing turbo boost, lack of power
Uneven boost between the turbos
Limp mode possible

P0249.d: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two. P0249 means the control circuit of actuator B reads low, typically the control wire shorted to ground. On GM's LGW twin-turbo less than 0.5 Ω to ground with the driver off in 10 of 20 samples sets it with the warning light in the first trip; older GM modules need two trips. Ford reports it on pneumatic wastegates after 2–3 s. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.
c: Control wire of wastegate B chafed through to ground
Valve or actuator winding B shorted
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Clearly less power, boost only at base level
Uneven boost between the turbos
Reduced engine power message possible

P024A.t: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Range/Performance
P024A.d: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P024A is the functional fault: the bypass does not follow its command, judged from the position sensor or from the expected temperature effect – Bosch describes comparing the cooler's efficiency with the valve closed and open, using modelled air temperature before and measured temperature after the cooler. FCA documents P024A, together with P026E, on the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia and 2018 Stelvio with the 2.0 turbo and fixed it with an engine software update, so check the software level first.
c: Bypass flap sticking, coked or oily (oil from crankcase ventilation or turbo)
Actuator weak or vacuum line leaking
Position sensor inaccurate or connector corroded
s: Check engine light on
Longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature
Possibly less power from boost limitation

P024B.t: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Stuck
P024B.d: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P024B means the bypass flap does not move at all despite being commanded – the position signal stands still or the air temperature shows no reaction. Bosch's patent describes exactly the case of a valve stuck closed or a blocked bypass, which raises emissions during warm-up. Stuck open, the charge air gets hotter and power drops; stuck closed, warm-up takes longer. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.
s: Check engine light on
Stuck open: higher charge air temperature, loss of power
Stuck closed: longer warm-up

P024C.t: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit
P024C.d: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. Its position sensor is usually built into the actuator, with a 5 V reference and a ratiometric signal. P024C is the general circuit fault of the position sensor, for manufacturers that do not split low and high. Bypass control is then switched off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.
c: Connector or wiring to the actuator's sensor part
5 V reference disturbed by another sensor
s: Check engine light on
Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power
Often nothing noticeable while driving

P024D.t: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P024D.d: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. Its position sensor is usually built into the actuator, with a 5 V reference and a ratiometric signal. P024D is the plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but does not match the commanded position or the end stops. Bypass control is then switched off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.
c: Flap or linkage misadjusted or sticking
End stops not learned after replacement
s: Check engine light on
Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power
Often nothing noticeable while driving

P024E.t: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P024E.d: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. Its position sensor is usually built into the actuator, with a 5 V reference and a ratiometric signal. P024E means the signal is below its lower limit – a signal wire shorted to ground or an open signal or 5 V reference wire. Bypass control is then switched off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.
c: Signal wire shorted to ground or open
s: Check engine light on
Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power
Often nothing noticeable while driving

P024F.t: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit High
P024F.d: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. Its position sensor is usually built into the actuator, with a 5 V reference and a ratiometric signal. P024F means the signal is above its upper limit – typically an open sensor ground or a signal shorted to voltage. Bypass control is then switched off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.
c: Signal shorted to 5 V or system voltage
s: Check engine light on
Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power
Often nothing noticeable while driving

P0250.d: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two. P0250 means the control circuit of actuator B reads high: the control wire is shorted to voltage, checked with the driver on. GM's LGW twin-turbo sets it at less than 0.5 Ω to battery voltage in 10 of 20 samples with the warning light in the first trip; older GM modules need two trips. Ford reports it on pneumatic wastegates after 2–3 s. Valve B can no longer be controlled, so that side runs on base boost.
c: Control wire of wastegate B shorted to voltage
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Clearly less power, boost only at base level
Uneven boost between the turbos
Reduced engine power message possible

P0251.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0251.d: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump. On older distributor pumps it was a solenoid that set the injected quantity; on common rail it is usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that lets only as much fuel into the pumping elements as the rail needs, instead of spilling the excess through a pressure valve. Manufacturers use different codes for this part: Ford P0001–P0004, GM Duramax P0090–P0092. P0251 is the general circuit fault of actuator A. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel uses it for an open circuit of the pressure regulator on the high-pressure pump: if the control wire does not show the expected voltage with the driver off for more than 1 s, the code sets with the warning light at once. Depending on the system, rail pressure and power are then limited.
c: Connector at the actuator corroded or loose, broken wire
Supply voltage to the actuator missing
Distributor pump: internal electronics or quantity valve faulty
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power, limp mode
Rough idle or hunting
Hard starting or stalling

P0252.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0252.d: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump. On older distributor pumps it was a solenoid that set the injected quantity; on common rail it is usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that lets only as much fuel into the pumping elements as the rail needs, instead of spilling the excess through a pressure valve. Manufacturers use different codes for this part: Ford P0001–P0004, GM Duramax P0090–P0092. P0252 is the range or performance fault of actuator A, and the meaning depends on the maker. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel sets it when the driver stage of the pump pressure regulator overheats – a sign of a shorted turn or excessive current – with the warning light at once; Ford checks the same under P0002 at a driver temperature above 170 °C. Generally the code can also mean the actuator does not achieve the expected effect.
c: Metering actuator with shorted turns, too low resistance (driver overheats)
Actuator mechanically sticking or dirty (fuel quality, wear debris)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power, limp mode
Fluctuating rail pressure, hunting idle

P0253.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0253.d: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0253 means the actuator A circuit reads low. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel uses it for a control wire shorted to ground for more than 1 s, with the warning light at once. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel, whose pump has two metering valves, also includes an open circuit (over 2.1 s) and goes into limp mode: limited pedal response and injection quantity, rail pressure capped at 60 MPa, warning light if the fault recurs on the next trip. Ford's equivalent is P0003, GM's P0091.
c: Control wire to the metering actuator chafed to ground
Connector or wire open (where makers include it under low)
s: Check engine light on
Limp mode with limited power and speed
Hard starting possible

P0254.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0254.d: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0254 means the actuator A circuit reads high or draws too much current – typically the control wire shorted to voltage. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel sets it after 1 s with the warning light at once. On Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel a short to voltage of more than 0.31 s stops the engine, because a permanently energised valve can no longer control quantity and pressure. Ford's equivalent P0004 sets above 3.7 A; GM uses P0092.
c: Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Engine stalls or will not start (Saab 3.0 diesel)
Limp mode, loss of power

P0255.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0255.d: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0255 reports brief open or short circuits in the actuator A circuit that come and go – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration. No manufacturer using it with exactly this meaning was found; a Ram 6.7 Cummins code list names it as a circuit performance fault instead. The description follows CARB's continuous circuit monitoring requirement and the documented A siblings.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the metering actuator connector
Actuator coil with a temperature-dependent fault
s: Check engine light (often goes out again)
Brief jerking or power dips
Occasional limp mode

P0256.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0256.d: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. Actuator B is a second metering actuator, for example on pumps with two metering valves such as on Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel. P0256 is its general circuit fault, the counterpart of P0251. No manufacturer using P0256 was found – Saab reports its two valves under other codes; the description follows CARB's circuit monitoring requirement and the A siblings.
c: Connector or wire to valve B open
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power, limp mode

P0257.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0257.d: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0257 is the functional fault of actuator B: the metering does not achieve its target. It is documented on Mack and Volvo heavy-duty common-rail diesels of 2018–2020 together with rail pressure codes (P0087, P016F, P228F) and P2A17/P2A1F; the cause can lie outside the actuator, for example an electronic pressure relief valve stuck open, a leak or poor low-pressure supply, so those faults are fixed first. Engine power may be derated.
c: Rail pressure or metering target not reached (leak, relief valve open)
Poor low-pressure supply (filter, lift pump, air)
Metering actuator or pumping element worn
s: Check engine light on
Power derate
Hard starting, low rail pressure when cranking
Jerking under load

P0258.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0258.d: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0258 means the actuator B circuit reads low. The only manufacturer found, Saab with its 3.0 V6 diesel of the early 2000s, uses it not for a second valve but for the shared supply of both metering valves: a short to ground or open for more than about 1 s triggers limp mode with limited pedal response and injection quantity, rail pressure capped at 60 MPa and idle raised to 1,000 rpm; the warning light comes on if it recurs on the next trip.
c: Supply wire, fuse or relay of the metering valves open or shorted to ground
Connector at the pump corroded or loose
Metering valve shorted to ground internally
s: Check engine light on (after the second trip)
Loss of power, limp mode
Raised idle speed in limp mode

P0259.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0259.d: Fuel metering actuator B is a second electrically controlled metering valve on a diesel injection pump; A has the codes P0251–P0255. P0259 means its circuit reads high or draws too much current – a short to voltage or a shorted turn. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel, whose pump has two metering valves, uses it for an internal short in one of the valves lasting over 2.1 s: limp mode with limited pedal response, injection quantity and rail pressure (60 MPa), and the warning light if it recurs on the next trip. GM and Ford use other codes for this part (P0090–P0092, P0001–P0004).
c: Control wire to the valve shorted to voltage, chafing
Connector at the valve corroded or wet
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Limp mode with limited power and speed
Hard starting, engine may stall

P025A.t: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit/Open
P025A.d: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025A means the control line from the engine module to pump module A is open or faulty. On Ford systems the pump module itself detects the bad command signal and reports it on the monitor line (11–16 V, 2–5 s); Ford uses P025A for the shared line to modules A and B. GM's pump module compares the enable line with the request on the data bus and sets P025A after about 1 s, with the warning light in the first trip; on some Ford vehicles the code does not light it.
c: Control line to the pump module open or shorted, often along the frame
Connector at the pump module corroded or wet (module often mounted on the frame)
s: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent)
Hard or no start
Rough idle, surging
Lack of power from wrong fuel pressure

P025B.t: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P025B.d: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025B means pump module A receives a signal, but an invalid command – the duty cycle is outside the valid window or implausible. Ford's module signals this with a 20 % (±4 %) duty cycle on its monitor line; the check runs continuously at 11–16 V over 2–5 s. Whether the warning light comes on depends on the vehicle. Typical causes are contact resistance in the control line or connector that distorts the duty cycle, a poor ground or a faulty module.
c: Contact resistance or corrosion in the control line or connector distorting the duty cycle
Interference or poor ground between engine module and pump module
s: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent)
Hard or no start
Rough idle, surging
Lack of power from wrong fuel pressure

P025C.t: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Low
P025C.d: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025C means the control circuit to pump module A reads low, typically a short to ground. On Ford's 3.0 diesel the pump module detects it; on the 6.7 it means a short on the low side of the pump relay – both within 0.5 s. FCA documents it with the warning light on and sometimes a start followed by stalling, often together with P01C6 and P016F; the checks cover the pump module connector, the low-pressure sensor and a ground point for water, corrosion and pushed-back pins.
c: Control line chafed to ground at the frame
Water or corrosion at the pump module connector
s: Check engine light on
Engine starts and dies again
Starting problems
Loss of power from low supply pressure

P025D.t: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit High
P025D.d: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025D means the control circuit to pump module A reads high, typically a short to voltage. On Ford's 3.0 diesel the pump module detects it; on the 6.7 it means a short to voltage on the low side of the pump relay – both continuously monitored and set within 0.5 s. Depending on the design the pump then runs all the time or not at all.
c: Control line shorted to battery voltage or another wire
Moisture in the connector (leakage to voltage)
s: Check engine light on
Pump runs all the time or not at all
Starting problems

P025E.d: Boost sensor A measures the pressure between charge air cooler and throttle (Ford TIP, GM TIAP). P025E counts brief excursions outside its valid voltage range that are each too short for the low or high code P0237/P0238 – Ford's limits are below 0.19 V and above 4.88 V. Ford counts these events continuously and sets P025E after 10 in one drive cycle. Boost control then runs on a substitute value or is switched off, leaving only base boost. Typical causes are a loose or corroded connector or a wire breaking under vibration and heat.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector
Wire or 5 V reference breaking from vibration or heat
Shared 5 V reference disturbed by another sensor
s: Check engine light on
Occasional loss of power, boost limited
Jerking on acceleration

P025F.d: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on twin-turbo engines or a second stage. P025F counts brief excursions of its signal outside the valid range that are too short for the low or high code – the counterpart of P025E, which Ford sets after 10 such events in one drive cycle. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found; the description follows CARB's input monitoring requirement and Ford's sensor A check.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector
Wire breaking from vibration or heat
s: Check engine light on
Occasional loss of power
Boost limited

P0260.t: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0260.d: P0260 reports brief dropouts or jumps in the circuit of fuel metering actuator B on a diesel injection pump that do not last long enough for the low or high code (P0258/P0259) – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration. No manufacturer using P0260 was found; the description follows CARB's continuous circuit monitoring requirement and Saab's diagnosis of the same two-valve pump, which recommends a wiggle test with the valves activated.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the metering valve B connector
Broken or chafed wire in the harness to the pump (vibration, heat)
Metering valve B with internal dropouts
s: Check engine light on
Occasional jerking or brief loss of power
Limp mode possible

P0261.d: P0261 means the control wire of the cylinder 1 injector – the side the engine module switches to ground – is shorted to ground. GM detects this with the driver off: on direct injection at 1 V or less, on port injection and Duramax diesels at 0.5 Ω or less to ground. Ford's 6.7 diesel has its driver chip report the short within 0.3 s. Most systems switch the warning light on in the first trip (some GM port-injection engines and Saab's 2.0 turbo after two) and shut the affected injector off, so the cylinder misfires. Ford petrol engines report all injector circuit faults as P0201 ff instead.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 1 injector chafed to ground in the harness
Injector connector damp or corroded, leakage to ground
Injector shorted to its housing internally
Open control wire (on some GM port-injection drivers this also reads low; P020x sets too)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301
Loss of power, rough idle
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0262.d: P0262 means the control wire of the cylinder 1 injector is shorted to voltage. GM detects this with the driver on: on direct injection by 25 A or more through the driver, on port injection and Duramax diesels by 0.5 Ω or less to the supply. On Ford's 6.7 diesel it means the injector's high side is shorted to its low side, reported within 0.3 s. Most systems switch the warning light on in the first trip (some GM port-injection engines and Saab's 2.0 turbo after two) and shut the affected injector off, so the cylinder misfires. Ford petrol engines report all injector circuit faults as P0201 ff instead.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 1 injector touching battery voltage or another supply wire
Injector coil shorted internally (too low resistance, overcurrent)
Short between supply and control wire in harness or connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301
Loss of power, rough idle
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0263.d: P0263 comes from the cylinder balance control of common-rail diesels: the engine module measures the crankshaft acceleration of each cylinder's power stroke, compares it with the average and gives a deviating cylinder more or less fuel. The code sets when the correction for cylinder 1 reaches its limit and the cylinder still does not keep up – GM at 95 % of a limit of about ±12–17 mm³ for 30 s, Ford above 90 % of the allowed 3.5–15 mg per stroke for 7.5 s; GM needs two trips. The code does not say whether there is too much or too little fuel – the correction value for cylinder 1 shows the direction: strongly negative means a leaking injector, strongly positive a weak injector or low compression. VW and Ram traced some cases to over-sensitive software, so check for updates before replacing injectors.
c: Injector of cylinder 1 worn, coked or leaking
Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive
Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Low compression on cylinder 1 (valve, rings, injector seal)
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, shaking or knocking
Loss of power or smoke
Higher consumption, poor cold start

P026A.t: Charge Air Cooler Efficiency Below Threshold
P026A.d: P026A means the charge air cooler is not cooling enough. The module compares the temperature drop across the cooler with the maximum possible (inlet minus ambient) or with a model: GM's 6.6 litre LML diesel sets it below 25 % efficiency, later GM diesels below 50 %, both after two trips; Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels when the measured temperature is 18–35 °C (3.0: 35–65 °C) off the model over about 10 s. GM's 3.0 twin-turbo petrol with a coolant-cooled charge air cooler sets it in the first trip when manifold air exceeds 110 °C or boost has been limited for a long time. Hot intake air costs power and raises NOx and soot.
c: Charge air cooler clogged on the outside (insects, leaves, dirt) or fins damaged
Coolant-cooled cooler: pump faulty, air in the low-temperature circuit, low coolant
Charge air or ambient temperature sensor inaccurate
Charge air cooler bypass stuck open
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power under load or in heat
High intake air temperature in live data

P026B.d: P026B is the engine-wide injection timing monitor: CARB requires diesels from 2010 to detect injection that is too early or too late overall, or a timing control at its limit. Unlike P020A ff (per cylinder) it concerns the engine as a whole. It is documented on the Ram 6.7 Cummins, together with the per-cylinder timing and balance codes; FCA describes it as set falsely by software and fixes it with an engine module update, without publishing thresholds. GM and Ford handle timing with per-cylinder codes instead (P01CB ff, P2B11 ff).
c: Injectors coked or worn (changed start of injection)
Rail pressure or fuel supply problems (pump, filter, fuel quality)
s: Check engine light on
Often nothing noticeable (false setting)
Possibly knocking, rough running or more smoke

P026C.t: Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected
P026C.d: From 2010, CARB requires diesel engines to detect when the commanded injection quantity is not delivered. The module estimates the fuel actually burned from airflow and the measured lambda (from the NOx or oxygen sensor) and corrects the quantity; if that correction passes a limit, the code sets. P026C means the engine gets less fuel than commanded. GM's 6.6 litre LML diesel checks it at idle with the vehicle stationary and the engine warm, setting it at a correction of −20 to −35 mm³ per stroke for 12 s; later GM diesels use the learned correction value (10 of 20 samples); both need two trips. FCA lists it with an injector cleaning procedure for deposits. Ford diesels do not use it. Typical causes are coked injectors, wrong airflow or lambda measurement and weak fuel supply.
c: Injectors coked or clogged (too little flow)
Airflow or boost measurement wrong, NOx sensor lambda inaccurate
Weak low- or high-pressure supply (filter, pump, rail pressure)
s: Check engine light on
Lack of power
Rough running or idle

P026D.t: Fuel Injection Quantity A Higher Than Expected
P026D.d: From 2010, CARB requires diesel engines to detect when the commanded injection quantity is not delivered. The module estimates the fuel actually burned from airflow and the measured lambda (from the NOx or oxygen sensor) and corrects the quantity; if that correction passes a limit, the code sets. P026D means the engine gets more fuel than commanded. GM's LML diesel sets it at idle at a correction of +16 to +35 mm³ per stroke for 12 s, two trips. Volvo trucks detect it as too little oxygen at the NOx sensors for the fuel flow and point to boost sensor, EGR valve and sensor, wrong injectors, turbo vanes and intake leaks. On GM's 2.8 litre diesel vans of 2020–2022 it could also be a software anomaly without driving problems. Symptoms are black smoke and more frequent filter regeneration.
c: Injector dripping or worn, or wrong injector type fitted
EGR valve not closing or EGR differential pressure sensor wrong
Boost sensor or turbo vanes faulty, intake leak
NOx or oxygen sensor reading wrong
s: Check engine light on
Black smoke, higher soot load, more frequent filter regeneration
Rough running or idle
Often nothing noticeable while driving

P026E.t: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Performance
P026E.d: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit with an electric pump. P026E means that pump is electrically sound but does not deliver as commanded – judged from feedback by the pump electronics or from the missing temperature drop. FCA documents it on the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia and 2018 Stelvio with the 2.0 turbo, together with P024A, and fixed it with a software update; thresholds are not published. Air in the circuit or low coolant lets the pump run dry; hot charge air then costs power.
c: Air in the low-temperature circuit or low coolant (pump runs dry)
Weak supply or ground, corroded connector
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power in heat or under load
Follow-up code P026A possible
Level in the auxiliary coolant tank drops

P026F.d: P026F is a general functional code for the coolant thermostat. CARB requires that the coolant reaches the temperature needed for other diagnostics in the approved time and comes within 11 °C of the thermostat's regulating temperature; from model years 2019–2021 petrol engines must also detect it dropping back below that temperature, and electric pumps or valves controlling coolant flow are monitored like a thermostat. The module follows coolant temperature against a heat model. No manufacturer using P026F was found – GM and Ford report thermostat faults as P0128, P01F0 or P2181 – so the description rests on CARB and the thermostat's function.
c: Thermostat stuck open or opening too early
Thermostat stuck closed or opening too late
Map-controlled thermostat: heating element or control faulty
Low coolant or air in the system
s: Check engine light on
Slow warm-up, weak heating (stuck open)
Low or fluctuating temperature gauge
Overheating (stuck closed)

P027A.t: Fuel Pump Module B Control Circuit/Open
P027A.d: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. Module B is a second pump module, for example on dual-tank commercial vehicles. P027A is the counterpart of P025A: the control line from the engine module to pump module B is open or faulty. No manufacturer using P027A was found – Ford reports line faults of both modules together under P025A, GM only uses P025A; the description follows CARB's circuit monitoring requirement and Ford's module B check. If the second tank's pump gets no valid command, fuel may run short when running from that tank.

Connector at the pump module corroded or wet (module often mounted on the frame)
s: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent)
Fuel shortage when running from the second tank
Starting problems, surging

P027B.t: Fuel Pump Module B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P027B.d: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. Module B is a second pump module, for example on dual-tank commercial vehicles. P027B means pump module B receives an invalid command or its feedback does not match. Ford's module signals this with a 20 % (±4 %) duty cycle on its monitor line, checked continuously at 11–16 V over 2–5 s; on Ford commercial vehicles the module B monitor line runs via the smart relay module and CAN to the engine module. Whether the warning light comes on depends on the vehicle.
c: Contact resistance or corrosion in the control or monitor line to module B
Relay module or CAN forwarding disturbed (Ford commercial vehicles)
s: Check engine light (vehicle-dependent)
Fuel shortage when running from the second tank
Surging, lack of power

P027E.t: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected
P027E.d: P027E is the cold-start counterpart of P026C: during cold start the engine gets less fuel than commanded, for example because a catalyst-heating injection does not arrive. The check probably works as in warm running, from airflow and lambda against the commanded quantity. The code covers only phases with the cold-start emission strategy active (extra injections to heat the catalyst, raised idle): CARB requires faults of elements also monitored elsewhere to be reported separately during the cold-start strategy. No manufacturer using this code was found; the description follows CARB and the warm-running counterpart.
c: Rail pressure builds too slowly at cold start (filter, wax, pump)
s: Check engine light on
Poor cold start, rough running when cold
Longer warm-up

P027F.t: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity A Higher Than Expected

The check probably works as in warm running, from airflow and lambda against the commanded quantity. The code covers only phases with the cold-start emission strategy active (extra injections to heat the catalyst, raised idle): CARB requires faults of elements also monitored elsewhere to be reported separately during the cold-start strategy. No manufacturer using this code was found; the description follows CARB and the warm-running counterpart.

Lambda/NOx sensor or airflow sensor reading wrong
s: Check engine light on

P028A.t: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Control Circuit/Open
P028A.d: Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler; a Deere patent describes such a fan that the module switches and reverses to blow out dirt. P028A means the fan's control circuit is open or has a general fault, detected by the driver stage. Without the fan the charge air is cooled less at low speed or in heat, which can lead to P026A and boost limitation. No manufacturer document using P028A was found; the description rests on CARB's output component requirement.
c: Wire or connector to the fan open or corroded
Fan relay or fan control module faulty
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Fan does not run
Loss of power in heat or traffic
Follow-up code P026A possible

P028B.t: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Performance/Stuck Off
P028B.d: Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler, switched by the engine module; a Deere patent describes such a fan that is also reversed to blow out dirt. P028B means the module commands the fan on but sees no effect – no speed or current feedback from a fan control module, or the charge air does not cool – although the circuit is electrically sound (circuit faults are P028A, P028D and P028E). The charge air then gets hotter, which can limit boost and power. No manufacturer document using this code was found; the description rests on CARB's output component requirement.
c: Fan relay or fan control module without output
s: Warning light (manufacturer-dependent)
Loss of power in heat or at low speed

P028C.t: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Stuck On
P028C.d: Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler, switched by the engine module; a Deere patent describes such a fan that is also reversed to blow out dirt. P028C means the fan runs although the module has switched it off – speed or current feedback, or the voltage at the output, does not match the off command. Typical causes are a welded relay contact or a shorted driver stage. The fan runs continuously and can drain the battery; the charge air tends to be too cold, which favours condensate. No manufacturer document using this code was found; the description rests on CARB's output component requirement.
c: Driver stage or fan control module shorted

The code does not say whether there is too much or too little fuel – the correction value for cylinder 11 shows the direction: strongly negative means a leaking injector, strongly positive a weak injector or low compression. Cylinder 11 only exists on diesels with twelve cylinders; GM and Ford documents stop at cylinder 8, so the description follows CARB and the siblings.
c: Injector of cylinder 11 worn, coked or leaking
Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive
Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Low compression on cylinder 11 (valve, rings, injector seal)
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, shaking or knocking
Loss of power or smoke
Higher consumption, poor cold start

P0294.d: P0294 means the control wire of the cylinder 12 injector – the side the engine module switches to ground – is shorted to ground. GM detects this with the driver off: on direct injection at 1 V or less, on port injection and Duramax diesels at 0.5 Ω or less to ground. Ford's 6.7 diesel has its driver chip report the short within 0.3 s. Most systems switch the warning light on in the first trip (some GM port-injection engines and Saab's 2.0 turbo after two) and shut the affected injector off, so the cylinder misfires. Ford petrol engines report all injector circuit faults as P0201 ff instead. Cylinder 12 exists only on twelve-cylinder engines; no manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford documents stop at cylinder 8 – so the description follows CARB and the codes for cylinders 1–8.

Injector connector damp or corroded, leakage to ground
Injector shorted to its housing internally
Open control wire (on some GM port-injection drivers this also reads low; P020x sets too)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0312
Loss of power, rough idle
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0295.d: P0295 means the control wire of the cylinder 12 injector is shorted to voltage. GM detects this with the driver on: on direct injection by 25 A or more through the driver, on port injection and Duramax diesels by 0.5 Ω or less to the supply. On Ford's 6.7 diesel it means the injector's high side is shorted to its low side, reported within 0.3 s. Most systems switch the warning light on in the first trip (some GM port-injection engines and Saab's 2.0 turbo after two) and shut the affected injector off, so the cylinder misfires. Ford petrol engines report all injector circuit faults as P0201 ff instead. Cylinder 12 exists only on twelve-cylinder engines; no manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford documents stop at cylinder 8 – so the description follows CARB and the codes for cylinders 1–8.

Injector coil shorted internally (too low resistance, overcurrent)
Short between supply and control wire in harness or connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0312
Loss of power, rough idle
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0297.d: P0297 is a condition code: the engine module detects that road speed – from the vehicle speed sensor or wheel and output shaft speed – exceeded the calibrated maximum. Electronic speed limiters cut fuel or throttle at that limit, and the event is stored. Ford uses the code on its petrol trucks and stores it without the warning light; no manufacturer publishes a threshold. Common triggers are descending with a trailer beyond the limiter speed, wheelspin on the driven axle, a wrongly programmed tyre size or axle ratio, or spikes in the speed signal. Unlike P0219 it concerns road speed, not engine speed.
c: Wrong tyre size or axle ratio programmed, larger wheels fitted
Speed signal disturbed (loose contact, interference, tone wheel)
s: Usually no warning light, code only stored
Vehicle limits speed at its maximum
With a disturbed signal: jumping speedometer, odd shifting

P0298.d: P0298 is a protection code: engine oil temperature – from its own sensor, often combined with the oil level sensor, or modelled – has exceeded the protection limit. Saab's 3.0 diesel limits injection quantity when the oil stays at 135 °C or more for over 10 s, until it cools down; a heavy-duty bus engine warns in two stages and then derates. Ford stores the code without the warning light, in line with CARB's exemption for overheat protection. Usual causes are high load in heat, cooling problems, a clogged oil cooler or stuck oil thermostat, and occasionally a sensor reading too high.
c: High load in heat (trailer, mountain pass, stop-and-go)
Cooling or fan problem (clogged radiator, fan, thermostat, low coolant)
Oil cooler clogged or oil thermostat stuck
Oil temperature or level sensor reading too high
Low oil level or wrong oil
s: Reduced power, quantity limited
Oil temperature warning
Usually no check engine light

P0299.d: P0299 means actual boost stays below target for a period although the control already demands more. Thresholds: GM petrol 30–55 kPa below target with the warning light in the first trip; GM diesels 10–50 kPa, two trips; Ford EcoBoost more than 4 psi (about 28 kPa) for 5 s with the wastegate already commanded fully closed; Ford diesels 30–40 kPa for 10–15 s, with a further underboost code P2263. Typical causes from manufacturer bulletins: a charge air leak, a wastegate that lost its preload or whose rod came off, a leaking bypass valve, sticking turbo vanes on diesels, and ice in the charge air cooler in winter. A faulty boost sensor can also fake underboost. Many engines then limit power.
c: Leak in the charge air path (hose off or torn, cooler leaking, clamps)
Wastegate faulty (rod off, preload lost, vacuum or solenoid, diaphragm)
Turbo vanes sticking or turbo worn (diesel)
Bypass valve leaking (torn diaphragm) or its control
Ice in the charge air cooler, boost sensor or connector, or software
s: Loss of power, sluggish acceleration
Limp mode, power limited
Check engine light on
Whistling or hissing from the charge air path under load

P029A.t: Cylinder 1 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit
P029A.d: These codes belong to an individual-cylinder fuel correction: a diesel's cylinder balance control measures each cylinder's crankshaft acceleration and adjusts its injection quantity; on petrol engines a cylinder-selective mixture control does the same. CARB requires the system to report when such a correction has used up its range or one cylinder causes an imbalance. P029A means the correction for cylinder 1 is at its upper limit: the module keeps giving this cylinder more fuel and still cannot even it out – a sign that the cylinder receives too little fuel or builds too little pressure. GM and Ford use other codes for this (P0263 ff, P219A ff); no manufacturer document describing this code with thresholds was found, so the description follows CARB and published patents.
c: Injector of cylinder 1 coked or partly clogged
Compression loss in this cylinder (valve, rings, leak at injector or glow plug)
Petrol: false air at this cylinder's intake (manifold gasket)
Injector correction code missing or wrong after replacement
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, vibration
Lack of power, possibly misfire

P02CA.d: Turbocharger B is a second, separately controlled turbo – on twin-turbo or two-stage systems, or one per bank. No manufacturer using the turbo B codes was found; twin-turbo engines such as GM's 3.0 V6 and Ford's 3.5 EcoBoost report boost faults under P0234/P0299 with a shared boost sensor, so the description follows CARB and the turbo A codes. P02CA means actual boost of turbo B stays above target although the control is already lowering it; for turbo A, GM petrol engines use 20–35 kPa, Ford EcoBoost more than 4 psi over 5 s. Boost is then limited.
c: Wastegate B stuck closed, linkage seized
Boost control valve or actuator B faulty, vacuum line swapped or leaking
s: Check engine light, reduced power, limp mode
Power cut under load
Possibly knocking (petrol)

P02CB.d: Turbocharger B is a second, separately controlled turbo – on twin-turbo or two-stage systems, or one per bank. No manufacturer using the turbo B codes was found; twin-turbo engines such as GM's 3.0 V6 and Ford's 3.5 EcoBoost report boost faults under P0234/P0299 with a shared boost sensor, so the description follows CARB and the turbo A codes. P02CB means actual boost of turbo B stays below target although the control demands more; for turbo A, GM uses 30–55 kPa (petrol) or 10–50 kPa (diesel). Typical causes are a charge air leak on that side, a wastegate stuck open or a worn turbo. Power is then limited.

Wastegate B stuck open or control valve faulty
Turbo B worn (bearing play, compressor wheel)
Exhaust leak ahead of turbine B

P02CC.t: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit
P02CC.d: The engine module learns a small-quantity correction for each injector: on overrun it gives one injector a tiny test injection (GM about 1.5 mm³), measures the resulting crankshaft acceleration and corrects the injector's activation time per rail pressure step. P02CC means the learned correction for cylinder 1 has reached its lower limit at at least one pressure step: the injector needs much less activation time than nominal – it delivers too much at small quantities or opens early. GM diesels set it at limits of roughly ±66–182 µs after two trips. It is documented on GM's 6.6 litre L5P and 2.8 litre diesels – on the 2.8 a worn drive belt caused it to return after injector replacement – and on Land Rover's 5.0 V8 petrol, where a software update is the first step. It differs from P01CC (over advanced), which some systems derive from the same learning.
c: Injector of cylinder 1 leaking or over-delivering at small quantities
Engine software (update available for some models)
Injector correction code not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Disturbed crankshaft signal (worn drive belt, tone wheel, dual-mass flywheel)
s: Check engine light on
Often nothing noticeable; possibly rough idle or knocking
Possibly smoke or higher consumption

P02D1.t: Cylinder 3 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Max Limit
P02D1.d: The engine module learns a small-quantity correction for each injector: on overrun it gives one injector a tiny test injection (GM about 1.5 mm³), measures the resulting crankshaft acceleration and corrects the injector's activation time per rail pressure step. P02D1 means the learned correction for cylinder 3 has reached its upper limit at at least one pressure step: the injector needs much more activation time than nominal – it delivers too little or opens late, for example from coking. GM diesels set it at limits of roughly ±66–182 µs after two trips. Older GM calibrations (LML) use only this code of the pair, for both directions. It is documented on GM's 6.6 litre L5P and 2.8 litre diesels – on the 2.8 a worn drive belt caused it to return after injector replacement – and on Land Rover's 5.0 V8 petrol, where a software update is the first step. It differs from P01CF (over retarded), which some systems derive from the same learning.

P02E0.t: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit/Open
P02E0.d: The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back. P02E0 means the motor circuit is open – cable, connector or motor winding. GM diesels detect more than 200 kΩ with the driver off, after about 1.5 s (6.6 litre LML: 7 s), two trips. On a fault the valve is switched off and the spring opens it: driving is usually little affected, but EGR control is restricted and filter regeneration may be blocked.

Motor winding of the valve open
Driver stage in the engine module
s: Check engine light on

P02E1.t: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Performance
P02E1.d: The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back. P02E1 means the valve does not follow its target position – GM's diesels set it when target and actual position differ by more than 10 % for about 1.2 s with a steady target, after two trips. On a fault the valve is switched off and the spring opens it: driving is usually little affected, but EGR control is restricted and filter regeneration may be blocked.

P02E4.t: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Open
P02E4.d: The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. P02E5.t: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Closed
P02E5.d: The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back. P02E5 means the valve stays more closed than commanded or does not return to its open rest position when unpowered – more critical than stuck open, because the engine lacks air. GM sets it at over 8 % more closed than commanded with more than 80 % duty for about 4 s, or after switch-off when the unpowered valve stays below 90 % open, with the warning light in the first trip. P02EC.t: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - High Air Flow Detected
P02EC.d: Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels control the air mass through the EGR valve and the intake throttle. P02EC means the measured air mass stays above target with the control at its limit – too little EGR, or the throttle cannot restrict enough – for 10 s (6.7) or 5 s (3.0). Typical causes are a stuck-closed EGR valve or clogged EGR cooler, a throttle stuck open or a mass airflow sensor reading too high. NOx rises; driving is usually unaffected. Other manufacturers using this code were not found.
c: EGR valve stuck closed or EGR cooler clogged
Mass airflow sensor reading too high
