P041C.t: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P041C.d: EGR temperature sensor B measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P041C means the signal is below its lower limit – very hot or shorted to ground; Ford puts below 0.10 V at about 961 °C. Thresholds: Ford diesel below 0.10 V for 3 s, Ford petrol below 0.32 V for 5 s, GM's Duramax LML below 0.46 V for 5 s, GM 2018 a resistance below 164 Ω; MIL after two trips. A substitute value is used and the EGR cooler check (P2457) is suspended.
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving
Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P041D.t: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P041D.d: EGR temperature sensor B measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P041D means the signal is above its upper limit – very cold or, far more often, an open circuit; Ford puts above 4.90 V at about −46 °C. Thresholds: Ford diesel above 4.90 V, Ford petrol above 4.94 V for 5 s, GM's Duramax LML above 4.84 V, GM 2018 a resistance above 859 Ω; MIL after two trips. A substitute value is used and the EGR cooler check is suspended.
c: Ground open or short to positive
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving
Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P041E.t: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P041E.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR temperature sensor B is the second temperature sensor in the EGR path; on GM diesels it sits before the cooler, on Ford diesels after it. P041E means its signal jumps. GM's diesels of 2016–18, the only documented users, set it when the measured resistance changes by more than 25 Ω between two samples 100 ms apart – faster than any real temperature change, so a loose contact or cracked sensor is the cause (40 of 50 samples, MIL after two trips). Dependent checks such as EGR cooler efficiency are then suspended.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector
Harness chafed or broken (heat at the EGR pipe)
s: Check engine light on, may come and go
Usually no noticeable symptom
Further EGR temperature or cooler checks suspended

P041F.t: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit Low
P041F.d: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air into the exhaust; switching valve A is the electrically driven valve that opens this path. GM checks the valve circuit in three codes – P0412 open, P041F shorted to ground, P044F shorted to positive – while other makers use P0413/P0414 or P0412 for everything. P041F means the control circuit is shorted to ground: GM checks with the driver switched off and sets the code at 0.5 Ω or less to ground (20 of 25 samples of 250 ms, above 11 V, MIL after two trips). The valve is then energised and open although not commanded; P0411 or P2440 may follow.
c: Water or corrosion in the valve connector
Valve coil shorted to its housing
s: Check engine light on (after two trips)
No change in driving
Secondary air readiness not set, possibly P0411

P0420.t: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P0420.d: The engine module checks whether the catalyst of bank 1 still converts enough. On petrol engines it estimates the oxygen storage capacity by comparing the sensors before and after the catalyst – a good catalyst smooths the rear signal. GM uses a test on overrun (ratio below 0.35 sets the code on the first trip), Ford an index ratio above 0.75 or fuel integration after fuel cut-off. On diesels P0420 concerns the oxidation catalyst, checked by its heat release during filter regeneration (GM Duramax LML, Ford below 45 % of the expected heat). Ford names oil-borne poisoning as the most common cause.
c: Catalyst aged or poisoned (oil consumption, silicone, coolant)
Catalyst overheated by misfire or rich running
Rear oxygen sensor sluggish, dirty or unsuitable
Exhaust leak ahead of or at the rear sensor
Diesel: oxidation catalyst sooted or poisoned, post-injection faulty
s: Check engine light on, otherwise often no change in driving
Emission test failed (higher HC, CO, NOx)
Rattling or loss of power if the catalyst has broken up

P0421.d: Catalyst 1 is the first catalyst in the flow direction of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1) – the close-coupled or warm-up catalyst that lights off first after a cold start; the older wording was Warm Up Catalyst. P0421 means it no longer converts enough. Mitsubishi V6 engines with manifold catalysts and GM's 3.0/3.2-litre V6 of 2004/05 with Bosch control report it: the rear sensor amplitude is compared with a model, and a quality factor above 0.625 (2004) or 0.375 (2005) sets the code after two trips. GM's small diesels use P0421 for the close-coupled oxidation catalyst, tested by heat balance during filter regeneration.

Misfire or rich running as prior damage
Sensor after the close-coupled catalyst sluggish or faulty
Engine module software (Mitsubishi: update for 2006 Eclipse V6)
s: Check engine light on, otherwise often no change in driving
Emission test failed (higher HC, CO, NOx)
Rattling or loss of power if the catalyst has broken up

P0422.d: Catalyst 2 is the second catalyst in the flow direction of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1) – the main or underfloor catalyst behind the close-coupled one; the older wording was Main Catalyst. P0422 means it no longer converts enough. Only GM's small diesels are documented with this code: they assess the underfloor oxidation catalyst separately from the close-coupled one (P0421) by heat balance during filter regeneration, with an exhaust fuel injector ahead of it. Petrol engines with several catalysts usually report P0420 instead.

Diesel: exhaust fuel injector coked, doses too little

P0423.t: Heated Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P0423.d: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of a support catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start (Emitec EMICAT, 12–48 V); it was tried on Californian petrol cars in the 1990s and is used today mainly on diesels, for example Audi's 3.0 TDI from 2014 and 48-volt diesel vans. P0423 means the heated catalyst of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1) no longer converts enough; CARB requires it to be assessed like any other catalyst. The only manufacturer reference is two Ram software bulletins for the 6.7-litre Cummins HO (model years 2025/26), which list P0423 without saying which part is meant.
c: Heater not working, catalyst active too late
Sensor used for the assessment faulty
s: Check engine light on
Higher emissions after a cold start
Otherwise usually unremarkable

P0424.t: Heated Catalyst Temperature Below Threshold Bank 1
P0424.d: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of a support catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start (Emitec EMICAT, 12–48 V); it was tried on Californian petrol cars in the 1990s and is used today mainly on diesels, for example Audi's 3.0 TDI from 2014 and 48-volt diesel vans. P0424 implements CARB's heated-catalyst rule for bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1): the catalyst must reach its intended temperature within a time set by the manufacturer after the start, measured by a temperature sensor or modelled from heating power. If it does not, the heater is too weak – supply voltage, contact resistance, an ageing element – or heat losses are too high. An open heater circuit is reported as P0429/P0439 instead. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.

Supply too weak (battery, 48 V system, relay, contact resistance)

P0425.t: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0425.d: Some engines – mainly diesels – measure the temperature at or in the catalyst with a thermistor in a voltage divider instead of only modelling it; most makers report exhaust temperature sensors under P0544 ff, P2031 ff or P2080 ff instead. Sensor 1 of bank 1 is the first catalyst temperature sensor on the side with cylinder 1. P0425 is the general circuit fault, used where the module does not separate low and high. FCA's 3.0-litre EcoDiesel uses this sensor (middle of the oxidation catalyst and particulate filter unit), but no document available to us names this particular code.

P042E.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P042E means the position-controlled EGR valve A is more open than commanded and cannot be closed. GM's diesels of 2016/17 set it when the valve stays too far open despite maximum closing duty (about 1–8 s); the 2018 tables check after switch-off whether it is below 5 % within 2 s – both with MIL on the first trip. Ford petrol engines compare the position with limits for 4 s, Ford diesels a deviation above 15 % for 25 s. Too much EGR causes rough idle, stalling and smoke; EGR control is switched off.

Actuator motor, gear or return spring faulty
Position sensor in the valve reads wrong
Weak supply to the drive or connector fault
s: Check engine light on (GM after one trip)
Rough idle, stalling, starting problems
Loss of power, possibly limp mode
Diesel: smoke, higher soot load

P042F.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P042F means EGR valve A does not follow the opening command: its actual position stays more closed than commanded although the actuator works with high opening duty. GM's diesels of 2016/17 set it after about 1–8 s with MIL on the first trip; a GM bulletin covers it on the 2017 Cruze diesel. Ford petrol engines use position limits for 4 s; Ford diesels report both directions under P042E. With too little EGR, NOx rises, petrol engines may knock and P0401 can follow.

Actuator motor or gear weak or faulty
Position sensor or connector gives a wrong value
s: Check engine light on (GM after one trip)
Usually no driveability problems
Possibly pinging (petrol) or higher NOx

The monitor only runs warm, in closed loop and without misfire, fuel or sensor faults.

No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB, which requires input circuits to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility, and the comparable exhaust temperature sensors.
c: Sensor or wire open (broken by vibration or heat)
Connector off or loose, ground wire open
s: Check engine light on
Usually no noticeable change (substitute value from the model)
Diesel: filter regeneration distorted or blocked, possibly further codes such as P2459 or P0420

P043E.t: EVAP System Leak Detection Reference Orifice Low Flow
P043E.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Systems with a leak detection pump (Bosch DM-TL at VW, Audi, BMW and Maserati, Denso's canister pump module at Toyota/Lexus) first measure a reference value with the pump working only through a built-in 0.5 mm (0.020 in) orifice; it is the yardstick for the small-leak test that CARB requires. P043E means the reference measurement shows too little flow – the vacuum (or with DM-TL the pressure and pump current) becomes stronger than expected, so the orifice or reference path is partly blocked, often by dirt or liquid after overfilling. GM and Ford do not use the code; Maserati fixed false triggering with software.
c: Reference orifice or pump module dirty or blocked by liquid (overfilled tank, splash water)
Leak detection pump faulty (weak or blocking pump, changeover valve stuck)
s: Check engine light on
EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set
Usually no change in driving

P043F.t: EVAP System Leak Detection Reference Orifice High Flow
P043F.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Systems with a leak detection pump (Bosch DM-TL at VW, Audi, BMW and Maserati, Denso's canister pump module at Toyota/Lexus) first measure a reference value with the pump working only through a built-in 0.5 mm (0.020 in) orifice; it is the yardstick for the small-leak test that CARB requires. P043F means the reference measurement shows too much flow – the reference vacuum or pressure does not reach the expected value, because the reference path or changeover valve leaks, the pump is weak, or air enters through leaking valves in the test path. The leak test can then not be judged, since a weak yardstick would hide leaks. GM and Ford do not use the code.
c: Leak detection pump faulty (weak pump, leaking changeover valve, liquid damage)
Pump supply or connector (contact resistance, corrosion)
Leaking hose between pump module and canister
s: Check engine light on
EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set
Usually no change in driving

P0440.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0440 is the general code for a fault in this system without further narrowing down – leak, purge flow or component. Today most makers use the specific codes instead (P0441 ff, P0455–P0457, P0496); the GM and Ford tables of 2006–2023 do not contain P0440. It appears in VW code lists and in an FCA bulletin for the Alfa Romeo 2.0, fixed by software, where FCA calls it incorrect flow. What sets it is therefore manufacturer-specific; CARB requires purge flow and leaks to be monitored.
c: Fuel cap leaking, loose or wrong
Leaking or cracked EVAP hoses, canister or vent valve
s: Check engine light on
Possibly slight fuel smell
Readiness or emission inspection not passed
No change in driving

P0441.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0441 means the actual purge flow does not match the target – too little, or flow although the purge valve is closed. CARB requires a fault when no purge flow is detected. Strategies differ widely: Saab's Trionic T7/T8 sets it for flow with the valve closed (tank pressure falling faster than 27.5–40 Pa/s), VW and Audi check purge flow with the leak detection pump, Honda/Acura for a sticking purge valve. GM and Ford do not use P0441 – they report flow with the valve closed as P0496 or P1450 and missing flow as P0455.
c: Purge valve stuck open or not sealing
Purge valve stuck closed, purge line blocked, kinked or off
Leak detection pump with tolerance fault (VW)
Canister saturated or damaged, turbo purge check valve faulty
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle or hard start after refuelling (valve stuck open)
Fuel smell
Possibly fuel trim codes

P0442.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0442 reports a small leak; what size that means depends on the maker. Ford detects 0.040 in (1 mm) with the engine running: the vent valve closes, engine vacuum pulls the tank down, the purge valve closes and a pressure rise above 2.5 inH2O in 15 s sets the code (0.020 in is P0456). GM uses the natural pressure change after switch-off for 0.020 in and averages several tests. Pump systems at VW and Audi compare against a reference leak. A worn or loose fuel cap is the most common cause.
c: Fuel cap seal worn, wrong or not clicked in
Cracked or porous EVAP hoses or leaking connections
Purge or vent valve does not seal
Filler neck corroded, tank or sender seal leaking
s: Check engine light on
Possibly slight fuel smell
Readiness or emission inspection not passed
No change in driving

P0443.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit
P0443.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0443 is the electrical check of purge valve A, which the module switches to ground in pulses; it compares the driver's feedback voltage with the commanded state. GM uses it for an open circuit (200 kΩ or more, 20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips) and reports shorts as P0458/P0459; Ford covers open and short in P0443 (5 s). Purging then stops, the canister is no longer regenerated, and the leak and purge monitors are suspended.
c: Purge valve connector corroded, loose or off
Purge valve coil open or shorted
Control wire broken or chafed, or supply missing (fuse, main relay)
s: Check engine light on
Possibly fuel smell (no purging)
EVAP leak test does not run

P0444.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Open
P0444.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0444 belongs to the older scheme of circuit, open and shorted codes for purge valve A; Saab's Trionic T7 and VW use it, while GM reports an open circuit as P0443 and Ford covers everything in P0443. Saab checks with the output switched off: below 2 V the supply through the coil is missing or the line is grounded – Saab combines both under P0444, sets it after about 1 s and pauses the check until the next drive. Purging then stops.
c: Purge valve connector off or corroded
Supply wire, fuse, main relay or control wire open
Control wire shorted to ground (Saab definition)
s: Check engine light on
Possibly fuel smell
EVAP monitors do not run

P0445.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Shorted
P0445.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0445 is the short-circuit code of the older scheme for purge valve A, used by Saab's Trionic T7 and VW; GM reports shorts as P0458/P0459, Ford covers them in P0443. Saab checks with the low-side output switched on: the voltage should then be near 0 V, and above 2 V means the line is shorted to positive or the coil is shorted, with the driver in current limiting. The code sets after about 1 s; the driver protects itself by switching off, so purging stops.
c: Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Possibly fuel smell
EVAP monitors do not run

P0446.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and closes for the leak test. By its wording P0446 is its control circuit, and Ford uses it that way for open and shorted circuits. GM, however, uses P0446 for vent system performance – a blocked vent path: while purging with the vent valve open, the tank must not build up vacuum; more than 2989 Pa for 5 s before 4 litres have been purged sets the code, MIL after two trips. GM reports vent circuit faults as P0449, P0498 and P0499. A blocked vent makes refuelling difficult.
c: Vent valve or filter blocked by dirt, dust or water (GM reading)
Vent valve electrically faulty, coil open or shorted (Ford reading)
Connector or wire to the vent valve corroded or open
Canister clogged with charcoal or liquid (overfilling)
Vent hose kinked or blocked by an insect nest
s: Check engine light on
Refuelling problems, nozzle clicks off early (blocked vent)
Hissing when opening the fuel cap (vacuum)
EVAP leak test does not run

P0447.t: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit Open
P0447.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0447 belongs to the older scheme for the vent valve circuit (P0446 circuit, P0447 open, P0448 shorted), used by Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X), VW and Nissan; GM reports an open vent circuit as P0449, Ford as P0446. On Subaru the valve is fed from the main relay and switched to ground by the module; if the voltage at the module output is missing or the coil is high-resistance (nominal 10–100 Ω), the code sets after two consecutive drives. The valve stays in its rest position and the leak test cannot run.
c: Vent valve connector corroded or off (underbody, splash water)
Vent valve coil open (resistance outside 10–100 Ω)
Wire to the module or supply from the main relay open
s: Check engine light on
EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set
Usually no change in driving

P0448.t: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit Shorted
P0448.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0448 is the short-circuit code of the older scheme for the vent valve. Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X) expects supply voltage above 10 V at the module output with the valve off; a short to positive or a coil below 1 Ω sets the code after two drives, and Subaru then also replaces the module, as its driver may be damaged. Nissan and Infiniti use P0448 differently, for a vent valve or vent path stuck closed by dust or water, with replacement of canister, valve and filler tube. GM and Ford do not use the code.
c: Vent valve or vent path blocked by dust, dirt or water (Nissan reading)
s: Check engine light on
Refuelling problems if the vent is blocked
EVAP leak test does not run

P0449.t: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit/Open
P0449.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0449 belongs to the newer scheme for the vent valve circuit – P0449 open, P0498 low, P0499 high – used mainly by GM and also by VW. The normally open valve is fed from the battery and switched to ground; with the driver off, the output should show supply voltage. A floating 2.6–4.6 V, or an impedance of 200 kΩ or more, means an open circuit (GM: 20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips). The leak test and the vent performance check P0446 are then suspended; purging continues.
c: Vent valve connector (usually at the canister or tank, underbody) corroded or loose
s: Check engine light on
EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set
Usually no change in driving

P044A.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044A is the general circuit fault of this sensor. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – Ford splits it into P044C/P044D – so the description follows CARB's requirement to check input circuits for continuity and range. Without the sensor, EGR flow and cooler checks are suspended.
c: Connector or wire to sensor C open or corroded
5 V reference or ground disturbed (with other sensor codes)
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving
EGR readiness not set, EGR possibly switched off

P044B.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044B means its signal is electrically valid but implausible – for example a pressure difference with the valve closed, or no reaction when it opens. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; Ford checks the DPFE plausibility under its own codes P139A–P139C (hoses swapped, front or rear hose off or blocked). EGR flow diagnosis is then suspended.
c: Pressure hoses off, swapped or blocked (soot, condensate)
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving
EGR readiness not set, EGR possibly switched off

P044C.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044C means its signal is below the lower limit. Ford petrol engines from 2020 set it below 0.25 V for 5 s – a value the sensor cannot produce, since 0.5 V already means −11 kPa – so the signal is shorted to ground, the 5 V supply is open or the sensor is faulty. EGR flow, hose and cooler checks are then suspended; MIL after two trips.
c: 5 V supply of the sensor open or shorted to ground
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving
EGR readiness not set, EGR possibly switched off

P044D.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044D means its signal is above the upper limit. Ford petrol engines from 2020 set it above 4.65 V for 5 s, beyond the measuring range that ends at 4.5 V (about +18 kPa) – typically an open sensor ground, a signal shorted to 5 V or positive, or a faulty sensor. EGR flow, hose and cooler checks are then suspended; MIL after two trips.
c: Signal shorted to 5 V or positive
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving
EGR readiness not set, EGR possibly switched off

P044E.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044E means short dropouts or jumps in its signal, too brief for P044C/P044D or with an impossible rate of change. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; Ford applies the same idea to sensor A as P046D, where a limit violation of only 0.4 s counts. EGR diagnosis is then suspended.
c: Loose contact in the connector or broken wire
Condensate in the sensor or hose (DPFE)
s: Check engine light on, may come and go
Usually no driving symptom
Code returns after clearing

P044F.t: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit High
P044F.d: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air into the exhaust; switching valve A is the electrically driven valve that opens this path. GM checks the valve circuit in three codes – P0412 open, P041F shorted to ground, P044F shorted to positive – while other makers use P0413/P0414 or P0412 for everything. P044F means the control circuit is shorted to positive or the coil is low-resistance: when the driver switches on, the line stays high. GM sets the code at 0.5 Ω or less to the supply (20 of 25 samples of 250 ms, above 11 V, MIL after two trips). The valve then does not open, secondary air is missing and P0411 may follow.
c: Control wire chafed against a supply wire
Water in the connector bridging to the supply
s: Check engine light on (after two trips)
No change in driving
Secondary air readiness not set, possibly P0411

P0450.t: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0450.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0450 is the general circuit fault of tank pressure sensor A; makers that separate the fault use P0452 or P0453. Only Audi (2022/23) is documented with the code, as an electrical fault of the tank ventilation pressure sensor; GM, Ford and Saab do not use it. The leak tests are then suspended.
c: Connector at the tank pressure sensor corroded or loose (underbody, splash water)
Damaged 5 V, ground or signal wire
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed
No change in driving

P0451.t: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance
P0451.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0451 is its plausibility check. GM checks during the engine-off leak test that the signal settles to ambient pressure with the vent open and averages several tests; Ford checks the offset after at least 4–6 hours off (±0.5 kPa). Saab's Bosch ME9 watches start pressure, the drop during purging and excessive oscillation. On Subaru a leaking or blocked hose between sensor and tank is a frequent cause.
c: Tank pressure sensor offset shifted or sluggish
Vent line or canister blocked (pressure does not release)
Sensor hose or port leaking, kinked or blocked
Tank overfilled, fuel in the lines
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed
No change in driving

P0452.t: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Low
P0452.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0452 means its signal voltage is below the lower limit: GM below 0.15 V (640 of 800 samples, MIL after two trips), Ford below 0.1 V for 5 s, Saab below 0.1 V for more than 5 s. Common causes are a signal wire shorted to ground, an interrupted or shorted 5 V reference or a faulty sensor. Leak and purge tests are then suspended.
c: Signal wire shorted to ground or connector corroded
5 V reference open or shorted (shared reference)
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed
No change in driving

P0453.t: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
P0453.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0453 means its signal voltage is above the upper limit: GM above 4.85 V (640 of 800 samples, MIL after two trips), Ford and Saab 9-4X above 4.9 V for 5 s. Ford states explicitly that an open circuit sets P0453, because the module's pull-up then drives the signal high. Other causes are a short to 5 V or battery voltage. Leak tests are then suspended.
c: Signal or ground wire open, connector off
Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed
No change in driving

P0454.t: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent
P0454.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0454 means the signal jumps. Ford checks continuously for a jump above about 1 kPa between two samples 100 ms apart or a brief open or short. GM (and the Saab 9-4X) checks only during the engine-off leak test: a jump of about 112 Pa within 1 s that refuelling cannot explain, 2 of 3 tests, MIL on the first trip. Saab's ME9 does not use the code. The engine-off small-leak test is then discarded.
c: Loose contact at the connector to the tank pressure sensor
Fuel sloshing in an overfilled tank or refuelling misdetected
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed
No change in driving

P0455.t: EVAP System Leak Detected - Large Leak
P0455.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0455 means a large leak or that no vacuum builds up. Ford pulls the closed system down with engine vacuum and expects about −2 kPa within 30 s; after refuelling it sets P0457 instead. GM sets the code if 20 litres have been purged without reaching 2740 Pa tank vacuum (once per cold start, MIL after two trips). Saab's ME9 uses a pressure drop below 525 Pa. The code also covers blocked purging, for example a purge valve stuck closed.
c: Fuel cap missing, not clicked in or seal faulty (or capless flap)
Hose off or cracked (canister, filler neck, purge line)
Vent valve stuck open or purge valve stuck closed
Canister or filler neck cracked or corroded
s: Check engine light on (possibly a check fuel cap message)
Possibly fuel smell
EVAP readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0456.t: EVAP System Leak Detected (very small leak)
P0456.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0456 reports a very small leak of 0.020 in (0.5 mm), as CARB requires. Ford uses the engine-off natural vacuum test: after switch-off the closed system must build at least about 190 Pa pressure or 125 Pa vacuum, judged statistically. Saab's Bosch ME9 also tests with the engine off for up to 45 minutes; VW and Audi use a leak detection pump. GM reports this leak size as P0442 instead. The code often appears only after many trips and depends on the weather.
c: Fuel cap seal worn or cap not clicked in
Purge or vent valve not sealing
Porous hoses or O-rings, hairline crack in canister or filler neck
s: Check engine light on (possibly a check fuel cap message)
Possibly fuel smell
EVAP readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0457.t: EVAP System Leak Detected (fuel cap loose/off)
P0457.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0457 is a large leak attributed to the fuel cap: Ford detects refuelling and treats a vacuum that is not reached afterwards (about −2 kPa in 30 s) as an open cap. CARB allows a separate check fuel cap lamp instead of the warning lamp, and the code is cleared once the cap is found tight again. Ford sets the lamp after two to three trips depending on calibration, Subaru after two. GM and Saab's ME9 do not use the code.
c: Fuel cap not closed, not clicked in or forgotten
Fuel cap seal faulty or non-original cap
Filler neck sealing surface damaged or capless flap sticking
s: Check fuel cap lamp or check engine light on
Fuel smell
EVAP readiness not set

P0458.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Low
P0458.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve A is switched to ground by the module and fed from the main relay. P0458 means its control wire is shorted to ground: GM detects it with the driver off, when the line sits at ground instead of supply (20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips); Saab's ME9 uses below 2.6 V at the output. The valve is then energised and open all the time, purging is uncontrolled – rough idle, rich mixture or hard starting after refuelling are possible.
c: Purge valve control wire chafed against ground
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle or rich mixture possible (valve permanently open)
Starting problems after refuelling possible

P0459.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit High
P0459.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve A is switched to ground by the module and fed from the main relay. P0459 means its control wire is shorted to positive, detected with the driver switched on, when the line should sit at ground (GM 20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips; Saab ME9 above 4.6 V). The valve then cannot open, the canister is not purged and fills up; the driver protects itself and the leak tests are suspended.
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage or supply
s: Check engine light on
Fuel smell when the canister is full
EVAP readiness not set

P045A.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045A is the general electrical fault in the drive circuit of valve B, typically an open circuit (for valve A GM uses 200 kΩ or more). GM lists this code among those that switch off the low-pressure EGR position control, but publishes no thresholds for it; the description follows the comparable valve A checks and CARB, which requires output circuits to be monitored. Low-pressure EGR is then switched off.
c: Connector at EGR valve B corroded or loose
Actuator motor in valve B open
s: Check engine light on
Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx
Usually no change in driving

P045B.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045B means the drive circuit of valve B is electrically valid, but the feedback – current, voltage or position response – does not match the command. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows the valve A counterpart P0404 and CARB, which requires output functions to be checked where feasible. Typical is a coked, stiff valve.
c: Contact resistance in connector or wiring
s: Check engine light on
Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx
Usually no change in driving

P045C.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045C means the drive circuit of valve B is shorted to ground (for valve A, P0489, GM uses 0.5 Ω or less with the driver off, MIL after two trips). The driver is switched off for protection and the valve stays in its rest position. GM lists this code among those that switch off the low-pressure EGR position control, but publishes no thresholds for it; the description follows the comparable valve A checks and CARB, which requires output circuits to be monitored.
c: Control wire chafed against ground (engine, exhaust)
Water or corrosion in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx
Usually no change in driving

P045D.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045D means the drive circuit of valve B is shorted to the supply, or the actuator draws overcurrent with the driver on (comparable to P0490 for valve A). The driver is switched off and EGR B stays inactive. GM lists this code among those that switch off the low-pressure EGR position control, but publishes no thresholds for it; the description follows the comparable valve A checks and CARB, which requires output circuits to be monitored.
c: Control wire shorted to a supply wire
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx
Usually no change in driving

P045E.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045E means valve B does not close: its actual position stays above the target despite the close command. On FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler, deposits in the low-pressure valve cause it; the bulletin prescribes a cleaning routine of nine ignition cycles that moves the valve repeatedly. Another FCA bulletin shows P045E following a position sensor fault (P0407/P0408). Too much EGR causes misfire, lack of power and smoke.
c: Soot or condensate deposits in the low-pressure valve
Valve position sensor fault as the trigger
Actuator gear or return spring faulty
Foreign matter or filter debris in the low-pressure circuit
s: Check engine light on
Lack of power, rough running, misfire
Possibly black smoke

P045F.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045F means valve B does not open: its actual position stays below the target despite the open command. GM lists the code among those that switch off low-pressure EGR control; Ford's comparable valve A check (P042F) compares the position with a calculated lower limit. Too little EGR raises NOx while driving stays normal. Icing or condensate can block a low-pressure valve – FCA runs its cleaning routine only above 0 °C.
c: Icing or condensate in the low-pressure circuit
Position sensor reports a wrong position
s: Check engine light on
Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx
Usually no change in driving

P0460.d: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. P0460 is the general circuit code for sensor A, the main or only fuel level sensor. Ford sets it instead of P0462/P0463 below 5 Ω or above 200 Ω for 30 s and until about 2012 also used it for a stuck sensor (fuel use compared over 100–120 miles); Saab's Trionic T8 uses it for a sensor that does not change. GM does not use P0460. The gauge then shows wrong values or a substitute, and level-dependent monitors do not run.
c: Resistor track worn or float arm sticking
Wire or connector at the tank unit open or shorted (corrosion)
Instrument cluster or gateway sends a wrong value (if the level comes via the bus)
Frequent topping up or overfilling (plausibility test fails without a defect)
s: Fuel gauge wrong, stuck or jumping
Range display and low-fuel warning wrong
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0461.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0461.d: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. P0461 is the plausibility check of sensor A within its valid signal range. GM compares the level change with calculated fuel use: less than 3 l change after 22 l (2018) or 38.2 l (2016) consumed sets the code, MIL after two trips. Ford reads it differently, as a noisy signal with jumps above 40 %. On the Saab 9-4X the gauge then drops to empty and the low-fuel lamp comes on. A GM bulletin names overfilling and frequent topping up as a false trigger.
c: Resistor track or wiper worn or dirty (sulphur deposits), arm sticking
Float deformed or soaked, or tank deformed
Overfilling or frequent topping up (no defect)
s: Fuel gauge wrong, stuck or jumping
Range display and low-fuel warning wrong
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0462.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low
P0462.d: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. Low and high refer to the signal, not the fuel level: on GM a full tank is about 40 Ω and a low voltage, while Ford judges the resistance directly. P0462 means the signal is below its lower limit: GM below 10 % of the 5 V reference (100 of 125 samples, MIL after two trips), Saab 9-4X below 0.25 V for 5 s, Ford a resistance below 5 Ω for 30 s. Typical is a signal wire shorted to ground or a shorted sensor. The gauge sticks at one end and a substitute value is used.
c: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed at tank or underbody)
Water or corrosion in the tank connector
s: Fuel gauge wrong, stuck or jumping
Range display and low-fuel warning wrong
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0463.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit High
P0463.d: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. Low and high refer to the signal, not the fuel level: on GM a full tank is about 40 Ω and a low voltage, while Ford judges the resistance directly. P0463 means the signal is above its upper limit: GM above 60 % of the 5 V reference (100 of 125 samples, MIL after two trips), Saab 9-4X above 4.7 V for 5 s, Ford a resistance above 200 Ω for 30 s. Typical is an open circuit – the pull-up then drives the signal high – a short to positive, or an interrupted resistor track. The gauge sticks at one end and a substitute value is used.

Resistor track interrupted or worn (sulphur deposits, wiper lifting)
s: Fuel gauge wrong, stuck or jumping
Range display and low-fuel warning wrong
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0464.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0464.d: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. At GM, P0464 is a by-product of the engine-off EVAP leak test: a jump in fuel level with the vent valve closed counts as possible refuelling and aborts the test; if a following check finds no real refuelling, the jump is counted as an intermittent sensor signal (change above 10 % not stable for 30 s, 2 of 3 samples). GM sets the code with MIL on the first trip, because otherwise the leak monitor would be defeated permanently. Ford does not use P0464 and reports jumps as P0461.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the tank connector or sensor terminal
Worn spots on the resistor track (wiper skipping)
Car parked on a steep slope or fuel sloshing after switch-off
s: Check engine light on (GM after one trip)
Fuel gauge occasionally jumps
EVAP readiness not set

P0465.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. A purge flow sensor – a heated thermistor in the purge line between purge valve and intake manifold, as described in a Ford patent – measures purge flow directly for the CARB purge monitor. Today indirect methods (fuel trim, tank vacuum) have largely replaced it; no manufacturer document available to us uses these codes. P0465 is the general circuit fault of the sensor (heater supply, signal or ground), which CARB requires to be checked continuously. The purge flow monitor can then not be evaluated.
c: Connector or wire at the purge flow sensor
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed
No change in driving

P0466.t: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0466.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Today indirect methods (fuel trim, tank vacuum) have largely replaced it; no manufacturer document available to us uses these codes. P0466 means the signal does not fit the purge valve state – the Ford patent judges the voltage difference between 100 % and 0 % purge duty against a calibrated value. The purge flow monitor can then not be evaluated.
c: Sensor dirty or sluggish (charcoal dust, fuel deposits)
Purge line blocked or purge valve sticking
Hose leaking ahead of the sensor
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed
No change in driving

P046A.d: Some engines measure the catalyst temperature with sensors instead of only modelling it. P046A compares catalyst temperature sensors 1 and 2 of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1): both are electrically valid, but their readings do not match – for example they differ after a long stop, or the difference does not fit the operating state. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; FCA's EcoDiesel has only one such sensor per bank, and most makers handle exhaust temperature sensors and their correlation under EGT codes such as P0544 ff or P24C2. The description follows CARB's plausibility requirement for input components.
c: One of the two sensors drifting (soot on the tip, ageing)
Sensors fitted or connected the wrong way round
Contact resistance at one sensor's connector
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving
Diesel: filter regeneration possibly changed

The description follows CARB's plausibility requirement for input components.

P046C.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensors A and B are depends on the maker: sensor A is usually the position sensor of EGR valve A; GM's Duramax diesels of 2017/18 use sensor B for the coolant temperature sensor at the inlet of the high-pressure EGR cooler, FCA for the position sensor of the low-pressure valve. P046C means the signal of sensor A is electrically valid but implausible. GM's diesels (6.6-litre Duramax LML and others from 2014) set it when the actual valve position deviates from the target by 5 % or more for 8 s, with offset learning completed and at least 11 V (MIL after two trips). Ford uses P0405/P0406/P046D for sensor A instead. EGR is then switched off or limited.
c: EGR valve coked and stiff, actual position does not follow
Position sensor worn or offset shifted
Contact resistance at connector or 5 V supply
Values not relearned after valve replacement
s: Check engine light on
EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx
Rarely jerking or lack of power

P046D.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensors A and B are depends on the maker: sensor A is usually the position sensor of EGR valve A; GM's Duramax diesels of 2017/18 use sensor B for the coolant temperature sensor at the inlet of the high-pressure EGR cooler, FCA for the position sensor of the low-pressure valve. P046D means brief excursions of sensor A out of its valid range, too short for P0405/P0406. Ford petrol engines from 2020 set it when the position signal stays above 95 % or below 5 % of its range for just 0.4 s, whereas 4 s set P0405/P0406; the check runs continuously during the EGR monitor above 8.25 V and 400 rpm. EGR is then switched off.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the EGR valve connector
Chafed wire with brief short to ground or positive
Position sensor in the valve worn
s: Check engine light on, may come and go
Usually no noticeable change
Occasional jerking when EGR switches off

P046E.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensors A and B are depends on the maker: sensor A is usually the position sensor of EGR valve A; GM's Duramax diesels of 2017/18 use sensor B for the coolant temperature sensor at the inlet of the high-pressure EGR cooler, FCA for the position sensor of the low-pressure valve. P046E means the signal of sensor B is valid but implausible. On GM's Duramax diesels, where it is the cooler inlet coolant temperature, the module compares it at a cold start after at least 8 hours off with two charge air temperature sensors; a deviation above 10 °C sets the code once per trip, MIL after two trips. A substitute value is then used and the EGR cooler check (P2457) is suspended.
c: Reference sensor (charge air temperature) inaccurate without its own code
Low coolant or air at the sensor
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving
EGR cooler check suspended

P046F.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensors A and B are depends on the maker: sensor A is usually the position sensor of EGR valve A; GM's Duramax diesels of 2017/18 use sensor B for the coolant temperature sensor at the inlet of the high-pressure EGR cooler, FCA for the position sensor of the low-pressure valve. P046F means jumps or dropouts of sensor B. GM's Duramax diesels set it when the value leaves a narrowing window around the last valid reading – 40 of 50 samples of 100 ms, MIL after two trips. A substitute value is then used and EGR cooler monitoring is suspended. Usually a loose contact or broken wire is the cause.
c: Loose contact at the sensor connector
s: Check engine light on, may come and go
Usually no change in driving

P0470.d: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. P0470 is the general circuit fault of sensor A. Ford's 6.7-litre diesel with a digital SENT sensor sets it when the sensor reports an error status or its raw data leave their limits for 5 s; a loss of communication is U0691 instead. Analogue sensors use it for an open or unspecified circuit fault where low and high are not separated.
c: Connector corroded or heat-damaged near the manifold
Broken or chafed signal or 5 V wire
s: Check engine light on
EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P0471.t: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0471.d: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. P0471 is the plausibility check of sensor A. Ford diesels compare it with ambient pressure with the engine off (at least 10 s stopped); a deviation above 15 kPa sets the code, including a sensor stuck mid-range. Ford petrol engines check it during the EGR monitor. FCA notes for Cummins diesels that P0471 often comes from real back pressure of a clogged particulate filter – then the sensor must not be replaced. Ford bulletins cover a sensor replacement on the 2.7 EcoBoost and coked sensing tubes on the 6.0 diesel.
c: Sensing tube or hose blocked or coked
Real high back pressure from a clogged particulate filter or catalyst
Leaking sensing tube or exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
s: Check engine light on
EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P0472.t: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P0472.d: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. P0472 means the signal voltage is below its limit – Ford diesels below 0.1 V for 2 s, Ford petrol engines below 0.21 V for 5 s. The cause is a signal shorted to ground, an interrupted 5 V reference or a faulty sensor; on Ford petrol engines the code must be clear before the EGR valve and hose checks run.
c: 5 V reference open or shorted (often shared with other sensors)
Connector damaged by heat or corrosion
s: Check engine light on

The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. P0473 means the signal voltage is above its limit – Ford diesels above 4.8 V for 2 s, Ford petrol engines above 4.80 V for 5 s. Typical is an open signal wire that the pull-up drives high, an open sensor ground, or a short to 5 V or battery voltage.
c: Signal wire open or sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
s: Check engine light on

P0474.t: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0474.d: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. P0474 covers jumps of sensor A – and at Ford diesels more: in operation the measured pressure is compared with a back pressure model, and a deviation above 500 kPa or below −100 kPa for 2 s sets the code (1300–2400 rpm, warm engine). Ford petrol engines include it in the electrical checks (5 s). A Ford bulletin fixed P0474 on the 2018 6.7-litre with a software update.
c: Loose contact at connector or wire near the hot manifold
Sensing tube partly blocked (sluggish, jumping values)
s: Check engine light on
EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P0475.d: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. P0475 is the general circuit fault of valve A, monitored like any output as CARB requires. VW's 2.0 TDI of 2015 sets it together with P0477/P0478, and the actuator electronics are replaced; Audi uses it for an electrical fault of the sound flap, Bentley for a shorted commutator in the flap motor. On the Navistar warm-up flap, a patent describes control to a target back pressure with the exhaust pressure sensor as feedback.
c: Wire or connector at the exhaust damaged or corroded
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function: sound unchanged, rattling
Diesel: longer warm-up, exhaust brake weak or EGR faults

P0476.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Range/Performance
P0476.d: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. P0476 is the function check: the valve does not reach its target position or the expected back pressure. With the Navistar warm-up flap, the module controls to a target back pressure using the sensor as feedback, so missing pressure despite actuation is a function fault. The only code-specific reference is Ducati's Diavel V4 motorcycle (2023): faulty flap motor movement from a wrongly seated cable bracket, with warning lamp and torque limitation until ignition off.
c: Exhaust pressure sensor or sensing tube giving wrong feedback
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function: sound unchanged, rattling
Diesel: longer warm-up, exhaust brake weak or EGR faults

P0477.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Low
P0477.d: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. P0477 means the control circuit of valve A is low. Audi uses it for a short to ground of the exhaust flap. VW's 2.0 TDI of 2009–12 sets it together with P047F, P048A–P048C and P0401 when salt has corroded the flap shaft and the flap sticks – a blocked motor can cause overcurrent or a voltage drop; on the 2015 engine it appears with P0478/P0475 and the actuator is replaced.
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function: sound unchanged, rattling
Diesel: longer warm-up, exhaust brake weak or EGR faults

P0478.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A High
P0478.d: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. P0479.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Intermittent
