P047E.t: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P047E.d: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. No manufacturer document available to us uses sensor B – it would be a second sensor, for example on bank 2 of a twin-turbo engine; the description mirrors sensor A. P047E means the signal of sensor B jumps or deviates from the model in operation (for sensor A Ford uses more than 500 kPa or below −100 kPa for 2 s).
c: Loose contact at connector or wire near the hot manifold
Sensing tube partly blocked (sluggish, jumping values)
s: Check engine light on
EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P047F.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Open
P047F.d: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. P047F means valve A stays open although it is commanded to close, detected by the flap's position sensor or by missing back pressure. On VW's 2.0 TDI and Audi's A3 TDI of 2009–12 the code appears with P0477, P048A–P048C and P0401: water and road salt corrode the flap shaft so the flap sticks; improved parts were introduced. As the flap drives the low-pressure EGR there, EGR flow is then too low.
c: Soot or carbon on the flap
Actuator or linkage faulty or unhooked
s: Check engine light on
EGR flow too low (P0401), higher NOx
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without effect, possibly louder exhaust

P0480.d: The engine module switches the radiator fan either through a relay, whose coil it pulls to ground, or with a PWM signal to a fan control module. The circuit is an output that CARB requires to be checked continuously. P0480 concerns the control circuit of fan 1. GM sets it for an open circuit – 200 kΩ or more with the driver off, 50 of 63 samples, above 11 V, MIL after two trips – and reports a short to ground or positive as P0691/P0692; Saab models on GM technology set it after 5 s (relay) or 1 s (PWM). FCA bulletins also name it with the warning lamp. Ford's OBD summaries do not contain the code. If the fan stops, the engine can overheat in traffic and the air conditioning weakens at standstill.
c: Fan relay (coil open) or fan control module faulty
Connector at fan or relay corroded, water ingress or pin pushed out
Control wire open or shorted to ground
Fan motor or fan assembly faulty
s: Check engine light on
Radiator fan does not run, or runs constantly
Overheating at standstill or in traffic
Air conditioning weak at standstill

P0481.d: The engine module switches the radiator fan either through a relay, whose coil it pulls to ground, or with a PWM signal to a fan control module. The circuit is an output that CARB requires to be checked continuously. P0481 concerns the second fan control circuit – depending on the design a second fan or a second speed stage; on GM and Saab, relays 2 and 3 switch the fans in series or parallel for low and high speed. GM sets it for an open circuit (200 kΩ or more, 50 of 63 samples, MIL after two trips) and reports shorts as P0693/P0694. Ford's OBD summaries do not contain the code. One fan stage then fails or runs constantly; cooling usually remains partly available.
c: Corrosion or water in relay or fan connector
Control wire open or shorted to ground
s: Check engine light on
One fan stage or fan not working, or running constantly
Temperature rises at standstill

P0482.d: The engine module switches cooling fan stages through relays, pulling each relay coil to ground. P0482 concerns the control circuit of the third stage or relay: with the driver off the line should sit at battery voltage through the coil, and the internal pull-up level means an open circuit (Saab ME9: more than 1 s, 10–18 V, engine running). On the GM-based Saab 9-5 of 2011 it is relay 3 (medium stage) of a two-fan network, with shorts reported as P0695/P0696. GM tables list P0482 only in fault groups; Ford's OBD summaries do not contain it. One fan stage then fails.
c: Fan relay 3 faulty (coil open) or not seated properly
Control wire open or high-resistance, corroded or backed-out pins
Relay coil supply missing (fuse, supply wire)
s: Check engine light on
One fan stage fails – temperature rises in traffic or when towing
Air conditioning weaker at standstill

P0483.d: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0483 checks the fan's function, not its circuit. With a speed sensor (GM viscous fans) commanded and actual speed are compared: GM's Duramax diesels of 2014–18 set it at more than ±500 rpm for at least 120 s, GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups of 2004–06 at more than 1000 rpm – MIL after two trips. Without a sensor Subaru (and the Saab 9-2X) judges indirectly: if coolant at 100 °C or more does not fall within 5 minutes at idle with the fan on, the code sets after two trips. Ford's OBD summaries do not contain it.
c: Viscous clutch worn or leaking, or its solenoid faulty – fan does not reach or leave target speed
Electric fan motor stiff or worn, or fan blocked
Fan speed sensor or wiring giving a wrong value
Radiator or condenser clogged, coolant low (Subaru logic)
s: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Constant fan roar, or temperature rise at standstill
Air conditioning weak at low speed

P0484.d: P0484 monitors the current drawn in the fan's load circuit: if it exceeds a threshold – blocked or stiff motor, shorted turns, a short in the load circuit – the code sets. This is only possible where the fan runs on a current-measuring semiconductor driver or fan module; plain relay circuits do not measure load current. Supplier patents (Bosch and others) describe current limiting or switch-off after a few seconds of overcurrent, ignoring the inrush current. No manufacturer table available to us lists P0484, so thresholds and warning-lamp behaviour remain open; CARB requires output components to be monitored.
c: Fan motor stiff (bearing damage) or blocked (foreign object, ice, bent blade)
Shorted turns or worn brushes in the fan motor
Short in the load circuit (pinched or chafed wire)
Fan control module faulty (wrong current measurement)
s: Warning lamp (depending on the maker)
Fan does not run, runs only briefly or at reduced power
Humming or grinding at the fan, possibly blown fan fuse
Overheating at standstill

P0485.d: P0485 monitors the supply or ground path of the fan or its control module – not the control line. It is typical of fans with their own module (PWM or LIN), which can report undervoltage or a missing ground. The high currents involved, often 20–60 A, make contact resistance at ground and supply connections and fuse holders the main cause. No manufacturer table available to us lists P0485, so thresholds and warning-lamp behaviour remain open; CARB requires output components to be monitored. The fan then runs intermittently or not at all.
c: Fan or fan module ground loose, corroded or broken
Fan fuse blown or fuse holder overheated or corroded
Relay power contact burnt – voltage drop under load
Connector at the fan scorched, water ingress
s: Warning lamp (depending on the maker)
Fan does not run or only intermittently
Overheating at standstill, weak air conditioning
Possibly burnt smell or discoloured connector

P0486.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensor B is depends on the maker: FCA uses it for the position sensor of the low-pressure EGR valve, GM's Duramax diesels for the coolant temperature sensor at the EGR cooler inlet. P0486 is its general circuit fault without a low or high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – makers report sensor B as P0407/P0408, P046E and P046F – so the description follows CARB's input component rules. EGR is then switched off or uses a substitute value.
c: Connector or harness to sensor B corroded or open (heat at the exhaust)
s: Check engine light on
EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change
Higher NOx

P0487.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The EGR throttle is a regulating flap ahead of the intake manifold on diesels: by closing partly it lowers manifold pressure below exhaust back pressure so that enough exhaust is recirculated, and it also helps filter regeneration and shuts off air at engine stop. It is usually a DC motor with position sensor. GM and Ford report this flap under P02E0 ff; no manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P0487 means its drive circuit is open or has a general circuit fault, detected by the output stage. The flap then stays open, so the EGR rate cannot be raised enough and filter regeneration may be blocked.
c: Connector at the flap corroded or loose, wire open
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power or limp mode possible
Shaking when the engine is switched off
Filter regeneration does not complete

P0488.t: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P0488.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The EGR throttle is a regulating flap ahead of the intake manifold on diesels: by closing partly it lowers manifold pressure below exhaust back pressure so that enough exhaust is recirculated, and it also helps filter regeneration and shuts off air at engine stop. It is usually a DC motor with position sensor. GM and Ford report this flap under P02E0 ff; no manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P0488 is its function check: the actual position reported by the sensor deviates from the target for too long, or the position signal is implausible – typically a coked, stiff flap or a broken gear. The flap then goes to its rest position or the engine enters limp mode, and the EGR rate cannot be controlled.
c: Flap coked by soot and oil mist (EGR plus crankcase ventilation)
Actuator gear or motor worn or broken
Position sensor in the flap faulty or implausible
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power or limp mode possible
Shaking when the engine is switched off
Filter regeneration does not complete

P0489.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0489 means the drive circuit of EGR valve A – solenoid, stepper or DC motor – is shorted to ground. GM's Duramax LML sets it at 0.5 Ω or less to ground for 3 s, GM's 2016 diesels after 96 of 120 samples, Ford diesels after 0.35 s, Saab's 2.0 TiD likewise – MIL after two trips. The valve is usually switched off; with low-side control a short to ground can keep it energised and open, causing rough idle or stalling.
c: Harness chafed at the exhaust with short to ground
EGR valve winding shorted to its housing
Water or corrosion in the connector
s: Check engine light on
EGR switched off
Rough idle or stalling if the valve stays open

P048A.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P048A.d: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048A means valve A is commanded open but its position feedback stays closed. On VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI of 2009–13 water and road salt corrode the shaft of the low-pressure EGR flap so it sticks; the code appears with P047F, P0477, P048B/P048C and P0401. The bulletins advise removing the flap and checking it moves freely, otherwise replacing it; improved parts were introduced. A closed flap keeps back pressure high.
c: Flap or flap shaft corroded or coked (stiff)
Flap actuator (motor or gear) faulty or too weak
Linkage between actuator and flap broken or misadjusted
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048B.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit
P048B.d: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048B is the general circuit fault or open circuit of valve A's position sensor or end switch. VW's 2.0 TDI of 2009–13 sets it with a corroded flap; on the 2015 engine it appears with P048E, P0475, P0477 and P0478 and the actuator with its integrated electronics is replaced; Bentley's V8 of 2023 reports it for bank 1 together with P048D. As the sensor sits in the actuator, a circuit fault often means actuator electronics.
c: Actuator with integrated position sensor faulty
Connector or wire at the underbody corroded, chafed or open
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048C.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P048C.d: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048C means valve A's position signal is electrically valid but does not match the commanded position or the learned end positions. It is documented only on VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI of 2009–13, together with P047F, P048A, P048B and P0401, caused by the corroded, sticking flap shaft. After replacing the actuator, the end positions must be relearned.
c: Flap or shaft corroded or coked (stiff)
End positions not relearned after replacement
Position sensor in the actuator drifting
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048D.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P048D.d: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048D means valve A's position signal is below its permitted voltage window – the signal wire is shorted to ground or the sensor's 5 V supply is missing. Bentley's Continental and Flying Spur V8 of 2023 report it for bank 1 together with P048B; the bulletin advises checking wiring and contacts, otherwise replacing the actuator and carrying out the basic setting.
c: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed at the underbody)
Position sensor or actuator faulty internally
5 V sensor supply open or shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048E.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P048E.d: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048E means valve A's position signal is above its window – an open signal pulled up, or a short to positive. VW's 2.0 TDI third generation of 2015 sets it together with P048B, P0475, P0477 and P0478: the flap is welded into the pipe, so with electronic faults only the actuator is replaced – an electrostatic-sensitive part that must be scrapped if dropped.
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048F.t: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P048F.d: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048F means valve A's position signal jumps, drops out briefly or changes faster than physically possible. Bentley stores sporadic sensor faults under the low code with a sporadic status instead. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows the sibling codes P048B–P048E and CARB.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the actuator connector
Wire broken by vibration or heat
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P0490.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0490 means the drive circuit of EGR valve A is shorted to battery voltage, or its output stage sees overcurrent. GM's Duramax LML sets it at 0.5 Ω or less to the supply for 3 s, GM's 2017 diesels at an H-bridge current above 8 A (160 of 200 samples), Ford diesels after 0.35 s – MIL after two trips. The output stage switches off for protection and the valve falls into its spring position, closed; EGR is off.
c: Harness shorted to a supply wire (chafing)
EGR valve with shorted turns (low resistance, overcurrent)
s: Check engine light on
EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change
Higher NOx

P0491.d: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; CARB requires the air flow to be monitored per bank. P0491 means too little air reaches bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1). VW and Audi calculate the injected air mass per bank from the front oxygen sensor's reaction during the cold-start phase; an Audi bulletin names values of 0.4–0.7 on both banks as too little together, often from coked air passages in the cylinder head. On VW/Audi V engines each bank has its own combination valve with a shared pump. Ford assigns the code to the bank 1 secondary air monitor; GM uses P0411 instead.
c: Secondary air passages in the cylinder head coked
Vacuum supply or changeover valve leaking, valve closes too early
Secondary air pump weak or water in the pump
Hose between pump and valve leaking or off
s: Check engine light on
No change in driving
Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Possibly no pump noise after a cold start

P0492.d: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; CARB requires the air flow to be monitored per bank. P0492 means too little air reaches bank 2 (the side without cylinder 1). VW and Audi calculate the injected air mass per bank from the front oxygen sensor's reaction during the cold-start phase; an Audi bulletin names values of 0.4–0.7 on both banks as too little together, often from coked air passages in the cylinder head. On VW/Audi V engines each bank has its own combination valve with a shared pump. Ford assigns the code to the bank 2 secondary air monitor; GM uses P0411 instead.
c: Secondary air passages in the cylinder head coked
Vacuum supply or changeover valve leaking, valve closes too early
Secondary air pump weak or water in the pump
Hose between pump and valve leaking or off
s: Check engine light on
No change in driving
Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Possibly no pump noise after a cold start

P0493.d: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0493 is documented only on GM petrol engines of 2004–06 with a viscous fan: the measured fan speed exceeds a limit that is hardly physically possible (about 6400 rpm), so it is effectively a plausibility check of the speed signal or a seized clutch at high engine speed. Two counts set it, with the warning lamp on the first trip – unlike P0495, which needs two trips. Ford, FCA and GM from 2014 were not found to use it.
c: Viscous clutch seized – fan runs rigidly with the belt drive
Interference or faulty signal from the fan speed sensor
Clutch solenoid or its control stuck at fully engaged
s: Check engine light on (first trip)
Loud fan roar at higher revs
Higher consumption, slightly less power

P0494.d: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0494 means fan 1 turns slower than commanded, judged from the speed reported by a LIN fan module or the clutch's speed sensor. GM's 2.0-litre turbo of 2020 uses a lower limit of about 59 % of the target at 750 rpm, rising to about 76 % at 2750 rpm and above. GM bulletins name an internal fan fault on the Equinox/Terrain 1.5 and water slowing the fan on the Hummer EV; Ford's 6.7-litre Super Duty uses it for the viscous fan and warns against replacing the clutch too quickly.
c: Fan motor or fan module faulty or worn (brushes, bearings, electronics)
Fan slowed or blocked (water, snow, ice, foreign object, distorted shroud)
Viscous clutch slipping or low on fluid, clutch valve faulty
High-resistance supply or ground, connector problems
Faulty speed signal (sensor or LIN feedback)
s: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Temperature rises at standstill or when towing
Air conditioning weak at standstill

P0495.d: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0495 mainly concerns viscous fans: with the fan commanded off it turns faster than the permitted drag speed, so the clutch does not release. GM thresholds: Duramax 2016 above 1500 rpm, Duramax 2018 above a calculated drag speed, petrol SUVs of 2004–05 above 1600 rpm without command – all with the warning lamp after two trips; Ford's 6.7-litre Super Duty uses it the same way. On GM's 2020 2.0-litre turbo with a LIN electric fan it means a reported speed above 2900 rpm.
c: Viscous clutch does not release (gummed, overfilled, seized)
Clutch solenoid or its control stuck open (short to positive, valve sticking)
Electric fan: module runs uncontrolled at full speed or relay sticking
s: Check engine light on
Loud fan roar even with a cold engine or at idle
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up

P0496.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0496 means vapour flows into the intake although the module is not purging – usually a purge valve that leaks or sticks open. GM and Saab seal the system after a cold start with the engine running; if tank vacuum exceeds 2491 Pa for 5 s, the code sets (fuel 10–90 %, MIL after two trips). Ford, which replaced its old code P1450 with P0496, also sets it for excessive vacuum during the leak test, for example with a vent valve stuck closed. Hard starting right after refuelling is typical.
c: Purge valve leaking or stuck open (charcoal dust in the seat)
Vent valve stuck closed or vent filter or line blocked
s: Check engine light on
Hard or long starting right after refuelling
Rough idle, rich fuel trim
Hissing vacuum when opening the fuel cap

P0497.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0497 is the counterpart of P0496: the module purges but sees too little or no purge flow, judged indirectly from fuel trim, idle control or tank vacuum – CARB requires missing purge flow to be detected. Code-specific use is documented only by Land Rover (5.0-litre V8) and in a GM fault group for systems with a sealed tank (Volt, ELR); standard GM and Ford systems use other codes, such as P0455. The canister is then not purged and saturates.
c: Purge valve stuck closed, does not open
Purge line off, kinked or blocked (check valve sticking)
Canister or vent filter blocked (e.g. after overfilling)
s: Check engine light on
Fuel smell around the car
Fuel nozzle clicks off early

P0498.t: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit Low
P0498.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and switched to ground by the module; P0449 (open), P0498 and P0499 form the newer code scheme for its circuit, used mainly by GM and Saab models with GM engines, while Ford uses P0446. P0498 means the control wire is shorted to ground: GM sees 0.5 Ω or less to ground with the driver off (20 of 25 samples), Saab below 2.6 V – MIL after two trips. The valve is then permanently energised and closed, so the tank is not vented and refuelling becomes difficult.
c: Vent valve control wire chafed against ground (underbody, tank area)
Corrosion or water in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Refuelling difficult, nozzle clicks off
Vacuum noise when opening the fuel cap

P0499.t: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit High
P0499.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and switched to ground by the module (GM scheme P0449/P0498/P0499; Ford uses P0446). P0499 means the control wire is shorted to positive: with the driver on the output stays high – GM sees 0.5 Ω or less to the supply, Saab above 4.6 V; MIL after two trips. The valve then cannot close, the system cannot be sealed, and the leak tests are suspended because they would otherwise report a large leak.
c: Control wire touching battery positive or the valve supply (chafed harness)
Vent valve coil with shorted turns, driver switches off
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set
Usually no change in driving

P049A.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels). P049A is the general flow fault of circuit B, used where the module does not separate too little from too much; CARB requires low and high flow to be detected, mostly by comparing air mass, manifold pressure or lambda with a model. No manufacturer document available to us uses P049A – GM has only position and actuator codes for its low-pressure EGR, FCA uses P049B. Low-pressure EGR is then switched off.
c: Low-pressure EGR valve sooted or sticking
Low-pressure EGR cooler or line blocked or leaking
Flap creating the pressure difference faulty
Sensors (air mass, pressure difference, position sensor B) implausible
s: Check engine light on
EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change
Higher NOx

P049B.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels). P049B means too little flow in circuit B: with the low-pressure valve open the module expects a change in fresh air mass or manifold pressure, or a modelled EGR volume, and the actual flow stays below the threshold. FCA documents it on the 3.0-litre EcoDiesel third generation in the 2020 Ram 1500, partly as a false trigger fixed by a software update; thresholds are not published.
c: Low-pressure EGR valve sooted or stuck closed
Low-pressure EGR cooler or line blocked
s: Check engine light on
Sluggish acceleration (FCA bulletin)
Higher NOx

P049C.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels). P049C means too much flow in circuit B – fresh air mass drops further than modelled, or EGR flows with the low-pressure valve closed; CARB explicitly requires a leaking valve to be detected. No manufacturer document available to us uses P049C; the closest is FCA's P045E for a low-pressure valve stuck open. Smoke, lack of power and rough idle follow, and low-pressure EGR is switched off.
c: Low-pressure EGR valve stuck open or not sealing (soot)
Position sensor B implausible (valve seemingly closed)
Leak between exhaust side and intake
Air mass meter reading too low
s: Check engine light on
Lack of power, black smoke
Rough idle or misfire, in extreme cases stalling

P049D.t: EGR A Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P049D.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P049D checks the learned zero point – the fully closed position – of EGR valve A. The module learns the position sensor voltage with the valve closed, at GM during the after-run following ignition off; if the learned value lies outside a window (GM 2018: 83.5–93.5 % of 5 V, GM 2016: 16.4–25.1 %) or the values scatter too much (GM Duramax LML above 30 %), the code sets – MIL after two trips at GM, immediately after learning at Ford. Usually soot at the seat keeps the valve from closing, or a new valve was not taught in.
c: Soot or deposits at the valve seat, valve does not close fully
Position sensor A faulty or characteristic shifted
New or cleaned valve not taught in, or wrong part
Position sensor circuit fault as the primary cause
s: Check engine light on
Usually no driveability effect
EGR possibly switched off, rough idle if the valve stays open

P049E.t: EGR B Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P049E.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels). P049E is the counterpart of P049D for valve B: the learned zero point of its position sensor lies outside the permitted window. GM lists it only in a fault group of its low-pressure EGR (whose position sensor is sensor C there, P044C/P044D), and in the 2016 calibration it is explicitly disabled; thresholds are not published. The description therefore follows GM's P049D strategy by analogy. Low-pressure EGR position control is then switched off.
c: Low-pressure EGR valve sooted, does not close fully
Position sensor of the low-pressure valve faulty or shifted
Harness or connector of the low-pressure valve
s: Check engine light on
EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change
Higher NOx

P049F.d: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve B is the second such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P049F is the general electrical fault of valve B. Audi uses it for sound flap 2 (2017–21, mostly sporadic, with P0475/P0477); on Bentley's Bentayga a commutator short in the flap motor caused by sludge triggers it – if the flap moves freely by hand, the actuator is replaced, otherwise the silencer or pipe.
c: Wire or connector at the actuator damaged
s: Check engine light on
Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P04AB.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit/Open
P04AB.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve B is a second electric purge valve, usually for the high-load purge line of a turbo engine, which purges to the compressor inlet when there is boost in the manifold (Ford patent). Many makers solve this path with one purge valve and passive check valves instead – Ford tests it as P04F0 – and then have no valve B. CARB requires every purge path to be checked. P04AB means the control circuit of purge valve B is open; the high-load path then does not purge. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the comparable purge valve A checks (for GM P0443/P0458/P0459).
c: Purge valve B connector loose or corroded
Coil of purge valve B open
Supply (fuse, main relay) or control wire open
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set
Usually no change in driving

P04AC.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit Low
P04AC.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve B is a second electric purge valve, usually for the high-load purge line of a turbo engine, which purges to the compressor inlet when there is boost in the manifold (Ford patent). Many makers solve this path with one purge valve and passive check valves instead – Ford tests it as P04F0 – and then have no valve B. CARB requires every purge path to be checked. P04AC means the control wire of purge valve B is shorted to ground: the valve stays energised and open, purging is uncontrolled and the mixture may run rich, especially at idle or after refuelling. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the comparable purge valve A checks (for GM P0443/P0458/P0459).
c: Control wire of purge valve B chafed against ground
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, rich mixture
Starting problems after refuelling

P04AD.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit High
P04AD.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve B is a second electric purge valve, usually for the high-load purge line of a turbo engine, which purges to the compressor inlet when there is boost in the manifold (Ford patent). Many makers solve this path with one purge valve and passive check valves instead – Ford tests it as P04F0 – and then have no valve B. CARB requires every purge path to be checked. P04AD means the control wire of purge valve B is shorted to positive: the valve cannot open and the driver may switch off for protection, so the canister is purged less under load. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the comparable purge valve A checks (for GM P0443/P0458/P0459).
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set
Usually no change in driving

P04AE.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Performance/Stuck Open
P04AE.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve B is a second electric purge valve, usually for the high-load purge line of a turbo engine, which purges to the compressor inlet when there is boost in the manifold (Ford patent). Many makers solve this path with one purge valve and passive check valves instead – Ford tests it as P04F0 – and then have no valve B. CARB requires every purge path to be checked. P04AE is the function check of purge valve B: flow, tank pressure or mixture react although the valve is commanded closed. It is documented on Subaru's FA24 turbo engines (Legacy/Outback 2.4, WRX, Ascent) as a known false trigger, fixed by an engine module software update – the bulletin advises checking the software before replacing the valve. Subaru publishes no thresholds.
c: Engine module software (Subaru FA24: known false trigger)
Purge valve B leaking or stuck open (charcoal dust, wear)
Purge lines swapped after a repair
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle or starting problems after refuelling
Often no change in driving (software false trigger)

P04AF.t: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Stuck Closed
P04AF.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve B is a second electric purge valve, usually for the high-load purge line of a turbo engine, which purges to the compressor inlet when there is boost in the manifold (Ford patent). Many makers solve this path with one purge valve and passive check valves instead – Ford tests it as P04F0 – and then have no valve B. CARB requires every purge path to be checked. P04AF is the flow check of the high-load path: under boost the module opens purge valve B, and if tank pressure or mixture do not react, the valve is stuck closed or the path is blocked – a FCA patent describes such a stepwise test. The canister is then not purged under boost and can saturate on load-heavy driving. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the comparable purge valve A checks (for GM P0443/P0458/P0459).
c: Purge valve B stuck closed (gummed, dirt)
Line to the compressor inlet off, kinked or blocked, check valve sticking
Engine module software or false trigger
s: Check engine light on
Fuel smell
EVAP readiness not set

P04B0.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Plug-in hybrids and range extenders with a sealed, pressurised tank have an electric valve in the vapour line between tank and canister. It is normally closed and opens before refuelling, so that the tank is depressurised – the filler flap is only released then – and refuelling vapour reaches the canister (Ford patent). P04B0 means the valve's control circuit is open. The valve then does not open, the tank cannot be depressurised and the filler flap may not open or only after a delay. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford reports its tank isolation valve as P2418/P2450 – so the description follows CARB and the component patent.
c: Connector at the tank valve (tank, underbody) loose or corroded
s: Check engine light on
Filler flap does not open after pressing the refuel button, or only after a delay
EVAP readiness not set

P04B1.t: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit Low
P04B1.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Plug-in hybrids and range extenders with a sealed, pressurised tank have an electric valve in the vapour line between tank and canister. It is normally closed and opens before refuelling, so that the tank is depressurised – the filler flap is only released then – and refuelling vapour reaches the canister (Ford patent). P04B1 means the control wire is shorted to ground, so the valve is permanently energised. With a normally closed valve the tank is then always connected to the canister: daily evaporation loads the canister and the tank cannot be sealed for the leak test. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford reports its tank isolation valve as P2418/P2450 – so the description follows CARB and the component patent.
c: Control wire chafed against ground (underbody, tank area)
s: Check engine light on
Possibly fuel smell
EVAP readiness not set

P04B2.t: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit High
P04B2.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Plug-in hybrids and range extenders with a sealed, pressurised tank have an electric valve in the vapour line between tank and canister. It is normally closed and opens before refuelling, so that the tank is depressurised – the filler flap is only released then – and refuelling vapour reaches the canister (Ford patent). P04B2 means the control wire is shorted to positive: the valve cannot be driven and does not open, the driver may switch off for protection. The tank cannot be depressurised before refuelling and refuelling vapour cannot reach the canister. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford reports its tank isolation valve as P2418/P2450 – so the description follows CARB and the component patent.
c: Valve coil with shorted turns (driver overcurrent)
s: Check engine light on
Filler flap does not open after pressing the refuel button, or only after a delay

P04B3.t: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Performance/Stuck Open
P04B3.d: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Plug-in hybrids and range extenders with a sealed, pressurised tank have an electric valve in the vapour line between tank and canister. It is normally closed and opens before refuelling, so that the tank is depressurised – the filler flap is only released then – and refuelling vapour reaches the canister (Ford patent). P04B3 is the function check: with the valve commanded closed, tank and canister must not equalise their pressure; if the tank pressure follows the canister, for example during purging or the leak test, the valve is stuck open. Ford checks its comparable tank isolation valve under P2450 via the pressure ratio between tank and canister. Daily evaporation then loads the canister, which hybrids with little engine running time cannot purge enough. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford reports its tank isolation valve as P2418/P2450 – so the description follows CARB and the component patent.
c: Valve leaking or stuck open (dirt, wear)
Line at the valve swapped or damaged
s: Check engine light on
Fuel smell
EVAP readiness not set

P04B4.t: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Stuck Closed
P04B4.d: Plug-in and some full hybrids keep the fuel tank sealed while driving, separated from the charcoal canister by a valve. When the driver presses the fuel button, the system opens the valve, lets the pressure escape into the canister and only then unlocks the filler door. A switch reports whether the door is open or closed, so that the tank can be sealed again afterwards. P04B4 is the function check of the valve between tank and canister: after the open command the tank pressure must move towards canister or ambient pressure, and if the rate of change stays below a threshold the valve counts as stuck closed (Ford patent). The tank then cannot be depressurised, the door does not unlock or only after a long delay, and during refuelling vapour cannot reach the canister. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.
c: Valve mechanically stuck (dirt, fuel in the valve, ice)
Vapour line kinked or blocked, liquid separator blocked
Tank pressure sensor sluggish or wrong
s: Check engine light on
Filler door does not open after pressing the button, or only after a long delay
Nozzle clicks off early when refuelling
Hissing or vapour when opening the cap

P04B5.d: Plug-in and some full hybrids keep the fuel tank sealed while driving, separated from the charcoal canister by a valve. When the driver presses the fuel button, the system opens the valve, lets the pressure escape into the canister and only then unlocks the filler door. A switch reports whether the door is open or closed, so that the tank can be sealed again afterwards. P04B5 means the door is not detected as closed and latched although the system expects it to be. Ford (C-Max and Fusion Energi 2013–17, MKZ hybrid) names a door not fully latched or opened by an accidental button press, with a message and the code in the third drive cycle; on the MKZ a door pressed during unlocking can confuse the latch – reset by pressing the button and waiting 12 s. Stellantis re-enables the check only after more than 16 miles and names a missing plunger or magnet, the cap tether blocking it, or a short to ground of the status line.
c: Door not fully latched after refuelling or opened by an accidental button press
Fuel cap tether blocking the plunger or latch
Plunger missing or loose, magnet or latch motor shifted or faulty
Status line of the door switch shorted to ground
s: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Fuel door open message in the instrument cluster
Door stays open or does not latch

P04B6.d: Plug-in and some full hybrids keep the fuel tank sealed while driving, separated from the charcoal canister by a valve. When the driver presses the fuel button, the system opens the valve, lets the pressure escape into the canister and only then unlocks the filler door. A switch reports whether the door is open or closed, so that the tank can be sealed again afterwards. P04B6 means that after a refuelling request and unlock command the switch still reports closed – the door does not open. According to the Ford patents the door is only released once tank pressure is below a threshold, so a valve that does not depressurise the tank has the same effect. On the 2026 Jeep Cherokee 1.6 hybrid P04B6 was stored without warning lamp as a software false trigger and is disabled by a reflash. Refuelling is then only possible via the emergency release.
c: Door latch, magnet or actuator blocked or faulty (ice, dirt, corrosion)
Door housing distorted after fitting, door jams
Tank cannot be depressurised (valve stuck closed, line blocked)
s: Filler door does not open despite pressing the button
Code often stored without warning lamp (Jeep)
Refuelling only via emergency release

P04B7.t: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P04B7.d: Plug-in and some full hybrids keep the fuel tank sealed while driving, separated from the charcoal canister by a valve. When the driver presses the fuel button, the system opens the valve, lets the pressure escape into the canister and only then unlocks the filler door. A switch reports whether the door is open or closed, so that the tank can be sealed again afterwards. P04B7 means the door switch signal drops out or jumps briefly – the state changes without the door moving, for example while driving. Typical are loose contacts or a broken wire at the bend into the door area. If the door state is unknown, the system leaves the tank open to the canister as a precaution and suspends the leak tests. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules and patents for the door switch.

Broken wire at the bend or grommet
Switch bouncing or worn, door seated loosely
s: Check engine light on
Fuel door open message although the door is closed, or missing when it is open

P04BA.t: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P04BA.d: Plug-in and some full hybrids keep the fuel tank sealed while driving, separated from the charcoal canister by a valve. When the driver presses the fuel button, the system opens the valve, lets the pressure escape into the canister and only then unlocks the filler door. A switch reports whether the door is open or closed, so that the tank can be sealed again afterwards. P04BA means the door switch signal is above its valid range – typically an open signal or ground line pulled up by the module, or a short to positive. If the door state is unknown, the system leaves the tank open to the canister as a precaution and suspends the leak tests. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules and patents for the door switch.
c: Signal or ground line open (pull-up drives it high)
s: Check engine light on
Fuel door open message although the door is closed, or missing when it is open
Door may not open or only after a delay
EVAP readiness not set

P04BB.t: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Circuit/Open
P04BB.d: On plug-in hybrids with a sealed, pressurised tank, pressing the fuel button (open request) starts a refuelling mode: the module opens the tank valve, releases the pressure into the charcoal canister and only then unlocks the filler door via an electric actuator (Ford patent). P04BB concerns the lock circuit: the module detects an open circuit in the output to the door actuator or its relay, which CARB requires for outputs. A separate lock output exists only on actuators that drive actively in both directions; spring-return actuators have only the unlock circuit. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's rules for input and output components and patents on the door actuator.
c: Open control wire or connector at the door actuator
Actuator motor or solenoid open internally
Actuator supply, fuse or relay not working
s: Filler door does not open or lock as commanded
Refuelling system message in the instrument cluster
Possibly check engine light

P04CE.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The code standard allows up to four EGR temperature sensors, A to D – for example before and after the cooler, or in the high- and low-pressure circuits; which is which depends on the maker. Sensor C is the third of them, usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot. P04CE is its general circuit fault, without separating low and high. FCA lists sensor C codes for its part 68142905A (Ram 2014 6.4 and 3.0 litre, Jeep and Dodge 3.6 Pentastar 2016) together with P040B, P0401 and P2457. Thresholds are not published. Without a valid temperature the EGR flow model is wrong, so the module uses a substitute value or switches EGR off.
c: Open or poor contact in signal or ground line
Connector or wire at the sensor corroded or worn by heat and vibration
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving (EGR on a substitute value or off)
Possibly EGR flow or cooler codes (P0401, P2457)

P04CF.t: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P04CF.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The code standard allows up to four EGR temperature sensors, A to D – for example before and after the cooler, or in the high- and low-pressure circuits; which is which depends on the maker. Sensor C is the third of them, usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot. P04CF is its plausibility check: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the model or other temperatures. Comparable checks on sensors A and B compare it after a long stop with coolant and intake air, or look for a temperature change during EGR operation (Ford diesels, GM diesels above 10 °C). No manufacturer document available to us uses P04CF; FCA lists P040B as the range code for its sensor C part.
c: EGR cooler or valve problem changes the real temperature
Comparison sensor (coolant, intake air, exhaust) faulty
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving (EGR on a substitute value or off)
Possibly EGR flow or cooler codes (P0401, P2457)

P04D3.d: The exhaust brake input is the driver's request for the exhaust or engine brake – a button or stalk on diesel pick-ups and trucks. On GM's 6.6-litre L5P, for example, the button must be pressed again after every start. GM uses the exhaust brake status as an enable condition for other emission monitors, which is why CARB requires the input to be checked. No manufacturer table available to us lists P04D3–P04D7; Hino's J08E truck engine checks P04D5 before its exhaust brake function test. P04D3 is the general circuit fault of the request input, used where the module cannot resolve the fault type further – an open circuit or, on bus-connected buttons, an invalid message.
c: Exhaust brake button faulty (contact, lighting board)
Open wire or connector between button and module
Fault in an intermediate module or bus message
s: Exhaust brake cannot be switched on, button lamp off or wrong
Possibly check engine light
More load on the service brakes downhill
