P0532.d: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0532 means the signal voltage is too low – GM below 3 % of the 5 V reference in 80 of 100 samples (about 2 s), from a signal shorted to ground, an open signal line or a lost 5 V reference; an empty system at ambient pressure usually still reads in range. The compressor is locked out. Warning lamp: GM type C without, Saab 9-4X with, Ford depending on vehicle.
c: Signal line open or shorted to ground
s: Air conditioning not cooling (compressor off)
Radiator fan running permanently
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0533.t: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P0533.d: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0533 means the signal voltage is too high – GM above 98 % of the 5 V reference in 80 of 100 samples, from a signal shorted to positive or an open sensor ground. Real very high pressure normally leads to a pressure cut-out within range instead. The compressor is locked out. Warning lamp: GM type C without, Saab 9-4X with, Ford depending on vehicle.
c: Signal line shorted to positive (e.g. 5 V reference)
Extreme overpressure (overcharge, blocked condenser, fan off)
s: Air conditioning not cooling (compressor off)
Radiator fan running permanently
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0534.d: P0534 reports too little refrigerant (a leak), not a sensor circuit: the module compares pressure or temperature in the circuit with a model, and the compressor is locked out for protection. FCA's 2020 Ram EcoDiesel sets it with the warning lamp; a software update fixed false setting. In GM's Volt, Spark EV and Lyriq the circuit also cools the traction battery – GM prescribes recovering and weighing the charge (Volt at least 800 of 950 g) and comparing the battery's refrigerant temperature sensors with ambient.
c: Refrigerant leak (condenser, joints, compressor shaft seal, service ports)
Traction battery chiller faulty (electric and hybrid only)
s: Air conditioning weak or not cooling
Compressor not engaging
Check engine light or high-voltage service message (electric)

P0535.d: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0535 is the general circuit fault; the compressor is usually locked out or run with a substitute value. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.
s: Air conditioning not or weakly cooling
Evaporator icing, airflow decreasing
Compressor cycling unusually

P0536.t: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0536.d: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0536 means the signal is valid but implausible – for example it differs from other temperature sensors after standstill, or does not drop after compressor engagement. Hella compares it with the cabin sensor with A/C off. Icing protection then works wrongly. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.
c: Sensor not seated correctly in the evaporator
s: Fluctuating or weak cooling
Evaporator icing
Compressor switching off too early

P0537.t: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0537.d: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0537 means the signal voltage is below its limit; with the usual NTC voltage divider that is a signal shorted to ground or a shorted sensor, read as implausibly warm – icing protection may then fail. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.
c: Condensate in the connector (leakage to ground)
s: Air conditioning not cooling
Possible icing
Compressor permanently on or locked out

P0538.t: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0538.d: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0538 means the signal voltage is above its limit – an open sensor, signal or ground line, or a short to positive; with an NTC that reads as implausibly cold, so the system assumes icing and usually locks out the compressor. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.
c: Connector off or corroded, wire open
s: Air conditioning not cooling (compressor locked out)
Vents blowing warm
Usually no check engine light

P0539.t: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0539.d: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0539 means short dropouts or jumps in the signal that do not add up to a lasting low or high fault – usually a loose contact or condensate corrosion at the connector; the compressor may switch off at times. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the connector
Broken wire from movement or chafing
s: Air conditioning failing at times
Cooling fluctuates
Usually no check engine light

P053A.d: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053A means its control circuit is open. GM's diesels of 2016 check it with 20 of 40 samples below 90 °C coolant without warning lamp, GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI in the Saab 9-5 with the lamp on the first trip – a difference even within GM. The heater then has no effect, which only matters in hard frost.
c: Fuse of the ignition supply blown
s: Often none, except in frost
Check engine light (depending on the maker)
In frost: oil leaks or loss of power from frozen ventilation

P053B.t: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Low
P053B.d: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053B means the low-side control line is shorted to ground, so the heater stays on regardless of command – it works in frost, but heats permanently. GM's diesels of 2016 check it with 20 of 40 samples below 90 °C coolant without warning lamp, GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI in the Saab 9-5 with the lamp on the first trip – a difference even within GM.
c: Heating element shorted to its housing
s: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Heater permanently on
Usually no change in driving

P053C.t: PCV Heater A Control Circuit High
P053C.d: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053C means the control line is shorted to positive: the driver cannot switch, the heater stays off, or the driver overloads and switches off. GM's diesels of 2016 check it with 20 of 40 samples below 90 °C coolant without warning lamp, GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI in the Saab 9-5 with the lamp on the first trip – a difference even within GM.
c: Heating element shorted internally (very low resistance, overcurrent)
s: Often none, except in frost
Check engine light (depending on the maker)
In frost: oil leaks or loss of power from frozen ventilation

P053D.d: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053D means the heater is electrically connected but its effect or current is implausible – current outside the target window, an overheated driver, or the expected warming does not occur. No manufacturer document available to us uses P053D; GM Europe checks this function under P052E. Frost protection is then uncertain.
c: Heating element aged (resistance outside 6–10 Ω, Saab reference)
Increased contact resistance at the connector
Partial short in the element (overcurrent, driver overheating)
s: Often none, except in frost
Check engine light (depending on the maker)
In frost: oil leaks or loss of power from frozen ventilation

P053E.d: P053E is the system code for crankcase pressure above an operating-point limit while the sensor itself is plausible. Normally the crankcase runs at a slight vacuum (GM: −1 to −5 inH2O). No manufacturer document available to us uses P053E – Ford reports the same under P051B (above 5 inHg at idle air flow). Excess pressure pushes oil past seals and the dipstick, carries oil mist into the intake and raises oil consumption. CARB requires the PCV system to be monitored.
c: Ventilation or oil separator blocked or frozen
Pressure regulating or PCV valve faulty
Increased blow-by (piston rings, turbo oil side)
Leaking vacuum reservoir or pump in the valve cover
s: Check engine light on
Oil leaks at seals, dipstick pushed out
Higher oil consumption, blue smoke

P053F.t: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 1
P053F.d: Petrol direct-injection engines often inject twice after a cold start, once late in the compression stroke, to heat the catalyst; this needs rail pressure within a window. P053F reports that the window was not reached often enough. Documented only by Ford's EcoBoost: over the whole cold-start phase it compares the time in the window with the phase duration against 0.70, once per cold start, with fuel level at least 15 % and the fuel sensors sound. The module then drops this mode, the catalyst lights off later; warning lamp after two trips. GM does not use P053F.
c: High-pressure pump weak or volume control valve sluggish
Pump follower or cam lobe worn
s: Check engine light on
Usually no noticeable driving symptoms
Possibly longer cranking or rough cold idle

P0540.d: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. Cummins checks it by the manifold temperature rise, Iveco by the battery voltage dip when the relay switches. P0540 is the general circuit fault of heater A without low/high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.
c: Heater relay faulty (contacts welded or burnt, solid-state relay shorted)
Power cable or ring terminal corroded or overheated, control connector
s: Check engine light on
Hard cold start, white smoke, rough cold idle
With welded relay: battery drained, heater stays on

P0541.t: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low
P0541.d: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. Cummins checks it by the manifold temperature rise, Iveco by the battery voltage dip when the relay switches. P0541 means the voltage in the monitored circuit stays too low – typically a control line or relay coil shorted to ground or open, so the relay does not switch and there is no preheating. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.
c: Relay control line shorted to ground (chafing)
Relay coil open or solid-state relay faulty
Connector at relay or module corroded
s: Check engine light on
Hard start in the cold
White smoke after cold start

P0542.t: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High
P0542.d: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. P0542 means the voltage stays high although the heater is commanded on – a control line shorted to positive or a relay that does not switch. A shorted or welded relay can also power the heater permanently; Ram recalled 6.7 L Cummins trucks because a shorted heater relay could start a fire. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.
c: Heater relay faulty (solid-state relay shorted, contacts stuck)
Control line shorted to positive, harness chafed on a power cable
s: Check engine light on
Battery drained when heater stays on
Burning smell or scorched wiring at the relay

P0543.t: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Open
P0543.d: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. P0543 means an open circuit at heater A – in the control line or relay coil, or depending on the maker in the power circuit or heating element itself. It is detected by driver diagnosis with the output off, by a missing voltage dip on switching on or by a missing temperature rise. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.
c: Broken cable, loose nut or ring terminal at the grid
Fusible link in the heater circuit
s: Check engine light on
Starting problems in the cold
White smoke or knocking while warming up

P0544.t: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0544.d: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P0544 is the general fault of bank 1 sensor 1. Ford's 6.7 L diesel uses it not as a circuit fault but for plausibility against an exhaust temperature model: after at least 6 h off it compares sensor and model over 200–400 s, a fault exceeding ±80 °C for 20 s, once per trip. GM's Duramax does not use P0544. The module then runs on a model value and may restrict filter regeneration.
c: Sensor aged or drifting, soot on the tip
Cable or connector damaged by heat or vibration
s: Check engine light on
Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning
Possible power reduction

P0545.t: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0545.d: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P0545 means the signal is below range: GM L5P below 142 Ω in 10 of 20 samples, GM LML below 0.65 V, Ford 6.7 L below 0.10 V for about 2 s, Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD below 0.1 V for 1 s. Usually a signal shorted to ground. GM USA uses two trips, GM Europe in the Saab one. The module uses a substitute value and blocks filter regeneration.
c: Signal line shorted to ground (chafed on the exhaust or bracket)
s: Check engine light on
Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning
Possible power reduction

P0546.t: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0546.d: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P0546 means the signal is above range: GM L5P above 922 Ω, GM LML above 2.21 V, Ford 6.7 L above 2.66 V for about 2 s, Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD above 4.9 V for 1 s. Most often an open circuit pulled up to the reference, otherwise a short to positive; live data then show −40 °C or the maximum. The module uses a substitute value and blocks filter regeneration.
c: Sensor element or internal lead open (vibration, heat)
Connector loose or corroded, broken wire
s: Check engine light on
Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning
Possible power reduction

P0547.t: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0547.d: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. Bank 2 sensor 1 exists only on V engines with a separate exhaust path per cylinder bank. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the thresholds known for bank 1 apply by analogy. P0547 is the general circuit fault, the counterpart of P0544.
c: Cable or connector damaged by heat or vibration
s: Check engine light on
Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning
Possible power reduction

P0548.t: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0548.d: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. Bank 2 sensor 1 exists only on V engines with a separate exhaust path per cylinder bank. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the thresholds known for bank 1 apply by analogy. P0548 means the signal is below range, usually a short to ground – for bank 1 GM uses below 142 Ω, Ford below 0.10 V.
s: Check engine light on
Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning
Possible power reduction

P0549.t: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0549.d: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. Bank 2 sensor 1 exists only on V engines with a separate exhaust path per cylinder bank. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the thresholds known for bank 1 apply by analogy. P0549 means the signal is above range, usually an open circuit or a short to positive – for bank 1 GM uses above 922 Ω, Ford above 2.66 V.
s: Check engine light on
Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning
Possible power reduction

P054A.t: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P054A.d: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054A means bank 1 was too far advanced. Mercedes (M276) traces it to slow oil pressure – 1 bar should be reached after about 3 s; Audi (Q5 3.2) and VW (Atlas 3.6 and 2.0 T) fixed it by software.
c: Oil pressure building too slowly when cold (oil level, viscosity, pick-up, pump)
Exhaust oil control valve sticking or screens clogged
s: Check engine light on, usually without noticeable symptom
Brief rattle on cold start
Rough idle while warming up

P054B.t: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
P054B.d: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054B means bank 1 stayed too far retarded. GM's test procedure checks oil level and pressure, a phaser sweep from 0 to 40° and the control valve at 7–12 Ω.
c: Oil pressure building too slowly when cold (oil level, viscosity, pick-up, pump)
Exhaust oil control valve sticking or screens clogged
s: Check engine light on, usually without noticeable symptom
Brief rattle on cold start
Rough idle while warming up

P054C.t: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
P054C.d: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054C means bank 2 of a V engine was too far advanced. Together with P054A it points to a common cause such as oil pressure or software (Mercedes M276, Audi 3.2).
c: Oil pressure building too slowly when cold (oil level, viscosity, pick-up, pump)
Exhaust oil control valve bank 2 sticking or screens clogged
Cam phaser bank 2 defective, locking pin
s: Check engine light on, usually without noticeable symptom
Brief rattle on cold start
Rough idle while warming up

P054D.t: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
P054D.d: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054D means bank 2 of a V engine stayed too far retarded. Only bank 2 points to that bank's valve or phaser; together with P054B to the oil supply.
c: Oil pressure building too slowly when cold (oil level, viscosity, pick-up, pump)
Exhaust oil control valve bank 2 sticking or screens clogged
Cam phaser bank 2 defective, locking pin
s: Check engine light on, usually without noticeable symptom
Brief rattle on cold start
Rough idle while warming up

P054E.t: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Lower Than Expected
P054E.d: Diesel only. At controlled idle the module compares the fuel quantity the idle governor needs for target speed with a model value; CARB sets the limit from 2013 at ±50 % of what a sound engine needs. Ford's diesel sets the codes beyond ±50 % for 5 s at standstill with warm engine and no filter regeneration; GM compares with 0.5 times a minimum map or 1.5 times a maximum map, 200 of 255 samples, type B. P054E means the engine holds idle with much less fuel than expected – more energy arrives than commanded, for example from injectors delivering too much, oil entering combustion or wrong injector correction codes.
c: Injectors delivering more than commanded (drift, coking, leaking needle)
Oil entering combustion (turbo seal, crankcase ventilation)
Rail pressure actually higher than measured
Wrong injector correction codes after replacement
s: Check engine light on
Rough or fluctuating idle
Blue or white smoke, knocking at idle

P054F.t: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Higher Than Expected
P054F.d: Diesel only. At controlled idle the module compares the fuel quantity the idle governor needs for target speed with a model value; CARB sets the limit from 2013 at ±50 % of what a sound engine needs. Ford's diesel sets the codes beyond ±50 % for 5 s at standstill with warm engine and no filter regeneration; GM compares with 0.5 times a minimum map or 1.5 times a maximum map, 200 of 255 samples, type B. P054F means the governor needs much more fuel than expected – the commanded quantity does not arrive or the engine has extra losses: clogged injectors, low compression, an EGR valve stuck open or additional load from accessories.
c: Injectors delivering too little (coked, high return flow)
Rail pressure actually lower, fuel supply (filter, air)
EGR valve stuck open or intake blocked
s: Check engine light on
Idle fluctuating or dropping
Smoke, higher consumption

P0550.d: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0550 is the general circuit fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Without the signal the engine can drop or stall at full lock, or the module raises idle permanently as a substitute.
c: Connector or wire open or corroded (splash zone at the pump)
Sensor or switch faulty, often also leaking
s: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Idle drops when steering at standstill, engine may stall
Raised idle (substitute value)

P0551.t: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P0551.d: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0551 means the switch reports high pressure where that is implausible – at speed there is hardly any steering. Mitsubishi sets it when the switch stays on through 10 drive-and-stop cycles; Saab's Trionic T8 after 600 s above 50 km/h, keeping raised idle as substitute and without warning lamp.
c: Pressure switch stuck closed or faulty internally
Signal line shorted to ground (ground means active)
Permanently high pressure (steering valve sticking, kinked line)
Vehicle speed signal faulty (Saab depends on P0501)
s: Permanently slightly raised idle
No load compensation when steering
Check engine light depending on the maker (Saab: none)

P0552.t: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P0552.d: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0552 means the signal of an analogue sensor is below range – an open 5 V supply, a signal shorted to ground or a faulty sensor, not low pressure. Toyota's 2007–08 Tundra set P0552/P0553 from a series sensor fault and replaced it with a revised part, with the warning lamp on.
c: 5 V supply open or signal shorted to ground
s: Check engine light on (Toyota)
Idle drops when steering at standstill
Possible fluid leak at the sensor

P0553.t: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P0553.d: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0553 means the signal is above range – usually an open sensor ground or signal pulled up, a short to 5 V or battery, or a faulty sensor; high pressure alone does not reach the limit (Toyota's sensor gives 4.05 V at 7000 kPa). Toyota's 2007–08 Tundra set it from a series sensor fault.
c: Sensor ground or signal line open
s: Check engine light on (Toyota)
Permanently raised idle or no load pre-control
Possible fluid leak at the sensor

P0554.t: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent
P0554.d: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0554 means the signal flutters. Mitsubishi sets it when the switch changes state at 10 Hz or more for 20 s above 50 km/h – no sound switch switches that fast. Causes are electrical (loose contact) as well as hydraulic: pressure pulsation from air or low fluid, or an unsteady pump.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at connector or wire
Low fluid or air in the system (pressure pulsation)
s: Idle speed jumping or fluctuating
Check engine light depending on the maker
Steering pump noise (air, low fluid)

P0555.d: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0555 is the general circuit fault without low/high distinction. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM splits circuit faults into P0557 and P0558. The module then assumes a substitute value and keeps vacuum available as a precaution.
c: Connector or wire to the sensor open or corroded
5 V reference disturbed (short at another sensor on the same reference)
s: Check engine light or brake booster warning
Stop-start inactive
Often no change in driving

P0556.t: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0556.d: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0556 means the signal is valid but implausible. GM compares it with intake vacuum (MAP) with the throttle nearly closed for over 3 s, filtered, type B with two trips. VW and Porsche also check the electric vacuum pump with it – Porsche compares the pressure at wake-up and 1.5 s later – so P0556 can also mean a weak pump or a leak. VW fixed false setting on the 2016–17 Jetta 1.4 T by software.
c: Leaking or kinked vacuum line or faulty check valve
Electric vacuum pump or its relay weak (hybrid, Porsche, turbo DI)
s: Check engine light and/or brake booster warning
Stop-start not working
Hard brake pedal with real vacuum loss

P0557.t: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P0557.d: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0557 means the signal voltage is too low: GM 2018 below 5 % of the 5 V reference in 320 of 400 samples (about 5 s), GM 2006 below 0.04 V; type B, two trips. Typical are a signal shorted to ground or an open signal or 5 V line. As low voltage means plenty of vacuum, the module would wrongly assume enough – so it uses a substitute value.
c: Signal line open or shorted to ground, connector loose or corroded
5 V reference open or shorted to ground
s: Check engine light or brake booster warning
Stop-start inactive
Often no change in driving

P0558.t: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P0558.d: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0558 means the signal voltage is too high: GM 2018 above 95 % of the reference in 2000 of 2400 samples (about 30 s), GM 2006 above 4.89 V; type B, two trips. Typical are a signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage or an open sensor ground. A real loss of vacuum does not set P0558 but P0556 or, depending on the maker, P050F.
c: Signal shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
s: Check engine light or brake booster warning
Stop-start inactive
Often no change in driving

P0559.t: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0559.d: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0559 means the signal jumps briefly – a loose contact or broken wire under movement – without staying out of range long enough for P0557 or P0558. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM catches dropouts through the sample counters of P0557/P0558. CARB requires input components to be checked for circuit faults.
c: Loose contact at the sensor connector (pin tension, corrosion)
Broken or chafed wire moving with the engine
s: Warning comes and goes
Stop-start inactive at times
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P055A.t: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit
P055A.d: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055A is the general circuit fault without low/high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – GM reports sensor B only as P055B–P055D. The module then uses a substitute value and may set cam phasers or valve lift to their base position.
c: Connector or harness to sensor B open, corroded or oily
Shared 5 V reference or ground disturbed
s: Check engine light on
Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted
Often no noticeable symptoms

P055B.t: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B Range/Performance
P055B.d: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055B compares sensors A and B with the phasers almost idle: GM sets it when they differ by more than 220 kPa below 1850 rpm, 80 of 100 samples. With the engine off, sensor B must read about atmospheric pressure (around 90 kPa); a GM bulletin for the 2014 2.5 L uses exactly that as a test. A real difference can also come from a clogged screen in the cylinder head feed.
c: Sensor A wrong (comparison fails because of A)
Real pressure difference: clogged screen, oil level or quality
s: Check engine light on
Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted
Often no noticeable symptoms

P055C.t: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B Low
P055C.d: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055C means the signal is too low – an open 5 V supply or signal line or a short to ground, not low oil pressure. GM sets it at a reading of 10 or less in 120 of 150 samples; real low pressure is P0524. The module uses a substitute value.
c: 5 V supply or signal open, connector loose or corroded
s: Check engine light on
Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted
Often no noticeable symptoms

P055D.t: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B High
P055D.d: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055D means the signal is too high – a signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage or an open sensor ground. GM sets it at a reading of 1000 kPa or more in 120 of 150 samples. Real excess oil pressure is reported separately, by Ford under P055F. The module uses a substitute value.
c: Signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V
s: Check engine light on
Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted
Often no noticeable symptoms

P055E.t: Oxygen Sensor Control Module System Voltage
P055E.d: Some engines use wide-band or NOx sensors with their own evaluation module that reports over CAN. That module measures its supply; outside its working range it sets P055E, and lambda control and the sensor diagnoses are suspended because no valid values exist. No manufacturer document available to us uses P055E – Ford's diesel monitors the comparable supply of its smart NOx/O2 sensor as P220A/P220B, below 8.5 V or above 16.5 V. CARB requires modules delivering emission-relevant signals to be monitored.
c: Fuse, relay or supply line to the sensor module
s: Check engine light on
Lambda control in open loop, possibly higher consumption
Further lambda or communication codes

P055F.t: Engine Oil Pressure Out of Range
P055F.d: P055F is a condition code: the measured oil pressure is above the maximum expected for speed and oil temperature – Ford, which documents it, calls it 'too high' and pairs it with P0524 (too low). Ford checks continuously for 5 s, only with plausible oil pressure, oil temperature and coolant sensors, as engine protection. Background are regulated oil pumps, whose control valve (P06DA ff) defaults to full pressure on failure. An electrically high signal is P0523 or P055D instead.
c: Oil pump control valve or variable pump stuck at high pressure
Sensor A reading high within range
s: Check engine light or oil pressure warning
Possible engine protection or power limit
Possible oil filter or seal leaks

P0560.d: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0560 is the general code without low/high split, used differently: Saab's 2002 9-5 transmission module sets it below 9 V or above 18 V for 1 s and goes into limp mode; Saab's EDC16 diesel only above 17 V (24 V charger or jump start); the GM-built 9-4X as a low-voltage code. GM's and Ford's engine modules use P0562/P0563 instead.
c: Jump start or charger at 24 V
Corroded or loose battery terminals or ground strap
s: Charge warning
Transmission limp mode (Saab)
Several modules report codes, starting problems

P0561.d: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. GM interprets P0561 as a difference between the module's two supply inputs: permanent battery and switched ignition supply may differ by at most 3 V, otherwise it sets after 50 of 63 samples. In the engine module that is type C without warning lamp, in GM's 9-speed transmission module type A with the lamp after one trip. Other makers use it for a fluctuating voltage.
c: Fuse, relay or line of the ignition supply (voltage drop)
Loose or corroded connector or ground at the module
s: Further voltage or communication codes
Transmission warning or check engine light (GM transmission module)
Sporadic dropouts of electrical functions

P0562.d: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0562 means the voltage is below its threshold with the engine running, when the charging system should deliver: GM 9 V or less at 400 rpm or more in 400 of 500 samples (about 5 s), type C. Saab's 9-4X modules may switch off temporarily below about 9 V. Many other modules, such as GM's brake module, set P0562 themselves.
c: Alternator or regulator delivering too little
Corroded terminals, ground straps or alternator cable
High quiescent current or many consumers at idle
s: Battery or charge warning lamp
Starting problems, dim lights
Codes in several modules

P0563.d: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0563 means the voltage is above its threshold: GM's engine module 18 V or more in 400 of 500 samples, type C; Saab's 9-4X above 18 V for 5 s. Typical are an overcharging regulator or a jump start or charger at 24 V. Saab's EDC16 diesel reports the same condition as P0560 instead.
c: 24 V jump start or fast charger
Missing battery or poor battery terminal (voltage spikes)
Alternator control line from the module (smart charging)
s: Charge warning
Bulbs burning out, flickering lights
Several modules switch off or report faults

P0564.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit
P0564.d: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0564 watches signal line A of the ladder: only voltage windows matching a button or no button are valid. GM sets it when the ratio sits in a gap between windows for over 0.5 s (2014: 2.5 s), the body module in the Saab 9-4X and 9-5 after an invalid voltage for 2 s. Cruise control is locked out for the ignition cycle.
c: Cruise or steering wheel switch faulty or dirty (moisture, worn contacts)
Clockspring or steering wheel connector with contact resistance
Supply or signal line to the body module open or shorted
s: Cruise control cannot be switched on or switches off
Cruise control locked out
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P056D.d: Diesels with SCR may have a separate module for AdBlue/DEF dosing (pump, heaters, dosing valve) talking to the engine module over CAN. It measures its supply; outside its window no safe dosing is possible, so dosing and SCR diagnoses are suspended and NOx rises, and if it persists the SCR warnings and power limits apply. No manufacturer document available to us uses P056D – Ford's diesel reports the dosing module supply as P21CB below 8.5 V and P21CC above 19 V. CARB requires SCR modules to be monitored.

P056E.t: Cold Start Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Performance
P056E.d: CARB requires every element commanded by the cold-start strategy to respond measurably in the commanded direction, with its own codes separate from the general monitoring of the same part. During catalyst heating the boost control is positioned deliberately – diesels close the variable turbine for load and heat, petrol engines open the wastegate so heat reaches the catalyst. P056E means boost control A (the first or only charger) did not follow its cold-start target. Its only documented user is Stellantis: the 2025 Ram 3500 cab chassis with 6.7 L Cummins lists it among codes that can light the warning lamp, fixed by a PCM software update; customers noticed hard cold starts and raised cold idle. Ford and GM do not use it.
c: Variable turbine or wastegate actuator stiff (coking, cold)
s: Check engine light on
Hard cold start or rough warm-up
Otherwise usually unremarkable

P056F.t: Cold Start Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Performance
P056F.d: CARB requires every element commanded by the cold-start strategy to respond measurably in the commanded direction, with its own codes separate from the general monitoring of the same part. During catalyst heating the boost control is positioned deliberately – diesels close the variable turbine for load and heat, petrol engines open the wastegate so heat reaches the catalyst. P056F is the same check for boost control B – a second charger on twin-turbo or sequential systems, or a second stage. No manufacturer document available to us uses P056F; the Ram 6.7 L with a single charger only lists P056E. The description follows CARB's cold-start rules.
c: Charger B actuator stiff or faulty
Vacuum or charge air line of charger B leaking
s: Check engine light on
Rough cold running
Otherwise usually unremarkable

CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0570 classically concerns the accelerate (plus) button. Ford's 2023 diesel uses it differently, only with adaptive cruise: the CAN message with the maximum acceleration request from the radar module to the engine module is faulty, checked every 10 ms, fault after 0.1 s. GM does not use P0570 (resume and accelerate share P0567).

Contact problem in steering wheel switch or clockspring

Cruise control locked out
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0571.d: Brake switch A is the brake light switch or its signal to the engine module. The module needs it to cancel cruise control and for brake-throttle override, stop-start, idle control and the shift interlock. As cruise control is simply switched off, CARB treats such faults as emission-neutral – usually without warning lamp. P0571 is the general fault, usually detected by plausibility: Saab's 3.0 TiD (Bosch) sets it when the car brakes three times from over 49 km/h to standstill at 1.6 m/s² or more without a switch signal; Bosch EDC16 then switches cruise control off. NHTSA found Hyundai and Kia setting P0571 with P0504 from misadjusted brake light switches. Ford and GM petrol engines use P0572/P0573 instead.
c: Connector, wire or brake light fuse
s: Cruise control cannot be set or switches off
Brake lights not working or permanently on
Possibly ABS/ESC warning (Hyundai/Kia)

P0572.d: Brake switch A is the brake light switch or its signal to the engine module. The module needs it to cancel cruise control and for brake-throttle override, stop-start, idle control and the shift interlock. As cruise control is simply switched off, CARB treats such faults as emission-neutral – usually without warning lamp. P0572 means the switch signal stays low – never pressed – although the car brakes. Ford petrol checks over 25 brake applications, Ford diesel over 40 decelerations; GM in the Saab 9-4X and 9-5 compares the input with the body module's message, 8 of 10 samples over 2 s. Cruise control is locked out; Ford shows only the wrench lamp.
c: Brake light switch faulty or misadjusted (not switching)
Brake light or switch supply fuse blown
Signal line open or shorted to ground, connector
s: Cruise control not working
Brake lights not lit (depending on cause)
Wrench lamp (Ford), no check engine light

P0573.d: Brake switch A is the brake light switch or its signal to the engine module. The module needs it to cancel cruise control and for brake-throttle override, stop-start, idle control and the shift interlock. As cruise control is simply switched off, CARB treats such faults as emission-neutral – usually without warning lamp. P0573 means the switch signal stays high – always pressed – although the car is not braking. Ford diesel checks over 40 accelerations, Ford petrol over 25 brake applications without warning lamp; GM in the Saab 9-4X compares the input with the body module, 8 of 10 samples over 2 s. Typical are a switch stuck closed, a pedal not fully returning or a short to positive. Cruise control is locked out.
c: Brake light switch stuck closed or misadjusted (pedal stop buffer missing)
Brake pedal not returning fully (floor mat, return spring)
s: Brake lights permanently on
Cruise control unusable

P0574.t: Cruise Control System Vehicle Speed Too High
P0574.d: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0574 is a condition code: cruise control is active, but road speed exceeds its upper limit or clearly exceeds the set speed – for example downhill when engine braking is not enough, or with an implausible speed signal. Cruise control is then switched off. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.

P0579.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Range/Performance
P0579.d: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. FCA uses two redundant lines with mirrored ladders: P0579 sets when signal 1 is outside its window while a button is pressed – for on/off it must lie between 0.235 and 0.353 V – and is active only while the button is held. Usual cause is oxidation at the six-pin steering wheel connector or the clockspring; the Jeep JK recall replaces the clockspring.

Cruise control locked out
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P057A.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit/Open
P057A.d: The brake pedal position sensor is an analogue 5 V sensor, usually Hall-type, giving the pedal position continuously instead of a switch – for brake lights, cruise control, stop-start, brake-throttle override and regenerative braking. GM (from about 2012) and Stellantis read it in the engine module, Saab's 9-4X and 9-5 in the body module; its learned rest position (about 1 V) must be relearned after replacement. P057A is the general circuit or open-circuit fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM reports an open circuit as P057C or P057D depending on the line, type A with one trip, and sets the pedal position to 0 %. Brake detection then relies on the brake light switch.
c: Connector at the sensor loose or corroded, pins pushed back
5 V reference, signal or ground line open
s: Check engine light on
Cruise control and stop-start inoperative
Possible power reduction

P057B.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P057B.d: The brake pedal position sensor is an analogue 5 V sensor, usually Hall-type, giving the pedal position continuously instead of a switch – for brake lights, cruise control, stop-start, brake-throttle override and regenerative braking. GM (from about 2012) and Stellantis read it in the engine module, Saab's 9-4X and 9-5 in the body module; its learned rest position (about 1 V) must be relearned after replacement. P057B means the signal is valid but the pedal does not move as expected or the rest position is wrong. GM rates pedal movement once per ignition cycle while driving at 8 km/h or more without throttle (fail below 0.40, pass above 0.80), type A, one trip. If the module sees the pedal slightly pressed, it cuts power – GM and Stellantis bulletins name misinstalled or wrongly learned sensors.
c: Sensor misinstalled or not learned after replacement
Contact fault on 5 V reference or signal causes wrong rest position learning
s: Check engine light on
Reduced power when accelerating
Cruise control and stop-start inoperative

P057C.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P057C.d: The brake pedal position sensor A is an analogue 5 V sensor giving pedal travel continuously; its rest position (about 1 V) is learned. GM reads it in the engine module from about 2012 and uses it as an enabling condition of transmission monitors – hence type A, warning lamp after one trip, unlike cruise control codes. On any circuit fault GM sets the pedal to 0 %, so brake detection relies on the brake light switch. P057C means the signal is too low – a short to ground: GM below 5 in 20 of 32 samples. GM bulletins for 2012–14 pick-ups and SUVs name connector X205 under the left defroster duct, with cruise, brake light and stability messages and reduced power.
c: Connector or terminals at sensor or inline connector (GM X205) loose, pushed back or corroded
Signal or 5 V reference shorted to ground
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor
s: Check engine light on (GM, one trip)
Cruise control, brake light or stability functions restricted
Reduced power when accelerating

P057D.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P057D.d: The brake pedal position sensor A is an analogue 5 V sensor giving pedal travel continuously; its rest position (about 1 V) is learned. GM reads it in the engine module from about 2012 and uses it as an enabling condition of transmission monitors – hence type A, warning lamp after one trip, unlike cruise control codes. On any circuit fault GM sets the pedal to 0 %, so brake detection relies on the brake light switch. P057D means the signal is too high: GM above 95 in 20 of 32 samples and calls this explicitly an open circuit – an open signal or ground line is pulled up. A short to 5 V or battery acts the same. 'High' means signal, not a fully pressed pedal. GM bulletins name connector X205 on 2012–14 pick-ups.
c: Ground or signal line open, connector X205 with poor contact
s: Check engine light on (GM, one trip)
Cruise unavailable, brake light or stability messages
Possible power reduction

P057E.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P057E.d: The brake pedal position sensor A is an analogue 5 V sensor giving pedal travel continuously; its rest position (about 1 V) is learned. GM reads it in the engine module from about 2012 and uses it as an enabling condition of transmission monitors – hence type A, warning lamp after one trip, unlike cruise control codes. On any circuit fault GM sets the pedal to 0 %, so brake detection relies on the brake light switch. P057E means implausibly fast signal jumps within the valid range: GM sets it at jumps above 11 in 5 of 20 samples. Brief interruptions can also make GM's engine module learn a wrong rest position – it then sees the brake pressed and cuts power; GM names fretting at the 5 V reference or signal.

Broken or chafed wire near the pedal
s: Check engine light on (GM)
Sporadic power reduction when accelerating
Cruise control cutting out sporadically

P057F.t: Battery A State of Charge Performance
P057F.d: P057F means the state of charge of battery A behaves implausibly or leaves its expected range – a performance code, not a circuit fault. Its documented use is on plug-in hybrids of the VW group: the 2025 Porsche Panamera E-Hybrid and Bentley Continental and Flying Spur set it in the high-voltage battery controller, which requests the warning lamp; both causes were software. CARB requires hybrids to monitor battery and charging performance. A use for a 12 V battery sensor was not found; GM and Ford do not list P057F.
c: Software of the battery controller (state of charge miscalculated)
State of charge not relearned after deep discharge, long standstill or disconnection
Faulty current or voltage measurement in the battery system
s: Check engine light on
Hybrid function restricted (less electric range or power)
State of charge display jumping

P0580.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Low
P0580.d: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0580 means signal line A is too low: GM at a ratio of 0–0.185 for over 2 s (short to ground or, depending on wiring, open circuit); FCA treats signal 1 below 0.216 V as circuit low. Work at the steering wheel involves the driver airbag.
c: Signal line shorted to ground (steering wheel wiring, clockspring)
Steering wheel or clockspring connector corroded or off
s: Cruise control cannot be switched on, indicator missing
Cruise control locked out
No check engine light

P0581.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit High
P0581.d: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0581 means signal line A is too high: GM at a ratio of 1.005–1.035 for over 2 s (short to power); FCA treats 4.706–5.0 V as circuit high. In FCA's recalls of the Jeep Wrangler JK (2007–2016), P0581 indicates a dusty clockspring, which is replaced. Ford lists it without warning lamp.
c: Signal line shorted to positive or ground open
s: Cruise control inoperative, on the Jeep JK possibly airbag warning
Cruise control locked out
No check engine light

P0582.d: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0582 concerns the vacuum valve circuit: an open circuit, checked with ignition on and cruise control active. Without current the vacuum valve stays closed – the safe state.
c: Connector at the servo loose or corroded
Vacuum valve coil in the servo open
Wire between servo and engine module open
s: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Cruise indicator goes out or flashes (depending on vehicle)
Usually no check engine light, code stored only

Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0583 means the voltage at the vacuum valve driver is too low – a control line shorted to ground or a shorted coil, so the valve could stay powered. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.

P0585.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A/B Correlation
P0585.d: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0585 means inputs A and B contradict each other although both voltages are valid – one reports a button, the other rest or another button. Documented only by FCA: a 2022 bulletin traces it to a SET+ button stuck by a badly seated trim, another names oxidised steering wheel contacts. FCA gives no thresholds; GM does not use P0585.
