P0587.t: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit Low
P0587.d: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0587 means the voltage at the vent valve driver is too low – the control line is shorted to ground, so the vent valve stays closed and the servo could hold vacuum; cruise control is therefore switched off, with braking safety from the dump valve. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.
c: Vent control line shorted to ground
s: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Cruise indicator goes out or flashes (depending on vehicle)
Usually no check engine light, code stored only

P0588.t: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit High
P0588.d: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0588 means the voltage at the vent valve driver is too high – a short to positive or a valve not drawing current. The vent stays open, the servo builds no vacuum and cruise control is switched off. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.
c: Vent control line shorted to positive
s: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Cruise indicator goes out or flashes (depending on vehicle)
Usually no check engine light, code stored only

P0589.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit
P0589.d: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0589 is the general fault of the second button input B. GM uses it only for one engine variant (LGW): the ratio lies in a gap between valid button windows for over 0.5 s. It is the counterpart of P0564 for input A.
c: Increased contact resistance shifting button voltages
s: Cruise or distance control unavailable
Cruise control locked out
No check engine light

P058A.d: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058A means the module reports an internal fault of its own over LIN. GM checks it every 250 ms above 9 V, without LIN faults and at outside temperatures of −20 to 50 °C. Battery data are then unreliable – stop-start is blocked and the alternator usually runs a fixed substitute voltage. Loss of communication is a separate U code.
c: Poor supply or ground at the sensor (loose terminal, corroded connector)
Sensor not relearned after battery replacement or disconnection
s: Check engine light on
Stop-start not available
No driveability problems

P058B.t: Battery Monitor Module Current Monitoring Performance
P058B.d: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058B concerns current measurement. In the sensor variant the module itself reports implausible current; GM's eAssist and stop-start engines compare it with their own reference and set it at 22 A difference in 160 of 200 samples. GM bulletins for the 2014–16 Malibu and Impala name a ground ring lying on the sensor's shunt or a loose terminal – current then bypasses the shunt.
c: Ground ring touching the shunt or loose
Fretting corrosion in the sensor connector, loose ground splice
Retrofitted loads grounded directly at the negative post
s: Check engine light, often sporadic
Stop-start inactive
Wrong state of charge display or battery warning

P058C.t: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Monitoring Performance
P058C.d: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058C concerns temperature measurement, which stands in for battery temperature in the charge voltage. GM compares two raw temperature values and sets it above 10 °C difference in 8 of 10 samples, also on values stored during sleep. FCA uses it too: on a 2016 Dodge Journey a blown 10 A fuse in the module supply set P058C with the battery light.
c: Heat from contact resistance at the terminal
s: Check engine light on
Battery warning light (FCA case)
Stop-start inactive

P058D.t: Battery Monitor Module Voltage Monitoring Performance
P058D.d: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058D compares the module's voltage with the system voltage measured by the engine module itself: GM sets it above 5 V difference in 32 of 40 samples, its eAssist and stop-start engines at 2 V in 160 of 200. GM bulletins for the 2014–18 Malibu and Impala name loose terminals, ground faults and an overheating dual battery isolation module – with smoke or a burning smell.
c: Loose or corroded terminal, ground ring or sensor connector
Poor ground, loose splice, fault at the dual battery isolation module
s: Check engine light on
Stop-start inactive, battery or charge warning
Rarely burning smell in the engine bay (GM)

P058E.t: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too High
P058E.d: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058E means the module reports a temperature above its plausible range: GM sets it above 120 °C in 4 of 5 samples. As the outside temperature must lie between −20 and 50 °C, such a value points to a sensor fault or strong local heating from contact resistance at the terminal or shunt. It suspends P058C.
c: High contact resistance at terminal or ground ring heating the sensor
Missing battery heat shield after repair
s: Check engine light on
Stop-start inactive
Possibly discoloured or scorched terminal

P058F.t: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too Low
P058F.d: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058F means the module reports a temperature below its plausible range: GM sets it below −43 °C in 4 of 5 samples, but only with an outside temperature above −20 °C – so the value is physically implausible, usually an open sensing circuit or faulty sensor. It suspends P058C; the charge voltage then lacks correct temperature compensation.
c: Battery sensor faulty internally (temperature element open)
Sensor software or initialisation after power loss
Supply or connector problem at the sensor
s: Check engine light on
Stop-start not available
No driveability problems

P0590.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Stuck
P0590.d: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0590 means input B reports a pressed button permanently – a button stuck or a voltage hanging in one window. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0590; FCA reports a stuck button with its own code P1593 or with P0585, and GM has no stuck code for input B. Counterpart of P0578 for input A.
c: Button stuck mechanically (trim, dirt, spilled drink)
Short in the button block's resistor ladder
Moisture or corrosion in the switch
s: Cruise control cannot be engaged, button noticeably sticking
Cruise control locked out
No check engine light

P0591.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Range/Performance
P0591.d: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0591 means signal 2 is outside its window while a button is pressed – for on/off FCA expects 0.900 V and sets the code above 0.980 V, active only while the button is held. Usual cause is oxidation at the six-pin steering wheel connector; in the Jeep Wrangler JK recalls it indicates a faulty clockspring. GM does not use P0591.
c: Oxidised steering wheel connector at clockspring or column module
s: Cruise control working sporadically or not at all
Cruise control locked out
No check engine light

P0592.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Low
P0592.d: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0592 means signal line B is too low: GM (engine variant LGW) at a ratio of 0–0.185 for over 2 s, a short to ground or open circuit; FCA treats signal 2 below 0.784 V as circuit low.
c: Line B shorted to ground (steering wheel, clockspring)
s: Cruise control and distance or mode buttons inoperative
Cruise control locked out
No check engine light

P0593.t: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit High
P0593.d: Cruise control buttons form a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage window. FCA uses two lines with offset windows – signal 1 is input A, signal 2 input B – and both must report the same button; GM evaluates the ratio to the reference. Any fault locks out cruise control; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, and GM and Ford set these codes without warning lamp. P0593 means signal line B is too high: GM at a ratio of 1.005–1.035 for over 2 s (short to power), FCA above 4.706 V with about 4.54 V at rest. In FCA's Jeep Wrangler JK recalls it is a typical sign of a dusty clockspring.
c: Line B shorted to positive or ground open
s: Cruise control inoperative, possibly airbag warning (Jeep JK)
Cruise control locked out
No check engine light

P0594.d: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0594 concerns the servo control or supply circuit: an open circuit. Where the servo is fed through the cruise contact of the brake light switch, braking interrupts this supply on purpose, so the brake switch and its wiring are typical causes and brake lights may be affected too. No manufacturer document available to us describes P0594 in detail.
c: Brake light switch (cruise contact) faulty or misadjusted
Supply line open or shorted to ground
s: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Usually no check engine light, code stored only
Possibly brake light problem as well (shared switch)

P0595.t: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Low
P0595.d: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0595 means the voltage in the servo supply or control circuit is too low – a short to ground or a missing 12 V source. As this supply feeds both valves, it is checked before P0583 or P0587. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.
c: Supply line from brake switch to servo shorted to ground
s: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Cruise indicator goes out or flashes (depending on vehicle)
Usually no check engine light, code stored only

P0596.t: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit High
P0596.d: Older engines without electronic throttle use a vacuum cruise servo on the throttle cable: a vacuum valve (closed when unpowered) opens the throttle with intake vacuum, a vent valve (open when unpowered) holds or releases it, and a dump valve fed through the brake switch vents it when braking. Where the engine module drives these valves, it checks each circuit and switches cruise off; CARB treats this as emission-neutral, usually without warning lamp. P0596 means the voltage in the servo supply or control circuit is too high, for example a short to positive keeping supply on while braking – safety-relevant, because the brake switch cut-off could then fail; cruise control is locked out. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.
c: Servo supply line shorted to positive
s: Cruise control cannot be engaged or switches off
Cruise indicator goes out or flashes (depending on vehicle)
Usually no check engine light, code stored only

P0597.d: A map-controlled thermostat is a wax thermostat with a built-in heating resistor (Valeo: about 10 Ω). Unheated it opens late, for hot running at part load; the engine module heats it by map under full load or towing so it opens earlier. CARB requires the thermostat to be monitored and the heater circuit counts as an output component. GM switches it to ground with a low-side driver and checks it every second, fault after 15 of 30 samples, type B; Hyundai/Kia/Genesis and VW/Audi use the codes as well. P0597 means the heater circuit is open – GM above 200 kΩ with the driver off. The thermostat then only works through its wax and opens late, so coolant runs hotter under load; Audi's 4.2 FSI also limits engine speed. Genesis (G80/G90 3.3 T, 3.8) replaced thermostats from an early production lot.
c: Heating resistor in the thermostat open
Connector at the thermostat loose or corroded, coolant in the connector
Broken wire or missing supply (fuse, relay)
s: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Coolant temperature higher than usual under load
Audi/VW: coolant warning and engine speed limit possible

P0598.d: A map-controlled thermostat is a wax thermostat with a built-in heating resistor (Valeo: about 10 Ω). Unheated it opens late, for hot running at part load; the engine module heats it by map under full load or towing so it opens earlier. CARB requires the thermostat to be monitored and the heater circuit counts as an output component. GM switches it to ground with a low-side driver and checks it every second, fault after 15 of 30 samples, type B; Hyundai/Kia/Genesis and VW/Audi use the codes as well. P0598 means the control line is shorted to ground – GM detects 0.5 Ω with the driver off. With a low-side driver the heater then stays on permanently and the thermostat opens early, so the engine runs cool; Kia's Cadenza bulletins list it with P0128 and replace the thermostat.
c: Internal short in thermostat or heater, coolant in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Engine slow to reach operating temperature (possibly P0128)
Weak cabin heating in winter, higher consumption

P0599.d: A map-controlled thermostat is a wax thermostat with a built-in heating resistor (Valeo: about 10 Ω). Unheated it opens late, for hot running at part load; the engine module heats it by map under full load or towing so it opens earlier. CARB requires the thermostat to be monitored and the heater circuit counts as an output component. GM switches it to ground with a low-side driver and checks it every second, fault after 15 of 30 samples, type B; Hyundai/Kia/Genesis and VW/Audi use the codes as well. P0599 means a short to positive or a shorted heating resistor – GM detects it with the driver on, when it cannot pull the line to ground. The heater has no effect, coolant runs hotter under load; Audi's 4.2 FSI reports it with P2181, shows the coolant warning and limits engine speed.
c: Heating resistor in the thermostat shorted
Coolant or corrosion in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Higher coolant temperature under load
Coolant warning and engine speed limit (Audi)

P059A.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit
P059A.d: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. A separately evaluated position sensor, as these titles assume, is described in Ford patents (Hall sensor on the motor or sensor on the linkage). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: today the sensor sits inside the LIN actuator, whose faults appear as P059F/P05AE, P05A1/P05B0 or U0284/U0285. Without position feedback the shutter is usually driven open. P059A (shutter A) is the general circuit fault of the position sensor – signal missing or wire open, without low/high split.
c: Position sensor in the actuator faulty (replaced as a unit)
Actuator connector corroded or with water ingress
Wire open in the front bumper harness (accident, rodents)
s: Check engine light on
Shutter stays in one position (usually open) or does not react
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up in winter

P059B.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P059B.d: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. A separately evaluated position sensor, as these titles assume, is described in Ford patents (Hall sensor on the motor or sensor on the linkage). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: today the sensor sits inside the LIN actuator, whose faults appear as P059F/P05AE, P05A1/P05B0 or U0284/U0285. Without position feedback the shutter is usually driven open. P059B (shutter A) means the signal is electrically valid but does not match the commanded position or learned travel – GM covers such deviations under P059F/P05AE instead.
c: Louvres blocked (ice, snow, debris, bent bracket) – sensor correct, position wrong
Position sensor in the actuator drifting or worn
Basic setting not learned after replacement
Shaft or linkage between motor and louvres broken
s: Check engine light on
Shutter stays in one position (usually open) or does not react
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up in winter

P059C.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit High
P059C.d: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. A separately evaluated position sensor, as these titles assume, is described in Ford patents (Hall sensor on the motor or sensor on the linkage). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: today the sensor sits inside the LIN actuator, whose faults appear as P059F/P05AE, P05A1/P05B0 or U0284/U0285. Without position feedback the shutter is usually driven open. P059C (shutter A) means the signal is above its valid range – usually an open ground or signal line pulled up, or a short to 5 V or battery; high refers to the signal, not the louvre position.
c: Signal shorted to supply or ground line open
Connector corroded or with water ingress
Position sensor in the actuator faulty internally
s: Check engine light on
Shutter stays in one position (usually open) or does not react
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up in winter

P059D.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit Low
P059D.d: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. A separately evaluated position sensor, as these titles assume, is described in Ford patents (Hall sensor on the motor or sensor on the linkage). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: today the sensor sits inside the LIN actuator, whose faults appear as P059F/P05AE, P05A1/P05B0 or U0284/U0285. Without position feedback the shutter is usually driven open. P059D (shutter A) means the signal is below its valid range – a signal shorted to ground or an open 5 V reference or signal line.
c: Signal shorted to ground or 5 V reference open
Bumper harness chafed or damaged (accident, parking knock)
Position sensor in the actuator faulty
s: Check engine light on
Shutter stays in one position (usually open) or does not react
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up in winter

P059E.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P059E.d: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. A separately evaluated position sensor, as these titles assume, is described in Ford patents (Hall sensor on the motor or sensor on the linkage). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: today the sensor sits inside the LIN actuator, whose faults appear as P059F/P05AE, P05A1/P05B0 or U0284/U0285. Without position feedback the shutter is usually driven open. P059E (shutter A) means the signal briefly drops out or jumps out of range without staying low or high – usually a loose contact.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the actuator connector
Broken wire in the front bumper harness
Position sensor in the actuator (wear, electronics)
s: Check engine light on
Shutter stays in one position (usually open) or does not react
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up in winter

P059F.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Performance/Stuck Off
P059F.d: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. P059F compares commanded and reached position. GM checks it in two stages – detection, then five clearing attempts – type B, two trips; Ford's 3.0 L diesel at over 6° deviation in operation or 20° when learning fully open. 'Stuck off' means stuck closed at Toyota (failure type 73) and Nissan; GM and Ford use P059F for any deviation. Typical are ice, snow, debris or a bent bracket – a closed shutter can make the engine run hot in traffic.
c: Louvres blocked by ice, snow or debris
Bent bracket or bumper part blocking the louvres
Actuator, gear or shaft faulty (shutter stays closed)
Louvres unhooked or rubbing on horn or intake duct
s: Check engine light on
Shutter not opening: engine temperature rises in traffic, fan running often
Often after frost, gone after thawing

P05A0.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Stuck On
P05A0.d: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. P05A0 is the counterpart of P059F: at Toyota failure type 72 means the actuator stuck open, 74 slipping; VW, Audi and Mazda use it for sticking in general (Mazda after up to three clearing cycles). GM and Ford do not use it. An open shutter does not harm the engine but costs drag and warm-up time. Several fixes were software updates (Mazda, Audi Q7, VW Jetta); Audi's 2022–24 A3 limits top speed to 100 mph with a shutter fault.
c: Debris or ice holding the louvres open or blocking them
Engine module or actuator software setting the code too early
s: Check engine light on
Grille shutter warning (Toyota, Audi), speed limit (Audi)
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up

P05A1.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance
P05A1.d: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. P05A1 checks whether the shutter reaches its end stops (fully closed and open), which serve as reference for the position sensor in the self-learning run. Ford's 3.0 L diesel sets it at deviations above 40° when learning closed, 20° when learning open or 20° in operation, after 10 s; a Ford patent detects the stop by stall current and requests recalibration. GM, Toyota and VW do not use it.
c: Louvres not reaching the stop (ice, debris, bent louvres or bracket)
Actuator or gear weak, linkage worn
Misassembled or not learned after replacement
Position sensor in the actuator faulty
s: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Shutter not opening or closing fully
Possibly higher engine temperature or consumption

P05A2.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit/Open
P05A2.d: An active grille shutter closes louvres in the grille to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators (Ford 3.0 L diesel, Toyota) check their own coil and supply and report over LIN; simpler ones (VW 1.8 T) have their own supply and a control line from the engine module. GM uses none of P05A2–P05A8. A fault usually only costs fuel and warm-up time. P05A2 concerns the control or motor coil circuit. Ford's 3.0 L diesel reports an open and a shorted coil under it, checked by the actuator at the start and 500 ms after each movement, fault after 10 s. Toyota uses P05A2 as a collective code with a failure-type byte for short to ground, short to positive, open or stuck.
c: Actuator motor coil open or shorted
Connector corroded or damaged (front bumper, splash water, stone chips)
s: Check engine light on
Shutter not moving (usually open)
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up

P05A3.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P05A3.d: An active grille shutter closes louvres in the grille to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators (Ford 3.0 L diesel, Toyota) check their own coil and supply and report over LIN; simpler ones (VW 1.8 T) have their own supply and a control line from the engine module. GM uses none of P05A2–P05A8. A fault usually only costs fuel and warm-up time. P05A3 means the control signal or response is implausible – the actuator does not react correctly. VW's 2014–16 Golf and Jetta 1.8 T set it with the warning lamp, often together with P05A0: first check for blockage by ice, snow, dirt or accident damage and drive to 80 °C, then the actuator's supply and control line; faulty actuator software was fixed by a new part.
c: Shutter blocked (ice, snow, dirt, accident damage)
Actuator with faulty software or defective
Control line or connector with contact resistance
Insufficient supply or ground at the actuator
s: Check engine light on
Shutter not moving or moving incompletely, often also P05A0
Slightly higher consumption

P05A4.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit High
P05A4.d: An active grille shutter closes louvres in the grille to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators (Ford 3.0 L diesel, Toyota) check their own coil and supply and report over LIN; simpler ones (VW 1.8 T) have their own supply and a control line from the engine module. GM uses none of P05A2–P05A8. A fault usually only costs fuel and warm-up time. P05A4 means the control circuit voltage is too high – a control line shorted to positive or a driver unable to pull it to ground. In this family high comes before low. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. Ford reports coil shorts under P05A2, Toyota with a failure-type byte.
c: Control line shorted to positive (front harness)
Water or corrosion in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Shutter not moving (usually open)
Slightly higher consumption, longer warm-up

P05A5.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Low
P05A5.d: An active grille shutter closes louvres in the grille to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators (Ford 3.0 L diesel, Toyota) check their own coil and supply and report over LIN; simpler ones (VW 1.8 T) have their own supply and a control line from the engine module. GM uses none of P05A2–P05A8. A fault usually only costs fuel and warm-up time. P05A5 means the control circuit voltage is too low – typically the control line shorted to ground; the actuator cannot be driven and stays put or opens. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. Toyota reports a short to ground as P05A2 with failure type 11.
c: Control line shorted to ground (chafing, accident)
s: Check engine light on

P05B8.d: After a crash the restraint control module tells the engine module that airbags or belt tensioners have fired; the engine module then cuts the fuel pump (Ford: until the ignition is cycled) and possibly the engine. P05C6 means the signal jumps faster than physically possible or drops out briefly – usually a loose contact or chafed wire; with digital sensors, corrupted messages.
c: Air or vapour bubbles at the sensor
s: Check engine light or warning (depending on the maker)
Coolant pressure or leak warning unavailable
Usually no change in driving

P05C7.d: The economy mode switch selects a fuel-saving mode (flatter pedal map, earlier upshifts, sometimes reduced A/C). It is usually a resistor ladder with 5 V reference read by the engine module; CARB names a driver-selectable eco mode as an off-cycle technology whose use must be counted. GM reports the same switch with its own codes P159F/P15A0, type B with warning lamp after two trips; P05C7–P05CA appear in no manufacturer document available to us. P05C7 means the switch circuit is open; eco mode cannot be selected and the vehicle runs in normal mode.
c: Wire or connector to the switch open
s: Eco mode not selectable
Eco indicator not working
Vehicle runs in normal mode

P05C8.d: The economy mode switch selects a fuel-saving mode (flatter pedal map, earlier upshifts, sometimes reduced A/C). It is usually a resistor ladder with 5 V reference read by the engine module; CARB names a driver-selectable eco mode as an off-cycle technology whose use must be counted. GM reports the same switch with its own codes P159F/P15A0, type B with warning lamp after two trips; P05C7–P05CA appear in no manufacturer document available to us. P05C8 means the signal is in range but implausible – between valid ladder steps or permanently pressed; GM accepts a press only for 0.094–1.5 s.
c: Contact resistance or corrosion shifting the voltage step
s: Eco mode switching unintentionally or not at all
Indicator flickering or off
Usually no check engine light

c: Signal or reference line shorted to ground
Shared 5 V reference loaded by another sensor
s: Eco mode not selectable
Eco indicator not working
Vehicle runs in normal mode

P05CA.d: The economy mode switch selects a fuel-saving mode (flatter pedal map, earlier upshifts, sometimes reduced A/C). It is usually a resistor ladder with 5 V reference read by the engine module; CARB names a driver-selectable eco mode as an off-cycle technology whose use must be counted. P05CA means the switch circuit voltage is too high – a short to positive or, with a resistor ladder, an open switch ground pulling the signal to the 5 V reference; GM's equivalent is P15A0. GM's test values: reference 4.8–5.2 V, signal at rest 0.06–0.25 V.
s: Eco mode not selectable
Eco indicator not working
Vehicle runs in normal mode

P05CB.d: P05CB means a control module has found that installed hardware does not match the vehicle configuration – a wrong variant or part number, an unprogrammed replacement module, or messages from another vehicle type. No admissible manufacturer document available to us uses P05CB. CARB requires a calibration verification number showing that emission software is valid for the vehicle, but no hardware code. Ford reports configuration and compatibility faults under P0610 (vehicle options) and P0630 (VIN not programmed or incompatible) instead. Typical cause is a replaced module or battery that was not matched or programmed.
c: Replacement module or battery with wrong part number or for another variant
Module not programmed or configured after replacement
s: Power limitation possible
Wrench or powertrain warning lamp
Further functions possibly disabled

P05CC.t: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 1
P05CC.d: During catalyst heating after a cold start the engine module commands a specific cam phaser position for more residual gas and exhaust heat; CARB requires this to be monitored under codes separate from the normal cam codes. These 'performance' codes are GM's current form (since about 2015/16; older GM engines and Ford use the direction codes P052A ff and P054A ff): fault when commanded and actual position differ by more than 4° or 6° once the target is stable. P05CC watches intake camshaft A on bank 1 – the cold-start counterpart of P0011. GM's 3.0 L twin turbo sets it above 4°, 60 of 100 samples, type B; the 2.0 L turbo in the Envision above 6° as type A after one trip. A GM bulletin for the 2024–25 Traverse, Enclave and Acadia (2.5 L turbo, electric phaser) names a damaged phaser motor with rattle, together with P0011/P0016.
c: Insufficient cold oil supply: wrong viscosity, low level, worn oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Phaser worn or lock pin not releasing; on electric phasers a damaged phaser motor
s: Check engine light on (GM mostly after two trips)
Often no noticeable symptoms, possibly rough cold idle
Rattle from the timing drive (GM electric phaser)

GM's 3.0 L twin turbo sets it above 4° in 150 of 200 samples, type B, two trips; GM states it is the same type of diagnosis as P0021.

P05D0.t: Driver Mode Select Switch A Circuit
P05D0.d: The driver mode select switch (tour, sport, eco, snow, off-road, towing) changes engine and transmission maps such as shift points, pedal map and cylinder deactivation, so CARB requires it to be monitored as an input. GM reads switch A as an eight-position resistor ladder in the body module and sets P05D1–P05D3 in its 2025 tables when a condition is present for 4 s within 5 s, type B with warning lamp after two trips. A fault blocks mode selection; the vehicle stays in its basic mode. P05D0 is the general circuit fault of switch A without low/high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM covers the same switch with the more specific P05D1–P05D3.
c: Connector at the switch or control panel corroded or loose
Switch faulty, e.g. liquid in the centre console
Wire to the reading module open
s: Drive mode cannot be changed, vehicle stays in normal mode
Mode display missing or jumping back
Check engine light (GM after two trips)

P05D1.t: Driver Mode Select Switch A Circuit Low
P05D1.d: The driver mode select switch (tour, sport, eco, snow, off-road, towing) changes engine and transmission maps such as shift points, pedal map and cylinder deactivation, so CARB requires it to be monitored as an input. GM reads switch A as an eight-position resistor ladder in the body module and sets P05D1–P05D3 in its 2025 tables when a condition is present for 4 s within 5 s, type B with warning lamp after two trips. Typical are a signal shorted to ground or a shorted switch.
c: Signal line to the body module shorted to ground (chafing in the console)
s: Drive mode cannot be changed, vehicle stays in normal mode
Mode display missing or jumping back
Check engine light (GM after two trips)

s: Drive mode cannot be changed, vehicle stays in normal mode

Switch worn or detent unclear (knob between two positions)
s: Selected mode not taken over or jumping
Check engine light (GM after two trips)
Mode display missing

P05D4 is its general circuit fault; additional modes such as off-road or towing may then not be selectable.

s: Additional drive modes not selectable
Check engine light possible

P05D7.t: Driver Mode Select Switch B Range/Performance
P05D7.d: The driver mode select switch (tour, sport, eco, snow, off-road, towing) changes engine and transmission maps such as shift points, pedal map and cylinder deactivation, so CARB requires it to be monitored as an input. GM reads switch A as an eight-position resistor ladder in the body module and sets P05D1–P05D3 in its 2025 tables when a condition is present for 4 s within 5 s, type B with warning lamp after two trips. P05D7 means its voltage lies between valid position windows or the position is implausible, like GM's dead-band check P05D3 for switch A.
s: Mode via switch B not or wrongly taken over
Check engine light possible
Mode display jumping

P05D8.d: Some turbo engines have an electrically controlled crankcase ventilation valve that decides when and how much blow-by gas is drawn into the intake (part-load versus full-load path). The engine module monitors its driver output; CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults and the PCV system to be monitored. Nissan's 1.5 L KR15DDT (Rogue 2024–25) sets P05D8/P05D9 with the warning lamp from a severed harness at the valve; Mercedes M270/M274 have such a valve but report it under P052E. P05D8 means the valve control circuit is open – wire, coil or connector; the driver sees no load.
c: Harness at the valve connector chafed or severed
Connector not latched or corroded after engine cover or intake work
s: Check engine light on
Often no noticeable symptoms
If the valve sticks: oil mist, blue smoke, rough idle

P05D9.t: PCV Regulator Valve Control Circuit Low
P05D9.d: Some turbo engines have an electrically controlled crankcase ventilation valve that decides when and how much blow-by gas is drawn into the intake (part-load versus full-load path). The engine module monitors its driver output; CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults and the PCV system to be monitored. Nissan's 1.5 L KR15DDT (Rogue 2024–25) sets P05D8/P05D9 with the warning lamp from a severed harness at the valve; Mercedes M270/M274 have such a valve but report it under P052E. P05D9 means the control line is too low – a short to ground of the control or supply line, or with a low-side driver too low a voltage when off.
c: Moisture or oil in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Often no noticeable symptoms
If the valve sticks: oil mist, blue smoke, rough idle

P05DA.t: PCV Regulator Valve Control Circuit High
P05DA.d: Some turbo engines have an electrically controlled crankcase ventilation valve that decides when and how much blow-by gas is drawn into the intake (part-load versus full-load path). The engine module monitors its driver output; CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults and the PCV system to be monitored. Nissan's 1.5 L KR15DDT (Rogue 2024–25) sets P05D8/P05D9 with the warning lamp from a severed harness at the valve; Mercedes M270/M274 have such a valve but report it under P052E. P05DA means the control line is too high – a short to battery voltage or, with a low-side driver, overcurrent when on. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05DA itself.
s: Check engine light on
Often no noticeable symptoms
If the valve sticks: oil mist, blue smoke, rough idle

P05DB.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P05DB.d: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored. A channel fault blocks the A/B correlation P05E0 and usually limits brake assist or regeneration. P05DB is the general circuit or open-circuit fault of channel B. Toyota's electronically controlled brake (RAV4 Hybrid 2024–25) reports channel B faults under it; while it is stored, the A/B correlation does not run.
c: Harness or connector at the pedal sensor (open, contact fault)
Retrofitted wiring near the pedal (e.g. trailer brake controller)
s: Brake or regeneration warning light
Check engine light
Regeneration or brake assist reduced, pedal feel changed

P05DC.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P05DC.d: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored. A channel fault blocks the A/B correlation P05E0 and usually limits brake assist or regeneration. P05DC means channel B leaves its learned or permitted working range without a clear short – for example from a misadjusted or uncalibrated sensor or contact resistance. No admissible manufacturer document available to us gives thresholds for it.
c: Pedal sensor misadjusted, misassembled or not calibrated
Contact resistance on signal line B
s: Brake or regeneration warning light
Check engine light
Regeneration or brake assist reduced, pedal feel changed

P05DD.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P05DD.d: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored. A channel fault blocks the A/B correlation P05E0 and usually limits brake assist or regeneration. P05DD means channel B is below its valid range – signal or shared 5 V reference shorted to ground (then sensor A reports as well). Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV sets it with the regeneration warning light and the check engine light; for channel A it uses below 0.2 V for 0.5 s.
c: Signal line B shorted to ground (harness at the pedal box)
5 V reference shorted to ground (also sensor A code)
s: Brake or regeneration warning light
Check engine light
Regeneration or brake assist reduced, pedal feel changed

P05DE.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit High
P05DE.d: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored. A channel fault blocks the A/B correlation P05E0 and usually limits brake assist or regeneration. P05DE means channel B is above its valid range – an open signal, ground or reference line or a short to positive. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV sets it with the regeneration warning light and the check engine light.
c: Signal line B or connector open
Shared ground or 5 V reference open (sensor A reports too)
Signal line B shorted to positive
s: Brake or regeneration warning light
Check engine light
Regeneration or brake assist reduced, pedal feel changed

P05DF.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P05DF.d: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored. A channel fault blocks the A/B correlation P05E0 and usually limits brake assist or regeneration. P05DF means channel B jumps or is noisy within its valid range – loose contacts or brief interruptions. Toyota lists it as a channel B code that blocks the correlation check; no admissible manufacturer document available to us gives thresholds.
c: Loose contact or fretting corrosion at the sensor connector
Broken or chafed wire in the moving pedal area
Sensor track or Hall element worn
Interference on the shared 5 V reference
s: Sporadic brake warning and check engine light
Regeneration cutting out at times
Code often only stored as history

P05E0.t: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P05E0.d: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems measure brake pedal travel with a two-channel sensor; the channels often run in opposite directions (Toyota RAV4 hybrid 2024–25: one rises from about 1 V, the other falls from about 4 V). P05E0 means both channels are electrically fine but no longer match each other. Toyota sets it when the relationship is invalid for 0.2 s and lights the lamp at once; Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV adds the regenerative brake warning. Braking falls back to plain hydraulics, so the pedal may feel hard and regeneration is off. GM notes for the CT6, Bolt, Malibu and Volt 2016–18 that the code can also appear without a defect if the driver rests a foot lightly on the brake (1.8–5.6 mm travel) for 60 s while accelerating. Single-channel faults are P057A–P057E and P05DB–P05DF.
c: Pedal travel sensor faulty internally (channels drift apart)
Contact resistance or corrosion in the connector or harness of one channel
Sensor not calibrated after replacement or pedal work
Foot resting lightly on the brake while accelerating (GM)
Brake or hybrid control module faulty
s: Check engine light or service warning
Brake, ABS or stability warning lamp
Hard brake pedal, reduced brake assist
Regenerative braking disabled (hybrid/PHEV)

P05E1.t: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P05E1.d: The refrigerant pressure sensor (three wires, 5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) tells the engine module the A/C pressure; it uses it to switch the radiator fan, to block the compressor at too high or too low pressure and to pre-control idle load. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility, but they need not light the lamp if they do not affect emissions. 'Intermittent/Erratic' means the signal jumps implausibly fast or briefly leaves its valid range without staying low or high long enough for those codes. Sensor A is usually the high-pressure sensor; GM and Saab report it only as P0532/P0533 (circuit low/high, at GM below 3 % or above 98 % of 5 V) and P0531, so no manufacturer document available to us uses P05E1 itself. Typically the compressor is blocked and the fan runs. GM rates sensor A faults without the lamp, the Saab 9-4X with it.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector (front end, splash water)
Chafed or broken wire (5 V, signal, ground)
Shared 5 V reference disturbed by another sensor
s: A/C intermittently not cooling (compressor switched off)
Radiator fan runs unnecessarily or irregularly
Idle speed fluctuates when A/C engages
Warning lamp depending on the maker

P05E2.t: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P05E2.d: The refrigerant pressure sensor (three wires, 5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) tells the engine module the A/C pressure; it uses it to switch the radiator fan, to block the compressor at too high or too low pressure and to pre-control idle load. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility, but they need not light the lamp if they do not affect emissions. 'Intermittent/Erratic' means the signal jumps implausibly fast or briefly leaves its valid range without staying low or high long enough for those codes. Sensor B is a second pressure sensor; which one depends on the maker – typically the low-pressure side or a second circuit in heat pump systems. Its other codes are P2515–P2518. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E2, so this follows the sensor A family. Expect the A/C or heat pump to switch off intermittently.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector
s: A/C or heat pump intermittently switched off
Heating or cooling output fluctuates
Warning lamp depending on the maker

P05E3.d: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. The only documented user of this code family is Volvo Trucks: since OBD 2021 a second park brake sensor (about 0.5 V applied, 3.5 V released) must agree with the old switch; the engine module reports the fault. No passenger car maker uses it verifiably. P05E3 is the general circuit fault – usually an open circuit or undefined state. Low and high signals are P05E4 and P05E5.
c: Broken wire or corroded connector at the park brake switch or sensor
Faulty diode in the switch circuit (Volvo)
Vehicle or brake module delivers a wrong status
s: Check engine light or OBD warning (heavy-duty)
Park brake warning in the cluster
Parked regeneration cannot be started
Stop-start or idle shutdown not working

P05E4.d: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. The only documented user of this code family is Volvo Trucks: since OBD 2021 a second park brake sensor (about 0.5 V applied, 3.5 V released) must agree with the old switch; the engine module reports the fault. No passenger car maker uses it verifiably. P05E4 means the signal is below the lower limit: on a three-wire sensor a signal shorted to ground or a missing 5 V supply; on a simple ground switch it looks like a permanently applied brake.
c: Sensor 5 V supply missing or shorted to ground
s: Check engine light or OBD warning (heavy-duty)
Park brake warning in the cluster
Parked regeneration cannot be started
Stop-start or idle shutdown not working

s: Check engine light or OBD warning (heavy-duty)

P05E6.d: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. The only documented user of this code family is Volvo Trucks: since OBD 2021 a second park brake sensor (about 0.5 V applied, 3.5 V released) must agree with the old switch; the engine module reports the fault. No passenger car maker uses it verifiably. P05E6 is the one code of the family with a manufacturer description: at Volvo both signals must change together and agree; if they contradict each other or one changes late, the code sets. Volvo advises starting the diagnosis with the brake released.
c: New pressure sensor and old switch report differently (switch point, delayed change)
Faulty diode in the switch circuit
Low air pressure or leak in the spring brake circuit
Switch or sensor sticking or faulty
s: Check engine light or OBD warning (heavy-duty)
Park brake warning in the cluster
Parked regeneration cannot be started
Stop-start or idle shutdown not working

P05E7.d: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. The only documented user of this code family is Volvo Trucks: since OBD 2021 a second park brake sensor (about 0.5 V applied, 3.5 V released) must agree with the old switch; the engine module reports the fault. No passenger car maker uses it verifiably. P05E7 means the signal jumps briefly without being permanently low or high – changes without operation, while driving or too quickly in a row. The status is then discarded and regeneration or stop-start is blocked.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at connector or splice
s: Intermittent check engine or park brake warning
Running parked regeneration aborts
Stop-start occasionally blocked

P05E8.t: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit/Open
P05E8.d: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05E8 means the control circuit is open: the driver sees missing voltage or high resistance.
c: Connector at the valve loose, corroded or spread
Output driver in the module faulty
s: Check engine light (if rated as emission related)
Oil too hot under load or slow warm-up, depending on rest position
Usually no noticeable driving symptoms

P05E9.t: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit Low
P05E9.d: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05E9 means the control circuit voltage is too low – control wire shorted to ground or shorted coil turns.
c: Control wire chafing against ground (block, bracket)
Moisture or oil in the connector
s: Check engine light (if rated as emission related)
Oil too hot under load or slow warm-up, depending on rest position
Usually no noticeable driving symptoms

P05EA.t: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit High
P05EA.d: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05EA means the control circuit voltage is too high – a short to battery or overcurrent at the driver, so the valve cannot be operated.
c: Control wire touching battery or ignition voltage
Valve coil shorted (overcurrent at the driver)
s: Check engine light (if rated as emission related)
Oil too hot under load or slow warm-up, depending on rest position
Usually no noticeable driving symptoms

P05EB.t: Cold Start SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P05EB.d: After a cold start a diesel heats its exhaust actively – retarded and post injection, intake or exhaust throttling, higher idle, EGR cooler bypass – so the SCR catalyst quickly reaches the temperature at which urea dosing can start (around 180–200 °C). P05EB sets when the measured temperature at the SCR inlet stays below the expected or modelled value within a set time after the start: the heating strategy is not working. CARB requires this 'catalyst warm-up' monitor for light-duty diesels from model year 2026 (20 %) to 2028 (100 %); GM 2025 and Ford 2023 tables do not contain the code yet. Volvo Trucks used it on 2016–17 heavy-duty engines and advised a software check instead of replacing parts. The lamp comes on; no power limitation from this code alone is known.
c: Engine module software or calibration (false trigger)
Exhaust temperature sensor before the SCR reads low or slow
Heating measure not effective: throttle, EGR cooler bypass or turbo vanes sticking
Post or retarded injection not effective (injectors)
Exhaust leak before the sensor or extremely cold conditions
s: Check engine light on
Usually no driving symptoms
Higher NOx emissions after cold start (not noticeable)

P05EC.d: To heat the exhaust after a cold start, a diesel shifts its start of injection, usually later, plus post injections. CARB requires faults of such elements during the cold start strategy to be reported under codes separate from normal operation – hence P05EC. GM's 2025 diesels compare the start of injection requested by the application software with the timing actually scheduled for the injector drivers, during cold start only; a deviation beyond ±4 or ±5 in 88 of 176 or 8 of 16 samples sets the code and the lamp in the first trip. Ford's 2023 diesel instead checks whether the cold start operating mode is really activated when requested (10 s). Mechanical injector timing faults in normal operation are P01CB ff and P020A ff; the petrol counterpart for ignition timing is P050B.
c: Engine module software or internal fault (request and execution differ)
Cold start mode blocked by other faults (coolant or fuel temperature, rail pressure)
s: Check engine light on
Usually no driving symptoms
Possibly more white smoke or rougher running after cold start

P05ED.t: Reductant Heater Control Module Supply Voltage
P05ED.d: Some diesels use a separate control module or power stage for the DEF heaters in tank, pump and lines; without heating, frozen fluid cannot thaw in winter and dosing stays blocked. P05ED reports that this module's supply voltage is outside its allowed window – a blown main fuse, an open feed or ground, or system voltage too low or too high. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Thresholds are not published; GM's L5P monitors the comparable heater supply under its own codes and flags a drop of more than 3 V below battery voltage while heating is requested. Start with fuse, feed, ground and battery or charging system.
c: Main fuse or feed wire to the heater module faulty, connector corroded (splash zone)
Weak battery or charging fault (system voltage too low or too high)
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
In cold weather: DEF frozen, dosing blocked, further heater codes

P05EE.d: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05EE means the supply circuit is open: when the supply is switched on, no voltage or current reaches the pump branch. Ford's comparable check flags a pump controller voltage below 6 V. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.
c: Connector at the pump or tank module corroded or loose
Open wire in the harness to the tank
Fuse or relay of the pump supply faulty
Pump or tank module open internally
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

P05EF.t: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P05EF.d: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05EF means the supply voltage is too low or the supply line is shorted to ground. GM's 6.6 L diesel monitors the same high-side driver under P1043 (short to ground with driver on, about 0.5 Ω, 3 s, first trip); Ford flags its pump controller voltage below 8.5 V. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.
c: Supply line shorted to ground (chafed against the frame)
High contact resistance or corrosion in the connector
Pump shorted internally or stiff (high current)
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

P05F0.t: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
P05F0.d: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F0 means the supply voltage is too high, or voltage is present although the supply is switched off (short to battery). GM's 6.6 L diesel monitors this as P1044 (two trips); Ford flags pump voltage above 16 V or controller voltage above 19 V. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.
c: Pump supply shorted to battery positive in the harness
Overvoltage from the charging system or a jump start
Moisture or corrosion causing leakage current in the connector
Relay or driver does not switch off
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

P05F1.t: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck On
P05F1.d: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F1 means the pump supply stays on although the module switches it off – typically detected after the switch-off command, e.g. during after-run, when the feedback still shows voltage. A welded relay or a shorted semiconductor switch is the usual reason. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.
c: External voltage or short to positive in the harness
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency
Pump keeps running after switch-off, battery drains

P05F2.t: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck Off
P05F2.d: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F2 means the pump supply cannot be switched on: after the switch-on command no voltage or feedback appears at the pump branch, so no pressure builds up. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.
c: Relay does not pull in or fuse blown
Open in the relay control or load circuit
Output driver in the engine module faulty
Electronics of the tank module faulty (no feedback)
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

P05F3.t: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
P05F3.d: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F3 means the driver detects an open relay control (coil) circuit. Ford's comparable relay check flags 'driver on but 0 V' or a heater relay current below 0.2 A, within 5 s. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.
c: Relay missing, coil open or not seated properly
Output driver in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply

P05F4.t: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P05F4.d: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F4 means the relay control circuit is shorted to ground or its voltage is too low. Ford's comparable heater relay check flags a current above 6 A with the driver on, within 5 s. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.
c: Output driver in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply

P05F5.t: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit High
P05F5.d: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F5 means the relay control circuit is shorted to battery positive: the voltage stays high although the driver is off. Ford's comparable check flags more than 5 V with the driver off, within 5 s. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.
c: Control line shorted to battery positive
Output driver in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply

P05F6.t: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck On
P05F6.d: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F6 is a function check on the load side: the relay stays closed although it is switched off, so the consumers keep their supply, e.g. during after-run. A patent by Delphi describes this kind of check via the voltage at the heater node. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.
c: External voltage on the load side (short to positive)
Output driver in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply
Consumers stay powered after switch-off, battery drains

P05F7.t: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck Off
P05F7.d: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F7 is the opposite function check: the relay does not close although it is commanded on, so the load side stays without voltage. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. If the relay fails, heaters, pump and SCR control drop out and dosing stops.
c: Relay contacts burnt or coil faulty, relay does not close
Fuse on the load side blown
Output driver in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply

P05F8.d: P05F8 is the function check of the DEF heater control module: its feedback does not match the command – heating current or power, temperature rise, or an internal module fault. The code is documented for Chrysler's 3.0 L EcoDiesel in the 2014 Ram 1500 and Jeep Grand Cherokee: several bulletins list it together with the heater codes P20BA, P20BE and P20C2, and the fix in each case was only reprogramming the engine module – a diagnostic that was too sensitive rather than a hardware defect. It is not on Chrysler's inducement list. Ford checks the same function under heater plausibility codes. Thresholds for P05F8 are not published. If it returns after a software update, check the heater elements in tank and lines and the module supply (P05ED).
c: Engine module software (Chrysler 3.0 L 2014: diagnostic revised by reflash)
Heater element or line in tank or hose with abnormal current
s: Check engine light on
Usually no driveability issue
DEF warning in cold weather, possible heater codes P20BA/P20BE/P20C2

P05F9.d: A discrete stop-start status line tells the engine module (or another module) whether stop-start is active, inhibited or has just stopped the engine. On most current cars this status travels over CAN instead, so a hard-wired line and these codes are rare; no manufacturer document available to us uses P05F9–P05FB. CARB names stop-start as its example of an 'emissions neutral' reaction: a module that simply disables stop-start when a fault appears may report it without the check engine light, which is what Ford does for its stop-start codes. P05F9 is the general circuit fault or open line. The typical reaction is that stop-start is disabled; the driver-operated stop-start switch has its own codes.
c: Open status line or connector problem
Sending module without supply or faulty
Wrong software or variant coding (stop-start set without hardware)
s: Stop-start does not work
Stop-start indicator or message in the cluster
Check engine light only with some makers

P05FA.d: A discrete stop-start status line tells the engine module (or another module) whether stop-start is active, inhibited or has just stopped the engine. On most current cars this status travels over CAN instead, so a hard-wired line and these codes are rare; no manufacturer document available to us uses P05F9–P05FB. CARB names stop-start as its example of an 'emissions neutral' reaction: a module that simply disables stop-start when a fault appears may report it without the check engine light, which is what Ford does for its stop-start codes. P05FA means the status line stays below its lower limit – a short to ground or a missing pull-up supply. Stop-start is then disabled.
c: Sending module pulls the line to ground permanently (faulty output)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Stop-start does not work
Stop-start indicator or message in the cluster

P05FB.d: A discrete stop-start status line tells the engine module (or another module) whether stop-start is active, inhibited or has just stopped the engine. On most current cars this status travels over CAN instead, so a hard-wired line and these codes are rare; no manufacturer document available to us uses P05F9–P05FB. CARB names stop-start as its example of an 'emissions neutral' reaction: a module that simply disables stop-start when a fault appears may report it without the check engine light, which is what Ford does for its stop-start codes. P05FB means the status line stays above its upper limit – an open line pulled up or a short to voltage. Stop-start is then disabled.
c: Open status line or connector off
Sending module faulty or without ground
s: Stop-start does not work
Stop-start indicator or message in the cluster

P05FC.t: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 2
P05FC.d: During a cold start, direct injection petrol engines usually raise rail pressure for finer atomisation with multiple injections while the catalyst heats up. P05FC monitors whether the actual rail pressure of bank 2 stays within the target window during this phase – only engines with separate rails and pressure sensors per bank (V or boxer engines with two high-pressure circuits) can set it. CARB lists fuel pressure as a cold start component that must respond measurably beyond what would happen without the strategy. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05FC; Ford checks the single-rail counterpart P053F and flags a fault when the share of cold start time inside the pressure window is 0.70 or less, and Kia replaced the engine module of the 2018 Stinger 2.0T for P053F with stumbling during warm-up. GM uses P2C1E–P2C20 instead.
c: High-pressure pump or volume control valve of bank 2 weak or sticking
Rail pressure sensor of bank 2 inaccurate
Leaking injector or pressure relief on bank 2
s: Check engine light on
Stumbling, hesitation or rough idle during warm-up
Poorer cold start
Usually normal once warm

P05FD.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Temperature Too High
P05FD.d: Electric variable-geometry turbo actuators use a DC motor with gearing, driven by an H-bridge in the engine module or in the actuator itself. Constant high load – sooted or stiff vanes, running against a stop, an internal motor short – drives up current and temperature. GM's 2025 diesels set P05FD when the H-bridge driver exceeds 170 °C in 240 of 300 samples (about 3 s) and light the lamp in the first trip. The driver then shuts off for protection, the actuator stops or returns to its rest position, and boost control is limited – underboost or overboost and reduced power can follow. GM Europe's earlier 2.0 diesels reported the same protection under P0046. Circuit faults of the actuator are P0045–P0048, the position sensor P2563 ff.
c: Vane mechanism sooted or stiff, actuator works constantly against resistance
Electric actuator faulty internally (shorted turns, bearing)
High ambient heat at the actuator (missing heat shield, exhaust leak)
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power or limp mode
Possibly underboost or overboost codes (P0299/P0234)
More smoke under load

P05FE.t: Active Grille Air Shutter C Performance/Stuck Off
P05FE.d: Active grille shutters close the air inlet when little cooling is needed, to reduce drag and speed up warm-up. P05FE is the performance check of a third shutter C – target and actual position do not match, as P059F does for shutter A and P05AE for shutter B. Only vehicles with three separately driven shutters could set it, and no manufacturer was found that uses a shutter C: GM and Ford use only A (upper) and B (lower). This description therefore follows A and B: control is suspended and the shutter stays where it is or opens; if it sticks closed, cooling air is missing under load. GM and Ford light the lamp for A and B after two trips. Ice and debris are frequent causes, and GM fixed false A/B codes in snow by software on the 2025 Equinox. Stuck on is P2C73.
