P06DA.d: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e. high pressure, when the valve is unpowered – the safe default – and at the low stage when powered. P06DA means the control circuit of this valve is open: it can no longer be powered, so the pump stays at high pressure. GM measures the voltage with the driver off and flags more than 200 kΩ after two trips; some GM modules set P06DB instead. GM checks the low-side driver at 11 V or more relay voltage over 40 of 50 samples (100 ms); Ford's smart driver reports output faults after 5 s with the battery at 11 V or more. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander uses the same code. The engine is not at risk, the pump just can no longer be regulated.
c: Connector at the control valve loose or corroded (often at the pump in the oil pan)
Valve coil open or valve broken
Supply (main relay) or control wire broken
s: Check engine light after two trips
Usually no noticeable symptom, oil pressure permanently high
Slightly higher fuel consumption

P06DB.t: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Low
P06DB.d: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e. high pressure, when the valve is unpowered – the safe default – and at the low stage when powered. P06DB means the control wire behind the valve is shorted to ground. With a low-side driver the valve is then powered all the time, so the pump stays at the low stage even at high load and speed. That endangers the engine, so GM flags a short below 0.5 Ω after just one trip, unlike open circuit and short to positive. GM checks the low-side driver at 11 V or more relay voltage over 40 of 50 samples (100 ms); Ford's smart driver reports output faults after 5 s with the battery at 11 V or more. A short to positive is P06DC, a pump stuck at low pressure without a circuit fault P06DE.
c: Control wire chafing against ground (engine block, oil pan)
Oil or moisture in the connector
s: Check engine light at once (GM after one trip)
Low oil pressure at high engine speed, possibly oil pressure warning
Possibly reduced power

P06DC.t: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit High
P06DC.d: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e. high pressure, when the valve is unpowered – the safe default – and at the low stage when powered. P06DC means the control wire is shorted to positive: the low-side driver can no longer pull it to ground, so the valve stays unpowered and the pump at high pressure – the safe state. GM checks this with the driver on and flags a short below 0.5 Ω after two trips. GM checks the low-side driver at 11 V or more relay voltage over 40 of 50 samples (100 ms); Ford's smart driver reports output faults after 5 s with the battery at 11 V or more. Apart from slightly higher consumption there are usually no symptoms. An open circuit is P06DA, a short to ground P06DB.
c: Valve coil shorted (looks like a short to positive at the driver)
s: Check engine light after two trips
Usually no noticeable symptom, oil pressure permanently high
Slightly higher fuel consumption

P06DD.t: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P06DD.d: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; unpowered it delivers high pressure. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start. P06DD means the pressure does not react and stays above the threshold – the pump acts as if the valve were stuck off, at high pressure; GM sets it after two trips. Yet GM bulletins for V8 and 2.5 L engines list P06DD with low oil pressure, too: broken valve tips, unseated valves, a loose pump drive gear or worn tensioners also stop the pressure from changing. Check oil level and pressure before replacing parts.
c: Control valve stuck or broken, screen clogged
Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludge
Mechanical pump or drive damage (tensioner, drive gear, pump face)
s: Check engine light after two trips
Oil pressure stays high – or, with pump damage, low or fluctuating
Possibly oil pressure warning
Slightly higher fuel consumption

P06DE.t: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Stuck On
P06DE.d: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; powered it runs at the low stage. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start. P06DE is the counterpart of P06DD: the commanded high stage is not reached and the pressure stays below the threshold, as if the valve were stuck on. Too little oil pressure at high load endangers the engine, so GM sets it after just one trip; a Ford patent raises idle speed in this case. A short to ground on the control wire (P06DB) has the same effect electrically. An FCA bulletin for the 3.6 L V6 fixes false codes by software.
c: Control valve stuck in the powered position
Low oil level, diluted or sludged oil, aeration
s: Check engine light at once
Oil pressure warning at higher engine speed possible
Possibly reduced power or raised idle
Valvetrain or chain tensioner noise from lack of oil

P06DF.t: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Memory Checksum Error
P06DF.d: A diesel glow plug control module has its own microcontroller. On power-up it forms a checksum over its memory and compares it with the stored value; P06DF means they differ, so the module's program or data cannot be trusted. Ford's 2023 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke list P06DF among the glow module checks, run at power-up and flagged on a RAM checksum mismatch after about 1 s. GM's L5P performs the same check on ROM (4.5 s, two trips) but reports it as P064C. CARB treats the module as a 'smart device' whose internal faults need not be pinpointed, so this is extra diagnosis by the manufacturer. The usual remedy is reprogramming or replacing the module; until then preheating may be missing.
c: Glow plug control module faulty internally (memory, controller)
Failed or interrupted programming of the module
Voltage dip or spike at power-up (weak battery, poor ground)
Moisture or corrosion in module or connector
s: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking
White smoke and knocking after cold start
Often no symptoms when warm

P06E0.t: Cylinder 11 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P06E0.d: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E0 means the circuit to the cylinder 11 glow plug is shorted to ground or draws overcurrent. For cylinders 1–8, GM's engine-module drivers flag below 0.11 Ω to ground after two trips, and Ford's 2023 Power Stroke more than 22 A for 0.3 s or 20–22 A for 2 s while heating. The channel is switched off and the plug stays cold; the other plugs keep working. An internally shorted plug or a chafed wire is the usual cause. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it needs at least 11 cylinders, and the only US OBD II diesel above eight, VW's Touareg V10 TDI, has ten; the description follows cylinders 1–8.
c: Plug wire chafed through to ground
Burnt connector or terminal nut, tracking through oil or moisture
Driver stage in the glow module defective
s: Check engine light (GM: also glow plug lamp)
Harder cold start in frost
Rough cold idle, white smoke after cold start
Cylinder 11 misfire when cold

P06E1.t: Cylinder 11 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P06E1.d: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E1 means the circuit to the cylinder 11 glow plug is shorted to positive: voltage is present although the driver is off, or no current flows when it is on. For cylinders 1–8, GM's engine-module drivers flag a short to positive below 0.5 Ω after two trips, and Ford's 2023 Power Stroke 0 A while commanded for about 1 s. The plug may glow permanently and fail early; the other plugs keep working. Wiring shorted to supply or a failed driver are the usual causes. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it needs at least 11 cylinders, and the only US OBD II diesel above eight, VW's Touareg V10 TDI, has ten; the description follows cylinders 1–8.
c: Plug wire shorted to supply in the harness
Driver stage in the glow module shorted (permanently on)
Moisture or corrosion bridging to a supply pin
s: Check engine light (GM: also glow plug lamp)

Rough cold idle, white smoke after cold start

P06E4.d: Control modules are woken by a dedicated wake-up line or a network wake-up – at ignition on, when a charging cable is plugged in, or on a timer for engine-off diagnostics and battery management. P06E4 means this wake-up signal is implausible: the module wakes too late or not at all, stays awake, or the line state does not match the network status. In practice the code appears mainly on hybrids: FCA fixes it on the Pacifica plug-in hybrid and the Wrangler 4xe with module software, where it remained as a permanent code that blocked emission inspections; GM's hybrid integration module lists it as a fault bundle. No manufacturer publishes thresholds or timing.
c: Module software (false setting, permanent code does not clear)
Wake-up line or connector open or shorted
Weak 12 V battery, voltage dips at wake-up
Engine or hybrid control module faulty
s: Check engine light
Permanent code blocks emission inspection
Possibly battery drain (module stays awake)

P06E5.d: P06E5 means glow plug control module 1 does not respond correctly to the glow command: its outputs do not switch or its internal drivers report faults or overheating. Ford's 2023 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke list P06E5 among the glow module checks, run continuously, with a fault after about 1 s when internal drivers for glow plugs, DEF heaters or relays fail to switch or overheat for more than 1 s – Ford does not assign each threshold to a single code. GM files the same check under P064C: on the L5P a plug commanded on but drawing under 3.2 A with 0 V at the plug for 3.5 s, on the LML a total current under 6.6 A; both after two trips. The plugs then heat partly or not at all, with hard cold starts and white smoke. There is no limp mode.
c: Glow plug control module faulty internally (drivers do not switch)
Poor supply or ground of the module (main feed, fuse, ground)
Module overheating (mounting location, short at a plug)
s: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking
White smoke and rough running after cold start
Often stored together with plug codes or P064C/P263C

P06E6.d: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. Supply C is a third such circuit. P06E6 is the general or open-circuit code of supply C: the module measures the output of its supply regulator and finds the voltage missing. Low and high are P06E7/P06E8. Only Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander lists P06E6 as a main code with sub-codes for low and high, called internal control module, without thresholds or the sensors fed. All sensors on the circuit then deliver invalid values, so several follow-up codes and limp mode are possible.
c: Open circuit or connector problem in the supply circuit
Short in the supply wire or a supplied sensor
Supply regulator inside the module faulty
s: Check engine light
Several sensor codes at the same time
Limp mode or reduced power possible
Possibly starting problems or rough running
