P0745.d: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0745 is the general code for this valve; the sub-codes P0746–P0749 follow. It is documented on Mitsubishi CVTs as a current plausibility check: at most 400 mA while 750 mA or more is commanded for 5 s, or 1.34 A or more for 1 s. A failure usually leaves the valve unpowered, so pressure goes to maximum: harsh shifts and, depending on the transmission, limp mode in a fixed gear.

P0746.t: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
P0746.d: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0746 means the valve is electrically fine but the commanded pressure does not build. GM's clutch-to-clutch units detect it as slip: 400 rpm or more for 1.5 s (T87), or clutch 1 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s three times (9-speed), after one trip; Allison when the oncoming clutch does not apply. Mitsubishi's dual-clutch flags 500 mA current deviation. Slipping or flaring on shifts, a missed gear and limp mode follow; GM's 9-speed bulletin checks clutch plates and replaces the valve body.

P0747.t: Pressure Control Solenoid A Stuck On
P0747.d: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P074A.d: 'Unable to engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – the opposite of 'stuck in gear', where a gear cannot be disengaged. Documented users are dual-clutch transmissions, whose shift forks are moved hydraulically and watched by travel sensors: GM's 8-speed in the 2020–23 Corvette, Maserati's MC20 and – for the odd gears only – Acura's RLX Sport Hybrid, whose 'odd gear monitor' is part of an emission recall with permanent codes. No manufacturer publishes thresholds. P074A means the second gear, on the even sub-gearbox, cannot be engaged; a gear that will not disengage is P072D, slip in an engaged gear P0732. GM's bulletin first runs a learn procedure and cleans valves only if system pressure codes are present; Maserati checks system pressure (20–30 bar). If neither helps, the mechanics are at fault.

P0750.d: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, newer GM units have separate low/high codes, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's 9-5: A = valve S2). P0750 is the general code for solenoid A and is used in practice for an open circuit: Ford's step automatics (2012–2023) set it when the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, with shorts to ground and power as P0973/P0974; Ram's 6.7 L with Aisin transmission calls it 'control circuit open', and a 2023 bulletin traces it to a leaking capacitor in the engine module. GM does not use P0750. With the solenoid unpowered the transmission falls back to a hydraulic default gear with maximum pressure.

P0751.d: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; together the solenoid states select the gear, and the module checks the result by gear ratio, slip or a pressure switch – the pattern of wrong gears shows which solenoid hangs off or on. Allison checks its pressure switch for 5 s after one trip. Ford's 'functionally failed off' covers the whole clutch circuit, and its 10R80 and 8F35 bulletins show purely mechanical causes such as a leaking clutch cylinder.

P075F.d: P075F is not a circuit fault but a condition: a working fluid level sensor reports a level above the target band – the counterpart of P070F. In the Allison patent the transmission module reports 'too high, drain a quart or more', measuring only with the vehicle at rest, warm fluid and low input speed. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. Overfilling makes rotating parts churn the fluid, which foams, pressure control becomes unsteady, fluid escapes at the vent and temperature rises; an FCA bulletin traces poor shifting after repairs to overfilling. Automatic transmission fluid level depends strongly on temperature – topping up cold often overfills.
c: Overfilled at fluid change or repair (wrong check temperature or procedure)
Measured under poor conditions (slope, cold fluid)
s: Transmission fluid level warning
Fluid escaping at the transmission vent
Foaming fluid, unsteady or harsh shifts
Transmission overheating

P0760.d: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's Aisin 9-5: C = valve S4, D = valve S5). P0760 is the general code for solenoid C and, at Ford, means an open circuit: the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, continuously; shorts to ground and power are P0979/P0980. On Ford's 6R80, 6F35/6F55 and 6R140, solenoid C is the proportional valve of the CB26 brake for second and sixth gear. If the solenoid supply is switched off, Ford transmissions keep park, reverse, neutral and fifth gear with maximum pressure.

The 2007 Allison 1000 checks pressure switch 3 for 5 s, after one trip. Ford's 'functionally failed off' covers the CB26 brake circuit; Dodge's Aisin AS6 uses the code for solenoid 3, while Mitsubishi uses it for pressure switches.

P0765.d: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's Aisin 9-5: C = valve S4, D = valve S5). P0765 is the general code for solenoid D and, at Ford, means an open circuit (0.5–5 s); shorts are P0982/P0983. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F transmissions solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch via a multiplex valve, on the 6R140 only the low/reverse brake; on the 2023 diesel its supply is shared with solenoid B and the converter clutch (P2669). A Ram 6.7 L bulletin traces P0765 to a leaking capacitor in the engine module.
c: Open or corroded wire, connector or internal harness
s: Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Limp mode in a fixed gear (Ford: fifth with maximum pressure)
No reverse or engine braking in first, or missing 4th–6th gears (Ford)

P0766.d: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; the module checks whether its clutch follows the command by gear ratio, shift time or a pressure switch. P0766 means solenoid D is commanded on but its clutch does not follow. Ford checks gear ratio over 10 events (2012) or 3 (2020–23 and the 2023 diesel); on the 6F transmissions solenoid D feeds two clutches, so Ford recognises a solenoid fault when both fail, while a single clutch fault sets ratio codes. Ford's 10R80 bulletins list it with a leaking clutch cylinder; Dodge's Aisin AS6 uses it for solenoid 4. GM does not use P0766.
c: Clutch or brake of this circuit leaking or worn (piston seal, linings)
Shift spool or proportional valve sticking (dirt, debris)
s: Upper gears (4th–6th) missing, or no reverse or engine braking in first (Ford)
Slip or engine flare on shifts
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0767.d: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; the module checks whether its clutch follows the command by gear ratio, shift time or a pressure switch. P0767 means solenoid D is commanded off but its clutch stays applied. Only Ford documents it, as 'functionally failed on': the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch does not release, which brakes or ties up the transmission in higher gears. Ford's 2023 diesel sets it after three release events; the 10R80 bulletins list it with a leaking clutch cylinder. A sticking spool or proportional valve is the usual cause.
c: Shift spool or proportional valve sticking in the applied position
Control wire shorted to ground (permanently powered)
s: Tie-up or jolt on shifts
Delayed shifts, engine revs high
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0768.d: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's Aisin 9-5: C = valve S4, D = valve S5). P0768 is the collective electrical code for solenoid D. GM's 2006 Allison tables flag a driver hardware fault for more than 0.1 s, after one trip; Saab's Aisin 5-speed (valve S5) checks current draw and enters limp mode with 'check gearbox'; Hyundai's 8-speed uses it for the valve of the 4 & overdrive clutch and replaces valve and electronic module, then the module if it returns. Ford does not use P0768.
c: Open or corroded wire, connector or internal harness
s: Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Limp mode in a fixed gear (Ford: fifth with maximum pressure)
Harsh shifts

P0769.d: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's Aisin 9-5: C = valve S4, D = valve S5). P0769 is an intermittent circuit or function fault of solenoid D. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: Ford watches the circuit continuously under its open and short codes (P0765, P0982, P0983), and GM's 2006 Allison tables count dropouts under P0768 or as an intermittent case of the pressure switch check. Brief dropouts make the module switch the solenoid off and enter limp mode until the next start.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the transmission connector
Chafed harness, dependent on temperature or vibration
s: Limp mode or jolt at times, then normal again
Warning lamp comes and goes

P076A.d: Shift solenoid H exists only on transmissions with eight or more solenoids. Ford's 10R80 ends at F, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch pressure valve codes; the only documented user of the H block is the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire, where it concerns the on/off solenoid of the park lock rather than a shift valve. Hyundai's bulletins name P076A both 'SBW park system fault' and 'on/off solenoid C (park – SBW)'. The remedy is replacing valve and electronic module or the park position switch and actuator, then the transmission module if the code returns. No other manufacturer uses P076A.
c: Park lock on/off solenoid or electronic module faulty
s: Check engine light
Park lock or range selection fault, shift-by-wire warning
Limp mode

P076B.d: Shift solenoid H exists only on transmissions with eight or more solenoids. Ford's 10R80 ends at F, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch pressure valve codes; the only documented user of the H block is the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire, where it concerns the on/off solenoid of the park lock rather than a shift valve. P076B means solenoid H is commanded on but does not take effect, like P0761 for solenoid C. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; Hyundai uses only P076A and P076D. The description follows the scheme for the other solenoids.
c: Clutch or brake of this circuit leaking or worn (piston seal, linings)
Shift spool or proportional valve sticking (dirt, debris)
s: Gears missing or skipped
Slip or engine flare on shifts
Limp mode
Check engine light

Ford's 10R80 ends at F, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch pressure valve codes; the only documented user of the H block is the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire, where it concerns the on/off solenoid of the park lock rather than a shift valve. P076C means solenoid H is commanded off but stays effective, like P0762 for solenoid C. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; Hyundai uses only P076A and P076D. The description follows the scheme for the other solenoids.
c: Shift spool or proportional valve sticking in the applied position
Control wire shorted to ground (permanently powered)

P076D.d: Shift solenoid H exists only on transmissions with eight or more solenoids. Ford's 10R80 ends at F, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch pressure valve codes; the only documented user of the H block is the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire, where it concerns the on/off solenoid of the park lock rather than a shift valve. Hyundai's bulletins for the G80/G90 name P076D 'on/off solenoid C (park – SBW)' and treat it as an electrical fault: replace valve and electronic module, load the valve data, and replace the transmission module if it returns. No other manufacturer uses P076D.
c: Park lock on/off solenoid or electronic module
s: Check engine light
Park lock or shift-by-wire warning
Limp mode

P076E.d: Shift solenoid H exists only on transmissions with eight or more solenoids. Ford's 10R80 ends at F, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch pressure valve codes; the only documented user of the H block is the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire, where it concerns the on/off solenoid of the park lock rather than a shift valve. P076E is an intermittent fault of solenoid H. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; manufacturers usually count such dropouts within their circuit codes. A loose contact at the transmission connector is the most likely cause.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the transmission connector
Chafed harness, dependent on temperature or vibration
s: Limp mode or jolt at times, then normal again
Warning lamp comes and goes

P076F.d: P076F means the ratio in seventh gear is wrong: input speed divided by output speed does not match the commanded gear, so a clutch slips or another gear is engaged. It only exists on transmissions with seven or more gears. Ford's 10-speed 10R80 and 10R140 list it in bulletins together with the other ratio codes and the check engine light – causes include a migrating sleeve on a clutch cylinder causing hydraulic leaks and sticking valve body valves. Ford's ratio check elsewhere flags more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times. On GM's Corvette with seven-speed manual gearbox, P076F is a plausibility check of the gear position sensor instead (ratio window 0.41–0.50), after one trip.
c: Hydraulic leak at the seventh gear clutch (Ford 10R80: clutch cylinder sleeve)
Sticking valves in the valve body or solenoid
Gear position sensor implausible or not learned (GM manual only)
s: Slipping or flaring engine speed in seventh gear
Harsh or delayed shifts
Check engine light, transmission warning, possibly limp mode

P0770.d: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0770 is the general code for solenoid E; Ford uses it for an open circuit, detected when the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, and on the 6R80/6F it covers all circuit faults of the solenoid. On Ram's 6.7 L with Aisin AS69RC a 2023 bulletin traces P0770 to a leaking capacitor in the engine module, together with other circuit codes. Limp mode follows; on the 6R80/6F engine braking in first or the 4th–6th gears may be missing.
c: Open or corroded wire or transmission connector
Transmission module or electronic module faulty
s: Transmission warning or check engine light
Limp mode in a fixed gear
Harsh shifts

P0771.d: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0771 is Ford's functional check by gear ratio over 10 events (2012) or 3 (2020–23, 2023 diesel). On the 6R80/6F it means the multiplex valve stays in its rest position, so solenoid D acts on the wrong clutch; valve and spool cannot be told apart. On the 6R140 the 4-5-6 clutch does not apply. Ford counts the whole clutch system in, and its 10R80 and 8F35 bulletins list P0771 with mechanical repairs. Slipping or missing gears and limp mode follow.
c: Valve body or multiplex valve sticking (debris, dirt)
Clutch, piston seal or clutch cylinder leaking or worn
Fluid level low or fluid contaminated
s: Slipping or flare on shifts
Missing gear (e.g. 4th–6th)
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0772.d: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0772 is the counterpart of P0771: the gear ratio shows that the multiplex valve is stuck in its spring-loaded position (6R80/6F) or that the clutch controlled by solenoid E does not release (6R140: 4-5-6 clutch). Ford flags it after 10 or 3 events, continuously, and again counts valve, spool and clutch in; its 10R80 bulletins list it for harsh or delayed shifts. Harsh shifts, tie-up and a wrong gear follow.
c: Clutch plates stuck or burnt, piston hanging
s: Harsh shift jolt, transmission ties up
Limp mode in a fixed gear
Check engine light

P0773.d: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0773 is the electrical code for solenoid E. GM's 2006 Allison tables flag a driver hardware fault for more than 0.1 s, cross-checked by pressure switch E, after one trip; Saab's Aisin 5-speed checks the current of valve S1 with fluid above 20 °C and shows 'check gearbox'; Hyundai/Genesis 8-speeds use it for clutch valve E and replace valve and electronic module. Ford does not use P0773.
c: Open or corroded wire or transmission connector
Transmission module or electronic module faulty
s: Transmission warning or check engine light
Limp mode in a fixed gear
Harsh shifts

P0774.d: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0774 is an intermittent electrical fault in the circuit of solenoid E. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: Ford's solenoid E table has no intermittent code, and GM's Allison tables catch intermittent cases through the pressure switch check. A loose contact or chafed wire is the likely cause.
s: Limp mode or harsh shifts at times
Warning lamp comes and goes

P0775.d: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0775 is the general code for valve B. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; the trade journal MOTOR names it as a performance code of line pressure valve B on Ford's 5R55, set together with ratio codes after a broken overdrive servo. Sub-codes for performance, stuck on, electrical and intermittent follow (P0776–P0779).
c: Valve body or pressure valve B worn or dirty
Line pressure wrong (load signal, main regulator)
s: Harsh or slipping shifts
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0776.t: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance/Stuck Off
P0776.d: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0776 means the valve is electrically fine but pressure stays too low. GM's 8-speed flags gear slip of 400 rpm for 1.5 s three times, the 9-speed clutch 2 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s, the CVT primary pressure below 200 kPa for 3 s – all after one trip. Mitsubishi's Jatco CVT flags secondary pressure 1.2 MPa off target; Nissan's bulletin calls for a mechanical CVT repair, a GM 6T70 bulletin a broken wave spring. Slipping, missing gears or lack of drive and limp mode follow.
c: Clutch, return spring or piston seal of the assigned clutch faulty
Valve body or pressure valve dirty or worn
Fluid level low, fluid worn, filter clogged
s: Slipping or missing gears
CVT: hesitation, lack of power
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0777.t: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On
P0777.d: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0777 means the valve is electrically fine but pressure stays applied – the off-going clutch does not release. GM's 9-speed flags clutch 2 slip below 50 rpm for 0.8 s on loaded downshifts, the 8-speed uses a torque and inertia phase test, Allison 25 rpm or less – all after one trip. GM's Honda-built five-speed cannot always separate it from P0746 and stores both. Harsh shift jolts, tie-up and a default gear follow.
s: Harsh shift jolt, transmission ties up
Limp mode in a fixed gear
Check engine light

P0778.d: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0778 is the electrical code for valve B. Allison compares current with the duty cycle after 125 ms, after one trip; Mitsubishi's 2009 CVT flags at most 400 mA with 750 mA commanded for 5 s; the 2022 Jatco CVT uses P0778 only for a short to ground; Saab's AF40 flags a deviation between commanded and feedback current of valve SLC1 and keeps only second gear and reverse. Harsh engagement, weak acceleration and no lock-up follow.
c: Harness or connector shorted or open
Pressure valve B coil faulty – often only replaceable with the valve body
s: Harsh engagement jolt
Weak pulling away and acceleration
Limp mode (Saab: second and reverse only)
Check engine light

P0779.d: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. In J2012 P0779 is an intermittent fault of valve B. The only manufacturer use found differs: Mitsubishi's 2022 Jatco CVT sets P0779 for an open circuit or short to positive in the secondary pressure valve circuit after 1 s (short to ground is P0778). The transmission then engages harshly, accelerates weakly and does not lock up.
c: Connector or wire open or loose contact
Short to positive in the harness
s: Harsh engagement at times
Weak acceleration, no lock-up
Check engine light

P077A.t: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Loss of Direction Signal
P077A.d: Some transmissions use an output shaft speed sensor that also reports direction of rotation: in a GM patent two offset Hall elements send one pulse per tooth whose width encodes forward or reverse. The direction is needed to detect rolling back on a hill (a Hyundai patent raises idle speed then), for hill hold, stop-start and the forward/reverse change. P077A means the sensor still delivers speed pulses but no usable direction information – the pulse width stays outside the direction windows or one Hall element has failed. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM checks direction coherence under P0721. Hill hold, auto hold or stop-start may then be disabled and the forward/reverse change runs in a substitute mode.
c: Output speed sensor faulty (one Hall element or direction channel failed)
Contact resistance in connector or wiring distorts the pulse
Wrong replacement sensor without direction function
Reluctor wheel damaged or air gap too large
s: Transmission warning or check engine light depending on manufacturer
Hill hold, auto hold or stop-start unavailable
Rolling back on a hill not caught

P077B.t: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Direction Error
P077B.d: Some transmissions use an output shaft speed sensor that also reports direction of rotation: in a GM patent two offset Hall elements send one pulse per tooth whose width encodes forward or reverse. The direction is needed to detect rolling back on a hill (a Hyundai patent raises idle speed then), for hill hold, stop-start and the forward/reverse change. P077B means the sensor reports a direction that does not fit – for example reverse while a forward gear is engaged and the input and intermediate shaft sensors confirm forward motion. GM's transmission modules list P077B as a blocking condition for other checks, but run the actual check under their own codes: direction contradicts the gear for 2.5 s above 500 rpm, after one trip. Speed and direction are then unreliable: hill hold and the park and reverse logic fall back to substitute modes.
c: Output speed sensor faulty (direction evaluation disturbed)
Wrong or incorrectly fitted sensor (orientation to the wheel)
Reluctor wheel damaged, metal debris on the sensor
Faulty reference (input or intermediate shaft sensor)
s: Check engine light or transmission warning
Hill hold off
Limp mode possible
Speedometer or cruise control unreliable

P077C.t: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Low
P077C.d: GM's transmission modules from 2019 to 2025 (9- and 10-speeds) also read the active output speed sensor's line voltage as an analog value. P077C means this voltage is below 0.25 V – a short to ground of under about 0.5 Ω between signal and module ground – for more than 0.05 s with the system above 10 V; GM rates it after one trip. GM then blocks the no-signal and ratio checks so that P0722 is not set instead of the actual short. Without output speed the transmission enters limp mode and road speed may be missing. On GM's 10-speed input and output sensors share a supply.
c: Signal or supply wire shorted to ground (chafing at the case)
Oil or moisture in the connector, corrosion
s: Check engine light at once (GM)
Limp mode or fixed gear
Speedometer or cruise control failed
Harsh shifts, no converter lock-up

P077D.t: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit High
P077D.d: GM's transmission modules from 2019 to 2025 (9- and 10-speeds) also read the active output speed sensor's line voltage as an analog value. P077D is the mirror of P077C: the voltage is above 4.75 V – a short to the module supply of under about 0.5 Ω – for more than 0.05 s, after one trip. GM then blocks the no-signal and ratio checks; a GM hybrid also blocks its idle diagnosis. Without usable output speed the transmission enters limp mode, and speedometer or cruise control may fail.
c: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Ground fault at the sensor, corroded connector
s: Check engine light at once (GM)
Limp mode
Speedometer or cruise control failed
Shift problems

P077E.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Measurement System Multiple Sensor Correlation
P077E.d: P077E is a plausibility check between several fluid temperature readings – for example sensors A and B, sump and valve body, or the module's internal temperature. If they differ by more than allowed after a settling time, such as a long stop, the code sets, without being able to blame a single sensor. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM checks each sensor alone (P0711, with the module temperature on the 6T70), and Ford has no multi-sensor check. A substitute value then limits converter clutch and shift adaption.
c: Contact resistance at a sensor connector or wire
Fluid level too low (sensor not wetted)
s: Transmission warning, possibly check engine light
Converter clutch applies late or not at all
Harsh cold shifts

P077F.d: P077F checks the ratio in a second reverse gear: input speed divided by output speed lies outside the tolerance band around the target ratio – a slipping clutch, a wrong gear or a sensor fault. Only transmissions with two reverse ratios need it, such as Mercedes' 7G-Tronic (−3.42 and −2.23, with the second reverse kept in limp mode) and its 5G-Tronic predecessor; GM's 9- and 10-speeds, Ford's 10R and ZF's 8HP have one. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the check works like the other ratio codes such as P0736.
c: Slipping clutch or brake in the second reverse power path
Fluid level low or fluid worn
Faulty input or output speed sensor
s: Reverse slips or engages late
Limp mode
Transmission warning or check engine light

P0780.d: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0780 is the collective code when the faulty shift is not assigned to a gear. GM's 2006 Aisin-type five-speed counts five shifts that are too long, too short or tied up with fluid above 60 °C and lights the MIL at once; GM's Honda-built unit flags a 3–4 shift that stays in the lower ratio after two trips; Saab's 2010 Aisin six-speed counts ten faulty shifts without MIL, limits torque and keeps second and reverse. Nissan fixed P0780 on the 2021 Rogue CVT with new software.
c: Fluid level wrong, fluid worn or contaminated
Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking
s: Harsh, delayed or missing shifts
Engine flare during shifts
Warning lamp
Limp mode with fixed gear, reduced power

P0781.d: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0781 names the 1–2 shift as the faulty one, up or down; slip in a steady gear is reported by the ratio codes instead. Lexus' AB60F six-speed (LX 570, 2008–11) lists P0781 among its transmission performance codes; the bulletin first checks fluid level, then installs new software and, if needed, a new transmission. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P0781.
c: Fluid level wrong, fluid worn or contaminated
Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking
s: Harsh, delayed or missing 1-2 shift
Engine flare during the shift
Warning lamp
Limp mode

Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0782 names the 2–3 shift as the faulty one, up or down; slip in a steady gear is reported by the ratio codes instead. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's 2006 Aisin-type tables run the same shift time check under P0780, Ford's under the solenoid codes.

Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking

Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0783 names the 3–4 shift as the faulty one, up or down; slip in a steady gear is reported by the ratio codes instead. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Honda-built five-speed checks exactly the 3–4 change, but reports it as P0780. Missing or late fourth gear and flare on the 3–4 shift are typical.

P0784.d: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0784 names the 4–5 shift as the faulty one, up or down; slip in a steady gear is reported by the ratio codes instead. It only exists on transmissions with five or more gears. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's 2006 five-speed tables run the shift time check under P0780. High engine speed on the motorway from a missing fifth gear is typical.
c: Fluid level wrong, fluid worn or contaminated
Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking
s: Harsh, delayed or missing 4-5 shift
Engine flare during the shift
Warning lamp
Limp mode

P0785.d: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0785 is the general circuit code for solenoid A. GM's 2006 tables use it for the 3-2 downshift solenoid circuit (more than 43 of 50 failed counts, after one trip); Saab's 2002 Aisin box for an open or short in the SLS circuit with warning lamp and limp mode; Hyundai's Genesis bulletins for the drive solenoid, replacing valve and electronic module and then the module if it returns. Limp mode, harsh 3-2 downshifts or – on the Genesis – no drive follow.
c: Connector or wire at the transmission (oil, corrosion)
Electronic module or transmission module driver
s: Warning lamp
Limp mode
Harsh 3-2 downshift (GM) or rough shifts (Aisin)
Genesis shift-by-wire: drive cannot be engaged

P0786.d: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0786 means the circuit is intact but the solenoid does not reach its target current. GM's 2006 Aisin-type five-speed flags a deviation of more than 80 mA for 2.75 s at a steady commanded current above 835 mA, with 11–16 V and fluid above 20 °C, and lights the MIL at once. Rough shifts and limp mode follow; low and high circuit faults are P0787/P0788.
c: Valve worn or coil resistance drifting
s: Rough shifts
Warning lamp
Limp mode

P0787.d: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0787 means current or voltage in the circuit is too low – an open circuit or short to ground. GM's 4L60-E checks the 3-2 downshift solenoid output (more than 43 of 50 counts) after one trip and then sets maximum line pressure, holds third gear and disables the converter clutch; GM's Aisin-type five-speed flags SLS current below 92 mA for 12.5 s. The opposite is P0788.

s: Warning lamp
Limp mode (GM: fixed third gear)
Harsh shifts from maximum pressure

s: Warning lamp

P078F.d: P078F is the circuit fault of a third transmission mode switch (C), after A (P071A–P071C) and B (P071D–P071F): its state is invalid or implausible. GM's transmission modules of 2023 and 2025 list the number only as a blocking condition for another check, without a description of their own; GM reports its drive mode selector today under P05D0–P05D3 (8-step resistor ladder, two trips). No manufacturer document available to us describes P078F itself. The mode then cannot be selected and the transmission stays on its normal schedule.
c: Switch or button faulty or sticking
Wire or connector open or shorted
Moisture or dirt in the centre console
s: Drive mode (sport, winter, tow) cannot be selected
Mode indicator missing
Transmission stays on the normal program

P0790.d: P0790 is the circuit fault of the normal/performance (sport or power program) selector of an automatic transmission – the older single code that preceded the mode switch codes P071A ff; the early J2012 list still called it 'circuit malfunction'. The switch is usually a button to ground or a resistor ladder; a fault is an invalid level, a permanently pressed button or an open circuit. No manufacturer document available to us describes it; GM uses P05D0–P05D3 for its drive mode selector today. The sport program is then unavailable or permanently on.
c: Wire or connector open or shorted
s: Sport or performance program unavailable or always on
Mode indicator missing or flashing

P0791.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0791.d: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. Ford uses P0791 as its only intermediate shaft code, for 'no or too little signal': while the vehicle drives under power (turbine at least 1500 rpm, output at least 650 rpm or 15 mph), the sensor reports below 250 rpm for 5 s – in the 2012 and 2020–23 summaries, with MIL. A Toyota bulletin for the U760 (Highlander, Venza, Camry 2009–10) replaces the countershaft sensor for P0791/P0793. GM's 10-speed has two such sensors but uses its own codes. Limp mode and harsh shifts follow.
c: Connector or wire at the transmission (oil, corrosion, chafing)
Reluctor wheel damaged or debris on the sensor
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or fixed gear
Harsh or delayed shifts
Follow-up pressure control codes (Toyota)

P0792.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0792.d: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. P0792 means a signal is present but implausible: intermediate shaft speed does not match turbine or output speed for the detected gear stage, exceeds a maximum or jumps unrealistically. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford uses only P0791, Toyota's bulletin P0791/P0793, GM its own codes; the logic follows GM's range checks for input and output sensors (P0716/P0721). Ratio codes, by contrast, point to clutch slip rather than a sensor fault.
c: Sensor delivering faulty pulses (air gap, reluctor wheel)
Mechanical slip interpreted as a sensor fault
s: Check engine light or transmission warning
Shift problems
Limp mode possible

P0793.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal
P0793.d: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. P0793 means there is no pulse signal from the intermediate shaft sensor although the vehicle is moving according to other speeds. Toyota's bulletin for the U760 six-speed lists P0793 with P0717 and P0791 and replaces the countershaft sensor with a revised part. Ford reports the same fault under P0791 (below 250 rpm for 5 s). Note that a 2007 Allison table's 'P0793' for shift solenoid 1 low is a typo for P0973. Limp mode and check engine light follow.
s: Check engine light
Limp mode
Harsh shifts
Accompanying codes P0717/P0791

P0794.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0794.d: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. P0794 means the intermediate shaft signal drops out or jumps briefly – not long enough for P0793 – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under movement. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the expected logic counts unrealistic jumps like Ford's P0718 for the turbine sensor (200 spikes within 1.5 s each). Occasional harsh shifts follow, and limp mode after several events.
c: Loose contact at the connector or broken wire
s: Occasional transmission warning
Harsh shift now and then
Limp mode, gone after restart

P0795.d: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0795 is the general code for valve C. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM's 8-speed uses only P0796/P0797 for its clutch 3 valve, Saab's AF40 only P0798 for valve SLC2. Sub-codes for performance, stuck on, electrical and intermittent follow (P0796–P0799).
c: Valve body or pressure valve C
s: Shift problems
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0796.t: Pressure Control Solenoid C Performance/Stuck Off
P0796.d: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0796 means valve C is electrically fine but pressure stays too low. GM's 6-speed flags 400 rpm slip in steady fourth gear with an intrusive test (4-5-6 clutch), the 8-speed 400 rpm for 1.5 s three times (clutch 3), the 9-speed clutch 3 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s, the CVT a line pressure deviation – all after one trip. GM noted false settings on 2017 8-speeds; a 9-speed bulletin calls for clutch inspection and a new valve body. Slipping, missing upper gears and limp mode follow.
c: Clutch, return spring or piston seal of the assigned clutch faulty
Valve body or pressure valve dirty or worn
Fluid level low, fluid worn, filter clogged
s: Slipping or missing upper gears
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0797.t: Pressure Control Solenoid C Stuck On
P0797.d: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0797 means valve C is electrically fine but pressure stays applied – the off-going clutch does not release. GM's 9-speed flags clutch 3 slip below 50 rpm for 0.8 s (0.15 s in other cases), the 8-speed uses a torque and inertia phase test, both after one trip; GM's 9-speed bulletin and Maserati's MC20 dual-clutch sheet list the code too. Harsh shift jolts and a default gear follow.

Limp mode in a fixed gear
Check engine light

P0798.d: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P079A.t: Transmission Friction Element A Slip Detected
P079A.d: The 'friction element slip' codes monitor a clutch that is commanded locked in a power-split hybrid transmission: the module calculates its slip from electric motor, engine and output speeds (target 0 rpm) and flags slip above a threshold for a minimum time, with sufficient line pressure and clutch torque; from 2016 GM also flags a calculated friction energy threshold at once. The letter matches the manufacturer's clutch number. P079A concerns clutch 1. On GM's Two-Mode SUVs and pickups (2008–13) that is the hybrid low/1-2 clutch, flagged above 200 rpm for 3 s after one trip; GM bulletins link it to a clogged line pressure orifice and the auxiliary oil pump. The Volt flags above 200 rpm in three attempts, Malibu Hybrid and Volt from 2016 190 rpm for 0.6 s or 8003 J. Chrysler's Pacifica PHEV fixes P079A by software, as a permanent code with MIL.
c: Clutch A plates worn or glazed
Too little line pressure: low or aged fluid, filter, auxiliary oil pump or blocked pressure orifice
Pressure or shift valve of clutch A or valve body sticking
s: Check engine light or 'service hybrid system' message
Limp mode with reduced power or restricted drive mode
Slipping, engine speed rises without drive
Jolt when the engine starts or stops

P07A2.t: Transmission Friction Element A Performance/Stuck Off
P07A2.d: Each friction element (clutch or brake) has three functional codes: slip while commanded locked (P079A ff), performance/stuck off – it does not apply or applies too weakly – and stuck on – it does not release. P07A2 concerns clutch A. Ford's DPS6 PowerShift dry dual-clutch (Fiesta, Focus) uses it for clutch A – input shaft 1 with gears 1, 3 and 5 – as 'functionally stuck off', next to the electrical codes of its electric clutch actuator; Ford publishes no thresholds. A GM bulletin for the 2017 LaCrosse and 2017–19 XT5 lists P07A2 as 'transmission clutch 1 performance' together with ratio codes, caused by a misaligned range actuator. GM's hybrids do not use it.
c: Clutch A plates worn or piston seal leaking
Too little apply pressure (fluid, pump, valve)
Clutch actuator or valve sticking (DCT: electric actuator)
s: Check engine light or transmission warning
Gear missing or slipping, weak acceleration
Limp mode

P07A3.t: Transmission Friction Element A Stuck On
P07A3.d: Each friction element (clutch or brake) has three functional codes: slip while commanded locked (P079A ff), performance/stuck off – it does not apply or applies too weakly – and stuck on – it does not release. GM's hybrid transmissions use only the stuck-on codes: when a clutch should release, the module expects slip to build and flags it if slip stays near zero – the Two-Mode SUVs (2008–13) at 80 rpm or less for 4.5 s with more than 320–350 Nm on the clutch, after two trips; the Volt Gen 1 and ELR when clutch 1 shows no slip while released ('applied or welded'), three attempts, after one trip; Volt Gen 2, Malibu Hybrid and CT6 plug-in by comparing actual slip with the target release profile, after one trip. Ford's DPS6 uses P07A3 for clutch A 'functionally stuck on'.
c: Clutch A stuck, welded or piston hanging
Valve or spool sticking in the applied position
s: Check engine light or 'service hybrid system' message
Jolt or tie-up on mode or gear changes
Engine stalls or drags when stopping
Limp mode with reduced power

P07A4.t: Transmission Friction Element B Performance/Stuck Off
P07A4.d: Each friction element (clutch or brake) has three functional codes: slip while commanded locked (P079A ff), performance/stuck off – it does not apply or applies too weakly – and stuck on – it does not release. P07A4 concerns clutch B. Only Ford's DPS6 PowerShift dry dual-clutch uses it, for clutch B – input shaft 2 with reverse and gears 2, 4 and 6 – as 'functionally stuck off', next to the electrical codes of the clutch B actuator; Ford publishes no thresholds. GM's hybrids report clutch 2 only as slip (P079B) or stuck on (P07A5). A clutch that does not apply means missing even gears or reverse and limp mode.

P07A7.d: Each friction element (clutch or brake) has three functional codes: slip while commanded locked (P079A ff), performance/stuck off – it does not apply or applies too weakly – and stuck on – it does not release. P07B2.t: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit/Open
P07B2.d: With electronic gear selection the park position sensor/switch reports the park request or position. On GM's shift-by-wire selectors (2017 LaCrosse, XT4/XT5, Bolt EV, later SUVs and pickups) it is the P button, read by two redundant analog sensors A and B with separate 'released' and 'pressed' voltage zones. P07B2 means the circuit of sensor A is open: the module sees a missing or undefined signal. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM covers an open analog circuit under its low and high codes (P07B3/P07B4), which CARB allows when an open cannot be told apart from an out-of-range value. P07BF.t: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P07BF.d: These low/high codes are a purely electrical check of the sensor's signal voltage at the module and run even with the vehicle at rest – unlike the circuit, range, no-signal and intermittent codes, which evaluate speed while driving. Low means a short to ground, high a short to supply or, depending on the circuit, an open. GM's transmission modules from 2019 (9-speed, 10-speed) flag below 0.25 V or above 4.75 V – a short of under 0.5 Ω – for more than 0.05 s with the system above 10 V for 5 s, after one trip. P07BF is the low side: a short to ground of the input sensor. A GM bulletin for 2019 nine-speed models (Enclave, Equinox, Malibu, XT4 and others) traces intermittent P07BF/P07C0 together with P0717 to an open inside the input speed sensor.
c: Signal or supply wire shorted to ground (chafing at the case)
Oil or moisture in the connector
s: Check engine light (GM after one trip)
Limp mode, harsh shifts, no converter lock-up

Low means a short to ground, high a short to supply or, depending on the circuit, an open. Intermediate shaft sensor B is a further sensor on a countershaft or planetary element. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM reports further 10-speed intermediate sensors under its own codes. The expected logic follows the other sensors (above about 4.75 V); the speed-based codes for sensor B are P2745–P2748.
c: Open circuit or broken wire inside the sensor
s: Check engine light (GM after one trip)
Limp mode, harsh shifts, no converter lock-up
Adaption frozen

P07CB.d: Many automatics have a thermostat in the fluid cooler circuit or a coolant-to-oil heat exchanger: a BMW patent describes a wax thermostat that bypasses the cooler until about 76 °C, a Ford patent a heat exchanger that warms transmission fluid from the coolant after a cold start. P07CB means this thermostat does not work as expected: fluid warms up too slowly (stuck open) or overheats (stuck closed). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM checks fluid warm-up under the temperature sensor code P0711 (below 15 °C after the warm-up time, two trips). The check works like CARB's engine thermostat monitor (P0128). Slow warm-up raises consumption and delays converter lock-up; overheating ages fluid quickly.
c: Transmission fluid thermostat stuck open or closed
Cooler lines or heat exchanger blocked or leaking
Very cold weather or short trips
s: Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Converter clutch applies late, higher consumption
Fluid overheating warning

P07CC.t: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit Low
P07CC.d: Transmission mode switches select alternative shift programs such as sport, winter or tow/haul; the J2012 family runs from A (P071A–P071C) and B (P071D–P071F) to C (base code P078F), D and E. No manufacturer document available to us uses switches C to E; GM reads its analog mode switch under its own codes (low below 21–29 % of 5 V, high from 94 %, two trips) and newer drive mode selectors under P05D0–P05D3. P07CC means the signal of mode switch C is below its lower limit – a short to ground or a button stuck against ground. The opposite is P07CD.
c: Moisture or dirt in the button
s: Mode C cannot be selected or stays active
Mode indicator missing or flashing
Transmission stays on the normal program

P07D7.d: P07D7 means gear 8 cannot be disengaged: the module commands a shift out of 8th, but the transmission stays in it. It is the counterpart to P07D8, where gear 8 cannot be engaged. The only documented user is Maserati's eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox in the MC20 (from model year 2023), whose bulletin lists it next to the other 'Stuck in Gear' codes: hydraulic actuators move the shift forks, and a fork that does not reach neutral is reported. The repair path there first runs a service fast-learn with valve flushing and new adaptation, then records system pressure – it should hold 20–30 bar; drops below 5 bar point to the mechatronic unit, a stable pressure to the gearbox itself. No thresholds or trip counts are published.
c: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
s: Transmission stays in gear 8 and will not downshift
Weak take-off after stopping
Transmission warning, limp mode

P07D8.d: 'Unable to Engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – here 8th. Documented users are eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes with hydraulically moved, position-monitored shift forks. A GM bulletin for the 2020–23 Corvette lists it with the MIL on, caused by a solenoid or internal switch sticking from debris: valve cleaning is only advised when system pressure codes are present as well, otherwise a service fast-learn; if that fails, the mechanics are damaged. Maserati's MC20 lists it with a pressure check of 20–30 bar. On a dual-clutch box the half carrying the even gears may be locked out. No published thresholds or trip counts.
c: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
s: Gear 8 skipped or never reached, higher rpm at cruise
Check engine and transmission warning lamp
Jerky shifts, possibly loss of one half of a dual-clutch gearbox

P07D9.d: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7. P07D9 covers 8th gear. Ford's 10R80 (F-150, Mustang, Ranger, Expedition and others) and 10R140 (2020 Super Duty) list it in bulletins on harsh or delayed shifts, caused by adaptive learning, sticking valve-body valves or a migrating sleeve in a clutch cylinder. Nissan's nine-speed Frontier and Titan set it with the MIL on; a Stellantis bulletin pairs it with P0731 on low-mileage vehicles with wrong factory adaptives. Hyundai's eight-speeds and GM's 10-speed do not use it.
c: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong
s: Slipping or flaring engine speed in gear 8
Harsh or delayed shifts
Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Gear 8 locked out, higher rpm at cruise

P07DA.d: Shift codes check the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded change with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, does not happen, flares or binds up two clutches. They continue the series P0781 '1-2 Shift' to P0784 '4-5 Shift'. No manufacturer document available to us uses P07DA or P07DB: Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion (speed must drop by more than 30 rpm on an upshift, flare above 300 rpm) without a gear-specific code, Ford's 10R80 feeds the solenoid function codes and GM the clutch valve codes. P07DA names the change between 6th and 7th gear, in either direction, as faulty; it exists only on transmissions with seven or more gears. Flags and thresholds follow the manufacturer's own logic.
c: Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
s: Harsh, delayed or missing 6-7 shift
Engine speed flares during the shift
Transmission warning, possibly MIL

P07DC.d: The series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA and P07FD for 9 and 10) covers a shift that leaves the starting gear but lands in a gear other than the commanded target – a skipped or overshot gear. A module can see this after the shift because the measured ratio matches the wrong gear. No manufacturer document available to us uses the series: Ford assigns such patterns to the shift solenoid that caused them (P0751 ff), newer GM automatics report clutch pressure valve codes. P07DC starts from gear 1. It differs from P0731 (wrong ratio while in gear 1, a slipping clutch), P072C (gear 1 cannot be left) and P0781 (the shift itself takes too long or flares). Detection, MIL and trip count therefore follow only by analogy from CARB's functional check and Ford's ratio and shift completion checks.
c: Shift or pressure control valve sticking in the valve body
Clutch or brake pack worn or leaking
Turbine or output speed signal wrong
s: Wrong or skipped gear when shifting out of gear 1
Harsh shift or engine speed jump
Transmission warning, possibly limp mode in a fixed gear
