P07E4.d: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E4 means park is not reached or not held within the allowed time. GM gives thresholds: 2 s in 2018 tables and the ICCM of its electronic range selector (2000 ms), 6–10 s in later tables, type B with the MIL after two trips; a 2018 bulletin for LaCrosse and XT5 blames a misaligned coupling of the range control module. Ford sets it with the wrench lamp instead of the MIL – on the 2020 Escape and Corsair a misrouted park release cable, on the Mach-E software – and applies the electric parking brake. Ram 1500 (2019) sets the MIL; Stellantis names a used manual park release as the most common cause.
c: Manual park release cable misrouted or actuated
Range actuator misaligned or its coupling offset
Park lock actuator or its ground faulty
Range or park position signal wrong
s: Park cannot be selected, 'Park not available' message
Electric parking brake applies automatically
Wrench lamp (Ford) or MIL (GM, Ram)
Vehicle may roll away if not secured

P07E5.d: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E5 means drive is requested but not reached in time. Only GM documents it: its electronic range selector (LaCrosse, XT5, XT4, 2025 Equinox and Terrain) allows 10 s in most tables, 3 s in the 2018 Diesel table and 2000 ms in the selector module, type B with the MIL after two trips. A 2018 bulletin blames a misaligned range control module coupling, its 2019 revision adds ratio codes; on the 2025 Equinox and Terrain it can appear after an over-the-air update and clears after a ten-minute rest. The car does not move forward or falls back to neutral.
c: Range control actuator misaligned or faulty
Software or after-effect of an over-the-air update
Forward clutch or line pressure missing
s: No drive in D
'Service Transmission' message, MIL
Range falls back to N or P

P07E6.d: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E6 means park cannot be left: the pawl stays engaged or its position feedback keeps reporting P. Ford documents it on the HF45 hybrid transmission (2023–24 Escape, 2022–24 Maverick), where the inverter control module monitors the park actuator – the P on the rotary selector flashes, the wrench lamp comes on and an internally failed actuator is replaced (about 13–14 h) – and on the 2024–25 Mach-E, where a high resistance in the park motor ground is fixed with new software and a ground harness. Maserati lists it for the MC20 dual-clutch gearbox. Ford keeps it off the MIL; GM tables do not list it.
c: High resistance at the park motor ground
s: Vehicle stays in P and cannot be driven away
P flashes on the selector, P in the cluster dark
Wrench lamp or 'Service vehicle soon'

P07E7.d: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E7 means drive cannot be left: after a request for P, N or R the transmission stays in D. It is the counterpart to P07E5, where drive cannot be engaged, and to P07E6 for park. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM's range selector module checks requested against reached range in the same way for P07E4 and P07E5 (2000 ms, two trips). With shift-by-wire the fault matters for safety, because the car cannot be put into park or neutral. Typical causes would be a sticking range actuator or selector shaft, a range sensor wrongly reporting D, or the selector or its software.
c: Range actuator or selector shaft sticking
s: Range stays in D despite the selector request
P or N cannot be reached, warning message
Warning lamp (depends on manufacturer)

P07E8.d: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07E8 is the open-circuit check of these sensor lines: if one sensor input is pulled above 4.5 V for 2.4 s with the ignition on, the code sets. Mitsubishi lists it with the MIL but without a fail-safe reaction, because the remaining sensors still identify the position. Low and high are P07EA/P07EB. GM and Ford use their own codes for their selectors.
c: Wire or connector between selector and shift module open
Position sensor in the selector faulty
s: Electric shift or check engine warning
Usually no noticeable restriction
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07E9.t: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Performance
P07E9.d: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07E9 is the plausibility check of the sensor voltage: valid levels lie only in defined on and off windows, and a sensor sitting for 2.4 s in a forbidden band in between (0.6–1.07, 2.12–2.67 or 3.28–4.5 V) sets it – typically contact resistance, moisture or a sensor beginning to fail. Mitsubishi defines no fail-safe reaction. Note the title: 'Circuit Performance', not 'Range/Performance'.
c: Corroded or damp connector, contact resistance
s: Electric shift or check engine warning
Usually no noticeable restriction
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07EA.t: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Low
P07EA.d: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07EA is the electrical low check: one sensor reads below 0.6 V for 2.4 s – a signal wire shorted to ground or a missing sensor supply. Mitsubishi defines no fail-safe reaction. If all bits drop out at once, P07EF follows and the transmission goes to neutral.
c: Selector sensor wire shorted to ground (chafed harness, connector)
Sensor supply in the selector open
s: Electric shift or check engine warning
Usually no noticeable restriction
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07EB.t: Transmission Range Control A Circuit High
P07EB.d: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07EB is the electrical high check: one sensor reads above 4.5 V for 2.4 s, a signal wire shorted to the supply. Mitsubishi uses the same threshold as for the open circuit P07E8 and separates the two only in its list of causes; there is no fail-safe reaction.
c: Signal wire shorted to 5 V or 12 V supply
s: Electric shift or check engine warning
Usually no noticeable restriction
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07EC.d: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07EC sets when a single bit does not change as the lever moves through its positions – it is stuck on or off. The other bits still identify the position, but the decision takes at least a second. Mitsubishi shows only the yellow electric-shift warning, without the MIL. Two or more stuck bits are P07ED.
c: One position sensor in the selector faulty
One sensor wire open or shorted
Dirt or sticking mechanism in the selector
s: Yellow shift warning or message
Selected range taken over with a delay of a second or more
No MIL (Mitsubishi)

P07ED.t: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Stuck
P07ED.d: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07ED is the step after P07EC: at least two bits are stuck, so the position can no longer be decoded reliably. Mitsubishi then puts the drive in neutral and blocks changes between P, R, N and D, lights the MIL and the red or yellow shift warning; the car cannot be driven and has to be towed.
c: Selector connector corroded or loose (several pins)
Liquid spilled into the center console
s: No range can be selected, vehicle in neutral
MIL and red or yellow shift warning
Vehicle cannot be driven (tow)

P07EE.t: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Range/Performance
P07EE.d: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07EE is the range and plausibility fault of the position code; Mitsubishi assigns it solely to the electric shift module itself – the pattern fits no position or contradicts itself. A generic scan tool shows the fault as P0914 'Gear Shift Position Circuit A'. Shifting is blocked, the drive goes to neutral and the MIL comes on; the usual repair is a software update or the module.
c: Electric shift module faulty (hardware or software)
s: Vehicle goes to neutral, shifting blocked
MIL and shift warning
Generic scan tool shows P0914

P07EF.t: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Low
P07EF.d: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07EF is the low state of the whole pattern: all eight bits report off, which is no valid code – typically a disconnected selector plug or a missing common supply or ground. Mitsubishi detects it already at standstill after about 10 s with the ignition on, puts the drive in neutral and lights the MIL.
c: Selector plug disconnected or its supply or ground open
s: Vehicle in neutral, no range selectable
MIL and shift warning
Fault appears right after switching the ignition on

P07F0.t: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit High
P07F0.d: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07F0 would be the high counterpart of P07EF: the position code reports a high state that matches no valid position, for example signal levels pulled up by a short to the supply. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – on Mitsubishi's selector 'all on' is the valid home position, so a high state cannot be told apart there. By analogy to P07EF a module would block range changes or select neutral.
c: Selector signal wires shorted to the supply
s: Shift warning or MIL (depends on manufacturer)
Range selection blocked or neutral

P07F1.t: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit
P07F1.d: P07F1 is the general circuit code of a third input or turbine shaft speed sensor, after sensor A (P0715) and B (P2765); low and high for sensor C are P07C3 and P07C4. No production use could be found in GM tables from 2015 to 2025, Ford's summaries of 2012 and 2020–23, Mitsubishi's code index or manufacturer bulletins; such a sensor would make sense on transmissions with three input shafts or a hybrid input. The check would follow P0715: no plausible signal while driving or an open circuit. The module then uses a substitute value, keeps the converter clutch open and shifts more harshly; with emissions impact CARB requires the MIL.
s: Check engine lamp (expected)
Harsh shifts, converter clutch stays open
Limp mode possible

P07F2.t: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit
P07F2.d: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F2 reports a fault in its communication. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift sets it when the module's start-up CAN check fails and blames the module itself; it switches to neutral only if the CVT or the whole system is affected too, and one of its two entries carries no MIL. GM (U18AA, U2409) and Ford (U101F, without MIL) report the same function under their own U codes.
c: Shift-by-wire module faulty or its software
s: Shift warning
Usually no restriction; neutral if the transmission is affected too
U codes in other modules possible

P07F3.t: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit Low
P07F3.d: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F3 is the electrical low check of its communication line: the line is shorted to ground and stays at a low level. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; the code fits a dedicated signal or redundancy line between selector, range control module and transmission or engine module rather than a CAN bus. GM handles a bus short under its own U2409 (bus off for 1 s, two trips). The module may block range changes or select neutral.
c: Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Shift warning
Possible shift lock or neutral (depends on manufacturer)

P07F4.t: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit High
P07F4.d: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F4 is the electrical high check of its communication line: the line is shorted to the supply and stays at a high level. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; as with P07F3 it fits a dedicated signal or redundancy line rather than a CAN bus, whose faults GM reports under its own U codes. The module may block range changes or select neutral.
c: Communication wire shorted to the supply
s: Shift warning
Possible shift lock or neutral (depends on manufacturer)

P07F5.t: Transmission Range Control Module System Voltage Low
P07F5.d: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F5 means its supply voltage is too low. No manufacturer document available to us uses the generic code, but GM checks exactly this under its own P17B0: battery voltage at the range control module at or below 9 V for 5 s within a 6 s window, type C without MIL. With too little voltage the actuator may not set the range or park pawl reliably; GM also suspends further checks of the module. A weak battery or a resistance in the module's fuse, supply or ground is the usual cause.
c: Fuse, supply or ground wire of the module with high resistance
High actuator motor current on a weak supply
s: Shift warning
Range or park lock reacts late or not at all
Often together with battery voltage codes

P07F6.d: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7. P07F6 covers 9th gear. Ford's 10R80 bulletins from 2023 to 2025 (F-150, Mustang, Ranger, Explorer, Transit, Expedition) list it with the other ratio codes; the causes are adaptive learning, the valve body and a migrating clutch cylinder sleeve. The 10R140 bulletin of 2021 does not mention it. Nissan's nine-speed Frontier and Titan set it with the MIL on; the repair check drives each gear 1–9 for at least 10 s in manual mode.
c: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong
s: Slipping or flaring engine speed in gear 9
Harsh or delayed shifts
Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Gear 9 locked out, higher rpm at cruise

P07F7.d: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7. P07F7 covers 10th gear, so in practice only ten-speed automatics. Ford's 10R80 lists it in all its ratio bulletins. On the 2020 Super Duty with the 10R140 a 2025 bulletin shows P07F7 alone, with the powertrain wrench lamp instead of the MIL and 10th gear locked out, caused by a migrating sleeve in a clutch cylinder that leaks; an earlier bulletin blames sticking main valve-body valves. GM's 10-speed reports through clutch valve codes instead.
c: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong
s: Slipping or flaring engine speed in gear 10
Harsh or delayed shifts
Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Gear 10 locked out, higher rpm at cruise

P07F8.d: P07F8 means gear 9 cannot be disengaged: the transmission stays in 9th despite the command to leave it. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. The family is documented only for 8th gear on eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes (Maserati MC20: P07D7 and P07D8; Corvette 2020–23: P07D8), where hydraulic actuators move shift forks under position monitoring. Nine- and ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford, GM and Nissan report faults in 9th gear as a ratio code (P07F6) or through solenoid and clutch valve codes. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.
c: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
s: Transmission stays in gear 9 and will not downshift
Weak take-off after stopping
Transmission warning, limp mode

P07F9.d: P07F9 means the transmission does not reach the commanded 9th gear – the counterpart to P07F8, where 9th cannot be left. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. 'Unable to Engage' is documented only for eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes, for example the 2020–23 Corvette (P07D8, MIL on, sticking solenoid from debris). Nine- and ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford, GM and Nissan report faults in 9th gear as a ratio code (P07F6) or through valve codes. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.
c: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
s: Gear 9 skipped or never reached, higher rpm at cruise
Check engine and transmission warning lamp
Jerky shifts, possibly loss of one half of a dual-clutch gearbox

P07FA.d: P07FA belongs to the series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA for 9, P07FD for 10): when leaving 9th gear, the transmission ends up in a gear other than the commanded target, or the shift out of 9th goes wrong. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Ten-speed users such as Ford's 10R family and GM's 10L report such faults through ratio or valve codes; Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion without a gear-specific code. Possible causes are a sticking shift or clutch valve, a worn or leaking clutch, or wrong adaptives.
c: Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
s: Wrong gear or harsh downshift out of 9th
Transmission warning, possibly limp mode

P07FB.d: P07FB means gear 10 cannot be disengaged: the transmission stays in 10th despite the command to leave it. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. The family is documented only for 8th gear on eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes (Maserati MC20, Corvette 2020–23); no dual-clutch gearbox with ten gears and these codes is known. Ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford and GM report faults in 10th gear as a ratio code (P07F7, on Ford's 10R140 with 10th gear locked out) or through valve codes. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.
c: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
s: Transmission stays in gear 10 and will not downshift
Weak take-off after stopping
Transmission warning, limp mode

P07FC.d: P07FC means the transmission does not reach the commanded 10th gear – the counterpart to P07FB, where 10th cannot be left. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. 'Unable to Engage' is documented only for eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes, for example the 2020–23 Corvette (P07D8). Ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford and GM report a missing 10th gear as a ratio code (P07F7) or through valve codes; Ford's 10R140 then locks out 10th. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.
c: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
s: Gear 10 skipped or never reached, higher rpm at cruise
Check engine and transmission warning lamp
Jerky shifts, possibly loss of one half of a dual-clutch gearbox

P07FD.d: P07FD closes the series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA for 9): when leaving 10th gear, the transmission ends up in a gear other than the commanded target, or the shift out of 10th goes wrong. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Ten-speed users such as Ford's 10R family and GM's 10L report such faults through ratio or valve codes; Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion without a gear-specific code. Possible causes are a sticking shift or clutch valve, a worn or leaking clutch, or wrong adaptives.
c: Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
s: Wrong gear or harsh downshift out of 10th
Transmission warning, possibly limp mode

P07FE.d: P07FE is the catch-all of the 'Stuck in Gear' family: the transmission stays in a gear it was commanded to leave, but the module cannot or does not name the gear. The gear-specific codes are P072B–P073C for reverse and gears 1–7, P07D7 for 8th, P07F8 for 9th and P07FB for 10th. No manufacturer document available to us uses P07FE; the gear-specific codes are documented on dual-clutch gearboxes such as Ford's DPS6 and Maserati's MC20, whose actuators move shift drums or forks. Typical causes are a sticking shift actuator or valve, low or unstable system pressure, mechanical damage, or a faulty position or speed signal.
c: Shift actuator or shift valve sticking
Mechanical damage in the gear train
Position or speed sensor signal wrong
s: Transmission no longer shifts and stays in one gear
Limp mode, transmission warning

P07FF.d: P07FF means the transmission does not work as expected during the cold-start phase, shortly after starting with cold, thick fluid – for example a gear preselection or a clutch or valve response outside the expected window. The only documented user is Mercedes-Benz: its 2024 bulletin for the eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox 8G-DCT in the compact models (A-Class, CLA, GLA, GLB) names P07FF together with P0921, with reverse not available, a possible limp-home mode and the MIL; after switching off and on everything works again, and the fix was new control unit software. No thresholds or trip counts are published. It is not CARB's cold-start emission strategy, which concerns engine and catalyst heating (P050A ff), but a functional check of the transmission.
c: Transmission control module software misjudging the cold phase
Shift valve or hydraulics too slow with cold fluid
Wrong or aged fluid, low level
s: Reverse not available (message in the cluster)
Check engine lamp on
Limp-home mode shortly after a cold start
Normal again after switching off and on

P0800.d: P0800 works like P0700 for the transmission: the transfer case control module has detected a fault of its own that it rates as emissions-relevant and asks the engine control module to turn on the MIL. The engine module only stores P0800; the actual fault – often C, U or manufacturer codes – sits in the transfer case module and needs a scan tool that addresses it. CARB requires monitoring of an electronic transfer case only where it feeds other diagnostics, for example the 4WD-low signal that GM uses as an enable condition; this is why most transfer case modules never request the MIL and P0800 hardly appears in manufacturer documents. A GM bulletin for 2020–23 trucks with 'Service 4WD' and the MIL points to wiring and terminal contact at the transfer case.
c: Fault in the transfer case system stored in its module (shift motor, sensor, clutch)
Wiring or connector at the transfer case (terminal tension, corrosion)
s: Check engine lamp on
'Service 4WD' or similar warning
All-wheel drive or low range cannot be selected

P0801.d: On GM manual gearboxes (Tremec T56/TR6060 in Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V and ATS-V) the engine module drives a solenoid that blocks reverse while the car moves forward. P0801 means its control circuit is open. GM's tables describe the check: the low-side driver's internal diagnosis flags an open line with at least 9 V and the engine above 250 rpm, 20 failures in 25 samples of 250 ms – about 6 s; in 2006 a 5 s comparison of commanded and actual driver state. GM rates it type C, emissions-neutral and without MIL, from 2019 with a 'service vehicle soon' note. Depending on how it fails, reverse cannot be engaged or is no longer blocked. The title was updated to the current J2012 wording with '/Open'.
c: Connector at the reverse inhibit solenoid loose or corroded
Harness between engine module and gearbox damaged
s: Reverse hard or impossible to engage
Reverse no longer blocked
Service note in the driver display, usually no MIL

P0802.t: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open
P0802.d: On older vehicles with a separate transmission module and no MIL message on the CAN bus, the transmission module signals 'MIL on' over its own wire to the engine module. P0802 checks this wire for an open circuit. GM's Duramax tables of 2004 and 2005 (Allison 1000) describe it: at key-on the transmission module briefly pulls the line active like a bulb check; if the engine module sees no off-to-on transition between 0.125 and 7 s after ignition, the line is treated as open – type B, MIL after two trips. Only then is P0700 evaluated. The wire itself must be monitored because an open line would stop transmission emission faults from lighting the MIL. Newer vehicles send the request over CAN, where faults appear as U codes.
c: MIL request wire or connector between the modules open or corroded
Transmission module without power or ground (fuse, relay)
Wrong or retrofitted transmission module without this line
s: Check engine lamp on
Transmission faults no longer light the MIL
Usually no change in driving

P0803.d: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid in the shifter housing that, at light load and low speed blocks the way from 1st into 2nd and 3rd so the driver shifts 1 to 4 – a measure for fuel economy ratings; the 1-4 lamp (P0804) shows it. P0803 means the solenoid control circuit is open. GM's tables check the low-side driver while it is off: too low a voltage or over 200 kΩ to ground, with at least 9 V and over 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms (2019 LT5: 20 of 25), type B with the MIL after two trips; shorts are P080C and P080D. An open circuit leaves the solenoid unpowered, so 1 to 2 always works. 'Skip-shift eliminators' with the wrong resistance are a frequent cause.
c: Solenoid unplugged or replaced by a skip-shift eliminator with the wrong resistance
Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded
s: Check engine lamp after two trips
1-4 lockout no longer works (1-2 always possible)
Otherwise no change in driving

P0804.d: With GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes, a '1-4' lamp in the cluster tells the driver that the lockout is active and to shift from 1st directly into 4th. P0804 means the control circuit of this lamp is faulty – open, shorted, or the lamp does not follow its command. No GM table from 2004 to 2025 available to us contains it, because newer cars switch the indicator by a CAN message from the instrument cluster without a separate engine-module line check; the code therefore mainly concerns older vehicles with a lamp driven directly by the engine module. The lockout itself (P0803) keeps working, only the hint is missing; there is no limp mode, and the MIL behavior is not documented.
c: Bulb or LED in the cluster faulty
Wire or connector between engine module and cluster open or shorted
s: 1-4 lamp never lights or stays on
Possibly check engine lamp
Lockout works without the hint

P0805.d: The J2012 family 'Clutch Position Sensor A' (P0805 circuit, P0806 range/performance, P0807 low, P0808 high, P0809 intermittent, P080A not learned) covers the position of a clutch – the pedal of a manual gearbox, the clutch actuator of an automated or dual-clutch gearbox, or a clutch inside an automatic. P0805 is the general circuit fault. Uses differ: Nissan's 2022 Pathfinder with its nine-speed automatic stores it in the transmission module, lights the MIL and disables idle stop ('Idle Stop System Fault'), fixed with new software. Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch gearbox uses it for the module-internal chip that drives the clutch A motor, so a control unit fault rather than an outside sensor. GM reads its clutch pedal sensor under P0806–P0808 only.
c: Clutch position sensor faulty (pedal or actuator)
Connector or harness open, corroded or shorted
Control unit internal fault (Ford DPS6: clutch motor driver)
s: Check engine lamp on
Idle stop disabled ('Idle Stop System Fault')
Jerky driving or harsh clutch engagement (dual clutch)

P0806.t: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0806.d: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0806 is the plausibility check. On GM's LT4 manual cars the pedal sensor is compared with gear detection: if it reports the clutch pressed while engine and output speed show a valid gear, a filtered position error above 4 % sets the code (above 5.6 mph, not in 4WD low), type A with the MIL after one trip. On Ford's DPS6 it reports a fault of the Hall sensors on the clutch A motor; Saab sets it for a frozen pedal signal and switches off cruise control.
c: Pedal sensor or Hall sensors of the clutch motor faulty
Pedal sensor misadjusted or not relearned after clutch work
Harness or connector with contact resistance
Master cylinder leaking, pedal does not fully return
s: Check engine lamp on
Cruise control and start-stop not working
Engine starts only with the pedal fully pressed, or not at all
Dual clutch: jerky take-off, limp mode

P0807.t: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0807.d: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0807 means the signal is too low. GM's three-wire pedal sensor on a 5 V reference has dead bands at both ends: below 4 % of the reference counts as low or open, 200 of 250 samples of 12.5 ms (about 3 s), engine not cranking, over 9 V, type A with the MIL after one trip. Saab names an open circuit or short to ground. With the clutch position unknown, cruise control, start-stop and starter release by the sensor are blocked.
c: Signal wire open or shorted to ground
5 V reference of the sensor missing
s: Check engine lamp on
Cruise control not working
Start-stop disabled, possibly no engine start

P0808.t: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0808.d: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0808 means the signal is too high. GM sets it above 96 % of the 5 V reference with the same 200 of 250 samples of 12.5 ms, type A with the MIL after one trip; Saab's 2012 9-3 above 4.8 V for longer than 0.6 s, with cruise control switched off. Typical causes are an open sensor ground or a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or battery voltage.
c: Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Check engine lamp on
Cruise control not working
Start-stop disabled

P0809.t: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0809.d: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0809 is documented only for Ford's DPS6 (Fiesta from 2011, Focus from 2012): the motor that operates clutch A carries three Hall sensors, one per phase, and while the motor turns they must produce a fixed sequence; a wrong sequence sets the code. The clutch B counterpart is P087E. The module then loses confidence in the clutch position, so clutch A with the odd gears 1, 3 and 5 is restricted. GM and Saab do not use P0809; Ford publishes no thresholds.
c: Clutch A actuator motor or its Hall sensors faulty
Loose contact at the actuator connector
s: Check engine lamp on
Jerky or judder take-off
Limp mode, odd gears missing

P080A.d: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P080A means the learned clutch position is missing or implausible. On GM manual cars the factory learns the pedal position 'clutch fully pressed', and the engine module then tracks it as the clutch wears; a learned value outside 9.0–36.0 % of travel sets the code (250 ms, type A, one trip), a factory counter keeps the MIL off during assembly. Saab clears it by relearning with the scan tool. A relearn is needed after replacing the pedal sensor, master cylinder, clutch or engine module.
c: Relearn not done after sensor, clutch or module replacement
Pedal sensor misadjusted or wrongly fitted
s: Check engine lamp on
Start-stop, cruise control or hill start assist disabled
Engine may start only with the pedal at the stop

P080B.t: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
P080B.d: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080B would be the range or performance fault of this circuit: electrically plausible, but outside the expected range for the command – for example a coil resistance outside its window, a partial short or contact resistance. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM's tables from 2006 to 2019 check the solenoid only electrically (P0803 open, P080C short to ground, P080D short to positive). CARB requires a functional check of outputs where feasible. The lockout may then work unreliably.
c: Solenoid coil with shorted turns or resistance out of range
Retrofitted skip-shift eliminator with the wrong value
Corroded connector at the gearbox (contact resistance)
s: Check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer)
1-4 lockout works not at all or only sometimes
Otherwise no change in driving

P080C.t: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P080C.d: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080C means the control line is shorted to ground: with the driver off it should sit at battery voltage through the coil but reads low (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to ground). GM checks it from 9 V (2015/16: 11–32 V) and above 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms, type B with the MIL after two trips; the 2019 LT5 uses 20 of 25 samples and type A, one trip. In the 2015/16 tables P080C also covers an open circuit. A low-side short keeps the solenoid energized, so the lockout may stay active.
c: Control wire chafed through to ground at gearbox or frame
Solenoid coil shorted to its housing
Older GM modules: circuit open or solenoid unplugged
s: Check engine lamp
1-4 lockout permanently active or not working
1-4 lamp possibly unrelated to the lockout

P080D.t: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit High
P080D.d: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080D means the control line is shorted to positive: with the low-side driver on, the line should be pulled to ground but reads high (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to the supply). The solenoid cannot be energized and the driver is protected or switched off. GM checks it only with the driver on, from 9 V (2015/16: 11–32 V) and above 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms, type B with the MIL after two trips in all tables from 2015 to 2019. Without power the solenoid does not lock, so 1 to 2 stays free.
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage (damaged harness)
Solenoid coil with shorted turns (resistance near zero)
Substitute resistor ('eliminator') with too low a value
s: Check engine lamp after two trips
1-4 lockout not working
Otherwise no change in driving

P0810.d: P0810 reports a control error of an electronically or hydraulically operated clutch: commanded and actual position differ too much or for too long. It is documented on Stellantis plug-in hybrids – Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe with the 8P75PH transmission – where it concerns the K0 disconnect clutch between engine and electric motor. According to the 2024 and 2025 bulletins the clutch adaptation ran at standstill or in electric mode, drive was lost until the next key cycle and the MIL came on; the cause was too tight setting parameters, fixed with new transmission software, partly together with P2885. On automated or dual-clutch gearboxes the same idea applies when the clutch actuator misses its target position.
c: Control unit software with too tight parameters
Clutch actuator or hydraulics (pressure, valve) faulty
Wrong or aged fluid, worn clutch
s: Check engine lamp on
Transmission warning message
Loss of drive until the next key cycle

P0811.d: P0811 means clutch A slips too much while it should be closed – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 1 with the odd gears. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch; thresholds are not published. Audi's seven-speed S tronic DL382 (A4 to A7 and Q5, 2020–24) sets it intermittently together with P081E and input speed sensor codes, partly also clutch temperature too high; the cause was the transmission module calculating wrong slip, and the fix was a new module. Genuine slip from wear or overheating shows as flaring take-off and burnt fluid. The module limits torque, may lock out the affected half and go to limp mode.
c: Transmission module calculating wrong slip (speed capture)
Clutch pressure or actuator too low
s: Transmission warning, limp mode
Engine flares, poor acceleration
Judder on take-off
Burning smell

P0812.d: P0812 concerns the input 'reverse engaged' at the engine or transmission module – the reverse or back-up lamp switch on a manual gearbox, or the R contact of a selector. Modules check it for open or stuck states and against a second source such as a gear position sensor or the direction from speed sensors. A Honda patent describes this double detection: reverse counts only when switch and gear position sensor agree; if only one reports R, it is a fault and engine speed is limited. No manufacturer document with thresholds is available to us. Back-up lamps, reversing camera or parking aids may fail; on automated manual gearboxes reverse may be blocked. CARB lets such safety and comfort inputs run without the MIL.
c: Reverse or back-up lamp switch faulty or misadjusted
Connector loose or wire broken (e.g. after clutch work)
Gear position sensor reporting the wrong position
s: Back-up lamps never or always on
Reversing camera or parking aid does not switch on
Usually no check engine lamp

P0813.d: P0813 concerns a signal 'reverse active' that a module puts out – usually the transmission module, on manual cars the engine or body module – for example to the back-up lamp relay, the reversing camera or the body module. Like other driver outputs it is checked by comparing commanded and actual state, which reveals an open circuit or a short. Saab's 2012 transmission module reports a short to positive on its park/neutral output in the same way. No manufacturer document with thresholds for the reverse output is available to us. Back-up lamps, camera or mirror tilt may stop working; driving itself is not affected, and CARB allows such outputs without the MIL.
c: Wire from module to relay or body module open or shorted
Back-up lamp relay or connected load faulty
s: Back-up lamps not working
Reversing camera or parking beeper does not activate
Stored code without driving effects

P0814.d: P0814 concerns the drive or data circuit of the range display – the PRNDL or PRNDM display or lighting on the selector, sometimes in the instrument cluster. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: the electronic shift module stores P0814 with the MIL on, the selector lighting flickers or goes dark, and in a 2020 bulletin the lever could be moved out of park during cranking so that the engine stalled. The cause was software in the shift module, fixed by reflashing; a 2022 bulletin adds P081C. A wrong or missing range display matters for safety because the driver cannot reliably see P, R or N. No thresholds are published.
c: Connector or wire to the selector display or cluster
Display LED or selector module faulty
Range sensor or transmission module delivering an invalid range
s: Range display on the selector flickers or stays dark
Check engine lamp (Jeep)
Lever can leave P during cranking, engine stalls (Jeep)

P0815.d: Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch. P0815 is the upshift switch. GM's 2019 and 2025 tables set it when 'tap up' stays on for more than 1 s in P or N, or permanently in a drive range; the 2018 hybrid table uses 2 s in P/N and 655 s in drive; type C without MIL. Ford's 6R80 and 6F35 SelectShift report a switch closed in P, R or N without MIL. On Saab's 9-4X with the 6T70 a Hall switch feeds a resistor network on one wire: a short to positive sets P0815 or P0816, a short to ground or an open sets P0826. Manual shifting is then disabled.
c: Tap switch or paddle sticking or faulty
Selector assembly (Hall sensor, resistor network) faulty
s: Manual up shifting not working
Transmission stays in the normal automatic mode
No check engine lamp

P0816.d: Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch. P0816 is the mirror of P0815 for the downshift switch. GM's 2025 table sets it when 'tap down' stays on for more than 1 s (100 ms raster, over 9 V), the 2018 hybrid table after 2 s in P/N or 655 s in drive, type C without MIL; Saab's 9-4X after 1 s in P/N or 10 minutes in a drive range; Ford's SelectShift when the switch is closed in P, R or N, without MIL. On selectors with a resistor network a short to positive in the downshift branch sets P0816. Manual shifting is disabled, automatic operation stays normal.
c: Downshift switch or paddle sticking or faulty
s: Manual down shifting not working
Transmission stays in the normal automatic mode
No check engine lamp

P0817.d: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P0817 is the general or open-circuit fault of this line. Saab sets it when the output reports 'start allowed' but the feedback shows 'off' for more than 100 ms, twice in a row, with 6–16 V and no limp mode; it rates the fault type D, without any lamp. The engine then cannot be started. Low and high are P081A and P081B; vehicles that send the start release over a bus often report similar faults as U codes or P0850.
c: Starter disable wire to the body module open or shorted
Connector corroded or pins pushed back
Transmission module with built-in range switch faulty
s: Engine does not crank in P or N
Start possible in only one of the two ranges
No check engine lamp

P0818.d: P0818 concerns a switch input that reports whether the driveline is disconnected – on four-wheel-drive vehicles typically the neutral position of the transfer case or an axle disconnect, on hybrids a disconnect clutch between engine and transmission, as a Ford patent uses the term. It matters for OBD because in transfer case neutral the engine runs without load and wheel speed does not match the ratio, so misfire, ratio and vehicle speed monitors must know about it; CARB requires monitoring only then. The check would be a circuit or plausibility test against the speed ratio. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0818, and which of the two meanings applies cannot be proven. All-wheel drive or neutral may then be unavailable.
c: Neutral or disconnect switch at the transfer case or axle faulty
Underbody wiring or connector corroded or damaged
Transfer case actuator does not reach its end position
s: All-wheel drive or neutral cannot be selected
'Service 4WD' or similar warning
Possibly check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer)

P0819.t: Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation
P0819.d: P0819 is the plausibility check between the tap-up and tap-down switches and the range sensor: a shift request may only appear in the manual gate or in drive. If a tap switch reports in P, R or N, or taps arrive without the manual gate being detected, the correlation is broken. GM's 2019 tables and Ford's 2012 SelectShift run exactly this check but assign the fault to the switch concerned as P0815 or P0816; no manufacturer with its own P0819 is documented. Manual shifting would be disabled while automatic operation stays normal, without the MIL. Causes are a sticking tap switch, a misadjusted range sensor or selector cable, or the selector wiring.
c: Range sensor or selector sensor misadjusted or faulty
s: Tap or manual mode not working
Range display partly wrong
No check engine lamp

P081A.d: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P081A means the start release line is too low – the output is shorted to ground or open. Saab's 2012 9-3 transmission module checks it in D, where the output must have a defined state, with 9–18 V, not in limp mode and continuously; no time threshold is published. Because the engine module then sees no 'P/N', the engine may not start.
c: P/N line to the engine module shorted to ground
Connector oxidized or pins pushed back
s: Engine does not start or only sometimes
Starter does not crank in P or N
No check engine lamp

P081B.d: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P081B means the start release line stays at positive, so the 'P/N' level is present in a drive range. Saab's 2012 9-3 checks it only outside P and N, with 9–18 V and not in limp mode. A short to positive could in principle allow a start in gear; the diagnosis catches it, and Saab names as the effect that the engine may not start because the release is refused.
c: P/N line shorted to positive (chafed against a supply wire)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Engine does not start or starts unreliably
Start release in the wrong range possible (safety risk)
No check engine lamp

P081C.d: P081C concerns the input 'park position' – the P contact of the selector or shift module, or the park pawl feedback – which controls switching off the ignition, key release, starter release and the 'not in park' warning. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: a 2022 bulletin lists P081C with the MIL on, with 'Vehicle not in Park' shown although P is engaged; the car cannot be switched off, modules stay awake and the battery drains. The cause was shift module software, fixed by reflashing. The check is a circuit or plausibility test of the P signal against the range sensor; no thresholds are published.
c: P contact or selector switch faulty or misadjusted
s: 'Not in park' message although P is engaged
Ignition cannot be switched off, battery drains
Check engine lamp (Jeep)

P081D.d: P081D concerns the input 'neutral' – the N contact of the selector or range switch, on manual cars a neutral switch or sensor for start-stop. Neutral serves for starter release, idle control without load, start-stop release and enabling other diagnostics. The check would be a circuit or plausibility test against the range sensor or speed ratio. No manufacturer document available to us uses P081D; its sister P081C is documented on the Jeep Compass, and Saab's range switch shows that P and N are the two start positions. The engine may then not start in N, start-stop is disabled and idle diagnostics may be suspended.
c: Neutral contact, range switch or neutral sensor faulty or misadjusted
s: Engine does not start in N (only in P)
Start-stop not working
Range display does not show N

P081E.d: P081E is the counterpart to P0811 for clutch B – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 2 with the even gears and reverse, which Audi calls 'clutch 2'. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch and flags slip above its limit. Audi's DL382 S tronic (2020–24) sets it intermittently with P0811 and input speed codes; the bulletins report a transmission malfunction and 'reverse gear unavailable', and the fix was a new transmission module with improved parts from late 2023. A failed clutch 2 typically means no reverse and no even gears.
s: Transmission warning, limp mode
Reverse or even gears not available
Engine flares on gear changes

P081F.t: Brake Transmission Shift Interlock (BTSI) Signal Correlation
P081F.d: The brake transmission shift interlock (BTSI) is a solenoid or actuator that locks the selector in park until the brake pedal is pressed, as US rule FMVSS 114 requires. 'Signal correlation' is the plausibility check between the interlock command or feedback and its input signals – brake switch and selector position: for example the lock released without a brake signal, or still active although the brake is pressed. The selector then cannot leave park, or it moves without the brake and the safety function is missing. Electrical faults of the lock solenoid have their own codes P0928–P0931. No manufacturer document with P081F is available to us; a GM service update for the 2016 Malibu and 2016–17 Volt explains the part and the 'won't shift out of park' complaint. CARB may exempt such safety parts from monitoring.
c: Brake lamp switch misadjusted or faulty
Interlock solenoid or locking mechanism sticking
Wire or connector to the selector
Selector module, control unit or software
s: Selector cannot be moved out of P
Selector moves out of P without the brake
Warning about brake or range

P0820.t: Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Circuit
P0820.d: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0820 is the umbrella code: the module does not tell X from Y, or sees an invalid combination of both axes that matches no gate position. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV, which names it 'shift lever position (main) circuit malfunction' and sets it for an impossible lever position, without published thresholds. GM reads its X/Y sensors under P082A–P082F instead. Range selection may be blocked and the vehicle stays in P or N.
c: Wire or connector between selector and module open or shorted
Position sensor in the selector assembly faulty
Sensor supply (5 V reference) or ground faulty
s: Range cannot be selected or only partly
Vehicle stays in P or N, or limp mode
Transmission warning, range display flashes or missing

P0821.t: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit
P0821.d: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0821 is the general circuit fault of X sensor 1 – an open or invalid signal – for modules that do not report low and high separately. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM reports the same axis in finer steps as P082A, P082B and P082C. A GM patent describes checking each sensor's x value separately: an invalid value makes that sensor unusable, and with a redundant sensor 2 the car can usually go on.
c: X position sensor in the selector assembly faulty
Signal wire or connector open or corroded
Liquid or dirt in the center console
s: Transmission warning in the cluster
Ranges partly not selectable
With both sensors failed the vehicle stays in P or N

P0822.t: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit
P0822.d: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0822 is the same for the Y axis – the second direction of movement, on an H-gate the select gate. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM reports the Y axis as P082D, P082E and P082F. A failed Y sensor can hide a gate change, for example into the manual gate or the reverse gate.
c: Y position sensor in the selector assembly faulty
Signal wire or connector open or corroded
Liquid or dirt in the center console
s: Transmission warning in the cluster
Manual gate or reverse not selectable
With both sensors failed the vehicle stays in P or N

P0823.t: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0823.d: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0823 watches X sensor 1 for short dropouts and jumps – a signal that changes faster than the lever can move, or briefly disappears. Such checks typically count jumps within a time window; no manufacturer publishes thresholds. GM folds a disturbed X signal (a frequency error of the PWM signal) into P082A, and its patent rejects a value at once if it was faulty before and differs from its partner.
c: Loose contact at the selector connector
Chafed or broken wire in the harness to the console
Sensor worn (potentiometer track) or Hall sensor disturbed
s: Transmission warning comes and goes
Selected range occasionally not accepted
Occasional limp-mode reaction

P0824.t: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0824.d: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0824 is the same for the Y axis: short dropouts or jumps of Y sensor 1. GM folds Y-axis disturbances into P082D; thresholds for P0824 are not published anywhere. The symptoms are an occasional warning, a gate change that is sometimes not recognized, and occasional limp mode.
c: Loose contact at the selector connector
Chafed or broken wire in the harness to the console
Sensor worn (potentiometer track) or Hall sensor disturbed
s: Occasional transmission warning
Gate change occasionally not recognized
Occasional limp mode

P0825.d: P0825 concerns a switch on the selector that reports pushing or pulling the lever – sequential + and – shifting – or the start of a shift movement, hence 'shift anticipate'. Its purpose: the control unit of an automated manual gearbox can prepare clutch and engine torque before the actual gear change is detected; a LuK patent describes such shift-intent detection, which reports intent when the lever signal exceeds a filtered, load-dependent reference and cancels on a reversal. A fault is typically a switch reporting 'pressed' without lever movement or never, implausible against the X/Y sensors. No manufacturer document with P0825 is available to us. Shift-intent detection is then off, gear changes are slower or sequential shifting is disabled.
c: Switch in the selector faulty or sticking
Wire or connector to the selector assembly
Liquid or dirt in the shift gate
s: Delayed or jerky gear changes (automated manual)
Sequential tapping not working
Transmission warning in the cluster

P0826.t: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit
P0826.d: Many selectors read tap-up and tap-down over one shared wire with voltage steps or a resistor network; P0826–P0828 cover this shared circuit, P0815/P0816 the single directions. P0826 is the general fault of the shared circuit. GM (6L80 in 2011, 2019, 2025, hybrids) sets it when the circuit shows an invalid voltage for at least 60 s with 8.6–32 V and 400–7500 rpm, without MIL. On Saab's 9-4X with the 6T70 a short to ground or an open sets P0826. Saab's 2003–04 9-3 Sentronic reports below 0.2 V or above 6.7 V for over 30 s under P0826 with a fault-type byte, lights 'Check gearbox' and locks the lever in P/N. Ram's 2025 heavy-duty trucks set it with P0827 and P085F and the MIL, fixed with transmission software. Manual shifting is then disabled.
c: Wire or connector between selector and module open or shorted
Selector assembly (Hall switch, resistor network, module) faulty
s: Tap or manual shifting not working
Transmission runs only in automatic mode
Transmission warning; lever locked in P/N (Saab 9-3)

P0827.t: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Low
P0827.d: Many selectors read tap-up and tap-down over one shared wire with voltage steps or a resistor network; P0826–P0828 cover this shared circuit, P0815/P0816 the single directions. P0827 means the shared circuit voltage is too low – a short to ground, depending on the design an open on a pulled-up input, or a switch held closed. The only documented user is Ram's 2025 heavy-duty truck with the 6.7 Cummins and eight-speed TorqueFlite HD: a 2026 bulletin lists P0827 with P0826 and P085F and the MIL; the display shows N although P is engaged, the engine cannot be switched off and limp mode is possible. The fix was new transmission software. Saab reports the same state under P0826 (below 0.2 V for 30 s), GM under P0826.
c: Tap switch held closed or selector assembly faulty
s: Tap or manual shifting not working
MIL (Ram)
N shown although in P, engine cannot be switched off (Ram)

P0828.t: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit High
P0828.d: Many selectors read tap-up and tap-down over one shared wire with voltage steps or a resistor network; P0826–P0828 cover this shared circuit, P0815/P0816 the single directions. P0828 means the shared circuit voltage is too high – a short to positive, or on ground-switching switches with a pull-up also an open. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: Saab's 9-3 Sentronic reports this state as P0826 (above 6.7 V for more than 30 s), Saab's 9-4X as P0815 or P0816, and GM as P0826. Manual shifting would be disabled while automatic operation stays normal.
c: Signal wire or selector ground open (pulled-up input)
s: Tap or manual shifting not working
Transmission warning in the cluster
No effect on driving in automatic mode

P0829.d: Shift codes check the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded change with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, does not happen, flares or binds up two clutches. P0829 covers the change between 5th and 6th gear in either direction; J2012 placed it here because P0785 ff were already taken, between P0781 '1-2 Shift' to P0784 '4-5 Shift' and P07DA/P07DB for 6-7 and 7-8. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion without a gear-specific code (speed must drop by more than 30 rpm on an upshift, flare above 300 rpm), Ford's automatics feed the solenoid function codes and GM the clutch valve codes. It exists only on transmissions with at least six gears; MIL and trip count follow the manufacturer.
c: Shift or clutch pressure valve for 5-6 sticking
Clutch or brake of 6th gear worn
Input or output speed sensor delivering wrong values
s: Harsh, delayed or missing 5-6 shift
Engine speed flares during the shift
Limp mode in a fixed gear, possibly MIL

P082A.t: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance
P082A.d: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. GM uses P082A–P082F on its electronic range selector (2019 tables, Cadillac XT4, 2025): a Hall sensor delivers a PWM signal, measured as duty cycle. P082A sets when the measured X position lies outside the lever's path (5.5 % duty cycle equals about 100 N of side force), the PWM signal has a frequency error, or X sensors 1 and 2 differ by more than 12 %; 3 of 4 samples in 2019, 10 of 12 in 2025 with an added angle check. Type B, MIL after two trips; the other sensor takes over.
c: Selector assembly faulty (Hall sensor, magnet, worn mechanism)

P0830.d: Clutch pedal switches A and B are digital inputs of manual gearboxes: they release the starter only with the pedal pressed, switch off cruise control and tell start-stop whether the clutch is open. Which switch is A or B is up to each manufacturer – FCA calls the pedal-up switch A. Ford's 2020–23 summary checks a dual switch over more than 40 pedal applications and reports a stuck switch without MIL (P0830 stuck high, P0833 stuck low, comparison P0704). P0830 is the general fault of switch A. On Ford it means the switch is stuck high. On a 2012–13 Jeep Wrangler with the six-speed manual, Chrysler reprogrammed the engine module for unwanted cruise control cut-outs with P0830; an FCA tip notes that a driver resting a foot on the pedal keeps the pedal-up switch on and sets the code. The MIL depends on the manufacturer.
c: Foot resting on the clutch pedal keeps the switch actuated
s: Cruise control switches off or cannot be activated
Start-stop disabled
Engine may not crank (starter interlock)

P0831.t: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit Low
P0831.d: Clutch pedal switches A and B are digital inputs of manual gearboxes: they release the starter only with the pedal pressed, switch off cruise control and tell start-stop whether the clutch is open. Which switch is A or B is up to each manufacturer – FCA calls the pedal-up switch A. Ford's 2020–23 summary checks a dual switch over more than 40 pedal applications and reports a stuck switch without MIL (P0830 stuck high, P0833 stuck low, comparison P0704). P0831 means switch A stays at ground or 0 V where a high level is expected – a short to ground, or an open supply on a positive-switching circuit. GM's 2006 Corvette and CTS-V with the LS2 and LS7 check it on manual gearboxes only, type C without MIL (400 of 500 samples of 100 ms; the table layout makes the sample count uncertain).
s: Cruise control switches off or cannot be activated

P0836.d: The four-wheel-drive switch tells the engine module which transfer case range is engaged. 4WD low changes the ratio of engine to road speed by about 2.7:1 on GM trucks, so GM uses 'not in 4WD low' as an enable condition for idle speed and clutch pedal checks; that is why CARB requires monitoring such inputs. P0836 is the general circuit fault of this switch – an open or an invalid state. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM reports the same part from 2006 to 2025 as P2771 '4WD Low Switch Circuit', comparing the switch position with the measured transfer case ratio while driving (from 15 mph, diesel 5 mph, 2–7 s), without MIL on gasoline and type B on diesel. Ford has no such code. The 4WD indicator may flash and dependent diagnostics may be suspended.
c: Position switch or sensor at the transfer case faulty
Wire or connector at the transfer case corroded or torn
Selector switch in the cabin faulty
s: 4WD indicator flashes or stays off
4WD range cannot be selected or display wrong
Possibly check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer)

P0837.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P0837.d: The four-wheel-drive switch tells the engine module which transfer case range is engaged. 4WD low changes the ratio of engine to road speed by about 2.7:1 on GM trucks, so GM uses 'not in 4WD low' as an enable condition for idle speed and clutch pedal checks; that is why CARB requires monitoring such inputs. P0837 means the signal is electrically valid but implausible: the reported position does not fit the driving state, or a multiplexed resistor switch sits between its position windows. GM runs this check on the same part under P2771: switch 'not low' while the transfer case ratio is 2.6–2.8, or 'low' at 0.9–1.1 (diesel windows 5.7–8.0 and 0.7–1.55), under load and in gear. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0837.
c: Shift linkage or transfer case not fully reaching the position
Position sensor out of tolerance (drifting resistance)
Mechanical fault in the transfer case (range jumps out)
s: 4WD indicator flashes or stays off
4WD range cannot be selected or display wrong
Possibly check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer)

P0838.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit Low
P0838.d: The four-wheel-drive switch tells the engine module which transfer case range is engaged. 4WD low changes the ratio of engine to road speed by about 2.7:1 on GM trucks, so GM uses 'not in 4WD low' as an enable condition for idle speed and clutch pedal checks; that is why CARB requires monitoring such inputs. P0838 means the switch signal is below its valid range – typically a signal wire shorted to ground or a switch shorted internally. Low and high refer to the signal, not to low range: with a pull-up and a switch to ground, a short to ground can look like a range permanently engaged, which GM describes for its 4WD low switch as 'ground (stuck on)'. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0838 or publishes thresholds.
c: Signal wire chafed through to ground
Water or corrosion in the connector (leakage to ground)
s: 4WD indicator flashes or stays off
4WD range cannot be selected or display wrong
Possibly check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer)

P0839.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit High
P0839.d: The four-wheel-drive switch tells the engine module which transfer case range is engaged. 4WD low changes the ratio of engine to road speed by about 2.7:1 on GM trucks, so GM uses 'not in 4WD low' as an enable condition for idle speed and clutch pedal checks; that is why CARB requires monitoring such inputs. P0839 means the switch signal is above its valid range – a short to positive or, with a pull-up circuit, an open in wire, switch or ground. GM describes the open for its 4WD low switch as 'continuous open (stuck off)': the module sees 'not in 4WD low' although low is engaged (ratio 2.6–2.8, diesel 5.7–8.0). No manufacturer document available to us uses P0839. Dependent diagnostics could then run wrongly in low range, so modules suspend them or use a substitute value.

s: 4WD indicator flashes or stays off

P083A.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit
P083A.d: Transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch G is one of up to eight pressure inputs (A to H) that SAE J2012 provides for automatic gearboxes. No maker could be found that uses the letter G: GM's tables up to 2025, Ford's summaries and Allison stop at A to E. The description therefore follows the general rule for gearbox inputs in California's OBD regulation, which demands circuit and plausibility checks, and the logic of the A and B codes. P083A is the general circuit fault, set when the module sees a fault on this input without telling low, high or plausibility apart.
c: Pressure switch or sensor in the valve body faulty or stuck
Harness or connector at the gearbox: fluid wicking, corrosion
Sticking valve in the valve body
s: Check engine or transmission warning lamp on
Limp mode with substitute gear or limited ratio
Harsh or delayed shifts

P083F.d: Manual cars often carry two clutch pedal switches: one near the top of the pedal travel for cruise control and start-stop, one near the floor that releases the starter. Pressing the pedal must switch them in a sensible order; P083F means their states contradict each other. Stellantis documents it for the 2025 Jeep Wrangler manual: the engine does not crank and start-stop is blocked, caused by corroded contacts in the clutch interlock switch, which is replaced. Ford checks the same pair over more than 40 pedal applications but reports it as P0704, without MIL.

P0840.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0840.d: Transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch A and B are inputs inside the automatic gearbox. A switch only reports pressure present or absent, a sensor reports a value. The letter is the maker's choice: Allison 1000 uses A and B for the switches on shift valves S1 and S2, GM's CVT for the primary and secondary pulley sensors, GM's 2025 8-speed A for the lube pressure sensor; Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes instead. P0840 is the general circuit fault. GM documents it for the 2006 Allison: the module compares the commanded position of valve S1 with the switch feedback and retries the valve if they disagree; it then tells an electrical, mechanical or sporadic case apart. Type A, MIL after one trip. From 2007 Allison reports the same test under P0842/P0843.

Sticking shift valve or dirt in the valve body
Harness or connector at the gearbox: fluid wicking, corrosion, chafing
Fluid level low or fluid contaminated
s: Check engine or transmission warning lamp on
Limp mode with a fixed gear, harsh or missing shifts
Torque converter clutch stays open, higher fuel use

P0848 means the B signal is too high. Allison sets it when switch 2 shows no pressure for over 0.175 s although valve S2 is applied, type A; GM's CVT when the second pulley sensor rises above 95 % duty cycle, a short to voltage or an open circuit. Mitsubishi treats it as a circuit fault to rule out first on its CVTs.
c: Signal or ground wire open, connector soaked with fluid
Switch stuck open or sensor faulty
Signal wire shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Too little pressure at the switch: low fluid level or sticking valve
s: Check engine or transmission warning lamp on
Limp mode with a fixed gear, harsh or missing shifts

P0849.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent
P0849.d: Transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch A and B are inputs inside the automatic gearbox. A switch only reports pressure present or absent, a sensor reports a value. The letter is the maker's choice: Allison 1000 uses A and B for the switches on shift valves S1 and S2, GM's CVT for the primary and secondary pulley sensors, GM's 2025 8-speed A for the lube pressure sensor; Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes instead. P0849 reports short dropouts of the B signal. GM bulletin 21-NA-033 for the Corvette C8 dual clutch lists it with P0841, P0844 and P0846: first the valves are cleaned and the clutches relearned, and only if the code comes back on its own is the circuit traced. Like the A counterpart P0844 it has no published thresholds.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the gearbox connector or control unit
Dirt in valve or sensor causing signal jumps
s: Warning lamp coming and going
Occasional shift shocks
Brief limp mode

P084A.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit
P084A.d: Transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch H is the last of up to eight pressure inputs (A to H) in SAE J2012; the letter is the maker's choice. Documented uses are rare: Mitsubishi sets P084A on its Jatco CVT8 (F1CJC/W1CJC) and Ford P084B on the 2020–23 Explorer 3.3 full hybrid. Mitsubishi uses P084A as a function check of the primary pulley pressure sensor: the module compares primary with secondary pressure and sets the code after 5 s outside the map at a steady ratio of 0.5 to 1.0. Electrical faults of both sensors come first as P0842/P0843/P0847/P0848; belt slip and wear debris in the fluid often follow, cured with a valve body or belt and pulley set.
c: Valve body with faulty primary or secondary pressure sensor
CVT belt or pulleys damaged, slip and debris in the fluid
s: Warning lamp on
Judder or slipping when pulling away
CVT limp mode with limited ratio

P084B.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit Range/Performance
P084B.d: Transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch H is the last of up to eight pressure inputs (A to H) in SAE J2012; the letter is the maker's choice. Documented uses are rare: Mitsubishi sets P084A on its Jatco CVT8 (F1CJC/W1CJC) and Ford P084B on the 2020–23 Explorer 3.3 full hybrid. P084B means the signal is valid but implausible. Ford bulletin 24-2019 covers the Explorer hybrid with its 10-speed: the code sets with the MIL or wrench lamp because software thresholds were too tight, and a PCM reflash fixes it, after which the shift adaptation relearns. Which measuring point Ford calls H is not stated. Otherwise the usual causes apply: sticking valve, drifting sensor, low fluid.
c: Control module software with too tight thresholds
Dirty or worn valve body, sticking valve
Fluid level low or fluid aged
s: MIL or wrench lamp on
Shift quality changes until the adaptation has relearned
Limp mode with substitute gear or limited ratio

P084C.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit Low
P084C.d: Transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch H is the last of up to eight pressure inputs (A to H) in SAE J2012; the letter is the maker's choice. Documented uses are rare: Mitsubishi sets P084A on its Jatco CVT8 (F1CJC/W1CJC) and Ford P084B on the 2020–23 Explorer 3.3 full hybrid. For P084C no maker is documented. It means the signal is too low: a switch closed although no pressure is expected, a sensor below its lower limit through a short to ground or missing 5 V supply, judged like A and B under California's rule for gearbox inputs.

Sensor faulty or switch stuck closed
