P084F.d: P084F concerns an output: a gearbox, hybrid or selector module passes the park/neutral status as a switched signal to other modules, for example for start release. The module watches its own driver for open circuits and shorts. Stellantis names the code for the 2019 Pacifica plug-in hybrid, where it came with a software fault that drained the 12 V battery; a hybrid control update fixes it. Saab's gearbox module reports the same kind of P/N output to the engine module under P081A/P081B. Strategy and MIL status are not published.
c: P/N output line or connector open or shorted
Output driver in the module faulty
Receiving module pulls the line wrongly
s: Engine or ready mode does not start in P/N
12 V battery drains while parked
Warning about gear or park position

P0850.d: The park/neutral input tells the engine control module whether the automatic is in P or N, or a manual gearbox in neutral. It releases the starter, prepares idle control for the load of an engaged gear and enables cruise control and other monitors. All documented makers check it for plausibility against driving state or a second source such as the gearbox module. On GM's 6T70 and Subaru the switch pulls the line to ground in P/N. P0850 is the general fault. Ford's 2023 diesels check the switch for plausibility at start-up and set the code after 1 s. On GM's 6T70, as in the Saab 9-4X, the module sees P/N while the range switch reports a gear for 0.2 s above 10 km/h and 75 Nm, type C without MIL; it then uses the range switch for start release.
c: Range or inhibitor switch faulty or misadjusted
Wiring or connector between switch, gearbox module and engine module
s: Engine does not crank in P or N
Engine cranks in a drive range (safety risk)
Rough or wrong idle
Cruise control not working

P0851.d: The park/neutral input tells the engine control module whether the automatic is in P or N, or a manual gearbox in neutral. It releases the starter, prepares idle control for the load of an engaged gear and enables cruise control and other monitors. All documented makers check it for plausibility against driving state or a second source such as the gearbox module. On GM's 6T70 and Subaru the switch pulls the line to ground in P/N. P0851 means the input wrongly reports P/N while the car drives under load. Subaru's manual sets it when the neutral switch stays on while the car goes from idle at standstill to at least 64 km/h three times, MIL after two trips, cruise control blocked. GM's LML Duramax compares it with the gearbox module above 24 km/h and 120 Nm, type B; GM petrol engines use type C.
c: Inhibitor or neutral switch faulty or misadjusted, stays closed
Gearbox module status wrong where it is the reference
s: MIL on (GM diesel, Subaru after two trips)
Cruise control not working
Rough idle when stopping

P0852.d: The park/neutral input tells the engine control module whether the automatic is in P or N, or a manual gearbox in neutral. It releases the starter, prepares idle control for the load of an engaged gear and enables cruise control and other monitors. All documented makers check it for plausibility against driving state or a second source such as the gearbox module. On GM's 6T70 and Subaru the switch pulls the line to ground in P/N. P0852 means the input wrongly reports a gear although P/N is selected: open wire, short to voltage or a switch that no longer closes. Subaru's manual sets it when neutral is never seen while the car changes three times between idle and 64 km/h, MIL after two trips. GM's LML Duramax sets it when the gearbox module reports P/N but the input does not, type B; the 6T70 after 0.2 s, type C.
c: Signal or ground wire or connector open
P/N or neutral switch does not close
s: Engine does not crank in P/N (automatic)
High or rough idle
Cruise control blocked

P0853.d: The drive switch input reports to the engine or gearbox module that range D is selected, usually through its own contact in the range switch or selector next to the park/neutral contact. No maker documents these codes; GM's tables up to 2025, Ford's summaries and Saab service data were searched. The description follows California's rule for inputs, circuit and plausibility checks, and the documented park/neutral input, which is checked against the gearbox module's range. P0853 is the general circuit or plausibility fault without telling low from high.
c: Range switch or D contact faulty or misadjusted
Wire or connector open or corroded
s: Fault stored, MIL depending on maker
Gear indicator wrong
Cruise control not working
Gearbox emergency program possible

P0856.d: The traction control input carries the request of the ABS/stability module to the engine module to cut torque when wheels spin. Older cars used a wire with a voltage or duty-cycle signal, hence the low and high variants; today it is a CAN message, where pure loss of communication sets U0121 or U0415 instead. California's OBD rule counts traction control as a safety-only system that may be exempted, so these codes normally carry no MIL. GM checks the CAN torque request from the brake module: a wrong protection value or rolling count in 6 of 10 messages, or three changes of request type within 200 ms, set it, type C without MIL. On the Saab 9-4X the brake module then switches traction and stability control off for the key cycle and stores C0242.
c: Fault in the engine module that prevents torque reduction, often with other engine codes
Software of engine or brake module, module faulty
CAN fault, connector or ground at the brake or engine module
s: Traction or stability control lamp on, system switched off
No torque reduction when wheels spin
Usually no check engine lamp
C0242 or similar in the brake module

P0857.d: The traction control input carries the request of the ABS/stability module to the engine module to cut torque when wheels spin. Older cars used a wire with a voltage or duty-cycle signal, hence the low and high variants; today it is a CAN message, where pure loss of communication sets U0121 or U0415 instead. California's OBD rule counts traction control as a safety-only system that may be exempted, so these codes normally carry no MIL. P0857 means the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the driving state, such as a request without wheel slip or switching too often. No maker documents the code; GM covers such checks under P0856. The receiving module ignores the request and traction control is disabled.
c: Software or calibration of brake or engine module
Loose contact or corrosion between brake module and engine module
Wheel speed fault in the ABS causing false slip detection
s: Traction or stability control lamp on, system switched off
Traction control intervenes unexpectedly or not at all
Engine power briefly reduced

P0858.d: The traction control input carries the request of the ABS/stability module to the engine module to cut torque when wheels spin. Older cars used a wire with a voltage or duty-cycle signal, hence the low and high variants; today it is a CAN message, where pure loss of communication sets U0121 or U0415 instead. P0858 means a wired signal stays below its lower limit: short to ground, an open line without pull-up, or a sending module without power. No maker documents the code; the request is discarded and traction control switched off.
c: Signal wire from brake module to engine module shorted to ground
Brake module without power or ground, or faulty
Input of the engine module faulty
s: Traction or stability control lamp on, system switched off
No torque reduction when wheels spin

P085A.t: Gear Shift Control Module B Communication Circuit
P085A.d: Gear shift control modules A and B are selector modules of shift-by-wire systems, such as Audi's selector lever J587 or Stellantis' rotary shift module. The codes cover a dedicated link to the gearbox module and the module's plausibility. If the selected range cannot be transferred reliably, the gearbox holds its range, goes to P at standstill or into limp mode. Modules on CAN report lost communication as U0103 or invalid data as U0404 instead; GM uses its own codes. P085A is the general fault of the link to module B: no or no valid frames. No maker documents it; California's rule requires missing communication of digital inputs to be stored separately.
c: Wire or connector between selector module and gearbox module: open, chafed, moisture in the console
Power or ground of the selector module
Software of selector or gearbox module
s: Selector or gearbox warning in the instrument cluster
Range cannot be selected or only with delay, car stays in P/N
Gearbox limp mode

P085F.t: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P085F.d: Many tip switches for manual gear selection share one signal line, with a voltage step for up, down and rest (family P0826 to P0828). P085F means the signal is electrically valid but sits between the allowed windows, changes implausibly or does not fit the selector position. Ram documents it on 2025 heavy-duty trucks with the 8-speed together with P0826/P0827: MIL on, a fixed substitute gear, harsh 2-3 shifts, the cluster showing N instead of P so the engine could not be switched off. A gearbox module update fixes it.
c: Contact resistance or moisture in switch or connector
Wiring damage between switch and gearbox module
s: Check engine lamp on
Limp mode with substitute gear
Wrong range shown (N instead of P)
Manual shifting not working

P0863.d: The TCM communication circuit is a direct link between gearbox and engine module outside the CAN bus. Subaru's 2005 WRX, sold as Saab 9-2X, uses a single 'AT diagnosis' wire: about once a second the gearbox module sends a frame with a start pulse of 40 ms low and 20 ms high, carrying among other things its request for the MIL. On CAN cars, loss of the gearbox module sets U0101 or U0402 instead. P0863 is the general fault of this link without telling range, low or high apart. No maker documents it on its own. Without the link the engine module receives no gearbox status, and a MIL request from the gearbox gets lost.
c: Wire or connector between engine and gearbox module open or corroded
Gearbox module without power or ground
Input of the engine module faulty
s: Check engine lamp on
Gearbox warning or limp mode possible
Gearbox faults not passed to the engine module

P0864.d: The TCM communication circuit is a direct link between gearbox and engine module outside the CAN bus. Subaru's 2005 WRX, sold as Saab 9-2X, uses a single 'AT diagnosis' wire: about once a second the gearbox module sends a frame with a start pulse of 40 ms low and 20 ms high, carrying among other things its request for the MIL. On CAN cars, loss of the gearbox module sets U0101 or U0402 instead. P0864 means signals arrive but in the wrong format: Subaru sets it after 60 s without a valid frame while driving above 500 rpm and 10.9 V, MIL after two trips. The service procedure checks shifting, then interference from aftermarket radios with bad grounds, then replaces the gearbox module. GM's 2005 2.8 and 3.6 V6 report it with U0101 when gearbox messages are missing for 2.5 s.
c: Gearbox module faulty or its software
Interference from retrofitted radio or phone with poor ground
Loose contact in wire or connector between the modules
s: Check engine lamp after two trips
Shift problems or limp mode possible
Often no noticeable effect

P0865.d: The TCM communication circuit is a direct link between gearbox and engine module outside the CAN bus. Subaru's 2005 WRX, sold as Saab 9-2X, uses a single 'AT diagnosis' wire: about once a second the gearbox module sends a frame with a start pulse of 40 ms low and 20 ms high, carrying among other things its request for the MIL. On CAN cars, loss of the gearbox module sets U0101 or U0402 instead. P0865 means the line stays low for more than 3 s, MIL after two trips. The engine module pulls the line up; the procedure measures below 1 V at the engine module pin with ignition on, checks the harness for a short to ground and then reads the gearbox codes or replaces the gearbox module.

Gearbox module faulty, holding the line low

P0866.d: The TCM communication circuit is a direct link between gearbox and engine module outside the CAN bus. Subaru's 2005 WRX, sold as Saab 9-2X, uses a single 'AT diagnosis' wire: about once a second the gearbox module sends a frame with a start pulse of 40 ms low and 20 ms high, carrying among other things its request for the MIL. On CAN cars, loss of the gearbox module sets U0101 or U0402 instead. P0866 means the line stays high for more than 3 s with no start pulse, MIL after two trips. Over 10 V at the engine module pin points to a short to voltage; a voltage switching between 1 and 4 V is a healthy signal. A gearbox module without power sends nothing, so the pull-up keeps the line high and the gearbox runs in a fixed gear.

Poor contact at a module connector
s: Check engine lamp after two trips
Gearbox in limp mode with fixed gear if its module has no power
Gearbox faults not passed to the engine module

P0867.d: P0867 to P0869 cover the system or line pressure of the gearbox as a whole: a pressure sensor measures it and the control module compares it with the pressure it commands. Faults of the sensor circuit itself have their own codes (Chrysler 68RFE P0932 ff), the single switches A to H have theirs (P0840 ff). Thresholds are not published; the codes are documented in bulletins for the Ram 68RFE and for the Tremec dual clutch of Corvette C8 and Maserati MC20. P0867 is the general pressure fault. GM's Corvette bulletin reads it as 'no system pressure': the pump delivers nothing or the fluid is almost gone, so valve cleaning is pointless and the gearbox needs a mechanical check. The car may lose drive completely.
c: Fluid level extremely low or leak
Fluid pump or its drive faulty
Pressure regulator or relief valve sticking
s: Transmission warning lamp or MIL on
Weak or no drive
Limp mode, car may be stranded

P0868.d: P0867 to P0869 cover the system or line pressure of the gearbox as a whole: a pressure sensor measures it and the control module compares it with the pressure it commands. Faults of the sensor circuit itself have their own codes (Chrysler 68RFE P0932 ff), the single switches A to H have theirs (P0840 ff). Thresholds are not published; the codes are documented in bulletins for the Ram 68RFE and for the Tremec dual clutch of Corvette C8 and Maserati MC20. P0868 means the measured pressure stays below target. Chrysler calls it 'Line Pressure Low' on the 68RFE and fixed some cases with a software update; on 2024 Ram trucks it came with P0841 from a failed rear thrust washer. On the Corvette a sticking pressure valve is typical. The module then commands maximum pressure.
c: Fluid level low, leak or clogged filter
Pressure control valve or solenoid sticking from dirt
Internal leakage or mechanical damage: thrust washer, seal rings, pump
Software calibration of the target pressure
s: Transmission warning lamp or MIL on
Slipping, delayed engagement
Limp mode
Overheating under load

P0869.d: P0867 to P0869 cover the system or line pressure of the gearbox as a whole: a pressure sensor measures it and the control module compares it with the pressure it commands. Faults of the sensor circuit itself have their own codes (Chrysler 68RFE P0932 ff), the single switches A to H have theirs (P0840 ff). Thresholds are not published; the codes are documented in bulletins for the Ram 68RFE and for the Tremec dual clutch of Corvette C8 and Maserati MC20. P0869 means the measured pressure stays above target. Chrysler lists 'Line Pressure High' among the 68RFE codes fixed by control module updates; on the Corvette and Maserati dual clutch a valve stuck in the high-pressure position is the usual cause, cured by cleaning or a new control unit. Harsh engagement is the typical sign.

Pressure control solenoid without power, gearbox falls back to maximum pressure

Harsh shifts and engagement shocks
Limp mode

P086A.d: Neutral position sensor A is a position sensor, usually a three-wire Hall sensor, on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox. It tells the engine module that neutral is selected, which start-stop needs before it may switch the engine off. Analog versions need a learned neutral value (P086F). Audi uses it as sender G701 on Q3 and A3, GM on the 2019 Corvette ZR1 with its 7-speed manual, where these codes suspend the gear ratio checks. P086A is the circuit fault: the signal is missing, typically an open supply or signal wire. Audi's bulletin for the sister codes P086D/P086E found the supply wires to G701 too short and lengthened them. Start-stop stays off.
c: Wire or connector to the sensor open or chafed
Corroded connector low on the gearbox
Supply output of the control module
s: Start-stop not working
Warning about the start system
MIL possible depending on maker

P086B.d: Neutral position sensor A is a position sensor, usually a three-wire Hall sensor, on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox. It tells the engine module that neutral is selected, which start-stop needs before it may switch the engine off. Analog versions need a learned neutral value (P086F). Audi uses it as sender G701 on Q3 and A3, GM on the 2019 Corvette ZR1 with its 7-speed manual, where these codes suspend the gear ratio checks. P086B means the signal is valid but implausible: it reports neutral although engine and road speed show a gear, never shows neutral, or lies outside the learned window. Patents describe learning neutral and rejecting unsteady runs.
c: Sensor or magnet target loose, misaligned or covered with metal debris
Learned value missing or wrong after gearbox, clutch or sensor work
s: Start-stop not working or behaving oddly
Warning about start-stop or start system

P086C.t: Neutral Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P086C.d: Neutral position sensor A is a three-wire Hall sensor on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox that reports neutral to the engine module; start-stop may only switch the engine off in neutral. Audi uses it as sender G701 on the Q3 and A3, GM on the 2019 Corvette ZR1 manual, where its faults suspend the gear ratio checks. Thresholds and MIL status are not published. P086C means the signal is below its lower limit: signal wire shorted to ground, supply missing or a sensor without output. GM lists it among the exclusions of its gear checks; the neutral state is then unknown and start-stop stays off.
c: Signal wire shorted to ground or supply wire open or chafed
Corrosion or water in the connector
5 V reference of the module disturbed
s: Start-stop not working
Start system warning in the cluster (Audi)
No noticeable change in driving

P086D.t: Neutral Position Sensor A Circuit High
P086D.d: Neutral position sensor A is a three-wire Hall sensor on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox that reports neutral to the engine module; start-stop may only switch the engine off in neutral. Audi uses it as sender G701 on the Q3 and A3, GM on the 2019 Corvette ZR1 manual, where its faults suspend the gear ratio checks. Thresholds and MIL status are not published. P086D means the signal is above its upper limit: an open signal or ground wire or a short to voltage. Audi's bulletin for the 2019–20 Q3 and 2022–23 A3 found the wires to G701 laid too short, so shifting pulled them apart; all three are lengthened by 20 mm. The cluster shows a start system fault.
c: Wire to the neutral sender broken or laid too short (Audi G701)
s: Start system fault message (Audi)
Start-stop not working
Fault appears after gear changes

P086E.t: Neutral Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P086E.d: Neutral position sensor A is a three-wire Hall sensor on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox that reports neutral to the engine module; start-stop may only switch the engine off in neutral. Audi uses it as sender G701 on the Q3 and A3, GM on the 2019 Corvette ZR1 manual, where its faults suspend the gear ratio checks. Thresholds and MIL status are not published. P086E means the signal jumps out of range for short moments or changes implausibly fast, typically a loose contact or a chafed wire that moves with the shift shaft. Audi often stores it together with P086D when the too-short G701 wiring only breaks contact now and then.
c: Wire at the neutral sender strained or cracked (Audi G701)
Loose contact or corrosion in the connector
s: Start-stop works only at times
Start system warning comes and goes

P086F.t: Neutral Position Sensor A Not Learned
P086F.d: Neutral position sensor A is a three-wire Hall sensor on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox that reports neutral to the engine module; start-stop may only switch the engine off in neutral. Audi uses it as sender G701 on the Q3 and A3, GM on the 2019 Corvette ZR1 manual, where its faults suspend the gear ratio checks. Thresholds and MIL status are not published. Analog neutral sensors need a learned neutral window to cover part and fitting tolerances. P086F means no valid value is stored, typically after a sensor, gearbox, clutch or module replacement, a software update or an aborted learn run; Schaeffler's patent rejects runs with an unsteady lever. FCA describes cruise control failing after service until the neutral learn is done, without new parts.
c: Learn procedure not done after replacing sensor, gearbox or module
Learn run aborted: lever strained, linkage misadjusted
Sensor fitted outside the learnable range or faulty
s: Start-stop not working
Cruise control cannot be set (FCA)
Fault appears after a workshop visit

P0870.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit
P0870.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0870 is the general fault. Allison's 2006 table uses it for the switch on valve S3: if it reports pressure for more than 20 ms with the valve at rest, the valve is retried twice and the case classed as electrical, mechanical or sporadic, type A. Ram corrected false P0870 'hydraulic pressure tests' on the 2019 68RFE with a software update.
c: Pressure switch C faulty (sticking, seal leaking)
Sticking shift valve or worn valve body bore
Wiring or connector at the gearbox
s: MIL or transmission warning lamp on
Limp mode with a fixed gear
Harsh or missing shifts

P0871.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit Range/Performance
P0871.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0871 means the switch does not follow the command or gear. On Ram's RFE it is the overdrive clutch switch: open in gears 1 to 3, closed in 4 to 6; it closes at about 1.5 bar and opens at 0.75 bar. Sonnax blames worn valve body bores in about 90 % of cases; on 2024 trucks it came with P0868 from a broken rear thrust washer. Allison 2006: switch without pressure 5 s after command, type A.
c: Worn valve body bores or shift valve plugs
Mechanical damage: thrust washer, clutch seals
s: MIL or transmission warning lamp on
Limp mode, often in 2nd or 3rd gear
Harsh engagement, neutral feeling in 4th gear

P0872.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit Low
P0872.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0872 means switch C reports pressure while its clutch is exhausted. GM checks it only when the 2-6 brake is commanded below 50 kPa, after a temperature-dependent delay, and counts one fault per clutch change: 10 on the 6L80, 18 on the 2010 6T70; listed as 'special no trip', without MIL. Allison 2007 sets it when switch 3 reports pressure for over 20 ms with the valve at rest, type A.
c: Pressure switch stuck closed or shorted internally
Signal wire shorted to ground inside the gearbox
Clutch circuit does not exhaust: dirt, sticking valve
s: Code stored in the gearbox module; on GM without MIL, on Allison with MIL
Harsh shifts, possibly substitute gear

P0873.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit High
P0873.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0873 means switch C reports no pressure although its clutch should be applied. GM checks it when the 2-6 brake is commanded above 700 kPa and sets it after 15 counts on the 6L80 or 20 on the 2010 6T70, without MIL. Allison sets it after 0.125 s (2006) or 0.175 s (2007) without pressure at an applied valve, then tells electrical from mechanical by the companion solenoid code, type A.
c: Signal wire or connector open (gearbox pass-through, harness)
Pressure switch does not close (diaphragm, seal)
Clutch pressure does not build: low fluid, leak, regulator valve
s: Code stored in the gearbox module; on GM without MIL, on Allison with MIL
Shift shock or slip in gears using clutch C

P0874.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit Intermittent
P0874.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0874 reports short dropouts or flutter of the C signal without a lasting low or high. It is documented only in GM bulletin 21-NA-033 for the Corvette C8 dual clutch, with MIL: dirt and sticking valves are cleaned, the clutches relearned, and only then the circuit traced. Thresholds are not published.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at connector or harness
Low fluid level, pressure drops in corners
s: Warning lamp coming and going
Occasional harsh shift or limp mode

P0875.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit
P0875.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0875 is the general fault of D. Allison's 2006 table uses it for the reverse pressure switch: it reports reverse while the range sensor shows P, N or a forward range for over 1 s, type A. Nissan's Kicks and Versa CVT reports the high clutch switch of the auxiliary gearbox as 'sensor/switch D'; together with P285A the control valve body is replaced.
c: Control valve body with pressure switch faulty (Nissan CVT)
s: MIL or transmission warning lamp on
Judder or reduced power (Nissan)
Reverse indication or shifting disturbed (Allison)

P0876.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Range/Performance
P0876.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0876 means D is electrically fine but implausible. Allison 2006: the reverse switch stays open in R, or does not drop out within 5 to 30 s after engine stop, type B with two trips. Mitsubishi's Jatco CVT sets it when the high clutch switch stays on for 1.5 s while the clutch should be exhausted. On Ram's 68RFE it came with P0871 from mechanical damage.
c: Valve body worn or dirty, valve sticking
s: MIL or transmission warning lamp on
Limp mode, harsh engagement

P0877.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Low
P0877.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0877 means switch D reports pressure while its clutch is exhausted. GM checks the 1-2-3-4 clutch below 50 kPa commanded and sets it after 5 counts, without MIL. Allison 2007 uses it for the reverse switch reporting R in a forward or park range for over 1 s, type A with MIL; it then suspends the gear ratio checks.
c: Pressure switch stuck closed or shorted internally
Signal wire shorted to ground inside the gearbox
Clutch circuit does not exhaust: dirt, sticking valve
s: Code stored in the gearbox module; on GM without MIL, on Allison with MIL
Harsh shifts, possibly substitute gear

P0878.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit High
P0878.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0878 means switch D reports no pressure although pressure is commanded. GM checks the 1-2-3-4 clutch above 700 kPa and sets it after 6 counts on the 6L80 or 8 on the 6T70, without MIL. Allison 2007 sets it when the reverse switch stays open in R or fails its check after engine stop, type A.
c: Signal wire or connector open (gearbox pass-through, harness)
Pressure switch does not close (diaphragm, seal)
Clutch pressure does not build: low fluid, leak, regulator valve
s: Code stored in the gearbox module; on GM without MIL, on Allison with MIL
Slip or shift shock in gears 1 to 4 (GM) or in reverse (Allison)

P0879.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Intermittent
P0879.d: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0879 reports short dropouts of the D signal. Like P0874 it is documented only for the Corvette C8 dual clutch in GM bulletin 21-NA-033, with MIL: clean the valves, relearn, then trace the circuit if the code returns. No thresholds are published.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at connector or harness
s: Warning lamp coming and going
Occasional harsh shift or limp mode

P087A.d: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. Ford sets P087A for a fault in that internal driver; wiring faults of the motor have their own codes (P090A, P090C, P090D). Ford's warranty extension 19N07 covers replacing the gearbox module when it is the cause, which is common here. Clutch B can then no longer be controlled safely.
c: Water or corrosion at the gearbox module connector
Clutch B motor or its wiring faulty
Weak supply to the gearbox module
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Jerky take-off or shifts
Reverse or even gears missing, limp mode

P087B.t: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P087B.d: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. Ford sets P087B for a Hall sensor fault on the clutch B motor: one Hall signal is missing or implausible, so the module no longer knows the motor and clutch position reliably. The counterpart for clutch A is P0806. Judder, missed shifts and limp mode follow, with MIL.
c: Hall sensor in the clutch B motor faulty
Wiring or connector between motor and gearbox module
Input of the gearbox module faulty
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Jerky take-off or shifts
Gears skipped, vibration

P087C.t: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P087C.d: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. For P087C no maker is documented; Ford folds Hall faults into P087B. The code means the sensor signal is below its limit: signal wire shorted to ground, supply missing or a sensor without output. As with sensor A (P0807), clutch B can then only run in limp mode.
c: 5 V supply to the sensor open
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Jerky take-off or shifts
Reverse or even gears missing, limp mode

P087D.t: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit High
P087D.d: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. For P087D no maker is documented. It means the sensor signal is above its limit: an open signal or ground wire with a pull-up, or a short to voltage. As with sensor A (P0808), clutch B can then no longer be position-controlled and the gearbox goes into limp mode.
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Jerky take-off or shifts
Reverse or even gears missing, limp mode

P087E.t: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P087E.d: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. Ford sets P087E for a sequence fault: when the clutch B motor turns, its three Hall sensors produce a fixed pattern; if a step is skipped or the order is wrong, motor and clutch position become unreliable. Typical are sporadic Hall dropouts and loose contacts. The counterpart for clutch A is P0809.
c: Hall sensor in the clutch B motor dropping out
Loose contact at motor or module connector
Evaluation in the gearbox module faulty
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Sporadic judder when pulling away or shifting
Delayed gear changes

P0880.d: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0880 is the general fault. Hyundai's 2017–19 six-speed automatics set it when the solenoid supply drops below 7 V or rises above 22 V: MIL on, limp mode in 4th gear. Hyundai's bulletin points to the valve body harness and the TCU fuses and expressly not to the gearbox.
c: Harness or connector between module and valve body damaged or corroded
TCU fuse or transmission relay faulty
Weak battery, charging fault, poor ground
s: MIL on
Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting
Harsh engagement into D or R

P0881.d: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0881 means the supply is electrically within range but implausible, for example differing from the engine module's system voltage or dipping when the solenoids switch on. No maker publishes a strategy for it.
c: Contact resistance in supply or ground, voltage drop under load
Internal measurement of the module faulty
s: MIL on
Occasional harsh shifts
Limp mode possible

P0882.d: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0882 means the supply is too low: Ford sets it below 9 V, continuously and with MIL. Chrysler's RFE, RLE and TE automatics test it when the key goes to run: if the module reads less than 3 V at the transmission control relay outputs while commanding the relay on, the code sets and the solenoids stay dead.
c: Weak battery or alternator not charging
Transmission relay, fuse or fuse box module faulty (Chrysler)
Corroded ground or supply wire, connector at the module
s: MIL on
Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting
Torque converter clutch stays open

P0883.d: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0883 means the supply is too high: Ford sets it above 16 V, continuously and with MIL; GM's counterpart P0563 sets at 18 V. Typical triggers are a failed alternator regulator or a jump start with 24 V. Overvoltage endangers the output stages, so the module may switch the solenoids off.
c: Jump start with 24 V or charger in boost mode
Poor battery ground, regulator measures wrongly
s: MIL on
Charging warning or unusually bright lights
Overvoltage codes in other modules

P0884.d: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0884 reports a brief loss of supply. Chrysler calls it 'power up at speed': the module notices on start-up that the vehicle is already moving, so it must have rebooted while driving. In field reports from NHTSA investigation PE07-027 on 2007 Jeeps it was stored after engine stalls, among others from an unlatched fuse box connector.
c: Loose or unlatched connector at fuse box or module
Ignition switch or relay with contact dropouts
s: Gearbox jerks or briefly enters limp mode while driving
Engine may stall with a combined powertrain module
Warning lamps flicker

P0885.d: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0885 means the coil circuit is open; the module checks its relay driver output at key-on. Ford lists it in its powertrain code list with or without MIL depending on vehicle; on FCA's 948TE nine-speed in the 2015 Cherokee and Chrysler 200 it was cured with a gearbox module reflash.
c: Wire between relay and module open, connector or fuse box contact
Fuse of the relay coil blown
s: MIL on
Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting
Harsh engagement into D or R

P0886.t: TCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P0886.d: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0886 means the coil control line is shorted to ground or the driver reports a short, so the relay pulls in unintentionally or the driver shuts down. No maker documents the code; its neighbours P0885 and P0887 are documented by Ford and FCA.
s: MIL on
Limp mode possible
Relay does not click or stays pulled in

P0887.t: TCM Power Relay Control Circuit High
P0887.d: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0887 means the coil control line sits high: a short to voltage or voltage present despite the command. FCA's 948TE nine-speed in the 2014–15 Cherokee, Chrysler 200 and Ram ProMaster City stored it with MIL, and three bulletins cured it with a gearbox module reflash, so an over-sensitive detection can cause it too.
s: MIL on
Shift problems or limp mode

P0888.d: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0888 is the general fault of the sense line, without telling low, high or range apart. No maker documents it on its own; Subaru uses the low variant P0890.
c: Wire between relay output and module
s: MIL on
Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting
Harsh engagement into D or R

P0889.t: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P0889.d: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0889 means the read-back voltage does not fit the switching state or the system voltage: clearly below battery voltage, a voltage drop across the contact or a delayed drop-out. No maker publishes a strategy.
c: Moisture or corrosion in relay or socket
s: MIL or gearbox warning
Occasional limp mode

P088A.d: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes. Its filter life monitor judges the pressure drop across the filter circuit; in Allison's patent a differential pressure valve operates a switch with temperature-dependent time limits. P088A, called 'filter maintenance alert' by Allison, is the early warning: the wrench symbol flashes. A faulty main valve body in some 3000/4000 units triggered it early (field action 2019FA07). After a filter change the monitor is reset by a selector sequence.
c: Filter changed without resetting the monitor
Faulty main valve body (Allison serial range)
s: Wrench or TRANS SERVICE indicator flashing
Usually no change in driving behaviour

P088B.d: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes. P088B is the second stage of the filter life monitor: the filter counts as heavily clogged or its change as overdue, and the CHECK TRANS lamp comes on. Isuzu names it the most common reason for that lamp on its Allison trucks, a maintenance item rather than a gearbox defect. Allison's patent allows limiting gearbox functions at this stage; the bulletins describe only the warning. Change the filter and reset the monitor.
c: Monitor not reset after the change
s: CHECK TRANS lamp on
Message to service the transmission filter
Rarely a gear limit

P088C.d: The reverse inhibit solenoid on GM's six-speed manual gearboxes (Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V, ATS-V) blocks reverse while driving forward and is released by the engine module. A low-side driver with built-in diagnosis watches the control line: above 9 V and 250 rpm, 20 faults in 25 samples of 250 ms (about 6 s) set the code. GM rates it type C without MIL; from 2019 a service message appears. P0801 is the open circuit. P088C means the control line is shorted to ground, so the solenoid is energised unintentionally or can no longer be switched off.
c: Wire between engine module and gearbox chafed to ground (tunnel, near exhaust)
Water or corrosion in the gearbox connector
s: Reverse cannot be engaged or is no longer blocked
Service message (GM from 2019), no MIL

P088D.d: The reverse inhibit solenoid on GM's six-speed manual gearboxes (Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V, ATS-V) blocks reverse while driving forward and is released by the engine module. A low-side driver with built-in diagnosis watches the control line: above 9 V and 250 rpm, 20 faults in 25 samples of 250 ms (about 6 s) set the code. GM rates it type C without MIL; from 2019 a service message appears. P0801 is the open circuit. P088D means the control line is shorted to voltage: when the driver switches on it sees too high a level or overcurrent, and the solenoid can no longer be operated, so reverse may stay locked.
c: Control wire shorted to a supply wire in the harness
Solenoid coil low-resistance or shorted (driver overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion between supply and control pin
s: Reverse cannot be engaged (lockout not released) or is not blocked
Service message (GM from 2019), no MIL

P088E.d: P088E means the module has found that a planetary gear set no longer keeps the fixed speed relation between its sun, carrier and ring gear, for example through broken planet gears, seized planet pins or stripped teeth. No maker's table or bulletin documents the code. It suits power-split hybrid transmissions, which measure speeds at several members: a Toyota patent compares the road speed calculated from engine, generator speed and planetary ratio with the measured one, flags a deviation of about 10 km/h for about 1 s and then drives electrically only. In stepped automatics such damage usually shows as ratio or slip codes.
c: Planet gears or pins seized or broken (lubrication, overheating)
Tooth damage on sun or ring gear
Speed sensor (engine, motor-generator, output) reading wrong
s: Grinding or whining from the gearbox
Power loss, limp mode (hybrids drive electrically only)
Possibly no drive

P0890.t: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
P0890.d: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0890 means the relay delivers no voltage despite the command. Subaru documents it in four bulletins from 2022 to 2025 (Ascent, WRX, Impreza, Crosstrek, Forester): after a short trip below 0 °C condensation freezes the ignition relay contacts, the starter does not crank and P0700 often comes along. Engine module software cycles the contacts; the 2025 Forester also gets a vented relay.
c: Relay contacts frozen or corroded (Subaru ignition relay)
Fuse or wire between relay and gearbox module
s: Starter does not crank after a short trip in frost (Subaru)
MIL on, P0700 in the engine module
False oil level or other warnings

P0891.t: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High
P0891.d: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0891 means voltage is present at the relay output although the relay is off: a stuck or welded contact or a back-feed. The module then cannot switch the solenoids off for a safe emergency gear, and it may stay powered after key-off and drain the battery. No maker documents the code.
c: Sense or output line shorted to voltage
s: MIL on
Battery drains overnight
Module stays awake after key-off

P0892.t: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent
P0892.d: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0892 reports a sense signal that drops out now and then, from a loose contact in relay, socket or wiring. Brief supply interruptions can reboot the module (compare P0884) and cause shift shocks. No maker publishes a strategy.
c: Loose contact in relay socket or connector
s: Sporadic gearbox warning
Brief limp mode or shift shock

P0893.d: P0893 means more shift elements are applied than the commanded gear allows, so the gearbox binds up. It is detected through speeds, when the ratio matches no valid gear and input speed collapses, or through commanded clutch capacities: a GM patent flags capacities above their limits for longer than roughly 200 to 500 ms and reacts by downshifting or falling back to the hydraulic limp mode. Nissan's 2020–22 Frontier and Titan nine-speed set it with all ratio codes and MIL; Land Rover cured P0893 on the ZF 9HP48 Evoque with gearbox software.
c: Shift or pressure valve sticking (dirt), control valve body faulty
s: Gearbox or engine warning lamp
Sudden limp mode, harsh jolts or judder
Strong braking or locking feeling during a shift

P0894.d: P0894 reports slip of a gearbox component, found by comparing speeds. GM's 4L60-E applies it to the torque converter clutch: with lock-up commanded, slip between 100 and 550 rpm for 12.75 s on the third attempt in 4th gear sets it, type B with MIL after two trips; the module first freezes adaptation and raises line pressure. Lexus (Aisin AB60F) and Allison 1000 use it for a slipping shift element or low pressure and name the fluid level first. On the 4L60-E a cracked converter clutch PWM solenoid is a known cause.
c: Converter clutch PWM solenoid cracked or regulator bore worn (GM 4L60-E)
Worn clutch plates or converter clutch lining
Pump not priming, cracked suction filter (Allison)
s: Engine speed rises without matching acceleration, mostly when warm
Shudder during lock-up
Harsh shifts from maximum pressure, limp mode possible

P0895.d: Shift time is the duration of the speed transition from the old to the new ratio, measured from input and output speed. Gearbox modules adapt fill time and pressure to keep it in a calibrated window; the code sets when adaptation is at its limit and the time is still outside. No maker could be found using these generic codes; Saab's 1994 900 automatic monitored the same with its own code P1832, a window of 0.3 to 1.3 s and a limp program. P0895 means the shift completes faster than the window: clutch pressure too high or applied too early, giving a harsh shift.
c: Pressure control valve stuck towards high pressure or line pressure too high
Shift adaptation faulty or reset, wrong software
Valve body: sticking spool, faulty damper or accumulator
s: Harsh, jerky shifts
Transmission warning lamp
Limp mode possible

P0896.d: Shift time is the duration of the speed transition from the old to the new ratio, measured from input and output speed. Gearbox modules adapt fill time and pressure to keep it in a calibrated window; the code sets when adaptation is at its limit and the time is still outside. No maker could be found using these generic codes; Saab's 1994 900 automatic monitored the same with its own code P1832, a window of 0.3 to 1.3 s and a limp program. P0896 means the transition takes longer than the window: the engine flares between gears from low pressure or worn plates. Long shifts heat the clutches, so a fixed gear is a common reaction.
c: Low or worn fluid, low pressure (pump, filter)
Pressure or shift valve sticking, leaking piston seals
s: Delayed shifts, engine flares between gears
Transmission warning lamp
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P0897.d: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes. Its oil life monitor counts down the remaining fluid life from operating hours, distance, shifts and load factors such as fluid temperature, open converter and retarder use. With little life remaining, TRANS SERVICE shows for two minutes after every start; if the change and reset do not follow within a set period, CHECK TRANS lights and P0897 becomes active. Correct calculation assumes approved fluid (TES 295/668).
c: Fluid changed without resetting the oil life monitor
Heavy duty (heat, stop-and-go, retarder) shortens calculated life
s: CHECK TRANS lamp on
TRANS SERVICE or wrench indicator after each start beforehand
Driving usually normal

P0898.t: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit Low
P0898.d: The MIL request circuit is a dedicated wire over which the gearbox module asks the engine module to switch on the MIL. Today that request travels over CAN and shows as P0700 in the engine module; older Subarus, also sold as Saab 9-2X, used a single serial wire with its own codes P0864 to P0866. P0898 means the request wire stays at ground: a short to ground or, with active-high logic, a gearbox module without power. The engine module can then not tell a real request from a wiring fault. No maker documents the code; Subaru's P0865 is the closest documented equivalent.
c: MIL request wire shorted to ground
Engine or gearbox module connector corroded
s: MIL on
Gearbox faults may not be indicated correctly

P0899.t: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit High
P0899.d: The MIL request circuit is a dedicated wire over which the gearbox module asks the engine module to switch on the MIL. Today that request travels over CAN and shows as P0700 in the engine module; older Subarus, also sold as Saab 9-2X, used a single serial wire with its own codes P0864 to P0866. P0899 means the request wire stays high: an open line held up by the engine module's pull-up, a short to voltage or, with active-low logic, a gearbox module without power. No maker documents the code; Subaru's equivalent is P0866, set after more than 3 s high with MIL after two trips.
c: Wire open (pull-up in the engine module)
Gearbox module without power or ground
s: MIL on
Gearbox faults may not be reported
Limp mode as well if the gearbox module has no power

P089A.t: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit
P089A.d: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089A, the general circuit fault of X sensor 2, is used by no maker found; GM reports circuit faults through duty-cycle low or high and frequency errors under P089B.
c: Wire or connector at the selector module open
Spilled liquid in the centre console
s: Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Range selection delayed or limited
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P089B.t: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P089B.d: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. GM sets P089B when X sensor 2 reports a lever travel outside the gate (tolerance 5.5 % of duty cycle), its frequency is faulty, or it differs from sensor 1 by more than 12 %; 3 of 4 samples every 25 ms. Type B, MIL after two trips.
c: Sensor 2 in the selector assembly faulty or drifting
Loose contact or interference on the PWM line
s: MIL after two trips
Range selection delayed or limited
Only P available if both sensors fail

P089C.t: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P089C.d: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. GM sets P089C when the duty cycle of X sensor 2 falls below 17 % (2019) or 5 % (XT4 and 2025): signal wire to ground, sensor without output or missing supply. Type B, MIL after two trips; sensor 1 carries on.
c: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Supply of the selector sensor open
s: MIL after two trips
Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P089D.t: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit High
P089D.d: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. GM sets P089D when the duty cycle of X sensor 2 rises above 88 % (2019) or 95 % (XT4 and 2025): open signal wire with pull-up, short to voltage or a sensor stuck high. Type B, MIL after two trips.
c: Signal wire open (pull-up) or shorted to voltage
s: MIL after two trips
Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P089E.t: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P089E.d: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089E, for jumping or briefly dropping X sensor 2 signals, is used by no maker found; GM catches signal disturbances through the frequency error under P089B. The counterpart for sensor 1, P0823, is unused as well.
c: Loose contact at the selector connector
s: Selector warning at times
Range selection hesitates sporadically

P089F.t: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit
P089F.d: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089F, the general circuit fault of Y sensor 2, is used by no maker found; GM reports that sensor under P08A0 to P08A2. In GM's patent a sensor counts as invalid as a whole once its X or Y value fails.
c: Wire or connector at the selector module open
Corrosion from liquid in the console
s: Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Range selection delayed or limited
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P08A0.t: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P08A0.d: Sensor 2 is the redundant second Hall sensor that reports the Y-axis travel of an electronic selector lever as a PWM duty cycle. GM uses it in its electronic range selection (ECM and ICCM tables 2019–2025, Cadillac XT4 among them). P08A0 is set when sensor 2 reports a lever path outside the shifter gate (tolerance 5.5 %, ICCM 6–11 % of duty cycle), its frequency check fails, or it disagrees with Y sensor 1 by more than 12 %. Debounce is 3 of 4 samples at 25 ms (2025: 10 of 12). Type B, MIL after two trips. Low/High of the same sensor are P08A1/P08A2. GM's patent lets the other sensor carry on; only when both are invalid may the module ask for park.
c: Sensor 2 in the selector assembly drifting or faulty
Selector mechanism worn, bent or binding, lever leaves its nominal path
Loose contact or interference on the PWM signal line
Spilled liquid in the centre console
s: Check engine light after two drives
Shift lever message or occasional unaccepted range selection
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P08A1.t: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P08A1.d: The selector lever's Y-axis sensor 2 is one of two redundant Hall sensors that send the lever travel as a PWM duty cycle. GM documents P08A1 for its electronic range selection: the code sets when the measured duty cycle of Y sensor 2 drops below 17 % (2019 ECM and ICCM tables) or below 5 % (Cadillac XT4 2019, ECM tables 2023–2025), checked 3 of 4 samples at 25 ms or 10 of 12 in later years. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a dead sensor output. Type B, MIL after two trips. Unlike P08A0 this is a pure signal limit, not a plausibility check; high is P08A2. Sensor 1 keeps the selector working.
c: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor supply open or connector backed out
Sensor 2 in the selector assembly without output
Connector corrosion from liquid in the console
s: Check engine light after two drives
Shifter warning message in the cluster
Normally no change in driving, sensor 1 takes over

P08A2.t: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit High
P08A2.d: Y sensor 2 is the backup Hall sensor of an electronic selector lever and reports the lever's Y-axis travel as a PWM duty cycle. GM uses P08A2 in its electronic range selection and sets it when the duty cycle of Y sensor 2 rises above 88 % (2019 ECM and ICCM tables) or above 95 % (Cadillac XT4 2019, ECM tables 2023–2025); 3 failures in 4 samples at 25 ms, in later calibrations 10 of 12. A signal line shorted to voltage, an open ground or an internal sensor fault are the usual reasons. Type B, MIL after two trips. Range/performance and low are P08A0 and P08A1; sensor 1 of the same axis reports via P082D to P082F. With one sensor still valid, the lever stays usable.
c: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Sensor ground open or high resistance
Internal fault of sensor 2 in the selector assembly
s: Check engine light after two drives
Shifter warning message in the cluster
Range selection normally still works via sensor 1

P08A3.t: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08A3.d: This code covers short dropouts or jumps in the signal of the second, redundant Y-axis sensor of an electronic selector lever. No manufacturer documents P08A3 publicly. GM, the only proven user of this sensor family, uses only range/performance, low and high (P08A0 to P08A2) in all OBD tables from 2016 to 2025 and catches an unsteady PWM signal through the frequency check inside P08A0. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires input components to be monitored for circuit faults and plausibility. GM's patent on two redundant lever sensors explains why a second sensor exists: if one becomes invalid, the other keeps range selection alive. Expect loose contacts in the console harness; the MIL status depends on the maker.
c: Loose or fretting contact at the selector connector
Harness chafed by console or lever movement
s: Stored fault that comes and goes, often without driver complaint
Occasional shifter warning message
Possibly check engine light, depending on the manufacturer

P08A4.t: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P08A4.d: An electronic selector lever with redundant sensing measures the X axis with two sensors. P08A4 means the two X readings no longer agree although each may be within its own limits. No manufacturer documents P08A4 publicly. GM, which runs dual PWM lever sensors, folds this comparison into the range/performance codes: P089B sets when X sensor 2 differs from sensor 1 by more than 12 % duty cycle. GM patents describe the principle: each sensor is checked against the gate and against its partner, and on disagreement the module trusts the more robust signal or commands neutral or park. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) demands such plausibility monitoring. Y-axis counterpart is P08A5, the whole system P08A6.
c: One of the two X sensors drifting
Magnet carrier or lever mechanism shifted or worn
Contact resistance on one sensor's signal path
s: Shifter warning message
Range selection refused or vehicle held in neutral or park
Check engine light, depending on the manufacturer

P08A5.t: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P08A5.d: P08A5 is the Y-axis twin of P08A4: the two redundant sensors that measure the selector lever's Y travel disagree beyond a calibrated limit. No manufacturer documents P08A5 publicly. In GM's electronic range selection the same check exists but is reported as range/performance: P08A0 sets when Y sensor 2 and Y sensor 1 differ by more than 12 % duty cycle, Type B. GM's patents show why redundancy matters: a disagreeing pair is resolved by trusting the more fault-tolerant signal, and if that is not possible the module selects neutral or park. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires such rationality checks for inputs. For the driver this means a refused or held range; repairs usually replace the selector assembly.
c: One of the two Y sensors drifting
Magnet carrier or lever mechanism shifted or worn
Contact resistance on one sensor's signal path
s: Shifter warning message
Range selection refused or vehicle held in neutral or park
Check engine light, depending on the manufacturer

P08A6.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor System - Multiple Sensor Correlation
P08A6.d: Here the module compares the combined gear lever position information with other evidence and finds no consistent picture. Two makers document it. FCA/Stellantis sets P08A6 in the PCM of 6-speed manual Jeeps such as the Wrangler JL as the all-gear-sensor check: the sensed gear is compared with a learned top-gear engine-to-road-speed ratio, so larger tyres trigger it until that ratio is relearned in sixth at 40–80 mph; a 4Low issue and software updates are also known, with MIL. Maserati's electronic shift module stores P08A6-64 for signal plausibility, leaving no gear selectable. Unlike P08A4/P08A5 it concerns the whole sensor system, not one sensor pair.
c: Tyre size changed without relearning the top-gear ratio (FCA manual)
Control module software needing an update
Internal fault or connector problem of the electronic shift module
Modified transfer case gearing, fault only in 4Low
s: Check engine light
Start-stop and gear indicator disabled, clutch overheat or service transmission message
On shift-by-wire, no gear can be selected

P08A7.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit/Open
P08A7.d: Sensor A is the analog or PWM sensor that reports how far the clutch pedal of a manual car is pressed; the engine controller needs it for start-stop, cruise control, gear detection and starter release. P08A7 is the general circuit or open-wire fault of that sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly: GM folds an open circuit into its low-signal code P08A9, and Ford lists only P08A9/P08AA for sensor A. Saab's 2012 9-3 used the older P0806 as a comparable circuit fault (Check Engine, cruise control off). Range/performance, low, high and erratic faults have their own codes P08A8–P08AB. Expect a warning lamp and disabled start-stop or cruise control until the wiring or sensor is repaired.
c: Loose connector or broken wire at the pedal sensor (pedal box wiring flexes with every clutch stroke)
Internal fault in clutch pedal position sensor A
Missing 5 V reference or sensor ground
Faulty sensor input in the engine control module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Start-stop and cruise control unavailable
Engine may not crank if the starter release relies on the sensor

P08A8.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P08A8.d: P08A8 flags a clutch pedal sensor whose signal is electrically valid but contradicts how the car is actually driving. GM uses it on manual cars since model year 2018 (before: P0806), e.g. the LV7 1.4 L engine and the 2019 Corvette ZR1 (LT5): when engine speed to output shaft speed shows that a gear is engaged and transmitting torque, but the pedal reads as pressed, the filtered position error must stay below 4 %. Enabled above 4.3 mph (LT5: 5.6 mph), not in 4WD low, torque above a table, no circuit, crank or speed sensor faults; Type A, MIL after one trip. Circuit faults are P08A9/P08AA. Typical result: start-stop and cruise control off, and the engine computer may misjudge clutch state.
c: Sensor loose or misaligned on the pedal bracket, so its reading no longer matches pedal travel
Worn or drifting sensor track giving an offset signal
Driver resting a foot on the clutch pedal, or a floor mat holding it down
Corroded connector adding resistance to signal or ground
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Start-stop and cruise control switched off
Rev-matching or hill-start functions may be disabled

P08A9.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P08A9.d: The sensor is designed with dead bands at both ends, so a signal near 0 V can only come from a fault. GM sets P08A9 when the signal stays below 4 % of the 5 V reference (low voltage or open circuit) for 400 of 500 samples taken every 12.5 ms, with the engine not cranking and system voltage above 9 V (10 V in some 2018 tables); Type A, MIL after one trip. GM used P0807 for this before 2018 and lists P08A9 for the LV7, the 2019 Corvette ZR1 and its 2018 OBDG04 engines. Ford's 2020–23 gasoline summary uses P08A9 for cars with dual PWM pedal sensors or a single analog sensor plus switches, detected in under a second. The high-side counterpart is P08AA; sensor B low is P08B6.
c: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground in the pedal area
Open signal wire or missing 5 V reference (connector off, broken wire)
Failed clutch pedal position sensor A
Shared 5 V reference pulled down by another sensor on the same circuit
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Start-stop and cruise control unavailable
Engine may refuse to crank on vehicles that release the starter via the sensor

P08AA.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P08AA.d: P08AA is the mirror image of P08A9: the pedal sensor signal climbs into the upper dead band that a healthy sensor never reaches. GM's threshold is above 96 % of the 5 V reference for 400 of 500 samples at 12.5 ms, engine not cranking, system voltage above 9 V; Type A, MIL after one trip. It replaced GM's pre-2018 P0808 and appears in the LV7, 2019 Corvette ZR1 and 2018 OBDG04 tables. Ford's 2020–23 gasoline summary lists P08AA for both its dual PWM and single analog clutch pedal sensor layouts, flagged in under a second. A lost sensor ground or a signal shorted to the reference are the usual triggers. Sensor B high is P08B7; the driver mostly loses start-stop and cruise control.
c: Open sensor ground wire or corroded ground pin
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage
Failed clutch pedal position sensor A
Faulty sensor input in the engine control module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Start-stop and cruise control disabled
Clutch status shown incorrectly in scan tool data

P08AB.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08AB.d: P08AB is meant for a clutch pedal sensor A signal that jumps, drops out briefly or changes faster than a foot could move the pedal, without staying out of range long enough for the low or high codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's published tables for the same sensor use only P08A8, P08A9, P08AA and P08AC, and its low/high checks need 400 of 500 bad samples, so short dropouts would go unnoticed there; Ford names only low, high and A/B correlation. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility. In practice the cause is usually a loose connector or a wire that breaks inside its insulation as the pedal moves. Start-stop and cruise control may cut out intermittently.
c: Loose or worn terminals in the pedal sensor connector
Wire breaking inside its insulation where the harness flexes with the pedal
Worn sensor track causing signal dropouts at certain pedal positions
Moisture or corrosion in the footwell connector
s: Start-stop or cruise control cutting out intermittently
Warning lamp that comes and goes
Erratic clutch pedal value in scan tool data while the pedal is held still

P08AC.d: The engine controller has to know at which pedal position the clutch is fully released or disengaged. GM teaches the fully applied position at the factory and then adapts it over time to clutch wear. P08AC is set when this learned value falls outside a window (LV7 1.4 L: 7–33 %, 2019 Corvette ZR1: 9–36 % of travel) or when the manufacturer's enable counter shows the learn was never completed; 250 ms loop, Type A, MIL after one trip. Before 2018 GM used P080A. After replacing the sensor, pedal parts, clutch or ECM, a relearn with a scan tool is needed; FCA, for example, issued a Renegade bulletin calling for a clutch pedal sensor learn. Circuit faults (P08A9/P08AA) must be cleared first.
c: Relearn not performed after replacing the sensor, clutch parts or engine control module
Learned position drifted out of the allowed window (worn clutch, wrong pedal stop, air in hydraulics)
Learn procedure aborted, for example by low battery voltage
Faulty or misaligned clutch pedal sensor preventing a valid learn
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Start-stop, cruise control or automatic parking brake release not working as expected

P08AD.d: A neutral position sensor tells the engine module whether a manual gearbox is in neutral, which start-stop, remote start and rev matching rely on. Sensor B is a second sensor or channel next to sensor A (P086A ff). P08AD flags an open or otherwise faulty sensor B circuit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Audi (sender G701) and GM (Corvette LT5) are only known to use the A codes. A GM patent shows why a B channel exists: two Hall sensors on the shift shaft give a PWM signal, and in neutral both must read the same. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring of such inputs. Expected effect: start-stop stays off; MIL status depends on the maker.
c: Wire to the sensor broken or stretched by shift shaft movement
Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded
s: Start-stop no longer switches the engine off
Start system warning in the cluster
Driving normally unaffected

P08AE.t: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P08AE.d: Sensor B is the second neutral sensor or channel on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox, complementing sensor A (P086A ff). P08AE means its signal is electrically present but implausible: it stays outside the expected window, does not change when gears are engaged, or reports neutral while the gear ratio says otherwise. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Audi's G701 and GM's LT5 Corvette are only known to use the A codes. Per a GM patent the neutral sensor is a Hall sensor pair with a PWM output that changes with every gear, so such a plausibility check is possible. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires rationality monitoring of inputs. Start-stop is usually disabled; repair often means adjusting or replacing the sensor.
c: Sensor B or its magnet misaligned after gearbox work
Worn shift shaft or detent giving an unclear neutral position
s: Start-stop unavailable
Start system or gear indicator message in the cluster
No noticeable change while driving

P08AF.t: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P08AF.d: The signal of neutral position sensor B, the second neutral sensor or channel of a manual gearbox, has fallen below its lower electrical limit. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a sensor without output. No manufacturer documents P08AF publicly; the A-sensor codes are documented by Audi (sender G701, three-wire Hall sensor) and by GM on the LT5 Corvette. A GM patent describes the sensor as two Hall elements on the shift shaft feeding a PWM signal to the engine module. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires low/high circuit monitoring of such inputs. High is P08B0, the A-sensor equivalent P086C. Start-stop is usually blocked; the MIL status is left to the manufacturer.
c: Signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Water or corrosion in the connector at the gearbox
s: Start-stop no longer works
Start system warning in the cluster
