Fault stored without driving complaint

P08B0.t: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit High
P08B0.d: P08B0 reports that the signal of neutral position sensor B on a manual gearbox is above its upper electrical limit. With a three-wire Hall sensor this usually points to an open signal or ground wire or a short to voltage. No manufacturer documents P08B0 publicly. For the A sensor Audi does: the 2019–20 Q3 and 2022–23 A3 store P086D/P086E because the wires to sender G701 were too short and were pulled apart by shifting, fixed by lengthening them 20 mm; the same harness logic applies to a B sensor. A GM patent explains the dual-Hall neutral sensor with PWM output. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring. Low is P08AF; start-stop is typically off.
c: Signal or ground wire pulled apart, harness too short
s: Start-stop does not switch the engine off
Start system warning in the cluster
Fault may come and go with gear changes

P08B1.t: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08B1.d: Neutral position sensor B, the second neutral sensor or channel on a manual gearbox's shift shaft, delivers a signal that drops out or jumps for short moments. No manufacturer documents P08B1 publicly. The closest documented case is on the A sensor: Audi's bulletin for the 2019–20 Q3 and 2022–23 A3 traces P086D/P086E to wires to sender G701 that were too short, so every gear change strained them; lengthening by 20 mm cures it. A Dura patent notes that a neutral signal must persist for a minimum time before start-stop may stop the engine, so a flickering sensor blocks the function. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring. Steady faults appear as P08AD, P08AF or P08B0.
c: Wire strained or partly broken by gearbox movement
Sensor B with intermittent internal fault
s: Start-stop works only now and then
Occasional start system message
Fault returns after clearing without visible cause

P08B2.d: On a manual gearbox with two neutral sensors or two channels, the engine module compares A and B. P08B2 means they disagree: one reports neutral, the other a gear, or their values differ beyond a calibrated limit, while each may look fine electrically. No manufacturer documents P08B2 publicly. A GM patent describes exactly this layout: two Hall sensors with their own magnets on the shift shaft, whose PWM outputs must be identical in neutral as an integrity check. Audi's G701 and GM's LT5 Corvette use only the A codes. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires rationality monitoring of inputs. Because neutral cannot be confirmed, start-stop and remote start stay off; usual fix is aligning or replacing the sensor.
c: One of the two neutral sensors drifting or faulty
Magnet on the shift shaft shifted or sensor misaligned after repair
Neutral position not relearned after component replacement
s: Start-stop unavailable
Start system warning in the cluster
Gear indicator may be blank or wrong

P08B3.t: Neutral Position Sensor B Not Learned
P08B3.d: Analog neutral sensors report a position value, and the control module must learn which value means neutral to cover part and fitting tolerances. P08B3 says no valid learned value exists for sensor B, typically after replacing the sensor, gearbox or module, after a software update, or after an aborted learn. No manufacturer documents P08B3 publicly; the A counterpart P086F is used by GM on the LT5 Corvette. A Schaeffler patent describes the learn: the driver engages neutral and the gears, and a run is rejected if the reading wanders too much in its roughly one-second window. FCA notes a neutral sensor learn procedure after service that restores cruise control. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) applies. Fix is usually a relearn by scan tool.
c: Learn procedure not done after sensor, gearbox or module replacement
Learn run aborted, lever unsteady or linkage misadjusted
Learned values erased by software update or module reset
Sensor mounted outside the learnable range or faulty
s: Start-stop unavailable
Cruise control may be inoperative
Appears right after a repair or software update

P08B4.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P08B4.d: Some manual cars read the clutch pedal with two independent sensors so a single failure can be detected; Ford's 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary describes such a dual PWM layout. Sensor B is the second channel. P08B4 is the general circuit or open-wire fault of that second sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly: Ford uses only P08B6/P08B7 for sensor B plus P08B9 for the A/B comparison, and GM's tables cover sensor A alone. The code therefore rests on CARB's requirement to monitor such inputs for circuit faults. Sensor A's counterpart is P08A7. As long as sensor A is healthy the controller can usually still judge the pedal, but start-stop is often locked out until the fault is fixed.
c: Loose connector or broken wire on the sensor B channel
Internal fault in clutch pedal position sensor B (often a shared housing with sensor A)
Missing supply or ground for sensor B
Faulty sensor B input in the engine control module
s: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
Correlation code P08B9 may be stored as well

P08B5.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P08B5.d: P08B5 covers a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal lies within its electrical limits but is implausible on its own, for example stuck at one value while the pedal moves or not matching the driving state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's dual PWM pedal sensor layout files any disagreement between the two channels under P08B9 rather than a B-only plausibility code, and GM applies the comparable in-gear plausibility check only to sensor A (P08A8: error above 4 % while a gear is engaged). CARB requires plausibility monitoring for inputs used by other diagnostics. If a manufacturer uses it, expect start-stop to be disabled; the clutch itself keeps working because it is hydraulically operated.
c: Sensor B drifting or worn so its value no longer follows pedal travel
Sensor loose or misaligned on the pedal bracket
Corrosion adding resistance in the sensor B circuit
s: Warning lamp on
Start-stop or cruise control unavailable

P08B6.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P08B6.d: P08B6 means the signal of the second clutch pedal sensor has dropped below its valid range. Ford lists it in the 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary under dual PWM clutch sensors, together with P08A9/P08AA for sensor A, P08B7 for sensor B high and P08B9 for the A/B comparison; monitoring runs continuously and needs less than one second to flag a fault. Ford does not mark the code as non-MIL, unlike its clutch switch codes. For a PWM sensor, low usually means the output is stuck at ground (no pulses or 0 % duty cycle), caused by a short to ground, a lost supply or a dead sensor. GM's published tables have no sensor B. The driver mainly notices a warning lamp and missing start-stop.
c: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Lost supply voltage to sensor B (open wire, connector off)
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B
s: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
P08B9 correlation code may set alongside

P08B7.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit High
P08B7.d: P08B7 is set when the second clutch pedal sensor reports a value above its valid range. Ford uses it on vehicles with two PWM clutch pedal sensors, as listed in its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary next to P08B6 (sensor B low), P08A9/P08AA (sensor A) and P08B9 (A/B correlation); the check is continuous and decides within one second. The clutch switch codes on the same page are marked non-MIL, the sensor codes are not. With a PWM output, high typically means the line is held at its pull-up level (100 % duty cycle), which points to an open signal or ground wire or a short to voltage. GM's published tables cover sensor A only. Effect for the driver: warning lamp, start-stop locked out.
c: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B, leaving the input at its pull-up level
Sensor B signal shorted to a voltage source
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B
s: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
Sensor B reading pinned at maximum in scan tool data

P08B8.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08B8.d: P08B8 is intended for a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal drops out briefly or jumps without staying out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford, the only maker found to publish sensor B codes, lists just low (P08B6), high (P08B7) and the A/B comparison (P08B9) for its dual PWM pedal sensors, so short glitches there would most likely surface as a correlation fault; GM covers sensor A only. CARB requires circuit and plausibility monitoring of such inputs. Likely culprits are worn connector terminals or a wire fatiguing where the harness moves with the pedal. Sensor A's counterpart is P08AB. Drivers may see start-stop drop out now and then.
c: Loose or worn terminals in the sensor B connector
Wire fatiguing where the harness flexes with pedal movement
s: Start-stop dropping out intermittently
Warning lamp that comes and goes

P08B9.t: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P08B9.d: P08B9 is stored when two independent measurements of the clutch pedal disagree. Ford uses it in two ways per its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary: with dual PWM sensors it compares sensor A with sensor B and decides within a second; with a single analog sensor plus two clutch switches it covers an in-range rationality fault or any switch-related mismatch, the switch part being judged over about 40 clutch cycles at different speeds. FCA patented a similar cross-check of the pedal sensor against the clutch interlock switch, which disables electronic stop-start on a mismatch and cannot always tell which part failed. Circuit faults of each sensor have their own codes (P08A9/P08AA, P08B6/P08B7).
c: One of the two sensors drifting or worn so the channels no longer agree
Sticking or misadjusted clutch switch on systems with one sensor plus switches
Corroded connector or wiring adding resistance to one channel
Sensor assembly or pedal stop misaligned after repairs
s: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
Cruise control unavailable

P08BA.d: Base code for the twelfth pressure control solenoid of an automatic transmission; which valve carries the letter L is up to the manufacturer. Toyota is the one documented user: bulletin T-SB-0094-24 for the 2024 Tacoma and Tacoma Hybrid lists it as P08BA71, actuator stuck, next to the stuck faults of solenoids A, C, D, G and H and a torque converter clutch stuck off. Because Toyota reports the fault type through the suffix, the stuck valve sits under this base code rather than under P08BB/P08BC. The MIL comes on. For trucks built before the production change Toyota's fix is a new transmission with torque converter, on the hybrid also the hybrid module. GM's Corvette dual clutch tables contain no L code.
c: Solenoid or its control valve sticking inside the valve body
Internal transmission fault from production, debris spreading through the hydraulics
Connector or harness fault at the solenoid
s: Check engine light on
Harsh, delayed or missing shifts
Transmission may hold a substitute gear

P08BB.t: Pressure Control Solenoid L Performance/Stuck Off
P08BB.d: Set when pressure control solenoid L is commanded but the pressure or shift element it serves does not respond, i.e. the valve acts as if it were stuck in its off state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Toyota, the only known user of letter L, reports a stuck valve as P08BA with suffix 71 instead. The closest documented analogue is GM's P08C4 for solenoid M on the Corvette dual clutch, where an intrusive routine moves the shift rods slightly and flags the valve when the expected rod travel stays below 100 µm. CARB requires such functional checks for transmission solenoids. P08BC is the opposite fault, P08BF to P08C2 cover the circuit. The driver notices missing or harsh shifts.
c: Valve spool held closed by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak supply pressure to the valve
Leaking seal or circuit downstream of the valve
s: Check engine light on
Missing, slipping or delayed shifts
Possible substitute gear operation

P08BC.t: Pressure Control Solenoid L Stuck On
P08BC.d: Set when pressure control solenoid L keeps applying pressure although the control module has commanded it off, so the element it feeds stays loaded. No manufacturer publishes this code. Toyota, the only documented user of letter L, files a stuck valve under P08BA71 instead. GM's P08C5 for solenoid M of the Corvette dual clutch shows how such a check can work: after a selector valve change the module watches the shift rods, and unexpected movement of one rod or relaxation of another within 200 ms points to a valve that keeps pressure on. CARB lists transmission solenoids as monitored output components. P08BB is the stuck off counterpart. For the driver this means shift shock, binding or a fallback gear.
c: Valve spool held open by debris
Worn bore in the valve body letting pressure through
Output stage or wiring keeping the solenoid energised
s: Check engine light on
Harsh engagement or binding during shifts
Transmission locked in a fallback gear

P08BD.d: Collective code for an electrical fault of pressure control solenoid L that the module does not break down further into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents it publicly; Toyota, the one known user of letter L, has only published the stuck fault P08BA71. Manufacturers that diagnose their solenoids in detail use the specific circuit codes instead, as GM does for solenoid M with P08C8, P08CA and P08CB, each fed by the diagnostic status of the output driver chip. CARB requires a circuit continuity check for every monitored transmission solenoid. The usual culprits are coil, connector or the internal harness; the driver sees the warning light and, depending on the valve, a restricted gear range.
c: Corroded connector or damaged internal harness
Faulty output stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine light on
Restricted gears or fallback gear

P08BE.d: Reports a fault of pressure control solenoid L that comes and goes, typically a circuit that drops out briefly or a valve response that is only occasionally implausible. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and in earlier packages the intermittent codes of the other pressure control solenoids also proved unused. Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, publishes only P08BA71. GM's circuit tests for the comparable solenoid M confirm a fault only after it persists for 150 ms, which is why brief dropouts tend to surface as a stored circuit code instead. CARB requires transmission solenoids to be monitored. Loose pins and chafed wires are the likely causes; symptoms are occasional shift flare or a short-lived fallback mode.
c: Loose or spread terminal at the solenoid or transmission connector
Debris making the valve hang only now and then
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional harsh or flaring shift

P08BF.t: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit/Open
P08BF.d: Points to an open control circuit of pressure control solenoid L: the module sees no load where the coil should be. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the only known user of letter L, has published just P08BA71. GM's open-load test for the analogous solenoid M (P08C8) shows the method: with the low-side driver switched off, the coil should pull the sense pin up to battery voltage; if the driver chip can hold it between roughly 1.7 and 3 V with a tiny current, the circuit is open. Confirmation takes 150 ms. P08C1 and P08C2 are the short to ground and short to power. Typical results are a fallback gear and the warning light.
c: Broken wire in the internal or external harness
s: Check engine light on
Transmission in fallback gear

P08C0.t: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08C0.d: Set when the control circuit of pressure control solenoid L is electrically intact but its behaviour is implausible, for example the current through the coil does not match the commanded value. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the only documented user of letter L, publishes only P08BA71. As an orientation, GM's tables for the comparable solenoid M list a current check next to the circuit tests: a deviation of more than 70 % for 60 ms or more than 400 mA for 300 ms between target and estimated current, without naming P08C9 for it. Causes are a coil with changed resistance, contact resistance or supply problems. P08BF, P08C1 and P08C2 cover clear open or short faults.
c: High contact resistance at connector pins
Unstable supply voltage to the transmission module
s: Check engine light on
Uneven shift quality

P08C1.t: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit Low
P08C1.d: Reports a control circuit voltage of pressure control solenoid L that is too low, usually a short to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, has published only P08BA71. GM's equivalent for solenoid M (P08CA) illustrates the check: while the low-side driver is switched on, the sense pin is examined and a value below about 1.7 V is read as a short to ground, confirmed after 150 ms with battery voltage between 8.75 and 18 V. Depending on the wiring, a ground short can energise the valve permanently or make it uncontrollable. P08C2 is the high counterpart, P08BF the open circuit. Expect a fallback gear and the warning light.
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Shorted turns in the solenoid coil
Fluid or moisture in the connector
s: Check engine light on
Transmission in fallback gear

P08C2.t: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit High
P08C2.d: Reports a control circuit voltage of pressure control solenoid L that is too high, typically a short to battery voltage or to a neighbouring output. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, has published only P08BA71. GM's equivalent for solenoid M (P08CB) uses two tests: with the low-side driver on, a sense voltage above 0.7 to 1.1 V, depending on supply voltage, means a short to power; at shutdown each output is also switched on in turn to detect a short to a neighbouring output, which is then stored and reported at the next start. A shorted valve usually cannot be switched off. P08C1 is the low counterpart, P08BF the open circuit.
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short between adjacent solenoid wires in the internal harness
Defective output stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine light on
Transmission in fallback gear

P08C3.d: Base code for the thirteenth pressure control solenoid; the letter is assigned by the manufacturer. GM uses letter M in the Tremec eight-speed dual clutch of the Corvette (RPO M1L/M1M): its 2023–2025 TCM tables name the part synchronizer actuation valve 1, which serves the odd-gear shaft, while valves 2 to 5 report under P27B9 onwards. GM does not set this base code but the specific ones: P08C4 and P08C5 for hydraulic sticking, P08C8, P08CA and P08CB for the circuit. No other manufacturer documents P08C3 publicly. If it appears, the module has seen a non-specific fault of this valve; the driver typically notices the warning light and rough or missing gear changes on that shaft.
c: Valve sticking from debris in the valve body
Fault in the solenoid wiring or connector
s: Check engine light on
Rough or missing shifts in odd gears
Possible fallback mode

P08C4.t: Pressure Control Solenoid M Performance/Stuck Off
P08C4.d: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch when synchronizer actuation valve 1, the valve for the odd-gear shaft, is hydraulically stuck off. The test runs inside a synchronizer recovery or integrity routine, started after a shift-related fault or when the stored gear does not match the sensed gears at start-up: the shift rods are moved slightly, and if a rod travels 100 µm or less where the valve should move it, a current profile check of the valve has to fail three times before the fault is confirmed. Type A, MIL at once. Bulletin 21-NA-033 blames debris; the fix is GDS valve cleaning three times, service clean and fast learn, and a new control valve body only if it returns.
c: Valve stuck closed by debris in the control valve body
Debris from a dislodged snap ring in the direct clutch assembly (bulletin 23-NA-197)
Low system pressure or fluid level
s: Check engine light on
Odd gears not engaged or engaged late
Noise from the transmission area

P08C5.t: Pressure Control Solenoid M Stuck On
P08C5.d: GM uses this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch when synchronizer actuation valve 1, serving the odd-gear shaft, keeps pressure on although it is commanded off. The check runs whenever the selector pilot valve changes position: a valve stuck on keeps pushing a shift rod, so after the switch the pressure is routed elsewhere. If within 200 ms one rod moves unintentionally by 1000 µm or more while another relaxes by 125 µm or more, and both position sensors are electrically fine, the fault is set. Type A, monitored continuously. Bulletins 21-NA-033 and 23-NA-197 list it with the other valve codes; debris in the control valve body is the main cause. P08C4 is the stuck off counterpart.
c: Valve held open by debris in the control valve body
Debris from a dislodged snap ring in the direct clutch assembly (bulletin 23-NA-197)
Worn valve bore in the control valve body
s: Check engine light on
Clunks or unwanted gear engagement on the odd shaft
Noise from the transmission area

P08C6.d: Collective code for an electrical fault of pressure control solenoid M without a finer split into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents it publicly. GM, the documented user of letter M on the Corvette dual clutch (synchronizer actuation valve 1), reports electrical faults only through the specific codes P08C8, P08CA and P08CB, which are derived from the diagnostic status of the low-side driver chip and confirmed after 150 ms. CARB requires a circuit check for every monitored transmission solenoid. A manufacturer setting P08C6 would point to coil, connector or harness of this valve; for the driver this means the warning light and restricted shifting on the affected shaft.
c: Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine light on
Restricted shifting or fallback mode

P08C7.d: Reports an on-and-off fault of pressure control solenoid M, such as brief circuit dropouts or occasional implausible responses. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, which uses letter M for synchronizer actuation valve 1 of the Corvette dual clutch, lists no intermittent code for it, and earlier packages found the intermittent codes of the other pressure control solenoids unused as well. GM's circuit tests need a fault to last 150 ms, so short dropouts mostly end up as P08C8, P08CA or P08CB once they persist. CARB requires transmission solenoids to be monitored. Loose terminals and chafed wires are the likely causes; symptoms are sporadic shift faults and a warning light that comes and goes.
c: Loose terminal at the solenoid or transmission connector
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Sporadic rough shifts

P08C8.t: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit/Open
P08C8.d: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for an open circuit at synchronizer actuation valve 1, the valve for the odd-gear shaft. The open-load test runs with the low-side driver switched off: an intact coil pulls the sense pin to battery voltage, so if the driver chip can hold it between about 1.7 and 3 V (each ±0.5 V) with a very small current, the circuit is considered open. The fault must persist for 150 ms with battery voltage between 8.75 and 18 V and the engine not cranking; it is suspended while P0882 or P0883 indicates a supply problem. Type A, MIL at once. Without this valve the odd shaft cannot be shifted reliably, so a fallback mode is likely.
c: Connector at the control valve body loose or corroded
Broken wire in the internal harness
s: Check engine light on immediately
Fallback mode with restricted gears

P08C9.t: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08C9.d: Meant for a control circuit of pressure control solenoid M that is not open or shorted but behaves implausibly, for instance a coil current that does not follow the command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, which uses letter M for synchronizer actuation valve 1 of the Corvette dual clutch, publishes only open, low, high and the two hydraulic codes for it; its tables do describe a current check that compares target and estimated current (more than 70 % for 60 ms or more than 400 mA for 300 ms), but without naming P08C9. CARB requires monitoring of transmission solenoids. Possible causes are a coil with drifting resistance, contact resistance or supply voltage problems; shift quality may suffer.
c: High contact resistance at connector pins
Unstable supply voltage to the transmission module
s: Check engine light on
Uneven shift quality

P08CA.t: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit Low
P08CA.d: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for a short to ground in the circuit of synchronizer actuation valve 1, which serves the odd-gear shaft. The test runs while the low-side driver is switched on: the sense pin should then sit at a defined level, and if the driver chip reports it below about 1.7 V (±0.5 V), a ground short is assumed. Confirmation takes 150 ms at 8.75 to 18 V battery voltage with the engine not cranking, and the check is suspended when P0882 or P0883 is present. Type A, MIL at once, monitored continuously. Valves 2 to 5 have their own low codes (P27BF onwards). The driver should expect a fallback mode until the wiring fault is repaired.
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Shorted turns in the solenoid coil
s: Check engine light on immediately
Fallback mode with restricted gears

P08CB.t: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit High
P08CB.d: GM uses this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for synchronizer actuation valve 1 (odd-gear shaft) in two situations. First, a short to battery voltage: with the low-side driver on, a sense voltage above 0.7, 0.9 or 1.1 V (±0.1 V), depending on supply voltage, counts as a shorted load, confirmed after 150 ms. Second, a short to a neighbouring output: at shutdown every output is switched on in turn, a cross-reaction is stored in memory and the code is set at the next start. Type A, MIL at once. The check pauses while P0882 or P0883 is present. A valve shorted to power cannot be switched off, so the transmission will usually go into a fallback mode.
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short to an adjacent solenoid wire in the internal harness
Defective driver stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine light on immediately
Fallback mode with restricted gears
Code may appear right after starting

P08CC.d: Base code for the tenth on/off shift solenoid of an automatic transmission; which valve gets the letter J is decided by the manufacturer. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's gasoline OBD summary ends its shift solenoid list at SS E, the Genesis 8-speed bulletin stops at solenoid F, and GM and Toyota label their later valves as pressure control or clutch solenoids, so J stays unused in the known sources. CARB requires automatic transmission solenoids to be checked for functional response and circuit faults. A manufacturer reporting the fault type through a DTC suffix, as Toyota does for pressure control solenoid L, would store such faults under this base code instead of P08CD to P08D4. Expect harsh, missing or substitute-gear shifts.
c: Shift solenoid J faulty (coil or valve)
Contaminated or degraded transmission fluid restricting the valve
Connector or harness fault between TCM and solenoid
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, delayed or missing shifts
Transmission may hold a substitute gear

P08CD.d: Set when shift solenoid J is switched on but the gear or clutch it controls does not respond, so the valve behaves as if stuck in its off position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest documented analogue is GM's P0751 on the 6-speed transmissions: the TCM commands first gear and flags shift solenoid A stuck off when slip reaches 400 rpm with the gear ratio out of window, a two-trip fault. Ford sets P0751 to P0771 when the obtained gear or shift pattern shows a solenoid functionally failed off after three solenoid events. CARB requires this kind of functional check. P08CE is the opposite fault, P08CF and P08D1 to P08D4 cover the circuit. The driver notices slipping, flare or a missing gear.
c: Solenoid or its shift valve held in the off position by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak supply pressure to the valve
Worn clutch pack or leaking seal in the circuit served by the valve
Solenoid coil too weak to move the valve
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Engine flare or slipping during or after a shift
A gear is missing or skipped
Transmission may hold a substitute gear

P08CE.d: Set when shift solenoid J is switched off but its clutch or shift valve stays applied, so the valve behaves as if stuck in its on position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's P0752 on the 6-speed transmissions is the nearest documented counterpart: with third gear commanded, the TCM flags shift solenoid A stuck on when the gearbox slip reaches 400 rpm while first or second gear is actually obtained, and the MIL comes on after one trip. Ford sets its stuck-on codes P0752 to P0772 from the gear or shift pattern actually reached. CARB requires such functional monitoring. P08CD is the opposite fault. Because an applied clutch can tie up the gearbox, drivers may feel a wrong gear, a harsh engagement or limp mode.
c: Solenoid or its shift valve held in the applied position by debris or varnish
Contaminated transmission fluid after internal wear
Control circuit shorted so the solenoid stays energised
TCM output driver does not switch off
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear or harsh engagement, possible binding feel
Transmission goes into limp mode

P08CF.d: General electrical fault of shift solenoid J, used when a manufacturer does not split the circuit fault into open, low, high or range codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The analogue for solenoid A, P0753, is used by Hyundai for Genesis G80 and G90 8-speed transmissions as Shift Control Solenoid Valve A Electrical; bulletin 21-AT-016HG lists electrical codes for valves A to F and has the solenoid replaced after checking the harness, without any J valve. Ford's electrical check flags a solenoid when driver feedback disagrees with the commanded state for 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB requires circuit monitoring when a functional check is not feasible. P08D1 to P08D4 are the detailed circuit codes. Shift quality usually drops at once.
c: Solenoid coil open or shorted internally
Damaged harness, corroded or loose connector at the transmission
Fault in the internal transmission harness or solenoid body
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh or missing shifts
Transmission may lock into a limp-home gear

P08D0.d: Reserved for a shift solenoid J fault that comes and goes instead of being present continuously, typically brief circuit dropouts or erratic valve response. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the intermittent codes of the earlier shift solenoids, such as P0754 for solenoid A, are not used in the GM and Ford sources checked either; those makers report dropouts through their open, short or functional codes. Ford runs its solenoid electrical checks continuously with 0.5 to 5 second filters, so short interruptions are caught there. CARB requires circuit monitoring of transmission output components in general. P08CF and P08D1 to P08D4 are the permanent electrical faults. Drivers notice occasional harsh shifts or a passing warning light.
c: Loose or corroded connector losing contact under vibration or heat
Chafed harness with intermittent short or break
Valve sticking now and then due to contaminated fluid
Solenoid coil failing only when hot
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional harsh or delayed shifts
Sporadic limp mode that clears after restart

P08D1.t: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08D1.d: Set when the control circuit of shift solenoid J is electrically intact but its measured values, usually solenoid current or driver feedback, lie outside the expected window for the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The analogue for solenoid A, P0972, is likewise not used in the GM and Ford sources checked; Ford reports such current faults by its own electrical current check, which flags feedback current out of range for 0.5 seconds. CARB requires output circuits to be checked for faults beyond plain opens and shorts. P08D2 and P08D3 cover low and high circuit voltage, P08D4 an open circuit, P08CF a general electrical fault. Shift quality may suffer because the valve no longer moves as intended.
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High resistance at connector pins or internal harness
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM or solenoid feed
Faulty current sensing in the TCM output stage
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh or irregular shifts
Possible limp mode

P08D2.t: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit Low
P08D2.d: Set when the TCM sees too little voltage on the control line of shift solenoid J, typically because the line or the coil is shorted to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J would be a tenth on/off valve, which none of the known transmission sources assigns. GM's analogue for solenoid A, P0973 on the 6-speed units, fails when the output driver reports a ground short for 1.2 of 1.5 seconds and lights the MIL after one trip; Ford names the same fault on its solenoids a short to ground. CARB requires such circuit checks. P08D3 is the high-side fault, P08D4 the open circuit. The TCM usually switches the valve off and runs a substitute gear.
c: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
Faulty output stage in the TCM
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission holds a substitute gear
Harsh or missing shifts

P08D3.t: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit High
P08D3.d: Logged when the control line of shift solenoid J reads higher than the commanded state allows, pointing to a short to battery voltage or, on some designs, an open coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In GM's tables the high code for solenoid A, P0974, covers both an open circuit and a short to power, fails after 1.2 of 1.5 seconds and needs two trips for the MIL, while Ford keeps opens apart and uses its high code for shorts to power only. Which reading applies to J therefore depends on the maker. CARB requires the circuit check. P08D2 is the low-side counterpart, P08D4 the dedicated open-circuit code. A valve that cannot be driven correctly leads to wrong or missing gears.
c: Control wire shorted to a voltage-carrying conductor
Open solenoid coil (on systems that report opens as high)
Moisture in the transmission connector bridging pins
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear or harsh engagement
Possible limp mode

P08D4.d: Dedicated code for an open control circuit of shift solenoid J: the TCM drives the valve but no current flows through wire, connector or coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The known analogues show why: Ford files an open circuit under the base code of each solenoid (P0750 for solenoid A) and GM includes it in the high-voltage code P0974, so neither needs a separate open code. Ford detects such electrical faults when driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB requires open and short checks on transmission outputs. P08D2 and P08D3 are the short-circuit codes. An unpowered valve rests in its default state, so a gear may be missing or locked.
c: Broken control wire or loose terminal
Transmission connector not fully seated after service
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
One gear missing or transmission stuck in one gear
Harsh shifts

P08D5.d: Base code for shift solenoid K, the eleventh on/off shift valve in SAE's lettering. Which valve carries the letter is up to the manufacturer, and none documents K publicly: Ford's gasoline OBD summary lists shift solenoids only up to SS E, Hyundai's bulletin 21-AT-016HG for the Genesis 8-speed ends at shift control solenoid F, and GM's 2016 to 2025 tables contain no code of the K group. Ford shows how a base code can be used: its P0750 stands for an open circuit of solenoid A. CARB requires functional and circuit monitoring of shift solenoids. P08D6 to P08DD split the fault into functional and circuit types. Expect harsh or missing shifts and possibly a fixed substitute gear.
c: Shift solenoid K faulty (coil or valve)
Harness or connector fault between TCM and solenoid
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, delayed or missing shifts
Transmission may hold a substitute gear

P08D6.d: Indicates that shift solenoid K was commanded on but the gear or clutch behind it never engaged, as if the valve stayed in its off position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A documented model is GM's P0751 for solenoid A on the 6-speed units: with first gear commanded, the TCM counts a fault when slip reaches 400 rpm and the measured ratio sits in a fixed window that points to the wrong gear, and it needs two trips to light the MIL. Ford infers a solenoid failed off from the obtained gear or shift pattern over three solenoid events. CARB requires this functional check. The reverse fault is P08D7. Typical signs are engine flare during shifts and a skipped gear.
c: Valve or shift spool held in rest position by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak line pressure
Leaking seal or worn clutch pack in the circuit fed by the valve
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Engine flare or slipping during shifts
A gear is skipped or missing

P08D7.d: Stored when shift solenoid K is switched off but the circuit it feeds stays pressurised, so a clutch remains applied. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's P0752 for solenoid A is the documented analogue: with third gear commanded, the TCM fails the valve when gearbox slip reaches 400 rpm while the transmission actually sits in first or second, and the MIL lights after a single trip. Ford flags stuck-on solenoids from the gear actually reached during its mechanical check. CARB demands this functional monitoring. P08D6 is the opposite fault, P08D8 and P08DA to P08DD the circuit faults. Drivers may notice a wrong starting gear, binding, harsh engagement or emergency mode.
c: Valve or shift spool jammed in applied position
Metal debris in the fluid after internal wear
TCM output or shorted wire keeps the solenoid energised
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear when pulling away
Binding or harsh engagement
Limp mode

P08D8.d: Collective electrical fault for shift solenoid K, used by makers that do not split circuit faults into low, high, open or range codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The pattern exists for earlier letters: Hyundai stores P0753 (shift control solenoid valve A electrical) on the Genesis G80 and G90 8-speed and, per bulletin 21-AT-016HG, replaces the solenoid once the harness checks out, with valves listed only up to F. Ford's electrical check fails a solenoid when the driver feedback contradicts the command for 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB requires circuit monitoring of transmission outputs. P08DA to P08DD are the detailed codes. The TCM usually reacts at once with altered shifting.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh or missing shifts
Transmission may lock into a limp-home gear

P08D9.d: Meant for a shift solenoid K fault that appears and vanishes, such as a connector losing contact over bumps or a coil dropping out when hot. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the sources checked even uses the intermittent code of solenoid A, P0754; GM and Ford catch brief interruptions with their open, short and functional codes instead. Ford runs its electrical checks continuously with 0.5 to 5 second filters. CARB asks for circuit monitoring of output components without prescribing an intermittent code. Unlike the permanent fault P08D8, the symptoms here come and go: an occasional hard shift or a warning light that is gone after a restart.
c: Loose or fretted terminal in the transmission connector
Chafed wire that touches only under vibration
Solenoid coil dropping out at high fluid temperature
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional harsh or late shift
Sporadic limp mode that clears after restart

P08DA.t: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08DA.d: Points to a control circuit of shift solenoid K that is neither open nor shorted, yet whose measured values, usually coil current, do not fit the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the analogue for solenoid A, P0972, is not used in the GM or Ford sources either. Ford covers the same failure with an electrical current check that trips when the feedback current stays out of range for 0.5 seconds. Causes are typically a coil with changed resistance, a high-resistance contact or a weak TCM driver. CARB requires output circuits to be checked beyond plain opens and shorts. P08DB, P08DC and P08DD cover low, high and open. The valve may switch late or incompletely.
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Corroded or loose pins adding resistance
TCM output stage no longer delivers correct current
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Delayed or soft shifts
Possible limp mode

P08DB.t: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit Low
P08DB.d: The TCM's output stage reports a voltage on the shift solenoid K control circuit below what the commanded state requires, the classic sign of a control wire rubbing through to ground or a coil with an internal short. No manufacturer documents this K code publicly. For solenoid A, GM's 6-speed tables set P0973 when a ground short is flagged for 1.2 out of 1.5 seconds, with at least 9 V supply and the engine running, and light the MIL after one trip; Ford lists P0973 as short to ground. CARB mandates the check. P08DC is the opposite fault and P08DD the open circuit. Many TCMs then disable the valve, so expect a limp-home gear.
c: Control wire rubbed through to ground
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission stays in a limp-home gear
Reduced acceleration due to missing gears

P08DC.t: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit High
P08DC.d: The monitored control line of shift solenoid K sits closer to supply voltage than it should, for instance because it touches a powered wire or, depending on the driver design, because the coil is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM treats the solenoid A version, P0974, as open or power short and fails it after 1.2 of 1.5 seconds, but lights the MIL only after two trips. Ford's P0974 means a short to power only, because Ford reports opens separately. CARB requires this circuit check. P08DB is the low counterpart, P08DD the open-circuit code. A valve shorted to power may stay energised, giving a wrong gear or harsh engagements.
c: Control wire touching a powered conductor
Open coil on systems that read opens as high
TCM low-side driver no longer pulls the line down
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear or harsh engagement
Possible limp mode

P08DD.d: Signals that the control circuit of shift solenoid K is open, so commanding the valve produces no current: a broken wire, a pushed-out terminal, a burnt coil or a failed internal transmission harness. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford handles opens through the base code of each solenoid, P0750 for solenoid A, while GM's tables fold them into the circuit-high code P0974, so a separate open code like this one stays unused in both systems. CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for opens. P08DB and P08DC are the short-circuit codes, P08D8 the general electrical fault. Without power the valve stays in its rest position, so one gear range drops out.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Some gears no longer available
Limp mode with fixed gear

P08DE.d: Base code for shift solenoid L, which in SAE's lettering would be the twelfth on/off shift valve of an automatic transmission. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. It must not be confused with pressure control solenoid L, which Toyota uses on the 2024 Tacoma under its own code family. Ford's gasoline summary stops at shift solenoid E, Hyundai's Genesis 8-speed bulletin at F, and GM's 2016 to 2025 OBD tables show no L shift solenoid. For a maker using base codes, Ford's practice is the model: P0750 there means an open circuit. CARB requires shift solenoids to be monitored. The detailed fault types are P08DF to P08E6. Shift quality and gear availability may suffer.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the solenoid circuit
Debris in the valve body affecting the valve
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh or erratic shifting
Possible substitute gear

P08DF.d: Functional fault of shift solenoid L: the TCM switches the valve on, but speed sensor data show that the intended clutch did not take up, so the valve acts as if stuck off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The detection logic is known from the analogue for solenoid A: Ford compares the obtained gear or shift pattern over three solenoid events, and GM's P0751 counts repeated slip of at least 400 rpm in a ratio window that does not match first gear, with the MIL after two trips. Typical causes are a valve jammed by debris, low line pressure or a leaking clutch circuit rather than wiring. CARB requires the check. P08E0 is the stuck-on fault. Expect flare or a missing gear.
c: Low line pressure or low fluid level
Leak in the clutch circuit fed by the valve
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Engine flare between gears
Gear missing or skipped

P08E0.d: Functional fault of shift solenoid L in the opposite direction: although switched off, the valve keeps its circuit applied, leaving engaged a clutch that should be released. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. As a model, GM's P0752 for solenoid A sets after one trip when gearbox slip reaches 400 rpm with third gear commanded but first or second actually engaged, and Ford's mechanical check reads a stuck-on solenoid from the gear the transmission really obtains. CARB requires such functional checks. Electrical causes are rare here; a seized spool or an output stage that never switches off is more likely. P08DF is the stuck-off fault. Possible effects are tie-up, harsh shifts and limp mode.
c: Shift spool seized in applied position
Contaminated fluid after clutch or bearing wear
TCM output stage does not switch off
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Drivetrain binding or harsh shifts
Limp mode

P08E1.d: General electrical malfunction of shift solenoid L, intended for transmissions whose TCM does not distinguish or separately report low, high and open circuit faults. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The equivalent electrical code is in real use for lower letters, for example P2709 for shift control solenoid valve F on the 2017 and 2018 Genesis G80 and G90 8-speed, where Hyundai's bulletin 21-AT-016HG calls for harness checks and solenoid replacement. Ford fails a solenoid electrically when the driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB requires the circuit check. P08E3 to P08E6 are the detailed codes, P08E2 the intermittent one.
c: Harness or connector damage on the solenoid circuit
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh shifts or fixed gear
Reduced driving performance

P08E2.d: Reserved for an unstable fault of shift solenoid L that is detected, disappears and may return, typically from a loose terminal, a chafed wire that only touches under vibration or a heat-sensitive coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The intermittent codes of the lower letters, beginning with P0754 for solenoid A, are absent from the GM and Ford documents checked as well; those systems record short dropouts as ordinary circuit or functional faults, Ford with continuous checks filtered over 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB asks for circuit monitoring in general. For diagnosis, freeze frame data and a wiggle test help more than a static resistance check. Symptoms appear only now and then.
c: Loose terminal or poor pin tension in the connector
Insulation chafed at a bracket or edge
Coil that fails intermittently when hot
s: Intermittent warning light
Occasional harsh shift
Limp mode that disappears after restart

P08E3.t: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08E3.d: Plausibility fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L: the circuit is not open or shorted, but voltage or current during actuation is implausible for the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the matching code for solenoid A, P0972, is likewise absent from the GM and Ford documents checked. Ford's electrical current check, which flags feedback current out of range for 0.5 seconds, shows how such a test works. Practical causes are coil resistance drifting with temperature, corroded pins adding resistance or a TCM output stage losing drive strength. CARB requires output circuits to be checked beyond opens and shorts. P08E4 to P08E6 are the clear-cut circuit codes. Shifts may feel soft or delayed.
c: TCM output stage losing drive strength
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Soft or delayed shifts
Possible limp mode

P08E4.t: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit Low
P08E4.d: Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L. Usually it means a short to ground on the control wire, less often a coil with shorted windings that pulls the voltage down. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's analogue for solenoid A, P0973 on the 6-speed units, needs a ground-short flag from the output hardware for 1.2 of 1.5 seconds and lights the MIL after one trip; Ford names P0973 a short to ground and runs the check continuously. CARB requires circuit monitoring. P08E5 is the high-voltage counterpart, P08E6 the open circuit. A shorted output usually forces the TCM into a safe substitute gear, and acceleration feels weaker.
c: Fluid or moisture in the connector creating a path to ground
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission locked in a substitute gear
Weak acceleration

P08E5.t: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit High
P08E5.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L, set when the line shows battery voltage or a floating high level while the TCM expects otherwise. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The analogue for solenoid A illustrates the two possible readings: in GM's 6-speed tables P0974 covers an open circuit as well as a short to power, fails after 1.2 of 1.5 seconds and needs two trips for the MIL, whereas Ford's P0974 only means a short to power. A wire chafed against a powered conductor inside the transmission harness is a typical cause. CARB requires the check. P08E4 is the low counterpart, P08E6 the open circuit. The valve may stay on, giving wrong gears.
c: Control wire chafed against a powered conductor
Open coil on systems that read opens as high
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear selected
Harsh engagement or limp mode

P08E6.d: Open circuit in the control path of shift solenoid L: harness, connector, internal transmission wiring or the coil itself no longer carry current, so the valve cannot be energised. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Among the documented analogues, Ford reports an open circuit through each solenoid's base code, P0750 for solenoid A, and GM counts it as part of the high-voltage code P0974; a stand-alone open code therefore has no known user. Ford's electrical checks need 0.5 to 5 seconds of mismatch between command and feedback. CARB requires the check. Measuring coil resistance at the transmission connector separates a coil fault from a harness break. P08E4 and P08E5 cover the shorts.
c: Break in the harness or internal transmission wiring
Connector unlatched or terminal backed out
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gear range missing or fixed gear
Harsh shifts

P08E7.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Enable Circuit
P08E7.d: Covers the enable line with which a drive motor control module activates the actuator of a clutch that couples or uncouples electric drive motor A from the wheels. The code sets when the module sees an electrical fault on that line, typically an open circuit or an implausible state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest known hardware is the front electric drive unit of the 2024 Corvette E-Ray, which has a disconnect clutch actuator, a clutch pawl and a position switch; GM lists separate faults there, such as P08ED and a lost-communication code for the actuator. CARB requires circuit checks on such output components. P08E8 and P08E9 are the low and high variants. The driver usually loses electric assist on that axle.
c: Enable wire open or connector at the clutch actuator not seated
Internal electronics fault in the disconnect clutch actuator
Corroded or water-damaged connector near the drive unit
Faulty enable driver in the drive motor control module
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
No electric drive or assist from the affected axle
All-wheel-drive or electric-only modes unavailable

P08E8.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Enable Circuit Low
P08E8.d: Set when the voltage on the enable line of the drive motor A disconnect clutch actuator stays below the expected range, usually because the wire or the actuator input is shorted to ground. The control module can then no longer switch the actuator on, so the clutch cannot be engaged or released on command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the comparable hardware is the front drive unit of the Corvette E-Ray with its disconnect clutch actuator, pawl and switch, for which GM publishes only P08ED and an actuator communication fault. CARB requires such circuit monitoring. P08E7 is the general circuit fault, P08E9 the high-side counterpart. Electric drive on that axle is typically disabled.
c: Enable wire chafed and shorted to ground
Internal short at the actuator enable input
Water ingress in the actuator connector
Faulty output stage in the drive motor control module
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive axle stays disconnected
Reduced performance, no electric launch or all-wheel drive

P08E9.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Enable Circuit High
P08E9.d: Set when the enable line of the drive motor A disconnect clutch actuator reads higher than it should, for example because it is shorted to a supply voltage or the line floats due to an open ground. The module then cannot reliably switch the actuator off or confirm its state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the nearest known application is the front electric drive unit of the Corvette E-Ray, whose disconnect clutch actuator and switch GM services as separate parts but describes only under P08ED and a communication code. CARB covers the fault through its output component monitoring. P08E8 is the low-side counterpart, P08E7 the general circuit fault. The system normally keeps the motor uncoupled.
c: Enable wire shorted to a supply circuit
Open ground or reference circuit of the actuator
Internal fault in the disconnect clutch actuator
Faulty output stage in the drive motor control module
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive on the affected axle switched off
Possible clunk when the system tries to couple the motor

P08EA.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Circuit
P08EA.d: Concerns the sensor or switch that reports where the pawl of the drive motor A disconnect clutch sits, i.e. whether the form-locking clutch is engaged or released. The code sets when the control module finds an electrical fault in that signal circuit, such as an open line or a signal outside its valid states. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM fits a drive motor disconnect clutch switch to the front drive unit of the Corvette E-Ray and blames it for P08ED; pawl clutches with dedicated position sensors are described in supplier patents such as one from Means Industries. CARB requires input circuit checks. P08EB and P08EC are the low and high variants, P08ED the plausibility fault. Electric drive on that axle is usually inhibited.
c: Faulty disconnect clutch position switch or sensor
Open signal or reference wire to the position switch
Corroded or loose connector at the drive unit
Faulty input stage in the drive motor control module
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive or all-wheel drive unavailable
Reduced acceleration in hybrid modes

P08EB.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Circuit Low
P08EB.d: Set when the pawl position signal of the drive motor A disconnect clutch stays below its valid range, which points to a short to ground in the signal wire, a missing sensor supply or a sensor that has failed low. The module then cannot tell whether the pawl has engaged. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the matching hardware is the disconnect clutch switch on the front drive unit of the Corvette E-Ray, which GM links only to P08ED, and supplier patents describe such position sensing on pawl or strut clutches. CARB requires out-of-range checks on these inputs. P08EC is the high-side fault, P08EA the general circuit fault. The system typically keeps the motor uncoupled and lights a warning.
c: Position signal wire shorted to ground
Missing supply voltage to the position switch
Position switch or sensor failed low
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive axle disabled
Hybrid modes with electric assist not selectable

P08EC.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Circuit High
P08EC.d: Set when the pawl position signal of the drive motor A disconnect clutch stays above its valid range. Typical reasons are an open signal or ground wire, which lets the input float high, or a short to a supply voltage. The module then has no trustworthy feedback on whether the clutch is engaged. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the closest documented hardware is the disconnect clutch switch on the Corvette E-Ray front drive unit, tied by GM only to P08ED, and patents on pawl or strut clutches with position sensors show the principle. CARB requires out-of-range monitoring. P08EB is the low-side fault, P08EA the general circuit fault, P08ED the plausibility check. Electric drive on that axle is usually locked out.
c: Open signal or ground wire of the position switch
Signal wire shorted to a supply circuit
Position switch or sensor failed high
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
No electric drive from the affected axle
All-wheel drive or electric launch missing

P08ED.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Performance
P08ED.d: A plausibility fault: the pawl position reported for the drive motor A disconnect clutch does not match what the control module commanded, or the clutch did not reach the expected position, even though the circuit itself is electrically intact. GM documents the code for the 2024 Corvette E-Ray, whose front electric drive unit uses a clutch pawl and a disconnect clutch actuator; bulletin 24-NA-165 says it is stored in the drive motor control module, lights the MIL and is usually caused by the disconnect clutch switch, which is replaced as an external part. Electrical faults of the same signal are P08EA to P08EC; actuator enable faults are P08E7 to P08E9. The driver mostly sees the warning lamp and loss of electric front drive.
c: Faulty drive motor disconnect clutch switch (GM E-Ray bulletin)
Disconnect clutch actuator not moving the pawl fully
Worn or binding pawl or clutch teeth inside the drive unit
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Electric front-axle drive unavailable or intermittent
Hybrid modes restricted

P0900.d: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator that opens and closes clutch A in an automated or dual-clutch transmission. The code sets when the module detects an open circuit, so it cannot energise the actuator. Ford documents it for the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox in the Fiesta and Focus, where each dry clutch is moved by a three-phase electric motor with hall sensors; P0900 is the open-circuit check of the clutch A motor, alongside P0902 (short to ground) and P0903 (short to power). Ford program 20B23 for some 2016-2017 Focus cars lists P0900 with a lit check engine light and erratic shifts caused by failed clutch actuator motors. P090A is the same fault on clutch B.
c: Failed clutch A actuator motor (open winding or internal fault)
Loose connector or broken wire between TCM and actuator
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM
s: Check engine light on
Erratic or missed shifts, vibration on take-off
Transmission in limp mode, possibly no drive

P0901.t: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0901.d: Set when the clutch A actuator circuit is electrically present but does not behave as expected, for instance when the measured current or response deviates too far from the target. Usage differs by maker. Ford lists P0901 among the DPS6 PowerShift codes, and trade guidance recommends swapping the two identical clutch motors: if the fault moves to clutch B, the motor is bad. Honda added P0901 on the 2015 TLX V6 nine-speed automatic for abnormal resistance in the clutch pressure control solenoid circuits, with failsafe gear hold and MIL. FCA recall 16V529 on 9-speed models also uses it to decide on a harness replacement. P0900, P0902 and P0903 are the pure circuit faults; P090B is the clutch B counterpart.
c: Weak or worn clutch A actuator motor (dual-clutch units)
High resistance in the transmission harness or sub-harness
TCM fault or outdated TCM software
s: Check engine light on
Shudder, harsh engagement or missed shifts
Failsafe mode with a held gear

P0902.t: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit Low
P0902.d: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a low state, in practice a short to ground on a motor or control line. Ford defines it exactly this way for the DPS6 PowerShift transmission: the TCM tests the three-phase clutch A motor for open circuit (P0900), short to ground (P0902) and short to power (P0903), next to hall sensor and sequence checks. Ford's TCM program 14M02 for 2011-2015 Fiesta and Focus also lists P0902 among the codes for which a failed TCM can be the cause, so the module itself is a real suspect besides the motor and harness. P090C is the same fault on clutch B. With the clutch no longer controllable, the gearbox goes into a fallback mode.
c: Clutch A actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
s: Check engine light on
No drive or only some gears available
Jerky take-off and shift faults

P0903.t: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit High
P0903.d: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a high state, meaning a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage. Ford names P0903 as the short-to-power test of the clutch A motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox of the Fiesta and Focus, part of a set with P0900 for an open circuit and P0902 for a short to ground. Ford's OBD summary gives no thresholds for these motor checks. Because both DPS6 clutch motors are identical, swapping them shows whether the motor or the harness and TCM side is at fault. CARB requires such circuit checks on transmission output components. P090D is the same fault on clutch B. The clutch is released and the vehicle may not drive normally.
c: Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Internal fault in the clutch A actuator motor
Faulty motor driver in the TCM
s: Check engine light on
Limp mode, gears missing or no drive
Harsh or delayed engagement

P0904.d: Circuit A of the gate select position sensor tells the control module of an automated manual gearbox where the shift mechanism stands in the select direction, i.e. which gate (for example 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 or reverse) is lined up. This generic circuit code sets when the module sees an electrical fault on that signal that is not covered by the more specific low, high or intermittent variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. Aisin AI and Isuzu patents describe such select stroke or select position sensors working next to an electric or hydraulic select actuator, and CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs of this kind. P0905 to P0908 are the siblings, P09A2 and P09A6 the same signal on circuits B and C. Without a valid gate signal the gearbox usually stops shifting or holds one gear.
c: Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector at the gate select sensor or actuator unit
Chafed or broken sensor wiring near the gearbox
Faulty gate select position sensor (often integrated in the shift and select actuator)
Faulty sensor input or reference supply in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops shifting or stays in one gear
Neutral indicator flashes or vehicle will not pull away

P0905.t: Gate Select Position Circuit A Range/Performance
P0905.d: Plausibility fault of the gate select position signal on circuit A in an automated manual gearbox. The signal is electrically within limits, but it does not fit what the control module expects: typical checks compare the measured select travel with the learned gate positions and the commanded target gate. No manufacturer documents this code in freely citable material. Patents by Aisin AI on select control with target and actual gate, and on fallback strategies after a stroke sensor failure, show how the module depends on this signal; CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0904, P0906 and P0907 cover the electrical faults, P0909 a select movement that misses its target. The driver typically sees a fallback mode with no or limited shifting.
c: Worn or drifting gate select sensor, main and redundant tracks disagree
High resistance at connector pins distorting the sensor voltage
Gate positions not relearned after actuator, clutch or TCM replacement
Loose or displaced magnet or sensor mounting on the select shaft
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox drops to neutral or refuses certain gears
Slow or jerky gear changes in fallback mode

P0906.t: Gate Select Position Circuit A Low
P0906.d: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Common causes are a short to ground on the signal line, a missing sensor supply, or an internal sensor defect; with many sensor designs a broken signal wire also reads low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Aisin AI and Isuzu describe select stroke and select position sensors with a defined voltage curve across the gates in their patents, so a value below that curve is clearly out of range; CARB calls for out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0907 is the matching high fault, P09A4 and P09A8 are the low faults of circuits B and C. Without a gate signal the gearbox usually locks gear changes or holds a safe gear.
c: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal defect of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gear changes possible or gearbox stays in neutral
Warning message about the transmission on the dashboard

P0907.t: Gate Select Position Circuit A High
P0907.d: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Typical causes are a short of the signal line to the sensor supply or to battery voltage, a broken sensor ground, or an internal sensor fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The patents of Aisin AI and Isuzu on select control show that the module derives the active gate directly from this sensor voltage, so a reading above the valid band leaves it blind in the select direction; CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0906 is the opposite low fault, P09A5 and P09A9 are the high faults of circuits B and C. For the driver this usually means a warning lamp and a gearbox that no longer changes gear or stays in a fallback gear.
c: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed

P0908.t: Gate Select Position Circuit A Intermittent
P0908.d: Points to a gate select position signal on circuit A that drops out or jumps for short moments in an automated manual gearbox, too briefly or too irregularly for a steady low or high fault. Loose terminals, a damaged harness that moves with the engine, or moisture in the connector at the shift and select actuator are the usual reasons. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. An Aisin AI patent explains why even short sensor dropouts matter: if a stroke sensor fails while driving, the controller can no longer confirm the engaged gear and must switch to a fallback strategy. CARB requires circuit and rationality checks on such inputs. P0904 to P0907 are the steady faults of the same circuit. Drivers often notice occasional neutral drops or refused shifts that vanish again.
c: Loose or spread terminals at the sensor or actuator connector
Harness damage that only opens or shorts under engine movement
Moisture or corrosion in the connector near the gearbox
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional drop to neutral or refused shift
Fault often disappears after restarting the engine

P0909.d: Set when the control module of an automated manual gearbox commands the select actuator to a new gate, but the measured select position does not reach the target within the allowed time and tolerance. Sensor and actuator circuits may be electrically fine; the fault lies in the closed loop as a whole. Typical reasons are a jammed or stiff select shaft or shift head, a worn or weak select motor, or a sensor offset. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. An Aisin AI patent describes select control with target and actual gates, and a Hyundai/Kia patent detects jammed or stuck shift actuators from motor current. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0910 to P0913 are the actuator circuit faults, P0919 the same error in the shift direction. The gearbox may refuse gears or stay in neutral.
c: Stiff or jammed select shaft, shift head or internal selector mechanism
Worn select motor (brushes, gears) with too little force
Select sensor offset or gate positions not relearned
Weak battery or voltage drop on the actuator supply
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Certain gears cannot be engaged or gearbox stays in neutral
Clicking or whirring from the actuator without a gear change

P090A.d: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator for clutch B, the second clutch of a dual-clutch transmission, and sets when the module finds an open circuit. Ford uses it on the DPS6 PowerShift of the Fiesta and Focus: the clutch B electric motor is tested for driver faults (P087A), hall sensor faults (P087B), sequence errors (P087E), an open circuit (P090A), a short to ground (P090C) and a short to power (P090D). Trade guidance for the DPS6 is to swap the two identical clutch motors; if the code moves to the clutch A equivalent P0900, the motor is defective, otherwise the harness or TCM is. CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. Shifting becomes erratic and the gearbox may refuse to drive.
c: Loose connector or broken wire to the clutch B motor
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM
s: Check engine light on
Even gears or reverse missing, erratic shifts
Limp mode or no drive

P090B.t: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit Performance
P090B.d: Set when the clutch B actuator circuit is electrically connected but the actuator does not respond as commanded, for example too slowly or with an unexpected current draw. Ford uses P090B on the DPS6 PowerShift transmission. Trade guidance for this gearbox starts with a visual check of the harness from the TCM to the clutch B motor, then swaps the two identical clutch motors: if the code becomes P0901, the motor with its built-in position sensor is faulty; if P090B stays, the circuit or TCM needs pinpoint testing. Ford's TCM program 14M02 for 2011-2015 Fiesta and Focus also lists P090B as a code where the TCM itself can be the cause. P090A, P090C and P090D are the pure circuit faults of clutch B.
c: Worn or sluggish clutch B actuator motor
TCM fault (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Damaged harness between TCM and clutch B motor
s: Check engine light on
Shudder or slipping in even gears and reverse
Delayed or missed shifts, possible limp mode

P090C.t: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit Low
P090C.d: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a low state, which on the documented application means a short to ground. Ford defines P090C as the short-to-ground check of the clutch B motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox, paired with P090A for an open circuit and P090D for a short to power. Ford's TCM program 14M02 for 2011-2015 Fiesta and Focus also lists P090C among the codes that a defective TCM can cause, so the module belongs on the suspect list along with the motor and its wiring. Swapping the identical clutch motors helps: if the fault moves to P0902, the motor is bad. CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. Expect missing gears, erratic shifts or no drive.
c: Clutch B actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
s: Check engine light on
Even gears or reverse unavailable
Limp mode or no drive

P090D.t: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit High
P090D.d: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a high state, i.e. a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage. Ford documents P090D as the short-to-power check of the clutch B motor in the DPS6 PowerShift transmission of the Fiesta and Focus. Ford customer satisfaction program 20B23, covering some 2016-2017 Focus cars, names P090D together with P0900 and several hall and driver codes as signs of failed clutch actuator motors, with erratic shifting, vibration and a lit check engine light; dealers replaced both motors. P090A and P090C are the open and ground faults of the same circuit, P0903 the clutch A equivalent. CARB requires circuit checks on such transmission outputs.
c: Failed clutch B actuator motor (Ford program 20B23)
Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Faulty motor driver in the TCM
s: Check engine light on
Erratic or missed shifts and vibration
Limp mode, possibly no drive

P0910.d: Concerns the drive circuit of the gate select actuator, the motor or valve that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox sideways from gate to gate. The code sets when the control module finds this output open or electrically faulty, for example when no current flows although the driver stage is switched on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Isuzu and Hyundai/Kia patents describe select and shift actuators as electric motors fed by the transmission controller; older and heavy-duty systems use hydraulic or pneumatic select cylinders with solenoid valves. CARB requires circuit checks on such outputs. P0911 to P0913 are the range, low and high variants, P0909 a select movement that misses its target. Without the select actuator the gearbox cannot change gates and stays in its current gear or neutral.
c: Open winding or worn brushes in the select motor
Broken actuator wire or terminal pushed out of the connector
Corroded actuator connector near the gearbox
Faulty actuator driver stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox cannot change between gates, only some gears available
Vehicle may stay in neutral and not drive off

P0911.d: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but the current, voltage or response measured on it does not fit the command, for example a current that is too high or too low for the requested movement. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Hyundai/Kia patent explains why controllers watch actuator current closely: jamming and sticking raise the motor load, and the motor can be damaged if this is not caught early. An Isuzu patent describes electric select actuators controlled by the transmission module. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0910, P0912 and P0913 are the clear electrical faults, P0909 the failure to reach a gate. Gear changes become slow or are blocked.
c: Worn select motor drawing abnormal current
Stiff select mechanism overloading the actuator
High resistance in actuator wiring or connector
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slow, hesitant or aborted gear changes
Gearbox enters fallback mode with limited gears

P0912.d: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state, which usually means a short to ground on a motor or control line, or an internal short in the actuator. Many controllers then switch the affected output off to protect the driver stage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Isuzu and Hyundai/Kia describe in their patents select and shift actuators built as electric motors and driven by the transmission controller, which is the hardware this circuit check covers; CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. P0913 is the matching high fault, P0910 an open circuit and P0911 a plausibility fault. With the select actuator disabled, the gearbox can no longer change gates.
c: Actuator wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in the select motor, e.g. from brush debris
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gate change possible, gearbox stays in current gear or neutral
Vehicle may not pull away

P0913.d: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Usual causes are a short of a motor or control line to battery voltage, or a driver stage in the module that no longer switches off; depending on the circuit design an open load can also read high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Patents by Isuzu and Hyundai/Kia describe electric select and shift actuators that the transmission controller powers directly, and CARB requires circuit checks on such outputs. P0912 is the opposite low fault, P0910 the open circuit, P0911 the plausibility fault and P0909 a select movement that misses its gate. The driver sees a warning lamp and a gearbox that can no longer change gates.
