Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure
Dual-clutch gearbox loses the even gears

P0968.t: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open
P0968.d: Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid C. GM's 8-speed assigns C to clutch 3 (C13567), the 9-speed to CB38 and the 10-speed to C23457910; an impedance above 200 kOhm for 0.3 s counts as open and sets a Type A code after one trip. In GM's dual-clutch gearbox, C is the redundant shutdown valve of the odd clutch, checked for open load while its output is switched off and confirmed after 150 ms. GM six-speeds report an open C solenoid as P0971, and neither Ford's summaries nor the Allison 1000 tables list C codes. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission output components. Low and high are P0970/P0971, performance P0969; the usual result is a lost gear range or limp mode.
c: Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness
Faulty output stage in the control module
s: MIL and transmission warning on
Gears that need clutch C are unavailable
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P0969.t: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0969.d: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid C. Publicly documented only for GM's front-drive six-speeds: on the Saab 9-4X 6T70, clutch pressure solenoid 3 feeds the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches through the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve. If measured current differs from the commanded current for 5 s, the module stores a Type C code and freezes the adaptations of both clutches. GM's 2016 table (C456/CBR1 solenoid) sets it after an invalid feedback for 4.4 of 5 s, also without MIL. Other GM users such as the 8- to 10-speeds list only open, low and high for C, and Ford does not use C. Drivers rarely notice more than gradually rougher 4-5-6 or reverse engagements. Electrical faults: P0968, P0970, P0971.
c: Solenoid 3 with internal fault, current no longer matches the command
Debris sticking the solenoid or the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve
High resistance in the internal connection to the module
s: Usually no warning light
Rougher shifts into 4th, 5th, 6th or reverse over time
Shift adaptation stops learning

P0970.t: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
P0970.d: Pressure control solenoid C circuit low, a short to ground in the driver. On GM's six-speeds C is the C456/CBR1 solenoid; on the Saab 9-4X 6T70 it is clutch pressure solenoid 3 for the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches. A short for 1 s (Saab) or 0.3 s (GM 2018 table) sets a Type A code: only reverse and 5th gear, no converter lock-up, maximum line pressure. GM's 8-speed uses C for clutch 3 (C13567), the 9- and 10-speeds for CB38 or C23457910 with less than 0.5 ohm counting as a short; GM's dual-clutch gearbox uses it for the odd-clutch shutdown valve. Siblings: P0968 open, P0971 high, P0969 performance. Since the solenoid sits in the valve body, repairs often mean the control solenoid valve assembly.
c: Internally shorted solenoid in the control solenoid valve assembly
Fluid or moisture in the connector
Faulty output stage in the control module
s: MIL on immediately
Limp mode in reverse and one forward gear
Weak acceleration from standstill

P0971.t: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit High
P0971.d: Pressure control solenoid C circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, as there is no separate open code there. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (clutch pressure solenoid 3, low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches) and GM's 2018 six-speed table set it after 1 s or 0.3 s as Type A, with limp mode in reverse and 5th gear at maximum line pressure. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use the code for their clutch solenoid C; GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the redundant odd-clutch shutdown valve, where too high a voltage at the sense pin with the output switched on counts as a short. Ford does not use C codes. Siblings: P0968 open, P0970 low, P0969 performance. A loose connector can make the fault come and go.
c: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Faulty output stage in the control module
s: MIL on, limp mode in a fixed gear
Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure
Fault comes and goes with temperature or vibration

P0972.t: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0972.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A: the circuit is not plainly shorted, yet its electrical behaviour does not fit what the module commands. Today's large makers rarely use the code. GM's 2007 table for the Allison 1000 six-speed used it for an open SS1 circuit: after three hardware fault samples the module opens the low-side driver as an intrusive test and reports P0972 if four more samples show no short to ground (400 ms, Type A, MIL at once). Newer GM Allison tables move that open to P097A. Ferrari's DCT bulletin reuses P0972 for a missing signal from the actuator 1 engage position sensor, not a solenoid. Ford and GM six-speeds report opens elsewhere. Shorts are P0973/P0974.
c: Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid A (Allison-type usage)
Loose or corroded terminal at the transmission connector or internal harness
Chafed or broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Transmission falls back to a fixed default gear
Missing or abrupt shifts

P0973.t: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
P0973.d: Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A, usually a short to ground. Ford lists it as SSA short to ground beside P0750 (open) for the 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140, checked by a driver feedback line within 0.5 to 5 s. GM six-speeds (6L/6T) call SS A the mode 2 solenoid and set P0973 after 1.2 of 1.5 s, MIL after one trip. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 needs 2 s, Type A, then only reverse and 5th remain. GM's 2016 Allison 1000 table folds ground short (0.42 ohm or less) and open (200 kOhm or more) into this code over 10 counts. Saab's Aisin gearbox in the 9-5 (2010) maps it to shift solenoid valve 2. High side is P0974.
c: Control wire to solenoid A chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid A or the control solenoid assembly
Fluid or metal debris bridging pins at the transmission connector
Faulty low-side driver in the transmission or powertrain module
s: MIL on after the first faulty trip on many vehicles
Limp mode with only a few gears, often reverse plus one forward gear
Harsh engagements due to maximum line pressure
Torque converter lockup and manual shifting disabled

P0974.t: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit High
P0974.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A. What it covers depends on the maker. Ford reserves it for a short to power on SSA, because an open SSA circuit sets P0750. GM six-speeds put both an open and a power short of the mode 2 solenoid here: 1.2 of 1.5 s, MIL only after two trips. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 waits 2 s, Type B, and then blocks 1st gear. GM's Allison 1000 tables of 2016 and 2023 treat it as a pure power short (0.39 ohm or less, 3 samples, 75 or 60 ms) and report opens separately. Saab's Aisin gearbox in the 9-5 (2010) sets it when solenoid valve 2 reads off while commanded on, 100 ms five times, Type A. Ground-side faults are P0973.
c: Open coil or broken wire where the maker reports opens under the high code (GM six-speed)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Spread or corroded pins at the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module
s: MIL on, on GM six-speeds only after a second faulty trip
First gear locked out, start-off in a higher gear
Missing or wrong shifts, possibly limp mode

P0975.t: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0975.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Three documented uses differ widely. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS2 circuit, confirmed by an intrusive low-side test (400 ms, Type A). FCA's 2016 recall for the 9-speed front-drive transaxle (Cherokee, 200, Renegade, 500X, ProMaster City) names P0975 with P0978, P0981 and P0984 as the codes set by intermittent high resistance from poorly crimped terminals in the range sensor harness under old TCM software; updated software reports that case as P0901 instead. Ferrari's DCT uses P0975 for a missing actuator 2 position signal. Low/high are P0976/P0977.
c: Poorly crimped terminals causing intermittent high resistance (FCA 9-speed recall)
Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid B
Outdated transmission software that misreads harness resistance
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Unexpected shift to neutral or loss of drive (FCA 9-speed)
Fixed default gear or harsh shifts

P0976.t: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Low
P0976.d: Low-voltage fault, normally a ground short, in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. On GM six-speeds SS B is the mode 3 multiplex valve; the 2016 table sets P0976 after 1.2 of 1.5 s without lighting the MIL, while the Saab 9-4X 6T70 version needs 2 s, is Type B and raises line pressure. Ford uses it for SSB short to ground, with P0755 for an open; on the 2023 Super Duty diesel SSB is fed by solenoid supply TSPC2, so a P2669 supply fault disables this check. GM's Allison 1000 merges ground short and open into it in 2016, but from 2022 reports opens as P097B and keeps P0976 for ground faults found by an intrusive test (120 ms, MIL after one trip). High side is P0977.
c: Solenoid B control wire shorted to ground or housing
Internal short in solenoid B or its valve body assembly
Moisture or debris bridging pins at the connector
Faulty driver in the transmission control module
s: Warning light or stored code, on some GM six-speeds without MIL
Firm shifts due to raised line pressure
Gears missing or limp mode

P0977.t: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit High
P0977.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. GM six-speeds put an open or a power short of the mode 3 multiplex valve here, 1.2 of 1.5 s; the 2016 table sets it without MIL, the 2019 table with MIL after one trip. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 treats it more severely than P0976: 2 s, Type A, high-side driver off, only reverse and 5th gear left, no converter lockup. Ford uses it strictly for SSB short to power, as in its 2012 and later summaries. GM's Allison 1000 checks for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three samples (75 ms in 2016, 60 ms in 2023). FCA 9-speed and Aisin uses are not documented for this code. Ground-side faults are P0976.
c: Open solenoid B coil or wire on GM six-speeds, where opens report as high
Control wire shorted to battery or a switched supply
Damaged pins or seals at the transmission pass-through connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module
s: Limp mode with only reverse and one high forward gear
Weak acceleration from rest
MIL or transmission warning, depending on calibration

P0978.t: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0978.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS3 circuit, but only while the commanded gear is not reverse trim, 5th or 6th; the table even prints the label Circuit Low beside an open-circuit test, an apparent typo. FCA lists P0978 among the four codes that the 2014–2016 9-speed transaxle set under old software when the range sensor harness had poor crimps. Ferrari's DCT bulletin uses it for a missing signal from the actuator 4 engage position sensor. Ford and GM six-speeds do not use it. Low/high are P0979/P0980, the current open code P097C.
c: Intermittent high resistance at crimped harness terminals (FCA 9-speed)
Open coil of shift solenoid C (Allison-type usage)
Transmission software that predates the manufacturer's fix
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Sudden neutral or default gear while driving
Erratic or missing shifts

P0979.t: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
P0979.d: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid C. GM uses it mainly on the Allison 1000 six-speed of its heavy pickups and chassis cabs: in 2016 a ground short of 0.22 ohm or less, stricter than the 0.42 ohm for SS1 and SS2, or an open of 200 kOhm or more counts after 10 samples (250 ms, Type A). From 2022 the open moves to P097C and P0979 needs an intrusive low-side test (120 ms, MIL after one trip). The Allison PS3 pressure switch test (P0872) also points to P0979 when its fault is electrical. Ford uses it for SSC short to ground beside P0760 open; on 6R80 and 6F, SSC drives the CB26 clutch. High side is P0980.
c: Solenoid C control wire shorted to ground
Internal short of solenoid C inside the valve body
Open coil on GM 2016 Allison calibrations, which report opens under this code
Faulty low-side driver in the control module
s: MIL on after the first faulty trip
Transmission holds a default gear
Rough or delayed shifts involving the affected clutch

P097A.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A, a code that later J2012 editions added; older lists still show P097A as reserved. GM is the only maker found that documents it: the 2022 to 2025 tables for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its heavy-duty trucks call it Shift Solenoid 1 Control Circuit Open. After one hardware fault the module flags pending, and after three samples it opens the low-side driver as a test; three more open readings at 9 to 18 V set the code (120 ms, MIL after one trip). The same gearbox once used P0972 for this and P0973 in 2016. Ford reports an open SSA as P0750, GM six-speeds as P0974, and Genesis folds all electrical faults of A into P0753.
c: Unplugged, corroded or pushed-out pin at the transmission connector
Broken wire in the internal or external transmission harness
Faulty low-side driver in the control module
s: MIL on after one faulty trip
Transmission in a fixed default gear
Shifts involving solenoid A missing

P097B.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Public use is again limited to GM's Allison 1000 six-speed in heavy-duty trucks, where the 2022 to 2025 tables label it Shift Solenoid 2 Control Circuit Open. SS2 shares high-side driver 2 with SS1 and SS3, so the open test only runs while that supply is on and free of P2669, P2670 or P2671. It confirms an open by switching the low-side driver off and needs three samples, 120 ms, MIL after one trip. Allison's 2007 table filed the same check as P0975, the 2016 table under P0976. Ford reports an open SSB as P0755, GM six-speeds as P0977. Low/high are P0976/P0977.
c: Loose or corroded terminal on the solenoid B circuit
Wire broken by vibration or heat near the transmission
Faulty driver stage in the control module
s: MIL on after one faulty trip
Default gear operation, some ranges unavailable
Harsh or missing shifts

P097C.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its 2022 to 2025 heavy-duty tables as Shift Solenoid 3 Control Circuit Open, with the same intrusive low-side test as SS1 and SS2: three samples, 120 ms, battery 9 to 18 V, MIL after one trip. It is the youngest of three codes for this one fault on that gearbox: 2007 used P0978, only outside reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear, 2016 merged it into P0979 with a 200 kOhm limit. Ford reports an open SSC under P0760, and no other maker was found using P097C. A related pressure switch code may set too, because SS3 strokes the S3 valve that switch PS3 watches.
c: Loose, wet or corroded pin in the transmission connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid C
Faulty low-side driver in the control module
s: MIL on after one faulty trip
Upper gears unavailable or fixed default gear
Possible additional pressure switch code

P097D.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. No maker documents this code publicly. GM's Allison tables that use P097A to P097C stop at shift solenoid 3, and Ford, which has a solenoid D in its 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140 gearboxes, reports an open SSD under the base code P0765, with P0982/P0983 for ground and power shorts. Any use would follow the CARB rule that every transmission output must be checked for lack of circuit continuity, plus the pattern of the A to C codes: a high-impedance reading confirmed by switching the driver. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F, SSD feeds either CBLR or C456 through a multiplex valve, so an open there would disturb first and upper gears alike.
c: Open coil of shift solenoid D
Disconnected or corroded terminal in the solenoid D circuit
Broken wire in the transmission harness
Faulty driver in the control module
s: Warning light or MIL on
Missing gears that depend on solenoid D
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P097E.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. No manufacturer was found that documents this code. Ford, the main user of an SSE, still reports an open SSE under P0770; its 2023 diesel summary pairs that with P0985 for ground and P0986 for power shorts, and powers SSE from supply TSPC1 together with SSA and SSC. In the 6R80 and 6F, SSE is an on/off solenoid that switches the multiplexing of SSD, while the 6R140 uses a variable force SSE for clutch C456. Without a public owner the code rests on the CARB demand for circuit continuity checks on transmission outputs and on GM's A to C pattern. Opens in shared supply wiring usually set P0657 first.
c: Open coil of shift solenoid E
Poor contact at the solenoid E terminal or lead frame
Broken signal wire to solenoid E
Faulty driver stage in the control module
s: Warning light or MIL on
Gears using solenoid E unavailable
Default gear operation

P097F.d: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid F. It is the only code in its family for letter F, since J2012 has no range/performance, low or high codes for F in this block. No maker was found to document it. Hyundai's Genesis bulletin for the eight-speed (2017–2018 G80 and G90) shows how F is handled in practice: an electrical fault of shift control solenoid F (labelled 8LR) is reported under P2709 and fixed by replacing the solenoid. Other makers with six or more clutches use their own codes. A P097F would follow the CARB requirement to test every transmission output for circuit continuity, by analogy with GM's open tests for solenoids 1 to 3.
c: Open coil of shift solenoid F
Loose or corroded terminal at the valve body connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid F
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
s: Warning light or MIL on
Gears that need solenoid F unavailable
Limp mode

P0980.t: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit High
P0980.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid C, meaning a short to supply. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed: the 2007 table wants four consecutive power-short samples (100 ms, Type A) and skips the check in reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear; later tables (2016, 2018) look for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three counts within 75 ms, and from 2022 within 60 ms, MIL after one trip. Ford uses it for SSC short to power in all its listed gearboxes, with P0760 for an open. Neither GM's 6L/6T six-speeds nor Saab's documented gearboxes use P0980. The ground counterpart is P0979, the open code for the Allison is P097C.
c: Solenoid C control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Shorted turns in solenoid C lowering its resistance
Adjacent pins bridged by fluid or debris in the connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module
s: MIL on after the first faulty trip
Solenoid C stuck energized, wrong gear or default gear
Harsh shifts

P0981.t: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0981.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. GM's Allison tables end at solenoid C, and Ford checks SSD only with P0765, P0982 and P0983, so the large North American users skip it. Two codegenau sources exist. FCA's recall S55 (NHTSA 16V-529) covers about 323,400 vehicles with the 9-speed front-drive transaxle; with old TCM software, intermittent high resistance from weak crimps in the range sensor harness could set P0981 or its siblings, and the remedy is new software plus, if a code is present, a new harness. Ferrari's DCT bulletin uses P0981 for a missing signal from the actuator 3 position sensor. Low/high for D are P0982/P0983.
c: Weak terminal crimps causing intermittent resistance (FCA recall S55)
Transmission software not yet updated by the recall
Solenoid D coil resistance out of range
Faulty driver stage in the control module
s: Unexpected shift to neutral while driving (FCA 9-speed)
MIL or transmission warning on
Default gear or harsh shifts

P0982.t: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Low
P0982.d: Low-voltage fault, in practice a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford is the documented user: its summaries list SSD with P0765 open, P0982 short to ground and P0983 short to power, checked continuously through the driver feedback within 0.5 to 5 s. Which clutch this hits depends on the gearbox. In the 6R80 and 6F, SSD is a variable force solenoid feeding CBLR or C456 via the SSE multiplex valve; in the 6R140 it drives CBLR alone. In the 2023 diesel summary SSD is fed from supply TSPC2 with SSB, the converter clutch and line pressure solenoid. GM's six-speed and Allison tables do not use P0982. Ferrari reuses it for an actuator 3 sensor reading too low.
c: Solenoid D control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid D or the main control assembly
Damaged internal lead frame or connector inside the transmission
Faulty driver in the powertrain or transmission module
s: MIL on and default gear operation
No engine braking in first or no reverse, depending on gearbox
Harsh shifts into upper gears

P0983.t: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit High
P0983.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford defines it narrowly as SSD short to power; the open circuit stays with P0765. On the 6R140 the solenoid outputs are run by a smart driver chip (ADLER) that does the open and short checks itself, while older units use a feedback line from the output stage; both need 0.5 to 5 s. Since SSD on Ford six-speeds controls the low/reverse clutch, either alone or through the multiplex valve, a constant power short can apply that clutch at the wrong time. The 2020–2023 gasoline summary keeps the same assignment. GM documents no P0983 for its geared automatics, and Ferrari uses it for an actuator 3 sensor reading too high. Ground faults are P0982.
c: Solenoid D control wire shorted to a supply
Faulty smart driver or output stage in the module
s: MIL on, default gear
Clunk or tie-up feel if the low/reverse clutch applies unintentionally
Upper gears blocked

P0984.t: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0984.d: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford checks SSE with P0770, P0985 and P0986 only, GM's documented tables never reach letter E, and even Ferrari's DCT list, which reuses most of its neighbours, skips P0984. The one codegenau source is FCA: in recall S55 for the 9-speed front-drive transaxle it names P0984 together with P0975, P0978 and P0981. Under old TCM software, a range sensor harness with poor crimps and intermittent high resistance could set them; with new software the same fault shows as P0901, and these four codes then point to a separate transmission problem. Otherwise the code rests only on the CARB rule for transmission output checks. Low/high are P0985/P0986.
c: Range sensor harness with weak crimps (FCA 9-speed recall)
TCM software below the recall level
Internal transmission fault when the code returns after the update
Faulty driver stage in the control module
s: Sudden neutral or loss of drive (FCA 9-speed)
MIL or transmission warning on
Limp mode

P0985.t: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Low
P0985.d: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford lists it for SSE on the 5R110W and 6R140 and in its 2020–2023 gasoline and 2023 diesel summaries, beside P0770 for an open; for the 6R80 and 6F, whose SSE is the on/off multiplex solenoid, the 2012 text names only P0770. Saab's 2010 9-5 with the Aisin six-speed uses P0985 differently, for shift solenoid valve 1: the module sees the circuit reading on while it is commanded off, 100 ms five times in a row, Type A; it then turns all solenoids off and freezes adaptation. Voltage must be 10.2 to 15.5 V and the engine above 400 rpm. High side is P0986.
c: Solenoid E control wire shorted to ground
Water or fluid in the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the transmission module
s: MIL on after the fault is confirmed
All solenoids off, fixed fail-safe gear (Saab/Aisin)
Missing upper gears on Ford gearboxes

P0986.t: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit High
P0986.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford means a short to power on SSE; an open sets P0770 and a ground short P0985. On the 6R140 SSE is a variable force solenoid for the C456 clutch, so a short to power can hold that clutch on. Saab's 2010 9-5 with the Aisin six-speed instead assigns P0986 to shift solenoid valve 1 and sets it when the circuit reads off although it is commanded on, which also catches an open coil: 100 ms, five times, Type A, all solenoids then switched off. GM's published transmission tables do not use the code. Because makers split opens differently, check the maker's table before replacing parts.
c: Solenoid E control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open coil or wire where the maker reads it as high (Saab/Aisin)
Bent or corroded terminals at the solenoid E connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module
s: MIL on, transmission in fail-safe gear
Tie-up or harsh shift if the controlled clutch stays applied
Adaptation frozen, shift quality worsens

P0987.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit
P0987.d: General circuit fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The only public user of switch E found, GM's 6T70/6T75 family (Saab 9-4X: switch 5 on the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutch regulator valve), reports only P0989 and P0990 for it, both as plausibility counts. P0987 is the slot for a module that sees a generic circuit fault on a fifth pressure sensor or switch, for example an open or out-of-range signal, without separating low from high. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs. Range/performance is P0988, low and high are P0989/P0990; switches A to D use P0840 to P0878. Typical effects are frozen shift adaptations and harsher shifts.
c: Failed pressure sensor or switch E
Open or shorted signal wire or poor connector contact
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: Warning light depending on manufacturer
Harsher or less consistent shifts
Possible limp mode

P0988.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Range/Performance
P0988.d: Range/performance fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the commanded clutch state or the pressure expected from other inputs. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's 6T70/6T75 family, the one public user of switch E (switch 5 on the low/reverse and 4-5-6 regulator valve), folds such plausibility checks into P0989 and P0990; its switch logic table shows which gears should pressurise the switch. Sonnax describes how these normally closed film switches in the valve body module fail through debris or delaminated films. CARB requires rationality checks of transmission inputs. Siblings: P0987 circuit, P0989 low, P0990 high.
c: Damaged or delaminated switch film, switch reacts late or not at all
Debris in the fluid holding the switch or its regulator valve
Low fluid level or real pressure deviation in the clutch circuit
s: Often no noticeable symptom at first
Shift quality worsens because adaptation stops
Warning light depending on manufacturer

P0989.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
P0989.d: Pressure switch E reads low, meaning no pressure, when it should show pressure. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; the normally closed switch sees pressure while both the low/reverse and the 4-5-6 clutch are released. The module counts clutch releases after which the signal stays low, checked with commanded clutch pressure at 50 kPa or less: 18 counts in GM's 2011 tables and on the Saab 9-4X, 17 in the 2016 table. It is a Type C or Special No Trip code without MIL, and the adaptations of both clutches are frozen. Sonnax lists P0989 among typical switch failures in this valve body module. P0990 is the stuck-high counterpart; switches A to D use P0840 to P0878.
c: Damaged or delaminated film in switch 5 of the valve body module
Debris keeping pressure away from the switch
s: No warning light, code stored only
Shifts into 4th to 6th or reverse gradually less smooth
Occasional limp mode if the fault persists

P0990.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit High
P0990.d: Pressure switch E reads high, meaning pressure, when it should be vented. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; applying the low/reverse or 4-5-6 clutch moves that valve and should exhaust the switch. If the signal stays high after such an apply, with commanded clutch pressure at 700 kPa or more, the module counts it: 15 counts on the Saab 9-4X, 30 in GM's 2016 table. It is a Type C or Special No Trip code, so no MIL, and the adaptations of both clutches are frozen. According to Saab, normal debris in the fluid can set it intermittently without noticeable symptoms. A short to voltage on the signal wire has the same effect. P0989 is the stuck-low case.
c: Switch 5 stuck open by a damaged film or debris
R1/4-5-6 regulator valve not moving, switch stays pressurised
Signal circuit shorted to voltage or open inside the module
s: No warning light, code stored only
Intermittent occurrence without noticeable symptoms
Shift quality declines over time

P0991.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Intermittent
P0991.d: The module has seen the signal of the fifth transmission pressure sensor or switch drop out or jump briefly, without a steady low or high reading. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The only switch E found in public sources is GM's TFP switch 5 in the 6T70/6T75 valve body module (Saab 9-4X 2011), a normally closed switch that GM monitors only through P0989 and P0990: signal stuck low at commanded pressure of 50 kPa or less, or stuck high, counted over clutch releases and logged as Special No Trip without MIL. An intermittent check would follow the CARB rule that transmission inputs be monitored for circuit faults. Steady faults are P0987 to P0990. Expect frozen shift adaptation and the odd harsh shift.
c: Loose or corroded contact at the valve body module connector
Debris or damaged diaphragm film making the switch contact flicker
Chafed internal harness that shorts or opens under vibration
Fault in the transmission control module input stage
s: Stored fault, often without warning light
Occasional harsh or flared shift
Shift adaptation frozen

P0992.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit
P0992.d: General circuit fault of a sixth transmission pressure sensor or switch, labelled F. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no gearbox with a switch F was found. GM's six-speeds stop at TFP switch 5 (letter E, P0989/P0990), and Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed monitors its 2-6 brake, high clutch and low-reverse brake switches under P0846, P0876 and P0988, which are letters B, D and E. Pressure switches like these sit in the valve body module and tell the module which clutch is applied; Sonnax describes them as normally closed film-and-piston switches. P0992 would be the code for an open or implausible circuit without a low/high split, as CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs. Range/performance, low, high and intermittent are P0993 to P0996.
c: Open or damaged signal wire or connector to the switch
Pressure switch or sensor failed inside the valve body module
s: Warning light depending on manufacturer calibration
Harsh or delayed shifts
Possible limp mode with a fixed gear

P0993.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Range/Performance
P0993.d: Pressure sensor or switch F is electrically intact, but its reading does not match what the module expects from the commanded clutch state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest documented logic is GM's for switch E (TFP switch 5, 6T70/6T75): the module checks after each clutch release whether the switch returns to its exhausted state and counts failures, at 50 kPa or less commanded pressure for the low case. A sixth switch would be checked the same way, plausibility against commanded pressure and gear, which CARB requires for transmission inputs. Typical causes are sticking regulator valves, debris and worn switch films rather than wiring. P0992 is the plain circuit fault, P0994/P0995 are low and high.
c: Sticking clutch regulator valve feeding the switch
Worn or delaminated switch film, debris in the switch
s: Harsh or flared shifts
Shift adaptation frozen
Warning light depending on calibration

P0994.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Low
P0994.d: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F stays low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. With a normally closed switch as described by Sonnax for GM's valve body modules, low means the contacts stay closed, so the module sees no pressure where pressure should be, or the signal wire is shorted to ground. GM's equivalent for switch E, P0989, flags a low signal when commanded pressure is 50 kPa or less and handles it as Special No Trip without MIL; Saab's 9-4X text gives 0 V as the low state and 12 V as high. For an analogue sensor, low would mean a voltage below its valid range. CARB requires such out-of-range checks on transmission inputs. P0995 is the high counterpart.
c: Switch stuck closed by debris or damaged film
Clutch circuit not reaching pressure (valve or seal leak)
s: Harsh or delayed shifts
Shift adaptation frozen
Possible limp mode

P0995.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit High
P0995.d: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F stays high: with a normally closed switch the contacts stay open, which looks like permanent pressure, or the wire is open or shorted to voltage. No manufacturer documents this use publicly. Hyundai/Genesis bulletins 17-AT-001-G and 21-AT-016HG list P0995 in their subject lines, but their tables pair it with Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit (SBC), and 21-AT-016HG prints the DTC as P095500; this is a misprint for P0955 and does not count as a use of P0995. GM's matching switch E code P0990 is a Special No Trip without MIL; Saab's 9-4X text treats an open and a short to voltage alike as high. CARB requires such checks on transmission inputs. P0994 is the low side.
c: Open signal wire or unplugged connector
Switch stuck open inside the valve body module
s: Harsh or delayed shifts
Shift adaptation frozen
Possible limp mode

P0996.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Intermittent
P0996.d: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F drops out or flickers for short moments without staying low or high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no transmission with a sixth pressure switch was found: GM's six-speeds end at switch 5 (E), Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed uses letters B, D and E. Because such switches are thin film-and-piston units inside the valve body module, as Sonnax shows, debris or a delaminated film can make the contact chatter, and connector or harness faults do the same electrically. CARB requires transmission inputs to be checked for circuit faults; an intermittent code is the slot for faults too short to set P0994 or P0995. Expect occasional rough shifts, often without a warning light.
c: Debris or delaminated film making the switch chatter
Chafed harness shorting or opening under vibration
s: Stored fault, often without warning light
Occasional rough or flared shift

P0997.t: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0997.d: The drive circuit of shift solenoid F works electrically but its measured current or voltage does not fit the command. No manufacturer was found to document this code. The users of the F block, Nissan's RE0F11A CVT and a 2019 Mitsubishi six-speed, list only P0998 and P0999. FCA's nine-speed bulletin 21-019-17 (2015 Chrysler 200 and Jeep Cherokee) shows how the slot is used for solenoids 2 to 5, with P0975, P0978, P0981 and P0984 for control circuit performance, but stops before a sixth solenoid. Genesis reports an electrical fault of its solenoid F under P2709 instead. CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for proper function. P097F is the open circuit, P0998/P0999 low and high.
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module
s: Warning light depending on calibration
Missing or harsh shifts into gears using this solenoid
Possible limp mode

P0998.t: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit Low
P0998.d: Low-voltage fault, typically a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid F. Two makers document it. Nissan lists P0998 as shift solenoid F in bulletin NTB15-037 for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT, whose two-speed auxiliary gearbox uses a low brake, a high clutch and a reverse brake; if the shop manual check points to the transaxle, the bulletin has only the control valve replaced. Mitsubishi's 2019 service manual for a six-speed automatic names P0998/P0999 the low clutch shift solenoid valve system and counts it among faults that can cause gear ratio errors. CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for circuit faults. P0999 is high, P097F open.
c: Solenoid or valve body (control valve) internal fault
Control wire shorted to ground in harness or connector
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or loss of a gear range
Harsh engagement or flare when shifting

P0999.t: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit High
P0999.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid F, from a short to voltage or, where the driver uses a pull-up, an open coil or wire. Nissan's bulletin NTB15-037 for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT names P0999 together with P0998 as shift solenoid F and calls for replacing the control valve rather than the whole CVT when diagnosis confirms the fault. Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed assigns P0998/P0999 to the low clutch shift solenoid; for its sister valve G it detects an open circuit as a high reading. Other makers handle F elsewhere: Genesis under P2709, Ford's summaries stop at solenoid E. CARB requires output circuit checks. P0998 is the low side.
c: Open solenoid coil inside the valve body
Open control wire or short to voltage
Connector pin pushed out or corroded
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or loss of a gear range
Harsh shifts

P099A.t: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit Range/Performance
P099A.d: The drive circuit of shift solenoid G is electrically intact, but current or voltage feedback does not fit the command. No manufacturer was found to document this code. The two documented users of the G control circuit codes report only the hard faults: Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed (low-reverse brake shift solenoid) uses P099B for a short and P099C for an open, and Nissan's RE0F11A CVT lists P099B/P099C. Hyundai and Genesis report their on/off solenoid G under P075A and P075D. The slot would follow the pattern FCA uses for solenoids 2 to 5 (P0975 to P0984, control circuit performance). CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for function. Low and high are P099B/P099C, open P09A0.
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module
s: Warning light depending on calibration
Harsh or missing shifts involving this solenoid
Possible limp mode

P099B.t: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit Low
P099B.d: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid G. Mitsubishi's 2019 service manual for a six-speed automatic uses it for the low-reverse brake shift solenoid: with transmission relay voltage at 2 V or more and the solenoid commanded on, the module sets P099B if the actual voltage stays below 3.7 V for 0.5 s. The check runs continuously; the solenoid is normally energised only in reverse and first-gear coasting. Nissan lists P099B as shift solenoid G in bulletin NTB15-037 for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT and replaces the control valve when diagnosis confirms it. P099C is the high side, P09A0 the generic open.
c: Control wire shorted to ground in harness or connector
Shorted solenoid inside the valve body
s: Check engine light
No reverse or no engine braking in first gear (Mitsubishi)
Limp mode

P099C.t: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit High
P099C.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid G. Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed uses P099C for an open circuit of the low-reverse brake shift solenoid: with the solenoid commanded off and transmission relay voltage of 2 V or more, a reading of 3.7 V or more for 0.5 s sets the code. So on this design an open shows up as high, not under P09A0. The drive cycle needs only 10 s with the ignition on. Causes named are the harness, connectors, the TCM and the solenoid in the valve body. Nissan lists P099C as shift solenoid G for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT, with control valve replacement as the fix. P099B is the low side, P099A performance.
c: Open control wire or connector between module and valve body
Open solenoid coil inside the valve body
s: Check engine light
No reverse or harsh reverse engagement (Mitsubishi)
Limp mode

P099D.t: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit Range/Performance
P099D.d: Electrical feedback from the drive circuit of shift solenoid H does not fit the command, although no hard short or open is seen. No manufacturer was found to document this code. Solenoid H means an eighth shift solenoid. The only documented H user, the 2017–2018 Genesis G80 and G90, reports its on/off solenoid for the shift-by-wire park function under P076A and P076D, outside this block. Ford's OBD summaries describe shift solenoid checks only up to E, with separate open, short to ground and short to power codes and 0.5 to 5 s electrical monitoring. CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for proper function. Low and high are P099E/P099F, the open circuit is P09A1.
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module
s: Warning light depending on calibration
Harsh or missing shifts involving this solenoid

P099E.t: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit Low
P099E.d: Low-voltage fault, typically a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid H. No manufacturer was found to document this code. A solenoid H exists only on transmissions with eight or more shift solenoids; Genesis' 2017–2018 G80/G90, the one documented H user, reports its park-function on/off solenoid under P076A and P076D. The closest documented logic is from lower letters: Mitsubishi detects a short on its solenoid G when the voltage stays below 3.7 V for 0.5 s while commanded on, and Ford's summaries store separate short-to-ground codes for solenoids A to E, checked continuously. CARB requires such circuit checks on transmission outputs. P099F is the high side, P09A1 the open circuit.
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P099F.t: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit High
P099F.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid H, from a short to voltage or, on pull-up driver designs, an open coil or wire. No manufacturer was found to document this code. Genesis' 2017–2018 G80/G90 shift-by-wire, the only documented H user, files its park-function on/off solenoid under P076A and P076D, and bulletin 21-AT-016HG fixes it by replacing valve and electronic module. For the high-side logic, Mitsubishi's six-speed is the nearest model: on solenoid G it treats 3.7 V or more for 0.5 s while commanded off as an open circuit. Ford's summaries give short to power its own code for each of solenoids A to E. CARB requires output circuit checks. P099E is the low side.
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P09A0.d: Open circuit or general circuit fault in the drive of shift solenoid G. It is a late addition to J2012: older code lists still show P09A0 to P09FF as reserved. No manufacturer was found to document it. The known users of the G block send opens elsewhere: Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed reports an open low-reverse brake shift solenoid as P099C, Nissan's RE0F11A CVT lists only P099B/P099C, and Hyundai/Genesis use P075A and P075D for their on/off solenoid G. Ford shows the usual split for solenoids A to E, with the open in the base code (P0750 and so on) and separate ground and power shorts. CARB requires every transmission output to be checked for circuit continuity. P099A to P099C are performance, low and high.
c: Broken control wire or unplugged connector
Pin backed out of the connector housing
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P09A1.d: Open circuit or general circuit fault in the drive of shift solenoid H, the eighth shift solenoid. Like P09A0 it is a late J2012 addition that older code lists still show as reserved. No manufacturer was found to document it. Genesis' 2017–2018 G80/G90, the only documented H user, reports its park-function on/off solenoid under P076A and P076D, and bulletin 21-AT-016HG has valve and electronic module replaced for those. Ford's summaries show what an open check looks like for solenoids A to E: a separate open code, run continuously with 0.5 to 5 s of electrical monitoring. CARB requires every transmission output to be checked for circuit continuity. P099D to P099F cover performance, low and high of solenoid H.
c: Broken control wire or unplugged connector
Pin backed out of the connector housing
s: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P09A2.d: General electrical fault on the second gate select position signal (circuit B) of an automated manual gearbox. The published designs from Isuzu (one select potentiometer) and Aisin AI (one select stroke sensor) show only a single sensor, so it is not documented whether B is a redundant second track of that sensor or a separate sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P09A4 and P09A5 are the more specific low and high faults of circuit B, P09A3 its plausibility fault; unlike circuit A (P0908) there is no intermittent variant. P0904 and P09A6 cover circuits A and C. Expect shifting to be restricted.
c: Loose, corroded or wet connector at the select sensor or actuator unit
Chafed or broken signal wire of circuit B near the gearbox
Faulty select sensor, often integrated in the shift and select actuator
Faulty input stage for circuit B in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox shifts slowly or locks out certain gears
Gearbox stays in one gear or neutral

P09A3.t: Gate Select Position Circuit B Range/Performance
P09A3.d: Plausibility fault of gate select circuit B: the signal is electrically valid but does not match what the module expects. That could be the reading of circuit A, the learned gate positions, or the target gate the module has commanded, as in the Aisin AI select control that compares actual and target gate. Which comparison applies depends on whether B is a redundant track or a separate sensor, and no manufacturer publishes that or uses this code in citable material. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P09A2, P09A4 and P09A5 are electrical faults of B, P0905 and P09A7 the same check on circuits A and C. A fallback mode with limited shifting is likely.
c: Worn or drifting select sensor, signal B no longer agrees with the reference
Gate positions not relearned after actuator, clutch or module replacement
Contact resistance at connector pins distorting signal B
Sluggish or worn select mechanism so the measured gate lags the commanded one
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gate selected or gears refused
Slow, jerky shifting in fallback mode

P09A4.t: Gate Select Position Circuit B Low
P09A4.d: Set when the gate select signal on circuit B stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Likely causes are a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or an internal sensor short; with potentiometer sensors like the select position sensor in an Isuzu patent, an open signal wire often reads low too. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, nor whether B is a second track or another sensor. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P09A5 is the opposite fault, P09A2 the general circuit fault, P0906 and P09A8 the low faults of circuits A and C. If A and B are both low, look for a shared supply or ground.
c: Signal wire of circuit B chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal short or broken wiper in the select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gear changes blocked or limited to a few gears
Transmission warning message in the instrument cluster

P09A5.t: Gate Select Position Circuit B High
P09A5.d: Indicates that the gate select signal on circuit B has stayed above its highest valid value for longer than allowed. Typical reasons are a short of the signal wire to the sensor supply or battery voltage, an open sensor ground, or a defective sensor. No manufacturer publishes how it uses this code or what circuit B physically is. An Aisin AI patent shows the consequence of losing select feedback: warning, request to stop, then a limp-home in first gear. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P09A4 is the low counterpart, P09A2 the general fault, P0907 and P09A9 the high faults of circuits A and C. A gearbox that can no longer confirm its gate restricts shifting.
c: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Limp-home mode with very limited gear choice

P09A6.d: Electrical fault on a third gate select position signal (circuit C) that fits none of the more specific C codes. Public AMT designs show far fewer channels: Aisin AI and Isuzu use one select sensor, and a Mannesmann Sachs patent combines motor encoders with an extra neutral position sensor. What a third channel is in practice remains open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P09A7 to P09A9 are the plausibility, low and high faults of C; as with circuit B there is no intermittent variant. P0904 and P09A2 cover circuits A and B. Gear changes may be limited.
c: Loose, corroded or wet connector at the select sensor or actuator unit
Damaged signal wire of circuit C in the gearbox harness
Faulty input stage for circuit C in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Delayed or missing gear changes
Vehicle reluctant to pull away

P09A7.t: Gate Select Position Circuit C Range/Performance
P09A7.d: Rationality fault on gate select circuit C: the value is electrically valid, yet it disagrees with the other select channels, the learned gate positions or the commanded movement. A Mannesmann Sachs patent shows why several select signals can exist: when one sensor fails, the remaining ones still allow controlled positioning before an emergency mode based on stored drive times takes over. No manufacturer documents this code or the role of circuit C publicly. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P09A6, P09A8 and P09A9 are electrical faults of C, P0905 and P09A3 the same check on A and B. The driver usually notices slower or restricted shifting.
c: Drifting or worn sensor so signal C disagrees with the other channels
Select positions not relearned after repair work on the actuator or gearbox
Loose sensor mounting or magnet shifting the measured position
Contact resistance in the connector of circuit C
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slower or hesitant gear changes
Some gears no longer offered

P09A8.t: Gate Select Position Circuit C Low
P09A8.d: The module stores this code when the gate select signal on circuit C remains below its valid range for a calibrated time. Common triggers are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or an internal sensor fault; depending on the sensor type, a broken signal wire can read low as well. No manufacturer documents this code publicly or explains what circuit C measures. Patents from Isuzu and Aisin AI show the select sensor as the feedback the module needs to line up the right gate. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P09A9 is the high counterpart, P09A6 the general C fault, P0906 and P09A4 the low faults of A and B.
c: Signal wire of circuit C shorted to ground
Sensor supply for circuit C missing or pulled down
Internal short in the sensor delivering signal C
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox holds one gear or drops to neutral
Transmission warning message in the instrument cluster

P09A9.t: Gate Select Position Circuit C High
P09A9.d: Logged when the gate select signal on circuit C sits above its highest plausible value for longer than a calibrated time. Usual suspects are a short to the sensor supply or battery voltage, an interrupted sensor ground, or a sensor with an internal fault. No manufacturer publicly documents this code, and the physical meaning of circuit C is not published either. An Aisin AI patent describes the fallback once select feedback is lost: warning, stop request and a limp-home in first gear. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P09A8 is the low counterpart, P09A6 the general C fault, P0907 and P09A5 the high faults of A and B. Shifting is usually curtailed.
c: Signal wire of circuit C shorted to supply or battery voltage
Internal fault of the sensor delivering signal C
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Limp-home mode, often in a single low gear
Gear changes refused while driving

P0A00.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0A00.d: General circuit fault on temperature sensor A in the separate coolant loop that cools the inverter and other drive electronics of a hybrid or electric vehicle. The module flags it when the sensor signal cannot be used at all, without a more specific low, high or plausibility verdict; those cases have their own codes P0A01 to P0A04. No manufacturer documents P0A00 publicly. GM's Two-Mode hybrid trucks monitor the same sensor only through P0A01 to P0A03, and CARB requires every input of the inverter thermal management to be checked for circuit faults. Without a valid reading the control unit usually limits electric drive power to protect the electronics.
c: Corroded or loose connector at the sensor in the inverter coolant loop
Damaged signal or reference wire between sensor and hybrid control module
Fault in the input stage of the hybrid or inverter control module
s: Hybrid system or check engine warning light
Reduced electric drive power
Inverter coolant pump or radiator fan running constantly as a precaution

P0A01.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0A01.d: The sensor delivers a value inside its electrical range, but it does not fit the other temperatures in the vehicle. GM uses this code on the 2013 Two-Mode hybrid Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra as a cold-start test: after the vehicle has stood for more than 28,800 s (8 h), the power electronics coolant temperature at power-up may differ from engine coolant temperature by no more than 30 °C, provided engine coolant and intake air agree within 15.75 °C. A failure is a Type B code with MIL after two trips. Nissan describes a similar comparison between inverter coolant and power element temperatures. Hard electrical faults are P0A02 and P0A03.
c: Sensor characteristic drifted, reading offset against the other temperature sensors
Added resistance at a corroded connector shifting the reading
Low coolant or air pocket at the sensor in the electronics loop
Fault actually in the engine coolant or intake air sensor used for comparison
s: Check engine light after two trips
Often no noticeable change in driving behaviour
Electric drive power limited when the electronics are hot

P0A02.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0A02.d: The signal voltage of the coolant temperature sensor in the electronics loop sits below its valid window. Because the sensor is an NTC thermistor, a low voltage means an implausibly hot reading, typically a short to ground. GM uses P0A02 on the 2013 Two-Mode hybrid Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra: the converted temperature reaches the 162.1 °C limit in 30 of 50 samples taken every 100 ms, after more than 10 s of propulsion active and with no intake air sensor fault (P0112, P0113) present. It is a Type B code with MIL after two trips. The opposite fault is P0A03. Expect a warning light and possibly reduced electric power.
c: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Moisture or coolant in the connector bridging signal to ground
s: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Displayed electronics temperature extremely high although the system is cool
Cooling fans and pump running at full output, drive power limited

P0A03.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0A03.d: The sensor signal voltage is above its valid window, which for an NTC thermistor reads as an impossibly cold coolant temperature. Typical reasons are an open circuit in the sensor or its wiring, or a short to a voltage source. GM monitors this on the 2013 Two-Mode hybrid Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra with a limit of -59.1 °C, counted as 30 failures in 50 samples at 100 ms intervals once propulsion has been active for over 10 s and the intake air sensor codes P0112 and P0113 are clear; Type B, MIL after two trips. P0A02 covers the reverse case. Because the system cannot see real heat any more, it often reduces electric power as a precaution.
c: Connector unplugged, loose or with a pushed-back terminal
Broken signal or ground wire of the sensor
Signal wire shorted to a voltage supply
s: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Electronics temperature shown far below ambient
Reduced electric drive power as a safeguard

P0A04.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0A04.d: The temperature signal from the drive electronics coolant loop jumps or drops out for short moments, then returns to normal. Coolant temperature changes slowly, so a sudden step that the physics cannot explain points to a loose contact rather than a real temperature change. No manufacturer documents P0A04 publicly. GM's Two-Mode hybrids check the same sensor only for steady faults (P0A01 to P0A03), and a Nissan patent shows how an inverter coolant sensor is compared with the power element temperature to catch implausible readings. CARB requires such inverter cooling inputs to be monitored. The driver may see a warning light that comes and goes, with occasional power reduction.
c: Loose or fretting terminal at the sensor or module connector
Partly broken wire that opens under vibration or heat
Sensor with an internal intermittent contact
s: Warning light that appears and disappears
Short, unexplained drops in electric drive power
Stored code with no steady fault on re-test

P0A05.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P0A05.d: The electric pump that circulates coolant through the inverter, converter and drive motor loop is driven by a control line from the hybrid module. P0A05 means that line shows an open circuit or a fault the driver cannot classify further. No manufacturer documents P0A05 publicly. GM's Chevrolet Volt tables cover the same pump under P0CE9, set when the control line is open or shorted in 16 of 20 samples at 250 ms, Type B with MIL after two trips. CARB requires inverter cooling outputs to be checked, and Toyota patents describe how pump faults are told apart from other cooling faults. Low and high faults are P0A06 and P0A07; pump B is P0B38. Without circulation the electronics heat up quickly and power is cut.
c: Pump connector loose or corroded, often from road splash at the low-mounted pump
Broken control wire between module and pump
Failed electronics or open winding inside the pump
Blown pump fuse or missing supply, so the control input sees no load
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Electric drive power reduced, especially in warm weather or under load
Follow-up inverter overtemperature codes such as P0A93

P0A06.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Low
P0A06.d: The control line of pump A in the drive electronics coolant loop sits at a voltage below what the module expects for the commanded state, usually because the line or the pump input is shorted to ground. Depending on the driver design, the pump then runs uncontrolled or not at all. No manufacturer documents P0A06 publicly; GM's Volt reports a short of the comparable pump control line under P0CE9 (16 of 20 samples at 250 ms, Type B). CARB requires circuit checks of inverter cooling outputs, and Toyota patents show why a failed pump must be separated from radiator or fan faults. P0A05 is the open case, P0A07 the short to voltage. A failing pump soon leads to power reduction.
c: Control wire chafed against the body and shorted to ground
Internal short at the pump's control input
Water or coolant in the pump connector
s: Hybrid system or check engine light
Electronics temperature rising quickly, power limited
Pump silent when commanded on, or running continuously

P0A07.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Control Circuit High
P0A07.d: The module measures a voltage on the pump A control line that is higher than the commanded state allows, typically because the line touches a supply wire or the pump input has failed internally. The pump in the inverter and motor cooling loop may then be stuck on or never receive a valid command. No manufacturer documents P0A07 publicly. GM's Volt flags a short to voltage on its equivalent pump line as P0CE9, with 16 failures in 20 samples at 250 ms and a two-trip MIL. CARB requires inverter cooling outputs to be monitored for such circuit faults; Toyota patents describe pump speed and coolant flow checks for the same loop. P0A05 and P0A06 cover open and short to ground.
c: Control wire shorted to a battery or ignition supply wire
Pump control electronics failed, pulling the input high
Output driver in the control module damaged
s: Hybrid system or check engine light
Pump running all the time, even with the vehicle off
Possible power limitation if cooling cannot be confirmed

P0A08.d: General fault on the status line through which the DC/DC converter reports its condition to the hybrid control module. The converter replaces the alternator: it steps the traction battery voltage down to charge the 12 V battery. When its self-diagnosis detects an internal problem it signals this back, and the controller reacts. P0A08 is the broad verdict for an unusable or implausible status signal; a signal stuck low or high has its own codes P0A09 and P0A10. No manufacturer documents P0A08 publicly in an official source. Toyota's Prius c recall shows the consequence of a dead converter: warning lights, then a draining 12 V battery that can shut the hybrid system down. Drivers should not keep driving for long.
c: Internal fault in the DC/DC converter reported by its self-diagnosis
Damaged or corroded status line or connector between converter and hybrid control module
Converter overheating due to a fault in the inverter/converter coolant loop
Faulty input stage in the hybrid control module
s: Hybrid system, battery or master warning light on
12 V battery is no longer charged and voltage drops while driving
Electrical consumers fail and the hybrid system may finally shut down

P0A09.d: The status signal that the DC/DC converter sends to the hybrid control module stays below its expected range, typically from a short to ground, an open line read as low, or a converter that pulls its status output down because of an internal fault. Mitsubishi uses P0A09 on the 2012-2013 i-MiEV for a DC-DC converter fault; its bulletins tie it to a failed on-board charger that blows the high-voltage fuse feeding the converter, after which the 12 V battery and drive battery stop charging. That usage predates the current split into P0A08, P0A09 and P0A10. Siblings: P0A08 covers the general circuit fault, P0A10 a signal stuck high. Expect warning lights and a 12 V battery that slowly runs flat.
c: Blown high-voltage fuse feeding the converter, e.g. after an on-board charger failure (Mitsubishi i-MiEV)
DC/DC converter internal fault pulling the status output low
Status line shorted to ground or chafed harness
Faulty input stage in the hybrid/EV control module
s: Power unit, battery or hybrid warning light on
12 V battery not charged, voltage drops
On EVs the drive battery may also stop charging

P0A0A.t: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A
P0A0A.d: The high-voltage interlock loop (HVIL) is a low-voltage signal loop routed through every HV connector, the service disconnect and component covers. If it opens, the control module opens the main contactors so no one can touch live parts. P0A0A is the general circuit fault on loop A. Stellantis sets P0A0A-00 on the Jeep Wrangler and Grand Cherokee 4xe when an HV connector is torqued but not fully seated after repair, and on the 2024-2025 Pacifica Hybrid it was traced to battery pack control module software; there the car will not start on either power source. Mercedes logs P0A0A00 in the DC converter of model line 243. CARB counts the HVIL as a safety-only system, so MIL behaviour varies. Low, high, performance and intermittent faults use P0A0B to P0A0E.
c: HV connector or service disconnect not fully seated after repair
Spread, bent or corroded interlock pins or damaged connector seals
Battery pack control module software fault (Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid 2024-2025)
s: Vehicle will not start or go into ready mode
Check engine and hybrid system warning on
High-voltage system switched off while the 12 V system still works

P0A0B.t: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A Performance
P0A0B.d: The interlock loop A responds electrically, but its behaviour does not match what the module expects – for example a loop resistance outside the window, a signal that does not follow the commanded test pattern, or two modules on the same loop disagreeing. Mercedes-Benz logs P0A0B00 in the battery management system, the DC converter and the on-board charger of model line 243 when the vehicle will not start; its listed causes include oxidised interlock pins in the low-voltage connectors, twisted or chafed harnesses and bent pins on HV components. Patent literature explains why voltage-based loops are prone to false alarms from contact resistance and interference. Unlike P0A0C/P0A0D this is not a clear short. Expect the HV system to stay off.
c: Oxidised interlock pins in low-voltage connectors raising loop resistance
Improperly connected HV connector or bent interlock pins on an HV component
Twisted or chafed interlock harness rubbing on the body
Faulty interlock driver or receiver in a control module
s: Vehicle cannot be started
High-voltage system warning in the instrument cluster
Several modules store interlock codes at the same time

P0A0C.t: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A Low
P0A0C.d: The voltage sensed on interlock loop A is too low while the module drives the loop – typically an opened loop or a short to ground. GM documents it codegenau: in its 2016 HPC2 table P0A0C sets when the sensed interlock voltage stays below 30 % of the 5 V test signal in 2 of 2 samples (12.5 ms each) with the 12 V supply above 10.2 V; it is Type A, so the MIL lights after one trip. The 2011 Volt tables used a 10 % threshold. Mercedes-Benz model line 243 stores P0A0C00 in the DC converter and on-board charger as a short to ground in the interlock circuit. The opposite fault is P0A0D. Since the loop guards against live HV parts, the system drops the contactors and the car will not drive on electric power.
c: HV connector, cover or service disconnect open, interrupting the loop
Interlock wire shorted to ground, e.g. chafed at a module or the body
Faulty interlock source or sense stage in the battery or hybrid module
s: Check engine light (GM Type A) and hybrid/EV warning
No ready mode, electric drive unavailable
Charging may be blocked

P0A0D.t: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A High
P0A0D.d: The voltage sensed on interlock loop A is higher than expected – most often a short to a voltage source, or the loop not being pulled down when the module expects it. GM checks both states: in the 2016 HPC2 table P0A0D sets when the sensed voltage exceeds 24 % of 5 V with the source switched off (5 of 8 samples) or 44 % with it switched on (4 of 6 samples), Type A with MIL after one trip. Hyundai's Sonata Hybrid 2011-2015 bulletins send P0A0D straight to the HEV safety plug, alongside high-voltage path and relay codes, with check engine light and no ready mode. Mercedes model line 243 stores P0A0D00 in the battery management as a short to positive. P0A0C is the low-side counterpart; both leave the HV system switched off.
c: Service/safety plug not fully inserted or with poor contact (Hyundai Sonata Hybrid)
Interlock wire shorted to a 12 V or reference voltage
Damaged interlock harness or connector after body or battery work
Faulty interlock stage in the battery or hybrid control module
s: No ready mode or ready light blinking
Check engine and charging warning lights on
Vehicle cannot be started

P0A0E.t: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A Intermittent
P0A0E.d: The interlock loop A signal drops out or jumps for short moments and then recovers, so the module sees an unstable loop rather than a lasting open or short. Typical are connectors with loose or spread contacts, harness sections that move with the body or drivetrain, and moisture in seals. No manufacturer documents P0A0E publicly; the GM tables only list P0A0C and P0A0D for the same loop. Reference designs and patents on interlock monitoring describe the loop as a current or voltage path through each HV connector and point out that contact resistance and interference can cause brief false trips. CARB treats the HVIL as a safety-only system. For the driver this means sudden HV shutdowns or no-starts that come and go; static faults use P0A0A to P0A0D.
c: Loose or spread interlock contacts in an HV or low-voltage connector
Harness section with a broken strand that opens under vibration
Moisture entering through a damaged connector seal
Electrical interference on the interlock line or a weak module input
s: Hybrid/EV warning that appears and disappears
Occasional loss of ready mode or sudden shutdown of electric drive
Intermittent no-start, often after rough roads or rain

P0A0F.d: The control module commanded an engine start – by the hybrid system or an automatic start/stop restart – but the combustion engine did not reach a self-sustaining run within the allowed attempts. The code describes the result, not the cause. Toyota sets P0A0F with MIL on the 2010-2013 Prius and Prius v when a separated purge VSV/PCV hose leans out the mixture, often with P3190, P3191 and P0171. Kia traced P0A0F on the 2017-2018 Niro hybrid to an A/C pressure sensor harness chafed by an idler pulley, which disturbs the engine ECU 5 V reference. Audi sets P0A0F00 on 2019 A6/A7 3.0 mild hybrids after the second failed automatic restart, with a drive system warning. Look at fuel, air, ignition and engine sensor faults first.
c: Vacuum leak, e.g. separated purge VSV/PCV hose at the throttle body (Toyota Prius)
Shorted sensor harness pulling down the engine ECU 5 V reference (Kia Niro)
Fuel delivery or ignition fault preventing combustion
Failed automatic restart of a mild hybrid with a cold engine (Audi A6/A7 2019)
s: Check engine light and hybrid or drive system warning
Engine does not start, or runs briefly and stops
Reduced power because the vehicle runs on the battery only

P0A10.d: The status signal from the DC/DC converter to the hybrid control module sits above its valid range, typically because the line is shorted to a voltage source, its ground or pull-down path is open, or the converter drives the output high after an internal failure. The converter supplies the 12 V system from the traction battery, and its self-diagnosis reports problems over this status path. No manufacturer documents P0A10 publicly in an official source; older lists that call it a hybrid battery voltage sense circuit are wrong for today's J2012. Siblings: P0A08 is the general status fault, P0A09 the low signal. A converter that stops working shows up as warning lights and a falling 12 V voltage until the hybrid system shuts down.
c: Status line shorted to 12 V or another supply
Open ground or signal return at the converter connector
DC/DC converter internal fault driving the status output high
Faulty input stage in the hybrid control module
s: Hybrid system or battery warning light on
12 V battery voltage falls while driving
Possible shutdown of the hybrid system if the 12 V battery runs flat

P0A11.d: General or open-circuit fault on the enable line with which the hybrid or battery control module tells the DC/DC converter that it may deliver power to the 12 V system. In typical designs a high enable level permits converter output, and a CAN message carries the same permission in parallel, so the two can be cross-checked. If the line is open, the converter cannot be switched on reliably and the 12 V battery is no longer charged. No manufacturer documents P0A11 publicly in an official source; Honda's hybrid recall shows what follows when the converter shuts down: charging warning, discharged 12 V battery, possible loss of drive. Low and high faults on the same line are P0A12 and P0A13; status line faults are P0A08 to P0A10.
c: Broken enable wire or unplugged connector between control module and converter
Corroded or pushed-out terminal at the converter enable pin
Faulty enable output driver in the control module
Faulty enable input inside the DC/DC converter
s: Battery or charging warning light on
12 V battery is not charged and runs down
Vehicle may lose motive power after a while

P0A12.d: The enable line to the DC/DC converter reads low when the control module is commanding it on. Because a low enable level usually means converter output is not permitted, the converter stays off and the 12 V system loses its charging source. Typical causes are a short to ground on the enable wire, a weak output driver in the module, or an input stage in the converter that loads the line. Older lists name this code DC/DC converter communication; today's J2012 wording is enable circuit low. No manufacturer documents P0A12 publicly in an official source, so the description rests on CARB and on patent descriptions of hard-wired enable lines. P0A11 covers an open line, P0A13 a line stuck high. Drivers see a charging warning and a draining 12 V battery.
c: Weak or failed enable output driver in the control module
s: Charging or battery warning light on
12 V voltage drops, electrical consumers misbehave
Hybrid system may shut down when the 12 V battery is flat

P0A13.d: The enable line to the DC/DC converter reads high when the control module expects it low, for example while the converter should be switched off. The usual reasons are a short to battery voltage on the enable wire, a stuck output driver, or a missing pull-down. Since a high enable level normally permits converter output, the converter may keep running when it should not – during shutdown, a fault or high-voltage disconnection – which the module treats as a safety and battery-drain risk. No manufacturer documents P0A13 publicly in an official source; the explanation relies on CARB and on patents describing hard-wired DC/DC enable lines cross-checked against a CAN request. P0A11 is the open line, P0A12 the low fault; status-side faults are P0A08 to P0A10.
c: Enable wire shorted to 12 V or another supply
Enable output driver in the control module stuck on
Open pull-down or ground reference at the converter input
s: Hybrid system or battery warning light on
12 V battery drains while the vehicle is parked
Converter-related functions disabled as a precaution

P0A14.d: Some vehicles use switchable or active engine mounts that the powertrain or a mount control unit changes between soft and firm, or drives with an actuator against vibration. P0A14 reports an open or undefined fault in the control circuit of mount A. Ford lists it in its 2020 to 2023 gasoline OBD summary as the active mount circuit check: the low-side driver reports the fault and it matures after about 5 seconds; mount B uses P0AB6 to P0AB8. Honda's active control engine mounts, for example on the 2008 Pilot V6, use P0A14 for the front mount actuator and P0AB6 for the rear. P0A15 and P0A16 cover low and high faults. The car stays drivable, but vibration may increase.
c: Mount actuator connector loose, corroded or unplugged after engine work
Open coil in the mount actuator or switching solenoid
Wire broken where the harness flexes with engine movement
Fault in the engine or mount control unit output
s: More vibration at idle or during cylinder deactivation
Warning light, depending on manufacturer
Shudder that feels like a torque converter problem

P0A15.t: Engine Mount A Control Circuit Low
P0A15.d: The control circuit of switchable or active engine mount A shows a voltage or current below the expected level, which usually points to a short to ground on the line or inside the actuator. Ford uses P0A15 in its 2020 to 2023 gasoline OBD summary for the active mounts: the low-level driver reports the fault and the PCM matures it after about 5 seconds; the partner mount B has P0AB7. Honda's active control engine mount system on the 2008 Pilot V6 assigns P0A15 to the front mount actuator and P0AB7 to the rear. Ford engineers describe these mounts as switched between a damping and a stiffening mode, so a stuck mount is felt as vibration. The open circuit is P0A14, the high fault P0A16.
c: Control wire chafed on the engine or subframe and shorted to ground
Shorted coil in the mount actuator or solenoid, often after fluid leakage
s: Noticeable vibration at idle or low speed
Warning light, depending on manufacturer
Cylinder deactivation may be suppressed

P0A16.t: Engine Mount A Control Circuit High
P0A16.d: The module sees a higher voltage on the control circuit of engine mount A than it should for the commanded state, usually a short to a supply line or a failed actuator input. The mount can then no longer be switched or driven as intended. Ford lists P0A16 in its 2020 to 2023 gasoline OBD summary under the active mount circuit check, matured after about 5 seconds once the driver reports the fault; mount B uses P0AB8.
