On Honda's active control engine mounts, such as the 2008 Pilot V6, P0A16 belongs to the front mount actuator and P0AB8 to the rear one. A Ford patent shows the mounts are toggled between soft and firm, so a fault means either harsh idle or more movement. See P0A14 and P0A15.
c: Control wire shorted to a battery or ignition supply
Mount actuator or solenoid failed with an open low side
Driver stage in the engine or mount control unit damaged
s: Harsh idle or more engine movement on take-off
Warning light, depending on manufacturer
Vibration during cylinder deactivation

P0A17.d: Some electric drive units measure the torque on the motor or generator shaft directly, for example with a magnetostrictive sensor inside a hollow motor shaft as described in Honda patents for hybrid drive systems. The control unit uses that value to check the torque it commands. P0A17 is the general circuit fault of this sensor, set when the signal is missing or cannot be evaluated at all. No manufacturer documents P0A17 publicly. CARB requires a monitoring plan for drive motor faults that affect propulsion or emission strategies, which covers such feedback sensors. Plausibility is P0A18, low and high P0A19 and P0A20, intermittent P0A21. Expect reduced electric power and a hybrid warning.
c: Loose or corroded sensor connector at the drive unit
Damaged sensor wiring between drive unit and control module
Torque sensor or its excitation electronics failed, often only replaceable with the drive unit
Input stage of the hybrid or motor control module faulty
s: Hybrid system warning light
Electric drive power limited or electric drive disabled
Higher fuel consumption because the engine runs more often

P0A18.d: The motor torque sensor delivers an electrically valid signal, but the torque it reports does not match what the control unit expects from the commanded motor current, speed and operating state. Typical checks compare measured and estimated torque or look for an offset when no torque is applied. Honda patents show such a sensor mounted inside the hollow output shaft of a traction motor, where electromagnetic noise is a known accuracy issue. No manufacturer documents P0A18 publicly. CARB requires approved monitoring of drive motor faults that impair propulsion. P0A17 is the plain circuit fault; P0A19 and P0A20 are out of range low and high. The drive system usually limits electric torque.
c: Sensor offset or gain drifted, reading off against the torque model
Electrical interference on the signal from damaged shielding or ground
Missing or outdated calibration after module or drive unit replacement
Mechanical fault in the drive unit that changes the real torque
s: Hybrid system warning light
Reduced or uneven electric assistance
Engine runs more often, fuel use rises

P0A19.d: The control unit watches the voltage of a torque sensor that measures load directly on the traction motor shaft, such as the magnetostrictive sensor in a hollow motor shaft shown in a Honda patent. P0A19 sets when the signal stays below its valid window for a calibrated time, typical of a short to ground, a broken supply or an open signal line pulled low. No manufacturer documents P0A19 publicly; CARB only requires an approved drive motor monitoring plan. P0A20 is the opposite fault, P0A18 a plausible voltage with wrong torque, P0A21 dropouts. The driver usually sees a hybrid warning and reduced electric drive power.
c: Sensor signal or supply line shorted to ground
Sensor reference or excitation supply missing
Corroded or loose connector at the drive unit
Torque sensor electronics failed, often replaced with the drive unit
s: Hybrid system warning light
Reduced electric drive power or electric drive disabled
Engine runs more often, higher fuel consumption

P0A1A.d: P0A1A reports a fault of the electronics that control the generator, either inside a hybrid inverter or in a belt starter-generator. Toyota lists P0A1A for the 2010-2015 Prius and 2012-2017 Prius V together with P0A94, P324E and P3004 as a malfunction inside the inverter assembly with converter; the repair can mean replacing the MG ECU, IPM transistors or the whole inverter. Audi stores P0A1A00 in the engine control unit of 2025 models with a Valeo 48 V starter-generator, paired with a 48 V system fault, and blames starter-generator software. CARB requires monitoring of the generator system. Effects range from a MIL to lost charging or no hybrid drive.
c: Internal failure of the inverter or generator control electronics
Control software fault, fixed by an update where the maker provides one
Supply, ground or bus connection to the module faulty
s: MIL and hybrid or charging warning on
Battery no longer charged, start-stop or hybrid drive unavailable
Vehicle may not reach ready state

P0A1B.t: Drive Motor A Control Module Performance
P0A1B.d: P0A1B flags a self-test failure of the processor that controls drive motor A, usually inside the inverter. In GM hybrid tables (2016) it sets when the processor fails an inhibit path test at power-down, three or more times, proving it could not take the system to a safe state; in 2011 tables internal SPI, RAM or cache faults in 28 of 32 samples count. Both are Type A, MIL on the first trip. Land Rover sets P0A1B in the inverter of 2024-25 PHEVs at start-up, VW lists P0A1B00 for the ID.4 front drive. Toyota uses subtype P0A1B-1F on the 2023-24 Corolla Hybrid. Drive motor B is P0A1C. Expect a red loss-of-drive warning.
c: Control software fault, several makers resolve it by reprogramming
Internal processor or memory fault in the inverter control board
Weak 12 V supply during start-up or shutdown
s: Loss of drive warning and MIL
Vehicle cannot be driven electrically or not at all
Fault may vanish after a full sleep cycle while the code stays stored

P0A1C.t: Drive Motor B Control Module Performance
P0A1C.d: P0A1C is the counterpart of P0A1B for the second electric machine, drive motor B, and reports that its control processor is no longer trustworthy. GM hybrid tables use it for the motor control processor B: in 2016 calibrations the code sets when an inhibit path test at power-down fails three or more times, in 2011 calibrations internal processor integrity faults such as SPI, RAM or cache errors are counted. Both are Type A with MIL on the first trip. The code concerns the control electronics, not a phase current sensor; those faults use their own codes. Expect a hybrid warning and loss of the affected motor function.
c: Internal processor or memory fault on the motor B control board
Calibration or software fault in the inverter
Unstable 12 V supply or ground to the inverter electronics
s: Hybrid warning and MIL
Reduced drive power or no electric drive

P0A1D.d: The hybrid powertrain control module coordinates engine, motors and battery. P0A1D says this module has reported an internal failure or is no longer working reliably. In GM hybrid tables (2013) the engine control module stores P0A1D when a message from motor control processor A signals a hybrid controller status failure in 3 of 4 counts, as a Type B code with MIL after two trips. GM 2016 tables list P0A1D among codes that limit engine power. Subaru warns for the 2014-16 Crosstrek Hybrid that generic OBD readouts may store P0A1D from a scan tool communication error; replace the module only if the code returns. P0E43 covers module B.
c: Internal fault of the hybrid control module
Code stored by a scan tool communication error, not by a real defect
Supply, ground or network fault at the module
s: MIL and hybrid warning on
Engine power reduced
Hybrid functions limited or unavailable

P0A1E.d: Mild and full hybrids often start the engine and recharge the battery with a belt-driven starter-generator that has its own control electronics. P0A1E means that controller has reported a fault or works incorrectly. Audi stores P0A1E00 in the starter-generator control module of the 2020-2022 Q3 mild hybrid and cures it with a software update. Ford logs P0A1E in the engine control module of 2021-2023 F-150 PowerBoost and 2020-2026 Explorer and 2020-2023 Aviator hybrids; its bulletins name a loose connection at the belt integrated starter-generator or its software. Drivers notice a wrench or MIL lamp, no start-stop and no electric-only driving.
c: Loose wiring connection at the starter-generator
Starter-generator software fault, fixed by update
s: Wrench lamp or MIL on, electrical system warning
Auto start-stop disabled
Electric-only driving unavailable

P0A1F.t: Battery Energy Control Module A Performance
P0A1F.d: The battery energy control module supervises cell voltages, current and temperatures of the high-voltage pack. P0A1F reports that this module failed its own integrity checks. In GM hybrid tables (2011) a single reset of the module by its software watchdog is enough, and the code sets in one trip. GM told dealers for the 2011-2012 Chevrolet Volt not to replace the module for P0A1F but to install a new calibration. FCA lists subtype P0A1F-09, internal component failure, on the 2018 Jeep Wrangler with eTorque and also fixes it by reflashing the battery pack control module. Lost communication with the module is U0111. Expect a MIL and limited hybrid function.
c: Module software fault, fixed by a new calibration
Internal hardware fault of the battery control module
Unstable 12 V supply causing module resets
s: MIL or service engine soon light on
Battery or hybrid warning, limited electric operation
Start-stop may be disabled

P0A20.d: This code covers the upper electrical limit of a torque sensor fitted to the traction motor shaft, for example the magnetostrictive design inside a hollow output shaft described in a Honda patent. The control unit sets P0A20 when the sensor voltage remains above the valid range for a calibrated time, which points to a short to the supply voltage, an open ground return or a sensor output stuck high. No manufacturer documents P0A20 publicly; CARB requires an approved drive motor monitor. Siblings: P0A19 low, P0A18 implausible torque, P0A21 intermittent, P0A17 general circuit. Expect a hybrid warning and limited electric torque.
c: Signal line shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
s: Hybrid system warning light
Electric drive torque limited
Reduced acceleration in electric mode

P0A21.d: Here the torque sensor on the traction motor shaft delivers a signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing permanently. Such shaft sensors, as in the Honda patent with a sensor inside a hollow motor shaft, sit in an area with strong electromagnetic fields and vibration, so loose terminals, chafed wires and interference are the usual suspects. P0A21 sets when the control unit counts too many implausible signal changes. No manufacturer documents P0A21 publicly; CARB demands an approved drive motor monitor. Steady faults would show as P0A19 or P0A20. The warning may come and go.
c: Loose or fretted terminal in the sensor connector
Chafed sensor wiring that shorts briefly under vibration
Damaged shield letting inverter noise into the signal
s: Hybrid warning that appears and disappears
Brief loss of electric assist

P0A22.d: In series or power-split hybrids a separate electric machine runs as generator, driven by the combustion engine. A Honda patent claims a torque sensor inside the hollow shaft of either the traction motor or this generator. P0A22 is the general circuit fault of the generator torque sensor: the control unit receives no usable signal at all, without a more specific low, high or intermittent pattern. No manufacturer documents P0A22 publicly; CARB requires an approved monitoring plan for the generator system. Related: P0A23 plausibility, P0A24 low, P0A25 high, P0A26 intermittent. Charging and engine-driven power generation may be limited.
c: Sensor connector at the generator unplugged, loose or corroded
Open circuit in the sensor harness
Generator torque sensor or its electronics failed
s: Hybrid system warning light
Reduced battery charging by the engine
Limited system power

P0A23.d: The generator torque sensor sends an electrically valid voltage, but the torque it reports does not fit the generator current, speed and engine load the control unit knows. Typical checks compare the measured value with a torque model or look for an offset while the generator is idle. Such a sensor can sit in the hollow generator shaft, as a Honda patent claims, where magnetic noise and ageing shift the reading. No manufacturer documents P0A23 publicly; CARB requires approved monitoring of generator faults. Pure wiring faults appear as P0A22, P0A24 or P0A25. The system tends to cap generator torque.
c: Sensor zero point or gain drifted
Electromagnetic interference from the generator or inverter
Contact resistance in the connector skewing the signal
s: Hybrid system warning light
Generator output limited, battery charges slowly

P0A24.d: P0A24 is stored when the voltage from the generator torque sensor stays under its lower diagnostic limit for a calibrated time. Electrically this means the line is pulled toward ground, the sensor supply is missing or the signal wire is broken. The sensor measures torque on the shaft of the engine-driven generator; a Honda patent describes such a sensor inside a hollow generator or motor shaft. No manufacturer documents P0A24 publicly; CARB requires an approved generator monitoring plan. The upper limit is P0A25, implausible but valid readings are P0A23, short dropouts P0A26. Electric generation may be cut back.
c: Sensor electronics failed with output stuck low
s: Hybrid system warning light
Reduced charging and system power

P0A25.d: With P0A25 the control unit sees the generator torque sensor signal above its permitted upper limit for longer than the calibrated debounce time. The common electrical explanations are a short from the signal line to the supply or battery voltage, an interrupted sensor ground, or a sensor output stuck at its maximum. The sensor belongs to the engine-driven generator of a hybrid; a Honda patent shows torque sensing inside a hollow generator or motor shaft. No manufacturer documents P0A25 publicly; CARB only demands an approved generator monitor. Opposite fault: P0A24; plausibility: P0A23; intermittent: P0A26. Generator torque is usually limited.
c: Signal line shorted to supply or battery voltage
s: Hybrid system warning light
Generator output limited

P0A26.d: P0A26 points to short interruptions or jumps in the generator torque sensor signal rather than a constant fault. The control unit counts implausible signal changes or brief out-of-range events and sets the code once a calibrated limit is exceeded. Because the sensor works next to the generator, as in the Honda patent with a sensor in a hollow generator or motor shaft, heat cycles, vibration and inverter noise favour loose contacts and chafed wires. No manufacturer documents P0A26 publicly; CARB requires an approved generator monitor. Permanent faults show as P0A24 or P0A25. Symptoms often appear only on rough roads.
c: Loose or fretted terminal in the sensor connector
Chafed wiring near the generator housing
Shield or ground damage letting inverter noise in
s: Hybrid warning that comes and goes
Brief drop in charging or system power

P0A27.d: P0A27 covers the circuit that tells the high-voltage battery to drop off the bus, i.e. the command path that opens the main contactors at key-off, after a fault or after a crash signal. Patents describe such a path as a dedicated hardware line in addition to CAN, so the contactors open within milliseconds. The code sets when commanded and actual state disagree. Honda lists P0A27 as High Voltage Contactor Stays Activated on the 2012-15 Civic Hybrid, where it is one of the codes that call for replacing the motor power inverter. P0A28 and P0A29 are the low and high voltage faults of the same line. The driver may see a hybrid warning and the car may refuse to start or power down.
c: Contactor or its driver does not release when power-off is commanded
Internal fault in the inverter/power unit that controls the contactors (Honda Civic Hybrid)
Damaged wiring or loose terminal on the hardwired power-off line
Crash or emergency shutdown signal stored or still active
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Vehicle will not enter ready mode or shuts down while driving
High-voltage system does not power down after key-off

P0A28.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Power Off Circuit Low
P0A28.d: The control unit watches the voltage on the line that commands the high-voltage battery to disconnect. P0A28 sets when that signal stays below its valid window for a calibrated time, typical of a short to ground or a lost supply on the line. No manufacturer documents P0A28 publicly; GM only lists it as a search keyword in a general pin-fit bulletin. Patents show the power-off path as a hardwired line next to CAN that opens the contactors within milliseconds; CARB requires hybrid components that can affect emissions to be monitored. P0A29 is the opposite fault, P0A27 a mismatch between command and contactor state. Expect a hybrid warning and, depending on strategy, no ready mode.
c: Power-off signal line shorted to ground
Poor terminal fit or corrosion at the battery or control module connector
Missing supply or blown fuse feeding the power-off circuit
Faulty driver stage in the battery or hybrid control module
s: Hybrid system warning light
Vehicle does not reach ready mode
Electric drive disabled, engine runs constantly

P0A29.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Power Off Circuit High
P0A29.d: P0A29 is stored when the voltage on the hybrid battery power-off line sits above its plausible range for longer than allowed, which points to an open line pulled up internally or a short to a supply voltage. No manufacturer explains P0A29 publicly; GM merely names it as a keyword in a generic bulletin on terminal fit. The circuit itself is the hardwired disconnect path that patents describe beside the CAN crash message, and CARB 1968.2 requires monitoring of hybrid components relevant to emissions. Related: P0A28 for a signal too low, P0A27 when the contactors do not follow the command. A stuck-high line can keep the system from powering up or from shutting down correctly.
c: Open power-off line or unplugged connector
Power-off line shorted to battery voltage
Spread or corroded terminals at the connectors
Faulty input or driver stage in the control module
s: Hybrid system warning light
Vehicle does not reach ready mode
High-voltage system stays active after switching off

P0A2A.t: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0A2A.d: A thermistor in the stator of traction motor A reports winding temperature so the inverter can cut torque before the insulation overheats. P0A2A is the general circuit fault; the failure type sits in the extension byte. McLaren uses P0A2A1C on the Artura when a short or broken wire drives the sensor voltage out of range and P0A2A29 for an invalid signal. GM instead splits the electrical faults into P0A2C and P0A2D. Siblings: P0A2B plausibility, P0A2C low signal (hot), P0A2D high signal (cold or open), P0A2E dropouts, P0A2F real overheating; P2DAC is the same fault on a second sensor B. Hyundai shows the sensor sits inside the transaxle. Expect a hybrid warning and reduced electric power.
c: Broken or shorted sensor wire between motor and inverter
Loose or corroded connector at the drive unit
Thermistor failed inside the motor or transaxle
Faulty sensor input in the inverter/motor control module
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Reduced electric drive power
Implausible motor temperature in live data

P0A2B.t: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0A2B.d: This is the rationality check: after a long soak, motor A's temperature should match other temperatures in the drive. GM compares it with the average inverter module temperature on its 2013 two-mode trucks and sets P0A2B, Type B, if they differ by more than 28 °C after at least 360 minutes off; the 2011 table uses 20 °C against coolant and transmission fluid, the 2013 MGU mild hybrid 25 °C. Hyundai's Sonata Hybrid bulletin lists the code with resistance specs for the NTC; Audi pairs it on the A7 e quattro with P0A2E and a worn connector. McLaren also files over-temperature under P0A2B98. P0A2C/P0A2D are hard electrical faults, P0A2F real heat. Expect reduced electric power.
c: Thermistor drifted out of its resistance curve
Added resistance from a worn or corroded connector (Audi A7 e quattro)
Fault in a reference temperature such as inverter or fluid temperature
Motor cooling problem that makes a real temperature look implausible
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Electric drive power limited
Motor temperature far off from other temperatures after a cold soak

P0A2C.t: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0A2C.d: The motor A sensor is an NTC thermistor, so its signal voltage falls as the winding heats; Hyundai's Sonata Hybrid bulletin gives about 11 to 13 kOhm at 20 °C for 2014-15 units. P0A2C means the voltage is too low, which the module reads as an impossibly hot motor: GM sets it on 2013 two-mode trucks above 230 °C (near 0 V), Type B, two trips; the 2011 table uses 184 °C, the 2013 MGU mild hybrid 236 °C. The usual cause is a signal wire shorted to ground or a shorted sensor. P0A2D is the opposite fault, P0A2F a real over-temperature that only counts while the sensor is in range. Hyundai reports a stuck 417 °F reading as a circuit fault. The driver sees a warning and derated electric drive.
c: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Thermistor internally shorted (often only with transaxle or motor)
Chafed extension harness between drive unit and inverter
Faulty sensor input in the inverter/motor control module
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Motor temperature shows a very high fixed value in live data
Electric drive power reduced or disabled

P0A2D.t: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0A2D.d: With an NTC thermistor, a high signal voltage stands for a cold motor, and a voltage close to the 5 V pull-up means the circuit is open. GM sets P0A2D on its 2013 two-mode trucks when the reading falls below -40 °C, Type B over two trips; if the fault is already present at start-up it waits until the motor has warmed up under load for at least 1.5 minutes. The 2011 table uses -41 °C, the 2013 MGU mild hybrid -48 °C with torque above 10 Nm. Typical causes are a broken signal or ground wire, an unplugged connector or an open sensor. Hyundai checks the sensor resistance at the transaxle connector. P0A2C is the low-voltage counterpart. Motor protection is lost, so electric power is limited.
c: Open signal or ground wire of the motor temperature sensor
Connector unplugged or terminal pushed out, often after drive unit work
Thermistor open inside the motor or transaxle
Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Motor temperature shows about -40 degrees in live data
Electric drive power limited

P0A2E.t: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0A2E.d: P0A2E flags short jumps or dropouts in the motor A temperature signal that are too brief or too erratic for the low/high checks. Bentley documents it for the Bentayga PHEV and Flying Spur Hybrid 2020-23: the resistance in the sensor crimp changes suddenly at high temperature, and only the sensor has to be replaced, although the engine and gearbox come out to reach it. Audi lists it on the 2021-22 A7 e quattro together with P0A4000 and/or P0A2B00, caused by contact wear in a coupling connector, fixed with new gold-plated pins. Siblings: P0A2C/P0A2D for a steady out-of-range signal, P2DB0 for sensor B. The car shows a MIL or HV warning and may limit electric drive.
c: Worn contacts in a coupling connector of the sensor line (Audi A7 e quattro)
Resistance jumps in the sensor crimp at high temperature (Bentley hybrids)
Chafed or loosely routed sensor wire with intermittent contact
s: Check engine light or high-voltage warning in the cluster
Fault comes and goes, often after hard driving
Gearbox or electric drive warning on some models

P0A2F.d: Unlike its siblings, P0A2F reports a real thermal problem: the sensor works, but motor A stays too hot. GM sets it on 2013 two-mode trucks when the temperature exceeds 200 °C and does not fall below the 135 °C reset level, Type B, provided no circuit or plausibility fault is active. The 2011 table uses 159 °C; on the 2013 MGU mild hybrid the limit is 165 °C, and torque is already cut linearly from 100 % to zero between 155 and 165 °C. Hyundai lists the code in its Sonata Hybrid sensor bulletin, so a skewed sensor can mimic it. McLaren handles over-temperature under P0A2B98 and points to the dielectric cooling circuit. Expect a warning and sharply reduced electric power.
c: Motor cooling failure such as a weak pump, low fluid or blocked cooler
Sustained high load such as towing or long climbs in electric mode
Temperature sensor reading too high while still within range
s: Hybrid system or check engine warning
Electric drive power drops sharply or is cut
Engine runs more often to support the drive

P0A30.t: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0A30.d: P0A30 is the general circuit code for the temperature sensor in the second traction motor (motor B). It is meant for faults the control unit can see on the sensor line but cannot classify as too low, too high or implausible. No manufacturer documents P0A30 publicly; GM two-mode hybrids and Mitsubishi (rear motor of the 2023 Outlander PHEV) use the specific codes P0A31 to P0A33 for the same sensor instead. CARB 1968.2 requires hybrid components whose failure can affect emissions to be monitored for circuit faults. Without a valid winding temperature the motor cannot be protected against overheating, so the system usually cuts electric drive power and lights a hybrid warning.
c: Loose, corroded or damaged connector between motor B and its control module
Chafed or broken sensor wiring at the drive unit
Thermistor in the motor winding failed (often only replaceable with the motor)
Faulty sensor input in the motor control module
s: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Reduced electric drive power
Motor B temperature missing or implausible in live data

P0A31.t: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A31.d: P0A31 checks whether the motor B temperature reading makes sense, typically after a long rest when all parts should be close to the same temperature. GM compares it with other temperatures: the 2011 tables flag a gap above 20 °C to the average of power-electronics coolant and transmission fluid after 6 h without propulsion (Type A); the 2013 two-mode trucks allow 28 °C against the inverter module after 360 min key-off (Type B, two trips). Mitsubishi (2023 Outlander PHEV rear motor) compares two coil sensors after 5,400 s soak and sets it at 13 °C difference. P0A32 and P0A33 cover hard circuit faults; P0A35 is only judged while this test passes. Expect a hybrid warning and limited electric drive.
c: Motor B thermistor reading drifted out of tolerance
Corroded terminals adding resistance in the sensor circuit
Comparison sensor (inverter, coolant or fluid temperature) is wrong
Uneven cooling of the drive unit, e.g. low fluid level
s: Hybrid warning light after a cold start
Motor B temperature differs clearly from other temperatures after a long rest
Electric drive limited as a precaution

P0A32.t: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0A32.d: P0A32 means the motor B temperature signal sits below its valid voltage range. GM uses an NTC thermistor, so a voltage near 0 V reads as an impossibly hot winding: the 2011 hybrid tables set it above 184 °C (Type A, one trip), the 2013 two-mode trucks above 230 °C (Type B, two trips). Mitsubishi sets it on the rear motor of the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the sensor voltage is 0.065 V or less for 0.5 s. A signal wire shorted to ground or a shorted thermistor is the typical cause. P0A33 is the opposite fault, P0A31 the plausibility check, and P0A35 a real over-temperature that GM only evaluates while no out-of-range fault is active. The system derates electric drive and warns the driver.
c: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Chafed harness between drive unit and motor control module
Faulty sensor input in the motor control module
s: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Motor B temperature shows an extremely high fixed value
Electric drive reduced or switched off

P0A33.t: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0A33.d: P0A33 is stored when the motor B temperature signal stays above its valid voltage range. With GM's NTC thermistor a voltage near 5 V reads as an impossibly cold motor: GM sets it below -41 °C in the 2011 tables (Type A) and below -40 °C on the 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips). Mitsubishi flags the rear motor of the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the voltage reaches 4.761 V or more for 0.5 s. That pattern points to an open sensor circuit, an unplugged connector or a short to a voltage source. P0A32 is the low-side fault, P0A31 the rationality check, P0A35 the over-temperature code. Because winding temperature is unknown, the system limits electric drive power and shows a warning.
c: Open sensor circuit or unplugged connector
Spread or corroded terminals at the motor or module connector
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source
s: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Motor B temperature shows about -40 °C regardless of conditions
Electric drive power limited

P0A34.t: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A34.d: P0A34 covers a motor B temperature signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing permanently. A winding temperature cannot change by tens of degrees within milliseconds, so such steps point to a loose contact, a chafed wire or a cracked solder joint. No manufacturer documents P0A34 publicly; GM and Mitsubishi only list the permanent faults P0A32 and P0A33 for this sensor, with debounce times of a few hundred milliseconds to seconds that a brief dropout may not meet. CARB 1968.2 requires circuit monitoring of emission-relevant hybrid components. The fault often comes and goes with vibration or heat, and the hybrid system may limit electric drive while it is active.
c: Loose or fretting terminal in the sensor connector
Wire insulation chafed through at a moving harness section
Cracked joint at the thermistor leads inside the motor
s: Hybrid warning that appears and clears on its own
Motor B temperature jumps in live data
Occasional loss of electric drive power

P0A35.d: Unlike the sensor codes, P0A35 reports that motor B is actually too hot according to a working sensor. GM's 2011 hybrid tables set it above 149 °C (Type A, one trip); the 2013 two-mode trucks use 200 °C, clear it only below 135 °C and run it only while P0A31 is not active (Type B). Mitsubishi sets it on the rear motor of the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the coil reaches 177 °C for one second and names the motor assembly, electric water pump, EV cooling circuit and radiator fan as suspects. Sustained heavy load, towing or a cooling fault are the usual triggers. P0A2F is the same check for motor A, P0A3D for the motor B inverter. The system cuts motor B torque until it has cooled down.
c: Electric coolant pump of the drive cooling circuit failed or weak
Low coolant or transmission fluid in the motor cooling path
Radiator fan not running or radiator blocked
Extended high load such as towing or long climbs
s: Noticeable loss of electric drive power
Hybrid system overheat or warning message
Engine runs more often to compensate

P0A36.d: P0A36 is the general circuit code for the temperature sensor in the hybrid generator, the machine that is mainly driven by the engine to produce electricity. It covers faults the module detects on the sensor line without classing them as low, high or implausible. No manufacturer documents P0A36 publicly; Mitsubishi (2023 Outlander PHEV) monitors its generator coil sensor with the specific codes P0A37 to P0A39 instead. CARB 1968.2 requires circuit monitoring for hybrid components that can affect emissions. With the generator temperature unknown, the system cannot protect the windings, so it usually restricts generator output and series operation and shows a hybrid warning.
c: Loose or corroded connector between generator and its control unit
Damaged sensor wiring near the transaxle
Generator coil thermistor failed (usually replaced with the generator)
Faulty input in the generator control unit
s: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Generator output or battery charging restricted
Generator temperature missing or implausible in live data

P0A37.d: P0A37 tests whether the generator temperature reading is believable. Mitsubishi documents it for the 2023 Outlander PHEV: once per drive cycle, after at least 5,400 s of soak and with the inverter switched off, the generator W-phase coil temperature is compared with the front motor coil and with the oil temperature. A gap of 26 °C to the motor or 22 °C to the oil, held for 0.8 s, sets the code. Suspects are the power drive unit, the coil sensor inside the generator and the wiring. P0A38 and P0A39 are hard voltage faults of the same sensor, P0A3B the real over-temperature. Mitsubishi is the only manufacturer found that documents P0A37 publicly. The driver sees a warning and generator use may be limited.
c: Generator coil sensor reading out of tolerance
Corroded connector or damaged harness in the sensor circuit
Fault in the power drive unit that evaluates the sensor
Comparison sensor (motor coil or oil temperature) reads wrong
s: Hybrid warning after the first start of the day
Generator temperature differs from oil temperature after a long rest
Generator operation possibly restricted

P0A38.d: P0A38 means the generator temperature signal has fallen below the range a healthy sensor can produce. Mitsubishi sets it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the voltage of the generator W-phase coil sensor is 0.1 V or less for at least 0.5 s while the generator control unit has at least 8 V supply. Such a low voltage usually comes from a signal wire shorted to ground or a shorted sensor; Mitsubishi lists the power drive unit, the generator coil sensor and damaged wiring or connectors as suspects. P0A39 is the matching high fault, P0A37 the plausibility check and P0A3B a genuine over-temperature. Mitsubishi is the only manufacturer found that documents P0A38. Expect a hybrid warning and restricted generator use.
c: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Damaged connector or harness between generator and power drive unit
Faulty sensor input in the power drive unit
s: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Generator temperature shows an implausibly high fixed value
Battery charging by the engine restricted

P0A39.d: P0A39 is the high-side counterpart of P0A38: the generator temperature signal stays above the range a working sensor can deliver. Mitsubishi sets it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the generator W-phase coil sensor voltage reaches 4.93 V or more for at least 0.5 s. A voltage that close to the reference typically means the sensor circuit is open, a connector is unplugged or a terminal has lost contact, less often a short to a supply. Mitsubishi points to the power drive unit, the coil sensor in the generator and the harness. P0A37 handles implausible but in-range readings, P0A3B a real overheat. No other manufacturer documents P0A39 publicly. The system cannot protect the generator and limits its use.
c: Open sensor circuit or unplugged generator connector
Spread or corroded terminals at the generator or power drive unit
Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage
s: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Generator temperature shows a very low fixed value
Generator output or series mode restricted

P0A3A.d: P0A3A flags a generator temperature signal that is interrupted or jumps only briefly. Since the thermal mass of a generator winding rules out sudden steps, such behaviour indicates a contact or wiring problem rather than a real temperature change. No manufacturer documents P0A3A publicly; Mitsubishi (2023 Outlander PHEV) only lists the permanent faults P0A38 and P0A39 for its generator coil sensor, each needing at least 0.5 s outside the valid voltage before it sets, so short dropouts would not trigger them. CARB 1968.2 calls for circuit monitoring of emission-relevant hybrid parts. Symptoms come and go, often with heat, vibration or moisture, and generator use may be restricted while the fault is present.
c: Loose or fretting terminal in the generator sensor connector
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Harness chafed against the transaxle housing
s: Hybrid warning that appears now and then
Generator temperature jumps in live data
Occasionally restricted battery charging by the engine

P0A3B.d: P0A3B reports that the hybrid generator itself has become too hot, with the temperature sensor working correctly. Mitsubishi documents it as generator coil temperature high on the 2023 Outlander PHEV: the monitor runs continuously and sets the code when the W-phase coil temperature criterion of 199 °C is met for one second. Mitsubishi's checks cover higher-priority codes, the radiator fan, and the EV oil cooling circuit that cools the generator; if those are fine, the generator is replaced. P0A37 to P0A39 are the sensor faults that must be ruled out first, P0A3E the over-temperature of the generator inverter. No other manufacturer documents P0A3B publicly. The system restricts generator output, which can cut charging and series-mode power.
c: Fault in the oil cooling circuit of the generator (low oil, leak, pump)
Internal generator fault such as damaged winding insulation
Power drive unit commanding excessive generator current
s: Hybrid system warning or overheat message
Reduced charging and power when the engine drives the generator
Battery state of charge drops during driving

P0A3C.t: Drive Motor A Inverter Over Temperature
P0A3C.d: P0A3C reports overheating of the inverter that powers drive motor A, usually measured at its IGBT power switches. Mitsubishi sets it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the front motor control unit reads 166 °C or more at the U-phase upper IGBT for 0.12 s; other switch positions have their own P30xx codes. Honda calls it motor control module overheating and lists it among the codes caused by a cracked solder joint in the 2012-15 Civic Hybrid motor power inverter, covered by a warranty extension. On the 2023-25 Accord Hybrid and 2025-26 Civic Hybrid, Honda links it to a PCU radiator damaged by road debris. P0A78 is the general inverter performance code, P0C11 to P0C13 are phase-specific. Power is cut to protect the inverter.
c: PCU or inverter radiator damaged or leaking (Honda Accord/Civic Hybrid)
Internal inverter defect such as a cracked solder joint (Honda Civic Hybrid 2012-15)
Low coolant or failed electric pump in the inverter cooling circuit
s: Hybrid system warning and check engine light
Strongly reduced drive power
Coolant loss from the inverter circuit

P0A3D.t: Drive Motor B Inverter Over Temperature
P0A3D.d: P0A3D is the over-temperature code for the inverter feeding drive motor B. On the 2023 Outlander PHEV this is the rear motor control unit, and Mitsubishi sets the code when its IGBT temperature is 156 °C or higher for one second. Mitsubishi's hints list the rear motor assembly, the electric water pump driven by the PHEV-ECU, the EV coolant circuit and the radiator fan, so cooling problems come before electronics. No other manufacturer documents P0A3D publicly; CARB 1968.2 requires monitoring of hybrid components that affect emissions. P0A35 is the over-temperature of motor B itself, P0C14 to P0C16 phase-specific inverter codes and P0A79 the general inverter performance code. Rear drive power is reduced until the inverter cools down.
c: Electric water pump of the EV cooling circuit failed
Low coolant or air in the EV cooling circuit
Radiator fan not running or radiator blocked
Internal fault in the rear motor and inverter assembly
s: Hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced rear-axle drive power
Fault appears after long climbs or high load

P0A3E.d: P0A3E reports that the inverter controlling the hybrid generator is too hot. Mitsubishi sets it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the generator control unit reads 156 °C or more at the U-phase IGBT for 0.12 s; the other switches report via P30AD to P30B1. Its hints are the power drive unit, the EV water cooling circuit and the radiator fan. Honda lists P0A3E among the PCU overheating codes on the 2023-25 Accord Hybrid and 2025-26 Civic Hybrid, where road debris can puncture the PCU radiator because the original guard is too weak. P0A3B is the generator's own over-temperature, P0A3C and P0A3D cover the motor inverters. Output is restricted, so charging and power drop and further warnings may follow.
c: PCU radiator punctured or leaking after road debris (Honda Accord/Civic Hybrid)
Low coolant or failed electric pump in the inverter cooling circuit
Internal fault in the power drive unit
s: Several hybrid warning lights at once
Reduced hybrid system performance
Coolant loss or visible damage at the front radiator area

P0A3F.t: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit
P0A3F.d: The rotor position of a traction motor is read by a resolver: one excitation coil and two pickup coils that return sine and cosine signals. P0A3F is the basic circuit code for motor A and mostly means the signal is gone. GM sets it when the sine or cosine amplitude drops below 2.3 V (Type A, one trip in the 2011 and 2016 tables); Mitsubishi (2023 Outlander PHEV front motor) watches the excitation voltage and fails it outside 1.0 to 2.86 V for 0.14 s. Field causes: a spread terminal at the X2 connector of the Chevrolet Bolt, low 12 V supply on the 2014 Subaru XV Crosstrek Hybrid (software fix), Stellantis Pacifica Hybrid. P0A40 covers a degraded signal. Expect lost propulsion or no electric drive.
c: Spread or poorly seated terminal at the resolver connector (documented on the Chevrolet Bolt)
Open or shorted excitation, sine or cosine wire between motor and inverter
Low 12 V auxiliary battery voltage disturbing the motor control module (Subaru, fixed by reprogramming)
Resolver coil failed inside the motor
Faulty resolver excitation or input stage in the inverter/motor control module
s: Sudden loss of propulsion, sometimes normal again after a restart
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle will not enter ready mode or electric drive is disabled

P0A40.t: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A40.d: P0A40 means the resolver of motor A still delivers a signal, but its quality is poor or implausible. GM calls this a degraded signal: the sine or cosine value exceeds 4.0 V, judged within 0.2 to 0.4 s of a 2 s window (Type A, one trip in 2016; Type B, two trips on the 2013 mild hybrid). Mitsubishi (2023 Outlander PHEV front motor) sets it when sine or cosine leaves the 2.1 to 2.9 V band for 0.17 s. Audi lists P0A4000 with an implausible signal on the A7 and Q5 e quattro and replaces rotor position sensor G713 after checking gold-plated connector pins; Bentley pairs it with P0C5100/P0C5B00 and inspects connectors for pin drag. P0A3F is the hard signal loss. Expect a drive system warning or no start.
c: Rotor position sensor (resolver) delivering a degraded signal, e.g. Audi G713
Worn, loose or contaminated contacts in the resolver connectors (Audi, Bentley)
Sensor wires pinched or misrouted on the gearbox housing after a repair
Faulty resolver evaluation in the inverter/motor control module
s: Drive system fault message in the instrument cluster
Vehicle cannot be started or will not enter ready mode
Electric drive disabled or torque jerks while driving

P0A41.t: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit Low
P0A41.d: P0A41 reports that a resolver signal of motor A sits below its permitted range, as happens with a sine, cosine or excitation wire shorted to ground, a shorted coil or a broken line pulled down by the input circuit. Kia documents it on the 2011-13 Optima Hybrid: an intermittent MIL or hybrid service lamp with P0A41 in the motor control unit, traced to internal shorts or poor pin fit in the sub-harness between the hybrid power control unit and the motor, checked against resistance specs. Bosch patents describe telling a short to ground from a short to supply by the offset of the coil lines. P0A42 is the high side, P0A3F the general loss of signal, P0A40 a degraded signal. Expect a warning lamp and possibly no electric drive.
c: Internal short in the resolver sub-harness between power control unit and motor (Kia Optima Hybrid)
Poor pin fit at the resolver connectors
Shorted resolver coil inside the motor
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control unit
s: Intermittent MIL or hybrid service lamp
Electric drive temporarily disabled
Code returns after clearing, often with vibration or heat

P0A42.t: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit High
P0A42.d: P0A42 is the counterpart to P0A41: a resolver line of motor A reads above its allowed range. Typical triggers are a sine, cosine or excitation wire shorted to a supply voltage, or an open coil whose line is pulled up by the bias resistors of the input circuit, which drives the converter into clipping. Kia covers it in the same Optima Hybrid 2011-13 bulletin as P0A41: intermittent MIL or hybrid service lamp, fixed by inspecting the HPCU-to-motor sub-harness for internal shorts and pin fit. Bosch patents explain why clipping alone is not enough and how the line offset reveals a short to supply or an open line. P0A3F is the general circuit fault. Expect a warning lamp and reduced or no electric drive.
c: Resolver wire shorted to a supply voltage inside the sub-harness (Kia Optima Hybrid)
Open sine or cosine line pulled high by the input circuit
Poor pin fit or corrosion at the resolver connectors
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control unit
s: Intermittent MIL or hybrid service lamp
Electric drive disabled or vehicle not ready
Reduced power until the fault clears

P0A43.t: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A43.d: P0A43 is set when the motor A resolver signal drops out or jumps only briefly, so that neither a steady low, high nor a lasting loss is confirmed. Stellantis uses it on the Pacifica Hybrid: NHTSA files show P0A43-00 stored in the hybrid control processor next to P0A3F and P0A45, and a 2026 parts review tells dealers to check active bulletins and flash the hybrid control processor before ordering a new power inverter module. No public set threshold exists. GM's Bolt bulletin shows how a slightly spread connector terminal causes such short dropouts. P0A3F, P0A41 and P0A42 cover permanent faults. Expect a warning that may vanish after a restart, sometimes with a short loss of drive.
c: Loose or spread terminal in the resolver connector, losing contact under vibration
Hybrid control or inverter software needing an update (Stellantis)
Chafed resolver wiring making intermittent contact
Intermittent fault in the power inverter module
s: Hybrid system warning or MIL that comes and goes
Brief loss of propulsion, normal again after restart
Code stored as history without current symptoms

P0A44.t: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit Overspeed
P0A44.d: P0A44 reports that the speed derived from the motor A resolver is above the highest speed the motor may run. Mitsubishi uses it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV front motor: set at 15,500 rpm or more for 0.5 s with module supply above 8 V, judged only when the position sensor itself is fault-free; the guided fix after other codes are ruled out is a new front motor. GM covers the same check under its own code P1B0D (above 11,500 rpm, Type A) instead of P0A44. A true overspeed can come from a slipping drivetrain or a mechanical fault; a false one from a corrupted speed signal. P0A3F to P0A43 cover the sensor circuit. The system cuts motor torque to protect the rotor.
c: Mechanical fault in the front motor or its drivetrain (Mitsubishi replaces the motor)
Real overspeed from wheel spin or a slipping coupling
Disturbed resolver signal producing a false speed value
Motor control module calculating speed incorrectly
s: Electric drive torque cut during acceleration or high speed
Hybrid/EV system warning and MIL
Reduced top speed in limp mode

P0A45.t: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit
P0A45.d: P0A45 is the general circuit code for the resolver of the second traction motor (B), usually meaning its signal is missing. GM sets it like P0A3F when sine or cosine amplitude falls below 2.3 V (Type A, one trip). Mitsubishi uses it for the rear motor of the 2023 Outlander PHEV: both sine and cosine below 0.12 V for at least 0.18 s; the resolver is part of the rear motor assembly, which is replaced. Toyota fixes P0A45 on 2016-18 RAV4 Hybrid models built before a production change with a new frame wire harness, and Stellantis lists it for the Pacifica Hybrid. P0A46 to P0A49 split out degraded, low, high and intermittent signals. Expect a hybrid warning, MIL and loss of the motor B drive.
c: Damaged or faulty frame/body wire harness to the rear motor (Toyota RAV4 Hybrid)
Poor contact at the motor B resolver connector
Resolver or control unit inside the rear motor assembly failed (Mitsubishi)
Hybrid control software needing an update (Stellantis)
s: MIL and hybrid system warning message
Loss of rear-axle electric drive or all-wheel drive
Reduced power or vehicle not ready

P0A46.t: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A46.d: P0A46 reports that the motor B resolver still delivers a signal, but one that is degraded or not plausible. GM uses the same check as P0A40 for its second motor: sine or cosine above 4.0 V, with a failure counted when it persists for 0.2 to 0.4 s of a 2 s window (Type A, one trip in the 2011 and 2016 tables). Mitsubishi (2023 Outlander PHEV rear motor) sets P0A46 when its internal resolver status words A, B or C stay failed for 0.18 s, and replaces the rear motor assembly. A GM-related patent explains the idea: a degraded signal shows as a large mismatch between sine and cosine amplitudes. P0A45 is a full signal loss. Expect a hybrid warning and loss of motor B drive.
c: Resolver of motor B delivering unequal or distorted sine/cosine signals
High contact resistance or moisture in the resolver connector
Fault inside the rear motor assembly incl. bearing damage (Mitsubishi)
Damaged shielding letting inverter noise into the resolver lines
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Rear or second motor disabled, reduced traction or power
Jerky torque delivery before the fault sets

P0A47.t: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Low
P0A47.d: P0A47 means a resolver signal of motor B is below its allowed range, typically from a sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground or a shorted coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Mitsubishi files low resolver signals of the 2023 Outlander PHEV rear motor under its own codes instead: P0C57 for sine and P0C61 for cosine at 0.3 V or less for 0.18 s. Kia uses the motor A twin P0A41 on the Optima Hybrid and blames shorts or pin fit in the sub-harness. CARB 1968.2 requires circuit monitoring of electric drive components, and Bosch patents show how a ground short is told apart by line offset. P0A48 is the high side, P0A45 the general circuit fault. Expect a warning lamp and reduced motor B drive.
c: Resolver sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground
Poor pin fit or water ingress at the motor B resolver connector
Shorted resolver coil inside motor B
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control module
s: MIL or hybrid service lamp
Second motor disabled, reduced traction or power
Fault may come and go with vibration or moisture

P0A48.t: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit High
P0A48.d: P0A48 reports a motor B resolver line reading above its allowed range, for example a sine, cosine or excitation wire shorted to a supply voltage, or an open coil whose line is pulled up by the input bias circuit until the converter clips. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Mitsubishi handles high resolver voltages on the 2023 Outlander PHEV with its own codes (P0C53/P0C5D at 4.9 V or more on the front motor, P0C58/P0C62 on the rear), and Kia uses the motor A twin P0A42 on the Optima Hybrid. CARB 1968.2 requires circuit checks of electric drive components; Bosch patents describe detecting an open sine or cosine line and a short to supply. P0A47 is the low side. Expect a warning lamp and loss of motor B.
c: Resolver line shorted to a supply voltage
Open sine or cosine line pulled high by the input circuit
Corroded or loose terminals at the motor B resolver connector
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control module
s: MIL and hybrid system warning
Second motor disabled, reduced traction or power
Vehicle may not enter ready mode

P0A49.t: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A49.d: P0A49 covers short dropouts or jumps in the motor B resolver signal that are too brief to count as a lasting loss, low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The motor A twin P0A43 is used by Stellantis on the Pacifica Hybrid, where dealers must check bulletins and reflash the hybrid control processor before replacing the power inverter module. GM shows on the Bolt that a slightly spread resolver terminal can cause brief signal loss and a sudden loss of drive, and forbids splicing resolver connectors because the circuits are sensitive. CARB 1968.2 requires detection of intermittent circuit faults of drive components. P0A45 is the permanent fault. Expect a warning that may clear after a restart.
c: Loose or spread terminal in the motor B resolver connector
Chafed or stretched resolver wiring near the rear axle or subframe
Moisture in the connector causing intermittent leakage
Hybrid control software needing an update
s: Hybrid warning or MIL that comes and goes
Brief loss of second-motor drive, often over bumps
Code stored as history without current symptoms

P0A4A.t: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Overspeed
P0A4A.d: P0A4A reports that the speed calculated from the motor B resolver exceeds the motor's permitted maximum. Mitsubishi uses it for the rear motor of the 2023 Outlander PHEV: set at 12,500 rpm or more for at least 1 s with supply above 8 V, and only judged once the rear position sensor codes P0A45, P0A46, P0C57, P0C58, P0C61 and P0C62 are ruled out; otherwise the rear motor assembly is replaced, bearing damage being one listed cause. GM uses its own code P1B0E (above 11,500 rpm, Type A) for this check on the second motor of its two-mode trucks. CARB 1968.2 requires monitoring of electric drive components. P0A44 is the motor A twin. Expect the rear motor to be shut off to protect it, with less traction.
c: Fault in the rear motor assembly, e.g. damaged bearing or control unit (Mitsubishi)
Real overspeed from rear wheel spin on low grip
Disturbed resolver signal producing a false speed value
s: Rear electric drive shut off, front-wheel drive only
Hybrid/EV warning and MIL
Reduced acceleration in limp mode

P0A4B.d: P0A4B covers the resolver that tells the inverter where the generator rotor stands; without a valid angle the generator cannot be commutated. Mitsubishi (Outlander PHEV 2023) runs the check continuously once the generator control unit has at least 8.0 V and sets P0A4B when its internal status flags stay failed for 0.23 s or 0.28 s; low and high signal levels go to separate codes there. Volvo lists P0A4B in the inverter generator module of its 2022-23 plug-in hybrids, as permanent or intermittent fault, with no-start complaints, and fixed false detections by software only. P0A4C is the plausibility check, P0A4D/P0A4E the low and high signal, P0A4F a sporadic signal, P0A50 overspeed. The driver sees a hybrid warning and may lose electric drive or engine start.
c: Damaged resolver wiring or connector between generator and inverter
False detection in the inverter monitor software (Volvo, fixed by update)
Resolver evaluation in the power drive unit faulty
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Engine does not start or crank in hybrid mode
Electric drive or charging by the generator disabled

P0A4C.d: P0A4C means the generator resolver delivers signals that are electrically present but implausible, so the computed rotor angle cannot be trusted. Mitsubishi documents the exact limits for the 2023 Outlander PHEV: the sine or cosine winding voltage must stay between 2.1 and 2.9 V; if either leaves that window for 0.28 s, or an internal status fault persists for 0.31 s, the generator control unit stores P0A4C. Typical triggers are a corroded or loose resolver plug, a chafed shield picking up noise, a winding that has drifted, or a faulty input stage in the power drive unit. P0A4B is the general circuit fault, P0A4D and P0A4E the hard low and high signal, P0A4F a sporadic dropout. Expect a hybrid warning, reduced power and possibly no engine start via the generator.
c: Damaged shielding letting interference onto the sine/cosine lines
Resolver winding drifted out of tolerance
Faulty resolver input stage in the power drive unit
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Reduced drive power or engine-only operation
Engine start via the generator not possible

P0A4D.d: P0A4D reports a generator resolver signal stuck below its permitted range, as caused by a sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground or a winding short. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Mitsubishi shows how the fault is judged but files it under its own codes: on the 2023 Outlander PHEV a sine or cosine voltage at or below 2.0 V for 0.21 s sets P0C66 or P0C6B instead of P0A4D. A Bosch patent describes distinguishing a short to ground from a short to supply by the offset of the receiver coil lines, which is the basis for low/high splitting. CARB requires such circuit checks for hybrid input components. P0A4E is the high side, P0A4B the general circuit fault, P0A4C plausibility. The hybrid system typically shuts the generator down and warns the driver.
c: Sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the resolver connector
Shorted resolver winding inside the generator
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Generator disabled, engine-only or no-start condition

P0A4E.d: P0A4E is set when a generator resolver signal sits above its permitted range, which usually points to an open signal line pulled up by the input circuit or a short to a supply voltage. No manufacturer documents P0A4E publicly. Mitsubishi evaluates the same condition on the 2023 Outlander PHEV but reports it under its own codes: a sine or cosine voltage of 4.9 V or more for 0.21 s stores P0C67 or P0C6C. A Bosch patent explains how the averaged offset of the receiver coil lines reveals whether a line is shorted to supply rather than to ground. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A4D is the low counterpart, P0A4B the general circuit code, P0A4C the plausibility check. The generator is usually shut off and the hybrid warning comes on.
c: Open resolver signal line or pushed-out terminal
Signal line shorted to a supply voltage
Faulty resolver input stage in the power drive unit
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Generator disabled, engine-only or no-start condition

P0A4F.d: P0A4F flags a generator resolver signal that drops out or jumps briefly and then recovers, as opposed to a steady fault. No manufacturer documents P0A4F publicly. Mitsubishi and Volvo handle short interruptions inside the general circuit code instead: Volvo lists P0A4B in its inverter generator module with the fault type intermittent, and Mitsubishi tells technicians to treat a resolver fault that cannot be reproduced as an intermittent malfunction of harness and connectors. CARB requires circuit continuity checks on hybrid input components. Loose terminals, fretting contacts, a chafed cable near moving parts or heat-related cracks are the usual suspects. P0A4B is the steady circuit fault, P0A4C plausibility, P0A4D/P0A4E low and high. Symptoms come and go, often with a brief loss of hybrid function.
c: Loose or fretting terminals in the resolver connectors
Chafed resolver cable that breaks contact under vibration
Heat-related cracks in wiring or solder joints
s: Hybrid warning that appears and clears again
Short loss of electric drive or jerky power delivery
Fault often linked to bumps or heat

P0A50.d: P0A50 says the generator speed derived from its resolver has exceeded the permitted maximum. Mitsubishi documents it for the 2023 Outlander PHEV: with at least 8.0 V at the generator control unit and the position sensor itself judged healthy, a speed of 15,500 rpm or more lasting 0.5 s stores P0A50, and the repair path ends with replacing the generator. Because a resolver fault would already be caught by P0A4B to P0A4F, an overspeed entry usually reflects a real mechanical overspeed, for example from a transaxle or clutch problem, or an internal generator fault. The drive motor counterparts are P0A44 and P0A4A. CARB requires hybrid components to be monitored. Expect a hybrid warning and the generator being shut off to protect it.
c: Internal generator fault (Mitsubishi repair path ends with generator replacement)
Mechanical fault in the transaxle or clutch letting the generator overrun
Incorrect speed calculation in the power drive unit
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Generator shut off, reduced power or engine-only drive

P0A51.t: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit
P0A51.d: P0A51 reports a fault in the circuit of the current sensor that measures the phase current of drive motor A. The inverter needs this value for torque control and overcurrent protection. No manufacturer documents P0A51 publicly with its criteria. A Toyota patent shows the principle: a control sensor and a monitoring sensor measure the same motor current, and if the control sensor sits in its ground-short range or the two differ beyond a threshold over several cycles, the system flags the sensor and opens the main relays, because a wrong reading could drive the inverter into overcurrent. CARB requires circuit checks of hybrid input components. P0A52 covers plausibility, P0A53/P0A54 low and high; P0A55 is motor B. The hybrid system usually shuts down drive motor A.
c: Current sensor in the inverter assembly failed
Sensor supply or signal line interrupted inside the inverter
Evaluation circuit on the motor control board faulty
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Drive motor A disabled, vehicle may not move or runs on engine only

P0A52.t: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A52.d: P0A52 means the current sensor of drive motor A delivers values that are electrically valid but do not fit the operating state. Typical checks compare the reading at zero current with its expected offset, or compare redundant sensors with each other. No manufacturer documents P0A52 publicly. A Hyundai patent describes compensating the sensor offset while no current flows and declaring the compensation abnormal when the offset leaves its allowed band; a Toyota patent compares a control sensor with a monitoring sensor and flags a lasting difference. CARB requires rationality checks of hybrid input components. P0A51 is the general circuit fault, P0A53 and P0A54 the hard low and high signal. A wrong current reading can cause torque errors, so the system limits or disables drive motor A.
c: Sensor offset drifted beyond the compensation range
Control and monitoring sensor disagree due to one degraded sensor
Electrical interference or poor ground on the sensor signal
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Reduced or jerky electric drive
Drive motor A disabled, engine-only operation

P0A53.t: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0A53.d: P0A53 is stored when the current sensor signal of drive motor A stays below its valid range, typically from a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a failed Hall element. No manufacturer documents P0A53 publicly. A Toyota patent explains why this matters: a sensor stuck in its ground-short range reports far less current than actually flows, so the current controller keeps raising the drive and can push the inverter into overcurrent; the described system therefore turns off the system relay and warns the driver once the condition repeats over consecutive cycles. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A54 is the high counterpart, P0A51 the general circuit code, P0A52 plausibility. Drive motor A is shut down.
c: Sensor signal line shorted to ground
Hall element of the current sensor failed
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
High-voltage system switched off, vehicle may not move

P0A54.t: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit High
P0A54.d: P0A54 signals that the current sensor output of drive motor A sits above its valid range, as caused by an open ground, a short to the sensor supply or an internal sensor fault that saturates the output. No manufacturer documents P0A54 publicly. Patents from Toyota and Hyundai show how inverter controllers judge current sensors: by checking the reading against fixed electrical limits, by comparing a control and a monitoring sensor, and by verifying the offset while no current flows. A reading pinned high would make the controller cut drive torque or trigger overcurrent protection without reason. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A53 is the low side, P0A51 the general circuit fault, P0A52 plausibility, P0A58 the same check on motor B.
c: Open ground of the current sensor
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply
Internal sensor fault with saturated output
s: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Drive motor A disabled or power strongly reduced

P0A55.t: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit
P0A55.d: P0A55 is the general circuit fault of the current sensor that measures the current of drive motor B, typically the second traction motor, for example on a rear axle. The inverter needs this signal for torque control and to protect its power switches. No manufacturer documents P0A55 publicly. A Toyota patent shows the principle behind such checks: a control sensor and a monitoring sensor watch the same motor current, and a sensor stuck in its ground-short range or a lasting gap between the two leads to the relays opening. CARB requires circuit checks of hybrid input components. P0A56 is plausibility, P0A57/P0A58 low and high; P0A51 is the same fault on motor A. Usually drive motor B is switched off and the car drives on reduced power.
c: Current sensor of drive motor B failed (usually inside the inverter)
Sensor supply or signal line interrupted or shorted
Evaluation circuit on the motor B control board faulty
s: Hybrid or electric drive warning with MIL
Drive motor B disabled, loss of electric all-wheel drive or reduced power

P0A56.t: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A56.d: P0A56 means the current sensor of drive motor B delivers electrically valid values that do not match the operating state, for example a zero-current offset outside its band or a reading that disagrees with a redundant sensor. No manufacturer documents P0A56 publicly. A Hyundai patent covering both the traction motor and the starter-generator flags an abnormal offset compensation by comparing an estimated power-module temperature with the measured inverter temperature; a Caterpillar patent checks that the phase currents of a motor add up to roughly zero. CARB requires rationality checks of hybrid input components. P0A55 is the general circuit fault, P0A57/P0A58 the hard low and high signal, P0A52 the motor A counterpart. Motor B is limited or switched off.
c: Current sensor offset drifted or offset learning disturbed
Current sensor of drive motor B degraded
Electrical interference on the sensor signal
s: Hybrid warning and MIL
Reduced or missing drive from motor B

P0A57.t: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0A57.d: P0A57 is set when the signal of the drive motor B current sensor stays below its valid range, usually from a signal line shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a failed Hall element. No manufacturer documents P0A57 publicly. A Toyota patent explains the risk of this failure: a sensor held in its ground-short range reports much less current than really flows, the current controller raises its output and can drive the inverter into overcurrent; the system described therefore opens the system relays and warns the driver once the condition repeats. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A58 is the high side, P0A55 the general circuit code, P0A56 plausibility, P0A53 the same check on motor A. Motor B is shut down.
c: Sensor signal line shorted to ground
Hall element of the current sensor failed
s: Hybrid warning and MIL
Drive motor B or the whole high-voltage system switched off

P0A58.t: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit High
P0A58.d: P0A58 reports that the output of the drive motor B current sensor sits above its valid range, for instance from an open sensor ground, a short to the sensor supply or an internal fault that saturates the output. No manufacturer documents P0A58 publicly. Patents from Toyota and Hyundai show how motor controllers judge their current sensors: against fixed electrical limits, by comparing a control with a monitoring sensor, and by checking the zero-current offset. A reading pinned high would make the controller withdraw torque or trip overcurrent protection although nothing is wrong in the motor. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A57 is the low side, P0A55 the general circuit fault, P0A56 plausibility, P0A54 the motor A equivalent.
c: Sensor ground open or high resistance
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply
s: Hybrid warning and MIL
Drive motor B disabled, reduced power

P0A59.d: P0A59 is the general circuit fault of the current sensor on the hybrid generator, the electric machine driven by the engine that charges the battery and often starts the engine. Its inverter uses the current reading to control generator torque. No manufacturer documents P0A59 publicly with criteria. Patents describe the same sensing on generators: Toyota for a motor that also works as an engine-driven generator, Hyundai for the hybrid starter-generator, where two phases are measured and the third is calculated, and Caterpillar for generator and traction motor sensors. CARB requires circuit checks of hybrid input components. P0A5A is plausibility, P0A5B/P0A5C low and high. Without a valid reading the generator is disabled, so charging and engine start can be affected.
c: Generator current sensor failed (usually inside the inverter)
Sensor supply or signal line interrupted or shorted
Evaluation circuit on the generator control board faulty
s: Hybrid warning and MIL
Engine runs constantly or the high-voltage battery is no longer charged
Vehicle may not enter ready mode

P0A5A.d: P0A5A means the generator current sensor delivers values that are electrically valid but implausible, for example a wrong zero offset or phase currents that no longer add up. No hybrid manufacturer documents P0A5A publicly with criteria. A Hyundai patent for a motor and hybrid starter-generator system measures two phase currents, derives the third from the zero-sum rule and detects a faulty offset compensation by comparing estimated power-module temperature with measured inverter temperature. A Caterpillar patent flags sensors on generator and traction motor when the phase currents do not sum to near zero. CARB requires rationality checks of hybrid input components. P0A59 is the circuit fault, P0A5B/P0A5C the hard low and high signal. The generator is limited or switched off.
c: Generator current sensor offset drifted or offset learning disturbed
Control module calibration requiring an update
s: Hybrid warning and MIL
Reduced charging or engine running more often

P0A5B.d: P0A5B indicates that the signal of the generator current sensor stays below its valid range, as caused by a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a failed sensing element. No hybrid manufacturer documents P0A5B publicly with criteria. A Toyota patent covering a motor that also serves as an engine-driven generator shows why the low side is critical: a sensor held in its ground-short range under-reports the real current, the controller keeps increasing the drive, and overcurrent becomes possible, so the system opens its relays after repeated detection. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A5C is the high side, P0A59 the circuit fault, P0A5A plausibility, P0A57 the motor B equivalent. Generator operation stops.
c: Sensor signal line shorted to ground
Sensing element of the generator current sensor failed
s: Hybrid warning and MIL
High-voltage system switched off or battery no longer charged

P0A5C.d: P0A5C means the generator current sensor output lies above its valid range, typically from an open sensor ground, a short to the sensor supply or a saturated sensor. No hybrid manufacturer documents P0A5C publicly with criteria. Patents describe how controllers of engine-driven generators and starter-generators supervise their current sensors: Toyota with a control and a monitoring sensor plus fixed signal limits, Hyundai with an offset check on the two measured phases from which the third is calculated. A falsely high reading makes the controller reduce generator torque or trip overcurrent protection. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A5B is the low side, P0A59 the circuit fault, P0A5A plausibility, P0A58 the motor B counterpart.
c: Sensor ground open or high resistance
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply
Generator current sensor with saturated output
s: Hybrid warning and MIL
Generator disabled, engine start or battery charging affected

P0A5D.t: Drive Motor A Phase U Current
P0A5D.d: P0A5D concerns the current in phase U of drive motor A, as seen by the inverter. Audi documents it on the 2021-23 Q5 e quattro (bulletin 2069917/1): P0A5D00, often with P0A6000 and P0A6300, is stored in the electric drive control module J841, the cluster reads Drive system: fault and the car may not start or drive. The cause was variance in welding the high-voltage phase conductors; the fix is a resistance and wiggle test of each phase lead and a new motor harness. Many inverters do not measure U at all: a Hyundai patent measures two phases and calculates the third from the zero-sum rule, so a U fault can also stem from the V or W sensor. P0A5E/P0A5F are the low and high variants, P0A60 and P0A63 phases V and W.
c: High-voltage phase cable or weld joint to drive motor A faulty (Audi Q5 e quattro)
Phase current sensor in the inverter failed
Winding fault in phase U of drive motor A
s: Drive system fault message and MIL
Vehicle does not start or the drive system cannot be activated

P0A5E.t: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Low
P0A5E.d: P0A5E means too little current flows, or is sensed, in phase U of drive motor A, the classic sign of an open phase. GM describes the check for the motor control processor of the 2016 Chevrolet Volt and in its 2018 hybrid tables: with the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V and a squared current command above 900 A2 (2016) or 4,900 A2 (2018), the absolute U current is sampled while the rotor is within 30 degrees of the U phase axis; below 9 A for 0.4 s of a 0.6 s window, P0A5E sets as Type A, MIL on the first trip. Each phase is tested in turn as the rotor turns. A Caterpillar patent likewise spots a dead sensor by a phase reading near zero. P0A61 and P0A64 are phases V and W, P0A5F the high side, P0A5D the general U code.
c: Open circuit in the phase U cable, connector or terminal
Phase U current sensor reads zero
Phase U switch of the inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase U in drive motor A
s: MIL and propulsion system warning
Rough or reduced electric drive, possible engine-only operation

P0A5F.t: Drive Motor A Phase U Current High
P0A5F.d: P0A5F reports excessive current in phase U of drive motor A, a condition the inverter treats as overcurrent. Hyundai documents it on the 2017 Ioniq Hybrid (bulletin 17-01-057-1, campaign T2J): coolant leaking inside the traction motor set the Check Engine and hybrid lights with P0A5F, P0A62 or P0A65, often together with the isolation fault P0AA6; drivers noticed weak acceleration and a dead air conditioner. The procedure runs an insulation breakdown test with the scan tool and replaces the motor if it fails. A Hyundai patent shows such inverters measure two phases and calculate the third. P0A5E is the low side, P0A5D the general U code, P0A62 and P0A65 the same overcurrent on V and W.
c: Internal coolant leak in the traction motor causing insulation breakdown (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)
Shorted winding or phase lead of drive motor A
Inverter power stage fault in phase U
s: Check Engine and hybrid warning lights
Reduced power when accelerating
Air conditioning inoperative (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)

P0A60.t: Drive Motor A Phase V Current
P0A60.d: P0A60 covers the current in phase V of drive motor A. Toyota uses it with sub codes: a field report filed with NHTSA describes a 2006 Highlander Hybrid whose master warning lit and which would not move; P0A60 sub code 501 had set first, followed by P0A63, P0A78 and P0AEF, all returning at once after clearing, and the inverter assembly was replaced. Another Highlander showed P0A60 and P0A63 together with the generator phase codes P0A72 and P0A75, again an inverter fault; Toyota lists only V and W phases there, matching inverters that measure two phases and calculate the third. Audi stores P0A6000 on the 2021-23 Q5 e quattro for a faulty high-voltage phase lead. P0A61/P0A62 are low and high, P0A5D and P0A63 phases U and W.
c: Internal fault in the inverter assembly (Toyota Highlander Hybrid)
High-voltage phase V cable or weld joint faulty (Audi Q5 e quattro)
Winding fault in phase V of drive motor A
s: Master warning or drive system fault message, MIL
Vehicle will not move or start

P0A61.t: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Low
P0A61.d: P0A61 indicates that phase V of drive motor A carries, or reports, too little current when it should be near its peak, pointing to an open phase V circuit. GM uses the same peak-axis test as for phase U on the 2016 Chevrolet Volt motor control processor and in its 2018 hybrid tables, here with the rotor within 30 degrees of the V phase axis: inverter above 50 V in normal PWM, squared current command above 900 A2 in 2016 and 4,900 A2 from 2018, a peak phase current under 9 A for 0.4 s within 0.6 s, Type A with MIL on the first trip. On inverters that sense only two phases a dead V sensor also corrupts the calculated third phase. A Caterpillar patent detects such a sensor by a near-zero phase reading. P0A62 is the high side, P0A5E and P0A64 cover U and W.
c: Open circuit in the phase V cable, connector or terminal
Phase V current sensor reads zero
Phase V switch of the inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase V in drive motor A
s: MIL and propulsion system warning
Jerky or weak electric drive

P0A62.t: Drive Motor A Phase V Current High
P0A62.d: P0A62 signals overcurrent in phase V of drive motor A. Hyundai lists it in bulletin 17-01-057-1 for the 2017 Ioniq Hybrid next to P0A5F, P0A65 and the isolation fault P0AA6: the bulletin traces them to coolant leaking inside the traction motor and checks the high-voltage insulation first. Check Engine and hybrid lights came on, acceleration weakened and the air conditioning stopped. The dealer first runs an isolation breakdown test with the scan tool, then checks the motor for coolant and replaces it if needed.
