As a related case, GM's bulletin 18-NA-342 describes a Chevrolet Volt showing Battery Too Cold, Plug in to Warm above -25 °C because of faulty temperature sensor readings, fixed by reprogramming. CARB requires hybrid battery temperature inputs and their plausibility to be monitored. Distinguish a genuinely cold pack, which warms up on the charger or through the battery heater, from a sensor or heater fault; sensor circuit faults have their own codes.
c: Vehicle parked unplugged in extreme cold
Battery heater or coolant heater not working
Temperature sensor reading too cold (sensor or software)
s: Battery too cold message in the cluster
Reduced electric power or electric drive unavailable
Charging slow or not possible until the pack warms up

P0AFE.t: Hybrid/EV Battery System Voltage Too Low for Voltage Step Up Conversion
P0AFE.d: Many hybrids raise the battery voltage with a step-up (boost) converter before it reaches the inverters; Toyota's second-generation Hybrid Synergy Drive, for example, boosts a pack of around 200 V to 500 V or more. The converter needs a minimum input voltage to reach its target without excessive current. P0AFE is set when the battery-side voltage is below that minimum, so the converter cannot boost properly. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires hybrid components such as converters to be monitored for functional faults. A deeply discharged or weak pack, a high-resistance connection or a voltage measurement fault are the obvious suspects. Expect reduced electric assist; a low pack voltage is reported separately as P0AFA.
c: Pack deeply discharged or weak under load
High-resistance connection between battery and converter
Converter input voltage measured too low
s: Hybrid system warning
Reduced acceleration and electric assist
Engine runs more often than usual

P0AFF.t: System Voltage Too Low for Voltage Step Down Conversion
P0AFF.d: A step-down (buck) DC/DC converter, often called the accessory power module, supplies the 12 V system from the high-voltage or 48 V bus. To regulate its output it needs an input voltage above a minimum. P0AFF is set when the input system voltage is too low for this conversion, so the converter cannot hold its 12 V output. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM monitors the related function in its 2013 eAssist table: P0CA2 flags a step-down failure of the 14 V power module after a shoot-through fault in its switching device, one trip, Type A. CARB requires such hybrid components to be monitored. Expect a charging system warning and a slowly draining 12 V battery.
c: High-voltage or 48 V bus voltage too low (discharged pack, open contactor)
High-resistance input connection or fuse of the DC/DC converter
s: Battery or charging system warning light
12 V battery discharges, electrical consumers fail
Hybrid or start-stop functions restricted

P0B00.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current
P0B00.d: P0B00 is the general fault for phase U of the three-phase motor that drives the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump, the pump that keeps line pressure while the engine is stopped. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM, which runs such pumps on the Volt, ELR, Spark EV and CT6, monitors phase U instead with the low-side code P0B01 and catches overcurrent on any phase with P0C28. A Hitachi patent for an idle-stop sub-oil pump shows that the inverter often derives every phase current from one DC-bus shunt, so a U fault may come from the shared sensor rather than the phase itself. Expect a warning lamp, a stopped pump and, depending on design, no engine auto-stop or a no-start. P0B01/P0B02 are the low and high variants, P0B03 and P0B06 phases V and W.
c: Loose, corroded or unlatched phase U connection at the pump motor
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty (shunt or phase sensor)
Power stage of phase U in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase U of the pump motor
s: MIL or hybrid/transmission warning message
Engine auto-stop disabled or no electric drive mode
Delayed engagement or harsh restart after a stop

P0B01.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current Low
P0B01.d: P0B01 means the pump inverter sees almost no current in phase U of the auxiliary fluid pump motor, typically an open phase. GM documents the check for the Volt motor control processor (2016) and its hybrid tables of 2018 and 2019: with the drive state in Run, the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V and a squared current command above 5 A2 (2016) or 14.97 A2 (2018), the peak current on the U axis is compared while the rotor is within 30 degrees of it; below 1 A for 0.4 s of a 0.6 s window, the code sets as Type A, MIL on the first trip. On the 2014-15 Chevrolet Spark EV, GM bulletin PI1433 links P0B01, P0B04 or P0B07, Service Vehicle Soon and reduced propulsion to an unlatched pump connector. P0B04/P0B07 are phases V and W, P0B02 the high side.
c: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase U lead or terminal of the pump motor cable
Phase U switch in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase U in the pump motor
s: Service Vehicle Soon light and MIL
Propulsion Power Reduced or Vehicle Speed Limited message

P0B02.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current High
P0B02.d: P0B02 reports excessive current in phase U of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor, an overcurrent condition that the pump inverter must cut off to protect its switches. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM handles the same case differently: on the Volt and later hybrids it sets P0C28 when the absolute current of any phase exceeds 35 A for a few milliseconds, Type A. A phase-specific high code therefore points to a shorted U lead, a shorted winding, a jammed pump or a U current sensor reading too high. The Hitachi idle-stop pump patent shows phase currents being reconstructed from one bus shunt, which makes a sensing error a real candidate. The pump usually stops; auto-stop or electric driving is blocked. P0B01 is the low side, P0B05 and P0B08 the same fault on V and W.
c: Phase U lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump binding mechanically, raising motor current
Current sensing in the pump inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in phase U of the pump motor
s: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump shuts down, auto-stop disabled
Harsh or delayed engagement after an engine stop

P0B03.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase V Current
P0B03.d: P0B03 covers a general current fault in phase V of the brushless motor of the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump. No manufacturer publicly describes a monitor for it. GM's 2013 eAssist (BAS Plus) tables name P0B03 only once, as a code that must be inactive before another speed check runs, without a description of its own. In GM's Volt and CT6 tables phase V is watched by the low-side code P0B04, and any overcurrent goes to P0C28. A GM, BMW and Daimler patent on a hybrid transmission pump explains why the pump matters: it must hold transmission pressure when the engine is stopped, otherwise gear engagement can be lost. The general code is a catch-all for implausible V current that fits neither low nor high. P0B04/P0B05 are the low and high variants, P0B00 and P0B06 phases U and W.
c: Poor contact in the phase V lead or pump connector
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Phase V power stage in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase V of the pump motor
s: MIL or transmission/hybrid warning
Engine auto-stop or electric mode no longer available

P0B04.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase V Current Low
P0B04.d: P0B04 indicates that phase V of the auxiliary fluid pump motor carries too little current, usually because the phase is open somewhere between inverter and winding. GM tests it on the Volt (2016) and in the 2018 and 2019 hybrid tables like its U and W siblings: in Run, with normal PWM, more than 50 V on the inverter and a minimum squared current command, the V current is sampled while the rotor sits within 30 degrees of the V axis. Under 1 A for 0.4 s out of 0.6 s (0.08 s windows in 2019) sets a Type A fault. GM bulletin PI1433 for the 2014-15 Spark EV names P0B04 with Service Vehicle Soon and reduced propulsion and points to the pump connector not being latched. P0B01 and P0B07 are phases U and W, P0B05 the high side, P0B03 the general V code.
c: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase V lead or terminal
Phase V switch in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase V in the pump motor
s: Service Vehicle Soon light and MIL
Reduced propulsion power or limited vehicle speed

P0B05.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase V Current High
P0B05.d: P0B05 flags overcurrent in phase V of the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor. No manufacturer publicly documents this specific code. GM monitors the same physical fault without naming the phase: P0C28 trips when any of U, V or W exceeds 35 A for about 10 ms within a 62 ms window, and a 2018 Cadillac CT6 plug-in service update shows how a faulty pump restart routine alone can push the current over that limit. Likely triggers for a V-specific high code are a short in the V lead, shorted turns, a seized or contaminated pump, or a restart against a stalled rotor. The Hitachi patent on sub-oil pump drives shows the phase currents come from a shared sensor. Auto-stop is usually blocked. P0B04 is the low side, P0B02 and P0B08 phases U and W.
c: Phase V lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump seized or contaminated, motor draws excess current
Pump restart logic in the inverter software causing overcurrent
Shorted turns in phase V of the pump motor
s: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Loss of propulsion or no-start in severe cases

P0B06.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current
P0B06.d: P0B06 is the general current fault for phase W of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor. No manufacturer publishes a monitor description for this exact code. GM covers phase W in its Volt, ELR and CT6 calibrations with the low-side code P0B07 and treats overcurrent on any phase as P0C28. CARB requires hybrid and transmission components whose failure affects emissions or other monitors to be checked for circuit faults and rationality, which is why manufacturers can use the general code for implausible readings. The Hitachi sub-oil pump patent describes a sinusoidal drive whose W current is calculated from a single bus shunt, so wiring, sensing and the power stage are all suspects. The pump stops and auto-stop is blocked. P0B07/P0B08 are the low and high variants, P0B00 and P0B03 phases U and V.
c: Poor contact in the phase W lead or pump connector
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Phase W power stage in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase W of the pump motor
s: MIL or transmission/hybrid warning
Engine keeps running at stops, no auto-stop

P0B07.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current Low
P0B07.d: P0B07 means phase W of the auxiliary fluid pump motor carries less current than commanded, the typical sign of an open W path. GM uses it on the Volt and later hybrids: below 1 A peak W-axis current for 0.4 s of 0.6 s, with the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V, sets a Type A fault. A GM service update for the 2017-18 Cadillac CT6 plug-in shows the code had been calibrated off; a W phase loss then shut the car down or prevented starting with no code and no MIL, until reprogramming of the drive motor power inverter module enabled P0B07 as Type A. On the 2014-15 Spark EV, bulletin PI1433 ties P0B01, P0B04 or P0B07 to an unlatched pump connector. P0B01 and P0B04 are phases U and V, P0B08 the high side, P0B06 the general W code.
c: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase W lead or terminal
Outdated inverter software (Cadillac CT6 plug-in, service update 18199)
Open winding of phase W in the pump motor
s: MIL and Service Vehicle Soon light
Loss of propulsion, vehicle shutdown or no-start

P0B08.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current High
P0B08.d: P0B08 is set when the current in phase W of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor rises above the permitted limit. No manufacturer documents this exact code in public sources. In GM's 2016 Volt calibration the equivalent protection is P0C28, which fails on any phase above 35 A or on a d-axis current below a temperature-dependent limit, both within milliseconds to protect the IGBTs. A W-specific high code points to a short in the W lead or winding, a binding pump or a sensing error; the Hitachi patent shows the W value may be calculated rather than measured directly. CARB requires such output drivers to be monitored for circuit faults. The pump shuts down, so start-stop and electric driving are restricted. P0B07 is the low side, P0B02 and P0B05 phases U and V.
c: Phase W lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump binding mechanically, raising motor current
Current sensing in the pump inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in phase W of the pump motor
s: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump shuts down, auto-stop disabled

P0B09.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P0B09.d: P0B09 concerns the power feed of auxiliary pump A's motor: the controller sees no valid supply voltage, usually because the circuit is open. GM documents it for its 2012-13 eAssist mild hybrids (BAS Plus): the hardware input reports an out-of-range voltage flag on the auxiliary pump circuit, enabled with ignition voltage above 9 V; failing for at least 0.375 s within a 1.2 s sample sets P0B09 as Type B, MIL after two trips. A related GM check, P2797, verifies during auto-stops that the pump draws power and that turbine speed does not flare on restart. A Hitachi patent on a battery-fed sub-oil pump shows the controller inhibits engine auto-stop when pump current behaves abnormally. Typical results: no auto-stop and a lamp. P0B0A/P0B0B are the low and high variants.
c: Blown fuse or open relay in the pump supply
Open supply wire or loose terminal at the pump connector
Poor ground connection of the pump motor
Voltage sensing input in the controller faulty
s: Engine auto-stop no longer occurs
MIL after two drive cycles
Shift flare or delayed drive engagement on restart

P0B0A.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P0B0A.d: P0B0A means the supply voltage measured at the motor of auxiliary pump A is lower than expected while the pump should be running. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's eAssist tables only cover the open-circuit case as P0B09. A Mikuni patent shows why the controller measures this voltage at all: it combines motor current, supply voltage and speed to judge the hydraulic load, so a sagging supply also falsifies pump diagnosis. Causes are high resistance in the feed or ground, a weak 12 V battery, a failing DC/DC converter or a voltage drop when the pump starts. CARB requires circuit checks on such outputs. The pump runs slowly or not at all and start-stop is usually inhibited. P0B09 covers an open circuit, P0B0B a supply that is too high, P0562 low system voltage in general.
c: Corroded terminal or high resistance in the pump feed or ground
Weak 12 V battery or poor charging
DC/DC converter or alternator output too low (hybrid)
Voltage sensing input in the controller faulty
s: Start-stop function inactive
MIL or transmission warning
Jerky drive-off after an engine stop

P0B0B.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Supply Voltage Circuit High
P0B0B.d: P0B0B reports a supply voltage at the motor of auxiliary pump A that is above the expected range. Subaru documents it on the 2014-15 XV Crosstrek Hybrid (bulletin 16-94-15R), together with P172A: a leaking O-ring at the electric oil pump relief valve can let CVT fluid into the pump motor. The check removes the three U, V and W cables at the oil pump inverter and reads AC voltage across them with the engine held at 1800 rpm in Park; 0.5 V or more means the drive motor and case assembly with the damaged seal must be replaced, less means the cause lies elsewhere. Subaru adds that P0C79, drive motor inverter voltage too high, appears only together with these codes and does not mean the inverter is faulty. P0B09 and P0B0A are the open and low variants.
c: CVT fluid entering the pump motor via a leaking relief valve O-ring (Subaru XV Crosstrek Hybrid)
Supply circuit shorted to a higher voltage source
Oil pump inverter or its voltage sensing faulty
s: Warning lamp on, hybrid or CVT function restricted
Possibly P0C79 stored at the same time

P0B0C.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Hydraulic Leakage
P0B0C.d: P0B0C says the circuit fed by auxiliary pump A loses pressure through a leak, so the pump cannot hold the demanded pressure. Stellantis documents it as P0B0C 7A for the 2023-26 Jeep Avenger and 2026 Compass with hybrid dual-clutch transmission outside the US (TSB 21-061-26): an internal leak at the parking pawl locking piston causes jerking and power loss and may stop the engine from restarting after a stop; with P07E4 or P07E6 present and more than 5 km on the clock, the piston or the transmission is replaced. How a controller can see a leak shows a Nidec patent: after a speed change the pump current keeps falling instead of recovering, and the pump is stopped. P0B0B and P0B09 cover the supply, P2797 a pump that does not deliver.
c: Internal leak at the parking pawl locking piston (Jeep Avenger/Compass hybrid DCT)
Worn seal or valve leaking inside the hydraulic circuit
External leak and low transmission fluid level
Internal wear of the auxiliary pump
s: Jerking and loss of power while driving
Engine fails to restart after a stop
Transmission warning, possibly with P07E4 or P07E6

P0B0D.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Control Module
P0B0D.d: P0B0D is an internal fault of the module that drives the auxiliary pump motor. GM documents it for the auxiliary transmission pump controller (ATPC) in its 2011 and 2014 hybrid tables and for the 2016 Cadillac ELR: it checks processor integrity, such as SPI hardware faults or a wrong seed and key between processors, with more than 9.5 V supply; 28 failures out of 32 samples in a 6.25 ms loop, detected within about 200 ms, set a Type A fault. Stellantis lists P0B0D-00 on the 2021-25 Jeep Wrangler 4xe and 2022-25 Grand Cherokee 4xe with the 8P75PH plug-in transmission (TSB 21-038-25, revised 21-041-26): MIL and limp mode, sometimes with U0287; the fix is a new in-pan electric pump. U0287 is lost communication with the pump module, P0C23 to P0C25 its circuit.
c: Electric pump with integrated control electronics failed (Jeep 4xe 8P75PH)
Processor or memory fault inside the pump control module
Supply voltage dips or poor ground at the module
s: MIL on
Transmission in limp mode
Possibly lost communication with the pump module (U0287)

P0B0E.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit
P0B0E.d: Many packs measure current with two channels or two sensors so the controller can cross-check them; sensor B is the second channel next to sensor A (P0ABF to P0AC3). P0B0E is its general circuit code. Toyota uses it as the base of internal codes on the 2020-25 RAV4 Hybrid: the sensor sends a voltage rising with current on channel IB0 (sensor A) and an inverse one on IB1 (sensor B). P0B0E11 (IB1 too low) and P0B0E15 (IB1 too high or open) are reported to a generic scan tool as P0B10 and P0B11, one trip, MIL on. GM monitors its fine-range channel B with P0B10, P0B11 and the A/B correlation P0B13. CARB requires circuit monitoring. State of charge then becomes uncertain.
c: Signal or ground wire of channel B damaged or connector loose
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective
s: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery power limited, less electric assist
Implausible state-of-charge display

P0B0F.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B0F.d: P0B0F flags a current sensor B signal that is electrically in range but implausible, for example an offset at zero current or a value that does not match the other measurement. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM handles comparable faults differently: on its dual-range sensor, the 2019 table P0B13 compares sensors A and B and fails when they differ by more than 10 A while both read between -20 and 20 A, 400 of 500 samples at 25 ms, Type A; offset errors of sensor A are P0AC0. CARB requires rationality checks for hybrid battery inputs. A drifting current reading corrupts the state-of-charge calculation, so the controller tends to narrow the usable battery window.
c: Current sensor B offset drift or ageing
Ground offset or high resistance in the sensor wiring
Sensor displaced on the busbar or magnetic interference
s: Hybrid or EV warning, MIL possible
State of charge jumps or drifts
Reduced battery power

P0B10.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Low
P0B10.d: P0B10 means the output of current sensor B lies below its valid range. GM uses a dual-range Hall sensor whose channel B covers small currents with high resolution: the 2019 battery energy control module table sets P0B10 when this fine current reads below -24 A (ADC count under 82) for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; the 2011 Volt table uses -23 A for 175 ms within 250 ms, one trip. Toyota reports P0B10 for the 2020-25 RAV4 Hybrid when the inverse channel IB1 voltage is excessively low (internal code P0B0E11), one trip, MIL on immediately. A short to ground or a lost sensor supply is typical. The high-side code is P0B11.
c: Sensor B signal line shorted to ground
5 V supply of the current sensor missing
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective
s: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery charge and discharge power limited
Engine runs more often, fuel use rises

P0B11.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit High
P0B11.d: P0B11 is set when current sensor B delivers a signal above its valid range. In GM's dual-range design, channel B is the fine channel for small currents: the 2019 battery energy control module table fails it above +24 A (ADC count over 4013) for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and the 2011 Volt table above +23 A for 175 ms within 250 ms, one trip. Toyota maps its internal code P0B0E15, excessively high or open IB1 channel voltage, to P0B11 on the 2020-25 RAV4 Hybrid, with one-trip logic and immediate MIL. An open ground, a signal shorted to the supply or a failed sensor are typical. The low-side code is P0B10, the sensor A equivalent P0AC2.
c: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply or 12 V
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective
s: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery power limited, less electric driving
Implausible state-of-charge display

P0B12.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B12.d: P0B12 covers a current sensor B signal that jumps or drops out in a way real current cannot, typically from a loose connector, a chafed signal wire or noise on the sensor ground. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM monitors its sensor B channel with the range limits P0B10 and P0B11 and compares it with sensor A through P0B13, which fails above a 10 A difference in 400 of 500 samples, Type A; an erratic channel often shows up there first. CARB requires circuit and rationality monitoring for hybrid battery inputs. Because the fault comes and goes, the code may be the only trace, but during dropouts the controller can still cut battery power or light a warning.
c: Loose connector or poor terminal contact at the current sensor
Electrical noise on the sensor ground
s: Intermittent hybrid or EV warning
Short power reductions during dropouts
Code stored without lasting symptoms

P0B13.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor A/B Correlation
P0B13.d: P0B13 compares the two pack current readings, sensor A and sensor B, and sets when they disagree. On the Chevrolet Volt GM pairs a coarse and a fine channel: the code fails when they differ by more than 10 A while both read between -20 and 20 A, for example 10 s within a 12.5 s window (2016) or 400 of 500 samples at 25 ms (2019), Type A, one trip. Bulletins show P0B13 on the GM Lyriq, Hummer EV and BrightDrop Zevo after suspect public chargers, and on the Audi Q5 PHEV and e-tron GT, where software of the battery controller caused it. Single-sensor faults use P0ABF to P0AC3 and P0B0E to P0B12. The driver sees a high-voltage warning and reduced power.
c: Battery controller software fault, fixed by update (Audi, GM)
Disturbance from an external charging station during charging
Offset drift of one of the two current channels
Internal communication fault between switching unit and current sensor
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Red battery or Service High Voltage message, request to stop safely
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Charging interrupted or refused

P0B14.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit
P0B14.d: SAE J2012 reserves up to four pack voltage measurements, A to D; voltage sense B is the second one. P0B14 is its general circuit code: the battery controller sees an electrical fault on this input, typically an open or implausible raw signal. Which tap a manufacturer calls B is not standardised. No manufacturer documents P0B14 publicly. For the comparable channel A GM checks pack-side voltage against fixed limits and against the sum of cell voltages (P0ABB to P0ABD). CARB requires battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems to be monitored like any input component. Range, low, high and erratic faults have their own codes, P0B15 to P0B18. The system usually limits or blocks high-voltage operation.
c: Voltage sense lead or its fuse open inside the pack
Sense connector at the battery controller loose or corroded
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B15.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B15.d: P0B15 marks pack voltage measurement B as electrically valid but implausible: the value lies within the sensor range yet does not match a reference, typically the sum of the cell voltages or another pack measurement. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM shows the principle on channel A: P0ABB fails when pack voltage and summed cell voltages differ by more than 12 V, 20 of 25 samples at 25 ms, Type A, one trip. CARB demands rationality checks for battery voltage sensors of the hybrid storage system. Hard circuit faults of channel B are P0B14, P0B16 and P0B17. Because state of charge and cell protection rely on this value, the controller restricts power or charging.
c: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel B
Faulty cell voltage acquisition distorts the reference sum
Increased contact resistance at sense terminals
Battery controller software needs an update
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Implausible state-of-charge or range display

P0B16.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Low
P0B16.d: P0B16 sets when pack voltage measurement B reports a value below its plausible minimum, usually an electrical cause such as a sense lead shorted to ground or an open input that pulls the reading down. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM uses the same logic on channel A: on its BECM P0ABC sets when the pack-side voltage drops below 24 V for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip. CARB requires out-of-range monitoring of battery voltage sensors in hybrid storage systems. The opposite fault is P0B17, implausible but in-range values are P0B15. Without a trustworthy pack voltage the controller may refuse to close the contactors or limit operation.
c: Sense lead of channel B shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B17.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit High
P0B17.d: P0B17 means pack voltage measurement B reads above its plausible maximum. Mercedes-Benz uses this exact code on the eSprinter 907: inaccurate BMS measurements can store P0B171C, voltage sensor B in the high-voltage battery module shorted to positive with the value out of range, together with P0ABD00 for sensor A. The result is an intermittent no-start or no Ready status, fixed by a BMS software update. GM checks channel A against 479 V on its BECM (P0ABD, Type A). CARB requires out-of-range monitoring of battery voltage sensors. The low counterpart is P0B16. A real overvoltage is not implied; the measurement itself is suspect.
c: BMS measurement inaccuracy, fixed by software update (Mercedes eSprinter)
Sense lead of channel B shorted to a higher potential
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
s: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B18.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B18.d: P0B18 reports that pack voltage measurement B jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. The controller detects implausibly fast changes or short signal losses that disappear again, so the fault often shows up as a history code. No manufacturer documents P0B18 publicly; GM, for example, monitors only channel A in its published tables (P0ABB to P0ABD). CARB requires battery voltage sensors of the hybrid storage system to be monitored for circuit faults. Steady faults of channel B use P0B14 to P0B17. Typical triggers are loose sense connectors or chafed leads that react to vibration and temperature, so symptoms come and go.
s: Warning appears and disappears, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B19.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit
P0B19.d: Voltage sense C is the third of up to four pack voltage measurements defined in SAE J2012. P0B19 is its general circuit code and sets when the battery controller finds this input electrically unusable, for instance open or without a valid raw value. Which measuring point a manufacturer assigns to C is its own choice. No manufacturer documents P0B19 publicly. GM shows the principle for channel A, checking pack-side voltage against limits and against the summed cell voltages (P0ABB to P0ABD). CARB requires battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems to be monitored as input components. The detailed fault types of channel C are P0B1A to P0B1D. High-voltage operation is usually limited.
c: Voltage sense lead C or its fuse open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B1A.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit Range/Performance
P0B1A.d: P0B1A flags pack voltage measurement C as in range but not believable. The controller compares it with a reference, usually the sum of the cell voltages or another pack voltage reading, and sets the code when the difference stays too large. No manufacturer documents P0B1A publicly. As an analogue, GM fails P0ABB on channel A once pack voltage and summed cell voltages differ by more than 12 V for 20 of 25 samples, Type A. CARB requires rationality monitoring for battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems. Electrical faults of channel C are P0B19, P0B1B and P0B1C. A distorted pack voltage undermines state of charge and cell protection, so power or charging is restricted.
c: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel C
Cell voltage acquisition faulty, reference sum wrong
Battery controller software needs an update
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Implausible state-of-charge or range display
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B1B.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit Low
P0B1B.d: P0B1B sets when pack voltage measurement C delivers a reading below its plausible lower limit. Typical electrical causes are a sense lead shorted to ground, an open fuse or resistor in the sense path, or a defective controller input. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM applies the same idea to channel A, where P0ABC sets below 24 V pack-side voltage for 1.6 s in a 2 s window, Type A. CARB calls for out-of-range monitoring of battery voltage sensors. The high counterpart is P0B1C and the plausibility code P0B1A. A pack voltage reading that is too low can prevent precharge and contactor closing, so the vehicle may not become ready to drive.
c: Sense lead of channel C shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
s: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B1C.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit High
P0B1C.d: P0B1C reports that pack voltage measurement C reads above its plausible upper limit. Usually the measurement path is at fault, for example a sense lead shorted to a higher potential, a defective controller input or a software error in the evaluation, rather than a real overvoltage of the pack. No manufacturer documents P0B1C publicly. GM checks channel A against a 479 V limit on its BECM (P0ABD, Type A, 1.6 s in 2 s), and Mercedes-Benz logs the matching channel B fault P0B17 on the eSprinter. CARB requires out-of-range monitoring of battery voltage sensors. The low counterpart is P0B1B. The controller typically blocks or limits high-voltage operation.
c: Sense lead of channel C shorted to a higher potential
Evaluation error in battery controller software
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B1D.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B1D.d: P0B1D stands for an unsteady pack voltage measurement C: the signal jumps, drops out for moments or changes faster than a real battery voltage can. Because the fault often clears itself, it is frequently found only as a stored code. No manufacturer documents P0B1D publicly; GM's published tables cover only channel A of this measurement (P0ABB to P0ABD). CARB requires circuit monitoring of battery voltage sensors in hybrid storage systems. Permanent faults of channel C are P0B19 to P0B1C, the same fault type on channels B and D is P0B18 and P0B22. Loose terminals, vibration and temperature changes are the usual suspects, so warnings tend to come and go.
c: Loose or corroded sense connector or terminal
Chafed sense lead with intermittent contact
s: Warning comes and goes, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B1E.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit
P0B1E.d: Voltage sense D is the fourth and last pack voltage measurement in the SAE J2012 scheme. P0B1E is its general circuit code: the battery controller treats this input as electrically faulty, for example open or without a usable raw signal. The assignment of D to a specific measuring point is manufacturer-specific. No manufacturer documents P0B1E publicly. GM illustrates the monitoring on channel A, comparing pack-side voltage with limits and with the summed cell voltages (P0ABB to P0ABD). CARB requires battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems to be monitored like other inputs. Detailed fault types of channel D are P0B1F to P0B22. High-voltage operation is usually restricted.
c: Voltage sense lead D or its fuse open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B1F.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit Range/Performance
P0B1F.d: P0B1F says pack voltage measurement D is electrically present but disagrees with what the controller expects, typically the sum of cell voltages or a parallel pack measurement. It is a plausibility fault, not an open or shorted circuit. No manufacturer documents P0B1F publicly. GM's analogous channel A check, P0ABB, fails at a deviation above 12 V from the summed cell voltages for 20 of 25 samples at 25 ms, Type A, one trip. CARB requires rationality checks for battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems. Circuit faults of channel D use P0B1E, P0B20 and P0B21. With a doubtful pack voltage the controller narrows the usable battery window and limits power.
c: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel D
Cell voltage acquisition faulty, reference sum wrong
Battery controller software needs an update
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Implausible state-of-charge or range display
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B20.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit Low
P0B20.d: P0B20 sets when pack voltage measurement D falls below its plausible minimum. The cause is usually electrical: a sense lead shorted to ground, an interrupted fuse or resistor in the measurement path, or a damaged controller input. No manufacturer documents P0B20 publicly. GM shows the analogous check on channel A, where its BECM sets P0ABC once pack-side voltage stays under 24 V for 1.6 s within 2 s, Type A, one trip. CARB requires out-of-range monitoring of battery voltage sensors in hybrid storage systems. The high counterpart is P0B21, plausibility faults are P0B1F. An implausibly low reading can block precharge, so the vehicle may not become ready.
c: Sense lead of channel D shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
s: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B21.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit High
P0B21.d: P0B21 means pack voltage measurement D reports more than its plausible maximum. As with the other high codes, the measurement path is the main suspect, for example a sense lead shorted to a higher potential, a faulty input stage or an evaluation error in software, not an actual overcharged pack. No manufacturer documents P0B21 publicly. For channel A GM's BECM sets P0ABD above 479 V for 1.6 s in 2 s, Type A, and Mercedes-Benz records the channel B variant P0B17 on the eSprinter. CARB requires out-of-range monitoring of battery voltage sensors. The low counterpart is P0B20. High-voltage operation is usually blocked or limited until the fault is cleared.
c: Sense lead of channel D shorted to a higher potential
Evaluation error in battery controller software
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
s: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B22.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B22.d: P0B22 completes the voltage sense D series and reports an intermittent or erratic pack voltage measurement D: the reading jumps, drops out briefly or changes implausibly fast, then recovers. Current code lists title it this way; the older label Generator Phase U Current Sensor Circuit does not belong to this number. No manufacturer documents P0B22 publicly; GM's published tables only cover channel A (P0ABB to P0ABD). CARB requires circuit monitoring of battery voltage sensors in hybrid storage systems. Steady faults of channel D are P0B1E to P0B21, the same fault type on channels B and C is P0B18 and P0B1D. Loose terminals or chafed sense leads are typical, so the warning comes and goes.
c: Loose or corroded sense connector or terminal
Chafed sense lead with intermittent contact
s: Warning comes and goes, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B23.d: P0B23 is the general fault for the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A, the first of up to four sub-batteries or energy stores (A to D) that the battery controller evaluates separately; which physical unit carries the letter is up to the manufacturer. The code says that the measured voltage of this unit no longer fits the expected value, without the finer split into unstable (P0B24), low (P0B25) or high (P0B26). No manufacturer documents P0B23 publicly; Bentley and Stellantis bulletins only show the specific siblings. GM watches the comparable whole-pack voltage with P0ABB to P0ABD. CARB requires the voltage sensors and cells of the hybrid storage to be monitored, with fault codes that point to the smallest replaceable unit.
c: Weak or failing cells or module in battery A
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery A
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Charging or recuperation restricted

P0B24.d: P0B24 reports that the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A is unstable: it swings or jumps more than the battery controller accepts instead of staying steadily too low or too high (P0B25, P0B26). Stellantis lists P0B24-00 with MIL on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe, together with pack voltage variation, cell balancing and state-of-health codes; the cure is new software for the battery pack control module or, on the 2025 Wrangler, for the hybrid control processor. Some of these Jeeps would not start or reported low 12 V batteries. Ford names P0B24 in the BECM of the 2025 Mustang Mach-E Extended Range, shown with the wrench lamp and fixed by reprogramming. Hardware causes are loose busbar or sense contacts.
c: Battery controller software (Jeep 4xe BPCM/HCP, Ford BECM updates)
Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery A
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery A
s: MIL on
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Vehicle may not start (Jeep 4xe)
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent

P0B25.d: P0B25 sets when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A drops below the window the controller expects. Bentley uses it in two different systems. In the 48 V Bentley Dynamic Ride anti-roll system it is stored in address 0021 (battery energy control module 2); if the highest and lowest cell readings differ by 0.5 V or more, an internal fault of the super capacitor is assumed and it is replaced. On the Bentayga and Flying Spur Hybrid the code appears in 008C, the high-voltage battery manager, with MIL and red battery warning, and the workshop must involve Bentley product support. GM checks pack undervoltage analogously with P0ABC (below 24 V). Unstable and high readings are P0B24 and P0B26. The driver loses roll control or battery power.
c: Internal fault of the energy store, e.g. Bentley 48 V super capacitor
Aged or unbalanced cells pulling the unit voltage down
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads
s: Bentley Dynamic Ride fault warning, roll control inactive
MIL on
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B26.d: P0B26 means the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A is above the permitted value. Bentley documents it in the 48 V Dynamic Ride system of the Continental GT and Flying Spur, stored in address 0021 with symptom code 28672; the prescribed repair is replacing the super capacitor. On the Bentayga it appeared with P16C5, traced to a broken solder joint inside the capacitor; on the Bentayga and Flying Spur Hybrid it shows up in the high-voltage battery manager 008C beside P0B25, with MIL and red HV warning. GM monitors the analogous pack overvoltage with P0ABD (above 479 V, Type A). Typical reasons are a failing energy store, an overcharged cell group or a measuring fault. Low and unstable readings are P0B25 and P0B24. Charging and recuperation are limited.
c: Failing energy store, e.g. Bentley 48 V super capacitor
Cell group charged too high, balancing not effective
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads
s: Bentley Dynamic Ride fault warning, roll control inactive
MIL on
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Charging or recuperation restricted

P0B27.d: P0B27 is the general voltage fault of hybrid/EV battery B, the second separately monitored sub-battery or energy store. It covers a voltage that does not match expectation without saying whether it is unstable (P0B28), too low (P0B29) or too high (P0B2A). That battery B exists in production systems is shown by Stellantis, whose Jeep Wrangler 4xe bulletin lists P0B28; P0B27 itself is not documented publicly by any manufacturer. GM's analogous monitors of the whole pack are P0ABB to P0ABD, for example a pack reading more than 12 V away from the sum of the cells. CARB requires the voltage sensors and cells of hybrid storage systems to be monitored. The driver gets a hybrid warning and reduced battery power.
c: Weak or failing cells or module in battery B
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery B
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Charging or recuperation restricted

P0B28.d: P0B28 flags an unstable voltage of hybrid/EV battery B: the reading fluctuates beyond what the battery controller tolerates. Stellantis documents it with P0B28-00 on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe: the MIL is on, and the bulletin warns that after 49 days with this MIL lit the vehicle is no longer allowed to start. The remedy is new software for the battery pack control module, issued first as a rapid service update and later as a regular bulletin; recall 95B must be completed first. The same bulletin lists P0B24 for battery A and codes for voltage variation and cell balancing. Steady low or high voltages of battery B are P0B29 and P0B2A. Besides software, loose busbar or sense contacts can produce the same pattern.
c: Battery pack control module software (Jeep 4xe update)
Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery B
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery B
s: MIL on
Start inhibited after a long period with the MIL lit (Jeep 4xe: 49 days)
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent

P0B29.d: P0B29 sets when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery B stays below the range the controller expects for the present state of charge and load. It is the low counterpart to P0B2A; fluctuating readings belong to P0B28 and the general fault to P0B27. No manufacturer publishes a definition of P0B29; Jeep 4xe bulletins confirm the use of a separately monitored battery B only through P0B28. GM handles the analogous whole-pack undervoltage with P0ABC (pack voltage below 24 V). CARB requires battery voltage sensors and cells to be monitored and the fault to be narrowed to the smallest replaceable unit. Weak or deeply discharged cells in that unit are the usual reason, so the controller cuts discharge power and may block driving in EV mode.
c: Aged cells with lost capacity in battery B
Deep discharge or self-discharge after standstill
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Electric-only driving unavailable

P0B2A.d: P0B2A is stored when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery B rises above its permitted upper limit. It mirrors P0B29 (too low), while P0B28 covers fluctuation and P0B27 the general fault. No manufacturer explains P0B2A publicly; the closest documented case is Bentley's P0B26 for battery A, where a failing 48 V super capacitor reads too high. GM's analogous whole-pack overvoltage monitor is P0ABD (above 479 V, Type A). CARB demands monitoring of battery voltage sensors and cells in hybrid storage systems. Likely causes are a cell group charged too high because balancing fails, or a measuring fault. To protect the cells the controller restricts charging and recuperation and may open the contactors.
c: Cell group in battery B charged too high, balancing ineffective
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Charging or recuperation restricted
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B2B.d: P0B2B is the general voltage fault of hybrid/EV battery C, the third sub-battery or energy store that a controller can monitor on its own. It signals an implausible voltage of this unit without the detail given by P0B2C (unstable), P0B2D (low) or P0B2E (high). Which modules form battery C, and whether a vehicle has a third unit at all, depends on the manufacturer; no manufacturer documents P0B2B publicly. As a reference GM monitors the voltage of the whole pack with P0ABB to P0ABD, among them a plausibility check against the cell sum. CARB requires voltage sensors and cells of hybrid storage to be monitored and faults to point to the replaceable unit. Expect a hybrid warning and limited battery power.
c: Weak or failing cells or module in battery C
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery C
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Charging or recuperation restricted

P0B2C.d: P0B2C indicates that the voltage of hybrid/EV battery C is unstable, meaning it changes faster or further than plausible for the current load, while a steady deviation would set P0B2D or P0B2E. No manufacturer documents P0B2C publicly. The pattern is known from the A and B siblings: on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe, P0B24 and P0B28 were cured with battery controller software, and Ford fixed P0B24 on the Mach-E the same way. CARB requires the voltage sensors of the hybrid storage to be monitored for circuit and rationality faults. Physically, a loose busbar screw, a corroded sense terminal or a cell with high internal resistance can make the voltage of unit C jump, so the warning often comes and goes.
c: Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery C
Battery controller software (pattern known from P0B24/P0B28)
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery C
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B2D.d: P0B2D means the voltage of hybrid/EV battery C is too low compared with what the controller expects. High readings of the same unit are P0B2E, fluctuating ones P0B2C. No manufacturer documents P0B2D publicly; the nearest published case is Bentley's P0B25 for battery A, where a 0.5 V spread between highest and lowest cell points to a defective energy store. GM's corresponding whole-pack check is P0ABC (pack below 24 V). CARB requires that cells and voltage sensors of hybrid storage are monitored and that faults identify the smallest replaceable unit. A worn or deeply discharged module in unit C is the most likely reason. The controller lowers discharge power, so acceleration in electric mode suffers and the engine may run more often.
c: Aged cells with lost capacity in battery C
Deep discharge or self-discharge after standstill
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Combustion engine runs more often (hybrid)

P0B2E.d: P0B2E is set when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery C exceeds its upper limit. It pairs with P0B2D for undervoltage; P0B2C covers unstable readings and P0B2B the general fault. No manufacturer publishes a description of P0B2E. GM's comparable monitor for the complete pack is P0ABD, which fails above 479 V and is Type A, so the MIL comes on at once. CARB requires monitoring of hybrid battery voltage sensors and cells and dedicated codes for the replaceable unit. An overvoltage reading usually comes from a cell group that ended up overcharged because balancing failed, or from a drifting measurement channel. The controller then blocks or reduces charging and regenerative braking; plugging in may be refused.
c: Cell group in battery C charged too high, balancing ineffective
Drifting voltage measurement channel or sense lead fault
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Charging or recuperation restricted
External charging refused

P0B2F.d: P0B2F is the general voltage fault of hybrid/EV battery D, the fourth and last sub-battery in this code family. The controller reports with it that the voltage of unit D is implausible, without specifying unstable (P0B30), low (P0B31) or high (P0B32). Only packs that the manufacturer splits into four separately monitored units can set it, and no manufacturer documents P0B2F publicly. For orientation, GM checks the whole pack with P0ABB to P0ABD, including a comparison of the pack voltage with the sum of all cells. CARB requires voltage sensors and cells of hybrid storage systems to be monitored, with codes pointing to the smallest replaceable unit. The driver sees a hybrid or battery warning and reduced power.
c: Weak or failing cells or module in battery D
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery D
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Charging or recuperation restricted

P0B30.d: P0B30 reports an unstable voltage of hybrid/EV battery D: the measured value fluctuates beyond the limit the controller allows. It differs from P0B31 and P0B32, which stand for a lasting low or high voltage, and from the general fault P0B2F. No manufacturer documents P0B30 publicly. The sibling codes for batteries A and B show the typical background: Stellantis and Ford corrected P0B24 and P0B28 by updating the battery controller software, and Jeep even blocks starting after 49 days with P0B28. CARB requires the hybrid storage voltage sensors to be monitored. Apart from software, poor contact at busbars or sense terminals and cells with high internal resistance make the reading of unit D jump.
c: Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery D
Battery controller software (pattern known from P0B24/P0B28)
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery D
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B31.d: P0B31 is stored when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery D stays below the expected range. High voltage of the same unit sets P0B32, fluctuation P0B30 and an unspecified deviation P0B2F. No manufacturer publishes a definition of P0B31; Bentley's P0B25 for battery A is the closest documented example, with the energy store replaced once the cell spread reaches 0.5 V. GM uses P0ABC for an undervoltage of the whole pack (below 24 V). CARB asks for monitoring of cells and voltage sensors in hybrid storage and for fault codes that single out the replaceable unit. Typical is a module in unit D that has aged faster or self-discharged during standstill. Discharge power and electric range drop, and the controller may stop electric driving.
c: Aged cells with lost capacity in battery D
Deep discharge or self-discharge after standstill
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist
Reduced electric range

P0B32.d: P0B32 sets when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery D goes above its permitted maximum. It is the high counterpart of P0B31; P0B30 covers unstable readings and P0B2F the general fault. No manufacturer documents P0B32 publicly; Bentley's P0B26 for battery A, cured by replacing the 48 V super capacitor, shows the same fault type on another unit. GM's analogous whole-pack monitor is P0ABD (above 479 V, Type A, MIL at once). CARB requires hybrid storage voltage sensors and cells to be monitored and codes to identify the replaceable unit. Causes are an overcharged cell group when balancing fails, a defective module or a measuring error. Charging and recuperation are cut back, and the contactors may open to protect the pack.
c: Cell group in battery D charged too high, balancing ineffective
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads
s: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
MIL on
Charging or recuperation restricted
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B33.d: The high-voltage service disconnect is the removable plug, usually fused, that splits the traction battery for safe servicing. A low-voltage detection loop runs through the plug, and the battery controller reads it to know whether the plug is seated; patents from Ford and Lear describe this loop, which opens before the main contacts part. P0B33 is the general circuit code for this detection input. No manufacturer documents P0B33 publicly. CARB requires such hybrid components to be monitored like any input. Performance, low, high and open have their own codes, P0B34 to P0B37; the separate high-voltage interlock loop uses P0A0A ff. Expect contactors to stay open: no ready mode, no charging.
c: Service disconnect plug not fully seated or locked after service
Chafed, open or shorted detection loop wiring between plug base and battery controller
Corroded or spread terminals in the plug or its base
s: Vehicle does not enter ready mode or will not start
High-voltage system warning and MIL on
Charging not possible

P0B34.t: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit Performance
P0B34.d: P0B34 covers a plausibility fault of the service disconnect detection: the signal is electrically within limits but does not match what the controller expects, for example a plug reported as removed while the high-voltage bus still shows voltage, or a state that changes without a matching event. Audi lists P0B3400 in the controller at address 008C of the 2025 Q5 e-hybrid, together with U029A00 and U059B00, and asks technicians to log the case in its pending service database; no threshold is published. CARB requires hybrid components to be checked for rationality as input devices. Pure circuit, low, high and open faults are P0B33, P0B35, P0B36 and P0B37. The car may refuse ready mode or charging.
c: Battery controller software fault (Audi case under investigation)
Loose plug or worn contacts giving an implausible detection state
Increased resistance in the detection loop
Communication fault between battery controller and other modules
s: Electrical system or high-voltage warning
No ready mode or charging interrupted
Related network codes stored at the same time

P0B35.t: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit Low
P0B35.d: P0B35 sets when the service disconnect detection signal stays below its lower limit. Where the loop is coded with a resistor in the plug, as in a Lear patent, a reading near zero typically points to a short to ground in the loop wiring; the exact meaning depends on how the manufacturer powers the input. Ford traced an intermittent short to ground in the low-voltage interlock wiring as the cause of its open-loop code P0B37 on the C-Max Energi, which shows how chafed harnesses act here. No manufacturer documents P0B35 publicly. CARB treats such signals as monitored hybrid inputs. High, open and performance faults are P0B36, P0B37 and P0B34. The contactors usually stay open.
c: Detection loop wire chafed and shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the plug base bridging to ground
Coding element in the plug shorted
s: No ready mode or stall with a stop-safely message
MIL and high-voltage warning on
Charging not possible

P0B36.t: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit High
P0B36.d: P0B36 sets when the service disconnect detection signal stays above its upper limit. With a pulled-up input this usually means a short to a voltage source or a missing coding element in the plug; on some designs an open loop also reads high, so manufacturers separate it with P0B37 only where they can tell the cases apart. Patents from Ford and Lear show the detection loop as a low-voltage circuit that closes through the plug and is read by a battery or vehicle controller. No manufacturer documents P0B36 publicly. CARB requires such hybrid inputs to be monitored for out-of-range values. Low and performance faults are P0B35 and P0B34. The high-voltage system normally stays switched off.
c: Detection loop wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open loop or missing contact read as high signal
Wrong or damaged service disconnect plug without proper coding
s: Vehicle not ready to drive
MIL and high-voltage warning on
Charging blocked

P0B37.d: P0B37 means the controller sees the service disconnect as open, either because the plug is really removed or because its detection loop is broken. Ford uses the code in the battery energy control module of the 2013-2016 C-Max Energi: bulletins SSM 46108 and TSB 17-0015 describe intermittent stalls or no crank with a Stop Safely Now message and MIL, stored with U3012 and, in another module, the interlock code P0A0A. The cause was an intermittent short to ground in the low-voltage interlock wiring, found by inspecting the harness for chafing. P0B33 to P0B36 cover circuit, performance, low and high faults. For the driver: the car shuts down or will not start.
c: Low-voltage interlock wiring chafed with intermittent short to ground (Ford C-Max)
Service disconnect plug removed, loose or not locked
Open terminal in the plug base or interlock connector
s: Intermittent stall or no crank
Stop Safely Now message and MIL
High-voltage interlock code stored in another module

P0B38.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
P0B38.d: Hybrid and electric drives cool the inverter and motor electronics with electric coolant pumps; J2012 numbers them A, B and C. P0B38 sets when the controller detects an open or general fault in the control line of pump B, typically by checking the driver output for missing load current. No manufacturer documents P0B38 publicly. FCA uses a pump B on the Jeep Compass and Renegade 4xe, where bulletins name its performance code P0C74, and Mercedes uses the pump A code P0A05 for an open control circuit of the low-temperature circuit pump on M264 engines. CARB requires output components of inverter thermal management to be monitored. Expect a coolant or hybrid warning and power reduction if electronics overheat.
c: Pump connector loose, corroded or terminal pushed out
Open control wire between controller and pump
Pump electronics or motor failed open
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty
s: Hybrid system or coolant warning, MIL on
Reduced electric drive power when electronics get hot
Pump not running audibly after switch-on

P0B39.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P0B39.d: P0B39 sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B is lower than the controller expects, usually a short to ground on the command line or a pump input that pulls the line down. On a low-side switched or PWM line the module sees the voltage stuck low while it commands the pump off. No manufacturer documents P0B39 publicly. Pump B is in service at FCA (Compass and Renegade 4xe, performance code P0C74), and Ford stores the pump A codes P0A06 and P0A07 in the PCM of the 2020 Explorer and Aviator hybrids. CARB requires these inverter cooling outputs to be checked for circuit faults. Open and high faults are P0B38 and P0B3A; running faults use P0C74 and P2D05 ff.
c: Control wire shorted to ground, often chafed at brackets
Pump electronics pulling the control input low
Coolant or water in the pump connector
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty
s: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning
Pump runs permanently or not at all, depending on circuit design
Power limitation at high load or heat

P0B3A.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
P0B3A.d: P0B3A sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B stays higher than expected, typically a short to battery voltage on the command line or, with some driver designs, an open pump input that floats high. The module then cannot switch the pump as requested. No manufacturer documents P0B3A publicly. As reference points, FCA has a pump B on its 4xe models with the performance code P0C74, and Ford lists the pump A high code P0A07 among PCM codes fixed by a battery controller update on the 2020 Explorer and Aviator hybrids. CARB requires inverter thermal management outputs to be monitored. Open and low faults are P0B38 and P0B39. Overheating protection may reduce power.
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Pump control input open so the line floats high
Controller software misjudging the circuit, fixed by update
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty
s: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning
Pump cannot be switched off or on as commanded
Reduced electric power when the inverter heats up

P0B3B.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit
P0B3B.d: Voltage sense A to Z and beyond are the cell or cell-group sense channels of the battery monitoring electronics, unlike the pack voltage sense codes P0ABA and P0B14 ff, which measure the whole pack. P0B3B is the circuit code for channel A. GM uses it in the battery energy control module as an open sense line check: neighbouring cell readings differ by 1.3 V or more, or a cell reads under 36 mV with balancing on, or a splice reads over 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V), for 0.6 s; Type A, one trip. Ford stores P0B3B with other open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV and 2023 Mach-E; Honda's 2014-2015 Accord Hybrid used it for a cell voltage sensor fault caused by inverter noise.
c: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent fault in the flexible printed circuit to the battery controller (Ford Mach-E)
Sensor software misreading inverter noise, fixed by update (Honda)
Internal failure of the traction battery requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
s: MIL or powertrain warning, Stop Safely Now message possible
No start or no charging
Fail-safe EV mode with limited speed and sudden loss of power

P0B3C.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Range/Performance
P0B3C.d: P0B3C flags a cell voltage channel A that reads plausible values but does not follow the other cells. GM runs this check in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 as a stuck-in-range test: while the average cell voltage moves by at least 0.005 V in one direction between samples, channel A must move as well; 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip. FCA names the code Voltage Sense 1 Circuit Performance on the Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid and fixes it, together with P0B41 and further channels, by reprogramming the battery pack control module. Circuit, low, high and erratic faults have their own codes. The system limits battery power or shuts down hybrid operation.
c: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack
s: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes
Reduced electric range or no electric drive
Contactor related codes stored at the same time

P0B3D.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low
P0B3D.d: P0B3D sets when cell voltage channel A reads below the lowest value a real cell can have, which points to the measurement rather than the cell. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, provided no open sense line, communication or balancing fault is active. FCA lists P0B3D as Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low on the 2019 Ram 1500 with eTorque mild hybrid, next to the pack-level code P0ABA, and cures it with a battery pack control module update. A genuinely low cell is reported with separate cell voltage codes. Expect reduced or blocked hybrid assist.
c: Battery pack control module software, fixed by update (Ram eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed
s: MIL on
Start-stop and electric assist unavailable
Hybrid battery power limited

P0B3E.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit High
P0B3E.d: P0B3E sets when cell voltage channel A reads above any value a healthy lithium-ion cell reaches, so the reading is treated as a sensing fault. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip. FCA uses the code on the 2021 Jeep Wrangler 4xe as Voltage Sense 1 Circuit High and on the 2019 Ram 1500 eTorque as Voltage Sense A Circuit High; in both cases a battery pack control module update removes a false MIL. A truly overcharged cell sets separate cell voltage high codes such as P0DE7 instead. Low, range and open faults are P0B3D, P0B3C and P0B3B. The car limits battery use.
c: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA)
Open sense line letting the input float high
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed
s: MIL on, possibly without noticeable drivability change
Electric drive or start-stop disabled
Charging limited

P0B3F.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B3F.d: P0B3F is reserved for a cell voltage channel A that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. No manufacturer documents P0B3F publicly. GM's 2019 tables show how the siblings on the same channel work: an open line test (P0B3B), a stuck-in-range test against the other cells (P0B3C) and fixed limits of 0.2 V and 4.8 V (P0B3D, P0B3E); an erratic test would watch for implausible jumps between samples. CARB requires battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system to be monitored as input components, with fault codes pinpointing the smallest replaceable unit. Loose connections at the cell taps or the monitoring board are the usual suspects. Hybrid power may be limited.
c: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines
s: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive or assist

P0B40.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit
P0B40.d: P0B40 is the circuit code of cell voltage sense channel B, the second cell or cell group the battery monitoring electronics measures; pack-level voltage uses P0ABA and P0B14 ff instead. GM applies the same open sense line test as on channel A: a 1.3 V jump between neighbouring cells, under 36 mV with balancing on, or splice voltage above 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V) for 0.6 s, Type A, one trip. Ford lists P0B40 among the open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV, where the fix is a new traction battery, and on the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and e-Transit, where an intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller is to blame. Expect no start or no charging.
c: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, e-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
s: Wrench indicator or MIL, Stop Safely Now message possible
No start condition
Battery cannot be charged

P0B41.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B41.d: P0B41 reports that cell voltage channel B gives values inside the normal range that fail a plausibility check against the other cells. In GM's 2019 tables Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 compares sample-to-sample changes: if the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V while channel B stays unchanged, a failure is counted, and 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip, with system voltage above 10.2 V. FCA calls it Voltage Sense 2 Circuit Performance on the Pacifica plug-in hybrid and lists it with P0B3C and further channels in battery pack control module update bulletins. Circuit, low, high and erratic faults of channel B are P0B40, P0B42, P0B43 and P0B44.
c: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack
s: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes
Electric drive reduced or unavailable
Contactor related codes stored at the same time

P0B42.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Low
P0B42.d: P0B42 sets when cell voltage channel B reads implausibly low, below what any usable cell would show. GM's battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and only when no open sense line, slave communication or balancing fault is present. FCA uses P0B42 as Voltage Sense 2 Circuit Low on the 2022 Grand Wagoneer and Wagoneer with the 5.7 L eTorque mild hybrid; its bulletin calls the MIL false, mentions inoperative start-stop and a car that seems to run on fuel only, and prescribes a battery pack control module update. Cells that are actually weak set separate cell voltage codes. High and range faults are P0B43 and P0B41.
c: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed
s: MIL on
Start-stop inoperative
Vehicle behaves as if running on the engine only

P0B43.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit High
P0B43.d: P0B43 sets when cell voltage channel B reads higher than a lithium-ion cell can physically reach in service, so the controller blames the measurement path. GM documents the criteria for its battery energy control module: cell voltage B at 4.8 V or above for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, with open sense line, communication and balancing faults ruled out first. Beyond GM, no manufacturer documents P0B43 publicly; FCA's sister code P0B3E for channel A shows that software in the battery controller can cause such readings. CARB treats battery voltage sensors as monitored input components. Overcharged cells use separate cell voltage codes. Low, range and open faults of channel B are P0B42, P0B41 and P0B40.
c: Open sense line letting the input float high
Battery controller software misreading the channel
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed
s: MIL and hybrid warning on
Charging or electric drive limited

P0B44.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B44.d: P0B44 is the J2012 slot for a cell voltage channel B whose reading jumps or drops out for short moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents P0B44 publicly. For orientation, GM's 2019 tables check channel B for open sense lines (P0B40), frozen values compared with the other cells (P0B41) and fixed limits of 0.2 V and 4.8 V (P0B42, P0B43); an erratic monitor would add a test for implausible steps between samples. CARB requires the storage system's voltage sensors to be monitored as inputs and faults to be pinpointed to the smallest replaceable unit. Typical causes are vibration-loosened cell taps and connectors on the monitoring board. Warnings may come and go with driving conditions.
c: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines
s: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive or assist

P0B45.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit
P0B45.d: Voltage sense C is the third cell or cell-group measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics, not a pack voltage input like P0ABA. P0B45 reports an electrical break in that channel. GM's battery energy control module sets it when its open sense line test fails for 0.6 s: adjacent cell readings at least 1.3 V apart, a cell below 36 mV while its balancing switch is on, or a splice above 0.1 V (bus bar splice 0.5 V); Type A, one trip. Ford lists P0B45 with the other open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid, fixed by a new traction battery, and on the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit, where an intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit is blamed. Expect no start or no charging.
c: Open cell sense tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel C
Intermittent flexible printed circuit between cells and battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
s: Vehicle does not start or does not become ready to drive
High-voltage battery no longer charges
Powertrain warning (wrench) and Stop Safely Now message

P0B46.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Range/Performance
P0B46.d: With P0B46 the channel C wiring is intact; the value on it looks plausible but no longer behaves like a real cell. GM's 2019 tables run the test in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2: whenever the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V in one direction, channel C has to follow; if it stays frozen in 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms, the code sets, Type A. The 2016 Chevrolet Volt uses a window of 7 out of 8 seconds instead. Chrysler calls the code Voltage Sense 3 Circuit Performance on the 2020 Pacifica plug-in hybrid and cures it by reflashing the battery pack control module. So before opening the battery, check the controller software level.
c: Battery controller software misjudging the channel, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Measuring chip input for channel C stuck at a constant value
High-resistance cell tap damping the channel C signal
s: MIL on without noticeable driving fault
Reduced electric power or hybrid assist
Contactor or precharge codes stored at the same time (Pacifica)

P0B47.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Low
P0B47.d: P0B47 is stored when channel C delivers a voltage too low to come from a working cell or block, so the controller blames the measurement rather than the battery. GM documents two implementations. On lithium-ion packs the battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, one trip, unless an open sense line, communication or balancing fault is already active.
