Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BE7.t: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BE7.d: P0BE7 means the output of the phase U current sensor in the motor A inverter has fallen below its valid range. GM converts the sensor voltage into amps and compares it with a limit: below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables and 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table, both Type A; below -700 A, Type B, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; below -440 A, Type B, two trips, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table; the 2011 Volt uses 800 A limits for these sensors. Such values are far beyond real phase currents, so the cause is electrical, typically a sensor signal pulled toward ground. GM's eAssist controller then runs current control without the sensors, which costs motor A performance.
c: Failed phase U current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no assist from drive motor A
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BE8.t: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BE8.d: P0BE8 is the high-side counterpart of P0BE7: the phase U current sensor of the motor A inverter reports a value above its valid range. GM's tables set it above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), Type A, one trip; above 800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; above 700 A, Type B, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; and above 440 A, Type B, two trips, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table. A reading this high without matching battery current points to the sensor or its supply rather than real current; genuine excess current is covered by separate overcurrent codes such as P0C01. The inverter then uses a fallback control strategy and motor A delivers less torque.
c: Failed phase U current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BE9.t: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit
P0BE9.d: P0BE9 covers a general circuit fault of the phase V current sensor in the motor A inverter, meaning an electrical problem the controller does not narrow down to an offset, low or high condition. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM's hybrid tables for the 2011 Volt, the 2012 two-mode trucks and the 2016 to 2019 models list only the specific siblings P0BEA, P0BEB and P0BEC; GM's BAS Plus (eAssist) table lists phase current codes only for U and W. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. Because the three phase currents are used together for torque control and their sum is cross-checked (P0BFD), a lost V signal normally forces reduced motor A operation.
c: Failed phase V current sensor inside the inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor control processor
s: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BEA.t: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BEA.d: P0BEA is the performance check of the phase V current sensor in the motor A inverter. GM implements it as an offset test: with no current flowing at start-up, the learned zero point must stay within 30 A (2011 Volt, 2016 tables, Type A; 2012 two-mode trucks, Type B, with P0BEB/P0BEC not active) or 35 A (2019 table, Type A, after a 0.4 s delay). A sensor whose zero has drifted would distort torque control and the phase current balance. Jeep names P0BEA among the phase current codes of the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV for EMEA markets, together with the turtle and Service 4WD lights; the remedy is a software update of the hybrid control processor and power inverter.
c: Zero offset of the phase V current sensor drifted beyond the limit
Faulty sensing electronics in the power inverter module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BEB.t: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BEB.d: P0BEB reports that the phase V current sensor in the motor A inverter outputs a signal below its valid range. GM compares the converted current with a lower limit: below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016 tables) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019 table), Type A, one trip; below -800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; below -700 A, Type B, two trips, on the 2012 two-mode trucks. Real phase currents never reach these values, so the code points to an electrical fault such as a sensor output pulled toward ground or a dead sensor. Unlike P0BEA, the sensor is not just shifted but out of its measuring range. Motor A is then run in a restricted mode.
c: Failed phase V current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BEC.t: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BEC.d: P0BEC is set when the phase V current sensor of the motor A inverter reports a value above its valid range. In GM's tables the limit is above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), Type A; above 800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt with PWM output disabled; and above 700 A, Type B, two trips, on the 2012 two-mode trucks. Because the check runs while the power stage is not switching or the value is far beyond any real current, it isolates a sensor or supply fault rather than an actual overcurrent. It pairs with P0BEB for the low side and P0BEA for offset. Expect reduced drive from motor A and further inverter codes in the memory.
c: Failed phase V current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BED.t: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit
P0BED.d: P0BED is the general circuit code of the phase W current sensor in the drive motor A inverter, for an electrical fault outside the offset, low and high categories. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's hybrid tables from the 2011 Volt to 2019, including the BAS Plus (eAssist) system, use P0BEE, P0BEF and P0BF0 instead. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. Phase W matters even on systems with only two sensors: GM's eAssist table measures U and W and, if either sensor fails, runs current control in an alternate mode without the sensors. Expect reduced motor A torque, and check for related inverter codes before replacing parts.
c: Failed phase W current sensor inside the inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor control processor
s: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power or assist from drive motor A

P0BEE.t: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BEE.d: P0BEE checks the phase W current sensor of the motor A inverter for a plausible zero point. GM learns the sensor offset at each start while no current flows and sets the code above 30 A (2011 Volt and 2016 tables, Type A; 2012 two-mode trucks, Type B) or above 35 A (2019 table, Type A). In GM's BAS Plus (eAssist) table P0BEE is one of the faults that switch current control to a sensorless alternate mode, and it blocks the phase sum check P0BFD. Jeep lists P0BEE as Drive Motor A Inverter Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Performance on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV (EMEA), with turtle and Service 4WD lights, fixed by a hybrid control processor update.
c: Zero offset of the phase W current sensor drifted beyond the limit
Faulty sensing electronics in the power inverter module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BEF.t: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BEF.d: P0BEF indicates that the phase W current sensor of the motor A inverter delivers a signal below its valid range. GM's limits: below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016 tables) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), Type A; below -800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; below -700 A, Type B, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; below -440 A, Type B, two trips, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table. These readings lie far outside real phase currents, so a sensor output stuck near ground, a failed sensor or a supply fault is the likely cause. In the eAssist system this fault puts current control into a mode that ignores the sensors, and it disables the U-V-W correlation check P0BFD, so motor A runs with reduced output.
c: Failed phase W current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no assist from drive motor A

P0BF0.t: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BF0.d: P0BF0 is the high-signal fault of the phase W current sensor in the motor A inverter. GM sets it above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table, Type A, one trip; above 700 A, Type B, two trips, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; above 440 A, Type B, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table; the 2011 Volt uses 800 A limits for this sensor family. A value this high without matching battery current points to the sensor, its supply or an open reference rather than to real overcurrent, which GM reports separately (P0C01). With P0BF0 active, GM's eAssist logic switches to sensorless current control and suspends P0BFD, so motor A is limited until repair.
c: Failed phase W current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BF1.t: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit
P0BF1.d: On hybrids with two electric machines, the inverter of drive motor B carries its own set of phase current sensors, which the motor control processor uses for torque control and to protect the power switches. P0BF1 is the general circuit code for the phase U sensor of motor B, meant for an electrical fault that is not classified as offset, low or high. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly: GM's tables for the 2011 Volt, the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks and the 2016 to 2019 models list only P0BF2, P0BF3 and P0BF4 for this sensor. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. Without a valid phase U value, motor B is usually limited or switched off.
c: Failed phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor B control processor
s: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B
Engine runs more often because electric drive is limited

P0BF2.t: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BF2.d: GM runs P0BF2 as the offset test of the phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter. Each time the vehicle is started, while no current flows through the motor, the controller learns the sensor's zero point and compares it with a limit: 30 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A) and in the 2016 tables (Type A, after 0.1 s), 30 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, power stage open, P0BF3/P0BF4 not active) and 35 A in a 2019 table (Type A, after 0.4 s). Jeep lists P0BF2 on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV for Europe, together with the other motor A and B phase current codes, the turtle light and Service 4WD; the fix there is a software update of the hybrid control processors.
c: Zero point of the motor B phase U current sensor drifted past the limit
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BF3.t: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BF3.d: P0BF3 is stored when the phase U current sensor of the motor B inverter reports a value below its valid range. GM converts the sensor voltage into amps and sets the code below -800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, 4 of 6 samples), below -700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips), and below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip). No real phase current of motor B reaches such values, so the reading reflects an electrical defect, typically a sensor output pulled toward ground or a dead sensor. The offset check P0BF2 covers a shifted zero instead. Motor B is then restricted or shut off.
c: Failed phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BF4.t: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BF4.d: P0BF4 is the upper-limit counterpart of P0BF3 for the phase U current sensor of drive motor B. GM's thresholds: above 800 A on the 2011 Volt, checked with PWM output disabled (Type A); above 700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips); above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables and 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip). Because the test runs with the power stage idle or the value lies far beyond any real current, it points to the sensor, its supply or an open reference rather than to genuine overcurrent; GM reports real excess phase current of motor B separately under P0C04 (above 600 A in the 2016 and 2019 tables). Motor B output is limited until repair.
c: Failed phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B
Further inverter or phase current codes stored

P0BF5.t: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit
P0BF5.d: P0BF5 stands for a general circuit fault of the phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter, an electrical problem the controller does not narrow down to offset, low or high. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM's hybrid tables for the 2011 Volt, the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks and the 2016 to 2019 models use only the specific siblings P0BF6, P0BF7 and P0BF8; GM's single-motor BAS Plus (eAssist) system has no motor B codes at all. CARB requires circuit monitoring of hybrid sensors. Since the three phase currents of motor B are used together and their sum is cross-checked (P0BFE), losing the V signal normally forces motor B into restricted operation.
c: Failed phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor B control processor
s: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power from drive motor B

P0BF6.t: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BF6.d: P0BF6 is the performance check of the phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter, implemented by GM as a zero offset test. The offset is learned at every start with no current through the motor and must stay within 30 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, P0BEB/P0BEC not active, as printed in the table) and in the 2016 tables (Type A, 0.1 s), within 30 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips) and within 35 A in a 2019 table (Type A, 0.4 s). A shifted zero would skew torque control and the phase current balance. Jeep names P0BF6 as Drive Motor B Inverter Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV (EMEA), fixed by reflashing the hybrid control processors.
c: Zero point of the motor B phase V current sensor drifted past the limit
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BF7.t: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BF7.d: P0BF7 reports that the phase V current sensor of the motor B inverter outputs a signal below its valid range. In GM's hybrid tables the converted current must fall below -800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, one trip), below -700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, 10 of 15 samples) or below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016) and 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), both Type A. Values like these are physically impossible for the motor phase, so the controller treats them as a sensor or circuit failure, for example a shorted output or a lost sensor supply. Unlike P0BF6 the sensor is not merely offset but outside its measuring range. Drive motor B then runs restricted.
c: Failed phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BF8.t: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BF8.d: P0BF8 sets when the phase V current sensor of drive motor B reports more current than its valid range allows. GM uses above 800 A on the 2011 Volt with the PWM output disabled (Type A), above 700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips) and above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip). Such a reading while the inverter is not switching, or far above the overcurrent limit, isolates a sensor-side fault such as a signal shorted to the supply or a broken reference ground. It pairs with P0BF7 for the low side and P0BF6 for offset; real overcurrent appears as P0C04. Expect motor B to be derated and further inverter codes in memory.
c: Failed phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B

P0BF9.t: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit
P0BF9.d: P0BF9 is reserved for a general circuit fault of the phase W current sensor in the drive motor B inverter, outside the offset, low and high categories that have their own codes. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's tables from the 2011 Volt through 2019, and Jeep's 2020 Renegade and Compass PHEV bulletins, refer only to the specific siblings, chiefly P0BFA. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. If the controller cannot trust phase W of motor B, it can no longer close the three-phase current balance checked by P0BFE and therefore limits or disables that motor. The sensor sits inside the inverter, so repair usually means replacing the inverter assembly.
c: Failed phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor B control processor
s: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B

P0BFA.t: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BFA.d: P0BFA checks the phase W current sensor of the motor B inverter for a plausible zero point. GM learns the offset at each start while no current flows and sets the code above 30 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, power stage open), above 30 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, only with P0BFB/P0BFC inactive), above 30 A after 0.1 s in the 2016 tables and above 35 A after 0.4 s in a 2019 table (both Type A). Jeep's EMEA bulletins for the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV put P0BFA first among the motor B codes, with MIL, turtle and Service 4WD lights, and cure it with new software for the hybrid control processor and auxiliary processor (power inverter module).
c: Zero point of the motor B phase W current sensor drifted past the limit
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BFB.t: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BFB.d: P0BFB indicates that the phase W current sensor of the motor B inverter delivers a signal below its valid range. GM's limits: below -800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, 4 of 6 samples at 10.4 ms), below -700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips) and below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip). The threshold lies well outside any phase current motor B can carry, so the likely cause is a sensor output stuck near ground, a failed sensor or a supply fault on the sensor board. P0BFA covers a shifted zero, P0BFC the high side. While the code is active, motor B delivers reduced or no torque.
c: Failed phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B

P0BFC.t: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BFC.d: P0BFC is the signal-high fault of the phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter. GM sets it above 800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, one trip), above 700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, 10 of 15 samples) and above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A). A reading this high with no matching battery current indicates the sensor, its supply or an open reference instead of actual current; true phase overcurrent of motor B is logged as P0C04, and the plausibility of all three phases together as P0BFE. With P0BFC stored the inverter derates motor B, and the hybrid system leans more on the engine and motor A.
c: Failed phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B
Engine runs more often because electric drive is limited

P0BFD.t: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Current Sensor Correlation
P0BFD.d: In a three-phase motor without a neutral connection the three phase currents must add up to roughly zero. P0BFD checks this for drive motor A: if the absolute sum of the U, V and W readings exceeds a limit, at least one sensor is wrong. GM's limits: 156 A on the 2011 Volt and 110 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type A, one trip), 110 A for 0.0032 of 0.0038 s in the 2016 and 2019 tables (Type A). GM's BAS Plus (eAssist) uses another balance, motor DC current plus accessory module current versus battery current, above 40 A, Type B, blocked while a phase sensor code is active. Jeep lists P0BFD on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV (EMEA), fixed by a software update.
c: One motor A phase current sensor reading wrong but still within its own limits
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BFE.t: Drive Motor B Phase U-V-W Current Sensor Correlation
P0BFE.d: P0BFE applies the phase balance test to drive motor B: the controller adds the U, V and W current readings, which should cancel out, and sets the code when the absolute sum stays above a limit. GM uses 156 A on the 2011 Volt and 110 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type A, one trip, main relay closed) and 110 A for 0.0032 of 0.0038 s in the 2016 and 2019 tables (Type A). It catches a sensor that reads wrong while each signal alone stays in range, unlike the per-phase codes P0BF2 to P0BFC. GM's single-motor eAssist has no such code. Jeep lists P0BFE on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV (EMEA) with the turtle and Service 4WD lights; reprogramming the hybrid processors is the fix.
c: One motor B phase current sensor reading wrong but still within its own limits
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced power from drive motor B

P0BFF.d: P0BFF is the general code for the current flowing through drive motor A, the electric machine the manufacturer labels A. It covers a current fault that is not classed as too low (P0C00) or too high (P0C01). No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. CARB requires hybrids to monitor electric motor performance. The closest documented check is GM's P0C01, which compares the sensed phase current with a fixed limit, and Stellantis lists P0C01 on the 2026 Wagoneer S with damaged three-phase cabling as the cause. A stored P0BFF means the motor controller no longer trusts the motor current, so it usually reduces electric drive power. Check the three-phase connections, the motor windings and the inverter.
c: Loose, corroded or damaged three-phase cable joint between inverter and motor A
Fault in the motor A inverter or its current measurement
Damaged stator winding of drive motor A
s: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Reduced electric drive power or limp mode
Other drive motor A current or phase codes stored

P0C00.d: P0C00 reports that the current of drive motor A is lower than the controller expects for the commanded torque, the counterpart of P0C01 (current high). No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM and Stellantis use only P0C01 from this group. CARB requires hybrids to monitor electric motor performance. Too little current points to a high-resistance three-phase joint, an open winding path or an inverter that cannot drive the phases. GM checks a missing phase separately as P0C05. The driver usually notices weak electric drive and a warning lamp; the vehicle may switch to engine-only or limp mode.
c: High-resistance or loose three-phase connection at motor A or the inverter
Inverter power stage for motor A not delivering current
Open or damaged winding in drive motor A
s: Weak or missing electric drive torque
Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Vehicle runs on the engine only or in limp mode

P0C01.d: P0C01 is the overcurrent check of drive motor A, meant to protect the inverter's IGBTs. GM sets it when any phase current exceeds 725 A on the 2011 Volt, 600 A on the 2012 two-mode trucks and in the 2016 to 2019 tables, or 396 A on eAssist; since 2016 a too negative d-axis current (about -540 to -310 A, depending on stator temperature) also counts. A fast and a slow counter catch sudden and intermittent faults; Type A, one trip. GM PIP5246 links it on Volt and ELR to a damaged motor 1 stator. Stellantis lists it on the 2018/19 Wrangler eTorque (motor generator unit) and on the 2026 Wagoneer S and Cherokee, there caused by cross-threaded three-phase cable bolts. Expect limp mode.
c: Damaged or improperly torqued three-phase cable joints (Stellantis S2608000006)
Damaged stator winding of motor A (GM PIP5246)
Failing power switch or current measurement in the inverter
s: Limp mode with warning lamp
Reduced propulsion or engine unavailable message
Rough running or loud noise from the motor generator

P0C02.d: P0C02 is the general current code for drive motor B, the second electric machine, such as the second motor of a two-motor hybrid or the rear motor of an electric all-wheel-drive system. It applies to a current fault that is neither classed as low (P0C03) nor high (P0C04). No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. CARB requires monitoring of electric motor performance. The documented relative is P0C04: GM checks the phase current of motor B against 600 to 725 A, and Stellantis lists P0C04 on the 2026 Wagoneer S and Cherokee with faulty three-phase cable joints. With P0C02 stored the controller usually cuts or limits the power of motor B. Inspect the phase cabling, the winding resistance and the inverter of motor B.
c: Loose, corroded or damaged three-phase connection of motor B
Fault in the motor B inverter or its current measurement
Damaged stator winding of drive motor B
s: Hybrid or electric drive warning lamp
Reduced power or loss of all-wheel drive
Limp mode

P0C03.d: P0C03 indicates that drive motor B draws less current than the controller expects for the requested torque. It is the low counterpart of P0C04 and the motor B twin of P0C00. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly, and the GM hybrid tables use only P0C04 and P0C08 for motor B. CARB requires hybrids to monitor electric motor performance. Low current typically comes from a high-resistance cable joint, an interrupted winding path or an inverter stage that does not switch; a single missing phase is reported by GM as P0C08. In practice motor B delivers little or no torque, a warning lamp lights up and the system may fall back to the other motor or the engine.
c: High-resistance or loose three-phase connection of motor B
Inverter power stage for motor B not delivering current
Open or damaged winding in drive motor B
s: Weak or missing torque from motor B
Warning lamp for the hybrid or electric drive
Reduced performance or limp mode

P0C04.d: P0C04 is the overcurrent check of drive motor B and protects the IGBTs of its inverter. GM flags it when the highest phase current exceeds 725 A on the 2011 Volt or 600 A on the 2012 two-mode trucks and in the 2016 to 2019 hybrid tables; the newer tables also fail a d-axis current below a stator-temperature curve of roughly -556 to -315 A. Fast and slow counters cover sudden and intermittent peaks, Type A, one trip. Stellantis names P0C04 with P0C01 on the 2026 Jeep Wagoneer S and Cherokee: cross-threaded or loose bolts on the three-phase cables between transmission and drive motor power inverter, checked by resistance against a 29 to 32 milliohm window. The car goes into limp mode with the MIL on.
c: Cross-threaded or loose three-phase cable bolts with metal debris (Stellantis S2608000006)
Shorted or damaged stator winding of motor B
Failing power switch or current measurement in the motor B inverter
s: Limp mode with red wrench or malfunction lamp
Sudden loss of electric drive power

P0C05.t: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Circuit/Open
P0C05.d: P0C05 detects an open or missing phase between the inverter and drive motor A. GM checks each phase as the rotor passes its axis: if the peak phase axis current stays below 9 A while at least 23 A is commanded, with the rotor within 30 degrees of that axis and over 35 V on the inverter, about 200 failed samples set the code. It is Type A, one trip, on the Volt and two-mode trucks and Type B, two trips, on eAssist. Jeep lists it on the 2018/19 Wrangler eTorque with P0C01, curing it by software or a new motor generator unit. Volvo uses it in the rear axle inverter of 2020 to 2022 PHEVs and advises clearing it and test-driving before replacing parts. Expect reduced electric power.
c: Loose or open three-phase terminal between inverter and motor A
Software fault, cured by update (Jeep TSB 08-144-23)
Internal fault of the motor generator unit or open stator winding
One-off event that does not return after clearing (Volvo TJ 36863)
s: Propulsion system performance message or warning lamp
Reduced electric drive power
Loss of 12 V charging or noise from the motor generator on mild hybrids

P0C06.t: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Circuit Low
P0C06.d: P0C06 belongs to the phase circuit group of drive motor A and reports that a U, V or W phase line sits too low, typically a short to the negative high-voltage rail or to chassis ground. P0C05 covers an open or missing phase, P0C07 the opposite high state. No manufacturer documents P0C06 for a drive motor publicly; GM's hybrid tables use only P0C05 from this trio. CARB requires hybrid input and output components to be monitored for circuit faults. Such a short usually also trips the inverter's overcurrent protection, so P0C01 or insulation faults may appear alongside. The motor controller shuts down motor A, which leaves the driver with reduced or no electric drive and a warning lamp.
c: Phase cable or winding shorted to ground or housing
Shorted low-side power switch in the motor A inverter
Insulation damage from heat, moisture or chafing
s: Electric drive shut down with warning lamp
Overcurrent or insulation codes stored at the same time

P0C07.t: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Circuit High
P0C07.d: P0C07 is the high member of the drive motor A phase circuit group: a U, V or W phase line reads higher than it should, most likely through a short to the positive high-voltage rail or a power switch that stays on. Its siblings are P0C05 for an open phase and P0C06 for a phase pulled low. No manufacturer documents P0C07 publicly; among these three, GM uses only P0C05, which watches for missing phase current. CARB requires circuit monitoring of hybrid input and output components. Because a stuck high phase drives uncontrolled current, the inverter normally disables motor A at once. The driver sees a warning lamp and loses some or all electric propulsion until the shorted part is replaced.
c: Shorted high-side power switch in the motor A inverter
Phase cable shorted to the positive high-voltage path
Faulty gate driver holding a switch on
s: Immediate shutdown of electric drive with warning lamp
Reduced performance or engine-only operation

P0C08.t: Drive Motor B Phase U-V-W Circuit/Open
P0C08.d: P0C08 is the open-phase check for drive motor B, the motor B twin of P0C05. GM runs it on the 2011 Volt and the 2012 two-mode trucks: each phase is checked as the rotor passes its axis, and a phase axis current below 9 A while at least 23 A is commanded, with the rotor within 30 degrees and over 35 V on the inverter, counts as a miss. Around 200 failed samples set it, Type A, one trip. Later GM tables up to 2016 keep the same logic. GM's eAssist has only one machine and no P0C08. The usual causes are a loose three-phase terminal, an open stator winding or an inverter stage that does not conduct. Motor B then delivers no torque, the MIL lights and drive power is reduced.
c: Loose or open three-phase terminal between inverter and motor B
Open stator winding in drive motor B
Inverter stage for motor B not conducting
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion power
Engine running more often than usual

P0C09.t: Drive Motor B Phase U-V-W Circuit Low
P0C09.d: P0C09 marks a U, V or W phase line of drive motor B that is pulled low, for example by a short to the negative high-voltage rail, to ground or by a power switch that conducts when it should not. It is the motor B twin of P0C06; the siblings P0C08 and P0C0A cover an open phase and a phase stuck high. No manufacturer documents P0C09 publicly, and GM's hybrid tables use only P0C08 for motor B phase circuits. CARB requires circuit fault monitoring of hybrid components. A low phase usually causes overcurrent too, so P0C04 or insulation codes often accompany it. The motor controller switches motor B off; the vehicle continues with reduced power and a warning lamp.
c: Phase cable or winding of motor B shorted to ground or housing
Shorted low-side power switch in the motor B inverter
Insulation damage from heat, moisture or chafing
s: Motor B shut down with warning lamp
Overcurrent or insulation codes stored at the same time

P0C0A.t: Drive Motor B Phase U-V-W Circuit High
P0C0A.d: P0C0A reports that a phase line of drive motor B reads too high, typically a short to the positive high-voltage rail or a high-side power switch that stays on. It mirrors P0C07 for motor A and completes the motor B trio with P0C08 (open) and P0C09 (low). No manufacturer documents P0C0A publicly; GM only uses P0C08 for motor B phase circuits, based on missing phase current. CARB requires hybrid components to be monitored for circuit faults. A phase stuck high leads to uncontrolled current, so the inverter switches motor B off immediately and P0C04 may be stored as well. For the driver this means a warning lamp, reduced propulsion and, on electric all-wheel drive, loss of the driven axle.
c: Shorted high-side power switch in the motor B inverter
Phase cable of motor B shorted to the positive high-voltage path
Faulty gate driver holding a switch on
s: Immediate shutdown of motor B with warning lamp
Reduced performance or loss of electric all-wheel drive

P0C0B.t: Drive Motor A Inverter Power Supply Circuit/Open
P0C0B.d: P0C0B flags a lost or interrupted supply inside the motor A inverter. GM reads it from the IGBT module status: when the gate drive supply falls below its threshold, the module reports a bias fault; on eAssist the 5 V rail below 3.5 to 4.3 V or the 15 V rail below 10.4 to 12.6 V counts, with run/crank above 7 V. The 2012 trucks enable it between 9.5 and 18 V; the 2016 to 2019 tables need 0.002 to 0.168 s of fault within short windows, Type A, one trip. Mercedes applies the code to the high-voltage supply of the inverter in the belt starter-alternator of P3 hybrids (subtypes 16 and 17) and replaces that unit. Expect loss of electric drive or engine start.
c: Failed gate-drive power supply inside the motor A inverter
Low 12 V feed, blown fuse or poor ground to the inverter control board
Open high-voltage feed to the inverter, e.g. in a belt starter-alternator (Mercedes LI15.40-P-077947)
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Electric drive or motor generator unavailable
Engine cannot be started, only electric driving possible (Mercedes P3 hybrids)

P0C0C.t: Drive Motor A Inverter Power Supply Circuit Low
P0C0C.d: P0C0C reports that the supply voltage of the motor A inverter is present but too low, while P0C0B covers a lost or open supply and P0C0D a supply that is too high. Which supply is meant depends on the maker: GM ties its sibling P0C0B to the gate-drive supply of the IGBTs, Mercedes to the high-voltage feed. Audi documents P0C0C on the 2025 and 2026 A6 and Q6 e-tron family: stored in the electric drive modules together with P0E8D, it comes with a red high-voltage fault warning to stop safely, and the bulletin calls for replacing the affected front or rear power electronics. CARB requires circuit monitoring of hybrid components. Without a stable supply the inverter cannot switch, so drive power is cut.
c: Internal fault of the drive power electronics (Audi TSB 2081725)
Weak 12 V supply, poor ground or high-resistance connector at the inverter
Weak 12 V battery or DC/DC converter output
s: Red high-voltage system warning asking to stop safely
Loss of drive power or vehicle will not get ready to drive

P0C0D.t: Drive Motor A Inverter Power Supply Circuit High
P0C0D.d: P0C0D reports that the supply of the motor A inverter is above its permitted range, while P0C0B stands for a lost or open supply and P0C0C for a supply that is too low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's tables for the sibling P0C0B show what the supply is: the gate-drive rails of the IGBT module, on eAssist a 5 V and a 15 V rail that are each watched against limits. A rail running too high stresses the driver stage and can falsify the switching of the power transistors. CARB requires hybrid components to be monitored for circuit faults. Expect the inverter to shut down or derate, with reduced or no electric drive.
c: Faulty voltage regulation of the gate-drive supply inside the motor A inverter
Excessive 12 V system voltage from the DC/DC converter or a charger
Supply or sense line shorted to a higher voltage in the harness
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, hybrid system warning
Reduced or no electric propulsion from motor A
Engine runs more often or the vehicle enters limp mode

P0C0E.t: Drive Motor B Inverter Power Supply Circuit/Open
P0C0E.d: P0C0E is the motor B counterpart of P0C0B: the inverter for the second motor has lost the supply of its gate-drive board. GM documents it on the Volt and the two-mode trucks. The IGBT module reports a bias fault through its status line when the supply of phase A, B or C fails. The 2011 Volt checks with high voltage above 100 V, the 2012 trucks with run/crank voltage between 9.5 and 18 V, both after one count, Type A. The 2016 Volt needs 0.002 s of fault in a 0.024 s window, the 2018 table 0.02 s, the 2019 table 0.168 s, always Type A, one trip. P0C0F and P0C10 cover low and high supply. Motor B can no longer be driven, so propulsion is reduced.
c: Failed gate-drive power supply inside the motor B inverter
Weak 12 V feed, blown fuse or poor ground at the inverter control board
Loose or corroded low-voltage connector at the power inverter module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion message, motor B unavailable
Engine runs continuously instead of electric driving

P0C0F.t: Drive Motor B Inverter Power Supply Circuit Low
P0C0F.d: P0C0F means the supply of the motor B inverter is present but below its permitted range. P0C0E covers a lost or open supply, P0C10 a supply that is too high, and P0C0C is the same fault on motor A. No manufacturer documents P0C0F publicly. GM's tables for P0C0E name the supply in question: the power feed of the gate-drive board, checked phase by phase with run/crank voltage between 9.5 and 18 V on the 2012 trucks. A sagging rail can no longer switch the power transistors fully, so the inverter protects itself. CARB requires circuit monitoring of hybrid components. The driver typically sees a warning and loses the electric drive of motor B.
c: Weak 12 V battery or DC/DC converter output feeding the inverter electronics
Corroded connector or poor ground raising resistance in the inverter supply
Failing internal gate-drive power supply in the motor B inverter
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, hybrid system warning
Reduced propulsion, motor B unavailable
Fault appears mainly with low 12 V voltage, e.g. after standing

P0C10.t: Drive Motor B Inverter Power Supply Circuit High
P0C10.d: P0C10 flags a supply of the motor B inverter that is above its permitted range. Its siblings are P0C0E for a lost or open supply and P0C0F for a low one; P0C0D is the motor A version. No manufacturer documents P0C10 publicly. GM uses only the open-circuit code P0C0E for this supply and describes it as the power feed of the gate-drive board, monitored through the status line of the IGBT module. An overvoltage on that rail can damage the driver circuits, so the controller shuts the inverter down. CARB requires hybrid components to be checked for circuit faults. Expect a warning lamp and loss of the electric drive provided by motor B.
c: Faulty voltage regulation of the gate-drive supply inside the motor B inverter
Excessive 12 V system voltage from the DC/DC converter or an external charger
Supply or sense line shorted to a higher voltage in the harness
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, hybrid system warning
Reduced propulsion, motor B unavailable
Vehicle limited to engine or reduced-power operation

P0C11.t: Drive Motor A Inverter Phase U Over Temperature
P0C11.d: P0C11 is a protective code: the temperature sensor at phase U of the motor A inverter reads a valid but excessive value. GM uses it across its hybrids. The 2011 Volt reads PIM sensor A against 98 °C, the 2012 two-mode trucks against 88 °C with a reset at 85 °C, both Type A; the 2016 Volt sets it above 126 °C for 1.2 s within 2 s, the 2019 table above 128 °C, Type A, one trip. On eAssist the single inverter code P0C11 sets above 118.2 °C as Type B, two trips. Sensor faults such as P0AEE block it. Phase V and W are P0C12 and P0C13. GM advises finding the cause of poor cooling. The inverter cuts power to protect itself.
c: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics cooling loop
Failed or weak electric coolant pump of the inverter loop
Clogged power electronics radiator or inoperative cooling fan
Sustained heavy load such as towing uphill in high ambient heat
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, often with a hybrid system overheat message
Reduced propulsion power until the inverter cools down
Electric drive unavailable, engine runs continuously

P0C12.t: Drive Motor A Inverter Phase V Over Temperature
P0C12.d: P0C12 sets when the inverter for motor A measures an excessive temperature at phase V while its sensor itself is plausible. In GM's 2011 Volt table that is PIM sensor C above 98 °C; the two-mode trucks of 2012 use 88 °C with an 85 °C reset, the 2016 Volt 126 °C for 1.2 s out of 2 s and the 2016 ELR 102.5 °C, all Type A, one trip. The sensor circuit codes of that thermistor, such as P0BD1 and P0BD2, have their own numbers and must be ruled out first. P0C11 and P0C13 are phases U and W, P0C15 is phase V on motor B. GM bulletin PIC6303A lists these overheat codes as a sign of insufficient cooling. Power is reduced while the inverter is hot.
c: Low coolant level or trapped air in the inverter cooling loop
Inoperative electric coolant pump of the power electronics
Blocked low-temperature radiator or failed cooling fan
Degraded thermal contact or failing power stage inside the inverter
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Propulsion power reduced, especially under load or in hot weather
Hybrid system overheat or service message

P0C13.t: Drive Motor A Inverter Phase W Over Temperature
P0C13.d: P0C13 covers phase W of the motor A inverter: the controller sees a credible sensor reading that exceeds the overtemperature limit. GM's 2011 Volt uses PIM sensor E with 98 °C, the 2012 two-mode trucks 88 °C, the 2016 and 2018 tables 126 °C for 1.2 s within a 2 s window and the 2019 table 128 °C for 1.5 s, always Type A, one trip, so the MIL comes on at once. The check is blocked while circuit or performance faults of the thermistor are active. Siblings are P0C11 for phase U and P0C12 for phase V; P0C16 is phase W on motor B. Because the code reports a real heat condition, the cooling system of the power electronics is the first place to look; output stays limited.
c: Coolant loss or air pocket in the power electronics loop
Electric coolant pump for the inverter stopped or running slow
Debris on the low-temperature radiator or cooling fan not running
s: Malfunction indicator lamp immediately after the fault
Reduced propulsion until temperatures drop
Engine runs more often, little or no electric driving

P0C14.t: Drive Motor B Inverter Phase U Over Temperature
P0C14.d: P0C14 is the motor B counterpart of P0C11: phase U of the second inverter has become too hot while its temperature sensor reads plausibly. GM documents it on the Volt and the two-mode trucks. The 2011 Volt compares PIM sensor B with 98 °C, the 2012 trucks use 88 °C with a reset at 85 °C, the 2016 Volt 131 °C for 1.2 s in 2 s and the 2019 table 131 °C for 1.5 s, all Type A, one trip. Sensor circuit codes such as P0AF2 or P0AF3 point to the thermistor instead and are checked first. P0C15 and P0C16 cover phases V and W. GM bulletin PIC6303A sends technicians to the cooling system when inverter overheat codes appear. Power from motor B is limited meanwhile.
c: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics cooling loop
Failed electric coolant pump of the inverter loop
Clogged low-temperature radiator or failed cooling fan
Long periods of high load on motor B, e.g. towing or steep climbs
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion power, especially under load
Hybrid system overheat message

P0C15.t: Drive Motor B Inverter Phase V Over Temperature
P0C15.d: P0C15 reports overtemperature at phase V of the motor B inverter, based on a sensor reading that is valid but above the limit. GM applies it on the Volt and the two-mode trucks: PIM sensor D above 98 °C on the 2011 Volt, 88 °C on the 2012 trucks, 102.5 °C on the 2016 ELR, 131 °C for 1.2 s within 2 s on the 2016 Volt and in the 2018 table, every time Type A with one trip. It is a protective diagnosis, not a wiring check; the thermistor's own codes P0BD6 and P0BD7 handle sensor faults. Phase U and W are P0C14 and P0C16, phase V on motor A is P0C12. GM bulletin PIC6303A names P0C15 among the overheat codes that call for a cooling diagnosis. Motor B output is restricted.
c: Coolant loss or air in the inverter cooling loop
Electric coolant pump of the power electronics not working
Blocked radiator for the power electronics or fan failure
Poor heat transfer or ageing power stage inside the inverter
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion until the inverter has cooled
Engine runs more often than usual

P0C16.t: Drive Motor B Inverter Phase W Over Temperature
P0C16.d: P0C16 is set by the motor B inverter when phase W runs too hot and the temperature sensor itself shows no fault. GM's tables give PIM sensor F above 98 °C for the 2011 Volt, above 88 °C with an 85 °C reset for the 2012 two-mode trucks, and 131 °C for 1.2 s within 2 s for the 2016 Volt, with 1.5 s in the 2019 table; each is Type A, one trip. Thermistor circuit codes such as P0BE0 and P0BE1 take priority and block the check. P0C14 and P0C15 are phases U and V, P0C13 is phase W on motor A. CARB allows some protective overtemperature strategies to run without MIL, but GM lights it here. Look for weak cooling first; until then motor B is derated.
c: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics loop
Electric coolant pump of the inverter failed or blocked
Dirty low-temperature radiator or inoperative fan
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion, notably at high load or high ambient temperature
Hybrid system overheat message

P0C17.t: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Not Learned
P0C17.d: P0C17 means the controller has no valid learned offset for the resolver of motor A, which it needs to align rotor position with the stator field. GM runs the learn at key-off and sets the code if it fails without a stored value: motor speed above 50 rpm, DC voltage below 192 V (200 V on the 2016 Volt), phase current below 15 A or a learn time over 1.4 s. The Volt is Type A, the 2012 two-mode trucks Type B. GM bulletin 21-NA-218 links it to missing high voltage or three-phase current, loose phase terminals or stator damage on Volt and ELR. Mazda requires the speed sensor learn on CX-90 and CX-70 PHEV after inverter or motor replacement. P0C4E reports a learned value out of range.
c: Offset learn not performed after replacing the inverter, motor or resolver
High voltage not reaching the inverter during the learn, e.g. contactor or HV cable fault
Loose three-phase ring terminals after a repair
s: Engine starts and stalls or will not start after a repair
Malfunction indicator lamp with reduced propulsion message
Electric drive unavailable

P0C18.t: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Not Learned
P0C18.d: P0C18 is the motor B version of P0C17: the resolver offset of the second motor has not been learned and no valid earlier value is stored. GM performs the learn at key-off; it fails if motor speed exceeds 50 rpm, DC voltage stays below 192 V, phase current stays below 15 A or the learn takes longer than 1.4 s. The Volt tables rate it Type A, one trip, the 2012 two-mode trucks Type B, two trips. GM bulletin 21-NA-218 notes that when P0C17 and P0C18 set together, a programming event is needed to allow a wide position sensor learn, and that missing high voltage at the drive motor control module can be the reason. P0C4F reports a learned value beyond its limit.
c: Offset learn not completed after replacing the inverter, motor B or its resolver
No high voltage at the drive motor control module, e.g. contactor fault or disconnected HV cable
Control module needs reprogramming to enable a wide position sensor learn
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after a repair or module programming
Reduced propulsion or vehicle will not enter ready mode
Motor B unavailable for driving or charging

P0C19.t: Drive Motor A Torque Delivered Performance
P0C19.d: P0C19 is a plausibility check: the torque that motor A actually delivers, calculated by the motor control processor, does not follow the slewed torque command. GM sets it when the difference exceeds 123 Nm for 0.1875 s within 0.2 s on the 2016 and 2018 tables, Type A, one trip; eAssist uses 36 Nm as Type B, two trips. The 2012 two-mode trucks check whether the sum of the three phase currents exceeds 110 A for 200 ms. Stellantis lists P0C19 on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe and the Wagoneer PHEV with P1B03, a resolver rationality fault, and cures it by reflashing the power inverter module. The electric drive shuts down and the engine takes over.
c: Implausible rotor position signal from the motor A resolver or its wiring
Faulty phase current sensing distorting the calculated torque
Internal fault of the inverter power stage or motor winding
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Electric drive shuts off and the engine takes over
Engine stop-start no longer works or a service hybrid system warning appears

P0C1A.t: Drive Motor B Torque Delivered Performance
P0C1A.d: P0C1A compares the torque command for motor B with the torque the motor control processor calculates as actually delivered. GM's 2016, 2018 and 2019 tables set it when the difference exceeds 132 Nm for 0.1875 s in a 0.2 s window, Type A, one trip, and only while listed resolver and motor control faults are inactive. The 2011 Volt and 2012 two-mode tables also list it, the trucks with a three-phase current sum above 110 A. Chrysler documents it on the 2017 to 2023 Pacifica Hybrid: with resolver codes P0A3F, P0A43 or P0A45 it points to a short in the internal wiring connector of the eFlite transmission, which is replaced. P0C19 is motor A. Expect limp mode.
c: Short in the internal transmission wiring connector (Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid 21-008-23)
Implausible rotor position signal from the motor B resolver
Hybrid control or inverter module software requiring an update
Faulty phase current sensing for motor B
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Vehicle in limp mode with reduced propulsion
Hybrid system warning, engine runs more often

P0C1B.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Too High
P0C1B.d: P0C1B is a protection code: the electronics that drive the auxiliary transmission fluid pump measure a valid but excessive internal temperature. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM shows the same function on the 2016 Cadillac ELR pump controller under its own code P1E37, an in-range overtemperature above 98 °C that could damage the inverter, checked only when the sensor itself is plausible. A Honda patent for a CVT pump explains the reaction: once the board temperature passes a limit, the control unit opens the pump relay and keeps the pump off until the fluid has cooled. The pump then stops, so start-stop and pressure support are lost. P0C1C to P0C1F cover faults of the temperature sensor itself and must be excluded first.
c: High transmission fluid temperature from heavy load, towing or a weak fluid cooler
Pump running against high resistance (binding, clogged filter) and heating its driver
Poor heat transfer from the module (mounting, contamination) or internal module fault
s: Engine auto-stop temporarily unavailable
Transmission or hybrid warning, MIL depending on manufacturer
Harsh engagement when driving off after a stop

P0C1C.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0C1C.d: P0C1C is the general circuit fault of the temperature sensor inside the auxiliary pump control module, used when the signal is invalid without fitting the low, high or range checks. No manufacturer documents it publicly. GM's 2016 ELR pump controller monitors its inverter sensor with own codes P1E34 to P1E36 instead, and the Honda CVT pump patent shows why the reading matters: it is the basis for switching the pump off before the board overheats. Without a valid value the controller cannot protect itself, so the pump usually runs restricted or stays off. CARB requires such sensors to be checked for circuit faults. Because the sensor is on the circuit board, the fix is normally the module or the pump assembly. P0C1D to P0C1F are the specific variants.
c: Temperature sensor or its measuring circuit on the module board faulty
Unstable supply or ground of the pump module distorting the sensor reading
Moisture or fluid inside the module housing
s: Warning lamp or transmission message
Start-stop function inactive

P0C1D.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0C1D.d: P0C1D means the internal temperature sensor of the auxiliary pump module delivers an electrically valid value that does not fit the other temperatures in the vehicle. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM's comparable check on the 2016 ELR pump controller, own code P1E36, runs after at least 6 hours of inactivity: the inverter reading is compared with the average of the power electronics coolant and transmission fluid temperatures, and a difference above 20 °C fails, Type B, MIL after two trips. A sensor that reads too low would let the board overheat unnoticed, which is why the Honda pump patent bases shutdown on this value. P0C1E and P0C1F cover voltage out of range, P0C1B real overtemperature.
c: Board temperature sensor drifted or measuring circuit out of tolerance
Reference value wrong because the transmission fluid or coolant temperature sensor is faulty
Internal fault of the pump control module
s: MIL after repeated detection
Start-stop restricted or unavailable

P0C1E.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0C1E.d: P0C1E reports that the signal voltage of the module's internal temperature sensor is below its valid range. With the usual NTC thermistor, low voltage corresponds to a very high temperature, so a short to ground looks like an overheated board. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM shows the scale on the 2016 ELR pump controller with its own code P1E35, labelled circuit low: a reading above 130 °C, near 0 V, for 250 of 350 samples at 10.4 ms sets a Type B fault, MIL after two trips. The Honda CVT pump patent uses this board value to cut the pump relay, so a shorted sensor can stop the pump although nothing is hot. P0C1F is the high side, P0C1B a genuine overtemperature.
c: Board temperature sensor or its signal path shorted to ground inside the module
Measuring circuit of the pump control module faulty
Fluid or moisture on the module board
s: Pump switched off as if overheated, auto-stop unavailable
MIL after two drive cycles

P0C1F.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0C1F.d: P0C1F means the internal temperature sensor of the auxiliary pump module delivers a voltage above its valid range, which for an NTC thermistor reads as an implausibly cold board and usually indicates an open sensor path. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM's ELR pump controller of 2016 shows the matching case under its own code P1E34, labelled circuit high: below -58 °C, near 5 V, for 250 of 350 samples sets the fault, Type B in the ELR tables. With such a value the controller loses its overtemperature protection; the Honda CVT pump patent shows that this protection is what keeps the driver board alive, so the pump is typically restricted. P0C1E is the low side, P0C1D the plausibility check, P0C1B real overtemperature.
c: Board temperature sensor open or its solder joint cracked
Measuring circuit of the pump control module faulty
Ground offset at the pump module shifting the sensor voltage
s: MIL after two drive cycles
Start-stop restricted, pump in protective mode

P0C20.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Phase U-V-W Circuit/Open
P0C20.d: P0C20 means at least one of the three motor phases of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump carries no current, typically an open lead, terminal or winding. GM uses it in the pump controller of the Chevrolet Volt (2011-15 tables) and the 2016 Cadillac ELR: with the inverter in Run, high voltage above 35 V and the rotor within 30 degrees of a phase axis, the peak current of that phase is checked; below 1 A for 200 counts sets the code, Type A, MIL on the first trip. Each phase is tested in turn as the rotor turns. The pump cannot build torque, so pressure support and electric operation are lost. Later GM tables split the check into the per-phase codes P0B01, P0B04 and P0B07; P0C21/P0C22 are the low and high variants.
c: Motor connector of the pump not fully seated, or loose phase terminal
Open phase lead between pump inverter and motor
Power switch of one phase in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding in the pump motor
s: MIL and Service Vehicle Soon message
Reduced propulsion or no electric drive mode
Engine restart harsh or delayed

P0C21.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Phase U-V-W Circuit Low
P0C21.d: P0C21 reports a low condition on the phase U, V or W circuits of the auxiliary pump motor, usually a phase lead shorted to ground or a voltage at a phase terminal that stays below what the inverter commands. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM watches the same wiring on the Volt and ELR with the open-circuit code P0C20 and catches shorts through overcurrent on P0C28 and its own phase current sensor codes P1E2A to P1E32. The Hitachi idle-stop pump patent shows that the inverter often reconstructs all phase currents from one DC-bus shunt, so a ground short and a sensing fault can look alike. The pump usually shuts down, auto-stop is blocked. P0C20 is the open circuit, P0C22 the high side, P0B01 to P0B08 the per-phase current codes.
c: Phase lead chafed through and shorted to ground or the transmission case
Transmission fluid or water in the motor connector creating a leakage path
Low-side switch or phase sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Motor winding shorted to the stator core
s: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump off, no engine auto-stop

P0C22.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Phase U-V-W Circuit High
P0C22.d: P0C22 reports a high condition on the U-V-W phase circuits of the auxiliary pump motor, for example a phase lead shorted to the supply or a phase voltage that stays high while the inverter should pull it down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. In GM's Volt tables the closest monitors are P0C28, which trips above 35 A on any phase within a few milliseconds to protect the IGBTs, and its own phase sensor codes P1E2B, P1E2E and P1E31 for readings above 30 A. The Hitachi sub-oil pump patent shows that phase currents are often calculated from a shared bus shunt, so a sensing error must be ruled out before the wiring is condemned. The pump stops and auto-stop is blocked. P0C21 is the low side, P0B02, P0B05 and P0B08 the per-phase high codes.
c: Phase lead shorted to supply voltage or to another phase
High-side switch of the pump inverter stuck conducting
Phase current sensing in the inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in the pump motor winding
s: MIL and hybrid or transmission warning
Pump shuts down, harsh engagement after stops

P0C23.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Circuit/Open
P0C23.d: P0C23 is set by the controlling module, usually the PCM, TCM or hybrid controller, when the circuit to the auxiliary pump control module is open. J2012 does not name the line further; in practice it is the command or enable wire. Ford's 2016 F-150 2.7L bulletin shows such a command: the PCM drives the pump with a duty cycle that a scan tool can vary from 20 to 90 percent. GM's ELR pump controller only runs its phase tests while a wake-up signal is on. No manufacturer publicly documents P0C23 itself. With the line open the pump gets no command and stays off, so auto-stop is disabled and pressure support is missing. P0C24 and P0C25 are the low and high variants, P0C2B to P0C2E the feedback line in the other direction.
c: Open command or enable wire between controller and pump module
Pushed-out or corroded terminal at the pump module or controller connector
Input stage of the pump control module faulty
s: Start-stop no longer works
MIL or transmission warning
Harsh engagement after an engine stop

P0C24.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Circuit Low
P0C24.d: P0C24 means the circuit from the controlling module to the auxiliary pump control module is held low, typically a short to ground on the command line. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. How the line is used is visible in Ford's 2016 F-150 2.7L bulletin, where the PCM commands the start-stop pump by duty cycle and the technician checks the pump by sweeping that command from 20 to 90 percent. A grounded line leaves the pump without a valid command or, depending on logic, permanently off. GM's ELR pump controller likewise depends on its wake-up signal to run. CARB requires output circuits of such components to be monitored. P0C23 is the open circuit, P0C25 the high side, P2796 to P2798 the classic pump control circuit codes.
c: Command wire shorted to ground, e.g. chafed at the transmission case
Fluid or corrosion in the pump connector pulling the line low
Output stage in the PCM/TCM or input of the pump module faulty
s: No engine auto-stop
MIL or transmission warning

P0C25.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Circuit High
P0C25.d: P0C25 reports that the circuit from the controlling module to the auxiliary pump control module sits high, for instance a command wire shorted to battery voltage or an output that cannot pull the line down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Ford's 2016 F-150 2.7L bulletin shows the type of signal involved: a PCM duty-cycle command that can be swept from 20 to 90 percent to prove pump operation. A line stuck high can be read as a constant full command or rejected as invalid, so the pump may run continuously or be shut off. GM's ELR pump controller also uses a separate wake-up line as enable. CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. P0C23 is the open circuit, P0C24 the low side, P0C2E the high fault on the feedback line.
c: Command wire shorted to battery or another supply voltage
Output stage in the PCM/TCM stuck high
Input stage of the pump control module faulty
s: MIL or transmission warning
Pump runs continuously or start-stop is disabled

P0C26.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Current
P0C26.d: P0C26 is the general motor current fault of auxiliary pump A: the current drawn does not match what the commanded operating point should need, without clearly being too low or too high. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Its siblings show what is monitored: Ford stores P0C27, current too low, on 2014-16 Fusion and 2015-16 Edge with the 6F35 start-stop transmission when air enters the pump supply tube, and GM sets P0C28 on the Volt and ELR when any phase exceeds 35 A. CARB requires such components to be checked for rationality. A general current code therefore points to aeration, low fluid, a binding pump or current sensing errors. The pump may be switched off and auto-stop blocked; P0C27 and P0C28 are the specific variants.
c: Low or aerated transmission fluid at the pump intake
Pump binding or contaminated, changing the motor load
Current sensing in the pump driver implausible
Outdated control software of the pump or controlling module
s: MIL or transmission warning
Harsh engagement after an auto-stop
Start-stop deactivated

P0C27.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Current Low
P0C27.d: P0C27 means motor A of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump draws less current than expected, a sign that the pump is not loaded, for example because it sucks air or turns without delivering. Ford documents it twice. TSB 16-0111 covers 2014-16 Fusion and 2015-16 Edge with the 6F35 transmission and start-stop: MIL, P0C27 in the PCM and a harsh engagement after an auto-stop, caused by air entering the pump supply tube on transmissions built up to 26 February 2016; a new tube with a check ball fixes it. TSB 18-2282 for the 2013-17 Fusion Energi and C-Max Energi lists P0C27 and/or P0C28 and calls for reprogramming the PCM and hybrid module. P0C28 is the high side, P0C26 the general code, P0C2A a stalled motor.
c: Air entering the pump supply tube (Ford 6F35, new tube with check ball)
Calibration of PCM and hybrid module (Ford Fusion/C-Max Energi)
Low transmission fluid level letting the pump draw air
High resistance or open circuit in the pump motor wiring
s: MIL on
Harsh transmission engagement after a start-stop event

P0C28.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Current High
P0C28.d: P0C28 is the overcurrent protection of auxiliary pump motor A. GM uses it on Volt, ELR and later hybrids: the inverter trips when any of the U, V or W phases exceeds 35 A, in 2016 within about 4 ms of a 62 ms window, or when the d-axis current falls below a stator temperature limit, Type A, MIL on the first trip. GM service update 18199 for the 2018 Cadillac CT6 plug-in traces P0C28 to a faulty pump restart logic in the software. Ford's TSB 18-2282 lists P0C27 and/or P0C28 on the 2013-17 Fusion Energi and C-Max Energi, fixed by reprogramming the PCM and hybrid module; Ford also reports P0C28 in the SOBDMC of the 2024-25 Mustang Mach-E LFP, solved by software. P0C27 is the low side.
c: Pump control software faulty (Cadillac CT6 update 18199, Ford Energi TSB 18-2282)
Pump seized, contaminated or running against blocked flow
Short between motor phases or to ground
Current sensing or power stage in the pump inverter faulty
s: MIL or service wrench lamp
Auxiliary pump shuts down, no auto-stop or electric mode

P0C29.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Driver Circuit Performance
P0C29.d: P0C29 means the driver stage of auxiliary pump A does not behave as commanded, for instance the pump does not reach its target or the activation is reported as implausible. Volkswagen Group documents it on the 7-speed DSG 0GC (DQ381): VW lists P0C29 for the 2018 Golf R as implausible activation of auxiliary hydraulic pump 1 (V475), often with clutch and gear actuator codes as consequences; Audi's bulletin for the 2017-18 A3, A3 Cabriolet and S3 with gearbox dated up to 26 September 2017 calls for replacing the auxiliary hydraulic pump when only P0C29 remains. The customer sees a Gearbox Malfunction warning. VW improved the pump from October 2017 production. P0C2A is a stalled motor, P0C26 to P0C28 current faults.
c: Auxiliary hydraulic pump V475 of early production faulty (VW/Audi 0GC)
Poor contact at the pump electrical connection
Transmission control software not updated per service action
s: Gearbox Malfunction warning in the instrument cluster
Consequential clutch or gear actuator codes, limp mode

P0C2A.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Stalled
P0C2A.d: P0C2A means motor A of the auxiliary pump is commanded but does not turn, or turns far slower than required. Ford documents it in TSB 17-2056 for the 2016 F-150 2.7L with start-stop built from 1 May 2016: with the fluid above 38 °C the technician commands the pump through the PCM at duty cycles from 20 to 90 percent; if it runs, the PCM gets new software, if not, the auxiliary pump is replaced. GM shows how a stall is detected on the ELR pump controller, under its own code P1E3A: commanded minus actual speed above 200 rpm while more than 6.8 Nm is requested, Type A. Sensorless pumps cannot measure speed directly, so a stall shows up as a speed or current mismatch. P0C29 covers the driver stage, P0C28 overcurrent.
c: Auxiliary pump seized or jammed by debris (Ford F-150 2.7L replaces the pump)
PCM calibration causing false stall detection (Ford TSB 17-2056)
Very cold, thick fluid or wrong fluid type raising drag
Open phase so the motor cannot develop torque
s: MIL on
Start-stop inactive, harsh engagement after stops

P0C2B.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Feedback Signal
P0C2B.d: P0C2B concerns the status signal the auxiliary pump control module sends back to the controlling module. GM uses it on the Two-Mode hybrid trucks and SUVs (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra, 2ML70): the hybrid controller expects a complete fault status message from the pump controller every 1.5 s; if it is missing or incomplete for 9.75 s with the vehicle in Run or Crank, the code sets as Type B, MIL after two trips. GM preliminary information PIP4751G stresses that P0C2B, with or without P2797, rarely means a bad pump: check the wiring, replace the pump control module if its date code is 089-11 or older, and note that a key held in Crank during a no-start can set it. P0C2C to P0C2E are the specific variants.
c: Wiring or terminal tension fault between hybrid controller and pump control module
Early pump control module (GM date code 089-11 or older)
Key held in crank for a long time during a no-start
s: MIL after two drive cycles
Bumps, lulls or surges around auto-stops

P0C2C.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Feedback Signal Range/Performance
P0C2C.d: P0C2C means the feedback signal from the auxiliary pump control module is present and electrically valid but does not make sense, for example a reported speed or status that contradicts the command. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Its siblings show the signal: on GM's Two-Mode trucks P0C2B watches a fault status message expected every 1.5 s, and on the 2021-23 Chevrolet Bolt EV and 2022 Bolt EUV GM bulletin 21-NA-148 pairs P0C2D with the pump performance codes P2797 and P2798, caused by bad solder joints in the low-voltage pump. CARB requires rationality checks for such inputs. Implausible feedback usually points to the pump electronics themselves. P0C2B is the general code, P0C2D and P0C2E the low and high variants.
c: Electronics of the pump module reporting wrong status or speed
Intermittent contact on the feedback line distorting the signal
Pump not following the command mechanically, so feedback and command differ
s: Service Vehicle Soon or MIL
Reduced propulsion power or no start-stop

P0C2D.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Feedback Signal Low
P0C2D.d: P0C2D reports that the feedback signal from the electric transmission fluid pump module stays low, below its valid range. GM documents it for the 2021-23 Chevrolet Bolt EV and 2022 Bolt EUV in bulletin 21-NA-148: the driver sees Propulsion Power is Reduced and a Service Vehicle Soon lamp, with P0C2D, P2797 or P2798 stored. The cause is a part quality spill in the low-voltage electric transmission fluid pump on the driver side of the drive unit, where a soldering process was out of specification; the motor is not serviceable, so the complete pump is replaced. In this EV the pump supplies fluid for cooling and lubricating the drive unit. P0C2B is the general feedback code, P0C2C the plausibility and P0C2E the high variant.
c: Faulty solder joints in the electric transmission fluid pump (Chevrolet Bolt, GM 21-NA-148)
s: Propulsion Power is Reduced message
Service Vehicle Soon lamp

P0C2E.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Feedback Signal High
P0C2E.d: P0C2E means the feedback line from the auxiliary pump control module sits above its valid range, for example shorted to supply voltage or no longer pulled down by the module. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM's use of the siblings shows what the line carries: on the Two-Mode hybrids P0C2B watches a status message from the pump controller every 1.5 s, Type B, and on the Chevrolet Bolt EV and EUV bulletin 21-NA-148 links the low variant P0C2D to bad solder joints inside the pump. A stuck-high line can hide real pump faults, so the controller usually stops relying on the pump. CARB requires circuit checks for such signals. P0C2D is the low side, P0C2C the plausibility check, P0C25 the high fault on the command line.
c: Feedback line shorted to supply voltage
Output stage of the pump control module no longer switching
Lost ground at the pump module letting the line float high
s: MIL or Service Vehicle Soon lamp
Start-stop or electric drive restricted

P0C2F.t: Internal Control Module Drive Motor/Generator - Engine Speed Sensor Performance
P0C2F.d: P0C2F is an internal plausibility check of the hybrid control processor: the engine speed it reads through its own sensor path must match other speed information. In GM's Two-Mode truck tables (12OBDG06, 13OBDG06) the HCP compares its SPI-sensed engine speed with the calculated transmission input speed and with the engine speed received over CAN; a deviation beyond 250 rpm above 1500 rpm, with a wider band at lower speed, in 160 of 320 samples sets it as Type A, MIL after one trip. Ford uses it on the 2021–2023 Mustang Mach-E as P0C2F:92 in the secondary OBD module C, paired with a 1 Pedal Drive fault message; bulletin 24-2187 fixes it by reprogramming the powertrain modules. Real sensor circuit faults have their own codes.
c: Control module software flagging the comparison falsely (Ford Mach-E, fixed by reprogramming)
Speed signals disagree because of a faulty input or a disturbed CAN signal
Internal fault of the hybrid control module
s: MIL or hybrid system warning
One pedal drive or regenerative functions switched off (Ford Mach-E)
Reduced hybrid assist or limited power

P0C30.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack State of Charge High
P0C30.d: P0C30 is the counterpart of P0A7D: the battery controller finds that the state of charge of the high-voltage pack stays above its usable window. CARB requires hybrid OBD to flag a state of charge that can no longer be kept inside the manufacturer's range. GM's 2019 hybrid table 19OBDG01 describes the method: the SOC is checked once per drive cycle, the controller first allows time for the motor to draw the charge back down, then counts the distance driven with excessive SOC; if that share exceeds half of a trip longer than 50 km, at speeds above 15 km/h and pack temperature at least −10 °C, the code is stored as Type B, two trips. No other manufacturer documents it publicly. The car limits regeneration and charging to protect the cells, so braking feel and fuel economy can change.
c: Wrong SOC estimate from a drifting pack current or voltage measurement
Battery or hybrid control software not drawing the charge down as intended
Electric assist blocked by another fault, so the pack cannot discharge
s: MIL after two trips
Reduced or no regenerative braking
Changed brake pedal feel and higher fuel consumption

P0C31.d: P0C31 reports that the cooling circuit of a second power inverter does not remove heat as expected; inverter A has its own code, P0A93. Vehicles with two separately cooled power electronics units, for example a front and a rear drive unit, need this second code. CARB requires hybrid OBD to monitor the parts used for inverter thermal management and, where feasible, to check the cooling performance itself. No manufacturer documents P0C31 publicly. For the analogous P0A93, Hyundai's 2011 Sonata Hybrid bulletin 14-HC-001 points to the electric water pump, and coolant pump faults of the B circuit are reported as P0B38 or P0C74. To protect the semiconductors the controller limits motor power. A low coolant level or trapped air is worth checking first.
c: Low coolant level or air trapped in the inverter B circuit
