P20E7 is set when the measured air pressure climbs above the permitted upper limit, for instance because the pressure control valve no longer throttles and passes full tank pressure, or because the path downstream of the sensor is narrowed so pressure builds up in front of it. Cummins bulletin TSB200096 shows how DEF crystals form in the air solenoid and the nozzle of air-assisted dosers, restricting flow and distorting the spray pattern. A skewed air pressure sensor gives the same reading. Airless systems in passenger cars do not have this circuit. No maker documents P20E7 publicly; CARB requires the air-assisted delivery to be monitored. Low pressure and leakage are P20E6 and P20CA.
c: Air pressure control valve no longer regulating and passing full supply pressure
DEF crystals or deposits restricting the nozzle or mixing path
Air pressure sensor reading too high
s: Check engine light and SCR warning
Irregular DEF spray, deposits in the exhaust and higher NOx
Engine derate if dosing is shut down

P20E8.d: Airless DEF systems hold the fluid at a set pressure ahead of the dosing valve with an electric pump, read by a pressure sensor. P20E8 means the measured value stays clearly below that target or cannot be built up at all. Ford's 2023 diesel summary (6.7 L and 3.0 L) sets it when the pressure is more than 200 kPa under setpoint or the pump fails to reach pressure control after five attempts; GM's 18OBDG04 table uses a deviation above 166 kPa or more than two failed build-ups and rates it Type A. Many makers report it in bulletins: Ford for air trapped in lines and loss of prime after storage, Hino for blocked vent or inlet connectors, Volvo and Mack for leaks, empty or frozen tanks, Chevrolet Colorado for a superseded pump. P20E9 covers overpressure, P208B a pump that does not run as commanded.
c: Air in the DEF lines or pump that lost its prime, for example after long storage
Clogged pump inlet, suction tube, filter or tank vent, often from contamination
External leak at a DEF line, connector or the dosing valve
Worn, crystallised or superseded DEF pump unit
s: Check engine light and DEF system warning message
No DEF dosing, rising NOx and a countdown to speed limitation or no restart
Pump can be heard running longer than usual after key on

P20E9.d: P20E9 is the overpressure counterpart of P20E8: during closed-loop control the DEF pressure ahead of the dosing valve rises clearly above its target. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets it at more than 150 kPa over setpoint; GM's 18OBDG04 table asks for the same 150 kPa excess while the pump runs below 3,200 rpm (Type A), and GM's 2025 DEF table 25OBDG04A uses a 63 kPa window for 4 s. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI data book names absolute limits of 650 and 795 kPa. Typical reasons are a blocked return path or dosing valve, deposits from contaminated fluid and a pressure sensor reading high. Audi traced Q7 TDI cases to a damaged AdBlue filter seal that let unfiltered fluid harm sensor and pump; Hino links it to debris in the tank. Ram and Jeep EcoDiesel software bulletins list it as well.
c: Blocked return path, restricted line or dosing valve not opening properly
Debris in the fluid after a damaged filter seal or dirty refilling
Reductant pressure sensor reading too high
Pump control software needing an update
s: Check engine light and DEF system warning
Dosing shut off, NOx warning and later inducement countdown

P20EA.t: Reductant Control Module Power Relay De-Energized Performance - Too Early
P20EA.d: Many SCR systems supply the reductant control module, and through it pump and heaters, via a power relay. After the key is switched off the relay should stay energised for a short after-run so the pump can empty the lines and the module can save its learned values, and only then drop out on the module's command. P20EA means the supply disappeared before that point. Fluid left in the lines can then freeze or crystallise, and stored data may be lost. No maker documents P20EA publicly. The monitoring follows the engine-module pair P068A/P068B: Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel reads back the relay voltage on its control line, and Ford's 2023 diesel summary checks the reductant control module relay (P21C7) by comparing commanded state with the measured voltage. A relay that drops out late is P20EB.
c: Worn relay contacts or coil interrupting the supply early
Loose fuse, terminal or ground in the relay or module feed
Battery disconnected or voltage collapsing right after shut-off
Reductant control module releasing the relay prematurely
s: Check engine light, often without noticeable driving symptoms
DEF lines not purged, risk of frozen or crystallised lines in winter

P20EB.t: Reductant Control Module Power Relay De-Energized Performance - Too Late
P20EB.d: Here the opposite of P20EA happens: after the reductant control module has finished its after-run and released the power relay, voltage is still present on the switched side, so the relay opens late or not at all. Typical reasons are welded contacts, a control line shorted to ground that keeps the coil energised, or a module that never ends its shut-down. The DEF module, pump and heaters may then stay powered with the engine off, which drains the battery and keeps the system awake. No maker documents P20EB publicly. The check mirrors P068B on the engine module, which Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel derives from the relay control circuit, and Ford's 2023 diesel summary flags a reductant relay voltage above 0 V while the output stage is off (P21C7). CARB requires such SCR components to be monitored.
c: Relay control line shorted to ground, keeping the coil energised
Reductant control module or network activity preventing shut-down
s: Check engine light
Battery drained after the vehicle has been parked
DEF pump or relay audible long after switching off

P20EC.d: P20EC means the engine computer has registered a temperature in the SCR catalyst of bank 1 above the limit its washcoat can tolerate. The limit depends on the formulation: vanadium-based SCR material starts to sublimate irreversibly above roughly 550 °C, as Navistar's patent US20190232224 and the US rule 40 CFR 1036.115 both state, and US heavy-duty certification requires engine makers to protect such catalysts from high temperatures. Copper and iron zeolites tolerate more. No manufacturer documents P20EC publicly with thresholds; Ford's 2023 diesels, for example, report aftertreatment overheating as P200C/P200E. Typical triggers are an uncontrolled exotherm during filter regeneration, fuel or oil reaching the exhaust, or a faulty temperature sensor. The code warns of possible lasting damage, so a later P20EE is a common follow-up.
c: Excess heat release during particulate filter regeneration
Unburnt fuel or oil reaching the exhaust (leaking injector, turbo seal)
SCR temperature sensor reading too high
Regeneration or thermal-management calibration needing an update
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Regeneration interrupted or power reduced to protect the aftertreatment
Later loss of NOx conversion (follow-up code P20EE)

P20ED.d: P20ED applies to systems with two SCR stages in series: a small pre-catalyst mounted close to the engine, often with its own dosing unit, ahead of the main SCR brick. The code says this front stage on bank 1 got hotter than permitted. Paccar's patent US11976582 explains why such close-coupled SCR units exist: they sit where exhaust heat arrives first, so they work soon after a cold start, but for the same reason they see the highest temperatures, including those released by the oxidation catalyst during filter regeneration. Vanadium formulations begin to sublimate above about 550 °C, and 40 CFR 1036.115 obliges heavy-duty engine makers to keep the catalyst below such limits. No manufacturer documents P20ED publicly. P20EC is the same fault on the main catalyst. Expect the MIL; damage later shows as P20EF.
c: Heat from oxidation catalyst or filter regeneration reaching the close-coupled stage
Fuel or oil entering the exhaust upstream of the pre-catalyst
Temperature sensor at the pre-catalyst reading too high
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Front SCR dosing stopped or regeneration interrupted
Higher NOx emissions after a cold start

P20EE.t: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P20EE.d: P20EE is the main monitor CARB requires for the NOx-reducing catalyst: the share of NOx removed by the SCR catalyst on bank 1, judged by the NOx sensors before and after it, has fallen below what the system needs. Ford's 2023 6.7 L diesel fails it when cumulative efficiency drops under 55 % with the SCR inlet at 200–320 °C. GM's 2018 diesels compare measured with expected efficiency, partly via an EWMA filter, as a Type A code. Ram and Jeep 3.0 L and 6.7 L diesels had bulletins replacing the SCR catalyst (18-064-15, 18-038-16), Isuzu N-Series and the 2015 Cruze diesel got new software. Because poor DEF also cuts efficiency, GM pairs this code with a DEF quality warning, and a speed limit may follow. Check DEF quality, dosing, leaks and NOx sensors before condemning the catalyst.
c: Diluted or contaminated DEF, or a clogged or leaking dosing valve
Upstream or downstream NOx sensor reading wrong
SCR catalyst aged, overheated or poisoned
Exhaust leak between the two NOx sensors
Calibration needing an update (several manufacturer bulletins)
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF or exhaust fluid quality warning in the instrument cluster
Speed limitation countdown on some vehicles if the fault persists

P20EF.t: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P20EF.d: P20EF concerns the front stage of an SCR arrangement with two stages on bank 1: the pre-catalyst no longer removes enough NOx. CARB allows catalysts in series to be monitored individually or together; this code is used where the front stage is checked separately, which requires a NOx sensor between the two bricks. Paccar's patent US11976582 describes such a layout and computes the front stage's efficiency from NOx entering and leaving it. Hino uses P20EF on 2016–2019 trucks with J08E and J05E engines; bulletin SB-18-024 corrected the workshop troubleshooting for it, without public thresholds. A failing front stage shifts load to the main catalyst, so overall NOx may still look acceptable at first. P20EE covers the main catalyst, P20ED overheating of the pre-catalyst. The driver mainly sees the MIL.
c: Front DEF dosing valve clogged, crystallised or leaking
NOx sensor before or between the stages reading wrong
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Higher NOx at low exhaust temperatures, for example after cold starts

P20F0.d: P20F0 is the bank 2 version of P20EC: the SCR catalyst in the second exhaust line has been exposed to temperatures above its permitted limit. It presupposes a V engine with one aftertreatment path per bank, which is rare; most diesels merge both banks into one SCR line and use only the bank 1 codes. No manufacturer documents P20F0 publicly. The physical background is the same as on bank 1: vanadium-based coatings degrade by sublimation above about 550 °C (Navistar patent US20190232224), and the US heavy-duty rule 40 CFR 1036.115 requires the engine design to keep the catalyst below its sublimation threshold. When only one bank overheats, the cause tends to sit on that bank, for instance a leaking injector, a misfiring cylinder or a wrong temperature sensor. Repeated events can permanently lower the bank 2 conversion (P20F2).
c: Leaking injector or misfire on bank 2 sending fuel into the exhaust
Excess heat during particulate filter regeneration on bank 2
Bank 2 SCR temperature sensor reading too high
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Reduced power or interrupted regeneration to protect the catalyst

P20F1.d: P20F1 reports an over-temperature of the SCR pre-catalyst on bank 2, the close-coupled front stage of a two-stage system in the second exhaust line. Both conditions must be met for the code to exist on a vehicle: separate aftertreatment per bank and a split SCR with a front brick near the turbocharger outlet. No manufacturer documents this combination publicly. Paccar's patent US11976582 shows why a front stage in that position is exposed to the hottest exhaust and to regeneration heat, and 40 CFR 1036.115 obliges heavy-duty engine makers to protect vanadium-based catalysts against temperatures that cause sublimation. Compared with P20F0, which covers the main bank 2 catalyst, the front stage heats up faster and reacts first to fuel slip from bank 2 cylinders. Lasting damage would show up as P20F3.
c: Fuel slip from bank 2 cylinders (injector leak, misfire, post-injection fault)
Pre-catalyst temperature sensor on bank 2 reading too high
Regeneration heat reaching the front stage
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Front-stage dosing or regeneration suspended

P20F2.t: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F2.d: P20F2 is the bank 2 twin of P20EE: the main SCR catalyst of the second exhaust line removes less NOx than required, judged by NOx sensors ahead of and behind it. CARB requires the NOx catalyst to be flagged once its conversion loss would push emissions past the regulatory multiple of the standard. No manufacturer documents P20F2 publicly; the widely used P20EE logic shows how such a monitor works. Ford's 2023 6.7 L diesel, for example, fails its catalyst below 55 % cumulative efficiency within a 200–320 °C inlet window, and GM compares measured with expected efficiency. A bank 2 code requires a dedicated SCR and sensor pair per bank. If both banks report low efficiency together, DEF quality or a shared supply fault is more likely than two worn catalysts. A speed limit may follow where the vehicle treats it as a DEF fault.
c: Poor DEF quality or bank 2 dosing valve fault
Bank 2 SCR catalyst aged or overheated
Exhaust leak between the bank 2 NOx sensors
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF quality warning, possibly with a countdown to reduced speed

P20F3.t: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F3.d: P20F3 states that the SCR pre-catalyst on bank 2 no longer converts enough NOx. It belongs to engines with a separate aftertreatment line per bank and a two-stage SCR in each, with a NOx sensor between front and main brick so that the front stage can be judged on its own, an option CARB grants for catalysts arranged in series. No manufacturer documents P20F3 publicly; Hino's use of the bank 1 code P20EF is the nearest documented case. The multi-stage SCR application US20150096287 explains the logic: each stage gets its own efficiency target, and a weak front stage can be hidden because the rear stage compensates, which is why it needs its own monitor. Typical faults are a blocked front dosing valve or a heat-damaged pre-catalyst. P20F2 covers the bank 2 main catalyst. The driver usually only sees the MIL.
c: Bank 2 front dosing valve blocked or crystallised
NOx sensor between the bank 2 stages reading wrong
Bank 2 pre-catalyst damaged by heat or contamination
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Increased NOx after cold starts

P20F4.d: The control unit compares the DEF quantity it commands with what the system actually delivers, judged from tank level, pump effort or the long-term correction the NOx feedback needs. P20F4 means too little fluid is really reaching the exhaust. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI data book sets it once the SCR adaptation value reaches 1.79, so dosing had to be raised far above plan; GM handles the same limit as P249D (factor above 1.99, Type B). Mercedes-Benz names leaks, a faulty valve and air pockets in the engine-side injector line on the Sprinter 907 with OM654 (LI49.20-N-079157); Jeep fixes it on the 2.2 L diesel Cherokee with dosing unit software (18-088-20). An Isuzu patent describes the tank-level versus commanded-quantity check. Underdosing raises NOx and can end in inducement. P20F5 is the opposite.
c: Partly blocked or crystallised dosing valve delivering less than commanded
Air pockets in the injector line, as Mercedes reports for the OM654 Sprinter
Leak in tank, pump or line so less fluid reaches the valve
Dosing control unit software requiring an update
s: Check engine light and DEF warning
DEF tank level falls slower than expected
Higher NOx emissions and, if unresolved, inducement countdown

P20F5.d: P20F5 is set when more diesel exhaust fluid is used, or has to be corrected away, than the control unit planned. In VW's 2014 Touareg TDI data book the trigger is an SCR adaptation value of 0.51 or lower: the NOx feedback keeps cutting the commanded dose because more fluid evidently reaches the catalyst than intended. GM maps the same idea to P249E (factor below 0.41, Type B). Likely reasons are a dosing valve that drips or does not close fully, an external leak downstream of the pressure sensor that empties the tank faster, or a pressure sensor reading low so the pump overdelivers. Jeep lists P20F5 with P20F4 on the 2.2 L diesel Cherokee and cures both with dosing unit software (18-088-20). An Isuzu patent also aims at a valve that keeps spraying. Overdosing risks ammonia slip and deposits.
c: Dosing valve dripping or not sealing between pulses
External leak at the valve or its supply line
Pressure sensor reading low, causing excess delivery
Dosing control unit software requiring an update
s: Check engine light and DEF warning
DEF tank empties faster than usual, white crust around the dosing valve
Ammonia smell or deposits in the exhaust

P20F6.t: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P20F6.d: Between pulses the dosing valve must seal tightly so DEF only enters the exhaust when commanded. P20F6 means the control unit concluded that the first valve on bank 1 stays open: the pressure collapses, or the pump has to work much harder to hold it than the commanded quantity explains. A Cummins patent describes this kind of check, comparing the measured pump effort with the expected flow; a strongly negative error points to a stuck-open valve, a leak or a disconnected line. FCA lists P20F6 for the Jeep Compass with the 2.0 L diesel (sales code EBS) in bulletins 18-034-20, 18-008-23 and 18-026-23 and cures it with control unit software; one case comes with system and DCU supply voltage too high. Overdosing risks ammonia slip and deposits. The stuck-closed counterpart is P208E, bank 2 is P20F7.
c: Crystals or debris on the valve seat keeping the valve from closing
Mechanically sticking or heat-damaged dosing valve
Control unit software misjudging valve closure, cured by an update
Leaking or detached line at the valve imitating an open valve
s: Check engine light and DEF warning
Higher DEF consumption, white deposits in the exhaust or ammonia smell
Dosing switched off and later inducement

P20F7.t: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P20F7.d: P20F7 is the bank 2 version of P20F6 and only applies to engines with a second exhaust line that has its own SCR catalyst and dosing valve, typically V engines with separate aftertreatment per bank. The control unit judges that this valve no longer closes, usually because pressure cannot be held or the pump must deliver far more than the commanded dose. No maker documents P20F7 publicly; on the bank 1 side FCA uses P20F6 on the 2.0 L diesel Jeep Compass and cures it with software. A Cummins patent explains the underlying comparison of pump effort and expected flow, where a large negative error means a stuck-open valve or a leak. CARB requires reductant delivery faults to be detected before emissions exceed the limits. Overdosing on one bank causes ammonia slip and deposits there. The stuck-closed code for bank 2 is P208F.
c: Crystals or debris on the bank 2 valve seat
Mechanically sticking or heat-damaged bank 2 dosing valve
Leaking or detached supply line at the bank 2 valve
s: Check engine light and DEF warning
Higher DEF consumption and deposits in the bank 2 exhaust
Dosing switched off and later inducement

P20F8.t: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 1)
P20F8.d: P20F8 means the intake manifold runner or swirl flaps on bank 1 do not follow the commanded position, judged by comparing set point and feedback from the position sensor. Unlike P2004/P2006, which state a direction (stuck open or closed), this code reports poor tracking anywhere in the travel. GM's 2018 diesels set it when the tracking error exceeds 10 % in 80 of 100 samples, with coolant at 60 °C or more and the smart actuator powered for at least 5 s, as a Type B code; the 2025 diesel table 25OBDG04B uses the same 10 % limit over 960 of 1,200 counts for a DC swirl motor. Mazda found P20F8 on 2023–2025 Mazda3, CX-30, CX-5 and CX-50 caused by the swirl valve motor overheating from frequent actuation and fixed it with new PCM software (bulletin 01-003/26). Drivers notice the MIL and sometimes rough idle or weaker low-end torque.
c: Flaps or shaft sticking from carbon and oil deposits (common on diesels with EGR)
Worn or overheating actuator motor or failed position sensor
Control software needing an update (Mazda bulletin 01-003/26)
Wiring or connector fault at the actuator
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Rough idle or hesitation at low speed
Less torque at low engine speed

P20F9.t: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 2)
P20F9.d: P20F9 is the bank 2 counterpart of P20F8: the runner or swirl flaps of the second cylinder bank do not track their commanded position. It needs a V engine whose banks have separately driven flaps, each with its own position feedback. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM and Mazda only use the bank 1 code P20F8. GM's diesel logic for P20F8 shows how such a test works: set point and measured position are compared continuously, and a deviation above 10 % in most samples counts as a fault with warm coolant and a supply above 11 V. CARB's comprehensive component rules require functional checks of such actuators where they affect emissions. Directional faults on bank 2 are P2005 (stuck open) and P2007 (stuck closed); electrical faults are P2011–P2013. Expect the MIL and possibly uneven running between banks.
c: Bank 2 actuator or position sensor faulty
Broken or detached linkage between actuator and flap shaft
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Uneven idle or reduced torque at low speed

P20FA.d: P20FA means the controller has found an open or otherwise faulty drive circuit for the second reductant (DEF/AdBlue) pump, called pump B or pump 2. No public service text explains which physical pump carries this letter; it is a driver channel of its own, separate from pump A (P208A). Ford stores P20FA together with P20FC and P20FD on 2023–2024 Super Duty and F-650/F-750 trucks with the 6.7L diesel (SSM 51891 and 52299, MIL lit) and asks technicians to check two connectors for seating and three more for water ingress and corrosion before normal diagnosis. FCA lists it as Reductant Pump 2 Control Circuit/Open for 3.0L EcoDiesel models and counts it among the faults that start the Service DEF countdown. With the pump unpowered, dosing stalls and NOx output climbs.
c: Water ingress or corrosion in the pump B connectors or harness
Connector not fully latched after assembly or repair
Open winding or internal break in pump B
Faulty output stage in the engine or DEF control module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Service DEF or AdBlue warning with countdown to restart lockout
Other SCR codes stored at the same time (P208A, P20FC, P20FD)

P20FB.t: Reductant Pump B Control Performance/Stuck Off
P20FB.d: P20FB is the functional check of reductant pump B: its circuit is electrically sound, yet the pump does not reach the commanded state or stays off when it should be running. No public threshold exists for pump B. For pump A, Ford's 2023 diesel summary flags P208B when pump speed misses its setpoint by more than 300 rpm or the speed control sits at its limit for 30 seconds, which shows the principle. FCA names P20FB Reductant Pump 2 Control Performance and has listed it in a series of PCM reflash bulletins for the 3.0L EcoDiesel in Ram 1500, Wrangler and Gladiator (2020–2021, e.g. 18-028-21 and 18-002-23), so on those trucks a software update comes before any parts. Genuine causes are a worn, frozen or blocked pump or a clogged filter.
c: Outdated PCM software (FCA 3.0L EcoDiesel, reflash bulletins)
Pump B worn, seized or blocked by crystallised fluid
Frozen DEF or failed tank heating in cold weather
Clogged pump filter or restricted lines
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF system warning, possibly with countdown to restart lockout
Code returns mainly after cold starts or long parking

P20FC.t: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P20FC.d: P20FC sets when the drive signal for reductant pump B reads too low, typically a ground fault on the line or a current draw beyond what the driver allows. Pump B has no published limits. For pump A, Ford's 2023 diesel summary reports the low fault (P208C) when pump current exceeds 5 A or the pump controller draws more than 15 A, checked with the driver off and confirmed after about 8 seconds; a similar logic is likely for pump B but undocumented. The only codegenau manufacturer evidence comes from Ford: 2023–2024 Super Duty and F-650/F-750 6.7L trucks may log P20FC alongside P20FA and P20FD, and the SSMs point to wet or corroded connectors first. Unlike P20FA, the circuit is not open but pulled down; unlike P20FD it is not stuck high.
c: Chafed wire shorting the pump B control line to ground
Water ingress or corrosion in the pump connectors
Pump B motor drawing excessive current (internal short or tight motor)
Faulty output stage in the control module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF system warning and reduced or no reductant dosing
Restart lockout after the inducement countdown if left unrepaired

P20FD.t: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit High
P20FD.d: P20FD indicates that the control line of reductant pump B sits too high, for instance shorted to battery voltage, so the controller can no longer regulate the pump properly. No limits are published for pump B. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets the matching pump A fault (P208D) when pump voltage exceeds 16 V or controller current passes 5 A while the driver is on, confirmed within about 2 seconds, which is quicker than the 8 seconds used for open and low faults. Ford is the only maker that documents P20FD itself: 2023–2024 Super Duty and F-650/F-750 trucks with the 6.7L diesel can store it together with P20FA and P20FC, and the SSMs direct technicians to inspect connectors for moisture and corrosion. A pump that cannot be controlled ends DEF dosing until repaired.
c: Pump B control line shorted to battery or supply voltage
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the pump connectors
Internal electrical fault in pump B
Faulty output stage in the control module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF system warning, dosing suspended
Countdown to restart lockout in the instrument cluster

P20FE.d: P20FE judges whether the first reductant metering unit actually delivers the quantity the SCR control asks for. GM's 2025 Duramax tables average a delivery compensation factor and set the code, Type A after one trip, once that factor passes 1.44, meaning the expected pressure drop no longer proves correct dosing. VW Group uses it on 3.0 TDI models: Porsche reflashed 2015–2016 Cayenne Diesel because the check was too sensitive in the cold; Audi tied it on 2012–2015 Q7 to a loose filter housing letting unfiltered AdBlue damage the pressure sensor and pump; VW's 2015 Touareg tip first checks the injector part number, then runs the metering quantity test. GM also updated software for it (23-NA-193, 24-NA-058). Unit 2 is P2EAD.
c: Partly blocked or crystallised dosing injector
Loose or damaged tank filter letting debris reach pump and sensor
Air in the dosing lines after service or low fluid level
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
AdBlue/DEF system warning in the cluster
Higher NOx, possible SCR efficiency codes (P20EE)

P20FF.d: P20FF is an internal fault of the module that runs the DEF pump and heaters, not of the pump itself. Ford's 2023 6.7L diesel strategy sets it when the pump motor controller exceeds 130 °C or reports an internal error, detected within about 5 seconds as part of the pump function check. In GM's 2025 Duramax tables the DEF controller logs it for a failed RAM pattern test at start-up, a checksum or calibration that does not match the software, or corrupt non-volatile memory; it is Type A and blocks most other DEF diagnostics while active. A 2020 GM heavy-duty bulletin notes that the cluster could wrongly show DEF Low for this code instead of Service DEF System and was fixed by reprogramming. Supply voltage faults have their own codes (P21CB, P21CC).
c: Internal memory or processor fault in the DEF control module
Software or calibration mismatch after programming
Poor power or ground connection causing module resets
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Service DEF System message, on some GM trucks wrongly shown as DEF Low
DEF dosing stops and the inducement countdown may begin

P2100.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit/Open
P2100.d: P2100 reports an electrical fault in the drive circuit of the first electronic throttle motor, usually an open line. Ford's 2012 summary uses it for an open circuit or a short to power or ground (no MIL, wrench lamp). GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 checks the bank 1 H-bridge three ways: open load above 200 kOhm, driver overtemperature and short to ground below 0.5 Ohm, each in one trip. Ford's 2024 summary even uses P2100 as the base code for several throttle faults with failure-type bytes. Ducati reports P2100 for the front-bank throttle motor of its V4. The throttle springs to limp position, so the engine runs with little power. Wrong position is P2101; low/high circuit are P2102/P2103; the B actuator is P210A.
c: Moisture or corrosion in the throttle body or ECU connector
Broken or chafed motor wire between ECU and throttle body
Open winding or worn brushes in the throttle motor
Damaged H-bridge output stage in the engine control unit
s: Throttle held in limp position, very low power
Engine or ETC warning lamp on
Little or no response to the accelerator pedal

P2101.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P2101.d: Here the controller compares where throttle A should be with where its position sensors say it is. GM's 2018 table 18OBDG03A flags a gap of more than 10 percent between measured and modelled position after 15 counts at 12.5 ms each, classed by GM as Type A with immediate MIL; the 2006/2007 tables used 8.4 percent. VW's 2014 data book accepts 4-50 percent deviation or a drive duty cycle above 80 percent. Ford sets it with MIL and wrench lamp; Mercedes-AMG M177 engines show it with corroded throttle connector pins, and GM issued field bulletins for the LGZ V6 and 2017 V8 trucks. Causes are mostly mechanical or contact problems, not a dead circuit (P2100). Expect reduced power or limp mode.
c: Carbon or ice makes the throttle plate stiff or sticky
High resistance at the throttle connector pins
Worn gear train or weak motor inside the throttle body
Deformed inlet duct or leak at the throttle body
s: Reduced engine power message or limp mode
Engine warning lamp on
Hesitation or uneven idle
Stalling in some cases

P2102.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit Low
P2102.d: P2102 means the output stage for throttle motor A sees a voltage or current that points to a short toward ground or an overloaded driver. GM lists P2100-P2103 together in its 2018 calibration as faults that limit engine power and default the throttle authority; a Bosch-based GM ECM of 2012 assigns its output-stage checks (short circuit, overtemperature or overcurrent, open load) to this group with about 0.1 s detection. Apart from such tables, no maker publicly documents P2102 on its own; many current ECUs report the same fault under P2100 with a failure-type byte. CARB requires circuit faults of output components to be detected. The throttle drops to limp position and power is cut. The high-side counterpart is P2103.
c: Motor wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Shorted winding or jammed motor drawing excess current
Water in the throttle connector bridging terminals
Faulty throttle driver in the engine control unit
s: Limp mode with throttle at fixed opening
Engine warning lamp on
Pedal input largely ignored

P2103.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit High
P2103.d: P2103 is the high-side fault of the throttle A drive: the output stage sees a voltage that suggests a short to battery, or on some layouts the supply relay of the throttle motor stays energized when it should be off. GM groups P2100-P2103 as power-limiting faults (18OBDG03A), and its Bosch-based 2012 ECM ties a power-stage short circuit to this range with about 0.1 s detection. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander list files P2100 and P2103 under the short name ETC MOT PWR, i.e. the supply of the throttle control motor, stored after one trip. The throttle is de-energized and power limited. Low-side faults are P2102, open circuit P2100.
c: Motor wire shorted to a battery-voltage feed
Throttle motor relay sticking on (where fitted)
Internal fault in the ECU throttle driver
s: Limp mode with very limited power
Engine warning lamp on
Engine may not start or stalls

P2104.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Idle
P2104.d: P2104 is a status code: it does not name a broken part but records that the throttle control has switched into a forced-idle failure mode. In Ford's 2012 summary this happens on second-generation ETC systems when two or three accelerator pedal sensor tracks are lost, so the computer can no longer read driver demand; the engine then holds a raised idle and ignores the pedal, with MIL and wrench lamp. The actual cause is stored alongside it, usually a pedal sensor code such as P2122-P2128 or P2138. CARB counts such default modes as malfunctions whenever they can raise emissions. Repair means fixing the causal code, then clearing P2104. Related states are limited power (P2106), limited rpm (P2110) and shutdown (P2105).
c: Failure of two or more accelerator pedal sensor tracks
Pedal sensor wiring or shared 5 V reference fault
s: Engine stays at raised idle, pedal has no effect
Engine and ETC/wrench warning lamps on
Car can only creep to a safe place

P2105.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Engine Shutdown
P2105.d: P2105 is the most severe throttle failure mode: the controller has decided that throttle control can no longer be trusted and stops the engine. In Ford's 2012 summary the trigger is a serious processor fault found by the separate monitoring processor (Ford calls it the Quizzer); all injectors are switched off and the wrench lamp comes on. Ford sets it without MIL, arguing that a shutdown cannot raise emissions, which matches the CARB idea of emissions-neutral default actions. The cause sits in the engine computer, its supply or a companion code such as P0606 or P2107. For the driver the engine dies or will not keep running. Milder states are forced idle (P2104), limited power (P2106) and limited rpm (P2110).
c: Monitoring processor detects an internal ECU fault
Unstable ECU supply or ground connection
ECU software fault cured by reprogramming
s: Engine shuts off or will not keep running
Wrench or ETC warning lamp, often without MIL

P2106.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Limited Power
P2106.d: P2106 tells you the throttle control is running in a reduced-power fallback. Ford's 2012 summary lists the reasons on second-generation ETC: loss of the MAF signal, one throttle position sensor, crank position or transmission speed sensors, a stuck throttle or a throttle motor circuit fault; it sets with MIL and wrench lamp, and a crank sensor code (P0320/P0322) also adds P2106. VW's 2014 data book uses it when an internal plausibility check of the engine computer fails. So P2106 almost always appears with another code that names the real defect, and that one is repaired first. The driver notices weak acceleration and a capped top speed. Forced idle is P2104, limited rpm P2110, shutdown P2105.
c: Failed input such as MAF, throttle position or crank sensor
Sticking throttle or fault in the throttle motor circuit
Failed internal check or software in the engine computer
s: Reduced power, sluggish acceleration
Engine and wrench/ETC lamp on
Limited road speed

P2107.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Module Processor
P2107.d: P2107 concerns the processor that runs throttle A control, which in most cars sits inside the engine computer rather than in a separate box. Ford's summaries define it as an internal processor fault or lost communication with the main CPU, detected within 60 ms, with MIL after two drive cycles and the ETC lamp at once; from 2024 Ford reports the same check as P2108 with a failure-type byte. Ford names P2107 with P2111/P2112 as the codes that catch a throttle unable to hold cold-start idle. FCA lists it in a 2022 PCM software update for the Jeep Gladiator 3.6L. Check supply, grounds and software before blaming the module. The B counterpart is P211E; module performance is P2108.
c: ECU software fault fixed by a reflash
Voltage dips or poor ECU ground
Internal hardware failure of the engine computer
s: Engine and ETC warning lamps on
Reduced power or limp mode
Possible stalling or no start

P2108.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Module Performance
P2108.d: P2108 marks a performance problem of the control function for throttle A, as opposed to a pure processor fault (P2107). VW's 2014 Touareg data book gives a concrete case: the time for the throttle to close below a reference point of 11.56 percent must not exceed 0.60 s. Ford's 2024-2025 summary uses P2108 as the base code for its throttle processor test, so P2107 there appears as P2108 with failure-type byte 49 (60 ms, MIL). Usage therefore differs by maker. Check the throttle body for deposits and the ECU for software updates, then supply and grounds. Symptoms range from a warning lamp to reduced power. The B counterpart is P211F; mechanical return problems also show up as P2119.
c: Throttle closes too slowly (deposits, weak spring)
ECU software issue needing an update
Supply voltage or ground problem at the ECU
s: Engine warning lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
Unstable idle after lifting off the pedal

P2109.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2109.d: P2109 flags an implausible rest reading on position signal A: with the throttle or pedal resting on its lower mechanical stop, the minimum learned at key-on falls outside the window the calibration accepts. Ford names its first throttle body sensor TP A, so on such layouts the code concerns the throttle. Subaru documents P2109: bulletin 09-102-23 traces it on the 2022 WRX to a throttle plate that has frozen shut and supplies new ECM software, and 09-97-22 adds improved detection logic for 2020-2022 Legacy and Outback. A Delphi patent describes several learn attempts before an obstruction is reported. Circuit faults on A have their own codes (P0120-P0123); P2113-P2117 run the same check for letters B to F. Expect a warning lamp and possibly limp mode.
c: Ice or carbon holding the throttle plate off its rest stop
ECM software with oversensitive detection (update available)
Rest position not relearned after cleaning or replacing the throttle body
Sensor A worn or drifted at the closed end of its track
s: Engine warning lamp, often after a cold or wet night
Raised or unsteady idle
Reduced power until the fault clears

P210A.t: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit/Open
P210A.d: Throttle actuator B only exists on engines with two electronic throttles, typically one per cylinder bank. P210A reports an electrical fault, mainly an open line, in the drive of that second motor. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 checks the bank 2 H-bridge just like bank 1: open load above 200 kOhm (0.8 s), driver overtemperature and short to ground below 0.5 Ohm, each one trip. Ducati links P210A to the rear-bank throttle motor of its V4 and points to moisture in the ECU connector. Ford's 2024 summary uses P210A as base code for all faults of its second throttle body. The engine runs on reduced power. Bank 1 is P2100; low/high circuit faults are P210C/P210D, position errors P210B.
c: Moisture or corrosion in the throttle B or ECU connector
Broken motor wire to throttle body B
Open winding in throttle motor B
Faulty bank 2 output stage in the ECU
s: Reduced power, one bank breathing poorly
Engine warning lamp on
Rough running or limp mode

P210B.t: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P210B.d: P210B is the position-control check for the second throttle on twin-throttle engines. The controller compares the commanded opening of throttle B with the measured one; GM's 23OBDG07 table flags a deviation beyond a rate-dependent limit for 0.5 s, one trip. Ford lists P210B with MIL and wrench lamp for its dual-throttle applications (2020-2023) and from 2024 shows it as P210A with byte 95, the type Ford describes as cross-wired on the A side. Mercedes-AMG M177 V8s store it as throttle actuator 2 signal above limit, together with P2101; the bulletin blames high resistance in the connector pins of both actuators. Bank 1 counterpart is P2101; an open circuit is P210A, motor current P211C.
c: High resistance at throttle B connector pins
Deposits or ice making throttle B sluggish
Worn gears or motor in throttle body B
Motor leads swapped after repair work
s: Engine warning lamp and reduced power
Uneven running between the two banks
Limp mode

P210C.t: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Low
P210C.d: P210C is reserved for a low-side fault in the drive circuit of the second throttle motor, for example a grounded motor lead or an overloaded output stage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Makers with two throttles report such faults differently: GM's 23OBDG07 table files a bank 2 short to ground below 0.5 Ohm and driver overtemperature under P210A, and Ford's 2024 summary hangs all throttle B faults on P210A with failure-type bytes. CARB requires circuit faults of output devices to be detected, so where P210C is used it behaves like its bank 1 sibling P2102. Expect the second throttle to be switched off, rough running and reduced power. High-side faults would be P210D, open circuit P210A.
c: Throttle B motor wire shorted to ground
Shorted or jammed throttle motor B
Faulty bank 2 throttle driver in the ECU
s: Reduced power and rough running
Engine warning lamp on

P210D.t: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit High
P210D.d: P210D covers the high-side fault of the second throttle drive: a voltage on the motor B circuit that suggests a short to battery, or a supply that stays live when the stage should be off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. On twin-throttle engines that publish their logic, GM (23OBDG07) and Ford (2024) collect the electrical faults of throttle B under P210A, so P210D will rarely be seen. The CARB rule for output components still applies: an electrical fault in an actuator that affects emissions must be detected and stored. If it appears, treat it like P2103 for bank 1: inspect wiring and connector of throttle B for chafing to a positive feed, then the motor and the ECU output. The engine runs on reduced power.
c: Throttle B motor wire shorted to battery voltage
Damaged or wet connector at throttle body B
Faulty bank 2 output stage in the ECU
s: Reduced power and uneven running
Engine warning lamp on

P210E.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C/F Voltage Correlation
P210E.d: P210E compares two redundant position signals, C and F, and sets when their voltages stop agreeing within the permitted tolerance. Which physical tracks carry these letters is up to the manufacturer: GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 uses C for the first sensor of a second throttle body, while Ford's summaries assign D, E and F to the three tracks of its pedal, so a C/F pair only arises on unusual layouts. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The same kind of check is documented under P2138: GM's 2023 table flags the D/E pedal pair at a difference of 0.12-0.18 V, the 2014 VW Touareg at 0.14-0.26 V. A single drifting track, contact resistance or a shared ground fault is the usual cause; the ECU then trusts neither signal fully and limits power.
c: One sensor track worn or drifted, so the pair no longer agrees
Corrosion or water in the connector shifting one signal
Fault in a shared ground or 5 V reference line
Faulty input stage in the engine control module
s: Engine or throttle warning lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
Hesitant or delayed response to the pedal

P210F.t: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P210F.d: P210F is a status code for the second throttle: the controller has capped engine speed because control of throttle B is no longer reliable. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Its bank 1 sibling P2110 is well described: in Ford's 2012 summary it follows the loss of both throttle position sensors or a fault found by the throttle plate controller, sets the MIL and wrench lamp and enforces an rpm limit with fuel and spark. P210F would play the same role on engines with two throttles; the root cause is stored as a separate code such as P210A, P210B or a throttle B sensor fault, and that is what gets repaired. CARB treats such fallback modes as malfunctions when they can raise emissions. Expect a hard rev limit.
c: Electrical or mechanical fault of throttle B (see companion code)
Loss of the position signals of throttle B
s: Engine will not rev past a fixed limit
Engine and wrench lamp on

P2110.t: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P2110.d: P2110 records that engine speed has been capped because throttle A can no longer be controlled safely. Ford's 2012 summary sets it on second-generation ETC when both throttle position sensors fail or Ford's throttle plate controller (TPPC) reports a fault, with MIL and wrench lamp; rpm is then capped by a pedal-dependent limit enforced through fuel and spark. FCA uses it widely: a Ram 1500 3.6L bulletin (09-023-23) pairs it with throttle icing (P2072, P2118), and Jeep Renegade/Fiat 500X PCM updates cure false settings. Repair the companion code first. Bank B counterpart is P210F; other fallback states are P2104-P2106.
c: Ice on the throttle plate after a cold soak
Loss of both throttle position sensor signals
PCM software setting the code falsely (update available)
Worn or faulty electronic throttle body
s: Engine will not rev beyond a low limit
Engine warning lamp on
Stop/start disabled or hard start in frost

P2111.t: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Stuck Open
P2111.d: P2111 means throttle A stays more open than commanded. Ford defines it precisely: the actual throttle angle exceeds the desired angle by more than 6 degrees for about 500 ms, with MIL after two drive cycles and the ETC lamp at once; it also catches a throttle that cannot bring cold-start idle down. Ford's 2020-2023 and 2024 summaries keep it with MIL, the latter as P2100 byte 72. Ford's SSM 50203 links it to moisture that freezes downstream of the throttle plate on the Ranger (2019-2021) and Bronco (2021). Carbon or a deformed plate can also hold the throttle off its seat. The opposite fault is P2112; bank B is P211A.
c: Water or ice in the intake behind the throttle
Carbon build-up holding the plate open
Broken return spring or worn gear in the throttle body
s: High idle speed or engine hard to slow down
Loss of power in freezing weather
Engine and wrench lamp on

P2112.t: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Stuck Closed
P2112.d: P2112 is the mirror image of P2111: throttle A opens less than commanded. Ford sets it when the actual angle stays more than 6 degrees below the desired angle for about 500 ms (MIL after two drive cycles, ETC lamp at once) and lists it in its 2020-2023 and 2024 summaries. Ford's SSM 50203 names it for Ranger/Bronco with ice behind the throttle. Mazda uses the number differently: its bulletins for the CX-9 and Mazda3 describe P2112 as a throttle motor current fault set after cold starts below freezing, cured by draining condensate or a PCM update. Ice, thick carbon or a jammed gear are the usual causes; the engine may idle poorly or lack power.
c: Frozen condensate locking the throttle plate
Jammed gear or weak motor in the throttle body
s: Lack of power after a cold start
Low or unstable idle, possible stalling
Engine and wrench lamp on

P2113.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Minimum Stop Performance
P2113.d: The engine computer checks whether position signal B reports a plausible value when the throttle or pedal rests against its lower mechanical stop. At key-on many systems learn this minimum and compare it with a tolerance window; a reading outside that window sets the code. Ford and GM label their second throttle position sensor as B, so on those layouts B means the throttle body, but neither maker publishes P2113 itself. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Subaru uses the A version (P2109). Ice, coking or a bent stop are typical triggers. P0220-P0223 cover the B circuit, P2109 and P2114-P2117 the other letters. The driver may see a warning lamp and reduced power.
c: Carbon deposits or ice keep the throttle plate off its rest stop
Position sensor B worn or drifted at the low end of its track
Minimum position not relearned after cleaning or part replacement
Corroded connector shifting the sensor B signal
s: Engine or ETC warning lamp on
Unstable or raised idle speed
Reduced engine power (limp mode)

P2114.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Minimum Stop Performance
P2114.d: This code reports that position signal C does not show a believable value while its throttle or pedal sits on the lower stop. The controller learns or expects a minimum reading within a tolerance band and flags a fault when the learned value falls outside it. Letter C is rarely assigned: Ford and GM use A/B for the throttle and D/E/F for the pedal, so C appears only on layouts with a third sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the logic follows the A version P2109 (Subaru) and the Delphi minimum-learn patent. P2113 and P2115-P2117 are the same test for other letters, P2136/P2137 compare C against A or B. Expect a warning lamp and possibly limited power.
c: Position sensor C worn or drifted near its rest position
Deposits, ice or a damaged stop prevent the rest position
Rest position not relearned after repair
Connector or wiring fault shifting the C signal
s: Engine or ETC warning lamp on
Irregular idle
Reduced power possible

P2115.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor D Minimum Stop Performance
P2115.d: Here the controller judges position signal D at the released (minimum) end of travel. On Ford and GM drive-by-wire systems D is the first accelerator pedal sensor, so the code means the pedal's idle reading is outside the expected window, for example because the pedal does not return fully or its sensor track has shifted. No manufacturer documents P2115 publicly; Ford and GM publish only circuit and correlation codes for D (P2120-P2123, P2138). P2116 and P2117 are the E and F counterparts, P2109 and P2113 refer to A and B. The engine may not return to idle cleanly, and the ECU may limit pedal response.
c: Pedal blocked by floor mat or weak return spring
Worn pedal sensor track D at the idle end
Aftermarket pedal tuning module or wrong pedal part
s: Warning lamp on
Engine does not drop to normal idle when the pedal is released
Dull or limited pedal response

P2116.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor E Minimum Stop Performance
P2116.d: The code covers the rest-position check of signal E. Ford, GM and Mitsubishi assign E to the second accelerator pedal sensor, which on many pedals runs at roughly half the voltage of sensor D (GM: APP 2 between 0.16 and 2.3 V). If the reading with the pedal released lies outside the learned or calibrated window, P2116 can be stored. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Circuit faults of the same sensor are reported separately (P2125, P2127-P2129) and disagreement between D and E as P2138; P2115 and P2117 handle D and F. Typical effects are a warning lamp, an unsteady idle and limited throttle response.
c: Pedal held off its stop by floor mat or sticking pivot
Worn or contaminated sensor track E
Moisture or corrosion at the pedal connector
s: Warning lamp on
Unsteady or raised idle
Limited throttle response

P2117.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor F Minimum Stop Performance
P2117.d: P2117 is the minimum-stop check for signal F. Ford lists F as the third accelerator pedal sensor on its older Gen2 throttle systems (circuit codes P2132/P2133, range P2131), while most current pedals carry only D and E, so the code can only occur on three-track pedals. The ECU flags it when the F reading at the released position lies outside the expected band. No manufacturer documents P2117 publicly. Siblings are P2115 (D) and P2116 (E); P2139 and P2140 compare F with D or E. A sticking pedal or a worn track usually lies behind it, with a warning lamp and reduced pedal response as the visible result.
c: Pedal does not return fully to its stop
Poor contact at the pedal connector
s: Warning lamp on
Idle speed does not settle
Reduced pedal response

P2118.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P2118.d: P2118 looks at how much current throttle motor A needs. A healthy throttle moves with modest current; a high or abnormal draw means the motor is fighting resistance. Ford lists P2118 with MIL and wrench lamp in its 2020-2023 summary (2024: P2100 byte 1D). The best-known trigger is a frozen throttle plate: Kia's 2022-2023 Carnival 3.5L bulletin describes limp-home mode after a cold soak and a revised ECM logic, Ram 1500 3.6L trucks get a de-icing kit (P2072, P2110, P2118), and Hyundai changed its hybrid ECM logic for what it calls ETC target position failure. Unlike P2101 (position error) or P2119 (spring return), this code points at the load on the motor. Bank B is P211C.
c: Ice on the throttle plate after a cold soak
Carbon or sludge loading the motor
Worn throttle motor or gear train
ECM logic too sensitive (software update available)
s: Limp-home mode after a cold start
Engine warning lamp on
No start or poor idle in frost

P2119.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P2119.d: This is a mechanical performance check of the electronic throttle body. GM calls it Throttle Closed Position Performance: after the motor is de-energized the return springs must bring the plate into its default (limp) position, e.g. 1.32-1.90 V on TP sensor 1 in GM's 2006 tables; 15 failed samples in a row set it. A Bosch-based GM ECM times the spring return at key-on (fault above 0.56 s). Toyota, Lexus, Ford (Ranger/Bronco, ice behind the throttle) and Mitsubishi use the code too. Unlike P2101 (position error while driven) or P2118 (motor current), P2119 points at a sticking or iced plate or a weak spring; the engine may enter limp mode.
c: Carbon deposits make the throttle plate stick
Water or ice in the intake behind the throttle body
Weak return spring or worn gear in the throttle body
ECM software that sets the code falsely (update available)
s: Engine warning lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
Hesitation or uneven acceleration
Raised or unstable idle

P211A.t: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Open
P211A.d: P211A means the second throttle on a twin-throttle engine stays further open than requested. Ford documents it in its 2020-2023 and 2024 summaries for applications with an ETB B, with MIL and wrench lamp and detection within 5 seconds; in 2024 it is shown as P210A with failure-type byte 72, matching P2111/P2100-72 for throttle A. For the A throttle Ford uses a 6-degree gap between desired and actual angle, and the B check is built the same way. With one bank getting extra air, idle rises and the engine runs unevenly; the controller usually limits power. Look for ice, carbon or a broken return spring at throttle body B. Bank 1 counterpart is P2111, stuck closed P211B.
c: Ice or carbon holding throttle B open
Broken return spring or gear in throttle body B
Faulty throttle motor B or its position sensor
s: High or hunting idle
Engine and wrench lamp on
Reduced power

P211B.t: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Closed
P211B.d: P211B is set when throttle B on a twin-throttle engine opens less than the controller asks for. Ford lists it for its dual-throttle applications in the 2020-2023 summary and in 2024 as P210A with failure-type byte 73, each with MIL, wrench lamp and detection in under 5 seconds; the A-side logic it mirrors is P2112, where actual angle trailing the target by more than 6 degrees counts as a fault. One bank is then starved of air: the engine feels weak, may stumble at idle and often drops into limp mode. Ice after a frosty night, heavy carbon or a jammed gear train in throttle body B are the usual suspects. The opposite direction is P211A, position control errors P210B.
c: Jammed gear or weak motor in throttle body B
s: Weak acceleration, limp mode
Rough idle
Engine and wrench lamp on

P211C.t: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P211C.d: P211C evaluates the current drawn by the second throttle motor. If throttle B needs clearly more current than expected to reach or hold its position, something is loading it mechanically or the motor itself is degrading. Ford names P211C first in its list for the second throttle body of twin-throttle engines (2020-2023) and in 2024 as P210A byte 1D, each with MIL, wrench lamp and detection within 5 seconds. The bank 1 version P2118 is known mostly from frozen throttle plates after cold soaks, as Kia and Ram bulletins show, so the same check applies to throttle B. Unlike P210B (position error) or P211D (spring and body check), the trigger here is motor load. The car usually goes into reduced power.
c: Ice or condensate binding throttle B
Worn motor or gears in throttle body B
s: Reduced power or limp mode
Engine and wrench lamp on
Uneven running in cold weather

P211D.t: Throttle Actuator B Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P211D.d: P211D is the mechanical check of throttle body B, the twin of P2119. GM's 23OBDG07 table describes four spring tests for bank 2: the opening and closing springs must bring the de-energized plate back to the defined limp position within set times (about 0.2-0.36 s per path), checked during offset learning and also at cold temperatures, each failing in one trip. Ford lists P211D with MIL and wrench lamp for its second throttle (2020-2023; 2024 as P210A byte 92). A sticking plate, a weak spring or ice keep the throttle from returning, so the safe fallback position cannot be guaranteed and power is limited. Position errors in operation are P210B, motor current P211C, stuck positions P211A/P211B.
c: Weak or broken return spring in throttle body B
Deposits or ice slowing the plate
Throttle adaptation not completed after service
s: Engine warning lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
Unstable idle

P211E.t: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Processor
P211E.d: P211E is the processor fault for the control of throttle B on engines with two electronic throttles. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The A version P2107 is well described: Ford treats it as an internal processor fault or lost link to the main CPU, detected in 60 ms, with MIL and an ETC lamp, and from 2024 reports it under P2108. Twin-throttle systems published by GM and Ford drive both throttles from the one engine computer and do not show a separate P211E. CARB requires on-board computers and their outputs to be monitored. If it appears, check ECU supply, grounds and software level before replacing hardware. Expect limp mode. Module performance for B is P211F.
c: Voltage dips or poor ground at the control unit
Internal hardware failure of the control unit
s: Engine and ETC warning lamps on
Limp mode with reduced power

P211F.t: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Performance
P211F.d: P211F covers a performance fault of the control function for throttle B, as distinct from a processor fault (P211E). No manufacturer documents this code publicly. For the A side, VW's 2014 data book gives a measurable example under P2108: the throttle must close below a reference point of 11.56 percent within 0.60 s. Ford uses P2108 from 2024 as base code for its processor test, which shows how differently makers fill this slot. On a twin-throttle engine P211F would apply the same kind of check to the second throttle. CARB requires such control functions to be monitored when they affect emissions. Check throttle body B for deposits and the ECU for updates; reduced power is likely.
c: Throttle B responds or closes too slowly
Control unit software needing an update
Supply or ground problem at the control unit
s: Engine warning lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode

P2120.d: P2120 is the general circuit check for signal D, which GM, Ford and VW all use for the first accelerator pedal track. GM's 2007 tables call it APP Sensor 1 Circuit: the ECM watches sensor 1 for steady or intermittent opens and shorts within its 0.325-4.75 V window and counts failures every 12.5 ms, setting the code at 19 of 39 counts. GM PIP3783D lists P2120 among the pedal codes on 2007-2014 full-size trucks and SUVs and blames weak pin grip in the inline connectors C109 and C205. Ford's 2024 summary uses P2120 as the base code whose failure types 16 and 17 replace P2122 and P2123. Range/Performance is P2121, low and high voltage P2122/P2123, dropouts P2124. With one track lost, the ECU cuts power.
c: Poor terminal tension or corrosion at pedal, inline or ECM connectors
Open or short in the sensor 1 signal, reference or ground wire
Internal fault in the pedal sensor, such as a cracked solder joint
s: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Sluggish or capped acceleration
Fault often intermittent and hard to reproduce

P2121.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Range/Performance
P2121.d: P2121 means pedal signal D is electrically intact but implausible. Ford's 2012 OBD summary sets it only on second-generation ETC systems, whose pedals carry three tracks D, E and F: if sensor D disagrees with the others by more than 1.1 degrees, the PCM stores P2121 without MIL but with the wrench lamp, and pedal response becomes rate-limited using the healthy tracks. Mitsubishi lists P2121 for the accelerator pedal sensor on the 2022 Outlander as a one-trip code that turns the MIL on. Newer Ford and GM systems with two tracks report such disagreement as P2138 instead. Circuit faults on D are P2120 and P2122-P2124; P2126 is the same check for track E. The car stays drivable but reacts softly to the pedal.
c: Worn or dirty track D giving an offset reading
Contact resistance at the pedal connector
Shared reference or ground line shifting one signal
s: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
Softened, delayed acceleration
Idle may rise when the brake is not pressed

P2122.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Low
P2122.d: P2122 sets when pedal track D falls below its lower voltage limit, typically from a short to ground, a missing 5 V reference or a broken signal wire. Limits differ by maker: Ford uses 0.25 V and since 2020 lights both MIL and wrench lamp (in 2012 only the wrench lamp); GM's 2007 tables use 0.325 V with 19 of 39 counts at 12.5 ms (Type A), GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 0.28 V for 0.2 s; the 2014 VW Passat flags anything under 0.61 V. GM bulletin 14636 extended coverage on 2009-2011 Impala and 2009 LaCrosse pedals with broken solder joints that set this and related codes. P2123 is the high counterpart, P2120 the general circuit code, P2127 the low fault on track E. The ECU limits power and pedal response.
c: Track D signal wire shorted to ground or chafed
Open or shorted 5 V reference feed to the pedal
Pedal sensor fault such as a cracked solder joint
s: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Pedal feels dead or reacts only slowly
Cruise control may be unavailable

P2123.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit High
P2123.d: P2123 is the high-voltage fault on pedal track D, usually an open sensor ground or a short to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage. GM's 2007 tables set it above 4.75 V (19 of 39 counts, Type A), a Bosch-based GM ECM from 2012 above 4.824 V lasting 0.2 s, and the 2014 VW Touareg above 4.89 V; Ford uses 4.75 V. A track pinned near the supply rail would read like a fully pressed pedal, so the controller rejects it, carries on with track E and caps engine output. GM PIP3783D lists the code among the very intermittent pedal faults on 2007-2014 full-size trucks and advises wiggling the harness and testing terminal tension. P2122 is the low counterpart, P2120 the general circuit code, P2128 the high fault on track E.
c: Open or high-resistance ground return of the pedal sensor
Track D signal shorted to the 5 V reference or battery voltage
Loose or spread terminals at pedal or inline connector
s: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Limited throttle opening despite full pedal
Fault may appear and vanish with harness movement

P2124.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Intermittent
P2124.d: P2124 covers brief dropouts or spikes on pedal track D that come and go too quickly to count as a steady low or high fault. Ford documents it: special service messages 46829 (2015-2017 F-150) and 46880 (2017 Super Duty built up to late August 2017) tie P2124, alongside other pedal codes and wrench, ABS, airbag and hill descent lamps, to a pedal harness routed behind the bracket between brake booster and brake pedal, where it gets pinched and damaged. GM publishes no separate intermittent code for track D and catches such glitches through the 19-of-39 counter of P2120, P2122 and P2123. Inspect the harness while moving the pedal slowly. Effects range from a passing warning lamp to sudden loss of pedal response.
c: Pedal harness pinched or chafed by a misrouted path
Loose terminal or weak pin tension at the pedal connector
Worn spot on track D inside the pedal sensor
s: Warning lamps that come and go, sometimes several at once
Brief loss of pedal response while driving
Reduced power mode after repeated dropouts

P2125.d: P2125 reports a general electrical fault in signal circuit E. GM uses it as Accelerator Pedal Position Sensor 2 Circuit: the ECM looks for a continuous or intermittent open or short in the sensor 2 circuit with a counter at 12.5 ms per count (19 of 39 counts). In GM's 2006 tables sensor 2 is valid between about 0.16 and 2.3 V. GM bulletin 14636 lists P2125 among the pedal codes caused by a broken solder joint inside the pedal (2009-2011 Impala, LaCrosse). Range/Performance is P2126, explicit low or high voltage P2127/P2128, dropouts P2129, and the D/E comparison P2138. With one pedal track lost the ECU usually limits engine power.
c: Internal fault in the pedal sensor (e.g. cracked solder joint)
Open or short in the sensor 2 wiring or 5 V reference
Loose or corroded pedal or inline connector
s: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Delayed or limited pedal response
Traction control may be switched off

P2126.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit Range/Performance
P2126.d: Signal E is electrically intact but its value does not fit the situation. Ford's 2012 OBD summary uses P2126 for the second pedal sensor on Gen2 throttle systems: it sets when sensors D and E disagree by more than 1.1 degrees, as a non-MIL fault with the wrench lamp. Mitsubishi lists P2126 as accelerator pedal sensor E on the 2022 Outlander. Many newer systems report the same disagreement as P2138 instead. P2125 is the general circuit fault, P2127/P2128 are voltage below or above limits, P2129 covers dropouts. The vehicle usually stays drivable with softened pedal response; on Ford the MIL stays off and only the wrench lamp lights.
c: Worn or dirty sensor track E giving offset readings
Contact resistance at the pedal connector
Shared reference or ground circuit shifting one signal
s: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
Softened or delayed acceleration
Idle may be raised when braking

P2127.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
P2127.d: P2127 reports that pedal track E reads below its lower limit. Because many pedals run the second track at roughly half the voltage of the first, the limit for E can sit lower than for D: GM's 2006 tables flag sensor 2 under 0.1625 V and the 2014 VW Passat under 0.27 V, against 0.61 V for track D. Full-scale designs use similar limits on both tracks: Ford 0.25 V, GM's 2023 table 0.28 V for 0.2 s, GM's Bosch-based 2012 ECM 0.625 V. Typical causes are a short to ground on the E signal wire, an open reference feed, or a worn spot at the closed end of the track. With E gone the ECU relies on track D alone and holds back torque. P2128 is the high fault on E, P2122 the low fault on D, P2125 the general E circuit code.
c: Track E signal wire shorted to ground
Open 5 V reference feed for the second track
Worn track E at the closed-pedal end
s: Engine warning lamp, on newer Fords together with the wrench lamp
Reduced power and slower pedal response
Traction control may be switched off

P2128.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit High
P2128.d: P2128 sets when pedal track E reads above its upper limit, typically from an open sensor ground, a short to 5 V or a broken track. Where E is a half-scale signal the limit lies far below the supply: GM's 2006 tables flag sensor 2 above 2.295 V and the 2014 VW Passat above 2.43 V. Pedals with two full-scale tracks use about 4.75 V (Ford, GM 2007, 19 of 39 counts) or 4.824 V for 0.2 s (GM's Bosch-based 2012 ECM). Since both tracks often share one ground, an open ground can set P2128 together with P2123. With E rejected the ECU steers on track D only and limits output; Ford's 2020-2023 summary lights MIL and wrench lamp. P2127 is the low fault on E, P2123 the high fault on D, P2138 the D/E comparison.
c: Open or high-resistance ground of the pedal sensor
Track E signal shorted to the 5 V reference
Broken track or solder joint inside the pedal sensor
s: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Weak acceleration even with the pedal fully pressed
Often stored together with P2123 if the ground is open

P2129.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit Intermittent
P2129.d: P2129 is meant for short dropouts or spikes in signal circuit E that do not last long enough for a steady low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM and Ford, which assign E to the second pedal sensor, catch such glitches inside their circuit codes instead: GM counts failures every 12.5 ms and flags the APP sensor 2 circuit after 19 of 39 counts (P2125/P2127/P2128), Ford uses 0.25/4.75 V limits. CARB requires circuit monitoring of input sensors; the code fits that duty. Check for loose pins and harness chafing with the pedal moved slowly. Effects range from a warning lamp to brief power cuts while driving.
c: Loose terminal or poor pin tension at the pedal connector
Worn spot or cracked joint inside the pedal sensor
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief hesitation or power loss while driving
Reduced power mode after repeated dropouts

P212A.d: P212A is the general circuit code for throttle position signal G, a letter that only comes into play on engines with more than one electronic throttle or extra position tracks. No manufacturer documents P212A publicly. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 assigns G to the second position sensor of the bank 2 throttle body on a twin-throttle engine, but reports its electrical faults through the separate codes P212C (below 0.195 V) and P212D (above 4.805 V), each after 0.14 s in one trip. CARB requires input components like this to be checked for circuit faults, and P212A is the catch-all slot for that duty. Check the connector, wiring and 5 V supply at the second throttle body. P212B covers plausibility, P212C-P212E low, high and intermittent faults.
c: Open or short in the sensor G signal, supply or ground wire
Corroded or loose connector at the throttle body
Failed position sensor inside the throttle body
s: Engine warning lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
Rough idle on twin-throttle engines

P212B.t: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Range/Performance
P212B.d: P212B means throttle signal G is electrically valid but its value does not fit. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 applies it to sensor 2 of the bank 2 throttle body on a twin-throttle engine: the code sets when the angle derived from sensor 2 differs from that of sensor 1 by more than about 5-6.25 %, or from the angle modelled from manifold pressure by more than 9 %, in one trip; the 2024 table repeats the check. Nissan uses P212B on the 2021-2023 Rogue with the 1.5 L KR15DDT engine; bulletin NTB23-021 cures a lit MIL without drivability complaints by ECM reprogramming. Circuit faults are P212A and P212C-P212E. Depending on the cause the engine may run normally or limit power.
c: ECM software setting the code without a real fault (update available)
Sensor G drifted or worn, disagreeing with its partner sensor
Deposits or sticking plate making the angle disagree with airflow
Contact resistance at the throttle body connector
s: MIL on, often without noticeable driving problems
Reduced power if the plausibility fault persists
Uneven idle on twin-throttle engines

P212C.t: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Low
P212C.d: P212C sets when position signal G reads below its lower electrical limit. The letter G only comes into play on engines with more than one electronic throttle. GM's 2023 and 2024 OBD tables (23OBDG07, 24OBDG07) give it to the second position sensor in the bank 2 throttle body of a twin-throttle engine: a raw voltage under 0.195 V lasting 0.14 s while the ECU is running stores the code within one trip. Usual culprits are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost 5 V feed to that throttle body or a damaged sensor track. P212D is the matching high fault, P212A the general circuit code, P212B the plausibility check of G. Once a bank 2 signal is lost, the ECU typically restricts power.
c: Signal wire of sensor G shorted to ground
5 V reference to the bank 2 throttle body open or pulled low
Worn or damaged track of position sensor G inside the throttle body
Corroded or loose terminals at the bank 2 throttle connector
s: Engine warning lamp on
Reduced engine power message
Uneven idle or hesitation on one bank

P212D.t: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit High
P212D.d: P212D is the high-voltage fault on throttle position signal G. GM documents it in the 2023 and 2024 tables (23OBDG07, 24OBDG07) for sensor 2 of the bank 2 throttle body on a twin-throttle engine: once the raw voltage climbs above 4.805 V for 0.14 s, the code is stored in a single trip. A reading that close to the supply rail usually points to an open sensor ground, an interrupted signal line that the input pulls up, or a short to the 5 V reference or battery voltage. Because both sensors of one throttle often share their ground, P212D can appear alongside a high fault on the first sensor of that throttle. P212C is the low counterpart, P212A the general circuit code. Expect a warning lamp and reduced power.
c: Open sensor ground at the bank 2 throttle body
Signal wire of sensor G shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Broken signal wire or pushed-back terminal
Internal fault in the position sensor of the bank 2 throttle
s: Engine warning lamp on
Reduced engine power message
Weak or delayed response to the accelerator

P212E.t: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Intermittent
P212E.d: P212E is reserved for brief dropouts or spikes on throttle position signal G, the kind that clear again before a steady low or high fault can be confirmed. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, which assigns G to sensor 2 of the bank 2 throttle body on a twin-throttle engine, reacts to such glitches with its range checks instead: P212C below 0.195 V and P212D above 4.805 V each need only 0.14 s. CARB requires input sensors to be monitored for circuit faults, which is the duty this slot covers. In practice the trigger is a loose terminal, a chafed wire near the engine or moisture in the connector. Check the harness while flexing it with the engine running. The fault may vanish between workshop visits.
c: Loose or worn terminal at the bank 2 throttle connector
Harness chafed by engine movement, breaking contact now and then
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Momentary contact loss on the sensor track
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief stumbles or power dips
Fault often not present at the workshop

P212F.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F/G Voltage Correlation
P212F.d: P212F checks whether the two redundant signals F and G still agree in voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the letters make it an unusual pair: GM's 2004-2005 truck tables use F for the third accelerator pedal track, while GM's 2023 table assigns G to the second sensor of a bank 2 throttle body. A meaningful F/G comparison therefore needs a layout where both letters sit on the same component, for example a second throttle body with two tracks. Comparable checks are documented under P2135 and P2138, where GM and Ford store a fault when two tracks differ by a few percent or degrees. A drifting track, contact resistance or a shared ground fault are the plausible causes; the ECU then limits power.
c: One sensor track worn or drifted so the pair disagrees
Contact resistance in the connector shifting one signal
Fault in a shared ground or 5 V reference line
s: Engine or throttle warning lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
Hesitant response to the pedal

P2130.d: P2130 is the general circuit code for signal F. GM used it on its 2004-2005 pickups and SUVs with a separate throttle actuator control module (TACM) and a pedal carrying three tracks, where F is APP sensor 3. The TACM flags a continuous or intermittent open or short when sensor 3 reads below 1.63 V or above 4.38 V, or when its learned rest voltage exceeds 4.28 V; each error adds 4 to a counter checked every 3 ms, passes subtract 1, and the code sets at 106. GM's 2004 tables rate it Type C, the 2005 tables Type A with immediate MIL. Ford's three-track pedals split the same duty into P2132 and P2133. Plausibility is P2131, dropouts P2134. With one track lost the other two still steer the engine, usually with reduced response.
c: Poor terminal contact or corrosion at the pedal connector
Open or short in the signal, reference or ground wire of track F
Third track inside the pedal sensor worn or failed
Faulty input in the throttle actuator control module or ECM
s: Engine warning lamp on
Softer or delayed response to the pedal
Reduced power message on some models

P2131.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit Range/Performance
P2131.d: P2131 means pedal track F is electrically intact but disagrees with the rest of the pedal. Two makers document it for three-track pedals. GM's 2004-2005 truck tables scale APP sensor 3 to the range of the other tracks and set P2131 only when it strays more than 0.26 V from each of the other two sensors, so the majority vote singles out track F; the counter runs every 3 ms and trips at 167 (Type C in 2004, Type A in 2005). Ford's 2012 summary sets it on second-generation ETC when F departs from the others by over 1.1 degrees, lighting the wrench lamp without MIL. Circuit faults on F are P2130 and P2132-P2134. The car stays drivable; the ECU follows the two healthy tracks and softens pedal response.
c: Worn or dirty track F giving an offset reading
Contact resistance at the pedal connector
Bent pedal bracket or binding mechanism distorting one track
