s: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
Softened, slower acceleration
Often no noticeable change while driving

P2132.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit Low
P2132.d: P2132 sets when signal F drops below its lower voltage limit. Ford uses it for the third accelerator pedal track of its second-generation electronic throttle: its 2012 OBD summary treats anything under 0.25 V as a continuity fault and lights only the wrench lamp, not the MIL. FCA's emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter lists P2132 among the codes that may appear after the engine control unit is reprogrammed. GM's TACM trucks of 2004-2005 fold low readings of sensor 3 into the general code P2130. Likely causes are a short to ground on the F signal, an open 5 V feed or wear at the closed end of the track. P2133 is the high fault on F, P2122 and P2127 the low faults on tracks D and E.
c: Signal wire of track F shorted to ground
Open or weak 5 V reference to the pedal sensor
Track F worn at the rest position
s: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
Delayed or rate-limited acceleration
Idle may stay raised until the brake is pressed

P2133.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit High
P2133.d: P2133 is the high-voltage fault on signal F. In Ford's second-generation electronic throttle the third pedal track counts as failed once it rises above 4.75 V; the 2012 summary reports it with the wrench lamp and without MIL. FCA lists P2133 in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter among the codes that can show up after the engine computer is reflashed. GM's 2004-2005 trucks with a TACM catch excessive readings of sensor 3 above 4.38 V under the general code P2130. A track pinned near the supply would mimic a pressed pedal, so the controller drops it and works with the remaining two. Typical causes are an open sensor ground or a short to 5 V. P2132 is the low counterpart, P2123 and P2128 the high faults on D and E.
c: Open ground line of the pedal sensor
Signal wire of track F shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Internal break in track F of the pedal sensor
s: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
Slower, limited acceleration
May appear together with high faults on other tracks if the ground is open

P2134.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit Intermittent
P2134.d: P2134 targets short interruptions on signal F that are too brief or too irregular for a confirmed low or high fault. No manufacturer publishes a detection rule for it. FCA does name P2134 in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter, among the codes that may appear once the engine control unit carries the new software. GM's 2004-2005 trucks with three-track pedals handle such glitches inside P2130, whose counter adds 4 for each faulty sample every 3 ms and removes 1 for each good one until it reaches 106. Ford reports problems on F only as P2131-P2133. Look for loose pins and chafing near the pedal while moving it slowly. Effects range from a passing warning lamp to brief hesitation.
c: Loose or spread terminal at the pedal connector
Pedal harness pinched or chafed near the footwell bracket
Worn spot on track F causing momentary contact loss
s: Warning lamp that appears and clears
Short hesitation when moving the pedal

P2135.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A/B Voltage Correlation
P2135.d: P2135 compares the two position tracks of the electronic throttle, A and B, and sets when they no longer describe the same plate angle. GM's 2006-2007 tables allow a 7 % offset at closed throttle rising to 10 % at full opening and count failures every 12.5 ms until 19 of 39 have failed. Ford flags more than 7 degrees of disagreement; its 2012 and 2020-2023 summaries show only the wrench lamp, the 2024 summary also the MIL. Mitsubishi lists P2135 for the 2022 Outlander as a one-trip MIL code. Nissan bulletin NTB21-080 cures P2135 on the 2020-2021 Frontier without driveability complaints by ECM reprogramming. Mercedes traced it on AMG M177 V8s to high resistance in the throttle actuator pins. The ECU then limits throttle opening.
c: Worn or contaminated position tracks in the throttle body
Raised contact resistance or corrosion at the throttle connector
ECM calibration prone to false detection (update available on some models)
Fault on the shared 5 V reference or ground of both tracks
s: Engine warning lamp or wrench lamp on
Reduced engine power, limited throttle opening
Rough or raised idle

P2136.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A/C Voltage Correlation
P2136.d: P2136 reports that position signals A and C disagree. On engines with two electronic throttles, C typically belongs to the second throttle body: GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 assigns C to sensor 1 of the bank 2 throttle. Mercedes-Benz documents P2136 for its M177 twin-turbo V8 in AMG C63, GLC63, SL63 and related models: bulletin LI07.10-P-080384 lists it with P2135, the A/G and B/G checks and actuator faults, traces the set to increased electrical resistance in the connector pins of both throttle actuators, and replaces the connector sockets with coated terminals. FCA also lists the code in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter. Expect a warning lamp and possibly reduced power.
c: Increased resistance in the throttle actuator connector pins
Position sensor in one throttle body drifted or worn
Carbon or ice making one throttle lag behind the other
s: Engine warning lamp on
Possible loss of power
Often stored together with P2135

P2137.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B/C Voltage Correlation
P2137.d: P2137 compares position signals B and C and sets when their voltages drift apart beyond the calibrated tolerance. No manufacturer publishes a detection rule for this pair; FCA merely lists P2137 in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter among the codes that may surface after the ECU is reprogrammed. Where the letters are known, B is the second track of the main throttle and C a sensor on a second throttle body (GM 23OBDG07). The neighbouring pair A/C is documented by Mercedes on the M177 V8, where corroded or high-resistance actuator pins set it, which is the most likely pattern here too. Unlike P2135, which stays within one throttle, this check spans two components. Expect a warning lamp and possibly reduced power.
c: High resistance or corrosion at a throttle connector
Track B or sensor C drifted or worn
Fault on a shared 5 V reference or ground
s: Engine warning lamp on
Possible loss of power

P2138.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D/E Voltage Correlation
P2138.d: P2138 is the standard plausibility check of a two-track accelerator pedal: D and E are pedal sensors 1 and 2 at GM, Ford and VW. GM's 2007 tables set it when the tracks differ by more than 10 % or their learned rest values by over 5 % (Type A); the 2023 table uses 0.12-0.18 V for 0.25 s in one trip. Ford flags more than 0.9 degrees and since 2020 lights MIL and wrench lamp; the 2014 VW Passat allows 0.17-0.70 V. GM bulletin 07-06-04-019F blames water entering the instrument panel to body harness connector, and special coverage N182188250 covers a pedal sensor connection on the Malibu (2016-2018), LaCrosse (2017-2018) and Regal (2018). Single-track faults have their own codes (P2122-P2128). The ECU reduces power.
c: Water or corrosion in a pedal or inline harness connector
Worn pedal sensor with one track drifting
Poorly crimped or loose terminals raising resistance
Aftermarket equipment tapped into pedal or 5 V reference circuits
s: Engine warning lamp with reduced engine power message
Sluggish, capped acceleration
Traction or stability control may be switched off on some models

P2139.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D/F Voltage Correlation
P2139.d: P2139 compares signals D and F, in practice the first and third tracks of a three-track accelerator pedal. No manufacturer publishes a detection rule for this exact code; FCA only lists P2139 in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter among codes that can appear after the ECU update. Makers with three-track pedals handle the comparison differently: GM's 2004-2005 trucks scale sensor 3 and test it against sensors 1 and 2 at 0.26 V, then blame the odd track through P2131 or P2126 instead of naming a pair, and Ford reports a deviating track F as P2131. A pair code like P2139 cannot say which of the two tracks is wrong, so check both with a scope while moving the pedal. Effects are a warning lamp and softened acceleration.
c: Track D or F of the pedal sensor worn or drifted
Contact resistance at the pedal connector
Fault on a shared ground or 5 V reference
s: Engine or wrench warning lamp on
Softened or delayed acceleration

P213A.d: P213A concerns the electrical drive of EGR throttle B, a second motor-driven regulating flap found on some diesel layouts. Such a flap closes partly so that pressure ahead of the intake falls below exhaust pressure and enough exhaust gas can be recirculated; it also cuts air at engine stop. The engine module watches the output stage of flap B and stores P213A when the circuit is open or the driver flags a fault it cannot assign to low or high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, so thresholds are unknown; CARB treats the flap as an output component whose circuit must be monitored. Flap A reports the same fault as P0487. Expect the flap to rest in its spring position, reduced EGR and possibly a power limit.
c: Loose, corroded or broken connector or wire at throttle B
Open winding in the throttle B actuator motor
Harness damaged by heat near the exhaust or EGR cooler
Faulty output stage in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
Engine shudder when switched off
EGR readiness not completed

P213B.t: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P213B.d: P213B is the functional check of EGR throttle B rather than an electrical one. The module compares the position it commands with the position the flap actually reaches, or judges whether the feedback is plausible; if the gap persists beyond a set time, P213B is logged. Regulating flaps sit in a stream of recirculated exhaust and crankcase vapour, so soot and oil deposits that make the blade stiff are the usual reason, followed by worn gears or a weak motor. No manufacturer documents P213B publicly; CARB requires output components to be checked for proper function, and EGR control to be monitored for reaching its limits. The same check for flap A is P0488; pure wiring faults on B appear as P213A, P213C or P213D. The driver notices hesitation, smoke or a power limit.
c: Flap stiff or stuck from soot and oil deposits
Worn gear train or weak actuator motor
Implausible position feedback from the flap sensor
Outdated engine software or missing flap adaptation
s: Check engine lamp on
Hesitation, black smoke or reduced power
Clicking or humming from the flap
Filter regeneration may be postponed

P213C.t: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B Low
P213C.d: P213C points to a low signal in the drive circuit of EGR throttle B: the output stage sees too little voltage where it expects supply potential, which almost always means a conductor of the flap motor is touching ground. Chafed harness sections near the exhaust, water in the connector or a motor winding shorted to its housing are typical. Depending on the bridge design the module either switches the output off or the motor stays partly energised. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, so no threshold or debounce time can be given; CARB demands separate detection of circuit faults on output components. For throttle A the matching short-circuit code is P2141. An open circuit on B is P213A, a function fault P213B. The flap usually falls back to its rest position and EGR is limited.
c: Chafed wire shorting to ground between module and flap
Water or corrosion in the flap connector
Actuator motor winding shorted to housing
Faulty output stage in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
Engine shudder when switched off

P213D.t: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B High
P213D.d: P213D is the opposite electrical fault to P213C on EGR throttle B: the drive line carries voltage where the output stage expects ground, or the driver measures excessive current. A wire touching battery positive, a shorted motor winding that pulls too much current, or a mechanically blocked flap that overloads the motor are the usual triggers. The output stage switches off to protect itself, so the flap returns to its spring position and stops regulating. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P213D; CARB requires output circuits to be checked for faults in both directions. Throttle A reports the same high condition as P2142, while P213A covers an open circuit and P213B a flap that moves but misses its target. Drivers notice the warning lamp, sometimes reduced power.
c: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Shorted turns in the actuator motor causing overcurrent
Faulty output stage in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Reduced power in some operating ranges
EGR readiness not completed

P213E.t: Fuel Injection System Fault - Forced Engine Shutdown
P213E.d: P213E records that the engine module stopped the engine on purpose because of a fault on the injection side – rail, high-pressure lines, pressure control or injectors. Continuing to run with an external leak, a rail pressure that can no longer be controlled or an injector that keeps delivering could cause a fire or engine damage. No manufacturer documents P213E publicly. The same reaction is documented on Saab's 9-5 V6 diesel under the older P0148: when the leak calculation exceeds 90 mm³ per crankshaft revolution the module stops the engine and the test only runs again in the next drive cycle. A code naming the root cause usually sits next to P213E; P213F is the counterpart for the fuel pump side. The car stalls or will not restart and should be checked before further use.
c: External leak at rail, high-pressure line or injector seal
Injector stuck open or leaking heavily
Rail pressure control valve or sensor no longer controlling pressure
Engine software misjudging the fault, update available
s: Engine shuts off while running
Engine cranks but does not start again
Fuel smell or visible fuel leak
Check engine lamp with further fuel system codes

P213F.t: Fuel Pump System Fault - Forced Engine Shutdown
P213F.d: P213F is the supply-side twin of P213E: the engine module shut the engine down because the fuel pump system – electric lift pump, its relay or control module, or the engine-driven high-pressure pump – no longer behaves in a way it can accept. No manufacturer documents P213F publicly, so the trigger is not known in detail. How closely pumps are watched can be seen in Ford's 2023 diesel summary: the lift pump relay circuits are checked for open and shorts within 0.2 s, and the duty-cycle feedback of the pump must stay between 78 and 82 %. A deliberate shutdown goes further than those circuit codes and is normally stored together with them. Injection-side faults are logged as P213E instead. The engine stops or will not restart; towing is usually needed.
c: Electric lift pump or its control module failed
Pump relay, fuse or wiring fault
Clogged filter or empty tank starving the pump
s: Engine shuts off while driving
No restart or very long cranking
Check engine lamp with fuel pump codes

P2140.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E/F Voltage Correlation
P2140.d: P2140 checks the second and third pedal tracks, E and F, against each other. As with P2139, no manufacturer explains its own trigger for this code, and FCA's emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter just includes it in the list of codes that may follow the ECU reflash. GM's 2004-2005 trucks show what the comparison looks like in practice: their P2126 sets when sensor 2 differs from sensor 1 by more than 0.20 V and from the rescaled sensor 3 by more than 0.26 V, so the E-to-F term is part of a vote rather than a code of its own. Because track E is often scaled differently from F, a fault on a shared reference can shift one signal more than the other. Warning lamp and reduced pedal response follow.
c: Track E or F of the pedal sensor worn or drifted
Shared 5 V reference or ground fault shifting one track
Contact resistance or moisture at the pedal connector
s: Engine or wrench warning lamp on
Reduced or delayed pedal response

P2141.t: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Low
P2141.d: P2141 flags a low signal in the drive circuit of EGR throttle A, the main diesel regulating flap that lowers intake pressure so exhaust gas can flow back. A wire of the flap motor touching ground, a winding shorted to the housing or a wet connector are the common reasons. Note how J2012 spreads flap A over two ranges: open circuit and range/performance sit at P0487 and P0488, low and high at P2141 and P2142; flap B uses P213A to P213D. P0489 sounds similar but concerns the EGR valve A drive, not the throttle. No manufacturer documents P2141 publicly, so no figures can be quoted; CARB requires circuit faults on output components to be reported. The module usually disables the flap, which then rests open, and EGR is reduced.
c: Chafed wire shorting to ground between module and flap
Moisture or corrosion in the flap connector
Actuator motor winding shorted to housing
Faulty output stage in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine shudder when switched off
Reduced power or limp mode

P2142.t: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A High
P2142.d: P2142 reports a high signal or overcurrent in the drive circuit of EGR throttle A. Either a motor lead has contact with battery voltage, or the motor draws more current than the output stage allows – from shorted turns or because carbon has jammed the blade. The driver then shuts down for protection, the flap springs back to its rest position and EGR regulation is lost. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P2142; CARB obliges the system to recognise circuit faults of output components in both directions. P2141 is the low counterpart, P0487 the open circuit and P0488 the function check of the same flap; flap B reports a high circuit as P213D. If the cause is mechanical, cleaning or replacing the flap removes it, a wiring short needs a harness repair.
c: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Flap jammed by carbon, motor overloaded
Shorted turns in the actuator motor
Faulty output stage in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
EGR readiness not completed

P2143.d: Vacuum-operated EGR valves are often run by a pair of solenoids: one feeds vacuum to the valve diaphragm to open it, the other – the vent solenoid – lets air in to release the vacuum and close the valve. Ford's EEC engine computers had separate outputs for EGR vent and EGR control, and a Kia diesel patent maps both solenoids by duty cycle, using the vent side whenever the measured EGR value is above target. P2143 means the module found the vent solenoid circuit open or otherwise faulty. Without a working vent the valve may close slowly or stay open longer than wanted, causing rough idle; many systems simply disable EGR. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P2143. Shorts are reported separately as P2144 and P2145.
c: Loose connector or broken wire at the vent solenoid
Open coil in the vent solenoid
Blown fuse or missing supply voltage to the solenoid
Faulty output stage in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Rough idle or stalling after deceleration
EGR readiness not completed

P2144.d: P2144 reports a low signal in the circuit that drives the EGR vent solenoid – the valve that bleeds vacuum from a vacuum-operated EGR valve so it can close. With the usual low-side switching, a control wire touching ground keeps the solenoid energised regardless of the command. Whether that leaves the EGR valve unable to open or unable to close depends on the plumbing, but in both cases the EGR rate can no longer be controlled. Ford's 2014 spark-ignition code list includes P2144 with the warning lamp and a continuous test, though Ford gives no threshold; no other public manufacturer document names the code. P2143 covers an open circuit and P2145 the high fault of the same solenoid. Typical results are rough running, higher NOx or a failed EGR readiness test.
c: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in the vent solenoid coil
Corrosion bridging terminals in the connector
Faulty output stage in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Rough idle or hesitation
Emissions test failure because of EGR

P2145.d: P2145 is the high fault in the vent solenoid circuit of the EGR system: the control line shows supply voltage while the module tries to pull it to ground, or the driver detects overcurrent through a shorted coil. The output then cannot switch the solenoid on, so the vent stays in its rest state – depending on design the EGR valve either cannot be released quickly or cannot be held, and the module normally stops using EGR. Ford's 2014 spark-ignition code list names P2145 alongside P2144, both with the warning lamp and a continuous test; thresholds are not given and no further manufacturer document is public. For the vent concept itself see Ford's separate vent and control outputs and Kia's duty-mapped vent solenoid. Open circuit is P2143, low fault P2144.
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Shorted vent solenoid coil drawing excess current
Faulty output stage in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
EGR inactive, sometimes pinging under load on petrol engines
EGR readiness not completed

P2146.t: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2146.d: Direct-injection and common-rail injectors are fed by a high-side driver in the engine module, often shared by several injectors. P2146 is the open or general fault of the first such supply. GM's 2009 Duramax diesel pairs injectors 1 and 4 in group 1 and sets P2146 when the driver sees an open, short or missing load for 6 ms, type A. VW's 2014 TSI and VR6 engines check the high-side current: below 2.6 A or above 14.9 A. GM petrol direct injection assigns the code to a single cylinder, the high-side control line of cylinder 1; in the Saab 9-5 2.0T a supply fault shared by cylinders 1 and 4 sets P2146 and P2155 together, after 1 s, type B, and the injector is shut off. GM bulletin PIP4924D links it to chafed V6 injector harnesses. Expect misfire and rough running.
c: Injector harness chafed through or wire open inside insulation
Loose, wet or corroded injector connector
Open coil or piezo stack in an injector of the group
Faulty high-side driver in the engine control module
s: Misfire on one or more cylinders
Rough running and loss of power
Check engine lamp on

P2147.t: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2147.d: P2147 means the common feed of injector group A is pulled toward ground. GM documents it in detail for its 2018 Duramax diesels: the high-side line to injectors 1 and 4 (group 1 on both the 2.8 L four and the 6.6 L V8) shows 0.5 Ω or less to ground while the driver is switched on; with the engine running and more than 11 V, 5 failures in 10 samples at 100 ms set it, type A, lamp on the first trip (2025 tables: 4 of 8). Ford's 2023 diesels report a short of group A to ground or battery found by the driver chip after about 0.2 s. On GM petrol direct injection such as the Saab 9-5 2.0T the code stands for low voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 1. Both injectors of the group usually stop, so two cylinders drop out. P2148 is the opposite fault.
c: Injector supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Injector of the group shorted internally to its body
Water in the injector harness connector
Faulty injector driver in the engine control module
s: Two cylinders misfire at once
Heavy loss of power, rough running
Check engine lamp on immediately

P2148.t: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2148.d: P2148 flags group A's injector supply as too high. On GM's 2018 Duramax the high-side terminal of injector 1 or 4 shows 0.5 Ω or less to supply potential while the driver is off; same 5-of-10 counting at 100 ms, type A. Ford's 2023 diesels give it a different meaning: the chip that produces the boosted injector voltage inside the module reports an internal fault – a pointer to the control unit rather than the harness. GM's petrol direct injection reads it as excess voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 1. Bulletins show software and hardware causes: Hino's 2016 J08 trucks set P2148 and P2151 falsely until the ECU is reprogrammed (SB-15-023), and GM PIP6034 replaces the PCM on 2024–25 2.5 L LK0 models. The low fault is P2147.
c: Injector supply wire shorted to battery voltage
Internal fault of the injector boost circuit in the module
Software falsely detecting the fault, reprogramming available
Injector of the group with internal short
s: Check engine lamp on
Misfire and rough running on the affected cylinders
Often no drivability complaint when the cause is software

P2149.t: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2149.d: P2149 is the open or general fault of the second shared injector supply. Group membership depends on the engine: GM's 2009 Duramax places injectors 7 and 6 in group 2 (6 ms, type A), whereas GM's 2018 tables pair injectors 2 and 5 in the V8 – so the cylinders must be looked up for each engine. VW's 2014 TSI and VR6 engines use the same current window as for group A, under 2.6 A or above about 14.7–14.9 A. GM petrol direct injection treats P2149 as the high-side control line of cylinder 2: on the 2023–24 Corvette LT6 bulletin 24-NA-106 traces it, with rail pressure codes, to water entering a wrong 12-way connector on bank 2. A Mercedes M254 bulletin lists P2149 among faults caused by fuel boiling in the low-pressure system.
c: Injector harness damaged or wire open
Water entering an injector harness connector
Open coil or piezo stack in an injector of the group
Low rail pressure from fuel vapour triggering follow-up faults
s: Misfire on the cylinders of group B
Rough running and reduced power
Check engine lamp on

P214A.t: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High
P214A.d: P214A reports that the exhaust entering the SCR catalyst was hotter than a calibrated ceiling while no particulate filter regeneration was active. The reading normally comes from the temperature sensor between the filter and the urea mixing section. Heat at this point is a threat to the SCR coating: Navistar's patent US20190232224 states that vanadia sublimates above roughly 550 °C, and 40 CFR 1036.115 obliges heavy-duty engine makers to shield vanadium catalysts from such temperatures. No manufacturer documents P214A publicly; Ram bulletins for the 6.7L Cummins name only the sibling P214D, and Ford flags aftertreatment overheating with P200C/P200E. P214B covers the same fault during regeneration, P214C the outlet side. Typical triggers are fuel or oil in the exhaust, overfuelling or a drifting sensor.
c: Unburnt fuel or engine oil reaching the exhaust (leaking injector, turbocharger seal)
SCR inlet temperature sensor reading too high or wrongly placed after repair
Overfuelling from injection or air-path faults (boost leak, EGR fault)
Engine control software with outdated temperature model
s: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power to limit exhaust temperature
Further codes for exhaust temperature or SCR efficiency

P214B.t: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration
P214B.d: P214B is limited to the regeneration phase. To burn soot out of the particulate filter, the engine control adds late injections or uses a separate exhaust fuel injector, and the oxidation catalyst converts that fuel into heat. The code sets when the gas leaving this hot zone arrives at the SCR inlet above the limit allowed during regeneration. Navistar's patent US20190232224 describes exactly this conflict: repeated regenerations push vanadium SCR material towards its sublimation point near 550 °C, so the layout and temperature control must keep the SCR below it. No manufacturer documents P214B publicly. Compared with P214A, suspicion falls on regeneration control: a dripping exhaust injector, excess post-injection or soot burning too fast. The control unit usually aborts the regeneration.
c: Exhaust fuel injector leaking or over-dosing during regeneration
Heavily loaded filter burning off too quickly
Excess post-injection quantity from a worn engine injector
Exhaust temperature sensor upstream of the SCR reading too high
s: Check engine light on, regeneration aborted
Filter warning or rising soot load because regeneration cannot finish
Reduced engine power

P214C.t: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High
P214C.d: P214C looks at the downstream end of the SCR catalyst: the temperature measured behind it rose above the permitted maximum outside regeneration. California's OBD rule lists SCR intake and outlet temperature as separate data values a diesel must report, so both points are watched on their own. An outlet reading that climbs above the inlet value hints at heat produced inside or just ahead of the brick, for instance hydrocarbons burning on the SCR or soot glowing in a combined filter-SCR unit, but a faulty outlet sensor is just as likely. The material limit is the same as on the inlet side, which 40 CFR 1036.115 and Navistar's patent US20190232224 describe for vanadium catalysts. No manufacturer documents P214C publicly. P214A is the inlet counterpart, P214D the outlet fault during regeneration.
c: SCR outlet temperature sensor faulty or reading too high
Hydrocarbons passing the oxidation catalyst and burning on the SCR
Fuel or oil entering the exhaust from the engine or turbocharger
s: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power
Implausible outlet temperature compared with the inlet value in live data

P214D.t: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration
P214D.d: P214D sets when the temperature behind the SCR catalyst exceeds its limit while the particulate filter is regenerating. It is the only code of this group with public manufacturer evidence. Ram pickups with the 6.7L Cummins use it: bulletin 18-053-14 (2014 Ram 2500/3500) reprograms the PCM partly to prevent unnecessary MIL events from P214D, and STAR case S2625000004 (2025–2026 Ram 3500 to 5500) groups it with exhaust temperature sensor codes such as P242B and P2470–P2472, asks for a check of battery voltage first and stresses identifying each sensor by name. That points to sensor faults and calibration as frequent causes, besides genuine overheating from hydrocarbons burning on the hot SCR during regeneration. P214B is the inlet counterpart.
c: Exhaust temperature sensor behind the SCR faulty, confused with another sensor or affected by low battery voltage
PCM software requiring an update (Ram 6.7L bulletins)
Regeneration fuel slipping through and burning on the SCR
s: Check engine light on
Regeneration aborted or repeated
Additional exhaust temperature sensor codes

P214E.t: Reductant Pump A Current Too High
P214E.d: P214E means the electronics driving the DEF (AdBlue) pump motor saw more current than the pump may draw. GM documents it on Duramax diesels: in the 2018 tables the DEF control module reports a motor high-current or current-limit error, and the ECM sets the code after 20 failed of 25 samples with the battery above 11 V; the 2025 tables use a hardware protection limit of 15 A plus separate motor current limits for pumping and for heating mode, in which the pump is driven to warm frozen fluid. Both are Type A, so the MIL comes on after one trip. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets P214E when the pump motor controller exceeds 15 A. GM bulletin 20-NA-039 traced P214E on the 2020 Silverado/Sierra 1500 3.0L to software. A seized or iced pump stops dosing; P2C11 is the low-current counterpart.
c: Pump motor seized, worn or blocked by crystallised or frozen fluid
Short in the pump motor winding or supply wiring, often after water ingress
ECM or reductant control module software (GM 20-NA-039)
Faulty driver stage in the reductant control module
s: Check engine light on after one trip
DEF system warning, possibly a countdown to speed limitation
Raised NOx emissions because dosing stops

P214F.t: Reductant Heater A Current Too High
P214F.d: P214F concerns heater A of the DEF system, which Ford and GM both assign to the heater inside the tank (heater circuit 1). The code says this element consumed more current or power than intended. Ford's 2023 diesel summary performs one check per heating cycle, right after a cold start, and decides within 2.2 s when tank heater power is higher than expected. GM's 2025 Duramax tables set P214F when heater 1 current passes 15 A in 40 consecutive 100 ms samples; that is Type A and lights the MIL after one trip; the 2015 tables detected a shorted tank heater through a conductance of at least 0.62 S, Type B. A shorted element, wet connector or chafed lead is the usual reason. Without tank heating, frozen DEF thaws late or not at all, so dosing and NOx reduction start late in winter. P21DD is the low-current counterpart.
c: Tank heater element internally shorted (often replaced with the tank sender unit)
Water ingress or corrosion in the heater connector
Chafed heater wiring shorted to ground
Faulty heater driver in the reductant control module
s: Check engine light on
DEF system warning in cold weather
Delayed DEF dosing after cold starts

P2150.t: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2150.d: P2150 reports the common feed of injector group B shorted toward ground. In GM's 2018 Duramax tables group 2 holds injectors 2 and 3 on the 2.8 L four-cylinder but injectors 2 and 5 on the 6.6 L V8; the test is the same as for group A – 0.5 Ω or less to ground with the driver on, 5 failed samples out of 10, type A with lamp on the first trip. Ford's 2023 diesels flag a short of group B to ground or battery, detected by the driver chip in roughly 0.2 s. GM petrol direct injection, documented for the Saab 9-5 2.0T, uses P2150 for low voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 2. Because both injectors of a diesel bank lose their feed, the engine runs on fewer cylinders. P2149 is the open circuit, P2151 the high fault of this group.
c: Group B supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Injector of group B shorted to its body
Moisture in the injector harness connector
Faulty injector driver in the engine control module
s: Two cylinders misfire together
Marked power loss and vibration
Check engine lamp on immediately

P2151.t: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2151.d: P2151 marks the group B injector supply as too high. GM's 2018 Duramax checks the high-side pins of the bank 2 injectors with the driver switched off and sets the code at 0.5 Ω or less to supply potential, 5 of 10 samples, type A. On Ford's 2023 diesels the same number stands for an internal fault reported by the boost voltage chip of the module, so a harness check alone rarely solves it. GM petrol direct injection uses it for excess voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 2. Bulletins point mostly to the control unit: Hino's 2016 J08 engines set P2148 and P2151 falsely and need new ECU software (SB-15-023), and GM PIP6034 replaces the PCM of 2024–25 Traverse, Acadia and Enclave with the 2.5 L LK0. P2150 is the low counterpart.
c: Internal fault of the injector boost circuit in the module
Software falsely detecting the fault, reprogramming available
Group B supply wire shorted to battery voltage
Injector of group B with internal short
s: Check engine lamp on
Misfire on the group B cylinders
Sometimes no noticeable symptom besides the lamp

P2152.t: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2152.d: P2152 belongs to the third shared injector supply, so it appears only on engines with at least three injector groups or, at GM petrol engines, at least three cylinders. GM's 2009 Duramax puts injectors 2 and 5 into group 3 and flags an open, short or missing load after 6 ms, type A. VW's 2014 Touareg V6 TDI stores it when the diagnostic signal of the group C power stage fails, and the Passat VR6 allows a wider high-side window for this group, below 2.3 A or above 18.6 A. In GM petrol direct injection it covers the high-side control line of cylinder 3; GM bulletin PIP4924D lists it among injector codes on 3.0 L and 3.6 L V6 engines whose injector harness rubs through. Misfire on the related cylinders is the usual effect.
c: Injector harness rubbed through at plenum, bolts or fuel line
Open coil or piezo stack in an injector of the group
Faulty power stage in the engine control module
s: Misfire on the group C cylinders
Rough running, reduced power
Check engine lamp on

P2153.t: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2153.d: P2153 reports the third shared injector supply shorted toward ground. GM's 2018 Duramax tables use it only for the 6.6 L V8, where bank 3 feeds injectors 6 and 7; the four-cylinder 2.8 L has just two banks and never sets it. The criterion matches the other low codes – 0.5 Ω or less between a high-side pin and ground while the driver is on, 5 of 10 samples at 100 ms, type A. Ford lists group C among the injector driver checks of its 2023 diesels and flags shorts to ground or battery after about 0.2 s. On GM petrol direct injection, shown in the Saab 9-5 2.0T procedure, P2153 means low voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 3, set after 1 s, type B. Open circuit and high fault of this group are P2152 and P2154.
c: Group C supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Injector of group C shorted to its body
Moisture in the injector harness connector
Faulty injector driver in the engine control module
s: Misfire on the group C cylinders
Loss of power and vibration
Check engine lamp on

P2154.t: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2154.d: P2154 is the high fault of injector supply group C. On GM's 2018 Duramax V8 it covers injectors 6 and 7: with the driver off, 0.5 Ω or less from a high-side pin to supply potential in 5 of 10 samples sets it, type A, one trip. Ford's 2023 diesels assign it to an internal error flagged by the module's high-voltage injector driver chip, a strong hint that the control unit itself is at fault. For GM petrol direct injection it means excess voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 3, and GM PIP6034 lists it with P2148, P2151 and P2157 on 2024–25 2.5 L LK0 crossovers, where an internal PCM hardware fault requires replacing the module. Group C exists only where an engine has a third bank or cylinder. The low and open faults are P2153 and P2152.
c: Internal hardware fault of the injector driver in the module
Group C supply wire shorted to battery voltage
Injector of group C with internal short
s: Check engine lamp on
Misfire on the group C cylinders
Rough running at idle

P2155.t: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2155.d: P2155 is the open or general fault of the fourth shared injector supply. On GM's 2009 Duramax V8 group 4 joins injectors 8 and 3; an open, short or missing load for 6 ms sets the code, type A. The Passat VR6 of 2014 runs four supply groups and checks group D against a high-side current window of under 2.6 A or above 14.9 A. GM petrol direct injection uses it for the high-side control line of cylinder 4. In the Saab 9-5 2.0T the supply lines are shared by cylinders 1 and 4, which is why a supply fault there stores P2146 and P2155 together (1 s, type B). The 2023–24 Corvette LT6 bulletin 24-NA-106 names P2155 among codes caused by water entering a wrong bank 2 connector. Rough running and misfire on the affected cylinders follow.
c: Injector harness damaged or wire open
Water entering an injector harness connector
Open coil or piezo stack in an injector of the group
Faulty power stage in the engine control module
s: Misfire on the group D cylinders
Rough running and reduced power
Check engine lamp on

P2156.t: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2156.d: P2156 reports the fourth shared injector supply shorted toward ground. GM's 2018 Duramax uses it only on the 6.6 L V8, where bank 4 combines injectors 3 and 8; the high-side pin reading 0.5 Ω or less to ground while switched on sets it after 5 of 10 samples, type A, lamp on the first trip. Ford's 2023 diesel summary stops at group C, so the code does not appear there. On GM petrol direct injection, as in the Saab 9-5 2.0T, P2156 stands for low voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 4, set after 1 s and handled as type B. Since the diesel bank feeds two injectors, two cylinders cut out at once and the engine shakes noticeably. P2155 marks an open circuit and P2157 a high fault in the same group.
c: Group D supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Injector of group D shorted to its body
Moisture in the injector harness connector
Faulty injector driver in the engine control module
s: Two cylinders misfire together
Strong vibration and power loss
Check engine lamp on immediately

P2157.t: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2157.d: P2157 flags the group D injector supply as too high. GM's 2018 Duramax V8 tests the high-side pins of injectors 3 and 8 with the driver off; 0.5 Ω or less to supply potential in 5 of 10 samples sets it, type A, one trip, and the 2025 tables require 4 of 8. For GM petrol direct injection, documented in the Saab 9-5 2.0T procedure, it means excess voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 4. GM's preliminary information PIP6034 for 2024–25 Traverse, Acadia and Enclave with the 2.5 L LK0 names P2157 alongside P2148, P2151 and P2154 and blames an internal PCM hardware fault – several high codes at once point to the module rather than to four separate wiring faults. P2156 is the low and P2155 the open circuit of this group.
c: Internal hardware fault of the injector driver in the module
Group D supply wire shorted to battery voltage
Injector of group D with internal short
s: Check engine lamp on
Misfire on the group D cylinders
Several injector high codes stored together

P2158.d: P2158 reports an electrical fault in the circuit of a second vehicle speed signal, sensor B. P0500 is the matching code for sensor A. Which pickup carries the letter B is up to the manufacturer: a transmission output sensor, one of the ABS wheel sensors or another wheel. The only public manufacturer reference comes from Ducati: on the Scrambler 800 of model year 2021, P2158 stands for the front wheel speed sensor and P0500 for the rear one, and both could appear together with U0323 after fitting the accessory anti-theft kit, a case in which no sensor or ECU needs replacing. No car maker documents P2158 publicly. California's OBD rule names the vehicle speed sensor among input components to be checked for circuit faults. Speedometer, cruise control, ABS functions or shift timing may suffer.
c: Speed sensor B defective or its tone ring damaged
Broken wire, corroded or loose connector in the sensor circuit
Retrofitted accessory interfering with the speed signal (Ducati anti-theft kit)
s: Check engine light on
Speedometer erratic or dropping out
Cruise control or ABS/traction functions unavailable

P2159.t: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2159.d: P2159 means the circuit of speed sensor B is electrically intact, but its signal does not fit: implausible jumps, dropouts or a value that disagrees with other speed sources. Two makers document it. Audi lists P2159 with fault environment code 8099 as a plausibility fault of speed sensor B on the 0B5 S tronic gearbox of the 2010–2014 RS5 and the S4, S5, S6 and S7; together with P0501 (sensor A) and gear selector codes it points to the gearbox-internal sensor module and its circuit board, which has to be replaced after case disassembly. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander engine control groups P2159 with P0500/P0501 as vehicle speed sensor faults, detected over two trips and lighting the MIL. P2158 is the pure circuit fault of the same sensor. Expect gearbox warnings, erratic shifting or a speedometer that jumps.
c: Faulty speed sensor or transmission sensor module (Audi 0B5)
Damaged tone ring, wrong air gap or metal debris on the sensor tip
Intermittent contact in wiring or connector
Wrong tyre size or speed factor configured
s: Check engine light or gearbox warning on
Erratic shifting or emergency gearbox mode
Speedometer jumping

P215A.d: P215A compares the vehicle speed used by the powertrain with the speed derived from the ABS wheel sensors and sets when the two disagree. Volvo and Mack trucks document it most clearly: with I-Shift or mDRIVE gearboxes the code appears once the difference exceeds 12 km/h (7.5 mph), and the advice is to verify the speed factor and the tyre size stored in the brake controller before testing sensors. A Volvo case traced P215A with throttle dropouts to a loose ABS module ground. GM's 2025 brake module tables use P215A, Type B with MIL after two trips, both when more than two wheel sensor signals look suspect at the same time and when the spread between fastest and slowest wheel exceeds about 52 mph while moving. Speedometer loss, cruise or traction faults follow. P215B and P215C compare against the output shaft.
c: Tyre size or speed factor not matching the vehicle (common after tyre or axle changes)
Faulty wheel speed sensor or damaged tone ring
Poor ABS module ground or wiring fault in the speed signal path
Fault in the transmission-side vehicle speed source
s: Check engine light on
Speedometer dropping out
ABS, traction or cruise control warnings, power dropouts

P215B.t: Vehicle Speed - Output Shaft Speed Correlation
P215B.d: P215B checks whether the vehicle speed, as the control unit has chosen it, matches the speed implied by the transmission output shaft. GM uses it widely in hybrids and EVs. The 2011 Volt tables set it, Type A with MIL after one trip, when wheel-based and output-shaft-based speed differ by more than 6.21 mph or when no secured speed source remains, counted over 400 of 800 samples of 25 ms. In the 2019 hybrid tables three sources are compared, output shaft, wheel sensors and motor speeds, and the code sets after 0.15 s when two of them disagree by more than 12.42 mph. GM bulletin 22-NA-089 links P215B on the 2017–2019 Bolt EV to a broken drive shaft washer damaging the wheel speed sensor, which is to be replaced. FCA lists P215B for the Pacifica Hybrid and fixes it with hybrid controller software.
c: Damaged wheel speed sensor (GM Bolt EV broken anti-click washer)
Faulty transmission output speed sensor or its wiring
Hybrid or transmission control software (FCA Pacifica Hybrid)
Lost speed message from another module on the data bus
s: Check engine light on after one trip
ABS, traction or stability lamps, systems switched off for the drive
Clicking noise from a front wheel (Bolt EV)

P215C.t: Output Shaft Speed - Wheel Speed Correlation
P215C.d: P215C compares the transmission output shaft speed with the output speed calculated back from the wheel sensors. Unlike P215B it does not judge the final vehicle speed but the agreement between these two measured sources. GM's 2019 hybrid tables set it as Type B, MIL after two trips, when the output shaft and the average from wheel and motor speeds differ by more than 50 or 60 rpm for 0.23 s. FCA uses the code widely: bulletin 21-031-14 updated the TCM of the 2014 Charger and 300 AWD with the 845RE gearbox because P215C set during braking, 21-022-23 reprograms the 2023 Charger 8HP50 for the same code, and on the 2014–2017 Jeep Cherokee a broken power transfer unit input spline produces P215C with P1720 and grinding noises, covered by a warranty extension. Shift quality or AWD functions may suffer.
c: Transmission control software too sensitive, for example under braking (FCA bulletins)
Mechanical driveline fault such as a broken transfer unit spline (Jeep Cherokee)
Faulty output shaft speed sensor or wiring
Faulty wheel speed sensor or mismatched tyre sizes
s: Check engine light on
Harsh or irregular shifting
Grinding noise or loss of all-wheel drive (transfer unit damage)

P215D.d: P215D says the second DEF pump, called pump B or pump 2, keeps running or stays powered although the controller has commanded it off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Pump B itself is documented: Ford's 6.7L Super Duty trucks of 2023 can store pump B circuit codes P20FA, P20FC and P20FD (SSM 51891), and FCA names the same channel Reductant Pump 2 on 3.0L EcoDiesel models. California's OBD rule asks for functional checks of output components, and a stuck-on state is the logical opposite of P20FB, Performance/Stuck Off. A driver stage that no longer switches off, a control line shorted on the switched side or a welded relay could cause it. Effects can include pressure that cannot be released, lines not purged at shutdown and a drained battery. P201F is the same fault on pump A.
c: Output stage in the control module no longer switching off
Pump control line shorted so the pump receives power permanently
Welded contacts in the pump supply relay
s: Check engine light on
Pump audible after switching off the engine
DEF system warning, possibly a flat battery after standing

P215E.t: Reductant Heater D Current Too Low
P215E.d: P215E says the fourth DEF heating element, heater D, drew less current than expected while it was switched on, so it is probably not warming the fluid. Which element carries the letter D depends on the maker; many SCR systems stop at three. No maker documents P215E publicly. GM's 2025 Duramax tables and Ford's 2023 diesel summary check only heaters A to C; GM flags their currents below 0.75 A across 40 readings, one per tenth of a second, as Type A; Ford watches power and current during each heating cycle. GM bulletin 21-NA-149 does show a heater D on the 3.0 L LM2, but only with circuit codes P20C5 and P20C8. The usual causes are an open or burnt element, high resistance at the connector or a missing heater feed. P215F is the high-current partner, P20C5 to P20C8 the control-circuit faults. In frost the fluid may thaw late.
c: Heating element D open or burnt through, often inside a heated line or pump assembly
Corroded or loose pins at the heater D connector limiting current
Heater feed fuse or relay open, so the element gets no voltage
Weak heater output stage in the engine or DEF control module
s: Check engine light together with a DEF or emission system message
Dosing starts late or not at all after cold starts in frost
Restart countdown or speed limitation if the fault stays active

P215F.t: Reductant Heater D Current Too High
P215F.d: P215F is set when heater D of the DEF system pulls more current than its design allows, which points to a partly shorted element or a leak path to ground in its wiring. The letter D is assigned by each maker, and many systems have only three heaters. No maker documents P215F publicly. As a guide, GM's 2025 Duramax tables trip the high-current codes of heaters A to C above 15 A in 40 samples of 0.1 s and treat them as Type A, and Ford's 2023 diesel summary detects an overloaded tank or line heater within 2.2 s. The controller usually switches the faulty element off to protect its driver, so the fluid in that area is no longer heated. Wet connectors, chafed leads and internal shorts are typical. The low-current partner is P215E; circuit faults are P20C5 to P20C8.
c: Heating element D partly shorted internally
Moisture or DEF crystals in the heater D connector bridging pins
Chafed heater lead touching ground or a neighbouring circuit
s: Check engine light with a DEF or emission system warning
DEF stays frozen in the affected area during cold weather
Blown heater fuse in some cases

P2160.t: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P2160.d: P2160 reports that speed signal B shows little or no activity although the vehicle is plainly moving. Which pickup carries the letter B is the manufacturer's choice. GM assigns P2160 to the transfer case output speed sensor of its four-wheel-drive models (table 18OBDG04): with a gear engaged, moderate pedal and torque, no braking and the transmission output turning, a raw sensor reading under 25 rpm for 4.5 seconds stores the code as Type B, so the MIL follows after two trips. A broken wire, a short to ground or a dead sensor are the usual reasons. P2161 covers dropouts and erratic readings, P2158/P2159 the circuit and plausibility of the same sensor. Four-wheel-drive and speed-dependent functions may be restricted.
c: Broken signal wire or short to ground between sensor B and the module
Speed sensor B itself delivers no pulses
Corroded or pushed-back pins at the sensor connector
Tone wheel loose or missing after transfer case or driveline work
s: Check engine lamp after two drives
Four-wheel-drive warning or 4WD modes unavailable
Speedometer or cruise control misbehaving on some models

P2161.t: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic/High
P2161.d: P2161 flags a speed signal B that behaves in ways no real vehicle can: it collapses for a moment, jumps or reads implausibly high. GM documents the code for the transfer case output speed sensor (18OBDG04). While the truck is driven in gear without braking, a drop of the sensor speed larger than a delta threshold starts a 3-second fail timer, and five such counts store the code as Type B. GM adds that one dropout can also start the P2160 timer, so whichever runs out first is recorded. Loose connector contacts, chafed wires, metal debris on the sensor tip or a cracked tone wheel are the typical culprits. P2160 means the signal is missing altogether; P2162 compares sensor B with sensor A.
c: Connector contact opening briefly under vibration
Signal wire chafed against the transfer case or frame
Metal debris on the magnetic sensor tip
s: Check engine lamp, often only on rough roads
Speedometer needle twitching
Sporadic four-wheel-drive or shift complaints

P2162.d: P2162 means two speed sources, A and B, disagree by more than the calibration permits although each circuit is electrically sound. Depending on the vehicle, A and B can be a transmission output sensor, a transfer case sensor or wheel sensors read through the ABS unit. No manufacturer documents P2162 publicly. GM shows how closely the sources are linked: when its transfer case sensor fails (P2160/P2161), the software substitutes driven-wheel speed multiplied by the axle ratio (18OBDG04). California's OBD rule names the vehicle speed sensor among inputs that must be checked for plausibility. Wrong tyre size or axle ratio, a damaged tone wheel or debris on one sensor are typical causes. Speedometer, shifting, cruise control and 4WD may suffer.
c: Tyre size or axle ratio differs from the programmed values
Metal debris or damage on one of the two sensors
Damaged or wrong tone wheel on one shaft or hub
Wheel speed signal from the ABS unit faulty
s: Check engine lamp
Speedometer reading wrong or unsteady
Harsh or mistimed shifts, possibly a fixed-gear fallback

P2163.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Maximum Stop Performance
P2163.d: P2163 concerns position signal A at the upper end of its travel: with the throttle or pedal resting on its maximum mechanical stop, the reading or the learned full-open value lies outside the band the calibration accepts. On Ford layouts A is the first throttle body sensor, while D to F belong to the pedal. Ford lists P2163 for the 2014 Boss 302S with MIL and wrench lamp. A Visteon patent shows the idea: the motor presses the plate onto its fully open stop for about 60 ms, the sensor value is stored, and a learned stop outside roughly 80 to 110 degrees is reported as a failure. Carbon, a bent stop or a worn sensor track are typical causes. P2109 is the matching closed-stop check; P2164-P2168 test the other letters. Reduced power is possible.
c: Carbon or a bent stop keeps the plate from reaching full opening
Sensor A track worn at the full-open end
Replacement throttle body not matching or not relearned
Contact resistance in the sensor connector shifting the signal
s: Check engine and throttle warning lamps on
Engine does not reach full power
Limp mode with limited throttle opening

P2164.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Maximum Stop Performance
P2164.d: P2164 is the full-travel test for position signal B. When the throttle or pedal is held at its upper stop, sensor B has to report a value inside a calibrated band; a reading or learned maximum outside that band sets the code. Ford and GM call their second throttle body sensor B, so on those designs the code points at the throttle body, yet no manufacturer documents P2164 publicly. The nearest evidence is Ford's listing of the A version P2163 and a Visteon patent that learns the open stop and rejects values beyond about 80 to 110 degrees. On many throttle bodies the second track runs opposite to the first, so comparing A and B at full opening helps to tell a sensor fault from a mechanical block. P2113 checks the closed stop of B; P0220-P0223 cover its circuit.
c: Sensor B track worn or drifted at the full-open end
Deposits or a damaged stop limit the plate travel
Corroded contact on the sensor B signal or reference pin
End positions not relearned after part replacement
s: Engine warning lamp on
Power limited at high throttle demand
Occasional limp mode

P2165.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Maximum Stop Performance
P2165.d: P2165 belongs to the rarely used letter C. It is set when position signal C, at the upper stop of its throttle or pedal, reports a value the controller cannot accept as full travel. Since Ford gives A and B to the throttle and D to F to the pedal, C only appears on layouts with a third sensor track or a different naming scheme. No manufacturer documents P2165 publicly; the description follows the A version P2163, which Ford lists, and a Visteon patent on learning the throttle's open stop. Before replacing parts, confirm that the vehicle really uses a sensor C; an aftermarket throttle body or pedal with a different characteristic can also produce the code. P2114 tests the closed stop of C, P2136/P2137 compare C with A or B.
c: Sensor C track worn at the end of travel
Replacement throttle or pedal with a different characteristic
Mechanical obstruction before the upper stop
Resistance in the sensor C wiring or connector
s: Engine warning lamp on
Reduced power at full load

P2166.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor D Maximum Stop Performance
P2166.d: P2166 refers to position signal D, which on Ford designs is the first track of the accelerator pedal. The code means the reading with the pedal pressed all the way does not match the calibrated maximum, for instance because the pedal never reaches its stop or the track is worn at the far end. No manufacturer documents P2166 publicly; it applies the logic of the A version P2163 and of the open-stop learning in a Visteon patent to the pedal. A thick floor mat, a bent pedal arm or a worn pedal module are typical causes. The engine computer may then cap the torque request, so the car feels as if it never reaches full power. P2115 covers the rest position of D, P2120-P2124 its circuit, and P2138 the D/E correlation.
c: Floor mat or object keeps the pedal from its stop
Pedal sensor track D worn at full travel
Bent pedal arm or damaged pedal bracket
Corroded pedal connector shifting signal D
s: Engine warning lamp on
No kickdown or no full power with the pedal floored
Possible limp mode

P2167.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor E Maximum Stop Performance
P2167.d: P2167 checks position signal E at maximum travel; on designs that call the pedal tracks D, E and F, E is the second pedal sensor. The code sets when E, with the pedal fully down, reports a value outside the accepted band. Because the second track usually has a different characteristic from the first, checking D and E side by side at full pedal reveals whether only E is off or the pedal itself is blocked. No manufacturer documents P2167 publicly; the logic mirrors P2163, which Ford lists, and the open-stop learning in a Visteon patent. Wear near the far end of the E track, contact corrosion in the pedal connector or an obstructed pedal are likely causes. P2116 covers the rest position of E, P2125-P2129 its circuit, P2138 the D/E check.
c: Pedal sensor track E worn at the full-travel end
Contact corrosion in the pedal connector
Pedal cannot reach its stop (mat, object, bent bracket)
s: Engine warning lamp on
Limited power with the pedal fully pressed
Possible limp mode

P2168.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor F Maximum Stop Performance
P2168.d: P2168 covers position signal F at maximum travel. Letter F only exists where the pedal carries a third sensor track; GM's 2004 engine table, for example, runs a third pedal sensor under the F circuit codes, whereas most current cars make do with two tracks. The code sets when F, with the pedal at its upper stop, reports a value outside the accepted range. No manufacturer documents P2168 publicly; its logic follows P2163, which Ford lists, and the open-stop learning in a Visteon patent. Before ordering a pedal module, confirm that the car has a sensor F and compare all three tracks at full pedal. A worn track, a poor connector contact or a pedal that cannot reach its stop are typical. P2117 tests the rest position of F, P2130-P2133 its circuit.
c: Third pedal track F worn at full travel
Poor contact on the sensor F pins
Pedal held short of its stop
s: Engine warning lamp on
Full power not available

P2169.t: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit/Open
P2169.d: The name points to a solenoid that lets an exhaust pressure regulator vent, but the only public, code-exact use found is on Jaguar Land Rover petrol models, where this code family belongs to the active exhaust valve: a solenoid in the tailpipe section switches a flap between quiet and sport sound. P2169 is the open or general fault of its control line. Land Rover documented P2169-13 (fault type 13 = open circuit) on the 2016 LR4 with the 3.0 supercharged V6 in bulletin SSM72392: the car configuration file enabled a valve that was never fitted, so the module saw an open circuit; reconfiguring cures it. Real cases mean a broken wire, loose plug or burnt-out coil. Exhaust pressure control valves, typical for diesels, have their own range P0475 to P0478. P2170 and P2171 cover the low and high faults.
c: Broken wire or loose connector at the exhaust valve solenoid, often from heat or road dirt
Vehicle configuration enables an active exhaust valve that is not fitted
s: Check engine lamp on
Exhaust sound no longer changes with the drive mode

P216A.t: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P216A.d: Injector group E exists only on engines with at least five cylinders or five separately fed injector groups. GM petrol direct injection uses one group per cylinder, and its 2024 tables (24OBDG07) state it plainly: injector E is cylinder 5. The code covers the high-side feed of that injector. Despite the word open in the title, GM uses it for shorts: the 2008 3.6 LLT sets P216A for the high side of cylinder 5 shorted to ground or battery and leaves open circuits to P0205; the 2024 tables flag less than 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver off or to supply with it on, after two events above 9 V, one trip. GM bulletin PIP4924D lists P216A on 3.0 and 3.6 V6 engines whose injector harness rubbed through against the plenum, valve cover bolts or fuel line. Cylinder 5 misfires.
c: Injector harness rubbed through at the intake plenum, valve cover bolts or fuel line
High-side driver in the engine control module faulty
s: Check engine lamp on, often with a cylinder 5 misfire code
Rough running and reduced power

P216B.t: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P216B.d: P216B reports the feed of injector group E pulled toward ground. In GM petrol direct injection, group E means the injector of cylinder 5, so the code appears on V6 and V8 engines. GM's 2016 3.6 LGX V6 and 2018 6.2 LT4 V8 tables treat it as the injector 5 high-side line being grounded: while the driver is switched on, 25 A or more flows through it. With at least 11 V, 10 failures out of 20 samples at 100 ms set the code, type A, so the MIL lights on the first trip. GM's preliminary information PI0631H for 2012 and 2013 Impala found the engine harness chafing against a transmission edge, which can ground a single circuit such as this one. The injector is shut off and cylinder 5 drops out. P216A is the general fault, P216C the short to voltage.
c: High-side wire of injector 5 chafed through to ground, for example on the transmission
Cylinder 5 injector shorted to its housing
Engine control module output stage faulty
s: Check engine lamp on immediately
Cylinder 5 misfire, noticeable shaking

P216C.t: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit High
P216C.d: P216C is the opposite fault of group E: the feed of the cylinder 5 injector carries voltage when it should not. GM tests it while the high-side driver is switched off; if 1 V or less remains between the signal and the controller supply, the line is treated as shorted to power. Its 2016 3.6 LGX V6 and 2018 6.2 LT4 V8 tables need at least 11 V and count 10 failures out of 20 samples at 100 ms, type A with the MIL on the first trip. Typical sources are a chafed wire touching another powered circuit or an injector winding contacting a live conductor; GM's PI0631H lists this code with dozens of others for the Impala harness that wears on the transmission. Because the injector may stay energised, the module cuts it off and cylinder 5 drops out. P216B is the short to ground.
c: Injector 5 feed chafed against a powered circuit
High-side driver in the engine control module leaking voltage
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the injector connector
s: Check engine lamp on immediately
Cylinder 5 misfire and rough idle

P216D.t: Fuel Injector Group F Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P216D.d: P216D is the general fault of injector group F, which GM petrol direct injection equates with cylinder 6; its 2024 tables (24OBDG07) call it injector F. GM uses this code for shorts on the high side rather than opens: the 2008 3.6 LLT sets it for cylinder 6 shorted to ground or battery, while an open on either side goes to P0206; the 2024 tables count two events of less than 0.5 ohm to ground or supply, above 9 V, one trip. Two bulletins name it. PIP4924D covers 3.0 and 3.6 V6 models such as Enclave, Traverse, CTS and Camaro with chafed injector harnesses. Bulletin 24-NA-106 for the 2023 and 2024 Corvette with the LT6 lists P216D as cylinder 6 alongside P2149, P2155 and P217D, all bank 2, caused by water in a wrong 12-way connector.
c: Injector harness rubbed through on V6 engines
Water in the bank 2 injector harness connector (Corvette LT6)
s: Check engine lamp on, cylinder 6 misfire
With the LT6 several bank 2 codes and fuel pressure faults at once

P216E.t: Fuel Injector Group F Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P216E.d: P216E marks the feed of injector group F, the cylinder 6 injector on GM petrol direct injection, as shorted toward ground. It therefore concerns GM V6 and V8 engines with direct injection. The 2016 3.6 LGX and the 2018 LT4 tables use a current test: with the driver on, 25 A or more through the high side counts as a short, and 10 failures in 20 samples taken every 100 ms at 11 V or more store a type A code with the MIL on the first trip. GM's PI0631H for the 2012 and 2013 Impala includes P216E among the circuits that a harness rubbing on the transmission can damage; GM adds that usually only one circuit is hit. Diagnosis compares the resistance from the injector 6 feed pin to ground with the module unplugged. P216F is the high fault.
c: Cylinder 6 feed wire chafed through to ground
Engine control module output stage faulty
s: Check engine lamp on immediately
Cylinder 6 misfire and loss of power

P216F.t: Fuel Injector Group F Supply Voltage Circuit High
P216F.d: P216F is set when the group F supply, on GM petrol direct injection the high-side line of cylinder 6, shows voltage while the driver is off. GM's criterion in its 2016 (16OBDG07A) and 2018 LT4 tables is 1 V or less between the line and the controller supply, which means the wire is practically at battery level. At 11 V or more, 10 failures out of 20 samples at 100 ms store it as type A, MIL on the first trip. A short to power can keep current flowing through the injector or overload the driver, so the module disables that cylinder. Look for insulation damage where the harness meets brackets or the transmission, as described for the Impala in PI0631H, and for a connector bridged by moisture. Several high codes on different cylinders at once point to the module. P216E is the short to ground.
c: Cylinder 6 feed shorted to another powered wire
Engine control module driver fault, especially with several high codes
s: Check engine lamp on immediately
Cylinder 6 misfire

P2170.t: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P2170.d: P2170 reports the control line of the exhaust pressure regulator vent solenoid pulled toward ground. Jaguar Land Rover uses it for the solenoid of the active exhaust valve; its March 2018 shop foreman call lists P2170-11, meaning the line is grounded, on 2018 Discovery Sport and Evoque with active exhaust. On 2018 and 2019 Evoque, Discovery Sport and E-Pace with the 2.0 Ingenium petrol, MIL and sometimes a restricted performance message appear. JLR suspected high resistance while the valve is switched and asks for a circuit check, a check that the flap moves freely by hand and that the heat shield sits centred on the valve; a cold-soak test in a freezer can reproduce a sticking valve. New PCM software cured unexpected valve operation (JLRTB02020NAS2) and drops the power limitation.
c: PCM software with an overly sensitive fault strategy, fixed by an update
Exhaust flap stiff, often from a misaligned heat shield or cold weather
Control wire chafed through to ground near the exhaust
s: Check engine lamp on
Restricted performance message on some models
Exhaust valve heard clicking at start-up

P2171.t: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit High
P2171.d: P2171 means the module sees too much voltage on the control line of the exhaust pressure regulator vent solenoid, usually because the line touches battery voltage or the solenoid shorts internally. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The closest evidence comes from its sibling: Jaguar Land Rover assigns P2170 to the solenoid of the active exhaust valve on its petrol models, so on those cars P2171 belongs to the same part with the opposite electrical fault. CARB requires output components like this to be checked for circuit faults whenever they can affect emissions or other monitors. Checking means measuring the control wire with the solenoid unplugged for foreign voltage and the coil for a too low resistance. The driver mostly notices a MIL and an exhaust sound that no longer switches.
c: Control wire shorted to a battery-fed circuit
Output stage in the engine control module faulty
s: Check engine lamp on
Exhaust flap stays in one position

P2172.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden High Air Flow Detected
P2172.d: P2172 is set when the engine abruptly takes in far more air than the throttle opening can explain, as if a large leak had appeared behind the throttle plate. The controller compares measured airflow (MAF or MAP based) with the flow its throttle model expects and reacts to a quick jump in the difference. FCA uses the code widely under the name High Airflow/Vacuum Leak Detected (Instantaneous Accumulation) and lists it in many PCM reflash bulletins, among them 18-030-17 for the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia 2.0 turbo; a STAR case on the 2019 Ram 1500 traces it to spread MAP sensor terminals. A Ford patent describes how closed-throttle leak flow is estimated and corrected against measured airflow. A slipped hose or an open PCV line are typical. P2173 is the slow version.
c: Hose, PCV line or brake booster line slipped off or split
Spread or pushed-out terminals at the MAP sensor connector
Engine software with oversensitive detection (reflash available)
s: Check engine lamp
High or hunting idle, hissing noise from the engine bay
Power reduction or limp mode

P2173.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - High Air Flow Detected
P2173.d: P2173 reports an air surplus that builds up gradually: across a longer stretch of driving the engine receives more air than the throttle model predicts, which points to a small leak, a cracked vent hose or a plate that no longer seals. FCA calls it High Airflow/Vacuum Leak Detected (Slow Accumulation). Bulletin 09-010-20 replaces the oil vapour inlet tube on the 2017-2018 Jeep Renegade with the 1.4 MultiAir turbo after leaks there set P2173-00 with jerking or limp mode, while 18-006-23 cures it on the 2019 Renegade 1.3 turbo with new PCM software, listed next to P2110. A Ram STAR case ties it to loose MAP connector terminals. A Ford patent shows how modelled and measured throttle flow are aligned. P2172 is the sudden version, P2175 the opposite deviation.
c: Cracked or loose crankcase ventilation or oil vapour tube
Small leak at an intake gasket or vacuum hose
MAP sensor connector with poor contact
s: Check engine lamp after some driving
Jerking or limp mode
Start/stop system deactivated on some models

P2174.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden Low Air Flow Detected
P2174.d: P2174 means the airflow fell abruptly well below what the current throttle opening should deliver. The controller sees a fast negative gap between measured airflow and its throttle-model estimate, as happens when the intake is suddenly blocked, the plate jams or a hose collapses under vacuum. No manufacturer documents P2174 publicly. FCA's sibling codes P2172/P2173 for excess air show the same model comparison in practice, and a Ford patent explains how estimated and measured throttle flow are reconciled; California's OBD rule requires such air-handling inputs to be monitored. Look for a collapsed or kinked intake duct, snow, leaves or a bag over the air inlet, a sticking throttle or a faulty airflow sensor. Expect a sudden loss of power. P2175 is the slow variant.
c: Air inlet suddenly blocked by snow, leaves or debris
Throttle plate sticking short of the commanded angle
Airflow or manifold pressure sensor reading too low
s: Sudden loss of power
Check engine and throttle warning lamps
Possible limp mode or stalling

P2175.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Low Air Flow Detected
P2175.d: P2175 tracks an air shortfall that develops slowly: over many operating points the engine receives less air than the throttle position predicts, and the learned correction finally exceeds its limit. A clogged air filter, carbon narrowing the throttle bore, a partly blocked intake or an airflow sensor drifting low are the usual reasons. No manufacturer documents P2175 publicly. GM bulletin PIP4578B illustrates the mechanism: with growing carbon deposits in a high-mileage throttle body, the computer learns to open the plate further, and after cleaning an idle relearn is needed. FCA's P2173 is the slow deviation in the other direction, and a Ford patent describes matching modelled with measured throttle flow. Expect sluggish response and unsteady idle. P2174 is the sudden variant.
c: Carbon build-up narrowing the throttle bore
Heavily clogged air filter or intake restriction
Idle or airflow adaptation not reset after throttle cleaning
s: Check engine lamp
Sluggish response and low power
Unsteady or low idle

P2176.t: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P2176.d: P2176 says the closed rest position of throttle A could not be learned. At key-on or after shutdown the controller drives the plate onto its lower stop and stores the sensor values; if they stay outside the window after the permitted attempts, the code is set. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 aborts the learn when the plate misses the closed target by over 1.5 % or sensor 1 lies outside 0.33-0.58 V (sensor 2: 4.42-4.67 V), within one trip; GM's hybrid tables rate it Type A. Honda bulletin 13-042 cures false P2176 on 2013 Accord, Civic and Crosstour with software, GM PIP4573B blames frozen crankcase ventilation below -23 °C, and PIP4578B carbon. A Delphi patent describes repeated learn attempts. P218A is the throttle B code.
c: Carbon on plate and bore preventing a clean closed position
Ice from a frozen crankcase ventilation holding the plate open
Engine software misjudging the sensor signals (update available)
Idle learn not performed after cleaning or module replacement
s: Check engine lamp right after start
High, surging or unstable idle
Reduced engine power after a cold start

P2177.d: P2177 means bank 1's long-term trim has to add too much fuel once the engine is off idle, at part load and while accelerating. Bosch-type systems learn this as a multiplicative factor that scales with airflow, unlike the additive idle part behind P2187. GM's 2005 V6 and 2008 3.6 LLT set it above a factor of 1.23, GM's 2023 and 2024 tables above 1.27, both over two trips. Saab's 9-5 2.0T of 2010 checks at 6.9 to 41.7 g/s, 18 to 80 % load and 1280 to 4000 rpm and needs 4 s in a row or 50 s in total. VW's 2014 CC 2.0 TSI allows up to +28 %. Lean at load points to a weak fuel supply, an air mass sensor reading low or leaks under boost. Bulletins: Mazda CX-7 A/F sensor wiring, Audi RS 3 and TT RS software, Mercedes M254 fuel boiling.
c: Fuel pressure too low under load, for example a weak pump or clogged filter
Air mass sensor reading too low or contaminated
Leak after the air mass sensor, often on the boost side
Calibration error or damaged A/F sensor wiring covered by bulletins
s: Check engine lamp on after two trips
Hesitation or lack of power when accelerating

P2178.d: P2178 is the rich-side limit of the bank 1 load adaptation: above idle the long-term trim has to take away more fuel than allowed. GM's Bosch-based V6 engines of 2005 and 2008 set it below a factor of 0.78, the 2023 and 2024 tables below 0.77, each after two trips. Saab's 9-5 2.0T uses the same window as for the lean code, 6.9 to 41.7 g/s, 18 to 80 % load and 1280 to 4000 rpm, and wants 4 s without break or 50 s in total. VW's 2014 CC 2.0 TSI accepts down to -21 %. A rich error that grows with load usually means an air mass sensor reading too high, excessive fuel pressure or injectors delivering too much. Mercedes saw it on the M254 with fuel boiling in the low-pressure side; Jaguar Land Rover lists P2178 with P0191 on Ingenium petrol engines and cured it with new PCM calibration.
c: Air mass sensor reading too high
Fuel pressure too high or injectors over-delivering
Calibration error fixed by a software update
Fuel vapour from purge or boiling fuel in the low-pressure system
s: Check engine lamp on after two trips
Higher fuel consumption, fuel smell

P2179.d: P2179 is the bank 2 version of P2177 on engines with a front oxygen sensor for each cylinder bank: the load-dependent, multiplicative share of bank 2's long-term correction has reached its lean limit. GM's 2005 2.8 and 3.6 V6 and the 2008 3.6 LLT use a factor above 1.23, GM's 2024 tables above 1.27, both over two trips. VW's 2014 Touareg sets it for the 3.0 TSI hybrid and the 3.6 VR6 when bank 2 adaptation exceeds +30 %. If both banks are lean at load, look at what they share: fuel pressure, the pump, the air mass sensor. If bank 2 alone is affected, the cause lies on that side, such as a restricted injector, an intake leak at that bank's manifold or a front sensor reading lean. No bulletin naming this code was found.
c: Low fuel pressure or air mass sensor fault, usually with P2177 too
Intake leak or front oxygen sensor fault on bank 2
