While the vehicle is above 5 km/h, accelerating by more than 0.1 m/s², the fluid is liquid and over 5 L remain, a level change below 0.3 mm within one second counts as a failed sample; after about 200 s of such samples the module sets the code as Type B, so the MIL comes on after two trips. Jaguar issued SSM73632 for the 2017 to 2018 F-Pace with P21C5-64 and blamed a level sensor calibration, fixed by new engine software. Electrical faults of the same sensor are P203A to P203E, sensor B stuck is P21C6.
c: Level sensor calibration in the engine software (update available, e.g. Jaguar)
Ultrasonic level sensor in the tank unit faulty
Crystal deposits or gas bubbles disturbing the echo
Fluid partly frozen or slush around the sensor
s: Check engine light on after two drives
DEF gauge stays at the same value while fluid is being used
DEF warning messages in the instrument cluster

P21C6.d: P21C6 applies only to DEF tanks with a second level measurement, labelled B. It is stored when that second reading is electrically fine but stays frozen at one value although the module expects it to change. No manufacturer documents P21C6 publicly. GM's 2025 diesel tables show how such a check works for sensor 1 (P21C5): during driving with noticeable acceleration and liquid fluid, a level change of less than 0.3 mm per second over roughly 200 s is judged as stuck. Older GM tanks with three discrete level contacts would equate B with contact 2, but GM covers that one only with circuit codes P21AA and P21AB. CARB demands rationality checks for such inputs. Wiring faults of sensor B are P21A8 to P21AC; an untrustworthy level can trigger DEF warnings.
c: Second level sensing element in the tank unit faulty
Float or contact held by crystals or debris
Calibration of the level evaluation needs a software update
s: Check engine light on
DEF gauge implausible or not moving
DEF warning in the instrument cluster

P21C7.t: Reductant Control Module Power Relay/Relays Control Circuit/Open
P21C7.d: P21C7 flags a break in the control line of the power relay, or group of relays, that supplies the DEF control module and the loads behind it. Ford's 2023 diesel summary evaluates it inside the same continuous heater relay check as P21C2 to P21C4, so on that design the relay also feeds the heating circuits. The code sets within 5 s if the output stage is on but the heater supply reads 0 V, or if the stage is off and voltage is still present, meaning the commanded and the actual relay state disagree. Without supply, DEF heating and possibly dosing stop, and SCR warnings follow. P21C8 and P21C9 are the low and high faults of this line; P20EA and P20EB judge when the relay drops out after the key is turned off.
c: Relay defective or missing from its socket
Open control wire or loose terminal between module and relay
Blown fuse in the relay or module feed
Driver in the controlling module faulty
s: Check engine light on
DEF heating and dosing do not work
SCR warning and countdown to restricted starting or speed

P21C8.t: Reductant Control Module Power Relay/Relays Control Circuit Low
P21C8.d: P21C8 means the control line of the DEF module's power relay, or relays, sits too close to ground. No manufacturer documents P21C8 publicly. Ford's 2023 diesel summary only shows the open-circuit sibling P21C7, judged by comparing the commanded relay state with the voltage on the switched side; a low-side code follows the same idea with a pin voltage below the expected window. What a short to ground does depends on the driver: if the module switches the coil on its ground side, the relay may stay energised and drain the battery after switch-off; if it switches the supply side, the relay never pulls in and the SCR system loses power. The engine module pair P0685/P0686 is the closest analogy. P21C9 is the high-side fault.
c: Control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Moisture in relay socket or module connector
Output stage in the controlling module faulty
s: Check engine light on
DEF system without power or permanently powered
Flat battery after the vehicle has been parked

P21C9.t: Reductant Control Module Power Relay/Relays Control Circuit High
P21C9.d: P21C9 is stored when the control line of the DEF module's power relay, or relays, carries more voltage than the driver state allows, typically because the wire touches a battery feed or the driver can no longer pull it down. No manufacturer documents P21C9 publicly. The closest published logic is Ford's 2023 diesel summary for P21C7, which flags voltage on the switched side while the output stage is off; a high-side code adds the specific diagnosis of a short to supply on the control pin. Depending on the driver layout the relay then either never releases, keeping pump and heaters live with the engine off, or never closes. P0687 is the equivalent code for the engine module relay, and a late drop-out after key-off is reported as P20EB.
c: Control wire shorted to a battery-voltage circuit
Relay contacts welded, switched side stays live
Driver in the controlling module shorted
s: Check engine light on
DEF pump or module audible or active with the engine off
Battery drained overnight

P21CA.t: Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage Circuit
P21CA.d: P21CA is the general code for the supply feed of the DEF control module: the voltage arriving at the module is missing or unusable, without the module assigning it to the low or high case. Volvo and Mack trucks use it, as P21CA00, on the aftertreatment control module that runs the SCR system. Volvo article KC-2040 describes a typical pattern: a battery or ground connection slowly loosens, the module voltage sinks below about 8 V, the module cuts power to the NOx, particulate and DEF sensors, communication codes such as U029D and U02A2 follow, and the truck enters SCR inducement and derate. Volvo stresses that this rarely means a bad module and first checks terminals, batteries, charging and the in-line fuse. P21CB and P21CC are the specific low and high codes.
c: Loose or corroded battery or ground connections of the module
Weak batteries or insufficient charging voltage
Faulty in-line fuse or damaged supply wire
s: Check engine light on
Several sensor communication codes at the same time
SCR inducement with power reduction

P21CB.t: Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage Low
P21CB.d: P21CB says the DEF control module receives too little supply voltage. GM measures it as a difference to system voltage: in the 2018 diesel tables a gap above 3 V between battery voltage and the supply of the SCR power module, seen in 40 of 50 samples taken every 100 ms with the powertrain relay in range and cranking excluded, sets the code; the 2025 tables apply the same 3 V gap to the permanent DEF supply against the gateway voltage for 3 s and classify it as Type B. Ford's 2023 diesel summary uses an absolute limit for its reductant pump controller, below 8.5 V within 5 s. Causes lie between battery and module: resistance in fuses, terminals or ground. P21CA is the umbrella code, P21CC the overvoltage case.
c: Voltage drop at fuse, terminal or ground of the module feed
Weak battery or low charging voltage
Damaged or corroded supply wire to the module
Internal voltage measurement of the module faulty
s: Check engine light on
DEF dosing or heating drops out intermittently
Further undervoltage or communication codes from the SCR system

P21CC.t: Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage High
P21CC.d: P21CC is the overvoltage counterpart of P21CB: the DEF control module sees a supply above what its electronics are designed for. Ford's 2023 diesel summary checks the reductant pump controller in a continuous loop and sets P21CC once its supply exceeds 19 V, deciding within 5 s. On a 12 V vehicle such values usually come from a charging system whose regulator has failed, from a jump start with a 24 V source, or from load dumps on a loose battery terminal; less often the module measures its own input wrongly. To protect pump and heaters the module usually stops working, so dosing pauses. GM's published diesel tables list only the low case. P21CA is the general supply code, and P0563 shows whether the engine module sees the same excess.
c: Jump start or charging with excessive voltage
Loose battery terminal causing voltage spikes
s: Check engine light on
DEF dosing paused, SCR warning
Battery or charging warning, bulbs unusually bright

P21CD.t: Reductant Quality Module Supply Voltage Low
P21CD.d: The DEF quality module measures the urea concentration in the tank and, on many tanks, shares a housing with the level sensor. P21CD reports that its supply voltage is too low. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets the code when the quality sensor supply falls below 10 V or rises above 20 V for 15 s, so on Ford the overvoltage case shares this code. Ford bulletin 19-2315 covers 2017 to 2019 Super Duty trucks with the 6.7 L diesel built up to 1 August 2018: water enters the four-pin connector C4851 at the level and quality module, corroding pins 1 and 4, and P21CD appears together with U02A2. The fix is a new tank harness, sometimes the tank. Without a valid quality reading the SCR system cannot verify the fluid, and P206B to P206D cannot run.
c: Water and corrosion in the quality module connector (Ford C4851)
Damaged tank harness or supply wire
s: Check engine light on
DEF quality or level warning in the instrument cluster
Communication code for the quality module stored as well

P21CE.d: P21CE says the DEF quality module as a unit is not working properly: it is supplied and talking to the controller, but its self-test or the plausibility of its output fails, so the controller cannot rely on the concentration it reports. This differs from P206B to P206D, which grade the measured concentration, and from P21CD, which concerns the module supply. Nissan uses P21CE on the 2019 Titan XD with the Cummins 5.0 L V8, often with P1349 for an erratic tank level, and a DEF system message may appear. Bulletin NTB20-005 has the technician follow the normal diagnosis and, if it leads to part replacement, first drain the tank and refill it with fresh fluid, reinstalling the pump with a new seal. Ford's 2023 diesel summary reports an internal quality sensor error as P206B instead.
c: Contaminated or degraded DEF disturbing the measurement
Crystals or air bubbles on the sensing element
Poor contact at the module connector
s: Check engine light on
DEF system error message in the display
Erratic DEF level reading

P21CF.d: P21CF flags an open drive circuit of the second injector on cylinder 1. Which of the two injectors is B depends on the maker: Ford gives the letter to the port injector and keeps A, coded P0201, for direct injection, whereas Mitsubishi calls its direct injectors B and files open circuits under the low code P21DB. Ford's 2020 to 2025 gasoline summaries test the B circuits continuously above 11 V and need 5 s. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 judges it in a separate injection module: over 200 kOhm on the switched-off low side in 20 of 25 samples, Type A with the MIL in the first trip. Ford bulletin SSM 49996 lists it with P21D0 and P21D1 on 2021 Bronco Sport 1.5 models with a harness damaged at the transmission. With direct injection still working, rough idle or P0301 is the usual sign.
c: Chafed or broken wire in the port injector harness (on the Bronco Sport near the transmission cover)
Open coil in the cylinder 1 port injector
Loose or corroded plug at the injector
Faulty driver stage in the engine module or separate injector module
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 1, often with P0301
Further harness codes stored at the same time

P21D0.d: P21D0 is the open-circuit code for the B injector of cylinder 2. Where that cylinder sits varies: GM's small-block V8 alternates odd and even numbers between the banks, so cylinder 2 opens the right bank, while Ford's V6 and V8 count one bank first and place it next to cylinder 1. Ford defines B as the port injector, the direct injector being A with P0202. Ford runs the check in every engine with combined port and direct injection, from the three-cylinder 1.5 to the 5.0 V8, continuously at 11 V or more for 5 s. GM's LT5 injection module samples the circuit every 100 ms once the powertrain relay supplies at least 11 V. On engines that run on port fuel alone at light load, like Ford's second 3.5 EcoBoost, the cylinder then misfires mostly at idle. Low and high faults are P21DE and P21DF.
c: Port injector of cylinder 2 with an open winding
Broken wire or pushed-back terminal in the injector harness
Output stage in the engine or injection module failed
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 2, mainly at idle and light load
Code P0302 stored as well

P21D1.d: P21D1 concerns the B injector of cylinder 3, which on Ford's 1.5 EcoBoost three-cylinder is the last one in the block. That engine combines port and direct fuel, and Ford names the port injectors B. Bulletin SSM 49996 for the 2021 Bronco Sport describes P21CF, P21D0 and P21D1 appearing together with transmission and other codes, in some cases with a no-crank condition, because the harness was damaged at the transmission cover; when all three B codes show at once, a shared wiring fault is far more likely than three bad injectors. Ford's summary checks the B circuits continuously above 11 V within 5 s. GM's LT5 V8 module flags an open low side once 20 of 25 samples fail. The direct injector of the cylinder is coded P0203.
c: Harness damage affecting several injectors at once (Ford Bronco Sport, transmission cover)
Open coil in the cylinder 3 port injector
s: Check engine light on
Rough running or misfire on cylinder 3
With harness damage also transmission codes or no crank

P21D2.d: P21D2 reports an open in the drive circuit of the B injector on cylinder 4. On four-cylinder engines with dual injection it is the last of the set, for example Ford's 2.0 EcoBoost from 2022 or the 2.3 introduced for the 2024 Mustang, both of which added port injectors to direct injection. Ford tests it like its siblings, continuously with at least 11 V and a 5 s window, and assigns letter A to the direct injector (P0204). Mitsubishi, whose Eclipse Cross uses B for the direct injectors, has no open code here and files such faults under the low code P21E2. On Ford's 3.5 V6 cylinder 4 opens the second bank. In GM's 2019 LT5 module the check samples every 100 ms. Expect a misfire on cylinder 4.
c: Open winding in the cylinder 4 port injector
Wire broken at a bend or clip near the intake manifold
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 4 (P0304)
Uneven idle

P21D3.d: P21D3 can only appear on engines with at least five cylinders and two injectors per cylinder. Documented users are Ford's dual-injection V6 and V8 engines (2.7 and 3.5 EcoBoost of the second generation, 5.0 V8 from 2018) and GM's supercharged LT5 V8. Ford defines B as the port injector; the direct injector of this cylinder is A, coded P0205. GM stores it as Type A once 20 of 25 samples fail. Ford's check is continuous above 11 V with a 5 s window. GM's LT5 injection module rates an open by the impedance seen with the driver off, 200 kOhm or more. On a V6 one bank then runs with a single weak cylinder, which fuel trims and misfire counters can reveal.
c: Open coil in the cylinder 5 port injector
Broken wire in the bank harness of the port injectors
Output stage in the engine or injection module failed
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 5 (P0305)
Fuel trim of one bank shifted

P21D4.d: P21D4 is the last B injector code on a six-cylinder engine. Ford's second-generation 2.7 and 3.5 EcoBoost V6 combine port and direct injection, label the port injectors B and test this circuit together with P21CF to P21D3, continuously above 11 V within 5 s; on these engines cylinder 6 is the rear cylinder of the second bank. On the 3.5 the direct system is shut down at low speed and light load and the engine runs on port fuel alone, so an open cylinder 6 port injector is most noticeable at idle and in gentle driving. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 also covers cylinder 6 in its injection module, Type A after 20 of 25 failed samples. The A-side direct injector code is P0206, the misfire code P0306; P21E6 and P21E7 are the low and high faults.
c: Port injector of cylinder 6 open internally
Damaged wire at the rear of the engine, hard to inspect
Connector not fully latched after earlier work on the intake
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 6 (P0306)
Slightly rough idle

P21D5.d: P21D5 belongs to V8 engines with a second injector per cylinder. Two are documented: Ford's 5.0 V8, which gained direct injection alongside its port injectors in 2018, and GM's 2019 LT5, the supercharged Corvette ZR1 engine with primary direct and supplemental port injection. Ford's summary lists P21CF to P21D6 as port injector circuits, continuous above 11 V, 5 s. On the LT5 the B injectors hang on a separate injection module whose low-side driver flags an open at 200 kOhm or more with the output off, in 20 of 25 samples at 100 ms, Type A with MIL in one trip. Ford counts its V8 one bank after the other, so cylinder 7 lies on the second bank; GM alternates banks, making 7 the last cylinder on the left. The A-side code for cylinder 7 is P0207, the misfire code P0307.
c: Open winding in the cylinder 7 port injector
Broken wire or terminal in the port injector harness of that bank
Separate fuel injection control module faulty (GM LT5)
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 7, on the LT5 mostly under high load
Reduced power at full throttle

P21D6.d: P21D6 is the highest B injector code that any manufacturer documents publicly: both Ford's port injector check (P21CF to P21D6) and GM's LT5 injection module list end here. On the LT5 the port injectors exist to add fuel under boost beyond what the direct system and its mechanical pump can deliver, so an open cylinder 8 injector shows up mainly at high load, where that cylinder can run lean and lose power; GM stores the fault as Type A from 20 failed samples out of 25 with at least 11 V on the powertrain relay. In GM's firing order cylinder 8 follows cylinder 1. On Ford's 5.0 V8 from 2018 it is the rear cylinder of the second bank and the check runs continuously for 5 s. The direct injector counterpart is P0208; P21D5 is cylinder 7.
c: Wire damage at the rear of the engine near the firewall
Output of the engine or separate injection module failed
s: Check engine light on
Misfire or lean running on cylinder 8 under load
Power loss at wide-open throttle

P21D7.d: P21D7 would mark an open drive circuit of the second injector on cylinder 9, which presupposes at least nine cylinders. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the published Ford and GM lists stop at cylinder 8 (P21D6). Engines with that many cylinders and two injection systems do exist, for example the V10 of the Lamborghini Huracán, which pairs direct with multipoint injection, but no source shows how its maker labels the two injectors. CARB requires that electrical output components such as fuel injectors be checked for circuit faults, so the logic would follow the documented siblings: a missing current or excessive impedance when the injector is switched. The direct injector of cylinder 9 would carry P0209 if it is the A side. A misfire on cylinder 9 (P0309) is the likely accompanying symptom.
c: Open coil in the second injector of cylinder 9
Broken wire or terminal in the injector harness
Driver stage in the engine control module failed
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 9 (P0309)

P21D8.d: P21D8 covers the second injector of cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A V10 with two injectors per cylinder is on record in the Lamborghini Huracán, whose engine combines direct and multipoint injection, yet which of them its software would call B is unknown. For comparison, Ford's eight-cylinder logic tests B circuits continuously above 11 V for 5 s, and GM's LT5 module rates an open by 200 kOhm or more with the driver off. CARB obliges makers to monitor injector output circuits whose failure can raise emissions. In practice the fault would show as a misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310) with that cylinder still fed by its other injector; the A-side equivalent would be P020A. Neighbours are P21D7 and P21D9.
c: Second injector of cylinder 10 open internally
Wiring or connector fault at the cylinder 10 injector
Output stage in the engine control module failed
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310)

P21D9.d: P21D9 is reserved for an open circuit of the second injector on cylinder 11 and therefore only makes sense on twelve-cylinder engines with dual injection. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no available source names a twelve-cylinder engine that uses it. Its meaning follows from the series: like P21CF to P21D6, it is an electrical check of the injector drive, not of fuel quantity. CARB requires such circuit monitoring for injectors whose failure affects emissions; Ford's documented B-injector check for up to eight cylinders runs continuously above 11 V and needs 5 s, which shows the typical scale. If it ever appears, check the injector coil resistance and the harness first. The direct counterpart in the A series is P020B, the misfire code for cylinder 11 is P0311.
c: Open coil in the second injector of cylinder 11
Damaged injector harness or loose plug
Faulty driver in the engine control module
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 11 (P0311)

P21DA.d: P21DA closes the circuit/open series of the second injectors with cylinder 12. It requires a twelve-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder; no manufacturer documents this code publicly and no available source names such an engine using it. The fault type is the same as for its documented siblings: the control unit switches the injector and sees no current or an impedance far above normal. GM's LT5 injection module, for example, treats 200 kOhm or more as open and stores a Type A fault after 20 of 25 samples. CARB demands this kind of electrical monitoring for injectors. Directly after this code the series continues with the low and high faults P21DB and P21DC for cylinder 1; the A-side open code for cylinder 12 is P020C, the misfire code P0312.
c: Second injector of cylinder 12 with open coil
Wire or terminal fault in the injector harness
Output stage of the controlling module failed
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 12 (P0312)

P21DB.d: P21DB means the drive circuit of the B injector on cylinder 1 is pulled toward ground. Two makers document it, with opposite meanings of B. Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross uses B for the direct high-pressure injector (its port injector faults are P0261 ff.) and sets P21DB when an interruption or a grounded line persists for 2 s with 10 to 16.5 V battery and over 10 V on the injector driver supply. One faulty cylinder loses both its injectors; with several faults direct injection is switched off and the engine runs on port injection with limited torque. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 tests the low side of its supplemental B injector with the driver off: below 0.5 Ohm to ground in 20 of 25 samples, Type A. Ford covers B faults only with P21CF to P21D6, opens and shorts together. P21DC is the high counterpart, P21CF the open circuit.
c: Injector wire chafed through to ground
Injector winding open or shorted to its housing
Engine or injection control module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 1 misfire or shut-off
Reduced torque when several cylinders are affected (Mitsubishi)

P21DC.d: P21DC is the high-side fault of the cylinder 1 B injector: the line carries voltage where the control unit expects it to be low, typically from a short to supply or between the two injector wires. On GM's 2019 LT5 V8 the FICM injection module looks at the low side of the supplemental injector while its driver is off; less than 0.5 Ohm toward power in 20 of 25 samples sets a Type A fault, so that injector can no longer be switched. Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross, where B is the direct high-pressure injector, needs a short circuit lasting 2 s and begins diagnosis on the negative DI line. Its manual warns against measuring the injector terminals, because the direct injection driver works with high voltage. Fail-safe, symptoms and codes P21DB (low) and P21CF (open) are closely linked.
c: Injector control wire shorted to a supply wire
Both injector wires shorted together in the harness
Driver stage of the control module damaged
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 1 runs weak or misfires
Torque limited if more cylinders fail (Mitsubishi)

P21DD.t: Reductant Heater A Current Too Low
P21DD.d: P21DD means heater A of the DEF system, which Ford and GM both assign to the tank heater (circuit 1), draws less current than expected while switched on, so it is likely open or barely heating. GM's 2025 diesel tables set it when heater 1 current stays below 0.75 A for 40 samples of 0.1 s during a positive command, Type A with MIL after one trip; the 2014 tables flagged an open tank heater when its conductance fell to 0.27 or 0.35 S (by table) or less at 11 V or more, evaluated a single time per drive, Type B. Ford's 2023 diesel summary tests once per heating cycle after a cold start: below 3 A or too little heater power. Ford bulletin 19-2315 links P21DD on 2017 to 2019 Super Duty 6.7 L trucks to water in connector C3613 at the pump and heater unit. P214F is the high-current partner.
c: Water and corrosion in the pump and heater connector (Ford C3613)
Missing heater supply due to relay, fuse or wiring fault
Heater driver in the control module faulty
s: Check engine light on
DEF stays frozen longer in winter, dosing starts late
DEF warning messages after cold starts

P21DE.d: P21DE is the low fault of the cylinder 2 B injector circuit. In Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross manual, B means the direct injector; the code covers both a break and a grounded wire on the two DI lines of cylinder 2, held for 2 s at 10 to 16.5 V, while the port injector of the same cylinder reports P0264. Diagnosis starts with the coil resistance at the intermediate connector, which should be 1.74 to 2.04 Ohm at 20 °C. On GM's 2019 LT5 V8 cylinder 2 is the front cylinder of the right bank; there a low side shorted to ground on the supplemental injector, below 0.5 Ohm, sets a Type A fault from its separate module. GM runs this check while the driver is switched off; a grounded low side can energise the injector without a command. P21DF is the high fault, P21D0 the open.
c: Injector line of cylinder 2 touching ground
Fault at the intermediate connector of the injector harness
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 2 (P0302)
Possible fuel smell or rich running if an injector stays open

P21DF.d: P21DF is set when the cylinder 2 B injector circuit shows a short toward supply. Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross applies it to the direct high-pressure injector and stores it after a 2 s short with the ignition on and the driver supply above 10 V; troubleshooting first inspects the negative DI wire of cylinder 2 up to the engine module and names the injector, the harness and the ECM as possible causes. The fail-safe is graded: with one cylinder affected, both injectors of that cylinder stop; with several, the engine falls back to port injection and torque is limited. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 judges the same title on its supplemental injector by less than 0.5 Ohm toward power on the low side, Type A. The port injector high code of this Mitsubishi cylinder would be P0265; P21DE is the low fault.
c: Negative injector line of cylinder 2 shorted to supply
ECM or injection module driver defective
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 2 switched off or misfiring
Less pulling power with multiple faults

P21E0.d: P21E0 reports a low circuit state on the B injector of cylinder 3. Mitsubishi lists it for the 2022 Eclipse Cross as the direct injector code and does not use the open code P21D1, so an interrupted wire and a short to ground both end up here once they last 2 s. Its procedure measures the injector across its two DI terminals at the intermediate connector, then the harness on both sides of that connector, and only then suspects the ECM. Port injector faults on the same cylinder are P0267 and P0268. On GM's 2019 LT5 V8 cylinder 3 is the second cylinder on the left bank; its supplemental injector fails this test with less than 0.5 Ohm between low side and ground in 20 of 25 samples while the driver is off, Type A in one trip. Expect a cylinder 3 misfire; P21E1 is the high fault.
c: Cylinder 3 injector wire broken or shorted to ground
Injector of cylinder 3 with open or shorted coil
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 3 (P0303)
Rough idle

P21E1.d: P21E1 is the high fault on the cylinder 3 B injector circuit. In Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross that is the direct high-pressure injector, and the module reacts to a short circuit lasting 2 s, checked with 10 to 16.5 V battery voltage. To confirm a repair, the manual points to its OBD drive cycle pattern 1. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 monitors the low side of the supplemental cylinder 3 injector in its separate FICM module and flags under 0.5 Ohm toward power as Type A with the MIL in the first trip. A short to power keeps the low side from ever reaching ground, so the injector cannot open, and switching against the short can strain the driver stage. P21E0 covers the low fault and P0268 the port injector high fault on Mitsubishi; a cylinder 3 misfire often follows.
c: Cylinder 3 injector line shorted to supply voltage
Damaged driver in the control module
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 3 not firing properly
Torque reduction if several injectors fail (Mitsubishi)

P21E2.d: P21E2 is the low fault of the B injector on cylinder 4, the last cylinder of an inline four. It is the final direct injector low code in Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross list, which uses B for the high-pressure injectors and sets it for an open or a short to ground lasting 2 s. If the engine has lost injectors on more than one cylinder, the control unit stops direct injection completely and limits torque, so a P21E2 stored together with other P21DB-series codes points to a shared cause such as the intermediate connector or the driver supply. The cylinder 4 port injector reports P0270 and P0271. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 uses P21E2 for the right-bank cylinder 4 supplemental injector, rating a low side under 0.5 Ohm to ground as Type A. P21E3 is the high fault.
c: Cylinder 4 injector wire open or shorted to ground
Intermediate connector fault affecting several cylinders
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 4 (P0304)
Noticeably less power with several codes (port injection only)

P21E3.d: P21E3 marks a high circuit state on the cylinder 4 B injector, normally a short to a supply line. On Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross, where B is the direct high-pressure injector, the fault must persist 2 s; it closes the manual's list of direct injector circuit codes for the four cylinders. Because the direct injector driver uses boosted voltage, Mitsubishi tells technicians not to probe the terminals with a voltmeter and to work with resistance and continuity checks instead. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 assigns the same code to the supplemental injector of cylinder 4, stored as Type A when the low side sits within 0.5 Ohm of power with the driver off. The low counterpart is P21E2, the port injector high code on Mitsubishi P0271; from P21E4 on, the series continues with cylinder 5.
c: Cylinder 4 injector line shorted to a supply wire
Driver stage in the ECM or injection module damaged
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 4 (P0304)
Engine runs with reduced torque if further cylinders are affected

P21E4.d: P21E4 flags a low state on the circuit of the second (B) injector serving cylinder 5. The only public OBD summary that lists it is GM's for the 2019 Corvette ZR1, whose supercharged LT5 V8 pairs direct injectors with port injectors and drives the supplemental ones from a separate fuel injection control module (FICM). While that driver is off, a low side reading 0.5 Ohm or less toward ground in 20 of 25 samples, taken every 100 ms, is judged a short and becomes a Type A fault with the MIL in the first trip. On GM's V8 numbering cylinder 5 is the third cylinder of the left bank, i.e. bank 1. Because a grounded low side can let the injector flow uncommanded, a rich bank 1 may follow. Ford's dual-injection engines report B shorts on this cylinder only as P21D3.
c: Low-side wire of the cylinder 5 B injector touching ground
Injector winding shorted to its housing
Moisture or corrosion in the injector connector
Driver stage in the injection control module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Rich running or fuel trim pulled back on bank 1
Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 5

P21E5.d: P21E5 means the cylinder 5 B injector circuit is pulled toward supply voltage. GM documents it for the LT5 V8 of the 2019 Corvette ZR1: the FICM looks at the low side of that injector while its driver is off and treats 0.5 Ohm or less toward power as a short. The test needs a running engine and at least 11 V at the powertrain relay, runs continuously and sets a Type A fault. A low side held at supply potential can never be switched to ground, so the injector stays closed. On this engine the port injectors were added mainly to supply extra fuel under boost, so a dead unit tends to show at high load, where cylinder 5 may run lean. The low-side counterpart is P21E4; the A injector of the same cylinder reports P0274 for the same fault type.
c: Low-side wire of the cylinder 5 B injector shorted to a supply wire
Supply and control wire of the injector bridged in the harness
Injector coil shorted across its terminals
Damaged output stage in the injection control module
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 5 lean or hesitant at full load
Part-load driving often feels normal

P21E6.d: P21E6 reports that the B injector circuit of cylinder 6 has found a path to ground. In GM's 2019 tables for the Corvette ZR1 LT5, cylinder 6 is the third position on the right bank, which GM counts as bank 2. The FICM samples the switched-off low side every 100 ms and needs 20 bad readings out of 25, so a solid fault is confirmed within about two and a half seconds; the limit is 0.5 Ohm or less toward ground, Type A. A ground on the low side completes the injector circuit whenever its feed is live, so fuel can enter cylinder 6 without a command. Typical traces are a rich bank 2, fuel-wetted spark plug on that cylinder and fuel trims at their lean limit. P21E7 is the high fault of the same injector, P0276 the low fault of the A injector.
c: Cylinder 6 B injector harness chafed against engine metal
Internal short to ground inside the injector
Injection control module output stuck low
s: Check engine light on
Rich condition on bank 2, possibly fuel smell
Fouled spark plug or misfire on cylinder 6

P21E7.d: P21E7 is stored when the B injector of cylinder 6 shows a short toward power. GM's 2019 Corvette ZR1 with the LT5 V8 is the documented user; there the FICM checks the low side only in the driver-off state, flags 0.5 Ohm or less to power, and needs at least 11 V at the powertrain relay with the engine running. The result is a Type A fault after one trip. With the low side tied to supply, every switching attempt would push current straight into the driver, so the injector on the right-bank cylinder 6 delivers nothing. A useful check is to unplug the injector: if the voltage on the control wire stays, the harness is at fault; if it disappears, the injector coil is suspect. P21E6 is the matching low fault and P0277 the A injector high code.
c: Cylinder 6 B injector control wire in contact with a live wire
Shorted turns in the injector coil
Output stage of the injection control module damaged by the short
s: Check engine light on
Lean condition on bank 2 under load
Cylinder 6 misfire at high load

P21E8.d: P21E8 covers a low, ground-side fault on the cylinder 7 B injector. GM lists it for the 2019 Corvette ZR1, where the LT5 V8 carries a direct and a supplemental injector per cylinder and cylinder 7 is the rearmost cylinder of the left bank (bank 1). The supplemental injectors have their own control module, the FICM, and that module stores the code: below 0.5 Ohm between low side and ground while its driver is off, 20 failures in 25 samples, continuous monitoring, Type A with the MIL in the first trip. Since the limit is close to a dead short, a slowly corroding connector usually shows up as a misfire before it trips this code. Expect rich running on bank 1. The neighbours are P21E9 (high) and, for the A injector, P0279; an open circuit on other makes appears as P21D5.
c: Cylinder 7 B injector wire grounded at the rear of the engine
s: Check engine light on
Rich mixture reported for bank 1
Misfire on cylinder 7

P21E9.d: P21E9 indicates that the low side of the cylinder 7 B injector carries supply voltage. On GM's 2019 Corvette ZR1 LT5, the FICM declares this when it sees 0.5 Ohm or less to power with the driver off, provided the engine runs and the powertrain relay delivers 11 V or more; Type A, one trip. The rear left cylinder then gets only its direct injector. As the extra port fuel on this engine is meant for boosted operation, the effect may be limited to full throttle, where bank 1 can turn lean. CARB demands that output components be checked for circuit faults, yet leaves it to the maker whether shorts to power get their own code; GM separates them, while Ford folds every B-injector short into the open code (here P21D5). Low fault: P21E8; A injector high: P0280.
c: Cylinder 7 B injector control wire shorted to battery voltage
Injector coil with too low resistance
s: Check engine light on
Bank 1 lean at full throttle
Less power at full throttle

P21EA.d: P21EA is the ground-short code for the B injector of cylinder 8 and the last low code in GM's 2019 FICM table for the Corvette ZR1 LT5, because the V8 ends there. Cylinder 8 is the rearmost of the right bank (bank 2). The module flags 0.5 Ohm or less between the switched-off low side and ground in 20 of 25 samples of 100 ms, with the engine running and 11 V or more at the powertrain relay, as a Type A fault. Mitsubishi's four-cylinder dual-injection engine never reaches this code, and Ford treats a B-injector short on cylinder 8 as P21D6. A grounded low side can hold the injector open, so bank 2 runs rich and fuel can wash the cylinder wall. P21EB is the high fault; the A injector low fault is P0282.
c: Cylinder 8 B injector wiring chafed through to ground
Water or corrosion in the cylinder 8 injector plug
s: Check engine light on
Rich running on bank 2
Hard hot start or misfire on cylinder 8

P21EB.d: P21EB is set when the cylinder 8 B injector circuit is shorted toward power. It closes GM's run of B-injector codes for the 2019 Corvette ZR1 LT5: the FICM sees the switched-off low side within 0.5 Ohm of supply in 20 of 25 samples and stores a Type A fault, lighting the MIL in the first trip. The supplemental injector of the right-rear cylinder can then no longer be opened, while the direct injector keeps working, so the car usually drives normally until high boost, where bank 2 may lean out. If several of these high codes appear together, a common feed or a shared connector is more likely than eight bad injectors. P21EA is the matching low fault, P0283 the A injector high fault and P0308 the misfire counter of this cylinder.
c: Cylinder 8 B injector control wire shorted to a feed wire
Shared harness connector shorted when several injectors are affected
s: Check engine light on
Lean bank 2 under boost
Normal behaviour at part load

P21EC.d: P21EC signals a low circuit state, usually a grounded wire or, depending on the maker, also a break, on the B injector of cylinder 9. It can only occur on an engine with at least nine cylinders and two injectors per cylinder. No manufacturer documents it publicly; GM's and Ford's lists stop at cylinder 8. The one such engine on record is Lamborghini's Huracán V10, which combines direct and multi-point injection; which of the two it calls B is not published. Its firing order alternates between cylinders 1 to 5 and 6 to 10, so cylinder 9 belongs to the second bank. CARB requires circuit monitoring of such output components. By analogy with GM's V8, a ground below about 0.5 Ohm on the switched-off low side would count. Open circuit: P21D7; high fault: P21ED.
c: Cylinder 9 B injector wire shorted to ground
Broken wire, if the maker reports opens under the low code
Injector coil shorted to housing or open
s: Check engine light on
Misfire or rough running on cylinder 9
Mixture deviation on the bank of cylinder 9

P21ED.d: P21ED is defined for a B injector circuit on cylinder 9 that reads high, meaning the control side is shorted to supply or, on some designs, the two injector wires touch. No manufacturer publishes thresholds or vehicles for it. Only engines with ten or more cylinders and dual injection could set it; Lamborghini's Huracán V10 with direct plus multi-point injection is the documented example, although its A/B naming is not public. CARB requires that an output component be flagged when it does not respond properly to commands, which is exactly the case here: the injector cannot be switched, so cylinder 9 depends on its other injector alone. Lean running at loads where both injectors work together is the likely result. Low fault: P21EC; A injector high fault: P0286.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 9 B injector shorted to power
Both injector wires bridged in the harness
Driver stage in the control unit faulty
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 9 lean in mixed injection operation
Misfire on cylinder 9 (P0309)

P21EE.d: P21EE is the low-circuit code for the B injector of cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10. In practice that points to a ten-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder, of which only Lamborghini's Huracán is documented: its V10 pairs a direct injector with a port injector at each cylinder and was presented as the first V10 to combine both. Lamborghini does not publish which set is B or whether it uses this code. With cylinders 1 to 5 on one bank and 6 to 10 on the other, cylinder 10 is on the second bank. A short to ground is the core fault; CARB lets a maker report a broken wire under the same code instead of a separate open code. Before replacing parts, read the open code P21D8 and the A injector low code P0288 as well. High fault: P21EF.
c: Damaged or corroded injector connector on cylinder 10
s: Check engine light on
Rough running or misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310)
Fuel trim deviation on the second bank

P21EF.d: P21EF stands for a high reading on the B injector circuit of cylinder 10. No public manufacturer document covers it, so the exact threshold is unknown; the closest documented model is GM's LT5 V8, where a switched-off low side within 0.5 Ohm of supply counts as a short and sets a Type A fault. A vehicle needs ten or more cylinders and two injectors each to use the code, which so far is documented only for Lamborghini's V10 in the Huracán. A short to power keeps the injector from ever opening, and switching against it strains the output stage, which may need replacement if the fault persisted. When P21EF shows up together with other high codes on the same bank, look for a common supply or connector. Low fault: P21EE; A injector high fault: P0289.
c: Cylinder 10 B injector control wire touching a live circuit
Short inside a connector shared by several injectors
Output stage overloaded by the short
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 10 weak or misfiring under load
Lean mixture on the second bank

P21F0.d: P21F0 is reserved for a low state, typically a wire touching ground, in the B injector circuit of cylinder 11. Setting it requires at least eleven cylinders with two injectors each, so in practice a V12 or W12 with combined port and direct injection. No such engine could be confirmed: Lamborghini's V12 family uses multi-point injection only, as do Aston Martin's V12 and Mercedes-AMG's M279. Accordingly no manufacturer documents the code. If a scan tool still shows it, check the cylinder count and whether the maker uses the number for something else. The generic logic follows CARB's circuit monitoring of output components; GM's V8 shows how it is usually judged (short to ground below 0.5 Ohm with the driver off). Open circuit: P21D9; high fault: P21F1.
c: Cylinder 11 B injector wire shorted to ground
Injector with internal short to ground
Code read on an engine without a cylinder 11 B injector (scan tool or maker-specific use)
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 11 (P0311)

P21F1.d: P21F1 describes a cylinder 11 B injector circuit that sits too high, i.e. its switched side is shorted to supply. The code exists in SAE J2012 for completeness of the cylinder series, but no public manufacturer source uses it, and no twelve-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder could be documented. CARB still requires an emission-relevant output to be checked for circuit faults, while allowing makers to combine fault types; a system could therefore report this short under the open code P21D9 instead. Electrically, a short to power keeps the injector from opening and loads the driver each time it switches. GM's LT5 V8 shows typical criteria for the same fault type, 0.5 Ohm or less to power in the driver-off state, Type A. Low fault: P21F0; A injector high: P0292.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 11 B injector shorted to power
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 11 lean or misfiring (P0311)

P21F2.d: P21F2 is the generic code for a low circuit state, usually a grounded control wire, at the B injector of cylinder 12. It would need a twelve-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder, and none could be documented: the V12s from Lamborghini and Aston Martin inject into the ports only. No manufacturer publishes the code in this sense. One maker does use the number differently: McLaren bulletin KA-01931 lists P21F205 and P21F22F on the Artura, a V6 plug-in hybrid, as high-voltage battery faults (safety design current too low/high), repaired by replacing battery parts. On an Artura it is therefore a battery fault, not an injector fault. For a genuine injector fault, CARB's circuit monitoring applies, and GM's V8 criteria (ground short below 0.5 Ohm) are a guide. High fault: P21F3.
c: Cylinder 12 B injector wire shorted to ground
Manufacturer-specific use of the number (McLaren Artura high-voltage battery)
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 12 (P0312)
Hybrid warning instead, if the code is a McLaren battery fault

P21F3.d: P21F3 ends the B injector series of SAE J2012: a high signal on the cylinder 12 circuit, caused by a short to supply on the switched side. The series runs from P21CF to P21DA for opens and from P21DB to P21F3 for low/high pairs; the A injector equivalent here is P0295. Public manufacturer documents only reach cylinder 8 (GM's LT5 V8) or cylinder 4 (Mitsubishi), and no twelve-cylinder with dual injection could be documented, since Lamborghini's and Aston Martin's V12s use port injection alone. Should the code appear, the injector cannot open; cylinder 12 then relies on its other injector, and the driver stage takes the brunt of each switching attempt. GM's criteria for the same fault type serve as a guide: within 0.5 Ohm of power with the driver off. Low fault: P21F2.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 12 B injector shorted to supply
Driver stage damaged by a lasting short
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 12 lean or misfiring (P0312)

P21F4.t: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 1)
P21F4.d: P21F4 reports that the second fuel path on bank 1 needs more added fuel than its adaptation may supply once the engine has left idle, in the part-load range. Engines with port and direct injection learn a correction for each path; Ford calls its direct system A and its port system B. Audi documents the code on the 2017 to 2018 RS 3 and TT RS with the 2.5 TFSI five-cylinder (DAZA), which pairs 250 bar direct with 7 bar manifold injection: bulletin 2059429/1 groups it with P21F5, P21F8, P2177, P2187 and P0087, reports MIL and weak performance, and prescribes ECM software 0005 instead of new parts. Without such a bulletin, suspect restricted port injectors or too little pressure in the low-pressure rail. The system A counterpart is P2177.
c: Outdated engine control software (Audi 2.5 TFSI, bulletin 2059429/1)
Port injectors of bank 1 restricted or delivering too little
Pressure in the low-pressure (port) fuel rail too low
Air mass sensor reading too low
s: Check engine lamp on
Weak performance or hesitation at part load
Often stored together with P2177 or P0087

P21F5.t: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 1)
P21F5.d: P21F5 is the rich limit for the second fuel path of bank 1 in the part-load zone above idle: the learned correction already removes as much fuel as allowed, yet the front sensor still sees surplus fuel. Audi lists the code for the 2.5 TFSI in the 2017 to 2018 RS 3 and TT RS, whose manifold injectors run on a 7 bar rail beside the high-pressure system, and cures it by reprogramming the engine control module (bulletin 2059429/1). In other cases, a port injector that leaks or opens too long, excessive pressure in the low-pressure rail or an air mass reading that is too high are typical. An FCA patent for such engines clears a mode-specific fault only after the monitor passes again in the same injection mode. Expect higher consumption; P2178 is the system A partner.
c: Outdated engine control software (Audi 2.5 TFSI, bulletin 2059429/1)
Port injector on bank 1 leaking or sticking open
Pressure in the low-pressure rail above specification
Air mass sensor reading too high
s: Check engine lamp on
Increased fuel consumption
Fuel smell from the exhaust

P21F6.t: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 2)
P21F6.d: P21F6 is the bank 2 form of P21F4 and only exists on V or flat engines whose cylinder banks each have their own front oxygen sensor and two injection paths. Here the part-load correction of the second path on bank 2 has reached its lean limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford, whose 5.0 Coyote V8 gained direct injection on top of port injection for 2018, reports a lean port-injection fault on bank 2 as P2BF2 instead, without load zones, once long-term trim exceeds 25 % together with short-term trim above 1 % for 2 s. CARB demands a fault once adaptive control has used up its permitted range. If bank 1 stays clean, look at bank 2 alone: a clogged port injector or a wiring fault on that bank's injector harness.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the bank 2 injector harness
Low pressure in the shared port fuel rail (if bank 1 also lean)
s: Check engine lamp on
Slight hesitation at part load

P21F7.t: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 2)
P21F7.d: P21F7 sets when the second fuel path on bank 2 has to remove more fuel above idle than its rich limit permits. It needs an engine with two banks, separate front sensors and dual injection; inline engines such as Audi's 2.5 TFSI only have the bank 1 codes. No manufacturer publishes criteria for P21F7. An FCA patent for port plus direct injection engines explains the idea behind such split codes: a fault seen while only one path is fuelling is assigned to that path, whereas a fault during mixed operation goes to a general code such as P0175. When only this bank is affected, a leaking port injector on bank 2 or a bank 2 front sensor that reads rich is plausible; if both banks are rich, check what they share, such as pressure regulation. P2180 is the system A counterpart.
c: Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich
Low-pressure regulation too high (if bank 1 also rich)
s: Check engine lamp on
Increased fuel consumption

P21F8.t: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
P21F8.d: P21F8 covers the idle zone: the second fuel path of bank 1 needs more extra fuel at idle than its adaptation allows. Airflow at idle is so small that a fixed amount of unmetered air or a slightly sluggish injector shifts the mixture a lot, which is why makers learn idle separately from part load. Audi is the only manufacturer naming the code publicly: bulletin 2059429/1 of May 2020 places it among the trim and fuel pressure codes of the 2017 to 2018 RS 3 and TT RS with the 2.5 TFSI and resolves them with new ECM software, stating that replaced parts are not reimbursed. On other engines, check for intake leaks behind the air mass sensor, a port injector delivering too little, or low pressure in the port fuel rail. P2187 is the matching code for system A.
c: Outdated engine control software (Audi 2.5 TFSI, bulletin 2059429/1)
Unmetered air entering behind the air mass sensor
Port injector on bank 1 delivering too little
Low pressure in the port fuel rail
s: Check engine lamp on
Unsteady or hunting idle

P21F9.t: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
P21F9.d: P21F9 reports that bank 1's second fuel path runs rich at idle even though its correction has already reached the lower limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Audi's 2.5 TFSI bulletin lists only the lean idle code P21F8 and the off-idle pair. Ford's port injection monitor shows how such a check works: it runs in closed loop with purge switched off, coolant at 70 to 110 °C and at least 12 % load, and flags a rich fault when long-term trim passes 25 % in the rich direction while short-term trim agrees, for 2 s (P2BF1, without separate idle cells). Typical causes at idle are a port injector that drips after closing, low-pressure regulation that is too high, or fuel vapour reaching the intake via crankcase ventilation. P2188 is the system A partner.
c: Port injector on bank 1 dripping after closing
Low-pressure fuel regulation holding too much pressure
Fuel vapour entering via crankcase ventilation (fuel-diluted oil)
s: Check engine lamp on
Rough idle and fuel smell
Higher consumption in town traffic

P21FA.t: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
P21FA.d: P21FA is the bank 2 version of the idle lean check for the second fuel path. It applies to engines with two cylinder banks, a front oxygen sensor per bank and dual injection, such as Ford's 5.0 V8, which has combined port and direct injection since 2018. No manufacturer publishes this code; Ford monitors its port system per bank without separate idle cells and would store the fault as P2BF2. At idle the per-bank correction reacts strongly to small absolute errors, so a leak at bank 2's intake runners or gasket, or a partly blocked port injector on that side, are the first suspects while bank 1 stays clean. Drivers may notice an uneven idle or nothing beyond the warning lamp. The system A equivalent is P2189.
c: Intake leak at bank 2 runners or gasket
Partly blocked port injector on bank 2
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading lean
s: Check engine lamp on
Uneven idle

P21FB.t: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
P21FB.d: P21FB means bank 2's second fuel path is rich at idle while its correction already sits at the rich limit. The code requires an engine with a separate front sensor per bank and two injection paths; no maker documents it publicly. CARB section (e)(6.2.2) is the legal basis: once adaptive fuel control has used up the adjustment the manufacturer allows, a fault must be stored. Rich idle on one bank only typically comes from a port injector on that bank that leaks or sticks open, or from a bank 2 front sensor that reports too rich. If both banks show rich idle codes, look at shared items such as low-pressure regulation or fuel entering through crankcase ventilation. Fuel smell and a rough idle are possible; P2190 is the system A sibling.
c: Port injector on bank 2 leaking or sticking open
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich
Low-pressure regulation too high or fuel from crankcase ventilation (if both banks rich)
s: Check engine lamp on
Rough idle and fuel smell

P21FC.t: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P21FC.d: P21FC is the lean check of bank 1's second fuel path in the upper load zone, the third cell next to idle (P21F8) and part load (P21F4). Under high load, delivery capacity matters most: a weak lift pump, a clogged filter or a low-pressure rail that sags at high flow show up here first. On engines combining both paths, the share of each depends on the operating point; Audi's 2.5 TFSI, for example, uses 95 % direct and only 5 % manifold injection at heavy load during warm-up, so the second path's share and its trim learning vary strongly. No manufacturer documents P21FC publicly; Audi's bulletin for that engine covers only the idle and off-idle codes. Hesitation under full load is possible. P2191 is the system A counterpart.
c: Weak in-tank lift pump or clogged fuel filter
Port rail pressure dropping at high flow
Port injectors on bank 1 flowing too little
Charge air leak behind the air mass sensor
s: Check engine lamp on
Hesitation or power loss at full load

P21FD.t: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P21FD.d: P21FD sets when the second fuel path on bank 1 is still rich at higher load although its learned correction has already taken away the permitted maximum. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. The FCA patent for port plus direct injection engines describes three separate monitors, one per injection mode, so a rich error that appears only while the port system fuels alone can be pinned on that system rather than reported as a general P0172. Possible causes are an air mass sensor reading high at large airflow, a regulator in the low-pressure circuit holding too much pressure, or port injectors that over-deliver at long opening times. Higher fuel consumption and sooty tailpipes may follow. P2192 is the system A counterpart, P21FF the bank 2 code.
c: Air mass sensor reading too high at large airflow
Low-pressure regulator holding too much pressure
s: Check engine lamp on
Increased consumption, sooty tailpipe

P21FE.t: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P21FE.d: P21FE is the bank 2 counterpart of P21FC: in the upper load zone the second injection path on bank 2 needs more enrichment than its adaptation may supply. It can only appear on two-bank engines with per-bank sensors and dual injection. No manufacturer documents it publicly, and Ford, which uses port plus direct injection on V engines such as the 5.0 Coyote from 2018, reports port-side lean faults per bank as P2BF2 without load cells. If only bank 2 is lean at high load, suspect restricted port injectors or harness trouble on that bank; if both banks set high-load lean codes, the supply side they share is more likely, for example the lift pump, the filter or the low-pressure sensor. A loss of pull at full throttle may be felt. P2193 belongs to system A.
c: Weak shared supply (lift pump, filter, low-pressure sensor) if both banks lean
Harness or connector fault on bank 2 injectors
s: Check engine lamp on
Loss of pull at full throttle

P21FF.t: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P21FF.d: P21FF closes the series: bank 2's second fuel path is rich in the upper load range although its correction already removes the largest reduction allowed. No manufacturer publishes criteria for it. Under CARB, a fuel system fault must be stored once adaptive control has exhausted the range the maker allows; threshold, load window and the number of trips are left to the manufacturer. On a V engine with dual injection, port injectors on bank 2 that over-deliver at long pulse widths, or excessive pressure in the shared low-pressure rail, would push this bank rich. If only bank 2 is affected, also compare the bank 2 front sensor signal with bank 1. Drivers rarely feel anything, but consumption rises. P2194 is the system A twin, P21FD the bank 1 code.
c: Port injectors on bank 2 over-delivering at long pulse widths
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich
Excessive pressure in the shared low-pressure rail
s: Check engine lamp on
Increased fuel consumption

P2200.d: P2200 is the general electrical fault reported for the front NOx sensor on bank 1, the unit ahead of the SCR catalyst. Such sensors carry their own control unit, which checks the probe wiring and reports the result over CAN. GM's 6.6L Duramax (LML) sets P2200 as a Type A fault once an open-circuit status keeps arriving for more than 0.5 s or 10 s, depending on calibration. Ford's 6.7L and 3.0L diesels use it for shorts or opens on the probe lines and for memory checksum errors inside the sensor controller. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI reacts to an error message or a validity ratio of at least 0.5. P2201 covers plausibility, P2202/P2203 a value out of range, P229E the downstream sensor. Dosing loses its feedback and the MIL comes on.
c: Internal fault in the NOx probe or its attached control unit
Damaged cable between probe and sensor control unit (heat, chafing)
Moisture or corrosion in the sensor connector
Unstable supply or ground at the sensor control unit
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No NOx value in live data from the upstream sensor
SCR or emissions warning, possibly followed by inducement countdown

P2201.d: Here the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 is electrically intact, yet its reading is not believable. Manufacturers test this in different ways. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI compares the reading with modelled engine-out NOx (deviation beyond 60 percent), checks a slow fall from 100 to 60 percent (over 4.5 s) and an offset outside +50/-30 ppm. Ford runs a self-test after shutdown and flags an offset above about 20 ppm low or 40 ppm high. GM's 3.0L Duramax (LZ0) watches internal pump-current stability, Type B over two trips. Ford TSBs 24-2136/24-2148 fix 2020-2023 6.7L trucks with a new sensor and software; Volvo and Mack warn that the code often results from another fault and ask for a conversion test first. P229F is the downstream twin.
c: Aged or poisoned NOx sensing element with offset or slow response
Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor letting in outside air
Fault elsewhere (EGR, fuelling, DEF dosing) that shifts real NOx output
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Often stored together with SCR efficiency codes such as P20EE
Increased AdBlue consumption or SCR warning

P2202.d: P2202 means the raw NOx value sent by the upstream sensor on bank 1 has dropped below the lowest figure a working sensor can report. Since the probe talks over CAN, the check concerns the transmitted value rather than a wire voltage. GM's Duramax diesels (6.6L LML and 3.0L LZ0) use a limit of minus 90 ppm, the LZ0 as Type B after two trips with dew point reached and supply in range; VW's 2014 Touareg TDI uses minus 105 ppm. GM bulletin 24-NA-094 lists P2202 among codes cured by an LZ0 software update on 2024 Silverado and Sierra 1500 pickups. A clearly negative value usually points to a drifting element or an internal sensor error. P2203 is the upper limit; P22A0 the same for sensor 2.
c: NOx sensing element drifted low or internally faulty
Damaged probe lead or connector between element and sensor module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Live data shows a negative NOx value upstream
SCR dosing may switch to a fallback strategy

P2203.d: P2203 flags a raw NOx value from the upstream sensor on bank 1 that lies above anything the engine can actually emit. The limits differ: GM sets 1,500 or 2,500 ppm on the 6.6L Duramax (LML) and 2,500 ppm on the 3.0L LZ0 (Type B, two trips), VW 1,655 ppm on the 2014 Touareg TDI. On 2023 and 2024 Silverado and Sierra 1500 pickups with the LZ0, GM bulletins 23-NA-193 and 24-NA-094 trace the code to software and prescribe an ECM update. Volvo and Mack class P2203 on the inlet sensor as a likely sensor failure and replace that sensor alone. P2202 is the lower limit, P2201 a plausible-looking but wrong reading, P22A1 the downstream counterpart. The MIL is on; SCR control loses a reliable input.
c: Upstream NOx sensor reading high due to internal failure
ECM software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0, bulletins 23-NA-193 and 24-NA-094)
Sensing element contaminated by oil ash or DEF deposits
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Implausibly high upstream NOx value in live data
Possible over-dosing of AdBlue or SCR efficiency codes

P2204.d: P2204 describes an upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 whose signal path works most of the time but keeps dropping out. Smart NOx sensors report the state of their measuring circuit (open wire, short or no error) to the engine computer over CAN; when such fault messages come and go faster than a steady circuit fault would allow, this code fits. No manufacturer publicly documents thresholds for P2204, so the logic is calibration-specific; CARB generally requires continuous detection of circuit-continuity faults on NOx sensors. Look for loose pins, heat-damaged cable near the exhaust and water in the connector. P2200 is the steady circuit fault, P2202/P2203 a value out of range. Expect a MIL and SCR warnings that may disappear and return.
c: Loose or corroded terminals at the NOx sensor connector
Harness near the exhaust damaged by heat or vibration
Intermittent internal fault in the sensor module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on, sometimes going out again
NOx value in live data dropping out briefly
SCR warning that comes and goes

P2205.t: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2205.d: The ceramic element of a NOx sensor only measures once its built-in heater has brought it to several hundred degrees. P2205 reports a break on the heater control side of the upstream sensor on bank 1. GM's 6.6L Duramax (LML) sets it after the sensor has reported an open heater for over 10 s with at least 11 V; on the 3.0L LZ0 it is an open load on the heater control pin. Both are Type A, so the MIL comes on after one trip. Volvo and Mack treat P2205 on the inlet sensor as a probable sensor failure, and GM bulletin 24-NA-094 lists it for an LZ0 software update on 2024 pickups. P2206 and P2207 are shorts low and high, P220E heater power out of range, P22A3 the downstream sensor.
c: Heater element in the NOx probe burnt through
Broken conductor in the lead between probe and sensor module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Upstream NOx sensor never becomes ready
SCR warning on the display

P2206.t: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2206.d: A NOx sensor needs its ceramic element heated to several hundred degrees before it can measure. P2206 means the heater control circuit of the first (upstream) NOx sensor on bank 1 reads low, typically a short to ground or a driver output stuck low. CARB requires diesel OBD to detect heater circuit opens and shorts that conflict with the commanded state. GM's 3.0L Duramax (LZ0) lists it as NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low; Volvo and Mack trucks treat P2206 on the inlet sensor as an internal sensor failure and replace the sensor. P2205 is the general heater circuit fault, P2207 the high side, P2208-P2211 the heater sense circuit. The SCR system loses NOx feedback.
c: Internal heater or control-unit fault in the NOx sensor
Heater wiring chafed to ground near the exhaust
Moisture or corrosion in the sensor connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
SCR or emissions warning on the display
Usually no change in driveability

P2207.t: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2207.d: P2207 is the high-side counterpart of P2206: the heater control circuit of the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 shows a voltage that is too high for the commanded state, typically an open heater element or a short to supply voltage. CARB requires the diesel OBD system to flag such circuit faults that contradict the command. GM lists P2207 as NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High for the 2024 Silverado/Sierra 3.0L diesel (LZ0). Without heating the sensor never becomes ready, so SCR dosing runs without NOx feedback. P2205 is the general heater circuit code, P2206 the low side, and P2208-P2211 concern the heater feedback circuit. P22A5 is the same fault on sensor 2.
c: Heater element inside the NOx sensor burnt open
Open circuit or short to voltage in the heater wiring
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
NOx readiness or SCR efficiency faults may follow

P2208.t: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2208.d: Besides the control line, the NOx sensor heater has a sense or feedback path through which the controller checks how the heater actually responds (current, resistance or element temperature). P2208 marks a general fault in this sense circuit of the upstream sensor on bank 1. GM calls it NOx Sensor Heater Feedback Circuit (3.0L LZ0 diesel); Volvo and Mack class P2208 on the inlet sensor as a sensor failure that requires replacement. CARB demands heater performance monitoring within the supplier's limits. P2209 is the plausibility check of the same feedback, P2210/P2211 low or high values, P2212 dropouts; P2205-P2207 concern the control side. MIL on, driveability normal.
c: Internal fault in the NOx sensor or its control unit
Damaged wiring between sensor element and sensor control unit
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
NOx sensor reports no valid value

P2209.t: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2209.d: P2209 is the performance check of the NOx sensor heater: the feedback is electrically present but shows that the element does not reach or hold operating temperature as expected. VW's 2014 TDI specification books (Passat, Touareg) set it when NOx control has not become active more than 180 s after the dew point was passed. Ford's 2023 diesel OBD summary uses P2209 as NOx signal readiness, judged by the ratio of actual to expected sensor on-time. GM names it Heater Feedback Performance. CARB requires both heater performance and NOx sensor activity monitoring. P2208 is the circuit fault, P2210/P2211 low or high values. MIL after confirmation, no limp mode.
c: Aged NOx sensor element that heats up too slowly
Low supply voltage or poor ground to the sensor
Prolonged cold or wet exhaust delaying dew-point release
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
NOx sensor not ready for long periods after start
Possible follow-up SCR efficiency faults

P220A.t: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P220A.d: A smart NOx sensor draws its own operating power, mostly for the probe heater. P220A means the supply reaching the upstream sensor on bank 1 is outside its window. Ford's 6.7L and 3.0L diesels flag above 16.5 V or below 8.5 V; GM's 3.0L Duramax (LZ0) flags below 9.9 V while the engine runs, Type B after two trips. On the 6.6L LML, GM feeds the sensor from a DC/DC booster in the glow plug module and sets P220A when that module reports its output shorted or overloaded (Type B). VW's 2014 Touareg TDI uses a 1.5 V deviation. Volvo and Mack advise checking supply wiring, fuses and relays rather than the sensor. P220B is the downstream sensor, P220C/P220D bank 2. The sensor stays inactive.
c: Blown fuse, faulty relay or poor ground in the sensor supply
Supply wire chafed, corroded or with high resistance
Supply booster in the glow plug control module (GM 6.6L LML)
Weak battery or charging-system voltage out of range
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Upstream NOx sensor shows no value or no communication
Other NOx sensor codes stored at the same time

P220B.t: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P220B.d: P220B concerns the second NOx sensor on bank 1, the one behind the SCR catalyst whose reading proves how well NOx is being converted. Its operating voltage is outside the allowed band. Ford applies the same 8.5 to 16.5 V window as for the front sensor; GM's 3.0L LZ0 flags under 9.9 V (Type B), and VW's 2014 Touareg TDI compares battery and sensor supply, faulting a gap above 1.5 V. GM's 2018 Equinox and Terrain with the 1.6L diesel (LH7) could log P220B through a software issue; PIP5615A points to bulletin 19-NA-009 and an ECM calibration. Volvo and Mack class it as a supply problem, not a sensor failure. Without this sensor the catalyst efficiency check cannot run. P220A is the front sensor.
c: Fuse, relay or ground fault in the downstream sensor supply
Supply wire to the rear sensor damaged under the vehicle
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Downstream NOx sensor shows no value
SCR efficiency monitor stays incomplete

P220C.t: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P220C.d: P220C is reserved for an engine with a separate exhaust path per cylinder bank, each with its own NOx sensors, and reports that the upstream sensor on bank 2 is not getting a proper supply voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the diesel pickups and trucks examined (Ford, GM, VW, Volvo/Mack) merge both banks into one SCR line and only use the bank 1 codes. By analogy with P220A, a fault would mean the supply sits outside a window like Ford's 8.5 to 16.5 V, or the supplying module reports a short. Smart sensors send their supply status over CAN, so the engine computer learns it from the sensor itself. Check fuse, relay, ground and wiring for that bank. P220D is the downstream sensor on bank 2.
c: Fuse, relay or ground fault in the bank 2 sensor supply
Supply wiring to the bank 2 upstream sensor damaged
System voltage out of range (battery or alternator)
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No NOx value from the bank 2 upstream sensor

P220D.t: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P220D.d: P220D covers the last position in this group: the downstream NOx sensor on bank 2, after that bank's own SCR catalyst, has a supply voltage outside its window. It only exists on engines whose two banks keep separate aftertreatment, which none of the publicly documented diesel applications do; no manufacturer lists the code with thresholds. Ford's bank 1 rear sensor code P220B uses 8.5 to 16.5 V, a useful reference. A dead rear sensor means the efficiency monitor for the bank 2 catalyst cannot finish. CARB requires NOx sensor diagnostics to catch wiring breaks and readings beyond range. P220C is the upstream sensor on the same bank, P220B the rear sensor on bank 1. Check supply fuse, ground and connector first.
c: Supply fuse, relay or ground fault for the bank 2 rear sensor
Corroded connector exposed to road spray behind the catalyst
Internal fault in the supply stage of the sensor module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
SCR efficiency monitor for bank 2 not completed

P220E.t: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P220E.d: P220E says the heater of the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 is not behaving as commanded. Ford's 6.7L and 3.0L diesels bundle several checks under it: an open heater found by the sensor hardware, a short to positive (over 5 V on the heater), a short to ground (0 V), and a duty cycle that differs from the expected one by more than 20 percent. Ford TSBs 24-2136 and 24-2148 cover 2020-2023 F-Super Duty and F-650/F-750 trucks with P220E alongside P2201 and P2209, fixed with a new sensor plus PCM and TCM software. Volvo and Mack state that P220E with failure type 93 usually calls for a new inlet sensor. P2205-P2207 are the plain heater circuit faults, P220F the downstream sensor.
c: Aged heater element in the upstream NOx probe
Heater wiring or ground with high resistance or shorts
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Upstream NOx sensor slow to become ready after start
Often stored with P2201 or P2209

P220F.t: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P220F.d: P220F is the heater check of the rear NOx sensor on bank 1, the one after the SCR catalyst. Ford's diesel summary (it titles the code as a heater sense circuit fault) flags a heater current under 0.4 A, a short to battery or to ground, or a heater duty cycle more than 20 percent away from the expected value. Volvo and Mack use P220F with failure type 93 for their outlet sensor and recommend replacing only that sensor when the code is confirmed. Because the rear sensor confirms catalyst efficiency, a cold sensor delays or blocks the SCR monitor. P220E is the upstream counterpart; P22A3-P22A5 are the plain heater circuit faults of sensor 2. The MIL comes on, while the engine runs normally.
c: Heater of the downstream NOx probe weak or failed
Heater wiring of the rear sensor shorted or with high resistance
Water or salt in the rear sensor connector
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
SCR efficiency monitor not completing

P2210.t: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2210.d: P2210 means the heater feedback signal of the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 sits below its permitted range. Typical electrical causes are a short to ground in the sense line or a failed measuring stage in the sensor electronics. GM lists the code as NOx Sensor Heater Feedback Circuit Low for the 2024 Silverado/Sierra 3.0L diesel (LZ0). CARB requires the OBD system to detect heater circuit faults that conflict with the commanded state. P2211 is the opposite direction, P2208 the general sense-circuit fault, P2209 a plausible but poor heating result, and P2206 a low reading on the control side. The sensor then delivers no usable NOx value; the MIL comes on.
c: Fault in the sensor element or its control unit
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No NOx reading in live data

P2211.t: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2211.d: P2211 flags a heater feedback signal above its permitted range on the upstream NOx sensor of bank 1. An open sense line, a short to supply voltage or an interrupted heater element that the electronics reads as maximum resistance are the usual reasons. GM lists it as NOx Sensor Heater Feedback Circuit High for the 3.0L Duramax (LZ0) in the 2024 Silverado/Sierra. Under CARB rules such circuit faults must be detected regardless of operating conditions. P2210 is the low direction, P2208 the general fault, P2209 the performance check and P2207 the high fault on the control side. The NOx sensor stays unready, SCR control falls back on modelled values, and the MIL lights up.
c: Interrupted heater element in the NOx sensor
Open sense line or short to voltage
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
NOx sensor stays not ready

P2212.t: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2212.d: Besides driving the heater, the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 has a sense path that reports back how the heater actually responds; GM measures heater resistance on a separate HTemp pin. P2212 means this feedback keeps dropping out or jumping instead of failing for good. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P2212; GM's 3.0L LZ0 tables cover only the steady cases (P2208 open, P2210 short to ground, P2211 short to power). CARB requires heater circuit faults that contradict the commanded state to be caught. Typical causes are a loose contact or cracked lead that opens with heat or vibration. P2209 is a plausible but poor heater response; P2205-P2207 concern the control side. The MIL may come and go.
c: Loose or corroded contact in the NOx sensor connector
Cracked conductor in the probe lead that opens with heat or vibration
Intermittent fault in the sensor module's heater measurement
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on, possibly intermittent
Upstream NOx value briefly invalid

P2213.d: P2213 mirrors P2200 for the second cylinder bank: the NOx sensor serving bank 2 ahead of its SCR catalyst reports a general electrical fault. That presumes an engine whose banks feed separate aftertreatment lines. No manufacturer documents P2213 publicly; even V8 diesels such as GM's 6.6L Duramax, Ford's 6.7L and the Cummins 5.0L in Nissan's Titan XD route both banks into a single SCR line and use bank 1 codes only.
