System switches to gasoline or will not enter gas mode

P22EF.t: Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
P22EF.d: The counterpart to P22EE: the drive line of the cylinder 6 gas injector stays near battery voltage even when the output stage should pull it down. For Ford pickups and vans converted with the Altech-Eco/TransEco CNG kit, the installer sheet gives as cause is a short to power; the same MIL rule applies (on for bi-fuel, off for dedicated CNG), and the column for the gas module version 1.4 marks this fault as not detected there, so on such units only the PCM catches it. Ford carries P22EF with MIL in its 2014 code list. Because the valve can no longer be opened, cylinder 6 runs lean or misfires while on gas, and a bi-fuel engine typically falls back to gasoline. Open wires are not reported here but under the Low code.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 6 gas injector touching a battery-voltage feed
Gas harness spliced or pinned incorrectly during the conversion
Moisture bridging supply and control pins in the injector plug
Output stage in the control module no longer switches
s: Check engine light on (bi-fuel versions)
Lean misfire on cylinder 6 in gas mode
Automatic change to gasoline operation

P22F0.t: Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Range/Performance
P22F0.d: Unlike the pure wiring faults P22EE/P22EF, this code is meant for a cylinder 6 gas injector circuit that is electrically intact but behaves implausibly, for example a current rise or switching response that does not fit the command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly: neither the Ford 2014 code list nor the Altech-Eco/TransEco CNG table contains it; both stop at Low and High for this cylinder. The basis is therefore the CARB requirement that output components be checked for proper functional response, not only for circuit continuity. If a manufacturer uses it, a sticking or fouled gas valve and resistance drift of the coil would be the likely triggers, with uneven running on gas.
c: Cylinder 6 gas valve sticking from oil or deposits carried in the gas
Coil resistance drifted out of the expected window
Corroded plug causing a slow current rise
s: Uneven idle or hesitation in gas mode
Cylinder 6 misfire count rising on gas only
Check engine light possible

P22F1.t: Cylinder 7 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22F1.d: A general circuit or open-wire code for the gas injector of cylinder 7, which only exists on V8 and larger engines. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford and the Altech-Eco/TransEco CNG system for Ford V8 and V10 trucks report an open circuit at this valve under the Low code P22F2 instead, which CARB allows: for output circuit faults a maker need not store separate codes for open, shorted low and shorted high. A manufacturer using P22F1 would set it when the driver sees no load current from the cylinder 7 valve, typically a severed wire, unplugged connector or burnt coil. In gas mode the cylinder gets no fuel and misfires; bi-fuel engines normally revert to gasoline.
c: Plug of the cylinder 7 gas injector loose or left off after service
Broken control or supply wire in the gas harness
s: Misfire on cylinder 7 in gas mode
Fallback to gasoline on bi-fuel vehicles
Check engine light on

P22F2.t: Cylinder 7 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Low
P22F2.d: Low voltage on the control line of the cylinder 7 gas injector. The code appears in Ford's 2014 code list with MIL and in the installer table of the Altech-Eco/TransEco CNG kits, which on Ford's V8 (F-150 5.0) and V10 (Super Duty 6.8) engines use the PCM to drive gas valves for all cylinders; cylinders 9 and 10 of the V10 get manufacturer codes there. That table lumps a short to ground and an open line into this code, so P22F1 is not used, and shows MIL on for bi-fuel and off for dedicated CNG. A grounded line can hold the valve open and flood cylinder 7 with gas, an open line starves it. In both cases gas operation is disturbed, while a bi-fuel truck can still run on gasoline.
c: Cylinder 7 injector control wire grounded on the engine or bracket
Open wire or poor pin contact (reported as Low)
s: Check engine light on (bi-fuel versions)
Cylinder 7 misfire or rich running on gas
Gas mode blocked or ended

P22F3.t: Cylinder 7 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
P22F3.d: Here the cylinder 7 gas valve drive line is held high, so the output stage cannot switch the valve on. Ford's 2014 list carries P22F3 with MIL; the Altech-Eco/TransEco table for its Ford V8 and V10 CNG systems names a short to power as cause, applies MIL only to bi-fuel trucks and notes that gas module version 1.4 cannot detect this fault itself. Compared with the Low code the picture is clearer: the valve stays shut and cylinder 7 receives no gas, giving a lean misfire on gas while gasoline operation is unaffected. On a dedicated CNG engine there is no second fuel, so the misfire persists until repaired. Under CARB rules such circuit checks run continuously.
c: Cylinder 7 control wire shorted to a switched or battery feed
Wiring error at the splice between factory and gas harness
Output stage in the control module open
s: Lean misfire on cylinder 7 in gas mode
Check engine light on (bi-fuel versions)
Gas operation dropped in favour of gasoline

P22F4.t: Cylinder 7 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Range/Performance
P22F4.d: Plausibility code for the cylinder 7 gas injector circuit: wiring passes the open/short checks, yet the electrical response of the valve does not match what the driver expects. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. For this cylinder, Ford's 2014 overview and the TransEco installer sheet for Ford V8/V10 engines contain just Low (P22F2) and High (P22F3) for this cylinder. The basis is CARB, which requires output components to be checked for correct functional response where feasible. Possible triggers would be a slow or sticking valve, often from compressor oil carried in natural gas, or a coil whose resistance has drifted. Expect intermittent stumbling on gas and possibly a misfire code for cylinder 7.
c: Cylinder 7 gas valve slow or sticking from oil residue
Injector coil resistance shifted with heat or age
Weak supply voltage to the gas injector bank
s: Intermittent stumble in gas mode
Misfire code for cylinder 7 possible
Check engine light possible

P22F5.t: Cylinder 8 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22F5.d: Open-circuit code for the gas injector of cylinder 8. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In the two manufacturer-side lists found, the Ford overview from 2014 and TransEco's sheet for gas-converted Ford V8 and V10 trucks, cylinder 8 has only P22F6 and P22F7, and the TransEco table explicitly assigns an open line to P22F6. CARB permits this shortcut for output circuits. Where P22F5 is used, the module would flag it when no current flows through the cylinder 8 valve after it is commanded on. Typical findings are a pulled or corroded plug at the rear of the bank, a wire broken by engine movement or an internally open coil. That cylinder then gets no gas, while gasoline mode stays usable on bi-fuel trucks.
c: Cylinder 8 injector plug corroded or disconnected
Wire fatigued at a flex point of the gas harness
Coil of the cylinder 8 gas valve open
s: Cylinder 8 misfire whenever the engine runs on gas
Change to gasoline on bi-fuel vehicles
Check engine light on

P22F6.t: Cylinder 8 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Low
P22F6.d: Cylinder 8 is the last cylinder with a generic gas injector code; beyond it the Altech-Eco/TransEco table for the Ford 6.8 V10 switches to manufacturer codes. P22F6 reports a control line for the cylinder 8 valve that is too low. That table counts a short to ground as well as an open line here, with MIL on bi-fuel vehicles only, and Ford's 2014 code list includes the code with MIL. For the driver the effect depends on the fault: a grounded line may keep gas flowing into cylinder 8 and enrich it, a broken one shuts it off. Either way the misfire shows up only in gas mode, which helps separate it from a gasoline injector fault such as P0208. Repair starts with the plug and harness at that valve.
c: Cylinder 8 control wire grounded through damaged insulation
Open wire or unplugged injector (reported as Low)
s: Check engine light on (bi-fuel versions)
Misfire on cylinder 8 only in gas mode
Gas mode not available

P22F7.t: Cylinder 8 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
P22F7.d: P22F7 means the drive line of the cylinder 8 gas injector cannot be pulled down and stays near supply voltage. Ford lists it with MIL in the 2014 code list; in the conversion data from Altech-Eco/TransEco the cause given is a short to power, keeps the MIL off on dedicated CNG engines and marks the fault as not detectable by gas module version 1.4. Many output stages shut themselves off under such a short to protect the driver, so the valve stays closed and cylinder 8 runs without gas. A bi-fuel truck usually leaves gas mode and drives on gasoline; a dedicated CNG engine keeps misfiring. Check for a pinched wire touching a supply line before replacing the valve or module.
c: Cylinder 8 control wire pinched against a supply line
Supply and control pins swapped in the gas harness
Damaged output stage in the control module
s: Cylinder 8 lean misfire in gas mode
Check engine light on (bi-fuel versions)
Vehicle stays on gasoline

P22F8.t: Cylinder 8 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Range/Performance
P22F8.d: Functional code for the cylinder 8 gas injector circuit, meant for cases where wiring is intact but the valve reacts outside the expected window. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Both at Ford (2014 list) and at Altech-Eco/TransEco the series stops at P22F6/P22F7 for this cylinder. The reference is therefore CARB, which asks for a check of proper functional response of output components and lets the maker define when it runs. Plausible triggers would be a valve that opens late or not fully, contamination from the gas supply, or a heat-soaked coil at the rear of the engine. Unlike the circuit codes, the fault may show only under certain loads, so a confirmation drive is usually needed after repair.
c: Cylinder 8 gas valve opening late or partly due to contamination
Coil degraded by heat at the rear of the engine
Contact resistance in the injector plug
s: Hesitation under load in gas mode
Cylinder 8 misfire code possible
Check engine light possible

P22F9.t: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P22F9.d: P22F9 concerns the NOx sensor ahead of the SCR catalyst on bank 1 and how fast it follows a rise in engine-out NOx. After a load step the control module times the sensor signal and compares it with the curve of its own NOx model. GM's 2025 diesel table starts both timers at 30 ppm and stops them at 220 ppm; a lag beyond 2 s or a relative delay above 10 % fails the check, rated Type B with the MIL after two trips. GM's 2016 diesel table used a 50 to 200 ppm window. GM bulletin 24-NA-058 cures P22F9 on 2024 Silverado and Sierra HD with the 6.6L L5P through new ECM software. P22FA covers the falling direction, P22FC the rear sensor. A sluggish front sensor feeds the urea dosing late information, so NOx output may climb.
c: Front NOx sensor aged or contaminated (oil ash, silicone, cleaning agents), reacting slowly
ECM calibration error, fixed by reprogramming (GM 24-NA-058 for the 2024 L5P)
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor diluting the gas sample
Soot or deposits covering the protective cap of the sensor
s: Check engine light on after two drives
Usually no noticeable change in driving
SCR efficiency codes may follow

P22FA.t: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response High to Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P22FA.d: P22FA mirrors P22F9 for the falling edge: when engine-out NOx drops, mostly as the driver lifts off into overrun, the front NOx sensor on bank 1 takes too long to come down. GM's 2014 Cruze 2.0 diesel fails it when the signal needs more than 1.8 s between 30 and 60 % of its starting value at 1320 rpm or more; the 6.6L LML allows 2.3 s for a drop from 70 to 40 %. GM's 2016 diesel table uses a short timer above 4 s or a long one above 8 s, Type B. Software was often the real cause: GM PI1485 reflashed 2015 Cruze diesels that showed P22FA alongside a dashboard warning about poor DEF quality, and FCA flashed the 3.0L diesel of the 2014 ProMaster (18-018-15) and the 2020 Ram 1500 (18-008-21, 18-002-23). The MIL comes on.
c: Engine software anomaly, cured by reprogramming (GM PI1485, FCA 18-018-15, 18-008-21)
Front NOx sensor aged or contaminated, signal decays slowly
Exhaust leak near the sensor disturbing the measurement
s: Check engine light on
Warning about poor DEF quality on some GM diesels
Usually no change in engine behaviour

P22FB.t: NOx Sensor Performance - Sensing Element (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P22FB.d: P22FB questions whether the measuring element of the front NOx sensor on bank 1 still reads true. GM's 2025 diesel tables hold its filtered value against modelled engine-out NOx and fail it below minus 36 % or above plus 77 % (version A) or outside minus 51 to plus 100 % (version B), as a Type A fault with the MIL in one trip. Volvo and Mack count P22FB-92 among the codes that mean a damaged inlet sensor. Software was behind many cases: Isuzu N-Series, Hino S-Series and Chevrolet Low Cab Forward trucks with the 5.2L 4HK1 got new DEF control unit calibrations, and GM 23-NA-213 pairs P22FB with P0402 on the 2024 6.6L L5P. Mazda's 2018 to 2019 CX-5 SKYACTIV-D stored it for a cancelled self-check (01-004-22). P22FE is the rear sensor.
c: Measuring cell of the front NOx sensor drifted or damaged (Volvo/Mack P22FB-92)
ECM or DEF control unit software, fixed by reprogramming (Isuzu SB22-L-001, GM 23-NA-159, Mazda 01-004-22)
Real engine-out NOx differs from the model, e.g. through an EGR fault (P0402)
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
s: Check engine light on, on GM's 2025 diesels already after one drive
Rough idle or surging if an EGR fault is behind it
Often no other noticeable effect

P22FC.t: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22FC.d: P22FC is reserved for the rear NOx sensor on bank 1, behind the SCR catalyst, when its signal climbs too slowly after NOx at that point increases. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the NHTSA bulletin index has no entry for it. GM, whose tables describe the front-sensor version P22F9, files the dynamic check of the rear sensor under P229F instead (2018 diesel fault bundle for the NOx2 dynamic test). CARB requires every NOx sensor to be watched for a loss of response rate before emissions pass the OBD limits (13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(5.2.2)(A)). Since a working SCR leaves little NOx downstream, a rising edge only shows during a dosing pause or a NOx burst. A slow outlet sensor can hide SCR faults; expect the MIL.
c: Rear NOx sensor aged or contaminated by urea deposits, oil ash or cleaning agents
Exhaust leak between SCR catalyst and sensor
Calibration of the test itself, check for software updates
s: Check engine light on
No change in driving behaviour

P22FD.t: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response High to Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22FD.d: P22FD stands for the falling edge at the rear NOx sensor on bank 1: after a NOx peak downstream of the SCR catalyst, the signal decays more slowly than permitted. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no bulletin in the NHTSA index names it. How such a check works is visible in GM's front-sensor test P22FA, which times the drop between two fractions of the starting value (on the 6.6L LML 2.3 s from 70 to 40 %), while GM itself puts rear-sensor dynamics into P229F. Engines with a third NOx sensor have P23C0 for the same fault at sensor 3. Section (f)(5.2.2)(A) of CARB's OBD II rule names response rate among the sensor faults to detect. A sluggish outlet sensor makes the SCR look weaker than it is and can lead to efficiency codes such as P20EE.
c: Rear NOx sensor aged or coated, signal falls too slowly
Urea crystals around the sensor tip after dosing faults
Exhaust leak close to the outlet sensor
s: Check engine light on
SCR efficiency code may appear as well

P22FE.t: NOx Sensor Performance - Sensing Element (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22FE.d: P22FE tests the measuring cells of the rear NOx sensor on bank 1. On GM diesels the check runs after the engine is switched off: the sensor alters its internal pump currents so that about 1000 ppm of oxygen sits in the second cavity, and the result is compared with a reference written into its memory at the supplier. Blocked cavities lower NOx sensitivity. The 2014 Cruze diesel faults a ratio above 150 % or below 50 %, the 2016 table 200 and 20 %, the 2025 tables 140/68 % and 125/75 %, Type B or, in 2025, Type A. Volvo and Mack treat P22FE-00 as grounds to replace the outlet sensor. Software fixed it in GM PIP5615A (2018 Equinox and Terrain 1.6L diesel), 23-NA-193 (2023 Silverado 1500 3.0L) and the 5.2L DCU calibrations from Isuzu, Hino and GM.
c: Measuring cavities of the rear NOx sensor clogged or cells drifted
ECM or DEF control unit software (GM PIP5615A, 23-NA-193, Isuzu SB22-L-001)
Contamination by urea residue, oil ash or additive cleaners
s: Check engine light on
Code sets after shutdown, so it often appears at the next start
Driving behaviour unchanged

P22FF.t: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P22FF.d: Diesel engines raise exhaust temperature on purpose so the SCR catalyst can reduce NOx; this code reports that the gas entering the SCR stays too cold despite that. Ford describes it for the 6.7L and 3.2L diesels under its monitoring of the exhaust temperature controller: the measured SCR inlet value is compared with the setpoint, and the fault sets when it lags more than 80 °C behind for 300 s (2015 model year, roughly 800-1600 rpm and 50-600 Nm, EGT and EGR inputs fault-free). Deutz EMR5 maps P22FF to SPN 4360 FMI 1, below the normal range. Volvo cut false P22FF settings with a 2021 engine software update (KC-589). P05EB covers cold starts, P214A the opposite case.
c: Long idling or light-load operation keeps exhaust cold
Exhaust leak ahead of the SCR cools the gas or skews the reading
Exhaust temperature sensor reading too low while still in range
Engine software with overly strict monitor (update available on some makes)
s: Check engine light on
Reduced NOx conversion, possible further SCR efficiency codes
Code returns after extended idling

P2300.t: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit Low
P2300.d: P2300 reports that the control line to ignition coil A is pulled towards ground. GM, Saab and VW assign coil A to cylinder 1. GM's 2019 engine tables check the low-side driver while it is switched off: if the line voltage lies in the band of a short below 100 ohms to ground in 50 of 63 samples (taken every 100 ms, battery above 11 V), the Type A fault turns on the MIL in the first trip. An open line belongs to P0351, a short to supply to P2301, the high-voltage side to P2302, misfire on cylinder 1 to P0301. FCA cured P2300-00 on 2023 Alfa Romeo 2.0 turbo engines with new PCM software. Hino uses the same number for the igniter coil of the exhaust burner on its 2011–2014 trucks. Expect rough running; the module may shut the cylinder off.
c: Coil A (cylinder 1) with an internal fault pulling the control input to ground
Control wire of coil A chafed through and touching engine ground
Water or corrosion in the coil A connector
Engine module driver or software fault (FCA 2023: PCM reflash)
s: Check engine light on
Misfire and rough running on cylinder 1
Noticeable loss of power
Fuel to cylinder 1 cut off by the engine module

P2301.t: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit High
P2301.d: P2301 is the mirror image of P2300: the control line of coil A, i.e. cylinder 1, carries voltage at a moment when the engine module is trying to pull it low. Saab's Trionic 8 in the 2003 9-3 sets it if the line stays above 2 V for longer than 1 s while the module grounds it; on that system the code also covers a broken line, the injector of cylinder 1 is shut off, closed-loop mixture control and fuel adaption are frozen, and the fault counts as healed after 2 s without the condition. GM tests the line with its driver switched on and treats less than 100 ohms to supply as a fault. Ford's coil-driver check runs from 200 rpm at 11–16 V and stops fuel to the cylinder for 30 s per detection. Usual finds: a coil with an internal short or a wire rubbing against a 12 V feed.
c: Coil A with an internal short feeding supply voltage onto the control input
Control wire of coil A rubbing against a 12 V line in the harness
Broken control line or loose pin (counts as P2301 on Saab Trionic 8)
Faulty output stage in the engine module
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 1 misfires, engine shakes at idle
Jerking and loss of power under load

P2302.d: P2302 looks at the high-voltage side of coil A – the secondary winding, the boot and the spark plug of cylinder 1 – rather than at the control line covered by P2300 and P2301. Only a few makers use it. FCA does on the 3.6-litre Pentastar V6 in 2015–2016 Dodge Caravan and Chrysler Town & Country vans, where the code name speaks of too little ionization on the secondary side of coil 1: the module judges combustion from the ion current across the plug gap, and a weak signal means the spark did not light the mixture properly. Bulletin 18-069-16 replaced the PCM on vans built between 27 July and 11 September 2015. Ford, by contrast, leaves even primary winding faults of its coil-mounted drivers to the misfire monitor, so they show up as P0301 or P0300. If misfire reaches a catalyst-damaging rate, CARB requires a flashing MIL.
c: Worn or fouled spark plug in cylinder 1, gap too wide
Cracked coil boot letting the spark jump to the cylinder head
Secondary winding of coil A breaking down
Ion-sense evaluation in the PCM (FCA 18-069-16: PCM replaced)
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 1, often together with P0301
Rough idle and hesitation

P2303.t: Ignition Coil B Primary Control Circuit Low
P2303.d: P2303 tells you that the trigger wire of coil B – cylinder 2 in GM, Saab and VW documentation – has found a path to ground. On the Saab 9-5 2.0 turbo (GM LDK engine, 2010) the check runs continuously below 6,000 rpm with 9–18 V on the ignition feed and sets after 4 s of uninterrupted short or 50 s added up; as a Type B code it turns on the MIL only after a second failing trip. Saab's test plan swaps the suspect coil with that of a healthy cylinder: if the code moves, the coil is bad, otherwise the wiring or the ECM. Ford bulletin 24-2406 warns that Bronco 2.3 (2021–2024) and 3.0 EcoBoost (2022–2024) engines may log P2303 against the wrong cylinder and need a PCM update. FCA's 2023 Alfa Romeo 2.0 turbo bulletins also list P2303-00. Open line: P0352.
c: Coil B (cylinder 2) faulty, pulling the control line low
Insulation damage on the coil B control wire touching ground
PCM software assigning the code to the wrong cylinder (Ford Bronco, FCA 2.0 turbo)
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 2
Engine runs on fewer cylinders, less power

P2304.t: Ignition Coil B Primary Control Circuit High
P2304.d: P2304 means the control line of coil B (cylinder 2) is held at too high a voltage – usually a short to a supply line, sometimes an internal coil fault. In VW's 2014 tables a primary control circuit counts as high once its signal voltage exceeds about 5.1–7.0 V, while the low code reacts to a current above 24 mA; the Touareg six-cylinder petrol table (engine code CGRA) names the coils directly by cylinder number. Saab's Trionic 8 (9-3, 2003) sets P2304 when more than 2 V remain on the line while the module grounds it, an open line included. A rarer cause is the module itself: Polaris put six 2026 Slingshots on dealer hold because their ECM triggered P2304, and shipped replacement ECMs. Ford's Bronco bulletin 24-2406 lists P2304 among the codes that a PCM reflash may need to remap to the right cylinder.
c: Coil B control wire shorted to a voltage-carrying line
Internal fault in coil B or its built-in driver
Engine module fault (Polaris Slingshot 2026: ECM replaced)
Interrupted control line on systems that report it here (Saab Trionic 8)
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 2 misfiring
Shaking at idle, weak acceleration

P2305.d: P2305 is about coil B's output side: the secondary winding, the connection to the plug and the spark plug of cylinder 2. Where a maker uses it, the module does not just watch whether the coil was switched, but whether a usable spark happened. Ion sensing is one way: as with Saab's Direct Ignition, a low voltage is applied across the plug outside the firing moment, and the resulting ion current tells the module whether the mixture burned – it can even replace the knock sensor. FCA names P2305 coil 2 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization on 2015–2016 Caravan and Town & Country 3.6 V6 and listed it with P0300–P0306 when misfire, rough running and the MIL called for a new PCM. Unlike P2303/P2304, a clean control line does not rule this code out; spark plugs and boots come first.
c: Spark plug of cylinder 2 worn, oily or with the wrong gap
Coil B boot cracked or damp, spark leaking away
Faulty ion-current evaluation in the PCM
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 2, sometimes only under load
Rough running, raised fuel consumption

P2306.t: Ignition Coil C Primary Control Circuit Low
P2306.d: With P2306 the engine module has seen the output for coil C, cylinder 3 at GM, Saab and VW, dragged down to ground. Ford explains where such a fault can sit on engines whose coils carry their own driver: the coil-driver chip in the PCM watches current and voltage at its output, so the culprit may be the PCM, the harness, the plug-in connection at the coil or the driver electronics inside the coil – but not the windings, which only the misfire monitor sees. The check is continuous, needs 200 rpm, positive torque and 11–16 V and decides within 1 s. VW's 2014 tables set the low code when the line draws more than 24 mA. Saab's Trionic 8 pairs cylinder 3 with cylinder 1 for its combustion signal. FCA lists P2306-00 for 2023 Alfa Romeo Stelvio 2.0 turbo engines fixed by PCM software.
c: Driver electronics inside coil C defective
Coil C control wire grounded through chafing or a pinched harness
Corroded or bent pins at the coil C connector
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 3
Uneven idle, possibly cylinder shut-off

P2307.t: Ignition Coil C Primary Control Circuit High
P2307.d: P2307 sets when the coil C control line, cylinder 3 in most layouts, is shorted to a voltage source. On GM's 3.6-litre LLT V6 (2008) the check is a continuity test against voltage that runs below 6,000 rpm with the battery between 9.99 and 18.1 V and needs 4 s at a stretch or 50 s in total. Do not trust the letter blindly on Ford: special service message 52342 for the 2021–2024 Bronco 2.3 and 3.0 EcoBoost explains that the PCM may file P2307 and its neighbours under the wrong cylinder, while still cutting fuel to the cylinder it has blamed. Ford's advice is a power balance test with its scan tool; the cylinder that drops out without a code of its own is the one to repair. Saab's Trionic 8 treats an open line on cylinder 3 as P2307 as well.
c: Coil C control wire touching a battery-voltage line
Coil C with an internal short to its supply
Code filed against the wrong cylinder by PCM software (Ford Bronco SSM 52342)
Broken control wire on systems reporting opens here (Saab Trionic 8)
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 3 misfires
Power loss, engine runs rough

P2308.d: P2308 points at the high-voltage path of coil C, normally cylinder 3: winding, boot and plug. The code is uncommon. FCA's 3.6 V6 in the 2015–2016 Caravan and Town & Country calls it coil 3 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization. For vans built from late July to mid September 2015 FCA bulletin 18-069-16 swapped the PCM and flashed current software, keeping the battery between 13.2 and 13.5 V on a charger during the flash; the labour allowance is half an hour. Ford and GM tables list no secondary-circuit code for coil C at all; there a weak spark only becomes visible as misfire (P0303). Because each misfire sends unburned fuel into the exhaust, CARB requires the MIL to flash once misfire rates threaten the catalyst. Check plug and boot before suspecting the module.
c: Spark plug of cylinder 3 worn or fouled
Boot of coil C leaking high voltage
FCA vans built 27 July–11 September 2015: PCM fault (bulletin 18-069-16)
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 3 with P0303 stored
Engine runs rough

P2309.t: Ignition Coil D Primary Control Circuit Low
P2309.d: P2309 stands for a grounded control lead to coil D – cylinder 4, which on a four-cylinder engine is the last coil in the row. In 2023 FCA released bulletins 18-022-23 and 18-023-23 for the Alfa Romeo Giulia and Stelvio with the 280 hp 2.0 turbo: P2300-00, P2303-00, P2306-00 and P2309-00 could set together with an EVAP purge code, and the remedy was PCM software rather than parts. On Ford petrol engines of 2020–2023 the coil codes P2300 to P2310 are among the faults that block automatic engine stop-start. On Saab's LDK-engined 9-5 of 2010 the same code needs 4 s of continuous or 50 s of cumulative short and is Type B. When all four low codes appear at once, suspect software or a shared harness section before replacing coils.
c: PCM software fault setting several coil low codes (FCA 2.0 turbo 2023)
Damaged harness section carrying several coil lines
Poor contact or moisture at the coil D connector
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 4
Auto stop-start no longer works (Ford)
Reduced power

P230A.t: Cylinder 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P230A.d: P230A belongs to a second series of cylinder imbalance codes. P219C reports that cylinder 1 runs a mixture unlike the others; P230A goes a step further and says the balancing function has already moved the fuel correction for cylinder 1 to its end stop without evening it out. Such individual trims exist where the control unit can tell cylinders apart, for example on VW's 2014 2.5 litre five-cylinder, which leans out one cylinder at a time and read the resulting roughness. No maker documents P230A publicly; Mercedes describes the same idea on its M260/M264 four-cylinders under its own code P1CEF85 and traced it to leaking valve seats. Cylinder 1 exists on every engine, so any layout can set the code. CARB requires an imbalance monitor on all 2014 and later petrol cars.
c: Injector of cylinder 1 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 1
Valve of cylinder 1 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 1
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 1
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell

P230B.t: Cylinder 2 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P230B.d: P230B singles out cylinder 2: its individual fuel correction has reached the limit during cylinder balancing and the imbalance remains. Audi is one of the few makers whose use of the code is on record. Its 2020 bulletin 2060348 for the A6 2.0 TFSI of the third EA888 generation explains that a calibration mistake filed a cylinder 2 imbalance under P230E, the cylinder 5 code, instead of the correct P230B; the guided fault finding still tested cylinder 2. P219D is the plain imbalance code for this cylinder and P0302 its misfire counter. Typical root causes are an injector delivering too much or too little, a leaking intake port seal or a valve that no longer closes tightly. The MIL is lit and the engine may idle unevenly.
c: Injector of cylinder 2 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 2
Valve of cylinder 2 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Calibration error in the cylinder assignment (Audi 2.0 TFSI Gen 3, bulletin 2060348)
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 2
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell

P230C.t: Cylinder 3 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P230C.d: P230C is the balance-limit code for cylinder 3. On three-cylinder engines this is the last cylinder of the row; on fours and larger engines it sits further inside. The engine control trims the fuel of each cylinder separately to even out mixture differences, and P230C means the trim for cylinder 3 is used up. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly and the NHTSA index lists no bulletin for it. Comparable data come from VW, whose 2014 Beetle table derives the plain imbalance codes from a per-cylinder fuel correction found by deliberate leaning, and from Mercedes, whose M260/M264 bulletins blame a leaking valve seat when cylinder 3 shows irregular mixture formation. A compression and leak-down test on cylinder 3 is worth doing before injectors are swapped.
c: Injector of cylinder 3 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 3
Valve of cylinder 3 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 3
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 3
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell

P230D.t: Cylinder 4 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P230D.d: P230D flags cylinder 4, so the engine needs at least four cylinders. The balancing function has run the individual fuel trim for that cylinder to its limit and the mixture still deviates. Audi's 2020 bulletin for the 2.0 TFSI (third-generation EA888) shows that this four-cylinder reports imbalance through the P230 series, which gives the code a real home, although the bulletin itself only names P230B and P230E. Mercedes lists irregular mixture formation at cylinder 4 among the faults caused by leaking valve seats on its M260/M264 four-cylinders. Swapping injector 4 with a neighbour shows whether the fault follows the injector; if it stays, look at intake sealing and compression. P219F and P0304 are the matching imbalance and misfire codes. The MIL comes on.
c: Injector of cylinder 4 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 4
Valve of cylinder 4 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 4
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 4
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell

P230E.t: Cylinder 5 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P230E.d: P230E concerns cylinder 5 and is genuine only on engines with five or more cylinders, such as inline fives, sixes and V8s. The balancing logic has exhausted the individual fuel trim for cylinder 5. Audi documents a special case: on the 2020 A6 with the four-cylinder 2.0 TFSI (EA888 Gen 3) a calibration error stored a cylinder 2 imbalance as P230E, so on that car the code really points at cylinder 2, while the guided tests still diagnose the right cylinder; the bulletin is informational and offers no fix. A P230E on a four-cylinder is therefore a reason to check the software and the bulletins first. VW's 2014 Golf table already includes the plain cylinder 5 code P21A0 for its five-cylinder; P0305 is the misfire counter for the same cylinder.
c: Injector of cylinder 5 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 5
Valve of cylinder 5 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Calibration error in the cylinder assignment (Audi 2.0 TFSI Gen 3, bulletin 2060348)
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 5
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell

P230F.t: Cylinder 6 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P230F.d: P230F is the balance-limit code for cylinder 6 and can only appear on engines with six or more cylinders, inline sixes, V6 units and larger. On a V6, cylinder 6 shares its bank and front oxygen sensor with two others, so its individual trim has to be estimated from that bank signal or from crankshaft speed. No maker documents P230F publicly, and no NHTSA bulletin mentions it. The series jumps from here to P231A for cylinder 7, because P2310 to P2319 are taken by ignition coil codes. Mercedes, which uses the series on its AMG M177 V8, shows that such a code can also be a software matter. Checks for cylinder 6 follow the usual order: injector delivery, intake sealing at that port, compression and valve tightness. P21A1 and P0306 belong to the same cylinder.
c: Injector of cylinder 6 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 6
Valve of cylinder 6 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 6
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 6
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell

P2310.t: Ignition Coil D Primary Control Circuit High
P2310.d: P2310 sets when the coil D control line, belonging to cylinder 4, carries voltage while the engine module tries to switch it to ground. Saab's Trionic 8 (9-3, 2003) uses a 2 V limit held for over 1 s and evaluates cylinder 4 together with cylinder 2 for its ion-based combustion signal; the injector of the affected cylinder is shut off. GM shows how much the warning behaviour can differ within one maker: its 2019 common engine table rates the coil short-to-power codes as Type A with the MIL in the first trip, whereas the 5.3-litre L84 V8 table of the same year makes P2310 a Type B code that waits for two trips. The Saab 9-5 2.0 turbo also runs it as Type B. VW's 2014 tables flag the high condition above roughly 5.1–7.0 V.
c: Coil D control wire shorted to a voltage source
Interrupted line reported as high on Saab Trionic 8
Defective driver in the engine module
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 4 misfiring, injector shut off
Rough idle

P2311.d: P2311 concerns the secondary side of coil D, usually cylinder 4. The secondary winding has thousands of turns of fine wire and delivers roughly 15–40 kV, so insulation that is merely tired can let the spark escape to ground instead of crossing the plug gap. Few control units watch this side as a circuit of its own; FCA's 3.6 Pentastar V6 does, naming P2311 coil 4 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization in bulletin 18-069-16 (2015–2016 Caravan and Town & Country, fixed by a new PCM). Most other makers leave such faults to misfire detection, so P0304 is the more frequent companion. Because misfire can overheat the catalyst, CARB lets misfire be evaluated in blocks of 200 revolutions and demands a flashing MIL at damaging rates.
c: Aged insulation in coil D or its boot letting the spark leak to ground
Spark plug of cylinder 4 worn, gap grown
Oil in the plug well softening the boot
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 4, worse in damp weather or under load
Flashing MIL at heavy misfire

P2312.t: Ignition Coil E Primary Control Circuit Low
P2312.d: P2312 is the first code of this series that only engines with five or more cylinders can set: it flags the control lead of coil E, i.e. cylinder 5, as shorted to ground. Examples with documented coil E checks are VW's 2.5-litre five-cylinder in the 2014 Passat (low above a current of 24 mA), the Saab 9-5 2.8 V6 (LAU) and GM's LT5 Corvette V8, whose 2019 table rates it Type B after two trips in 50 of 63 samples. On the Saab V6 coil 5 sits on bank 1 together with coils 1 and 3 and shares their supply, so a short there can bring P2300, P2306 and P2312 at once. Ford's 2024 message 52455 for 6.8 and 7.3-litre Super Duty, E-Series and F-650/750 engines lists P2312 among codes that may be filed against the wrong cylinder.
c: Short in the coil supply shared by one bank (Saab LAU: coils 1, 3, 5)
Coil E control wire chafed against ground
Wrong cylinder assignment in PCM software (Ford SSM 52455)
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 5
Rough running, less power

P2313.t: Ignition Coil E Primary Control Circuit High
P2313.d: P2313 reports that the control line of coil E, cylinder 5, is shorted to positive, and therefore needs an engine with at least five cylinders. Saab spells out the conditions for its 9-5 2.8 V6 (LAU, 2011): engine running at 400–5,000 rpm with 10–18 V, a check on every crank revolution once 20 have passed, and a fault after more than 4 s or 30 s in total; P2313 is a Type B code. Saab adds a practical warning: aftermarket gadgets spliced into the coil wiring can set it. Ford bulletin 24-2406 includes P2313 for the 3.0 EcoBoost V6 in 2022–2024 Bronco models built up to 13 February 2024, where a PCM reprogram corrects the cylinder assignment. VW's 2014 Passat five-cylinder tables count anything above about 5.1–7.0 V on the line as high.
c: Coil E internally shorted to supply
Aftermarket device spliced into the coil wiring (Saab LAU note)
Coil E control wire touching a 12 V line
PCM cylinder mapping error (Ford Bronco 3.0, TSB 24-2406)
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 5 misfiring
Hesitation and jerking under load

P2314.d: P2314 reports a fault on the high-voltage side of coil E, which only five-cylinder and larger engines have; it normally fires cylinder 5. The control line may be perfectly sound; what failed is the energy reaching the plug or the combustion that should follow. FCA is the documented user: on the 3.6-litre Pentastar V6 of 2015–2016 Caravan and Town & Country models it is coil 5 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization, one of six such codes that bulletin 18-069-16 tied to a faulty PCM in a short build window. GM, Ford and VW tables cover coil E only on the primary side (P2312, P2313, P0355). Practical checks are the plug of cylinder 5, the boot and a swap test with a neighbouring coil; if the code stays with the cylinder, look at the plug or the module.
c: Spark plug of cylinder 5 worn or fouled
Coil E secondary winding or boot damaged
PCM fault on FCA vans from the 2015 build window
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 5
Rough idle, slight vibration

P2315.t: Ignition Coil F Primary Control Circuit Low
P2315.d: P2315 indicates that the switching line of coil F – cylinder 6 – is grounded, so six-, eight- and larger engines only. Several makers name the cylinder outright: VW's 2014 Touareg table for the six-cylinder petrol engine CGRA speaks of the ignition coil of cylinder 6, Saab's 9-5 2.8 V6 of coil 6, and GM's 2008 3.6 V6 (LLT) lists P2315 with the other five ground-short codes. On the Saab V6, coil 6 shares the bank 2 supply with coils 2 and 4, while coils 1, 3 and 5 hang on bank 1, so a supply fault on one bank shows as a set of odd or even codes. Ford's general summary covers the series up to P2327. Ford's 2024 bulletins on wrongly mapped coil codes list the E and G codes but not P2315.
c: Fault in the bank 2 coil supply affecting coils 2, 4 and 6 (Saab LAU)
Coil F control wire chafed to ground near the rear of the engine
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 6
Engine shakes, power down

P2316.t: Ignition Coil F Primary Control Circuit High
P2316.d: P2316 means the coil F control line, cylinder 6, sits at a voltage it should not have while the module switches it – a short to supply or a fault inside the coil. In VW's 2014 Touareg tables the high threshold is a signal voltage above about 5.1–7.0 V. GM's 2019 table for the supercharged LT5 V8 in the Corvette checks the line with the driver switched on, accepts it only if no path below 100 ohms to supply exists, and rates the result Type B: 50 failed checks in 63 and two trips before the MIL comes on. Saab's 9-5 2.8 V6 sets P2316 after 4 s or 30 s in total within 400–5,000 rpm, and notes that the ignition coil could also log misfire P0300 or P0306. If the fault is intermittent, wiggling the harness while watching the cylinder 6 misfire counter helps find it.
c: Coil F control wire shorted to a supply line
Intermittent contact in the harness near coil F
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 6, P0306 may also be stored
Intermittent stumbling

P2317.d: P2317 concerns the high-voltage side of coil F, which serves cylinder 6 on engines with six or more cylinders. With coil-on-plug designs there is no separate lead any more – Ford notes that individual coils did away with plug wires – so a secondary fault lies in the coil, its boot or the plug. FCA's 3.6 Pentastar V6 is the documented user: P2317, coil 6 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization, is the last of the six ion-sense codes in bulletin 18-069-16 for 2015–2016 Caravan and Town & Country. The principle comes from systems such as Saab's Direct Ignition, which measure ion current across the plug to recognise misfire and knock. Ford, GM and VW record coil F only on the primary side; a weak spark there appears as P0306.
c: Spark plug of cylinder 6 worn or wrongly gapped
Coil F boot cracked or contaminated
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 6
Uneven running, especially under load

P2318.t: Ignition Coil G Primary Control Circuit Low
P2318.d: P2318 says the command wire of coil G, cylinder 7, is touching ground, so it only occurs on V8, V10 or V12 engines. GM's 2019 table for the 5.3-litre L84 truck V8 lists it as a Type B code (50 of 63 failed samples, battery above 11 V, MIL after two trips). Ford covers the series up to P2327 for its V10 and adds that the PCM cuts the injector of the affected cylinder; special service message 52455 (2024) for the 6.8 and 7.3-litre petrol engines in Super Duty, F-53/F-59, E-Series and F-650/750 trucks names P2318 among codes the PCM may pin on the wrong cylinder, so a power balance test should confirm which cylinder really drops out. Open-circuit faults on coil G use P0357, misfire on cylinder 7 is P0307.
c: Water or corrosion at the coil G connector
Control wire of coil G grounded by heat or chafing damage
PCM cylinder mapping error on Ford 6.8/7.3 (SSM 52455)
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 7
V8 runs noticeably rough, power reduced

P2319.t: Ignition Coil G Primary Control Circuit High
P2319.d: P2319 sets when the coil G control line, belonging to cylinder 7 of a V8 or larger engine, shows a short to voltage. GM's 2019 tables include it for the LT5 Corvette V8 as a Type B code with 50 of 63 failed samples. Ford describes the protective reaction in detail: after a coil-driver fault the injector of that cylinder stays off for 30 s; on six- and eight-cylinder engines as many as two cylinders can be shut off at the same time. After the pause the injector is switched on again, and if the fault returns within about 0.1 s fuel is cut once more. Message 52455 from Ford (2024) on 6.8 and 7.3-litre trucks lists P2319 with the other codes that may point to the wrong cylinder; the real culprit is the cylinder that drops out in the power balance test without a code of its own.
c: Coil G control wire shorted to a supply line
Code assigned to the wrong cylinder by PCM software (Ford SSM 52455)
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 7 shut off for periods of 30 s (Ford)
Rough running and loss of power

P231A.t: Cylinder 7 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P231A.d: P231A takes the series to cylinder 7; since P2310 to P2319 are ignition coil codes, the versions for cylinders 7 to 12 start at P231A. Only engines with eight or more cylinders can set it. Mercedes-Benz documents it for the 2022 to 2024 SL with the AMG M177 V8 (LI07.61-P-077382): the ME control unit reports irregular mixture formation at cylinder 7 and disables the injector quantity adjustment. The remedy is new ME software; if the latest version is already installed and P231A00 is still present, Mercedes asks for a technical case to be opened instead of parts being replaced. On other engines the causes match smaller ones: injector 7, an intake leak at that port, valve sealing. P21A2 and P0307 cover the same cylinder; the MIL is on.
c: Injector of cylinder 7 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 7
Valve of cylinder 7 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 7
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell

P231B.t: Cylinder 8 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P231B.d: P231B is the balance-limit code for cylinder 8, the last cylinder of a V8 and an inner one on V10 and V12 engines. The fuel trim for that cylinder has hit its stop while balancing. No maker documents P231B publicly; the nearest evidence is Mercedes' bulletin for the AMG M177 V8 in the SL, which shows that this engine uses the cylinder 7 to 12 range and treats it partly as a software issue, together with CARB's rule that the stored code should locate the cause as precisely as the method allows. On a V8, cylinder 8 shares a bank with three others, so cross-check the bank code P219A or P219B, the misfire counter P0308 and the imbalance code P21A3. Injector 8, the intake gasket and compression come next.

P231C.t: Cylinder 9 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P231C.d: P231C points to cylinder 9 and therefore exists only on ten- and twelve-cylinder engines, a small group of mostly high-performance and heavy-duty petrol units. The balancing logic has pushed the fuel trim for cylinder 9 to its limit. No manufacturer documents the code publicly and the NHTSA index has no bulletin for it. With five or six cylinders per bank, singling out one cylinder through the oxygen sensor is harder than on a four, so such engines lean on crankshaft speed analysis or active tests. Mercedes calls the underlying function injector quantity adjustment for cylinder balancing, and its M177 bulletin shows the series in use on large engines. CARB lets a maker store a bank code when a cylinder cannot be resolved. Check injector 9, intake sealing and compression, and compare P0309 and P21A4.

P231D.t: Cylinder 10 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P231D.d: P231D is the cylinder 10 code of the balance-limit series. On a V10 it marks the last cylinder, on a V12 one of the inner ones; smaller engines cannot set it. The individual fuel correction for cylinder 10 has reached its end stop while the controller tried to equalise the mixture. No maker publishes a description, and no NHTSA bulletin lists it. The principle is the one Mercedes describes on its M260/M264 four-cylinders as injector quantity adjustment for cylinder balancing, with P1CEF85 when it nears the upper limit, there often caused by worn valve seats. CARB's imbalance monitor (13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(6.2.1)(C)) applies to these engines too. Look at injector 10, the intake runner seal and valve tightness, and check whether P0310 or P21A5 are stored as well.

P231E.t: Cylinder 11 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P231E.d: P231E belongs to cylinder 11 and can only come from twelve-cylinder engines, V12 or W12. The per-cylinder fuel trim for cylinder 11 sits at its limit during balancing. There is no public manufacturer description and no NHTSA bulletin. On such engines six cylinders share each bank, so one deviating cylinder shifts the bank sensor signal only slightly; that is one reason CARB accepts a bank or misfire code where a single cylinder cannot be resolved. Mercedes' M177 bulletin for the cylinder 7 code of the same series shows that a software update can be the real remedy. In the workshop, compare the trim values and misfire counts of cylinder 11 (P0311, P21A6) with its neighbours before the injector is replaced.

Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 11
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell

P231F.t: Cylinder 12 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance
P231F.d: P231F closes the balance-limit series at cylinder 12, the last cylinder of a twelve-cylinder engine. It says the balancing routine has used up the fuel trim for that cylinder without matching it to the rest. Public manufacturer documentation is missing, and the NHTSA index contains no bulletin naming it. CARB's monitor requirement, and its demand that the stored code identify the cylinder wherever the method allows, apply to these rare engines as well. A V12 has two independent banks, so compare the matching bank code (P219A or P219B) with the misfire counter P0312 and with P21A7 before fitting parts. Mercedes' bulletins for its four-cylinders, where worn valve seats caused balancing faults, are a reminder that the injector is not always the culprit.
c: Injector of cylinder 12 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 12
Valve of cylinder 12 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 12
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 12
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell

P2320.d: P2320 points at the high-voltage half of coil G, normally the coil on cylinder 7, so only engines with seven or more cylinders can log it. FCA is the maker on record: STAR case S2118000002 from March 2021 for the 2020–2021 Ram 1500 names P2320 as coil 7 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization. Insufficient ionization means the PCM saw too little ion current across the plug gap after the spark, a sign of weak or missing combustion in that cylinder. FCA's first step is a pull-push-pull check of the coil connector to see whether it is fully seated and locked, followed by normal diagnosis if the code returns. A shorted control wire on the same coil instead sets P2318/P2319, an open one P0357. Expect a rough-running engine and often P0307 alongside.
c: Coil 7 connector not fully seated or latched (FCA)
Spark plug of cylinder 7 worn, fouled or with wrong gap
Coil G secondary winding or boot breaking down
Ion-current evaluation in the PCM faulty
s: Check engine light on
Misfire felt on cylinder 7, often with P0307
Engine shakes at idle or under load

P2321.t: Ignition Coil H Primary Control Circuit Low
P2321.d: With P2321 the engine module has seen the switching line of coil H pulled to ground; on a V8 coil H is the final one, on a V10 it is number eight. GM's 2019 tables, which label the code as cylinder 8, carry it for the LT5 Corvette and the L84 5.3-litre truck engine: a Type B fault after 50 bad readings in 63 samples taken every 100 ms with the system above 11 V. For 2014 Silverado and Sierra 1500 trucks with the L83 engine, GM information PIP5147 lists P2321 among the coil codes and advises checking the coil plugs for water or discoloured terminals, swapping the coil to another cylinder and adding dielectric grease. Ford lists it as well in its coil driver group. An open circuit on the same coil is P0358.
c: Water ingress or corrosion in the coil H connector (GM PIP5147)
Coil H control wire chafed through to ground
Coil driver stage in the engine module damaged
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 8 misfires or drops out
Rough idle and weaker pulling power

P2322.t: Ignition Coil H Primary Control Circuit High
P2322.d: P2322 is the counterpart to P2321: the coil H control line, cylinder 8 on most V8 layouts, reads as if it were tied to voltage. GM monitors it the same way on the 2019 LT5 and L84 engines, as a Type B code, flagged once 50 of 63 samples fail. Ford names P2322 in two special service messages from 2024: SSM 52455 for 6.8 and 7.3-litre petrol trucks (Super Duty, F-53/F-59, E-Series, F-650/750) and SSM 52342 for the Bronco. Both say the PCM may file the code under the wrong cylinder and will cut fuel to the cylinder it blames; a power balance test shows the cylinder that genuinely drops out. Ford's OBD summaries add that fuel to the affected cylinder stays off for 30 s and is cut again as soon as the fault reappears. GM PIP5147 also covers P2322 on 2014 trucks.
c: Coil H control wire shorted to a voltage-carrying line
PCM assigns the code to the wrong cylinder (Ford SSM 52455/52342)
Output stage in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
One cylinder repeatedly shut off for about 30 s (Ford)
Noticeable vibration and loss of power

P2323.d: P2323 concerns the spark side of coil H, the coil on cylinder 8. It is the last code of FCA's ion-sensing series: STAR case S2118000002 (2021) for the 2020–2021 Ram 1500 reads it as coil 8 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization, and an older FCA parts review lists it together with the cylinder misfire codes P0301–P0308. On such systems the coil boot doubles as a measuring path, so a loose connector, a cracked boot or a worn plug can weaken the ion signal just as a failing coil can. FCA asks technicians to reseat and lock the connector first and only then to work through the regular test plan. GM and Ford, which use coil H codes on their V8s, document only the primary side (P2321/P2322); misfire on cylinder 8 is P0308.
c: Coil 8 connector loose or not latched (FCA)
Worn or fouled spark plug on cylinder 8
Coil H boot cracked or tracking to the head
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 8 misfire, frequently stored with P0308
Rough running when accelerating

P2324.t: Ignition Coil I Primary Control Circuit Low
P2324.d: Coil I is the ninth coil, so P2324 only appears on ten- or twelve-cylinder petrol engines. The documented user is Ford: its OBD system summaries (2012 and 2020–2023) group P2324 with the other codes for a coil driver shorted to ground, monitored continuously from 200 rpm with the battery between 11 and 16 V, and Ford's 2014 code interpretation list marks it as a MIL code. The candidate engine in Ford's range is the 6.8-litre Modular V10 of the E-Series and heavy trucks, for which Ford also specifies a 40-1 crank wheel. After a driver fault the PCM shuts the injector of that cylinder for 30 s and retries. GM's tables end at coil H, so no GM engine uses this code. Opens on coil I are P0359, misfire on cylinder 9 is P0309.
c: Coil I control wire grounded on the engine or exhaust side
Moisture or corroded pins at the coil I plug
PCM coil driver for cylinder 9 failed
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 9 cuts out, rough running
Reduced towing or climbing power

P2325.t: Ignition Coil I Primary Control Circuit High
P2325.d: P2325 flags a short to voltage on the trigger line of coil I, the ninth ignition output. Ford is again the only maker that lists it publicly: in its OBD summaries P2325 sits among the codes for a coil driver shorted high, and the 2014 Ford code list shows it as a MIL-lighting code checked with the engine running. The PCM judges current and voltage on the driver against open and short limits; when it trips, it stops fuel to that cylinder to protect the catalyst, waits 30 s and turns the injector back on, repeating the cut within about 0.1 s if the fault is still there. That makes the symptom a pulsing loss of one cylinder rather than a steady miss. On a Ford V10 the cause is mostly the coil or a chafed wire; P2324 is the ground-side fault on the same coil.
c: Coil I control wire touching a 12 V feed
PCM driver stage for coil I faulty
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 9 drops out in roughly 30 s cycles
Uneven idle and vibration

P2326.d: P2326 would report a fault in the high-voltage output of coil I – coil, boot or plug of the ninth cylinder. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. FCA's ion-sensing secondary codes, the closest analogue, end at coil 8 (P2323), and Ford, the one maker with public coil I codes, monitors that coil only on its driver side (P2324/P2325). A system that set P2326 would have to judge spark quality on the plug, for example via ion current as in Saab's Direct Ignition, or via secondary voltage. In practice, a weak spark on a ten- or twelve-cylinder engine shows up through misfire detection, which CARB's OBD II rules require for every cylinder: expect P0309. Check plug, boot and coil on cylinder 9 first if the code ever appears.
c: Spark plug on cylinder 9 worn or bridged
Coil I boot perforated or oil-soaked
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 9 (P0309)
Hesitation under heavy load

P2327.t: Ignition Coil J Primary Control Circuit Low
P2327.d: P2327 is the highest ground-side coil code Ford publishes: its driver short-circuit-low list in the 2012 and 2020–2023 OBD summaries runs from P2300 up to P2327 and stops there, matching a ten-coil engine such as the 6.8-litre Modular V10. Coil J serves the tenth cylinder in Ford's count. The check runs continuously between 200 rpm and about 3,200 rpm under positive torque and finishes in under a second; Ford's 2014 code list ranks it as a MIL code. Because Ford also cuts the injector of a faulty-coil cylinder, a grounded coil J line feels like a dead cylinder that keeps coming back. Engines with twelve cylinders could log it too, but no such maker documents it. Related: P0360 for an open circuit, P0310 for misfire on cylinder 10.
c: Coil J (cylinder 10) failed with internal short
Coil J signal wire shorted to ground near the rear of the engine
Corroded or water-filled coil J connector
PCM driver for coil J defective
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 10 missing, engine shakes
Higher fuel consumption from cylinder shut-off cycles

P2328.t: Ignition Coil J Primary Control Circuit High
P2328.d: P2328 marks the end of Ford's published coil list: it is the last entry in the driver short-circuit-high group of the 2012 and 2020–2023 OBD summaries, and the 2014 Ford code list puts it directly before the evaporative codes with a MIL flag. It tells you the switching wire of coil J, the tenth coil, carries voltage where the driver expects a path to ground, or that the coil draws a current outside the allowed window. The protective logic is the same as for the other Ford coils – fuel to that cylinder is withdrawn for 30 s and restored – while internal module faults of the coil driver IC are reported separately as P06D1. Use a wiring diagram for the V10 to find where the coil J lead runs next to battery feeds.
c: Coil J control wire shorted to battery voltage
PCM output for coil J damaged
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 10 switched off at intervals
Engine runs rough and pulls weakly

P2329.d: P2329 covers the secondary side of coil J, meaning the spark path to the plug of cylinder 10. No public manufacturer source assigns it. Ford, whose V10 is the obvious ten-cylinder candidate, lists coil J only on the primary side (P2327/P2328) and in its 2014 code list skips every secondary code of the series. FCA's insufficient-ionization codes stop after coil 8. The code therefore stays a reserved SAE slot; a weakening coil J or a carbon-tracked boot would in practice be caught by the misfire monitor as P0310, which CARB requires to identify the misfiring cylinder. Diagnosis would follow the usual sequence of swapping coil and plug with a neighbouring cylinder and watching whether the fault moves.
c: Carbon tracking on the coil J boot
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310)
Jerking under acceleration, worse when damp

P232A.d: P232A is stored by the engine module when the transmission control module has demanded that the engine be switched off. A TCM sends such a request over the vehicle network when it decides that keeping the engine running could harm the transmission or the vehicle, typically after a serious internal transmission or module fault; the root cause then sits as a separate code in the TCM. No manufacturer document openly available describes P232A with thresholds. GM runs a comparable engine–transmission cross-check under P06AF: the ECM expects a fixed CAN pattern from the TCM and, after 6 of 12 bad counts or 2 s, sets a Type A fault that can stop the engine. CARB treats the TCM as a diagnostic-critical unit. For the driver it means a stalled engine that may not restart until the fault is cleared.
c: Serious transmission fault detected by the TCM (stored there as its own code)
Disturbed CAN communication between TCM and engine module
Low battery voltage or poor supply/ground at the TCM
Mismatched or outdated TCM/engine software after repair or replacement
s: Engine shuts off while driving or at idle
Engine cranks but does not stay running until the fault is cleared
Transmission warning and further codes in the TCM

P232B.t: Cylinder 11 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit
P232B.d: Common-rail diesels keep a small-quantity correction for every injector. During overrun fuel cut the module fires one injector alone with a tiny known amount (GM: about 1.5 mm³), judges the torque from crankshaft acceleration and records how much the energizing time has to change at each rail pressure level. P232B says this learned value for injector A of cylinder 11 has reached its lower bound at one or more pressure levels: the injector needs much less time than nominal, so it delivers too much or opens early. CARB demands a fault once such a feedback correction has used up its range. An eleventh cylinder means a V12 diesel; among passenger cars only Audi's Q7 V12 TDI, sold from 2008 to 2012, had one. No manufacturer documents P232B publicly; P232C is the upper limit.
c: Injector of cylinder 11 leaking or delivering too much at small quantities
Injector correction code not or wrongly entered after replacement
Disturbed crankshaft speed signal falsifying the torque evaluation
s: Check engine light on
Often no noticeable change; possibly louder combustion noise or rough idle
Possibly smoke or higher fuel consumption

P232C.t: Cylinder 11 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Max Limit
P232C.d: P232C is the upper-limit partner of P232B for injector A in cylinder 11. The small-quantity learning has found that this injector needs far more energizing time than the nominal map to produce the expected torque pulse, and the stored correction has hit its maximum at one or more rail pressure levels. Typical reasons are coking, wear or a sticking needle, so the injector delivers too little or opens late. GM's 2018 diesel tables describe the logic for cylinders 1 to 8: every new learned value is checked, the saturation status is kept per pressure level in non-volatile memory, the code sets if any level is saturated, and it is Type B (MIL after two trips). CARB requires such a fault when a fuel feedback has run out of authority. Only twelve-cylinder diesels have a cylinder 11; no maker publishes P232C.
c: Injector of cylinder 11 coked, worn or sticking (delivers too little)
Injector correction code missing or wrong after replacement
Poor fuel quality or contamination promoting deposits
s: MIL on after two trips
Rough idle or uneven running at low load
Possibly harder starting or more smoke

P232D.t: Cylinder 12 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit
P232D.d: The offset-learning codes for injector A of cylinders 1 to 10 sit at P02CC to P02DF; cylinders 11 and 12 were placed separately at P232B to P232E, and P232D is the lower limit for cylinder 12, the last cylinder of a V12. The engine module calibrates each injector in overrun with small test injections and crankshaft-acceleration feedback (GM: test quantity around 1.5 mm³, values kept per rail pressure level). At the lower bound the injector reaches the expected torque with clearly shorter energizing than nominal – a sign of over-delivery or leakage. CARB counts an exhausted fuel feedback correction as a malfunction. Twelve-cylinder diesels are very rare in OBD-regulated vehicles – Audi sold a V12 TDI Q7 from 2008 to 2012 – and no maker documents P232D publicly; the second injector per cylinder has its own B series from P2C52.
c: Injector of cylinder 12 leaking or opening early
Correction code not programmed after fitting a new injector
Crankshaft signal disturbed (tone wheel, sensor, flywheel)
s: Check engine light on
Possibly harsher combustion noise or knocking at idle
Possibly more smoke or consumption

P232E.t: Cylinder 12 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Max Limit
P232E.d: P232E closes the row of injector A offset-learning codes: cylinder 12, upper limit. The learned extra energizing time for this injector has run to the top of its range for at least one rail pressure level, meaning the injector needs much longer activation than its nominal map to give the expected small-quantity torque – it under-delivers or opens late, often from coking or wear. In GM's 2018 diesel logic for the analogous cylinder 1–8 codes, the fault stays stored until no pressure level is saturated any more, and it is Type B. CARB requires detection once the fuel feedback has no adjustment left. Only V12 diesels have a twelfth cylinder, in passenger cars just Audi's Q7 V12 TDI; no manufacturer documents P232E. The lower limit is P232D, cylinder 11 uses P232B/P232C.
c: Injector of cylinder 12 coked or worn (delivers too little)
Injector correction code missing or wrong
High resistance in the injector wiring slowing the opening
s: MIL on after two trips
Uneven idle, possibly harder starting
Often no other noticeable change

P232F.t: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P232F.d: P232F checks the downstream oxygen signal of bank 1 while fuel is cut on deceleration and the exhaust holds almost pure air. GM uses it on the 2023 6.6L L5P Duramax (Silverado HD, Sierra HD): the O2 value of sensor 2, the downstream NOx sensor, is compared with that of sensor 1 once the latter is stable in overrun; if the filtered difference leaves the window of +3.01 % to −3.18 %, a Type B fault is stored. The test runs only while P2297 is being evaluated and after 30 g of air have passed since. CARB requires rear-sensor monitoring and, where a full check is not feasible, at least a rich-to-lean check during fuel shut-off. Ford tests its rear petrol sensor in overrun too but files results under P013A, P013E or P2270. Code lists give P239E the same title. Causes are a drifting sensor, an exhaust leak or wiring faults.
c: Downstream sensor drifting or aged (on GM diesels the O2 signal of NOx sensor 2)
Exhaust leak near the downstream sensor
Damaged sensor wiring or connector (chafing, corrosion)
Leaking injector or upstream sensor fault distorting the overrun comparison
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving behaviour
MIL only after two trips with the fault (GM Type B)

P2330.t: Ignition Coil K Primary Control Circuit Low
P2330.d: P2330 belongs to coil K, the eleventh coil, which only twelve-cylinder petrol engines have – V12 units such as those built by BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Lamborghini or Ferrari, or the VW group's W12. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the published coil lists stop earlier (Ford at J, GM at H). The meaning follows from the analogous lower codes: the module sees the coil K driver line held at ground potential, as GM describes for its cylinder 8 code P2321 (short to ground judged against controller voltage limits, 50 of 63 samples). Under CARB's comprehensive component rules such a circuit fault on an output must be detected. Wiring and connector of that one coil should be checked before the module is suspected; an open circuit would be P0361.
c: Coil K control wire damaged and grounded in the bank harness
Coil K driver in the engine module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 11 not firing
Slight roughness, often hard to feel on a V12

P2331.t: Ignition Coil K Primary Control Circuit High
P2331.d: P2331 is the short-to-power version for coil K, cylinder 11 in a straightforward count. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; neither Ford nor GM, whose OBD descriptions explain the primary codes in detail, build engines with eleven or more coils. By analogy with Ford's description of P2301 to P2328, the driver would register current or voltage above the short-circuit limit while switched, and many systems then disable the injector of that cylinder to keep raw fuel out of the catalysts – Ford does this for 30 s at a time. On a V12 the loss of one cylinder is subtle, so the warning light may be the first sign. Look for a coil lead rubbing against a supply wire and for a coil with internal leakage; the low-side partner is P2330.
c: Coil K signal wire shorted to a supply wire
Engine module output for coil K defective
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 11 may be fuel-cut temporarily
Slightly uneven idle

P2332.d: P2332 reserves a code for trouble between coil K and the plug of cylinder 11. No manufacturer documents it publicly: the only published secondary-circuit series, FCA's ion-current codes, covers coils 1 to 8, and twelve-cylinder makers do not release their code lists. Ion-current sensing, known from Saab's Direct Ignition, would be one way to detect such a fault; another is evaluating the secondary voltage. On a V12 with coil-on-plug, the high-voltage path is short – coil tower, boot, plug – so the usual faults are a perforated boot, oil in the plug well or an eroded plug. Whatever the source, CARB still demands cylinder-specific misfire detection, so P0311 is the more likely code to appear. P2330/P2331 cover the primary wiring of the same coil.
c: Oil in the plug well of cylinder 11
Spark plug of cylinder 11 worn out
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 11 (P0311)
Faint vibration at idle

P2333.t: Ignition Coil L Primary Control Circuit Low
P2333.d: P2333 is the ground-short code for coil L, the twelfth and final coil letter in the SAE scheme. It fits only V12 or W12 engines. There is no public manufacturer documentation for it; the published lists of Ford and GM end at coils J and H. Read by analogy with GM's description of its lower coil codes, the module compares the voltage on the coil L control line with its own limits and records a short to ground after repeated bad samples. CARB's comprehensive component monitoring obliges the system to catch this kind of circuit fault. Note that the letter is a fixed SAE slot, not a cylinder number; a maker may assign coil L to a cylinder other than 12, so the service information of the vehicle decides which coil to inspect. The open-circuit partner is P0362.
c: Coil L control wire chafed to ground
Damaged or corroded coil L connector
Coil L output stage in the engine module failed
s: Check engine light on
One cylinder (usually 12) not firing
Mild roughness at idle

P2334.t: Ignition Coil L Primary Control Circuit High
P2334.d: P2334, the last primary-side coil code of the series, reports a short to voltage on the coil L trigger line. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; it can only occur on engines with twelve individual coils. GM's comparable cylinder 8 code P2322 shows how such a check works: while the driver is on, the line voltage lies outside the controller's acceptable band, counted as a Type B fault with the MIL after two trips. Typical causes are a coil lead rubbing through onto a supply wire or a coil with internal leakage; on many V12 engines reaching the coils means removing covers or intake parts, which raises the labour time. P2333 is the ground-side counterpart.
c: Coil L control wire shorted to a voltage source
Engine module output for coil L defective
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 12 intermittently dead
Hardly noticeable loss of smoothness

P2335.d: P2335 closes the ignition coil block of J2012: a fault on the high-voltage side of coil L, the twelfth coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the reviewed ion-sensing or secondary-monitoring documents reaches past coil 8. Its practical relevance is therefore small; a V12 with a failing coil L, a cracked boot or a worn plug on the last cylinder will normally report it as misfire on cylinder 12 (P0312), and with catalyst-damaging misfire CARB rules require the MIL to flash. If the code does appear, swap coil and plug with another cylinder of the same bank and see whether the fault follows. P2333/P2334 belong to the primary circuit of the same coil; P2332 is the neighbouring coil K secondary code.
s: Check engine light on, possibly flashing with heavy misfire
Misfire on cylinder 12 (P0312)

P2336.t: Cylinder 1 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
P2336.d: The engine module listens to the knock sensors and assigns each vibration burst to the cylinder whose combustion falls into that crank-angle window, so it can retard spark on one cylinder alone. P2336 means the knock intensity attributed to cylinder 1 has exceeded the calibrated threshold. Stellantis lists P2336 to P2339 in bulletin 09-009-26 (May 2026) for the plug-in hybrid 2.0L turbo four (sales code ECX) in the 2024–2025 Jeep Wrangler 4xe and 2023–2025 Grand Cherokee: with the MIL lit and audible knocking, machining debris and casting sand are named as the cause and the whole engine is replaced. GM and Saab file a single knocking cylinder under P0324 instead (more than 8 s). Lasting knock can damage pistons, so the code should be followed up soon.
c: Engine damage from machining debris or casting sand (Stellantis 2.0L PHEV, bulletin 09-009-26)
Carbon deposits or hot spots in cylinder 1
Fuel with too low octane rating
Cylinder 1 running lean (injector delivering too little)
s: Check engine light on
Knocking or pinging noise from the engine
Less power because spark is retarded

P2337.t: Cylinder 2 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
P2337.d: P2337 is the cylinder 2 entry of the per-cylinder knock series P2336–P2347. Using crank position, the engine module splits the knock sensor signal into one window per combustion event and compares the vibration level in cylinder 2's window with its threshold; above it the code is stored and spark for that cylinder is pulled back. The only manufacturer document found that names it is Stellantis bulletin 09-009-26 for the 2.0L turbo plug-in hybrid engine of the Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe: it extends the engine warranty without time or mileage limit, requires a lit MIL plus one of P2336–P2339, blames debris and foundry sand left in the engine and replaces it completely. One cylinder alone over the limit points to a local cause rather than poor fuel, which would hit all cylinders.
c: Internal damage from debris left in the engine (Stellantis 2.0L PHEV)
Deposits on piston or valves of cylinder 2
Wrong or worn spark plug in cylinder 2
Mechanical noise falling into cylinder 2's knock window
s: MIL on
Audible knocking, especially under load
Reduced power or sluggish acceleration

P2338.t: Cylinder 3 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
P2338.d: P2338 sets when the knock signal assigned to cylinder 3 rises above its threshold. Because one or two knock sensors serve several cylinders, the module relies on the crank-angle window to tell which cylinder knocked; a code for just one cylinder therefore suggests something local: carbon build-up, a hot spot, a lean-running injector, a wrong spark plug, or mechanical noise that happens to fall into that window. Low-octane fuel tends to raise knock on every cylinder. Stellantis names P2338 with P2336, P2337 and P2339 in bulletin 09-009-26, which covers the 2.0L PHEV engine in Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe models from Jeep, where foundry sand and machining chips are the cause and the engine is exchanged. Persistent knock can hole or melt pistons, so it should not be ignored.
c: Carbon build-up or a hot spot in cylinder 3
Injector of cylinder 3 delivering too little (lean, hot combustion)
Engine damage from casting sand or chips (Stellantis 2.0L PHEV)
Knock sensor loose or wrongly torqued, picking up noise
s: Check engine light on
Pinging under acceleration
Noticeably less power

P2339.t: Cylinder 4 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
P2339.d: P2339 covers cylinder 4.
