The controller keeps track of how hot element A gets when it slips during launches and shifts and sets the code once that value passes its limit; the code is a warning of thermal overload rather than proof of a broken part. Which physical clutch carries letter A depends on the gearbox. No maker documents P270A publicly with thresholds. A comparable protection exists under maker codes: Audi's S tronic in the 2010-2012 S4/S5 stores P174000 (clutch temperature monitoring) and P17D800 when it limits torque because the clutch is too hot. Expect reduced power or a warning message; letting the car cool and driving gently often clears the condition, while repeated events point to slip or a cooling fault.
c: Repeated launches, creeping or towing that load element A with long slip phases
Worn element A slipping because of low apply pressure or worn linings
Low or aged transmission fluid reducing cooling of the clutch
Restricted fluid cooler or faulty cooling valve
s: Reduced engine power or gearbox warning message
Harsh or slipping engagement of the affected gear
Burnt smell of transmission fluid after heavy use

P270B.t: Transmission Friction Element B Temperature Too High
P270B.d: P270B concerns the shift element lettered B. A multi-plate clutch has no sensor of its own, so the controller usually derives its heat from the energy turned into warmth while the plates slip and from the oil temperature, then compares the result with a limit. When B exceeds it, P270B is logged and the transmission software protects the element, typically by cutting engine torque or changing shift timing. No maker publishes P270B with thresholds, and the letter mapping differs from gearbox to gearbox. Volkswagen's 0AM dual-clutch training material shows the general idea: once the mechatronic unit reaches 139 °C, engine torque is reduced. P2701 covers element B taking too long to apply, which is a separate test, though a slow apply raises slip and can lead to P270B as well.
c: Slow or weak apply of element B creating extra slip (pressure or seal problem)
Stop-and-go, steep grades or trailer loads
Implausible fluid temperature input distorting the calculated value
s: Torque reduction or limited acceleration
Changed shift points or skipped gears
Shudder when element B engages

P270C.t: Transmission Friction Element C Temperature Too High
P270C.d: With P270C the controller reports that clutch or brake C has run hotter than its permitted limit. Typical triggers are long slip phases: creeping in heavy traffic, holding the car on a slope with the throttle, or a trailer launch. If the situation keeps recurring under normal driving, the element itself may be slipping because apply pressure is low or its linings are worn, and the fluid should be checked for level, smell and debris. There is no public maker documentation for P270C; which element carries letter C must be taken from the gearbox's own clutch chart. Audi documents the same protective idea under its own codes for the S tronic of the S4/S5 (2010-2012), where a fault in the clutch cooling oil valve can appear together with the clutch temperature entries. Sibling codes P270A to P270F differ only in the element.
c: Creeping or holding on a grade with the throttle instead of the brake
Element C slipping from low apply pressure or worn plates
Faulty clutch cooling oil valve or restricted cooler (where fitted)
s: Warning in the cluster with reduced power
Gear using element C avoided or held only briefly
Hot, darkened fluid

P270D.t: Transmission Friction Element D Temperature Too High
P270D.d: P270D is stored when the thermal state of shift element D rises above the controller's limit. The heat comes from friction during slip, so anything that lengthens slip on D counts: a sluggish apply, leaking seals in its hydraulic circuit, or hard use with a heavy load. Cooling also matters, because the fluid carries the heat away; a blocked cooler, a low level or oil that has lost its properties make the code more likely. Publicly, no manufacturer documents P270D or its thresholds, and the letter must be matched to a clutch with the specific gearbox data. CARB treats transmission controls as monitored powertrain components. For the driver the code mostly means a protective torque or gear limit; it does not by itself prove mechanical damage, but it should be investigated if it returns.
c: Leaking seals in the apply circuit of element D lengthening slip
Blocked or undersized fluid cooler, especially when towing
Old or wrong fluid with reduced friction and cooling properties
s: Limited torque or gear range for protection
Transmission temperature warning
Flare or slip on shifts involving element D

P270E.t: Transmission Friction Element E Temperature Too High
P270E.d: P270E reports an over-temperature of the shift element labelled E. Because the value is normally calculated rather than measured inside the clutch, a wrong input can also trigger it: an implausible fluid temperature signal or incorrect slip data from the speed sensors would distort the estimate. Before suspecting the clutch, check for stored sensor codes such as P0711 or speed sensor faults, and confirm the fluid level. If those are fine, real slip of element E under load is the likely reason. No vehicle maker documents P270E publicly; Audi's S tronic bulletin for the 2010-2012 S4/S5 shows a related case under maker codes, where poor contact on the mechatronic circuit board produced clutch temperature and torque limitation entries. The car usually stays drivable with reduced performance.
c: Faulty fluid temperature or speed sensor signal distorting the calculated temperature
Real slip of element E under load
Poor internal contact in the transmission control electronics
s: Gearbox warning with reduced performance
Additional sensor codes stored
Slipping or delayed shifts through element E

P270F.t: Transmission Friction Element F Temperature Too High
P270F.d: P270F closes the A-to-F series and signals that element F has exceeded its temperature limit. Only gearboxes with at least six shift elements carry a letter F, so the code belongs to modern multi-speed automatics, but no maker publishes its use or thresholds. It should be kept apart from P2787, which reports a hot clutch in general (for example a dual-clutch or launch clutch) without a letter, and from P0218, which concerns overall fluid over-temperature. P2705 is the apply-time test for the same element F. CARB lists transmission controls among the powertrain parts the OBD system must check. VW's 0AM dual-clutch material describes the typical reaction to overheating, a cut in engine torque. If the code repeats under ordinary driving, slip of F or a cooling fault should be checked.
c: Element F slipping due to low pressure or wear
Severe duty such as towing, mountain driving or repeated launches
s: Torque reduction and warning message
Gears using element F temporarily unavailable
Harsh or slipping shifts

P2710.d: P2710 is the sporadic counterpart to P2709: the circuit of shift solenoid F drops out now and then and recovers, so a check at standstill often finds nothing. In Ford's 2024 OBD summary it equals P2706 with the intermittent byte 1F in the general solenoid list and in the 8F57 and 8F24 tables; the tables for 10R60/10R80 and 8F35/8F40 instead list P2710 for a short to supply voltage. The electrical test runs continuously and reports a fault once the smart driver has signalled a problem for 1.5 s. CARB requires automatic transmission solenoids to be monitored for circuit faults as comprehensive components. No other maker publishes the code with details. Loose pins, rubbing wires near the valve body or moisture in a connector are the usual suspects, and the fault may show only when hot or on rough roads.
c: Loose or spread terminal at the transmission or module connector
Wire rubbing through intermittently inside or outside the case
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Heat-dependent internal break in the solenoid coil
s: Occasional harsh shift or brief fail-safe operation
MIL that comes and goes with the fault
No fault found during a static circuit test

P2711.d: P2711 is set when the transmission controller sees the drivetrain act as if a gear were no longer properly engaged although it never commanded that, for example because a clutch drags or a gear does not engage as selected. Volkswagen Group uses it on DSG gearboxes: Audi bulletin 2029069 for the 2009-2010 A3 and TT logs it as 19143 P2711 004, with a lit gear display and shudder on the first launch, and blames a clutch that drags too strongly; VW bulletin 2028714 for 2009-2012 Jetta, Golf, CC, Eos and 2012 Passat with the 02E calls it an implausible shift sequence, caused by debris in the clutch pack, where the selected gear may not engage after start-up. Both replace the multiple clutch (beyond about 18,500 or 19,000 miles); improved clutches entered production in March 2010.
c: Excessive drag torque in the dual clutch (worn or early-production plates)
Shift fork or gear actuator not holding the gear
s: Gear indicator flashing or lit in the cluster
Shudder on the first drive-away
Selected Drive or Reverse does not engage after start-up

P2712.d: P2712 targets gearboxes whose clutches or shift forks are worked by a separate hydraulic power unit, typically an electric pump that charges a pressure accumulator. Such a system loses pressure only slowly when sealed; if pressure drops faster than expected or the pump has to recharge too often, the controller concludes there is a leak. No manufacturer documents P2712 publicly. The principle is described in Volkswagen's training booklet for the dry seven-speed DSG 0AM: an electric pump fills a 0.2 l gas accumulator, switches off at about 60 bar according to the pressure sensor and restarts near 40 bar. CARB counts automatic transmission controls among the monitored output components. A leaking accumulator, valve or seal can end in lost gears; P0944 covers a general pressure loss of the hydraulic unit.
c: Internal leakage at valves or seals of the hydraulic unit
External oil leak at housing, lines or connector seals
s: Hydraulic pump running often or for long periods
Gears not engaging or delayed engagement
Gearbox warning and emergency mode

P2713.d: P2713 is the umbrella code for pressure control solenoid D; it names the valve but not the kind of fault, so the failure type byte behind it carries the detail. Toyota works this way. Bulletin T-SB-0076-24 lists P271371 (actuator stuck) among several valve codes on the 2024 Tacoma and fixes it by replacing gearbox and torque converter, while T-SB-0160-18 names P27137F for 2017-2018 Highlander and Sienna with the eight-speed transaxle, where whine, harsh shifts or reduced power lead to a remanufactured unit. GM and Ford instead use the separate codes P2714 to P2721. Which clutch valve D feeds differs by gearbox, so only the maker's data can say what is affected. Expect the MIL and rough or missing gears.
c: Internal transmission damage that makes the valve or its clutch stick (Toyota replaces the unit)
Pressure control solenoid D sticking from debris or wear
Wrong fluid level or degraded fluid
Wiring or connector fault on the valve circuit
s: MIL lit with further transmission codes
Harsh, late or missing shifts
Whine noise or reduced power in some vehicles

P2714.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Performance/Stuck Off
P2714.d: P2714 says the clutch served by solenoid D does not apply as commanded, so the gearbox slips in a gear that needs it. In GM's 2016 table 16OBDG03 valve D is clutch 4 (C2-3-4-6-8) on the eight-speed and the 2-6 brake on the T76 six-speed; slip of 400 rpm or more for 3 s, counted over three events, sets it after one trip. GM bulletins call it solenoid valve 4 stuck off: on the 10L80 a loose retainer ring lets the input internal gear separate (PIP6008), on the gasoline 10L1000 the C4 piston seal degrades (24-NA-148), on the VT40 CVT a sticking clutch regulator valve is blamed (PIP5819). On the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box it means the even-clutch redundant shutdown valve, Type A, as does Ford's TR9070. Loss of a gear or reverse is typical.
c: Leaking clutch piston seal or damaged clutch housing (GM 10L1000 C4)
Regulator or line pressure valve stuck by debris or sediment
Internal mechanical failure such as a dislodged retainer ring (GM 10L80)
Low fluid level reducing apply pressure
s: Slipping or flare in gears that use the affected clutch
No reverse or no forward drive in some cases
MIL lit and transmission in a substitute mode

P2715.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Stuck On
P2715.d: With P2715 the opposite of P2714 has happened: the clutch fed by valve D keeps holding although the controller wants it released, so it drags into the next gear. GM checks this on its eight-speed through torque-phase and inertia-phase tests on clutch 4, and its 2018 table 18OBDG04 links the code on the nine-speed to C4 exhaust delay times (Type A). On the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch unit, more than 1 bar on the even clutch during the check marks the redundant shutdown valve as stuck on; Ford's TR9070 uses the same pairing. Subaru warns in bulletin 16-142-23 that 2022 Legacy, Outback and Ascent CVTs can log it falsely when a VDC fault limits lock-up; a freeze-frame lock-up duty under 95.2 % points to the chassis fault. Harsh shifts or binding follow.
c: Debris holding a valve in the applied position
Solenoid D or redundant shutdown valve mechanically stuck
False detection during a stability-control fail-safe (Subaru CVT)
Faulty TCM/solenoid assembly (GM 2-mode hybrid date codes)
s: Harsh shift or binding as two clutches overlap
Vehicle feels braked when pulling away
MIL lit, transmission may hold a safe gear

P2716.d: P2716 is the general electrical code for pressure control solenoid D: the output stage sees a wrong current or voltage on the coil, without saying whether the circuit is open, grounded or shorted to supply. No manufacturer documents P2716 publicly. The makers that publish data on valve D split its electrical checks instead: GM's 2016 eight-speed table uses P2718, P2720 and P2721 with 0.3 s fail times, and Ford's 2024 summary gives the same three codes for open load, shorted switch and shorted load. CARB requires the circuits of transmission solenoids to be monitored as comprehensive components. When a controller does use this broad code, the cause is usually a coil, a connector or the harness, and the gearbox drops into a fail-safe mode with fixed gears.
c: Open or shorted coil in solenoid D
Loose, corroded or not fully seated connector
Faulty driver stage in the TCM
s: MIL lit and transmission in fail-safe mode
Fixed gear or missing gears
Harsh engagement after start

P2717.d: P2717 reports that the circuit or response of solenoid D drops out briefly and then comes back. Unlike a hard open or short, the fault is gone by the time the vehicle reaches the workshop, so a static measurement often looks fine. No manufacturer documents P2717 publicly. Ford shows the principle on its shift solenoids: the 2024 OBD summary attaches failure byte 1F (circuit intermittent) to the base code, and P2710 is the counterpart for shift solenoid F. Under CARB rules a solenoid circuit must be watched continuously. Typical triggers are spread terminals, a wire rubbing through near the valve body, or moisture in the connector, and the fault often appears only when hot or on rough roads. The gearbox may stay in a substitute mode until the engine is restarted.
c: Spread or loose terminal at transmission or TCM connector
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Occasional harsh or flared shift
MIL that comes and goes
No fault found during a workshop check

P2718.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit/Open
P2718.d: P2718 points to an open control circuit of solenoid D: the coil draws no current because a wire, pin or the winding itself is broken. GM's 2016 eight-speed table runs the open check on the clutch 4 valve and fails it after 0.3 s within a 0.5 s window (one trip); the 2017 and 2018 nine-speed tables use an impedance measurement. In 2018 GM issued service update N182193520 for 8L45 and 8L90 units in Camaro, Colorado, Corvette, Silverado and others because the valve body connector might not be fully seated, setting P2718 or P2720 and forcing limp-home. For the even-clutch shutdown valve of the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box, it stands for open load, seen while switched off (Type A); Ford's TR9070 also files open load here.
c: Valve body solenoid connector not fully seated (GM 8L45/8L90)
Broken wire or pushed-out pin in the harness
s: Limp-home mode with limited forward gears
MIL on immediately
Harsh engagements

P2719.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2719.d: P2719 means the electrical readings on the control circuit of solenoid D are implausible, although neither a clear open nor a clear short is present. In GM's 2016 table 16OBDG03 the T76 six-speed flags it when the hardware layer reports an invalid voltage in at least 4.4 of 5 seconds; valve D is the 2-6 brake there, and the code is listed without MIL. Bulletin PI0893 matches this for the 2013 6T70/6T75 in Enclave, SRX, XTS, Equinox, Malibu, Traverse, Acadia and Terrain: P2719, P2728 and P0965 are Type C codes that may be stored falsely at fluid temperatures from -0.5 to 0 °C in Park or Neutral, cause no drivability issue and need no parts. Only if the code stays active above 0 °C is normal circuit diagnosis due.
c: False history code near freezing fluid temperature in Park/Neutral (GM 6T70/6T75)
High resistance at a terminal or splice
s: Stored history code without noticeable symptoms
No MIL on GM vehicles (Type C)
Occasional shift quality changes if the fault is real

P271A.t: Park Pawl Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P271A.d: With park-by-wire the pawl is moved by an actuator instead of a cable, and a position sensor tells the controller whether it is engaged. P271A means the signal of sensor A has dropped below its valid band. Ford's 2026 safety recall 26V688 shows a real case: on 2026-2027 Lincoln Nautilus Hybrid and 2027 Corsair Hybrid with the HF55 hybrid transmission, an unvalidated anti-rust oil inside the Integrated Park Module attacked the circuit board coating, the rotary sensor circuit corroded and its output voltage sank. Dealers found P271A. Owners saw a wrench lamp with Service Vehicle Soon or Shifting System Error, could not leave Park, or the car shifted to Neutral while moving. The fix is a new module with current software.
c: Corrosion on the park module circuit board (Ford HF55, recall 26V688)
Sensor A signal wire shorted to ground
Missing or low reference voltage to sensor A
s: Vehicle cannot be shifted out of Park
Unexpected shift to Neutral while driving
Service warning such as Shifting System Error

P271B.t: Park Pawl Position Sensor A Circuit High
P271B.d: P271B is the upper-limit partner of P271A: the signal from park pawl position sensor A reads above its plausible range. Typical electrical causes are a broken ground or signal wire, which lets the input float towards the reference, or a short to a supply line. No manufacturer documents P271B publicly. The closest published case concerns the same sensor at its lower limit, Ford's recall 26V688 for the Integrated Park Module of the HF55 hybrid transmission, which shows what is at stake: if the controller cannot trust the pawl position it may refuse to leave Park or drop to Neutral. Most systems carry a second sensor B as a cross-check (P271C/P271D), so a single high reading is normally caught before the pawl moves unintentionally.
c: Open sensor ground or signal wire
Signal wire shorted to reference or battery voltage
Corroded or loose connector at the park actuator
s: Shift system warning on the display
Park cannot be selected or released

P271C.t: Park Pawl Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P271C.d: P271C covers the second park pawl position sensor, B, whose signal has fallen below the valid range. Park-by-wire designs often fit two position signals so that a single faulty reading cannot release or engage the pawl by itself; sensor B is the backup or comparison channel to sensor A. A low reading points to a short to ground, a missing reference voltage or a sensor that has failed low. No manufacturer documents P271C publicly; the only published field case in this family is Ford's recall 26V688, which concerns sensor A in the park module of the HF55 hybrid gearbox. With one channel lost the controller usually still knows the pawl state from the other, but it will warn the driver and may limit shifting into or out of Park.
c: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Reference voltage to sensor B missing or low
Corrosion inside the park actuator module
s: Shift system warning, vehicle usually still drivable
Delayed or refused Park engagement

P271D.t: Park Pawl Position Sensor B Circuit High
P271D.d: P271D is logged when the signal of park pawl position sensor B sits above its upper limit. Electrically this is the mirror image of P271C: an interrupted sensor ground, an open signal line pulled up inside the controller, or contact with a supply wire. No manufacturer documents P271D publicly, so neither thresholds nor debounce times are known; Ford's recall 26V688 for the park module of the HF55 hybrid transmission is the only published case in this sensor family and involves sensor A. Because the pawl decides whether the car can roll away, controllers treat any doubt about its position conservatively. Expect a shift system warning and checks of wiring and connector at the actuator before the module itself is replaced.
c: Open ground or signal wire of sensor B
Signal shorted to a voltage source
Moisture or corrosion in the actuator connector
s: Shift system warning on the display
Park function restricted

P271E.d: P271E is a broad performance code for the transmission as a whole, used when the controller finds that the gearbox does not deliver what it should even though no single sensor or valve has failed. Honda applies it to the CVT of the 2016-2020 HR-V: service bulletin A21-046 adds P271E with new PCM software that detects early slip of the primary drive belt. When it sets, the D indicator flashes, the MIL comes on and engine output is cut to protect the belt from breaking. Companion bulletin A21-047 extends CVT warranty to 7 years or 150,000 miles because the belt is now OBD-monitored, and the inspection uses a magnet to look for metal shed by the belt. Other makers may use P271E with other meanings, so the maker's own diagnosis decides what was measured.
c: Slipping or deteriorating CVT drive belt (Honda HR-V)
Insufficient clamping or line pressure in the transmission
Control software without the latest calibration
s: Flashing D indicator and MIL on
Reduced engine power
Engine flare or weak acceleration

P271F.t: Electronic Gear Shift - Position Not Learned
P271F.d: P271F tells the technician that the controller of an electronically actuated gear shift lacks valid learned positions, so it cannot place the shift elements precisely. Automated and dual-clutch gearboxes store the end and engagement points of their actuators; after replacing a control unit or mechanical parts, or after the stored values are lost, these must be learned again with a scan tool or during a defined drive. The code is a status message rather than a defect report. No manufacturer documents P271F publicly. Volkswagen's 0AM DSG booklet shows the underlying idea: its control unit adapts where both clutches and each gear selector sit whenever a gear is engaged. Unlike P0914 or P0919, which point to the selector position circuit or its control, P271F concerns missing calibration.
c: Learn procedure not run after replacing the control unit or transmission parts
Learn procedure aborted (conditions not met, low battery voltage)
Learned values lost after a software update or power interruption
Actuator or position sensor fault preventing a successful learn
s: Gearbox warning, gear selection limited or blocked
Rough or imprecise engagement
Code returns until a successful learn

P2720.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit Low
P2720.d: P2720 reports a low signal on the control line of solenoid D, which in practice is a short to ground. GM's 2016 eight-speed table sets it on the clutch 4 valve after a 0.3 s ground-short flag within one trip; the six-speed tables do the same for their valve D. On the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch transmission the TCM checks the line while the low-side driver is on: if the sense voltage stays under about 1.7 V for at least 100 ms, the even-clutch shutdown valve is shorted to ground (Type A). Ford's TR9070 logs its shorted switch case under this code. GM's service update N182193520 names P2720 next to P2718 when the 8L45/8L90 valve body connector is not fully latched, so a poor connection can produce it as well as a pinched wire.
c: Control wire pinched or chafed against ground
Valve body connector not fully seated
s: MIL on and limp-home operation
Limited forward gears
Harsh shifts

P2721.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit High
P2721.d: P2721 is logged when the control line of solenoid D reads too high, typically because it touches battery positive. GM's 2016 six-speed tables describe it as circuit high covering an open or a short to power, set after 0.3 s in one trip, so on those units an open line can land here too. The 2023 Corvette dual-clutch TCM tests with the driver on and sets it when the sense voltage exceeds a limit that rises with supply, about 0.7 V below 11.5 V and 1.1 V above 15.5 V (Type A); Ford's TR9070 calls this shorted load. Subaru bulletin 16-149-25 lists P2721 on 2020-2023 Legacy, Outback and Crosstrek with the TR580 CVT: condensation reaches the control valve connector, and a new control valve and connector cover fix it.
c: Moisture in the control valve connector (Subaru TR580)
Control wire shorted to a supply circuit
Open circuit on units that report it as high (GM six-speed)
Faulty solenoid D or TCM driver
s: MIL on and fail-safe operation
Shift shock or missing gears
Fault may follow wet weather or washing

P2722.d: P2722 is the base code for pressure control solenoid E and leaves the type of fault open. No manufacturer documents P2722 publicly. The pattern can be seen on the neighbouring valve: Toyota stores P2713 for solenoid D with a failure type byte appended, so a scan tool would show the same structure for E. GM and Ford instead publish dedicated codes for E, from P2723 (stuck off) and P2724 (stuck on) to P2727, P2729 and P2730 for the circuit. On GM's eight-speed valve E feeds clutch 5, on its nine-speed the C5 clutch, on the Allison 1000 the solenoid GM calls PCS 1, and on the 2023 Corvette and Ford TR9070 dual-clutch units the line pressure pilot valve. CARB covers such solenoids as comprehensive components.
c: Wiring or connector problem on the solenoid E circuit
s: MIL lit with possible further transmission codes
Irregular shifting or fail-safe gear
Engagement delay into drive or reverse

P2723.t: Pressure Control Solenoid E Performance/Stuck Off
P2723.d: P2723 means valve E fails to build the pressure its clutch needs, so that element slips or does not engage. GM's eight-speed table ties E to clutch 5 (C4-5-6-7-8-R) and sets the code after 400 rpm of slip lasting 3 s. On the Allison 1000 GM's tables call the valve PCS 1: if the on-coming clutch has not taken hold after 2 s of slip during a forward shift, a Type A fault follows. Bulletin PIP5100A adds a field cause: shrink-wrap from an aftermarket spin-on filter can block the PCS 1 feed hole, giving no or intermittent reverse. On the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch unit it is the system pressure pilot valve, failed when pressure stays more than 3 bar above target (Type A). Subaru lists P2723 among CVT codes in 18-241-26.
c: Blocked feed orifice in the separator plate (foreign material, GM Allison 1000)
Low fluid level or pump losing prime, especially on cold starts
Solenoid E or its regulator valve sticking
Worn clutch seals leaking apply pressure
s: Delayed, intermittent or no reverse
Slip or flare in affected gears
MIL on and range inhibit or fail-safe mode

P2724.t: Pressure Control Solenoid E Stuck On
P2724.d: P2724 flags valve E as delivering pressure when it should not, so its clutch stays engaged too long. On the Allison 1000 GM watches the off-going element during shifts: an accumulated fail time of 0.3 s on upshifts, 0.5 s on closed-throttle downshifts or 3 s on direction changes counts as stuck on (Type A). On the nine-speed the check runs through exhaust-delay tables for clutch C5, on the eight-speed through torque and inertia phase tests on clutch 5. The 2023 Corvette dual-clutch TCM reverses the sense for its system pressure pilot valve: a pressure 3 bar below target means stuck on, rated Type B. GM's PIP5646 links P2724, P2727 and P2729 on 2019-2020 Silverado and Sierra 8L90 to rear wheels locking after a hot soak, cured by a new TCM.
c: Valve or regulator held in the applied position by debris
s: Wheels lock or vehicle stops abruptly at low speed
Tie-up or harsh shift feel
MIL on, transmission may hold a safe gear

P2725.d: P2725 covers an unspecified electrical fault of pressure control solenoid E. The driver notices a coil current or voltage that does not fit the command but does not classify it further. No manufacturer documents P2725 publicly. GM splits the electrical checks of valve E into P2727, P2729 and P2730; on the Allison 1000 these are Type A tests on the solenoid GM calls PCS 1, including a ground-short check every 6.25 ms. Ford's 2024 summary uses the same three codes for its TR9070 line pressure pilot valve. CARB demands circuit monitoring of transmission solenoids. A controller using P2725 would point to the same suspects: coil, connector, harness or driver. Depending on the gearbox the result is a default gear or a pressure fallback.
c: Damaged wiring between TCM and solenoid
s: MIL lit and default gear
Firm shifts from fallback pressure
Code returns at once if the fault is permanent

P2726.d: P2726 describes a fault on solenoid E that is there one moment and gone the next. The controller has seen short drop-outs in the circuit or in the valve's response, not a lasting failure, which makes the code hard to reproduce. No manufacturer documents P2726 publicly. Ford's 2024 OBD summary shows how such cases are handled elsewhere: an intermittent circuit on a transmission solenoid is stored with failure byte 1F, and its TR9070 table lists the line pressure pilot valve under the P272x numbers. CARB requires transmission solenoid circuits to be monitored. Practical suspects are a terminal that loses tension, a harness moving with the engine, or water in the plug. Wiggle tests while watching live data help more than resistance checks on a cold unit.
c: Harness damaged by engine movement or heat
Water or corrosion in the plug
s: Sporadic harsh shift or brief fail-safe
MIL that switches on and off
No fault visible at standstill

P2727.t: Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit/Open
P2727.d: P2727 is set when the control circuit of solenoid E is open, so no current can flow through the coil. GM's eight-speed table checks the clutch 5 valve for an open-circuit flag over 0.3 s, and on the Allison 1000 the test on PCS 1 is rated Type A. The 2023 Corvette dual-clutch TCM looks at its system pressure pilot valve while switched off: a sense voltage between roughly 1.7 and 3.0 V means open load, confirmed after 150 ms (Type A). Ford's TR9070 maps open load of its line pressure pilot valve to the same code. A field case without wiring damage exists: GM's PIP5646 series for 2019-2020 Silverado and Sierra with the 8L90 names P2727 among the codes behind sudden rear-wheel lock-up and replaces the TCM.
s: MIL on and limp-home gear
Rear wheels may lock at low speed (GM 8L90 case)
Harsh or missing shifts

P2728.t: Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2728.d: P2728 marks the circuit of solenoid E as working but not plausible. GM uses it in two ways. On the Allison 1000 (16OBDG08, 17OBDG04) the TCM compares desired with actual current on PCS 1; a gap of at least 0.5 A in 10 of fewer than 20 samples sets a Type A fault with MIL. On the T76 six-speed table of 2016, where valve E serves the 1-2-3-4 clutch, an invalid voltage flag for 4.4 of 5 s sets it without MIL. Bulletin PI0893 explains the second case for 2013 vehicles with the 6T70/6T75: as a Type C history code next to P2719 and P0965 it can appear falsely with fluid between -0.5 and 0 °C in Park or Neutral and needs no parts. MIL behaviour therefore depends on the gearbox.
c: Coil current deviating from command (resistance change, poor contact)
False history code near 0 °C fluid temperature (GM 6T70/6T75)
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM
s: MIL on Allison-equipped trucks
History code without symptoms on GM six-speeds
Firm shifts if pressure control is degraded

P2729.t: Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit Low
P2729.d: P2729 indicates the control line of solenoid E is pulled low, usually by a short to ground. On the Allison 1000 GM detects this when the output connection has almost no impedance to ground and confirms it within 75 ms (Type A). The eight-speed and six-speed tables of 2016 flag the low state for 0.3 s and set it after one trip. For the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch transmission, a sense voltage below roughly 1.7 V with the driver on, held for 150 ms, identifies a ground short at the system pressure pilot valve (Type A); Ford's TR9070 stores its shorted switch case under this number. GM bulletin PIP5646B for 2019-2020 Silverado and Sierra 8L90 shows that P2729 can also come from a failing TCM rather than the harness.
s: MIL on and fail-safe mode
Abrupt stop or wheel lock at low speed in the GM 8L90 case
Limited gear selection

P272A.t: Transmission Range Select Motor Control Circuit
P272A.d: P272A refers to the control circuit of the electric motor that moves the gearbox into the selected range in shift-by-wire designs. Mitsubishi documents it for the 2022 Outlander with CVT: the shift actuator has two three-phase windings fed through separate relays, and motor A is the one reported as range select motor. With ignition on and the actuator at rest, a phase that reads low although no phase is energised sets the code; a second test after ignition off turns relays A and B off in turn and briefly rotates the motor. Listed causes are an open relay A circuit, an open phase wire, a relay stuck off, the coil or the electric shift module. If only one winding fails nothing changes for the driver; with both lost shifting is blocked and the drivetrain goes to neutral.
c: Shift actuator relay A open or stuck off
Open U, V or W phase wire to motor A
Faulty motor coil A in the shift actuator
s: MIL and shift warning, often no change in driving
Gear selection refused, vehicle in neutral (second fault)

P272B.t: Transmission Range Select Motor Control Circuit Current Too High
P272B.d: P272B flags excessive current in the circuit of the range select motor, normally caused by a winding or wire shorted to supply. On the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander with CVT, Mitsubishi checks this with ignition on: when one of the two phases that should be energised shows the non-energised voltage level (9-16 V instead of about 0 V), the code is set. The service text lists short circuits to power on either the A or the B winding, the connectors or the electric shift module as causes, so the code does not prove which winding is at fault. Unlike the open-circuit code P272A, the fail-safe is drastic: shifting is prohibited and the powertrain goes to neutral. The MIL comes on, and the yellow shift warning depends on road speed.
c: Motor coil A or B phase shorted to power
Damaged harness between shift module and actuator
s: Vehicle stays in neutral, no gear can be selected
MIL and shift system warning

P272C.d: P272C concerns the control circuit of the motor that engages and releases the park pawl. In the shift actuator of the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander with CVT this is winding B, powered through its own relay B, while winding A is reported under P272A. The detection mirrors that code: with ignition on and the actuator idle, any phase of B reading low without being energised triggers it, and an after-run test with ignition off switches the relays off one at a time and turns the motor a little. Causes named are an open relay B circuit, an open phase line, relay B stuck off, coil B or the shift module. Because the other winding can still drive the actuator, a single fault has no effect on driving; only when both circuits fail are shifts blocked and the car placed in neutral.
c: Shift actuator relay B open or stuck off
Open phase wire to motor coil B
Faulty motor coil B in the actuator
s: MIL on, Park still works normally
Shifting blocked if the other circuit also fails

P272D.t: Park Pawl Motor Control Circuit Current Too High
P272D.d: P272D reports overcurrent in the park pawl motor circuit, the counterpart of P272B for the second winding. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander CVT service data sets it with ignition on when one of two phases of motor B that ought to carry current sits at the idle voltage level instead of near 0 V, the pattern of a line shorted to supply. As with P272B, the causes list shorts to power on both coil A and coil B plus the shift module, so the code number alone does not isolate the winding. The response is immediate: shifting is locked out and the powertrain is held in neutral, the MIL lights and, depending on speed, the shift warning lamp as well. A motor that draws too much current may also leave the pawl unable to reach its end position.
c: Motor coil B or A phase shorted to power
Chafed harness at the shift actuator
s: Shifting locked out, vehicle held in neutral
MIL and shift warning lamp on
Park may not engage fully

P2730.t: Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit High
P2730.d: P2730 is stored when the control line of solenoid E sits too high, pointing to contact with a supply voltage. GM's Allison 1000 logic looks for a power short at the PCS 1 output and treats it as Type A. Its 2016 six-speed tables word the code as circuit high for an open or a power short, so there a broken wire may show up as P2730 instead of P2727. The 2023 Corvette dual-clutch TCM switches the driver on and compares the sense voltage with a limit that depends on supply, about 0.7 V at low and 1.1 V at high battery voltage (Type A); Ford's TR9070 calls the same fault shorted load. No public bulletin links P2730 to a particular repair, so standard tracing of harness, connector and solenoid applies.
c: Control wire chafed against a supply circuit
Open line on units that report it as high (GM six-speed)
s: MIL on and transmission in fail-safe
Harsh or missing shifts
Code sets again immediately after clearing

P2731.d: P2731 is the parent code for pressure control solenoid F; the standard title names the valve without the kind of fault. GM gives it a concrete job on its nine-speed (GF9) units, where valve F feeds the C6 clutch and the selectable one-way clutch. The 2020 table 20OBDG03A uses P2731 for a stuck-on check in first gear: when the releasing clutch keeps slipping less than 50 rpm for 0.25 s on a garage shift, 0.8 s on a power downshift or 0.15 s otherwise, a Type A fault is logged. GM bulletins call it solenoid valve 6 performance. PIP5556 (2018 Equinox and Traverse) blames a slow one-way clutch release and advises no repair for intermittent cases; 18-NA-097 and service update N182200080 cure stuck-in-first or hesitation complaints with new TCM software.
c: Selectable one-way clutch releasing too slowly
Solenoid F or its regulator valve sticking
s: Hesitation or weak acceleration from low speed
Tie-up feel on the 1-2 shift or stuck in first gear
MIL on, sometimes only intermittently

P2732.t: Pressure Control Solenoid F Performance/Stuck Off
P2732.d: P2732 says that the clutch behind valve F does not take up torque although the solenoid works electrically, so the gearbox slips wherever that clutch is needed. On GM nine-speed units valve F serves clutch C6; the TCM counts a failure when C6 slip stays at 200 rpm or more for 3 s, and three such events give a Type A fault after one trip (tables 18OBDG04 and 20OBDG03A). GM bulletins name the code solenoid valve 6 stuck off. On the 10L80 in 2024 Silverado and Sierra 1500, PIP6002 and 24-NA-181 replace the valve body, and 25-NA-014 and 25-NA-080 trace the loss of reverse and of gears above third to a wrongly stamped spacer plate together with a worn check ball. On the 10L1000 with the 6.6 gas engine, 24-NA-148 pairs P2732 with P2714 and a worn C4 piston seal.
c: Mis-stamped spacer plate or worn check ball in the valve body (GM 10L80)
Worn clutch piston seal losing apply pressure (GM 10L1000)
Solenoid F or regulator valve sticking closed
Low fluid level or aerated fluid
s: No reverse
Transmission will not shift beyond third gear
Slip or flare and MIL on

P2733.t: Pressure Control Solenoid F Stuck On
P2733.d: P2733 is the reverse case of P2732: valve F keeps pressure on its clutch after the TCM has commanded it off, so the off-going element still carries torque during the shift. GM checks this on its nine-speed units by watching C6 slip while shifting. If slip stays below 50 rpm for 0.8 s during power downshifts or 0.15 s on any other shift, one failure is counted; three of them give a Type A fault in one trip (18OBDG04, 20OBDG03A). GM shares the logic with P2731, which covers the same check in first gear. Bulletin 21-NA-169 for low-mileage 9T45/50/60 units lists P2731 to P2733 together and, with clean fluid, renews the solenoid assembly together with the valve body. Drivers notice tie-up, flare or harsh shifts.
c: Solenoid F held open mechanically (solenoid body)
Debris holding the regulator valve in the apply position
s: Tie-up or bind-up feel during shifts
Harsh shifts or engine flare
MIL on and fail-safe gear

P2734.d: P2734 is the catch-all electrical code for solenoid F: the driver stage notices coil current or voltage at odds with the command, without saying whether the line is broken, touching ground or touching battery voltage. Public documentation of P2734 by any maker is lacking. Those that publish data on valve F use the specific circuit codes instead: GM's 2025 table 25OBDG03A runs P2736, P2738 and P2739 on the same valve, which there feeds a clutch of the nine- or ten-speed, the line pressure circuit of the eight-speed or the binary pump of the CVT. Ford's 2024 summary maps the odd clutch cooling valve of its TR9070 dual-clutch unit to the same three codes. CARB counts such solenoids as comprehensive components whose circuits must be checked for faults.
c: Corroded, loose or damaged connector at the valve body
Chafed or broken wire in the solenoid F circuit
Faulty output stage in the TCM
s: MIL on with limp-home mode
Harsh, late or missing shifts

P2735.d: By its standard title P2735 reports that solenoid F or its circuit fails only now and then, so a static check in the workshop often finds nothing. GM uses the code differently on the dual-clutch gearbox of the 2023 and 2024 Corvette: there valve F is the clutch cooling valve, and P2735 stands for a stuck lube valve. The TCM triggers a current-profile test on the valve during stable driving with fluid at 60 °C or warmer and a cooling flow target below 3 l/min; if the result keeps indicating failure, it sets the code. GM rates it Type C, so it does not switch on the MIL. Other makers do not document P2735 publicly. Intermittent wiring or connector faults on valve F are the generic reading, while the Corvette case points to the cooling valve itself.
c: Clutch cooling/lube valve sticking (GM Corvette dual-clutch)
Loose or corroded connector causing dropouts
Harness chafing that opens under vibration
s: Often no noticeable symptom, code stored without MIL (GM)
Occasional harsh shift or clutch judder
Clutch overheating warning after hard driving

P2736.t: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit/Open
P2736.d: P2736 points to an open control circuit on solenoid F, meaning the coil path is interrupted. GM documents the code for several gearboxes. On the eight-speed of 2016 valve F is the line pressure solenoid, and an open-circuit flag for 0.3 s within 0.5 s sets the fault in one trip. In 25OBDG03A the same valve drives clutches on the nine- and ten-speed or switches the CVT's binary pump, and an impedance above 200 kOhm to ground over the same window is a Type A fault. The Corvette dual-clutch TCM tests its clutch cooling valve while switched off and flags open load at a sense voltage of roughly 1.7 to 3.0 V for 150 ms. Ford's TR9070 uses P2736 for open load on the odd clutch cooling valve. Line pressure faults usually bring a limp mode.
c: Valve body connector not fully seated
s: MIL on and limp-home mode
Firm shifts from maximum line pressure or missing gears

P2737.t: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2737.d: The standard title describes implausible readings on the control circuit of solenoid F that are neither a clean open nor a short. GM's 2025 table 25OBDG03A fills the code with a hydraulic test on its CVT, where valve F switches the binary oil pump between half and full capacity. With the vehicle below 2 mph, accelerator released, engine between 600 and 1,200 rpm, fluid above 50 °C and the garage shift finished, the TCM compares the averaged pressures from the primary and secondary pulley sensors in both pump modes. If the differences stay too large, the valve is judged not to follow its command; GM classes this Type B, so the MIL comes on after two trips. Other makers do not publish P2737. A failed pump valve can reduce clamping pressure and lead to belt slip.
c: Binary pump control valve sticking (GM CVT)
Primary or secondary pulley pressure sensor reading wrong
High resistance in the solenoid F circuit
s: MIL on after two trips
Belt slip, flare or reduced power
Whine from the CVT

P2738.t: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit Low
P2738.d: P2738 reports a control line on solenoid F that reads too low, which in practice means a short to ground. In GM's 2025 table 25OBDG03A an impedance below 0.5 Ohm between the signal and controller ground, lasting 0.3 s inside a 0.5 s sampling period, is a Type A fault in one trip; the valve there controls a clutch on the nine- or ten-speed, line pressure on the eight-speed or the CVT binary pump. The eight-speed table of 2016 uses the same timing. The Corvette dual-clutch TCM tests the clutch cooling valve with its driver switched on and sets P2738 when the measured pin voltage remains below roughly 1.7 V for 150 ms. Ford's TR9070 labels the same condition shorted switch on the odd clutch cooling valve. A grounded line can energise the valve permanently.
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Fluid or metal debris bridging connector pins
s: MIL on and fail-safe gear
Harsh engagements or clutch drag

P2739.t: Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit High
P2739.d: P2739 appears when solenoid F's control line sits too high, usually because it touches battery voltage. GM reacts faster here than for the low case: 25OBDG03A needs only 0.06 s within 0.13 s before the Type A fault is set. The Corvette dual-clutch TCM checks its clutch cooling valve with the driver on and sets P2739 above a sense threshold that rises with supply voltage, from roughly 0.7 V at a supply under 11.5 V to roughly 1.1 V beyond 15.5 V. It also runs a neighbour test at shutdown, switching each low-side output in turn; if two outputs turn out to be shorted together, the result is saved and the code appears at the next start. Ford's TR9070 uses P2739 for shorted load on the odd clutch cooling valve. A shorted coil can overload the driver.
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short between two solenoid lines in the harness or connector
s: MIL on and limp-home mode
Shifts missing or valve function lost

P273A.t: Transmission Friction Element G Apply Time Range/Performance
P273A.d: P273A carries the apply-time test of P2700 to P2705 on to a seventh shift element, G. The controller measures how long element G needs from command to full engagement and stores the code if this time is implausibly long or short. Only gearboxes with more than six clutches and brakes need a letter G, and no manufacturer documents P273A publicly. Ford shows how the series is used: its 10R80 bulletins (from 21-2315 onward) list apply-time codes up to P2705 for element F and none beyond, and Ford's 2012 summary explains that a ratio check cannot tell a valve fault apart from other faults in that clutch circuit. CARB requires monitoring of automatic transmission controls. A slow G apply can mean worn plates, leaking piston seals or low pressure; the driver feels flare or harsh shifts.
c: Leaking piston seals in the apply circuit of element G
Pressure control or shift solenoid feeding element G sticking
Worn plates or wrong clearance of element G
Adaptive shift values out of range after repair or software update
s: Engine flare or harsh shift into gears using element G
MIL lit, possibly with ratio codes
Fail-safe gear operation

P273B.t: Transmission Friction Element H Apply Time Range/Performance
P273B.d: P273B is the apply-time check for an eighth shift element, H, and therefore only applies to gearboxes with at least eight clutches and brakes. The test is the same as for its siblings: the time between command and full engagement is compared with a calibrated window, and a result outside it sets the code. No manufacturer documents P273B publicly. Ford's 2012 OBD summary notes that its newer automatics report clutch faults through solenoid stuck-on/stuck-off codes instead of the older element codes, which shows these generic apply-time codes are optional for a maker. CARB still expects transmission controls to be monitored where they affect emissions. Element H shares nothing with P273A except the method; mixing up the letters across gearboxes leads to the wrong part being replaced.
c: Pressure loss in the apply circuit of element H (seals, valve body)
Worn friction plates of element H
s: Delayed or harsh shifts involving element H
MIL lit
Transmission in fail-safe mode

P273C.t: Gear Shift Control Module A Supply Voltage Low
P273C.d: Gear shift control module A is the electronic selector used where the gearbox is shifted by wire – lever, rotary knob or push buttons – which turns the driver's choice into a message for the transmission control module. P273C means the supply voltage that this module sees, or reports, has fallen below its lower limit. No manufacturer documents P273C or its threshold publicly. A weak supply matters because a selector that resets or browns out can no longer confirm P, R, N or D; the gearbox then keeps its range or refuses to leave Park. Stellantis shows how sensitive these modules are: for a rotary selector stuck in Park, its 2022 case advised pulling and refitting fuse F94 to restart the module. Check battery, fuse, feed and ground first.
c: Weak or discharged 12 V battery, voltage dips at start
Corroded fuse contact, feed wire or ground of the selector module
Alternator or DC/DC converter not supplying enough voltage
Internal fault in the gear shift module
s: Selector warning, range cannot be changed
Vehicle will not shift out of Park
Gear indicator flickers or goes blank

P273D.t: Gear Shift Control Module A Supply Voltage High
P273D.d: P273D is the over-voltage counterpart of P273C: the gear shift control module A, the electronic selector of a by-wire gear selection, registers a supply above its permitted maximum. No manufacturer documents P273D publicly or names the limit. Excess voltage typically comes from the charging side – a regulator that has failed, jump-starting with a 24 V source or a booster left on – and may also be misread if the module's own measurement drifts. Audi gives an example of the latter on 2019–21 A6/A7 models: the selector lever J587 judged its voltage too strictly, logged faults and blocked range selection until a software update. Modules usually protect themselves by ignoring inputs, so expect a selector warning and a gearbox that holds its current range.
c: Jump-start or charger delivering excessive voltage
Selector module misjudging its supply (software or hardware)
s: Selector or gearbox warning in the cluster
Range selection blocked
Other over-voltage faults in several modules

P273E.t: Gear Shift Control Module A Over Temperature
P273E.d: P273E is a condition code: the gear shift control module A – the shift-by-wire selector unit – reports that its internal temperature exceeds the safe limit. No manufacturer documents P273E or its threshold publicly. Heat in such a unit can come from outside, for example a console exposed to strong sun or a module mounted near the exhaust tunnel, or from inside, when driver stages for lock solenoids, motors or illumination draw too much current. Because a hot module may give wrong position data, it typically reduces its functions; the vehicle may refuse range changes or hold Park until the unit cools. A code that returns at normal temperatures suggests an internal defect, while one tied to heat waves points to cooling or mounting.
c: Internal fault or overloaded output stage in the selector module
High ambient or radiant heat at the module location
Shorted lock solenoid or actuator driven by the module
s: Selector warning, functions limited
Range changes refused until the module cools

P273F.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Over Temperature Condition
P273F.d: P273F is a condition code, not a wiring fault: sensor B delivers a valid reading, but that reading lies above the overheating limit the calibration allows. No manufacturer publishes P273F or its threshold. The analogous code for sensor A is P0218; Saab's Aisin automatic, for instance, sets it once the fluid stays above 170 °C for over 10 s. Where sensor B measures the oil leaving the cooler, as on GM and Ford dual-clutch units, a high value hints that the cooler itself is no longer removing heat. Typical reactions are a warning message, reduced torque or an altered shift and clutch strategy. Look for towing or track use, low fluid, a blocked cooler or a failed cooler valve before suspecting the sensor.
c: Sustained high load – towing, track use, long climbs
Fluid cooler clogged or cooler valve not opening
Fluid level low or fluid aged
Sensor B reading too hot while still in range
s: Transmission overheating message
Reduced torque or changed shift pattern
Burnt-smelling or darkened fluid

P2740.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit
P2740.d: P2740 is the umbrella circuit code for a second transmission fluid temperature sensor, labelled B. The control module supplies the thermistor with a reference voltage and flags an electrical fault when the returned signal leaves its plausible window, without separating short from open. Where B is documented, it sits outside the sump: Ford's TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox and a GM dual-clutch module of 2023/24 both use it for the fluid leaving the cooler, but report electrical faults through the split codes P2742/P2743 rather than P2740. No manufacturer publishes P2740 itself. Without a valid B value the module relies on sensor A or a default, so cooler control and hot-fluid protection get coarser; shifting usually remains normal.
c: Loose, corroded or damaged connector or lead to sensor B
Sensor B thermistor open or shorted internally
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: Warning lamp or transmission message
Fluid temperature B shows an implausible fixed value on the scan tool
Cooler or hot-fluid protection works with a substitute value

P2741.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2741.d: P2741 flags a sensor B signal that is electrically intact but physically impossible or inconsistent. The clearest published test is a rate check: GM's 2023/24 dual-clutch module calls the cooler-outlet reading faulty when its filtered gradient exceeds 700 °C per second, confirmed over five samples, as a Type B code (MIL after two trips). Mitsubishi's Twin Clutch SST in the 2009 Lancer uses a jump of 10 °C or more within 80 ms, lasting 400 ms; there the sensor sits in the transaxle-mounted control unit, so a returning code means replacing the transaxle. Ford lists P2741 as the consistency check of the TR9070 cooler-out sensor. Unlike P2742/P2743 the voltage stays in range; a loose pin or sensor drift is typical.
c: Contact resistance or loose pin causing signal jumps
Sensor B thermistor drifting or responding erratically
Fault in a control unit with built-in sensor (e.g. Mitsubishi TC-SST)
s: Warning lamp after repeated detection
Fluid temperature B jumps on the scan tool
Temperature-dependent clutch or cooler control restricted

P2742.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P2742.d: P2742 reports that the sensor B signal sits below its valid range, and how low is defined differs by maker. GM's 2023/24 dual-clutch TCM treats a cooler temperature sensor value under 200 mV, with hysteresis, for at least 500 ms as too low, Type B; for the usual NTC thermistor that equals an extremely hot reading or a signal wire shorted to ground. Ford's TR9070 lists P2742 as the out-of-window-low test of its cooler-out sensor. Mitsubishi's 2009 Twin Clutch SST instead relates Low to the computed temperature: −40 °C or colder for 400 ms, naming the transaxle-integrated unit as suspect. Real overheating with a sound sensor belongs to P273F. Afterwards the module ignores sensor B and uses a substitute.
c: Signal lead of sensor B chafed through and touching ground
Control unit with built-in sensor faulty (Mitsubishi TC-SST)
s: Warning lamp after two trips on GM
Scan tool shows sensor B extremely hot (GM, Ford) or extremely cold (Mitsubishi)
Protective strategy with substitute temperature

P2743.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P2743.d: P2743 is the counterpart of P2742: the sensor B signal is above its valid range. In GM's 2023/24 dual-clutch TCM the cooler temperature sensor must exceed 4745 mV for 500 ms, Type B; with an NTC thermistor fed from 5 V that points to a broken wire, an unplugged connector or a short to supply voltage, and the reading looks extremely cold. Ford uses P2743 as the out-of-window-high check of the TR9070 cooler-out sensor. Mitsubishi's 2009 Lancer Twin Clutch SST again reasons in temperature: 150 °C or more for 400 ms sets the code, and it advises checking the CAN bus first because bus faults can produce a false entry. Without B the module can no longer judge the cooler outflow and falls back on sensor A.
c: Open circuit – broken lead or unplugged connector at sensor B
Signal lead shorted to a voltage source
CAN fault or control unit with built-in sensor (Mitsubishi TC-SST)
s: Warning lamp or transmission message
Scan tool shows sensor B extremely cold (GM, Ford) or extremely hot (Mitsubishi)
Cooler control falls back on sensor A

P2744.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2744.d: P2744 covers brief dropouts or jumps in the sensor B signal that do not last long enough for the steady low or high codes. No manufacturer documents P2744 publicly; the makers that do use sensor B (GM and Ford dual-clutch units, Mitsubishi Twin Clutch SST) file erratic readings under P2741 instead. By analogy, Ford's 2012 strategy for the main sensor names P0714 alongside open, short and in-range checks. CARB requires such inputs to be watched for wiring faults and for readings beyond their scale. Practical causes are a loose terminal in the gearbox connector, a chafed lead near hot or moving parts, or corrosion that only acts under vibration or heat. The fault often vanishes at the workshop, so freeze-frame data and wiggle tests matter.
c: Loose or spread terminal in the transmission connector
Harness to sensor B chafing on hot or moving parts
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Short spikes in fluid temperature B on the scan tool

P2745.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit
P2745.d: P2745 is the general circuit code for a second intermediate shaft speed sensor, called B. Such a sensor reads a shaft that turns between input and output, on a dual-clutch box typically the second clutch shaft. Ford's 2024 OBD summary documents it: its ten-speed automatics carry two intermediate sensors (the eight-speeds only one), and P2745 means sensor B has an open circuit or a short to ground, while a short to battery appears as P07C8. These hardware checks mature in roughly 1.5 s and run even when the car stands still. On Ford's TR9070 dual-clutch unit, the even-gear clutch shaft sensor is filed under the same P2745 family. Without the signal the module loses one ratio reference, so harsh shifts or a fixed limp-home gear are likely.
c: Signal or supply lead to sensor B broken or chafed to ground
Corroded or loose pins at the transmission connector
Internal fault of intermediate shaft speed sensor B
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module
s: Check engine light and transmission warning
Harsh or delayed shifts
Limp-home mode with a fixed gear

P2746.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2746.d: P2746 means the sensor B signal exists but does not make sense. GM's 2023/24 dual-clutch TCM uses it for the clutch 2 speed sensor: with that clutch fully closed and no microslip, its speed must equal engine speed, and a gap of 150 rpm or more for 1.1 s sets the code; further tests compare it with the speed derived from the output shaft and watch synchronizer speed during gear engagement (above 200 rpm for 50 ms). GM lists it as Type A, so the MIL comes on at the first failure. Ford's 2024 summary bundles three checks of sensor B here: dropouts (800 rpm lost within 10 ms, ten times), noise (2,500 spikes of 300 rpm within 50 ms) and a mismatch with gear and other sensors lasting 2.5 s.
c: Metal debris on the sensor tip or incorrect air gap to the reluctor
Interference or poor shielding causing signal spikes
Slipping clutch making the speed comparison fail
Damaged or loose reluctor ring on the shaft
s: Check engine light, often immediately
Jerky clutch engagement or erratic shifts
Limp-home mode or one half of the gearbox disabled

P2747.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit No Signal
P2747.d: P2747 is meant for the case where sensor B stays silent although the car is clearly moving. No manufacturer documents P2747 publicly. Ford's 2024 summary describes exactly this test for its intermediate sensors – vehicle inferred to be driving under positive torque, yet the sensor shows under 250 rpm lasting 2.5 s – but for sensor B it names only P2745, P2746 and P2748, so Ford apparently files missing pulses elsewhere. For the older single-sensor layout, Ford's 2012 strategy flags the intermediate shaft below 250 rpm for 5 s with turbine and output turning. Typical reasons are a sensor that has died internally, an open supply, or a reluctor that no longer passes the sensor. The module substitutes a calculated speed or goes into limp mode.
c: Sensor B failed internally and delivers no pulses
Open supply or signal wire, unplugged connector
Reluctor ring displaced or sensor not seated in its bore
s: Warning lamp and transmission message while driving
Limp-home mode, often stuck in one gear
Rough or missing upshifts

P2748.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2748.d: P2748 records short interruptions in the sensor B circuit that heal before a permanent fault can be confirmed. Ford is the one maker that documents it: in the 2024 OBD summary, P2748 is the intermittent check of intermediate shaft sensor B on its ten-speed automatics, run continuously alongside the circuit code P2745 and the plausibility code P2746 within a 30 s monitoring window. Because the signal recovers, the fault often appears only under vibration, at high fluid temperature or when the harness flexes with engine movement. Freeze-frame data showing speed, gear and temperature at the moment of the dropout narrow the search. Replacing the sensor without checking pins and harness rarely ends the problem; drivers may notice occasional harsh shifts.
c: Terminal with weak contact pressure in the sensor or gearbox connector
Harness rubbing through and touching ground intermittently
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Occasional harsh shift or shift flare

P2749.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit
P2749.d: P2749 covers an electrical fault in the circuit of a third intermediate shaft speed sensor, C. No manufacturer documents P2749 publicly, and it is unclear which transmission carries three such sensors: Ford's ten-speeds stop at B, and dual-clutch units have only two clutch shafts. CARB requires transmission inputs like this to be watched for broken circuits and readings beyond their span. Following Ford's published logic for sensors A and B, a module would detect an open or a short to ground in hardware within about 1.5 s, independent of driving. The split codes P07C9/P07CA cover low and high voltage separately. If it occurs, start with the live value of sensor C next to the other speeds, then check connector, wiring and sensor resistance.
c: Open or grounded wire between module and sensor C
s: Check engine light
Harsh shifts or limp-home mode

P274A.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor C Circuit
P274A.d: P274A is the general circuit code for a third transmission fluid temperature sensor, labelled C. Few gearboxes carry three fluid sensors, and no manufacturer publicly documents which measuring point C stands for or what limits apply to P274A. CARB obliges the module to detect broken circuits and readings outside the possible span on such inputs. By analogy with the main sensor, the module watches a thermistor fed through a pull-up resistor and stores this code when the circuit fails without stating whether it is shorted or open; makers that split the fault use P274C/P274D. A substitute value from another sensor normally keeps the car drivable, though temperature-dependent adaptation and protection functions may be restricted.
c: Connector or lead to sensor C damaged or corroded
s: Warning lamp
Implausible value for temperature C on the scan tool
Restricted adaptation or protection functions

P274B.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P274B.d: P274B means the sensor C signal is within electrical limits but does not fit the other information, for example because it barely changes while the gearbox warms or contradicts the other temperature values. The only public manufacturer reference is Ford bulletin 20-2044: 2020 Super Duty trucks with the 6.7 L diesel, built up to 5 February 2020, could light the MIL with P274B, often together with P203B and P2201, purely through PCM software; the remedy is reprogramming, about 0.6 h of labour. Ford does not say which measuring point C is. On other vehicles a sensor drifting with age, a high-resistance connection or contaminated fluid are more likely. P274A, P274C and P274D cover outright electrical faults.
c: PCM software (Ford 2020 Super Duty 6.7 L, TSB 20-2044)
Sensor C drifting or slow to respond
Added resistance in connector or lead
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Temperature C stays nearly constant while driving

P274C.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor C Circuit Low
P274C.d: P274C indicates that the sensor C signal has fallen below the lowest value the module accepts. With the negative-temperature-coefficient thermistors normally used for fluid temperature, a low voltage corresponds to very hot fluid, so the usual culprit is a signal lead touching ground or a sensor with an internal short; real heat rarely drives the reading that far. No manufacturer publishes P274C with a threshold. As orientation, Ford's 2012 strategy flags its main sensor below 0.05 V held for 5 to 12 s. Note that some makers, such as Mitsubishi on sensor B, define low by the computed temperature instead, which reverses the meaning. The module then discards C and works with a replacement value.
c: Signal lead of sensor C shorted to ground
s: Warning lamp
Temperature C shows an extremely hot value

P274D.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor C Circuit High
P274D.d: P274D is set when the sensor C signal climbs above its highest permitted value. On a thermistor supplied with 5 V via a resistor, that happens when the circuit opens – a broken wire, a corroded or unplugged connector – or when the signal line touches a voltage source; the display would then show fluid colder than any real climate produces. No manufacturer documents P274D publicly. For the main sensor, Ford's 2012 strategy uses above 4.6 V, and GM's 2023 dual-clutch module above 4745 mV for its sump sensor, both as electrical limits rather than temperatures. Until the fault is cleared the transmission may keep a cold-fluid strategy with delayed converter lock-up or more cautious clutch control.
c: Open circuit in sensor C lead or connector
s: Warning lamp
Temperature C shows an extremely cold value
Late converter lock-up or cautious shifting

P274E.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor C Circuit Intermittent
P274E.d: P274E stands for an unsteady sensor C signal: short interruptions or spikes that recover before a permanent low or high fault can mature. No manufacturer publishes this code or its debounce logic. Comparable intermittent coverage exists for the main sensor, where Ford's 2012 transmission strategy lists P0714 next to the open, short and in-range checks. Because the signal returns to normal, the warning may come and go, and the stored freeze frame is often the best clue: note temperature, speed and road condition when it appeared. A terminal with poor contact pressure, a harness rubbing on the case or moisture in the connector are typical; replacing the sensor without checking the wiring rarely helps.
c: Harness rubbing on the transmission case
s: Intermittent warning lamp
Temperature C drops out briefly on the scan tool

P274F.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor C Over Temperature Condition
P274F.d: P274F means sensor C reports a plausible value that is nevertheless above the overheat limit set in the calibration. It is a condition report rather than a circuit defect, and no manufacturer documents its threshold or the location of sensor C publicly. For the main sensor the equivalent is P0218, which Saab's Aisin gearbox stores at over 170 °C held longer than 10 s. Depending on where C measures – for example at a clutch pack or in a cooler line – the trigger may be a heavily loaded clutch or a restricted oil flow rather than overall sump heat. Expect protective measures such as torque limits or a changed shift pattern; let the unit cool, then check fluid level, condition and the cooling circuit.
c: High load or heavy clutch slip
Restricted oil flow or clogged cooler
Sensor C reading too hot within range
s: Overheating warning
Limited torque or altered shifting

P2750.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P2750.d: P2750 says that sensor C produces pulses whose speed is implausible – it disagrees with what the engaged gear and the other shaft speeds predict, jumps too fast or carries noise. No manufacturer documents P2750 publicly. The published checks for neighbouring sensors show what such a test looks like: GM's 2023 dual-clutch TCM compares its clutch 2 sensor with engine speed when the clutch is locked and faults it at 150 rpm difference for 1.1 s, and Ford counts dropouts and noise spikes on sensor B and flags a gear mismatch after 2.5 s. A mechanical cause is just as possible as an electrical one: swarf on a magnetic sensor tip, a cracked reluctor, or slipping clutches that make the ratio comparison fail.
c: Metal particles on the sensor tip distorting the signal
Electrical interference on the signal lead
Internal clutch slip making the speeds disagree
s: Check engine light after driving
Erratic shift points or flare between gears

P2751.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit No Signal
P2751.d: P2751 is reserved for a sensor C that sends no pulses at all while the vehicle is demonstrably under way. No manufacturer documents P2751 publicly. For comparison, Ford's intermediate shaft logic treats a reading below 250 rpm as missing – for 2.5 s on the 2024 ten-speeds, for 5 s on the 2012 transmissions – and it only runs once turbine and output speeds prove that the gearbox is turning. Unlike the circuit code P2749, nothing has to be electrically wrong: a sensor whose electronics have quit, or a toothed wheel that has shifted away from the sensor face, also ends in silence. Expect the module to switch to a substitute speed or a limp-home gear, and confirm on a test drive with the scan tool showing sensor C.
c: Reluctor missing, loose or too far from the sensor
s: Warning lamp during the drive
Limp-home gear or missing shifts

P2752.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit Intermittent
P2752.d: P2752 flags a sensor C circuit that cuts out now and then, briefly enough that neither the circuit code P2749 nor the no-signal code P2751 matures. No manufacturer documents P2752 publicly. The closest published counterpart is Ford's P2748 for sensor B on its ten-speed automatics, an intermittent check that runs continuously beside the circuit and plausibility tests. CARB expects every such transmission input to be monitored for circuit faults. In practice the culprit is mechanical stress on the wiring: a terminal that loosens when hot, insulation worn through on a bracket, or water that wicks into the plug. Watching sensor C while flexing the harness, and reading the freeze frame, are the most useful steps.
c: Insulation worn through at a bracket or edge
s: Sporadic warning lamp
Occasional rough shift

P2753.d: P2753 is set when the control module finds no closed circuit to the actuator that regulates transmission fluid cooling, usually an electrically switched coolant valve that opens or shuts the flow of engine coolant through the fluid heat exchanger. With the valve output open, the module cannot steer warm-up or cooling of the gearbox oil. Audi uses the code on the 2023 Q7 and SQ7: diagnostic notice AOS-26-09 of February 2026 supplies a tester hotfix because P275300 was stored without a matching guided test. Under CARB rules such an output must be checked for circuit continuity. Unlike P2754 and P2755 no short is involved, only missing continuity from a broken wire, loose pin or burnt coil. Fluid may run hotter under load or warm up more slowly.
c: Open coil in the transmission fluid cooling valve
Loose or corroded connector at the valve, often after coolant contact
Broken control wire between module and valve
Faulty output stage in the control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Transmission fluid warms up slowly or runs hot when towing
Transmission overheat warning in severe cases

P2754.t: Transmission Fluid Cooler Control Circuit Low
P2754.d: P2754 reports that the drive line to the transmission fluid cooling actuator sits at too low a voltage, which in practice means a short to ground or a heavily loaded output. The module then cannot switch the coolant valve or cooler control as intended, and depending on design the valve may remain permanently open or closed. No manufacturer documents P2754 publicly. Audi applies the neighbouring open-circuit code P2753 to the cooling valve on the 2023 Q7 and SQ7, which shows where the fault sits; CARB requires output components to be monitored for shorts as well as opens. Typical culprits are chafed insulation touching the body, water in the connector or a shorted winding. Many output stages shut themselves off to protect against overload.
c: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Water or coolant in the valve connector
Shorted turns in the valve coil
s: Check engine lamp on
Fluid temperature higher or lower than normal for the conditions
Usually no change in shift behaviour

P2755.t: Transmission Fluid Cooler Control Circuit High
P2755.d: With P2755 the module sees a high level on the cooler actuator line at a moment when its driver should pull it down, the signature of a short to battery voltage or of a low-side driver that no longer switches. The cooling valve then either cannot be activated or stays energised all the time. No manufacturer publishes P2755; the component is the same one that Audi diagnoses on the 2023 Q7 and SQ7 under the open-circuit code P2753, and CARB treats such outputs as monitored comprehensive components. A damaged harness rubbing against a powered wire, a defective valve with an internal short to its supply pin, or a failed output transistor are the usual findings. Unlike P2754 a fuse rarely blows, so the fault can persist unnoticed until fluid temperatures drift.
c: Control wire shorted to a battery-voltage line
Valve internally shorted to its supply terminal
Module output transistor no longer switching
s: Check engine lamp on
Cooling valve permanently on or off
Slower warm-up of the transmission in cold weather

P2756.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid
P2756.d: P2756 is the base code for the solenoid that meters apply pressure to the torque converter clutch. On its own it names only the component; in UDS-based systems a failure-type byte says what went wrong. Toyota shows this use in bulletin T-SB-0160-18 for the 2017–2018 Highlander and Sienna with the eight-speed automatic: P27567F, a stuck-off result for the lockup pressure solenoid, is one of eleven transmission codes that justify a remanufactured transaxle when a whine, harsh shifts or reduced power accompany it. The more specific siblings P2757 to P2764 split the same component into functional and electrical faults. For the driver a fault here typically means no or unstable converter lockup, higher engine speed at cruise and more heat in the fluid.
c: Internal transmission damage or debris in the valve body (Toyota 8-speed)
Lockup pressure solenoid sticking or worn
Wiring or connector fault on the solenoid circuit
s: Converter lockup missing or unstable
Higher engine speed and fuel use at steady speed
Whine noise or harsh shifts (Toyota 8-speed)

P2757.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P2757.d: P2757 means the converter clutch was commanded to apply, yet the speed difference between engine and turbine stayed too large, so the lockup never really happened. It is a functional verdict: the circuit may be electrically sound while the valve, the hydraulic feed or the clutch lining fails to deliver. Toyota uses it on the 2014–2019 Corolla CVT, where it points to shift solenoid SL; bulletin T-SB-0150-16 replaces the valve body. On 2016 Ram 3500 to 5500 trucks with the Aisin AS69RC six-speed, bulletin 21-027-16 traces it to a dislodged snap ring inside the converter, and an FCA tech tip notes the code returns during a light-throttle lockup attempt. Expect higher revs at cruise, more fuel use and hotter fluid.
c: Sticking lockup solenoid or valve body (Toyota CVT solenoid SL)
Internal converter fault such as a dislodged snap ring (Ram AS69RC)
s: Engine speed stays high at steady cruise
Higher fuel consumption
Transmission fluid runs hot
Check engine lamp on

P2758.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Stuck On
P2758.d: P2758 is the opposite of P2757: the converter clutch stays engaged although the module has asked it to release. Ford detects it when slip remains below 20 rpm while the release command is active and input torque is above 60 Nm, and the fault has to show up in more than one gear.
