Ford's 2012 gasoline and 2023 diesel summaries flag P2758 as non-MIL: a locked converter can make the engine stall or the car shudder, but does not raise emissions or fuel use. Mitsubishi lists P2758 for the CVT of the 2022 Outlander as a one-trip code with MIL, so lamp behaviour depends on the maker. Typical symptoms are a stall when stopping, a jolt on engagement or rough idle in gear. A sticking valve or dirty fluid is the usual root.
c: Lockup pressure valve stuck in the apply position
Debris or varnish in the valve body
s: Engine stalls or nearly stalls when coming to a stop
Shudder or jolt when selecting a gear
Warning lamp depends on manufacturer (Ford none, Mitsubishi MIL)

P2759.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Electrical
P2759.d: P2759 is a general electrical fault on the control circuit of the converter clutch pressure solenoid, used where a module cannot distinguish an open from a ground or supply short. No manufacturer documents P2759 publicly. The principle is visible in Ford's 2012 summary: the TCC output is pulse-width driven and a feedback line from the driver reveals opens and shorts, while makers such as GM report each case separately under P2761, P2763 and P2764. CARB requires this circuit check for transmission outputs. A meter test of coil resistance and of each wire to ground and to battery usually narrows it down quickly. Until repaired, many controllers inhibit lockup, so cruise rpm and fluid temperature rise slightly.
c: Damaged wire or connector between TCM and solenoid
s: No converter lockup
Slightly higher fuel consumption
Warning lamp on

P275A.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor D Circuit
P275A.d: P275A flags an electrical fault in the circuit of transmission fluid temperature sensor D, the fourth position in the SAE lettering. A gearbox with four separate fluid temperature inputs is rare, and no manufacturer publicly assigns sensor D or describes when P275A is stored. CARB requires every such powertrain input to be checked for interrupted circuits and for values beyond the sensor span. The general circuit code fits modules that cannot or do not distinguish between an open and a short; where they can, P275C and P275D apply. Diagnosis follows the usual path: read the live value of D next to the other temperature readings, inspect the connector, then measure the resistance of sensor and lead.
c: Fault in connector or lead of sensor D
s: Warning lamp
Temperature D missing or implausible on the scan tool

P275B.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P275B.d: P275B is the rationality code for sensor D: the circuit is electrically sound, yet the value does not behave like real fluid temperature. Published tests on other fluid sensors show what modules look for – a warm-up check (GM's 2025 TCMs expect the main sensor to pass 15 °C within a calibrated time), a stuck-value check and a rate check against impossible jumps, such as Mitsubishi's rejection of 10 °C changes within 80 ms on its dual-clutch sensor B. Which of these a maker applies to D is not documented publicly, and no manufacturer lists P275B. Ageing of the thermistor, a contact with added resistance or oil sludge on the sensor tip can all produce a believable but wrong reading.
c: Sensor D thermistor aged or slow
Sludge or deposits on the sensor tip
s: Warning lamp after repeated detection
Temperature D lags behind or deviates from the other readings

P275C.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
P275C.d: P275C reports that sensor D delivers less signal than the module considers possible. Read against an NTC thermistor this means a reading far hotter than the fluid could be, which almost always points to a pinched or melted lead touching ground, or to a short inside the sensor body. P275C is not documented by any manufacturer. As a frame of reference, GM's 2023 dual-clutch TCM judges its sump sensor too low below 200 mV for 500 ms. Mitsubishi shows that the meaning can also be inverted, since its dual-clutch unit sets the sensor B low code at −40 °C or colder. Before replacing parts, unplug the sensor: if the value jumps to the cold end, the fault lies in the sensor, otherwise in the harness.
c: Pinched or melted lead of sensor D touching ground
s: Warning lamp
Temperature D shows an impossibly hot value

P275D.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor D Circuit High
P275D.d: P275D is stored when the sensor D signal rises past the top of its window. With a thermistor on a pull-up resistor the voltage climbs towards the supply when current can no longer flow, so an interrupted lead, a pushed-back terminal or an unplugged connector is the usual explanation, followed by a short to a voltage source. No manufacturer publishes P275D with limits; for the main sensor GM's 2024 dual-clutch TCM uses more than 4745 mV over 500 ms, and Ford's 2012 strategy more than 4.6 V. A quick check is to measure the resistance from the module side or to bridge the connector briefly with a suitable resistor. Until repaired, the gearbox may treat the oil as cold.
c: Interrupted lead or pushed-back terminal at sensor D
Signal lead shorted to a voltage source
s: Warning lamp
Temperature D shows an extremely cold value

P275E.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent
P275E.d: P275E marks an intermittent sensor D circuit: the value drops out or spikes for moments and then returns, too briefly for P275C or P275D. Public manufacturer documentation for this code is lacking; the closest published counterpart is the main sensor's P0714, which Ford's 2012 strategy names among its fluid temperature checks. Such faults typically follow mechanical or thermal stress, appearing on rough roads, after a long run or once the gearbox is hot. Depending on what the module uses D for, drivers may notice little beyond the warning lamp. Useful steps are logging D during a test drive and flexing the harness while watching the reading, then repairing the terminal rather than swapping the sensor blindly.
c: Heat-damaged lead that fails when hot
Sensor D with an internal loose connection
s: Warning lamp that appears sporadically
Dropouts of temperature D in a data log

P275F.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor D Over Temperature Condition
P275F.d: P275F is the overheating condition for sensor D: the reading is valid and above the calibrated limit. No manufacturer documents the code, the limit or where sensor D sits. The sensor A equivalent P0218 gives an idea of the logic – Saab's Aisin automatic sets it beyond 170 °C lasting over ten seconds and recommends fresh fluid afterwards, because overheated oil loses its additives. A transmission that reports heat at a fourth measuring point is usually working at its edge: heavy trailer, steep climbs, slipping clutch or converter, or a cooler that cannot keep up. The module typically protects itself with altered shifting or less torque; the code is not an electrical fault, so check fluid and cooling first.
c: Heavy trailer or long steep climbs
Cooler blocked or not keeping up
s: Overheating warning or message
Changed shifting or reduced power
Dark or burnt-smelling fluid

P2760.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Intermittent
P2760.d: P2760 records a converter clutch control circuit that drops out now and then and recovers by itself. Ford names it in its 2024 OBD summary as the circuit-intermittent result of the TCC solenoid, written as P0740 with failure byte 1F; its electrical check compares the driver feedback with the commanded state and reacts when they disagree for 1.5 seconds. Because the fault comes and goes, a static measurement in the workshop often finds nothing, and the freeze-frame data is the best clue. Loose terminals at the transmission case connector, a wire rubbing on a bracket or moisture that only causes trouble when hot are the classic causes. The driver may notice lockup cutting in and out, felt as a brief rpm flare at cruise.
c: Loose or spread terminal at the case connector
Wire chafing intermittently against a bracket
s: Lockup drops out briefly, felt as an rpm flare
Fault not reproducible in the workshop
Warning lamp may come and go

P2761.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit/Open
P2761.d: P2761 says the TCM has lost continuity to the converter clutch pressure solenoid. GM documents the check in its six-speed TCM tables (16OBDG08 for the MW7 unit in Silverado/Sierra, 18OBDG04 for the T87A): with the driver switched off, an impedance of 173 kΩ or more counts as open, while 9.6 kΩ or less does not; after three hardware counts an intrusive test opens the low-side driver, and two confirming counts set the Type B code. The same tables block the stuck-off test P0741 while P2761 is pending. On 2023 Ram heavy-duty trucks with the 6.7 l Cummins, bulletin 1807223 lists P2761 among codes caused by a leaking capacitor inside the engine controller, so the solenoid is not always to blame.
c: Broken wire or backed-out pin to the solenoid
Internal controller fault (Ram 6.7 l ECM capacitor leak)
s: No torque converter lockup
MIL on after two trips (GM Type B)
Higher cruise rpm and fuel use

P2762.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2762.d: P2762 covers a solenoid circuit that is neither open nor shorted but does not behave as commanded. In GM's six-speed TCM tables for the MW7 (2016) and T87A (2018) the module compares desired with measured solenoid current; a gap of 0.5 A or more in at least 40 of fewer than 80 samples sets the code as Type B, with battery voltage above 10 V. For the T76 six-speed of 2016, GM instead calls it a rationality test that fails when the hardware layer reports an out-of-range voltage in 4.4 of 5 seconds, and lists it without MIL. Rising coil resistance, a weak supply or ground, or a current-sensing fault in the TCM are typical. Lockup may feel harsh or soft, since the pressure no longer follows the target.
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Weak supply voltage or poor ground at the TCM
Current sensing fault inside the TCM
s: Harsh or slipping converter lockup
Shudder at light throttle in higher gears
Warning lamp depending on application (GM T76 none)

P2763.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit High
P2763.d: P2763 means the control circuit of the lockup pressure solenoid reads high. GM's 2018 T87A table treats it as a short to power, at 1.16 Ω or less to a voltage source while the driver is on, Type B. Its 2016 tables add variants: on the T76 six-speed the high-voltage flag also covers an open circuit and must persist 4.4 of 5 seconds over two trips; on the T54 CVT the module sets it when at least 750 mA is commanded but 200 mA or less flows for over 5 seconds. Subaru cites P2763 in bulletin 16-149-25 for the TR580 CVT in 2020–2023 Legacy, Outback, Crosstrek and Forester Wilderness: condensation can wet the valve-body connector, cured with a redesigned control valve plus connector cover. Ford's 2012 6R80 also files TCC driver faults here.
c: Moisture in the valve-body connector (Subaru TR580)
Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open circuit where the maker includes it in this code (GM T76/T54)
s: No converter lockup, higher cruise rpm
Transmission warning and MIL
Other solenoid high codes at the same time (Subaru)

P2764.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P2764.d: P2764 is the low counterpart of P2763: the lockup solenoid circuit is pulled toward ground. GM's 2018 T87A table defines it as 0.01 Ω or less to vehicle ground, checked while the driver is off every 6.25 ms. In 2016, the T76 six-speed sets it on a ground-short flag in 4.4 of 5 seconds after a single trip, and the T54 CVT when the hardware sees a ground short for 480 ms or longer while lockup is on. FCA's remanufactured-transmission note for the 62TE adds a twist: if P0740 or P2764 come with jerking or slipping and the solenoid tests good, the torque converter itself has failed and must be replaced. Ford's 2012 6R80 also monitors its TCC driver under this code. Lockup is usually disabled until repair.
c: Solenoid winding shorted to its housing
Failed torque converter when the solenoid tests good (FCA 62TE)
s: No lockup and higher fuel consumption
Jerking or slipping (62TE)
MIL after one trip on some GM units

P2765.t: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit
P2765.d: P2765 is the circuit code of a second input speed sensor, B, and what B measures varies. On Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch box (2012) it is the input shaft 2 sensor for reverse and the even gears, faulted when the TCM hardware detects a circuit failure. Audi bulletin 2032211/3 for the 0B5 S tronic (S4/S5 2010–14, RS5/S6/S7 2013–14) lists P2765 among codes caused by a faulty sensor module G676 carrying the input speed sensors; it is replaced with its harness, which means removing the gearbox. Nissan's NTB14-019 (2014 Rogue, CVT8) ties P2765 to moisture on the pins of the secondary speed sensor. Mitsubishi's 2019 CVT uses it for the turbine sensor: under 150 rpm for 5 s with the primary pulley above 500 rpm.
c: Moisture or corrosion at the sensor B connector pins
Defective sensor B or integrated sensor module inside the gearbox
Open or shorted wiring between sensor and TCM
s: Check engine light and gearbox malfunction message
Limp-home mode, sometimes without reverse or even gears
Slow take-off and no torque converter lock-up

P2766.t: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2766.d: P2766 marks a sensor B signal that is present but erratic or implausible. Ford's 2012 strategy applies it to the DPS6 dual-clutch box, where sensor B reads input shaft 2. In Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT, sensor B is in fact the secondary pulley sensor on the output side: with the converter locked and engine, primary pulley and input speeds within 1,000 rpm of one another, a pulley ratio above 2.9 or below 0.3 for 5 s sets the code, two trips, MIL on. Infiniti bulletin ITB20-027 for the 2019 QX50 CVT covers a permanent P2766, among other transmission codes, that will not clear after the prescribed procedure; the fix is a new TCM. Erratic signals point to a dirty sensor, interference, or a loose fit.
c: Sensor B fouled with metal debris or not seated firmly
Interference or poor ground on the signal circuit
TCM fault keeping the code stored permanently
s: Check engine light after two drives
Sluggish acceleration, manual mode unavailable
Torque converter lock-up disabled

P2767.t: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit No Signal
P2767.d: P2767 reports that pulses from sensor B are missing. Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch box of 2012 checks input shaft 2 for lack of signal under this code, alongside P2765 for circuit faults and P2766 for erratic readings. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT, whose sensor B watches the secondary pulley, looks for a sudden collapse: a speed of at least 1,000 rpm that reads zero only 10 ms later, held for 0.5 s – a pattern typical of a wire or plug letting go, rather than a slow sensor death. It is a two-trip code with MIL there; the fail-safe gives slow starts and acceleration, no lock-up and no manual mode. Check connector and harness first, then the sensor; where B sits inside a sealed unit, the repair may involve the whole assembly.
c: Connector or terminal letting go, open signal wire
Sensor B failed with no output
s: Warning lamp and transmission fail-safe
Slow start-off and weak acceleration
Manual shift mode not available

P2768.t: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2768.d: P2768 stands for a sensor B signal that drops out or jumps only now and then. Audi bulletin 2067653/9 (2024) covers 2020–24 A4, A5, A6, A7 and Q5 models with gearboxes built from 15 June 2020 to 30 November 2023: if P276800 is stored as passive/sporadic, alone or with P071800, control unit J217 or, where not sold separately, the mechatronic unit is replaced; an active entry calls for normal guided diagnosis. Drivers see a gearbox fault message, limp mode or no reverse. Nissan bulletin NTB20-086 treats a permanent P2768 on 2019 Sentra and Versa with the RE0F11A CVT as a TCM fault. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT sets it when the output-side sensor B claims more than 16,212 rpm for 2 s, an impossible value.
c: Transmission control unit fault on affected production batches
Loose contact or damaged wire in the sensor B circuit
Electrical noise producing false speed spikes
s: Gearbox malfunction message, intermittent
Limp mode, loss of power or no reverse gear
Occasional missed up- or downshifts

P2769.d: P2769 reports a low level on the converter clutch circuit, in practice a short to ground. It belongs to the P0740 family for converters with a single TCC solenoid, unlike P2764, which refers to a dedicated pressure control solenoid. Ford uses it in its 2024 OBD summary for the 6R80, 6R140, 10R60, 10R80 and the 8F front-drive units: P2769 carries failure byte 11 (short to ground), P2770 byte 12 (short to power) and P0740 byte 13 (open). The electrical test runs continuously and flags a mismatch between driver feedback and commanded state lasting 1.5 seconds. The TCM then disables lockup, so engine speed stays higher at cruise and fluid temperature climbs. A pinched harness at the case connector or a shorted coil are typical.
c: TCC control wire pinched or chafed to ground
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
s: No converter lockup
Higher rpm and fuel use at highway speed
Check engine lamp on

P276A.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Motor Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P276A.d: P276A means the power feed to the motor of a second electric transmission fluid pump, labelled B, is interrupted. Such pumps keep hydraulic pressure or lubrication alive when the engine-driven pump is idle, for instance during stop-start or in a dual-clutch gearbox. No manufacturer documents P276A publicly. Audi shows what pump B is in bulletin 34-17-25 for the 2017 A4, A5, A6 and 2018 Q5 with seven-speed dual-clutch units 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL: the gear oil pump V553, which reports supply faults to the TCM under P276B00. CARB requires such actuators to be checked for open circuits. A blown fuse, a corroded pump connector or a broken supply wire are typical; with the pump dead the gearbox may restrict stop-start or limit performance.
c: Blown fuse in the pump supply
Broken supply wire or relay contact
s: Transmission warning lamp
Stop-start deactivated
Reduced performance or limp mode in some designs

P276B.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Motor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P276B.d: P276B is set when the supply voltage reaching the motor of auxiliary transmission pump B sags below its lower limit. Audi names this code in bulletin 34-17-25 (revision of September 2017) covering 2017 A4/A5/A6 models and the 2018 Q5 fitted with the 0CJ, 0CK or 0CL twin-clutch gearbox. Pump B there is the gear oil pump V553, and P276B00 may appear together with lost communication U28A00, stuck-on P27A600 and performance P27A300. The bulletin attributes a rattle from under the car to a supplier assembly issue and calls for a new pump with new bolts; transmission fluid must not reach the electrical connector during removal. Apart from that case, weak batteries, high-resistance grounds and partial shorts can pull the voltage down.
c: High resistance in supply or ground of the pump
Low system voltage from a weak battery
s: Rattle noise from under the vehicle (Audi)
Transmission warning lamp
Further pump B codes stored

P276C.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Motor Supply Voltage Circuit High
P276C.d: P276C flags an excessive voltage on the motor supply of auxiliary pump B. Either the circuit is shorted to another powered line, the pump module measures wrongly, or the vehicle charging system itself overshoots. No manufacturer documents P276C publicly. Audi's bulletin 34-17-25 identifies pump B on its 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL dual-clutch units as the gear oil pump V553 and lists the low-voltage sibling P276B for it; P0B0B is the matching high code for pump A. CARB requires actuators to be watched for out-of-range electrical values. An overvoltage can overheat the pump electronics, so many modules switch the pump off. Before replacing parts, measure the charging voltage at running engine and inspect the supply wiring for chafing.
c: Supply wire shorted to another powered circuit
Faulty measurement in the pump control electronics
s: Transmission warning lamp
Pump switched off, stop-start unavailable
Other overvoltage codes if charging is at fault

P276D.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Motor Current
P276D.d: P276D is the general current code for the motor of auxiliary transmission pump B: the measured current does not fit the commanded speed or load, without the module saying whether it is too low or too high. The narrower siblings P276E and P276F carry that distinction, and P0C26 is the same check for pump A. No manufacturer documents P276D publicly. For the component, Audi's bulletin 34-17-25 names the gear oil pump V553 as pump B in its 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL dual-clutch gearboxes and describes an assembly defect that made the pump rattle. CARB requires that electric actuators are checked for proper function. Worn brushes or bearings, a jammed impeller, contaminated fluid or a bad ground typically change the current draw before the pump fails.
c: Worn bearings or binding impeller in pump B
Poor ground or connector resistance at the pump
s: Noise from the pump area
Transmission warning lamp
Stop-start or shift quality restricted

P276E.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Motor Current Low
P276E.d: P276E tells you that the motor of a second electric transmission fluid pump, called B, takes less current than its commanded duty would require. A small draw usually means the motor is not really working: a broken winding, worn brushes, extra resistance in the feed or ground, or an impeller spinning freely because it has no fluid to move. No manufacturer documents P276E publicly. Ford shows the same check for pump A in its 2024 OBD summary for the 10R60/10R80 and 8F57 gearboxes, where an under-current reported by the pump becomes P0C27 (UDS P0C26_18). What pump B is depends on the car; Audi names the gear oil pump V553 on its 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL twin-clutch units. P276F covers the opposite case. Expect stop-start to be withheld while the fault is present.
c: Worn brushes or open winding in the pump B motor
Corroded connector or high-resistance feed/ground to the pump
Low fluid level so the impeller runs without load
Faulty current measurement in the pump controller or TCM
s: Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Engine stop-start no longer operates
Delayed or harsh drive engagement after an engine restart

P276F.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Motor Current High
P276F.d: P276F is stored when the motor of auxiliary pump B pulls more current than the module allows. Excess draw points to a motor that is working too hard or is electrically damaged: a dragging bearing, debris or varnish in the pump, very cold thick fluid, a partially shorted winding or a chafed lead touching ground. No manufacturer documents P276F publicly. Ford's 2024 OBD summary shows the matching pump A logic for the 10R60/10R80 and 8F57 transmissions, where the pump itself reports an over-current that the TCM files as P0C28 (UDS P0C26_19). To protect wiring and electronics, most controllers then switch the pump off, so the vehicle loses the functions that depend on it. If the motor stops completely, P277C is the more specific code; P276E is the low-current sibling.
c: Dragging bearing or debris inside pump B
Chafed pump lead shorting to ground
s: Warning lamp with transmission fault message
Stop-start function disabled
Possible whine or rattle from the pump area

P2770.d: P2770 flags a high level on the torque converter clutch circuit, meaning a short to the battery supply on the TCC solenoid or its wiring. Ford documents it in the 2024 OBD summary for the 6R80, 6R140, 10R60/10R80 and the 8F front-drive families: P2770 corresponds to UDS P0740_12, while P0740_13 covers an open line and P2769 (P0740_11) a short to ground. One table even shows P0744, the older code for the same short to power, beside P2770 under the same failure byte. The electrical check runs at all times; the stated monitoring duration for an electrical fault is 5 seconds. The TCM then keeps the converter unlocked, so cruising rpm and fluid temperature rise and fuel use worsens. A harness rubbing against a powered wire or a damaged case connector are the usual finds.
c: TCC circuit chafed against a powered wire
Damaged or contaminated transmission case connector
Internal short in the TCC solenoid
Faulty TCC output driver in the TCM/PCM
s: MIL on
No converter lockup, higher rpm at highway speed
Higher fuel consumption and fluid temperature

P2771.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Low Switch Circuit
P2771.d: P2771 concerns the input that reports whether the transfer case sits in its low range. GM uses it on 2016 Silverado/Sierra with the MW7 gearbox as a plausibility test in the TCM: if the switch says high range while gear ratio math says low, or the reverse, for at least 0.5 s with fluid between 20 and 130 °C, the Type B code sets. The 2014 LML diesel ECM runs a similar comparison from turbine speed, output speed and ratio. GM's PIP4966B links P2771 on 2007–2011 trucks with Magna transfer cases to a speed-sensor tone wheel shifting on its shaft, or output shaft play, that corrupts the speed signal. Toyota's T-SB-0093-25 shows P2771 with subtype 11 (short to ground) on 2024–2025 Tacoma, fixed with a new shift actuator and breather hose. P2772–P2774 split the fault types.
c: Loose tone wheel or moving output shaft in the transfer case (GM PIP4966B)
Transfer case shift actuator damaged, e.g. by water through the breather (Toyota Tacoma)
Low-range switch or position encoder defective
Damaged wiring or corroded connector between switch and control module
s: Check engine light, often together with a flashing 4WD indicator
Erratic speedometer or ABS warning when a speed signal is affected
Low range not engaging, or transfer case disengaging under load

P2772.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Low Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P2772.d: P2772 flags a low-range switch whose signal is electrically valid but does not fit what the drivetrain is actually doing. No manufacturer documents P2772 publicly. The natural cross-check is the one GM describes under P2771: the control unit derives the active range from turbine or input speed, output speed and the resulting ratio, then compares that with the switch. A switch reporting low while the ratio shows high, or a switch that never changes after a range shift, fits this code. Root causes are mostly mechanical: a worn shift fork or encoder, a switch out of adjustment, or a speed signal disturbed by shaft play. CARB requires such rationality checks for inputs to monitored systems. The driver may see a flashing 4WD lamp or find low range unavailable.
c: Low-range switch or encoder worn or out of adjustment
Range shift not completed (shift fork, actuator or linkage)
Output or turbine speed signal distorted, so the calculated range is wrong
s: Flashing 4WD indicator or range message on the cluster
Low range refused or engaged only after several attempts
Warning light depending on manufacturer

P2773.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Low Switch Circuit Low
P2773.d: P2773 is stored when the signal line of the low-range switch stays below its permitted voltage band, typically because it is pulled to ground. No manufacturer documents P2773 publicly. Toyota shows that the fault type exists in practice but files it differently: on 2024–2025 Tacoma the short to ground appears as P2771 with failure byte 11, and bulletin T-SB-0093-25 traces it to a shift actuator damaged through the transfer case breather. Typical triggers for a low signal are chafed insulation touching the body, water in the actuator or connector, or a switch shorted internally. Unlike P2772 this is a purely electrical finding, and unlike P2774 the reading is too low rather than too high. The vehicle may ignore low range or default the 4WD system.
c: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Moisture in shift actuator or connector (Toyota Tacoma breather issue)
s: 4WD indicator flashing and warning light on
Low range cannot be selected or is reported permanently

P2774.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Low Switch Circuit High
P2774.d: P2774 reports that the low-range switch input sits above its valid voltage range. With a pulled-up signal line this usually points to an open circuit, a broken ground at the switch or a short to battery voltage. No manufacturer documents P2774 publicly; the monitoring logic follows the CARB demand for out-of-range checks on inputs, and the switch itself is the one GM and Toyota describe under P2771. A connector pushed off at the transfer case after service work or a wire torn by the propeller shaft are frequent physical reasons. In contrast to P2773 the module sees too much voltage, and in contrast to P2772 the reading is not merely implausible but outside the electrical window. Low range may be unavailable or the 4WD lamp may flash.
c: Open signal or ground wire, connector unplugged at the transfer case
Signal wire shorted to battery voltage
s: Warning light and flashing 4WD indicator
Low range not recognised after selection

P2775.d: P2775 covers an upshift paddle or tip switch whose voltage is electrically possible but belongs to neither of its two legal states. GM's twin-clutch TCM tables for 2023 and 2024 read the plus paddle as an analogue input: pressed should give 2.2–3.52 V, released 3.826–4.744 V. If the voltage sits outside both windows for 120 s, P2775 sets as Type C, so without MIL. Ford's 2024 summary for the TR9070 twin-clutch gearbox lists P2775 as illegal voltage on the upshift paddle input. Contact wear, moisture or a resistor drifting inside the switch are the usual reasons. A paddle held too long belongs to P0815, readings beyond the band to P2776 or P2777. Manual shifting by paddle is normally disabled.
c: Worn or dirty contacts or drifting coding resistor in the paddle
Added resistance in the clock spring or steering wheel connector
Moisture or spilled liquid in the switch
s: Upshift paddle has no effect, manual mode unavailable
Message on the cluster, normally no check engine light

P2776.d: P2776 means the upshift switch input has dropped below the lowest voltage the module accepts. In GM's 2023 twin-clutch TCM the TAPUP input is supposed to stay above 2.519 V even with the paddle pulled; a lower reading, held for at least 150 ms with battery voltage between 8.75 and 18 V and the engine not cranking, sets P2776 as Type C without MIL. Ford's 2024 TR9070 summary assigns P2776 to the out-of-window-low case of the upshift paddle. A low reading normally means the signal wire is touching ground, for example chafed at the clock spring, or the switch is shorted inside. Compared with P2775 the value is clearly outside the band, and P2777 is the mirror image. Tap upshifts stop working while normal automatic driving continues.
c: Signal wire shorted to ground, e.g. in the clock spring area
Liquid in switch or connector creating a leak path to ground
s: Upshift paddle or tip function inoperative
Manual mode message, no check engine light on GM

P2777.d: P2777 is the over-voltage counterpart for the upshift switch. GM's 2023 twin-clutch TCM watches the TAPUP input and counts up a timer once it exceeds 4.774 V; after 150 ms above that limit, with supply voltage in the 8.75–18 V band, the code is logged as Type C, so no MIL. Ford's July 2024 OBD summary lists P2777 as out-of-window-high on the TR9070 upshift paddle. Because the released paddle already rests near the top of the range, an open signal circuit, a missing switch ground or a disconnected steering wheel plug pushes the reading over the limit quickly. A short to battery voltage is less common. P2776 is the opposite case, P2775 the implausible but in-range one. The paddle does nothing until the circuit is repaired.
c: Open signal or ground circuit, steering wheel connector loose
Broken track in the clock spring
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source
s: Upshift paddle without function
Driver information message about manual shifting

P2778.d: P2778 is meant for an upshift switch signal that jumps around or drops out briefly instead of staying in one state. No manufacturer documents P2778 publicly. GM's 2023/2024 twin-clutch TCM and Ford's TR9070 split the same paddle input into low, high, implausible and stuck faults (P2775–P2777, P0815) but list no intermittent check, so on those cars a flickering contact will rather end up as one of these. CARB expects inputs to be watched for circuit and rationality faults, which is the frame this code fits. Practical causes are a clock spring with a cracked track that opens at certain wheel angles, a loose crimp in the column connector, or a worn paddle contact. Symptoms come and go: occasional ignored upshifts or unwanted gear requests.
c: Clock spring track cracked, opening at certain steering angles
Loose terminal or poor crimp in the column or wheel connector
Worn or bouncing contact in the paddle
s: Upshift requests occasionally ignored
Occasional unwanted upshift requests
Fault comes and goes, often depending on steering angle

P2779.d: P2779 is the plausibility fault of the downshift paddle or tip switch. GM's 2023 and 2024 TCM tables for the twin-clutch gearbox define two voltage windows for the minus paddle: 2.2–3.52 V when pulled and 3.826–4.744 V at rest. A reading caught between or around these windows for 120 s is treated as invalid and logged as Type C, no MIL. The same tables use P0816 for a minus paddle held too long. Ford's TR9070 entry in the 2024 OBD summary calls P2779 an illegal voltage on the downshift paddle input. Because the value is still inside the electrical range, suspects are a corroded contact, a drifting resistor in the switch or added resistance in the clock spring rather than a plain short. Paddle downshifts are usually locked out.
c: Corroded contacts or drifting coding resistor in the minus paddle
Added resistance in the clock spring
Corrosion in the steering wheel connector
s: Downshift paddle inoperative
Manual mode refused, usually no MIL

P277A.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Hydraulic Leakage
P277A.d: P277A is not an electrical fault. The motor of auxiliary pump B runs, yet the oil it delivers escapes before pressure can build, so the module concludes that the hydraulic path around the pump leaks. Typical suspects are a damaged pump seal or O-ring, a check valve that does not close, worn bores in the valve body or a fluid level so low that the pump draws air. No manufacturer documents P277A publicly. How such a test can look is shown by GM's 2025 TCM tables for pump A on a CVT: during an engine auto-start the pump is commanded, and if both pulley pressure sensors stay under 200 kPa while more than 400 kPa is requested, a performance code follows. P0B0C is the leakage code for pump A. Without pressure, stop-start restarts may be harsh or disabled.
c: Damaged pump seal or O-ring at the pump mounting
Low transmission fluid level letting the pump draw air
Check valve in the pump circuit not sealing
Worn valve body bores causing internal leakage
s: Stop-start disabled or rough engine restarts
Delayed drive engagement after standstill
Warning lamp, possibly fluid traces under the gearbox

P277B.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Driver Circuit Performance
P277B.d: P277B concerns the power stage that energises the motor of auxiliary pump B, wherever it sits: inside a separate pump controller or in the transmission module. The stage is switched on, but what comes back – current, speed or a status signal – does not fit the command, so the module rates the driver as implausible rather than reporting a plain open or short. No manufacturer documents P277B publicly. For pump A, Ford's 2024 OBD summary (10R60/10R80, 8F57) lists a related case: the pump flags implausible current together with implausible speed, stored as P0C29 (UDS P0C29_92). Overheated or failing driver electronics, a poor ground, low system voltage and a pump that loads the stage abnormally are the usual triggers. The gearbox then runs without the pump's support, which mainly affects stop-start.
c: Failing output stage in the pump controller or TCM
Poor ground or low system voltage at the driver
Pump motor loading the driver abnormally
Loose or corroded pins between driver and pump
s: Transmission warning or service message
Stop-start unavailable
Jerky drive-off after engine restarts

P277C.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Motor Stalled
P277C.d: P277C means the motor of auxiliary pump B is commanded to turn but stands still or nearly so. Volvo uses it: its technical journal 36774 covers 2024–2027 mild-hybrid S60, S90, V60/V90 Cross Country, XC40, XC60 and XC90 models with the Aisin TG-81SC eight-speed, where the TCM stores P277C07. If the code shows up only intermittently, no warning appears and stop-start still works, Volvo says to clear it and not to replace anything. Confirmed with a warning and dead stop-start, gearboxes built before serial 25M8L30144 are replaced, while later units go to engineering support first. Ford's pump A equivalent is P0C2A, which its 2024 summary links to a pump that may have lost prime. A jammed impeller or seized bearing is the classic cause.
c: Jammed impeller or seized pump bearing
Known hardware issue in early gearboxes (Volvo TG-81SC before the serial break)
Pump lost prime because of low fluid
One-off detection without a real fault
s: Transmission warning message in the cluster
Stop-start not working
Shifts too early, too late or erratic

P277D.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Motor Over Temperature
P277D.d: P277D reports that the motor or the integrated electronics of auxiliary pump B have become too hot. Pumps of this kind measure their own temperature and stop before damage occurs; the code records that protective shutdown. Heat builds up when the pump runs long at high load, for example many stop-start phases in hot traffic, when it drags mechanically, when the fluid is overheated or degraded, or when its cooling path is blocked. No manufacturer documents P277D publicly. For pump A, Ford's 2024 summary of the 10R60/10R80 and 8F57 gearboxes has the counterpart: an over-temperature message from the pump becomes P175A, in UDS form P0C29_4B; P0DE4 is the generic pump A code. Once the pump has cooled it may work again, so a recurring code calls for checking current draw and fluid condition.
c: Long high-load operation in hot conditions
Mechanical drag raising motor current and heat
Faulty temperature sensing in the pump electronics
s: Stop-start temporarily unavailable, especially in hot weather
Warning lamp or transmission message

P277E.t: Clutch A Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement
P277E.d: P277E reports that a gear on the shaft served by clutch A dropped out of engagement by itself while that clutch was carrying the drive, without any shift being commanded. GM's 2023 TCM tables for its dual-clutch gearbox run this check continuously: if the synchronizer of the driving gear shows a speed difference although the odd-gear clutch slips by less than 50 rpm, and this lasts 1000 ms, the code is stored as Type A with immediate MIL. Ford's 2024 OBD summary lists it for the TR9070 dual-clutch unit as an unintended disengagement on the shaft carrying the odd gears. P277F covers the even shaft, P2711 is the generic version without a clutch letter. Drivers notice a sudden loss of drive or a jump to neutral, usually followed by limp mode with some gears blocked.
c: Worn shift-fork detent or rounded engagement teeth on an odd gear
Shift rod drifting due to internal hydraulic leakage or a weak actuator
Fork end positions not relearned after repair or module replacement
Faulty shaft speed signal making a slip appear at the synchronizer
s: Sudden loss of drive as if the gearbox had shifted into neutral
Odd gears locked out, limp mode with reduced gear choice
Warning lamp and transmission message in the cluster

P277F.t: Clutch B Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement
P277F.d: P277F is the even-gear twin of P277E: the controller has found that a gear carried by the shaft of clutch B lost its engagement on its own while the car was driving through that clutch. The evidence comes from speed sensors, which show the synchronizer of the active gear turning at a different speed even though clutch B is practically locked (GM: slip below 50 rpm, 1 s confirmation, Type A in the 2023 dual-clutch TCM tables). Ford's 2024 summary assigns the code to the even clutch shaft of its TR9070 gearbox. Typical reasons are worn fork detents or engagement teeth, a shift rod that creeps because of hydraulic leakage, or a fork position learned wrongly after a repair. The even gears are then often locked out, and a relearn with a scan tool is normally part of the fix.
c: Worn detent or engagement teeth on an even gear or its sleeve
Shift rod of the even shaft creeping due to leakage in the hydraulic unit
Wrong or missing fork position learning after repair
s: Momentary loss of drive in an even gear
Even gears unavailable, gearbox skips between odd gears
Warning lamp with stored transmission fault

P2780.d: P2780 tells you the downshift switch voltage has fallen under its lower limit. GM's twin-clutch TCM (tables 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07) checks the TAPDN input against 2.519 V; if the signal stays under that mark for 150 ms while the supply is inside 8.75–18 V and the starter is not engaged, P2780 is logged as Type C, no MIL. In Ford's TR9070 listing from July 2024, P2780 is the out-of-window-low entry for the downshift paddle. A minus-paddle signal pulled toward ground usually comes from a wire rubbed through near the steering column, a pinched harness behind the wheel trim or an internal short in the switch. P2781 is the high-side failure, P2779 the implausible value within range. Manual downshifts are lost; automatic operation carries on.
c: Signal wire rubbed through or pinched to ground
s: Downshift paddle has no effect
Manual mode not available, normally no check engine light

P2781.d: P2781 sets when the downshift switch input climbs above its upper voltage limit. GM's 2023 dual-clutch TCM tables cap the TAPDN signal at 4.774 V; staying above it for 150 ms produces a Type C entry, no MIL. Ford's TR9070 table in the 2024 summary uses P2781 for the out-of-window-high case of the downshift paddle. GM has a field case: Service Update N212350930 (February 2024) covers about 23,500 Chevrolet Corvettes of model year 2021 whose TCM wrongly reported P2781 as permanent, which could fail an inspection that reads permanent codes; the fix is new TCM software. Real faults are mostly an open signal or ground wire or a loose plug at the wheel. P2780 is the low-side twin, P2779 the in-range plausibility fault.
c: Open signal or ground circuit, loose connector at the wheel
TCM software reporting a false permanent code (2021 Corvette, N212350930)
Broken track in the clock spring
s: Downshift paddle not working
Permanent code shown at an emissions inspection although the paddle works (software case)

P2782.d: P2782 targets a downshift switch signal that flickers, bounces or vanishes for moments. No manufacturer documents P2782 publicly. The documented paddle monitors (GM's dual-clutch TCM tables of 2023/2024, Ford's TR9070 entry) cover low, high, implausible and held-too-long (P2779–P2781, P0816) without a separate dropout test, so such a fault there tends to surface under those codes. CARB's requirement to monitor transmission inputs for circuit and rationality faults is the basis for this code. A clock spring that loses contact only at certain steering angles is the classic cause, followed by a loose pin in the column connector and a minus paddle with a bouncing contact. The driver notices sporadic missed or unexpected downshifts that disappear again.
c: Clock spring losing contact at certain steering angles
Loose pin in the steering column connector
Bouncing or worn contact in the minus paddle
s: Downshift occasionally missed
Sporadic unexpected downshift request

P2783.d: P2783 warns that the torque converter is at risk of overheating. Ford's 2012 OBD summary shows one concrete use in its 6F front-drive six-speed. There, two valves route oil to the converter clutch; if the control valve hangs in its applied setting, no oil flows through an open converter and it heats up. The hardware was designed so the PCM can expose this: in third gear or higher with the clutch commanded open, it switches on shift solenoid E, which moves the second valve. If the converter then locks although it should stay open, P2783 is stored. Ford made the fault MIL-relevant and changes shift and lockup schedules to keep the clutch engaged as much as possible. Unlike P0218, which watches a fluid temperature sensor, this code addresses the converter itself.
c: TCC control valve stuck in the apply position
Debris or varnish in the valve body
Restricted converter or cooler oil flow
s: MIL on
Changed shift and lockup behaviour
Transmission overheating, burnt fluid smell

P2784.d: P2784 belongs to transmissions with two input or turbine speed sensors whose readings can be compared. When both are healthy their values agree, or differ only by a known ratio; P2784 is set when they drift apart for longer than the module tolerates while each circuit on its own looks fine. No manufacturer documents P2784 publicly, so it stays open which sensor pairs are compared in practice. The individual circuits have their own codes: P0715 family for sensor A and P2765 to P2768 for sensor B. Mitsubishi's 2019 CVT shows how sensor B can be the turbine sensor, diagnosed when it reads below 150 rpm for 5 s while the primary pulley turns faster than 500 rpm. Metal debris on a magnetic tip, a loose sensor or a damaged tone wheel are typical causes.
c: Metal debris on a magnetic speed sensor tip
One sensor giving a weak or distorted signal
Damaged tone wheel or excessive air gap
Signal interference from poor shielding or connectors
s: Harsh or erratic shifts
Emergency mode with fixed gear
MIL on

P2785.d: P2785 indicates that the actuator which opens and closes the clutch has become hotter than the controller allows. In automated manual and dry dual-clutch gearboxes this part is usually an electric motor or an electro-hydraulic unit; creeping, hill starts and stop-and-go traffic make it work hard, and the controller measures or models its temperature to protect windings and electronics. No manufacturer documents P2785 publicly with thresholds; CARB treats such gearbox actuators as monitored output components. A related case is Stellantis bulletin 21-040-26 for European Jeep Renegade and Compass with the 7-speed hybrid dual-clutch, where particles blocking an actuator pump lead to clutch faults. Unlike P2787, this code concerns the actuator rather than the friction lining. Expect limited torque or a lock-out until it has cooled.
c: Long creeping, repeated hill starts or towing in slow traffic
Stiff release bearing or lever forcing high actuator current
Worn actuator motor or blocked actuator pump
Faulty temperature sensing or outdated control software
s: Gearbox warning and request to stop or let the system cool
Reduced engine torque or harsh, delayed take-off
Vehicle may refuse to engage a gear until cooled

P2786.t: Gear Shift Actuator Temperature Too High
P2786.d: P2786 is stored when the drive that moves the shift forks inside an automated gearbox runs too hot. Single-clutch automated manuals use electro-mechanical or electro-hydraulic actuators to push the selector across and along the gate, and some dual-clutch designs drive their forks with motors as well. Rapid repeated shifting, a stiff linkage or a fork that binds forces long current pulses that heat the motor and its driver. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, so the exact trigger is unknown; the logic is the thermal protection CARB expects for monitored gearbox output components. It differs from P2785, which concerns the clutch actuator, and from P0919 or P0920, which report position or electrical faults of the shift drive. Until it cools the gearbox may hold its gear, refuse shifts or stay in neutral.
c: Binding shift fork, selector shaft or linkage raising actuator load
Very frequent shifting, e.g. manual mode on hilly roads or in traffic
Worn shift actuator motor or low hydraulic pressure in the shift unit
Temperature model or software error in the gearbox controller
s: Shifts refused or delayed, gearbox stays in current gear
Transmission warning in the instrument cluster
Gearbox may select neutral and only restart after cooling

P2787.d: P2787 means the controller has calculated or measured a temperature for clutch A above its permitted limit. Two quite different uses are documented. Stellantis bulletin 21-040-26 lists P2787-00 as clutch 1 overtemperature for 2022-2025 European Jeep Renegade and Compass with the 1.5 litre mild hybrid and the 7HDT300 dual-clutch gearbox; the MIL is on, P27F3 for clutch 2 and actuator motor phase faults may appear too, and particles blocking an actuator pump are named as the cause. Mercedes-Benz bulletin LI33.30-N-080795 for the Sprinter 907 with on-demand all-wheel drive shows P27874B in the transfer case unit N15: a failed front differential lets the coupling slip and overheat, and all-wheel drive is switched off. Clutch B has its own code, P27F3.
c: Clutch slipping because its actuator or actuator pump does not deliver full force
On all-wheel-drive couplings, damaged front differential forcing constant slip
Repeated launches, creeping or towing with high clutch slip
Worn friction lining reducing torque capacity
s: Overheating message, odd gears or all-wheel drive unavailable
MIL or transmission warning lamp on
Shudder or slipping when pulling away

P2788.t: Auto Shift Manual Adaptive Learning at Limit
P2788.d: P2788 is the system-level code for an automated manual gearbox whose learned correction values have reached the end of their allowed range. Such units learn the clutch bite point, engagement speed and the end stops of the shift and select movements so that gear changes stay smooth as parts wear; when a value would have to move beyond its limit, the controller can no longer compensate and stores this code. No manufacturer documents P2788 publicly; it falls under the comprehensive component rules of CARB 13 CCR 1968.2. Allison's bulletins on the related P2789 show the usual route: check whether engine torque data are plausible and whether newer software exists before replacing parts. Also check clutch wear, actuator travel and whether a relearn was skipped after repair. P2789 and P278F are the clutch-specific versions.
c: Worn clutch moving the bite point beyond the learnable range
Basic setting or relearn skipped after clutch, actuator or module work
Worn or sticking shift and clutch actuators changing their travel
Outdated software or implausible engine torque signal
s: Jerky take-off and harsh or slow shifts
Transmission warning lamp
Clutch slip or engine flare during shifts

P2789.t: Clutch A Adaptive Learning at Limit
P2789.d: P2789 says the controller has pushed its learned fill or pressure corrections for a clutch to the edge of the permitted window and still cannot reach the shift quality it aims for. The code is well documented by Allison for its 1000/2000 Series automatics, where it lights the Check Transmission lamp and the Prognostics view flags the affected clutch as not OK. Tech tip TT8008EN covers Thomas Built school buses whose natural-gas Cummins ISB engines report torque inaccurately, causing flares on the first two upshifts (C3/C4); TT7994 covers IC Bus models with a PSI 8.8 litre propane engine making more torque than expected (C3); SIL 34-1K2K-19 describes low-mileage units with C1 at its limit and calls for B191 or newer TCM software. In dual-clutch boxes P278F is the clutch B sibling.
c: Outdated transmission calibration needing a reflash
Engine reports torque inaccurately, so clutch adaptation drifts
Worn clutch plates or leaking clutch piston seals
Degraded fluid or a sluggish pressure control solenoid
s: Check Transmission or warning lamp on
Engine flare or slip during upshifts
Harsh or delayed engagement of the affected clutch

P278A.d: P278A is the general circuit fault of the kickdown switch, the contact at the end of accelerator pedal travel that asks the transmission for the lowest possible gear. No manufacturer documents P278A publicly. Many current cars no longer have an electrical switch: Mazda states for the 2024 CX-90 that its kickdown element only adds a felt detent and sends no signal, the pedal position sensor alone deciding. Where a real switch or message exists, the transmission control checks it; Eaton's Endurant HD gearbox logs fault 167 if the kickdown message from the pedal is missing or invalid for 5 s. CARB requires circuit monitoring for such inputs. P278B to P278E name the fault type more precisely. Without the signal, full-throttle downshifts may be weaker or later.
c: Kickdown switch in or under the pedal defective
Wiring or connector of the pedal module damaged
Kickdown message missing on the data bus (networked designs)
s: No forced downshift at full throttle
Reduced acceleration when overtaking

P278B.d: P278B describes a kickdown switch whose state contradicts the pedal position. No manufacturer documents P278B publicly. The obvious cross-check is the accelerator pedal sensor: a switch reporting kickdown at part throttle, or staying open although the pedal is pressed to the stop, is implausible. Mazda's 2024 CX-90 bulletin shows how tight the link is, since there the pedal sensor alone defines kickdown and the mechanical detent only gives feel; on cars with a real contact, a worn detent, a misadjusted switch or a floor mat holding the pedal back can create exactly this mismatch. CARB asks for rationality checks on inputs like this. Unlike P278C and P278D the voltage itself is valid. Expect missing or unexpected kickdown shifts.
c: Kickdown switch misadjusted or detent worn
Floor mat or object preventing full pedal travel
Pedal position sensor offset so that both signals disagree
s: Kickdown missing at the pedal stop
Unexpected downshift at part throttle

P278C.d: P278C is recorded when the kickdown switch line reads lower than the module allows. No manufacturer documents P278C publicly, and many modern pedals have no electrical kickdown contact at all, as Mazda notes for the 2024 CX-90. On designs with a wired switch the cause is usually the signal pulled to ground: insulation damaged where the harness passes the pedal bracket, a switch contact welded or shorted, or water from the footwell reaching the plug. Depending on the circuit logic the module may then read a permanent kickdown request or none at all. CARB demands such out-of-range checks for inputs. Unlike P278D the signal sits too low, unlike P278B it is not just implausible. Shift behaviour at full throttle becomes unreliable.
c: Signal wire shorted to ground at the pedal bracket
Water from the footwell in the connector
s: Kickdown always or never active, depending on circuit
Unexpected downshifts or lack of downshift at full throttle

P278D.d: P278D means the kickdown switch circuit shows a voltage above its permitted maximum. No manufacturer documents P278D publicly. With the usual pull-up input this is the reading of an interrupted line: the pedal module unplugged after a repair, a broken wire at the hinge of a floor-mounted pedal, or a missing ground at the switch. A short to battery voltage produces the same picture but is rarer. For networked pedals the comparable case is a message that is missing or flagged as invalid, as Eaton describes for the kickdown signal of its Endurant HD gearbox (fault 167, 5 s). CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P278C is the low-voltage twin. Kickdown requests are lost until the circuit is restored.
c: Open signal or ground wire, pedal module unplugged
Signal wire shorted to battery voltage
s: No kickdown at full throttle
Slower acceleration from speed

P278E.d: P278E stands for a kickdown switch signal that drops out or toggles irregularly. No manufacturer documents P278E publicly; the monitoring idea follows CARB's call for circuit checks on inputs, and Eaton's Endurant HD diagnostics show the networked equivalent, where a kickdown message that is invalid or absent for 5 s is logged as fault 167. Intermittent faults at the pedal usually come from a contact that bounces as the detent wears, a connector that loosens with pedal vibration, or a harness that flexes with every pedal stroke until a strand breaks. Because the fault is not permanent, a scan with the car at rest often finds nothing. The driver feels kickdown working on one occasion and not on the next.
c: Bouncing switch contact due to worn detent
Wire strands breaking where the harness flexes with the pedal
s: Kickdown works only sometimes
Fault not reproducible when stationary

P278F.t: Clutch B Adaptive Learning at Limit
P278F.d: P278F flags that the learned values for clutch B have run out of room. In a dual-clutch gearbox this is usually the clutch for the even gears; the controller keeps adjusting its touch point and pressure or travel so that handovers between the two clutches stay seamless, and stores the code once a correction hits its end stop. No manufacturer documents P278F publicly with set conditions; CARB requires such transmission functions to be monitored. What the clutch A sibling P2789 shows in Allison's bulletins applies here too: software and an implausible engine torque signal are checked first, worn or damaged plates second. On dry clutches, wear increases the release travel until the learned range is used up. Expect shudder on even gears, slow or rough handovers and a warning lamp; P2788 is the system-level code.
c: Worn clutch B lining or plates shifting the touch point
Clutch adaptation not reset or relearned after repair
Clutch B actuator or release mechanism sticking or losing pressure
Outdated software or inaccurate engine torque information
s: Shudder or slip when an even gear takes over
Rough or slow shifts between gears
Transmission warning lamp

P2790.d: P2790 is the basic circuit fault for the signal that tells the controller in which direction the selector mechanism is moving across the gate, that is sideways between the shift lanes of the H pattern. In automated manual gearboxes the select actuator or its sensor provides this information; on some shift-by-wire levers it comes from the lever itself, so the exact part depends on the manufacturer. A circuit code means the signal is missing or of the wrong type, for example an open wire or a dead sensor, rather than a value that is merely too low or too high (those are P2791 and P2792). No manufacturer documents P2790 publicly; CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires circuit checks for such gearbox inputs. Results range from refused gear changes to a vehicle that stays in one gear or will not pull away.
c: Open wire or loose, corroded connector at the select sensor
Failed select direction sensor or select actuator electronics
Fault in the shift lever module where it supplies the signal
Defective input stage in the transmission controller
s: Gear changes refused or gearbox stuck in one gear
Vehicle may not move off from standstill
Warning lamp with transmission message

P2791.d: P2791 is set when the gate select direction signal sits below the lowest value the controller accepts. For a voltage-type sensor this usually points to a short to ground on the signal wire, a missing reference supply or a sensor pulling the line down internally; with switch-type inputs the contact may read as permanently closed to ground. The circuit fault P2790 and the high-side fault P2792 cover the other failure types of the same signal. No manufacturer documents P2791 publicly, so thresholds and debounce times are unknown; the check is one of the out-of-range tests CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 demands for transmission inputs. Measure supply and signal at the sensor connector before replacing the select actuator. The gearbox typically blocks lane changes and may freeze the current gear.
c: Signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Sensor reference voltage missing or shorted
Select direction sensor failed with low output
s: No change between shift lanes, limited gear choice
Gearbox holds the current gear or selects neutral
Transmission warning lamp

P2792.d: P2792 reports a gate select direction signal stuck above its valid band. Common reasons are a short between the signal line and a supply voltage, a broken sensor ground that lets the input float up, or an open signal wire on inputs with an internal pull-up resistor; a sensor with a failed output stage can also hold the line high. Which hardware provides the signal, actuator sensor or lever module, depends on the maker, and none of them documents P2792 publicly with limits. The test belongs to the out-of-range checks of CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 for transmission inputs. P2791 is the low-side counterpart and P2790 the general circuit fault. Typical effects are blocked sideways selection, shifts limited to one lane and a transmission warning.
c: Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage
Broken sensor ground or open signal line pulled up internally
Select direction sensor failed with high output
s: Sideways selection blocked, shifts possible only in one lane
Gearbox may stay in gear or neutral
Transmission warning lamp

P2793.d: P2793 covers the circuit that reports the shift direction, the fore-and-aft movement along a lane that actually engages or releases a gear, as opposed to the sideways lane choice monitored by P2790. Depending on the design, an automated manual reads it from a sensor on the shift actuator, while shift-by-wire systems may take it from the lever or a separate selector module. The controller stores the circuit fault when the signal is absent or not valid at all; signals that are present but too low or too high set P2794 or P2795. No manufacturer documents P2793 publicly with set conditions; CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires such inputs to be checked for circuit integrity. If the controller cannot tell which way the shift is going, it usually stops shifting, keeps the engaged gear and turns on the warning lamp.
c: Open circuit or poor contact at the shift direction sensor connector
Failed shift direction sensor on the actuator
Faulty shift lever or selector module where it sends the signal
s: No up- or downshifts, gearbox keeps the current gear
Selector input ignored
Warning lamp and transmission message

P2794.d: P2794 means the shift direction signal, which tells the controller whether a gear is being pushed in or pulled out along its lane, reads lower than the permitted minimum. The usual suspects are a signal line rubbed through to ground, a collapsed sensor supply shared with other sensors, or water in a connector creating a leakage path to ground. Because the same supply often feeds several gearbox sensors, other low-voltage codes stored at the same time point to the supply rather than this sensor. No manufacturer documents P2794 publicly with thresholds; the test is one of the range checks CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 sets for transmission inputs. P2793 covers a missing or invalid signal and P2795 the opposite limit. With this fault the gearbox normally freezes the gear in use.
c: Signal line chafed through to ground
Shared sensor supply pulled down by another sensor or wiring
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
s: Gearbox stays in the current gear
Manual shift requests ignored
Transmission warning lamp

P2795.d: P2795 is the upper-limit fault of the shift direction signal: the value seen by the controller is higher than any real sensor position could produce. That pattern fits a signal wire touching a battery or 5 volt feed, a lost sensor ground, or an interrupted signal line on an input that is pulled up inside the module. A sensor whose output stage has failed may also report a constant high level. No manufacturer publishes set conditions for P2795; the check belongs to the range tests in CARB 13 CCR 1968.2. P2794 is the low-side twin and P2793 the plain circuit fault. When diagnosing, compare the ground drop at the sensor with the controller ground before suspecting the actuator. Until the fault is cleared the gearbox usually refuses to change gear and lights its warning lamp.
c: Signal wire shorted to battery or 5 V supply
Lost sensor ground or open signal line pulled up internally
Shift direction sensor stuck at a high output
s: Gear changes refused, current gear held
Selector or paddle inputs have no effect
Transmission warning lamp

P2796.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P2796.d: P2796 points to an interrupted control line between the module and the motor of auxiliary pump A. GM's 2025 TCM tables define the test: provided the battery supplies 9 to 15 V, the controller sees more than 200 kΩ from signal to ground in at least 20 of 25 samples taken every 100 ms; the code is Type B, so the MIL comes on after two trips. On Ford's 10R60/10R80 and 8F57 automatics the pump itself reports that the PWM command signal is missing, filed as P2796_31. Ford TSB 26-2010 covers the 2022–2025 F-150 Lightning, where P2796 or P2797 in the secondary OBD modules B and C may stem from software, often first logged at 0 °C or below; reprogramming is the fix. P2798 and P2799 are the short-circuit siblings, P27A2 the same fault on pump B.
c: Broken control wire or unplugged pump connector
Poor terminal contact at the pump or module
Open circuit inside the pump electronics
s: MIL or wrench indicator on
Stop-start inoperative
Reduced performance message on electrified models

P2797.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Performance/Stuck Off
P2797.d: P2797 says pump A was asked to deliver but no useful pressure resulted. GM checks this on CVTs during an engine auto-start: with the pump commanded and over 400 kPa requested at both pulleys, both pressure sensors reading under 200 kPa for more than 0.525 s set the Type B code. GM bulletin 19-NA-200 (Malibu 2019–2025, Trailblazer, Encore GX, 2025 Equinox) blames an internal pump failure and replaces pump and harness. Subaru found false detections on 2023–2024 Legacy and Outback 2.4 turbo CVTs, caused by forward clutch engagement at restart, and released TCM files (16-145-23R). Stellantis traces P2797 on some 2026 Charger, Grand Cherokee and Wagoneer models with the 880RE eight-speed to a failed oil pump motor (21-053-26). Stop-start is usually the first casualty.
c: Internal failure of the auxiliary pump or its motor
Control software misjudging pump output (TCM update available)
Low fluid or internal leakage preventing pressure build-up
s: MIL on
Stop-start inoperative
Shock or surge when the engine restarts at a stop
Service transmission message

P2798.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Control Circuit Low
P2798.d: P2798 reports the control circuit of auxiliary pump A pulled low, which in practice means a short to ground. In GM's 2025 TCM tables the controller registers less than 0.5 Ω between the signal and controller ground in 20 of 25 samples at a 100 ms rate, with battery voltage between 9 and 15 V; it is a Type B fault with the MIL after two trips. On the Chevrolet Bolt EV (2021–2023) and Bolt EUV (2022–2023), GM bulletin 21-NA-148 groups P2798 with P2797 and P0C2D: the 12-volt fluid pump on the left of the drive unit came from a batch with faulty soldering, and the pump is replaced as a unit because it cannot be repaired. Drivers get a message that propulsion power has been reduced. P2796 covers an open line, P2799 a short to voltage.
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Internal defect in the pump electronics (e.g. faulty solder joints, Bolt EV/EUV)
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the connector
Faulty control output in the module
s: Reduced propulsion power message on electric vehicles
Service vehicle soon lamp or MIL
Stop-start disabled on combustion models

P2799.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Control Circuit High
P2799.d: P2799 is set when the control line of auxiliary pump A sits at too high a level, normally because it touches a powered wire. GM's 2025 TCM tables are the only public manufacturer description: the module measures under 0.5 Ω from the signal line to a voltage source in 20 of 25 samples spaced 100 ms apart, provided supply voltage is between 9 and 15 V, and treats the result as Type B with the MIL after two trips. The tables also show that the pump may be fed by one of several high-side drivers, and the check only runs while the relevant driver is on. CARB requires such actuator circuits to be monitored for shorts. Look for chafed harness sections near hot or moving parts and pins bridged by moisture. With the pump unusable, stop-start and pressure support at restart are lost.
c: Control wire shorted to a powered circuit
Moisture bridging pins in the pump connector
Internal short in the pump electronics
Faulty high-side driver in the module
s: MIL after two drive cycles
Stop-start inoperative
Rough engagement after an auto-start

P279A.t: Transfer Case Gear High Incorrect Ratio
P279A.d: P279A fires when the transfer case should be in its high range, but the measured ratio says otherwise. GM explains the check in its 2019 ECM tables (section for the LCV engine): the ratio is calculated from transmission output speed divided by transfer case output speed, both from real sensors. If the control module commands 4WD high and the result falls in the window for low range or for neutral, the fault counts. It needs 7 seconds of failure within a 10-second window, output shaft speed above 500 rpm, positive engine torque and pedal input, no PTO operation and no active speed sensor faults. GM rates it Type A, so the MIL lights after one trip. Likely reasons are a range shift that did not complete, a worn shift fork or a slipping range sleeve. P279B and P279C cover the other two states.
c: Range shift to high not completed by the shift motor
Worn shift fork or range sleeve slipping out of high
Implausible transfer case output speed signal
Mismatched tire sizes affecting the computed ratio
s: MIL and 4WD warning on
Unexpected low-range feel or loss of drive
Grinding from the transfer case

P279B.t: Transfer Case Gear Low Incorrect Ratio
P279B.d: P279B is the reverse case of P279A: 4WD low has been commanded, yet the transfer case behaves like high range or neutral. For a vehicle crawling off-road this is a real safety concern, because the expected reduction and engine braking are missing. In GM's 2019 ECM tables (LCV section) the module divides transmission output speed by transfer case output speed and flags the fault if the result lands in the high or neutral window. Timing and conditions match the high-range test: 7 s of failure within 10 s, output shaft above 500 rpm, engine torque and pedal applied, no PTO and no active speed sensor faults; Type A, so one failing trip turns on the MIL. A shift motor that stalls before the low position, worn planetary teeth or a broken fork are the likely culprits. P279C covers neutral.
c: Shift motor stopping short of the low position
Worn or damaged reduction planetary set
Broken or bent range shift fork
Faulty speed signal distorting the ratio
s: No reduction in 4WD low, weak crawling and engine braking
4WD warning lamp and MIL
Clunking or grinding when selecting low range

P279C.t: Transfer Case Gear Neutral Incorrect Ratio
P279C.d: P279C applies when neutral is commanded on the transfer case, as is done for flat towing, but the shafts still turn with a fixed ratio that matches high or low range. The transfer case therefore still transmits drive. GM's 2019 ECM tables (LCV section) use the same output-speed ratio as for the other two range tests, but allow more time before deciding: the failure must last 10.5 seconds within a 15-second window. Enable conditions again require output shaft speed above 500 rpm, engine torque and pedal input and no PTO use; the fault is Type A. For towing this matters: a vehicle believed to be in neutral can drive the transmission and damage it. Range motor problems, a sticking shift sleeve and incorrect position feedback are the main suspects; P279A and P279B are the high and low counterparts.
c: Range shift motor not reaching neutral
Sticking shift sleeve keeping a range engaged
Wrong position feedback from the range sensor
s: Vehicle still drives or creeps with neutral selected
Neutral request rejected, 4WD warning on
MIL on

P279D.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Range Signal Circuit
P279D.d: P279D concerns the signal that tells the powertrain which transfer case range is active: 4WD high, 4WD low or neutral. Drivetrain controllers need it to apply the right ratio, torque limits and shift logic. GM documents the code for its 2008 Two-Mode Hybrid in the hybrid control module (HCP), where the range arrives as a network message: the module checks its alive rolling counter, which must increase by one each time, and a protection value that must match the primary value. Five failed samples out of eight while the ignition is in run or crank set the code, with MIL after one trip. Other designs read the range from a switch or sensor wire, so the same code can also mean an open circuit. P279E, P279F and P27A0 cover plausibility, low and high faults of this signal.
c: Open circuit or bad connector on the range switch or sensor
Range message from the transfer case module corrupted or out of sequence
Faulty transfer case control module or range sensor
Software mismatch between the modules after a replacement
s: Check engine lamp
4WD range indicator wrong, flashing or unavailable
Range change between high and low refused

P279E.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Range Signal Circuit Range/Performance
P279E.d: P279E flags a 4WD range signal that is electrically present but does not make sense: it may show a range the transfer case cannot be in, jump between high, low and neutral without a request, or contradict what the speed ratio across the transfer case shows. Such a plausibility check typically compares the reported range with commanded shifts and with the measured ratio monitored by P279A to P279C. No manufacturer documents P279E publicly with set conditions; GM's 2008 Two-Mode Hybrid control module shows how the same range information is validated by its circuit code P279D, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires rationality checks for such inputs. Causes are a misadjusted or worn range sensor, a shift motor stopping between positions, or wiring that intermittently loses contact.
c: Worn or misadjusted transfer case range sensor
Transfer case shift motor stopping between ranges
Intermittent contact in the range signal wiring
s: 4WD indicator shows a range that does not match the actual drive
Range shifts refused or completed only partly
Warning lamp

P279F.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Range Signal Circuit Low
P279F.d: P279F means the wired 4WD range signal is below the lowest valid level. Many transfer cases report their range through a resistor-coded switch or a position sensor that produces a defined voltage for each of high, low and neutral; a reading under the lowest of these bands points to a short to ground, a missing sensor supply or a sensor that pulls the line down. No manufacturer documents P279F publicly; GM's 2008 Two-Mode Hybrid data list the circuit code P279D for the same range information, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires range checks on such inputs. The high-side fault is P27A0, the plausibility fault P279E. Look for chafed harness sections near the transfer case and exhaust and for corroded connectors before replacing the encoder.
c: Range signal wire shorted to ground near the transfer case
Range switch or encoder failed with low output
s: 4WD range indicator dark or flashing
4WD low or range changes unavailable
Warning lamp on

P27A0.t: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Range Signal Circuit High
P27A0.d: P27A0 is logged when the line reporting which transfer case range is engaged (4WD high, 4WD low, neutral) reads above its highest valid level. Range encoders usually present a defined voltage or resistance band for each position; a value above all bands typically means the wire is open and pulled up inside the module, the encoder lost its ground, or the line touches a battery feed. No manufacturer documents P27A0 publicly. GM's 2008 Two-Mode Hybrid tables carry the same range information under P279D, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 asks for out-of-range checks on such inputs. P279F is the low-side partner, P279E the plausibility fault. With the range unknown, the module may refuse range changes or fall back to a default torque strategy.
c: Range signal wire or encoder ground interrupted (corroded or loose connector near the transfer case)
Signal wire chafed against a powered conductor
Transfer case range encoder or switch defective
s: 4WD indicator flashing or showing no range
Shift between 4WD high and low refused
Warning lamp or driveline message

P27A1.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Stuck On
P27A1.d: P27A1 means auxiliary transmission fluid pump A keeps running although the controller has not asked for it, or the module still sees current or rotation with the command off. Such electric pumps hold pressure in the gearbox while the engine rests during stop-start or hybrid operation. A pump that cannot be switched off usually points to a high-side driver or relay stuck closed, a control line shorted to battery voltage, or pump electronics that ignore the command. No manufacturer documents P27A1 publicly. Ford's 2024 summary for the 10R60/10R80 and 8F57 gearboxes shows that the smart pump returns its own speed and current, which is what makes an unwanted run visible; GM's 2025 tables watch the pump drivers for shorts (P2798, P2799). Expect extra battery drain and pump noise.
c: High-side driver or pump relay stays closed
Pump control or enable line shorted to battery voltage
Integrated pump electronics ignore the off command
s: Pump hum from the gearbox after the engine or ignition is off
12 V battery discharged after standing
Stop-start disabled and warning shown

P27A2.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Control Circuit/Open
P27A2.d: P27A2 flags a broken control circuit between the module and auxiliary pump B, the second electric fluid pump on gearboxes that carry two. While its output is energised, the controller compares the voltage on the line with the level an intact load would pull it to; a floating line reveals the interruption. No manufacturer documents P27A2 publicly. GM's 2025 TCM tables describe the identical test for pump A as P2796: more than 200 kΩ to ground in at least 20 of 25 samples taken every 100 ms, with 9 to 15 V supply, Type B. Audi ties its pump B codes to the gear oil pump V553 of the 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL twin-clutch units. P27A4 and P27A5 are the shorted variants. Typical faults are a cracked wire, a pushed-back pin or an open motor winding; stop-start is normally withdrawn.
c: Control wire broken in the harness to pump B
Pump connector unplugged, pin pushed back or corroded
Open motor winding or internal connection in pump B
s: Stop-start no longer active
Transmission warning or MIL
Harsh engagement when driving off after a restart

P27A3.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Performance/Stuck Off
