P27A3.d: P27A3 means auxiliary pump B was commanded but did not deliver: no pressure build-up, too little speed or a motor that does not respond at all. Audi documents the code. Its bulletin 34-17-25, revision 3 from 2017, covers model year 2017 A4, A5, A6 and the 2018 Q5 with the 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL seven-speed twin-clutch boxes and names P27A300, next to P27A6, P276B and U28A0, as possible companions of a rattling gear oil pump V553; a supplier assembly defect was the cause, and the pump is renewed with new bolts. For pump A the matching code is P2797, which GM's 2025 CVT tables set when both pulley pressures stay below 200 kPa during an engine auto-start. Mechanical seizure, low fluid or a weak motor are typical; stop-start goes offline.
c: Pump B mechanically defective or seized (e.g. assembly fault on Audi V553)
Fluid level too low, pump draws air
Worn pump motor or high resistance in its supply
s: Rattle from below the car near the gearbox
Stop-start disabled
Delayed or harsh engagement after an engine restart

P27A4.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Control Circuit Low
P27A4.d: P27A4 indicates that the control line of auxiliary pump B is pulled toward ground. The module checks the line while its driver is switched on; if the measured level stays close to zero, the circuit counts as shorted low. No manufacturer documents P27A4 publicly. GM's 2025 TCM tables give the mirror test for pump A as P2798: under 0.5 Ω between signal and controller ground in more than 20 of 25 samples at 100 ms spacing, evaluated only with battery voltage between 9 and 15 V and the feeding high-side driver on; it is Type B, so the MIL follows after two trips. A short of this kind can also blow a fuse or trip the driver's overcurrent protection. Check for insulation worn through against the housing or subframe and for water in connectors. P27A5 covers the high side.
c: Control wire insulation chafed through to ground
Water or corrosion bridging pins to ground in the pump connector
Internal short to ground inside pump B
s: Stop-start unavailable
MIL or transmission warning after repeated trips
Blown fuse in the pump supply possible

P27A5.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Control Circuit High
P27A5.d: P27A5 sets when the control line of auxiliary pump B sits at a level that only a connection to a voltage source can explain. In practice the wire touches a powered conductor, or moisture links it to a neighbouring supply pin. No manufacturer documents P27A5 publicly. For pump A, GM's 2025 TCM tables call the equivalent P2799 and judge it by an impedance below 0.5 Ω from signal to a voltage source in 20 of 25 checks, carried out only while the relevant driver is active and supply voltage is between 9 and 15 V; it is a Type B fault. Depending on how the circuit is built, such a short can leave pump B unable to switch off, which links this code to P27A6. Audi's pump B is the V553 on its 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL gearboxes. Repair centres on the harness; the pump itself is seldom at fault.
c: Control wire chafed against a powered conductor
Moisture bridging the control pin to a supply pin
Faulty output stage in the controlling module
s: Stop-start switched off
Pump B may run continuously or not at all
MIL after two trips on Type B systems

P27A6.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Stuck On
P27A6.d: P27A6 reports that auxiliary pump B keeps running, or keeps drawing current, while the controller has it switched off. Audi lists P27A600 in bulletin 34-17-25 for 2017 A4, A5 and A6 and 2018 Q5 models with 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL dual-clutch gearboxes; there the code may appear together with a rattle from the gear oil pump V553, which Audi traced to an assembly fault at the supplier and cures with a new pump. More generally, a pump that will not stop points to its own control electronics, a driver or relay that remains closed, or a control wire shorted to voltage, the case covered by P27A5. On pump A the same fault is P27A1. Apart from noise, a pump that never rests drains the 12 V battery and wears out early.
c: Pump B module or electronics defective (e.g. Audi V553 supplier fault)
Driver output or relay remains closed
Control line shorted to battery voltage
s: Pump noise or rattle from the gearbox area with the engine off
Weak or flat 12 V battery
Transmission warning stored

P27A7.t: Pressure Control Solenoid A Data Incompatible
P27A7.d: P27A7 means the transmission controller holds no usable calibration curve for pressure control solenoid A. Each valve body is measured at the factory, and GM writes its current-to-pressure data into TCM memory; at every start-up the module checks that record. GM's 2020 table 20OBDG04 flags it when the data are missing after a replacement or brand-new TCM is fitted, belong to another solenoid class, fail the checksum, or contain axis points that fall instead of rise, rated Type A after one trip. On the nine-speed valve A is line pressure, on the ten-speed clutch C1, on the CVT the secondary pulley; the 2019 hybrid table 19OBDG01 lists it in the HPC1 too. The MIL comes on, and shifting is usually rough until the data are reprogrammed.
c: New or service TCM installed without loading the solenoid characterization data
Valve body replaced but the data for its part number not written to the TCM
Data set for a different solenoid class or valve body entered
Programming aborted, leaving a corrupted block (checksum error)
s: MIL on right after start-up
Harsh engagements or firm shifts from imprecise line pressure
Transmission may run a substitute program

P27A8.t: Pressure Control Solenoid B Data Incompatible
P27A8.d: With P27A8 the TCM rejects the stored characterization record of pressure control solenoid B. GM's 2016 eight-speed table 16OBDG03 ties B to clutch 2 (CB12345R) and logs the code within one trip when that record is marked as not programmed. From 2017 on (17OBDG04, 18OBDG04, 20OBDG04) the letter stands for the converter clutch valve of the nine-speed, clutch C2 of the ten-speed and the primary pulley of GM's CVT, checked once during controller initialization and rated Type A. A blank or mismatched block nearly always follows a module swap or valve body job where the part-number-based download was skipped. Expect the MIL; lock-up or shift quality may suffer until the data are written.
c: Characterization download skipped after TCM or valve body replacement
Data loaded for the wrong valve body part number
TCM non-volatile memory corrupting the stored block
s: MIL illuminated
Converter lock-up shudder or no lock-up on the nine-speed
Uneven upshifts involving the affected clutch

P27A9.t: Pressure Control Solenoid C Data Incompatible
P27A9.d: P27A9 concerns solenoid C. GM's controller compares the calibration it holds for this valve with the valve body actually fitted; if the block for C is absent, of the wrong device class, damaged or non-monotonic, the fault is stored at power-up and lights the MIL in that same trip (Type A in 20OBDG04 and in the 2025 table 25OBDG03A). Valve C feeds clutch C1 (CB123456) in the nine-speed, clutch C3 in the ten-speed and line pressure in the CVT; on the 2016 eight-speed it is clutch 3 (C13567). Without valid data the module cannot turn a pressure request into the right current, so clutch fill and shift timing for that element drift. The cure is loading the matching valve body data, not a new solenoid.
c: Replacement TCM fitted without solenoid C data
Valve body or solenoid assembly swapped without updating the TCM
Stored data corrupted, checksum no longer matches
s: MIL on in the first drive after the fault
Slipping or harsh application of the clutch fed by valve C
On the CVT, unstable line pressure and belt slip risk

P27AA.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Data Incompatible
P27AA.d: P27AA is set when the TCM finds the calibration block for pressure control solenoid D unusable. Which hardware that is depends on the gearbox: GM's 2016 eight-speed assigns D to clutch 4 (C23468), while the 2017-2020 tables put the nine-speed's C2 clutch (CB29), the ten-speed's C5 clutch and the CVT's C1 clutch behind the same letter, so the D used by stuck-off code P2714 is not always the same part. GM checks it once at start-up, Type A. Ford handles the same task differently: its 10R60/10R80 summary reports a bad or empty TRID block holding solenoid data under its own codes P163E and P163F. Reprogramming the data that belong to the fitted valve body clears the fault.
c: Solenoid data not loaded after a transmission or TCM repair
Used TCM from another vehicle still carrying its old valve body data
Wrong valve body part number used for the download
s: MIL and stored DTC at key-on
Rough shifts into gears using the clutch behind valve D

P27AB.t: Pressure Control Solenoid E Data Incompatible
P27AB.d: Solenoid E's characterization data failing the TCM's plausibility test produces P27AB. In GM's 2018 table 18OBDG04 the record is written at vehicle assembly according to the valve body part number and must be rewritten by the dealer whenever the valve body is serviced; a missing or partial block, a device class mismatch, a checksum error or falling axis values all count as failures (Type A, one trip). Valve E is clutch 5 (C45678R) on the 2016 eight-speed, clutch C3 (CB38) on the nine-speed, clutch C4 on the ten-speed and the converter clutch on the CVT. The solenoid itself may be perfect; what is wrong is the table the controller uses to drive it, so harsh or flared shifts can appear.
c: Valve body serviced without rewriting the solenoid data
Incomplete programming session after TCM replacement
Solenoid class in the data does not match the TCM calibration
s: MIL lit
Flare or bump on shifts using the clutch behind valve E
On the CVT, irregular torque converter lock-up

P27AC.t: Pressure Control Solenoid F Data Incompatible
P27AC.d: P27AC reports invalid calibration data for pressure control solenoid F. On GM's 2016 eight-speed this is the line pressure solenoid, and the TCM logs the fault in one trip once the data are found unprogrammed. Later GM tables assign F to the nine-speed's C4 clutch, the ten-speed's C6 clutch and the CVT's binary pump; the 2025 table 25OBDG03A still carries the check, with the same start-up test and Type A rating. Because line pressure or pump control rides on this valve in some layouts, a bad record can affect every gear, not just one shift. Typical triggers are a replacement controller or valve body installed without the data download; a faulty solenoid coil sets circuit codes instead.
c: TCM swapped and solenoid F data never loaded
Remanufactured valve body with a new ID not entered into the TCM
Data block damaged by a voltage drop during programming
s: MIL on
Firm or soft shifts throughout when line pressure depends on valve F
Possible fixed-gear substitute mode

P27AD.t: Pressure Control Solenoid G Data Incompatible
P27AD.d: P27AD flags the stored data for pressure control solenoid G as not matching the hardware. GM's 2016 eight-speed table names G the torque converter clutch solenoid and sets the code in one trip. In the 2017 to 2020 tables G is clutch C5 (C57R) on the nine-speed, the line pressure valve on the ten-speed and, only on CVTs with electronic range select, mode valve A; there it is a Type A fault checked at controller start. The 2025 table 25OBDG03A no longer lists G, ending its characterization checks at F. When the line pressure valve of a ten-speed is affected, shift feel can change across all gears. Reloading the valve body data with a scan tool is the usual repair.
c: Solenoid G data missing after TCM programming
Valve body changed without matching data
TCM calibration for a different transmission variant
s: MIL illuminated
Converter clutch or range mode problems, depending on transmission
General shift harshness on ten-speed units

P27AE.t: Pressure Control Solenoid H Data Incompatible
P27AE.d: P27AE is the highest letter GM publicly checks for characterization data. It is absent from the 2016 eight-speed table and first appears in 17OBDG04, where H stands for the nine-speed's C6 clutch (C6789) and the ten-speed's torque converter clutch; 20OBDG04 adds mode valve B on CVTs with electronic range select. The test is identical to its siblings: one pass at TCM initialization, failure if the data are absent, of another device class, fail their checksum or show decreasing axis points, then Type A after one trip. On a ten-speed, wrong data for H mainly shows up as poor or shuddering lock-up. Since only the data are at fault, a dealer-level download, not a mechanical repair, normally ends it.
c: Replacement TCM delivered blank and not set up with valve body data
Valve body or solenoid service without data update
s: MIL on
Shudder or missing converter lock-up on ten-speed units
Higher fuel consumption if lock-up is suppressed

P27AF.t: Pressure Control Solenoid J Data Incompatible
P27AF.d: No manufacturer documents P27AF publicly. By its wording it would mean that the TCM considers the stored calibration of a ninth pressure control solenoid, letter J, invalid. GM's published characterization monitor (P27A7 to P27AE, Type A, run at TCM start-up) stops at H, and Ford reports faulty solenoid data on its 10R and 8F transmissions with its own codes P163E and P163F instead of this series. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires transmission output components to be monitored, so a maker with more valves could use J. If it appears, the logic of the GM siblings applies: data missing after a module or valve body change, wrong data set, or a damaged block. A drivable car with MIL and rough shifts is the likely result.
c: Solenoid data not loaded after TCM or valve body replacement
Data set for another valve body variant
Corrupted calibration block in TCM memory
s: MIL illuminated
Rough or inconsistent shifts involving the element behind valve J

P27B0.t: Pressure Control Solenoid K Data Incompatible
P27B0.d: P27B0 closes the data-incompatible series with letter K, and no public manufacturer document uses it. It would describe a tenth pressure control solenoid whose calibration record in the transmission controller is missing, mismatched or corrupt. For comparison, GM's 2020 table checks the records of valves A to H once per power-up and rates failures Type A; the ten-speed there needs only eight such valves. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 is the legal basis for monitoring such output components. Practically, a workshop would treat K like its siblings: confirm the valve body ID, load the matching data and clear the code. A broken coil or wiring would produce circuit codes instead, not this data fault.
c: Valve K data never programmed into a new or used TCM
Valve body ID in the TCM differs from the fitted unit
Software update overwrote or damaged the data block
s: MIL on
Shift quality problems on gears using valve K

P27B1.t: Internal Control Module Transmission Range Select Performance
P27B1.d: P27B1 belongs to a family of codes raised by an independent supervision layer in the transmission or powertrain module. That layer repeats key transmission decisions in parallel and flags the main software when both results disagree, as a guard against unintended vehicle motion. Ford's 2024 OBD summary places P27B1 only in its table for the TR9070 dual-clutch transmission, filed as UDS P0701_96 for a safety-goal violation tied to the clutch shafts; the 2020–2023 issue does not list it. No other manufacturer documents the code publicly. P27B2 to P27B6 cover range control, gear selection, direction, ratio and speed sensing. Because the trigger is usually software or an implausible input rather than a broken part, updates and the related sensor codes are checked first.
c: Supervision or main software calibration in the module
Implausible clutch shaft speed or position input
Internal fault in the transmission control module
s: Transmission warning or wrench light
Restricted gear selection or default gear

P27B2.t: Internal Control Module Transmission Range Control Performance
P27B2.d: P27B2 is set when the monitoring layer cannot confirm that the gearbox is really in the range the main software intends. In GM's 2024 tables for heavy-duty trucks, the TCM checks actual solenoid and pressure switch states with the pattern expected for the range; if they disagree for a full second, the code is logged, lighting the MIL on the first trip. Ford's 2020–2024 summaries treat it as a non-MIL fault on cars with electronic shifting, recognised in less than 3 s. Ford bulletins tie it to electronic shifter events: SSM 47877 (Navigator 2018/19 and Nautilus 2019, stuck in park after R or D was chosen from remote start without braking), SSM 49642 (Explorer and Aviator built for 2020/21, park release used in the plant) and TSB 25-2362 (2023–2025 Escape and Corsair hybrids, 2025 Maverick hybrid, MIL from SOBDMC software).
c: Module software (Ford fixes by reprogramming, e.g. TSB 25-2362)
Unusual operating sequence such as selecting a gear after remote start without braking
Solenoid or pressure switch state not matching the commanded range
s: Vehicle stuck in park or will not start
Warning lamp or transmission message
Range change refused

P27B3.t: Internal Control Module Transmission Gear Select Performance
P27B3.d: P27B3 is the monitoring code for the path that turns a chosen gear into actuator commands. In Ford's wording it supervises the actuator manager. In the 2020–2023 summary it is non-MIL on park-by-wire vehicles; the 2024 edition links it to the selectable one-way clutch (SOWC) of the eight- and ten-speed automatics, with UDS P0701_9A for an electrical SOWC fault and P0701_94 for a failed shut-off path or an unintended application, both non-MIL and detected within one second. In Ford's TR9070 dual-clutch table, P27B3 additionally covers a fault in safety-relevant CAN transmit signals. No other manufacturer documents P27B3 publicly. The trigger can be software, a wiring problem at the SOWC actuator or the actuator itself.
c: Electrical fault at the selectable one-way clutch actuator (Ford 8/10-speed)
Safety-relevant CAN transmit signal faulty (Ford TR9070)
s: Wrench light or transmission message
Certain gears or engine braking functions blocked

P27B4.t: Internal Control Module Transmission Gear Direction Control Performance
P27B4.d: P27B4 concerns the direction in which the vehicle actually moves compared with the selected gear. GM's 2024 heavy-duty TCM tables compare the direction reported by the output speed sensor with the direction implied by solenoid and pressure switch states; disagreement for one second sets the code with MIL on the first trip. Ford's 2024 summary splits it into unintended launch (UDS P073D_48) and wrong driving direction (P073F_48), listed as non-MIL on eight- and ten-speed automatics. Despite that listing, Ford bulletins report a MIL and point to software: TSB 20-2074 for 2020 Super Duty trucks with 6.2 or 7.3 L petrol engines and the 10R140, TSB 20-2336 for the 6.7 L diesel, and TSB 26-2096 for the 2022 F-150 Lightning, where the wrench light comes from the SOBDMC.
c: Module software strategy (Ford reprograms PCM or SOBDMC)
Faulty direction information from the output speed sensor
Solenoid or pressure switch reporting a state that does not match the gear
s: MIL or wrench light
Forced idle or reduced power
Gear engagement blocked until restart

P27B5.t: Internal Control Module Transmission Gear Ratio Control Performance
P27B5.d: P27B5 sets when the supervision software doubts the ratio the transmission is running. Ford describes two triggers in its 2024 summary for the eight- and ten-speed automatics: protection against overspeeding a driveline element (UDS P0701_B1) and a plausibility test of the shaft speed ratio (P0701_64), both non-MIL; the 2020–2023 edition likewise keeps it without MIL on electronically shifted models. Detection takes less than a second. Ford TSB 20-2336 covers 2020 Super Duty trucks with the 6.7 L diesel built up to 19 August 2020, where P27B5 could come with a MIL, other codes and a forced idle; PCM reprogramming was the remedy. Genuine clutch slip or a speed sensor fault can create the same mismatch, so incorrect-ratio codes such as P0730 and sensor codes need checking too.
c: Implausible input, intermediate or output shaft speed signal
Real slip of a clutch producing an unexpected ratio
s: Warning lamp or wrench light
Forced idle or torque reduction
Transmission held in a fixed gear

P27B6.t: Internal Control Module Transmission Speed Sensor Performance
P27B6.d: P27B6 is the supervision check on the transmission speed signals. GM's 2024 heavy-duty TCM tables work out the output speed that should result from turbine speed and the current gear ratio and set the code, MIL on the first trip, when the raw output speed deviates by 10 or more for at least 10 seconds while output speed is at least 50, the range is not neutral and no shift is under way. Ford's summaries list it as non-MIL; the 2024 issue names tie-up protection (UDS P0701_92) and unintended deceleration (P0701_96) on its eight- and ten-speed automatics. Ford TSB 18-2211 dealt with a lit MIL and P27B6 on 2018 F-150 trucks with 2.7, 3.5 or 5.0 L engines built until 4 May 2018 by reprogramming the PCM. Pure sensor circuit faults carry P0715 or P0720.
c: Turbine or output speed sensor delivering an implausible signal
Damaged tone wheel or interference on sensor wiring
s: MIL or wrench light
Harsh or abrupt deceleration events
Fixed gear or limited shifting

P27B9.t: Pressure Control Solenoid N Performance/Stuck Off
P27B9.d: P27B9 says pressure control solenoid N does not build hydraulic force when commanded. On dual-clutch gearboxes this letter belongs to the second synchronizer pressure valve: Ford's 2024 summary lists it for SPV2 of the TR9070, and GM's 2023 Corvette table 23OBDG07 calls it shift solenoid 2 hydraulically stuck off. GM runs a synchronizer integrity routine after a shift-related fault or when the gear remembered at shutdown disagrees with the sensors at start-up; small test movements of the shift rods that stay at or below 100 micrometres with valve 2 actuated set the code, Type A, and 24OBDG07 keeps it. The driver may find gears on that rod unavailable.
c: Valve spool sticking closed from debris or varnish
Low or contaminated transmission fluid reducing supply pressure
Leak in the synchronizer actuator circuit
Mechanically binding shift rod or fork
s: MIL on
Certain gears cannot be selected; gear skipping
Substitute mode with reduced gear set

P27BA.t: Pressure Control Solenoid N Stuck On
P27BA.d: P27BA is the opposite fault to P27B9: solenoid N keeps applying pressure when it should be released. GM's dual-clutch table 23OBDG07 (Corvette) describes the effect of a synchronizer valve 2 stuck on as a constant push on one shift rod. Because the selector routes that pressure differently once the selector moves to another position, one rod relaxes or another moves although no movement was commanded; the TCM watches the rod position sensors for this, Type A, and 24OBDG07 keeps the check. Ford's TR9070 list pairs the same code with SPV2 hydraulically stuck on. Possible consequences are a gear dragging in, gear clash or a forced protective mode, because two gears on one shaft must never engage together.
c: Valve spool stuck open by contamination
Worn solenoid armature not returning to rest
Fluid contaminated with clutch or synchronizer wear particles
s: MIL and transmission warning
Gear clash or grinding on shifts
Limp mode with restricted gears

P27BB.d: P27BB is a catch-all electrical code for pressure control solenoid N, and no manufacturer documents it publicly. The two makers known to use solenoid N, GM on the Corvette dual-clutch unit (23OBDG07) and Ford on the TR9070, both split electrical faults of this synchronizer valve into separate codes instead: P27BD covers an open load, P27BF a grounded line and P27C0 a line shorted to battery voltage. A controller with a less detailed driver stage could report all of these under P27BB. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires circuit monitoring of such output components. Checks therefore cover coil resistance, connector pins inside the transmission and the harness to the TCM.
c: Solenoid N coil open or shorted
Corroded or loose internal transmission connector
Damaged harness between TCM and transmission
Faulty output driver in the TCM
s: MIL on
Gears served by solenoid N unavailable

P27BC.d: P27BC reports that the signal or response of pressure control solenoid N drops out now and then rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the GM and Ford dual-clutch documents that use solenoid N for the second synchronizer valve (23OBDG07, Ford TR9070 list) only publish its permanent electrical and hydraulic faults. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 counts automatic transmission solenoids among the outputs whose circuits must be watched for faults. Loose terminals, a chafed wire that touches only under vibration or heat, or a coil that opens when hot are the usual suspects. Because the fault comes and goes, freeze-frame data and a wiggle test with the harness moved are more useful than a single static measurement.
c: Loose or spread terminal at solenoid N or TCM
s: MIL that comes and goes
Occasional missed or delayed shifts

P27BD.t: Pressure Control Solenoid N Control Circuit/Open
P27BD.d: P27BD stands for an open control circuit of solenoid N. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table 23OBDG07 names the part synchronizer actuation valve 2 and tests it while its low-side output is switched off: the driver chip tries to hold the pin at a small voltage with a tiny current, which only works without a load connected. A pin voltage between about 1.7 and 3.0 V after more than 5 ms off, confirmed for 150 ms, sets the code as Type A; the check runs continuously with battery voltage between 8.75 and 18 V and is suspended by supply voltage codes P0882/P0883. Ford's 2024 list uses P27BD for open load of SPV2 on the TR9070. Broken wiring, a loose connector or an open coil are typical.
c: Broken control wire between TCM and solenoid
s: MIL on in the same trip
Gears on the affected shift rod blocked
Transmission substitute mode

P27BE.t: Pressure Control Solenoid N Control Circuit Range/Performance
P27BE.d: P27BE means the control circuit of solenoid N is electrically intact but behaves implausibly, for example a measured current that does not follow the command. No manufacturer documents P27BE publicly. GM's Corvette dual-clutch table 23OBDG07 does monitor exactly this for synchronizer valve 2, comparing target current with the current estimated from duty cycle and battery voltage, but files a deviation above 70 % for 60 ms or above 400 mA for 300 ms under P27C0 rather than here. Ford's TR9070 list also has no entry for it. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 asks for a functional check of automatic transmission solenoids and, where none is feasible, at least circuit fault detection. Likely causes are a coil with drifting resistance, high connection resistance or a weak driver stage.
c: Solenoid N coil resistance out of specification
High resistance at connector or crimp
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM
s: MIL on
Slow or incomplete gear engagement on one shift rod

P27BF.t: Pressure Control Solenoid N Control Circuit Low
P27BF.d: P27BF indicates the control line of solenoid N is pulled too low, in practice a short to ground. GM's 23OBDG07 table for the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox checks synchronizer actuation valve 2 while its low-side switch is on: should the sense-pin voltage fall below about 1.7 V (tolerance 0.5 V), the driver chip reports a ground short; 150 ms confirmation, battery between 8.75 and 18 V, engine not cranking, Type A. With the line grounded the solenoid can be energized permanently and the controller loses control of it. Ford's TR9070 table calls the same event shorted switch on SPV2. A pinched harness against the case or water in a connector are frequent reasons.
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Moisture or corrosion bridging the connector
Solenoid winding shorted to its housing
s: MIL on immediately
Unintended gear actuation or locked-out gears
Limp mode

P27C0.t: Pressure Control Solenoid N Control Circuit High
P27C0.d: P27C0 reports too high a voltage on the control line of solenoid N, usually a short to battery or to a neighbouring output. On the Corvette with GM's dual-clutch gearbox (table 23OBDG07, 2023), synchronizer actuation valve 2 is flagged when the sense voltage stays above roughly 0.7 to 1.1 V, depending on supply voltage, while the low-side switch is on, or when actual current misses the target by over 70 % for 60 ms or by over 400 mA for 300 ms. A separate test at shutdown energizes the outputs one by one to find two lines shorted together, stores the result and sets P27C0 at the next start. All are Type A; 24OBDG07 keeps the code. Ford's TR9070 list names it shorted load on SPV2.
c: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Two solenoid lines shorted together in the harness or connector
Partially shorted solenoid coil drawing wrong current
Damaged output stage in the TCM
s: MIL on
Shift rod cannot be actuated; gears missing
Code returns at every start after a shutdown test

P27C1.t: Pressure Control Solenoid P Performance/Stuck Off
P27C1.d: P27C1 is logged when pressure control solenoid P is commanded but the shift rods it serves barely move. In GM's Corvette dual-clutch documentation (23OBDG07, unchanged in 24OBDG07) the part is shift solenoid 3; with the selector valve in one position it pushes rod 3, in the other rod 4, both in the A-to-B direction. During GM's intrusive synchronizer check, run after a shift fault or a gear mismatch found at power-up, travel of 100 µm or less on the commanded rod counts as no response, Type A. Ford's 2024 summary assigns the code to SPV3 of the TR9070. Gears selected via rods 3 and 4 may be locked out and the gearbox may run on a reduced set of ratios.
c: Valve spool of solenoid P held in the closed position by debris or varnish
Low, aerated or degraded transmission fluid so no pressure builds
Leaking seal on the shift rod actuator piston for rods 3/4
Mechanically binding shift rod or fork
s: MIL on with transmission warning
Certain gears skipped or not selectable
Delayed or failed launch in affected gear

P27C2.t: Pressure Control Solenoid P Stuck On
P27C2.d: P27C2 means solenoid P keeps pressurizing after it should have vented. GM's dual-clutch Corvette table 23OBDG07 (and 24OBDG07) detects this on shift solenoid 3 by watching what happens just after the selector valve switches: if one of rods 3 and 4 travels 1,000 µm or more within 200 ms without a command while the other one drops back by at least 125 µm, valve 3 is judged hydraulically stuck on, Type A. Which rod moves and which relaxes depends on the selector position. Ford's 2024 overview gives P27C2 to SPV3 on the TR9070. Unwanted rod motion can drag a gear in, so the controller usually blocks the affected gears; clunks or a sudden neutral are possible.
c: Spool of solenoid P jammed in the open (pressure-applying) position
Wear particles in the fluid keeping the valve from closing
Worn valve bore letting pressure bypass to the actuator
s: MIL on and gears blocked by the controller
Clunk or grinding during gear changes
Unexpected loss of drive (neutral)

P27C3.d: P27C3 is the general electrical fault code for pressure control solenoid P. No manufacturer documents it publicly. Where solenoid P is known to exist, on GM's Corvette dual-clutch box (23OBDG07, shift solenoid 3) and Ford's TR9070 (SPV3), electrical faults are reported in finer detail: P27C5 for an open load, P27C7 for a shorted switch and P27C8 for a shorted load or excessive current error. A controller with simpler output diagnostics might summarize any of these as P27C3. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires monitoring of transmission output circuits. Measure coil resistance at the transmission connector, then check terminals and the lead to the control unit.
c: Solenoid P winding open or shorted
Damaged or corroded pin in the transmission connector
Chafed or broken lead between solenoid and TCM
Faulty output stage in the TCM
s: MIL on
Gears on the affected shift rods unavailable
Transmission in emergency mode

P27C4.d: P27C4 indicates that solenoid P works most of the time but its circuit or response briefly drops out. No manufacturer documents the code publicly; GM's Corvette DCT table 23OBDG07 and Ford's TR9070 list, which both use this solenoid as synchronizer valve 3, only publish hard faults such as P27C5, P27C7, P27C8 and the hydraulic codes P27C1/P27C2. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 counts transmission solenoids among monitored outputs. Intermittent dropouts usually come from fretting corrosion at terminals, a conductor broken inside its insulation, or a solenoid whose winding opens when it reaches operating temperature. Logging data while flexing the harness and warming the unit helps catch it.
c: Wire strand broken inside intact-looking insulation
Solenoid winding that opens at operating temperature
s: MIL that comes and goes
Occasional harsh or missed shift

P27C5.t: Pressure Control Solenoid P Control Circuit/Open
P27C5.d: P27C5 reports an open control circuit on solenoid P. GM's Corvette dual-clutch table 23OBDG07 tests synchronizer actuation valve 3 for this while its low-side driver (a TLE8242 chip) is off: an intact coil pulls the sense pin up towards battery voltage, whereas without a load the driver manages to hold it in a window of about 1.7 to 3.0 V. If that persists for 150 ms after the output has been off for over 5 ms, the code sets as Type A, with battery voltage 8.75-18 V and no P0882/P0883 present; 24OBDG07 retains it. Ford's 2024 table lists open load of SPV3 on the TR9070 as P27C5. Look for a broken wire, an unplugged connector or an open coil.
c: Connector not latched or pin pushed back
Broken control wire between TCM and solenoid
s: MIL on immediately
Shifts on rods 3 and 4 in A-to-B direction not possible
Limp mode with restricted gears

P27C6.t: Pressure Control Solenoid P Control Circuit Range/Performance
P27C6.d: P27C6 describes a control circuit for solenoid P that is neither open nor shorted but behaves outside its expected range, for example current that does not track the command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM does run such a plausibility test on synchronizer actuation valve 3 of the Corvette dual-clutch unit (23OBDG07), comparing the estimated current with the target, yet assigns a failure to P27C8, not to P27C6; Ford's TR9070 table has no range code for SPV3 either. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 expects functional or at least circuit monitoring of automatic transmission solenoids. Suspects are a winding whose resistance changes with temperature, corroded contacts adding resistance, or unstable supply voltage.
s: MIL on
Inconsistent shift quality on the affected rods

P27C7.t: Pressure Control Solenoid P Control Circuit Low
P27C7.d: P27C7 points to a control circuit of solenoid P that is too low, effectively a short to ground on the switched side. GM's 23OBDG07 Corvette dual-clutch table checks synchronizer actuation valve 3 with its low-side switch on and expects the sense resistor voltage to be pulled down only so far; a reading under about 1.7 V (±0.5 V) for 150 ms is reported by the driver chip as a ground short, Type A, provided the engine is not cranking and battery voltage lies between 8.75 and 18 V. With that line grounded, valve 3 may stay energized regardless of command. Ford lists the same failure as a shorted switch on SPV3 of the TR9070. Inspect harness routing near the case and the connector for moisture.
c: Control wire shorted to ground against the case
Moisture or oil bridging pins in the connector
Solenoid winding shorted to its housing
s: MIL on
Unwanted application of rods 3/4, gears blocked
Limp mode

P27C8.t: Pressure Control Solenoid P Control Circuit High
P27C8.d: P27C8 signals too high a level in the control circuit of solenoid P. GM's Corvette DCT tables 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07 store it for synchronizer actuation valve 3 in three situations, all Type A. First, with the low-side switch on, the sense voltage stays above a supply-dependent limit of 0.7, 0.9 or 1.1 V (below 11.5 V, 12-15 V, above 15.5 V battery). Second, the current estimated from duty cycle and supply deviates from its target by more than 70 % (60 ms) or by more than 400 mA (300 ms). Third, a shutdown routine switches each output separately, detects valve 3 shorted to a neighbour and sets the code at the next start. Ford calls it shorted load on SPV3 of the TR9070.
c: Control line shorted to battery voltage
Control line shorted to a neighbouring solenoid output
Solenoid P coil with too low resistance (shorted turns)
s: MIL on, possibly at the start after a previous drive
Gears of rods 3/4 unavailable
Limp mode

P27C9.t: Pressure Control Solenoid R Performance/Stuck Off
P27C9.d: Solenoid R is the fourth synchronizer pressure valve on the dual-clutch units that use it, and P27C9 says it failed to move anything. GM's 2023 and 2024 Corvette tables (23OBDG07/24OBDG07) call it shift solenoid 4; it acts on the same two rods as valve 3 but drives them back from B towards A. The integrity check commands that motion for each selector position and expects more than 100 µm of rod travel; anything less marks valve 4 hydraulically stuck off, Type A. Ford's TR9070 table lists P27C9 for SPV4. As the opposite direction is affected, the gearbox may be unable to move those rods back, so certain gears can be neither selected nor released.
c: Spool of solenoid R stuck closed
Supply passage or screen to valve R clogged by debris
Leaking actuator seal on the B-to-A side of rods 3/4
s: MIL on with transmission message
Gear stays engaged or cannot be selected
Reduced gear range

P27CA.t: Pressure Control Solenoid R Stuck On
P27CA.d: P27CA is the stuck-on fault of solenoid R, GM's shift solenoid 4 on the Corvette dual-clutch transmission. The detection in 23OBDG07 mirrors that of valve 3 because both valves share rods 3 and 4, only with opposite pushing direction: a selector change followed by an uncommanded jump of one rod of at least 1 mm inside 200 ms plus a 0.125 mm relaxation of its partner points to valve 4 holding pressure. The check runs continuously, rated Type A, and is retained in 24OBDG07. Ford pairs the code with SPV4 of the TR9070. A valve that cannot vent tends to leave a rod loaded, which may show up as gear grinding or a protective lock-out of gears.
c: Spool of solenoid R jammed open
Debris lodged in valve R preventing venting
Internal wear of solenoid R armature or seat
s: MIL on
Grinding or clunk when changing gears
Gears locked out by the controller

P27CB.d: An electrical fault of unspecified kind on solenoid R is what P27CB stands for. There is no public manufacturer description of this exact code. GM (shift solenoid 4 in the Corvette DCT table 23OBDG07) and Ford (SPV4 of the TR9070, 2024 overview) both use solenoid R, yet they break its wiring faults down into P27CD, P27CF and P27D0 rather than one lumped code. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 obliges the module to detect circuit faults on such actuators. In practice the same checks apply as for the detailed codes: winding resistance against specification, pin fit inside the gearbox connector, insulation of the harness and, last of all, the output stage of the TCM.
c: Solenoid R winding resistance out of specification
Poor pin fit in the gearbox connector
s: MIL on
Gear selection limited
Emergency mode possible

P27CC.d: With P27CC the transmission controller has seen solenoid R lose its circuit or its effect for short moments only. A public, code-specific manufacturer description does not exist. The two known users of solenoid R, GM's Corvette dual-clutch transmission (23OBDG07, valve 4) and Ford's TR9070 (SPV4), document only lasting electrical faults and stuck conditions for it. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires output monitoring for automatic transmission solenoids. Since the fault may have healed by the time the car reaches the workshop, freeze frame records, the number of occurrences and a careful look for oil wicking into connectors or a loose pin are more telling than one resistance reading.
c: Transmission fluid wicking into the connector
s: Intermittent MIL
Sporadic rough or delayed shift

P27CD.t: Pressure Control Solenoid R Control Circuit/Open
P27CD.d: P27CD is set when the control circuit of solenoid R appears open, so the module cannot energize the valve. On GM's Corvette with dual-clutch transmission (23OBDG07, again in 24OBDG07) the part is synchronizer actuation valve 4. The test runs with the output switched off: without a coil in the circuit, nothing pulls the sense voltage up to battery level, and it remains between roughly 1.7 and 3.0 V; held for 150 ms, this stores the code as Type A. Ford's TR9070 overview uses P27CD for open load of SPV4. Since valve 4 moves rods 3 and 4 in the B-to-A direction, those shifts become impossible. Causes are mainly a pushed-out terminal, a cut lead or a burnt winding.
c: Terminal pushed out of the connector housing
s: MIL on
Shifts on rods 3 and 4 in B-to-A direction not possible
Limp mode

P27CE.t: Pressure Control Solenoid R Control Circuit Range/Performance
P27CE.d: P27CE would be stored if the control circuit of solenoid R stayed electrically connected yet produced values that make no sense to the controller. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. On the Corvette dual-clutch transmission GM checks valve 4 for a mismatch between commanded and estimated current (over 70 % for 60 ms, or 400 mA for 300 ms in 23OBDG07), but that check reports P27D0. Ford's 2024 list for the TR9070 likewise offers only open load, shorted load and shorted switch for SPV4. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 sets the general monitoring duty. Typical reasons would be rising contact resistance, a solenoid with partly shorted turns, or a weak TCM driver output.
c: Rising contact resistance in the circuit
Solenoid R with partly shorted turns
s: MIL on
Shift feel varies on rods 3 and 4

P27CF.t: Pressure Control Solenoid R Control Circuit Low
P27CF.d: P27CF tells that the control line of solenoid R is held low, as if shorted to ground. On the Corvette dual-clutch transmission GM (23OBDG07, still present in 24OBDG07) monitors synchronizer actuation valve 4 while energized; the driver chip compares the sense pin with a threshold of roughly 1.7 V and, after 150 ms below it, reports a ground fault rated Type A. Ford's TR9070 list gives P27CF to a shorted switch on SPV4. A ground short bypasses the driver, so the valve can apply rods 3 and 4 towards A when no shift is wanted; the controller then usually locks the affected gears. Chafed insulation, a crushed harness clip or a coil shorted to its housing are typical finds.
c: Chafed insulation grounding the control line
Harness crushed at a clip or bracket
Solenoid R coil shorted to its housing
s: MIL on
Unwanted rod movement, gears locked out
Limp mode

P27D0.t: Pressure Control Solenoid R Control Circuit High
P27D0.d: P27D0 is the high-side counterpart of P27CF for solenoid R: the control line reads too high, most often because it touches battery voltage or another output. GM applies the same driver diagnostics to synchronizer actuation valve 4 of the Corvette dual-clutch box as to the other valves (23OBDG07, 24OBDG07): a sense voltage stuck above 0.7-1.1 V while switched on, a large gap between target and estimated current, or a cross-short to a neighbouring line found during the switch-off routine and reported on the next start, each Type A. Ford's TR9070 overview lists shorted load of SPV4 under this code. A coil with too few ohms can also cause it, so measure resistance before replacing the harness.
c: Cross-short to a neighbouring solenoid line
Solenoid R coil resistance too low
s: MIL on, sometimes only after restart
Gears on rods 3/4 not available
Limp mode

P27D1.t: Pressure Control Solenoid S Performance/Stuck Off
P27D1.d: P27D1 flags pressure control solenoid S as unable to produce force. Only GM documents it publicly: in the Corvette dual-clutch tables 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07 it is shift solenoid 5, the only one of these valves serving a single rod, rod 5, which it moves in both directions depending on the selector position. If the intrusive integrity routine sees 100 µm or less of travel on rod 5 while valve 5 is applied, the fault is stored as Type A. Ford's TR9070 has just four synchronizer valves, so the code does not appear there. Gears carried on rod 5 become unavailable; fluid condition, a sticking spool or a leak in the rod actuator are the first things to check.
c: Spool of solenoid S sticking closed
Leak at the rod 5 actuator piston
s: MIL on
Gears on rod 5 unavailable
Gearbox in substitute mode

P27D2.t: Pressure Control Solenoid S Stuck On
P27D2.d: With P27D2 the TCM concludes that solenoid S applies pressure that was never requested. GM is the only maker publishing it, for shift solenoid 5 of the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox (23OBDG07, carried over to 24OBDG07). Because valve 5 serves rod 5 on its own, there is no partner rod to relax; instead the trigger is far larger: rod 5 must drift 4,000 µm or more within 200 ms after the selector valve changes position although its force target is zero. The result is Type A with the MIL. Ford's four-valve TR9070 does not have the code. Expect the gears on rod 5 to be blocked and possibly a harsh engagement or a fallback mode.
c: Spool of solenoid S jammed open
Particles keeping valve S from venting
Worn armature or seat in solenoid S
s: MIL on
Harsh engagement or clunk
Gears on rod 5 blocked, fallback mode

P27D3.d: P27D3 reports an electrical problem with pressure control solenoid S without saying which kind. No manufacturer publishes this code. GM, the only maker known to fit a fifth synchronizer valve (Corvette dual-clutch, 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07), monitors that valve with separate codes from the S block: P27D5 open load, P27D7 short to ground and P27D8 short to battery, current error or a short to a neighbouring output found at shutdown, all Type A. P27D3 would therefore come from a controller that does not differentiate. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 calls for circuit checks on transmission actuators. Check the coil, connector and harness first.
c: Solenoid S coil open or shorted
Corroded or loose connector at the transmission
Damaged wiring between TCM and solenoid S
s: MIL on
Gears on rod 5 unavailable
Limp mode possible

P27D4.d: P27D4 means the controller noticed solenoid S dropping out now and then, electrically or in its effect, without the fault staying present. No manufacturer publishes this code. GM, whose Corvette dual-clutch gearbox has a fifth synchronizer valve for rod 5 (tables 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07), reports lasting wiring faults on it as P27D5, P27D7 and P27D8 and its stuck states as P27D1 and P27D2; a separate sporadic code is not listed there. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 still requires transmission actuators to be monitored. For the driver it can mean an occasional refusal of the rod 5 gears. Wiggle-test the harness with the engine running, inspect the gearbox connector seal and check whether the fault follows heat.
c: Gearbox connector seal leaking, terminals corroding
Harness conductor breaking under engine movement
Solenoid S winding dropping out when hot
s: MIL comes and goes
Rod 5 gears occasionally refused

P27D5.t: Pressure Control Solenoid S Control Circuit/Open
P27D5.d: P27D5 stands for an interrupted control circuit of solenoid S. GM uses it for synchronizer actuation valve 5 in the Corvette DCT, documented in 23OBDG07 and again in 24OBDG07. While the low-side output is off, a working coil pulls the sense pin up to supply voltage; the driver chip then tries to hold that pin low with a tiny current. If it manages to, the pin settles at roughly 1.7 V to 3 V, and after 150 ms this counts as open load, Type A with MIL. The test only runs between 8.75 and 18 V supply, not during cranking, and is suppressed when P0882 or P0883 is present. Ford's TR9070 has no valve S. With valve 5 dead, rod 5 cannot be moved and its gears drop out.
c: Terminal pushed back in the gearbox connector
Broken control wire between TCM and valve
s: MIL on
Gears on rod 5 missing
Emergency program

P27D6.t: Pressure Control Solenoid S Control Circuit Range/Performance
P27D6.d: P27D6 would indicate that the circuit of solenoid S is still closed but its electrical behaviour does not fit what the module commands. There is no public manufacturer description. On the Corvette dual-clutch transmission GM does compare target and estimated coil current of valve 5 (a 70 % gap held 60 ms, or a 400 mA gap held 300 ms, per 23OBDG07), yet files that result under the high-circuit code P27D8, so P27D6 stays unused there. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 only sets the general duty to check actuator circuits. If another controller stores it, likely culprits are added resistance at a crimp, a coil whose ohms have drifted with age and heat, or a TCM output stage losing strength.
c: Added resistance at a crimp or pin
Solenoid S coil resistance out of specification
s: MIL on
Uneven shifts into rod 5 gears

P27D7.t: Pressure Control Solenoid S Control Circuit Low
P27D7.d: P27D7 reports the control line of solenoid S stuck at too low a level, typically a short to ground. GM applies it to synchronizer actuation valve 5 on the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox (23OBDG07, carried into 24OBDG07): with the output switched on, the sense pin should be pulled down only partly; if it drops below roughly 1.7 V and stays there 150 ms, the driver chip flags a ground short and the TCM stores a Type A fault. As the coil is switched on the ground side, a grounded line can leave valve 5 powered without command, pushing rod 5 against the intended gear. Ford's TR9070 does not use solenoid S. Look for chafed insulation near brackets and for a coil shorted to its housing.
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Solenoid S coil shorted to its housing
Faulty low-side driver in the TCM
s: MIL on
Unintended rod 5 movement, gears locked
Limp mode

P27D8.t: Pressure Control Solenoid S Control Circuit High
P27D8.d: P27D8 says the control line of solenoid S sits too high. GM bundles three checks for valve 5 of the Corvette dual-clutch box under it (23OBDG07, 24OBDG07), all Type A. First, with the output on, a sense voltage above 700, 900 or 1,100 mV, depending on whether supply is below 11.5 V, between 12 and 15 V or above 15.5 V, means a short to battery. Second, coil current that misses its target by more than 70 % for 60 ms or by 400 mA for 300 ms. Third, a short to a neighbouring output found while every output is cycled at shutdown; it is stored in memory and set on the next start. Ford's TR9070 has no valve S. An energized valve 5 then fails to move rod 5, so its gears stay out of reach.
c: Control wire touching a supply line
Short to the wire of another valve output
Solenoid S coil with shorted turns
s: MIL on, possibly only after the next start
Rod 5 gears out of reach
Limp mode

P27D9.t: Pressure Control Solenoid T Performance/Stuck Off
P27D9.d: P27D9 is logged when solenoid T fails to build the pressure it is asked for. Ford's 2024 OBD overview for the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox assigns it to the selector pilot valve (SELPV) when that valve stays hydraulically off. That pilot valve moves the selector valve, which decides which shift rods the synchronizer valves SPV1 to SPV4 act on; Ford keeps separate codes for the selector valve and the whole selector mechanism (P178D, P178B). No thresholds are published. GM's Corvette dual-clutch box has the same kind of valve but files its stuck-off fault under P2829, not P27D9. If the selector cannot switch, part of the gear set is unreachable. Fluid level, contamination and the pilot valve itself are the first checks.
c: Selector valve spool binding in its bore
s: MIL on
Several gears unavailable
Gearbox in fallback mode

P27DA.t: Pressure Control Solenoid T Stuck On
P27DA.d: P27DA marks solenoid T as delivering pressure while it should be vented. Ford lists it in the 2024 overview for the TR9070 for a selector pilot valve whose hydraulic output stays on; neighbouring entries P178C and P178A cover the selector valve and the complete selector mechanism stuck on. Ford gives no detection limits. For comparison, GM detects the same fault on the Corvette selector pilot valve (code P282A, 23OBDG07) during a synchronizer integrity routine: small test movements of the rods show whether the selector sits in the opposite position to the one commanded, and a current-profile check of the pilot valve separates it from the selector spool. A selector locked in one position sends shifts to the wrong rods, so the TCM blocks gears.
c: Selector pilot valve held open by dirt
Worn seat or armature in solenoid T
Abrasion particles from clutch or synchronizer wear
s: MIL on
Gears locked out, wrong gear engagement possible
Fallback mode

P27DB.d: P27DB is a catch-all for electrical trouble on solenoid T that does not name the kind of fault. No manufacturer publishes it. The only known valve T is the selector pilot valve of Ford's TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox, and Ford's 2024 overview splits that valve's wiring faults into P27DD for open load, P27DF for a shorted switch and P27E0 for a shorted load instead of using this code. GM's Corvette has a comparable pilot valve but numbers it under the K block (P282D to P2830). CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 demands circuit monitoring of transmission actuators in general. Diagnosis follows the detailed codes: coil ohms, connector pins, harness insulation, then the TCM.
c: Solenoid T coil open or shorted
Corrosion or poor fit at the gearbox connector
Defective TCM output for solenoid T
s: MIL on
Restricted gear choice
Limp mode possible

P27DC.d: With P27DC the module reports that solenoid T misbehaved only briefly before working again. No maker has published a description of this code. Ford's TR9070, the only known application of a valve T (selector pilot valve, 2024 overview), is covered by lasting electrical codes and by stuck-on and stuck-off codes, none of them sporadic. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires the transmission actuators to be monitored. Because the selector pilot valve decides which rods the shift valves reach, even a short dropout can make a gear selection fail or arrive late. Freeze-frame data showing temperature and road conditions at the moment of the fault help more than a single resistance check in the workshop.
c: Loose pin in the gearbox connector
Particles briefly holding the valve spool
s: MIL lights up from time to time
Occasional failed or late gear selection

P27DD.t: Pressure Control Solenoid T Control Circuit/Open
P27DD.d: P27DD tells that the control circuit of solenoid T is open, so no current reaches the coil. Ford's 2024 OBD overview gives this code to open load on the selector pilot valve of the TR9070 dual-clutch transmission; the document lists the fault type only, without limits. How such a test usually works is shown by GM for the corresponding pilot valve of the Corvette, there coded P282D: with the output off, a sense voltage stuck in the 1.7 to 3.0 V window for 100 ms reveals the missing load (23OBDG07). A dead pilot valve leaves the selector in its rest position, so the synchronizer valves can only reach one group of rods. A displaced terminal, a broken lead or a burnt winding are the usual finds.
s: MIL on
Only some gears selectable
Fallback mode

P27DE.t: Pressure Control Solenoid T Control Circuit Range/Performance
P27DE.d: P27DE would be set if the circuit of solenoid T is intact but delivers readings the controller considers implausible. No manufacturer documents the code. For the selector pilot valve of the TR9070, Ford's 2024 summary knows just three electrical faults, namely open load, shorted load and shorted switch, and GM checks the comparable Corvette pilot valve under its own K-block codes. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 prescribes the general circuit and function monitoring for such actuators. Where a module does use P27DE, it hints at a gradual change rather than a clean break: a terminal with rising contact resistance, a coil whose resistance has crept away from nominal, or an output stage in the TCM that no longer regulates current properly.
c: Rising contact resistance at a terminal
Solenoid T resistance drifted from nominal
TCM output no longer regulating current
s: MIL on
Hesitant or inconsistent gear selection

P27DF.t: Pressure Control Solenoid T Control Circuit Low
P27DF.d: P27DF points to a control line of solenoid T pulled too low. In Ford's 2024 OBD summary it is the shorted-switch fault of the selector pilot valve on the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox, meaning the switched side of the coil is tied to ground and the valve can be powered permanently. Ford publishes no thresholds. GM's equivalent test on the Corvette selector pilot valve (P282F in 23OBDG07) flags a sense voltage below roughly 1.7 V for 100 ms while the output is on. A permanently applied pilot valve holds the selector in its working position, so the shift valves keep acting on the same rods and the controller has to fence off gears. Inspect for insulation damage and a coil shorted to ground.
c: Damaged insulation letting the wire touch ground
Solenoid T coil shorted to ground
s: MIL on
Gears fenced off, shifts limited to some gears
Limp mode

P27E0.t: Pressure Control Solenoid T Control Circuit High
P27E0.d: P27E0 reports a control line of solenoid T sitting too high. Ford's 2024 overview of the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox uses it for a shorted load on the selector pilot valve, a coil or line bypassed to battery so the driver cannot pull current through the winding. Limits are not stated by Ford. On the Corvette, GM tests its comparable pilot valve under P2830 with a supply-dependent voltage limit of 0.7 to 1.1 V, a current-deviation check and a shutdown scan for shorts to neighbouring outputs (23OBDG07). Since the pilot valve then cannot be applied, the selector stays at rest and the gears on the other rod group are lost. Check for a wire touching a feed, shorted coil turns and a cross-short to adjacent valve lines.
c: Control wire shorted to a supply feed
Cross-short to an adjacent valve line
s: MIL on
Gears of one rod group lost
Fallback mode

P27E1.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Pressure Too Low
P27E1.d: P27E1 is a hydraulic verdict, not a wiring one: electric auxiliary pump A was running on command, yet the pressure it built stayed below what the module expected. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM shows how such a check works on its CVTs (2025 TCM tables): during an engine auto-start, with more than 400 kPa requested, both pulley pressure sensors reading under 200 kPa for over 0.525 s set the broader performance code P2797, Type B. Wiring faults on the pump belong to P2796 and its siblings, leakage to P0B0C, and pump B has P27E2. Worn pump gears, a clogged intake screen, low fluid or a leaking check valve are typical. Stop-start is usually blocked, and restarts after a stop may engage harshly.
c: Worn pump gears or internal leakage inside pump A
Low or aerated transmission fluid, pump draws air
Intake screen of the pump partly blocked by debris
Check valve in the pump circuit not sealing
s: Stop-start function disabled
Jerky or delayed engagement when the engine restarts after a stop
MIL or transmission warning lit

P27E2.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Pressure Too Low
P27E2.d: P27E2 flags that the second electric pump, B, delivered too little pressure although it was driven. Nobody publishes this code openly. Where a gearbox carries a pump labelled B, it is often a separate unit on the outside of the case: Audi's bulletin 34-17-25 calls oil pump V553 of the 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL seven-speed twin-clutch boxes pump B and lists P27A3, P27A6 and P276B for it, but not P27E2. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires such actuators to be checked for proper function. Compared with P27A3, which covers no delivery at all, P27E2 points to a pump that works but weakly; P277A singles out hydraulic leakage, P27E1 is the same check on pump A. Expect stop-start or clutch cooling to be restricted.
c: Pump B worn, motor running but delivering too little
Leaking O-ring or pressure line between pump B and the gearbox
Fluid level too low for pump B to prime
Weak battery or poor ground slowing the pump motor
s: Stop-start no longer stops the engine
Reduced clutch cooling, power limited when hot
Warning light on

P27E3.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Valve Circuit/Open
P27E3.d: The control valve named here decides where the oil from the electric auxiliary pump goes. Volkswagen's training book for the 0GC seven-speed DSG shows such a layout: pressure regulator N218 shifts a spring-loaded changeover piston that sends the flow of pump V475 either to the mechatronic unit or to clutch cooling. No maker publishes P27E3 itself. The code reports that the valve's drive circuit is broken or so resistive that the module measures no proper current: a cut wire, a lifted pin or an open coil. Without the valve the pump flow can end up in the wrong branch, so stop-start or cooling support may be dropped. P27E5 and P27E6 cover shorts, P27E4 a valve that responds wrongly.
c: Broken conductor in the valve control line
Pin backed out or corroded at the gearbox connector
s: Stop-start unavailable
Warning light with stored open-circuit fault

P27E4.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Valve Circuit Range/Performance
P27E4.d: P27E4 is the plausibility check for the auxiliary pump control valve: the circuit is intact, but its current or its hydraulic effect does not match the command. No manufacturer lists the code publicly, so the logic can only be inferred. In a layout like Volkswagen's 0GC dual-clutch box, where a pressure regulator moves a changeover piston to steer the oil of the electric pump, a sticking piston or a coil with drifting resistance would cause exactly this mismatch. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 asks for both electrical and functional monitoring of transmission actuators. Dirty fluid and varnish are the usual reasons a valve hangs. Unlike P27E3, P27E5 or P27E6 the wiring tests pass here; P27E1 may follow if pressure stays too low.
c: Valve or changeover piston sticking from contaminated fluid
Contact resistance at the connector distorting the current
s: Stop-start works only sometimes
Harsh engagement after an auto-start
Warning light on

P27E5.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Valve Circuit Low
P27E5.d: P27E5 sets when the voltage on the auxiliary pump control valve line is pulled toward ground, typically by chafed insulation touching the case or by a coil shorted internally. No manufacturer documents the code openly. For orientation: in Volkswagen's 8-speed 09P and 0GC transmissions the electric pump V475 keeps pressure while the engine is stopped, and a regulator-driven valve routes its flow; a grounded drive line would leave that valve in its spring position. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires circuit monitoring for such outputs. The controller usually switches the output off to protect its driver. P27E6 is the opposite fault, a short to supply; P27E3 an open. Check the harness where it passes brackets or the oil pan.
c: Control line chafed through and touching ground
Fluid or water in the connector bridging to ground
s: Stop-start switched off
MIL lit

P27E6.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Valve Circuit High
P27E6.d: P27E6 means the control valve circuit of the auxiliary pump reads higher than allowed, as if the line were tied to battery voltage. A wire rubbing against a live conductor in the same harness, or a driver stage that no longer switches off, are the classic triggers. The code is not documented by any manufacturer in public. As a model of the hardware, VW's 0GC and 09P training books describe an electric pump V475 whose oil is steered by a pressure-regulated changeover valve; a permanently energized drive would hold that valve in one position. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 calls for detecting such shorts. Because the valve cannot be released, the module typically disables stop-start. Low is P27E5, open circuit P27E3.
c: Control line shorted to a supply wire in the harness
Corrosion bridging adjacent pins in the connector
Output stage in the control module stuck on
s: Stop-start inoperative
Warning light on, possibly further pump codes

P27E7.d: 'Transmission Range Control' belongs to shift-by-wire, where the selected range travels as an electrical signal instead of a cable. Only channel A is documented in public: Mitsubishi's 2022 manual sets P07E8 when one of eight electric shift sensors in the selector rises above 4.5 V for 2.4 s with the ignition on, and names no fail-safe reaction. A B channel, which P27E7 would cover, is not described by any manufacturer, so P27E7 is best read as the same open-circuit test on a second, redundant circuit. GM's internal range selection uses a separate set of B codes, P27EF to P27F2, for its valve position sensor. Inspect selector connector and harness; the vehicle may refuse some ranges or shift to park only.
c: Loose or corroded connector at the electric selector
Broken wire between selector and control module
Sensor inside the selector assembly failed open
s: Warning about the shift system in the cluster
Some ranges not accepted from the selector

P27E8.t: Transmission Range Control B Circuit Performance
P27E8.d: P27E8 is the plausibility test for range control circuit B: the signal is neither open nor shorted, yet its value makes no sense, for example a level stuck between the valid on and off windows. The title reads Circuit Performance, without Range. No manufacturer publishes the code. Mitsubishi's 2022 shift-by-wire CVT shows the A version, P07E9: a selector sensor voltage sitting for 2.4 s in a forbidden band (such as 2.12 to 2.67 V) counts as a fault, with no fail-safe action because the other sensors still identify the position. A second channel would be judged the same way. Contact resistance, moisture in the selector or an aging Hall element are the likely sources. Open, low and high are P27E7, P27E9 and P27EA.
c: Contact resistance at selector terminals shifting the voltage
Spilled drink or moisture inside the selector
Position sensor in the selector degrading
s: Intermittent shift system warning
Displayed range occasionally flickers or lags

P27E9.t: Transmission Range Control B Circuit Low
P27E9.d: P27E9 reports that a line of range control circuit B sits too close to zero volts, pointing to a grounded line or a sensor that pulls its output down. It is not described publicly by any manufacturer. The documented counterpart on channel A is Mitsubishi's P07EA (2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift): an input under 0.6 V on one of the eight selector sensors for 2.4 s sets it, the cause being a grounded or open sensor line, and the vehicle keeps driving normally. With shift-by-wire there is no mechanical link to fall back on, so redundant channels matter. Look for pinched wiring under the console. The sensor B counterparts in GM's internal range selection are P27F1 and P27F2.
c: Harness pinched under the center console, shorted to ground
Sensor supply interrupted, output drops to zero
s: Shift system warning on the display
Usually no change in how the car drives

P27EA.t: Transmission Range Control B Circuit High
P27EA.d: With P27EA, a signal of range control circuit B reads near the supply voltage, which usually means a short to a power wire or a broken ground return that lets the line float high. No manufacturer documents the B code openly. Mitsubishi's channel A twin, P07EB, sets above 4.5 V on one of the eight sensors in the electric selector for 2.4 s and lists a short to power as cause; normal driving remains possible. A missing sensor ground produces the same picture as a short to battery, so check the ground pin before replacing the selector. In shift-by-wire systems a high reading on one channel is cross-checked against the remaining channels. P27E9 is the low counterpart, P27E7 the open circuit.
c: Signal line shorted to a supply wire
Sensor ground open, signal floats high
s: Shift system message in the cluster
Car usually still drives normally

P27EB.t: Transmission Range Control A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit/Open
P27EB.d: GM uses this code on automatics with internal electronic range selection (ETRS), where hydraulic mode valves within the valve body set park, reverse, neutral and drive. Mode valve A carries a Hall position sensor. In the 2020 tables for the T87A 10-speed RWD unit, P27EB sets when the raw sensor voltage lands in an invalid band between 1.263 and 1.504 V, debounced at 0.100 s per 0.163 s window, with at least 9 V battery voltage; it is Type A, so the MIL lights on the first trip. Such a level fits neither valve state and usually means a broken signal wire or a failing sensor. Shorts are P27ED and P27EE, implausible movement P27EC; valve B has P27EF. Range changes may be limited until the cause is fixed.
c: Signal wire of the mode valve A sensor broken or loose
Hall sensor on mode valve A failing
Damaged internal transmission harness or pass-through connector
s: MIL on after the first trip
Range selection restricted or delayed

P27EC.t: Transmission Range Control A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P27EC.d: P27EC is GM's movement check for mode valve A of its internal range selection: after the TCM commands park, drive or reverse, the position sensor must report the new state within a set delay; the logic also watches line pressure and clutch slip. Both the 2018 nine-speed and 2020 ten-speed tables rate it Type A. Bulletins show it is often hydraulic: 21-NA-169 has the valve body replaced on low-mileage 9T45/50/60 units when P27EC or P27F0 appear with clean fluid, PIP6069 says to renew the valve body rather than the TCM on 2024 full-size trucks and SUVs with the 10L80, and 19-NA-200 notes that on the 2025 Equinox a failed auxiliary pump or harness sets P27EC before P2797.
c: Mode valve A sticking inside the control valve body
No hydraulic pressure from a failed auxiliary pump during auto stop
Mode valve A position sensor reading wrong
s: Delayed or refused shift into park, drive or reverse
MIL on, stop-start may be disabled
Transmission in reduced operating mode

P27ED.t: Transmission Range Control A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P27ED.d: P27ED tells that the Hall sensor on mode valve A of GM's internal range selection delivers almost no voltage. In both the 2018 9-speed and the 2020 10-speed RWD tables the limit is a raw value under 0.414 V for 0.100 s within 0.163 s, with at least 9 V on the battery; GM itself blames a grounded or interrupted line. The code is Type A and lights the MIL on the first trip. Because the TCM then cannot confirm whether the valve has left park, the movement check P27EC is suspended while P27ED is active. Look at the sensor connector inside the transmission and the pass-through plug. High is P27EE, the invalid middle band P27EB, and valve B uses P27F1 for the same fault.
c: Sensor signal shorted to ground in the internal harness
Hall sensor on mode valve A failed
s: MIL lit immediately
Shifts out of park slow or blocked

P27EE.t: Transmission Range Control A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P27EE.d: The opposite of P27ED: the position sensor of mode valve A reads higher than any valid state. GM's TCM tables for the T87A nine-speed of 2018 and the rear-drive ten-speed of 2020 set P27EE when the raw signal exceeds 2.538 V for 0.100 s inside a 0.163 s sample, describing it as a short to voltage on the sensor circuit; the MIL comes on at once (Type A). A sensor that has lost its ground return can also float upward and mimic a short. While the fault is present, GM blocks the plausibility test P27EC and several pressure checks, since the valve position is unknown. Repairs usually involve the internal harness or the sensor; valve B reports the same condition as P27F2, the open band as P27EB.
c: Sensor signal shorted to a voltage source
Sensor ground open, signal drifts high
s: MIL on from the first trip
Range changes restricted, possible reduced mode

P27EF.t: Transmission Range Control B Position Sensor/Switch Circuit/Open
P27EF.d: P27EF concerns the second mode valve, B, of GM's internal electronic range selection. Its Hall sensor is expected to sit clearly high or clearly low; GM's 2018 9-speed and 2020 10-speed RWD tables treat a raw value between 1.263 and 1.504 V, held for 0.100 s of a 0.163 s sample, as an illegal level. A level in that gap typically comes from an interrupted signal line or a sensor that has stopped switching. The tables show the same timing as for valve A, but the MIL column for P27EF is left blank in both editions, so the illumination type is not stated. Mode valve B is involved in neutral and drive states, so shifting may be limited. Low and high are P27F1 and P27F2, the movement test P27F0.
c: Mode valve B sensor signal line interrupted
Hall sensor on mode valve B no longer switching cleanly
Fluid or corrosion at the transmission pass-through connector
s: Transmission warning, neutral or drive engagement may be restricted
Fault stored in the TCM

P27F0.t: Transmission Range Control B Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P27F0.d: P27F0 checks whether mode valve B really moves. In GM's 2020 table for the T87A 10-speed RWD transmission, the TCM expects the valve B sensor to follow commands to park, reverse, neutral high or low, neutral shift and drive within a delay; if the final state is not reached under adequate line pressure, the Type A code sets. The electrical sensor codes P27EF, P27F1 and P27F2 must be clear for the test to run. In GM bulletin 21-NA-169, aimed at 9T45/50/60 automatics with under 19,000 km, P27F0 sits beside P27EC in the group where the valve body is replaced if the fluid looks healthy; dark, burnt fluid means the clutches need inspection too. Drivers notice delayed or refused range changes.
c: Mode valve B sticking in the valve body
Insufficient line pressure to move the valve
Position sensor B reporting late or wrong state
s: Delay or refusal when selecting neutral, drive or reverse
MIL on, transmission may enter a protective mode

P27F1.t: Transmission Range Control B Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P27F1.d: P27F1 reports a valve B position signal that has collapsed toward ground in GM's internal range selection. GM describes the trigger as a ground short or open circuit on the mode valve B sensor line and uses the same 0.414 V limit, 0.100 s debounce and 9 V minimum supply as on valve A; both table editions, 2018 and 2020, rate it Type A, MIL on the first trip. As long as P27F1 is active, the TCM cannot verify valve B and drops its movement test P27F0. Hall sensors need a supply and a ground, so a dead supply pin also produces a low reading. Typical repairs concern the internal harness, the pass-through seal or the sensor. Valve A's counterpart is P27ED; high is P27F2.
c: Valve B sensor line shorted to ground
Sensor supply missing at the internal connector
Hall sensor on mode valve B failed
s: MIL comes on on the first trip
Neutral or drive engagement slow or blocked

P27F2.t: Transmission Range Control B Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P27F2.d: With P27F2 the TCM sees the valve B position sensor above its valid range, which GM interprets as a short to voltage on that circuit. The threshold is 2.538 V, which must persist 0.100 s in a 0.163 s sampling period; GM applies it to internal range selection in the 2018 T87A nine-speed and the 2020 rear-drive ten-speed. The 2020 table rates it Type A; in the 2018 edition the MIL entry for P27F2 is blank. With valve B unconfirmed, GM suspends the movement test P27F0. Apart from a real short, a lost sensor ground can push the reading up, so measure the ground before replacing parts. P27EE is the same fault on valve A, P27F1 the low reading and P27EF the illegal mid-band level. Shifting into neutral or drive may be restricted.
c: Valve B sensor line shorted to a voltage source
s: Warning light and stored transmission fault
Neutral or drive selection restricted

P27F3.d: P27F3 reports that the second clutch of a gearbox, usually the clutch on the even-gear side of a dual-clutch unit, has exceeded its permitted temperature, either measured or calculated from slip and load. Stellantis is the one maker with a public, code-exact document: bulletin 21-040-26 (May 2026) lists P27F3-00 as clutch 2 overtemperature on European 2022-2025 Jeep Renegade and Compass with the 1.5 L mild hybrid and the 7HDT300 dual-clutch box. The MIL is lit, and gear groups or reverse may become unavailable. Particles that block a pump in the electric clutch actuator are named as the cause, and the actuator cylinder is replaced. P2787 is the same verdict for clutch A. Repeated creeping or hill starts make it worse.
c: Pump in the electric clutch actuator blocked by particles
Long slipping phases from creeping, towing or hill starts
Worn clutch 2 that needs more slip to transmit torque
Insufficient clutch cooling or low or aged fluid
s: Malfunction indicator and transmission warning lamp on
Even gears or reverse temporarily unavailable
Judder or burning smell when pulling away

P27F4.t: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator A Performance/Stuck On
P27F4.d: P27F4 concerns the mechanical result of the shift lock, not its wiring: actuator A was commanded but stays in its active state or does not reach the requested position. Whether active means locked or released depends on the design. No manufacturer documents P27F4 publicly. Ford reports the same kind of fault as P0929 from its shifter module: bulletin 25-2045 for 2021-2024 F-150 lists a shifter that will not leave Park or will not stow, with the wrench lamp rather than the MIL. FCA recall 16V-249 explains the risk of a failed interlock solenoid on 2016 Grand Cherokee: the lever could stay trapped in Park or Neutral. Check for binding in the shifter, then supply and ground of the actuator. P27F5 is the opposite stuck state.
c: Lock pin or actuator binding in the shifter mechanism
Faulty gear shift module or its software
Implausible brake pedal signal keeping the lock commanded
s: Selector cannot be moved out of Park despite pressing the brake
Shift system warning or wrench lamp in the cluster
Clicking from the shifter with no release

P27F5.t: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator A Stuck Off
P27F5.d: With P27F5 the control unit concludes that shift lock actuator A remains in its passive state although it was told to act. Depending on the design, that can leave the lever free to leave Park without the brake, which defeats the brake interlock, or permanently blocked. No maker publishes this code. FCA recall 16V-249 describes a badly crimped harness terminal on the interlock solenoid of 2016 Jeep Grand Cherokee that cut solenoid function. Ford reports a shift lock actuator that misses its target position as P0929 and fixes it with a new module or software (SSM 51057). Typical culprits are a loose terminal, a weak coil or a broken return spring. P27F4 covers the actuator stuck in its active state; wiring faults are P0928 to P0931.
c: Loose or badly crimped terminal at the lock solenoid
Weak solenoid coil that no longer moves the lock pin
Broken return spring or worn lock pin
Shifter module software misjudging the actuator position
s: Selector leaves Park without the brake pedal being pressed
Lever stays blocked in Park or Neutral
Shift system warning message

P2800.t: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit (PRNDL Input)
P2800.d: P2800 is the general circuit code for the second signal path that tells the modules which selector position (P, R, N, D, L) is engaged.
