It applies when that signal is unusable without a clear low, high or frequency pattern. Ford's 2019 hybrid OBD summary lists it for the eCVT range sensor with the wrench lamp and no MIL, judged in under a second; one section also sets it when the gear position message from the engine module over CAN is invalid. Ford's 2024 summary uses P2800 as the base number for its TRS B sub-faults. Ford message SSM 47790 ranks P2800 among the most frequent codes on Fusion, MKZ and C-Max hybrids built 2013-2019, caused by water or corrosion in several connectors. Sensor A has P0705.
c: Water entry or corrosion in connectors along the sensor circuit
Chafed or broken wiring between sensor and module
Invalid gear position message from another module over CAN
s: Wrench lamp or MIL on, gear display missing or wrong
Engine does not start in Park or Neutral
Trouble selecting a drive position

P2801.t: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2801.d: Here the B signal of the range sensor is electrically present but its content does not make sense. On sensors with a pulse-width output, Ford checks the carrier frequency: its 2024 summary sets P2801 (UDS P2800_38) on the 6R80, 6R140, 10R60 and 10R80 automatics when the frequency leaves 125 Hz plus or minus 25 Hz, while the 2012 summary applies the same test to the 250 Hz signal of the DPS6 dual-clutch box. On the hybrid eCVT, Ford's 2019 summary instead compares two sensor angles and fails it beyond 3.85 degrees, with the wrench lamp only. Ford SSM 49822 lists P2801 among range and fluid temperature sensor codes on 2020-2021 Super Duty trucks with the 10R140. P0706 is the A-side counterpart.
c: Range sensor electronics producing a wrong signal frequency
Damaged or loose pins at the transmission connector
Sensor shifted on its shaft so the angles disagree
s: Warning lamp with shift quality or gear display issues
Transmission uses a fixed substitute range strategy

P2802.t: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit Low
P2802.d: P2802 means the B signal of the range sensor sits too low, usually a ground short or a duty cycle collapsing toward zero. GM's tables for 2020 and 2025 place the check in the engine module, which reads internal range sensor B on its own wire: a circuit impedance under 0.5 ohm to ground for 0.5 s within a one-second window sets the code as Type A, MIL in the first trip. Ford's 2024 summary sets it (P2800_84) on its six- and ten-speed automatics when the duty cycle drops below 8 %. Ford's hybrid sedans and the C-Max showed P2802 alongside P2800 once water had entered connectors (SSM 47790). P2803 is the high fault and P0707 the matching low fault of sensor A.
c: Signal wire of sensor B shorted to ground
Water or corrosion in a connector of the circuit
Range sensor output stage failed low
s: MIL or wrench lamp on
No start in Park, missing gear indication
Stop-start or shift functions restricted

P2803.t: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit High
P2803.d: P2803 is stored when the output of range sensor B reads too high, which typically points to an open circuit or a short to supply voltage. In GM's 2020 and 2025 tables the engine module watches its own range sensor input for this: either under 0.5 ohm to the voltage source or above 200 kilohms to ground for 0.5 s sets a Type A fault. Ford's 2024 summary flags a duty cycle over 92 % (P2800_85). In practice Ford saw P2803 together with P2804 and fluid temperature codes on 2020-2021 Transit vans, where partly seated or damaged pins in four connectors were to blame (SSM 49242 and 49510). On 2021 Bronco Sport, bulletin 21-2331 tied it to PCM calibration and fixed it by reprogramming. Low is P2802.
c: Open signal circuit or pushed-out connector pin
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source
Module calibration misreading the signal, fixed by software
s: MIL on, often with transmission temperature codes
Shift system warning in the instrument cluster
Wrong or missing gear display

P2804.t: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2804.d: P2804 points to a B signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing permanently. Ford is the main user: its 2024 OBD summary books it as the general electrical fault of TRS B (UDS P2800_01), checked continuously, with up to 30 s allowed for pattern recognition and 2 s for analog faults. On 2020-2021 Transit vans, Ford's messages SSM 49242 and 49510 describe P2804 appearing with P2803, P0708, P0709, P0710 and P0713 and the MIL lit, and send technicians to four connectors to look for partial seating or pushed pins before any further diagnosis. The 2021 Bronco Sport bulletin 21-2331 lists it as well. Wiggle tests on the harness with the selector moved through all positions help to catch it.
c: Connector not fully seated or pin pushed back
Harness chafing that opens the circuit under vibration
Worn contacts or electronics inside the range sensor
s: MIL comes and goes, often with several transmission codes
Gear display flickers
Occasional shift system warning

P2805.d: Both range sensor signals are valid on their own, yet they do not agree. Many designs output two complementary pulse-width signals whose duty cycles must add up to 100 %. GM reads signal A in the transmission module and signal B in the engine module and sets P2805 as Type A when the sum is off by more than 4.849 % (2020 table) or 5.2 % (2025) for 1 s of 1.5 s. Ford allows plus or minus 4 % on its six- and ten-speed automatics (2024) and used the same principle on the DPS6 (2012). Audi bulletin 2051686 for 2016-2017 A6 links P280500 with a no-start and a gearbox message, cured by a new drive position sensor G676 plus TCM. Single-signal faults are P0705-P0709 and P2800-P2804.
c: Range sensor with one drifting output
Added resistance or poor ground in one of the two signal paths
Fault in the reading control module
s: MIL and gearbox warning on
Engine will not start or selector position not accepted
Substitute gear or limp operation

P2806.d: P2806 says that the selector position reported by the range sensor and the actual mechanical position of the gearbox do not line up. Ford is the only public user found. Its 2019 hybrid OBD summary lists the code for the eCVT with the wrench lamp and without the MIL; one section defines a park pawl check behind it: if the park motor turns more than 9 radians while the pawl should already be engaged, the code is set. Another section for the same family checks sensor voltages against fixed windows for each position. Common causes are a sensor moved on its shaft after service, a worn selector cable or linkage, or a damaged park mechanism. Re-adjust or replace the sensor and confirm Park holds before driving.
c: Range sensor not aligned correctly after transmission work
Stretched selector cable or worn linkage
Park pawl or park motor mechanism damaged
s: Wrench lamp, gear display differs from lever position
Vehicle may roll in Park
Start refused in Park or Neutral

P2807.d: P2807 is the umbrella code for pressure control solenoid G; the fault type follows in the extra byte. Which hydraulic function G controls is set by each maker. Toyota uses it on its eight-speed automatics: bulletin T-SB-0160-18 lists P28077F (actuator stuck off) on 2017-2018 Highlander and Sienna together with other solenoid codes, whine, harsh shifts and reduced power, and supplies a remanufactured transaxle. T-SB-0076-24 for the 2024 Tacoma names P280771 (actuator stuck) and replaces gearbox and converter. GM's 2016 eight-speed table assigns G to the converter clutch. Specific sibling codes are P2808 to P2815. Debris in the valve body is the usual root cause, so fluid analysis comes first.
c: Debris or wear particles jamming the valve
Solenoid G worn or electrically weak
s: MIL on with harsh or delayed shifts
Whine noise from the transmission
Reduced power or limp mode

P2808.t: Pressure Control Solenoid G Performance/Stuck Off
P2808.d: P2808 means valve G does not deliver the pressure or effect it is commanded to give. GM documents two very different applications. In the 2016 eight-speed table G is the converter clutch valve: with at least 750 kPa commanded, slip of 130 rpm or more in lock mode for 4 s, counted three times, sets the code, and the MIL needs two trips. In the 2023 table for the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox, G is the proportional valve of the electronic limited-slip differential; after a fault triggers a recovery routine, failed current profile checks show the valve hydraulically stuck off, logged as Type B. For the driver this means converter slip and higher fuel use, or a differential that no longer locks. The opposite fault is P2809.
c: Valve G stuck by contamination so pressure stays low
Worn converter clutch lining that slips despite pressure
Low fluid level or internal leak in the circuit
s: MIL on, engine speed higher than expected at cruise
Higher fuel consumption and transmission heat
Limited-slip function inactive on Corvette

P2809.t: Pressure Control Solenoid G Stuck On
P2809.d: P2809 is the reverse case: valve G keeps acting although it should have released. On GM's 2016 eight-speed automatics, where G operates the converter lockup clutch, the converter shows almost no slip, between minus 50 and plus 30 rpm, while the clutch is commanded off; after 1.5 s and six fail counts the controller stores the code, with the MIL lit in the first trip. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table uses the same code when the differential lock valve stays hydraulically engaged, found during a recovery routine and logged as Type B. A converter clutch that does not release can stall the engine when stopping or make the car shudder at low speed. Contaminated fluid and a sticking valve are the leading suspects.
c: Valve G held open by debris
s: Engine stalls or shudders when coming to a stop
MIL on
Differential stays locked on Corvette, tyre scrub in tight turns

P280A.t: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Not Learned
P280A.d: P280A means the module holds no valid learned reference for range sensor A, so it cannot translate the raw signal into a reliable selector position. This is typical after replacing the sensor, the gearbox or the control module, after a software update, or when a learn run was aborted. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 only requires that transmission inputs are checked. Why learning matters is shown by Ford's 2019 hybrid summary, which accepts each selector position only inside narrow voltage windows of the sensor, and by Audi bulletin 2051686, which calls for all basic settings after a new TCM and position sensor. A relearn with a scan tool is normally the fix. P280B is the B side.
c: Learn procedure skipped after replacing sensor, gearbox or module
Learn run aborted, for example by low battery voltage
Learned values cleared by a software update
Sensor signal outside the learnable window
s: Warning lamp right after a repair or update
Engine does not start or gear display missing

P280B.t: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit Not Learned
P280B.d: P280B flags missing or invalid adaptation values for the second range sensor signal. Where a design reads A and B in different modules, as GM does with sensor A in the TCM and sensor B in the engine module, a replaced or reprogrammed engine controller can lose the B reference while A is still learned. No maker documents P280B publicly, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 gives only the general duty to monitor transmission inputs. GM's correlation check P2805 shows how closely both paths are compared afterwards: their duty cycles must add up to 100 % within about 5 %. Without a valid B reference the plausibility checks against A cannot run. Perform the learn with a scan tool once circuit codes P2800-P2804 are cleared.
c: Module reading sensor B replaced or reprogrammed without learn
Open circuit faults on sensor B preventing the learn
s: Warning lamp after module replacement
Gear position checks disabled, possible start refusal

P2810.d: P2810 is a collective electrical code for solenoid G: the control unit sees a fault in coil or wiring but does not split it into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents P2810 publicly. The makers that do use valve G report electrical faults more precisely. GM's 2020 table lists the open circuit as P2812 with the ten-speed line pressure valve and the eight-speed converter clutch valve as G, and Ford's 2024 summary books the even clutch cooling valve of its TR9070 dual-clutch box under P2812, P2814 and P2815. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires such output circuits to be monitored. If the code does appear, measure the coil resistance and check the connector and the supply from the module.
c: Coil of solenoid G open or shorted internally
Damaged internal harness or lead frame
Faulty output stage in the control module
s: MIL on and harsh shifts
Transmission in default pressure or limp mode

P2811.d: With P2811 the module records that valve G misbehaved only for moments, electrically or in effect, and then recovered. No maker publishes a description of this exact code. GM's preliminary information PIP5799 for 2019-2021 vehicles with 10L60 to 10L1000 automatics shows where such faults usually hide: G there is solenoid valve 7, the line pressure valve, and electrical faults on it (P2812 or P2814) are cured by a new valve body if normal diagnosis finds nothing. Because the line pressure valve affects every gear, even short dropouts can cause a single harsh shift. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires the actuator to be monitored. Freeze-frame temperature data and a wiggle test of the gearbox harness help more than one static measurement.
c: Loose terminal or fretting corrosion in the gearbox connector
Intermittent contact inside the valve body solenoid assembly
Coil that fails only when hot
s: Occasional harsh shift, then normal again
MIL that comes and goes

P2812.t: Pressure Control Solenoid G Control Circuit/Open
P2812.d: P2812 signals an open control circuit of solenoid G. GM uses it widely: on the 2016 eight-speed (TCC valve) the hardware open flag must stand for 0.3 s of 0.5 s, one trip; the 2020 table, now with the ten-speed line pressure valve as well, asks for 0.6 s of 0.65 s and rates it Type B; on the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box it is the limited-slip valve, detected by a driver chip test with the output off and confirmed after 150 ms. GM's PIP5799 replaces the 10L valve body when normal diagnosis finds nothing. Ford's 2024 summary books the open load of the even clutch cooling valve on the TR9070 dual-clutch box as P2812. Harsh shifts or lost converter lockup follow.
c: Open coil in solenoid G or in the valve body assembly
Open terminal or corroded pin in the transmission connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty output driver in the control module
s: Check engine light on
Harsh shifts on line pressure designs
No converter lockup or limited-slip function

P2813.t: Pressure Control Solenoid G Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2813.d: On paper P2813 is a plausibility fault in the control circuit of solenoid G, but its main real-world use is hydraulic. Nissan-built CVTs label it as the select solenoid, which applies the forward and reverse clutches. Mitsubishi's 2022 service data for such a CVT sets it in two ways: engagement after N to D or to R happens too fast, under 0.4 s or 0.3 s with input speed at 200 rpm or less, three times in one drive cycle; or the clutch slips with 0.95 MPa commanded, adding up to 30 s. The MIL follows after two trips. Nissan bulletin NTB16-110 covers it on four-cylinder Altima (2013-2017) and Rogue (2014-2017) together with judder codes and replaces the valve body or a CVT section. Expect engagement shock or a sluggish start.
c: Select solenoid valve sticking in the valve body
CVT wear with belt slip or clutch damage
Added resistance in the solenoid circuit
s: Strong shock when selecting D or R
Slow start and weak acceleration
MIL after the second trip

P2814.t: Pressure Control Solenoid G Control Circuit Low
P2814.d: P2814 reports that the drive line of solenoid G is pulled toward ground, typically a chafed wire or a coil shorted to ground. GM's 2020 tables name G as the line pressure valve on nine- and ten-speed boxes and the converter clutch valve on the eight-speed; a resistance of about 0.5 ohm to ground, present for 0.3 s out of a 0.5 s sample, sets a Type A fault. In the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box G drives the limited-slip differential, and a pin voltage under roughly 1.7 V while switched on stores it as Type B. Ford's 2024 summary uses it for a shorted switch on the even clutch cooling valve of the TR9070. GM's PIP5799 replaces the 10-speed valve body when P2812 or P2814 has no other cause. Expect firm shifts or a fixed line pressure.
c: Solenoid G control wire chafed through to ground in the gearbox harness
Solenoid G coil with internal short to its housing
Fault inside the valve body assembly (GM 10-speed, PIP5799)
Damaged output stage in the transmission control module
s: MIL or transmission warning on, often with a fault message
Firm shifts because line pressure falls back to a fixed value
Converter clutch no longer locks up (eight-speed applications)
Limited-slip differential inactive on dual-clutch Corvettes

P2815.t: Pressure Control Solenoid G Control Circuit High
P2815.d: P2815 is the opposite electrical case: the driver of solenoid G sees battery voltage where the load should pull the pin down. In GM's 2016 eight-speed table, where G is the converter clutch pressure valve, the flag must stand for 0.3 s of a 0.5 s window and one trip is enough. The 2023 Corvette dual-clutch software, with G as the limited-slip valve, also books two further checks here: estimated current deviating from target by over 70 % for 60 ms or by 200 mA for 300 ms, and a short to a neighbouring output found during the shutdown test and set at the next start, rated Type B. Ford lists a shorted load on the TR9070 even clutch cooling valve under this code. Check the harness for contact with a supply wire before replacing parts.
c: Control wire of solenoid G touching a supply voltage wire
Solenoid coil with shorted turns drawing too much current
Two solenoid outputs shorted together inside the harness or valve body
Faulty driver stage in the transmission module
s: MIL lit and transmission in a substitute program
Harsh engagement or missing converter lockup
Code may appear only after the next engine start (shutdown test)

P2816.d: P2816 is the general code for pressure control solenoid H; a fault type byte usually narrows it down. The valve H stands for depends on the maker. Toyota uses the code on its eight-speed automatics: bulletin T-SB-0160-18 lists P28167F (actuator stuck off) for 2017-2018 Highlander and Sienna together with whine, harsh shifts and reduced power, and offers a remanufactured transaxle, while T-SB-0076-24 for the 2024 Tacoma names P281671 (actuator stuck) and replaces gearbox and torque converter. Mercedes-Benz lists P281600, a malfunction of pressure regulating valve 8, among the faults its guided repair tool handles on the 8G-DCT (transmission 724.1). Specific variants are P2817 to P281E.
c: Internal transmission damage leaving debris in the hydraulics (Toyota eight-speed)
Valve H sticking in its bore
s: MIL on, sometimes reduced engine power
Harsh or erratic shifts
Whining noise from the transmission

P2817.t: Pressure Control Solenoid H Performance/Stuck Off
P2817.d: P2817 means valve H fails to produce the effect it is commanded to give. On GM nine- and ten-speed automatics H is the converter clutch valve: too much slip in lock mode (130 rpm) or a large slip error in controlled mode, counted three times, sets a Type A fault. GM's PIP6005 traces the code on 2024-2025 Enclave, Traverse and Acadia with the 8T65 to a seal on the turbine shaft that was harmed when the converter went in; torque converter and seal are replaced. Honda calls H the O/P shift solenoid of its CVT: bulletin 19-047 covers 2016-2018 Civic 1.5 L, 2017-2018 CR-V and some 2018-2019 Accord, where the module misread drive pulley pressure as too high, and new software fixes it. The flashing D lamp, converter slip or poor fuel economy follow. P2818 is the reverse fault.
c: Valve H stuck or hydraulically unable to apply
Damaged turbine shaft seal letting converter clutch pressure escape (GM 8T65)
Misjudged pressure signal in older control software (Honda CVT)
s: MIL on or flashing D indicator
Converter clutch slips, engine speed higher than usual at cruise
Increased fuel consumption

P2818.t: Pressure Control Solenoid H Stuck On
P2818.d: P2818 reports that valve H stays effective when it should be released. In GM's eight-speed table for the 8L90, H is the default valve: in Park at 400-900 rpm, with fluid between 0 and 40 °C and a converter clutch test pressure of 600 kPa, slip of 6 rpm or less for 0.5 s counts as a fail, and the MIL follows after two trips. Bulletin PI1405 repeats cold starts in that range and replaces the gearbox if the code returns; 15-07-30-002 instead reprograms the module against firm 1-2 and 3-1 shifts with P0606 or P2818. On the ten-speed H is the converter clutch valve; GM bulletin 24-NA-230 links a stuck-on clutch on 2024-2025 Silverado and Sierra 1500 to the engine stalling when D or R is selected, mostly due to the valve body.
c: Valve in the valve body sticking in the applied position
Internal transmission fault that persists when cold (PI1405)
s: Engine stalls when coming to a stop or when D or R is selected
Firm upshifts or downshifts, shudder
MIL on, code may set only at low fluid temperature

P2819.d: P2819 is a collective electrical code for solenoid H: the module knows that coil or wiring is faulty but does not say whether the circuit is open or shorted. Mercedes-Benz uses it on the 8G-DCT dual-clutch gearbox (transmission 724.1 in the A-Class, CLA and GLA/GLB families): P281900, an electrical fault of pressure regulating valve 8, is one of the codes its guided diagnosis tool in XENTRY handles, alongside P281600 for a functional fault of the same valve. GM, by contrast, reports H circuit faults as separate codes P281B, P281D and P281E. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires transmission output circuits to be checked for such faults. Measure coil resistance and the connection to the module before replacing the valve or the mechatronic unit.
c: Coil of valve H open or shorted
Poor contact between valve and mechatronic or module board
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Limp-home mode with restricted gears
Jerky starts or rough shifts

P281A.d: P281A marks a fault at valve H that comes and goes, either electrically or in its hydraulic effect. There is no public manufacturer description of P281A. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 calls for monitoring of such actuators but does not prescribe an intermittent code. GM's 2020 tables show why short dropouts are hard to catch: the H circuit codes P281B, P281D and P281E only set when a fault flag stays active for at least 0.3 of every 0.5 s, so a contact that opens for a few milliseconds may only show up as a rough shift. Typical places for such faults are loose terminals at the gearbox connector, cracked solder joints in a mechatronic unit and coils that fail only when hot. Freeze-frame data and a wiggle test with live data help more than a single resistance check.
c: Loose or corroded terminal at the transmission connector
Coil of valve H failing only at operating temperature
Cracked solder joint in an integrated mechatronic unit
s: Occasional harsh or delayed shift
Warning lamp that comes and goes
Short spells of limp-home mode

P281B.t: Pressure Control Solenoid H Control Circuit/Open
P281B.d: P281B stands for an open control circuit of solenoid H. GM's 2020 tables apply it to the converter clutch valve of nine- and ten-speed automatics and to the T93 eight-speed default valve; an impedance of about 200 kilohm, seen for 0.3 s of 0.5 s, sets a Type A fault in one trip. On the T87a eight-speed controllers an open default valve circuit is filed as P281D instead. In the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box H is the redundant shutdown valve of the differential lock; with the output off, the driver tries to hold the pin low with a tiny current, and if it succeeds the load is missing, confirmed after 150 ms as Type B. Broken wires, a backed-out terminal or an open coil are the usual causes; converter lockup or the differential lock is then lost.
c: Terminal pushed back or loose in the connector
Broken wire in the internal or external transmission harness
s: MIL on after one trip
No converter clutch lockup, higher engine speed at cruise
Limited-slip differential disabled (Corvette dual-clutch)

P281C.t: Pressure Control Solenoid H Control Circuit Range/Performance
P281C.d: P281C is meant for a circuit of solenoid H that is electrically intact but does not behave plausibly, for example when the measured current fails to follow the commanded value. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 only demands functional monitoring of output circuits. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch software does run exactly such a test on its H valve, comparing the current estimated from duty cycle and battery voltage with the target, but files a deviation of over 70 % or 200 mA under the high-side code P281E. On the G side, Nissan-built CVTs use the matching code P2813 mainly for a hydraulic engagement fault. If P281C appears, check coil resistance against specification and look for high contact resistance.
c: Coil resistance of valve H outside specification
Corroded or loose contacts raising circuit resistance
Unstable supply voltage to the solenoid driver
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Shift quality varies from drive to drive
Possible substitute program

P281D.t: Pressure Control Solenoid H Control Circuit Low
P281D.d: P281D signals that the control line of solenoid H is shorted to ground. In GM's 2016 eight-speed table H is the on/off default valve; the low flag must persist for 0.3 s within 0.5 s and one trip lights the MIL. The 2020 tables extend this to the nine- and ten-speed converter clutch valve, using about 0.5 ohm to ground as the limit and rating it Type A, and add that T87a eight-speed controllers also report an open default valve circuit as P281D, so an interrupted wire can hide behind this code. On the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box the redundant shutdown valve of the differential is checked while switched on; a voltage below about 1.7 V at the output pin is held for 150 ms before the Type B code is stored.
c: Control wire of solenoid H shorted to ground
Open default valve circuit reported as low (GM T87a eight-speed)
Coil insulation failure inside solenoid H
s: MIL on after a single trip
Transmission in default gear or fixed pressure mode
Converter lockup or differential lock unavailable

P281E.t: Pressure Control Solenoid H Control Circuit High
P281E.d: P281E sets when the line to solenoid H carries supply voltage where the module expects the load to pull it down. GM's 2020 tables cover the converter clutch valve on nine- and ten-speed automatics and the default valve on the eight-speed with the same timing as the low code: 0.3 s within 0.5 s, Type A, one trip. On the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch gearbox the threshold for the shutdown valve of the differential lock rises with battery voltage, from about 0.7 V to 1.1 V at the pin. The same code also covers a valve current that strays from its target and a short to a neighbouring output, which the shutdown test detects and saves, so P281E can appear right after a restart. Look for pinched wires next to supply lines and for water in connectors.
c: Control wire of solenoid H shorted to a voltage source
Moisture in the transmission connector bridging pins
Short between solenoid H and a neighbouring output
s: MIL on, possibly right after starting
Converter clutch or differential lock function lost
Firm shifts in a substitute program

P281F.d: P281F is the umbrella code for pressure control solenoid J; usually a failure-type byte narrows it down, or the module stores one of the specific codes P2820 to P2827 instead. Which valve carries the letter J is up to each manufacturer. Mercedes-Benz lists P281F00, a malfunction of pressure regulating valve 9, among the faults its Intelligent Predictive Repair routine in XENTRY evaluates on transmission 724.1, the 8G-DCT dual-clutch unit of model series 118, 177 and 247; electrical faults of that valve appear there as P282200. GM and Ford document only the specific J codes. Drivers notice harsh or missing gear changes. A guided test of valve and hydraulic circuit should come before the mechatronic unit is replaced.
c: Valve J sticking due to abrasion particles in the fluid
Fault inside the mechatronic unit or valve body
Coil or connector fault at valve J
s: Harsh or delayed gear changes
Transmission warning message or MIL
Limited gears or emergency mode

P2820.t: Pressure Control Solenoid J Performance/Stuck Off
P2820.d: P2820 says valve J, though electrically sound, fails to deliver its hydraulic effect when commanded. On GM ten-speed automatics J is the default disable valve; if it sticks off, the box drops into its hydraulic limp gear (2nd or 7th) while another gear is requested. GM's 2020 tables detect this through gear ratio and clutch slip (50 rpm) and log Type A after 0.25 s. GM PIP5551 blames casting debris or blocked spacer plate orifices on 2017-2018 Malibu with the GF9 nine-speed. Toyota maps P2820 to the SLP valve of the Corolla CVT; T-SB-0289-17 (2014-2017 Corolla, 2017 iM) and S-SB-0002-18 (2016 iM) swap the CVT and reflash the ECM. In the Corvette and Ford TR9070 dual-clutch boxes J holds the park lock, so a stuck-off valve leaves the car in Park.
c: Casting debris or dirt blocking valve J or its passages
Restricted orifice in a spacer plate
Outdated control logic that misjudges the valve (Toyota CVT)
Internal transmission damage requiring a replacement unit
s: Transmission suddenly holds 2nd or 7th gear
Binding or jerky drive when the wrong clutches engage
Vehicle will not leave Park on dual-clutch models
MIL on

P2821.t: Pressure Control Solenoid J Stuck On
P2821.d: P2821 is the mirror image of P2820: valve J keeps acting after the module has released it. GM bulletin PIP5557 (revisions up to C) concerns 2018 Cruze, Equinox, Malibu and Traverse with nine-speed automatics (RPO M3D, M3E, M3H, M3U, M3V) that stay in second gear and will not pass about 30 mph. When the regular diagnosis finds nothing, the 0.5 mm orifice 33 in the spacer plate is checked against a light and the plate is replaced together with the TCM update from 18-NA-121. In the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box J is the park lock engaging valve: below 3 km/h the TCM drains the lock piston through J alone, and if the position sensor keeps reporting the lock as released, the valve counts as stuck on (Type B). Ford's TR9070 puts the same fault of its park lock valve here.
c: Blocked orifice in the valve body spacer plate
Valve J or its spool stuck in the applied position
TCM software requiring the update released with the repair
Park lock piston or latching valve not draining (dual-clutch)
s: Stuck in second gear, no upshift
Top speed limited to about 50 km/h
Park lock does not engage as expected
MIL on

P2822.d: P2822 gathers electrical faults of solenoid J without saying whether the circuit is open or shorted; a failure-type byte adds that detail. Mercedes-Benz uses the code on two gearboxes, and in both J is pressure regulating valve 9. For the 9G-Tronic (transmission 725.0), information LI27.60-P-064292 reports P282212, a short to positive at valve 9, together with P060C00 on new C-, E- and S-Class cars (series 205, 213, 222) as they leave transport mode; there the fix is to let the car sleep and then clear the memory, while the note stresses that real faults remain possible. On the 8G-DCT, P282200 is part of the IPR guided test. GM splits J wiring faults into P2824, P2826 and P2827. Start with coil resistance and the gearbox connector.
c: Short to positive in the valve J circuit
Signal timing when leaving transport mode on new vehicles (Mercedes 9G-Tronic)
Open or shorted coil of valve J
Corrosion or loose pins at the transmission connector
s: Transmission warning or MIL
Emergency mode with fixed gear
Code present on a new car without driveability complaint

P2823.d: P2823 is reserved for a fault at valve J that appears and disappears, either in its wiring or in its hydraulic action. No manufacturer publishes a description of this code. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 obliges makers to monitor transmission output devices for circuit and functional faults, yet leaves it to them whether to split off intermittent codes. The systems that do use the J series show why such faults are elusive: GM's 2020 circuit tests need the flag in 0.3 of every 0.5 s, and the 2023 Corvette waits 150 ms before confirming a J fault, so very brief dropouts may never be logged and only appear as an odd shift or a park lock that reacts late. Read the freeze frame, flex the harness at the transmission plug with live data running and inspect pins for corrosion or spread contacts.
c: Loose or spread pin at the transmission connector
Coil that drops out only when hot
Valve J sticking now and then due to contaminated fluid
s: Occasional rough or unexpected shift
Warning that comes and goes
Sometimes delayed park lock response

P2824.t: Pressure Control Solenoid J Control Circuit/Open
P2824.d: P2824 reports an open in the control line of solenoid J. GM's 2016 table for T87 eight-speed controllers uses J for the on/off boost valve of clutch 2 and flags the code in one trip once the fault persists 0.3 s within a half-second sample. In the 2020 tables the code is limited to T93 ten-speed controllers, where J is the default disable valve, and an impedance near 200 kilohm between signal and ground leads to Type A. The 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box tests its park lock engaging valve while switched off: if the pin can be held between about 1.7 and 3 V with a tiny current, no load is connected, and after 150 ms a Type B code is set. Ford's TR9070 files an open park lock valve here. Broken wires, backed-out terminals or an open coil are typical.
c: Broken wire between TCM and valve J
Terminal pushed back or not latched in the connector
Faulty output driver in the TCM
s: Hydraulic limp gear or no shifting
Park lock cannot be operated (dual-clutch models)
MIL on after one or two trips

P2825.t: Pressure Control Solenoid J Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2825.d: P2825 would flag a J control circuit that is intact but behaves implausibly, for example a current that does not track the duty cycle the module commands. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 only requires functional checks of output circuits in general terms. The Corvette dual-clutch software of 2023 does run such a comparison on its J valve, the park lock engaging valve, estimating current from duty cycle and battery voltage, but it books a deviation above 70 % for 60 ms or 200 mA for 300 ms under the high-side code P2827. If P2825 is stored, compare coil resistance with specification at operating temperature, measure contact resistance at the terminals and check the driver supply; a sluggish valve can mimic this fault.
c: Coil resistance out of specification when hot
Sluggish valve J changing the electrical load
s: Shift quality varies
MIL or transmission warning

P2826.t: Pressure Control Solenoid J Control Circuit Low
P2826.d: P2826 indicates that the line to solenoid J is pulled to ground. GM's 2020 tables name three uses for J: the clutch select valve of the nine-speed, the default disable valve of the ten-speed and the boost valve of the eight-speed. About 0.5 ohm to ground for 0.3 of 0.5 s gives a Type A fault, and T87a eight-speed controllers also log P2826 when the J circuit is open, so a broken wire can hide behind it. The 2016 eight-speed table already set it after one trip with the same window. On the 2023 Corvette the park lock engaging valve is checked while energized; a pin voltage below roughly 1.7 V for 150 ms yields Type B. Ford's TR9070 assigns a shorted switch at its park lock valve to this code. Chafed insulation at brackets is a frequent cause.
c: Control wire shorted to ground through chafed insulation
Coil of valve J shorted to its housing
Open J circuit reported as low on GM T87a controllers
s: Limp gear or loss of boost pressure
Park lock fault message (dual-clutch models)
MIL on

P2827.t: Pressure Control Solenoid J Control Circuit High
P2827.d: P2827 sets when the J control line shows supply voltage although the load ought to pull it low. In GM's 2020 tables it covers the nine-speed clutch valve, the ten-speed default disable valve and the eight-speed boost valve, using the same 0.3-of-0.5 s window and Type A rating as the low code. On the Corvette's 2023 dual-clutch unit, where J engages the park lock, the limit grows with battery voltage from about 0.7 to 1.1 V; this code also takes a current estimate that misses its target by more than 70 % (60 ms) or 200 mA (300 ms). A further check at shutdown looks for a short to the next output and raises it at the following key cycle; all of these are Type B. Ford files a shorted load at the TR9070 park lock valve here. Check for wires touching a supply line.
c: Control wire shorted to a supply line
Short to a neighbouring solenoid output
Shorted coil turns lowering the load
s: Limp gear or blocked park lock function
Code returns right after a restart
MIL on

P2828.d: P2828 serves as the catch-all code for solenoid K and is normally refined by a failure-type byte or replaced by one of P2829 to P2830. Mercedes-Benz is the maker found to name it directly: on the 8G-DCT dual-clutch gearbox of model series 118, 177 and 247, P282800 denotes a malfunction of pressure regulating valve 10 and P282B00 an electrical fault of the same valve. Both belong to the IPR routine in XENTRY Diagnosis, which Mercedes set up because many repairs on transmission 724.1 had not solved the complaint. GM uses K on the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box for the selector pilot valve, but only with the specific codes. Since K may be a clutch, selector or cooling valve, effects range from rough shifts to missing gears.
c: Valve K sticking because of contaminated fluid
Fault in the mechatronic unit carrying valve K
s: Rough shifting or missing gears
Transmission warning or MIL
Emergency mode

P2829.t: Pressure Control Solenoid K Performance/Stuck Off
P2829.d: P2829 means valve K remains hydraulically inactive although it is commanded on. In GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch transmission K is the selector pilot valve, which steers the selector spool of the shift-rod hydraulics. The check runs inside a synchronizer integrity routine that starts after a gear or component fault: the TCM orders small rod movements and measures them. If the rods respond as though the selector were off (no more than 100 µm of intended travel, over 100 µm on the complementary rod) and the valve's current profile check fails three times, with cooler-out oil at 40 °C or warmer, the Type A code is stored. Ford handles the same selector pilot valve of its TR9070 under P27D9 rather than a K code. Gear selection on one shaft may be lost.
c: Selector pilot valve stuck in the off position
Abrasion particles in the transmission fluid
Selector spool itself stuck (same symptom, different part)
s: Some gears unavailable
Hesitation or failed gear preselection
MIL on

P282A.t: Pressure Control Solenoid K Stuck On
P282A.d: P282A reports the reverse of P2829: K holds the selector mechanism in its pressurized state after being switched off. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch software uses the same synchronizer integrity routine, this time with a test case whose selector target is hydraulic off. When the measured rod motion matches the on position and the selector pilot valve's current profile check keeps failing, the TCM blames the pilot valve rather than the selector spool and stores a Type A fault. Ford's TR9070 summary lists the matching stuck-on case for its selector pilot valve as P27DA. A pilot valve hanging open may route pressure to the wrong shift rod, so the controller can lock out gears or choose a limp mode. Dirty fluid and worn valve bores are the usual mechanical reasons.
c: Selector pilot valve stuck in the applied position
Worn valve bore causing internal leakage
s: Gears locked out or limp mode
Clunk or unexpected rod movement during shifts
MIL on

P282B.d: P282B covers electrical faults at solenoid K when the module does not break them down into open, low or high. Mercedes-Benz uses P282B00 on the 8G-DCT (transmission 724.1) for an electrical fault of pressure regulating valve 10; its 2025 information LI27.00-P-077141 includes the code among those the IPR guided routine analyses before parts are replaced, while P282800 stands for a functional fault of that valve. GM, on the 2023 Corvette, instead reports K wiring faults separately as P282D, P282F and P2830. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 forms the legal basis for monitoring such outputs. Typical findings are a broken coil winding, a damaged conductor inside the mechatronic unit or corrosion at the plug; drivers may notice rough engagement or a warning message.
c: Broken coil winding in valve K
Damaged internal conductor in the mechatronic unit
s: Rough clutch engagement
Transmission warning or MIL
Emergency mode

P282C.d: P282C is intended for an intermittent problem at solenoid K. No manufacturer publishes a description; CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires monitoring of transmission actuators without prescribing a separate code for sporadic faults. The only documented K application, GM's selector pilot valve in the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box, confirms its circuit faults after a 100 ms debounce, so a contact breaking for a shorter time can escape the memory while still upsetting the choice of shift rod. On any car with this code, heat and vibration are the prime suspects: check connector locking, pin tension and the internal leads of the mechatronic unit while watching live data, and save the freeze frame before clearing anything.
c: Weak pin tension or unlatched connector
Heat-related dropout of the coil or internal lead
s: Occasional failed gear preselection
Warning that disappears after restart

P282D.t: Pressure Control Solenoid K Control Circuit/Open
P282D.d: P282D marks an open control circuit of solenoid K. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch software applies it to the selector pilot valve. With the low-side output off, a connected coil would pull the sense pin up to battery voltage; the driver instead attempts to keep the pin near ground using a very small current, and if the voltage settles between roughly 1.7 and 3 V the load is considered missing. Once 100 ms of confirmation have passed, the TCM logs a Type A fault and lights the MIL in the same drive. The test only runs between about 8.75 and 18 V and not during cranking. Ford's TR9070 reports an open selector pilot valve as P27DD rather than under K. Broken wires, a pushed-back terminal or an open coil leave the selector unable to switch between shift rods.
c: Broken wire to the selector pilot valve
Terminal pushed back in the connector
s: Gears on one shaft unavailable
MIL on immediately
Limp mode

P282E.t: Pressure Control Solenoid K Control Circuit Range/Performance
P282E.d: P282E is meant for a solenoid K control circuit whose behaviour strays from what the TCM expects although there is no clean open or short. No manufacturer documents it publicly, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 states the monitoring duty only in general form. GM's K valve in the 2023 Corvette illustrates what such a check could look like: the TCM derives valve current from duty cycle and supply voltage and compares it with the request, yet a miss of more than 70 % for 60 ms or 400 mA for 300 ms is stored as P2830, not as P282E. Coil resistance rising with heat, a poor ground or a weak driver stage are the likely technical causes. Measure resistance cold and warm and compare actual and requested current in live data.
c: Poor ground or supply to the driver stage
Weak output stage in the TCM
s: Uneven gear preselection
MIL or transmission warning

P282F.t: Pressure Control Solenoid K Control Circuit Low
P282F.d: P282F reports a ground fault on the control line of solenoid K. On the 2023 Corvette, GM checks the selector pilot valve while its low-side output is switched on; the TCM compares the voltage at the sense pin with a lower limit of about 1.7 V, and a reading below it points to a ground short. After 100 ms the module stores a Type A code, so the MIL lights during the same trip. Battery voltage has to lie between 8.75 and 18 V and the engine must not be cranking. Ford's TR9070 summary uses P27DF for a shorted switch at its own selector pilot valve instead. Expect gears on one clutch shaft to be blocked; chafed insulation inside the transmission harness is the first thing to look for.
c: Control wire to valve K shorted to ground
Damaged insulation inside the transmission harness
Coil of valve K shorted to ground internally
s: Gears on one clutch shaft blocked
MIL on in the same trip
Limp mode

P2830.t: Pressure Control Solenoid K Control Circuit High
P2830.d: P2830 is set when the K control line carries voltage where the switched-on low-side driver should pull it down. GM applies it to the selector pilot valve of the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box with a limit that climbs as supply voltage increases, from about 0.7 V below 11.5 V to 1.1 V above 15.5 V, confirmed after 100 ms. The same code also records a current estimate that misses the target by more than 70 % for 60 ms or by 400 mA over 300 ms; a short to an adjacent output, which a shutdown test writes to memory, is reported at the next start as well. Every variant is rated Type A, unlike the Type B rating of the park lock valve J. Ford's TR9070 lists a shorted load at its selector pilot valve as P27E0. Look for wires rubbing on supply lines and for moisture in connectors.
c: Control wire shorted to a supply line
Short to an adjacent solenoid output
s: Gear preselection fails, limp mode
Code back immediately after restart
MIL on

P2831.d: P2831 is the general circuit code for the position signal of shift fork A in automated manual and dual-clutch gearboxes. How makers fill it varies widely. Mercedes-Benz uses P283100 for an electrical fault of the shift fork A position sensor in the 8G-DCT (transmission 724.1) and lists it among the codes of its guided repair tool. Ford's 2012 summary for the DPS6 dual-clutch box of Fiesta and Focus has no fork sensor at all: there P2831 marks a fault in the internal TCM chip that sets the current of the shift drum A motor, the drum that moves the forks for first, third and fifth gear. GM and Ford's TR9070 split position circuit faults into the specific codes P2833 to P2835 instead. Gear changes on the affected shaft may be refused.
c: Shift fork A position sensor electrically defective
Fault in the module's motor current controller (Ford DPS6)
Poor contact at the sensor or module connector
s: Transmission warning, gear display may flash
Odd gears unavailable or limp-home mode
Delayed engagement or no drive when starting off

P2832.t: Shift Fork A Position Circuit Range/Performance
P2832.d: P2832 means the fork A position reading is electrically valid but disagrees with what the gearbox is doing. GM's 2023 table for the Corvette dual-clutch box runs this as a consistency check on rod 1: when clutch shaft and output speeds prove a gear is engaged with over 600 N applied, yet the sensor sits more than 1100 µm away from the learned engaged position, a Type A fault follows a confirmation time; a matching test watches disengagement. Ford's 2024 summary lists P2832 as the consistency code of rod position sensor 1 on the TR9070. Mercedes-Benz names it a malfunction of the fork A sensor on the 8G-DCT, and Ford's 2012 DPS6 summary uses it for a position error of shift drum A, including a blocked motor.
c: Sensor magnet or mounting shifted on the shift rod
Learned fork positions no longer valid after repair or wear
Shift rod, fork or drum binding mechanically
s: Gear on the odd shaft not engaged or dropped
Clunks or long pauses during shifts
Limp-home mode with warning lamp

P2833.t: Shift Fork A Position Circuit Low
P2833.d: P2833 reports a fork A position signal stuck at the low end. On the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox the rod 1 sensor sends a pulse-width signal; GM's 2023 table sets the code when no pulses arrive and the pin stays under 2.0 V, or when the duty cycle drops below 8 %, each confirmed for 150 ms, with the 5 V sensor supply in range and rated Type A. Ford's 2024 summary calls the same case on the TR9070 a pulse width below its window, input stuck at zero. Mercedes-Benz uses P283300 when the fork A sensor circuit is shorted to ground in the 8G-DCT. Because a supply fault can mimic this pattern, GM blocks the test while supply codes such as P0642 are present. The gearbox then can no longer place the gears on that rod reliably.
c: Signal wire of the fork A sensor shorted to ground
Open signal line letting the input float low
s: Warning lamp and limp-home mode
Gears of one shaft locked out
Car may only pull away in a fallback gear

P2834.t: Shift Fork A Position Circuit High
P2834.d: P2834 is the high-side counterpart: the fork A position input sits at the upper limit. In GM's 2023 Corvette table the rod 1 sensor is flagged when pulses stop and the pin voltage stays above 3.5 V, or when the duty cycle climbs over 92 %; after 150 ms a Type A fault is stored, but only while the sensor supply lies between 4.5 and 5.5 V and the battery between 8.75 and 18 V. Ford's 2024 summary for the TR9070 describes the same condition as pulse width above its window, input stuck at one. On the Mercedes-Benz 8G-DCT the code means the fork A sensor circuit has shorted to positive. A signal wire touching the sensor supply or a sensor whose output transistor no longer switches are the usual explanations.
c: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V sensor supply or battery voltage
Sensor output transistor no longer pulling low
s: Warning lamp with stored code
Shifts on the affected shaft blocked
Reduced driveability in limp-home mode

P2835.t: Shift Fork A Position Circuit Intermittent
P2835.d: P2835 covers a fork A position signal that is present but unsteady. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table checks the carrier frequency of the rod 1 sensor and sets a Type A fault once it leaves the 1500 to 2500 Hz band for 150 ms; Ford's 2024 summary calls the same check on the TR9070 frequency out of range. In Ford's 2012 DPS6 summary for Fiesta and Focus the code has another meaning: the shift drum A motor reports its rotation through three Hall sensors, and P2835 sets when their pattern appears in the wrong order. Dropouts usually come from loose terminals, damaged shielding or interference on the signal wire. The driver may notice an occasional refused or delayed shift and a warning lamp that is not always on.
c: Intermittent contact at the sensor or module connector
Interference or damaged shielding on the signal line
Faulty Hall sensor in the shift drum motor (Ford DPS6)
s: Occasional refused or late shift
Warning lamp that comes and goes
Hesitation or no drive when pulling away

P2836.d: P2836 is the umbrella circuit code for the shift fork B position input. Mercedes-Benz stores P283600 when its 8G-DCT dual-clutch transmission (724.1) detects an electrical defect at the fork B sensor and includes it in the code set evaluated by its Intelligent Predictive Repair routine in XENTRY. Ford's 2012 summary gives the number a different job on the DPS6 gearbox of Focus and Fiesta: a fault in the motor-current chip (ATIC) inside the TCM that drives the second shift drum, which according to its stuck-in-gear codes serves second, fourth, sixth and reverse. GM's Corvette software and Ford's TR9070 never use P2836 and report fork B problems through P2837 to P283A. Usually the gears moved by fork B are withdrawn and a substitute program takes over.
c: Electrical defect in the fork B position sensor (Mercedes 8G-DCT)
Failed current-control chip for the second shift drum motor in the TCM (Ford DPS6)
Corroded or loose contacts between sensor and module
s: Transmission warning and stored code
Gears of fork B skipped or unavailable
Delayed engagement from Park or no drive (Ford DPS6)

P2837.t: Shift Fork B Position Circuit Range/Performance
P2837.d: P2837 flags a fork B position reading that is electrically sound but contradicts the gearbox state. GM's Corvette summary from 2023 maps fork B to rod 2 on the odd-gear shaft. A Type A fault follows when the speed sensors confirm a gear under more than 600 N of shift force while the sensor sits over 1100 µm from the learned engaged point, and a second test catches a rod that hardly moves after a release command. Setting the code also starts a synchronizer recovery routine for the odd shaft. Ford's 2024 summary uses P2837 for the consistency test of TR9070 rod sensor 2 and keeps rod drift apart as P284E. For Mercedes-Benz it is a fork B sensor malfunction in the 8G-DCT; the DPS6 text from Ford (2012) reads it as a position error of the second drum, a blocked motor included.
c: Learned rod 2 positions no longer matching after repair or wear
Rod, fork or synchronizer binding so the gear does not engage or release cleanly
Sensor magnet or carrier loose on the rod
Blocked second shift drum motor (Ford DPS6)
s: Gear jumps out or is not engaged on fork B
Noticeable pause or clunk while the gearbox retries the shift
Warning lamp and limited gear selection

P2838.t: Shift Fork B Position Circuit Low
P2838.d: P2838 is stored when the fork B position input reads at the bottom of its range. The Corvette's rod 2 sensor, fed by GM from the same 5 V reference A as rod 1, has to send a pulse-width signal; if pulses are missing while the pin is below 2.0 V, or the duty cycle drops under 8 %, the module waits 150 ms and logs a Type A fault. Faults of reference A itself (P0642, P0643) suspend this test, so a supply problem shows up under those codes and tends to hit rod 1 as well. Ford's TR9070 summary describes the pattern for rod sensor 2 as a pulse width below its window with the input stuck at zero. Mercedes-Benz reads P283800 on the 8G-DCT as a fork B sensor shorted to ground. Gears on that rod are then locked out.
c: Fork B sensor signal wire chafed through to ground
Sensor output no longer producing pulses
Break in the signal or supply wire leaving the input low
s: Warning lamp with transmission in limp-home mode
Gears on rod 2 or fork B no longer selected
Rough or delayed shifts around the locked-out gears

P2839.t: Shift Fork B Position Circuit High
P2839.d: P2839 covers the other end of the scale: the fork B input is pinned high. GM's 2023 Corvette table for rod 2 sets it when pulses stop and the pin carries more than 3.5 V, or once the duty cycle passes 92 %. The test runs all the time except during cranking, and only while system voltage lies between 8.75 and 18 V and reference A between 4.5 and 5.5 V; 150 ms of the condition produce a Type A code. Ford's TR9070 lists P2839 for rod sensor 2 when the pulse width climbs above its window and the input stays at one, and on the 8G-DCT Mercedes-Benz reserves it for a fork B sensor with a short to battery positive. Check the harness for a signal wire rubbing against a supply line and confirm the sensor ground before replacing the sensor or module.
c: Signal wire of the fork B sensor touching the 5 V or battery supply
Open sensor ground letting the output float high
Sensor output stage stuck in the high state
s: Warning lamp and fault message in the cluster
Fork B gears blocked, fewer gears available
Reduced acceleration in the substitute program

P283A.t: Shift Fork B Position Circuit Intermittent
P283A.d: P283A means the fork B signal is arriving, but not cleanly. For rod 2 of the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox GM measures the period of the sensor carrier and reacts once the equivalent frequency drops below 1500 Hz or rises above 2500 Hz for 150 ms, logging a Type A fault. Ford's 2024 summary files the matching frequency check of TR9070 rod sensor 2 under this number. On the DPS6 of the 2012 Focus and Fiesta it means something else: the second shift drum motor reports its rotation through three Hall elements, and P283A appears when their switching pattern comes in the wrong order. Mercedes-Benz has no intermittent fork B entry in its 8G-DCT list. Loose pins, damaged shielding and electrical noise are typical, so the fault comes and goes with temperature and vibration.
c: Loose or spread terminal in the fork B sensor connector
Electrical noise coupling into the signal line through damaged shielding
Faulty Hall element in the second shift drum motor (Ford DPS6)
s: Sporadic warning lamp that clears after a restart
Occasional hesitation or refused shift
Intermittent engagement problems when pulling away (Ford DPS6)

P283B.d: P283B is the generic circuit code for the shift fork C position sensor. The only public manufacturer listing that uses it comes from Mercedes-Benz: on the 8G-DCT dual-clutch transmission (724.1) P283B00 stands for an electrical fault of the fork C sensor and belongs to the codes covered by its XENTRY repair routine for this gearbox. GM's Corvette software, in which fork C is rod 3 on the even-gear shaft, and Ford's TR9070, which calls it rod position sensor 3, do not set P283B and break circuit faults down into P283D, P283E and P283F instead. Ford's 2012 DPS6 has just two shift drums and no fork C code. Once the reading is lost, the gears this fork engages are normally dropped and the transmission continues in a fallback mode.
c: Fork C position sensor with an internal electrical fault
Poor contact or moisture at the sensor or TCM connector
Damaged sensor input in the transmission control module
s: Transmission warning in the instrument cluster
Gears handled by fork C no longer engaged
Emergency mode with reduced performance

P283C.t: Shift Fork C Position Circuit Range/Performance
P283C.d: P283C is the plausibility code for fork C, which GM's 2023 Corvette table assigns to rod 3 on the even-gear shaft. Besides the force and speed comparison during shifts (over 600 N, more than 1100 µm off the learned point, Type A), a static monitor runs here: with no shift force on the rod, the reading must stay inside tolerance bands around the learned neutral or engaged point. A drift is only confirmed once clutch speed can be checked against engine speed and output speed against the driven wheels. A confirmed fault triggers recovery of the even shaft synchronizer. Ford's TR9070 uses P283C for rod sensor 3 consistency and logs drift separately as P277E, while Mercedes-Benz describes it as a malfunction of the fork C sensor on the 8G-DCT.
c: Rod 3 creeping out of position because of worn detent or fork
Position values not relearned after gearbox or sensor work
Synchronizer actuation on the even shaft not reaching target position
s: Even gears drop out or refuse to engage
Grinding or a knock during shifts on the even shaft
Warning lamp, gearbox limits gear choice

P283D.t: Shift Fork C Position Circuit Low
P283D.d: P283D reports the fork C input stuck low. In the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox GM feeds the rod 3 sensor from reference B rather than reference A, so its enable test watches that second 5 V rail and pauses while P0652 or P0653 are present. Within those limits the code sets after 150 ms if no pulses are seen and the pin stays below 2.0 V, or if the duty cycle falls under 8 %; it is classed Type A. For rod sensor 3 of the TR9070, Ford reports a zero-stuck input whose pulse width falls short of the window. Mercedes-Benz interprets P283D00 on the 8G-DCT as a fork C sensor shorted to ground. Because rods 3 and 4 share reference B on the Corvette, a supply fault there would also disturb fork D.
c: Fork C signal line shorted to ground in the gearbox harness
Fork C sensor no longer switching its output
Damaged supply wire from reference B to the sensor
s: Limp-home mode with warning lamp
Gears of fork C unavailable
Possibly further fork D codes if the shared supply is affected

P283E.t: Shift Fork C Position Circuit High
P283E.d: P283E is the high-side fault of the fork C circuit. GM's 2023 summary checks the Corvette rod 3 sensor for two signs: no pulses at all with the pin above 3.5 V, and a duty cycle above 92 %. Either one, held for 150 ms with reference B in its 4.5 to 5.5 V window and the engine not cranking, stores a Type A code. Ford lists P283E for TR9070 rod sensor 3 as a pulse width beyond the upper limit, input stuck at one. Mercedes-Benz uses P283E00 on the 8G-DCT for a fork C sensor with a short to positive. In practice a pinched harness where the signal touches a feed, water in a connector bridging pins, or a sensor that has lost its ground are the usual finds. Fork C gears stay unavailable until the circuit is repaired.
c: Pinched harness with the fork C signal touching a feed wire
Water in the connector bridging signal and supply pins
Fork C sensor without ground connection
s: Warning lamp and gearbox fault message
Fork C gears locked out
Jerky driving in the substitute program

P283F.t: Shift Fork C Position Circuit Intermittent
P283F.d: P283F stands for an unstable fork C position signal rather than a hard short or open. The rod 3 sensor in GM's Corvette dual-clutch gearbox runs at a carrier between 1500 and 2500 Hz; if the measured period puts it outside that band for 150 ms, the module records a Type A fault, as long as reference B and battery voltage are valid. Ford's TR9070 summary assigns the frequency check of rod sensor 3 to this code. Mercedes-Benz does not list it for the 8G-DCT, and Ford's DPS6 has no fork C at all. Because the signal survives most of the time, the cause is usually mechanical stress on the wiring: a connector that moves with engine rocking, corrosion on a terminal or a cracked insulation near hot parts. Shifts may falter only now and then.
c: Fork C connector working loose under engine movement
Cracked insulation near hot components letting noise in
s: Occasional stutter or delay on even-gear shifts
Warning lamp appears only now and then

P2840.d: P2840 is the overall circuit code for the shift fork D position input. Mercedes-Benz is the one maker that publicly documents it: in the 8G-DCT (transmission 724.1) of its compact models, P284000 marks an electrical fault of the fork D sensor, and the gearbox has a fifth fork E with its own codes from P2863 upward. The other two published dual-clutch strategies skip this code. GM's Corvette software treats fork D as rod 4 on the even shaft and reports its electrical faults as P2842, P2843 or P2844, and Ford's TR9070 summary does the same for rod position sensor 4. With the position of fork D unknown, the module cannot confirm whether its gear is in or out and normally withholds those ratios until the fault is gone.
c: Electrical failure of the fork D position sensor
Damaged wiring between fork D sensor and the TCM
Transmission control module input or software fault
s: Gears of fork D withheld, gearbox skips them
Transmission warning lamp
Reduced driving comfort in emergency mode

P2841.t: Shift Fork D Position Circuit Range/Performance
P2841.d: P2841 indicates that fork D reports a believable voltage but an implausible position. GM's 2023 table runs the rod 4 consistency test in the Corvette only when neither the even-clutch speed signal nor the output speed signal has shown an electrical fault for at least 100 ms, so the comparison has trustworthy speeds behind it. During engagement the sensor must reach the learned engaged point within 1100 µm once over 600 N push the rod; during release, a rod that stays within 1000 µm of its starting point counts against it. Type A, with a recovery attempt on the even shaft synchronizer. Ford's 2024 summary uses P2841 for TR9070 rod sensor 4 consistency and P277F for its drift, and Mercedes-Benz names it a fork D sensor malfunction on the 8G-DCT.
c: Rod 4 or its synchronizer sticking so the fork lags behind the command
Outdated learned positions after a clutch or sensor replacement
Fork D sensor or magnet shifted in its mount
s: Hesitation or repeated attempts on even-gear shifts
Gear not held, slipping back to neutral
Warning lamp with reduced gear range

P2842.t: Shift Fork D Position Circuit Low
P2842.d: P2842 sets when the fork D sensor signal collapses toward zero. GM's 2023 Corvette table expects a pulse train from the rod 4 sensor and flags the circuit if pulses vanish with less than 2.0 V present, or if the duty cycle is lower than 8 %, both held for 150 ms; the resulting fault is Type A. In Ford's TR9070 summary the matching rod sensor 4 entry covers a too-narrow pulse and an input frozen at zero. Mercedes-Benz uses P284200 on the 8G-DCT for a fork D sensor shorted to ground. Since a missing sensor feed produces the same low picture, measure the 5 V supply at the connector first; on the Corvette that feed is shared with rod 3, so a combined P283D points to the supply rather than to one sensor.
c: Fork D signal wire shorted to ground or housing
No 5 V feed reaching the sensor
s: Warning lamp, fork D gears blocked
Transmission in emergency program
Additional fork C code if the shared feed is at fault

P2843.t: Shift Fork D Position Circuit High
P2843.d: P2843 means the fork D position line is sitting near supply level. GM's 2023 Corvette table raises it for rod 4 when there is no pulse activity and more than 3.5 V on the pin, or when the duty cycle is above 92 %; after a 150 ms confirmation a Type A code is set. The monitor is held off while P0652 or P0653 report a reference B problem and whenever battery voltage leaves the 8.75 to 18 V band, which keeps low-voltage starts from producing false entries. Ford's TR9070 counterpart is a rod sensor 4 signal held at logic one with too long a pulse, and in Mercedes-Benz's 8G-DCT list P284300 describes a positive short of the fork D sensor. A signal wire in contact with a feed or an open sensor ground is the likely cause.
c: Fork D signal wire in contact with a feed wire
Open ground circuit of the fork D sensor
Internal short in the sensor pulling its output high
s: Fault message and warning lamp
Some even gears no longer selected
Limp-home operation

P2844.t: Shift Fork D Position Circuit Intermittent
P2844.d: P2844 points to a fork D signal whose timing wanders. GM's Corvette dual-clutch software derives the rod 4 sensor frequency from its period and expects 1500 to 2500 Hz; leaving that window for 150 ms stores a Type A fault, and the check is skipped while cranking or with reference B out of tolerance. Ford's 2024 summary books the frequency test of TR9070 rod sensor 4 under P2844. Mercedes-Benz lists no intermittent code for fork D in its 8G-DCT set; it only has the electrical code P2840 and the malfunction code P2841 for this sensor. Because fork D shares the even shaft and reference B with fork C on the Corvette, checking whether P283F is stored as well helps separate a common harness section from a single sensor. Expect sporadic shift hesitation and a lamp that may go out again.
c: Chafed or loose harness section shared with the fork C sensor
Intermittent terminal contact at the fork D sensor
Sensor with an unstable output frequency
s: Sporadic hesitation on shifts
Warning lamp that may go out again

P2845.t: Shift Fork A Position Sensor Incorrect Neutral Position Indicated
P2845.d: P2845 means the fork A sensor reports neutral although the gearbox state says a gear is engaged, or it reports an engaged position where neutral is expected. Public manufacturer documentation for P2845 is lacking, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 only asks that transmission inputs be checked for plausibility. How such a check works is visible in GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table: the module learns neutral and engaged positions for every rod and, with no shift force applied, expects the reading to stay inside tolerance bands around them, but it stores deviations under other codes. A shifted sensor magnet, a worn fork or lost learned values after a repair are likely triggers; a relearn with a scan tool is the first step, followed by a mechanical check.
c: Neutral position not learned or lost after repair or software update
Sensor magnet or target shifted on the rod
Worn fork or detent changing the neutral position
s: Gear display shows N while a gear is engaged, or the reverse
Shifts refused, transmission in limp-home mode
Warning lamp on

P2846.t: Shift Fork B Position Sensor Incorrect Neutral Position Indicated
P2846.d: P2846 flags a mismatch between the neutral reading of the fork B position sensor and the gear state the transmission module expects. Either the sensor claims fork B rests in neutral while the shaft speeds prove its gear carries load, or it reports an engaged fork where the module has commanded neutral. No manufacturer publicly documents P2846. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires transmission inputs to be checked for rationality, and GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table shows one way to do it: an unloaded rod has to read within a tolerance band around the learned neutral or engaged point. GM books such deviations for its second rod under P2837, though. Likely triggers are lost learned positions, a loosened sensor target or a worn detent; a relearn comes first.
c: Learned neutral position of fork B missing after repair or module replacement
Magnet or target on the fork B rod loosened or shifted
Worn detent letting fork B settle off its neutral point
s: Gears served by fork B refused or skipped
Transmission warning with reduced performance
Gear indicator disagrees with the actual gear

P2847.t: Shift Fork C Position Sensor Incorrect Neutral Position Indicated
P2847.d: With P2847 the module has decided that the neutral signal from the fork C sensor cannot be trusted. Before a dual-clutch or automated manual box preselects a gear on a shaft, it must know that the other forks on that shaft are out; a false neutral could let two ratios mesh at once, so the module normally locks the affected gears out. No published manufacturer strategy uses P2847, so the code rests on the general CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 demand for plausible transmission inputs. In GM's Corvette software, the comparable static check for the third rod, which sits on the even shaft, is filed as P283C. Typical background: sensor or magnet moved during a transmission repair, positions never relearned, or a fork bent by a hard shift.
c: Fork C sensor or magnet repositioned during transmission work without relearn
Fork C bent, so neutral lies outside the learned band
Position sensor output drifting with temperature or age
s: Gears of fork C locked out, jumps between remaining ratios
Warning lamp and stored transmission code
Harsh or delayed shifts on the affected shaft

P2848.t: Shift Fork D Position Sensor Incorrect Neutral Position Indicated
P2848.d: P2848 is the neutral-plausibility code for the fourth fork. It sets when the fork D sensor signal and the logical state of that fork disagree about neutral, even though the signal itself is electrically sound. None of the published strategies uses the number: Mercedes-Benz lists four separate fork D sensor faults for its 8G-DCT (724.1), from P284000 to P284300, but not this one; Ford's TR9070 summary routes a doubtful reading of shift rod sensor 4 into the consistency code P2841, and GM's Corvette table handles rod 4 the same way. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 still expects the input to be monitored. In practice the box withholds the gears on fork D until a learn routine with a scan tool succeeds or a mechanical defect is fixed.
c: Fork D positions not relearned after software update or repair
Sensor of fork D loose in its mount
Wear on fork pads or synchronizer sleeve shifting the rest position
s: Gears of fork D unavailable
Drive system warning, emergency program

P2849.d: P2849 says that fork A did not travel when the module ordered it to, so its gear could not be put in or taken out. The reading may be valid; the fork itself is not following the command. No manufacturer publishes a strategy for P2849, and the code relies on the CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 rule that transmission components be checked for proper function. GM's 2023 Corvette table shows how a frozen rod is found: an intrusive integrity routine nudges each rod in both directions through its synchronizer valves and expects more than 100 µm of travel. GM, however, charges a rod that never moves to its position sensor and logs it under the first rod's consistency code P2832. Causes range from a seized rod or broken fork to a failed actuator.
c: Fork A actuator or its control valve not moving the rod
Shift rod of fork A seized in its bore or blocked by debris
Broken fork or damaged synchronizer sleeve jamming the shift
s: Gear of fork A will not engage or stays engaged
Limp-home mode with limited gears
Clunking or grinding during shift attempts

P284A.d: P284A is stored when fork B stays put although the transmission module commanded a move, for instance from neutral toward an engaged gear or back. Published strategies avoid this code. Ford's 2024 summary for the TR9070 dual-clutch box diagnoses the same symptom per gear rather than per fork, with failure-to-engage codes such as P073F and failure-to-disengage codes such as P072B, while GM's Corvette software folds a motionless rod into its position-sensor consistency checks. The CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 functional check of transmission components covers the case either way. For the driver, the gears carried by fork B disappear; if the fork hangs in an engaged gear, the module may have to drive around it on the other shaft. Inspection usually means opening the gearbox.
c: Fork B actuator, solenoid or hydraulic supply failing to apply force
Synchronizer of fork B gears jammed or damaged
Contaminated fluid restricting the fork B actuator
s: Gears of fork B missing or a gear stays engaged
Warning lamp and emergency mode
Rough starts or lack of drive in some gears

P284B.d: P284B reports a third fork that refuses to travel. Two situations matter: stuck in neutral, which merely costs the gears of fork C, and stuck in an engaged gear, which is more serious because that shaft then turns with a fixed ratio and a second gear on the same shaft must never be selected. No published OBD strategy assigns P284B, so the code rests on what CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 demands for transmission parts. A hydraulic counterpart can be seen in GM's Corvette table, where stuck-on and stuck-off failures of the selector pilot valve, which steers oil to the rods, set P282A and P2829. Before replacing parts, check fluid level and condition and any valve or actuator codes, since a fork rarely jams without a reason upstream.
c: Selector or pilot valve not routing pressure to the fork C rod
Fork C or its rod mechanically jammed
s: Car stays in one gear on one shaft or skips the fork C gears
Transmission warning lamp

P284C.d: P284C applies when fork D, the fourth of the generic shift forks, fails to answer an actuation request. Whether the drive is hydraulic, as in most wet dual-clutch boxes, or electric, as in automated manuals with motor-driven drums, the module sees the request but no travel at the position sensor. No manufacturer documentation for P284C is public. Mercedes-Benz, for example, lists several fork D sensor codes for the 8G-DCT (724.1) and even a fifth fork E, yet no stuck code for D. The requirement comes from CARB 13 CCR 1968.2, which demands functional monitoring of transmission parts. A stuck fork usually forces an emergency program with few gears; repairs can range from an actuator or valve body to a full gearbox overhaul.
c: Fork D actuator motor or hydraulic valve failed
Shift drum or rod binding at fork D
Module output stage not driving the fork D actuator
s: Gears of fork D unavailable or stuck engaged
Emergency program, reduced speed
Warning in the instrument cluster

P284D.d: P284D means fork A has crept away from the position of the gear it is supposed to hold, without any shift being commanded. Several makers use it. Audi bulletin 2078846 covers 2025 A5 and Q5 models with the DL382 and DL552 dual-clutch boxes: the cluster reports a drive system fault with limited performance, and if guided fault finding finds no cause, the gear position distance sensors G487 to G490 are calibrated ten times in a row; a later revision adds a combined software update. Mercedes-Benz names P284D00 for its 8G-DCT, and Ford's 2024 summary links it to rod drift of shift rod 1 in the TR9070. GM's Corvette software runs it as a Type A drift check on rod 1, after which a synchronizer recovery routine starts on the odd shaft.
c: Gear position sensors poorly calibrated (Audi DL382/DL552)
Leaking fork A actuator or weak detent letting the rod creep
s: Message about a drive system fault with limited performance
First or seventh gear cannot be selected (Audi report)
Gear may jump out under load

P284E.d: P284E reports that fork B drifted while no shift was asked for. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table describes the test on rod 2 in detail: with no actuating force applied, the measured position must stay inside wide limits around the learned point of the gear verified as engaged by clutch-shaft and output speed readings; leaving them for 500 ms is a fault. The code also sets if the drift correction, which acts on narrower limits, triggers ten times or stays active for over 5 s. The DTC is Type A and launches a resynchronization routine on the odd shaft. Ford's TR9070 documentation from 2024 assigns P284E to drift of shift rod 2, and Mercedes-Benz lists P284E00 for its 8G-DCT as fork B moving on its own.
c: Synchronizer pressure valve for fork B leaking and pushing the rod
Weak detent or worn gear dog teeth on fork B gears
s: Gear on the odd shaft pops out or is re-engaged with a jolt
Warning lamp, possible limp-home mode

P284F.d: P284F covers drift of fork C away from its held gear. In GM's Corvette software this is rod 3, which sits on the shaft of the even clutch; the check compares the rod position with the learned point for the gear that the even clutch speed and the output speed confirm, and sets a Type A code once the wide limit is exceeded long enough or the drift correction keeps firing. The repair routine that follows works on the even shaft. Ford is inconsistent: its 2024 TR9070 table for the four rod sensors lists rod 3 drift as P277E, whereas a second table in the same summary, sorted by shift rod, gives P284F. Mechanical causes are the same as for the other forks, though only the gears of fork C are withdrawn while the fault is active.
c: Residual pressure on the fork C actuator from a leaking valve
Rod 3 sensor reading offset so the fork appears to move
Worn detent or synchronizer parts at fork C
s: Even-shaft gear disengages unexpectedly
Shift flare or jerk while cruising
Warning lamp with stored code

P2850.d: P2850 closes the drift series for the four main forks: fork D has shifted position although the module neither commanded a change nor applied force to it. GM uses the code for rod 4 of the Corvette dual-clutch unit, again as a Type A fault that runs continuously and hands over to the even-shaft synchronizer recovery. Ford's 2024 summary names P2850 for shift rod 4 drift in its per-rod table but uses P277F for the same fault in the sensor table, so the stored number may depend on the software level. A creeping fork can partly disengage its gear under load; the module then reselects the gear or blocks it. Besides valves and detents, a sensor that loses its learned reference after a module swap can produce the same picture.
c: Leaking synchronizer or selector valve moving the fork D rod
Positions not relearned after module or sensor replacement
