Weak detent or rounded dog teeth on fork D gears
s: Gear of fork D slips out under load
Gears of fork D blocked, emergency program

P2851.t: Shift Fork Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P2851.d: P2851 is meant for a plausibility comparison between the position sensors of forks A and B. Both readings may be in range on their own, yet together they describe an impossible state, such as both forks engaged at once, or they move in step in a way that points to a shared supply or ground fault. No maker publishes a strategy for this pair code. In GM's Corvette dual-clutch software, rods 1 and 2 on the odd shaft do share a sensor reference supply, but faults are kept per rod as P2832 and P2837; Ford's TR9070 likewise assigns one consistency code to each rod sensor. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires the rationality check without prescribing the pair form. Expect the module to drop the odd or affected gears until the cause is found.
c: Shared supply or ground of the A and B sensors disturbed
One of the two sensors drifting while still in range
Corroded contacts at the internal transmission connector
s: Gears of forks A and B locked out
Warning lamp, limp-home mode

P2852.t: Shift Fork Position Sensor C/D Correlation
P2852.d: P2852 pairs the position sensors of forks C and D and sets when their readings do not fit together. In GM's numbering these are rods 3 and 4, both on the even shaft and fed from the second sensor reference; a reference fault there would shift both signals together. No published OBD summary actually uses P2852: GM keeps rods 3 and 4 apart with P283C and P2841, and Ford's TR9070 lists consistency faults for shift rod sensors 3 and 4 in the same two codes. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 is therefore the only basis. Diagnosis starts with the two signals in live data while each fork is moved by a scan-tool test; if both deviate in the same direction, wiring or supply is more likely than the sensors themselves.
c: Reference voltage feeding the C and D sensors out of tolerance
Sensor C or D reporting a shifted value
Input circuit fault in the transmission module
s: Gears of forks C and D unavailable
Transmission fault message, reduced power

P2853.d: P2853 is set when the pressure measured at clutch A falls short of what the control model predicts. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table applies it to clutch 1, the odd-gear clutch, as a Type A fault in two ways: the model expects more than 1 bar while the sensor shows under 0.5 bar for 5 s, or the measured value stays below the model by more than a calibrated margin for too long. GM labels this result a pressure discharge fault and requests recovery of the odd-side clutch. Ford's 2024 summary gives the same number to measured odd clutch pressure below target on the TR9070. A real pressure loss weakens or prevents engagement, so launch and odd gears suffer; sensor offset faults have their own codes such as P0844.
c: Clutch A pressure control valve sticking or delivering too little
Leaking seal or piston ring in the clutch A circuit
Low fluid level or clogged filter reducing supply pressure
s: Weak or delayed launch, engine flares
Odd gears unavailable, limp-home mode
Warning lamp on

P2854.d: P2854 is the even-side partner of P2853: the pressure sensor of clutch B reports less than the control model expects. In GM's Corvette software clutch 2 drives the even gears; the check uses the same logic as on clutch 1, with a modeled value above 1 bar facing a reading under 0.5 bar for 5 s, plus a second path that watches the absolute gap between model and sensor. Both lead to a Type A code and a recovery request for the even clutch. Ford's TR9070 summary of 2024 maps measured even clutch pressure below target to P2854. Because the dual-clutch box can still drive on the odd gears, the car usually stays mobile in a reduced mode, but shifts into second and the following even gears are lost.
c: Clutch B pressure control valve restricted by debris or wear
Seal leak in the clutch B feed or piston
Foamed or overheated fluid lowering effective pressure
s: Even gears skipped, car runs in odd gears only
Slipping or flare on shifts into even gears
Transmission warning

P2855.d: P2855 points the other way from P2853: clutch A carries more pressure than the model calls for. GM's Corvette table for clutch 1 uses three paths, all Type A. The measured pressure sits above the model by more than a set difference long enough to be confirmed; the absolute gap grows too large with the reading on the high side; or, while the idle clutch is being held at its hold pressure, where it should pass no torque, the reading climbs more than about 1.2 bar above that level for 300 ms. GM calls this a pressure charge fault and requests the odd clutch recovery. Ford's 2024 TR9070 summary sets P2855 when odd clutch pressure exceeds target. Excess pressure makes the clutch drag or grab, giving harsh launches and possible binding.
c: Clutch A pressure control valve sticking toward high output
Excessive line pressure feeding the clutch circuit
Clutch adaptation values out of date after repair
s: Harsh engagement or jerky creep from standstill
Drag felt as if the brakes were applied
Limp-home mode with warning lamp

P2856.d: P2856 flags too much pressure at clutch B, the even-gear clutch in GM's and Ford's dual-clutch layouts. For the Corvette unit GM checks clutch 2 with the same high-side logic as clutch 1, including the hold-pressure case: an open clutch held at its standby pressure must not rise well above that point, because it would then pass torque while the other clutch is driving. A Type A code follows, and the even clutch recovery routine is requested. Ford's 2024 summary lists P2856 on the TR9070 for even clutch pressure above target. Both clutches carrying torque at once can make the car shudder or brake itself, so continuing on the odd gears with clutch B open is the likely fallback.
c: Clutch B pressure control valve hanging in a high-pressure position
Safety shutdown valve for clutch B not venting
Clutch B pressure sensor reading high within its range
s: Shudder or binding during shifts
Even gears blocked, emergency program
Warning lamp

P2857.t: Clutch A Pressure Engagement Performance/Too Low
P2857.d: P2857 reports that clutch A did not build up enough holding force when the control unit asked it to engage, so the expected ratio or torque transfer never appeared. Mitsubishi documents it for the CVT with two-speed auxiliary gearbox fitted to Mirage and Mirage G4 models from 2014 to 2022: while that gearbox is shifted into its first ratio, a measured ratio of 2.232 or more for 2 s counts as a fault, provided the pedal is at least 7.8 % open, the engine turns 450 rpm or more and D or B is selected. Nissan lists the same number as a clutch A pressure fault on the Kicks and Versa CVT, and Mercedes-Benz uses it on the 8G-DCT when multidisk clutch 1 fails to close. Drivers typically notice slipping, a flaring engine on take-off or a reduced-power mode.
c: Control valve (valve body) not delivering the commanded apply pressure to clutch A
Worn clutch A linings or leaking piston seals
Low, aerated or aged transmission fluid
s: Engine speed flares on take-off without matching acceleration
Hesitation or reduced power, transmission emergency mode
Warning lamp with stored transmission code

P2858.t: Clutch B Pressure Engagement Performance/Too Low
P2858.d: P2858 is the clutch B counterpart of P2857: the element that should close for the second stage never reaches the pressure needed to carry torque. In Mitsubishi's Mirage CVT the check runs while the auxiliary gearbox changes up to its second ratio; if the ratio still reads 2.232 or higher after at least 2 s, the TCM concludes the box is hanging in neutral between the stages. Nissan groups P2858 with further pressure and judder codes on the 2018–2021 Kicks and 2020–2021 Versa: the technician removes the control valve and inspects the belt, replacing the whole CVT if the belt shows slip marks and only the valve body if it does not. Expect hesitation, rising engine speed without matching acceleration and a fail-safe mode.
c: Control valve unable to raise clutch B pressure
Slip damage inside the transmission (belt, clutch B linings)
Fluid level or quality outside specification
s: Second stage or even gears engage late or not at all
Engine revs rise at cruising speed, acceleration lags
Reduced power with warning lamp

P2859.t: Clutch A Pressure Disengagement Performance/Too Low
P2859.d: P2859 concerns the release side of clutch A: during a ratio change the control unit sees that the pressure handover is not working as planned, so the old and new power paths overlap or the wrong ratio persists. Mitsubishi's Mirage CVT shows how this is tested. With the first auxiliary ratio commanded, a fault is logged when the ratio stays within 10 % of the second ratio (0.900–1.100) for 0.5 s, if it leaves the plausible window (0.911 or less, 2.732 or more) for 0.2 s, or if the high clutch pressure switch reads on for 1.5 s at up to 10 km/h while its target pressure is zero. Nissan lists P2859 among the Kicks/Versa CVT pressure codes, and Mercedes-Benz calls it a general malfunction of multidisk clutch 1 on the 8G-DCT. Harsh or doubled shifts follow.
c: Outgoing clutch not venting in time, so both elements carry torque
Sticking pressure control solenoid or valve in the valve body
Clutch pressure switch reporting pressure that is not there
s: Harsh, doubled or tied-up shifts
Wrong gear stage held, engine speed too low or too high
Transmission warning and emergency program

P285A.t: Clutch B Pressure Disengagement Performance/Too Low
P285A.d: With P285A the module reports a release-side pressure fault involving clutch B. Mitsubishi's Mirage CVT evaluates it while the auxiliary gearbox is commanded into its second stage: a ratio that remains within 10 % of the first stage (1.639–2.003) for 0.5 s, or that drops to 0.500 or below or climbs to 1.500 or above for 0.2 s, sets the code. On the Nissan Kicks and Versa the number carries extra weight: if it appears together with P0875, the fluid pressure switch D code, Nissan has the control valve replaced straight away without the belt inspection required for the other codes. In daily driving the car may refuse the upper stage, flare between shifts or drop into a limp program, while the lower stage often stays usable.
c: Defective control valve, especially when P0875 is stored at the same time
Leak in the clutch B circuit preventing a clean handover
Faulty clutch pressure switch or its wiring
s: Upper stage or even gears not available
Flare between shifts, then a hard engagement
Limp mode with warning lamp

P285B.d: P285B covers the electrical drive of the actuator that moves fork A, for designs where an electric motor rather than oil pressure shifts the gears. The module sets it when the output stage sees no load, typically a broken winding, a cut lead or a connector that has backed out. Ford documents the code for the DPS6 dual-clutch box of 2012: shift drum A, which positions the forks for 1st, 3rd and 5th, is turned by a three-phase motor geared 61.44:1 to the drum, and an open motor circuit is logged as P285B. Ford flags it for the MIL. Sibling faults on the same drum are split off: driver chip (P2831), hall sequence (P2835), short to ground (P285D), short to power (P285E) and lost drum position (P2832). Without drum A the odd gears cannot be selected.
c: Loose, corroded or backed-out connector at the fork A actuator motor
Broken lead between transmission module and actuator motor
Open phase winding inside the actuator motor
Failed motor output stage in the transmission module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and transmission warning
First, third or fifth gear not available, car may only move in the even gears
Jerky starts or refusal to pull away

P285C.d: P285C is the functional counterpart to the electrical fork A actuator codes. The circuit may be intact, yet the actuator does not achieve what it is asked to do: it moves too slowly, draws an unexpected current or leaves the fork short of its target. No manufacturer publishes a detection strategy for P285C. Ford's 2014 code catalogue lists it under the wrench lamp column only, not the MIL column, and Ford's DPS6 description routes a blocked drum motor into the position error P2832 rather than into this code. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 nevertheless asks for functional monitoring of transmission outputs. Possible causes are a sluggish motor, a binding drum or rod, and worn reduction gearing. Expect harsh or slow changes into the gears served by fork A.
c: Worn or sluggish fork A actuator motor
Shift drum, rod or fork A binding mechanically
Worn reduction gearing between motor and drum
Low supply voltage to the module during shifts
s: Slow or harsh shifts into the gears of fork A
Wrench or transmission warning without engine lamp
Occasional gear skipping or neutral moments

P285D.t: Shift Fork A Actuator Circuit Low
P285D.d: P285D points to a fork A actuator line pulled toward ground: a chafed motor phase touching the case, water in the connector, or a short inside the motor. To protect its driver, the module normally shuts the output down at once. In Ford's 2012 OBD summary for the DPS6 gearbox this exact fault, a short to ground on the shift drum A motor, carries P285D; the MIL is requested, as Ford's 2014 code catalogue confirms. That drum handles 1st, 3rd and 5th. Ford keeps the open circuit (P285B) and the short to battery voltage (P285E) separate, and a fault of the motor driver chip itself appears as P2831. A grounded phase can also blow the module's driver, so the wiring should be checked before a replacement module is fitted.
c: Actuator motor lead chafed through against the transmission case
Water or corrosion in the actuator connector
Internal short of a motor winding to its housing
s: Engine lamp on, odd gears locked out
Car starts in second gear or will not move off
Code returns immediately after clearing

P285E.t: Shift Fork A Actuator Circuit High
P285E.d: P285E is logged when a line of the fork A actuator carries supply voltage where the module expects it to be switched low. Usual explanations are a harness short to a battery-fed wire or a low-side transistor in the module that no longer turns on; with some driver designs, an unloaded output can also read high. Ford names the code for its 2012 DPS6 dual-clutch unit as the short-to-power fault of the shift drum A motor, the drive that sets the forks for gears 1, 3 and 5, and lists it as a MIL code in its 2014 catalogue. The low-side companion is P285D, the open circuit P285B. Because a phase stuck at battery potential prevents controlled rotation, the module stops the motor and leaves the odd gears unavailable until the short is cleared.
c: Actuator lead shorted to a battery-fed wire in the harness
Low-side driver in the transmission module not switching
Bridged pins in the actuator or module connector
s: Engine lamp lit, gears 1, 3 and 5 unavailable
Gearbox stays in an even gear or neutral

P285F.d: With P285F the module reports that the drive circuit of the fork B actuator is open: current cannot flow when the motor or valve is energised. In Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch box, the second shift drum is turned by its own three-phase motor and places the forks for reverse plus 2nd, 4th and 6th; an open motor circuit there is P285F and requests the MIL. The 2012 Ford summary prints that paragraph under the heading of drum A again, but its codes and gear list clearly belong to drum B. Further checks on the same motor are P2836 for the driver chip, P283A for the hall pattern and P2837 when the drum position becomes unreliable. A car with P285F usually loses reverse and the even gears, so manoeuvring may become impossible.
c: Fork B actuator connector loose or with spread terminals
Open wire in the harness to the fork B actuator
Burnt or broken winding in the fork B motor
s: No reverse gear, even gears missing
Engine lamp and gearbox fault message
Car drives only in 1st, 3rd and 5th with large rpm steps

P2860.d: P2860 says the fork B actuator is electrically present but underperforms: travel takes too long, the target position is missed, or the effort needed to move it is out of line with what the module expects. No maker has published how it detects P2860. In the Ford code catalogue of 2014 it carries only the wrench symbol, so Ford treats it as a drivability fault without MIL, and in the DPS6 summary a jammed motor on the even-gear drum is booked under P2837 instead. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 still requires functional checks of transmission actuators. On a vehicle that stores P2860, look at the mechanical side first: a stiff drum or fork, contamination in the selector track, or a motor whose brushes or bearings are worn.
c: Stiff shift drum, rod or fork B
Fork B actuator motor with worn bearings or brushes
Debris or wear in the selector track
s: Delayed engagement of reverse or the even gears
Wrench lamp or gearbox message, engine lamp off
Clunk or shudder during upshifts to 2nd, 4th or 6th

P2861.t: Shift Fork B Actuator Circuit Low
P2861.d: P2861 is set when a fork B actuator line reads near ground although the module has not switched it there, the classic signature of a short to ground. Ford's 2012 DPS6 summary assigns exactly this case on the motor of the drum for reverse and the even gears to P2861, and the 2014 Ford catalogue marks it as a MIL fault. Look for a motor phase rubbed through on a bracket, corrosion bridging a terminal to the shield, or a winding that has contacted the motor housing. The other circuit faults on this motor are kept apart: P285F for an open lead, P2862 for a short to battery voltage, P2836 for the driver chip. Once the output is disabled, the car typically drives on in gears 1, 3 and 5 only, without reverse.
c: Fork B motor lead rubbed through on a bracket or the case
Corrosion bridging a terminal to ground in the connector
Fork B motor winding shorted to its housing
s: Reverse not selectable
Engine lamp on, only odd gears in use

P2862.t: Shift Fork B Actuator Circuit High
P2862.d: P2862 indicates that a fork B actuator line sits at or near battery voltage when it should be pulled low. In practice this is a short to a powered conductor or a module transistor that stays open. Ford documents P2862 in its 2012 OBD summary as the short-to-power check of the DPS6 motor that turns the drum for reverse and gears 2, 4 and 6; the 2014 catalogue lists the MIL for it. Ford handles the open circuit as P285F and the ground short as P2861. Because the module cannot regulate the motor phases safely, it stops the motor and leaves that drum where it is; depending on where it stops, the box may be stuck without reverse or in one even gear. Inspect the harness routing near hot or moving parts before condemning the module.
c: Fork B actuator wire shorted to a powered conductor
Module output transistor for fork B stuck
Insulation melted near the exhaust or a hot component
s: Engine lamp, no reverse or stuck in one even gear
Large rpm jumps because only odd gears are used

P2863.d: P2863 is the general circuit code for the position sensor of a fifth shift fork, used where the module cannot or does not distinguish between low, high and erratic signals. Only transmissions with five forks need it, such as eight-speed dual-clutch units. Mercedes-Benz lists P286300 for the 8G-DCT (724.1) in its 2025 service information on guided diagnosis, described simply as a disturbed position sensor, next to its own entries P2864, P2865 and P2866 for malfunction, ground short and positive short. GM's Corvette dual-clutch software, which also has a fifth rod, skips this umbrella code and reports the electrical faults of rod 5 only as P2865, P2866 and P2867. Without a valid fork E signal, the module withholds the gears on that fork.
c: Poor contact at the fork E sensor or module connector
Fork E position sensor failed internally
Sensor reference supply shared with other sensors disturbed
s: Gears on fork E blocked, drive continues in remaining gears
Drive system warning in the instrument cluster
Unusual shift sequence or skipped gears

P2864.t: Shift Fork E Position Circuit Range/Performance
P2864.d: P2864 sets when the fork E position signal is electrically fine but contradicts what the shaft speeds show. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table uses it as the Type A consistency check of rod 5, which belongs to the even-gear clutch shaft. During an engagement with more than 600 N of rod force, the code matures if speeds prove the gear is in but the sensor stays over 1100 µm from the learned engaged point; similar tests run during disengagement, at rest (500 ms with clutch and output speeds cross-checked), and in an intrusive routine that expects at least 100 µm of travel. GM also uses P2864 to start a synchronizer recovery routine. Mercedes-Benz lists P286400 as a fork E sensor malfunction on the 8G-DCT. A relearn is the usual first step.
c: Learned positions of rod 5 missing or outdated after repair or software update
Sensor magnet on the fork E rod shifted or loose
Synchronizer actuation valve for rod 5 sticking, so the rod barely moves
Implausible even-shaft or output speed signal misleading the check
s: Gears on fork E locked out, warning lamp on
Harsh or aborted shifts on the even shaft
Reduced performance mode

P2865.t: Shift Fork E Position Circuit Low
P2865.d: P2865 means the fork E position input is stuck low. On GM's 2023 Corvette, whose rod 5 sensor sends a pulse-width signal, the TCM runs two Type A checks under this number: no pulses at all while the pin rests below 2000 mV, or a duty cycle under 8 %, each confirmed after 150 ms. The test is suspended while cranking, outside 8.75 to 18 V battery voltage, or when the sensor reference supply leaves its band. Mercedes-Benz names P286500 on the 8G-DCT plainly as a short to ground of the fork E position sensor. Look for a signal wire grounded in the harness, a sensor with an internal short, or a missing reference voltage. The high-side counterpart is P2866, the frequency fault P2867.
c: Fork E sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Fork E sensor with internal short or failed output stage
Sensor supply missing because of an open feed
s: Warning lamp with fork E gears blocked
Fault returns at once after clearing

P2866.t: Shift Fork E Position Circuit High
P2866.d: P2866 is the high-level fault of the fork E sensor input. GM's Corvette TCM, reading rod 5 as a pulse-width signal, stores it as Type A in two situations: the line delivers no pulses and stays above 3500 mV, or the duty cycle climbs past 92 %. Either must persist for 150 ms, and the check pauses during cranking or when battery or reference voltage lies outside its window. On the Mercedes 8G-DCT the matching entry P286600 is described as a short to positive of the fork E sensor. Possible reasons are a signal lead touching a supply wire, an open ground of the sensor that lets the line float up, or a sensor that latches its output. P2865 is the low counterpart; a signal that pulses at the wrong rate sets P2867 instead.
c: Fork E signal wire touching a supply voltage wire
Open ground of the fork E sensor letting the signal float high
Sensor electronics holding the output permanently high
s: Gears of fork E withheld, warning shown
Engine lamp after a short drive

P2867.t: Shift Fork E Position Circuit Intermittent
P2867.d: P2867 reports that the fork E sensor signal is present but unsteady. GM's Corvette TCM times each cycle of the digital rod 5 signal and sets the code, Type A, when the frequency drops below 1500 Hz or rises above 2500 Hz for at least 150 ms, with the same voltage and cranking exclusions as the low and high tests. So the sensor keeps pulsing, just not at a rate the module accepts. Such dropouts are usually caused by a loose pin, a chafed shield picking up interference, or a sensor beginning to fail with heat. The Mercedes 8G-DCT diagnosis list names fork E sensor faults but not this number. Unlike P2865 and P2866, the fault may come and go, so a stored code without symptoms is common at first.
c: Loose or fretted terminal in the fork E sensor circuit
Damaged shielding letting electrical noise into the signal
Sensor electronics failing intermittently when hot
s: Sporadic warning, sometimes without noticeable effect
Occasional lockout of fork E gears

P2868.t: Shift Fork E Position Sensor Incorrect Neutral Position Indicated
P2868.d: P2868 concerns the neutral information from the fork E sensor. The signal is electrically valid, but the module judges that the neutral it shows does not fit the real state of the fifth fork, either neutral claimed while a gear on that fork transmits drive, or a fork that seems engaged where neutral has been commanded. No manufacturer documents P2868 publicly. GM's Corvette software, the one published strategy with a fifth rod, compares an unloaded rod 5 with its learned neutral and engaged bands but books deviations under the consistency code P2864; the Mercedes 8G-DCT fork E entries do not include this number either. Monitoring of this input is still demanded by CARB 13 CCR 1968.2. Lost learned values and a shifted sensor magnet are the usual suspects.
c: Learned neutral of fork E lost after module swap or repair
Magnet or target on the fork E rod displaced
Worn detent or bent fork moving the rest position
s: Gears served by fork E refused
Gear display does not match the gear actually engaged
Warning lamp with limp-home program

P2869.d: P2869 states that fork E does not follow its commands: a gear on that fork cannot be engaged or released, although the position input itself may be working. No manufacturer publishes a strategy for P2869; the basis is the CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requirement to check transmission components for function. The only public method for a fifth rod comes from GM's 2023 Corvette table. There an intrusive integrity routine pushes rod 5 both ways via synchronizer valve 5 and expects more than 100 µm of movement; if nothing moves, GM decides between sensor and valve with a current profile test of the valve and records the sensor fault under P2864, while valve 5 circuit faults use P27D5 to P27D8. Typical causes are a seized rod, a broken fork or a jammed synchronizer.
c: Fork E rod seized in its bore or blocked by debris
Actuator or hydraulic valve of fork E not moving the rod
Synchronizer or sleeve of fork E jammed or broken
s: One gear stays engaged or cannot be selected
Transmission emergency mode, warning lamp
Grinding or clunking from the gearbox

P286A.d: P286A flags fork E creeping out of the position that belongs to its current gear, although no shift was requested and no force is being applied. GM uses the code in the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch TCM as the Type A drift fault of rod 5: as long as even clutch speed and output speed confirm the gear the module believes is engaged, the measured rod position must stay inside wide tolerance limits around that gear, and leaving them for a confirmation time sets P286A. The test is blocked if the rod 5 sensor already has an electrical or consistency fault. GM also lists P286A among the triggers of a synchronizer recovery routine. A drifting fork can let a gear partly disengage under load; worn detents, leaking actuation valves and lost references are typical.
c: Weak detent spring or worn detent notch on the fork E rod
Leaking synchronizer actuation valve pushing the rod
Position reference of rod 5 lost after repair
s: Gear on fork E jumps out or shudders under load
Unexpected reshift or brief loss of drive
Warning lamp and stored transmission code

P286B.t: Clutch A Pressure Engagement Too High
P286B.d: P286B means the pressure applied to clutch A during engagement exceeded the level the control unit had planned. A clutch pressed too hard closes abruptly, which shows up as a jolt, a harsh launch or a shunt through the driveline. No manufacturer documents P286B publicly; the basis is CARB 13 CCR 1968.2, which asks for functional monitoring of automatic transmission controls. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch software performs a comparable check under another number: clutch 1 is reported as a Type A fault under P2855 when its measured pressure rises clearly above the model, for example more than about 1.2 bar above the hold level for 300 ms. Typical causes are a sticking pressure control valve, a sensor that reads high or adaptation values lost after a repair.
c: Clutch A pressure control valve sticking towards high output
Clutch adaptation values missing or wrong after repair or software update
Clutch pressure sensor reading higher than actual
s: Harsh launch or jolt when clutch A closes
Clunk through the driveline during shifts
Warning lamp, possibly limp mode

P286C.t: Clutch A Pressure Disengagement Too High
P286C.d: P286C sets when clutch A still holds too much pressure while it is supposed to open. The residual force keeps the clutch dragging, so in a dual-clutch or planetary layout two power paths can briefly work against each other; the result is shudder, a braking feel during shifts or creeping with neutral selected. No manufacturer publishes a strategy for this exact code. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 still expects transmission outputs to be checked for function, and GM's 2023 Corvette table illustrates the principle by watching the hold pressure of an open clutch, reported there as P2855 or P2856. Likely sources are a slow-draining or stuck valve, a blocked exhaust port in the valve body or an offset in the pressure sensor.
c: Valve or exhaust passage for clutch A not venting fully
Debris or clutch material in the valve body
Pressure sensor showing residual pressure that is not real
s: Shudder or binding during shifts
Vehicle creeps or feels braked in neutral
Clutch overheating warning possible

P286D.t: Clutch A Engagement Time Performance/Too Slow
P286D.d: P286D sets when clutch A takes longer to engage than the control unit allows. Volvo uses it in the inverter module (IEM) of the electric rear axle drive on its T8 plug-in hybrids: the rear e-motor is coupled to the wheels through a clutch, and when coupling is too slow, electric rear drive and all-wheel drive drop out and the MIL may light. Volvo first cured intermittent cases on 2016–2018 cars with new IEM software (TJ 33723); for the permanent fault on 2020–2022 models the latest journal also prescribes only a calibration update, whereas an earlier issue allowed replacing the rear drive unit if the code came back. In conventional transmissions the same title covers clutches that fill slowly because of low or aerated fluid.
c: Outdated control module calibration (Volvo IEM software)
Slow clutch fill from low, aerated fluid or a restricted feed
Internal fault of the clutch or drive unit
s: Electric rear drive or all-wheel drive unavailable
Delayed engagement with a pause in drive
MIL or hybrid warning

P286E.t: Clutch A Engagement Time Too Fast
P286E.d: P286E is the opposite of P286D: clutch A reaches its engaged state sooner than the control unit expects. An overly quick engagement usually means the fill phase is being skipped, because the piston was already partly applied, the pressure control overshoots or adaptation values are too aggressive; the driver feels a bang on take-off or during shifts. No manufacturer documents P286E in a public source. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires functional checks of transmission controls, and Mitsubishi's monitoring of the Outlander PHEV engine clutch shows how engagement can be judged from the speed difference across the clutch, which collapses to almost zero once it has closed. A software update or relearn comes first, followed by checks of the valve body.
c: Clutch adaptation values too aggressive or not matched to new parts
Pressure control overshooting due to a sticking solenoid
Clutch piston not fully retracted before the next apply
s: Bang or jerk when clutch A engages
Harsh take-off from standstill

P286F.t: Clutch A Disengagement Time Performance/Too Slow
P286F.d: P286F tells that clutch A needs too long to release. Torque then keeps flowing after the control unit has ordered the clutch open, which disturbs shifts and can make the vehicle creep or stall the engine at a stop. Ford lists the code as an MIL item in its 2014 diagnostic code catalogue. In Ford's DPS6, clutch A serves first, third and fifth gear and a spring pushes it open when its electric motor is switched off. Volvo stores P286F00 in the rear-axle inverter module of its T8 hybrids and handles it, together with P286D00 and P287100, through an IEM software update (TJ 33723).
c: Control module software needing an update (Ford PCM/TCM, Volvo IEM)
Release mechanism or return spring of clutch A sticking
Clutch wear shifting the release point beyond the learned value
s: Shudder or clunk on shifts out of odd gears
Creeping or engine stalling when stopping
MIL on, reduced function

P2870.t: Clutch A Disengagement Time Too Fast
P2870.d: P2870 flags clutch A opening faster than the control unit intended. During a shift the outgoing clutch has to pass torque smoothly to the incoming one; if it lets go too early, engine speed flares and the shift feels like a slip followed by a thump. No manufacturer publicly documents P2870. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 is the basis, and GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch software shows that clutch pressure is compared with a model throughout operation, so deviations in either direction can be caught. Typical triggers are a leaking piston seal, a pressure control valve that dumps oil too quickly, unsuitable adaptation values or low fluid, any of which shortens the release ramp. The transmission often reacts with firmer, slower shift programs.
c: Leaking clutch A piston seal letting pressure drop too fast
Pressure control valve venting faster than commanded
Adaptation values not suited to the current clutch condition
s: Engine flare during shifts, then a thump
Firmer substitute shift program

P2871.d: P2871 means clutch A does not close, or slips so much that it behaves as if open. Mitsubishi documents this for the clutch in the front transaxle of the 2023 Outlander PHEV, which links the engine to the wheels in parallel mode: once parallel mode has been active for 2 s, the PHEV-ECU counts how often the speeds before and after the clutch differ by 75 rpm or more for 2 s, and after eight such events the code sets and the MIL lights. Mitsubishi points to a worn clutch, low fluid, a leaking or contaminated valve body, the oil pump, pressure regulator or relief valve, and very low ambient temperature. Volvo also stores P287100 in the rear-axle inverter of its T8 hybrids and clears it with IEM software.
c: Worn clutch A that slips under load
Low transaxle fluid or external leak
Valve body, oil pump, pressure regulator or relief valve not supplying pressure
Control unit fault or outdated software
s: Engine cannot drive the wheels directly, only series or electric drive
Engine speed rises without extra thrust
MIL on

P2872.d: P2872 is set when clutch A stays closed although it should be open. Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV uses it for the engine clutch in the front transaxle: in EV mode, or in series mode where an open clutch would leave a large speed gap, the front motor turns at 750 rpm or more, yet input and output of the clutch differ by 8 rpm or less for 3.5 s. Both the hybrid warning and the MIL come on. In the workshop the front wheels are lifted and turned by hand; if the crankshaft pulley rotates with them, the transaxle is replaced, and a failed pressure test leads to a new valve body. Ford also lists P2872 as an MIL code. A clutch stuck closed drags the engine along, can stall it at a stop and loads the driveline.
c: Clutch A plates seized or welded together
Foreign material holding the proportional valve in the apply position
Control unit commanding or reading clutch state incorrectly
s: Engine turns with the wheels in EV mode, unusual noise or drag
Engine stalls when the vehicle stops
Hybrid system warning and MIL

P2873.t: Clutch B Pressure Engagement Too High
P2873.d: P2873 is set when clutch B is applied with more pressure than planned while it engages. In dual-clutch designs clutch B usually carries the even gears and reverse, as in Ford's DPS6 and GM's Corvette unit, so the fault tends to surface as jerky shifts into second, fourth or reverse and a hard bite when manoeuvring. Manufacturer documentation for P2873 is not public. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 calls for functional checks of transmission controls; in GM's 2023 Corvette table the comparable high-pressure check of clutch 2 appears under P2856, classed as Type A. Worth checking are a sticking pressure control solenoid for clutch B, line pressure set too high, a sensor that over-reads, or adaptation values that have drifted.
c: Clutch B pressure control solenoid sticking high
Drifted or reset adaptation values for clutch B
s: Jerky shifts into even gears or reverse
Hard bite when manoeuvring
Warning lamp, limp mode possible

P2874.t: Clutch B Pressure Disengagement Too High
P2874.d: P2874 indicates that clutch B keeps excess pressure while it is being released or should already be open. Clutch B then goes on carrying torque alongside the engaged path, which can be felt as binding, vibration during upshifts from even gears or a car that pulls while in neutral; an overheated clutch is a typical consequence. No manufacturer publishes P2874-specific criteria. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 sets the general requirement, and GM's Corvette dual-clutch module illustrates the approach: it watches the hold pressure of the open clutch and, if that rises too far, starts the recovery routine for that side. Candidates are a valve that fails to vent, debris in the valve body, a seized shutdown valve or a stuck actuator.
c: Clutch B valve not venting pressure on release
Contamination in the valve body from clutch wear
Seized shutdown valve or clutch B actuator
s: Binding or vibration on upshifts from even gears
Car pulls in neutral
Clutch temperature warning

P2875.t: Clutch B Engagement Time Performance/Too Slow
P2875.d: P2875 tells that clutch B takes too long to grip once the control unit has asked for it. Slow filling leaves a gap in drive during shifts into the gears served by clutch B, with a flare of engine speed before the clutch finally holds. No manufacturer explains P2875 in a public document; the requirement for functional monitoring comes from CARB 13 CCR 1968.2. Comparable timing logic is visible in Volvo's rear-axle clutch, which reports slow coupling as P286D00, and in Mitsubishi's Mirage CVT, which waits 2 s for the second auxiliary ratio before flagging P2858. Typical root causes are low or aerated fluid, a partly blocked filter or valve passage, worn seals that leak during fill, or an actuator motor that has lost speed.
c: Low or aerated fluid slowing the fill of clutch B
Partly blocked filter or valve passage
Worn seals leaking while the clutch fills
s: Delayed shifts into even gears with engine flare
Noticeable pause in drive during shifts
Warning lamp

P2876.t: Clutch B Engagement Time Too Fast
P2876.d: P2876 flags clutch B closing faster than its programmed fill and apply profile allows. Instead of a smooth handover the clutch grabs abruptly, which is often noticed as a knock when selecting reverse or when a dual-clutch box shifts into an even gear. No public manufacturer document describes P2876. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 demands functional checks of transmission control outputs, while the Corvette transmission software GM published for 2023 shows how a module compares clutch behaviour with an internal model to catch such deviations. Possible reasons are pressure overshoot from a sticking solenoid, adaptation values that do not suit new clutch linings after a repair, a timing error in the sensor signal, or a calibration fault in the software.
c: Adaptation values not relearned after clutch or mechatronic work
Clutch B solenoid overshooting its target pressure
Software calibration fault in the control unit
s: Knock when engaging reverse or even gears
Abrupt, harsh shifts

P2877.t: Clutch B Disengagement Time Performance/Too Slow
P2877.d: P2877 means clutch B releases too slowly after the command to open. While it lingers, the outgoing clutch fights the incoming one, so shifts out of even gears and reverse feel heavy, the car may shudder or the engine can be pulled down at a stop. Ford includes P2877 as an MIL code in its 2014 diagnostic code list. In Ford's PowerShift (DPS6) design clutch B serves reverse and the even gears, and each dry clutch is returned to the open position by a spring once its electric actuator motor is switched off, so a slow release points to that mechanism or to clutch wear. Beyond that no manufacturer publishes detection criteria, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 provides the legal basis. On wet systems check the vent path of the clutch valve.
c: Clutch B actuator or return spring not opening the clutch quickly
Clutch B wear or glazing changing the release behaviour
Restricted vent path on wet-clutch systems
s: Heavy or shuddering shifts out of even gears and reverse
Engine pulled down or stalling at a stop
MIL on

P2878.t: Clutch B Disengagement Time Too Fast
P2878.d: P2878 reports that clutch B lets go sooner or more abruptly than the release ramp held in the control unit. During a powershift the outgoing clutch has to keep carrying torque until the incoming one has taken over; if clutch B drops out early, the engine flares for a moment and the next gear arrives with a jolt, mostly on shifts away from reverse and the even gears. No manufacturer publishes detection criteria for P2878; CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 is the legal basis. Ford's DPS6 summary shows why timing errors arise on dry designs: a motor turns a screw-driven fulcrum, hall sensors count its travel from an end stop, and a spring pulls the clutch open as soon as the motor lets go. A lost position count, a weak hold or adaptation values that no longer match the linings all shorten the release.
c: Clutch B adaptation values no longer matching the linings
Actuator position count lost or misread by the hall sensors
On wet systems a clutch B valve venting pressure too quickly
Low fluid level or aerated fluid
s: Brief engine flare followed by a jolt when shifting
Harsh shifts out of even gears or reverse
Warning lamp, firmer substitute shift program

P2879.d: P2879 is set when clutch B does not reach the torque it is asked for, or stays open altogether, so a large speed difference remains across it. No manufacturer publishes a test written for P2879. Mitsubishi shows the method on the clutch A sibling P2871 of the 2023 Outlander PHEV: once parallel mode has run for 2 s, the PHEV-ECU counts phases in which input and output differ by at least 75 rpm over 2 s, and the eighth such phase sets the code with MIL. Ford's 2012 DPS6 summary files the matching clutch B motor fault as P07A4, functionally stuck off; there clutch B drives reverse and the even gears. A car with this fault may refuse reverse, skip 2nd, 4th and 6th or flare without pulling. Worn linings, low apply pressure, a failed actuator motor and wiring faults are the usual suspects.
c: Worn or glazed clutch B slipping under load
Insufficient apply pressure from valve body, pump or regulator
Clutch B actuator motor or its drive failed
Wiring fault or control unit not commanding the clutch
s: Reverse or even gears missing
Engine speed rises without thrust
MIL and limp mode

P287A.d: P287A means clutch B stays closed, or keeps transmitting torque, at a moment when it should be open. Ford lists P287A as an MIL code in its 2014 code catalogue. In the DPS6 gearbox Ford describes for 2012, clutch B carries reverse together with 2nd, 4th and 6th and is pushed open by a return spring once its electric motor backs off; the older summary books that motor case as P07A5. Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV flags the clutch A counterpart P2872 if a clutch meant to be open shows a slip of 8 rpm at most for 3.5 s while the front motor spins at 750 rpm or above. Applied to clutch B, the result is two clutches pulling at once: shudder, a strong pull in neutral or a stalled engine at a standstill. The TCM normally locks out the affected half of the gearbox.
c: Clutch B actuator or return spring not opening the clutch
Clutch B plates seized or welded after overheating
On wet systems a valve held in the apply position by debris
Control unit or wiring commanding apply continuously
s: Shudder or binding, strong pull in neutral
Engine stalls when the car stops
MIL on, gears locked out

P287B.t: Shift Fork A Calibration Not Learned
P287B.d: P287B says that the control unit has no valid learned reference positions for shift fork A and therefore cannot place it accurately in neutral or in its gears. On electrically shifted dual-clutch boxes such as Ford's DPS6, drum A moves the forks for 1st, 3rd and 5th; the TCM knows each detent only as an angle, roughly 10, 90 and 190 degrees, derived from hall sensors on a motor that turns 61.44 times per drum revolution. Ford's 2014 list carries P287B, then worded simply as shift fork calibration not learned, as an MIL code. GM's 2023 Corvette TCM shows the comparable logic under P287C, which checks stored synchronizer rod positions at start-up. Typical triggers are a new or reflashed TCM, an interrupted learn routine, or a fork position fault that makes the learn fail.
c: TCM replaced or reprogrammed without running the fork learn
Learn routine aborted by low voltage or other fault codes
Fork A position or drum fault preventing a valid learn
Worn fork, drum groove or detent
s: Odd gears engage late, roughly or not at all
MIL or transmission warning
Learn procedure with scan tool does not complete

P287C.d: P287C means the transmission controller finds its trim or adaptation data missing, invalid or unfinished. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch TCM runs the check at initialisation, covering end-of-line and online values such as clutch preload, kiss point, fill volume, rod and parking lock positions, and learn routines left incomplete; the code is Type C, without MIL. Honda and Acura describe a trap on the 9-speed automatic of the 2015-16 TLX, 2016 MDX and 2016 Pilot: a replacement TCM arrives without trim data, sets P287C at each ignition cycle and then refuses the teach-in; clearing the code without cycling the key lets the procedure run. Mercedes lists P287C00 for the 8G-DCT as an unfinished first start-up of the transmission unit, and Ford's TR9070 summary as a learn data fault.
c: Replacement TCM installed without trim or learn data
Initial start-up or learn routine not completed
Stored data rejected after a software update
Memory fault inside the control unit
s: Rough or inconsistent shifts after TCM work
Learn or teach-in procedure refused
Transmission warning, often without MIL

P287D.t: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Torque Out Of Range
P287D.d: P287D means the motor of the electric auxiliary transmission pump produces a torque outside its expected band, as estimated by the pump controller from phase current and speed. Too little torque hints at a pump that runs dry or draws air; too much hints at a dragging rotor, cold thick fluid or a blocked passage. No manufacturer documents P287D publicly; the duty to monitor the pump stems from CARB 13 CCR 1968.2. Neighbouring cases set the scene: Ford's TSB 17-2056 has the 2016 F-150 2.7L with start-stop store P0C2A when its auxiliary pump does not run, and FCA lists P2797, pump performance, for the Pacifica plug-in hybrid. Because the pump keeps clutches filled while the engine is stopped, a fault often disables start-stop or causes a harsh engagement on restart.
c: Low fluid or air drawn into the auxiliary pump
Dragging pump rotor or blocked suction or delivery path
Worn pump motor or faulty integrated controller
s: Start-stop or electric drive no longer available
Harsh engagement after engine restart
MIL on

P287E.d: In a parallel hybrid, the engine disconnect clutch (often called K0) sits between the combustion engine and the electric motor and is opened for electric driving. P287E reports that the control module sees no plausible current path through the actuator that operates this clutch, typically a pressure control solenoid in the transmission valve body or an electric actuator. An open wire, a loose connector or a burnt-out coil are the classic triggers. No manufacturer publicly documents this exact code; Audi traces a related stuck-open fault on the A3 e-tron to the pressure valve of clutch 0 in the mechatronic unit. Without a working actuator the engine can no longer be coupled reliably, so electric-only or limp-home operation is likely. Circuit Low/High are covered by P2880/P2881.
c: Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector at the transmission or actuator
Broken wire in the actuator feed or return line
Open coil in the clutch pressure solenoid or actuator
Failed output stage in the transmission or hybrid control module
s: Malfunction or transmission warning in the instrument cluster
Engine does not start or cannot drive the wheels
Reduced power or limp-home operation

P287F.t: Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
P287F.d: P287F concerns the actuator of the clutch that couples the engine to the electric motor of a parallel hybrid. The circuit is not broken; instead, the electrical feedback (current, voltage or duty cycle) does not match what the control module expects for its command, or the clutch reacts to the command differently than the model predicts. Rising coil resistance, a sticking valve, contaminated fluid or wrong adaptation values can cause this. No manufacturer documents P287F publicly. Audi shows how closely software and hydraulics interact here: for slip faults on the Q5 and A7 plug-in hybrids it prescribes a software update, a fluid level check, a hydraulic test and a touch point adaptation of the clutch. Open circuit and short faults belong to P287E, P2880 and P2881.
c: Clutch solenoid or actuator with drifting resistance or sticking spool
Low, aged or contaminated transmission fluid
Lost clutch adaptation values or outdated control software
High contact resistance at connector pins
s: Jerky or delayed engine engagement when switching from electric to hybrid mode
Transmission warning, sometimes only intermittently
Limited hybrid functions or limp-home operation

P2880.t: Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Circuit Low
P2880.d: P2880 is stored when the signal in the actuator circuit of the engine disconnect clutch stays below its permitted window. In practice this usually means a short to ground on the control side, or a feed that has lost supply voltage, so that the solenoid or actuator is either energised permanently or not at all, depending on which side is affected. The control module normally switches the output off to protect itself. No manufacturer publishes a description of this code; the circuit monitoring follows the general CARB demand that output components of the powertrain be checked for electrical faults. Whether the clutch then rests open or closed depends on its design; the Ford F-150 PowerBoost and the Audi plug-in hybrids use hydraulic clutches inside the transmission. Compare P2881 for the high side.
c: Chafed control wire shorted to ground or housing
Missing supply voltage (fuse, relay, feed wire)
Internal short in the clutch solenoid coil
Faulty output stage in the control module
s: Hybrid or transmission warning lamp
Engine cannot be coupled, only electric driving available
Limp-home mode after the output is switched off

P2881.t: Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Circuit High
P2881.d: P2881 is the counterpart to P2880: the monitored signal in the circuit of the disconnect clutch actuator is above the upper limit. A control line touching battery voltage is the textbook case; an open return line or a missing ground at a low-side driver can produce the same reading, because the module then sees full voltage where it expects a pulled-down level. The clutch can no longer be commanded precisely. Public manufacturer documentation for P2881 was not found; on the Audi A3 e-tron the clutch between engine and motor is operated by a pressure regulating valve in the dual-clutch mechatronic unit, which shows what kind of actuator is involved. Wiring is checked first; swapping the actuator only makes sense after the harness has passed resistance and short tests.
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open return line or missing ground on the actuator
Moisture bridging pins in the transmission connector
Faulty voltage sensing in the control module
s: Warning lamp with hybrid system message
Harsh or missing engine engagement
Limited driving mode

P2882.d: P2882 means the clutch between combustion engine and electric motor slips more than allowed while it is supposed to be closed: the speed on the engine side and the speed on the motor side drift apart. Audi documents this code (P288200, symptom 20954) for the Q5 e quattro of 2020–2024 and the A7 e quattro of 2021–2022; the driver sees a gearbox fault message, and the code is stored in the engine control module. Audi blames faulty gearbox software, reflashes the Q5 e-drive module (J841) where needed and then checks fluid level, hydraulics and the clutch touch point. Mitsubishi monitors its comparable engine clutch through speed differences but files the result under P2871. Real wear or low fluid remain possible causes on older vehicles.
c: Transmission or electric drive software with faulty slip evaluation
Low transmission fluid level reducing clutch pressure
Clutch touch point not or wrongly adapted
Worn clutch plates or leaking hydraulic seal
s: Gearbox malfunction message in the cluster
Engine revs flare while torque on the wheels lags behind
Hybrid mode limited, more electric-only operation

P2883.t: Engine Disconnect Clutch Temperature Too High
P2883.d: P2883 protects the disconnect clutch from overheating. Most systems do not measure the friction plates directly; the control module models their temperature from slip speed, transmitted torque and fluid temperature, and sets the code when the estimate passes its limit. Long creeping, repeated engine starts under load, towing on steep grades or a clutch that slips for other reasons push the value up. Mercedes-Benz lists P288300 as clutch temperature too high among the codes its predictive repair tool evaluates for the 8F-DCT dual-clutch transmission (type 724.1, conventional and hybrid versions); the bulletin does not say which clutch it refers to. The module usually restricts torque or slip phases until the clutch has cooled, so the fault can disappear on its own.
c: Heavy load such as towing, creeping or stop-and-go on grades
Clutch slipping due to low pressure or wear
Restricted transmission fluid cooling or low fluid level
Temperature model in the control software too conservative
s: Warning to let the transmission cool down
Reduced power or restricted starting off
Smell of hot fluid after heavy use

P2884.d: P2884 reports that the disconnect clutch stays open although the control module has asked it to close, so the running engine cannot pass torque to the transmission. Audi documented the code (P288400, held in the gearbox module J217) on the 2016–2017 A3 e-tron: a gearbox warning and limp-home mode, traced to a mechanically defective pressure valve of clutch 0; if it is the only stored code, the mechatronic unit is replaced. Ford names P2884 together with P2885 and P2886 for F-150 PowerBoost trucks of model years 2021 to 2026 with the 10R80 modular hybrid transmission; there the wrench indicator lights, the code sits in the PCM, and Ford revised its pinpoint test for the clutch. The car often remains drivable on electric power alone.
c: Faulty clutch pressure regulating valve in the mechatronic unit
Insufficient hydraulic pressure (fluid level, pump, leak)
Mechanical damage in the clutch pack or piston
s: Gearbox warning or wrench indicator
Engine runs but does not drive the vehicle
Limp-home or electric-only driving

P2885.d: P2885 is the more general engagement code: the clutch does close, but the process does not run as planned – it takes too long, synchronisation of engine and motor speed fails, or torque arrives with a jolt. It does not claim that the clutch is permanently open or closed; those cases have P2884 and P2886. Jeep lists P2885 with MIL illumination on 2024 Wrangler 4xe plug-in hybrids built up to late March 2024 and cures it by reflashing the powertrain, transmission and auxiliary hybrid control modules (bulletin 08-051-24). Ford includes P2885 in its F-150 PowerBoost message for 2021–2026 trucks. For the driver this usually means a noticeable shunt or hesitation when the engine joins in, followed by a warning.
c: Outdated software in hybrid, transmission or engine control module
Weak hydraulic supply, e.g. auxiliary pump or low fluid
Clutch fill and touch point adaptation out of range
Faulty speed signal on engine or motor side
s: Jolt or hesitation when the engine is coupled in
MIL or wrench indicator
Hybrid mode restricted

P2886.d: P2886 is the opposite failure to P2884: the control module commands the disconnect clutch to open, yet engine and electric motor keep turning together. The engine is then dragged along during electric driving, which costs range and can stall it when the vehicle stops. Ford lists P2886 next to P2884 and P2885 for F-150 PowerBoost trucks from 2021 to 2026, stored in the PCM with the wrench indicator lit, and points to an updated pinpoint test for the clutch in the 10R80 hybrid transmission. Mitsubishi detects the same condition on the 2023 Outlander PHEV by a speed difference of no more than 8 rpm across the clutch, but uses its own code P2872 for it. Typical causes are a sticking valve, residual pressure or welded clutch plates.
c: Clutch control valve stuck in the apply position
Residual pressure from a blocked drain or faulty pump control
Control software misjudging the clutch state
s: Engine turns during electric driving or stalls when stopping
Reduced electric range
Warning lamp and restricted hybrid mode

P2887.d: P2887 is the general circuit code for the actuator that engages and releases the park lock in park-by-wire transmissions. It covers faults that are not specifically open, low or high, and some manufacturers use it as a base code that carries a failure-type byte. Ford's 2024-25 summary does just that: on its front-drive 8-speed automatics the open, ground-short and power-short cases also appear as P2887 with bytes 13, 11 and 12, and on the TR9070 dual-clutch box a bare P2887 marks a parking lock hold solenoid mechanically stuck on. Volvo's Technical Journal 36754 concerns several 2024 models whose TCM stores P288772 with the message Transmission Service Required; the remedy is new TCM software, and Volvo explicitly says not to replace the gearbox.
c: Control software misjudging the actuator circuit
Loose, corroded or damaged actuator connector or harness
Park lock actuator or hold solenoid sticking or failed
s: Transmission service message or warning lamp
P cannot be selected or released reliably

P2888.d: P2888 flags an open circuit in the park lock actuator path: the output stage switches on but finds no load. Ford's 2024-25 OBD summary maps it, alongside P2887_13, for the 8F24, 8F35/8F40 and 8F57 front-drive automatics, and in the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox as an open load on the parking lock hold solenoid, where it can also be reported as P2887_01. Typical findings are a broken wire or backed-out pin at the transmission connector, a burnt-out coil, or an internal break in the actuator. Depending on the design, the controller can then no longer hold or move the lock as commanded, so the car may stay in P, or the system refuses shift requests and keeps the lock applied for safety. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires circuit continuity checks on electronic transmission outputs.
c: Broken wire or backed-out terminal at the actuator connector
Open coil in the park lock actuator or hold solenoid
Output stage in the control unit not switching
s: Vehicle stays in P or will not accept a gear
Shift system warning

P2889.d: P2889 reports that the park lock actuator circuit sits lower than it should, as a rule because the line touches ground. Ford's 2024-25 summary pairs it with P2887_11, a short to ground, on the 8F24, 8F35/8F40 and 8F57 automatics; for the TR9070 dual-clutch unit it is called a shorted switch on the parking lock hold solenoid, meaning the switching side of the stage is pulled to ground. Chafed insulation where the harness passes brackets, moisture or corrosion in the connector and a coil shorted to its housing are typical finds. Some layouts would then energise the actuator permanently, others cannot switch it at all, so the controller blocks the function and warns the driver. Repairs start with resistance and insulation checks against ground, measured with the connector unplugged.
c: Harness chafed through and shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the actuator connector
Actuator coil shorted to its housing
s: Park lock function blocked, warning shown
Difficulty selecting or leaving P

P288A.d: P288A is set when the park lock actuator circuit reads higher than allowed, typically because it has contact with battery voltage or the load itself is shorted. Ford's 2024-25 summary books it as P2887_12, short to power, on Ford's three transverse 8-speed automatics (8F24, 8F35/8F40, 8F57); on the TR9070 dual-clutch transmission the same code stands for a shorted load on the parking lock hold solenoid, so the coil resistance has collapsed and the stage sees excessive current. Possible sources are a harness rubbed against a live feed, a wrongly repaired splice, a shorted coil or an internal actuator fault. The control unit protects its stage by switching off, which leaves the lock in whatever state it was. Measuring coil resistance and checking for voltage on the control line with ignition on usually separates wiring from actuator.
c: Control line shorted to a battery-voltage feed
Shorted turns in the actuator or hold solenoid coil
s: Shift system warning, park lock function switched off
Car stays in its last position, P or drive range

P288B.d: P288B means the park lock actuator is electrically intact but does not do what it is told, for example the lock fails to move in time. Ford's 2024-25 summary calls it functionally stuck off on its front-drive 8-speeds and mechanically stuck off on the TR9070 dual-clutch box. Several bulletins cure it with software: Ford 21-2107 for the 2020 Escape with 8F24, which could drop into Park during start-stop and lit the wrench lamp; Nissan NTB20-038 for the 2020 Titan, where two attempts were needed to leave Park; Audi 2080044 for 2025 A5 and Q5 models that could not select P; and FCA for the 2017-18 Pacifica Hybrid, where P288B became a permanent code that blocked smog checks. Only if it returns after an update is the actuator or wiring suspect.
c: Control software needing an update (Ford, Nissan, Audi, FCA)
Sluggish or sticking park lock actuator or pawl mechanism
Low supply voltage or poor connection under load
s: P cannot be selected or needs several attempts to leave
Unexpected shift to P during start-stop
Warning lamp or MIL

P288C.t: Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P288C.d: P288C does not look at the clutch itself but at the electronic switch inside the control module that powers its actuator. Modern driver chips measure their own current and junction temperature; if either exceeds the limit, they shut down and report this condition. Behind it is usually an actuator drawing too much current – a partly shorted coil, a jammed electric motor in electromechanical designs – or a harness fault that loads the output. Ambient heat around a module mounted on the transmission can add to it. No manufacturer has published a description of P288C. CARB requires such outputs to be monitored for proper function. Unlike P2880, which reacts to a voltage level, P288C points to overload, so the actuator should be measured before the module is condemned.
c: Actuator coil or motor drawing excessive current
Partial short in the actuator wiring
Control module overheating from heat or poor cooling
Defective driver chip in the control module
s: Clutch actuator switched off, engine cannot be coupled
Warning lamp, often after long or hot drives
Limp-home operation

P288D.t: Shift Fork B Calibration Not Learned
P288D.d: P288D is the fork B counterpart of P287B: the stored learn values that tell the control unit where fork B or its drum sits in each gear are missing or rejected. No manufacturer documents P288D publicly, and Ford's 2014 catalogue still knew only one fork calibration code, P287B, which suggests the split into A and B came later. On Ford's DPS6, drum B handles reverse plus the 2nd, 4th and 6th gears, with detents near 10, 90, 190 and 280 degrees, so a missing reference mainly hits reverse and the even gears. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires transmission functions of this kind to be monitored. Before relearning, check for drum B position or motor faults such as P2837 or P2836, because the learn usually aborts while those are present; after a TCM swap the procedure is simply part of the job.
c: Fork learn not carried out after TCM or mechatronic work
Drum B position or motor fault aborting the learn
Worn or bent fork B, worn drum groove
s: Reverse or even gears hesitant or unavailable
Transmission warning, possibly MIL

P288E.t: Shift Fork A Actuator Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P288E.d: P288E is a self-protection code of the output stage that powers the actuator of shift fork A. The driver reports a current above its limit or an excessive chip temperature, and the module throttles or switches off that actuator. No manufacturer documents P288E publicly. Ford's DPS6 shows where such a stage sits: a motor driver chip inside the TCM, which Ford calls the ATIC, sets the current of the three-phase motor for drum A, yet Ford books faults of that chip as P2831, not P288E. Plausible triggers are a shorted winding or lead, a drum or fork that binds so the motor stalls at full current, repeated shift attempts against a blockage, and heat in the transmission housing. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 sets the monitoring duty. With fork A out of action, 1st, 3rd and 5th may no longer engage.
c: Shorted winding or lead in the fork A actuator circuit
Binding drum or fork stalling the actuator under full current
High transmission temperature adding heat to the driver
Defective driver stage in the control unit
s: Odd gears do not engage, car may start in 2nd
Transmission warning and limp mode

P288F.t: Shift Fork B Actuator Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P288F.d: P288F tells that the driver for the shift fork B actuator has crossed its current or temperature limit, after which the TCM curbs or stops the actuator to save the electronics. Public manufacturer criteria for P288F are not available. Ford's DPS6 summary gives the setting: drum B, turned by its own three-phase motor, moves the forks that engage reverse and the gears 2, 4 and 6, and Ford files driver chip faults on that motor under P2836 instead. An actuator that pushes against a seized drum, a fork worn into its groove or a short in the motor lead drives current up, and hot fluid or a hot engine bay adds thermal stress. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 provides the general basis. In practice the vehicle may refuse reverse or fall back to odd gears only, which makes parking and manoeuvring awkward.
c: Short in the fork B actuator motor or its lead
Seized drum B or fork worn into its groove
Driver stage in the TCM failing
s: Reverse not available, even gears skipped
Warning lamp and limp mode

P2890.d: Some engines use the spark plug as a combustion sensor: between sparks a measuring voltage is applied, and the hot, ionised gas lets a small current flow whose shape reveals misfire and knock. P2890 is the basic circuit fault for this measurement on cylinder 1 – the module receives no usable ion signal from that cylinder at all. Saab built the principle into its Trionic engines: on the four-cylinder T8 the coil of cylinder 1 feeds its ion signal to a separate processing module, which also decides whether cylinder 1 or 4 is on the firing stroke, because the engine has no camshaft sensor. A dead cylinder 1 signal can therefore disturb synchronisation as well. Saab used its own codes; no manufacturer publicly documents P2890.
c: Ignition coil of cylinder 1 with failed ion measuring stage
Open ion signal wire or connector between coil 1 and the processing module
Faulty ion processing module or engine control module input
s: MIL with reduced knock and misfire monitoring on cylinder 1
Longer cranking if cylinder identification is affected
Retarded ignition and less power as a precaution

P2891.t: Cylinder 1 Ion Current Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2891.d: Here the ion signal of cylinder 1 is present but implausible: its level or waveform does not fit engine speed and load, or it differs clearly from the other cylinders. Fouled or worn spark plugs are a frequent reason, since soot or oil deposits form a leakage path that distorts the small measuring current; a cracked insulator or water in the plug well has a similar effect. In Saab's later processing module (9-3 from 2009), cylinder 1 enters on its own ion input and is combined with cylinder 3 in a combustion signal used for synchronisation and misfire detection, so a distorted cylinder 1 signal affects that pair. No manufacturer documents P2891 publicly. Electrical opens and shorts are covered by P2890, P2892 and P2893.
c: Sooted, oil-fouled or worn spark plug in cylinder 1
Moisture or oil in the plug well of cylinder 1
Ion measuring stage of coil 1 drifting
Real combustion fault in cylinder 1 (mixture, compression)
s: MIL, sometimes together with misfire codes
Rough idle or hesitation
Reduced power due to cautious knock control

P2892.t: Cylinder 1 Ion Current Sense Circuit Low
P2892.d: P2892 says the ion measurement of cylinder 1 delivers a signal that stays below the expected range. Electrically this points to a signal line shorted to ground or a measuring stage that no longer builds up its bias voltage; Saab, for example, applies around 120 V across the plug gap between sparks to obtain the current. A heavily fouled plug can also drag the level down by bleeding off the measuring voltage. When the reading is stuck low, the module can no longer judge combustion in cylinder 1 and typically falls back to a safe ignition map. No manufacturer has published this code; on Saab Trionic T8 engines the cylinder 1 ion line runs from coil pin 4 to the processing module. The high-side fault is P2893, the cylinder 2 equivalent P2896.
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 1 shorted to ground
Coil 1 no longer generates its measuring voltage
Spark plug of cylinder 1 with leakage path through deposits
s: MIL and stored fault for cylinder 1
Noticeably less power from retarded ignition
Possibly unreported misfires on cylinder 1

P2893.t: Cylinder 1 Ion Current Sense Circuit High
P2893.d: With P2893 the ion signal from cylinder 1 sits above its plausible ceiling. A signal line touching a supply voltage is the most direct explanation; crosstalk from the ignition primary circuit or a defective evaluation stage that saturates can show the same picture. Because knock is recognised from fast oscillations superimposed on the ion current, a signal pinned high leaves no room for that information, and the module will usually retard timing on cylinder 1 for safety. Saab's ion detection module, for instance, receives the cylinder 1 trigger on pin 9 and the matching ion input on pin 16, both of which can be checked for foreign voltage. A public manufacturer description of P2893 does not exist. Compare P2892 for the low reading and P2897 for cylinder 2.
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 1 shorted to a voltage source
Internal fault in coil 1 coupling ignition voltage into the signal
Saturated input in the ion processing module
s: MIL with cylinder 1 ion fault
Reduced power and possibly higher fuel consumption
Knock may go unnoticed on cylinder 1

P2894.d: P2894 covers a general fault in the ion current circuit of cylinder 2: the processing electronics get no evaluable signal from this plug. Which physical position cylinder 2 occupies depends on the maker's numbering. On Saab's Trionic four-cylinder, cylinders 2 and 3 are fired together by waste spark during start-up, and only the ion signals tell the engine management which of the two actually burned; a missing cylinder 2 signal can thus prolong cranking. In the 2009 Saab 9-3 module, cylinder 2 has its own ion input and trigger line and feeds the second combustion signal together with cylinder 4. No manufacturer publishes P2894; checking coil 2, its wiring and the plug comes first, and swapping coils between cylinders shows whether the fault moves.
c: Ignition coil of cylinder 2 with dead ion measurement
Interrupted ion signal path from coil 2
Defective cylinder 2 input in the processing module
s: MIL with a stored cylinder 2 ion fault
Hard or longer starting in some cases
Cautious ignition timing and slightly less power

P2895.t: Cylinder 2 Ion Current Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2895.d: P2895 is set when cylinder 2 delivers an ion signal that is electrically intact but does not behave plausibly – for example, it shows almost no combustion peak at normal load, or it scatters strongly from cycle to cycle compared with the neighbouring cylinders. Because the ion current is a direct image of combustion, a genuine problem in cylinder 2 such as a lean injector, a leaking valve or low compression can trigger this code just as well as a dirty plug. That makes it worth reading misfire counters and fuel trims before replacing parts. Saab processes the raw signal with filters that separate the slow combustion part from the fast knock ringing. No manufacturer describes P2895 publicly; electrical faults on cylinder 2 belong to P2894, P2896 and P2897.
c: Worn or fouled spark plug in cylinder 2
Combustion fault in cylinder 2 (injector, valve, compression)
Coil 2 measuring stage drifting with temperature
s: MIL, sometimes with misfire code P0302
Uneven running felt mainly at idle
Increased fuel consumption

P2896.t: Cylinder 2 Ion Current Sense Circuit Low
P2896.d: P2896 reports a cylinder 2 ion signal that remains under its lower limit. A ground short on the line from coil 2, a cracked plug insulator that drains the measuring voltage to the cylinder head, or a coil whose bias generator has failed can all produce a near-zero reading. Where several cylinders share a harness section or connector, a chafed spot can hit cylinder 2 alone if only its conductor is damaged, so the wiring along the cam cover deserves a look. On Saab's 2009 four-cylinder module the cylinder 2 ion input is pin 7, which allows measuring the line directly. No manufacturer publishes this code. Without a usable signal, misfire and knock detection for cylinder 2 lose their basis. P2897 is the high counterpart; cylinder 1 reports the same condition as P2892.
c: Chafed ion signal wire of cylinder 2 touching ground
Cracked spark plug insulator in cylinder 2
Measuring voltage generator in coil 2 failed
s: MIL with ion fault on cylinder 2
Engine runs on a safe ignition map with less power
Misfire on cylinder 2 may not be detected

P2897.t: Cylinder 2 Ion Current Sense Circuit High
P2897.d: P2897 applies when the ion current reading of cylinder 2 is stuck above the range the module accepts. Typical electrical reasons are a signal line that has contacted a supply or ignition feed, a damaged coil 2 that leaks primary voltage into its measuring output, or a missing ground at the coil that shifts the reference. Since the processing electronics compare the cylinders, a single high channel is easy to isolate: exchanging coil 2 with another position and watching whether the code follows is a quick test. On Saab's 2009 module the ignition trigger for cylinder 2 arrives on pin 10, which helps when tracing the wiring. No manufacturer documents P2897 publicly. The low case is P2896; cylinder 1 has the matching code P2893.
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 2 in contact with a voltage source
Coil 2 leaking primary voltage into the measuring output
s: MIL and stored cylinder 2 ion fault
Less power due to retarded timing on cylinder 2
Knock protection for cylinder 2 limited

P2898.d: P2898 marks a basic circuit failure in the ion current measurement of cylinder 3: the engine computer receives nothing it can evaluate from that spark plug. With ion sensing, the plug doubles as a probe, because a bias voltage across the gap drives a small current through the burning, conductive gas. On Saab's Trionic four-cylinders, cylinder 3 shares its start-up spark with cylinder 2 until synchronisation is reached, and only the combustion signal reveals which of the two really burned. The T7 version groups cylinders 3 and 4 on one detector, whose open line to the engine module Saab reports with its own code P1334. No manufacturer publicly documents P2898 itself; coil 3, its connector and the plug are the first checks.
c: Ignition coil of cylinder 3 whose ion measuring stage has failed
Loose or corroded connector at coil 3 or broken ion signal wire
Faulty cylinder 3 input in the ion processing module or engine module
s: MIL with ion fault stored for cylinder 3
Starting may take longer while cylinder identification is uncertain
Engine runs with cautious ignition timing and somewhat less power

P2899.t: Cylinder 3 Ion Current Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2899.d: With P2899 an ion signal from cylinder 3 does arrive, yet it fails the plausibility check: its amplitude is too weak for the current load, it fluctuates without reason, or it no longer matches the pattern of the remaining cylinders. Because the measurement mirrors how hot and how highly compressed the burning charge is, an actual combustion weakness in cylinder 3 can be the cause just as much as a degraded plug with a leakage path. In Saab's 2009 detection module, cylinder 3 enters on its own input and is merged with cylinder 1 into the first combustion signal, while a band-pass branch extracts knock ringing from the same raw trace. No maker documents P2899 publicly. Hard electrical faults on cylinder 3 are P2898, P289A and P289B.
c: Spark plug of cylinder 3 with deposits or excessive gap wear
Weak combustion in cylinder 3 (lean injector, low compression)
Damaged plug boot or moisture at the coil 3 connection
s: MIL, possibly together with P0303
Slight roughness at idle or under light load
Knock control retards timing more than usual

P289A.t: Cylinder 3 Ion Current Sense Circuit Low
P289A.d: P289A applies when the ion reading of cylinder 3 stays below the lower plausibility limit. Usually the signal path is pulled to ground somewhere, or the coil no longer supplies the measuring voltage of roughly 80 V that Saab's T7 cassette keeps across each gap between sparks. A cracked insulator or heavy carbon tracking on the plug can drain that voltage as well. Saab's own documentation shows why a dedicated code helps: on T7 four-cylinders a combustion signal shorted to ground produced no specific fault code at all, so synchronisation failed and only misfire codes appeared. With a stuck-low cylinder 3 signal, misfire and knock judgement for that cylinder is lost. The high-side fault is P289B.
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 3 chafed through to ground
Carbon tracking or cracked insulator on the cylinder 3 plug
Coil 3 no longer builds up its measuring voltage
s: MIL with low ion signal on cylinder 3
Misfire codes or no misfire detection for cylinder 3
