s: Code stored, MIL depending on manufacturer
Possible icing of the ventilation line in frost

P2CC1.d: P2CC1 is the general fault of a second sense line through which the engine controller reads the actual charging voltage. In the charging system, generator means the alternator; a sense input taps the voltage at the rectifier or battery without load current, so wiring losses do not distort it. Remy describes such a Kelvin sense lead on Chrysler alternators, connected straight to the rectifier plate behind a 2.4 kΩ protective resistor; that terminal is labelled B, which is not the circuit letter of this code. A circuit B is presumably needed only where a second alternator or measuring point exists. No manufacturer documents P2CC1 publicly; Deutz, for example, lists only circuit A codes (P063A, P063C, P063D) for its alternator. Range, low and high: P2CC2 to P2CC4.
c: Sense wire B, its fuse or connector open or corroded
Second alternator or its regulator faulty
Sense input in the engine control module faulty
s: Battery or charging warning lamp on
Charging voltage regulated to a fixed or unsuitable value

P2CC2.t: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit B Range/Performance
P2CC2.d: P2CC2 means the voltage arriving on generator sense circuit B is within electrical limits but does not agree with what the controller expects, such as the battery voltage measured elsewhere, the commanded set point or the reading of sense circuit A. The usual cause is a voltage drop: corroded ring terminals, a loose ground strap or a damaged fusible link make the sensed value lag behind reality. Because the sense lead itself carries no current, any noticeable difference between it and the output terminal points to resistance in one of the paths. No manufacturer documents P2CC2 publicly. CARB only requires charging-system inputs to be monitored when they influence emissions or feed other diagnostics, so the code often stays without MIL. Circuit A's equivalent is P063B.
c: Voltage drop from corroded terminals, loose ground strap or damaged fusible link
Alternator B delivering too little or unstable output
Battery with high internal resistance distorting the comparison
s: Charging warning lamp on or flickering
Battery not fully charged or charging voltage fluctuating

P2CC3.t: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit B Low
P2CC3.d: P2CC3 is stored when generator sense circuit B reports a voltage below its lower limit, in practice often close to zero. Typical causes are an open sense lead, a blown fuse in it or a short to ground; on Chrysler alternators, according to Remy, an internal 2.4 kΩ resistor shields the sense terminal against such a ground fault. The risk lies in the regulation: if the controller believed a too-low reading, it would raise field current and overcharge the battery, which is why a controller that has recognised the fault can fall back to a substitute value or a fixed set point instead. No manufacturer documents P2CC3 publicly. CARB demands MIL monitoring of charging inputs only where emissions or other diagnostics depend on them. High signal: P2CC4; circuit A low: P063C.
c: Sense wire B broken or its fuse blown
Sense wire B chafed and shorted to ground
Corroded sense terminal at the alternator or module
s: Charging warning lamp on
Charging voltage too high or held at a fixed value
Overcharged battery, bright lights

P2CC4.t: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit B High
P2CC4.d: P2CC4 indicates that generator sense circuit B reads above its upper limit. Either the line is shorted to a higher voltage, or the voltage at the measuring point really is excessive, for example because the regulator keeps the field fully energised; Remy warns that a full-field alternator can quickly push the system above 16 V. A meter separates the two cases: with the engine running, compare the sense voltage with the voltage directly at the battery posts. No manufacturer documents P2CC4 publicly. CARB does not require a MIL for charging inputs unless emissions or other monitors are affected, so the battery warning light is the more likely signal. Sustained overvoltage can damage lamps and electronics. Low signal: P2CC3; circuit A high: P063D.
c: Regulator of alternator B stuck in full field, real overvoltage
Sense wire B shorted to a higher-voltage line
Sense input of the engine control module faulty
s: Charging warning lamp on
Very high system voltage, bulbs failing early
Battery gassing or smelling

P2CC5.t: Generator Inverter Power Supply B Circuit/Open
P2CC5.d: P2CC5 concerns supply B inside the inverter that drives a hybrid's generator (motor-generator), typically a low-voltage rail feeding the gate drivers of the power transistors. Which supply gets the letter B is defined by the manufacturer; a second inverter channel or second generator would also fit. The code covers a missing supply or an interrupted feed. No manufacturer documents P2CC5 publicly. GM's 2019 hybrid tables show the principle with P0C0B for the drive motor A inverter: the IGBT module flags a bias fault when its supply dips below a threshold, and 0.168 s of failures within a 0.2 s window set a Type A code. CARB requires circuit monitoring of hybrid components. Without gate supply the generator cannot be switched at all. Supply A: P0E0F.
c: Supply B for the gate drivers failed inside the inverter
12 V feed, fuse or connector of the inverter interrupted
Poor ground connection of the inverter control electronics
s: Hybrid system warning light and MIL on
Generator out of operation, vehicle may not become ready to drive

P2CC6.t: Generator Inverter Power Supply B Circuit Low
P2CC6.d: P2CC6 means supply B of the generator inverter is present but below its permitted level. A weak gate driver feed is dangerous for the power stage: transistors that are not driven fully on run in a lossy partial state and heat up quickly, so the inverter typically blocks the generator. No manufacturer documents P2CC6 publicly. Ford's summary for its 2019 power-split hybrids places the related supply A code P0E10 among the generator-side gate signal faults together with P0BCE and P0BCF, which suggests the same home for supply B. Causes range from a failing internal regulator to low 12 V input during start-up or a corroded ground. CARB requires circuit monitoring for hybrid parts. Siblings: P2CC5 (open) and P2CC7 (high).
c: Internal regulator of supply B delivering too little voltage
Low 12 V input to the inverter, e.g. weak auxiliary battery
Corroded ground or connector of the inverter
s: Hybrid system warning light and MIL on
Generator limited or switched off, reduced hybrid performance

P2CC7.t: Generator Inverter Power Supply B Circuit High
P2CC7.d: P2CC7 is set when supply B of the generator inverter exceeds its upper limit. Gate inputs of IGBTs tolerate only a limited voltage, so overvoltage on the driver rail puts the switches at risk and the inverter is normally shut down. Ford shows that such rails have a hard ceiling: in its 2019 hybrid OBD summary a motor or generator gate drive supply above 15.08 V counts as a fault, although Ford reports it under a rotor position circuit voltage check, and for the variable voltage converter the window runs from 0.1 V to 15.3 V. No manufacturer documents P2CC7 publicly. A faulty internal regulator or a short between supply rails is most likely. CARB demands circuit monitoring of hybrid components. Siblings: P2CC5, P2CC6; supply A high is P0E11.
c: Regulator of supply B inside the inverter faulty
Short between two internal supply rails
Overvoltage in the 12 V system from a DC/DC converter fault
s: Hybrid system warning light and MIL on
Generator blocked, battery no longer charged while driving

P2CC8.d: Some engines measure how fast a coolant pump turns with a dedicated speed sensor, for instance on a pump that can be engaged and released or on an electric pump read back by the controller. P2CC8 is the general fault of that sensor's circuit: the signal is absent or cannot be used, without the controller deciding whether it is too low or too high. No manufacturer documents P2CC8 publicly. GM's patent US20160047374A1 describes how a measured pump speed, compared with the target, lets the controller diagnose an electric main coolant pump; Audi's patent US8915127B2 shows that without such a signal a switchable pump can only be judged indirectly through cylinder head temperature. CARB requires monitoring of coolant flow devices other than a thermostat. Expect a MIL and a default pump state.
c: Failed speed sensor delivering no usable signal
Damaged wiring or loose connector at the sensor
Missing reference voltage or ground for the sensor
s: MIL on
Coolant pump held in a default state, warm-up may change

P2CC9.d: P2CC9 means the coolant pump speed sensor delivers a clean electrical signal whose value does not make sense. The controller compares it with what the pump should be doing: a belt-driven pump has to follow engine speed in a fixed ratio once engaged, an electric pump should match its commanded speed. A gap can come from the sensor itself (wrong air gap, damaged trigger wheel, drifting electronics) or from a real pump problem such as a slipping belt or clutch. No manufacturer documents P2CC9 publicly. GM's patent US20160047374A1 builds its electric pump diagnosis on exactly this difference between measured and target speed. CARB asks for rationality checks on such inputs. Unlike P2CC8, P2CCA and P2CCB, the wiring is usually fine, so check the pump drive before replacing the sensor.
c: Slipping belt or clutch, so the pump turns slower than expected
Sensor loose, wrong air gap or damaged trigger wheel
Sensor electronics drifting or dropping pulses
s: MIL on after repeated detection
Engine may run warmer than usual or take longer to warm up

P2CCA.t: Coolant Pump Speed Sensor Circuit Low
P2CCA.d: P2CCA is stored when the signal line of the coolant pump speed sensor remains below its lower limit, so no pulses or levels above the threshold arrive. Most often the signal wire is shorted to ground, the sensor has lost its supply voltage and therefore cannot switch, or its output stage has failed in the off state. No manufacturer documents P2CCA publicly. The measured pump speed matters to the controller because, as GM's patent US20160047374A1 explains, it is compared with the target speed to judge whether the pump works; with a dead signal that check is impossible. CARB requires out-of-range checks of such inputs. Measure supply and ground at the sensor plug first, then the signal wire to ground. The opposite level is P2CCB, implausible values P2CC9.
c: Sensor supply voltage missing because of an open feed
Sensor output stage failed in the low state
s: MIL on
Pump speed reads zero in live data although the engine runs

P2CCB.t: Coolant Pump Speed Sensor Circuit High
P2CCB.d: P2CCB covers the upper end of the coolant pump speed sensor signal: the input stays above its permitted maximum. On sensors with an open-collector output and a pull-up resistor in the controller, an interrupted signal wire or a sensor that has lost its ground leaves the line resting high, so the open case often lands here rather than under P2CCA. A short between the signal wire and a voltage feed has the same effect. No manufacturer documents P2CCB publicly. GM's patent US20160047374A1 shows why the controller needs a valid reading: it judges the pump by comparing measured and target speed. CARB requires range checks for inputs like this. Checking the sensor ground and the signal wire for continuity usually finds the fault. Low levels are P2CCA, a general circuit fault P2CC8.
c: Open signal wire, input pulled up by the controller
Lost ground connection at the sensor
Signal wire shorted to a voltage feed
s: MIL on
Pump speed missing or stuck at an implausible value in live data

P2CCC.d: P2CCC continues the state-of-health series for sectioned traction batteries in the P2 block: after A (P0A7F) and B to F (P0EDD to P0EE1), section G is the seventh. The controller has concluded that this part of the pack has lost too much usable capacity or power. Audi uses the code on the Q5 PHEV as P2CCC00 for battery group 7 in hybrid battery management unit 008C. Its February 2025 reporting obligation 2076982/1 links the entry to a yellow engine lamp and a too-short displayed electric range and asks for a call to technical assistance before any part is changed; bulletin 2079556/1 of September 2025, covering model years 2020 to 2024, then calls for replacing the module behind the entry. CARB wants faults of individual storage parts such as cells to name the smallest unit a workshop can renew. Section H is P2CCD.
c: Battery module of group 7 lost capacity or power
Single weak cell block dragging the section down
State-of-health estimate of the battery controller wrong
s: Yellow engine warning lamp on
Displayed electric range too low
Electric driving mode unavailable or ends early

P2CCD.d: P2CCD reports that section H, the eighth subdivision of a traction battery, has aged past the limit its controller accepts. In practice this code only exists on large packs that the battery management splits into at least eight separately judged groups. Audi's Q5 PHEV is such a case and the only published one: there P2CCD00 stands for battery group 8 in control unit 008C, which makes it the last link of a chain beginning with P0A7F00 for group 1. The 2025 Audi bulletins list it as stored either intermittently or statically, with the MIL on and guided fault finding offering no measure, and prescribe swapping the single module concerned; if more than two modules are named, a technical assistance ticket must come first. Expect less electric range and power. Group 7 is P2CCC, section I would be P2CCE.
c: Battery module of group 8 worn out
Module aged faster due to heat or uneven cooling
Faulty state-of-health judgement by the battery controller
s: MIL on
Shorter electric range
Less power in electric mode

P2CCE.d: P2CCE is reserved for the ninth section, I, of a traction battery whose controller rates the health of each section on its own. The fault is a capacity or power verdict, not an electrical one: section I no longer delivers what a healthy unit should. No manufacturer publicly documents P2CCE. The nearest published use is Audi's Q5 PHEV, which splits its pack into eight groups and therefore stops at P2CCD for group 8; a battery with nine or more independently monitored modules would continue here, followed by P2CCF for section J. CARB asks for a state-of-health monitor for hybrid storage and, for faults of cells, sensors and cell balancing, for codes that isolate the smallest replaceable unit. Where it is used, expect the MIL, a shorter electric range and, as with Audi's siblings, the replacement of a single module rather than the whole battery.
c: Module or cell group of section I aged beyond its limit
Uneven pack temperature stressing this section
Misjudged state of health in the battery controller
s: MIL or hybrid system warning on
Shorter electric range

P2CCF.d: P2CCF belongs to the deterioration series that rates each section of a divided traction battery on its own; J is the tenth section after A (P0A7F), B to F (P0EDD–P0EE1) and G to I (P2CCC–P2CCE). It is not an electrical fault: the controller has decided that the modules of section J have given up more usable capacity or power than allowed. No manufacturer publicly documents P2CCF. The nearest documented case is the Audi Q5 PHEV, whose battery manager reports eight groups and therefore ends at P2CCD. CARB wants faults of individual storage parts such as cells to point at the smallest unit a workshop can renew; a lettered section series follows that logic. Overheating of the same section has its own code, P2D4E. Likely consequences are the MIL, less electric range and possibly reduced drive power.
c: Modules of section J worn beyond the accepted capacity or power limit
Section J repeatedly ran hotter than the rest of the pack
Health estimate of the battery controller wrong after software or sensor issue
s: MIL or hybrid system warning on
Electric range noticeably shorter
Less power available in electric driving

P2CD0.d: With P2CD0 the battery controller reports that section K, the eleventh separately judged part of the high-voltage battery, has exceeded its ageing limit. Such a verdict normally rests on comparing what this section stores and delivers with its neighbours over many charge cycles, so it rarely appears suddenly after one event. No manufacturer publishes P2CD0; published section-level codes stop at eight groups (Audi Q5 PHEV, P2CCD). Only a battery split into eleven or more monitored units would ever reach it. California's OBD rule requires such codes to narrow faults down to the smallest unit that can be replaced. Before a module is renewed, a thermal cause should be ruled out, since overheating of section K is reported separately as P2D4F. Range and available power drop, and the MIL usually lights.
c: Cells of section K lost capacity faster than the other sections
Internal resistance of section K increased, limiting power
Uneven coolant flow leaving section K warmer over years
s: Warning lamp for engine or hybrid system
Shorter range on a full charge
Weaker acceleration on battery power

P2CD1.d: P2CD1 marks section L, the twelfth subdivision of the high-voltage pack, as worn: its usable capacity or power capability has fallen below what the controller accepts. The code only makes sense for packs whose management tracks twelve or more groups individually; no carmaker documents it publicly, and the largest published series, Audi's Q5 PHEV, ends with group 8. The Californian requirement that storage faults pinpoint the smallest replaceable unit explains why separate codes exist up to N. In the workshop, cell voltages of section L are compared with the rest both at rest and under load, and a balancing problem or a sensing fault (P0BBD, voltage variation) is excluded before a module is replaced. Overheating of this section is the separate code P2D50.
c: Section L has reached the end of its usable life
One weak cell block pulling the whole section down
Faulty voltage sensing making section L look weaker than it is
s: MIL illuminated
Battery charge falls faster than usual

P2CD2.d: P2CD2 flags section M, the thirteenth part of a sectioned high-voltage battery, as degraded in capacity or power. Unlike sections J to L, M has no matching over-temperature code in the available code lists, so the thermal history of this section has to be read from general pack temperature data. No manufacturer publicly documents P2CD2, and no published battery is divided into thirteen individually rated groups; Audi's Q5 PHEV with eight groups is the largest series on record. For cell and sensor faults and for cell balancing, CARB asks for separate codes per smallest replaceable unit; balancing failures are reported under other codes. Drivers notice less electric range and weaker response in electric mode, and the warning lamp comes on.
c: Section M degraded by age and charge cycles
Long standstill at low charge damaged cells of section M
Cell balancing of section M no longer working
s: Hybrid or engine warning lamp on
Reduced electric-only range
Sluggish response in electric mode

P2CD3.d: P2CD3 closes the lettered deterioration series: N is the fourteenth section of a drive battery whose management assesses each section's condition separately. When it sets, section N can no longer hold or release the energy expected of it, even though wiring and sensors may be intact. No manufacturer documents P2CD3 publicly, and no published battery reaches fourteen individually rated groups; Audi's Q5 PHEV stops at group 8 (P2CCD). CARB obliges diagnostics of storage parts such as cells to name the smallest unit that can be swapped; a pack split this finely would reach codes up to here. Distinguish it from P0BBD, which reports a voltage spread between cells, and from the whole-pack code P0A7F. Typical effects are the MIL, reduced electric range and at times limited power.
c: Cells in section N aged beyond the acceptance limit
Earlier replaced neighbour modules leave section N as the weak link
Battery controller misjudges section N after a reset or update
s: MIL or hybrid warning
Electric range clearly reduced
Drive power limited at times

P2CD4.t: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A/B Correlation
P2CD4.d: P2CD4 is a plausibility check between two refrigerant pressure sensors that serve one A/C or heat pump circuit: the module flags it when the pair disagrees beyond what the system allows, even though each sensor is electrically fine. Bentley documents the code as P2CD400 in the thermal management ECU (address 00C5) of 2025 Continental GT and GTC models as well as the Flying Spur; campaign ED35 corrects its handling with a software update. In related Audi models, bulletin 87 22 35 shows that one to three combined pressure and temperature sensors sit on the high or low side of the loop, so A and B are maker-defined positions. No public threshold exists. Circuit faults of each sensor are P0530 ff. and P2515 ff. Expect limited compressor operation or weaker cooling.
c: Thermal management software misjudging the sensor comparison (Bentley 2025 campaign)
One pressure sensor drifting or failing internally while still in range
Contact resistance at one sensor connector shifting its signal
s: A/C cools weakly or the compressor is limited
Code stored in the thermal management or climate module

P2CD5.d: Bypass valve C is a third compressor recirculation valve, which only exists on layouts with three charging paths or stages; on lift-off it routes boosted air back to the compressor inlet so the compressor does not surge. It is not the wastegate. P2CD5 says the valve no longer moves when commanded and stays in one position. No manufacturer documents P2CD5 publicly. GM shows the two usual methods on its A and B valves: the 2019 Corvette LT5 flags P23AA when the position error exceeds 25 % for 1 s while the valve speed stays within ±10 %/s (Type A), and the 2019 CT6 twin-turbo infers a stuck dump valve on bank 2 from airflow and pressure behaviour (P00C4). A circuit fault on valve C is P25F8, a general mechanical fault P25FC. Stuck shut means surge noise on lift-off, stuck open means missing boost.
c: Valve or piston seized by oil and soot deposits from the crankcase breather
Electric actuator or diaphragm of the valve worn or failed
Missing vacuum or control signal on a pneumatically operated valve
Position feedback reports movement wrongly although the valve works
s: Fluttering or surging noise from the intake when lifting off the throttle
Boost builds slowly or stays low when the valve is stuck open
Warning lamp on and engine power limited

P2CD6.d: A fourth boost pressure sensor, D, is only needed where charge pressure is read at four points, for example on twin-turbo engines with two stages per bank or on combinations of supercharger, turbocharger and electric compressor. Which tap gets the letter is up to the manufacturer. P2CD6 is the umbrella fault for this sensor's circuit when the module does not or cannot separate low, high and implausible readings; those have their own codes P2CD7 to P2CD9. No manufacturer documents P2CD6 publicly, and no lost-communication code for a digital sensor D is defined. CARB requires every such input to be checked for circuit faults. By analogy with sensor A, Ford's 2024 petrol engines check the signal continuously and need 5 s to register a fault. Boost control on the affected path is usually cut back.
c: Corroded or loose connector, chafed wire at sensor D
5 V reference or sensor ground interrupted
Input stage of the engine control module faulty
s: Warning lamp on
Reduced boost and noticeably less power
Other sensor codes at the same time if a shared 5 V supply is affected

P2CD7.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P2CD7.d: With P2CD7 the boost sensor D signal is electrically valid but does not fit the other pressure readings or the engine's air model. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the checks used for sensor A show what it would cover. Ford's 2024 petrol summary compares barometric, manifold and boost pressure at key-up after at least 10 s off, allowing roughly 2.1 to 2.7 inHg between pairs, and repeats a two-way comparison at low throttle below 1,500 rpm. The GM-designed Saab 2.0 turbo expects 50 to 115 kPa with the engine stopped and treats deviations as a two-trip Type B fault. Typical reasons are a blocked or leaking pressure tap, oil in the sensor port and drift. Unlike P2CD6, P2CD8 and P2CD9, wiring is rarely to blame here. Expect a lamp and reduced boost.
c: Sensor D drifted or contaminated with oil
Leaking seal or blocked port at the sensor's measuring point
Charge air leak in the section monitored by sensor D
Sensor with the wrong pressure range fitted
s: Warning lamp on
Boost limited, weaker acceleration
Scan tool shows sensor D value differing from barometric pressure with the engine off

P2CD8.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor D Circuit Low
P2CD8.d: P2CD8 is stored when the voltage from boost sensor D falls below the lowest value a healthy sensor can output. Since these sensors rise in voltage as pressure rises, a reading near zero almost always points to the electrics: signal shorted to ground, an interrupted 5 V supply, or a broken signal wire that the module pulls low. No manufacturer publishes limits for sensor D. For sensor A, Ford's 2024 petrol engines use under 0.19 V held for 5 s, and the GM-developed Saab 2.0 turbo under 0.09 V for more than 5 s as a Type B fault. If other 5 V sensors report low at the same moment, the shared reference circuit is the first suspect. The module then stops regulating boost on that path. Too high is P2CD9.
c: Signal wire of sensor D shorted to ground
5 V reference to the sensor open or shorted
Sensor D internally failed with output stuck low
s: Warning lamp on
Only base boost available, clear loss of power
Live data shows sensor D at or near minimum pressure even under load

P2CD9.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor D Circuit High
P2CD9.d: P2CD9 reports a boost sensor D voltage above the highest valid level. A signal pinned near the reference rarely reflects real overboost; more often the signal wire touches 5 V or battery voltage, the sensor ground is open, or a broken signal line floats up through a pull-up inside the module. No carmaker publishes a sensor D limit. Sensor A figures give an idea of the spread: Ford's 2024 petrol summary sets the high code above 4.88 V for 5 s, Saab's GM-based 1.6 turbo above 4.8 V and the 2.0 turbo already above 3.9 V for 5 s. Because the module would otherwise read excessive pressure, it typically disables boost control on that path and falls back to wastegate base pressure. P2CD8 is the low-voltage counterpart.
c: Sensor ground open or high resistance at the connector
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Sensor D internally failed with output stuck high
s: Warning lamp on
Engine runs on base boost only with reduced power
Live data shows sensor D at maximum even at idle

P2CDA.t: Alternative Fuel Tank A Vacuum Insulation Deteriorated
P2CDA.d: P2CDA concerns cryogenic fuel storage, in practice liquefied natural gas (LNG) and possibly liquid hydrogen, kept in a double-walled tank whose gap is evacuated. Once that vacuum softens, heat leaks in, the liquid boils faster and pressure climbs until the relief valve vents gas. Chart, a maker of LNG truck tanks, separates true vacuum loss from other causes by an eight-hour pressure rise test combined with an outer shell that feels cold or shows condensation. A Caterpillar patent lets the ECM compare pressure at key-off and key-on against a predicted rise and rate hold time, with under one day flagged as poor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The tank pressure sensor codes start at P019E. Expect shorter standing times before venting and lost fuel.
c: Vacuum between inner and outer tank wall lost through a leaking weld, fitting or seal
Gradual vacuum decay from outgassing over years of service, tank due for pump-down
Dent or impact damage to the outer shell breaching the insulation space
Pressure rise from another cause (economizer, pressure regulator, sensor) misread as insulation loss
s: Tank pressure rises quickly while the vehicle stands, relief valve vents gas
Frost or condensation on the outer tank shell
Fuel loss and shorter standing time after refuelling

P2CDB.t: Cold Start Cylinder 1 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P2CDB.d: P2CDB is part of the monitoring of cold start emission strategies: some engines shut off cylinders or hold intake valves closed right after a cold start to heat the catalyst faster, and CARB requires the commanded elements of such a strategy to be checked while it is active. CARB also asks for faults found during the cold start strategy to carry codes distinct from the ordinary ones, which is why this code exists beside P3402. No manufacturer documents P2CDB publicly. Ford monitors P3402 continuously during deactivation, entry and exit from 400 rpm, once oil pressure has had about two seconds to build. A Ford patent chooses the valve state at start by engine temperature and detects latch pin motion from a dip in solenoid current. Expect higher cold start emissions and a cylinder 1 misfire.
c: Latch pin of the switchable rocker or lifter on cylinder 1 sticking, often from contaminated oil
Wrong oil grade or low oil level slowing the switching while the oil is still cold
Cylinder 1 control solenoid responding sluggishly at low temperature
Engine control software misjudging the cold start test, cured by an update
s: Check engine lamp after a cold start
Rough running in the first minutes after starting a cold engine
Misfire code for cylinder 1 stored alongside

P2CDC.t: Cold Start Cylinder 2 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P2CDC.d: With P2CDC the control unit reports that cylinder 2 did not take the valve state that the cold start routine asked for. Timing matters here: in a Ford patent on electrically latched rockers, intake deactivation is wanted at engine start, yet the cam of cylinder 2 sits on its lobe, so its latch pin cannot move at first. That is normal; the solenoid is pulsed again after roughly 200 to 280 crank degrees and only then must a current dip prove the pin moved. A missing dip with the cam on base circle points to a seized pin or a pumped-up lash adjuster. No maker documents P2CDC publicly; outside the cold start phase GM files the same failure on the L84 as P3499 and the generic code is P3410. The driver mainly notices a shaky warm-up.
c: Latch pin on cylinder 2 seized by dirt or varnish in the oil
Hydraulic lash adjuster pumped up so the rocker stays loaded on base circle
Weak cylinder 2 solenoid or high resistance in its connector
Worn cam lobe or collapsed lifter on cylinder 2
s: Uneven idle while the engine warms up
Warning lamp, sometimes with a cylinder 2 misfire code
Engine control may suspend the cold start strategy

P2CDD.t: Cold Start Cylinder 3 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P2CDD.d: P2CDD flags cylinder 3 when its deactivation or intake valve control misbehaves during the cold start phase. No maker documents this code publicly, so the closest evidence comes from neighbouring checks. GM's L84 V8 judges cylinder 3 outside cold start under P349A: if filtered manifold pressure stays above a threshold while the cylinder should be sealed, and that happens in 22 of 25 chances, a Type B fault (lamp after two trips) is set. A Delphi patent explains the cold start purpose: fuel and spark are cut on chosen cylinders, their valves are closed, and the remaining cylinders burn more fuel so the exhaust reaches the converter hotter. If cylinder 3 keeps breathing, that heating benefit fades and cold start emissions rise; P3418 covers its ordinary performance check.
c: Cylinder 3 valves keep opening because the switching element does not unlock
Insufficient oil pressure or flow to the switching gallery right after a cold start
Cylinder 3 control solenoid sticking or leaking internally
Manifold pressure signal biased, so a sealed cylinder looks like it still breathes
s: Malfunction lamp, typically after repeated cold starts
Vibration or rough idle shortly after a cold start
Engine takes longer to settle into normal running

P2CDE.t: Cold Start Cylinder 4 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P2CDE.d: On a four-cylinder engine cylinder 4 is the last one in the count; P2CDE reports that cylinder 4 did not follow the cold start valve command. Engines may do two different things during a cold start. A Delphi patent closes the intake and exhaust valves of selected cylinders after start-up and reopens them once the converter is hot enough to work, around 350 °C. A Ford patent on latched rockers instead sets the valve state at key-on according to whether it is a cold or a warm start, for example deactivating intake valves to cut the air spring while cranking. Either way the controller must see the commanded state reached. No manufacturer documents P2CDE publicly; its normal-operation counterpart is P3426. Drivers notice a harsh start or a shaky first minute.
c: Switchable rocker or lifter on cylinder 4 not changing state
Cylinder 4 solenoid drawing too little current due to corroded terminals
Aged or overdue engine oil impairing the hydraulic switching when cold
Implausible coolant or oil temperature signal triggering the cold start strategy wrongly
s: Harsher cranking or start-up shake
Rough first minute after a cold start
Check engine lamp

P2CDF.t: Cold Start Cylinder 5 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P2CDF.d: P2CDF only occurs on engines with at least five cylinders, mostly V6 and V8 units, and says cylinder 5 did not respond correctly to the cold start deactivation or intake valve command. The Delphi patent behind this idea chooses cylinders that sit farthest from the converter along the exhaust, so less heat is lost in the manifold; in its V8 tests the exhaust ran at least 75 °C hotter at equal load. Which cylinders qualify depends on the manifold layout of the engine. No maker documents P2CDF publicly. GM's L84 uses P349C to flag a cylinder 5 that keeps breathing in normal operation, and the generic counterpart is P3434. If this code sets, the catalyst warms more slowly and cylinder 5 may misfire.
c: Deactivation lifter or rocker on cylinder 5 failing to lock or unlock
Restricted oil gallery or screen feeding the switching elements of that bank
Faulty cylinder 5 control valve in the valve lifter oil manifold
Calibration issue in the engine control module
s: Lamp on after cold starts, sometimes with a cylinder 5 misfire code
Ticking or tapping valve noise when cold
Rough idle until the engine is warm

P2CE0.t: Cold Start Cylinder 6 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P2CE0.d: P2CE0 closes this series of cold start codes; numbering ends at cylinder 6 although many deactivation engines have eight cylinders. It indicates that cylinder 6 did not reach the valve state demanded during the cold start routine. No manufacturer documents P2CE0 publicly. Related evidence shows how such faults look in the field: a 2025 Ram bulletin (18-002-25) for the 2023 Ram 1500 with the 5.7 L Hemi MDS eTorque lists cylinder 6 deactivation and reactivation codes (P3441, P1416) with rough idle and misfire during warm-up, and fixes them with new PCM software. GM's L84 marks a cylinder 6 that keeps breathing as P349D, Type B. Look at software and oil supply before replacing lifters; the generic check outside cold start is P3442.
c: Deactivating lifter or rocker on cylinder 6 not switching
Engine control software that misjudges or mis-times the cold start switching, fixed by reprogramming
Low or delayed oil pressure after a cold start
Cylinder 6 control solenoid or its wiring degraded
s: Rough idle or misfire while warming up
Check engine lamp, often with a cylinder 6 misfire code
Cylinder deactivation may stay disabled afterwards

P2CE1.d: P2CE1 reports an interrupted circuit at intake air heater C, part of the grid-type pre-heat system a diesel uses to warm the incoming air for cold starts. Volvo and Mack use exactly this code on heavy trucks: their 2019 solution K53338075 for 11, 13 and 16 litre engines, including Mack MP7, MP8 and MP10, from US10+OBD13 onwards lists P2CE1-13, the suffix marking an open circuit, among the pre-heat relay codes. It warns that an ohmmeter check of the supply power cable may miss a damaged cable and asks to renew relay and cable together; a 2019 EMS software release also improved relay robustness for these codes. Heavy-duty OBD rules call for circuit continuity checks on intake air heaters. P0543 and P2605 are the open-circuit codes for heaters A and B.
c: Damaged supply power cable between relay and heater, not always visible on an ohmmeter
Pre-heat relay contacts or output burnt open
Poor terminal tension at the heating element or relay plug
Heating element C itself burnt through
s: Hard starting and long cranking in cold weather
White smoke after a cold start
Engine warning lamp

P2CE2.t: Intake Air Heater C Circuit Range/Performance
P2CE2.d: P2CE2 is the plausibility test for intake air heater C: the circuit is neither open nor shorted, but current draw, voltage drop or heating effect do not fit the command. Under the heavy-duty OBD rules a glow plug or intake air heater must react properly to commands and its circuit must show plausible current and voltage drop. No manufacturer documents P2CE2 publicly. Volvo and Mack, the only makers seen using heater C codes, list for their pre-heat relay issue the Range/Performance codes of heaters A and B (P2604-7F, P2606-7F) together with the open, low and high codes of heater C, but no C plausibility code. Their repair path still fits: terminal tension, EMS software level, then relay and supply cable. Expect sluggish cold starts and white smoke.
c: Extra resistance from corroded terminals or a worn supply cable lowering heater current
Pre-heat relay switching with excessive voltage drop
Heating element C aged, drawing current outside the expected window
Weak batteries or poor main ground distorting the current and voltage reading
s: Longer cranking on cold mornings
White smoke and rough running until warm
Warning lamp without an open or short code for heater C

P2CE3.t: Intake Air Heater C Circuit Low
P2CE3.d: P2CE3 means the signal in the circuit of intake air heater C reads too low, as with the control or feedback line shorted to ground or a relay output pulled down. Volvo uses it with the suffix -11, which in the failure type scheme denotes a ground short. The August 2020 EMS change log for Volvo trucks with US17 and OBD2019 engines lists P2CE3-11 among the codes reduced by a pre-heat relay robustness update released in February 2019, and Volvo's 2020 supplementary instruction KC-15 for the pre-heat relay includes it as well. That instruction applies only from US10+OBD13 trucks onward and has relay and supply power cable replaced as a pair. P2CE4 is the high-side code, P2CE1 the open circuit; for heater A the low code is P0541.
c: Control or feedback wire of heater C chafed through to ground
Pre-heat relay with an internal fault pulling its output low
Outdated engine management software, addressed by a Volvo update
Moisture or corrosion in the relay connector creating a path to ground
s: Pre-heat not working, hard cold starts
White smoke after starting in cold weather
Fault lamp on the dash

P2CE4.t: Intake Air Heater C Circuit High
P2CE4.d: P2CE4 is stored when heater C's circuit shows an excessive signal, typically a short to battery voltage on the control line or a relay that remains switched on. Volvo and Mack document it as P2CE4-12, the suffix standing for a short to battery. It appears in their pre-heat relay instructions for Volvo VN/VNL/VNR/VNX/VHD and Mack Anthem, Granite, Pinnacle and other models from 2014, where technicians first check terminal tension at element and relay and the EMS software, then fit a new relay, supply cable and an updated two-point bracket (2022 version). A heater stuck on can flatten the batteries and overheat the cable, so this fault deserves quick attention. P2CE3 is the low-side code, P2CE1 the open circuit; heater A and B use P0542 and P2608.
c: Pre-heat relay contacts welded or stuck closed
Control line of heater C shorted to a battery-voltage wire
Faulty supply power cable or loose bracket mounting affecting the circuit
Engine control module output stage for the relay faulty
s: Batteries drained after the truck has been parked
Hot or discoloured cable near the heater
Warning lamp and possibly hard starting if the heater no longer switches

P2CE5.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor C Circuit
P2CE5.d: Two manufacturers use P2CE5, with different meanings. In GM's 2025 diesel tables 25OBDG04A and 25OBDG04B, sensor C is the downstream relative pressure sensor that reads gauge pressure behind the particulate filter. Despite the circuit title, GM uses the code as an offset test without exhaust flow: with the engine stopped the reading should be zero, and an offset learned more than 2.20 % away from its nominal value sets a Type B fault without debounce. Ford's 2024–25 petrol summary, which covers particulate filters on both banks, uses P2CE5 for the general circuit fault of a digital SENT sensor C, registered within 5 s; lost communication with it is U0696. A drifted sensor, condensate in the hose or a damaged connector are typical. Regeneration and back pressure monitoring lose a measured input.
c: Sensor C zero point drifted (offset at standstill too large)
Condensate or soot in the sensing hose holding pressure
Damaged connector or wiring of a digital sensor C
s: Warning lamp on, usually after two trips on GM diesels
Particulate filter regeneration may run less accurately or more often
Usually no noticeable change in driving

P2CE6.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P2CE6.d: P2CE6 marks a sensor C reading that is electrically valid but physically wrong. GM's 2025 diesel tables use it for a frozen downstream relative pressure signal: during transients, with engine speed changing faster than 150 rpm/s and fuel and airflow also changing quickly, the signal must move; too little variation (25OBDG04B: 0.14 % or less in 40 of 50 samples) sets a two-trip Type B code. Ford's 2024–25 petrol filter strategy runs three checks under P2CE6: an offset test after shutdown that fails at an average of 16 to 32 hPa, a rationality test that fails when the reading stays at or above the flow-based expectation for 20 s in total, and a derivative test over 2 s when exhaust flow changes by more than 225 m³/h. Hoses, condensate and drift are more likely than wiring.
c: Sensing hose to sensor C kinked, blocked or disconnected
Condensate or frozen water in the sensing line
Exhaust leak near the measuring point
s: Warning lamp on
Particulate filter regenerations triggered too early or too late
Filter monitoring (missing substrate test) cannot complete

P2CE7.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor C Circuit Low
P2CE7.d: P2CE7 means the raw signal of filter pressure sensor C has dropped below its electrical floor, the typical picture of a signal wire shorted to ground or a lost 5 V supply. GM's 2025 diesel tables, where C is the relative pressure sensor behind the particulate filter, set it when the raw value is under 0.02 % in 158 of 200 samples taken every 12.5 ms with the ignition in range and the engine not cranking; it is Type B, so the lamp follows on the second trip. Ford's 2024–25 petrol summary uses the same code for an analog sensor C on its gasoline particulate filters, with a limit of 0.3 V held for 5 s. Checking reference, ground and signal at the plug comes before replacing the sensor. The high counterpart is P2CE8; sensor D has P2CEC.
c: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground, often from heat damage near the exhaust
5 V supply to the sensor interrupted
Sensor C internally failed with output stuck low
s: Warning lamp on
Live data shows sensor C at minimum regardless of engine load
Regeneration planning relies on a soot model only

P2CE8.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor C Circuit High
P2CE8.d: P2CE8 is the high-side electrical fault of filter pressure sensor C: its output sits above the range a working sensor can produce. GM's 2025 diesel tables aim this test at a broken line or a battery-voltage short and set the code when the raw signal of the downstream relative pressure sensor exceeds 99.80 % in 158 of 200 samples (12.5 ms task), Type B with two trips. On Ford's 2024–25 gasoline particulate filters with analog sensors the limit is 4.73 V for 5 s. An open sensor ground or a signal wire touching the 5 V reference are the usual electrical causes; heat-damaged harness sections near the exhaust deserve a close look. Because a pinned-high value would look like an extremely full filter, the controller ignores it. Low voltage is P2CE7, the D sensor equivalent P2CED.
c: Sensor ground or signal wire open
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Sensor C internally failed with output stuck high
s: Warning lamp on
Live data shows sensor C at maximum even at idle
Regeneration requests may become more frequent

P2CE9.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2CE9.d: P2CE9 catches a sensor C signal that jumps rather than drifts. GM's 2025 diesel tables call this a quick change check: when two consecutive raw samples of the downstream relative pressure sensor differ by more than 20 %, the sample counts as failed, and 99 failures in 200 samples set a Type B code. The test is suspended while cranking and whenever an electrical low or high fault is already present, so it really targets short dropouts. Ford's 2024–25 petrol summary lists P2CE9 within its continuous analog circuit check for gasoline particulate filters, with about 5 s to register and no separate threshold published. Loose terminals that open under engine vibration, a harness rubbing on a bracket or moisture entering the connector are the usual finds; wiggling the harness during live data helps. Sensor D uses P2CEE.
c: Loose or corroded terminal in the sensor C connector
Harness rubbing through on a bracket or exhaust part
Intermittent internal fault of the sensor
s: Warning lamp on, sometimes after rough roads or rain
Pressure value jumps in live data
Fault may disappear and return

P2CEA.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor D Circuit
P2CEA.d: Sensor D is the fourth slot for particulate filter pressure and only appears in Ford's 2024–25 petrol OBD summary, which watches a filter on each bank (missing substrate codes P226D and P226E); Ford does not say publicly which letter belongs to which filter or tap. For a digital SENT sensor D, P2CEA covers any circuit failure, monitored without pause with 5 s to register, while lost communication with the same sensor is U0697. GM's 2025 diesel tables stop at sensor C, where P2CE5 is an offset test instead. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored for circuit faults. A damaged connector, a harness melted by exhaust heat or a failed sensor are the likely finds. Without the value, back pressure for that filter is only estimated and the substrate check may not run.
c: Damaged or corroded connector at sensor D
Harness to sensor D damaged by exhaust heat
s: Warning lamp on
Particulate filter monitoring for one bank incomplete
Usually no change in driveability

P2CEB.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P2CEB.d: P2CEB says sensor D reports a pressure that is electrically fine but does not match what the exhaust flow should produce. Ford is the only maker found using it, in its 2024–25 petrol summary for engines with a gasoline particulate filter per bank. The functional check starts only after the electrical tests have passed and uses three tests: after shutdown, once inlet gas has been at 250 °C or more for 600 s, an average reading of 16 to 32 hPa fails the offset test; while running, the rationality test fails once readings at or over the pressure predicted from flow add up to 20 s; and a pressure that does not follow a flow change of more than 225 m³/h within 2 s fails the derivative test. Hoses, condensate and sensor drift are the main suspects; P2CE6 is the C counterpart.
c: Sensing hose to sensor D cracked, kinked or disconnected
Condensate in the sensing line after short trips
Sensor D drifted or responding slowly
s: Warning lamp on
Missing substrate test for that bank cannot be completed
Usually no noticeable change while driving

P2CEC.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor D Circuit Low
P2CEC.d: P2CEC is set when an analog filter pressure sensor D delivers less voltage than it can in normal service. In Ford's 2024–25 petrol summary, the only public source using sensor D, the limit is 0.3 V for 5 s, checked continuously alongside the A, B and C sensors of the gasoline particulate filters. Practically this means a signal shorted to ground, a 5 V supply that has dropped out, or an open signal line that the module pulls down. A shared reference fault would bring other sensor codes up together. GM does not use sensor D; its C sensor counterpart P2CE7 shows a similar ground-short logic on 2025 diesels. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. The pressure drop across that bank's filter is then unknown. Too high is P2CED, intermittent P2CEE.
c: Signal wire of sensor D shorted to ground
5 V reference to sensor D open or pulled down
Sensor D failed with output stuck low
s: Warning lamp on
Live data shows sensor D at minimum
Further 5 V sensor codes if the shared supply is affected

P2CED.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor D Circuit High
P2CED.d: With P2CED the analog output of filter pressure sensor D lies above its usable top end. Ford's gasoline OBD document for 2024–25, with filters on both banks and up to four pressure sensors, sets the code above 4.73 V lasting 5 s. That usually traces back to an open sensor ground, a signal line touching the 5 V reference or battery voltage, or an open signal wire on an input with a pull-up. A real pressure that high would mean an almost fully blocked filter, which the separate functional test P2CEB and the restriction monitor would show differently. No other maker documents sensor D; GM's diesel tables only cover C (P2CE8). Disconnecting the sensor and watching the reading jump helps locate the fault side. The low-voltage code is P2CEC.
c: Sensor ground open or high resistance
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Sensor D failed with output stuck high
s: Warning lamp on
Live data shows sensor D at maximum with the engine at idle
Filter monitoring for that bank incomplete

P2CEE.t: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2CEE.d: P2CEE stands for brief dropouts or jumps in the sensor D signal that do not last long enough for the low or high codes. Ford's 2024–25 petrol summary includes it in the continuous analog check of its gasoline particulate filter sensors, about 5 s to register, with no separate threshold given. Ford also lists P2CEE in bulletin 20-2257: 2019–2020 F-150 trucks with the 2.7L EcoBoost built up to 4 July 2020 could light the MIL with this and ten other codes because of PCM software, and the fix was a PCM reprogram (0.3 h labour). So before chasing wiring on such a truck, check the software level. Otherwise the usual reasons are a terminal losing contact under vibration, a chafing harness or moisture in the plug. Sensor C has the matching code P2CE9.
c: Loose or corroded terminal in the sensor D connector
PCM software setting the code falsely (Ford bulletin 20-2257, F-150 2.7L)
Harness to sensor D chafed or intermittently shorted
Intermittent internal fault of sensor D
s: Warning lamp on, sometimes only now and then
Pressure value of sensor D jumps in live data
Possibly stored together with other, unrelated codes after a software issue

P2CEF.d: P2CEF concerns a second thermostat that regulates its own part of the cooling system; stuck open means coolant passes through it before the intended temperature, so that circuit warms too slowly or stays too cool. Lotus documents the code in bulletin 131-26007 for the four-cylinder Emira, where thermostat A is the medium-temperature thermostat: the MIL may light and the driver may see a warning about low coolant temperature; the coolant is filtered for particles and the cold thermostat checked for a recessed piston and free travel in hot water. Mercedes-AMG lists P2CEF00 on M139 engines (CLA 45/GLA 45 facelift) with its own wording, an electrical fault of the thermostat, and blames debris, fixed by a revised thermostat. CARB requires monitoring of multi-thermostat systems.
c: Debris in the coolant holding the thermostat valve off its seat
Worn or leaking wax element, piston no longer returns
Earlier thermostat version superseded by the maker (Mercedes M139)
s: Engine warning lamp
Low coolant temperature warning or slow warm-up
Weaker cabin heating in cold weather

P2CF0.d: P2CF0 is the closed-side counterpart of P2CEF: auxiliary thermostat A fails to open, so the circuit it governs gets too little flow and its temperature climbs past the regulating point while other parts of the engine may look normal. No manufacturer documents P2CF0 publicly. The same component is described by Lotus for the four-cylinder Emira, where A is the medium-temperature thermostat and the workshop test checks that the cold piston is retracted and extends in hot water; a unit that never extends would match this code. Wax thermostats usually stick shut when the wax charge leaks or dirt jams the piston. CARB has required monitoring plans since 2019–2021 for systems with several thermostats and temperature sensors. Overheating in that loop is the risk, so it needs prompt attention.
c: Wax element lost its charge, thermostat no longer opens
Piston jammed by deposits or debris
Air pocket around the element after a coolant service, so it never sees hot coolant
s: Engine warning lamp
High temperature in one cooling circuit or an overheating warning
Possible power reduction to protect the engine

P2CF1.d: P2CF1 covers a further auxiliary thermostat, labelled B, that stays open, so its loop loses its warm-up phase and runs below the intended temperature. Which loop B controls is the maker's choice: engines with split cooling may regulate head, block, oil or heater flow with separate thermostats, each needing its own temperature sensor for diagnosis. No manufacturer documents P2CF1 publicly, and the only published auxiliary thermostat case, Lotus bulletin 131-26007, concerns thermostat A (P2CEF). CARB demands that the OBD system detect a thermostat that keeps coolant from reaching its regulating temperature and, for gasoline vehicles from 2019–2021, one that lets it drop again; for multiple thermostats it asks for an approved plan. Fuel use and heater output suffer.
c: Valve held open by debris or a weak return spring
Worn wax element that no longer retracts fully
Temperature sensor of that loop reading too low and faking the fault
s: Engine warning lamp
Slow warm-up and higher fuel use in cold weather
Weaker cabin heating

P2CF2.d: P2CF2 is logged when auxiliary thermostat B does not open: the temperature in its loop keeps rising beyond the opening point while the controller expects it to level off. The loop assigned to B differs by maker, so the actual consequence can be an overheating cylinder head, hot engine oil or, if B guards a smaller branch, merely a local hot spot that the main gauge does not show. No manufacturer documents P2CF2 publicly; for thermostat A on the four-cylinder Lotus Emira the published check is whether the piston extends in hot water, and the same test applies here. Wax thermostats fail closed mainly through a leaking wax charge or a jammed piston. CARB covers systems with several thermostats under its cooling monitor. Treat it as an overheating risk.
c: Leaking wax charge, thermostat stays shut
Piston seized by corrosion or deposits
Temperature sensor of that loop reading too high
s: Engine warning lamp
Overheating warning or high oil temperature
Reduced power to protect the engine

P2CF3.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Underspeed
P2CF3.d: P2CF3 is set when battery coolant pump A turns more slowly than the controller commands, although it is powered and not fully blocked. Typical reasons are a sluggish bearing, deposits on the impeller, low supply voltage or a pump motor that has lost strength; a faulty speed signal can produce the same picture. Ford uses P2CF3 on 2020 hybrids: bulletin 20-2221 (Escape HEV produced until 10 June 2020, code stored in the BECM) and 20-2293/20-2345 (Explorer, Aviator and Police Interceptor Utility hybrid) clear it, along with other pump codes, by reprogramming once the coolant level has been confirmed as correct. In Ford's 2024 OBD summary underspeed is a separate pump failure category (B2). Overspeed or dry running is P2B29, a seized pump P0CFF. The battery may run warmer and power may be limited.
c: Worn bearing or deposits slowing the pump
Battery controller software misreading pump speed (Ford 2020 hybrids)
Voltage drop on the pump feed or ground under load
Implausible speed feedback from the pump electronics
s: MIL or hybrid system warning
Battery temperature higher than usual
Reduced drive or charging power

P2CF4.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump B Supply Voltage Circuit
P2CF4.d: P2CF4 is about the power feed of the second battery coolant pump, B: the pump or its control unit sees a supply voltage outside the permitted window, or none at all. Unlike the control-circuit codes P0E1A to P0E1C, which watch the command line, this code looks at the line that actually powers the motor, typically a fused 12 V feed plus ground. Ford's 2024 OBD summary handles the matching failure type (1C, supply voltage out of range) for its auxiliary coolant pumps, requiring a battery voltage of 11 V or more before a five-second check. No manufacturer publicly documents P2CF4 itself; the pump A counterpart P0C4B appears in Ford's 2020 hybrid bulletin 20-2345. Without pump B, battery cooling capacity falls, and charging or drive power may be reduced.
c: Blown fuse or faulty relay in the pump B feed
Corroded connector or poor ground on the pump B supply
Weak 12 V battery or DC/DC output dragging the supply down
Internal fault in the pump electronics misreading the supply
s: MIL or hybrid warning on
Pump B silent when commanded
Charging or drive power limited when the battery warms up

P2CF5.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump B Stuck/Stalled
P2CF5.d: P2CF5 means battery coolant pump B does not turn at all although it is commanded and powered: the rotor is blocked, or the pump electronics has given up after failed start attempts. A seized bearing, debris or deposits after coolant work, a failed motor winding or frozen coolant in a weak mixture are the usual suspects. Ford's 2024 summary lists the corresponding pump fault type as actuator stuck (71). No manufacturer publicly documents P2CF5; pump A's equivalent, P0CFF, appears in Ford's 2020 hybrid bulletins 20-2293/20-2345, where reprogramming the battery controller resolved it. If pump B merely runs too slowly, P2CF7 applies; overspeed or air is P2CF6. A stalled pump stops flow through its part of the battery loop, so expect power limits, slower charging and a warning lamp.
c: Pump B rotor or bearing seized
Debris or deposits jamming the impeller after coolant work
Pump motor or its electronics failed
Coolant frozen due to insufficient antifreeze
s: Warning lamp for hybrid system or engine
Charging slower or interrupted
Power reduced as battery temperature rises

P2CF6.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump B Overspeed/Air in System
P2CF6.d: P2CF6 reports that battery coolant pump B spins above its commanded speed. Once a centrifugal pump loses its load it accelerates, so the most common explanation is air or a low level in the loop, which the title names directly. Ford shows the pattern on the 2022–2023 F-150 Lightning: under programme 23B09, battery coolant tube assemblies made of the wrong material could leak, and P2B29, the pump A version, could set without any other effect; the remedy was new tubes. Overspeed/dry run (B1) is likewise a separate pump fault category in Ford's 2024 summary. No manufacturer publicly documents P2CF6 for pump B. Bleeding the loop with the prescribed procedure and finding the leak come first; a loose impeller or false speed feedback is rarer. Underspeed is P2CF7, a blocked pump P2CF5.
c: Air left in the battery loop after service or poor bleeding
Leak at a battery coolant tube or joint lowering the level
Impeller slipping on the shaft or broken
False speed feedback from the pump electronics
s: Gurgling or whining from the pump area
Coolant level in the battery reservoir drops
MIL or hybrid warning, sometimes without other effect

P2CF7.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump B Underspeed
P2CF7.d: P2CF7 is the underspeed fault of battery coolant pump B: the pump turns, but clearly below the commanded speed for longer than the controller tolerates. Compared with the stall code P2CF5 the rotor is still moving, so friction, a partly obstructed impeller, coolant that is too viscous in the cold or a sagging supply are likelier than a dead motor. Ford's 2024 summary handles underspeed (B2) as a distinct pump fault type. No manufacturer publicly documents P2CF7; the same fault on pump A, P2CF3, was cleared by reprogramming the battery controller on 2020 Ford hybrids (bulletin 20-2221, Escape HEV). Check supply voltage and ground under load, the condition of the coolant and the pump itself. Battery temperatures may rise and the system may cut power.
c: Worn bearing or deposits slowing pump B
Supply voltage of pump B dropping under load
Wrong or aged coolant too viscous at low temperature
Battery controller software misjudging pump speed
s: MIL or hybrid system warning
Battery runs warmer than normal

P2CF8.t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P2CF8.d: P2CF8 is raised by the driver of coolant bypass valve D when it measures excessive current or overheats and protects itself. No manufacturer documents P2CF8 publicly, and the meaning of D varies: Ford's 2020–2025 gasoline summaries define valve D as the cabin heating valve and report only the smart driver's circuit fault P26BD, plus P26BF from 2024, while GM's 2019 and 2025 tables use the D stuck codes P26C0/P26C2 for the engine block rotary valve. The nearest documented logic is GM's P23C6 for valve C: motor overcurrent with a controller-specific limit of 8.1–12.8 A, 2 s within 5 s, Type B. A seized valve or a shorted motor or coil is the usual trigger. Depending on the loop, heater output or engine warm-up is affected.
c: Valve stiff or seized, so the motor or solenoid draws excess current
Shorted winding in the valve actuator
Valve wires partly shorted to ground or to each other
Overheated or faulty output stage in the control module
s: Engine warning lamp
Cabin heat weak or not adjustable (heater valve)
Engine warms up abnormally if the valve sits in the engine loop

P2CF9.t: Belt Integrated Starter Generator Belt Tensioner Control Circuit/Open
P2CF9.d: P2CF9 applies to belt starter-generator systems whose belt tensioner is moved by an actuator rather than by a spring alone. Patents describe the idea: Ford raises belt tension for engine starts and boost and lowers it while charging (US 9,297,445, with an actuator that falls back to high tension when unpowered); a Hyundai/Kia patent uses a solenoid with three tension stages (US 10,648,544); a later Ford patent switches an active tensioner between high and normal positions (US 12,577,903). P2CF9 means the controller sees an open or otherwise faulty drive circuit to that actuator. No carmaker has published the code; hydraulic tensioners such as on FCA eTorque have no control circuit. Possible effects: belt slip on restart, noise, disabled stop-start or assist, MIL.
c: Broken wire or loose connector in the tensioner drive circuit
Open coil or motor winding in the tensioner actuator
Output stage in the controlling module failed
s: Belt squeal or slip during automatic restarts
Stop-start or electric assist disabled
MIL or system warning on

P2CFA.t: Belt Integrated Starter Generator Belt Tensioner Control Circuit Low
P2CFA.d: P2CFA is logged when the control line of an electrically adjusted BISG belt tensioner reads too low, typically a ground short or a driver that holds the line down permanently. The tensioner's reaction varies with the design: Ford's patent US 9,297,445 describes an actuator that defaults to high belt tension when power is lost, which protects starts but costs efficiency, while a solenoid unit like the one in Hyundai/Kia's US 10,648,544 may rest in its spring position. No manufacturer publicly documents P2CFA. California's rules demand a circuit check on output components; in this case that means comparing the commanded state with the voltage or current returned by the driver. Chafed wiring near the hot accessory drive is a prime suspect. An open circuit is P2CF9, a high signal P2CFB.
c: Tensioner control wire chafed through to ground
Internal short in the tensioner actuator
Water or corrosion bridging pins at the actuator plug
s: Stop-start no longer active
Belt noise at start or under load
Warning lamp on

P2CFB.t: Belt Integrated Starter Generator Belt Tensioner Control Circuit High
P2CFB.d: P2CFB mirrors P2CFA on the high side: the tensioner control circuit of a belt integrated starter generator shows a voltage above the expected range, usually from a wire touching a battery-voltage feed or a driver stage that cannot switch off. The actuator may then be held in one position permanently. Ford's patent US 12,577,903 explains why that matters: an active tensioner is switched to high tension for the start phase, when the BISG transmits the greatest torque, and the control unit watches for belt slip during cranking. A tensioner stuck at the wrong tension risks slip at start or extra belt and bearing wear in normal driving. No manufacturer publicly documents P2CFB; patents and the CARB circuit-monitoring rules are the basis here. P2CF9 covers an open circuit, P2CFA a low signal.
c: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Output stage in the module unable to switch off
Actuator electronics reporting an implausibly high level
s: Belt slip or squeal at engine start
Faster belt wear or bearing noise
MIL on, stop-start or assist unavailable

P2CFC.d: P2CFC is the general fault of the output that powers the compressor clutch coil directly, unlike P0645, which covers a clutch relay. Ford is the documented user and runs it in a body module, not the PCM. Special service messages 50811 and 51380 list P2CFC, often with P0645 and P2CFD, in the HVAC module of 2020–2023 Explorer and Aviator; the cause was spread or pushed-out terminals at body control module C, so pins are checked before that module is replaced. SSM 53061 reports P2CFC in the same module on F-150 trucks of 2021–2024 and Super Duty models of 2023–2024 and says voltage left on the clutch field coil while uncommanded is no reason for a new module. Ford's OBD summaries omit the code. The compressor stays off and only warm air comes out.
c: Spread or pushed-out terminals at the body control module connector
Open or burnt clutch field coil
Damaged wire or connector between module and compressor
Faulty clutch output in the controlling module
s: A/C blows only warm air
Compressor clutch does not engage
Code stored in the HVAC or body control module, usually without engine lamp

P2CFD.d: P2CFD means the voltage on the clutch coil output reads lower than the module expects for the commanded state, most often because the line or the coil is grounded. With a high-side driver that short pulls the feed down, so the clutch cannot engage and the driver may protect itself; on a low-side design a grounded line would hold the clutch in instead. Ford is the documented user: on Explorer and Aviator built for 2020–2023, SSMs 50811 and 51380 group P2CFD with P2CFC and P0645 as climate-module codes caused by damaged terminals at body control module C. No public threshold exists; the closest published logic is GM Europe's relay check for P0646 on the 2011 Saab 9-5. The general fault is P2CFC, the opposite level P2CFE.
c: Clutch feed wire chafed through and touching ground
Damaged terminals at the body control module (Ford SSM 50811/51380)
Clutch coil shorted internally to its housing
s: No cooling, compressor clutch stays disengaged
Possibly blown fuse in the clutch feed

P2CFE.d: P2CFE reports a clutch coil output that sits higher than it should, typically because the line touches a battery feed. Then the clutch may stay energized after the module switches off, so the compressor keeps running and can ice the evaporator; a low-side driver instead shuts down and the clutch never engages. No manufacturer documents P2CFE publicly. Ford, which drives the clutch from a body module, publishes only P2CFC and P2CFD; its SSM 53061 notes that voltage remaining on the field coil circuit when not commanded is no reason to replace that module, which shows how such a high reading is assessed. The relay counterpart P0647 is described for the 2011 Saab 9-5 as a short to voltage. CARB requires monitoring of A/C components where they alter engine control.
c: Clutch control wire shorted to a battery-powered circuit
Output stage in the module stuck switched on
Moisture bridging pins in the compressor or module connector
s: Compressor runs even with A/C switched off
Iced evaporator, weak airflow after a while
Alternatively no cooling at all if the driver shuts down

P2CFF.t: A/C Clutch Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P2CFF.d: P2CFF does not come from a voltage comparison but from the protective logic of the clutch output itself. Modern smart switches limit their current and switch off once the junction gets too hot; the TI TPS1HB16-Q1, a typical automotive high-side switch, shuts down from 150 °C and retries within milliseconds, and the module logs this as overcurrent or overtemperature. On the clutch circuit that points to a coil with shorted turns, a partly grounded feed or a driver stressed by heat. No manufacturer documents P2CFF publicly; Ford, which powers the field coil from body control module C, only names P2CFC and P2CFD. Plain open, low and high faults are P2CFC to P2CFE. The clutch drops out repeatedly or stays disengaged, so cooling cuts in and out.
c: Clutch field coil with shorted turns drawing too much current
Feed wire partly shorted to ground
Output stage overheating from poor module cooling or an internal fault
s: Cooling cuts in and out
Compressor clutch disengages under load or after warm-up

P2D00.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Stuck/Stalled
P2D00.d: P2D00 reports that coolant pump A of the motor electronics loop, which cools the inverter and drive-motor electronics, does not rotate although commanded. It opens its own series P2D00–P2D0E (stuck, overspeed/air, underspeed, supply voltage and module overtemperature for pumps A to C) and should not be confused with the Hybrid/EV electronics pump codes P2C66–P2C68. Ford uses P2D00 on 2020 hybrids: bulletins 20-2221 (Escape HEV, stored in the BECM) and 20-2345 (Explorer, Aviator, Police Interceptor Utility, stored in the PCM) list it with P2D01–P2D04 and fix it by reprogramming after the coolant level has been checked. Without a software cause, a seized rotor or debris is behind it. Without flow the inverter heats up and the system derates power.
c: Battery or powertrain controller software misreading the pump (Ford 2020 hybrids)
Debris jamming the impeller after coolant work
Pump motor or integrated electronics failed
s: MIL on
Reduced drive power when the inverter gets hot
Hybrid system warning message

P2D01.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Overspeed/Air in System
P2D01.d: P2D01 is logged when the first electric pump of the motor electronics loop, which carries heat away from the inverter and drive-motor electronics, spins faster than commanded. A centrifugal pump that suddenly has nothing to push races, so the title points straight at air or a low coolant level. Ford lists P2D01 on 2020 hybrids: bulletin 20-2221 (Escape HEV built up to 10 June 2020, code in the BECM) and 20-2293/20-2345 (Explorer, Aviator and Police Interceptor Utility hybrid, code in the PCM). In both cases the degas bottle is checked first, and only with a correct level is the software update the fix, rated at 0.4 h. Ford's 2024 summary treats overspeed or dry running as its own pump fault type (B1). The seized pump is P2D00, slow running P2D02. Expect reduced power if the inverter heats up.
c: Low coolant level or trapped air in the motor electronics loop, for example after service work
Monitoring strategy in the control software (Ford 2020 hybrids, cured by reprogramming)
External leak at hoses, connectors or the pump housing that keeps drawing in air
Loose impeller or false speed feedback from the pump electronics
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Coolant level in the degas bottle at or below minimum
Gurgling or whining from the electric pump
Reduced drive power when the inverter runs hot

P2D02.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Underspeed
P2D02.d: With P2D02 the controller sees pump A of the motor electronics cooling loop turning, but clearly below its target speed for longer than allowed. The rotor is not locked, which separates it from P2D00; a stiff bearing, deposits on the impeller, cold and thick coolant or a supply that sags under load are therefore more likely than a dead motor. Ford names P2D02 in the 2020 Escape HEV bulletin 20-2221 (BECM) and in the PCM-based bulletins 20-2293/20-2345 for the hybrid Explorer, Aviator and Police Interceptor Utility: with the coolant level confirmed, new software resolved the lamp. Ford's 2024 summary keeps underspeed as a separate pump fault type (B2), checked over 5 s with at least 11 V. Excess speed is P2D01. Less flow lets the inverter warm up and may limit power.
c: Stiff bearing or deposits on the impeller of pump A
Control software strategy (Ford 2020 hybrids, fixed by reprogramming)
Voltage drop on the pump feed or ground under load
Wrong, contaminated or aged coolant raising viscosity at low temperature
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Higher inverter or motor electronics temperatures in live data
Power limitation under sustained load

P2D03.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Supply Voltage Circuit
P2D03.d: P2D03 concerns the power feed of motor electronics coolant pump A rather than its command line: the pump, or the module reading its status, finds the supply outside its allowed window or missing. That points to a blown fuse, a corroded connector, a weak ground or a 12 V system that drops too low. The command-side faults of the same pump are P0A05 to P0A07; Ford's 2019 hybrid summary checks those with 6 to 19 V on the 12 V net. Ford lists P2D03 in the 2020 hybrid bulletins 20-2221 (Escape HEV) and 20-2293/20-2345 (Explorer, Aviator, Police Interceptor Utility hybrid), where reprogramming after a coolant check cleared it. In the 2024 summary the matching pump fault type is 1C, supply voltage out of range. A pump without proper power stops cooling the inverter.
c: Corroded connector, loose terminal or poor ground at pump A
Blown fuse or faulty relay in the pump feed
Weak 12 V battery or DC/DC converter output too low
Software strategy on 2020 Ford hybrids, cured by reprogramming
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Pump A runs intermittently or not at all
Further low-voltage codes in other modules

P2D04.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Control Module Overtemperature
P2D04.d: P2D04 refers to the small electronics built into coolant pump A of the motor electronics loop: its own temperature has exceeded the limit, and the pump usually reports this before cutting back or switching off to protect itself. Heat builds up when the pump works hard against a restriction, runs dry, sits close to a hot component or has an internal electrical fault. Ford's 2019 hybrid summary still lumped such internal reports under P0C73 (confirmed pump fault for more than 1.25 s); Ford's 2020 hybrid campaigns for the Escape (20-2221) and for Explorer, Aviator and the police utility (20-2293, later 20-2345) name P2D04 separately and fix it with a software update once the coolant level is right. Ford's 2024 summary calls the type 98, system overtemperature. If the pump shuts down, the inverter may overheat and power drops.
c: Pump running dry or with too little coolant, so it loses its own cooling
Blocked or kinked line forcing the pump to work at high load
Internal fault in the pump control electronics
Software strategy on 2020 Ford hybrids, cured by reprogramming
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on, sometimes only after longer drives or in hot weather
Pump stops temporarily and restarts after cooling down
Inverter overtemperature warning or reduced power

P2D05.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Stuck/Stalled
P2D05.d: P2D05 opens the pump B block of the motor electronics series: the second electric pump in the loop that cools inverters and drive-motor electronics is commanded and supplied, yet its rotor does not move. Where a vehicle has two electric drive units, B may be the pump serving the second inverter. A seized bearing, debris after a coolant change, a burnt winding or coolant that froze in a weak mixture can lock it. No manufacturer publicly documents P2D05. Ford's 2024 summary shows the fault type as actuator stuck (71) for its auxiliary pumps, and on pump A the 2020 Ford hybrids store the equivalent P2D00. CARB requires the outputs of inverter thermal management to be monitored. Slow running is P2D07, overspeed P2D06. A stalled pump cuts flow, so derating and warnings follow.
c: Seized bearing or blocked rotor in pump B
Debris or deposits in the loop after repairs or coolant change
Failed motor winding or pump electronics unable to start the motor
Coolant frozen because the antifreeze ratio is too low
s: Malfunction or hybrid system warning lamp on
No pump noise or vibration when the pump should run
Rising temperature of the second inverter, power limited

P2D06.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Overspeed/Air in System
P2D06.d: P2D06 says pump B of the motor electronics loop turns above its commanded speed, the classic sign of a pump that has lost its coolant column to air or a falling level. Ford documents a real case: customer satisfaction programme 23B09 covered 72 F-150 Lightning trucks of model years 2022–2023, built between 28 and 30 September 2022, whose high-voltage battery coolant tubes were made of the wrong material. A shrinking tube spigot could leak, and P2D06 could set together with the battery pump code P2B29, without the driver noticing anything; the fix was replacing both tube assemblies. So the leak need not be near pump B itself. Ford's 2024 summary handles overspeed/dry run as type B1. Bleed the loop and look for the leak; stalled is P2D05, underspeed P2D07.
c: Coolant leak anywhere in the shared loop, such as faulty battery coolant tubes (Ford 23B09)
Air left in the loop after filling without the prescribed bleeding procedure
Impeller slipping on the shaft or implausible speed feedback
s: Often none apart from the stored code
Falling level in the degas bottle or traces of coolant
Inverter overtemperature warning and reduced acceleration if the loss continues

P2D07.t: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Underspeed
