Hose between module and canister split or off
s: Check engine light on
Evaporative leak test never completes, readiness stays open
Possible refuelling message or locked filler flap on some hybrids

P2DDB.t: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Stuck On
P2DDB.d: P2DDB reports a leak detection pump that keeps running, or keeps moving air, after the engine computer has turned it off. GM names P2DDB in its 2025 summary tables only as a blocking code for the ELCP leak test, while its own stuck-on check runs as P145D: with the pump commanded off, the switching valve is moved from vent to pump position halfway through the test, and a pressure shift above 1,000 Pa within 8 s, or more than 1,180 Pa of vacuum after 14 s in a later step, shows the pump is still pulling; Type B over two trips. Mitsubishi files a pump stuck on together with stuck off as P24C0. Because a running pump distorts every reference reading, the leak result becomes useless. Hard circuit faults point to P2401 or P2402 first; stuck off is P2DDA.
c: Internal fault of the leak check module (pump or its electronics)
Pump supply permanently live, e.g. stuck relay or shorted output stage
Control wire chafed against a powered line
s: Check engine light on
Humming from the tank area after the car is switched off
Leak test results unusable, EVAP readiness incomplete

P2DDC.t: Fuel Injection Quantity C Lower Than Expected
P2DDC.d: P2DDC is the shortfall code for a third injection path, C. Engines that need it split their injection into more parts than A and B, for example by injector group or by operating mode; the split is defined by the maker, and none documents P2DDC openly. How narrowly such a monitor is allowed to run shows in GM's 2025 diesel tables for path A: warm coolant above 70 °C, 1,100 to 1,800 rpm, 18 to 40 mm³ per stroke, steady fueling and at least 20 km/h, and only in normal and SCR warm-up combustion modes, not during filter regeneration. Its correction may add at most about 12 to 41 mm³; if path C lacks more than that, the code follows. Likely culprits are injectors of this group and weak supply pressure.
c: Injectors of group C coked or partly blocked
Low-pressure supply weak (lift pump, filter, air in fuel)
High resistance in injector wiring of group C
s: Check engine light on
Reduced power at part load
Hesitation when accelerating

P2DDD.t: Fuel Injection Quantity C Higher Than Expected
P2DDD.d: P2DDD flags excess fuel from injection path C: the quantity really burned, as estimated from airflow and lambda, sits above the request. Besides the classic leaking injector, a possible trigger after repairs is a replacement injector whose individual flow code was not programmed into the engine control, so the module calculates with the wrong flow curve. Another is an EGR valve that leaves too little fresh air, which the estimate can read as surplus fuel. GM lets its system-A adaptation take away only about 8 to 14 mm³, depending on speed and load. No manufacturer documents P2DDD publicly. P2DDC is the shortfall in path C, P2DE1 the cold-start excess; smoke and higher consumption are what drivers notice.
c: Injector of group C leaking or nozzle worn
Injector correction code not programmed after replacement
EGR valve not closing fully, too little fresh air
s: Check engine light on
Dark smoke under load
Higher fuel consumption

P2DDE.t: Fuel Injection Quantity D Lower Than Expected
P2DDE.d: P2DDE covers a fourth injection path, D, delivering too little fuel. The letter is assigned by the manufacturer; no one documents this code openly. CARB section 1968.2 (f)(4.2.2) sets two ways to catch it: either the shortfall is detected before emissions pass the malfunction threshold, or, where no injection fault can push emissions that high, once the control has used up its range and the commanded quantity cannot be reached. Since 2013 the monitor must also count how often it runs. Ford's diesels turn the global version of this finding into a lean code, P0171, below a fueling error of -0.15. Look first at the injectors of group D, then at fuel supply and the air and lambda signals. P2DDF is too much in D.
c: Injectors of group D blocked or worn
Fuel supply weak (pump, filter, rail pressure)
Air mass or lambda signal inaccurate
s: Check engine light on
Lack of power
Occasional stumbling or misfire-like running

P2DDF.t: Fuel Injection Quantity D Higher Than Expected
P2DDF.d: P2DDF says injection path D sends more fuel than the engine control asked for. The estimate behind it depends heavily on the air side: if the airflow meter reports too little air, or the NOx or oxygen sensor shows a richer lambda than real, the module sees a surplus that the injectors never delivered, so sensors deserve a check before injectors are replaced. GM also weights its limits with ambient pressure, so altitude alone should not trip the test. Ford's diesels judge the global error over 15 percent rich as P0172, with coolant between 70 and 120 °C. No manufacturer documents P2DDF itself. Excess fuel in D means soot, smoke and, on diesels, faster filter loading; P2DDE is the shortfall.
c: Airflow, NOx or oxygen sensor reading wrong
Injector of group D leaking or nozzle eroded
Boost or intake leak after the airflow meter
s: Check engine light on
Black smoke, particulate filter loading faster
Fuel consumption up

P2DE0.t: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity C Lower Than Expected
P2DE0.d: P2DE0 is the cold-start shortfall for path C. Its partner P2DE1 is used by Honda, which treats it as a rich fault of its cold-start mixture control: that check compares the ratio the PCM commands just after a cold start with what the wide-band sensor measures. By the logic of the pair, P2DE0 would be the lean side, but no public Honda or other maker document covers P2DE0 itself. For petrol engines, CARB section 1968.2 (e)(11.1.3) requires cold-start faults to be stored apart from the same faults found later. Fuel shortfall when cold can stem from low fuel pressure, an air leak behind the airflow meter or injectors that atomise poorly; stalling or stumbling soon after starting is typical. P2DDC is the warm counterpart.
c: Fuel pressure too low at start (pump, regulator, check valve)
Unmetered air entering behind the airflow meter
Injectors of group C dirty, poor spray when cold
Cold-start calibration in engine control software
s: Check engine light on after a cold start
Stalling or stumbling shortly after a cold start
Long cranking when cold

P2DE1.t: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity C Higher Than Expected
P2DE1.d: P2DE1 is the only code of this family with public manufacturer use. Honda names it Cold Start Air Fuel Ratio Control System Rich: during the cold-start emission strategy the PCM checks whether the mixture measured by the LAF (wide-band) sensor is richer than commanded. Bulletin 22-009 for the 2021 Accord Hybrid says the LAF sensor may misjudge the mixture as rich under certain fuel and shutdown conditions; bulletin 23-100 for the 2021-22 HR-V blames a PCM miscalculation. Both cure it with new PGM-FI software and light the MIL. Version 2 of 23-100 also has the oil level checked after a warm-up and the oil changed if above the upper mark. Real causes besides software are leaking injectors and faulty air or coolant temperature signals.
c: Injector leaking, extra fuel during cold start
Coolant temperature or airflow signal wrong
s: Check engine light on after a cold start
Usually no noticeable driving problem
Oil level above the upper mark possible

P2DE2.t: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity D Lower Than Expected
P2DE2.d: P2DE2 reports that path D fell short of its fuel request during the cold-start strategy. On petrol direct-injection engines this phase is short and precise: GM's 2025 tables run catalyst heating with a split injection only while the catalyst is under 550 °C, coolant between -12 and 66 °C and the engine has run less than 20 seconds, and they check missing pulses separately under P2B95. CARB section 1968.2 (e)(11.2.4) lists split or multiple injections among the features that must respond during the strategy. A pulse that opens but delivers too little, from deposits on the injector tip or a high-pressure pump slow to build pressure, would fit P2DE2. No manufacturer documents the code; P2DDE is the warm version.
c: Deposits on injector tips of group D
High-pressure pump slow to build pressure after start
s: Check engine light on after a cold start
Rough idle in the first seconds after a cold start
Often nothing noticeable once warm

P2DE3.t: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity D Higher Than Expected
P2DE3.d: P2DE3 is the excess counterpart of P2DE2: during the cold-start strategy path D injected more than commanded. Nobody publishes this exact code, and the big diesel makers show why it is rare: GM's 2025 diesels judge fuel quantity in the SCR warm-up mode with the ordinary A codes P026C/P026D, keeping only rail pressure (P2C1F, more than 16 MPa below target) and injection timing (P05EC) as separate cold-start codes; Ford's 6.7 litre diesel files cold-start fuel balance errors under the cylinder codes. CARB only demands a response check of commanded quantity during cold start from 2026 on. A dripping injector, a stuck pressure regulator or a coolant sensor reading too cold suggest themselves; expect white smoke and fuel smell. P2DDF is the warm case.
c: Pressure regulator sticking, rail pressure too high when cold
Coolant temperature sensor reading too cold
s: Check engine light on after a cold start
White smoke and fuel smell when cold
Rising oil level over time

P2DE4.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Stuck Engaged
P2DE4.d: Some hybrids and electric drive units can uncouple electric drive motor A from its axle through a clutch, so the motor stops turning when its torque is not needed. P2DE4 means the clutch stays closed although the control module has asked it to open; position feedback or speeds still show a coupled motor. No manufacturer documents P2DE4 publicly. Comparable hardware sits in the front drive unit of the 2024 Corvette E-Ray, which has a clutch pawl, a disconnect clutch actuator and a position switch; GM logs a faulty switch there as P08ED. A Schaeffler design for such a disconnect is spring-loaded towards the engaged state and needs current to release, so a dead actuator leaves it coupled. The motor is then dragged along, costing efficiency, and the system may restrict operation. The opposite fault is P2DE5.
c: Disconnect clutch actuator does not move to the open position (motor, solenoid or linkage)
Clutch position switch reports engaged although the clutch has opened
Shift sleeve, pawl or teeth jammed or loaded with torque in the engaged state
Control module software or calibration error in the disconnect strategy
s: Warning lamp or hybrid/drive system message
Higher energy consumption, electric range reduced
Drive unit noise at speed, possible speed or mode limitation

P2DE5.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Stuck Disengaged
P2DE5.d: P2DE5 is the reverse of P2DE4: the module commands the clutch of drive motor A to close, yet the motor stays uncoupled from the wheels. The motor may spin up without the axle following, or the position signal never reaches the engaged state. No manufacturer documents P2DE5 publicly. With a dog clutch the classic cause is tooth-on-tooth contact: a BorgWarner patent notes that a motor-driven actuator alone cannot tell whether the sleeve reached its end stop or is blocked by the splines, which is why a position sensor or current evaluation is added. GM's Corvette E-Ray front unit lists the disconnect clutch actuator and its switch as separately serviceable parts. The axle then lacks electric drive: no electric launch, no all-wheel traction from that motor and little or no recuperation through it.
c: Actuator motor or solenoid fails to push the clutch into engagement
Clutch teeth blocking on each other, speed synchronisation not reached
Position switch or sensor stuck at disengaged
Worn or broken internal parts of the clutch or fork
s: Warning lamp, hybrid or all-wheel-drive fault message
No electric drive or reduced traction from the affected axle
Combustion engine starts more often, reduced recuperation

P2DE6.t: Drive Motor A Clutch Actuator Performance
P2DE6.d: Whereas P2DE4 and P2DE5 describe the clutch end state, P2DE6 judges the actuator that moves the clutch of drive motor A: its circuit is intact, but it acts too slowly, draws implausible current or does not reach the commanded position within the expected time. No manufacturer documents P2DE6 publicly. The closest documented hardware is GM's Corvette E-Ray, whose front electric drive unit combines a 120 kW motor with a clutch pawl and a disconnect clutch actuator commanded by the module that also drives the motor. A BorgWarner patent shows how such an actuator can be judged: the motor current peaks as the sleeve reaches its end position, giving a usable stop signal. CARB lets each maker define the drive motor monitor in an approved plan. Electrical faults of the actuator enable line are P08E7 to P08E9.
c: Actuator motor or gearing worn, sluggish movement
Increased friction at fork, sleeve or pawl, e.g. from contaminated fluid
Low supply voltage or resistance in the actuator feed
Position switch or sensor reporting late or erratically
s: Warning lamp or drive system message
Delayed or jerky coupling of the electric axle
Electric drive of that axle temporarily disabled

P2DE7.t: Cold Start Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Range/Performance
P2DE7.d: California requires a fault found while the cold-start warm-up strategy runs to be stored apart from the same fault found later. P2DE7 is that cold-start counterpart of P26BB for coolant valve C. GM's 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG03B) set it when the valve's measured angle is more than 12° off its target after the target has settled, or when the valve moves slower than calibrated, during 4 of 5 seconds. Extra conditions are a low-flow coolant mode (also during auto-stop), active catalyst warm-up, closed-loop position control without soft opening, soft closing or anti-stick routine, and outlet coolant above −20 °C. Type B, MIL after two trips. A slow valve can let coolant circulate too early, so engine and catalyst heat up later. Position-sensor faults (P23C3 ff.) block the test.
c: Rotary valve sluggish from deposits or worn seals
Valve actuator motor or gearing weak
Position sensor reading drifting without a circuit fault
Engine control software needing an update
s: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Engine and cabin heater warm up more slowly
Usually no change in driveability

P2DE8.t: Cold Start Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Stuck Open
P2DE8.d: P2DE8 is GM's cold-start variant of P26C0 for valve D, the block rotary valve that sits between two mechanical end stops and meters coolant through the engine block. In the 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG03B) a failure counts when requested and measured position differ by more than 5° while the raw feedback is above 50°, i.e. on the open side; 4 of 5 seconds give a Type B fault, MIL on the second trip. Unlike P26C0 it only runs in low-flow coolant mode with catalyst warm-up active. Further conditions: at least 11 V, command between −5° and 115° and steady within 5° for 3 s, block coolant above −34 °C, and no calibration run in the last 37 s. An open block valve lets the block lose heat during warm-up, which delays catalyst light-off. The closed-side counterpart is P2E81.
c: Block rotary valve sticking in an open position (deposits, wear)
Valve actuator unable to drive the valve to the closed side
Chafed or corroded engine harness to the valve
End-stop learn values implausible after repair or power loss
s: Check engine light on after two trips
Slow warm-up, weak cabin heating in cold weather
Possibly higher fuel consumption on short trips

P2DE9.t: Cold Start Engine Coolant Pump Underspeed
P2DE9.d: Engines with an electric main water pump run it at a tightly metered speed after a cold start so the block heats quickly. P2DE9 flags that during this phase the pump turns too slowly. GM's 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG03B) filter the gap between requested and reported pump speed and fail the check when it exceeds 200 rpm for 8 of 10 seconds, with low-flow coolant mode and catalyst warm-up active, the request steady within 50 rpm for at least 3 s, and inlet coolant at −40 °C or warmer; two calibrated limits exist because the reachable speed depends on system voltage. Type B, MIL after two trips. Outside the warm-up phase the same fault is P2B85; pump faster than requested during cold start is P2E82. CARB demands such separate cold-start codes and a monitoring plan for electric water pumps.
c: Worn pump bearing or debris at the impeller slowing the rotor
Low supply voltage at the pump (battery, ground, connector)
Faulty pump electronics or speed feedback
Wrong or aged coolant, very thick when cold
s: Check engine light on after two trips
Uneven warm-up, local hot spots possible
Often no noticeable symptom

P2DEA.d: P2DEA says the intake valves of cylinder 1 do not reach the lift the engine computer asks for, or get there too slowly. It is the first of a row of per-cylinder lift checks. CARB's rule for valve timing and lift systems demands that such systems be watched for missing the commanded position and for reacting too slowly, and explicitly lists one cylinder's lift pin failing to move as a case the failure analysis must cover. A GM patent shows how such a single-cylinder fault can be found without extra sensors: crank speed yields each cylinder's indicated mean effective pressure, and if its coefficient of variation does not shift by roughly 5 percent after a commanded lift change, that cylinder is flagged as stuck in high or low lift. No manufacturer documents P2DEA publicly. Expect rough running, a cylinder 1 misfire and the lamp.
c: Switching element or hydraulic link of cylinder 1 sticking (sludge, wear)
Low oil level, wrong oil or restricted oil feed to the lift actuator
Cylinder 1 lift solenoid sluggish though electrically intact
Damaged cam follower, valve spring or lifter on cylinder 1
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle or shaking at low load
Misfire code for cylinder 1 at the same time

P2DEB.d: P2DEB singles out cylinder 2: its intake valve lift misses the target or follows a command too late. Lift control for each cylinder separately is the hallmark of electro-hydraulic systems like Fiat's MultiAir, sold by Schaeffler as UniAir: per cylinder, a solenoid decides how much of the cam stroke is passed through an oil-filled chamber to the intake valves; once it opens, the link collapses and a spring takes over. FCA reports faults on its 2.4 L MultiAir with its own per-cylinder P1xxx codes (P1037, P103A, P103D, P1040 for a valve shorted to ground) and has technicians measure the PCM driver pins, which should read about 15 kOhm and never below 10 kOhm, before buying a new actuator. Nobody documents P2DEB itself publicly. Symptoms: cylinder 2 misfire, rough idle.
c: Cylinder 2 solenoid in the lift actuator responding slowly or leaking internally
Aged, contaminated or wrong-grade engine oil in the hydraulic chamber
Air in the high-pressure chamber after oil starvation or service
Damaged driver stage in the engine control module
s: Check engine light on
Misfire felt at idle, cylinder 2 misfire count rising
Reduced power at higher load

P2DEC.d: P2DEC applies only to cylinder 3: the lift its intake valves actually achieve is outside the commanded window or arrives too late. Under the CARB rule, a maker must run a failure analysis of any plausible hydraulic or mechanical defect, naming broken return springs, blocked oil passages and a single cylinder's lift pin as examples, and must catch the resulting errors before tailpipe emissions pass the threshold. Two-step valvetrains with fixed states get a relief: they only have to detect faults that actually exceed it. Because a cylinder stuck in the wrong lift fills differently from its neighbours, its combustion becomes unsteady, which is exactly what crank-speed methods like GM's patented one measure. No public manufacturer document names P2DEC; an open or shorted actuator would set a circuit code instead.
c: Lock pin or switching follower of cylinder 3 not latching
Partly blocked oil passage to the cylinder 3 element
Broken return spring in the lift mechanism
s: Check engine light on
Uneven idle, often with a cylinder 3 misfire entry
Higher fuel consumption

P2DED.d: P2DED is the cylinder 4 member of the per-cylinder lift checks: the engine computer finds this cylinder's lift off target or slow to follow. On four-cylinder engines with hydraulic lift control the oil comes first. FCA's tech tip for the 2.4 L Tigershark MultiAir asks the technician to exclude a low oil level, a filter or viscosity outside spec, old or diluted oil and a clogged screen in the oil gallery on top of the block, which feeds the MultiAir unit, before any actuator is replaced. FCA itself stores MultiAir faults under its own P1xxx numbers; P2DED is not documented publicly by any maker. Since MultiAir throttles the intake through the valves, a sticking cylinder 4 shows up as uneven idle, misfire or weaker pull. CARB counts such lift errors as emission faults.
c: Low, aged, diluted or wrong-viscosity oil
Clogged oil screen in the gallery feeding the lift unit
Oil filter not meeting the maker's specification
Worn cylinder 4 section of the lift actuator
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 4, rough idle
Hesitation when accelerating

P2DEE.d: P2DEE can only occur on engines with five or more cylinders and means the intake valve lift of cylinder 5 is outside the commanded range or late. Two-step lift reached V6 engines such as the 3.6 L Pentastar, which FCA updated for 2016. An FCA patent built around switchable roller finger followers, each with an oil control valve, detects a valve stuck in the wrong lift mode from the ripple of camshaft speed taken from the cam position sensor: a filtered amplitude minus a stored nominal value, squared, gives a stuck-valve index that is checked against a threshold within about two engine cycles. Whether a given make stores such a fault as P2DEE is not published. Expect a cylinder 5 misfire, rough idle and the lamp.
c: Switching roller finger follower of cylinder 5 stuck in one mode
Oil control valve for the lift switching sticking or contaminated
Oil pressure too low to move the lock pins
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 5
Ticking from the valvetrain on one bank

P2DEF.d: P2DEF covers cylinder 6, typically on a V6 or straight six: its intake valves do not reach the commanded lift or take too long to switch. Detection follows the same idea as for the other cylinders; for the driver the reaction matters more. GM's patent on stuck lift mechanisms reports which cylinder failed and whether it hangs in high or low lift, and the engine computer may then drive every mechanism into one default lift, stop further switching, limit engine speed and turn on the MIL. When several cylinders on one bank or the whole engine are off target, P2DF0, P2DF1 or P2DF2 are the matching codes instead. No manufacturer documents P2DEF publicly; CARB treats any lift error that raises emissions as an OBD fault.
c: Lift mechanism of cylinder 6 stuck in high or low lift
Restricted oil feed to the cylinder 6 element
Actuator for cylinder 6 slow despite correct wiring
s: Check engine light on
Engine speed limited or lift switching disabled (substitute mode)
Cylinder 6 misfire, rough running

P2DF0.d: P2DF0 means that intake valve lift on bank 1 as a whole does not follow the command, rather than one cylinder. Continuously variable systems explain why: BMW's Valvetronic turns an eccentric shaft with an electric motor controlled by the DME, moving an intermediate arm between camshaft and rocker, while Nissan's VVEL uses a DC motor to rotate a control shaft; one shaft sets lift for all cylinders it serves, so a stiff shaft, worn motor or wrong position reading hits them together. A Bosch patent checks lift plausibility by comparing the air flow predicted from valve lift and engine speed, plus a tolerance, with the air mass meter. No manufacturer documents P2DF0 publicly; CARB requires checks for both wrong and late lift. Bank 2 is P2DF1, the whole system P2DF2.
c: Eccentric or control shaft on bank 1 stiff from wear or sludge
Lift adjusting motor of bank 1 worn or weak
Shaft position sensor reading offset or loosened
Air mass meter error or intake leak making the lift appear wrong
s: Check engine light on
Reduced power, engine may fall back to throttle control
Rough idle across several cylinders

P2DF1.d: P2DF1 is the bank 2 counterpart of P2DF0 and therefore only appears on V engines or boxers, on the side without cylinder 1. Nissan's VVEL, used on the VQ37VHR V6 and on V8 engines, is a good example: on the 2014 QX80 V8 both banks carry a separate VVEL ladder assembly with an actuator and a control shaft position sensor. Infiniti's bulletin ITB14-041 for the 2014 QX80 warns never to loosen the ladder adjusting bolts or the sensor mounting bolts, because the cam lift stroke then goes out of adjustment and ladder plus cylinder head must be replaced. A wrong reading from that sensor or a binding shaft therefore shows up as a lift error on one bank only. No manufacturer documents P2DF1 publicly; under CARB's VVT section the lift system must be watched for both kinds of deviation.
c: Control shaft or ladder assembly on bank 2 binding
Control shaft position sensor on bank 2 moved or faulty
Lift actuator motor of bank 2 weak
Oil sludge in the bank 2 lift mechanism
s: Check engine light on
Uneven running between the banks, possible fuel trim difference
Reduced power

P2DF2.d: P2DF2 points to the intake valve lift system as a whole rather than to one cylinder or bank, typical for inline engines where one actuator sets lift for every cylinder, as on four-cylinder Valvetronic engines; Toyota's Valvematic also varies lift continuously. Plausibility is usually judged on air flow: a Bosch patent derives the expected flow from lift and engine speed, compares it with the air mass meter and falls back to a throttle-based model once the valves sit at full lift and the engine runs conventionally. Toyota's campaign F0N updated the software of about 20,200 Corolla Eco cars of 2014 (2ZR-FAE) whose continuous lift control could light the engine lamp and cut power. No manufacturer documents P2DF2 publicly by number; CARB makes such lift monitoring mandatory. Bank-specific faults use P2DF0 or P2DF1.
c: Lift actuator motor or its gear worn
Engine control software needing an update (known on some models)
Eccentric or control shaft stiff from wear or sludge
Faulty air mass reading or intake leak falsifying the plausibility check
s: Check engine light on
Noticeably reduced power, engine in substitute mode
Rough idle and higher fuel consumption

P2DF3.t: Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Position Not Learned
P2DF3.d: The clutch between combustion engine and electric machine in a P2 hybrid is only usable when the controller knows where its actuator begins to transmit torque. P2DF3 is a status code: that learned position is missing or invalid, often after a battery disconnect, module replacement, software update or clutch repair, before the learn routine has completed. No manufacturer documents P2DF3 publicly. An Aisin patent stores clutch torque against actuator stroke, measured by a Hall sensor, and explains that hybrids starting on the motor rarely give a chance to relearn it. Ford instead learns a liftoff pressure for its hydraulically applied clutch. Without valid values engine starts and engagement jerk, or the controller keeps the engine coupled. Electrical and mechanical faults have other codes (P287E ff., P2D8D).
c: Learn routine not yet completed after battery disconnect, repair or module replacement
Learn repeatedly aborted because enable conditions were not met
Actuator position sensor delivering implausible values during the learn
Clutch wear or actuator fault pushing the learned value out of its window
s: Warning lamp or hybrid system message
Jerky engine start or clutch engagement
Electric-only driving restricted

P2DF4.d: Electric coolant pumps are usually commanded through a PWM wire or a LIN bus, and pump E is the fifth such pump in a vehicle's lettering; what it cools depends on the manufacturer. P2DF4 reports an open or otherwise faulty command line to pump E. No manufacturer documents P2DF4 publicly. Ford shows the pattern for its pumps A and B in the 2024 gasoline OBD summary: the base code is fault type 13 (circuit open), set when the module's smart driver reports an output fault, monitored continuously above 11 V over 5 seconds. Bosch's PDE pump, a typical example, carries its own motor and diagnostic electronics and takes speed commands via PWM or LIN. With an open line many pumps default to a fixed speed or stop, so the cooled component may overheat. Shorts are P2DF5 and P2DF6.
c: Pump connector loose, corroded or with pushed-back pin
Broken command wire in the harness
Pump electronics with failed control input
Faulty output driver in the commanding module
s: Warning lamp on
Pump runs at fixed speed or not at all
Temperature warning or power reduction of the cooled component

P2DF5.t: Coolant Pump E Control Circuit Low
P2DF5.d: P2DF5 means the command line of coolant pump E sits too low, typically shorted to ground, so the module's driver cannot pull it up to the commanded level. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In Ford's 2024 gasoline OBD summary the matching fault type is 11 (circuit low), again flagged by the smart driver for pumps A and B, continuously above 11 V. Because a PWM pump reads duty cycle, a line held at ground can mean zero duty; depending on the pump design this is read as stop, as maximum speed or as a fault state. CARB requires output components to be checked for shorts as well as for proper response. Look for chafed insulation against body or engine parts and water in the connector. The open circuit is P2DF4, a short to voltage P2DF6, the pump power feed P2DFA.
c: Command wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion bridging the command pin to ground
Internal short in the pump's control input
Output stage of the commanding module defective
s: Warning lamp on
Pump stopped or stuck at one speed
Rising temperature of the component served by pump E

P2DF6.t: Coolant Pump E Control Circuit High
P2DF6.d: P2DF6 is set when the command line of coolant pump E stays high although the module wants it low, most often because it touches a battery-voltage wire. No manufacturer documents P2DF6 publicly. For pumps A and B, Ford's 2024 gasoline document assigns fault type 12 (circuit high), raised by the smart driver once battery voltage reaches 11 V. A PWM line pinned high looks like a constant full command, so many pumps run at maximum speed regardless of the actual cooling need; this drains extra current and may disturb warm-up or cooling strategies. A short inside the pump electronics can cause the same picture. Check the harness for contact with feed wires and measure the line with the pump unplugged. Low-side faults are P2DF5, an open line P2DF4.
c: Command wire shorted to a battery-voltage wire
Internal fault in the pump electronics pulling the line high
Corrosion bridging adjacent pins in the connector
Commanding module's output stage stuck high
s: Warning lamp on
Pump audible at full speed all the time
Slower warm-up of the affected loop

P2DF7.t: Coolant Pump E Overspeed/Air in System
P2DF7.d: When an electric pump draws air instead of liquid, its impeller loses load and the rotor races above the commanded speed. P2DF7 reports this for coolant pump E; the title already names trapped air as the usual cause. No manufacturer documents P2DF7 publicly. Ford names the condition overspeed or dry run and codes it B1 for the cabin-heating and component-cooling pumps in its 2024 gasoline summary, checked whenever the battery delivers 11 V or more. GM's 2025 ECM tables show how overspeed is judged on the electric main pump (P26CE): the filtered difference between requested and actual speed turns negative beyond a calibrated limit for 8 of 10 seconds, Type B. Typical triggers are a low coolant level, an incomplete bleed after service, or a leak that sucks in air. Running dry also heats the pump electronics, see P2DFB.
c: Air pocket left after coolant service or component replacement
Low coolant level from a leak in the loop
Damaged or loose impeller, rotor spins freely
Implausible speed feedback from the pump electronics
s: Warning lamp or coolant level message
Gurgling or whining from the pump area
Overheating or derating of the cooled component

P2DF8.d: P2DF8 means coolant pump E keeps turning, but slower than the module asked for. No manufacturer documents P2DF8 publicly. Ford's 2024 gasoline summary treats underspeed as fault type B2 of its pumps A and B, monitored continuously from 11 V over 5 seconds. GM's 2025 ECM tables show a concrete limit for the electric main pump (P2B85): the filtered gap between requested and reported speed must stay above a calibrated threshold for 8 of 10 seconds. Air can produce underspeed as well as overspeed: GM bulletin 24-NA-160 explains that on the Corvette E-Ray an air pocket made the battery coolant pump halt to protect itself, which its module logged as underspeed (P0E3C), and calls for bleeding first. Other causes are bearing wear, debris and low supply voltage. A rotor that does not turn at all is P2DF9.
c: Bearing wear or debris dragging on the rotor
Air pocket causing the pump to slow or pause for self-protection
Voltage drop in the pump feed or ground
s: Warning lamp on
Insufficient cooling or heating of the served circuit
Power reduction possible at high load

P2DF9.d: P2DF9 covers the hard case: coolant pump E is powered and commanded, but its rotor does not start or comes to a standstill. Brushless pumps sense this internally, for instance from current flowing without commutation feedback, and pass the result to the commanding module. No manufacturer documents P2DF9 publicly. In Ford's 2024 gasoline document the matching entry for pumps A and B is fault type 71, a stuck actuator, watched without interruption from 11 V. A GM patent on electric coolant pump diagnostics compares measured pump current with a value expected from speed, coolant temperature and valve positions, and flags a flow fault when either current or speed deviates too far. Seized bearings, a jammed impeller, frozen or sludged coolant and a burnt winding are typical. Slow but turning is P2DF8.
c: Seized bearing or impeller jammed by debris
Frozen, gelled or sludged coolant (wrong mixture)
Burnt winding or failed pump electronics
Rotor stuck after long standstill, deposits on the bearing
s: Warning lamp on
No coolant flow in the affected circuit
Overheating warning or power limitation

P2DFA.t: Coolant Pump E Supply Voltage Circuit
P2DFA.d: Unlike P2DF4 to P2DF6, which concern the command line, P2DFA concerns the power feed of coolant pump E. Smart pumps measure the voltage at their own supply pin and report when it leaves the window they need to run reliably. No manufacturer documents P2DFA publicly. Ford codes a feed outside its permitted band as fault type 1C for its two auxiliary pumps (2024 gasoline summary), judged over 5 seconds once 11 V are present. Bosch rates its PDE pumps for the 12 V network with integrated electronics and selective error feedback to the vehicle. Suspects are a blown fuse, a relay with worn contacts, a loose ground, corroded terminals or a weak battery; a voltage-drop test with the pump running reveals hidden resistance. The pump may stop or run reduced, so the served circuit is undercooled.
c: Blown fuse or relay with burnt contacts in the pump feed
Loose or corroded ground of the pump
Weak 12 V battery or charging fault
Resistance in feed wire or connector
s: Warning lamp on
Pump stops intermittently, often with other low-voltage faults
Reduced cooling of the served component

P2DFB.t: Coolant Pump E Control Module Overtemperature
P2DFB.d: Electric coolant pumps carry their own driver electronics, and P2DFB reports that those of coolant pump E have run too hot. Which loop pump E serves differs between makers. No manufacturer documents P2DFB publicly, but its siblings show the pattern: Ford's 2024 gasoline summary lists over temperature as fault type 98 of its auxiliary pumps A and B, watched continuously from 11 V with a 5 second monitoring time, and Ford's 2019 hybrid summary lets the engine coolant pump send its module temperature over LIN, setting P26D2 above 130 °C for 5 seconds. Because the liquid it moves also cools the electronics, low level, trapped air, a stiff impeller or heat from nearby exhaust parts are the usual triggers. The pump then slows or stops, and the served loop may overheat.
c: Coolant level too low or air trapped in the pump, so the electronics lose their cooling
Impeller or bearing running stiff, motor draws high current and heats up
Driver electronics inside pump E faulty or reporting temperature wrongly
Heat shield missing or pump too close to hot exhaust or turbo parts
s: Warning lamp or message about the cooling system
Reduced cabin heating or cooling of the component served by pump E
Pump runs at reduced speed or stops for a while, often together with air or stall codes

P2DFC.d: P2DFC states that the liquid loop cooling the high-voltage battery is losing coolant. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. A GM patent explains how such a verdict is reached: a float or reed switch in the reservoir at the highest point of the loop is sampled in windows of a few seconds, only while the car stands level, the pump turns fast enough to purge air and pack temperature is in range; a low reading in two of the last three drive cycles counts as a leak, stores a code and lights the MIL. GM's Chevrolet Volt applies this under its own code P1FFE: sensor voltage of 1.38 to 2.84 V in 16 of 20 samples at standstill, seen twice within three key cycles, Type A. Since leaking coolant can reach the cells, charging or propulsion may be blocked. Sensor wiring faults are P2BE0 to P2BE3.
c: Leaking hose, clamp or quick connector in the battery coolant loop
Leak at the battery chiller, heat exchanger or cooling plates inside the pack
Loop not filled or bled correctly after a repair
Level sensor reporting low although the level is correct
s: Hybrid or EV system service message and MIL
Charging blocked or drive power reduced
Coolant level in the battery reservoir visibly low, possibly traces of coolant under the car

P2DFD.d: Some turbocharged and hybrid engines cannot count on intake vacuum to empty the charcoal canister, so an electric purge pump moves the fuel vapour into the intake. P2DFD means this pump does not achieve the expected effect, for instance the pressure or speed it should reach. Nissan uses the code on the 2022 Rogue with the KR15DDT engine: bulletin NTB22-066 has the technician reseat the pump connector under the intake tube and run the engine for a minute before any further diagnosis. Hyundai names P2DFD00 among the codes linked to EGR condensation and intake icing on Tucson and Santa Fe hybrids, addressed by an ECM update (26-01-081H), and keeps its own code P1DFD00 for pump target speed. A Continental patent uses a pressure sensor in the pump module for plausibility checks. CARB demands purge flow monitoring.
c: Pump connector not fully latched (Nissan Rogue 2022)
Purge pump motor or impeller worn, pump no longer reaches its speed or pressure
Purge hose cracked, disconnected or blocked between canister, pump and intake
Condensation or ice in the intake path, needs ECM update (Hyundai hybrids)
s: MIL on, usually without noticeable change in driving
EVAP readiness not complete, emissions inspection may fail
Occasional fuel smell when the canister is not purged

P2E00.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor A Circuit
P2E00.d: Gear lever position sensor A is the first of up to four sensors through which an electronic selector tells its control module where the lever sits. In the designs GM and Toyota document, A and B form a redundant pair that each report the full lever position; GM's patent US9249877 has each of its two sensors deliver an x and a y value. P2E00 is the umbrella circuit fault of sensor A: an open line, a lost supply or a signal the module cannot evaluate, without splitting it into low or high. No manufacturer documents P2E00 publicly; in its 2025 ECM tables GM lists only P2E01 for this sensor and suspends that test while lost-communication U codes are stored. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring of such transmission inputs. With sensor B valid, shifting usually continues.
c: Loose connector or chafed wire at the selector assembly
Supply or ground of sensor A interrupted
Sensor A inside the selector assembly failed
Input stage of the evaluating module faulty
s: Warning lamp or shift-system message
Gear selection still possible through sensor B, sometimes delayed
With a second fault, the vehicle may stay in P or N

P2E01.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor A Range/Performance
P2E01.d: Here sensor A of the gear lever delivers values that are electrically valid but not believable. Two makers document the code. Lexus lists it as a signal plausibility failure (internal code P2E00-64) on 2022–24 NX models; bulletin L-SB-0050-22 cures it, together with P2E05, by reflashing the floor shift unit with revised logic, expressly without replacing it. GM's 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG04B) name it gear lever position sensor 1 performance: the sensor flags an internal error inside its SENT data, seen as alpha/beta at or above 99.84 %, in 160 of 200 samples and only while no communication fault is stored; Type B, MIL after two trips. GM checks the X and Y axes of the same sensor separately under P082A and P082D. Per GM's patent the partner sensor can take over.
c: Selector logic needs a software update (Lexus NX 2022–24)
Sensor A reports an internal error
Magnet or lever mechanism shifted, so sensor A reads off the gate
s: MIL on after two trips
Shift-system message, selector still works through sensor B
Often no noticeable driving difference

P2E02.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P2E02.d: P2E02 says the signal of gear lever position sensor A is stuck below the lowest value a healthy sensor can output. Typical reasons: the signal wire touches ground, the reference voltage is missing, or the sensor output has collapsed. No manufacturer publishes P2E02. The closest documented check is GM's per-axis version on the Cadillac XT4 electronic selector (19OBDG03D): X sensor 1 sets P082B, Y sensor 1 P082E, when the PWM duty cycle falls under 5 % in 3 of 4 samples at 25 ms, Type B. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) asks for out-of-range detection on transmission inputs and keeps circuit and rationality faults under separate codes. The high counterpart is P2E03, sensor B low is P2E06. With a valid partner sensor the lever normally keeps working.
c: Signal wire of sensor A shorted to ground
Sensor reference voltage missing or pulled down
s: Warning lamp and shift-system message
Lever position shown on the display jumps or is missing
If sensor B also fails, no range can be selected

P2E03.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor A Circuit High
P2E03.d: With P2E03 the module sees the signal of sensor A above the highest value the sensor can legitimately send. On a pulled-up input this happens when the signal wire is open; it also follows a short to the supply or a lost sensor ground. No manufacturer publishes P2E03. GM checks the same kind of fault axis by axis on the XT4 selector: P082C and P082F set when the duty cycle of X or Y sensor 1 rises above 95 % (19OBDG03D, 3 of 4 samples, Type B, MIL after two trips). GM's patent explains the consequence: a coordinate that fails makes that sensor's whole position signal invalid, and the module relies on the second sensor. P2E02 is the low side, P2E07 the same high fault on sensor B. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires this two-sided check.
c: Signal wire of sensor A open at a connector
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
s: Warning lamp after two trips
Shift-system message, ranges still selectable via sensor B
Start or range change refused if both sensors are affected

P2E04.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor B Circuit
P2E04.d: Sensor B is the second, redundant gear lever position sensor; it measures the same lever travel as sensor A so that a single failure does not leave the driver without range selection. Toyota names it gear lever position sensor B in the floor shift assembly of the Lexus NX, and GM's tables call the equivalent device sensor 2, with X and Y values of its own (P089B to P08A2). P2E04 is the general circuit fault of sensor B, set when its line is open or its signal cannot be read, with no low/high distinction. No maker documents P2E04 itself. GM's patent US9249877 describes the logic behind the pair: if a coordinate of one sensor fails its test, that sensor is ignored and the other decides. A fault here therefore removes the backup, not the function.
c: Connector or wire of sensor B at the selector loose or damaged
Sensor B in the selector assembly failed
Separate supply branch of sensor B interrupted
s: Warning lamp or shift-system message
Selector works normally on sensor A alone
Any further sensor fault can block range changes

P2E05.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor B Range/Performance
P2E05.d: P2E05 flags implausible data from sensor B, the backup gear lever sensor. It is one of the few codes of this family with public manufacturer use. On 2022–24 Lexus NX 250/350 and 2022 NX 350h/450h+, Toyota stores it as P2E04-64, a plausibility failure of sensor B, often alongside P2E01; bulletin L-SB-0050-22 (revised October 2023) changes the floor shift assembly logic by reflash, with 0.8 h labour and no part swap. In GM's 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG04B) P2E05 belongs to gear lever position sensor 2: an internal error reported over the second SENT channel, threshold 99.84 %, 160 failures in 200 samples, blocked by lost-communication codes U1194, U1196, U13E1 and U13E3; Type B, two trips. Axis checks of that sensor are P089B and P08A0.
c: Floor shift assembly logic outdated (Lexus NX bulletin L-SB-0050-22)
Sensor B signals an internal error
Sensor B or its magnet misaligned after a repair in the console
s: MIL on, usually without a driveability change
Shift-system warning may appear and disappear
Often stored together with P2E01

P2E06.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P2E06.d: The signal of sensor B, the redundant gear lever sensor, has dropped under its permitted minimum. Electrically that points to a short to ground in its signal line, a dead sensor or a missing feed on its own supply branch. P2E06 is not published by any manufacturer. GM catches the same condition per axis on the XT4 selector as P089C (X) and P08A1 (Y), each when the PWM duty cycle of sensor 2 stays below 5 % for three failures in four samples; Type B with a two-trip MIL. Because sensor A still delivers a full position, the driver usually notices only the warning; GM's patent lets the module carry on with the remaining valid signal. Sensor A low is P2E02, sensor B high P2E07. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires such out-of-range checks.
c: Signal line of sensor B shorted to ground
Supply branch of sensor B dead
s: Warning lamp after two trips
Selector keeps working on sensor A
Range selection lost if sensor A fails as well

P2E07.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor B Circuit High
P2E07.d: P2E07 is the high-side circuit fault of gear lever position sensor B: its signal reads above anything the sensor may legitimately produce. An interrupted signal line on an input with pull-up, a short to battery or reference voltage, or a broken sensor ground are the classic causes. No maker publishes P2E07. On the Cadillac XT4 electronic shifter GM monitors sensor 2 axis by axis and sets P089D or P08A2 above 95 % duty cycle, 3 out of 4 samples on a 25 ms loop, Type B. Sensor A carries the selector meanwhile, which is the purpose of the redundancy described in GM's patent. P2E06 is the low fault of the same sensor and P2E03 the high fault of sensor A; both A and B high at once suggests a shared ground or connector.
c: Signal line of sensor B open
Signal line shorted to battery or reference voltage
s: Warning lamp and shift-system message
Normal shifting via sensor A
With P2E03 present as well, range selection may be blocked

P2E08.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor C Circuit
P2E08.d: A third gear lever position sensor, C, only exists on selectors with more than the usual redundant pair. Toyota's patent US10180184 shows such a design: four Hall sensors in a row face a magnet in the shift lever, the voltages they produce encode the position, and if any one of them is faulty the other three still allow limp-home driving. Which job the letter C has in a given vehicle is not published; no manufacturer documents P2E08 or any other sensor C code. P2E08 is the general circuit fault of that sensor – open wiring, missing supply or an unreadable signal – before any low/high split (P2E0A, P2E0B). CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires the module to detect circuit faults of such transmission inputs. GM's lever tables only know sensors 1 and 2.
c: Connector or wiring at the selector assembly faulty
Sensor C inside the selector failed
s: Warning lamp or shift-system message
Shifting continues on the remaining sensors
A further sensor fault may force neutral

P2E09.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor C Range/Performance
P2E09.d: P2E09 means sensor C produces an electrically valid signal that contradicts the lever position given by the other sensors. No manufacturer documents this code or names the role of a sensor C, so the logic can only be inferred from the component. In Toyota's four-Hall-sensor selector patent (US10180184) a sensor counts as abnormal when the difference between its voltage and those of its neighbours leaves a preset tolerance. The patent also explains a weak spot: a sensor frozen at a mid value is hard to spot until the driver moves the lever to a particular position. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) asks for such rationality checks on transmission inputs under a code separate from circuit faults. Sensors A and B have the same check as P2E01 and P2E05, which Lexus and GM use.
c: Sensor C output frozen at an intermediate value
Magnet or lever mechanism worn or displaced
Plausibility logic of the selector software too strict
s: Warning appears only after certain lever movements
Range display briefly disagrees with lever position
Limp-home with restricted selection possible

P2E0A.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor C Circuit Low
P2E0A.d: For P2E0A the module reads the signal of gear lever sensor C below the window a working sensor can occupy. On a voltage-output Hall sensor like those in Toyota's four-sensor selector patent (US10180184), this means a signal line pulled to ground, a missing feed or a sensor that has stopped driving its output. The same patent counts disconnection and short circuits as faults that can be detected continuously, and lets the remaining three sensors run a limp-home mode. No manufacturer documents P2E0A or tells what sensor C measures. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) demands detection of out-of-range input values. The high side is P2E0B; GM's comparable per-axis low checks on its two-sensor lever are P082B and P089C, with a 5 % duty-cycle limit.
c: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground
s: Warning lamp or shift message
Limp-home on the remaining sensors
No noticeable change while other sensors are valid

P2E0B.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor C Circuit High
P2E0B.d: P2E0B: sensor C of the gear lever reports more than its maximum valid signal. That is the typical picture of a broken signal wire on a pulled-up input, contact with the feed line or a lost sensor ground. No manufacturer documents P2E0B, and the function of a third lever sensor is nowhere specified publicly. Toyota's patent US10180184 shows why a selector might carry one: with four Hall sensors one can drop out while three still define the lever position; only if another abnormality follows does the patent foresee a fail-safe such as a shift to neutral. On GM's two-sensor lever, duty cycles above 95 % raise the per-axis codes P082C and P089D. Low is P2E0A. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires two-sided range checks on such inputs.
c: Signal wire of sensor C open
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
s: Warning lamp or shift message
Selector keeps working with the other sensors
Neutral forced if another sensor also fails

P2E0C.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor D Circuit
P2E0C.d: Sensor D is the fourth and last letter in this family of gear lever position sensors. A layout that needs four is described in Toyota's patent US10180184: four Hall sensors lined up along the shift direction under one magnet, whose voltage pattern flips when the lever moves sideways, so both shift and select movement can be read. P2E0C covers a general electrical fault of sensor D – interrupted wiring, no supply, signal not evaluable – without saying whether it is too low or too high (those are P2E0E and P2E0F). No manufacturer documents P2E0C, and none says which part of the lever D is assigned to. Circuit checks on transmission inputs are mandatory under CARB 1968.2 (e)(15). If only D is lost, a four-sensor design can still recognise the position.
c: Selector connector or wiring of sensor D faulty
Module input for sensor D faulty
s: Warning lamp or shift-system message
Gear selection usually still works
Neutral fail-safe possible after a second sensor fault

P2E0D.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor D Range/Performance
P2E0D.d: With P2E0D the fourth lever sensor, D, stays within its electrical limits but its reading does not fit the lever position. No manufacturer documents P2E0D. Toyota's four-sensor patent (US10180184) gives a model for such a test: the module compares the voltage differences between the Hall sensors with a preset tolerance and declares one abnormal if it falls outside. A second check in the patent matters while driving: the remaining sensors must not report a range for the opposite direction of travel, which guards against a wrong forward/reverse change. A sensor stuck at a middle value may pass until a specific lever position is selected, so the code can appear late. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires rationality checks of transmission inputs. Sensor C's equivalent is P2E09.
c: Sensor D frozen at a middle value
Magnet position in the lever changed by wear or impact
Selector software tolerance needs an update
s: Code appears only after selecting a certain position
Warning lamp or shift message
Limp-home with fewer sensors

P2E0E.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor D Circuit Low
P2E0E.d: P2E0E is set when the output of gear lever position sensor D drops beneath its lowest plausible level, usually near 0 V or 0 % duty cycle. Likely reasons are a ground short in the D signal path, a sensor without feed or a Hall element whose output died. No maker publishes P2E0E or a meaning for sensor D. Toyota's patent US10180184 treats such hard electrical faults as continuously detectable and keeps the shift position available from the three other sensors; a second abnormality then calls for a fail-safe such as neutral. For comparison, GM flags low per axis on its two-sensor XT4 lever below 5 % duty cycle (P082E, P08A1). Out-of-range detection is a CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) duty. Sensor D high is P2E0F, sensor C low P2E0A.
c: Signal path of sensor D shorted to ground
Hall element of sensor D failed low
s: Shift-system warning
Selector still usable on the other sensors
Shift to neutral if another sensor fails

P2E0F.t: Gear Lever Position Sensor D Circuit High
P2E0F.d: P2E0F closes the series: sensor D, the fourth gear lever position sensor, reads above the top of its valid range. An open signal wire where the module input pulls up, contact with a voltage-carrying wire or a lost sensor ground produce this picture. No manufacturer documents P2E0F, nor the role of sensor D in a real selector. In the four-Hall-sensor arrangement of Toyota's patent US10180184 a high fault of one element leaves three sensors to determine the position, and the module watches them for a reading that would mean the opposite direction of travel. GM's two-sensor lever detects high faults per axis above 95 % duty cycle (P082F, P08A2). P2E0E is the low counterpart and P2E0B the high fault of sensor C. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) calls for such range checks.
c: Signal wire of sensor D open
Signal wire touching a voltage-carrying wire
s: Warning lamp or shift message
Normal shifting on the remaining sensors
Neutral fail-safe after a further fault

P2E10.t: Gear Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit
P2E10.d: P2E10 is the general circuit code for the sensor reporting where the gear selection actuator stands, the motor-driven unit that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual or dual-clutch gearbox to the wanted gear or gate. The control module stores it when signal or supply of that sensor are electrically faulty in a way the dedicated low, high or erratic codes do not cover. No manufacturer documents P2E10 publicly. Ford's 2012 summary for the DPS6 dual-clutch box illustrates the principle: Hall elements in each shift drum motor tell the TCM where the drum stands, and from that the engaged gear. CARB counts such transmission sensors among the comprehensive components that need circuit checks. Without a usable position the gearbox usually refuses shifts or holds one gear. P2E11 to P2E14 are the specific siblings.
c: Corroded or loose connector, damaged harness at the actuator
Position sensor in the actuator failed (often only replaceable with the actuator)
Sensor reference voltage missing or loaded down by another fault
Input stage in the transmission control module faulty
s: Transmission warning and MIL
Gearbox holds one gear or goes to neutral (limp mode)
Shifts refused or engaging drive or reverse not possible

P2E11.t: Gear Selection Actuator Position Sensor Performance
P2E11.d: With P2E11 the position sensor of the gear selection actuator delivers values that are electrically fine but do not fit the situation: the reading stays put although the actuator was driven, or it contradicts the gear that shaft speeds prove to be engaged. No manufacturer documents P2E11 publicly. In GM's TCM tables of 2023 for a dual-clutch box (23OBDG07) one can see how such a plausibility test works on a shift rod sensor under P2832: when speed sensors confirm an engaged gear with more than 600 N of shift force applied, yet the reading lies over 1100 µm from the learned engaged position, a Type A fault follows. Ford's DPS6 flags a comparable loss of confidence in the shift drum position, including a blocked motor, under the same P2832. Typical causes are a shifted sensor magnet, mechanical wear or lost learned values.
c: Learned end positions lost or outdated, e.g. after battery disconnect or part replacement
Sensor magnet or sensor mounting shifted, reading offset
Wear or binding in the selection mechanism, actuator does not reach its target
s: Delayed or harsh shifts, gear sometimes not engaged
Transmission warning, possibly limp mode with fixed gear
Fault may clear after a relearn procedure

P2E12.t: Gear Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low
P2E12.d: P2E12 sets when the signal of the gear selection actuator's position sensor stays below the lowest valid level. Usual reasons are a short to ground on the signal line, a missing 5 V reference or a defect inside the sensor; with many designs an interrupted signal wire also reads low. No manufacturer documents P2E12 publicly. For a comparable digital rod position sensor, GM's 2023 dual-clutch TCM tables (P2833) give concrete limits: no pulses while the pin sits below 2000 mV, or a duty cycle under 8 %, confirmed after 150 ms with a supply between 4.5 and 5.5 V, Type A. CARB calls for out-of-range checks on such transmission inputs. If several sensors share the reference, other codes often appear at once. The high counterpart is P2E13; the gearbox usually falls back to a safe gear.
c: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
5 V reference missing or pulled down by another sensor on the same supply
Internal short in the position sensor
s: MIL and transmission warning immediately
Limp mode, no gear changes or only one gear
Further sensor codes if the shared 5 V supply is affected

P2E13.t: Gear Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High
P2E13.d: P2E13 is the opposite case to P2E12: the position signal of the gear selection actuator sits above its highest plausible value. A short between the signal line and a supply wire is the classic cause; an open ground or, on pull-up inputs, a broken signal wire produce the same picture. No manufacturer documents P2E13 publicly. GM's 2023 TCM tables for a dual-clutch gearbox treat the high fault of a rod position sensor (P2834) as missing pulses with the pin above 3500 mV, or a duty cycle above 92 %, judged for 150 ms and only with valid sensor supply and battery voltage, Type A. CARB requires such out-of-range tests on transmission sensors. Measuring the line with the sensor unplugged separates a harness short from a sensor defect. The gearbox then normally stops shifting or keeps a fixed gear.
c: Signal wire shorted to a supply or 5 V reference line
Sensor ground open or high resistance
Position sensor faulty, output stuck high
Moisture in the actuator connector bridging pins
s: MIL and transmission warning
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Shift lever input ignored

P2E14.t: Gear Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2E14.d: P2E14 covers a position signal from the gear selection actuator that is present but unsteady: it drops out for moments, jumps or carries an implausible frequency or pattern, without staying low or high long enough for P2E12 or P2E13. No manufacturer documents P2E14 publicly. Two related checks show what erratic means in practice. GM's 2023 dual-clutch TCM tables reject a rod position sensor whose carrier frequency leaves the 1500 to 2500 Hz band for 150 ms (P2835, Type A). Ford's 2012 DPS6 summary watches the three Hall signals of each shift drum motor and sets P2835 if their sequence comes out of order. Loose pins, harness chafing that only touches under vibration, and electrical noise are typical. Drivers notice sporadic refused shifts or brief neutral drops that later vanish.
c: Loose or fretted terminal in the actuator connector
Harness chafing that only shorts or opens under vibration or heat
Interference from damaged shielding or nearby motor wiring
Sensor with an internal intermittent fault
s: Occasional refused or delayed shifts
Short drops to neutral while driving
Warning lamp that comes and goes

P2E15.t: Intermediate Shaft Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit
P2E15.d: P2E15 is the basic circuit code for the position sensor of a second selection actuator, one assigned to the intermediate shaft (layshaft) of the gearbox rather than to the main gear selection, which has P2E10 to P2E14. Which gearboxes use such an actuator, and what exactly it engages there, no manufacturer documents publicly for this code. Schaeffler's LuK paper on electric dual-clutch actuators shows the general idea: separate electric motors handle the shift and the select movement, while the select motor moves the shift finger axially into the gate that is needed. The control module needs the position feedback to know whether the selection has been made. CARB requires circuit checks on such transmission sensors. If the signal fails electrically, gear changes that involve this shaft are blocked. P2E16 to P2E19 are the specific variants.
c: Connector or harness to the intermediate shaft actuator damaged or corroded
Position sensor of the actuator failed
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: Transmission warning and MIL
Some gears unavailable or gearbox in limp mode
Vehicle may only drive in a restricted range of gears

P2E16.t: Intermediate Shaft Selection Actuator Position Sensor Range/Performance
P2E16.d: P2E16 flags a position reading from the intermediate shaft selection actuator that is electrically valid but not credible, for example a travel that does not match the commanded movement or the learned end stops. No manufacturer documents P2E16 publicly. Why learned references matter is explained in Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch summary from 2012: its clutch actuators sense motor position with Hall elements that only count steps, so the system must sweep from one end stop to the other to know the absolute position. If counts are lost or the mechanism no longer reaches its stops, the computed position drifts away from reality. GM judges plausibility of a rod sensor against shaft speeds (P2832 in 23OBDG07). A relearn after battery work or repair may clear the fault; otherwise check the mechanism.
c: End stops not learned or lost after battery disconnect or repair
Actuator or selection linkage binding, target position not reached
Sensor or its magnet shifted, reading offset
s: Harsh, slow or failed shifts involving the intermediate shaft
Transmission warning, possibly limp mode
Fault returns until a relearn has been done

P2E17.t: Intermediate Shaft Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low
P2E17.d: P2E17 tells you the position signal of the intermediate shaft selection actuator is stuck at the bottom of its range or below it. On the bench this usually turns out to be a signal line touching ground, a dead reference supply, or a sensor whose output stage has failed. No manufacturer documents P2E17 publicly. As a reference point, GM's 2023 dual-clutch TCM tables call a rod position sensor low (P2833) when pulses are missing with less than 2000 mV at the pin or when the duty cycle drops below 8 %, Type A. CARB requires transmission inputs to be checked for values outside their range. Start with the connector at the gearbox, then the reference voltage, then the sensor. The matching high fault is P2E18; for the main gear selection actuator the low fault is P2E12.
c: Output stage of the position sensor failed
Signal wire interrupted (on sensors that then read low)
s: MIL and transmission warning
Limp mode with limited gears
Code returns at once after clearing

P2E18.t: Intermediate Shaft Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High
P2E18.d: Here the position sensor of the intermediate shaft selection actuator reports a value above its upper limit. Most often the signal line has contact with battery voltage or the 5 V feed, or the sensor has lost its ground so the output floats upward. No manufacturer documents P2E18 publicly. For a rod sensor, GM's transmission tables from 2023 (23OBDG07) use this rule under P2834: no pulses with more than 3500 mV on the pin, or a duty cycle above 92 %, checked for 150 ms while battery voltage lies between 8.75 and 18 V, Type A. CARB treats such sensors as comprehensive components with mandatory range checks. A voltage check of signal and ground with the actuator plugged in narrows it down quickly. The low fault of the same sensor is P2E17, the high fault of the main selection actuator P2E13.
c: Signal line shorted to battery voltage or the 5 V feed
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
s: MIL and transmission warning
Certain gears blocked, limp mode
Poor acceleration because the gearbox holds an unsuitable gear

P2E19.t: Intermediate Shaft Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2E19.d: P2E19 is stored when the intermediate shaft selection actuator's position sensor delivers a signal that flickers, drops out briefly or changes faster than the mechanism could physically move. Because the fault comes and goes, the code often shows as pending or with only a few occurrences. No manufacturer documents P2E19 publicly. As an example of what counts as erratic for a digital rod sensor, GM's dual-clutch tables (2023) name a carrier frequency outside 1500 to 2500 Hz for 150 ms (P2835). In Ford's DPS6 an out-of-order Hall pattern from a shift drum motor sets P2835 as well. Wiggle-testing the harness at the gearbox while watching live data is the usual way to find the spot. Steady electrical faults of the same sensor are P2E17 and P2E18.
c: Loose or corroded terminal at the actuator or gearbox connector
Harness rubbing on the housing, contact only under vibration
Sensor with an internal intermittent fault
s: Sporadic shift faults that disappear again
Warning lamp only now and then
Short limp-mode episodes

P2E1A.t: Drive Motor A Inverter Voltage Sensor A/B Correlation
P2E1A.d: P2E1A sets when the two DC voltage readings inside the drive motor A inverter, sensor A and sensor B, stop agreeing although they should describe the same high-voltage potential. Each value may pass its own range test; the fault lies in the mismatch. No manufacturer documents P2E1A publicly. Mitsubishi shows such a cross-check on the 2023 Outlander PHEV, where sensor A reads capacitor 1 and sensor B the main channel of capacitor 2: a gap of at least 50 V lasting 0.2 s is booked under the single-sensor codes P0D2E or P0E8D. Ford's 2019 hybrids file a gap above 60 V between the inverter input and output sensors under P0DA8. Two channels alone cannot show which one is wrong, so Mitsubishi adds the rear motor voltage as a third reference. Expect a warning and limited electric drive.
c: One of the two voltage measuring channels in the inverter has drifted
Fault in the inverter or power drive unit electronics
Poor high-voltage connection between the two measuring points
Control software with an unsuitable comparison window
s: Hybrid system or drive warning lamp, MIL possible
Reduced or no electric drive power
Further inverter voltage codes stored at the same time

P2E1B.t: Drive Motor A Phase X Current Sensor Circuit
P2E1B.d: P2E1B reports an electrical fault in the circuit of the phase X current sensor of drive motor A, without a separate low or high verdict. X, Y and Z name a second three-phase winding group: a Mitsubishi Electric patent on two-group motors for hybrid drives couples one current sensor to the conductor of each of the six phases. No manufacturer documents P2E1B publicly. Ford's 2019 hybrids supervise a reference voltage for the motor current sensors and flag it outside 4.5 to 6 V for 500 ms; a fault there would hit every phase at once. CARB allows a sensor mounted on a board inside a control unit to report wiring and range faults under one shared code, so P2E1B may stand in for P2E1D and P2E1E. Since the sensor sits in the inverter, the repair is usually that unit.
c: Phase X current sensor in the inverter failed
Reference supply or ground of the current sensors faulty
Loose or corroded low-voltage connector at the inverter
Defect on the motor control board that evaluates the sensor
s: Hybrid system warning lamp and MIL
Reduced electric drive or no electric drive
Rough or noisy motor operation under load

P2E1C.t: Drive Motor A Phase X Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2E1C.d: P2E1C means the phase X current sensor of drive motor A delivers a value that is electrically valid but implausible. No manufacturer documents P2E1C publicly; GM's U/V/W counterparts show the usual test, a zero check. While no current flows through the motor, the controller learns each sensor's offset: the 2016 Volt fails it above 30 A after 0.1 s, the Cadillac ELR in the same 2016 tables above 30 A within about 83 ms, a 2019 table above 35 A after 0.4 s, always Type A with MIL after one trip. A shifted zero distorts torque control and the phase balance. CARB wants rationality faults kept in a code of their own, apart from circuit and range faults (P2E1B, P2E1D, P2E1E). The X/Y/Z set only exists on motors with a second winding group. Sensor drift, heat damage or a weak reference are likely.
c: Zero offset of the phase X sensor has drifted
Sensor gain error after ageing or overheating
Unstable reference voltage for the current sensors
Fault in the measuring stage of the inverter control board
s: Hybrid warning lamp and MIL
Electric drive limited, uneven torque at low speed
Code returns after clearing at the next start

P2E1D.t: Drive Motor A Phase X Current Sensor Circuit Low
P2E1D.d: P2E1D says the phase X current sensor signal of drive motor A lies below its lowest valid value. Phase current flows in both directions, so the sensor reports a signed quantity; low therefore means a reading more negative than any real current, not a weak current. That other case, too little current in an energised phase, is P2C6A. No manufacturer documents P2E1D publicly. GM's U-phase counterpart on the 2016 Volt trips below -700 A for 0.05 s within a 0.1 s window, Type A, MIL after one trip. Such a value points to the measuring path: a signal shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a failed sensor inside the inverter. Where such a sensor sits is shown in a Mitsubishi Electric patent: on the lead from the inverter to the X winding. Expect a hybrid warning and reduced drive. High side: P2E1E.
c: Sensor signal shorted to ground inside the inverter
Supply voltage of the phase X sensor missing
s: Hybrid warning lamp and MIL
Sharp loss of electric drive power
Vehicle may only drive in a reduced mode

P2E1E.t: Drive Motor A Phase X Current Sensor Circuit High
P2E1E.d: P2E1E flags a phase X current sensor signal of drive motor A above the top of its valid range. No manufacturer documents P2E1E publicly. GM's U-phase counterpart on the 2016 Volt trips above 700 A for 0.05 s within 0.1 s, Type A. The same table stops real overcurrent at 600 A through P0C01, and Ford's 2019 hybrids treat more than 600 A for 400 microseconds as motor overcurrent. The sensor limit thus lies beyond any current the inverter would tolerate, so a reading that high almost always comes from the measuring side, for instance a signal shorted to the sensor supply or an open sensor ground. Genuine excess current in phase X is P2C6B. The inverter limits or stops drive. Low side: P2E1D.
c: Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply
Open ground of the phase X current sensor
Phase X current sensor failed high
s: Hybrid warning lamp and MIL
Electric drive cut off or strongly limited
Possible jolt when the inverter shuts down

P2E1F.t: Drive Motor A Phase Y Current Sensor Circuit
P2E1F.d: P2E1F stands for a circuit fault of the phase Y current sensor of drive motor A that is not sorted into a low or high case. No manufacturer documents P2E1F publicly, and even the U/V/W equivalents of this general code see little use: GM's 2013 to 2019 hybrid tables cover the phase sensors with offset, low, high and sum checks only, while Ford's 2019 hybrid summary says that current sensor faults of its motor inverter end up in the phase current codes P0A5D, P0A60 and P0A63 or in P0BFD. Which code a car stores for the same defect thus depends on the maker. Y is the middle phase of the second winding group; a Mitsubishi Electric patent gives each of X, Y and Z its own sensor. Check the inverter's low-voltage connector and supply first. Range check: P2E20; low and high: P2E21, P2E22.
c: Phase Y current sensor in the inverter failed
Poor contact at the inverter's low-voltage connector
s: Hybrid warning lamp and MIL
Electric drive limited or switched off
Other phase current codes may be stored as well

P2E20.t: Drive Motor A Phase Y Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2E20.d: P2E20 is set when the phase Y current sensor of drive motor A reads within its electrical limits but not believably. No manufacturer documents P2E20 publicly. Besides the zero check, a current balance can expose a sensor with a wrong gain. GM's eAssist table checks whether motor DC current and the input current of the accessory power module match the battery pack current; a mismatch above 40 A in 90 of 96 samples, taken every 2.08 ms, sets the U-V-W correlation code P0BFD as two-trip Type B. While a single sensor code is active, GM skips that balance and runs current control in a mode that does not rely on the sensors. The Mitsubishi Electric patent that defines X/Y/Z windings measures all six phase currents one by one. A drifting sensor or a disturbed reference is likely. X and Z range faults: P2E1C, P2E24.
c: Gain error of the phase Y sensor
Zero offset of the phase Y sensor shifted
Disturbed reference voltage of the current sensors
Motor control software needing an update
s: Hybrid warning lamp and MIL
Less electric assist, torque not as requested
Motor whine or slight vibration

P2E21.t: Drive Motor A Phase Y Current Sensor Circuit Low
P2E21.d: P2E21 records that the phase Y current sensor of drive motor A reports a value under the bottom of its scale. No manufacturer documents P2E21 publicly. GM's eAssist logic shows a clean way to test for this: the low and high checks of its U and W sensors run while PWM output is disabled, so the inverter is not switching and no phase current can flow. A reading below -440 A in 4 of 6 samples, one every 10.4 ms, then sets the U-phase code as two-trip Type B. Anything that far out at rest can only come from the measuring chain, for example a grounded signal line or a dead sensor supply. Too little real current in phase Y is a different fault, P2C6D. In a Mitsubishi Electric design, X, Y and Z form the second star-connected set. High side: P2E22; X and Z low: P2E1D, P2E25.
c: Phase Y sensor signal shorted to ground
s: Hybrid warning lamp and MIL
Electric drive limited
Engine runs more often than usual on hybrids

P2E22.t: Drive Motor A Phase Y Current Sensor Circuit High
P2E22.d: P2E22 is stored when the phase Y current sensor signal of drive motor A sticks above its upper limit. No manufacturer documents P2E22 publicly. On GM's 2016 Cadillac ELR the U/V/W counterparts fail above 800 A, judged as 4 bad samples out of 6 at 10.4 ms intervals, Type A. Notably, the V-phase checks only run while no U-phase sensor code is active, and W waits for V in the same way, presumably so that one shared fault does not set a code on every phase. If P2E22 shows up together with high codes of X or Z, look for such a common cause first, for example the sensor reference. On its own, a short between signal and supply line, or a lost sensor ground, is the likely culprit; real overcurrent in phase Y is P2C6E. Mitsubishi Electric's two-group motor patent lists a dedicated Y sensor beside those for X and Z. Low side: P2E21.
c: Phase Y signal shorted to the sensor supply
Open ground of the phase Y sensor
Shared sensor reference faulty, other phases affected too
s: Hybrid warning lamp and MIL
Electric drive switched off or strongly limited
High codes of other phases stored at the same time

P2E23.t: Drive Motor A Phase Z Current Sensor Circuit
P2E23.d: P2E23 points to a wiring or circuit defect around the phase Z current sensor of drive motor A that is not classed as low or high. Whether a Z sensor exists at all depends on the design. A Hyundai patent on hybrid motor drives notes that an inverter may carry three sensors or only two, since the three currents of a star winding cancel out and the controller can compute the missing one. A computed phase cannot raise a sensor circuit code, so P2E23 presumes a measured Z, as in the Mitsubishi Electric layout with one sensor each for X, Y and Z. No manufacturer documents P2E23 publicly. The Hyundai text also names loose connectors from vibration, heat and corrosion as typical disturbances of such sensors. Inspect the inverter's low-voltage plug first. Range: P2E24; low and high: P2E25, P2E26.
c: Loose or corroded low-voltage connector at the inverter
Phase Z current sensor in the inverter failed
Supply or ground of the Z sensor interrupted
s: Hybrid warning lamp and MIL
