c: Exhaust lifter of cylinder 7 stuck in the unlocked state
Oil pressure or oil quality inadequate for switching
Exhaust control valve slow or sticking
s: Check engine lamp on
Hard knock or jolt when cylinder 7 is reactivated
Possible misfire on cylinder 7 (P0307)

P3455.t: Cylinder 7 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3455.d: P3455 points to a ground fault on the line that would drive an exhaust-only actuator on cylinder 7. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. On GM V8 engines, AFM and DFM alike, a single lifter oil solenoid serves intake and exhaust of each cylinder, so a grounded line there sets the intake-side code P3451: the low-side driver is switched off, the output reads under 0.5 ohm to ground, and 20 of 25 checks taken every 250 ms must fail (Type B). On FCA's Hemi, MDS wiring rubbed through by the heat shield behind the driver-side head, next to cylinder 7, shows up as P3449. With its control line grounded, the actuator could switch on uncommanded, so the cylinder may lose its valve motion while fuel still flows. P3453 is the open, P3456 the short to power.
c: Actuator wire chafed through against the cylinder head or a heat shield
Actuator coil shorted to its housing
Output stage in the engine control module damaged
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder deactivation locked out
Rough running or misfire on cylinder 7 if the actuator pulls in unbidden

P3456.t: Cylinder 7 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3456.d: P3456 would flag a cylinder 7 exhaust valve actuator whose control line is shorted to supply voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. According to NHTSA's summary of the DFM system, GM drives its deactivation solenoids with peak-and-hold current drivers for fast, repeatable switching, and one solenoid serves both valves of the cylinder, so a short to power is caught under the intake-side code P3452 instead (below 0.5 ohm to power with the driver on, 20 of 25 samples, Type B). CARB requires such a check for any emission-relevant output, which is why the exhaust code exists at all. A short to ground on the same channel is P3455, an open circuit P3453, a mechanical fault P3454.
c: Actuator wire of cylinder 7 shorted to battery voltage
Exhaust actuator coil with shorted turns
Current driver in the control module failed
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine does not enter reduced-cylinder mode

P3457.d: Cylinder 8 is not among the cylinders that classic Active Fuel Management or Chrysler's MDS shut off (both use 1, 4, 6 and 7), so P3457 is documented only for newer designs. GM's 2019 tables list it for the L84 with Dynamic Fuel Management, which can deactivate every cylinder: more than 200 kohm with the low-side driver off, 20 of 25 samples every 250 ms from 425 rpm, Type B. GM's AFM/DFM information bulletin adds that the LTA and LT2 engines deactivate cylinders 2, 3, 5 and 8. GM also notes that some controllers store P3459 together with an open. P3458 is the function code for cylinder 8, P3459 and P3460 the short-circuit codes.
c: Wire to the cylinder 8 solenoid broken or chafed in the lifter valley harness
Open winding in the cylinder 8 solenoid
Poor contact at the solenoid connector
Engine control module output stage faulty
s: Check engine lamp on
Dynamic cylinder deactivation inhibited
P3459 may be stored alongside on some GM controllers

P3458.d: P3458 describes a cylinder 8 that does not deactivate or reactivate as commanded although its control circuit is electrically fine. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, the only maker with published cylinder 8 deactivation codes, files this failure under P349F on the L84: during a commanded skip, filtered manifold pressure stays above a threshold, which means the intake and exhaust valves kept working; the test runs with air charge above 120 mg and MAP/BARO between 0.30 and 0.95, and 22 failures in 25 opportunities give a Type B code. Bulletin 20-NA-204 adds that on 2021 full-size SUVs with L84 and L87 a voltage dip during cranking can set P349F without any hardware fault. Electrical faults are P3457, P3459 and P3460.
c: Cylinder 8 deactivation lifter not unlocking or relocking
Oil pressure too low or oil aerated
Cylinder 8 solenoid valve sluggish or its screen blocked
False entry after low voltage while cranking, fixed by ECM update (GM analogue 20-NA-204)
s: Check engine lamp on, sometimes going out again
Shake or roughness in light-load cruising
Misfire on cylinder 8 (P0308)

P3459.t: Cylinder 8 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3459.d: When the ground-side control line of the cylinder 8 deactivation solenoid touches ground, the ECM stores P3459. GM publishes this test for the 2019 L84 V8 with Dynamic Fuel Management: driver off, impedance below 0.5 ohm to ground, a minimum of 11 V on the relay feed and 425 rpm, 20 errors in 25 samples, Type B. Some GM controllers log P3457 at the same time. Because a DFM engine may skip any cylinder, a fault on cylinder 8 shuts down a system that otherwise uses this cylinder routinely; GM's LTA and LT2 also include cylinder 8 in their fixed deactivation set. A ground short on the solenoid's high-side feed has its own GM code, P311A. P3460 is the short to power.
c: Cylinder 8 control wire grounded through damaged insulation
Internal short in the cylinder 8 solenoid
Output driver in the engine control module damaged
s: Check engine lamp on after the second trip
Engine runs on all eight cylinders at all times
Higher fuel consumption

P3460.t: Cylinder 8 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3460.d: P3460 reports a short to supply voltage on the control circuit of the cylinder 8 deactivation solenoid, found while the output is switched on. GM lists it for the 2019 L84: under 0.5 ohm between output and controller power, 20 of 25 samples spaced 250 ms apart, Type B, with the same 11 V and 425 rpm enable limits as the other cylinder 8 circuit checks. GM's table contains a slip here: the strategy column for P3460 speaks of the cylinder 7 solenoid, while code and component name cylinder 8. Typical causes are harness damage against a feed wire or a solenoid with shorted turns; the visible result is that the engine stops using cylinder 8 deactivation. Siblings: P3457 (open) and P3459 (short to ground).
c: Cylinder 8 control wire in contact with a voltage source
Shorted turns in the cylinder 8 solenoid
Faulty driver in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder deactivation inactive, slightly higher fuel use

P3461.d: In the J2012 scheme, P3461 marks lost continuity to an exhaust-side actuator of its own on cylinder 8. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In the published sources, cylinder 8 is deactivated only by GM's newer V8s (DFM on the L84 and L87, a fixed 2-3-5-8 pattern on the LTA and LT2), and per NHTSA those engines feed both lifters of a cylinder from one solenoid, leaving no separate exhaust wiring to test. A GM patent application likewise uses one shared hydraulic valve and only staggers the exhaust valves ahead of the intake valves; only a separate exhaust actuator would fall under CARB's continuity check for output components. P3462 to P3464 are the other cylinder 8 exhaust codes, P3457 the intake-side open.
c: Wire or plug to the cylinder 8 exhaust actuator broken
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder deactivation no longer active

P3462.d: With P3462 the ECM would be saying that the exhaust valve of cylinder 8 ignores deactivation commands even though nothing is wrong electrically. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM covers the exhaust side of cylinder 8 on the 2019 L84 with its own code P3190, Cylinder 8 Trapped High Pressure Exhaust Charge: if crankshaft jerk, normalized by engine speed, exceeds a load-dependent threshold while the cylinder is deactivated, the exhaust valve is judged not to have opened, and 66 failures in 100 samples set a Type B code. Ford patented the complementary check for an exhaust valve that keeps opening after deactivation, based on exhaust pressure. Symptoms range from vibration in reduced-cylinder mode to a misfire on cylinder 8 (P0308).
c: Exhaust lifter of cylinder 8 failing to relock in time
Oil supply to the lifter gallery insufficient
s: Check engine lamp on
Vibration while cylinders are deactivated
Misfire on cylinder 8 (P0308)

P3463.t: Cylinder 8 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3463.d: P3463 would mean that the control line of a dedicated cylinder 8 exhaust actuator is shorted to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. On the only engines with documented cylinder 8 deactivation, GM's L84 and its relatives, one solenoid handles both valves, and GM reports a ground short on it as P3459, testing for less than 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver off. NHTSA's summary of the system lists solenoid driver circuit faults among the reasons the ECM inhibits deactivation, which is also what a driver would notice here: the engine keeps all eight cylinders running and uses a little more fuel. P3461 covers an open, P3462 the function and P3464 a short to power in this exhaust group.
c: Cylinder 8 exhaust actuator wire shorted to the engine block
Exhaust actuator shorted to ground internally
Driver stage in the engine control module faulty
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine stays on all eight cylinders

P3464.t: Cylinder 8 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3464.d: P3464 is stored once the line to a stand-alone cylinder 8 exhaust actuator sits at a high level, typically a wire touching battery voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. According to GM bulletin 20-NA-038, cylinder 8 is switched off only by DFM engines and by the LTA and LT2, whose fixed pattern is 2, 3, 5 and 8; classic AFM uses 1, 7, 6 and 4. On those engines a single solenoid also moves the exhaust lifter, and GM lists a short to power on it as P3460: with the low-side driver commanded on, less than 0.5 ohm to supply, 20 of 25 samples, Type B. Its malfunction text says cylinder 7, a copy slip in the 2019 table. The shorted output cannot pull in, so cylinder 8 simply stays active. P3463 is the ground fault.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 8 actuator touching a battery feed
Shorted turns in the actuator coil, resistance far too low
Output stage in the engine control module failed
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine keeps running on all eight cylinders, slightly higher fuel use

P3465.d: P3465 flags an open circuit to the actuator meant to shut down cylinder 9 or hold its intake valve closed. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Among such engines, Mercedes' M137 V12 (S 600 and CL 600, 1998 to 2002) had a shut-off system built around a solenoid pack and oil pressure tubes, whereas Audi's R8 V10 idles a whole bank by stopping injection and ignition. For orientation, GM treats the comparable circuit on its V8s as open above 200 kohm with the driver off, 20 failures in 25 samples. P3467 and P3468 cover shorts on the same line, P3466 a mechanical fault, P3469 the exhaust side of cylinder 9.
c: Broken or chafed wire to the cylinder 9 actuator
Open coil in the cylinder 9 solenoid
Loose or corroded connector at the solenoid pack
Output stage in the engine control module failed
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder shut-off no longer engages
Slightly higher fuel consumption at part load

P3466.d: P3466 is the plausibility test for cylinder 9: its actuator circuit is electrically sound, yet the cylinder fails to change state when the engine computer commands it. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. In valve-based systems the switching happens hydraulically; NHTSA's account of GM's design describes oil pressure moving locking pins inside the lifter. The Mercedes M137 V12, whose shut-off system relied on a solenoid pack and oil pressure tubes, is known for trouble with exactly those parts, exactly the kind of fault this code targets. Bank-switching V10 and W12 engines from Audi and Bentley leave the valves running and have nothing comparable to check. P3465, P3467 and P3468 are the electrical faults of cylinder 9.
c: Oil level, pressure or quality too poor to switch cylinder 9
Leak at the oil tubes or solenoid pack feeding cylinder 9
Solenoid valve slow or sticking mechanically
s: Check engine lamp on
Misfire count on cylinder 9 (P0309)
Rough running while switching between full and partial mode

P3467.t: Cylinder 9 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3467.d: With P3467 the control line of the cylinder 9 deactivation or intake valve actuator reads too low, which usually means it is touching ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Twelve-cylinder engines with cylinder shut-off do exist, for instance Mercedes' M137 and Lamborghini's Aventador V12 introduced in 2012, but no published diagnostic list connects this number to them. GM's matching test on its V8 engines looks for less than 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver switched off and only runs above 11 V and 425 rpm. On a low-side driven solenoid, a ground fault can keep the coil energised, so the cylinder may drop out when it should fire. Siblings: P3465 open circuit, P3468 short to voltage.
c: Cylinder 9 control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the cylinder 9 solenoid
Faulty driver in the engine control module
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder deactivation disabled
Possible misfire on cylinder 9 if the actuator stays energised

P3468.t: Cylinder 9 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3468.d: P3468 indicates that the control circuit for the cylinder 9 deactivation or intake valve actuator is pulled high, typically by a short to battery voltage that the module notices once it switches the output on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Most engines above eight cylinders that shut cylinders down, such as Audi's R8 V10 and Bentley's W12, do so bank by bank without dedicated valve actuators; Mercedes' M137 V12, by contrast, used a solenoid pack. GM's eight-cylinder version of this check counts below 0.5 ohm to controller power with the driver on, 20 of 25 samples. Expect the module to shut the output off and run all cylinders. P3465 (open) and P3467 (ground short) are the other electrical faults here.
c: Cylinder 9 control wire touching a supply wire
Shorted turns in the cylinder 9 solenoid coil
Output stage of the engine control module damaged
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine runs on all cylinders at all times

P3469.d: P3469 is set when the circuit driving a separate exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 9 is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. A distinct exhaust actuator only exists where intake and exhaust valves are switched independently; a GM patent at least shows that the exhaust valves can follow their own timing, being deactivated before the intake valves and reactivated before them too. GM's own production system uses one solenoid per cylinder for both valves, and the publicly described ten- and twelve-cylinder systems (Audi R8 V10, Bentley W12) keep the valves moving altogether. So an open circuit here can only concern an engine that carries such hardware. P3471 and P3472 report shorts, P3470 a functional fault, P3465 the intake side.
c: Open or chafed wire to the cylinder 9 exhaust actuator
Exhaust actuator coil of cylinder 9 open
Connector at the exhaust actuator loose or corroded
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder shut-off blocked

P3470.d: P3470 covers a cylinder 9 exhaust valve that does not follow its deactivation command although the control circuit shows no electrical fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. The risk behind it is described in a Ford patent: an exhaust valve that keeps opening after shut-off spoils the gas cushion in the cylinder and can be detected from changes in exhaust pressure. The opposite case, a valve that stays shut on reactivation, traps hot gas under pressure. Neither the Lamborghini Aventador V12 nor the Huracán V10 publishes how their bank shut-off works, and Audi's V10 simply cuts injection and ignition, so this check has no known user. Electrical faults of the same actuator: P3469, P3471, P3472.
c: Exhaust switching element of cylinder 9 stuck
Insufficient oil pressure for the exhaust switch
s: Check engine lamp on
Knock or jolt when cylinder 9 comes back in
Misfire on cylinder 9 (P0309)

P3471.t: Cylinder 9 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3471.d: A low reading on the control line of the cylinder 9 exhaust valve actuator triggers P3471, most often a wire grounded against the engine or body. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Because known shut-off systems on engines above eight cylinders either drop a whole bank by fuel and spark (Audi R8 V10) or close the valves with one shared actuator per cylinder (as in GM's design), a separately wired exhaust actuator on cylinder 9 would be unusual. If such a circuit is present, test it the same way as the intake circuit: resistance to ground with the connector unplugged, then the coil. P3469 is the open-circuit fault, P3472 the short to voltage, P3467 the matching intake code.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 9 grounded
Internal short in the exhaust actuator
s: Check engine lamp on
Partial-cylinder mode unavailable

P3472.t: Cylinder 9 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3472.d: P3472 records a high voltage level on the cylinder 9 exhaust valve control circuit, the pattern of a wire shorted to a supply feed or of a coil with shorted windings. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Engines that could in principle have a cylinder 9 with deactivation include the Mercedes M137 V12, the Lamborghini Aventador V12 and Bentley's W12; for none of them is a separate exhaust actuator documented, and the Bentley engine is described as leaving its valves working during shut-off. A US patent from GM shows that the exhaust side has a sequence of its own: there the exhaust valves stop before the intake valves and also return first. P3469 (open) and P3471 (low) complete the electrical set.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 9 shorted to voltage
Shorted windings in the exhaust actuator
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder deactivation switched off by the control module

P3473.d: P3473 reports an open circuit to the deactivation or intake valve actuator of cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. The V10 engines known for cylinder shut-off are Audi's 5.2 FSI in the R8 and Lamborghini's Huracán from model year 2016. Audi says its system idles one bank in the upper four gears by switching off injection and ignition, so it needs no valve actuator that this code could watch. On a twelve-cylinder engine with valve deactivation the code would mean a broken wire, an open coil or a bad connector at cylinder 10. P3475 and P3476 deal with shorts, P3474 with the mechanical result, P3477 with the exhaust valve.
c: Wire to the cylinder 10 actuator open or chafed
Corroded or loose connector at cylinder 10
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine no longer switches to reduced-cylinder mode

P3474.d: P3474 is about function rather than wiring: cylinder 10 should shut down or come back, but measured engine behaviour says it did not, while its control circuit is intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Audi's R8 V10, one of the few ten-cylinder engines with shut-off, works without valve switching; Audi reserves the valve-closing method with zero-lift cams on axially sliding sleeves for its 4.0 TFSI V8. Where valve deactivation is used, causes lie in the oil supply or in a sticking switching element, and NHTSA's description of GM's lifters with oil-pressure locking pins shows how small leaks spoil the switch. P3473, P3475 and P3476 are the electrical codes of cylinder 10.
c: Oil pressure or oil condition not sufficient to switch cylinder 10
Lifter or cam sleeve at cylinder 10 sticking
Oil screen or passage to the cylinder 10 actuator blocked
s: Check engine lamp on
Misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310)
Tapping noise from the valve train

P3475.t: Cylinder 10 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3475.d: P3475 points to a short to ground on the circuit that controls deactivation or the intake valve of cylinder 10. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. The Lamborghini Huracán's V10 runs on five cylinders at light load and the Aventador V12 on six below 135 km/h, yet neither maker publishes code-level diagnostics, and Audi's sister V10 manages without valve actuators. For a sense of the test, GM's eight-cylinder version of the low check needs below 0.5 ohm to ground while the output is off, sampled every 250 ms. Check the wire to cylinder 10 for chafing first, then the actuator itself. P3473 handles an open line, P3476 a short to voltage, P3479 the exhaust counterpart.
c: Cylinder 10 control wire grounded through chafing
s: Check engine lamp on
Reduced-cylinder mode unavailable
Possible misfire on cylinder 10

P3476.t: Cylinder 10 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3476.d: P3476 is logged when the control circuit of the cylinder 10 deactivation or intake valve actuator sits at too high a level, usually a short to a battery-fed wire found while the output is active. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. On the V10s that offer shut-off, Audi describes the bank being stopped by cutting fuel injection and ignition in the upper gears, so cylinder 10 has no valve actuator there. A twelve-cylinder engine with valve switching, such as Mercedes' M137 with its oil-pressure solenoid pack, is the kind of design this code was written for. The control module then usually blocks deactivation for the rest of the trip. Electrical siblings: P3473 and P3475.
c: Cylinder 10 control wire shorted to a supply
Cylinder 10 actuator coil with shorted turns
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder deactivation locked out for the drive

P3477.d: P3477 belongs to engines that switch the exhaust valve of cylinder 10 through its own actuator, and it reports that this actuator's circuit is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Ten-cylinder engines with shut-off, the Audi R8 V10 and the Lamborghini Huracán, deactivate a bank rather than individual valves; Audi names injection and ignition as what is stopped. GM's patent on valve deactivation shows that the exhaust side has its own timing requirement, with solenoid-driven hydraulic control valves stopping and restarting the exhaust valves ahead of the intake valves. Diagnose as a plain open circuit: connector, wire, coil. P3479 and P3480 are the shorts, P3478 the functional fault, P3473 the intake circuit.
c: Wire to the cylinder 10 exhaust actuator interrupted
Exhaust actuator coil of cylinder 10 open
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine keeps all cylinders active

P3478.d: P3478 describes a cylinder 10 exhaust valve that does not switch as commanded although its actuator circuit is fine. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. When an exhaust valve keeps working after shut-off, the trapped gas is pumped out and the cylinder cools, which a Ford patent proposes to catch through exhaust pressure. Cooling is also why Bentley alternates the idle bank of its W12 to protect cylinders and converter; Bentley, like Audi on the R8 V10, shuts down banks rather than individual valves. The code therefore only applies to engines with switchable exhaust valves, which none of the known V10 or V12 systems publicly use. P3477, P3479 and P3480 are the electrical faults.
c: Exhaust switching element at cylinder 10 stuck
Oil pressure too low for the exhaust switch
s: Check engine lamp on
Harsh jolt as cylinder 10 is reactivated
Misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310)

P3479.t: Cylinder 10 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3479.d: P3479 shows a short to ground, or another cause of a low signal, on the control line of the cylinder 10 exhaust valve actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Engines with ten or more cylinders that deactivate cylinders include Audi's R8 V10, Lamborghini's Huracán V10 and Aventador V12, and Bentley's W12; the published descriptions of all of them talk about whole banks, not about a valve actuator per cylinder. If an engine does carry one, the check mirrors the intake low test known from GM's V8s: resistance to ground with the output off. Repair is wiring or actuator work around cylinder 10. Siblings: P3477 (open), P3480 (high), P3475 (intake low).
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 10 shorted to ground
s: Check engine lamp on
Fuel-saving cylinder shut-off inactive

P3480.t: Cylinder 10 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3480.d: If the control line of the cylinder 10 exhaust valve actuator is held near supply voltage, the engine computer stores P3480. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. A ten-cylinder engine has no cylinder 11 or 12, so P3480 is the last exhaust-valve code a V10 could ever use; the R8 V10 still does without it because its shut-off works through injection and ignition. Sorting out a high circuit means looking for a wire chafed against a feed, a backprobe left in a connector, or a coil with shorted windings. P3477 (open) and P3479 (low) are the other electrical faults of this actuator, P3476 the intake equivalent on cylinder 10.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 10 shorted to a feed
Shorted windings in the exhaust actuator coil
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder shut-off disabled

P3481.d: P3481 marks an open circuit to the actuator for deactivation or the intake valve of cylinder 11, a cylinder only V12 and W12 engines possess. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Bentley's W12, the best documented twelve-cylinder with shut-off, stops one complete bank of six and, according to its engineering chief, leaves the valves operating; the ECU alternates between bank A and bank B using intake and exhaust sensor data so cylinders and catalytic converter stay warm. With no valve actuator, there is no circuit for P3481 to check. On a design that has one, it means a broken wire, connector or coil. P3483 and P3484 report shorts, P3482 the function, P3485 the exhaust side.
c: Wire to the cylinder 11 actuator broken
Actuator connector at cylinder 11 loose or corroded
Driver stage in the engine control module failed
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine stays on all twelve cylinders

P3482.d: P3482 is the functional check for cylinder 11: the actuator circuit is electrically fine, but the cylinder does not actually go dormant or wake up when told to. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Bentley's Bentayga and Continental W12 can run on six of twelve cylinders, yet the published description has the valves keep working, so a valve-switching failure cannot arise there. Engines that do close valves rely on oil pressure acting on switching lifters, as NHTSA's review of GM's lifter design lays out in detail; contaminated or low oil and worn locking pins are the usual reasons for a missed switch. The electrical counterparts on cylinder 11 are P3481, P3483 and P3484.
c: Contaminated or insufficient oil for switching cylinder 11
Worn or sticking locking pins at cylinder 11
Oil screen to the cylinder 11 actuator clogged
s: Check engine lamp on
Misfire on cylinder 11 (P0311)
Noticeable shudder when switching modes

P3483.t: Cylinder 11 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3483.d: P3483 is stored for a low signal on the control circuit of the cylinder 11 deactivation or intake valve actuator, in practice a short to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Cylinder 11 exists only on twelve-cylinder engines; among those with shut-off are Bentley's W12, Lamborghini's Aventador V12 and, historically, Mercedes' M137. GM's analogous V8 test treats under 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver off as a fault once 20 of 25 samples agree, with the enable conditions of 11 V system voltage and 425 rpm. A grounded line can energise the actuator continuously and take cylinder 11 out at the wrong time. Siblings: P3481 (open) and P3484 (high).
c: Cylinder 11 control line shorted to ground
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder shut-off disabled
Possible misfire on cylinder 11

P3484.t: Cylinder 11 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3484.d: P3484 signals that the control circuit of the cylinder 11 deactivation or intake valve actuator is too high, for example because its wire is shorted to a battery feed and the module detects it when switching the output on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Twelve-cylinder engines that shut down cylinders, notably the Bentley W12 in Bentayga and Continental GT and the Lamborghini Aventador V12, describe their systems as switching off a whole bank, with Bentley stating that the valves keep moving. P3484 thus fits only a design with a dedicated valve actuator at cylinder 11. The control module will normally cancel deactivation and run on all cylinders. P3481 and P3483 are the remaining electrical faults.
c: Cylinder 11 control wire touching battery voltage
Cylinder 11 actuator coil with shorted turns
s: Check engine lamp on
Reduced-cylinder mode cancelled

P3485.d: P3485 is triggered by an open circuit on a separate exhaust valve actuator at cylinder 11. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Bentley's engineers say their W12 shut-off leaves both valve sets working, and they rotate the dormant bank to keep it hot; Lamborghini's Aventador V12 and Audi's group V10 likewise talk only about banks. No published system on an engine of this size switches the exhaust valve of an individual cylinder. A GM patent explains why exhaust timing is a topic of its own: its hydraulic control valves deactivate the exhaust valves first and bring them back first. Electrically, treat P3485 like any open actuator line. P3487 and P3488 report shorts, P3486 a functional fault.
c: Open wire to the cylinder 11 exhaust actuator
Coil of the cylinder 11 exhaust actuator open
Connector at the exhaust actuator corroded
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine no longer drops to half its cylinders

P3486.d: P3486 flags a functional problem with the exhaust valve of cylinder 11: the circuit is healthy, but the valve does not reach the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. With a twelve-cylinder engine the consequences of a valve that keeps opening are that the cylinder pumps cold air through the exhaust and the converter cools, the issue Bentley avoids on its W12 by alternating banks. A Ford patent shows how such a leaking exhaust valve can be spotted from exhaust pressure. The reverse fault, a valve that stays shut, compresses trapped gas when the cylinder returns. As none of the known V12 or W12 systems switches valves individually, there is no documented user. P3485, P3487 and P3488 are the electrical faults.
c: Exhaust switching element of cylinder 11 jammed
Oil supply inadequate for exhaust switching
s: Check engine lamp on
Knock when cylinder 11 reactivates
Misfire on cylinder 11 (P0311)

P3487.t: Cylinder 11 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3487.d: P3487 would tell of a grounded control wire feeding a dedicated exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 11. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; cylinders 9 to 12 only exist on engines with nine or more, and J2012 keeps these codes for them. The closest real design is Mercedes' Active Cylinder Control on the CL 600 and S 600 V12 around 2000: it shut down one bank, and according to Wikipedia two solenoids uncoupled that bank's exhaust valves to keep pressure in the idle cylinders. That is one circuit per bank, not per cylinder. GM's V8 analogue flags a ground short below 0.5 ohm with the driver off. Grounded wiring could engage the actuator by itself and silence cylinder 11 when it is meant to fire. Siblings: P3485 (open), P3488 (high).
c: Actuator wire chafed through to engine ground
Actuator coil shorted to its housing
Moisture in the actuator connector bridging to ground
s: Check engine lamp on
Bank shut-off no longer offered
Possible misfire on cylinder 11 (P0311)

P3488.t: Cylinder 11 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3488.d: With P3488, the cylinder 11 exhaust actuator line sits too high, most often since the wire has picked up battery voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; cylinders 9 to 12 only exist on engines with nine or more, and J2012 keeps these codes for them. Later V12 and W12 designs give it no job: Bentley's W12 idles a bank of six with its valves still moving, while the Aventador from Lamborghini parks one bank under 135 km/h. Only Mercedes' V12 of around 2000 uncoupled exhaust valves, using two solenoids for that bank. GM's comparable V8 check calls a circuit high below 0.5 ohm to supply while the driver is on, 20 of 25 samples, Type B. The actuator then cannot be engaged, and the engine just runs on all cylinders. P3487 is the ground fault.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 11 actuator touching a battery feed
Shorted turns in the actuator coil
Output stage in the engine control module failed
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine stays on all twelve cylinders

P3489.d: P3489 reports that the circuit to the actuator for deactivation or the intake valve of cylinder 12, the highest cylinder number in this code series, is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Twelve-cylinder engines with shut-off span Mercedes' late-1990s V12, which deactivated every second cylinder in the firing order, Lamborghini's Aventador V12 that shuts down one cylinder bank below 135 km/h, and Bentley's W12. The Mercedes engine used a hydraulic solenoid pack, the kind of part such a circuit would drive; the bank-based systems publish no equivalent. Comparable logic on GM V8s calls a circuit open above 200 kohm with the output idle. P3491 and P3492 report shorts, P3490 a functional fault, P3493 the exhaust valve.
c: Wire to the cylinder 12 actuator open or chafed
Loose or corroded connector at cylinder 12
Output stage of the control module failed
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine no longer runs in reduced-cylinder mode
Somewhat higher fuel use on the highway

P3490.d: P3490 concerns the mechanical result on cylinder 12: the actuator circuit passes its electrical checks, but the cylinder does not deactivate or reactivate as intended. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. In a V12 up to six cylinders can be stopped, and on a valve-switching design the commanded state depends on oil pressure reaching the switching parts; Mercedes' M137 suffered exactly there, with failures of its solenoid pack and oil pressure tubes. Lamborghini's and Bentley's twelve-cylinder engines shut whole banks and publish no valve monitoring. NHTSA's GM lifter description explains what can stick: spring-loaded locking pins moved by oil. Electrical faults on cylinder 12: P3489, P3491, P3492.
c: Oil pressure or quality inadequate to switch cylinder 12
Leak in the oil supply to the cylinder 12 actuator
s: Check engine lamp on
Misfire on cylinder 12 (P0312)
Vibration at light load

P3491.t: Cylinder 12 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3491.d: A ground fault on the control line of the cylinder 12 deactivation or intake valve actuator produces P3491. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. The Aventador's cylinder deactivation system, introduced in 2012, shuts down one bank of six below 135 km/h, and Bentley's W12 drops one bank; neither publishes cylinder-level diagnostic codes. On GM V8s the corresponding low test watches for under 0.5 ohm to ground while the output is switched off, every 250 ms, and needs 20 hits in 25 samples. Because a grounded low-side line powers the actuator, the cylinder can be shut off against the module's will. P3489 (open) and P3492 (high) are the other circuit faults, P3495 the exhaust low.
c: Cylinder 12 control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the cylinder 12 actuator
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder shut-off blocked
Possible misfire on cylinder 12

P3492.t: Cylinder 12 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3492.d: P3492 records a high condition on the control circuit of the cylinder 12 deactivation or intake valve actuator, generally a short to a supply voltage seen while the output is commanded on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. The Variable displacement overview notes that a V12 can stop up to six cylinders, and the production engines doing so (Mercedes M137, Lamborghini Aventador, Bentley W12) differ widely in method, from a hydraulic solenoid pack (M137) to bank shut-off with the valves left running (Bentley). Only a design with valve actuators has a cylinder 12 actuator to short. Expect deactivation to be inhibited and the engine to run on all twelve. P3489 and P3491 are the electrical siblings, P3496 the exhaust high code.
c: Cylinder 12 control wire shorted to supply voltage
Shorted turns in the cylinder 12 actuator
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine runs permanently on twelve cylinders

P3493.d: P3493 applies to a separately controlled exhaust valve on cylinder 12 and reports that its actuator circuit is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Bentley's W12 and the Lamborghini Aventador V12 shut off banks; Bentley explicitly keeps the valves operating, and Lamborghini describes only the switch to six cylinders below 135 km/h. A GM patent treats the exhaust valves as a step of their own, stopping them before the intake valves, while GM's later production design drives both valves of a cylinder from one solenoid. An open exhaust circuit on cylinder 12 therefore points to a rare design. P3495 and P3496 are the short-circuit codes, P3494 the function, P3489 the intake side.
c: Wire to the cylinder 12 exhaust actuator open
Coil of the cylinder 12 exhaust actuator interrupted
s: Check engine lamp on
Partial-cylinder operation unavailable

P3494.d: P3494 is set when the exhaust valve of cylinder 12 does not follow its command although the actuator circuit is electrically intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Valve-based shut-off traps a charge in the cylinder; if the exhaust valve keeps opening, that cushion leaks away, which a Ford patent proposes to detect through exhaust pressure, and if it sticks shut on reactivation, compressed gas loads the valve train. The Aventador V12 and Bentley W12 sidestep this by bank shut-off without published valve switching, and for the Mercedes M137 with its hydraulic solenoid pack no public code assignment is known. Electrical faults of this actuator: P3493, P3495, P3496; intake function: P3490.
c: Exhaust switching element at cylinder 12 sticking
Oil pressure or quality insufficient for the exhaust switch
s: Check engine lamp on
Jolt or knock on reactivation of cylinder 12
Misfire on cylinder 12 (P0312)

P3495.t: Cylinder 12 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3495.d: P3495 points to a low signal, usually a short to ground, on the control line of the cylinder 12 exhaust valve actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. The twelve-cylinder engines with deactivation (Bentley W12, Lamborghini Aventador V12, Mercedes M137) are not documented with a dedicated exhaust actuator per cylinder; the newer ones shut entire banks and keep the valves moving, as Bentley states for its W12. Where such an actuator does exist, the diagnosis follows the usual path: connector unplugged, resistance of the wire to ground, then the coil itself. P3493 is the open circuit, P3496 the short to voltage, and P3491 the low fault on the intake side of cylinder 12.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 12 grounded
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder deactivation inactive

P3496.t: Cylinder 12 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3496.d: P3496 is the final code of the per-cylinder valve block: it marks the cylinder 12 exhaust valve control circuit as too high, typically a short to battery voltage or a coil with shorted turns. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Bentley built its last W12 in 2024 after describing a shut-off that idles one bank of six under part or trailing throttle, and the Lamborghini Aventador V12 shut one bank below 135 km/h; neither documents an exhaust actuator for cylinder 12. The clearest public account of exhaust valves following their own switching sequence remains a GM patent. Should the code appear, the module will disable deactivation. P3493 (open) and P3495 (low) complete the set, P3497 is the bank 2 system code.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 12 shorted to battery voltage
Shorted turns in the exhaust actuator coil
s: Check engine lamp on
Cylinder shut-off disabled

P3497.d: P3497 is the bank 2 counterpart of P3400: the control unit concludes that deactivation on the bank that lacks cylinder 1 is failing as a whole, and it blames no single cylinder circuit. Honda's VCM V6 links it to rocker arm oil pressure switch C (P3400 belongs to switch B); bulletin 13-055 for the 2013 Odyssey and Pilot shows both codes after cold starts with oil pressure above 92 psi, which moved the spool valves and cut cylinders the ECU had not selected. The fix there was a new relief valve spring. Ram lists P3497 for the 2023 5.7 l Hemi eTorque and cures it with PCM software (18-002-25). Expect a warning lamp, misfire codes and rough running during warm-up.
c: Low oil level, wrong grade or overdue oil change on bank 2
Excess oil pressure on cold start, e.g. weak relief valve spring
Switchable rocker arm or lifter on bank 2 sticking or not latching
Rocker arm oil pressure switch of bank 2 reporting wrongly
Engine control software needing an update
s: Check engine lamp on
Misfire codes on bank 2 cylinders, mostly after a cold start
Rough idle while the engine warms up
Reduced-cylinder mode no longer used, higher fuel use

P3498.d: P3498 flags a mechanical failure on cylinder 1: the control unit commanded it off, but its valves kept opening. This differs from P3402, which concerns the control side, and from the wiring codes P3401, P3403 and P3404. GM runs the check on its 5.3 l L84 and 6.2 l L87 Dynamic Fuel Management V8s by watching filtered manifold pressure every 90 crank degrees; if it stays above a threshold while cylinder 1 should be resting, 22 failures in 25 chances log a Type B code. Mazda's 2.5 l engines, which deactivate cylinders 1 and 4, show it together with P349B when a rocker arm has dropped out or broken (SA-041/18, SA-022/19); Mazda then authorises a replacement engine. Drivers notice the lamp, rough running or a loss of power.
c: Switchable rocker arm of cylinder 1 dropped out or broken (Mazda)
Deactivation lifter of cylinder 1 stays locked (GM DFM)
Lifter oil solenoid of cylinder 1 sticking or with protruding pole piece
Overdue oil changes or wrong oil grade
s: Check engine lamp on
Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 1 (P0301)
Clatter from the cylinder head and loss of power
Cylinder deactivation no longer used, higher fuel use

P3499.d: P3499 reports that cylinder 2 did not stop exchanging gas when told to deactivate. On GM's DFM V8s (L84, L87) one oil solenoid in the lifter valley feeds both lifters of the cylinder; oil pressure pushes spring-loaded pins inward which lets the outer lifter shell ride the cam while the valve remains closed. If those pins stay engaged, the engine computer sees manifold pressure that is too high during the skipped events and, after 22 of 25 failed opportunities, stores this Type B code. GM's 2019 Silverado and Sierra information PIP5584 names a faulty oil control solenoid as one cause. The electrical side of cylinder 2 has its own codes (P3409, P3411, P3412), and the control-performance code is P3410. Expect a lamp and lost economy.
c: Locking pins in the cylinder 2 lifters do not retract
Lifter oil solenoid of cylinder 2 not delivering oil pressure
Code stored without a real fault, ECM software update needed
s: Check engine lamp on
Higher fuel consumption because cylinder 2 is no longer skipped
Ticking from the lifter area

P349A.d: P349A states that cylinder 3 kept its valves working while the engine computer had switched it off. GM picks this up on its L84 and L87 V8s through manifold pressure that stays too high during the skipped strokes, Type B after 22 failed checks out of 25. Not every stored P349A means a worn lifter. For the 2021 Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and Escalade, GM explains (PIP5731, later bulletin 20-NA-204) that a voltage dip while cranking could make the ECM drop the deactivation outputs for one trip and log this code in history without a real defect; the cure is new ECM software and a road test with a warm engine at 30 to 45 mph. If it returns, the lifters and the solenoid of cylinder 3 need checking. P3418 covers the control side.
c: Voltage dip at cranking disabled the outputs, ECM software outdated
Deactivation lifter of cylinder 3 does not unlock
Lifter oil solenoid of cylinder 3 sticking
Low or aged oil slowing the switching
s: Code stored in history with no noticeable concern
Check engine lamp on if the fault is real
Ticking noise or higher fuel use

P349B.d: P349B is set when cylinder 4 fails to shut its valves on command. On Mazda's 2.5 l Skyactiv-G with cylinder deactivation (CX-5 and Mazda6, 2018-2019), cylinders 1 and 4 can be switched off; service alerts SA-041/18 and SA-022/19 tie P349B, P3498, P3400, P0304 and P0340 to a rocker arm that fell out of place or broke. Technicians are told to check the oil change records as well, and Mazda handles such cases with a replacement engine. GM's L84 and L87 use the code for cylinder 4 with the same manifold pressure test as for the other seven cylinders, Type B. Circuit faults would be P3425, P3427 and P3428, the control-performance code P3426. Expect noise from the head, rough idle and weak pull.
c: Rocker arm of cylinder 4 fallen out of place or broken (Mazda)
Long oil change intervals or unsuitable oil
Deactivation lifter of cylinder 4 stuck locked (GM DFM)
Oil control solenoid of cylinder 4 faulty
s: Rough idle and misfire on cylinder 4 (P0304)
Clatter or knocking from the valve cover area
Lack of power
Check engine lamp on

P349C.d: P349C means that cylinder 5 stayed active although the engine computer had requested a skip. GM documents it for its Dynamic Fuel Management V8s (L84 with 5.3 l, L87 with 6.2 l), where every cylinder may be skipped; the classic AFM V8s rest only cylinders 1, 7, 6 and 4. Detection compares filtered manifold pressure with a deactivation threshold, and a Type B code follows after 22 failures out of 25. For 2019 Silverado and Sierra trucks, GM's PIP5584 blames the lifter oil solenoid of the affected cylinder: replace it and inspect the remaining solenoids for a pole piece that stands proud of the surface. Wiring faults for cylinder 5 appear as P3433, P3435 and P3436. The driver sees the lamp and pays with higher fuel use.
c: Lifter oil solenoid of cylinder 5 faulty, pole piece protruding
Lifters of cylinder 5 do not unlock
Dirt in the oil blocking the solenoid or lifter bores
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine no longer skips cylinders, fuel use rises
Vibration at light load

P349D.d: P349D indicates that cylinder 6 drew in and pushed out air during events in which it should have stayed sealed. The test logic rests on a simple effect: every intake stroke leaves a dip in manifold pressure, so a resting cylinder should leave none. Ford's patent US8667835B2 and Delphi's US7314034B1 describe tracking these pulses event by event. GM applies the idea to its L84 and L87 V8s with filtered manifold pressure, 22 failures out of 25, Type B. The older GM AFM V8s also switch off cylinder 6, but there faults surface through the bank code P3400. Likely causes are a lifter whose locking pins do not release, a sticking solenoid or poor oil. P3442 is the control-performance sibling, P0306 the misfire code of this cylinder.
c: Locking pins of the cylinder 6 lifters do not release
Low oil level or degraded oil
Intake leak or MAP sensor fault distorting the pressure pulses
s: Check engine lamp on
Higher fuel use in light-load cruising
Ticking from the engine valley

P349E.d: P349E covers cylinder 7: deactivation was commanded, yet the cylinder kept its valve events. In GM's DFM design the intake lifter is unlocked first, while the exhaust lifter can only release once its cam lobe is back on the base circle; a sluggish pin therefore tends to leave the exhaust side working. GM's L84 and L87 check spots this through manifold pressure at each 90 degrees of crank rotation and stores a Type B code once 22 out of 25 opportunities have failed. Tula Technology, a specialist in skip-fire control, patented a check that combines intake pressure pulses with measured versus modelled crankshaft acceleration (US9891137B2). The wiring codes for cylinder 7 are P3449, P3451 and P3452. A driver may hear ticking and see the lamp.
c: Sluggish locking pin, mostly in the exhaust lifter of cylinder 7
Oil solenoid of cylinder 7 not opening fully
s: Ticking from the valve train
Check engine lamp on
Cylinder deactivation inhibited, higher consumption

P349F.d: P349F reports that cylinder 8 failed to go quiet when commanded. California's OBD rule requires makers to analyse every plausible hydraulic or mechanical failure of variable valve systems and mentions, among its examples, a lift-mechanism pin of one cylinder that will not shift; codes like this one follow from that duty. GM implements it for cylinder 8 on its L84 and L87 DFM V8s: filtered manifold pressure above the deactivation threshold in 22 out of 25 chances, rated Type B, so the lamp lights on the second faulty trip. GM's LT2 and LTA engines also rest cylinder 8, but no public GM table assigns P349F to them. Typical causes are a lifter stuck in its locked state, a failing oil solenoid or sludge. P3458 is the control-side code, P0308 the misfire code.
c: Lifter of cylinder 8 stuck in its locked state
Weak or sticking oil solenoid of cylinder 8
Sludge or debris in the lifter oil passages
Stored after a voltage dip at cranking, ECM software update needed
s: Check engine lamp on after two trips
Engine stays on all cylinders, fuel use rises
Ticking noise at idle

P34A0.d: P34A0 is reserved for a cylinder 9 that keeps its valves moving after the engine computer has ordered it off, which presumes an engine with at least nine cylinders and per-cylinder valve switching. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The twelve-cylinder engines with deactivation found so far work bank by bank; Bentley's W12 in the 2020 Bentayga Speed, for example, alternates between two complete banks of six. A monitor would work like GM's tests for cylinders 1 to 8 (P3498 to P349F), where manifold pressure that stays too high in skipped events reveals a cylinder that is still breathing. CARB requires such mechanical checks for valve control systems. P3466 is the control-performance code for cylinder 9.
c: Switching lifter or rocker of cylinder 9 stuck
Oil control valve for the deactivation not switching
s: Check engine lamp on
Rough running in reduced-cylinder mode
Higher fuel use

P34A1.d: P34A1 would mean that cylinder 10 kept opening its valves while it was supposed to be deactivated. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; it only makes sense on V10, V12 or W12 engines. Lamborghini, for instance, gave the Aventador LP 700-4 a Cylinder Deactivation System that rests one bank at speeds under 135 km/h, but no public diagnostic table lists P34A1. The physics of a check is shared with smaller engines: Ford's patent US8667835B2 watches the rise and fall of manifold pressure across successive intake events and compares it with the commanded pattern. Causes would mirror those of the V8 codes P3498 to P349F: a stuck switching element, a faulty oil control valve or poor oil. P3474 covers the control side of cylinder 10.
c: Switching element of cylinder 10 not unlocking
Oil level too low or oil aged
s: Check engine lamp on
Reduced-cylinder mode no longer offered
Uneven running at low load

P34A2.d: P34A2 names a mechanical deactivation fault on cylinder 11: the valves continued to operate although the cylinder had been switched off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The nearest production example is the Active Cylinder Control that Mercedes fitted to the 5.8 l V12 of the CL 600 and S 600 from 2001; it idled one bank and uncoupled its exhaust valves by means of two solenoids; a stuck switching element there would produce exactly the fault this code describes. For eight-cylinder engines GM uses P3498 to P349F, judged by manifold pressure and stored as Type B after 22 failures in 25 checks. P3482 is the control-performance code for cylinder 11, and a misfire there would be P0311.
c: Valve switching element of cylinder 11 jammed
Oil pressure supply to the switching parts disturbed
s: Check engine lamp on
Rough running when one bank is shut down
Higher fuel use

P34A3.d: P34A3 closes the series at the twelfth cylinder: cylinder 12 was commanded to deactivate, but its valves did not stop. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A dedicated check is needed because CARB's misfire definition excludes cylinders that are deliberately shut off, so the misfire monitor will not flag a skipped cylinder that still pumps air without fuel. Delphi's patent US7314034B1 confirms the state of each cylinder from the pattern of intake or exhaust pressure pulses, close to the principle GM applies to cylinders 1 to 8. On V12s that switch bank by bank, a defect would first show as rough running and a warning lamp. P3490 handles the control side of cylinder 12.
c: Lifter or rocker switching element of cylinder 12 stuck
Oil control valve of the deactivation sticking
s: Check engine lamp on
Rough running at light load
Higher fuel use

P34A4.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P34A4.d: P34A4 flags an electrical problem of any kind in the temperature sensor circuit of intake camshaft actuator A on bank 1: a wire broken somewhere, a plug that has worked loose, or a value no valid window accepts. Such a sensor belongs to electrically driven phasers; an Aisin patent places it on the motor driver board and reduces motor current once that board stays hot. NTN-SNR lists P34A4 as the inlet-side temperature sensor with an electrical fault. Nissan uses this family on the electric intake valve timing of the 2018 Pathfinder and QX60 but only publishes the range codes P34A5 and P34A9; a public text on P34A4 itself is not known. Without a valid temperature the controller can no longer guard the motor and normally restricts phasing. Low and high faults are P34A6 and P34A7.
c: Plug at the actuator loose or corroded, sensor wire broken
Temperature sensor in the actuator or its electronics failed
Fault in the module that drives the electric phaser
s: Check engine light on
Intake cam phasing on bank 1 restricted or held in its base position
Often no noticeable change while driving

P34A5.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Range/Performance Bank 1
P34A5.d: P34A5 means the temperature reported for intake cam actuator A on bank 1 passes the electrical checks yet makes no sense. Nissan describes the code for the 2018 Pathfinder (R52) and the Infiniti QX60 built before 18 December 2017: the MIL came on after starts at ambient temperatures around or below 0 °C. The remedy in bulletin NTB18-016 was a new electric intake valve timing control module with updated software, followed by a position learning run for the actuator; the revised bulletin NTB18-016a hands this over to the reprogramming campaign NTB18-072. Timing codes such as P0011 must be fixed before this one. Away from that software case, look for a drifting sensor or a loose contact. Drivers usually notice nothing. Bank 2 is P34A9.
c: Software of the electric valve timing module (Nissan 2018: cold-start false alarm)
Temperature sensor drifting out of its expected range
Intermittent contact at the actuator plug
s: Check engine light on, often after a cold start
Usually no driveability complaint

P34A6.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P34A6.d: With P34A6 the temperature signal from the intake cam actuator on bank 1 sits under its minimum. No source available to us names the sensor type. If it is the usual NTC thermistor, low voltage corresponds to high temperature, so a signal line shorted to ground or an internally shorted sensor looks to the module like an overheated actuator. Electric phasers guard their motor and driver against heat – Aisin describes cutting the current in stages while the board temperature stays high – so a false hot value can make the controller hold the phaser back. NTN-SNR names P34A6 as a too-small signal of the inlet temperature sensor. No carmaker publishes this code in detail. High is P34A7, bank 2 P34AA.
c: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed at the cylinder head)
Actuator really overheated by a sluggish phaser
s: Check engine light on
Intake phasing on bank 1 limited, less pulling power

P34A7.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P34A7.d: P34A7 is set when the temperature sensor of intake camshaft actuator A on bank 1 delivers a voltage above its upper limit. Most often the sensor wire or its ground is interrupted, or the signal touches a supply voltage; with an NTC-type sensor this reads as an implausibly cold actuator. The module then lacks a usable value for its thermal protection and usually switches to a cautious phasing strategy. NTN-SNR assigns P34A7 to the inlet camshaft adjustment with too high a signal. Nissan fits such sensors to the electric intake phaser of the 2018 Pathfinder and QX60 but has not published this particular code. Check the actuator plug and the harness routing over the engine first. Low is P34A6.
c: Signal or ground wire of the sensor interrupted
Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage
s: Check engine light on
Intake phasing on bank 1 reduced
Mostly no noticeable effect while driving

P34A8.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P34A8.d: P34A8 mirrors P34A4 on bank 2: the module detects an open or otherwise faulty circuit at the temperature sensor of intake cam actuator A on the side without cylinder 1. Only V and boxer engines have this bank. The one documented user of the family, Nissan's electric intake valve timing on the 2018 Pathfinder and QX60, monitors both banks separately (range codes P34A5 and P34A9), yet P34A8 itself turns up in no manufacturer document we could find. NTN-SNR describes it as an electrical fault of the inlet-side temperature sensor on the second bank. Typical findings are a corroded plug, a chafed harness near the cylinder head or a failed sensor. Range, low and high are P34A9, P34AA and P34AB.
c: Plug at the bank 2 actuator corroded or not latched
Harness chafed near the cylinder head
s: Check engine light on
Intake phasing on bank 2 restricted

P34A9.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Range/Performance Bank 2
P34A9.d: P34A9 covers the plausibility check of the temperature sensor at intake cam actuator A on bank 2. Nissan names it together with P34A5 in bulletins NTB18-016 (2018 Pathfinder) and ITB18-009 (2018 QX60): vehicles built before 18 December 2017 could store one or both codes and switch on the MIL when started in freezing weather. Nissan traced this to the electric intake valve timing control module and first replaced the module with one carrying newer software; a later revision moved the fix to a reprogramming campaign. If P0021 or other timing codes are stored, they take priority. Outside this case, a sensor whose reading wanders or a poor contact at the bank 2 actuator are the candidates. Bank 1 is P34A5.
c: Poor contact at the bank 2 actuator plug
s: Check engine light on after a start in freezing weather
Engine runs normally in most cases

P34AA.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P34AA.d: P34AA reports that the temperature sensor of the bank 2 intake cam actuator signals a voltage below its permitted range. Whether that equals a hot reading depends on the sensor design, which no public source names; with the common NTC thermistor it would mimic overheating, and the controller could limit the actuator current or stop phasing on that bank. In practice a signal wire grounded against the cylinder head, cables pinched during earlier engine work or a shorted sensor are the usual suspects. NTN-SNR lists P34AA as too small a signal of the inlet temperature sensor on the second bank; a manufacturer text is not public. Compare bank 1 (P34A6) and the high code P34AB.
c: Signal wire grounded against the cylinder head
Cables pinched during earlier engine work
s: Check engine light on
Intake phasing on bank 2 suspended, slightly less power

P34AB.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P34AB.d: P34AB stands for a voltage above the upper limit at the temperature sensor of intake cam actuator A, bank 2. An interrupted signal or ground line is the classic cause, as is a short to a higher voltage; a plug pushed off during a service visit often explains it. Because the actuator motor warms up under load, the controller depends on this value – the Aisin patent lowers the current step by step while a high temperature persists – and without it the bank 2 phaser is usually held back. NTN-SNR names the code for the inlet side of the second bank; no carmaker publishes it. The bank 1 equivalent is P34A7, the low code P34AA.
c: Plug at the actuator off or not latched after service
Signal shorted to a higher voltage
s: Check engine light on
Intake phasing on bank 2 held back

P34AC.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor A Circuit Bank 1
P34AC.d: P34AC covers any electrical fault in the circuit of position sensor A of the intake cam actuator on bank 1. On engines with an electric intake phaser this sensor tells the controller where the drive motor stands. Mitsubishi has the code in its 2022 Outlander manual: the electric intake valve timing module logs it when the sensor voltage is too low or too high for one second or longer, and names wiring with an open or short as well as the actuator itself. In fail-safe the phaser is parked at its base angle, the intake runner valve opens, EGR stops and the cold-start stratified mode is dropped. The check runs once the engine has been above 2,000 rpm for a second and first appears as a pending code. Low and high are P34AE and P34AF.
c: Actuator harness open or shorted, plug loose
Position sensor in the electric actuator failed (actuator replacement)
Electric valve timing control module faulty
s: Check engine light on
Intake cam held in its base position, less torque at low revs
Rougher cold start, slightly higher consumption

P34AD.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor A Range/Performance Bank 1
P34AD.d: P34AD covers a plausibility fault: the position sensor A signal from the intake actuator on bank 1 is electrically present but does not agree with what else the module knows. On the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander, which turns its intake phaser electrically, the control module checks the motor position against the phase seen by the intake camshaft sensor and logs P34AD when the two disagree; wiring faults and the actuator are given as causes. In practice a worn or slipping actuator, a position that was not relearned after repairs or a disturbed cam signal come first; Nissan, which uses the same kind of electric intake valve timing, requires a position learning run after module replacement. The phaser then stays at its base angle.
c: Electric actuator worn, sticking or slipping
Actuator position not relearned after repair
Intake camshaft sensor signal or timing drive disturbed
s: Check engine light on
Intake cam timing fixed, weaker response at low revs
Possibly accompanying timing codes such as P0011

P34AE.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor A Circuit Low Bank 1
P34AE.d: P34AE says the voltage from position sensor A on the bank 1 intake side remains under its minimum. The 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander, whose intake cam is moved by an electric motor, evaluates the code in the electric valve timing module and points to an open or shorted actuator circuit or a faulty actuator; unlike the circuit and high codes, no delay time is stated. Typical findings are a signal line touching ground, a missing sensor supply or a shorted Hall element in the motor. The module then stops phasing and keeps the intake cam at its base angle, which costs low-end torque; because the stratified cold start is also dropped, starts from cold may run rougher. P34AF is the high code, P34B2 the bank 2 code.
c: Hall sensor in the actuator motor shorted (actuator replacement)
s: Check engine light on
Less pulling power at low revs
Rougher running after a cold start

P34AF.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor A Circuit High Bank 1
P34AF.d: P34AF is logged when position sensor A on the bank 1 intake phaser reports a voltage above its upper limit for at least one second. Mitsubishi covers the code in its 2022 Outlander manual and, besides the harness, points to the Hall sensor of motor 1 in the electric actuator – a hint that position sensor A is a Hall element inside the phaser motor. A broken ground lead of the sensor, a signal line in contact with supply voltage or a dead Hall sensor are the usual causes; since the sensor is built into the actuator, a sensor fault normally means a new actuator. Fail-safe parks the intake phaser at its base angle, opens the intake runner valve and switches off exhaust gas recirculation. Low is P34AE, bank 2 P34B3.
c: Sensor ground open or plug corroded
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Hall sensor of the actuator motor failed (actuator replacement)
s: Check engine light on
Intake phaser held in its base position, reduced power
Slightly higher fuel consumption

P34B0.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor A Circuit Bank 2
P34B0.d: P34B0 concerns the electrical circuit of position sensor A of the intake cam actuator on bank 2, so it only concerns V and boxer engines. No manufacturer publishes it. Mitsubishi documents the bank 1 code P34AC for the 2022 Outlander, which uses only the bank 1 codes: there the sensor reports the angle of the electric phaser motor, and a voltage outside its window for a second sets the fault. A two-bank engine with electric phasers would watch its second actuator in the same way. Mercedes, by contrast, files the sensors of its CAMTRONIC lift actuators under the position sensor A codes of camshaft B (P34BD, P34BE), so what the actuator is depends on the maker. Check plug, harness and actuator on bank 2.
c: Plug or harness to the bank 2 actuator open or shorted
Position sensor in the actuator failed
s: Check engine light on
Bank 2 intake phasing held in its base position
Possibly less power and uneven running between banks

P34B1.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor A Range/Performance Bank 2
P34B1.d: P34B1 means the intake-side position sensor A of bank 2 delivers an electrically sound but implausible value. No public manufacturer document uses this code. The nearest published example is the bank 1 code P34AD on the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander, where the electric phaser module checks the motor position against the intake camshaft sensor and flags a mismatch. Mercedes uses the same fault type on the exhaust side for its CAMTRONIC lift actuators (P34BD, P34C1); bulletin LI05.20-P-080192 answers it with an engine software update and actuators of a newer part number. On bank 2 an actuator that binds or has worn, a lost learned position or a camshaft signal problem (compare P0021) are likely. The bank 2 phaser is then locked at its base angle.
c: Actuator on bank 2 sticking or worn
Learned actuator position lost or software outdated
s: Check engine light on
Bank 2 intake timing fixed, reduced power
Possibly further timing codes such as P0021

P34B2.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor A Circuit Low Bank 2
P34B2.d: P34B2 is set when position sensor A on the intake phaser of bank 2 delivers a voltage below its permitted window. Public manufacturer information on this code is lacking. On the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander the bank 1 version P34AE is evaluated by the electric valve timing module and traced to the actuator circuit or the actuator. Mercedes calls the corresponding low code of its CAMTRONIC exhaust sensors on bank 2 (P34C2) a ground short and, in bulletin LI05.20-P-080192, has the engine harness by the bulkhead inspected for scorching. A grounded signal wire, a missing sensor supply or a shorted sensor are therefore the first things to rule out on bank 2. High is P34B3, bank 1 P34AE.
s: Check engine light on
Bank 2 intake phasing switched off
Possibly codes from other sensors on the same supply

P34B3.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor A Circuit High Bank 2
P34B3.d: P34B3 marks a signal above the upper limit from position sensor A on the intake phaser of bank 2. An interrupted ground, a signal wire touching a supply voltage or a worn-out sensor are the usual findings. No carmaker publishes the code. The nearest documented case is Mitsubishi's bank 1 code P34AF on the 2022 Outlander: the high value must persist for at least a second, and the Hall sensor of the actuator motor is listed as a possible cause. With an electric phaser the sensor therefore sits inside the actuator, and a sensor fault usually means replacing the actuator. NTN-SNR lists P34B3 as the inlet-side position sensor A on the second bank with too high a signal. The engine keeps running with the bank 2 phaser at its base angle.
c: Signal wire touching a supply voltage
Hall sensor in the actuator defective (actuator replacement)
s: Check engine light on
Bank 2 intake phaser held at its base angle

P34B4.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P34B4.d: P34B4 reports that the circuit of the temperature sensor on camshaft actuator B, bank 1, cannot be evaluated: an open line, a disconnected plug or a reading that fits no valid state. In the supplier list of NTN-SNR the letter B stands for the outlet camshaft, so the code targets an exhaust phaser turned by an electric motor whose electronics need heat protection. An Aisin patent mounts such a sensor on the motor control board and calls the intake shaft merely an example. We found no carmaker that publishes P34B4; the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander, for instance, drives only its intake cam electrically and shifts the exhaust cam with an oil control solenoid. Expect restricted exhaust phasing until the circuit is repaired. Low and high faults: P34B6, P34B7.
c: Plug at the exhaust actuator not seated or wire broken
Temperature sensor in the actuator electronics failed
Faulty input stage in the controlling module
s: Malfunction indicator lamp lit
Exhaust cam timing on bank 1 fixed or limited
Driving usually unaffected

P34B5.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Range/Performance Bank 1
P34B5.d: P34B5 is the rationality check for the temperature reading of exhaust-side actuator B on bank 1: the circuit is intact, yet the value or its behaviour is not believable. CARB asks for such checks on VVT input sensors wherever feasible, ideally catching readings that are wrongly high as well as wrongly low. How a carmaker judges this reading is not public, and no maker publishes P34B5 at all. The intake twin P34A5 shows a likely pattern: Nissan traced cold-start alarms on the 2018 Pathfinder to module software and cured them with an update. The value matters because, in Aisin's patent, a board temperature above a release threshold for a set time moves the phaser off its end stop to cut holding current. Bank 2: P34B9.
c: Module software judging the value wrongly (update available?)
Temperature sensor in the actuator drifting
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, sometimes only after a cold start
No noticeable change in engine behaviour in most cases

P34B6.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P34B6.d: Circuit Low means the voltage on the signal wire of the exhaust actuator B temperature sensor (bank 1) stays under its lower limit. Which temperature that stands for depends on a sensor curve that no public source gives; with a thermistor whose resistance falls as it warms, a short to ground would look like extreme heat. Aisin's patent shows what a hot reading triggers: the controller lowers the motor current and may even switch the motor off at a preset threshold, so exhaust phasing loses authority. In the NTN-SNR catalogue P34B6 appears as an undersized outlet-side signal. Wires rubbing on the cylinder head and a sensor shorted inside are the main suspects. No carmaker documents P34B6. High: P34B7; bank 2: P34BA.
c: Signal wire chafed through and touching ground
Sensor element shorted inside the actuator
Actuator driver genuinely overheated by a binding phaser
s: Malfunction indicator lamp lit
Exhaust phasing on bank 1 reduced, slightly rougher idle possible

P34B7.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P34B7.d: P34B7 sets when the heat reading delivered by exhaust actuator B, bank 1, sits above its upper limit. Electrically this points to an open signal line, a detached sensor ground or contact with battery or reference voltage; with a negative-coefficient element the module would see an implausibly cold actuator. A cold reading harms nothing by itself, but it robs the controller of its heat protection – in Aisin's design the reading decides when the holding current at the end stop must be cut back – so the module will typically stop relying on electric phasing. NTN-SNR describes P34B7 as an excessive outlet-side signal. No manufacturer text on this code is published. CARB obliges the OBD system to recognise such open or shorted circuits. Low counterpart: P34B6.
c: Signal line or sensor ground interrupted, plug corroded
Signal line shorted to a supply wire
Sensor element open inside the actuator
s: Malfunction indicator lamp lit
Exhaust cam on bank 1 held in its default position

P34B8.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P34B8.d: P34B8 is the circuit fault for the heat sensor inside exhaust camshaft actuator B of bank 2, the row without cylinder 1 on a V or flat engine. If P34B4 is stored at the same time, a shared feed, a common ground or the control module is more likely than two failed sensors at once. The code family presumes an electrically driven exhaust phaser with its own heat-sensitive driver: NTN-SNR files it under outlet camshaft adjustment, and Aisin's patent explains why such a driver carries a temperature sensor at all. A carmaker using P34B8 could not be found in bulletins or official service information. In practice: check plug and harness on bank 2 first, then the actuator itself. For a signal stuck low or high on bank 2 see P34BA and P34BB.
c: Connector or harness at the bank 2 exhaust actuator open
Shared supply or ground faulty (when bank 1 also reports)
Temperature sensor in the bank 2 actuator failed
s: Malfunction indicator lamp lit
Exhaust phasing on bank 2 restricted, banks may run slightly unevenly

P34B9.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Range/Performance Bank 2
P34B9.d: With P34B9 the bank 2 exhaust actuator reports a temperature that is electrically valid but does not make sense. A two-bank engine offers an obvious yardstick: after a long cold soak both exhaust actuators should read almost the same, and under equal load they should warm alike. Whether any carmaker applies such logic to P34B9 is not published; the code appears only in lists such as the one from NTN-SNR. CARB requires VVT input components to be checked for rationality where feasible, not just for open and shorted circuits. A drifting sensor, a contact resistance that shifts the reading or outdated module software are the plausible causes. In Aisin's design a false hot value would cut motor current needlessly. Bank 1: P34B5.
c: Contact resistance at the plug shifting the value
s: Malfunction indicator lamp lit
Usually no change in driveability

P34BA.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P34BA.d: P34BA tells that the temperature signal from bank 2's exhaust actuator is pulled under its lower limit. Typical sources are a signal wire that has found ground, for instance where the harness runs close to hot exhaust parts, or a sensor element shorted inside the actuator. If the controller reads the low voltage as heat, it protects the actuator by reducing its current, as Aisin describes, so the bank 2 exhaust timing may no longer follow its target and timing codes such as P0024 can follow. The code is catalogued by NTN-SNR; no maker publishes it, so any threshold remains unknown. Repairs range from mending a wire to replacing the actuator, because the sensor sits in its electronics. Bank 1 low: P34B6; bank 2 high: P34BB.
c: Harness near exhaust parts damaged, signal shorted to ground
Sensor element shorted inside the bank 2 actuator
Input of the controlling module faulty
s: Malfunction indicator lamp lit
Bank 2 exhaust timing limited, possibly with additional timing codes

P34BB.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
