U0112.t: Lost Communication With Battery Energy Control Module B
U0112.d: U0112 is logged when a second battery energy control module, B, stops talking on the bus while a partner still waits for its data. Mitsubishi's 2018 Outlander PHEV is a documented case: the main battery management unit (BMU) supervises a sub-BMU inside the traction pack and stores U0112 once that unit's frames have been missing for 0.3 s, after the BMU has seen 8–16 V for more than 2 s; the check follows drive-cycle pattern 1, and the CAN pair between the two units should measure 100–140 Ω. VW's 2014 Touareg Hybrid lists the code for absent BECM messages, and GM's Saab 9-4X list assigns it to its battery module. Module A has U0111. Typical results are a hybrid warning, less electric range or no READY.
c: Open, shorted or chafed CAN lines between main and sub battery module inside the pack
Corroded or loose connector at the traction battery
Battery module B internally faulty or without supply
s: MIL or hybrid system warning
Reduced electric range or electric drive unavailable
Vehicle does not reach READY

U0113.t: Lost Communication With Emissions Critical Control Information
U0113.d: Unlike its neighbours, U0113 does not name one unit but a class of data: messages a controller depends on for emission control, for instance torque, speed or aftertreatment status supplied by another node. CARB's OBD II rule wants silence from a digital input recognised as a fault of its own with a dedicated code, and U0113 is the generic slot for that situation. Ford's 2014 five-digit code interpretation for its engine controllers includes U0113; which frames belong to it and how long they may be absent is not published by any maker. Implausible data of the same kind falls under U0441. Because the engine then has to use substitute values, a lit MIL and possibly reduced power are the likely outcome.
c: Fault in the CAN wiring or connectors carrying the emission-related frames
Sending module without power, ground or wake-up
Software or configuration mismatch after module replacement or update
s: MIL on
Engine on substitute values, possibly reduced power
Further U codes in other modules

U0114.t: Lost Communication With Four-Wheel Drive Clutch Control Module
U0114.d: U0114 says the controller of a four-wheel-drive clutch has gone quiet. Such a unit sets how much torque reaches the secondary axle by clamping a multi-plate coupling, as in Haldex-type on-demand drivelines whose later generations carry their own integrated electronics. It needs wheel speeds, engine torque and brake status from the bus and is usually missed by the engine, transmission or ABS controller. Ford's 2014 powertrain code interpretation lists U0114, but no maker publishes timing or lamp logic for it. A transfer case controller has U0102, a complete all-wheel-drive module U011D, invalid clutch data U0414. In practice the car drives on one axle with an AWD warning; engine running and emissions stay unaffected.
c: Clutch module without power or ground (fuse, connector near the rear axle)
Water or corrosion in the module connector exposed under the car
Chafed or open CAN lines to the rear of the vehicle
s: AWD/4WD warning in the cluster
Drive only on the primary axle, wheelspin on slippery roads
Possibly stability control warning

U0115.d: U0115 is set when a second engine or powertrain controller, ECM/PCM B, vanishes from the bus; U0100 belongs to unit A. What B stands for depends on the maker: GM's Saab 9-5 and 9-4X lists call it ECM 2, Mercedes-Benz assigns U011500 to its drivetrain control unit. In the 2021 S 580, the 48 V integrated starter alternator logged U0115 with U0168 because of its own software; the MIL went out after three drive cycles, release 20.B cured it (LI15.40-P-073663). The DC/DC converter of the EQB and electric G-Class records it after wake-up faults (LI54.10-P-079533). Mazda (09-027-26) sees it on the CX-90/CX-70 PHEV, together with P0AB9, as a cold-weather no-READY caused by moisture at luggage-area connector 3002-411.
c: Software fault in the reporting or the B controller (updates released)
Water ingress or corroded terminals on the bus or relay connectors
Controller B not powered or not woken up in time
s: MIL or engine/drive system warning
No start or no READY on hybrids
Often no driveability complaint when the code is software-related

U0116.t: Lost Communication With Coolant Temperature Control Module
U0116.d: U0116 means a module no longer hears the coolant temperature control module, a separate controller for engines with electronically managed cooling. Depending on the design it may command electric pumps, map-controlled valves or fans and pass coolant status on to the engine controller. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; its companions P25AF (MIL request from that module) and U0456 (invalid data from it) are likewise known only from code lists. The basis is CARB's rule that missing communication from a digital input gets its own code, plus the general principle that electronic engine controls cut power when temperature control is uncertain. Expect a temperature or cooling warning and, as a precaution, reduced engine output.
c: Cooling module without power or ground (fuse, relay, ground point in the engine bay)
Heat-damaged or corroded connector near the engine
Damaged CAN or LIN wiring to the module
Coolant temperature control module internally faulty
s: Engine temperature or cooling system warning
Cooling fan or electric pump running continuously
Reduced engine power as protection

U0117.t: Lost Communication With PTO Control Module
U0117.d: U0117 points to a lost link with the power take-off (PTO) control module, which engages and governs an engine-driven output for auxiliary equipment such as a tipper body, aerial bucket or recovery winch. CARB defines such a PTO unit and lets the engine controller pause monitor counters while it runs, so dependable PTO status on the bus matters for OBD bookkeeping. Saab's 2011 9-5 and 9-4X U-code lists, both taken over from GM's global electrical architecture, carry the code as loss of the power take-off control module; neither these nor any other maker's documents give timing or lamp rules. U0465 stands for invalid PTO data, P064B for a PTO module fault. For the operator the attached equipment cannot be engaged or its engine-speed control drops out.
c: Faulty upfitter wiring or connector between chassis and PTO controller
PTO module without power or ground
Vehicle configuration expects a PTO module that is missing or not programmed
s: PTO cannot be engaged or disengages
Elevated idle or remote engine speed control unavailable
Warning message in the cluster

U0118.t: Lost Communication With Fuel Additive Control Module
U0118.d: U0118 concerns the fuel additive control module, which on some diesel cars meters a fuel-borne catalyst from a separate tank into the fuel. The additive lowers the temperature at which trapped soot burns in the particulate filter from above 600 °C to roughly 350–450 °C. If the engine controller no longer receives this module, it cannot be sure that dosing continues, and the regeneration strategy loses its footing. No manufacturer documents U0118 publicly; the text rests on CARB's requirement for a separate lack-of-communication code and on the known function of fuel-borne catalysts. Neighbours are U0467 (invalid data), P2584 (MIL request) and P2585 (warning lamp request) from the same module. Left unrepaired, the filter tends to clog, bringing a DPF warning and reduced power.
c: Additive module unplugged or its fuse removed, e.g. after filter work
Corroded connector at the additive tank or module under the vehicle
Damaged CAN wiring to the additive module
Fuel additive control module internally faulty or not coded
s: MIL and particulate filter warning
Regeneration fails, filter loads up
Reduced power in later stages

U0119.t: Lost Communication With Fuel Cell Control Module
U0119.d: U0119 is the slot for losing the fuel cell control module, the controller that runs the hydrogen stack of a fuel cell vehicle: air compressor, hydrogen supply, humidity, stack cooling and the electrical output handed to the drive. Older code tables still label U0116–U0120 as reserved, so some scan tools show no text for it. No manufacturer documents the code publicly; Toyota, Hyundai and Honda have sold series fuel cell cars, yet their service data are not open. As a general frame, CARB asks for a dedicated code whenever a digital partner falls silent. U0468 covers invalid data from the same module, U0293 the hybrid/vehicle system controller. Once the link drops, the vehicle controller cannot request stack power: expect a system warning, operation only from the buffer battery or no READY.
c: Fuel cell controller without 12 V supply or ground
Damaged CAN wiring or connector between stack controller and vehicle controller
Software fault or missing update in one of the controllers
Fuel cell control module internally faulty
s: Fuel cell or drive system warning
Power limited to the buffer battery
Vehicle does not reach READY

U011A.t: Lost Communication With Exhaust Gas Sensor Module A
U011A.d: U011A appears when the engine controller loses exhaust gas sensor module A, the electronics that heat and evaluate a wide-band oxygen probe (or a similar exhaust sensor) and send the result as bus data instead of analogue signals. Chrysler's bulletin 25-002-14, which replaces 25-003-13 and 25-004-13, lists it for 2010–2012 Ram 2500/3500 pickups with the 6.7 L Cummins among oxygen-sensor faults; the prescribed fix is an overlay harness with new connectors at the sensor module before any part is changed. Module B has U016D, invalid data from A is U041B. Since the controller loses the oxygen value it needs for combustion and aftertreatment control, the MIL lights and soot-model or regeneration functions may be restricted.
c: Heat-stressed wiring or poor terminal contact at the sensor module connector
Sensor module without power or ground
Exhaust gas sensor module internally faulty
s: MIL on
Further oxygen-sensor codes stored
Particulate filter regeneration restricted

U011B.t: Lost Communication With Rocker Arm Control Module A
U011B.d: U011B covers the first rocker arm control module. On overhead-cam engines that shut cylinders down or change valve lift, a solenoid routes engine oil to unhook a pin coupling two rocker arms; the cam-driven arm then moves on its own and the valve stays shut. Where a maker hands this switching to a dedicated controller, the engine controller sets U011B when that unit's messages stop. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. CARB requires lost digital communication to be coded separately and also obliges makers to supervise systems that vary valve timing or lift. U011C is the second module, U041C stands for invalid data from this one. Expect the MIL, switching of valve lift or cylinder deactivation locked out and higher fuel use.
c: Rocker arm module without power or ground
Oil-soaked or heat-damaged connector on the cylinder head
Damaged CAN wiring between module and engine controller
Rocker arm control module internally faulty
s: MIL on
Cylinder deactivation or valve lift switching inactive
Higher fuel consumption

U011C.t: Lost Communication With Rocker Arm Control Module B
U011C.d: U011C is the partner of U011B for rocker arm control module B, for example the controller of the second cylinder bank or of a second group of switchable rocker arms where the task is split across two units. The engine controller expects cyclic status from it, such as the confirmed lock state per cylinder, and records U011C once those frames fail to arrive. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and it remains open which production engines use a separate B module at all; the entry relies on CARB's call for separate lack-of-communication codes and its monitoring rules for valve lift and control. Invalid data from this module is U041D. Without the B unit the affected cylinders usually stay in full-lift mode: MIL, possibly uneven running and more fuel.
c: Module B without power or ground
Contaminated or loose connector at the second cylinder head
Open or shorted CAN lines to module B
Rocker arm control module B internally faulty
s: MIL on
Affected cylinders remain in full-lift mode
Uneven running or higher consumption

U011D.t: Lost Communication With All Wheel Drive Control Module
U011D.d: U011D signals a lost all-wheel-drive control module. In contrast to a single coupling controller (U0114) or a transfer case module (U0102), this unit manages an entire on-demand AWD system, deciding when and how much torque goes to the secondary axle, which in some cars is driven by its own electric motor. It draws wheel speed, steering and torque data from the bus and reports its state to stability control. No manufacturer documents U011D publicly; Stellantis, for one, files the case under U0102, which its Jeep Wrangler bulletin 23-033-25 calls Transfer Case Control Module/AWD. Typical consequences are an AWD warning lamp and drive on one axle only; emissions are not affected, so a MIL is not expected.
c: AWD module without power or ground
Water or corrosion at the module connector near the rear axle
Chafed or open CAN wiring to the module
s: AWD warning lamp or message
Drive on one axle only
Stability control may also show a warning

U011E.t: Lost Communication With Throttle Actuator B Control Module
U011E.d: U011E reports that the controller for throttle actuator B has gone silent. Most engines use a single electronic throttle whose motor the engine controller drives itself; a separately housed throttle controller is covered by U0107. SAE reserves B for a second actuator with its own bus-connected driver, but which production engines use one is not documented, and no manufacturer describes U011E publicly. CARB's rule for separate lack-of-communication codes is the formal basis. If control of an electronic throttle is lost, springs return the plate to a fixed limp-home opening that allows only slow driving. Software incompatibility with a throttle controller is U0308, invalid data U0408. Expect MIL, reduced power and possibly an idle-only engine.
c: Throttle B controller without power or ground
Damaged CAN wiring or connector to the controller
Throttle actuator B control module internally faulty
s: MIL on
Limp-home mode with reduced power
Poor throttle response or idle only

U011F.d: U011F concerns the V2X module, the radio unit through which a car exchanges messages with other vehicles, roadside infrastructure, pedestrians' devices or the network (vehicle-to-everything), either via short-range DSRC/ITS-G5 or via cellular C-V2X. It passes alerts such as an approaching hazard or signal-phase information on to the driver and to assistance systems. Another module stores U011F once the V2X unit's periodic frames stop. No manufacturer documents the code publicly; since the module has no role in emission control, a MIL is not expected. U042A covers invalid V2X data, U0198 a lost telematics module. For the driver the connected warnings simply disappear, sometimes with a cluster message; the car drives normally.
c: V2X module without power or ground
Damaged bus wiring or connector, e.g. after roof or antenna work
Software or configuration fault in the V2X or gateway module
s: Connected traffic and hazard warnings unavailable
Possible service message in the cluster

U0120.t: Lost Communication With Starter/Generator Control Module
U0120.d: U0120 means the starter/generator control module, which drives an electric machine that can both crank the engine and produce electrical power, has dropped off the bus. Mitsubishi documents it for the Outlander PHEV (2018 and 2022): the hybrid controller (PHEV-ECU) sets U0120 when, after its supply has been within 10–16 V for more than 5 s, no frames from the generator control unit (GCU) housed within the power drive unit arrive for 0.3 s; confirmation uses the second of Mitsubishi’s OBD-II drive patterns, and whether the GCU itself has stored U0120 decides between replacing the GCU or the PHEV-ECU. Ford's 2014 powertrain code list also contains U0120. On 48 V mild hybrids with a belt or integrated starter generator it applies likewise. Expect lost start-stop or hybrid functions, a charging warning and the MIL.
c: Fault on the CAN lines between hybrid controller and generator control unit
Starter/generator control unit faulty (replacement if it stores U0120 itself)
Low 12 V supply or poor ground at the power electronics
s: MIL and hybrid or charging warning
Start-stop or engine start by the electric machine unavailable
Battery not charged while driving

U0121.t: Lost Communication With Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module A
U0121.d: U0121 is stored by any listener that stops receiving the ABS/ESC module, so it often shows up in engine, transmission, cluster and gateway at once. GM treats it as Type C without MIL (Chrysler bulletins list it with MIL): the 2019 LTG engine table watches frames $0C1/$0C5 (0.5 s) and the 2025 TCM table waits over 10 s; while it is active, the ECM skips wheel-speed plausibility checks. Ford's 2023 diesel ECU flags the ABS master message after 5 s; Mitsubishi's PHEV-ECU checks it at 10–16.5 V. Field causes: water in the EBCM connector (GM PIT5499A), ground G907A (Jeep), ABS software that locks the car in Park (Chrysler 08-043-26), an ESC restart on the Audi e-tron (2072977/1). GM 16-NA-177 calls a history U0121 in the front camera harmless.
c: Water ingress or corroded terminals at the ABS/EBCM connector
Poor ground point or supply fuse of the ABS module
ABS/ESC software that fails to wake up or restarts (update released)
s: ABS, ESC and brake warning lamps on
Speedometer or gear display erratic, several U codes
Reduced brake assistance or vehicle stays in Park
Start-stop and driver assistance unavailable

U0122.t: Lost Communication With Vehicle Dynamics Control Module
U0122.d: U0122 tells you that a networked controller, often the engine or hybrid ECU, has stopped receiving the cyclic frames of the stability control unit (ESC/VSC/ASC, usually combined with the ABS hydraulic unit). Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV documents it in the PHEV-ECU: with 10–16 V present for at least 5 s and the motor switch on, a broken link to the ABS/ASC unit lasting 2 s or more stores U0122-00, and Mitsubishi verifies the repair with an OBD-II test drive pattern. Saab's 9-5 code list names the partner Vehicle Stability Control Module, and Subaru released ECM software for the 2019 Ascent that changes how its ECM detects U0122. U0121 and U0129 point at the ABS and brake modules instead. Stability and traction aids usually switch off.
c: Missing fuse, supply or ground at the stability/ABS unit
Damaged CAN wiring or faulty gateway between the bus segments
Receiving controller software reports the loss too eagerly (update exists, e.g. Subaru)
s: ESC, traction control and ABS warning lamps on
Stability and traction control unavailable
MIL on in some vehicles (engine or hybrid ECU stores the code)

U0123.t: Lost Communication With Yaw Rate Sensor Module
U0123.d: U0123 is stored when the stability controller or another listener misses the messages of a networked yaw rate sensor, the unit that measures how fast the car rotates around its vertical axis. Without that signal ESC cannot compare the actual turn with the steering input. No manufacturer explains U0123 in an openly accessible document; Ford merely lists it among the OBD codes of the 2014 Boss 302S. GM bulletin PIT5187A shows how such sensors are packaged today: yaw rate, inertia and multi-axis sensor are names for one combined module, which is why newer GM cars report it under U0125. Lateral acceleration has its own code U0124, invalid yaw data is U0513. Expect ESC and traction lamps on; driving remains possible.
c: Loose or corroded connector at the yaw rate sensor (often under the centre console or seat)
Fuse, supply or ground of the sensor module missing
Damaged chassis CAN wiring to the sensor
Yaw rate sensor module internally failed
s: ESC and traction control warning lamps on
Stability control switched off for the rest of the trip
Often stored together with U0124 when both signals come from one housing

U0124.t: Lost Communication With Lateral Acceleration Sensor Module
U0124.d: With U0124 a controller reports that the frames from the lateral acceleration sensor module have stopped. This sensor tells the stability system how strongly the vehicle is being pushed sideways in a bend; together with yaw rate and steering angle it lets ESC detect skidding. In many cars the lateral and yaw sensing sit in one package, so U0123 and U0124 tend to appear as a pair and point to a shared supply or connector fault. Public manufacturer documents for U0124 itself are missing; the description rests on the J2012 title, CARB's network monitoring rules and GM's note that one inertial module carries all these signals (PIT5187A). Bad lateral data is coded U0536. ESC and traction aid go offline, braking stays normal.
c: Corroded or loose plug at the acceleration sensor module
Power or ground of the sensor module interrupted
Chafed bus wires on the way to the sensor
s: ESC/traction warning lamp lit
Stability control deactivated
Frequently logged together with U0123

U0125.t: Lost Communication With Multi-axis Acceleration Sensor Module A
U0125.d: U0125 concerns the inertial measurement unit that bundles yaw rate plus lateral and longitudinal acceleration on one bus node. GM uses the code widely: the 2019 XT4 brake controller (EBCM) flags a missing IMU frame after 0.1 s, the 2025 object-detection module after 0.05 s and then disables adaptive cruise; both are Type C without MIL. Saab's 9-5 list adds symptom bytes 71, 72 and 74 for invalid data, wrong message counter and checksum. Field cases: a broken wire at connector X411 under the left rear (Equinox/Terrain, PIT5171B) and an EBCM reflash for 2020 Equinox (N192285670). Stellantis calls the part Dynamics Sensor. U0123/U0124 name single-axis modules instead.
c: Wire broken inside the insulation or rubbed through near a chassis connector (GM X411)
Loose or corroded plug at the inertial sensor
Brake controller software that drops the sensor (reflash released)
s: Service ESC / StabiliTrak message, traction and ABS lamps
Adaptive cruise control or all-wheel drive unavailable
Electric parking brake warning on some models

U0126.t: Lost Communication With Steering Angle Sensor Module
U0126.d: U0126 means the steering wheel angle sensor, usually mounted on the steering column, is no longer heard on the bus. ESC needs this value to know the path the driver intends. Mitsubishi's 2019 Outlander PHEV sets U0126 in the PHEV-ECU when it loses its CAN link to the wheel-angle sensor and demands calibration after a sensor swap. Mercedes reports U012600 with check-engine lamp after remote start, traced to software and the column module (LI27.00-P-073106). GM PIT5755 warns that some 2020 Silverado HD brake controllers log the same fault as U0131. Saab's list uses symptom bytes 71/72/74/5A. U0428 covers invalid angle data. Expect ESC warnings, sometimes a MIL.
c: Loose or damaged connector or clock-spring harness at the steering column
Power or ground of the steering angle sensor missing
Module software reporting the fault wrongly or after remote start (update)
Steering angle sensor faulty; recalibration needed after replacement
s: ESC and traction lamps on, stability control inactive
Check engine lamp on some models
Lane or park assist functions unavailable

U0127.t: Lost Communication With Tire Pressure Monitor Module
U0127.d: U0127 is logged when the tyre pressure monitoring module, the receiver that collects the radio signals of the wheel sensors, stops answering on the vehicle network. In the VW group the gateway (address 0019) stores it: Audi bulletin 2065474 for A6/A7/RS 6/RS 7 2019–2022 finds the module J502 unreachable and blames moisture entering through its pressure equalisation element; the fix is a new module and bracket. Bentley 2057947 (Continental GT, Flying Spur) shows the same pattern, as static or intermittent fault. Faulty wheel sensors set other codes such as U0430 instead. Only the TPMS warning lights; engine and brakes are unaffected, no MIL.
c: Moisture inside the TPMS module through its vent element
Pins, power or ground at the TPMS module connector faulty
Damaged bus wiring to the module
s: TPMS warning lamp or message in the cluster
Tyre pressures not displayed
Scan tool cannot reach the TPMS module

U0128.t: Lost Communication With Park Brake Control Module
U0128.d: U0128 signals that the electric parking brake controller has dropped off the bus. GM rates it very differently by node: the 2017 engine table waits 10 s for the park brake message and treats a miss as Type A (MIL at once), while the 2019 chassis controller (ICCM) needs only 1 s but files it as Type C without MIL; from model year 2018 GM folds this ICCM check into U0121. Saab's 9-5 list adds subtypes 71, 72 and 74 for corrupt frames. FCA names U0128 among the codes of a 2019 Cherokee 3.2 L PCM update. In GM Silverado trucks it appears with many other U codes when a harness fault upsets the whole network (PIT5713A). U0135/U0136 cover further park brake modules. The parking brake may not apply or release.
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the park brake module missing
Chafed or corroded bus wiring, often affecting several modules at once
Weak battery causing the module to drop out (stored code)
Controller software issue fixed by reprogramming
Park brake control module internally faulty
s: Service Parking Brake message or brake warning lamp
Electric parking brake does not apply or release
MIL on in vehicles where the engine controller stores it

U0129.t: Lost Communication With Brake System Control Module A
U0129.d: U0129 points to the brake system control module A, in GM vehicles the OBD node with diagnostic ID 7E5. GM's 2019 LTG engine table checks frames $0C1, $0C5, $0D1, $1C6 and others every 500 ms (one of them 10 s) and needs two trips to set the MIL; the 2018 hybrid controller and the 2025 ECM treat it as Type A, the 2017 table as Special Type C. Stellantis calls the partner Brake System Control Module 1. GM N192267870 adds a software case: after a jump start the 2019 Silverado ECM stored U0129 with U0101/U0140 and lit the service engine lamp. U0121 covers the ABS module, U0418 invalid brake data. Brake assist and stop-start may be reduced.
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the brake control module faulty
Low battery or jump start leaving stored network codes (ECM update released)
Damaged or corroded CAN wiring to the brake module
Brake system control module internally faulty
s: MIL or service engine lamp plus brake/ESC warnings
Gear selection or stop-start blocked on some vehicles
Several other U codes stored at the same time

U012A.t: Lost Communication With Chassis Control Module A
U012A.d: U012A reports that chassis control module A is silent. The unit behind the letter A varies between brands; GM uses the code in several engine and transmission tables. The 2016 ECM for the L20 engine waits for message $4DB and logs a missing frame as Type B, so the MIL comes after two trips; the 2020 ten-speed transmission controller watches frame $1F7 from the integrated chassis control module (ICCM) and treats the loss as emissions-neutral Type C. GM's 2015 engine table even uses U012A for a lost fuel pump control module, more than 0.5 s without a message, also Type B. U012B is the B module, U042B invalid data from module A. Effects range from chassis warnings to engine trouble.
c: Power, ground or fuse of chassis module A missing
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged
Voltage dip leaving a stored code
s: MIL on in vehicles where the engine controller logs it
Chassis functions controlled by module A unavailable
Hard start or stalling if the module drives the fuel pump

U012B.t: Lost Communication With Chassis Control Module B
U012B.d: U012B is the counterpart to U012A for a second chassis controller, labelled B. No manufacturer documents U012B in an openly available source, so its exact job (air suspension, damping, steering or another chassis task) depends on the vehicle. Logic follows the usual network rule that CARB requires and GM spells out for module A: a receiving controller expects a periodic message, and if it stays away for a calibrated time while supply and ignition are valid, the receiver stores the code for the silent partner. GM's tables for U012A list Type B on engine nodes and Type C on the transmission, so the warning lamp behaviour is maker specific. Invalid data from module B is U042C.
c: Fuse, power or ground of chassis module B interrupted
Damaged bus line or connector to module B
Chassis module B internally faulty or not programmed
s: Chassis warning message in the cluster
Functions handled by module B (e.g. suspension) unavailable
Scan tool cannot reach module B

U012C.t: Lost Communication With Active Vibration Control Module
U012C.d: U012C covers the controller that drives active engine mounts or inertial shakers to cancel engine vibration, for example in cars that switch off cylinders. Such a unit needs engine speed and load from the network to generate a counter-phase force; a Honda patent (US 10360893) describes a separate AVC control unit with actuators and acceleration sensors that adapts its cancelling output to engine rotation. No manufacturer publishes a description of U012C itself, so the setting rule is the general one from CARB's network monitoring: the receiving controller stores the code when expected frames stay away. Engine mount actuator wiring has its own codes, P0A14 and following; invalid data is U042D. Expect more cabin vibration, usually no MIL.
c: Power or ground of the vibration control unit missing
Bus wire or connector damaged near engine or subframe
Active vibration control module internally faulty
s: Noticeable engine vibration at idle or in cylinder deactivation mode
Humming or booming noise in the cabin
Fuel saving mode may stay disabled

U012D.t: Lost Communication With Generator A Control Module
U012D.d: U012D is stored when the powertrain controller loses contact with the regulator of generator A. In many Ford models this is the smart alternator, which the PCM commands over a LIN line that it often shares with the active grille shutters; for that reason U012D usually shows up together with U0284/U0285 and U042E. Ford bulletins name the culprits: water in connector C202 (Bronco Sport 1.5 L, SSM 49496, with MIL and/or Check Charging System), LIN wire VE181 shorted to ground against a bracket of the left engine mount (F-150 2.7 L, SSM 50737). Stellantis saw the same codes on a 2019 Renegade with an exposed shutter connector. Generator B uses U012F. The battery may run down.
c: Water or corrosion in a connector of the shared LIN line (grille shutter, C202)
LIN wire chafed and shorted to ground near an engine mount bracket
Generator regulator internally faulty or without supply
s: Check Charging System message or battery lamp
MIL on in some models
Battery discharges, voltage unstable
Active grille shutter codes stored as well

U012E.t: Lost Communication With Camshaft Position Control Module
U012E.d: U012E applies to engines whose camshaft phaser is driven by its own electronic unit rather than an oil control solenoid, as with electric intake valve timing. Mitsubishi bulletin TSB-23-11-003 for the 2022 Outlander lists U012E next to U0101, U0122, U0146, U0155 and U042F as communication codes of the engine controller and links it in the warranty chart to the electric intake valve timing control module circuit. Without the module the engine controller cannot adjust intake timing, so power and exhaust quality suffer; the code counts as emissions relevant, and a MIL is to be expected, although no maker states it openly. U042F flags invalid data from the same unit; P0010 ff. cover the actuators themselves.
c: Power or ground of the electric valve timing module interrupted
CAN wiring or connector at the engine damaged by heat or oil
Camshaft position control module internally faulty
s: MIL on
Reduced power and poorer response, especially at low engine speed
Rough idle or higher fuel consumption

U012F.t: Lost Communication With Generator B Control Module
U012F.d: U012F is reserved for vehicles with a second generator, labelled B, whose regulator or control electronics talk to the powertrain or hybrid controller over a bus. That can be a second alternator on heavy-duty trucks or a further motor-generator in a hybrid drive. No manufacturer explains U012F in an open document; the closest documented case is the A unit under U012D, where Ford's smart alternator hangs on a LIN line and loses contact through wet connectors or chafed wires. CARB's network monitoring rules apply in the same way. If generator B goes quiet, the controller can no longer set its output, so charging power drops and the battery or high-voltage system may run short. U0120 covers a starter generator.
c: Wet or corroded connector in the bus line to generator B
Fuse, power or ground of the generator B electronics missing
Bus wire chafed against engine or bracket
Generator B regulator or control module faulty
s: Charging system warning
Battery voltage falls during driving
Hybrid system warning or reduced electric drive on hybrids

U0130.t: Lost Communication With Steering Effort Control Module
U0130.d: U0130 is logged when a controller on the network stops hearing the steering effort control module, which varies how much assistance the driver gets at the wheel, usually depending on road speed. Saab's 2011 9-5 code list maps U0130 to its electric power steering control module and adds failure-type bytes 71 (data not valid), 72 (message counter wrong) and 74 (checksum error), while a separate power steering module keeps U0131. Ford reports U0130 in the battery energy control module of the 2012–2018 Focus Electric after a high-voltage battery swap and clears it with a programmable module installation, without naming the partner. Expect a steering warning and possibly heavier steering; no public MIL rule exists.
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the steering effort module missing
Damaged CAN wiring or loose connector at the steering module
Module configuration or software not matched after a repair (e.g. Ford after HV battery replacement)
s: Steering system warning lamp or message
Steering feels heavier or no longer adapts to speed
Further communication codes stored in several modules

U0131.t: Lost Communication With Power Steering Control Module A
U0131.d: U0131 means a listener on the bus has missed the cyclic frames of power steering control module A, normally the electric steering unit on rack or column. GM documents several receivers: the ECM of 2019 models flags it after 10 s without message $1E5 as a Type C, emissions-neutral fault and then stops basing auto-stop decisions on steering angle; the EBCM reacts after 0.025 s, and the 2025 EOCM3 after 0.05–0.25 s, switching off adaptive cruise (Special Type C, no MIL). FCA, by contrast, reports a lit check-engine lamp on Jeep models. Bulletins blame a blown 80 A mega fuse (Ford Transit Connect), PSCM software (Ford Super Duty 2020) and a chafed transmission harness (Jeep Cherokee diesel). Steering assist may drop.
c: High-current fuse, supply or ground of the steering module open (e.g. Ford mega fuse F2)
Chafed or damaged harness on the bus or wake-up line (e.g. Jeep Cherokee, GM circuit 5986)
Steering module software, fixed by an update (Ford Super Duty 2020)
Power steering control module internally failed
s: Reduced or no steering assist, heavy steering
EPS or steering fault message in the cluster
Adaptive cruise control switched off (GM)
Check-engine lamp on some vehicles (e.g. Jeep)

U0132.t: Lost Communication With Suspension Control Module A
U0132.d: U0132 is set when a module stops receiving suspension control module A, the controller for air springs, ride height or damping. GM names the K5 automatic level control module of 2021 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban and Yukon with air suspension: it goes silent, a leveling or headlamp service message comes up, and removing two fuses for a few minutes revives it (PIT5795). GM's 2025 EBCM flags missing level-control frames after 250 ms as Type C without MIL. FCA links U0132 on Ram 2500/3500 with rear auto-level air suspension to ASCM software and a lit MIL (TSB 08-175-21). Audi Q5/Q7 and Bentley store U013200 in the gateway, cured by a J775 update or a fuse reset. Module B is U0139. Leveling may stop.
c: Suspension module locked up, recovers after a power cycle (GM PIT5795, Bentley)
Suspension module software, fixed by an update (FCA Ram, Audi J775)
Fuse, supply or CAN wiring of the suspension module faulty
s: Air suspension or leveling warning in the cluster
Ride height control or headlamp leveling inoperative
MIL on some vehicles (e.g. Ram heavy duty)

U0133.t: Lost Communication With Active Roll Control Module
U0133.d: U0133 indicates that the active roll control module, which drives hydraulic or electromechanical anti-roll bars to reduce body lean in corners, no longer answers on the bus. No manufacturer publicly ties U0133 to that module: Saab's 2011 9-5 list uses the number for its air suspension control module instead, so older vehicles may interpret it differently. Systems of this kind exist, for instance on the Bentley Bentayga, where the adaptive suspension unit J775 acts as master for the roll stabiliser units J924 (front axle) and J1096 (rear axle) and their software must match (TPI 2055643). Invalid roll-module data is U0434; suspension modules A and B lose contact under U0132 and U0139. Expect a chassis warning and noticeably more body roll.
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the roll control module faulty
Software of master and stabiliser units not compatible after a replacement (Bentley TPI 2055643)
s: Chassis or suspension warning lamp
More body roll when cornering
Sport or dynamic driving modes unavailable

U0134.t: Lost Communication With Power Steering Control Module - Rear
U0134.d: U0134 is stored when a controller loses contact with the rear power steering control module, the actuator unit of a rear-wheel or four-wheel steering system. Such systems turn the rear wheels by a few degrees, opposite to the front ones at low speed for a smaller turning circle and in the same direction at higher speed for calmer lane changes. No manufacturer explains U0134 in a publicly available document. CARB obliges manufacturers to detect missing communication from digital inputs as a separate fault, while electronic steering only falls under OBD monitoring where other diagnostics depend on it, so the code is mainly a chassis matter. U0131 belongs to the front steering, U0435 to invalid rear-steer data. Usually the rear wheels stay centred.
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the rear steering module faulty
Corroded or wet connector at the rear axle actuator
Rear steering control module internally faulty
s: Steering system warning lamp or message
Larger turning circle, rear wheels no longer steer

U0135.t: Lost Communication With Differential Control Module - Front
U0135.d: U0135 reports that the front differential control module has dropped off the network. Such a module operates an electronically controlled clutch pack or locker in the front axle, either to move torque from one front wheel to the other or to lock both for traction off road. No manufacturer documents U0135 in public; the closest documented case is the rear counterpart U0136, which GM's 2019 ECM tables monitor on the Cadillac XT4. CARB requires a separate code for lost communication with a digital input but leaves driveline modules to the manufacturer unless other diagnostics rely on them. U0436 covers implausible front-differential data, U0114 and U0102 the AWD clutch and transfer case. The front differential then usually works as an open one.
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the front differential module faulty
Water or corrosion in the connector near the front axle
Front differential control module internally faulty
s: 4WD, locker or traction warning lamp
Front locker or torque vectoring not available

U0136.t: Lost Communication With Differential Control Module - Rear
U0136.d: U0136 is set when a listener misses the rear differential control module, which operates an electronic limited-slip or twin-clutch rear drive unit. GM's 2019 tables document it in the ECM of the Cadillac XT4 (LSY engine): if message $1CF from the rear drive module stays absent for 10 s while bus A is active and supply exceeds 11 V, the ECM stores U0136 as a Type B fault, so the MIL comes on after two trips. Saab's 2011 9-5 list (XWD all-wheel drive) also names the rear differential module and adds byte 71 for invalid data. Implausible rear-differential data has its own code U0437; the front axle uses U0135. Rear torque distribution switches off with a warning, and the car usually continues with front-wheel drive.
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the rear drive module faulty
Corroded or damaged connector at the rear axle, exposed to spray water
Rear differential control module internally faulty
s: AWD or rear differential warning
Car drives with front-wheel drive only, less traction
MIL after two trips on GM vehicles

U0137.t: Lost Communication With Trailer Brake Control Module
U0137.d: U0137 means the trailer brake control module, which energises a towed trailer’s electric brakes in step with the tow vehicle's braking, is missing on the bus. Ford uses the code widely: on 2022 F-150 trucks without that module the ABS unit may store U0137 by mistake, and it can then be ignored (SSM 50418); on F-150, Expedition, Navigator and Ranger of 2021–2024 the IPC, BCM or PSCM log it together with a warning that the trailer brake module has failed, solved by disconnecting the battery and module and reprogramming the trailer module (SSM 53236). Ram 1500–3500 with integrated trailer brake module can show Park Assist System Disabled with U0137 (FCA 9004253). Invalid data from this module is U0438. Check the trailer brakes before towing.
c: Trailer or ABS module software, fixed by reprogramming (Ford SSM 53236, 50418)
Improperly seated connector, damaged harness or water intrusion at the module (FCA 9004253)
Module retrofitted or configured incorrectly (dealer-installed tow package)
Trailer brake control module internally faulty
s: Trailer brake fault message in the cluster
Trailer brakes not applied or gain control inoperative
Park assist disabled on some Ram trucks

U0138.t: Lost Communication With All Terrain Control Module
U0138.d: U0138 is logged when another module no longer receives the all-terrain control module, the unit behind the selector that lets the driver pick a terrain or drive mode such as snow, sand or mud and then adapts traction control, throttle response and shift points. Ford lists U0138 in the OBD code tables of its 2014 vehicles and marks it as available in all three self-test modes, without an entry in the lamp column. More public manufacturer detail is missing. CARB treats such a link as a digital input whose loss of communication must carry its own code. Implausible data from this module is U0439; the transfer case and AWD clutch use U0102 and U0114. The mode selector stops working and a 4WD or traction warning appears.
c: Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the terrain module faulty
Loose or corroded connector at the module or the mode selector
s: Terrain or drive mode cannot be selected
4WD or traction control warning lamp

U0139.t: Lost Communication With Suspension Control Module B
U0139.d: U0139 reports lost contact with suspension control module B, at GM the semi-active damping system (SADS). GM's 2025 tables let the ECM watch two SADS messages, $035 with a 10 s limit and $364 with 325 ms, and set U0139 as Type B with the MIL after two trips; the EBCM treats missing damper frames for 250 ms as Type C. Bulletins PIT6007 and PIT6007A (2020–2024 Corvette, Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon with Magnetic Ride Control) describe a check-engine lamp with U0139 in the ECM and no other symptom, cleared by pulling the K19 module fuse for one minute. PIT5457 lists it with high resistance in wake-up circuit 5986. Saab and Ford's 2014 list carry the code too. Damping then usually stays at a fixed setting.
c: Suspension module software locks up, recovers after a fuse reset (GM PIT6007)
High resistance or open in the module wake-up line (GM circuit 5986)
Fuse, supply, ground or CAN wiring of the damping module faulty
Suspension control module B internally faulty
s: Check-engine lamp, often without any other symptom (GM)
Service Suspension message, adaptive damping inactive
Harsher or softer ride than usual

U013C.t: Lost Communication With Accelerator Pedal Module
U013C.d: U013C applies to an accelerator pedal module that reports over a data bus instead of analog sensor lines. In a drive-by-wire system the pedal module carries the driver's torque request to the engine or drive controller, so that controller has to fall back to a safe state as soon as the pedal messages disappear. No manufacturer documents U013C publicly; most pedals still use two analog tracks, whose faults appear as circuit codes such as P2122 or P2127 instead. CARB requires lack of communication from a digital input to be detected separately and stored as its own fault code. U043D covers implausible pedal data. Expect reduced power or idle only, a warning lamp and, depending on the manufacturer, the MIL.
c: Loose or corroded connector at the pedal module (footwell moisture)
Supply, ground or bus wiring of the pedal module faulty
s: No response to the accelerator, engine stays at idle
Reduced power warning
MIL on depending on the manufacturer

U013D.t: Lost Communication With Vacuum Sensor A
U013D.d: U013D stands for lost communication with vacuum sensor A, a networked sensor that reports the vacuum in the brake booster or a vacuum reservoir. Engines with little manifold vacuum, such as turbocharged direct-injection units, and hybrids use this value to switch on an electric vacuum pump or to throttle the engine so the brake assist stays sufficient. No manufacturer documents U013D in public; GM's 2019 ECM tables show the analog form of this sensor with codes P0556 to P0558, classified as Type B. CARB demands a separate code for lost communication of digital inputs. Sensor B uses U013E, invalid data from sensor A U043E. Possible effects: brake assist warning, start-stop disabled, MIL depending on the manufacturer.
c: Loose or corroded connector at the vacuum sensor on the booster
Supply, ground or bus wiring of the sensor faulty
s: Brake booster or brake assist warning
Electric vacuum pump runs constantly or start-stop disabled
MIL on depending on the manufacturer

U013E.t: Lost Communication With Vacuum Sensor B
U013E.d: U013E concerns vacuum sensor B, the second networked vacuum sensor in vehicles that measure at more than one point, for example in the booster chamber and in a separate reservoir, or that read a redundant value. The receiving module, typically the engine or brake controller, sets the code when the frames of this sensor stop arriving. No manufacturer has published a description of U013E, and public sources do not reveal which vehicles carry two bus vacuum sensors. For orientation: GM's ECM tables cover the analog booster pressure sensor with P0556 to P0558, and CARB requires lost communication from a digital input to get its own code. U013D is sensor A, U043F invalid data from sensor B. Similar effects to U013D are likely.
c: Loose or corroded connector at vacuum sensor B
Supply, ground or bus wiring shared with sensor A faulty
s: Brake system or brake assist warning
Often stored together with U013D when both sensors share wiring

U013F.t: Lost Communication With Pedestrian Alert Control Module
U013F.d: U013F reports that the pedestrian alert control module has gone silent. Electric and hybrid cars need it to produce a warning sound at low speed, because they are otherwise almost inaudible; FMVSS 141 in the US and UN R138 in Europe make such a sound mandatory. GM describes the system on the 2022 BrightDrop EV600: the module creates a tone whose pitch and volume follow the vehicle's speed, plays it through one front and one rear speaker below 30 km/h whenever a driving gear, forward or reverse, is engaged, and is driven by the BCM over LIN. No manufacturer explains U013F itself in public. Circuit faults of the module appear as P0DED to P0DEF. The car drives normally, but pedestrians may not hear it, so the fault deserves a prompt repair.
c: Water or corrosion at the module, a speaker or their connectors
Supply, ground or LIN/CAN wiring of the module faulty
Pedestrian alert control module internally faulty
s: No warning sound when driving slowly
Pedestrian alert fault message in the cluster

U0140.t: Lost Communication With Body Control Module
U0140.d: U0140 is among the most frequent network codes: a listening controller misses the frames of the body control module, which handles lights, locks, wipers and often the power mode that wakes other units. The code sits in the listener, not in the BCM. GM watches it in many nodes; its 2019 ECM tables expect certain BCM frames within 500 ms, others within 10 s, rate the fault Type C without MIL and then assume zero A/C compressor load, whereas the 2025 ECM and brake module count it as Type B with MIL after two trips. Saab lists failure-type bytes 71, 72 and 74 (bad data, counter, checksum). Ford's 2017-18 Escape stored it in the front controls module after incomplete configuration (SSM 47040), FCA's 2021 300 with MIL until a PCM flash. U0141 to U0145 cover further body units.
c: BCM fuse, power feed or ground missing or corroded
Chafed bus line or loose, wet connector between BCM and the listening modules
Weak battery, jump start or voltage dip leaves a stored history code
BCM or listener software or configuration out of date (Ford SSM 47040, FCA 18-013-22)
s: Lights, central locking, wipers or interior lamps misbehave or fail
Radio, climate controls or gauges blank or erratic
Same code stored in several modules at once
MIL on in some vehicles (GM 2025 Type B, FCA PCM)

U0141.t: Lost Communication With Body Control Module A
U0141.d: U0141 names the first of several body controllers. Unlike U0140, which stands for the single main BCM, the letter suits cars that spread body tasks over more units, and each maker decides which one is A. Mitsubishi uses U0141 for an ETACS timeout: its body controller ETACS-ECU stops sending, and keyless entry, liftgate, airbag, brake and steering units log the loss; bulletin TSB-19-42B-003 revised the procedure for Outlander, Lancer and Outlander Sport up to 2019. FCA labels the module IPM (BCM) or, in older airbag lists, the front control or totally integrated power module; on the 2021 Chrysler 300 a PCM flash cures a MIL that comes with it. On the 2023-24 Audi e-tron the gateway stores U014100 when the ignition will not switch on, cured by a software update of the comfort control unit J393.
c: Power, fuse or ground of body module A missing
Software of module A or of the listener needs updating (Audi J393, FCA PCM)
Bus wire or connector to module A damaged or loose
s: Keyless entry, liftgate or other body functions inoperative
Ignition cannot be switched on (Audi e-tron case)
MIL or several warning lamps on
Code stored in many modules at once

U0142.t: Lost Communication With Body Control Module B
U0142.d: U0142 reports that a second body controller, labelled B, has stopped talking. No maker explains publicly which unit carries this letter; depending on the design it may be a rear body module, a power distribution box or a comfort unit next to the main BCM (U0140) and module A (U0141). The only manufacturer document found that mentions the code is Toyota's 2014 Prius plug-in pre-delivery sheet: the short pin is pulled for shipping to save the battery, so U0142, U0155 and U0100 are expected and simply erased once it is refitted. That makes clear how easily a dormant or unpowered module produces this code. GM's U0100-U02FF logic applies: listeners expect the module's periodic availability message at 9-16 V and log its absence. Invalid data from module B is U0443. Usually no MIL.
c: Module B without power: fuse, transport short pin or relay missing
Flat battery or battery disconnect leaves a history code
Damaged bus wire or loose connector to module B
s: Body functions handled by module B do not work
Scan tool cannot reach module B
Often only a stored code without noticeable fault

U0143.t: Lost Communication With Body Control Module C
U0143.d: With U0143 a listener reports that body controller C has gone quiet. The letter only means a third body unit; its role is set by the maker. Ford is the one maker found using the code publicly: on the 2021 F-150 the trailer module stores U0143:87, the suffix marking a missing message, because of software parameters in that module. Ford's SSM 50217 calls it harmless, with no warning or drivability effect, and announced an over-the-air update of the trailer module from March 2022. So on these trucks a lone U0143 in the trailer module is no reason to replace anything. Elsewhere the usual network rule applies: a supervised periodic message from module C is missing while supply voltage is valid. U0140 to U0142 cover the other body modules, U0444 invalid data from C.
c: Software parameters in the listening module (Ford F-150 trailer module)
Power, fuse or ground of module C missing
Bus line or connector to module C damaged
s: Often none; code found only during a scan
Functions of module C (for example trailer-related outputs) unavailable
Scan tool cannot reach module C

U0144.t: Lost Communication With Body Control Module D
U0144.d: U0144 is logged by one or more control units that no longer receive the cyclic messages of the body controller J2012 calls Body Control Module D. In GM's network logic every node broadcasts a state-of-health message with ignition on; if it stays away while the supply is between 9 and 16 V, the listeners store a code naming the silent unit, not themselves. No manufacturer documents U0144 publicly: GM's U-code list knows only U0140, and Stellantis uses the neighbour U0145 for a BCM LIN bus. What the D unit does is maker-specific, typically a body sub-controller for doors, seats or lighting. U0140 to U0143 and U0145 cover the other body modules. Expect dead comfort functions, no MIL.
c: Fuse, power or ground of the body module D missing
Chafed bus wire or loose, wet connector on the way to module D
Weak battery or voltage dip, so the module drops off the bus (history code)
Body module D internally faulty or not programmed
s: Body functions handled by module D (locks, lighting, seats) do not respond
Scan tool cannot reach module D
Same code stored in several other modules

U0145.t: Lost Communication With Body Control Module E
U0145.d: U0145 means the network has lost contact with the body controller J2012 labels E. Receiving modules expect its periodic messages; GM's generic logic sets such a code when a supervised message carrying the sender's availability fails to arrive at 9-16 V. Stellantis is the one maker found using U0145 publicly: a 2023 STAR case lists U0145-00 as a LIN bus 3 fault stored in the body control module next to U0140-00, and asks technicians to trace the bus harness and check for loose or pushed-out terminals before replacing the BCM. So on Stellantis vehicles the code points at a LIN branch hanging off the BCM. U0140 to U0144 cover the main and other body modules. MIL stays off; lights, locks or other LIN-driven functions may fail.
c: Loose, spread or pushed-out terminal in the bus harness (Stellantis case)
Open or short on the LIN/CAN line to module E
Power or ground of module E missing
Body module E or BCM internally faulty
s: Individual body functions such as lights or locks inoperative
Code appears together with U0140 in several modules
Fault comes and goes when the harness is moved

U0146.t: Lost Communication With Serial Data Gateway Module A
U0146.d: U0146 means the first gateway, the node that routes messages between bus segments, is silent; GM calls it serial data gateway module, Ford, Audi and GM's tables just Gateway A. GM's 2019 ECM expects message $3CF at least every 10 s with the battery above 11 V and treats a gap as Type B, so the MIL lights if it recurs on a second trip. Field case: on 2017 Silverado, Sierra, Tahoe, Yukon and Escalade the gateway's processor could stay powered yet fall silent on every CAN channel, leaving dead gauges, no crank or stalling plus U0146 and many other codes; pulling its fuse for a minute helps until new software, bent or backed-out terminals are the other cause (PIT5586G). On the 2022-24 Audi Q4 e-tron the engine unit logs U014600 when the application server inside the gateway has a hardware or software fault. U0447 is invalid gateway data.
c: Gateway software hangs and stops routing although powered (GM PIT5586G, Audi ICAS)
Bent, backed-out or loose terminals at the gateway connectors
Gateway fuse, power or ground missing
s: Instrument cluster gauges dead or fluctuating
No crank, no start or stalling
Many U-codes in several modules and multiple warning messages
MIL on (GM Type B)

U0147.t: Lost Communication With Serial Data Gateway Module B
U0147.d: U0147 points to a second gateway, B. Large vehicle networks often use more than one routing node, for example a central gateway plus a separate unit that connects the car to the outside world. That is how FCA uses the code: in a field report on a 2014 Jeep Grand Cherokee, filed with NHTSA in investigation PE15-021, U0147 is listed as lost communication with the telematics gateway, next to an open circuit on cellular antenna 1 and U0184 for the radio. On such vehicles the code therefore concerns connected services such as emergency call or remote functions rather than driving. Other makers do not document U0147 publicly. A routing module of this kind filters and forwards messages between domains, as Bosch describes for its central gateways. U0146 and U0148 to U0150 cover gateways A and C to E, U0448 invalid data from B.
c: Power, fuse or ground of gateway B missing
Bus wiring or connector to gateway B faulty
Telematics unit acting as gateway B faulty or in a fault state (FCA)
Gateway B software hangs after an update or voltage dip
s: Connected services, emergency call or remote app functions unavailable
Modules behind gateway B not reachable with a scan tool
Further codes such as radio communication or antenna faults

U0148.d: U0148 reports that the third gateway, Gateway C, has gone silent. A gateway links separate bus segments (CAN, LIN, Ethernet) and forwards messages between them, so when it drops out, every module behind it disappears too. GM's procedure for U0100-U02FF explains the mechanism: listeners expect a periodic state-of-health message and log the missing sender once it fails to arrive at 9-16 V. No manufacturer documents U0148 publicly; GM's U-code list contains only U0146 for its serial data gateway. Unlike U0146 and U0147 for gateways A and B, or U0149 and U0150 for D and E, this code names the C unit, whose role differs by maker. Often several other U-codes appear at once; MIL usually off.
c: Fuse, power or ground of gateway C missing
Damaged bus wiring or corroded connector at gateway C
Gateway C software fault or incomplete programming
s: Several modules behind the gateway unreachable at once
Many U-codes stored across the vehicle
Multiple warning lamps or messages in the cluster

U0149.d: U0149 names Gateway D as the module whose messages no longer arrive. Vehicles with several gateways split the network into domains, and each gateway routes traffic between its own bus segments; losing D therefore cuts off the domain it serves. Following GM's generic U0100-U02FF logic, a receiving module stores the code when the expected periodic message with the sender's availability is missing while voltage is normal. No manufacturer documents U0149 publicly, and GM only lists U0146 for a single gateway. U0146 to U0148 cover gateways A to C, U0150 the fifth one. A history-only entry after a battery disconnect or flat battery is often harmless; an active one usually comes with many other U-codes. No MIL as a rule.
c: Gateway D without power or ground
Open or shorted bus wiring, wet or corroded connector at gateway D
Low battery voltage or battery disconnect (history code only)
s: Group of modules in one domain does not answer
Many U-codes stored at the same time
Functions of the cut-off domain inoperative

U014A.t: Lost Communication With Battery Energy Control Module C
U014A.d: U014A concerns a third battery energy control module, C. Hybrid and electric vehicles use such units to watch cell voltages, temperatures and state of charge and to protect the pack; distributed or modular designs give several sub-packs their own controller, which is where letters beyond A and B come in. No manufacturer documents U014A publicly. The best documented relative is U0111 for module A: in GM's 2018 hybrid tables the hybrid powertrain controller flags missing BECM messages after 500 ms, once bus communication has run for at least 5 s and the battery holds 10.2 V or more, and rates it Type B with MIL after two trips. Without data from C the system cannot judge that part of the pack, so expect reduced power, blocked charging or no ready mode. U0111, U0112 and U014C cover modules A, B and D, U044B invalid data from C.
c: Low-voltage supply, fuse or ground of battery module C missing
Bus wiring or connector inside or at the battery pack damaged or corroded
Moisture or coolant in the pack affecting module C
Battery module C internally faulty or not programmed
s: Hybrid or EV system warning, reduced power
Charging refused or stopped
Vehicle may not enter ready mode

U014B.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Inductive Charging Module
U014B.d: U014B covers the vehicle-side controller of a wireless charging system. Inductive charging transfers energy without a plug, through a coil in a ground pad and a receiving coil under the car; the SAE J2954 standard, finalised in 2020, defines power classes of 3.7, 7.7 and 11 kW and relies on resonant coupling with about 85 percent efficiency. The module on board rectifies the received power, checks alignment and reports to the battery and charge controllers; if its messages stop, those controllers log U014B. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, and wireless charging is still rare in series production. The practical effect is that wireless charging does not start or is interrupted, while charging by cable and driving normally continue. U044C covers invalid data from this module.
c: Supply, fuse or ground of the inductive charging module missing
Wiring or connector to the underbody receiver damaged by water, salt or impact
Software of module and charge controller not matching
s: Wireless charging does not start or stops
Charging warning message, cable charging still works
Module not reachable with a scan tool

U014C.t: Lost Communication With Battery Energy Control Module D
U014C.d: U014C is the fourth slot in the battery controller family and points at module D. Such a letter is only needed where a pack is split into many sub-packs with their own monitoring boards, or where a vehicle carries an extra battery, for example a second traction pack or a separate 48 V unit, each reporting to a master controller. The master or the hybrid controller logs U014C once D's frames stop. No manufacturer explains the code publicly. As a guide, GM rates the comparable U0111 for module A as a Type B fault in its 2018 hybrid tables after a 500 ms gap, so a MIL is plausible here too. While D is silent, its cells cannot be supervised; the system will usually cut power, open contactors or refuse charging to stay safe. U0111, U0112 and U014A cover modules A to C.
c: Supply or ground of battery module D missing
Internal pack communication line or connector to D faulty
Master controller configured for a module D that does not match
s: Battery or hybrid system warning
Reduced drive power or no ready mode
Charging not possible

U014D.t: Lost Communication With Mirror Control Module B
U014D.d: U014D concerns the second networked mirror unit. Modern mirrors carry motors for adjustment and folding, a heating element, auto-dimming glass, turn-signal repeaters or blind-spot lamps, and the electronics for them often sit on the bus as their own node. J2012 provides two such units, and the receiver, usually the body or door controller, stores U014D when unit B stops replying. No manufacturer documents U014D publicly. FCA assigns the A slot, U0213, to the interior mirror: in STAR case S2108000013 the body controller logged it after a configuration restore wrongly marked a combined rear-view mirror unit as fitted, without any customer effect. Which mirror B is therefore depends on the make, often an outside mirror. Expect that mirror's adjustment, folding or heating to fail; no MIL. U044F is invalid data from B.
c: Broken wire in the flexing harness between body and door
Fuse, power or ground of mirror module B missing
Vehicle configuration expects a mirror module that is not fitted (FCA case for module A)
Water ingress or impact damage in the mirror housing
s: Mirror adjustment, folding or heating inoperative on one side
Blind-spot or turn-signal lamp in the mirror dark
Often no other effect; code found during a scan

U014E.t: Lost Communication With Multi-axis Acceleration Sensor Module B
U014E.d: U014E concerns a second inertial sensor module, B. Such a unit combines accelerometers and gyroscopes, measures turning rate and acceleration across and along the car, and sends the values over the bus. A second module typically appears where functions need redundant or separately mounted motion data, for instance brake-by-wire, driver assistance or rollover detection alongside the stability system. No manufacturer documents U014E publicly. Module A (U0125) is well documented: GM's 2019 brake controller for the XT4 flags a missing inertial frame after only 0.1 s and rates it Type C without MIL. A gap from module B would hit the functions that depend on it, so stability control, adaptive cruise or lane assistance may shut down with a warning while normal braking stays available. U0123 and U0124 cover single-axis sensor modules.
c: Connector or wiring of sensor module B corroded or broken
Power or ground of module B missing
Receiving controller software not matching module B
s: Stability control or traction warning on
Driver assistance such as adaptive cruise unavailable
Normal braking unaffected

U0150.d: U0150 is the last code of the gateway block and points at Gateway E. Gateways are central nodes that connect bus systems of different speed and type and forward only the messages each side needs. When E stops sending, the modules that expect its traffic log U0150, the way GM's U0100-U02FF procedure describes for any silent sender: a supervised periodic message is missing although supply voltage is in range. No manufacturer documents U0150 publicly; GM's U-code list ends its gateway entries at U0146. U0146 to U0149 refer to gateways A to D. Before suspecting the gateway, check power, ground and the bus lines to it; a code stored only in history after battery work needs no repair. MIL normally stays off.
c: Gateway E fuse blown or ground loose
Bus line to gateway E chafed or connector corroded
Gateway E software fault, update or reprogramming needed
s: Modules routed through gateway E not reachable by the scan tool
Several functions fail together
Warning messages in the instrument cluster

U0151.t: Lost Communication With Restraints Control Module
U0151.d: U0151 means the airbag control module, which reads crash sensors and fires airbags and belt pretensioners, no longer reaches a listener. Names vary: GM and Saab say sensing and diagnostic module, FCA occupant restraint controller, Honda SRS unit. GM's 2025 ECM allows most of its messages a gap of about 10 s and rates the loss Type C without MIL; the brake controller reacts after 100 or 250 ms, also Type C. The airbag lamp is the usual warning. Exceptions exist: on the 2024 electric Dodge Charger U0151 comes with the MIL and a car stuck in Park until the controller gets new software (08-015-26). On 2008-10 Accords the gauge module sets it when the SRS unit has failed, covered by a 15-year warranty extension; on 2018-20 Mazda CX-3s a stalled head-up display blocked the CAN bus and left U0151 in the ABS unit.
c: Airbag module fuse, ground or connector faulty (often under the seat or centre console)
Airbag control module internally failed (Honda Accord 2008-10)
Airbag module software needs updating (Dodge Charger 2024)
Another node blocks the bus, for example a faulty head-up display (Mazda CX-3)
s: Airbag warning lamp stays on
Airbags may not deploy in a crash if the module has failed
Several warning lamps or MIL on (Dodge Charger 2024)
Scan tool cannot communicate with the airbag module

U0152.t: Lost Communication With Side Restraints Control Module - Left
U0152.d: U0152 is the left-hand partner of U0153: a separate controller for the side restraints on the left no longer sends. In most cars side impacts are detected by satellite sensors in sills, B- or C-pillars that feed the central airbag unit; Bosch, for example, mounts its peripheral acceleration sensors on the left and right of the body and links them over the PSI5 sensor interface. Some architectures go further and give each side its own module on the vehicle bus, and only those can set this code. No manufacturer documents U0152 publicly. The listener, usually the main restraints module, logs the loss when the periodic message of the left unit is missing while voltage is in range. The airbag lamp lights and left-side or curtain protection may be lost; there is no MIL. U0151 is the main module, U0453 invalid data from the left unit.
c: Connector under the left seat or in the pillar loose or corroded
Power or ground of the left side module missing
Water ingress at the sill or door damaging wiring or module
Left side restraints module internally faulty
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side or curtain airbag possibly not ready
Code stored in the main airbag module

U0153.t: Lost Communication With Side Restraints Control Module Right
U0153.d: U0153 means the airbag system no longer hears from the separate control module for the right-side restraints. Some vehicles split the job: a central airbag unit plus side units that evaluate side impact sensors and fire side or curtain bags. When the right unit's periodic messages stop, the receiving modules store U0153, in the same way GM's U0100-U02FF logic treats any silent node. No manufacturer documents U0153 publicly; GM's list stops at U0151 for its single sensing and diagnostic module. U0152 is the left-hand twin, U0151 the main restraints module. The airbag warning lamp comes on and side protection on the right may be unavailable; no MIL. Work on airbag components belongs in a workshop.
c: Loose or corroded connector at the right side module (B-pillar or under the seat)
Power or ground of the right side module missing
Bus wiring damaged after seat or trim work
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side or curtain airbag may not deploy
Scan tool cannot reach the right side module

U0154.t: Lost Communication With Restraints Occupant Classification System Module
U0154.d: U0154 is stored when the occupant classification module goes silent. This unit evaluates sensors in the front passenger seat, such as a weight mat or pressure bladder, and tells the airbag controller whether the seat is empty, holds a child seat or an adult, so that the passenger airbag can be suppressed or allowed. Chrysler is the maker found documenting the code: its restraint controller fault list, submitted to NHTSA in investigation PE11-019, names U0154 as lost communication with the occupant classification module, next to B223D for a fault reported by that module itself. Mercedes-AMG is a special case: on 2023 C- and S-Class models U015400 appears in the AMG drive unit with the engine lamp, put down to Ethernet wake-up timing. Normally the airbag lamp and passenger airbag indicator react. U0455 is invalid data from this module.
c: Connector under the passenger seat loose, damaged or pulled during seat work
Power or ground of the classification module missing
Classification module or seat sensor internally faulty
Network wake-up timing or software issue (Mercedes-AMG 2023)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag on/off indicator wrong or flashing
Passenger airbag deactivated or in a default state

U0155.t: Lost Communication With Instrument Panel Cluster (IPC) Control Module
U0155.d: U0155 says a listener no longer receives the instrument cluster, which shows speed and warnings and on many cars also produces chimes and turn-signal ticks. The cause is not always the cluster: on 2017 GM full-size trucks and SUVs several modules logged U0155 when the serial data gateway hung, so dead gauges came from the gateway (PIT5586G). The code can also trigger the MIL. Honda's 2021 Accord and HR-V and 2022 Odyssey lit it with U0155 after the evaporative leak check, when shutdown commands between units did not match; new engine software fixed it (21-021). Ford's 2020 Explorer showed MIL and wrench lamp with U0155 and U0100 due to gear shift module software (SSM 49218). FCA writes Cluster/CCN, Saab Instrument Cluster. U0423 covers invalid cluster data, U0156 the information center.
c: Cluster fuse, ground or connector behind the dash faulty
Gateway hangs and stops forwarding cluster messages (GM PIT5586G)
Software of another module causes false loss of communication (Honda 21-021, Ford SSM 49218)
s: Gauges dead, frozen or sweeping
No chimes or turn-signal ticking
MIL on in some vehicles (Honda 2021-22, Ford Explorer 2020)
Several warning lamps and codes in many modules

U0156.t: Lost Communication With Information Center A
U0156.d: U0156 concerns information center A, the display and infotainment unit that shows messages, audio, navigation or vehicle settings. Two makers document the code. Mazda calls the partner the connectivity master unit, its infotainment head unit: on 2019-20 Mazda3 and CX-30 the vehicle and body controllers store U0156:00 with an in-vehicle network malfunction message (SA-029/20), and on 2024-25 CX-90 and CX-70 the engine controller logs it alongside a blank center screen, dark interior lights and a start only with the key held near the button, because the 25 A fuse F1 removed for transport was not fully seated (SA-040/24). Volvo's central electronic module sets U015600 on 2011-15 S60, S80, XC60 and XC70 when the Sensus screen stays black after a memory chip fault (TJ 25872). U0157 is center B, U0457 invalid data from A.
c: Supply fuse of the unit missing or not fully seated (Mazda SA-040/24)
Infotainment unit internally faulty, for example memory chip (Volvo TJ 25872)
Infotainment software hangs or needs an update
Bus wiring or connector behind the dash faulty
s: Center display black, no audio or navigation
Network malfunction or several warning messages in the cluster
Climate or vehicle settings that run through the screen unavailable

U0157.t: Lost Communication With Information Center B
U0157.d: U0157 is set when the second information display, Information Center B, stops transmitting on the vehicle bus. J2012 provides two such driver information displays, A (U0156) and B, separate from the instrument cluster (U0155) and the head-up display (U0158); which screen counts as B is up to the manufacturer. The setting logic is the generic one GM documents for U0100-U02FF: a monitored periodic message is missing while the supply sits between 9 and 16 V, and every module waiting for it logs the code. No manufacturer documents U0157 publicly; GM's list carries only U0155 and U0158. The display stays dark or frozen, the rest of the car is mostly unaffected, and no MIL comes on.
c: Display unit B without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Bus line or connector behind the dashboard damaged
Display software hang or failed update
s: Secondary display dark, frozen or showing no data
Messages normally shown on display B missing
Code stored in several modules

U0158.t: Lost Communication With Head Up Display
U0158.d: U0158 means the head-up display, which projects speed, navigation arrows or warnings into the windscreen, has stopped answering the module that supervises it, usually the instrument cluster. GM lists it in the Saab 9-5 (2011) U-code table and covers it in bulletin 22-NA-113: on 2020-2022 Cadillac CT4/CT5 with RPO UV6 the cluster stores U0158 when LIN messages arrive at an awkward moment while the HUD enters standby, leaving it blank until reset; the fix is a cluster reflash and pulling the HUD fuse. Stellantis notes for the 2021 Jeep Grand Cherokee WL and the 2024-25 Charger/Wagoneer S that the cluster may log it when leaving transport mode; clearing is enough there. U0459 covers implausible HUD data. No MIL.
c: HUD stuck in standby due to message timing, cured by cluster software (GM CT4/CT5)
Stored entry from transport/logistics mode on new vehicles (Stellantis)
HUD fuse, supply or ground interrupted
LIN/CAN line or connector under the dashboard faulty
s: Head-up display blank or frozen
Brightness, height or page settings have no effect
Display returns after an ignition cycle

U0159.t: Lost Communication With Parking Assist Control Module A
U0159.d: U0159 reports that parking assist control module A, which evaluates the ultrasonic sensors and drives the distance warnings, has fallen silent. GM spells out the check for the brake module: the 2019 Cadillac XT4 EBCM (19OBDG03D) and the 2020 brake module tables (20OBDG03C) set it when the automatic-parking braking request is missing for more than 0.25 s, Type C, no MIL. GM bulletins PIT5507E (2014-2018 full-size trucks and SUVs) and 20-NA-099 (CT6) cure start-up U0159 entries with new park assist software. Ford SSM 51486 (2023 Super Duty) and VW TSB 01-24-02 (2024 ID.4) treat it as a harmless ABS entry; Stellantis S2108000149 asks for module updates. Park assist then switches off.
c: Park assist module software fault, fixed by reprogramming (GM PIT5507E, 20-NA-099)
Modules on different software levels (Stellantis S2108000149)
Park assist module without power or ground
Harmless entry after remote start or wake-up (Ford, VW)
Bus line or connector in the bumper/rear area damaged
s: Park assist unavailable or Service Parking Assist message
Park assist switch cannot turn the system on or off
Code stored in brake module, cluster or BCM

U015A.t: Lost Communication With Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module B
U015A.d: U015A concerns a second anti-lock brake controller, module B. Vehicles prepared for automated driving need braking that still works after a single fault, so suppliers pair two independent units, for example Bosch's iBooster with the ESP control unit. If the partner that monitors module B, typically the primary brake controller or the driving automation computer, no longer receives its periodic messages, U015A is stored. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the setting idea follows GM's generic rule for lost-communication codes (supervised message missing at 9-16 V). U0121 is ABS module A, U045B flags implausible data from B. Expect a brake or assistance warning and blocked automated functions.
c: Brake module B without power or ground (own fuse in redundant layouts)
Bus line or connector to module B in the engine bay corroded or open
Brake modules on incompatible software after repair
