ABS control module B internally faulty
s: Brake system or driver assistance warning in the cluster
Automated driving or adaptive cruise functions unavailable
Code stored in the primary brake controller

U015B.t: Lost Communication With Power Steering Control Module B
U015B.d: U015B is set when the second power steering controller, module B, stops sending. Redundant steering for automated driving splits the electronics into two paths so one can keep assisting if the other fails; Bosch describes such a fail-operational design with an electrical fallback giving roughly half the normal assist. A listener such as the primary steering unit or the driving automation computer logs U015B when B's messages are missing, following the pattern GM documents for its U0100-U02FF codes at 9-16 V. No manufacturer documents U015B publicly. Module A is U0131, implausible data from B is U045C. Normal steering usually continues on path A, but automated steering is blocked and a steering warning may appear.
c: Steering module B without power or ground (separate supply path)
Connector at the steering rack or column wet, loose or corroded
Steering modules not matched after replacement or update
Power steering control module B internally faulty
s: Steering system warning in the cluster
Lane centring or automated steering unavailable
Steering assist possibly reduced

U015C.t: Lost Communication With Automated Driving System Control Module A
U015C.d: U015C points to automated driving system control module A, the computer that fuses camera and radar data for adaptive cruise, lane centring and emergency braking. Stellantis documents it in detail. In 2024-25 Dodge Charger and Jeep Wagoneer S with Active Driving Assist (TSB 08-256-25 to 08-259-25), MIL plus U015C-00 and U045D-00 call for new software in the front long-range radar. TSB 08-190-24 reflashes the Central ADAS Decision Module on early 2024 Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer. Case S2508000095 (2026 Wagoneer) shows CADM2 logging U015C with an Ethernet link error, traced to tight cable routing. U015D is module B. Assistance features drop out and the MIL can light.
c: Software in front radar or ADAS decision module outdated (Stellantis TSBs)
Ethernet cable routed too tight, connector pins loosened
ADS control module A without power or ground
ADS control module A internally faulty
s: Automatic Emergency Braking Unavailable message
Adaptive cruise and lane settings not stored between drives
MIL on (Stellantis)

U015D.t: Lost Communication With Automated Driving System Control Module B
U015D.d: U015D names automated driving system control module B. Where the driving assistance computer is split into two halves, each half and the navigation and motion module watch the other over Ethernet. Stellantis case S2508000095 for the 2026 Jeep Wagoneer lists U015D-00 in the CADM and in the GNMM, together with Ethernet link and time-sync faults. Replaced modules showed no defect; the cause was harness routing that pulled on the Ethernet plugs and loosened pins. The fix is to inspect and replace the harness, which must not be spliced, and to correct the position of clip C121. The driver sees blind-spot warnings, mirror lamps staying lit and disabled ADAS. U015C is module A, U045E implausible data from B.
c: Ethernet harness too taut, pins pushed out or fretted (Stellantis S2508000095)
Harness clip in wrong position, connectors under strain
ADS control module B without power or ground
ADS control module B internally faulty
s: Blindspot Alert Unavailable message
Blind-spot lamps in the mirrors stay lit
Driver assistance features disabled intermittently

U015E.t: Lost Communication With Automated Driving System Interface Module A
U015E.d: U015E concerns interface module A, the link that passes commands from an automated driving computer to the base vehicle's brakes, steering and powertrain and reports their state back. Such interfaces belong to the act layer of the sense-think-act chain that Bosch uses to describe automated driving. When its messages stop, the automation computer can no longer command the actuators, so it has to hand control back to the driver or reach a safe stop. No manufacturer documents U015E publicly, and SAE J3016 defines only the automation levels, not the hardware. U015F is interface module B, U015C and U015D are the control modules, U045F flags implausible data from A.
c: Interface module A without power or ground
Bus or Ethernet connection to the interface damaged or strained
Interface and automation computer on mismatched software
s: Automated driving mode cannot be activated
Takeover request or controlled stop during automated driving
Driver assistance warning in the cluster

U015F.t: Lost Communication With Automated Driving System Interface Module B
U015F.d: U015F is the companion code for automated driving system interface module B. A second interface lets a fail-operational design keep a path to the vehicle actuators when the first one drops out, which matters most above SAE level 2, where the system rather than the driver watches the road. When B goes silent, the remaining path may still work, but redundancy is gone, and most systems then refuse to engage or ask the driver to take over. No manufacturer documents U015F publicly; the setting rule matches GM's generic description: a supervised periodic message is missing while supply sits between 9 and 16 V. U015E is module A, U0460 flags implausible data from B. Manual driving stays unaffected.
c: Interface module B fuse, supply or ground faulty
Connector or line of the redundant bus path damaged
Module B not updated together with the other ADS modules
s: Automated driving unavailable, redundancy fault message
Request to take over steering and braking
Code stored in the automation computer

U0160.t: Lost Communication With Audible Alert Control Module
U0160.d: U0160 is stored when the audible alert module, the unit that produces chimes for an open door, unfastened belt, key left in or lights on, drops off the bus. GM uses it: the Saab 9-5 (2011) U-code list calls the unit Chime Alarm Control Module, and by GM's generic procedure the code appears once the chime unit's cyclic status frame stays away while the supply is within 9 to 16 V. Many newer vehicles let the instrument cluster or the radio play these tones, so a separate module exists only on some models. U0461 covers implausible data from this module; U013F concerns the external pedestrian sound generator, a different device. Warning tones fall silent or sound constantly; no MIL.
c: Chime module fuse blown or ground loose
Connector or bus line behind the dashboard damaged
Vehicle configured for a separate chime module that is not fitted
s: No chime for open door, belt or lights
Chime sounds continuously or at wrong times
Code stored in the BCM or cluster

U0161.d: U0161 says the compass module no longer reports. In many vehicles the electronic compass sits in the interior mirror or the overhead console: a pair of perpendicular magnetic sensors measures the earth's field, and the module sends the heading to a display. A Gentex patent describes such a mirror compass and mentions output over the vehicle bus. The receiving unit, usually the instrument cluster or an overhead display, stores U0161 when the expected heading messages stop; the general rule is GM's description for U0100-U02FF codes. No manufacturer documents U0161 publicly. U0462 flags implausible compass data. The heading display shows dashes or disappears; no MIL and no effect on driving.
c: Compass module or mirror without power or ground
Connector at the mirror or headliner loose, e.g. after windscreen replacement
Data line in the A-pillar or headliner damaged
Compass module or mirror electronics faulty
s: Compass heading missing or shown as dashes
Compass calibration not possible
Code stored in the cluster or overhead module

U0162.t: Lost Communication With Navigation Display Module
U0162.d: U0162 indicates that the navigation display, typically the screen unit of the head unit, no longer answers. Subaru documents it in two settings. TechTIPS 10/2015 describes a 2015 Legacy/Outback with Fujitsu Ten navigation that stored U0162 together with U0100, U0101 and U0122; the real cause was a wire not locked into the under-hood fuse box, which unseated the 30 A fuse feeding the IG2 relay. Bulletin 07-205-22 (2021 Crosstrek, 2020-22 Forester) has the rear vehicle detection module store U0162 and light the SRVD warning; new SRVD software improves CAN traffic with the head unit. U0163 is the navigation control unit, U0463 implausible display data. Map and screen may fail; no MIL.
c: Supply interrupted, e.g. loose terminal at the fuse box (Subaru TechTIPS)
Software of the receiving module, e.g. rear radar control unit (Subaru 07-205-22)
Connector behind the head unit loose after radio work
Navigation display or head unit faulty
s: Navigation screen dark or not responding
Rear vehicle detection warning lamp on (Subaru)
Several communication codes stored at once

U0163.t: Lost Communication With Navigation Control Module
U0163.d: U0163 is logged when the navigation control module, the computer that works out position and route, stops communicating. In many cars this function is built into the head unit, in others it is a separate box behind the trim. Listeners such as the instrument cluster, a camera unit or the telematics module show turn arrows or a map on their own screens and therefore watch its messages; GM's general rule for U0100-U02FF codes applies: supervised message missing at 9-16 V. No manufacturer documents U0163 in an openly accessible source. U0162 refers to the navigation display, U016A to a separate GPS receiver, U0464 to implausible navigation data. Navigation, map and route guidance fail; no MIL.
c: Navigation unit fuse, supply or ground faulty
Connector at the head unit or navigation box loose or corroded
Navigation software hang or failed map/software update
s: Navigation and route guidance unavailable
Turn arrows missing in the cluster or head-up display
Code stored in the cluster or other display modules

U0164.t: Lost Communication With HVAC Control Module
U0164.d: U0164 is stored by any module that stops hearing the HVAC control module, the unit that runs blower, flaps and temperature selection. GM documents two monitors in its 2025 tables (25OBDG03B): the body control module watches several HVAC frames and flags a gap longer than 12.5 s at 11-18 V, and the central gateway reacts after 6.5 s once a frame is overdue by 2.5 times its period; both are Type B, so the MIL can come on after two trips. Ford SSM 47040 (Escape 2017-2018) finds U0164 in the BCM and starts with a battery reset; GM PIT5586G and Stellantis case S2308000122 (Wagoneer) trace it to gateway or inline bus connectors. U0165 is the rear unit, U010F the A/C module. Climate controls go dead.
c: Loose or spread terminals at gateway or inline bus connectors
HVAC module without power or ground
Incomplete module configuration or hung module, cleared by battery reset (Ford)
s: Climate control panel dark or not responding
Blower, temperature or defrost stuck at last setting
Check engine light on some GM models after two trips
Code stored in several modules at once

U0165.t: Lost Communication With HVAC Control Module - Rear
U0165.d: U0165 names a second climate unit, the rear HVAC control module, fitted in vans, minivans and large SUVs that heat and cool the back rows with their own blower and flaps. The code says this rear module has gone quiet on the network; the front unit is covered by U0164. No manufacturer documents U0165 publicly, and the GM/Saab and Ford code lists checked here skip it. The trigger follows the pattern GM gives for every code from U0100 to U02FF: the module's periodic availability message fails to arrive while the supply lies between 9 and 16 V, and each listener records the fault. Rear vents then stop reacting or keep a fixed setting, while the front climate and the engine run normally. No MIL is expected.
c: Rear HVAC module without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Bus wiring to the rear unit chafed under trim or at sliding-door area
Vehicle coded for rear climate that is not fitted
s: Rear climate controls without function
Rear blower stuck off or at one speed
Front climate keeps working normally

U0166.t: Lost Communication With Auxiliary Heater Control Module
U0166.d: U0166 reports that the auxiliary heater control module has stopped communicating. Such heaters, burning fuel or working electrically, warm the coolant or the cabin air before or during a drive and are common on diesels and cold-climate packages. GM lists the code in the engine controller of the 6.6 L LML Duramax (14OBDG10): it fails when no message from the heater module has come in for more than 2.5 s after the ignition has been on for at least 3 s at 9-16 V, and it is a special Type C fault that does not light the MIL. The Saab 9-5 U-code list and Ford's 2014 Boss 302S code list also include U0166. U0164 is the main HVAC module. In practice the extra heater stays off, so warm-up and cabin heat take longer in winter.
c: Heater module fuse blown or ground corroded (often underbody mounting)
Corroded heater connector from road splash
Bus line to the heater damaged
s: Auxiliary or parking heater does not start
Slow engine and cabin warm-up in cold weather
Code stored in the engine or climate controller

U0167.t: Lost Communication With Vehicle Immobilizer Control Module
U0167.d: U0167 means the vehicle immobilizer control module, which checks the transponder in the key and then releases the engine controller, can no longer be heard on the bus. Since the key handshake cannot complete, the engine typically cranks without firing or does not crank at all. Ford's 2014 Boss 302S code list and the Saab 9-5 code list contain U0167. Triumph reported it in 2024 on Speed 400 and Scrambler 400 X motorcycles after an immobiliser software update: the bike would not start, and switching off fully and repeating the calibration download was the remedy. Chrysler deviates from the J2012 name: a 2011 Jeep field report filed with NHTSA assigns U0167 to an intrusion transceiver module. U0168 is the separate security module.
c: Immobilizer module or antenna ring without power or ground
Interrupted or faulty immobilizer software update (Triumph 2024)
Bus or connector at the steering column damaged
s: Engine cranks but does not start, or no crank
Immobilizer or key symbol flashes
Key not recognised

U0168.t: Lost Communication With Vehicle Security Control Module
U0168.d: U0168 points to the vehicle security control module, which handles anti-theft and key authorisation and in many layouts also hosts the immobilizer handshake. Chrysler shows the link: its 2011 field report names U0168 for the SKREEM/WCM, and bulletin 18-023-13 (Grand Voyager 2.8 L diesel 2012-2013) treats it as a sign of a failed ignition handshake that new PCM software fixes. Jeep TSB 08-088-25 (Grand Cherokee 4xe 2024) lists it with MIL and a no-start. Mercedes stores U0168 in the 48 V starter-alternator of the 2021 S 580 for the electronic ignition lock; the MIL clears after three drive cycles. GM's Saab list calls it the keyless entry module. U0167 is the immobilizer module, U0427 invalid security data.
c: Engine or security module software mishandles the key handshake (Chrysler, Jeep, Mercedes updates)
Security module without power or ground
Bus line or connector to the security module faulty
Security or keyless entry module faulty
s: No start or delayed start
Check engine light on (Jeep 4xe, Mercedes S 580)
Keyless entry, alarm or key detection not working

U0169.t: Lost Communication With Sunroof Control Module
U0169.d: U0169 is set when the sunroof control module drops off the vehicle network. This unit drives the motors for the glass panel and, where fitted, the sun blind, keeps track of their positions and provides the anti-pinch reversal. No manufacturer documents U0169 publicly; GM's U-code list and the bulletins in the NHTSA index do not contain it. The generic trigger described by GM for lost-communication codes applies: a periodic message expected from the module is absent at a supply of 9-16 V, and the listening body controller logs the code. Because the module usually sits in the roof next to the opening, water from blocked drains is a plausible culprit besides fuses and connectors. The roof ignores its switch and comfort closing; no MIL. U046A is invalid sunroof data.
c: Sunroof module fuse blown or ground loose
Water at module or connector from blocked roof drains
Headliner wiring or connector to the module damaged
s: Sunroof does not open or close electrically
Comfort closing with the key no longer closes the roof
Roof positions or one-touch function lost

U016A.t: Lost Communication With Global Positioning System Module
U016A.d: U016A covers the global positioning system module, the receiver that supplies position, speed and time to navigation, telematics and emergency-call functions. Ford uses the code: its 2014 Boss 302S code list includes it, and SSM 54351 explains that 2026 Transit vans built without a telematics control unit may log U016A in the module Ford calls SOBDMC, alongside U0146 in the ABS module. Since nothing is fitted there, no repair is needed in that case. On vehicles that do carry the receiver, the usual causes are a lost supply or a bus fault at the module. Navigation then shows a wrong or frozen position and connected services may lose location data, while driving is unaffected and no MIL comes on. U046B is invalid GPS data.
c: Module not fitted on this build, code without fault (Ford Transit 2026)
GPS or telematics unit without power or ground
Bus wiring or connector at the receiver faulty
s: Navigation shows wrong or no position
Telematics or emergency call reports location unavailable
Clock or compass no longer updated by satellite

U016B.t: Lost Communication With A/C Compressor Control Module
U016B.d: U016B appears when the control module of the electric A/C compressor, the inverter fed from the high-voltage battery in hybrids and EVs, stops talking to its partners. In GM's 2016 Volt table (16OBDG01) the engine controller watches frame $222 and fails after 10 s, Type B with MIL after two trips. GM bulletin 18-NA-096 (Volt and CT6 plug-in 2017-2018) explains a MIL with U016B after service: the compressor was unplugged while the bus was still awake, and a power-down followed by a battery disconnect clears it. PIC6609 (Blazer EV, Equinox EV, Optiq 2025) finds the compressor's low-voltage harness chafing against the right front driveshaft, with charging limited to 26 %. Saab lists the code as well. Cabin and battery cooling suffer.
c: Compressor unplugged while the bus was awake, stored code without real fault (GM 18-NA-096)
Compressor low-voltage harness chafed on axle shaft or bracket (GM PIC6609)
Compressor control module without 12 V supply or ground
s: Air conditioning blows warm
Check engine or service high voltage message, charging possibly limited
Reduced battery cooling or charging power in heat

U016C.t: Lost Communication With Fuel Pump Control Module B
U016C.d: U016C concerns fuel pump control module B, the second pump driver in vehicles with two pumps or two tanks; module A has U0109. Ford's 2020-2023 gasoline OBD summary watches pump B through its duty-cycle feedback line: a signal stuck at 0 % or 100 % sets U016C within 2-5 s at 11-16 V. Roush CleanTech's propane-converted Ford trucks pass the state of the second fuel pump relay to the PCM through a smart relay module, so wiring, fuse or relay faults on that path trigger it too. Stellantis case S2108000100 (Ram 1500 2021) shows U0109 and U016C together with a check engine lamp and crank-no-start, cured by cleaning frame ground G803A. CARB requires lost digital links like this to be detected. Fuel supply is at risk; MIL expected.
c: Loose or corroded frame ground at the pump module (Ram G803A)
Fuse or relay for pump B or its driver open
Feedback or bus wiring between pump driver B and PCM damaged
Fuel pump control module B faulty
s: Check engine light on
Crank but no start, or stalling
Lack of power or rough running under load

U016D.t: Lost Communication With Exhaust Gas Sensor Module B
U016D.d: U016D refers to exhaust gas sensor module B, a second smart sensor unit in the exhaust that heats a probe, evaluates it and reports oxygen or NOx readings as bus data instead of an analog voltage. Module A has U011A. Which sensor counts as B depends on the maker, for instance the other bank or a probe further downstream behind an SCR catalyst. No manufacturer documents U016D publicly, and the NHTSA bulletin index has no entry for it. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 obliges OBD to flag a lost digital link from such an input with its own code, and exhaust and NOx sensors are emission monitors in their own right, so the MIL is normally lit. Mixture correction, catalyst checks or urea dosing may fall back to defaults. U046E is invalid data from module B.
c: Sensor module connector or harness damaged by exhaust heat or corrosion
Sensor module without power or ground (fuse, relay)
Bus line to the module chafed under the vehicle
Sensor module B or integrated probe electronics faulty
s: Check engine light on
Readiness monitors for catalyst or exhaust sensors not complete
Diesel: SCR or emission warning, possibly reduced power

U0170.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor A
U0170.d: U0170 is the first slot in the J2012 block for remote restraint sensors: sensor A has gone silent for the airbag control unit or another listener. Chrysler follows that scheme. In the Jeep airbag tables it handed to NHTSA (Wrangler JK 2007-2010, Compass/Patriot MK, Liberty KK, Grand Cherokee WK and Commander XK 2008) U0170 is the up-front left satellite acceleration sensor, and B1B70 reports an internal fault of that same part. GM assigns the number differently: the Saab 9-5 and 9-4X U-code lists give it to the passenger presence detection module, and GM bulletin PI1202 shows the SDM logging U0170 on 2013-14 Enclave, Traverse and Acadia when a harness rubbing on the exhaust disturbs the LAN. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Connector at the front satellite sensor unplugged or corroded, often after front-end repairs
Sensor A or its bracket damaged in a frontal knock
On GM vehicles (passenger presence module) chafed or pinched low-speed LAN wiring
Sensor input of the airbag control unit faulty
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Early frontal crash detection on the left reduced (Chrysler)
On GM vehicles further U-codes in several modules at the same time

U0171.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor B
U0171.d: U0171 says the airbag control unit receives nothing more from restraint sensor B. Chrysler documents it as the up-front right satellite acceleration sensor, the mirror image of U0170, in each Jeep airbag listing it supplied for investigation PE11-019, starting with the 2007 Wrangler; an internal defect of that unit is logged separately as B1B71. Front satellites of this kind sit inside the crumple zone. Bosch notes that they sharpen frontal crash detection beyond what the sensors inside the central unit can do, so without B the decision for the right half rests on less information. The location is exposed to spray, salt and collision damage, so after front-end body work an unplugged or wet connector is the first suspect. Other makes may give B another position. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Connector of the right front sensor not reconnected after bumper or front-end work
Water or road salt in the sensor connector at the front
Front satellite sensor B damaged in a collision
Sensor line to the airbag unit open or shorted
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal impact sensing on the right side relies on the central unit only
Code comes back immediately after clearing while the fault persists

U0172.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor C
U0172.d: U0172 marks a lost link to restraint sensor C. Chrysler uses it for the first left side satellite acceleration sensor in the Jeep tables of NHTSA file PE11-019. The Wrangler JK has just this one sensor on each side, whereas Compass/Patriot, Liberty, Grand Cherokee and Commander add a second left unit reported as U0173. Bosch fits side sensors of this type to load-bearing parts such as sills, seat cross members and the B- or C-pillar, because a side impact leaves almost no crush space and the airbag unit must decide within a few milliseconds. With sensor C missing, left side and curtain airbag deployment may be degraded. An internal fault of the sensor appears as B1B72 instead. Water in the footwell or seat removal are typical triggers. No MIL.
c: Water in the left footwell or sill area reaching the sensor connector
Connector disturbed during seat, carpet or trim removal
Left side satellite sensor failed after a side knock
Airbag control unit input or configuration faulty
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side and curtain airbag deployment may be impaired
Fault can be intermittent with wet carpets or after rain

U0173.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor D
U0173.d: U0173 tells that the airbag control unit no longer receives data from remote crash sensor D. Such satellite sensors sit in the crumple zone, doors or pillars and report acceleration in one or two axes so the control unit can judge direction and severity of an impact. Chrysler documents the code: in its 2006-2010 Jeep airbag code list U0173 stands for the second left-side satellite acceleration sensor, beside U0170/U0171 (front left/right), U0172 (left side 1) and U0175/U0176 (right side). Which position letter D has on other makes is their choice. The airbag warning lamp lights, protection on that side may be reduced, and there is no MIL. Diagnosis and repair belong to trained staff only.
c: Loose or corroded connector at satellite sensor D
Sensor line damaged, e.g. in the door or pillar area
Satellite sensor D failed (water ingress, impact)
Sensor input of the airbag control unit faulty
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side impact detection on the affected side reduced
Code stays active until the sensor link is restored

U0174.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor E
U0174.d: U0174 refers to restraint sensor E, the fifth remote crash sensor in J2012 lettering. No manufacturer documents U0174 publicly. Chrysler's Jeep tables in NHTSA file PE11-019 go from U0173 straight to U0175, so slot E is simply not used there. Where it is fitted, such a sensor usually hangs on a two-wire PSI5 line that carries power and data at once: the control unit sends sync pulses and expects the reply in a fixed time slot, so an open wire, a short or a dead sensor shows up as missing frames. Before buying parts, check with a scan tool whether the airbag unit is really configured for sensor E; a replacement unit with the wrong coding can complain about sensors the car does not have. U0475 is the invalid-data partner. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Connector at sensor E loose, wet or corroded
Airbag unit coded for a sensor E that is not fitted (e.g. after unit replacement)
Two-wire sensor line open or shorted
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Scan tool lists sensor E as not responding
Deployment paths depending on sensor E may be blocked

U0175.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor F
U0175.d: U0175 is set when restraint sensor F stops reporting. Chrysler names it the right side satellite acceleration sensor 1 throughout the restraint code lists of the NHTSA probe PE11-019, from the 2007 Wrangler JK to the 2008 Grand Cherokee and Commander; its counterpart on the left is U0172, and B1B75 flags an internal defect of the sensor. On the passenger side the part sits low on the body structure, so wet carpets, a removed passenger seat or a slipped connector under the trim are common findings. Bosch offers single-axis sensors and two-axis versions that also measure longitudinal acceleration, which is why a mounting position and part number must match the vehicle. Side airbags must fire within milliseconds, and without F the right-hand decision is weaker. No MIL.
c: Moisture in the right footwell or sill reaching the connector
Connector or line disturbed when the passenger seat was removed
Wrong sensor version or mounting orientation after replacement
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side and curtain airbag readiness reduced
Fault may appear only on bumpy roads (loose contact)

U0176.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor G
U0176.d: U0176 points to restraint sensor G. In Chrysler's usage, as recorded in the NHTSA investigation PE11-019, it is the second right side satellite acceleration sensor. Of those Jeeps, only MK (Compass/Patriot), KK (Liberty), WK and XK (Grand Cherokee, Commander) carry it, together with its left twin U0173; the Wrangler JK lists no second side sensor at all, so U0176 on a Wrangler of those years hints at wrong configuration rather than a broken part. Internal faults of this sensor appear as B1B76. A second sensor per side usually sits further back, for example near the C-pillar, which Bosch names as a mounting point, and helps cover rear-seat occupants and long curtain airbags. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Connector behind the rear side or pillar trim loose or damaged
Line to the rear right sensor pinched or chafed
Airbag unit configured for a second side sensor the vehicle does not have
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side impact detection for the rear right area reduced
Code stays active until sensor link or configuration is corrected

U0177.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor H
U0177.d: U0177 is stored when crash sensor H, the eighth remote sensor of the restraint system in J2012 lettering, stops reporting to the airbag control unit. Remote acceleration or pressure sensors detect front, side or rear impacts early and feed the central unit that decides on deployment. No manufacturer documents U0177 publicly. Chrysler's Jeep airbag list from 2006-2010 shows how the block is used, assigning U0170 to U0176 to front and side satellites, but ends before H; so U0177 only appears on vehicles with very many satellites. Siblings U0170 to U0176, U0178 and U0179 name the other sensor positions. Result: airbag warning lamp on, possibly reduced protection in one zone, no MIL. Leave airbag work to a workshop.
c: Connector at sensor H loose, wet or corroded
Sensor wiring damaged by trim or body work
Airbag control unit input faulty or wrong configuration
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Impact detection in the zone of sensor H unavailable
Code returns immediately after clearing

U0178.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor I
U0178.d: U0178 covers restraint sensor I, the ninth remote crash sensor; unlike many letter series, J2012 does use the letter I here. No manufacturer documents U0178 publicly. High sensor counts come mainly from combining sensor types: Bosch connects two or four door pressure sensors to the airbag unit in addition to the acceleration sensors on the body structure, so a four-door car can easily exceed eight satellites. A pressure sensor in the door cavity registers the pressure rise when the door is pushed in. Its wiring passes through the door hinge area, where repeated opening can break conductors, and water inside the door can reach the connector. Such sensors are often linked via PSI5, a two-wire interface. U0479 reports invalid data from the same sensor. No MIL.
c: Broken wire in the door hinge passage
Water inside the door at the sensor connector (failed vapour barrier)
Sensor interface of the airbag unit faulty
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Fault may come and go with door movement
Impact detection in the zone of sensor I unavailable

U0179.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor J
U0179.d: U0179 closes the J2012 block for remote restraint sensors and names sensor J, the tenth position (the letter I is used as well, see U0178). The airbag control unit checks that each connected satellite keeps sending; if sensor J falls silent, the unit stores U0179, switches on the airbag warning lamp and may disable the deployment paths that rely on it. No manufacturer documents U0179 publicly, and Chrysler's published Jeep list stops at the sixth satellite (U0176), so this code is rare. Bosch describes peripheral sensors in front, side and rear positions, which explains why up to ten slots exist. U0170 to U0178 cover sensors A to I, U0151 the airbag unit itself. No MIL; repairs only by trained staff.
c: Connector at sensor J loose or corroded
Open or shorted line between sensor J and the airbag unit
Crash sensor J failed, e.g. after a minor impact
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Restraint deployment relying on sensor J may be disabled
Scan tool shows sensor J as not responding

U017A.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor K
U017A.d: U017A is logged when restraint sensor K, the eleventh remote crash sensor, has stopped sending data to the restraints module. No manufacturer documents U017A publicly; the Chrysler Jeep lists in NHTSA file PE11-019 end at the sixth satellite. Why J2012 reserves so many slots becomes clear from supplier data: a current Bosch airbag control unit serves 12 PSI5 sensor interfaces, a premium version up to 18. Higher letters therefore belong to well-equipped vehicles, for example with rear-impact sensors, which Bosch also lists as a mounting option. After rear-end repairs or work in the boot floor, check first whether such a sensor was reconnected. Deployment that depends on sensor K may be switched off; the airbag lamp lights, the MIL stays off.
c: Sensor K not reconnected after rear-end or boot floor repairs
Sensor line damaged along the rear body
Airbag unit configuration does not match the fitted sensors
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Restraint functions depending on sensor K may be disabled
Scan tool shows sensor K as absent

U017B.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor L
U017B.d: U017B means sensor L of the restraint system, the twelfth remote crash sensor in J2012 order, no longer answers. No manufacturer documents U017B publicly, so which component sits behind the letter depends on the car. One example of how sensor counts grow: airbag control units can also run pedestrian protection, fed by acceleration sensors or by a pressure tube in the front bumper. In the Bosch pressure tube system, an air-filled silicone tube in the bumper has a pressure sensor at each end, and the unit can raise an active bonnet or fire a windscreen airbag 10 to 15 ms after striking a pedestrian. Bumper replacement or a parking knock are then typical reasons for a lost sensor. The airbag or pedestrian protection warning lights; no MIL.
c: Sensor or its connector not refitted after bumper replacement
Sensor or wiring damaged by a minor front or side knock
Corroded connector in an exposed mounting position
s: Airbag or pedestrian protection warning on
Protective function assigned to sensor L disabled
Fault appears after body or bumper work

U017C.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor M
U017C.d: U017C is stored once restraint sensor M, the thirteenth remote crash sensor, falls silent. No manufacturer documents U017C publicly. For diagnosis it matters whether the code is current or only stored: according to the PSI5 working group, a brief drop in supply makes a sensor restart and send initialisation data first, so a loose contact can leave a history entry without a lasting fault. Wiggle tests on the connector and harness while watching live status are therefore more useful than replacing parts. Mechanical fit counts too: Audi, for example, inserts its capacitive door pressure sensors into the inner door panel with a seal and turns them to lock, and a poorly seated sensor after trim work can fail. U047D reports invalid data instead of silence. No MIL.
c: Intermittent contact at sensor M connector (history code)
Sensor not seated or sealed correctly after trim work
s: Airbag warning lamp on or flickering
Code stored as history after the lamp went out again
Impact detection in the zone of sensor M unavailable while active

U017D.t: Lost Communication With Restraints System Sensor N
U017D.d: U017D concerns restraint sensor N, the last of the fourteen sensor letters A to N; the two codes that follow belong to seat belt pretensioner modules. No manufacturer documents U017D publicly, and the Chrysler Jeep tables in NHTSA file PE11-019 never go past G. Bosch scales its premium airbag units to as many as 18 sensor inputs, so a fourteenth satellite is possible but rare. Most such sensors talk PSI5, an open interface developed from Autoliv, Bosch and Continental designs that sends Manchester-coded current pulses at 125 kbit/s over a twisted pair. That pair carries supply and data together, so a wiring repair must keep the twist and use approved crimp connectors. U047E is the invalid-data counterpart. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Connector at sensor N loose or corroded
Earlier wiring repair untwisted or with unsuitable connectors
Airbag unit expects a sensor N that is not installed
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Scan tool reports no response from sensor N
Restraint deployment relying on sensor N may be disabled

U017E.t: Lost Communication With Seat Belt Pretensioner Module A
U017E.d: U017E reports that seat belt pretensioner module A no longer communicates. Such modules drive electric, reversible belt tensioners: Audi pre sense pulls the front belts tight by small motors when it senses emergency braking or skidding and releases them if no crash follows. On the 2015 A3, the airbag unit J234 runs the left and right tensioner modules J854/J855 over LIN; the pyrotechnic tensioners are separate. Audi bulletin 2081251 (2025-26 A5, A6, Q5, Q6 e-tron) asks for a report when U017E00 and U017F00 come with a proactive occupant protection fault message. Stellantis calls the U017E partner seatbelt sensor 1 in PCM-update bulletins for the 2021 300, Charger and Challenger, there with a lit MIL.
c: Connector at the belt retractor module in the pillar loose or damaged
New retractor with control module not coded or basic setting not done
Harness damaged or wrongly routed (Jeep JL, shifter area)
Software issue in the module or a listener such as the PCM (FCA 2021)
s: Warning message for pre-crash occupant protection
Belt no longer pre-tightened during emergency braking
Airbag lamp on; on some FCA models MIL as well

U017F.t: Lost Communication With Seat Belt Pretensioner Module B
U017F.d: U017F is the second pretensioner module code: module B has dropped off its link to the airbag unit. Audi documents it together with U017E00 in bulletin 2081251 for 2025-26 A5, A6, Q5 and Q6 e-tron models, where both codes accompany a proactive occupant protection warning and dealers are asked to file a case report. Two such modules are typical because each front seat gets its own motorised retractor, as on the 2015 A3 with J854 and J855. Keep U017F apart from Audi's B130474/B130574: those describe a deviating tensioning actuator, not a lost link. If a retractor with control unit was replaced after a collision, Audi requires a basic setting with the scan tool. Pyrotechnic pretensioners are wired separately. No MIL.
c: Retractor with control module replaced but not coded or basic-set
Supply or bus connector at module B loose
Bus line between airbag unit and module B damaged
s: Pre-crash protection fault message in the instrument cluster
Reversible belt tightening on one seat inoperative
Often stored together with U017E

U0180.t: Lost Communication With Automatic Lighting Control Module
U0180.d: U0180 belongs to the automatic lighting control module, the unit that evaluates a light sensor and switches the headlamps on at dusk, in tunnels or with the wipers. Once it is silent, the auto-light feature can no longer be commanded. The only public bulletin found comes from GM and fits poorly: PIE0348 and PIE0348A (Cadillac ATS 2013-2016, CTS 2014-2016 with premium amplifier) tie U0180 or B1325 to lost audio, chimes and turn-signal clicks, sometimes after rain or a car wash, without naming the module, so GM's use may differ from the J2012 name. Expect the lights to stay in manual mode or default to on; no MIL. U0181 and U0182 are the levelling and front lighting modules, U0481 invalid data.
c: Light sensor or lighting module without power or ground
Moisture at connectors after rain or car wash (GM PIE0348)
Bus or LIN line to the windscreen sensor damaged
s: Automatic headlamps no longer switch on or off
Headlamps stay on as a default
GM Cadillac: no audio, chimes or turn-signal sound

U0181.t: Lost Communication With Headlamp Leveling Control Module
U0181.d: U0181 says the module that controls automatic headlamp levelling has dropped off the bus. That module reads ride-height sensors on the axles and drives the actuator motors in the headlamps to keep the beam at the right angle under load. GM uses the code: the Saab 9-5 (2010-2011) U-code list names it Lost Communication With Headlamp Leveling Control Module, and a GM bulletin for the 2017-2021 GMC Acadia and Cadillac XT5 lists U0181 among the U-codes caused by a chafed dash harness or water in the BCM. Per GM it sets when the module's supervised periodic message is missing at 9-16 V. U0180 is the automatic lighting module, U0182 and U0183 the front and rear lighting modules. No MIL; beam height may stay fixed.
c: Levelling module without power or ground
Chafed harness or water in connectors or BCM area (GM Acadia/XT5)
Corroded connector at the module near the headlamp
Headlamp levelling module faulty or not coded
s: Headlamp beam height no longer adjusts
Headlamp or lighting warning in the cluster
Oncoming traffic dazzled or road poorly lit when loaded

U0182.t: Lost Communication With Lighting Control Module Front
U0182.d: U0182 is logged when the front lighting control module stops talking on the bus. This module drives front lamp functions such as swivelling or adaptive beam patterns. GM lists it as Lost Communication With Lighting Control Module - Front in the Saab 9-5 (2010-2011) U-code list. Chrysler uses it for the adaptive front lighting module: a 2014 Jeep Grand Cherokee field report filed with NHTSA shows U0182-00 Lost Communication With Adaptive Front Lighting Control Module next to other network codes. GM's logic: the code sets when the module's supervised periodic message stops arriving at 9-16 V. U0181 is the headlamp levelling module, U0183 the rear lighting module. No MIL; cornering or adaptive light may fall back to a basic beam.
c: Front lighting module without power or ground
Corroded connector in the engine bay or headlamp area
Bus line to the module chafed or open
s: Adaptive or cornering light inoperative
Lighting warning lamp or message in the cluster
Front lamps fall back to a fixed default beam

U0183.t: Lost Communication With Lighting Control Module - Rear A
U0183.d: U0183 refers to rear lighting control module A, the unit that drives tail, brake, turn and in some designs reversing lamps at the back of the vehicle. A second rear unit, B, has U0252, the front module U0182. Such modules are found where LED rear lamps are switched and checked electronically, for example in a tailgate. No manufacturer documents U0183 publicly; neither GM's U-code list nor the NHTSA bulletin index carries it. GM's generic description for codes U0100-U02FF gives the trigger: an expected periodic message from the module goes missing while the system voltage is 9-16 V. Rear lamps may fail, fall back to a default pattern or raise a bulb warning. That matters for being seen, although no MIL is involved.
c: Rear lighting module without power or ground
Wiring broken in the tailgate or boot lid hinge loom
Corroded connector at the rear lamp or module
Rear lighting control module A faulty
s: Tail, brake or turn lamps at the rear not working
Bulb or lighting warning in the cluster
Rear lamps in a fixed default mode

U0184.d: U0184 is logged when the radio or infotainment head unit no longer answers on the bus; cluster, gateway, HVAC or amplifier store it, often several at once. GM bulletin 16-NA-115 (many 2014 GM models) reprograms the radio when it stays silent, shows a dark display or fails to wake up. Ford SSM 49695 (F-Super Duty 2020-2021) first rules out transport mode, then pulls fuse F32 in the BCM for five minutes before reseating the audio module connector. Stellantis case S2208000124 notes that the code can set when the radio wakes late on the audio CAN bus and to inspect the security gateway terminals before replacing anything. The Saab 9-5 list carries it too. Sound, display and phone functions fail; no MIL. U0186 is the amplifier.
c: Radio software hang or wake-up problem, fixed by reset or reprogramming (GM, Ford)
Spread or pushed-out terminals at radio or security gateway (Stellantis)
s: Radio dead, screen blank or no sound
Phone, reversing camera or voice control not available
U0184 stored in several modules

U0185.t: Lost Communication With Antenna Control Module
U0185.d: U0185 indicates that the antenna control module has stopped communicating. This unit, frequently an amplifier or tuner box near the rear screen, the roof fin or a bumper, conditions radio, TV, satellite or GPS signals and in some designs raises or lowers a motorised mast. U0185 has no public manufacturer documentation; neither the GM list nor the NHTSA bulletin index uses it. The listening module, typically the radio, logs it when the antenna unit's periodic message disappears; GM names 9-16 V as the precondition for this whole class of codes. Reception becomes weak or drops out and a power mast may stay where it is. There is no effect on driving and no MIL. U0184 is the radio, U0486 invalid antenna data.
c: Antenna module without power or ground
Water ingress at roof fin or rear-screen amplifier
Bus wiring or connector to the antenna unit damaged
s: Poor or no radio reception
Satellite, TV or GPS reception lost
Power antenna does not move

U0186.t: Lost Communication With Audio Amplifier A
U0186.d: U0186 means the external audio amplifier A has dropped off the bus; the radio or cluster store it, and the speakers usually go quiet. GM PIC6153 (Volt 2016 with premium audio) warns against replacing the amplifier and asks to inspect its X1 connector, especially pin 4 (B+) and pin 8 (ground). Chrysler bulletin 08-020-14 (Ram, Durango, Grand Cherokee 2013-2014) flashes the amplifier when it shows as absent in the wiTECH network view, after a power cycle via fuse F71. Mazda SA-070-22 (Mazda3, CX-30) traces U0186:08 to a backed-out MOST pin at the connectivity master unit, reproducible by tapping the dash. GM's Saab list calls it the speaker amplifier. Sound lost or crackling; no MIL. U0262 is amplifier B.
c: Spread or backed-out terminals at amplifier or head unit connector (GM, Mazda)
Amplifier software stops bus communication, fixed by flash (Chrysler)
Amplifier fuse blown or ground loose
s: No sound or radio muted
Crackling or intermittent audio
Chimes or warning tones missing

U0187.t: Lost Communication With Digital Disc Player/Changer Module A
U0187.d: U0187 opens the J2012 series for networked disc players and changers: module A is the main CD or DVD drive, while U0188 to U0190 cover B to D. In many older cars the changer sat apart from the head unit, in the glovebox, under a seat or in the trunk, and reported to it over a data line. U0187 has no public manufacturer documentation; GM lists no disc drives at all and the NHTSA bulletin index has no match. The radio records the code when the drive's periodic message stays away, following the logic GM gives for all loss-of-communication codes. Discs can then not be played or ejected, the rest of the sound system keeps working, and there is no MIL. A removed or never-fitted drive can also leave this entry behind.
c: Disc unit A without power or ground
Data line or connector to the changer (glovebox, seat, trunk) damaged
Drive removed or head unit coded for a drive not fitted
s: CD or DVD source missing or not selectable
Disc cannot be loaded or ejected
Other audio sources work normally

U0188.t: Lost Communication With Digital Disc Player/Changer Module B
U0188.d: U0188 means the second networked disc player or changer, module B, no longer answers. Disc changers hold several CDs or DVDs and were often mounted apart from the radio, in the dash, a console or the boot, and linked to the infotainment bus. Receiving units set a lost-communication code once the expected periodic message of a node is missing, as GM's U0100-U02FF procedure explains for all such codes. No manufacturer documents U0188 publicly; GM's U-code list has no disc player entries at all. U0187 names player A, U0189 and U0190 players C and D. Many newer cars have no disc drive, so a stray entry can also come from wrong coding. Only playback from that unit is lost; no MIL.
c: Disc unit B without power or ground
Bus or connector to the changer (often in boot or console) damaged
Unit removed or vehicle coded for a device not fitted
s: Disc source B missing or not selectable
Discs not ejected or not played
Code stored in the radio or head unit

U0189.t: Lost Communication With Digital Disc Player/Changer Module C
U0189.d: U0189 covers the third disc player or changer on the bus, module C. Systems with more than one drive are found mostly in rear-seat entertainment or luxury setups, where a front unit and separate rear players feed different screens. The head unit or another listener stores U0189 once module C's cyclic messages stop arriving; GM describes this mechanism for all U0100-U02FF codes, with voltage required to be between 9 and 16 V. No manufacturer documents U0189 publicly, and GM's published list contains no disc player codes. U0187 and U0188 name modules A and B, U0190 module D. Check whether the vehicle really has a third drive before chasing wiring. Only that source fails; no MIL, no effect on driving.
c: Disc unit C fuse blown or ground loose
Connector or bus wiring to the rear player damaged
Vehicle coded for a third drive that is not fitted
s: Rear or third disc source unavailable
Rear screen shows no disc content
Code stored in the head unit

U018A.t: Lost Communication With Headlamp Leveling Control Module B
U018A.d: U018A covers headlamp leveling control module B. Cars with separate levelling electronics in each headlamp, or with a central controller plus lamp-side units, need a second address; U0181 is the first module. The electronics set the beam angle from ride-height sensor data so that load or pitch does not dazzle oncoming traffic, which LED and xenon lamps usually require. No manufacturer documents U018A publicly, and it appears neither in GM's U-code list nor in the NHTSA bulletin index. The trigger is the same as for other lost-communication codes in GM's description: a periodic message missing at 9-16 V supply. Beam height on one side may freeze or drop to a low default, a lighting warning is possible, the MIL stays off. U048B is invalid data from B.
c: Levelling module B without power or ground
Corroded connector at the headlamp from moisture
Bus line to the headlamp damaged after a front-end repair
Headlamp levelling module B faulty or not coded
s: One headlamp no longer adjusts its beam height
Headlamp or lighting warning in the cluster
Uneven or very low beam pattern

U0190.t: Lost Communication With Digital Disc Player/Changer Module D
U0190.d: U0190 is the last code in the J2012 disc player block and names module D, a fourth networked drive or changer. When that unit goes silent, the modules expecting its periodic traffic store U0190; GM's procedure for U0100-U02FF adds that a code stored only in history after a flat battery or a module disconnected with the bus awake is not a reason to replace parts. No manufacturer documents U0190 publicly, and a fourth disc drive is very rare in practice, so the code is unusual. A changer is a mechanical unit that loads discs from a magazine, which makes power supply and mounting location the first checks. U0187 to U0189 cover modules A to C. Only disc playback from D is lost; no MIL.
c: Disc unit D without power or ground
History entry after flat battery or unit unplugged with bus awake
Connector or bus line to module D damaged
s: Disc source D missing
Magazine not loaded or ejected
Code stored in the head unit

U0191.d: U0191 means the television tuner has dropped off the vehicle network. J2012 simply calls it Television: a receiver for mostly digital terrestrial TV that hands the picture to the central display or to rear screens. GM fills the slot under that name in the Saab U-code lists of the 9-5 from 2010-2011 and the 9-4X from 2011; the NHTSA bulletin index has no matching entry. A listening unit, usually the radio or the display, records the code once the tuner's cyclic frames stay away while supply voltage is normal (GM: 9-16 V). The TV source then disappears or stays black, while radio and navigation carry on. U0492 reports invalid data from the same tuner, U0184 concerns the radio. No MIL.
c: TV tuner without power or ground (fuse, connector)
History entry after flat battery or tuner unplugged with bus awake
Bus line or connector to the tuner damaged
s: TV source missing from the media menu
Black screen or no-signal message when TV is selected
Code stored in radio or display unit

U0192.d: U0192 is reserved for a personal computer that exchanges data with the vehicle network, for example a built-in carputer, a docked laptop in a police or service vehicle, or a PC-based infotainment unit. When that node stops sending, a listening module stores the code. No manufacturer documents U0192 publicly: the Saab U-code lists from GM omit it, the NHTSA bulletin index has no match, and GM's preliminary information PIP5094 only names it among keywords for checking terminal fit before circuit tests. GM's procedure for U0100-U02FF gives the usual rule, a supervised periodic message missing at 9-16 V. First confirm that a PC is fitted at all; a stray entry after a retrofit or recoding is likely. U0493 is invalid data. No MIL, driving unaffected.
c: Network coding expects a PC that is not fitted or was removed
Retrofit interface, dock or bus connector to the PC faulty
PC or its interface without supply, or shut down
Onboard PC faulty or software hung
s: PC functions or data no longer available in the vehicle
Code stored without any noticeable fault

U0193.t: Lost Communication With Digital Audio Control Module A
U0193.d: U0193 reports that digital audio control module A no longer sends its messages. Makers fill this slot differently. GM calls it Lost Communication With Digital Radio Receiver Control Module in the Saab 9-5 (2010-2011) U-code list, i.e. the separate receiver for digital or satellite radio, and its 2017-2021 GMC Acadia and Cadillac XT5 bulletin lists U0193 among codes caused by harness chafing or water in the BCM. Chrysler's 2006-2010 Jeep code list uses U0193 for a traffic information receiver module. GM's logic: a supervised periodic message is missing at 9-16 V. U0194 is module B, U0184 the radio, U0186 the amplifier. Digital radio or traffic data drops out; no MIL.
c: Digital receiver module without power or ground
Chafed harness or water in connectors (GM Acadia/XT5)
Bus wire or connector to the receiver damaged
s: Digital, satellite radio or traffic data unavailable
Radio shows no signal for the digital source
Code stored in radio and other modules

U0194.t: Lost Communication With Digital Audio Control Module B
U0194.d: U0194 marks the second digital audio control module, B, as silent on the bus. GM uses the code but does not name the module publicly: on the 2013-2014 Buick Enclave, Chevrolet Traverse and GMC Acadia the radio stores U0194 together with many other U-codes when the harness of the rear side object detection sensors rubs on the exhaust and disturbs the network. Ford lists U0194 among codes on 2017 C-MAX vehicles with water in the active grille shutter connector, again without stating the module. The setting rule follows GM's U0100-U02FF logic: a supervised periodic message is missing at normal voltage. U0193 is module A, U0184 the radio. Audio features may cut out; no MIL of its own.
c: Network harness chafed elsewhere in the car disturbing the bus (GM Lambda)
Water in a bus connector (Ford C-MAX)
Audio module B without power or ground
s: Radio shuts off or audio source drops out intermittently
Many U-codes stored at the same time
Cluster or other modules act up together with the radio

U0195.t: Lost Communication With Subscription Entertainment Receiver Module
U0195.d: U0195 concerns the subscription entertainment receiver module, the box that decodes a paid broadcast service such as SiriusXM satellite radio. Earlier code lists named it Satellite Radio Receiver Module, and makers have used it in that sense: Chrysler's code list for 2006-2010 Jeep models, filed with NHTSA in a defect investigation, reads U0195 as Lost Communication With SDARS, the satellite digital audio receiver. The radio or gateway records the code once the receiver's periodic frames stop at normal voltage, as GM explains for all U0100-U02FF codes. No newer bulletin in the NHTSA index names U0195. Satellite channels vanish or show no subscription signal, terrestrial radio keeps playing. U0193 is digital audio module A, U0496 invalid data. No MIL.
c: History entry after low battery voltage or jump start
Bus line or connector to the receiver damaged or corroded
s: Satellite radio band missing or showing no signal
Subscription service cannot be activated
Code stored in the radio or gateway

U0196.t: Lost Communication With Entertainment Control Module - Rear A
U0196.d: U0196 refers to rear entertainment control module A, the unit that gives rear passengers their own audio or video source, headphone zones and screen control. GM's Saab U-code lists assign it to the rear audio control module for the 9-5 (2010-2011) and the 9-4X (2011), meaning the rear audio panel with headphone sockets. The front radio or the gateway logs U0196 when that panel's cyclic messages are no longer received at normal voltage, following GM's logic for U0100-U02FF. The NHTSA index lists no bulletin for this code. Rear buttons, headphone output or rear monitors stop working, while the front system usually plays on. U0191 is the TV tuner, U0184 the radio, U0497 invalid data from the rear unit. No MIL.
c: Rear entertainment unit without power or ground
Bus wiring to the rear unit pinched or connector loose (seat, console, headliner)
History entry after low battery voltage
s: Rear audio controls or headphone sockets dead
Rear screens dark or no source selectable
Code stored in radio or gateway

U0197.t: Lost Communication With Telephone Control Module
U0197.d: U0197 says the telephone control module, in most cars the Bluetooth hands-free unit, has gone quiet on the bus. FCA uses it widely under the name Hands Free Phone Module. Bulletin 08-112-14 covers 2013-2015 Town & Country, Grand Caravan, Compass, Patriot and Wrangler plus 2013-2014 Challenger, Avenger and 200 with Bluetooth not working; new HFM software loaded over USB cures it. Bulletin 08-083-19 (Journey 2012-2019, Charger and 300 2012-2014) adds that the MIL may come on with U0197-00 when the module fails to boot or no longer shows up in the wiTECH network view; a reflash is the fix. GM's Saab lists call it the telephone control module. Hands-free calls and voice control drop out. U0198 is the telematics unit, U0498 invalid data.
c: Hands-free module software hangs at boot (FCA update)
Bus line or connector to the phone module faulty
s: Phone does not pair or calls are not possible hands-free
Display reports the hands-free module is still loading
MIL on in some FCA models

U0198.t: Lost Communication With Telematic Control Module
U0198.d: U0198 marks the telematic control module as silent; that unit holds the cellular modem for remote apps, emergency and assistance calls. Ford's APIM stores it on 2012-2018 Focus Electric, Fusion Energi and C-MAX Energi when the TCU hangs: SSM 46534 and 47198 report a drained battery, dead MyFord Mobile features and no modem ESN, cured by pulling the TCU fuse for five minutes and reprogramming. For the 2023 Super Duty, SSM 51578 treats U0198:87 in the BCM after a self-test as a false history entry to ignore if the MIL is off. Mazda SA-029/20 (Mazda3, CX-30) ties U0198:00 in the BCM to the emergency call unit; GM PIT5422 (Equinox, Terrain) traces it to water in connector X901. U0197 is the phone module, U0499 invalid data.
c: Telematics unit hung or outdated software (Ford TCU reprogramming)
Water or corrosion in a body harness connector (GM X901)
Low-speed bus wire pinched or chafed in the roof or body
False history entry from a module self-test (Ford Super Duty)
s: Remote app, emergency or assistance call unavailable
Battery drained overnight (Ford plug-in models)
Network warning in the cluster, often with further U-codes

U0199.t: Lost Communication With Door Control Module A
U0199.d: U0199 reports that door control module A has dropped off the bus; most makers assign it to the driver's door. Chrysler bulletin 08-061-12 (300 and Charger 2005-2010) calls it the driver door module: the front windows and central locking stop working, a one-minute battery disconnect is tried first, and the module is replaced if contact does not return. Volkswagen tech tip 97-21-02 (Atlas, Golf, Jetta, Tiguan, Taos 2019-2022) sees U019900 or U020000 with many warnings and windows moving on their own, caused by loose pins in the connector at the driver's A-pillar, on the comfort CAN lines. Ford SSM 53980 (F-Super Duty 2023-2025) blames ground G201, to be torqued to 8 Nm. U0200 to U0202 cover doors B to D, U049A invalid data. Normally no MIL.
c: Loose or backed-out pins in the door-to-body connector (VW)
Broken wires in the door hinge harness
s: Power windows and locks on the door inoperative
Windows move on their own or several warning lamps light up
Mirror adjustment or switch lighting dead

U019A.d: U019A is stored when the tachograph stops sending on the vehicle bus. Tachographs log speed, distance and driving time in trucks and buses; in the EU every newly registered vehicle of that class has needed a digital unit since May 2006. Many engine and body controllers take road speed from the tachograph frame, so the fault reaches beyond the logbook. Deutz lists U019A-00 as a communication fault with the tachograph in the fault table of its EMR L1 main engine controller and pairs it with SPN 1620 and FMI 2. No passenger-car maker documents the code publicly. Possible effects are a missing speed reading, inactive cruise control or speed limiter and a tachograph warning; whether a MIL lights is up to the engine maker. U049B is the invalid-data counterpart.
c: Tachograph without power, ground or ignition signal
CAN wiring or connector behind the tachograph damaged
Tachograph replaced or recalibrated without matching the bus configuration
s: Tachograph warning or speed display missing
Cruise control or road speed limiter unavailable
Code stored in the engine controller

U019B.t: Lost Communication With Battery Charger Control Module A
U019B.d: U019B means battery charger control module A, the on-board charger of a plug-in vehicle, is no longer heard on the bus. Ford's 2014 OBD code list flags U019B as MIL-relevant, in line with CARB's rule that plug-in hybrids must detect charger faults that stop or slow charging. Audi bulletin 93 23 96 (A7 e quattro 2021-2022) finds U019B00 in hybrid manager J840 with a no-start and a charge plug shown as locked, caused by damaged wires at couplings T6bl and T8bd. On the 2025 e-tron GT the gateway logs it with a yellow electrical fault while a software fix is pending. Ford SSM 52527/52831 (F-150 Lightning 2022-2023) pair it with U0293 and a dead intelligent backup power feature, due to gateway software. U01BB and U027A cover chargers B and C.
c: Damaged wires at harness couplings exposed to the environment (Audi A7 PHEV)
Gateway or controller software (Ford Lightning, Audi e-tron GT)
Charger without 12 V supply, ground or wake-up signal
s: Vehicle does not charge or charge plug stays locked
Electrical system warning, drive system cannot be activated
Export power or backup power features unavailable

U019C.t: Lost Communication With Glow Plug Control Module 2
U019C.d: U019C points to a second glow plug control module, needed where a diesel has more preheating channels than one unit drives, for example one module per cylinder bank. No manufacturer documents U019C publicly; it is absent from GM's diesel tables and from the NHTSA bulletin index. The partner code U0106 for module 1 shows the logic: GM's 2015 engine diagnostics table fails it when no GPCM frame has arrived for more than 0.25 s during a 10 s test and rates it Type B. CARB requires glow plugs to be checked for correct current and response to commands, which presumes a live link to the module. The plugs on the affected side may stay cold, giving hard cold starts, rough running and white smoke while warming up; an MIL is to be expected. U049D is invalid data.
c: Glow plug module 2 without supply, ground or ignition feed
Water or corrosion in the module connector near the engine
Bus line to module 2 chafed or connector loose
s: Hard starting when cold
White smoke and rough idle until warm
Preheat lamp behaves oddly, MIL on

U019D.t: Lost Communication With Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor
U019D.d: U019D concerns a temperature sensor at a direct ozone reduction (DOR) catalyst that reports over the network rather than a plain wire; the wired versions have P2567-P2571. A DOR catalyst is a coating on the radiator or A/C condenser that turns ozone in the passing air into oxygen, such as Engelhard's PremAir, first fitted by Volvo on the S80 and by Nissan on the Sentra CA. CARB grants an NMOG credit for it only with an OBD monitor, and 13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(14) sets the malfunction criteria; under LEV III the credit reaches 5 mg/mi. No manufacturer documents U019D publicly. Without sensor data the DOR monitor cannot run, so the credit is unsupported and a MIL is to be expected. Driving is unaffected. U049E is invalid data.
c: Sensor connector at the radiator corroded or damaged by road debris
Sensor left unplugged or radiator replaced after front-end repair
Bus or supply line to the sensor broken
s: MIL on without noticeable driving fault
DOR monitor shown as not complete

U019E.t: Lost Communication With Transmission Range Control Module
U019E.d: U019E covers the transmission range control module, in shift-by-wire designs the electronics that engage park, reverse, neutral or drive on behalf of the driver's selector. Ford lists U019E in its 2014 OBD code list without the MIL marker it gives emissions-related codes. No further public manufacturer source was found; NHTSA's bulletin index is silent on it as well. The neighbouring code U0103 belongs to the selector itself, gear shift control module A, which reports the driver's request to this unit. Shift-by-wire needs a redundant data path, so losing the range module typically means a refused gear change, a prompt to secure the car or an automatic move to park. U049F is invalid data, U01BA the park lock module.
c: Range control module without power, ground or wake-up
Bus connector at the transmission corroded or loose
Low battery voltage during cranking or parking
s: Gear selection refused or vehicle stays in park
Shift system warning in the cluster
Transmission engages park on its own when stopping

U019F.t: Lost Communication With Engine Coolant Pump Control Module
U019F.d: U019F means the electric engine coolant pump, which carries its own control electronics, has stopped answering. Mercedes documents it on two engines: on the M256 six-cylinder the engine controller stores U019F00 or U019F87 with a red coolant warning; LI20.10-P-075374 checks the 12 V and 48 V plugs of pump M75/11, its ground and fuse F153/2 and, if the pump touches the heat shield, insulates it or replaces the controller. On C350e and GLC350e hybrids the check engine lamp lights as well; MED40 software or a new pump fixes it. Ford SSM 46857 and 47790 (C-MAX, Fusion, MKZ hybrids) report it with an MIL from water in connectors such as C1651. Mazda warns that swapped pumps on the CX-90/CX-70 PHEV set it. U04A0 is invalid data.
c: Pump supply plug, 48 V connector or ground loose or dirty (Mercedes)
Water or corrosion in front-end connectors (Ford hybrids)
Similar-looking pumps swapped or wrong part ordered (Mazda PHEV)
s: Red coolant temperature warning
MIL or check engine lamp on
Engine power reduced to protect against overheating

U01A0.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module A
U01A0.d: U01A0 names battery interface control module A, the first slave board that reports cell voltages and temperatures of its pack section to the battery controller. GM's 2016-2019 plug-in hybrid tables explain how the code arises: the battery system module talks to eight such boards over a UART daisy chain; once U179C shows that data has stopped, it switches the boards into an internal loopback test and stores the code of the first board it still cannot reach, in 2016 after 5 s above 10.2 V, Type A with MIL on the first trip. Because A sits next to the master, a break ahead of A silences every board in the chain while only A gets named. Audi lists U01A000 for the 2016 A3 Sportback e-tron, which then refuses to make the drive system ready.
c: Chain wiring or connector between battery controller and module A interrupted
Module A without supply from its cell group or low-voltage feed
Battery interface control module A defective
Chain interface of the battery controller itself faulty
s: Vehicle does not become ready to drive, red hybrid/EV warning
MIL on after the first failing trip (GM Type A)
Further module codes or U179C stored at the same time

U01A1.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module B
U01A1.d: U01A1 refers to battery interface control module B. In GM's eAssist mild hybrids it is the second and final board: bulletin PIT5513D lists two high-voltage battery interface control modules, K112A and K112B, for Silverado and Sierra trucks of 2016 to 2018 and the 2018 LaCrosse, and the GM tables 16OBDG07B and 19OBDG03B accordingly contain only U01A0 and U01A1. Their rating is milder than in the plug-in hybrids: Type B, so the MIL waits for a second failing trip; the 2016 table asks for more than 9.1 V and 4.5 s. If B is logged alone, the fault lies at B or at the link from A to B; both letters together point rather to a shared feed or the master side. GM placed these powerpacks and both boards under parts restriction via its technical assistance center.
c: Chain connection between module A and module B interrupted or corroded
Battery interface control module B (GM K112B) defective
Common low-voltage feed of the powerpack interrupted (then usually A as well)
s: MIL only after two consecutive failing trips (GM Type B)
Start-stop and electric assist unavailable
Hybrid system warning message

U01A2.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module C
U01A2.d: U01A2 is stored when battery interface control module C, the third board of the chain, stays silent. How a controller reaches that verdict is spelled out in GM's 2016 hybrid table: the battery system module first logs U179C for one or more missing boards, then orders all boards into a loopback mode that bypasses the daisy chain. A board that answers in this mode still has power and working logic, so the master can separate a broken link from a dead unit and names only the first board it fails to recover; the code passes again once data returns for 100 ms. Audi bulletin 2081028 for the Q5 e (model years 2022 and 2024) lists U01A200 among the codes for modules A to H behind an electrical system malfunction warning.
c: Chain link between module B and module C broken (connector, ribbon, pin)
Module C fails the loopback test, board defective
Battery controller software that misreads the chain (update available)
s: Electrical system or hybrid warning in the instrument cluster
Reduced drive power or no electric driving
Code returns immediately after clearing

U01A3.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module D
U01A3.d: U01A3 marks a lost link to battery interface control module D. Before this generic block existed, GM used proprietary numbers for the same fault: the GM U-code list published for the 2011 Saab 9-4X names U2603 to U2606 as the battery energy control module losing hybrid battery interface modules 1 to 4. GM's 2018 hybrid table still groups these older numbers together with U01A0-U01AC and U179C in one fault bundle, so scan reports from different model years may show either form for the same board. In GM's 2016-2019 plug-in tables D is the fourth of eight boards and is rated Type A. One oddity to keep in mind: invalid data from module D is reported as U02A0, outside the U04A row used by its siblings.
c: Chain connection from module C to module D interrupted
Battery interface control module D defective
Scan tool or software generation reports the board under the older GM number
s: MIL and hybrid/EV warning (GM Type A)
Limited power, electric range shortened
Cell voltages of one pack section shown as unavailable

U01A4.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module E
U01A4.d: U01A4 concerns battery interface control module E. Whether such a code points to one board or to a whole broken chain depends on the wiring scheme. In a plain daisy chain a break silences all boards behind it, and GM's logic names only the first. Some monitoring chips allow a closed ring instead: TI's BQ79616 offers an isolated differential daisy chain with an optional ring, and a CATL patent (US11031789) describes a controller that, after the loop breaks, drives the two remaining halves through its two serial ports. In such designs a lone E code is much more telling, since boards beyond the gap are still heard from the far end. GM's eight-board plug-in tables of 2016-2019 rate the loss of E as Type A.
c: Chain link between module D and module E interrupted (open chain)
Module E itself defective (likely in ring designs when neighbours still report)
Return path of a ring layout damaged in addition to the main path
s: Battery warning and reduced output
Only module E reported missing although later boards are silent too (open chain)
MIL on the first trip (GM Type A)

U01A5.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module F
U01A5.d: U01A5 says the battery controller no longer receives data from interface module F. Once such a board drops out, the cells it covers are unsupervised: no voltage readings, no temperatures and no balancing for that section. GM therefore puts all of these codes into a fault bundle called BICM Loss of Comm in its 2018 hybrid table, which blocks battery diagnostics that would otherwise misfire on missing values. On the road the controller shields the pack, so reduced power, refused charging or opened contactors are to be expected. Audi bulletin 2078135 for the 2016 A3 Sportback e-tron describes a drive system that cannot be activated and a red warning lamp, with U01A500 among the A-H codes plus P0AA500 and P0A7D00. GM monitors F as Type A from 2016 to 2019.
c: Chain connection between module E and module F interrupted
Battery interface control module F defective
Board F loses supply because its cell group or sense tap is open
s: Drive system cannot be activated, red warning lamp
Charging refused or stopped early
Other battery diagnostics suspended while the code is active

U01A6.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module G
U01A6.d: U01A6 means battery interface control module G no longer reports to the battery controller. Because these boards sit inside the high-voltage pack, the chain runs between modules whose ground levels differ by hundreds of volts, so the link has to be galvanically isolated; Wikipedia's battery management article names optical couplers and radio as the hardware routes. Diagnosis therefore starts on a de-energised pack: note which neighbouring letters still report, then look at G's plugs for corrosion, coolant or moisture and carry out an insulation test before swapping parts. GM's 2016-2019 plug-in tables classify G as Type A, lighting the MIL in the first failing trip, and Audi's bulletins for the 2016 A3 e-tron and the Q5 e list U01A600 together with the other seven letters.
c: Chain link between module F and module G interrupted
Moisture or coolant at the chain connectors of module G
Isolating coupler (transformer, optocoupler) on the link to G failed
Battery interface control module G defective
s: MIL and battery warning lamp
Insulation fault code stored alongside if moisture has entered
Reduced power or no ready mode

U01A7.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module H
U01A7.d: U01A7 refers to battery interface control module H. On packs with exactly eight boards it is the tail of the chain: the GM plug-in hybrid tables for 2016 to 2019 stop at U01A7, and both Audi bulletins (A3 Sportback e-tron 2016, Q5 e 2022 and 2024) list precisely U01A000 to U01A700. Since the master always names the first board it cannot reach, H on its own excludes a break further up; the cause sits in H itself, its supply or the final link leading to it. A fault earlier in the chain shows up as a lower letter, even though H then falls silent as well. GM's 2016 table requires 5 s above 10.2 V and rates the fault Type A, so the MIL lights on the first trip; 2018 to 2019 the time is 4.5 s.
c: Final chain link from module G to module H interrupted
Battery interface control module H defective
Termination or return line at the end of the chain faulty
s: MIL on the first trip (GM Type A)
Electrical system or hybrid warning, power reduced
All other module letters report normally

U01A8.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module I
U01A8.d: U01A8 is the code for battery interface control module I and is only needed on packs with more than eight monitoring boards. GM's 2018 hybrid table contains it solely inside the fault bundle BICM Loss of Comm (U01A0-U01AC), adding that GM shares software across programs and only codes valid for the vehicle at hand apply; there is no monitor entry of its own, so neither threshold nor MIL type is published for I. Packs of that size exist: according to Wikipedia, the Ultium battery of the Hummer EV holds 24 modules, but which systems really use U01A8 remains undocumented. When it appears, the battery controller has lost the ninth board of its chain while the eight before it still answer. CARB requires separate codes per replaceable unit.
c: Chain connection between module H and module I interrupted
Battery interface control module I defective
Battery controller configured for more boards than fitted
s: Battery or hybrid warning, power limited
Charging blocked

U01A9.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module J
U01A9.d: U01A9 stands for battery interface control module J, the tenth board. Apart from wiring, a typical trigger after repairs is configuration: monitoring chips in a chain usually get their address when communication starts. NXP's MC33771C cell controller, for instance, receives its address during initialisation and supports up to 63 nodes per chain, and a Nuvoton patent (US20210184474) describes addresses handed out one after another at start-up in daisy-chained supervisors. A replaced or reordered board that fails to take its slot may therefore go missing for the master. Software mismatch with the same board has its own code, U0342.
