No manufacturer documents U01A9 with a monitor of its own; GM only lists it in the 2018 bundle BICM Loss of Comm.
c: Chain connection between module I and module J interrupted
Board J not addressed or registered after module replacement
Battery interface control module J defective
s: Code appears right after battery repair or module replacement
Vehicle not ready to drive or power limited

U01AA.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module K
U01AA.d: U01AA covers battery interface control module K, the eleventh board, so only large packs can set it at all. Not every design uses wires for this link: GM's Ultium platform monitors its cells by radio, a system developed with Analog Devices, which according to Wikipedia needs about 90 % less wiring. With such a layout a lost module is a radio node the controller no longer hears; checks then move from harness and plugs to the node's supply, interference and the correct registration of any replacement board. No manufacturer publicly ties U01AA to a vehicle; GM includes it only in the fault bundle of its 2018 hybrid table, which lists module codes up to M, without a monitor entry or MIL type of its own.
c: Wired link to K interrupted or, in wireless systems, radio link lost
Replacement board K not registered with the battery controller
Battery interface control module K defective
s: Battery warning, reduced range and power
DC fast charging limited or refused

U01AB.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module L
U01AB.d: U01AB points at battery interface control module L, the twelfth position. The link to such a board has to bridge a large voltage offset, because the lowest and highest boards of a stack sit hundreds of volts apart. NXP's MC33771C, as one example, talks over a two-wire twisted pair coupled through transformers or capacitors at up to 2 Mbit/s, and Wikipedia's battery management article mentions optical isolation and radio as the alternatives. A broken coupling element or a damaged twisted pair at L can therefore cut the board off while it still measures correctly. No vehicle maker documents U01AB with a threshold of its own; GM lists it only in the 2018 fault bundle BICM Loss of Comm, so how the MIL behaves depends on the individual system.
c: Twisted-pair chain line to module L chafed, pinched or unplugged
Isolating transformer or capacitor on the link to L failed
Battery interface control module L defective
s: Battery or hybrid warning
Power limited, charging may be blocked

U01AC.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module M
U01AC.d: U01AC belongs to battery interface control module M and is the last one GM mentions: its 2018 hybrid table ends the fault bundle BICM Loss of Comm at U01AC, i.e. thirteen boards, whereas GM's model-specific tables from 2016 to 2019 only monitor A to H. For diagnosis the order of events matters more than the letter. GM first sets the summary code U179C for one or more silent boards and only afterwards names the first board it cannot reach, so a workshop should record all stored module codes, U179C and the invalid-data and software codes of the same letter (U04AD, U0346) before clearing, then compare the count with the boards actually fitted. No manufacturer publishes a threshold or MIL type for M.
c: Chain connection between module L and module M interrupted
Battery interface control module M defective
Controller calibration expects more boards than the pack contains
s: Summary code for missing boards stored together with U01AC
Battery warning and reduced output

U01AD.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module N
U01AD.d: U01AD names battery interface control module N, the fourteenth board in a monitoring chain. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and even GM's broad fault bundle stops at M. The reason such codes exist at all lies in CARB's rule 1968.2, section (e)(15.2.3): hybrid OBD systems must supervise the electronic inputs of the energy storage system, such as cell voltage and temperature sensing, and store separate codes that pinpoint the smallest unit replaceable in service. A pack built from many separately replaceable monitoring boards thus needs one code per board. In a daisy chain of the kind GM describes, a stored U01AD would mean that the boards up to M still answer and N is the first one lost. Neighbouring codes for N are U04AE and U0347.
c: Chain connection between module M and module N interrupted
Battery interface control module N defective
s: Battery warning, power and charging limited
Cell data of one pack section missing in the scan tool

U01AE.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module O
U01AE.d: U01AE concerns battery interface control module O, which only exists in systems with at least fifteen monitoring nodes; no manufacturer documents the code publicly. Wikipedia distinguishes three ways to organise battery management: centralised (one controller wired to every cell), modular (several controllers, each covering a group of cells) and distributed (a board per cell with a single communication cable). Only the last two need an internal link and thus codes like this one; for modular hardware the article cites a ceiling of 255 nodes, while NXP specifies 63 for one MC33771C chain. With O missing, its section of the pack is unmonitored, and the controller will typically warn, limit power and hold off charging until the board is heard again.
c: Internal link to module O interrupted
Battery interface control module O defective
Board O without supply from its cell group
s: Warning lamp, power reduced
Charging postponed or refused

U01AF.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module P
U01AF.d: U01AF closes the row and stands for battery interface control module P, the sixteenth monitoring board; no manufacturer documents it publicly. Some packs exceed that count: according to Wikipedia the Hummer EV battery consists of 24 Ultium modules, although that platform monitors wirelessly and GM does not publish how it maps modules to codes. The code is easily mixed up with its neighbours. U0111, U0112, U014A and U014C mean that a battery energy control module itself has vanished from the vehicle network, and U019B points to the on-board charger. U01AF, by contrast, describes a sub-board inside the pack that only the battery controller can see, so that controller must itself be awake and reachable to log it.
c: Internal link to module P interrupted
Battery interface control module P defective
s: Battery warning while the battery controller itself still communicates
Power limited, charging blocked

U01B0.t: Lost Communication With Battery Monitor Module
U01B0.d: U01B0 says the 12 V battery monitor module, a small sensor on the negative battery post that reports voltage, current, temperature and state of charge, has stopped replying. GM polls it over LIN: its 2018 engine tables (18OBDG03A) flag the code once frame 18_C02 has been absent for 1.25 s, the 2025 body controller tables (25OBDG04A) after 12.6 s; both rate it Type B, two trips. GM bulletins 15-NA-087 and 22-NA-214 list it with a disabled stop/start system and a lit MIL, have the battery and LIN wiring checked first and the sensor swapped last; afterwards it must relearn, which a parasitic drain above about 250 mA blocks. Volkswagen lists U01B000 with MIL in the engine controller of the 2024 Atlas. U04B1 is the invalid-data partner.
c: Loose, corroded or damaged LIN connector or wire at the battery sensor
Weak or deeply discharged 12 V battery
Battery monitor sensor faulty (GM replaces it after the checks)
Parasitic drain preventing the sensor relearn
s: Stop/start system disabled, message in the driver display
MIL on
Battery state of charge shown wrongly or battery saver functions inactive

U01B1.t: Lost Communication With Particulate Matter Sensor B
U01B1.d: U01B1 concerns a second particulate matter sensor in a diesel exhaust, used where a layout needs two of them. Such smart sensors carry their own control unit, which heats the element, measures soot build-up and sends the results to the engine controller over CAN. U01B1 is stored when that controller stops receiving frames from sensor B. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. For the single sensor, GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG04A) set the counterpart U02A3 after more than 10 s without its messages, Type B, which shows how the check works. CARB 1968.2 relies on the PM sensor to prove filter efficiency, so without sensor B the filter monitor for its branch cannot finish. Expect a MIL and no change in how the car drives; U04B2 applies if frames arrive with invalid content.
c: Heat-damaged or corroded harness or connector at sensor B near the exhaust
Sensor control unit without supply voltage or ground (fuse, relay)
Control unit of PM sensor B faulty
s: MIL on
Particulate filter monitor shows as not complete

U01B2.t: Lost Communication With Planetary Gear Set Control Module
U01B2.d: Hybrid transmissions such as the two-mode system developed by GM, Daimler, Chrysler and BMW use two or three planetary gear sets plus clutches to switch between power-split and fixed-ratio operation. A planetary gear set control module would run those shift elements and report their state to the hybrid or transmission controller. U01B2 means this module has gone off the network, so the controller no longer knows which gear-set state is engaged. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. CARB 1968.2 counts transmission and hybrid control units among the monitored powertrain parts, so a MIL is likely wherever the code is used. Expect a hybrid system warning together with reduced power or a limited fallback mode; U04B3 covers implausible data from the same module.
c: Damaged CAN wiring or connector at the transmission
Module without supply voltage or ground
Planetary gear set control module faulty
s: Hybrid system warning
Reduced power or limited fallback mode
MIL on

U01B3.t: Lost Communication With Brake Blending Actuator
U01B3.d: The brake blending actuator divides each braking request between regeneration by the drive motor and the friction brakes, keeping pedal feel steady while the share shifts. Bosch states that its electromechanical iBooster, together with the ESP hev unit, can blend up to 0.3 g of deceleration. U01B3 is stored when the unit coordinating the brakes, normally the hybrid or brake controller, no longer hears this actuator. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. Lost recuperation raises energy use and, on hybrids, engine running time, and CARB 1968.2 expects hybrid systems to detect faults that disable regenerative braking. The friction brakes then do all the work: expect weaker recuperation, a changed pedal and a brake or hybrid warning. U04B4 is the invalid-data code.
c: CAN wiring or connector fault at the brake actuator
Actuator without supply voltage, often after low 12 V voltage
s: Little or no regenerative braking
Changed brake pedal feel
Brake or hybrid system warning

U01B4.t: Lost Communication With Brake System Control Module B
U01B4.d: Brake system control module B is the second brake controller in a two-unit layout, often the electric brake booster beside the stability control unit. GM's 2018 table for the CT6 plug-in hybrid (18OBDG01) has the engine controller flag U01B4 when frame $4FB from BSC2 has been missing for 10 s on the high-speed bus, Type B, two trips. Porsche technical information 105/25 (Taycan from 2020, Cayenne and Panamera from 2024) shows U01B400 in the PSM unit as lost contact with the brake booster, paired with C114113 when the booster's roughly one-minute run-on after switch-off was cut short; the MIL lights, yet no part needs replacing, erasing the memory with a charger connected suffices. U0129 is module A, U04B5 invalid data from B.
c: Booster run-on interrupted at switch-off (Porsche, no part fault)
Damaged CAN wiring or connector at the brake module
Low 12 V supply during start or shutdown
Brake system control module B faulty
s: MIL on, sometimes with brake or stability warnings
Driver assistance functions unavailable
Changed brake pedal feel if the booster is affected

U01B5.t: Lost Communication With Catalyst Heater Control Module
U01B5.d: Electric catalyst heating lets the converter start working within seconds of a cold start. Emitec's EMICAT disc runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to 300 A; in high-voltage hybrids Vitesco feeds it through a dedicated DC/DC converter, one form of the separate power electronics that make up a catalyst heater control module. U01B5 means the engine controller has lost contact with that unit, so it can neither command heating nor confirm it took place. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. Under CARB 1968.2, section (e)(2), OBD must verify that a heated catalyst hits its target temperature on schedule, and that check depends on the module. The driver sees a MIL; cold starts emit more and warm-up may run less smoothly; U04B6 covers invalid data from the unit.
c: Heat or corrosion damage at the heater module connectors near the exhaust
Module supply or high-current fuse open
s: MIL on
Higher emissions and possibly rough running after a cold start

U01B6.t: Lost Communication With Fuel Heater Control Module
U01B6.d: A fuel heater warms diesel ahead of the filter so that paraffin wax, which separates out in the cold, cannot clog the element; ordinary diesel turns to gel at roughly −15 to −19 °C. Newer designs use a microcontroller: a patent describes a heater controller that sets power from outside air temperature in open loop or from fuel temperature in closed loop, and cuts out when battery voltage falls too low. Where such a unit reports to the engine controller over the network, U01B6 means it has stopped answering and the heater state is unknown. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and whether a MIL follows depends on how the maker rates the heater for emissions. In frost, expect hard starting, power loss or stalling from a waxed filter; in mild weather often nothing is noticed.
c: Corroded or loose connector at the filter housing heater
Heater module supply fuse or relay failed
s: Hard starting or stalling in frost
Power loss from a clogged fuel filter in cold weather
Often no symptom in mild weather

U01B7.t: Lost Communication With Switch Input Module A
U01B7.d: A switch input module collects a group of buttons, for instance in a door trim, steering wheel or centre console, and sends their states to other units as network messages instead of wiring every switch on its own. A patent by Eaton describes the idea: a central unit queries every switch by its address and accepts only answers whose address and state are valid. U01B7 is set when module A stops responding, so the receiver, often the body controller, treats its buttons as unknown. Which switches belong to module A is up to each carmaker; no manufacturer documents this code publicly. Typically a whole group of buttons does nothing and their indicator lamps stay dark, while all other systems keep working. U04BA is the invalid-data code; modules B and C have U01B8 and U01B9.
c: Loose connector or broken wire at the switch panel
Liquid spilled into the switch module
s: A group of buttons without function
Switch backlight or indicator lamps dark

U01B8.t: Lost Communication With Switch Input Module B
U01B8.d: Carmakers that fit more than one switch input module count them A, B, C. A modular layout patented by BCS Automotive Interface Solutions shows why there can be several: a main switch module, for example for the lighting, is extended by satellite modules of different kinds, and coding contacts in the connectors tell the main unit which type is plugged in. U01B8 means the second module, B, has gone silent while the others may still work normally. The allocation is specific to each vehicle, and no maker documents U01B8 publicly, so the wiring diagram decides which buttons are affected. Check supply, ground, bus wires and connector of module B before replacing it. The driver sees only the buttons of module B fail. U04BB covers implausible data, U01B7 and U01B9 the siblings.
c: Connector of module B unplugged, loose or corroded
Missing supply voltage or ground at module B
s: Buttons served by module B without function
Other switch groups still working

U01B9.t: Lost Communication With Switch Input Module C
U01B9.d: Module C is the third switch input module. Such units often hang off a sub-bus: a Yazaki patent on door electronics shows a door unit that takes commands from CAN and forwards them over a LIN sub-bus to local nodes such as switches, window lift and mirror. When module C drops off, the receiver logs U01B9 and normally treats the affected switch states as released, a safe default. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, so only the vehicle's own wiring diagram reveals which buttons and which bus segment belong to C. Because only operating elements are concerned, the MIL stays off. A wire broken where the harness moves, at a door hinge, seat rail or steering column, is a likely cause. U04BC handles invalid content from C.
c: Wire broken in a moving harness section (door hinge, seat rail, steering column)
Fault in the unit that hosts the sub-bus of module C
s: Buttons served by module C ignored
Fault appears or disappears when moving a door, seat or the steering wheel

U01BA.t: Lost Communication With Park Lock/Pawl Control Module
U01BA.d: With park-by-wire, an electric actuator drives the parking pawl into a toothed wheel on the transmission output; no cable links it to the selector, so the park lock module alone decides when the pawl may drop in, normally only at standstill because at speed it would just ratchet over the teeth. U01BA is set when the transmission or vehicle controller loses contact with this module. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. Ford, for one, has no separate unit: its 2024 OBD description monitors park-by-wire through the gear shift module and the transmission range control module, whose implausible data set non-MIL codes, and the transmission controller reads the park position sensors itself (P07B3–P07BD). Ford's 2012 description shows the general rule for such network codes: a message that does not arrive counts as lost communication (U0140), one that arrives with values out of range as invalid data (U0422). U019E differs, as it concerns the module that selects the whole transmission range. Without confirmed pawl position the car may refuse to leave Park, or it tells the driver to set the electric parking brake, and a warning to secure the vehicle appears. U04BD reports invalid data from the same module.
c: Connector or wiring fault at the park lock actuator on the transmission
Low 12 V supply, e.g. weak battery
s: Vehicle will not shift out of Park or Park not confirmed
Warning to secure the vehicle with the parking brake

U01BB.t: Lost Communication With Battery Charger Control Module B
U01BB.d: Battery charger control module B is, by its name, a second on-board charger, as fitted on some electric cars to raise AC charging power. Polestar uses the code differently: Technical Journal 37630 (2026, vehicle type 359 from model year 2025) lists U01BB00 in the central computer GCCC when its only AC charger, the grid-to-HV converter GHCA, has failed. In that case AC charging stops while DC fast charging still works, and the converter is diagnosed and replaced. So the letter does not always mean a physical second unit. CARB 1968.2 makes plug-in vehicles responsible for spotting charger faults that block charging or reduce its rate. Expect a charging fault message and no AC charging; U019B and U027A cover chargers A and C, U04BE invalid data from B.
c: On-board charger unit failed (Polestar GHCA replaced)
Charger without 12 V supply, ground or wake-up signal
Bus wiring or connector at the charger damaged
s: AC charging impossible while DC fast charging works
Charging fault message or charge port LED error

U01BC.t: Lost Communication With Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump B
U01BC.d: Engines with a water-cooled charge air cooler run a separate low-temperature coolant loop with an electric pump, usually a LIN slave of the engine controller. Rheinmetall's pumps of this kind are driven via PWM or LIN, and Bosch's PCE pump has a built-in diagnostic function reported to a higher-level unit. U01BC applies where a second pump, B, serves this loop. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. For pump A, GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG04B) declare lost LIN contact after 2.5 s without a pump response while the pump is enabled, Type A, one trip, a sign of how strictly such losses are treated. CARB 1968.2 requires charge air undercooling to be detected, which a silent pump would hide. Expect a MIL and reduced boost or power when hot; U02A9 is pump A.
c: Water or corrosion in the pump connector at the front of the engine bay
Pump supply fuse or relay open
Electric coolant pump B electronics or motor faulty
s: MIL on
Reduced power or boost, especially in hot weather

U01BD.t: Lost Communication With DC/DC Converter Control Module C
U01BD.d: Electrified cars may carry several DC/DC converters, each turning one direct voltage into another: the main unit supplies the 12 V system from the traction battery, others feed 48 V consumers or single heavy loads. Vitesco, for instance, added a dedicated DC/DC converter in high-voltage hybrids purely to power the electrically heated catalyst. U01BD means the third converter module, C, has stopped communicating, so the hybrid or vehicle controller loses its status, voltage and current readings. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's 2014 OBD list carries the sibling U0298 for converter A without a MIL flag, a hint that such codes stay non-MIL unless the converter serves an emissions function. Expect an electrical system warning and load shedding; U0298 and U0299 cover A and B.
c: Low-voltage supply, wake-up line or connector of converter C faulty
Converter shut down by an open high-voltage interlock or contactor state
DC/DC converter C control electronics faulty
s: Electrical system or 12 V warning
Comfort loads switched off to save energy

U01BE.t: Lost Communication With Drive Motor A Clutch Actuator
U01BE.d: Some electrified drivetrains can uncouple a drive motor from its wheels so that an idle motor is not spun by the road. The Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray has such a disconnect: GM bulletin 24-NA-273 (January 2025, 2024–2025 models with LT2 engine) ties U01BE with a lit MIL to an internal microchip fault in the M162 drive motor disconnect clutch actuator, and the remedy is a new actuator. A Rivian patent shows why the actuator matters: before engagement the motor speed is matched to the output speed, and the control system judges from the motor's reaction whether the clutch has engaged. With the actuator silent, the system can neither couple the motor nor confirm its state, so electric drive on that axle is lost. U04BF covers invalid data from the actuator.
c: Internal electronic fault in the clutch actuator (GM M162 replaced)
Connector or wiring fault at the actuator on the drive unit
Actuator without supply voltage or ground
s: MIL on
Electric drive on one axle or all-wheel drive unavailable
Reduced acceleration

U01BF.t: Lost Communication With Battery Management Control Module
U01BF.d: A battery management control module watches cell voltages, temperatures and current and decides how much power a pack may deliver or accept. The J2012 name does not tie it to the high-voltage battery. GM's 2024 and 2025 tables (24OBDG07, 25OBDG03B) assign U01BF00 to the central gateway module, which sets it when supervised messages from a unit GM calls LIBI are missing for 2.5 times their nominal period, with supply above 7 V and an active power mode; the fault matures after 6.5 s and is Type B, two trips. No other manufacturer documents the code publicly. Depending on what the module guards, expect battery or electrical warnings and limited charging or power. U04C0 is the invalid-data partner, U0111 the battery energy control module A, U01B0 the 12 V battery sensor.
c: Bus wiring or connector between gateway and battery module damaged
Module supply interrupted or 12 V voltage too low
s: Battery or electrical system warning
Charging or drive power limited
MIL on (GM Type B)

U0200.t: Lost Communication With Door Control Module B
U0200.d: U0200 means door control module B has dropped off the bus; most makers use B for the front passenger door. For the 2005–2010 Chrysler 300 and Charger, bulletin 08-061-12 names it the passenger door module and replaces it when locks and windows stay dead. Audi bulletin 2051276 (Q5 2018) finds U020000 in gateway J533 with a dead passenger window or lock switch, sometimes U10BA00 or U111100 in the driver door, and cures it with a one-minute fuse reset and new software for J387. Stellantis case S2423000040 (Durango 2023) sees U0200-00 with an intermittent passenger lock and checks pins, the lock rod and finally the latch. VW tech tip 97-21-02 pairs U019900 or U020000 with loose pins at the A-pillar. Usually no MIL; U0501 is invalid data.
c: Passenger door module software (Audi Q5 J387 update)
Loose, bent or corroded pins in the door or A-pillar connector
Broken wires in the door hinge harness
s: Passenger window or lock switch inoperative
Door does not lock or unlock centrally, sometimes intermittent
Child lock or door warning message in the cluster

U0201.t: Lost Communication With Door Control Module C
U0201.d: U0201 stands for door control module C, in the generic list the next door unit after driver (A) and front passenger (B), so on four-door cars usually a rear door. Audi, for example, gives each rear door its own controller (J388, J389, diagnostic addresses 00BB and 00BC), and its Q3 bulletin 2063376 deals with their child lock motors, but no Audi document names U0201. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The number also has a history: GM's 2011 code list for the Saab 9-5 assigns U0201 to the transfer case controller instead, so on older GM vehicles the scan tool's own text decides. Where it means a door, expect a rear window, lock or child lock that no longer responds; a chafed harness at the door hinge is a frequent reason. U0502 covers invalid data.
c: Chafed or broken wires in the rear door hinge harness
Loose or corroded pins in the door connector
s: Rear window, lock or child lock inoperative
Door or child lock warning in the cluster

U0202.t: Lost Communication With Door Control Module D
U0202.d: U0202 means the body network no longer hears from door control module D, which most four-door layouts give to the right rear door. FCA STAR case S1908000143 (Rev. A, August 2020) records it on a minivan with Stow 'n Go seating: U0202 for the right rear door module came together with U0201 (left rear), U0230 (power liftgate) and the interior bus codes U0010/U0011, while the owner had a no-start, many lit warning lamps and single wiper strokes. The cause was a chafed body harness beside the right B-pillar, at the outer mount of the passenger seat or along the floor routing next to the seat storage bins, including splice S910. A dead rear window or lock on that side is typical; no MIL.
c: Body harness chafed at the B-pillar or under the seats (FCA minivan)
Broken wires in the rear door hinge harness
s: Right rear window or lock inoperative
Several warning lamps and further U-codes at the same time
Possible no-start or unrequested wiper stroke when the bus wiring is damaged

U0203.t: Lost Communication With Door Control Module E
U0203.d: U0203 reports a missing door control module E. For the 2011 Saab 9-5, GM fills this slot with the left rear door switch panel, so on these GM platforms E is the electronics behind the rear left window and lock switches rather than a fifth door. GM preliminary information PIT5606J (GMC Acadia and Cadillac XT5, 2017–2021) lists U0203 among a crowd of U-codes that show up together when the instrument panel harness rubs through at the steering column next to the intermediate shaft, or when water reaches the body control module through a blocked HVAC drain or enters connectors such as X200, X201 and X500. Door locks cycling while driving or seats moving by themselves belong to that picture. The code alone sets no MIL.
c: Instrument panel harness chafed at the steering column (GM Acadia/XT5)
Water at the body control module or in body connectors
Broken wires between rear door and body
Rear door switch panel module faulty
s: Left rear window or lock switches without function
Door locks cycle on their own while driving
Many other lost-communication codes stored at once

U0204.t: Lost Communication With Door Control Module F
U0204.d: U0204 is set when door control module F stops answering. On the 2011 Saab 9-4x, whose U-code list comes from GM, the letter F belongs to the right rear door switch panel, the mirror-image partner of U0203 on the left. Before any repair, GM preliminary information PIC5741A (2013 Cadillac ATS, 2010–2013 SRX) is worth knowing: U0204, together with a long series of other communication codes and an instrument self-test, may appear only because the scan tool plug sits loosely in a diagnostic socket with spread terminals, most often ground pins 4 and 5. Checking and replacing those terminals comes first. With a genuine dropout, the window and lock switches at the right rear stop responding. No MIL is set.
c: Spread terminals in the diagnostic connector, false entries while testing (GM)
Broken wires in the right rear door hinge harness
Loose or corroded door connector pins
Rear door switch panel module faulty
s: Right rear window or lock switches inoperative
Codes appear together with an instrument self-test when the scan tool is plugged in

U0205.t: Lost Communication With Door Control Module G
U0205.d: U0205 covers door control module G. The generic list reserves eight door module slots, A to H, so G only comes into play on vehicles carrying more door electronics than four side doors; which unit gets the letter is the maker's choice. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Door modules usually run windows, locks, mirrors and switch lighting and often act as master for small LIN nodes like a window lifter or mirror switch. For comparison, Chrysler bulletin 08-061-12 on the 2005–2010 300 and Charger first has the battery disconnected for about a minute and orders a new door module only if it still stays off the bus. Invalid data from unit G is U0506. A MIL is not expected.
c: Broken or chafed wires at the door transition
Missing fuse, power or ground feed of the door module
Door module faulty or hung after a voltage drop
s: Window, lock or mirror on the affected door inoperative
Door switch lighting dark

U0206.t: Lost Communication With Folding Top Control Module
U0206.d: U0206 indicates that the folding top control module, which drives the hydraulic or electric mechanism of a convertible roof and watches its end positions, has fallen silent on the bus. Lamborghini names U020600, stored in control unit 00C5, in its Revuelto baseline update bulletins L74X-A.11.25 (model year 2024) and L74X-A.05.25 (2025): if the entry shows up during the SVM code step, the technician adds it to the test plan and runs the guided update programming for the unit. Beyond these bulletins no maker documents the code publicly. Usual consequences are a roof that will neither open nor close and a roof warning in the cluster. Invalid data from the same module is U0507. No MIL.
c: Module software needs an update after programming (Lamborghini Revuelto)
Fuse, power or ground of the top module missing
Harness or connector in the top compartment damaged or wet
s: Convertible top neither opens nor closes
Roof or top warning in the instrument cluster

U0207.t: Lost Communication With Moveable Roof Control Module A
U0207.d: U0207 concerns moveable roof control module A, the electronics of a power sunroof or glass roof. GM uses it: the 2011 Saab 9-5 list names the moveable roof control module, and GM preliminary information PIT5606J (GMC Acadia, Cadillac XT5 2017–2021) counts U0207 among the codes that appear after water gets in – mostly at the upper windshield corners hidden under the glass, rarely past the outer sunroof seal or a drain hose – or when the dash harness rubs at the steering column. Since roof modules sit in the headliner close to the drains, a leak can reach the unit or its plug. A sunroof that ignores its switch is the usual sign; U020A is the second roof unit, U0508 invalid data. No MIL.
c: Water leak at windshield corners, sunroof seal or blocked drain hose
Dash harness chafed at the steering column (GM Acadia/XT5)
Corroded connector at the roof module
s: Sunroof does not respond to the switch
Damp headliner or water marks near the A-pillar
Further U-codes in several modules

U0208.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module A
U0208.d: U0208 says seat control module A has dropped out, mostly a driver's seat unit. The letter is used differently: FCA radio bulletin 08-108-14 (2015 Cherokee, Grand Cherokee, Ram) calls it the heated seat control module and removes a false U0208-00 on the Cherokee with new Uconnect radio software; Audi bulletin 2067722 (Q7 2017–2024, SQ7) finds U020800 with a dead driver seat when road salt under the driver-side sill carpet has oxidised splice B304; Ford SSM 55168 (2027 Expedition, Navigator) sees U0208 in several modules when the driver seat module goes quiet, also stopping the power running boards, with a software fix due. GM's 2011 Saab list names the memory seat module. No MIL.
c: Splice under the driver-side carpet corroded by salt water (Audi Q7/Q8)
Seat module or radio software (Ford SSM 55168, FCA 08-108-14)
Seat harness pinched or unplugged under the seat
s: Power or memory seat does not move
Seat heating or ventilation cannot be switched
Power running boards fail (Ford Expedition/Navigator)

U0209.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module B
U0209.d: U0209 means seat control module B is no longer heard. On GM cars of 2010–2015 with heated front seats (LaCrosse, Regal, Verano, Camaro, Cruze, Equinox, Malibu, Sonic, Volt, Terrain) the HVAC module logs it when both seat heaters quit: preliminary information PIC5954 blames intermittent software in seat heating module K29, which is reset by pulling its fuse for five minutes, and PIC5954B adds a reprogramming; replacing the module is ruled out. The 2011 Saab 9-5 list also calls it the front seat heating module. Newer GM SUVs fill the slot differently: PIT5762F (2020–2023 Tahoe, Escalade, Corvette and others) names the driver seat bolster memory module and treats a history entry as ignorable. No MIL.
c: Seat heating module software hangs (GM K29, reset and reprogram)
Stored history entry from a software anomaly (GM 2020–2023 SUVs)
Fuse or supply of the seat module
Seat harness damaged under the seat
s: Both front seat heaters inoperative
Side bolster adjustment of the driver seat does not react

U020A.t: Lost Communication With Moveable Roof Control Module B
U020A.d: U020A stands for moveable roof control module B, a second roof unit beside module A (U0207); which drive it controls, for instance a separate sunshade or a further glass panel, depends on the maker. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Related service experience comes from roof modules in general: Kia service action SA595 (bulletin 363, 2025 K4) updates the roof control module because a software logic error left the sunroof unable to open or close, and the update contains a reset of the module for sunroof initialisation. Power roofs usually need such a re-learn after a power loss or module replacement before they travel fully again. Invalid data from unit B is U050B. No MIL.
c: Roof module software or missing initialisation
Wet or corroded connector in the headliner
Fuse or ground of roof module B
s: Second roof panel or sunshade does not move
Roof stops halfway or needs repeated button presses

U020B.t: Lost Communication With Door Control Module H
U020B.d: U020B is the last of the eight door module slots and flags lost contact with door control module H. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and on ordinary four-door cars the letter stays empty. Where it is assigned, the receiving unit, usually body control module or gateway, misses the cyclic messages of that door unit; the body control module itself keeps locking and lighting alive, so only functions local to that door fail. A loose plug between door and body is the best first suspect: Volkswagen tech tip 97-21-02 links door module dropouts with U019900 or U020000 to poorly seated pins at the A-pillar; that check suits any door unit. U050C is invalid data. No MIL.
c: Poorly seated or corroded pins in the door-to-body connector
Wire break in the door transition
s: Window, lock or switches of one door inoperative
Door ajar or door system warning in the cluster

U020C.t: Lost Communication With Wireless Accessory Charging Module A
U020C.d: U020C means wireless accessory charging module A, the inductive Qi pad usually placed in the centre console, no longer talks on the network. No manufacturer documents this code publicly with module and threshold. The pad takes no part in driving, so its loss only switches off phone charging and the related display messages. How such modules are serviced shows Ford TSB 22-2485 (2020–2022 Bronco, Bronco Sport, Escape, Expedition, Explorer, F-150, Super Duty, Maverick, Corsair, Navigator): poor charging with MagSafe iPhones is cured by updating the module software. For a lost-communication entry the console plug, its fuse and a unit stuck after an update are the first checks. U050D is invalid data; no MIL.
c: Fuse or supply of the charging pad
Loose or damaged connector under the console
s: Phone does not charge on the wireless pad
No charging status shown on the centre display

U020D.t: Lost Communication With Wireless Accessory Charging Module B
U020D.d: U020D is the second wireless charging slot, B, meant for vehicles with two inductive pads, for example a further one for rear passengers. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The early GM system shows what sits behind such a unit: preliminary information PIC6049 (2015 Cadillac ATS, CTS, Escalade, Chevrolet Tahoe, Suburban, GMC Yukon with option K4C) placed the wireless charging module under technical assistance restriction and asks for phone model, receiver cover and charging habits before any replacement. A pad that pauses because the phone is hot is no network fault. A genuine U020D means pad B stays dead while pad A still charges. U020C covers pad A, U050E invalid data. No MIL.
c: Fuse or supply of charging pad B
Connector or harness to the second pad
s: Second wireless pad does not charge, first still works
Charging indicator for that pad missing

U0210.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module C
U0210.d: U0210 flags lost contact with seat control module C. GM fills the slot in two ways: the 2011 Saab 9-5 list assigns it to the rear seat heating module, while bulletin 23-NA-206 and its predecessor PIT5762F (2020–2023 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon, Corvette, CT4, CT5) name the passenger front seat bladder control module, i.e. the air cells for lumbar support or massage. There U0210 is one of many history codes caused by software anomalies; they set no MIL or message and are simply ignored, whereas a current U0210 is diagnosed as usual. A real dropout shows as dead rear seat heaters or a passenger lumbar or massage function that no longer reacts. No MIL.
c: History entry from a software anomaly (GM 2020–2023, ignore if not current)
Fuse or supply of the seat module
s: Rear seat heating inoperative
Passenger lumbar support or massage does not react
Code stored only in history without any complaint

U0211.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module D
U0211.d: U0211 reports that seat control module D is absent from the bus. GM bulletin 21-NA-131, which replaces PIT5796A (2020–2021 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and 2021 Corvette, CT4, CT5), names it the memory seat module: the driver assistance controller EOCM records U0211 and invalid data U0512 when software in the memory seat module misbehaves. Auto entry and exit or memory recall then fail, the backrest stops short of full recline, and Super Cruise may drop out with a service message. Reprogramming the driver seat memory module is the cure. Honda bulletin 25-051 (2024 Prologue) removes the same code with new software for the radio control module A11. No MIL.
c: Seat harness or connector under the driver seat
s: Seat memory and easy entry/exit inoperative
Backrest will not recline fully
Driver assistance message or Super Cruise unavailable

U0212.t: Lost Communication With Steering Column Control Module
U0212.d: U0212 means the steering column control module, which reads stalks and steering wheel buttons such as wipers, turn signals and cruise switches, is missing from the network. Ford's 2023 diesel OBD summary lets the engine computer set it once the SCCM's message has been absent for more than 5 s, while the 2014 Ford list carries it with no MIL flag. GM bulletin 20-NA-114 (CT4, CT5, Escalade, Tahoe, Yukon, Suburban, Corvette 2020–2021 with electric column lock N06) calls U0212 in IPC, BCM or gateway a wrong mapping and has it diagnosed as U0236. Stellantis note 9100447 (Pacifica, Voyager 2024–2025) wants BCM checks, switch and airbag plugs and wiper or turn signal tests before a new SCCM.
c: False code mapping with electric column lock (GM N06, diagnose U0236)
Switch or airbag connectors at the column loose or corroded
Harness chafed at the base of the steering column
s: Wipers, turn signals or steering wheel buttons inoperative
Cruise control unavailable
Code stored in several modules without any complaint

U0213.t: Lost Communication With Mirror Control Module A
U0213.d: U0213 is set when mirror control module A stops reporting. In FCA vehicles A is the interior mirror: STAR case S2108000013 (2021 Jeep Grand Cherokee) found the BCM storing U0213-00 after a Restore Vehicle Configuration had wrongly marked the combined rear view mirror module CRVMM as fitted, for instance after enabling reverse camera grid lines per RRT 08-099-20; cars without that mirror then wait for messages that never come, while the driver notices nothing. Jeep bulletin 23-033-25 (2024–2025 Wrangler, India and Asia-Pacific) lists U0213-00 among the codes of a multi-system repair bundle. U014D is mirror module B, U0514 invalid data. The mirror itself sets no MIL.
c: Mirror module enabled in configuration but not fitted (FCA)
Mirror connector at the windshield loose
s: Code active without any noticeable fault
Auto-dimming or camera display in the mirror inoperative

U0214.t: Lost Communication With Remote Function Actuation Module
U0214.d: U0214 stands for the remote function actuation module, the receiver for key fob, passive entry or phone as a key. Ford calls it RFA: SSM 51571 (Mustang Mach-E 2021–2023) and SSM 54773 (Nautilus 2021–2023) describe phone as a key failing and U0214 in several modules because the RFA hangs in programming mode following an over-the-air update; one minute without the RFA fuse in the BCM and a reprogramming bring it back. GM bulletin 15-NA-004 (Acadia 2013–2016) lists U0214 with many other codes when the slow LAN line feeding the remote door lock receiver gets squeezed by the rear HVAC duct in the headliner, giving intermittent no-crank. Ford's 2014 list marks no MIL.
c: RFA module stuck in programming mode after an update (Ford)
LAN wire to the receiver pinched in the headliner (GM Acadia)
Fuse or supply of the receiver module
s: Key fob, keyless entry or phone as a key inoperative
Intermittent no crank or radio and HVAC dropouts

U0215.t: Lost Communication With Door Switch A
U0215.d: U0215 is logged when door switch unit A, a keypad with its own small controller, stops answering on the bus. NXP application note AN2205 shows how such a keypad usually works: it is a LIN slave that never speaks unprompted; the body controller asks it roughly every 100 ms and expects a four-byte reply holding key states and LIN error flags. If that reply goes missing, the master records the loss. In the GM manual for the 2011 Saab 9-5 these checks run only between 9 and 16 V, and a history entry is dropped after 50 clean ignition cycles. No manufacturer documents U0215 publicly, and which door carries letter A depends on the maker. U0516 reports invalid data from the same switch. Usually only the keys of one panel fail; no MIL.
c: LIN or supply wire broken where the harness flexes at the door hinge
Switch unit A without battery feed or ground
LIN line shorted to ground or battery (often silences several nodes at once)
Electronics in switch unit A failed
s: Window, mirror or lock keys on one panel do nothing
Panel backlighting stays dark
Code returns after clearing, sometimes only when the door is moved

U0216.t: Lost Communication With Door Switch B
U0216.d: U0216 reports that door switch unit B has dropped off the network. FCA uses the code on the 2014 Jeep Cherokee (KL) and its text names the driver door switch as the missing partner, so B is the driver's panel there. Bulletin 08-013-15, which replaced 08-111-14 and was also issued as rapid response transmittal 15-021, covers vehicles built up to 11 July 2014: after the battery had been disconnected, the cluster could show Start/Stop Not Available and the BCM held U0216. The cure was new BCM software, followed by restoring and aligning the Proxi configuration whenever the start/stop message had appeared. On other vehicles a wiring fault in the driver door remains the usual suspect. No MIL.
c: Vehicle configuration (Proxi) no longer consistent after battery disconnect
Damaged wiring or connector between driver door and body
s: Cluster message Start/Stop Not Available
Code appears after the battery was disconnected
Keys on the driver's switch panel may not respond

U0217.t: Lost Communication With Door Switch C
U0217.d: U0217 is set when door switch unit C no longer answers its master. How much breaks then depends on the door architecture. In NXP's LIN door reference SG2034 the driver's control switch panel is itself the LIN master and commands the front and rear window lifters, door locks and mirror as slaves; in the AN2205 layout the keypad is only a slave whose key states are read by the body controller, or alternatively by the window nodes. If the lost unit is the driver's panel, the remote buttons for the other windows can go dead together with its own keys, while a passenger panel usually affects one window. No manufacturer documents U0217 publicly, and the letter-to-door mapping is set by the maker. No MIL.
c: Broken wire in the flexing harness between door and body
Corroded or loose connector at the switch panel
Fault in the door or body module that polls the panel
s: Other windows can no longer be operated from the driver's panel
Keys on the affected panel inoperative
Mirror adjustment from the panel unavailable

U0218.t: Lost Communication With Door Switch D
U0218.d: U0218 means door switch unit D has gone silent. Rear-door panels are often bus nodes in their own right; on the 2011 Saab 9-5, GM even gives the left and right rear door switch panels separate codes. A detail worth knowing is the window lockout: the driver's panel sends a child-lock bit in its LIN reply, and according to NXP AN2205 the BCM or the individual window modules evaluate this bit and block the rear keys. When a rear panel stops answering, its window can often still be run from the driver's side; if the driver's panel is the one missing, the lockout status may be gone as well. No manufacturer documents U0218 publicly; letter D is assigned per make. No MIL.
c: Broken wire in the harness passage to the door
Moisture or corrosion at the switch panel connector
Body or door module not polling the panel correctly
s: Window key in one door has no effect
Same window still moves from the driver's panel
Rear window lockout behaves unexpectedly

U0219.t: Lost Communication With Door Switch E
U0219.d: U0219 means the networked door switch unit E is no longer heard. In modern doors the switch packs for windows, mirrors and locks are often small bus nodes, typically LIN slaves under a door or body module, so each panel can report its own communication loss. The master that polls switch E stores U0219 once its replies stop; GM documents this setting rule for the whole U0100-U02FF range. No manufacturer documents U0219 publicly; GM's U-code list uses its own entries (U0203/U0204) for rear door switch panel modules instead. The letter E is assigned by the maker, so the door concerned must be taken from the vehicle's documentation. U0215 to U0218 and U0220 cover the other switches. Window or lock buttons fail; no MIL.
c: Broken wire in the door hinge area (flexing harness)
Water ingress into the door switch pack
Switch unit E without power or ground
s: Window, mirror or lock buttons in one door inoperative
Switch illumination off
Fault changes when the door is opened or closed

U0220.t: Lost Communication With Door Switch F
U0220.d: U0220 reports that door switch unit F has stopped communicating. Water is a well-documented enemy of such units. GM recall 14V404 (bulletin 14309) covered 2005–2007 TrailBlazer, Envoy, Rainier and Saab 9-7X: salty melt water reaching the driver-door module corroded its circuit board, so lock and window switches worked only now and then, windows could move by themselves and the board could overheat; dealers fitted a new module. On 2014–2018 GM pickups and SUVs, bulletin 18-NA-079 traces LIN losses of the driver window switch to water at the door-to-body connector X500, using GM's own code U1538. No manufacturer documents U0220 itself; the letter is assigned per make. No MIL.
c: Water or salt slush inside the switch unit, corroded circuit board
Broken wire in the door harness
Switch unit failed without visible moisture
s: Window or lock keys work only intermittently
Window moves without a button press
Heat or burnt smell at the door switch panel

U0221.t: Lost Communication With Door Switch G
U0221.d: U0221 is stored when door switch unit G no longer replies. The weak spot is often the passage between door and body, where the harness bends at every opening. FCA STAR cases S1808000031 and S2108000106 (Jeep Compass 2018–2021) describe it: corrosion at the driver door-to-body connector and a badly seated rubber grommet led to intermittent windows, locks and mirrors, rear windows lowering on their own, door-ajar warnings, start/stop dropouts and LIN complaints; the fix was cleaning the connector, seating it fully and aligning the grommet. Those cases list B-codes, not U0221. No manufacturer documents U0221 publicly; which door carries G depends on the maker. No MIL.
c: Corroded door-to-body connector behind a poorly sealing grommet
Wire chafed or broken inside the grommet
s: Windows, locks and mirrors fail intermittently
Door-ajar warning while driving
Start/stop function stops working at times

U0222.t: Lost Communication With Door Window Motor A
U0222.d: U0222 says door window motor A, a motor with its own electronics, is no longer heard. GM uses it on 2021–2025 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban and Yukon with air leveling (RPO F47): PIT5981B lists U0222 to U0225 as codes that can sit beside a low or leaning air suspension, a Service Leveling System message or short-term inflates that do nothing. The link is the door-ajar switch, wired directly to each window motor; while a motor is silent, the door state is unknown and the scan tool shows closed by default. GM saw this mostly on upfitted vehicles such as armored cars or limousines. On its 2014–2018 trucks GM still used its own U1534 for the driver window motor. No MIL.
c: Door wiring altered or damaged during an upfit (armored car, limousine)
Broken bus or supply wire in the door harness
Electronics of window motor A failed
Water or corrosion at the motor connector
s: Air suspension low, leaning or not leveling
Service Leveling System message in the driver information center
Door shown as closed in scan data although it is open
Window in the affected door does not move

U0223.t: Lost Communication With Door Window Motor B
U0223.d: U0223 points to door window motor B dropping out of communication; GM lists it in PIT5981B together with A, C and D for its 2021–2025 full-size SUVs. Smart motors keep learned data: Atmel's AVR480 reference stores blocking points and anti-pinch parameters in EEPROM and acquires them while the window is first operated. GM TechLink (April 2021, Equinox and Terrain 2018–2021) warns that after unplugging the motor or the door harness the motor must be normalised, otherwise express-up and the small upward index when the door shuts are lost. A lost learn is a different fault from U0223, though: a motor without its learned values still answers on the bus. Both often show up after work inside the door. No MIL.
c: Motor or door connector not fully reconnected after door trim work
Broken wire in the door harness
Electronics of window motor B failed
Blown fuse or missing ground for the motor
s: Window in the affected door does not move at all
Express-up unavailable
Fault appears right after door panel or glass work

U0224.t: Lost Communication With Door Window Motor C
U0224.d: U0224 means door window motor C no longer reports in; GM's PIT5981B names it among the four window motor codes of its 2021–2025 full-size SUVs. Inside such a motor sits more than a driver stage: NXP's AN3147 reference counts Hall pulses to track glass position, detects pinching or stall and reports chip status such as overvoltage or overtemperature to the LIN master. The anti-pinch logic has to meet FMVSS 118, which permits automatic closing only if the glass reverses before it squeezes a test rod with 100 N or more. With the motor silent, the master sees neither position nor protection status, so functions built on them, such as one-touch closing, are generally unavailable. No MIL.
c: Broken bus or supply wire in the door harness
Motor electronics damaged (overvoltage, overheating, Hall sensor board)
Fuse or ground for motor C missing
s: One-touch up and down unavailable
Window in the affected door does not move
Glass stops at random points or not at all

U0225.t: Lost Communication With Door Window Motor D
U0225.d: U0225 marks door window motor D as missing from the bus. GM's PIT5981B names U0225 last in its list for 2021–2025 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban and Yukon and notes that the cases came mainly from vehicles altered by upfitters, so door wiring touched during a conversion deserves the first look. How the loss is noticed is shown in NXP's AN2960 window-lift example: each slave carries a response-error signal for its last frame, which lets the master watch every node, and a slave that no longer answers its header at all is exactly what a lost-communication code describes. GM asks for such faults to be fixed before the air suspension is judged. No MIL.
c: Door wiring changed during a vehicle conversion
LIN wire to motor D chafed, open or shorted
Electronics of window motor D failed
s: Window in the affected door inoperative
Air suspension not leveling on vehicles with door-ajar input via the motor
Further lost-communication codes from other door nodes

U0226.t: Lost Communication With Door Window Motor E
U0226.d: U0226 is stored when door window motor E stops answering. No manufacturer documents U0226 publicly, and the door behind letter E is the maker's choice. Water, however, is a proven cause of failure for window motors with built-in electronics. Tesla bulletin SB-18-11-005 R1 replaced both front window motor and regulator units on Model 3 cars built before about January 2018 because water could get inside the motors and make them fail. GM bulletin 18-NA-079 found water and corrosion at the driver window motor connector on 2014–2018 trucks and replaced motor and door harness together. A leaking door membrane or water deflector is therefore worth checking first. No MIL.
c: Water inside the motor housing or its electronics
Door membrane or water deflector not sealing
Broken wire in the door harness
s: Window stops working, often after rain or a car wash
Window moves jerkily before failing completely
Corrosion or moisture visible at the motor plug

U0227.t: Lost Communication With Door Window Motor F
U0227.d: U0227 reports that door window motor F cannot be reached. Besides wiring faults, the LIN sleep and wake cycle is worth understanding here. In NXP's AN2960 window-lift example the motor node drops into low-power mode on a go-to-sleep request, or after four seconds without bus traffic, behaviour that LIN 2.0 makes mandatory for slaves, and it becomes active again on bus activity or through a wake pin. A node that fails to wake, for instance because of an unstable supply or a damaged transceiver, looks to the master like a lost node. No manufacturer documents U0227 publicly, and letter F is assigned by the maker. U0528 is the matching invalid-data code. No MIL.
c: Weak or interrupted supply or ground at the motor
LIN transceiver in the motor electronics damaged
Broken wire in the door harness
Software fault in the LIN master (door or body module)
s: Window fails intermittently
Window and its one-touch function inoperative

U0228.t: Lost Communication With Door Window Motor G
U0228.d: U0228 concerns door window motor G, the last letter of this group. No manufacturer documents U0228 publicly. GM shows that a networked window motor does not automatically mean these generic codes: in the 2011 Saab 9-5 the body control module runs the front passenger and driver motors as devices 0 and 4 on LIN bus 3 and the two rear motors on LIN bus 4, and flags a lost motor with GM's own U1530, U1534, U1540 or U1544. Some motors do without Hall sensors; a Gentherm patent derives speed and pinch events from the current ripple, which still calls for electronics at the motor and thus a bus node. Which door carries G is up to the maker. No MIL.
c: Broken bus or supply wire in the door harness
Electronics of window motor G failed
s: Window in the affected door does not move
Pinch protection and one-touch operation unavailable

U0229.t: Lost Communication With Heated Steering Wheel Module
U0229.d: U0229 means the heated steering wheel module no longer answers. GM PIT5883G (December 2022) explains one harmless case: many 2022–2023 GM models were built during a parts shortage with the heated wheel disabled (RPO 00G); there U0229, together with U152B or U1530, may be stored, should be ignored and lights no warning. Ford SSM 47850 shows why the module's location varies: on cars with adaptive steering, heating is handled by the SECM, a steering effort controller inside the wheel, while other cars carry a separate HSWM. Power for the rim heater and its thermistor passes through the clockspring, as a Ford patent illustrates. U052A covers invalid data from the module. No MIL.
c: Module without fuse feed or ground
Heated wheel disabled from the factory (GM RPO 00G), code to be ignored
Clockspring interrupted (when the module sits in the steering wheel)
Heated steering wheel module failed or not configured
s: Steering wheel heating does not switch on
Heater button indicator does not respond
Code stored without any noticeable fault (feature not fitted or disabled)

U022E.t: Lost Communication With Object Detection Maintenance Control Module A
U022E.d: U022E reports that object detection maintenance control module A has stopped talking on the vehicle network. The J2012 name points to a unit that keeps the detection sensors of the driver assistance system usable, for example by washing or heating camera, radar or lidar covers; patent US11077472B2 describes such a cleaning device for an object detection sensor. No manufacturer documents U022E publicly, so the real job of module A, its bus and its mounting place come from the maker's wiring data. GM's general logic for the U0100-U02FF range applies: a receiving unit misses the periodic status message at 9-16 V and stores the code. U022F is module B, U052F flags implausible data from A. Expect sensor cleaning or assistance warnings; no MIL is known.
c: Module A without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Damaged or corroded bus wiring to module A
Washer fluid or water ingress at the module or its plug
Module A faulty or not programmed
s: Sensor cleaning or sensor blocked warning
Driver assistance features unavailable

U022F.t: Lost Communication With Object Detection Maintenance Control Module B
U022F.d: U022F is the B counterpart: a control unit expects messages from object detection maintenance control module B and receives none. Cars with many cameras and radars could split sensor upkeep, such as washer pumps, nozzle valves or cover heaters, across two units, and B would then serve the second group; which sensors that is stays the maker's choice, because no manufacturer documents U022F publicly. Setting follows the GM pattern for lost communication codes, a missing periodic status frame with supply between 9 and 16 V. If U022E is stored as well, check a shared fuse, ground or bus branch before suspecting either unit. U0530 covers invalid data from B. A soiled sensor may then remain uncleaned, and assistance functions can shut down.
c: Fuse, ground or bus branch shared with module A interrupted
Module B faulty or software not matching
s: Sensor blocked or cleaning unavailable message
Camera or radar based assistance switched off

U0230.t: Lost Communication With Rear Gate Module
U0230.d: U0230 means the rear gate module, which runs a powered liftgate or tailgate with its drive, latch, cinch motor and pinch detection, has dropped off the bus. Toyota bulletin T-SB-0038-15 (Highlander and Highlander HV 2008-2013) names U0230 together with B2222 when the power back door reverses at the end of its travel or clunks at the striker, and gives a hinge and hatch inspection and repair. GM PI PIT5422 (Equinox, Terrain 2010-2015) blames moisture and corroded terminals in connector X901, high on the liftgate, for U0230 and other low speed LAN codes. A Chrysler STAR case (S1908000143) found it as Power Liftgate Module code beside chafed wiring at the right B-pillar. Saab lists the slot as Liftgate Control Module. Power operation of the gate fails; no MIL.
c: Water or corrosion in the harness connector at the liftgate
Wires broken in the flexing harness between body and gate
Bus wiring chafed along the body (seat or pillar area)
s: Power liftgate does not open or close electrically
Gate reverses or stops during power closing
Several lost communication codes stored at once

U0231.t: Lost Communication With Rain Sensing Module
U0231.d: U0231 shows that the rain sensing module on the windscreen, an optical unit that registers droplets and often ambient brightness too, no longer answers. It usually sits on a LIN line below a body or wiper controller, which stores the code. FCA bulletin 08-050-22 Rev. A (Jeep Grand Cherokee WL 2021) lists U0231-00 among a group of LIN lost communication codes that appear without a MIL and are cured by new body control module software. When the sensor is silent, automatic wiping falls back to the fixed stages and, where the same unit measures light, the automatic headlamp function can be lost. After a windscreen replacement, a loose plug behind the mirror cover is a classic cause. U0532 covers invalid data from the same sensor.
c: Sensor plug not seated after windscreen or mirror work
LIN wire damaged in the headliner or A-pillar
s: Automatic wipers inoperative, manual stages still work
Automatic headlamps not switching

U0232.t: Lost Communication With Side Obstacle Detection Control Module A
U0232.d: U0232 means side obstacle detection control module A, one of the rear corner radars for blind spot and cross traffic warning, is missing from the network. Saab's 2011 list puts A on the left; Toyota bulletin T-SB-0063-19 (Tacoma 2016-2018) calls U0232 loss of the blind spot slave module. Volvo journal TJ 30858 (XC90, S90, 2016-2018) has the right unit log U023292 for its partner and prescribes new software. Ford TSB 24-2180 (Expedition, Navigator 2022-2024) finds U0232 in the IPMA when mud, snow or ice packs behind the bumper and adds shields. A Chrysler STAR case (Durango 2020) traced it to an open fuse 95 and a pinched circuit in the liftgate. Blind spot alerts go dark; no MIL.
c: Mud, snow or ice packed between radar and bumper cover
Open fuse or pinched wiring in the rear body or liftgate
s: Blind spot system unavailable message
Mirror warning lamps do not light
Rear cross traffic alert inoperative

U0233.t: Lost Communication With Side Obstacle Detection Control Module B
U0233.d: U0233 is stored when side obstacle detection control module B no longer reports. In the Saab 2011 list B is the right hand unit, which matches Volvo TJ 30858 (XC90, S90, 2016-2018): there the left sensor logs U023392 for the right one, and a software update is the fix. Toyota reverses the roles on the Tacoma 2016-2018 (T-SB-0063-19), where U0233 means the blind spot master is lost, listed alongside axis misalignment codes C1AC1/C1AC2. Ford TSB 24-2180 for Expedition and Navigator 2022-2024 sees U0233 and U0232 together in the IPMA with sensor blocked messages, blaming dirt build-up or corroded radar wiring. Because the two radars often talk to each other, a single cause can trigger both codes. Side warnings stop; no MIL.
c: Dirt, snow or ice build-up behind the rear bumper
s: Blind spot or cross traffic alert unavailable
Sensor blocked message without any obstacle

U0234.t: Lost Communication With Convenience Recall Module
U0234.d: U0234 states that the convenience recall module has fallen silent on the network. Convenience recall means stored personal settings brought back on request or by key, typically seat, outside mirror, pedal and column positions and audio presets; patent US7525931B2 shows such a recall session started by a networked door module message. No manufacturer documents U0234 publicly, and many brands place this job in seat or door modules that carry their own codes, such as U0208 for a memory seat module, so the unit behind the code must be taken from the maker's data. GM's general logic applies: periodic status message missing while supply is 9-16 V. U0535 covers invalid data. Memory buttons stop working; driving is unaffected, no MIL expected.
c: Module without power or ground (fuse, connector under seat or door)
Harness under the seat pinched by seat travel
s: Memory buttons for seat and mirrors without function
Driver profile not recalled with the key

U0235.t: Lost Communication With Front Distance Range Sensor - Single Sensor or Center
U0235.d: U0235 means the forward long range radar, the single or centre sensor that measures the gap to traffic ahead for adaptive cruise and collision warning, has gone quiet. GM's 2025 OBD summary 25OBDG04B lets the object calculation module EOCM3 set it when any of six radar data bursts is absent for more than 0.25 s at 9-16 V, skipped in transport mode, after resets and during bus-off; adaptive cruise is then disabled and the code is Special Type C, so no MIL. GM PI PIC6606 (Cadillac Optiq 2025) reports Collision Alert or Driver Assist unavailable with a current U0235 and prescribes a BCM update plus a new long range radar after checking the wiring. Ford's 2014 list carries it without MIL. U023D/U023E are the corner sensors.
c: Radar connector or wiring at the front end damaged (often after a collision)
Weak 12 V supply or BCM calibration (GM PIC6606)
Fault on the object or chassis bus shared with other modules
s: Adaptive cruise control unavailable
Collision alert or driver assist unavailable message

U0236.t: Lost Communication With Column Lock Module
U0236.d: U0236 reports that the column lock module, which electrically bolts and frees the steering shaft as theft protection, has stopped communicating. It has nothing to do with the steering angle sensor (U0126). GM bulletin 20-NA-114 for 2020-2021 Cadillac CT4, CT5 and Escalade, Chevrolet Tahoe and Suburban, GMC Yukon and export Corvette with electric column lock (RPO N06) states that U0212 stored by the cluster, body module or gateway is mis-mapped there and has the technician diagnose U0236 instead. Saab's 2011 U-code list names the slot Steering Column Lock Module. Since the start system usually waits for confirmation that the lock has released, a mute lock module can bring a steering lock warning or a refusal to start. U0537 covers invalid lock data; no MIL documented.
c: Column lock module without power or ground (fuse, connector at column)
Harness at the steering column chafed or plug loose after column work
Low battery voltage during start request
s: Steering lock or service steering column warning
Engine does not crank or start
Steering wheel stays locked

U0237.t: Lost Communication With Digital Audio Control Module C
U0237.d: U0237 means a third digital audio unit, module C, has gone silent. Ford uses the code in its newer infotainment layout: SSM 49737 (Mustang Mach-E 2021) and its follow-up SSM 51778 (2020-2022 Escape, Edge, Explorer, Expedition, F-150, Mach-E) list U0237 and U0238 when the speakers fall silent, chimes move to the instrument cluster and neither the ACM (audio control module) nor the digital signal processor (DSP) answers. The cause there is DSP software; the fix is a hard reset by disconnecting the 12 V battery and a DSP reflash. GM fills the slot differently: Saab's 2011 list names U0237 Multimedia Player Interface Module. U0238 is module D, U0193/U0194 are A and B, U0538 covers invalid data. No sound, no MIL.
c: Audio DSP software hung or outdated (Ford SSM 49737/51778)
s: No sound from the speakers
Warning chimes only from the instrument cluster

U0238.t: Lost Communication With Digital Audio Control Module D
U0238.d: U0238 is set when digital audio control module D stops sending. In Ford and Lincoln vehicles this is the digital signal processor for audio that drives the amplified speaker set, and the code is mostly logged by the ACM, the audio control module. SSM 52999 covers 2023-2024 Escape with Bang and Olufsen sound: intermittent silence with U0238 in ACM or APIM, cured by DSP reprogramming. SSM 54751 for 2024-2026 Nautilus with 28 speakers and 2025-2026 Navigator has the technician pull the DSP fuse for a minute, notes that a new or reflashed DSP will not help, and expected a fix by Q2 2026. Earlier SSM 49737 (Mach-E 2021) lists it with U0237. U0539 covers invalid data from D. Audio drops out; no MIL.
c: DSP fuse open or with poor blade contact
s: Intermittent or permanent loss of audio
Premium sound system without output

U0239.t: Lost Communication With Entrapment Control Module A
U0239.d: U0239 means entrapment control module A no longer sends messages. Such a unit watches a power closing panel, a window, sunroof, sliding door or gate, for a trapped object and reverses the motor. In the US, FMVSS 118 sets the reversal limits for windows and roof panels that close without constant switch input; anti-pinch electronics such as Microchip's LIN window lift design or TI's TIDA-01389 sunroof driver detect a jam from motor current or Hall pulses. No manufacturer documents U0239 publicly, so which panel module A protects comes from the maker's documentation. GM's rule applies: status message missing at 9-16 V. U0240 is module B, U053A invalid data from A. Typically one-touch or automatic closing is blocked; no MIL.
c: Module A without power or ground
Bus wire broken in door hinge or roof harness
Water in the module or plug (door, roof drain)
s: One-touch or automatic closing does not work
Window or sunroof needs re-initialisation

U023A.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Module A
U023A.d: U023A reports loss of image processing module A, usually the windscreen camera feeding lane keeping, auto high beam and collision warning. Ford calls it IPMA: Mustang 2024 (SSM 52077) logs U023A in the SCCM after a remote start with Pre-Collision Assist unavailable, and F-150 2021-2023 (TSB 24-2267) shows U023A:08 after SCCM programming, fixed by IPMA software. GM PIT5482 (2016 Tahoe, Escalade, Silverado and others) forbids replacing the front camera for a history U023A with Service Front Camera; PIC5814 (2013 ATS, XTS, SRX) says the short range radars log it at every shutdown, no repair needed. Toyota T-TT-0352-15: Highlander meters swapped from cars without LDA keep it for good. Ford's 2014 list: no MIL.
c: Camera module software or low power mode handling (Ford IPMA)
History code logged at power down without real fault (GM PIC5814)
Instrument cluster swapped from a car without lane departure alert (Toyota)
Camera plug or wiring at the windscreen damaged
s: Service front camera or pre-collision assist unavailable message
Lane keeping and auto high beam off
Code only stored as history

U023B.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Module B
U023B.d: U023B points to image processing module B. GM uses it on its newer Super Cruise vehicles: PI PIC6607 (2026 Cadillac LYRIQ and VISTIQ) lists U023B SYM00 as a history entry next to U3000, U1624, U0140 and U053C and states that these do not explain a Super Cruise unavailable message, so the image processing module must not be replaced for them; the real fault is found with GM's Super Cruise diagnosis. Ford names its 360 degree camera computer IPMB, for example on the 2020-2021 Explorer, Aviator and Corsair (SSM 49980, blue screen, reflash and camera alignment), so on Ford a U023B concerns that unit. Only a current code with a matching symptom needs wiring and supply checks. U053C covers invalid data from B; no MIL.
c: Power, ground or bus wiring to module B interrupted
s: Super Cruise or camera based assistance unavailable
Surround view camera image blank

U023C.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Module C
U023C.d: U023C covers image processing module C, which GM uses for the video processing module (VPM) of its surround vision system. Bulletin 21-NA-209 (2021 Cadillac Escalade and Escalade ESV with RPO UXP) describes a black radio screen showing a triangle and a struck-through camera, with U023C and B1A62 current in the VPM K157; VPM software is the cause, and the repair is pulling fuse F28 for a minute, then reprogramming the VPM. GM's 2025 OBD summary 25OBDG04B lets EOCM3 set U023C when the surround vision data or the auxiliary camera status messages are absent for more than 0.25 s; the EOCM then disables adaptive cruise, and as a Special Type C code it leaves the MIL off. U053D covers invalid data from C.
c: Fuse or supply to the video processing module
Camera or bus wiring to the module damaged
s: Black display with crossed-out camera symbol
Surround view cameras unavailable
Adaptive cruise control disabled

U023D.t: Lost Communication With Front Distance Range Sensor - Left
U023D.d: U023D means the left front distance range sensor, a short range corner radar that watches the area ahead and to the left of the bumper, has stopped reporting. Corner radars widen the field of view of the central long range radar, which helps adaptive cruise pick up cutting-in traffic. GM's 2025 summary 25OBDG04B is the only public manufacturer record: EOCM3 sets U023D when any of six left front radar bursts is missing for more than 0.20 s at 9-16 V, not in transport mode, not right after a reset and not during bus-off; adaptive cruise is disabled, Special Type C, no MIL. A crash repair or bumper work near the left headlamp is the usual suspect. U0235 is the centre sensor, U023E the right one, U043B invalid data.
c: Connector or harness at the left front corner damaged (collision, bumper work)
Road salt corrosion at the radar plug
s: Adaptive cruise control unavailable
Front cross traffic or collision assist limited

U023E.t: Lost Communication With Front Distance Range Sensor - Right
U023E.d: U023E is the mirror image for the right front corner: the short range radar on the passenger side of the front bumper no longer delivers its object data. Together with the left unit (U023D) and the centre long range radar (U0235) it gives adaptive cruise and collision assistance a wider view of vehicles merging into the lane. Publicly only GM documents the code, in its 2025 OBD summary 25OBDG04B, where EOCM3 flags U023E after a gap of more than 0.20 s in any of the six right front radar bursts, with the usual exclusions for transport mode, resets and bus-off; adaptive cruise is then switched off and the code is classed Special Type C, so the MIL stays off. If U023D and U023E set together, look at a shared supply or bus. U043C covers invalid data.
c: Right front corner radar wiring damaged after collision or bumper removal
Supply or bus fault shared with the left corner radar
s: Adaptive cruise control switched off
Driver assistance warning on the cluster

U0240.t: Lost Communication With Entrapment Control Module B
U0240.d: U0240 flags the second anti-trap unit, entrapment control module B, as missing on the network. Where a vehicle has more than one automatically closing panel, for example a sunroof plus a power sliding door, each may carry its own reversal electronics, and B denotes one of them as assigned by the maker; no manufacturer documents U0240 publicly. The protection itself is defined by FMVSS 118, which limits the squeezing force and requires reversal before a test rod is trapped, and by the reversal logic in anti-pinch modules that compare motor current with a learned profile. GM's lost communication logic still applies: a periodic status message stays away with supply at 9-16 V. Pair with U0239 for module A. Automatic closing may be disabled; no MIL.
c: Module B without power or ground
Wiring broken in a moving harness (sliding door, roof frame)
s: Automatic close function of a panel disabled
Panel only moves while the switch is held

U0241.t: Lost Communication With Headlamp Control Module A
U0241.d: Headlamp control module A runs the electronic front lighting, for example beam levelling, cornering light or LED segments. Ford calls it HCM; it sits on the vehicle network and logs network faults of its own, as on the 2017 Lincoln MKZ after remote start (SSM 46508). U0241 is stored by a listener such as the body controller, cluster or gateway once the periodic frames of module A stop arriving within its timeout; no maker publishes that limit. Land Rover names U0241-00 among several U codes on the 2015 LR4, caused by a console cooler box that stays powered after switch-off and disturbs other modules, cured by reflashing the ABS unit (SSM72146). Expect a headlamp warning and adaptive functions held at a basic beam. Module B is U0242; corrupt data from A give U0542.
c: Headlamp module without power or ground (fuse, connector at the lamp)
Damaged or corroded bus wiring in the front end, often after a collision or lamp replacement
Network disturbed by another module or accessory staying awake (Land Rover cooler box)
Headlamp module software fault or internal failure
s: Headlamp or adaptive lighting warning in the cluster
Cornering, levelling or matrix functions inactive, basic low beam only
Several U codes in other modules at the same time

U0242.t: Lost Communication With Headlamp Control Module B
U0242.d: Many cars fit one control module per headlamp, and the second one carries letter B. Jaguar labels the pair HCMA and HCMB on the 2020 XE (SSM74402), Bentley addresses them as light control left and right on the Continental GT (campaign 2056293/1), and a 2024 scan-tool release lists an HCMB for the Land Rover Discovery Sport.
