Which side B serves is not published. U0242 itself appears in no maker document; a receiver such as the body controller or gateway records it when the expected frames from B are missing. Because the two units share fuses, grounds or a bus branch on many cars, U0241 and U0242 stored together point to that common part rather than to two dead modules. The driver sees a lighting warning and the B-side lamp limited to basic functions. Data errors from B are U0543.
c: Module B without power or ground, e.g. blown fuse or loose lamp connector
Fault in a fuse, ground or bus branch shared with module A
Headlamp replaced without programming or with mismatched software
s: Lighting warning in the cluster
Headlamp on one side without adaptive or LED functions
Daytime running or position light out on one side

U0243.t: Lost Communication With Parking Assist Control Module B
U0243.d: Parking assist module B is a second parking controller beside the main one, which J2012 covers with U0159. Stellantis uses the code by name: on 2021–2023 Jeep Grand Cherokee and 2022–2023 Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer the cluster and the module listed as ETM store U0243-00 for lost contact with the central vision park assist module (CVPAM), which handles the surround view cameras, while body, steering and blind spot modules log U0159 (case S2208000172). Customers see a blue screen in the camera views. The first step is to pull fuse F48 (10 A) for five seconds so the module restarts; software arrived through recall 56A. Stellantis adds that the scan tool shows the CVPAM as PAM. Without module B, camera views and parking aids drop out; driving is unaffected. Data errors from B are U0544.
c: Camera/park module hung by software, recovers after a power reset or update
Module B without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged or corroded
s: Blue or blank screen in surround, front or rear camera view
Parking aid unavailable message
U0159 stored in several other modules at the same time

U0244.t: Lost Communication With Running Board Control Module A
U0244.d: Power running boards fold out when a door opens and stow when doors close or the vehicle starts moving; Ford's running board control module (RBM) runs the motors. Ford documents U0244 directly: on 2027 Expedition and Navigator the boards intermittently refuse to move and the cluster shows a running board fault message; the driver seat module (DSM) holds C1008:15 or C1009:15 while other modules record U0208 and U0244. The cause is DSM software, and the DSM may not even answer a network test until the seat switch is pressed. Five minutes parked with doors shut restores operation for a while, and an over-the-air update was announced (SSM 55168). Older RBMs fall back from Auto to Off after a low-voltage event (SSM 50154). Boards may stay out or in. B is U0251, data errors from A U0545.
c: Software fault in the module hosting the running board function (Ford 2027: driver seat module)
Low or fully discharged battery that left the module offline
Damaged or corroded wiring and connectors exposed under the body
s: Power running board fault message in the cluster
Boards stay extended or retracted
Seat heating, cooling or memory affected at the same time (Ford 2027)

U0245.t: Lost Communication With Entertainment Control Module - Front
U0245.d: The front entertainment module is the head unit with radio, navigation and the central display. Mitsubishi uses U0245 for this unit and spells out the logic: in its workshop manuals the combination meter sets the code when, with ignition on, 10–16 V and an intact supply fuse, it receives nothing from the audio visual navigation unit for 2,500 ms; a 2019 manual has the camera ECU apply the same 2,500 ms limit to the multivision display. Several modules may therefore hold U0245 at once. Mitsubishi warns that a display audio software update for 2017–2018 Outlander, Outlander PHEV and Eclipse Cross leaves U0245 in several systems, which is erased afterwards (TSB-18-54-004). The driver loses radio, screen and anything shown on it. Rear units have U0196 and U0249; invalid data from the front unit are U0546.
c: Head unit rebooting or being updated, code left behind as history (erase afterwards)
Head unit without power or ground (fuse, connector behind the dash)
CAN wiring or connector between head unit and receiving module faulty
s: Radio and central display dark or frozen
Rear camera image or climate display on the screen missing
U0245 stored in several modules at once

U0246.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module E
U0246.d: Seat control module E belongs to the letters beyond driver and passenger units. Ford fills it with the front seat climate control module (SCME), which runs heating and the backrest and cushion fans of the front seats; its 2024 module list in a scan-tool release names SCME that way. On 2015–2016 Edge and 2016 Explorer weak backrest cooling was fixed by a new blower and, on Explorer, an as-built update of the SCME, after first checking the SCME for stored codes (TSB 16-0080). No maker document cites U0246 itself. A module that commands the seats, such as the body controller, the climate unit or the touchscreen module, would log it when SCME frames vanish. Heated or ventilated front seats then stop and their buttons do nothing. F is the rear climate unit (U0247); bad data from E are U0547.
c: Loose, pinched or corroded connector under the front seat
Climate seat module without power or ground (fuse)
Module replaced or updated without correct configuration
s: Front seat heating and ventilation inoperative
Seat climate buttons or touchscreen entries without response

U0247.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module F
U0247.d: In Ford's module naming, letter F stands for the rear seat climate control module (SCMF), the unit that heats and, where fitted, ventilates the second-row outboard seats; a 2024 scan-tool release lists it next to SCME for the front seats and SCMG/SCMH for the multi-contour seats. Ford's climate seat bulletins show how such a unit is serviced: stored codes are read in the module first, then blower or configuration are addressed (TSB 16-0080 for the front SCME). No public maker text uses U0247. It would be stored by the module passing rear seat requests, typically the body controller or rear climate panel, when SCMF frames are missing. Because the rear unit often sits under the second-row cushion, folding seats can strain its harness. Rear seat heating or cooling then stops. Front climate seats are U0246; implausible data from F are U0548.
c: Harness or connector strained by folding or sliding the second-row seat
Rear climate seat module without power or ground
Module internally faulty, for example after liquid spilled on the seat
s: Rear seat heating or ventilation inoperative
Rear seat climate buttons without response

U0248.t: Lost Communication With Remote Accessory Module
U0248.d: No manufacturer explains publicly what the remote accessory module does or when U0248 is set. The name suggests a body-side unit that switches accessories outside the main controllers. Separate codes exist for Ford's SYNC interface unit (APIM, U0253) and for a remote start module (U0254). For the 2011 Saab 9-5, GM explains how lost-communication codes arise in general: receivers check for expected signals, some serving as a sender's heartbeat; when one stops, they fall back to default values and record a lost-contact code for that sender. The same GM code list has no entry for U0248. Any listener would follow that scheme once this module falls silent. What the driver notices depends entirely on the accessory involved; driving is unaffected. Invalid data from it are U0549.
c: Module without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Retrofitted or removed accessory, module configured but not present
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged
s: Accessory function controlled by the module inoperative
Code stored in other modules without noticeable fault

U0249.t: Lost Communication With Entertainment Control Module - Rear B
U0249.d: Rear B is the second rear entertainment unit; GM applies the code to a concrete part. Its 2011 Saab 9-5 code list names U0249 as lost communication with the rear radio audio control module, the rear seat audio controls with their own headphone outputs. On 2013–2014 Buick Enclave, Chevrolet Traverse and GMC Acadia the radio and the HVAC module stored U0249 within a long list of U codes when the side object sensor harness at the right rear rubbed through on the muffler and disturbed the LAN wiring; the cure was repairing and rerouting that harness (PI1202). The case shows that one chafed lead can silence modules far from the damage. Without unit B, rear audio controls, headphone sound or the second rear screen stop. Rear unit A is U0196, invalid data from B U054A.
c: Chafed or burnt network wiring elsewhere in the vehicle (GM: harness on muffler)
Rear unit without power or ground
Loose or corroded connector at the rear unit
s: Rear audio controls or headphone outputs dead
Second rear screen without picture
Many U codes across modules, radio may switch off while driving

U024A.t: Lost Communication With Interior Lighting Control Module A
U024A.d: Interior lighting control module A switches and dims cabin lights such as dome, footwell and ambient strips. In newer cars these are often small LIN nodes under a master, usually the body controller. A Microchip demo board for LIN ambient light illustrates the traffic: the master sends colour and brightness per zone and polls a status frame back. GM's Saab 9-5 documentation states that on a LIN subsystem the primary module records a lost-contact code for any node that stops answering, and that is the route by which U024A is normally stored. No manufacturer documents U024A publicly, so timeouts are unknown. Typical findings are a loose plug at a roof or door light unit or a LIN line chafed in the headliner. Cabin lights stay dark or on, and ambient colours freeze. Module B is U02BF; corrupt data from A give U054B.
c: Loose or corroded plug at a roof, door or footwell light unit
LIN line chafed or pinched in headliner, door or trim
Lighting module without power or ground
s: Interior lights do not come on or stay on
Ambient lighting colour or brightness cannot be changed

U024B.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module G
U024B.d: Ford assigns seat control module G to the driver's multi-contour seat (SCMG), which runs massage and lumbar adjustment. Two Ford bulletins name U024B. TSB 19-2293, later 19-2390, covers multi-contour seats from the 2013 MKZ to 2019 F-150, Explorer, Expedition and Navigator: massage and lumbar respond only now and then from the switch or touchscreen, sometimes with B1471, U024B or U024C, because terminals fret in the SCMG and SCMH connectors; new pigtails and a rerouted harness fix it. SSM 53226 adds that on 2020–2021 F-Super Duty an SCMG software update by FDRS can misconfigure the module so the SYNC module (APIM) stores U024B; running the SCMG configuration app clears it. Expect driver massage and lumbar to drop out. The passenger unit H is U024C; invalid data from G are U054C.
c: Fretting corrosion in the SCMG connector terminals under the seat
Module misconfigured after a software update (configuration app not run)
Seat harness strained by seat travel or poor routing
s: Driver seat massage and lumbar inoperative or intermittent
Seat settings on the SYNC screen without response
B1471 stored alongside

U024C.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module H
U024C.d: Seat control module H is Ford's passenger multi-contour seat module (SCMH), the mirror of the driver unit G. It shares the fretting connector problem of TSB 19-2293: on the listed Ford and Lincoln vehicles passenger massage and lumbar act up, sometimes with U024C stored, and the repair replaces the SCMH connector and reroutes the harness. In SSM 53226 the APIM of 2020–2021 F-Super Duty sets U024C when the SCMH was misconfigured during an FDRS update, and Ford wants the SCMH configuration app run after the SCMG one. A related Lincoln case shows the limit of the code: on 2022 Explorer and Aviator intermittent passenger massage came from SCMG/SCMH configuration with no code at all (SSM 50591). So a missing U024C does not clear the module. Passenger massage or lumbar then fail. Driver unit G is U024B; data errors from H are U054D.
c: Fretting corrosion in the SCMH connector terminals
SCMH misconfigured after a software update
Passenger seat harness strained by seat movement
s: Passenger seat massage or lumbar inoperative or intermittent
Passenger seat functions unavailable on the SYNC screen

U024D.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module J
U024D.d: Ford uses seat control module J (SCMJ), also called power fold seat module (PFSM), for the electrically folding third row. On 2025 Expedition and Navigator a software fault made the seats ignore the 3L, Both and 3R buttons; a relearn with the engine running and the liftgate open, holding Both for one minute and five seconds more after the seats stop, restores them until an update arrives (SSM 53681). SSM 54613 reports uneven upright seats after an obstruction reset on 2025–2026 models, cured by a second reset. A 2024 scan-tool release also lists SCM-J for several Ford models. No bulletin cites U024D. The code stands for an SCMJ that has gone silent on the bus, so supply, ground and the harness that flexes with the seat come before software. Third-row folding stops. Data errors from J are U054E.
c: Harness or connector damaged where it flexes with the folding seat
Fold seat module without power or ground (fuse)
Module software locked up, needs relearn or update
s: Third-row power fold buttons without effect
Seats stop half-way or stand misaligned

U024E.t: Lost Communication With Side Obstacle Detection Control Module C
U024E.d: Side obstacle detection modules are radar units that watch the blind spots and crossing traffic. Left and right units have their own codes, U0232 and U0233; letters C and D cover extra units. Ford names all four in SSM 51903 and its successors 53018 and 53569: SODL, SODR, SODCMC and SODCMD on 2021–2025 Ford and Lincoln models. After a module swap these units store U2100 when left unconfigured and U3002 when carrying another vehicle's VIN, and the VIN Write application in FDRS fixes it. U024E itself is in no public maker text; it is set by a module that consumes radar data, for example the cruise control or gateway module, when unit C stops sending. Bumper damage, a wet connector or a wrong replacement are likely triggers. Blind spot and cross-traffic alerts switch off with a message. D is U024F; invalid data from C are U054F.
c: Radar connector or harness in the bumper damaged, wet or corroded
Replacement or used module not configured for the vehicle
Radar module without power or ground
s: Blind spot system unavailable message
Blind spot and cross-traffic alerts missing

U024F.t: Lost Communication With Side Obstacle Detection Control Module D
U024F.d: Module D is the fourth side radar in Ford's scheme beside SODL, SODR and SODCMC. Ford's bulletins list SODCMD among units that log U2100 or U3002 after replacement on 2021–2025 models; SSM 53569 adds that a VIN mismatch can also follow swapping a tail lamp from another car, and that radar modules cannot move between vehicles without programming. Which corner D covers is not published. No maker document uses U024F. It is set by a receiving module once D's frames stay absent. Wiring at the rear deserves a look first: GM found on 2013–2014 Enclave, Traverse and Acadia that the side object sensor harness rubbing on the muffler disturbed the whole LAN and set many U codes (PI1202). The driver sees a side assist warning and the affected zone unwatched. C is U024E; corrupt data from D are U0550.
c: Rear radar harness chafed or heat-damaged near exhaust or bumper
Module or tail lamp from another vehicle fitted without programming
Radar module without power or ground
s: Side assist or blind spot warning message
One monitoring zone without alerts

U0250.t: Lost Communication With Impact Classification System Module
U0250.d: Within the airbag system, an impact classification module sorts a collision by type and force, so that airbags and belt pretensioners fire in the right combination and stage. U0250 is logged when its messages no longer reach the network, most plausibly by the restraint control module. No manufacturer publishes a description, timeout or fault type for this code. Patent US7832762 on crash sensing over a vehicle bus explains why such a link is monitored at all: sensors and the occupant protection controller exchange their data as messages, so a missing node removes input from the deployment decision. Expect the airbag warning lamp to light and the restraint system to run without that information until the fault is gone. Work on it belongs in a workshop. Restraint module loss is U0151; invalid data from this unit are U0551.
c: Loose or corroded connector or damaged harness to the module, often after body repair
Module damaged in a collision or not set up after replacement
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code also stored in the restraint control module

U0251.t: Lost Communication With Running Board Control Module B
U0251.d: Letter B denotes a second running board controller, which only exists where each side has its own unit. Ford's documented power running boards rely on a single running board control module (RBM): its 2015–2022 bulletins describe one RBM that logs U3003:16 and turns the feature from Auto to Off after a low or flat battery (SSM 50154) and one whose software flips the setting on F-Super Duty (SSM 52411). No manufacturer publishes a vehicle that uses U0251. Under the J2012 scheme, a body controller or gateway would set it once frames from unit B stop. Because such units live under the body near the board motors, water, road salt and stone damage at plugs and wiring are the main suspects. The driver finds the board on one side stuck in or out. Unit A is U0244; invalid data from B are U0552.
c: Water or salt corrosion at underbody connectors and wiring
Low or flat battery that left the module offline
s: Running board on one side does not deploy or retract
Running board fault message in the cluster

U0252.t: Lost Communication With Lighting Control Module - Rear B
U0252.d: Module B for rear lighting is the second unit driving lamps at the back end, and in practice it is often the trailer electronics. GM's code list for the 2011 Saab 9-5 assigns U0252 to the trailer interface control module. Ford does the same: on 2021-2023 F-150, 2022-2024 F-150 Lightning, Expedition, Navigator and the 2024 Ranger, the body control module, cluster or steering module records U0252, often with U0137, when the trailer module (TRM) drops off CAN; a five-minute power-down and new TRM software cured it (SSM 53236). Super Duty trucks of 2023-2025 showed the same pair when ground point G201 was not torqued correctly (SSM 53980), and a BCM self-test may leave a harmless U0252:87 history entry (SSM 51578). Trailer lamps or trailer brake messages fail; no MIL.
c: Trailer or rear lighting module stuck off the bus, software needs reset or update (Ford TRM)
Loose or badly tightened body ground shared with the module (Ford G201)
Damaged or corroded harness and connectors at the rear or tow bar area
Stored history entry from a module self-test without a real fault
s: Trailer brake module fault or trailer warning in the cluster
Trailer lamps or rear lighting functions inoperative
Further U codes such as U0137 in body control module, cluster or steering module

U0253.t: Lost Communication With Accessory Protocol Interface Module
U0253.d: The accessory protocol interface module is Ford's SYNC computer (APIM), which connects touchscreen, phone and voice functions with the vehicle network. Other modules log U0253 when its frames stop arriving, and Ford bulletins show several listeners: the headlamp module of the 2017 Lincoln MKZ after a remote start, cured by new HCM software (SSM 46508); the FCIM switch panel of 2015-2017 F-150 trucks, which froze under heavy CAN load (SSM 46902); and the ABS module of the 2021 F-150 with U0253:00, an informational entry without symptoms that new ABS software removed (SSM 50290, 51329). Mach-E owners (2021-2023) saw the drive mode reset to normal while driving because of APIM software, and the ABS sometimes held U0253 as well (TSB 24-2012). Settings sent from the screen may be lost.
c: APIM or receiving-module software fault, fixed by reprogramming or over-the-air update
APIM without power or ground (fuse, connector behind the center display)
Network overload or a module locking up after remote start or battery work
Internal failure of the SYNC module
s: Center screen dark, frozen or rebooting
Drive mode or settings fall back to default, message Drive Mode Not Available
Code stored in ABS, headlamp or switch module without noticeable fault

U0254.t: Lost Communication With Remote Start Module
U0254.d: A remote start module runs the engine from a key fob or app so the cabin can be heated or cooled before departure. GM's list for the 2011 Saab 9-5 treats it as a network node of its own under U0254. Subaru documents the code for 2020 Legacy and Outback models with the genuine accessory Remote Engine Starter: the central gateway stored U0254 during an all-systems check because of a software interface mismatch between gateway and starter, although the accessory worked normally. The bulletin allows ignoring the code on its own, and later replacement starter units carry revised U0254 logic (15-258-19, revised as 15-258-19R). With a real fault the starter is unpowered, unplugged or defective, so remote start fails while normal driving is unaffected. Corrupt frames from it are U0555.
c: Software interface mismatch between gateway and accessory starter (Subaru), no real fault
Poor installation, loose connector or missing supply of an accessory or aftermarket starter
Starter removed or disconnected while the vehicle configuration still expects it
Internal failure of the remote start module
s: Remote start does not work or stops after a short time
Code found only during a full system scan, no other complaint

U0255.t: Lost Communication With Front Display Interface Module
U0255.d: The front display interface module is the central screen in the dashboard. Ford calls it FDIM; in the U-code table of the 2011 Saab 9-5, a GM design, the same node is the info display module with U0255. GM also shows the code inside a wider network failure: on 2017 Silverado, Sierra, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and Escalade, the serial data gateway (SDGM) could lock up while still powered, or its X1/X2 terminals lost tension, and U0255 then appeared among many U codes together with dead gauges, a blank radio display or even no crank. The first step was pulling the gateway fuse for one minute, with gateway software to follow (PIT5586G). So when U0255 shows up with a dozen siblings, the gateway or a shared branch is the suspect, not the screen. A dead display alone points to its own supply. Combined units use U0257.
c: Gateway module locked up or its connector terminals loose, many U codes at once (GM SDGM)
Display without power or ground (fuse, connector behind the screen)
Damaged bus wiring to the display after dashboard work
Internal failure of the display module
s: Central screen black or frozen
Audio, climate or vehicle settings cannot be shown or changed
With gateway faults also dead gauges, warning messages or no crank

U0256.t: Lost Communication With Front Controls Interface Module A
U0256.d: Module A of the front controls interface collects radio and climate key presses in the middle of the dash and passes them to the network. At Ford this is the FCIM; for the 2011 Saab 9-5 GM labels U0256 as the infotainment faceplate control module. Ford cites the code directly: on 2023 Super Duty trucks a wrong measurement sequence during the body control module self-test could leave U0256:87 and several other codes in history status; if the BCM has no other codes, the MIL is off and the truck drives normally, they are to be ignored (SSM 51578). That the panel itself can go silent is shown by 2015-2017 F-150 trucks, where heavy CAN traffic froze the FCIM so A/C, radio and window switch control failed until a battery reset (SSM 46902). A real loss disables its keys; panel B is U025D.
c: Panel locked up by heavy network traffic, cleared by battery reset or new software
History entry left by a body controller self-test without a real fault (Ford :87)
Loose connector or missing supply at the panel after dashboard work
Internal failure of the control panel
s: Radio and climate keys on the center panel without function
Several warning lamps or messages at once, intermittent operation
Code only as history entry in the body controller, no complaint

U0257.t: Lost Communication With Front Controls/Display Interface Module
U0257.d: Some vehicles combine keys and screen in a single front controls/display interface module. Ford calls such a unit FCDIM, for example with the small audio display on the Escape (2013-2016) and the 2016 Transit Connect, Transit and Focus (SSM 47234), while the 2011 Saab 9-5 reserves U0257 for a unit merging info display and faceplate. Audi documents the code itself for the 2026 Q3: the panoramic display (KX2) ignored touches on the central MMI screen, and U025700 was active in information electronics control unit 1 (address 005F). The display's own software was to blame; dealers replace the display, while improved software follows from model year 2027 (TSB 2082126/1). A silent unit leaves both its keys and its screen without function; separate units use U0255 and U0256.
c: Software fault in the combined display unit (Audi panoramic display)
Unit without power or ground, or connector not fully seated after dashboard work
Internal failure of the combined controls/display unit
Fault on the infotainment bus branch shared with other units
s: Screen does not respond to touch or stays dark
Radio preset or menu keys without function or erratic

U0258.d: Despite its name this unit has nothing to do with the audio tuner: Ford's radio transceiver module (RTM) handles the wireless link to keys and remote accessories. On the 2021-2022 Bronco Sport, Ford traced No Key Detected messages to blocked key frequencies or a flat key battery and advised laying the key in the forward console tray, the backup position close to the RTM (SSM 50341); RTMs in recent F-150 and Super Duty trucks work on a changed frequency, so only one accessory keypad part fits (SSM 54546). No manufacturer documents U0258 itself publicly, nor a timeout. A receiver such as the body control module would set it when RTM messages stop on the bus. Keyless entry, key detection at start-up or remote functions may then fail; corrupt RTM data are U0559, a remote start module is U0254.
c: Transceiver without power or ground, or loose connector
Open or shorted data line between transceiver and its master module
Transceiver software or configuration not matching after replacement
Internal failure of the radio transceiver
s: No Key Detected or key not recognized at start-up
Keyless entry, remote locking or keypad without function

U0259.t: Lost Communication With Special Purpose Vehicle Control Module A
U0259.d: A special purpose vehicle control module is extra electronics for converted vehicles such as police cars, ambulances or work trucks. GM sells one from 2024 as Universal Vehicle Module (option KGU) and calls it special purpose vehicle control module for Silverado and Sierra pickups and the Tahoe and Blazer EV police vehicles. It reads switches and serial data, drives configurable outputs, offers a subset of J1939 data to upfitter equipment, and retrofitting it requires BCM and ELM reprogramming (PIT6315, Upfitter bulletin 203-b). Deutz's EMR engine controller for off-highway machines lists U0259-00 as a timeout of its tractor-trailer bridge. When slot A stops sending, the conversion functions it controls drop out, while the base vehicle normally drives on. Slots B to D are U025A to U025C, invalid data U055A.
c: Add-on controller without power or ground from the body builder's circuits
Damaged or wrongly spliced bus wiring from the conversion
Retrofit without the required vehicle configuration and module programming
Internal failure of the special purpose controller
s: Light bar, siren or other conversion functions inoperative or stuck
Upfitter switches or configurable inputs without effect

U025A.t: Lost Communication With Special Purpose Vehicle Control Module B
U025A.d: U025A concerns the second slot for special purpose controllers. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Why more than one slot exists becomes clear from an Audi patent: it describes a configurable control module for police cars, fire engines, taxis or vehicles for disabled occupants, linked through CAN, LIN or other interfaces, that turns a standard car into a commercial vehicle by adding function units. A conversion may thus carry several such boxes, for example one for the light bar and one for a tail lift. GM's 2024 Universal Vehicle Module shows the typical layout of one such unit. A listening module sets U025A when frames from unit B stop; which module listens and how long it waits is not published. Start at the body builder's wiring and fuses. Driving is normally not affected; U055B covers corrupt data.
c: Second add-on unit unpowered, often via a switched or separately fused upfit circuit
Faulty splice or connector where the conversion joins the vehicle bus
Unit removed or replaced while the vehicle still expects it
s: Functions of the second conversion unit inoperative
Warning or message from the conversion control panel

U025B.t: Lost Communication With Special Purpose Vehicle Control Module C
U025B.d: With U025B a module on the bus reports that controller C (third slot of four) has gone quiet. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's body builder bulletin for its 2023 Super Duty shows a pitfall that applies to all slots: the Upfitter Integration System module only cooperates with the programming tool when it, the SYNC module and the body control module carry matching software, and trucks built before 12 June 2023 need a reflash first. A partly updated set can therefore leave an add-on unit unanswered. The Audi patent on configurable conversion modules adds that such units may hang on CAN, LIN or other links, so the missing node is not always on the main bus. Check software levels and the conversion paperwork before replacing hardware. Base vehicle functions normally remain; U055C means corrupt data.
c: Software of vehicle modules and add-on unit not at matching levels
Controller C without power or ground from the upfit circuits
Fault on the sub-bus or link through which the unit is attached
s: Conversion functions of unit C inoperative
Programming or configuration tool cannot reach the unit

U025C.t: Lost Communication With Special Purpose Vehicle Control Module D
U025C.d: U025C is the last of the four lost-communication codes for special purpose controllers and covers unit D. No manufacturer documents it publicly, and none of the published systems names more than one such controller. GM's Universal Vehicle Module passes a subset of J1939 data to third-party devices; those devices read a separate output and are not members of the vehicle network, so their failure would not set a U025x code. Ford's Upfitter Integration System likewise feeds body equipment one way through J1939. A code for slot D therefore suggests a fourth add-on unit that sits directly on the vehicle bus, or a vehicle configuration that expects one. Verify first whether such a unit is fitted at all, then check its supply and bus connection. Driving is normally unaffected; corrupt data from D are U055D.
c: Vehicle configuration lists a fourth add-on unit that is not fitted or was removed
Unit D without power, ground or bus connection
s: Functions of the fourth conversion unit inoperative
Code stored without any noticeable complaint

U025D.t: Lost Communication With Front Controls Interface Module B
U025D.d: Front controls interface module B is a second switch panel at the front where the controls are split over two units. Ford uses this name (FCIMB): on 2023 Transit vans having SYNC 3 Lite and parking aid at the rear only, the parking aid disable switch sits in that panel, and vans built between 15 March and 2 June 2023 ignored it, since the park aid module carried a wrong configuration (SSM 51837). Mercedes fills the code differently: in its 8G-DCT transmission controller (724.1, models 118, 177 and 247) U025D00 means faulty communication with the head unit (LI27.00-P-077141). The module behind U025D therefore depends on the maker, and the description in the scan tool decides. A real loss disables the keys on the second panel or, at Mercedes, data from the head unit; panel A is U0256, corrupt data from B are U055E.
c: Second panel without power or ground, or connector loose after dashboard work
Head unit not on the bus where the maker maps U025D to it (Mercedes)
Wrong configuration of the panel or of the module that uses its switches
Internal failure of the second control panel
s: Switches on the second front panel without function
Functions that rely on head unit data unavailable (Mercedes)

U025E.t: Lost Communication With Electronic Brake Booster Control Module A
U025E.d: Instead of a vacuum servo, an electronic brake booster uses a pedal travel sensor and an electric motor for the assist, which also lets regenerative braking be blended in, as in Bosch's iBooster. Mitsubishi documents U025E-00 in the engine control module of the Outlander PHEV from 2023, where it means lost contact with the EBA, the electric driven intelligent brake unit. With the power switch on and 10 to 16.5 V, no brake unit signals for 4 s set the code; it is stored when the fault recurs after the next start and belongs to the CAN monitor of the OBD drive cycle, which covers faults that light the check engine lamp. PHEV-ECU and ABS unit log their own timeouts. Ford shows the knock-on effect: a supply interruption at its booster lit the ABS and stability lamps (SSM 51374). Unit B is U025F.
c: Damaged CAN wiring or connector between engine or brake controllers and the booster unit
Fault in the booster's power supply (high-current fuse, ground, 12 V battery)
Internal failure of the electric brake unit
Failure of the receiving engine control module
s: Check engine lamp after repeated detection (Mitsubishi)
Brake, ABS or stability warning lamps on
Harder brake pedal or reduced regenerative braking

U025F.t: Lost Communication With Electronic Brake Booster Control Module B
U025F.d: U025F concerns a second electronic brake booster control unit, B. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none states which physical unit would carry the letter. Bosch describes where two units make sense: in automated vehicles its integrated power brake, which merges boosting and stability control in one unit, is backed by a separate redundant brake unit, and the iBooster together with ESP supplies the redundancy such cars require. Ford's booster (Escape, Explorer, Bronco Sport, Aviator and Corsair of 2020-2021) shows that a power interruption at that unit lights the ABS and stability lamps through a code in the ABS module (SSM 51374). If unit B goes silent, expect brake or driver-assist warnings and the loss of the backup path, which can switch off automated driving. Unit A is U025E.
c: Second brake unit without power or ground (separate fuse or supply path)
Damaged bus wiring or connector to the redundant unit
Internal failure of brake unit B
s: Brake system or driver-assist warning in the cluster
Automated or assisted driving functions unavailable

U0260.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Switch Module A
U0260.d: Many power seat switches now contain electronics that scan the keys and report the result over a LIN or multiplex link rather than carrying motor current. A Lear patent describes a seat motor assembly with integrated electronics that talks to an external switch over a one- or two-wire multiplex link. Mercedes shows such a switch failing for series 206 to 297, for example C-, E- and S-Class, GLC and EQS: the door-mounted switch group for seat adjustment (front left: SSE-VL) could remain in sleep mode after a software error, so the seat did not move although the quick test stored no fault; unplugging the switch resets it, new switch software prevents a repeat (LI82.00-P-080029). No manufacturer documents U0260 publicly. When switch module A stops sending, its seat cannot be adjusted from it; switch B is U0261.
c: Switch module software stuck in sleep mode, reset by unplugging and fixed by update
Loose or corroded connector or broken wire at the switch in the door or seat trim
LIN line to the seat module shorted or open
Internal failure of the switch module
s: Seat cannot be adjusted with its switch
Memory, lumbar or massage keys on that switch without function

U0261.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Switch Module B
U0261.d: Seat control switch module B is a further switch unit with its own electronics, serving another seat or seat row; which position the letter stands for is not published. Lincoln bulletins show how closely switch and seat module interact: power seats in the second row of the 2025 Navigator did not slide when the switch was pressed, the rear seat modules SCMK/SCML held B167F:11, and the cure was to run their configuration routines in the scan tool (SSM 54226); on 2022 Aviators missing lumbar settings on the screen were traced to seat module software or a wrong seat switch part level (SSM 51056). So a switch complaint may be a seat module setup issue. No manufacturer documents U0261 publicly. Usually the seat module notices when switch B stops reporting, and that seat then ignores its keys. Switch A is U0260, C and D are U0271 and U0272.
c: Seat module configuration or software not matching the switch (Lincoln SCMK/SCML)
Loose connector or chafed wire under the seat or in the trim of the second switch
Wrong part level of the seat switch after production or replacement
Internal failure of switch module B
s: Passenger or rear seat does not move with its switch
Seat settings missing in the center display

U0262.t: Lost Communication With Audio Amplifier B
U0262.d: Large sound systems may use a second external amplifier, audio amplifier B. Such amplifiers take part in network traffic: a patent on modular add-on sound systems explains that the factory amplifier decodes gain commands that the head unit sends over the CAN bus, and that a replacement amplifier must therefore understand the maker's bus format, such as GMLAN. No manufacturer documents U0262 publicly or says which speakers B drives. The single-amplifier case shows typical causes: on the 2023 Mazda CX-50, static or silence with U0186:08 (amplifier unreachable) and U2145:08 came from rear harness connectors 0920-114 and 0920-115D that were not locked (SA-058-22). For B, a receiver such as the head unit sets the code once its frames stop. The speakers fed by B fall silent; U0563 means corrupt data.
c: Amplifier connector not locked or pushed back, often in the rear harness
Amplifier B without power or ground (own fuse, switched supply)
Aftermarket audio installation that removed or bypassed the second amplifier
s: Some speakers silent while others still play
Static, crackling or sound dropping out

U0263.t: Lost Communication With Speech Recognition Module
U0263.d: A speech recognition module turns spoken commands into actions for phone, audio or navigation. Some makers place it in a separate box: FCA built Uconnect Voice Command into its hands-free unit (HFM) of 2012-2017 Journey, Charger and 300. Old software could leave it stuck while loading, unresponsive and off the bus, or deaf to the voice key on the steering wheel, and a reflash cured it (08-055-17 REV. A). FCA records such a silent unit as U0197, the telephone module code, not as U0263. GM shows that a voice complaint need not lie in the recognition unit: on the 2014 Cadillac ATS the cluster displayed Unable to Start Speech Recognition although voice control worked, fixed by cluster software (PIC6008C). No manufacturer documents U0263 publicly. Voice commands are then ignored; U0564 means corrupt data.
c: Voice module software hangs during start-up, fixed by reflash
Voice module without power or ground, or connector loose
Fault message created by cluster or head unit software although the module works
Internal failure of the speech recognition module
s: No reaction to the voice button on the steering wheel
Message that speech recognition cannot be started
Hands-free phone functions unavailable where combined in one module

U0264.t: Lost Communication With Camera Module - Rear
U0264.d: The rear camera module supplies the reversing picture; whichever unit expects its messages stores U0264 when they stop, depending on the brand the radio, the body controller, the cluster or a central vision module. FCA uses it widely: a 2021 Ram 1500 logged it in the radio after connector XY552A worked loose once the tailgate had been off (S2108000050), and 2019–2020 Ram heavy-duty trucks with surround view set it in the CVPM next to B217A-92. On a 2019 Mazda3 a new rear camera plus old CMU software gave U0264:00 and a black center screen, so the CMU is updated first (09-021/19). Land Rover pointed it at the camera control module of its five-camera system (LTB00551NAS1); for the Transit, Ford calls a U0264 in a newly fitted BCM ignorable (SSM 47123). The reversing view is lost, driving is not.
c: Camera connector in tailgate or liftgate loose or not fully seated, often after body work
Pinched or chafed wire in the liftgate, camera fuse blown
New camera paired with outdated software in the display or vision module
Rear camera or camera control module internally faulty
s: Black or blank screen when reverse is selected
Camera system fault message, surround view button greyed out
Code stored in radio, cluster or body controller, sometimes with blind spot faults

U0265.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor A
U0265.d: GM gives sensor A a clear identity: its bulletins describe U0265 as lost contact with the front view camera on the windshield (B174W), the camera for forward collision alert and steering assistance. On 2020 Cadillac CT4 and CT5 with forward collision alert that camera could reset itself; U0265 then came with U0566, U1962 and P25A2, a brake module request that can switch on the MIL, plus Service Driver Assist and Steering Assist Reduced messages. Reprogramming the camera was the cure, and only a frequent, easily repeated set of all three codes justified a new one (N202305180, PIC6404). On the 2024 Corvette the cluster could log U0265 because of camera software, with an amber braking-assist lamp that went out again; GM says reprogram and relearn, do not replace (25-NA-050). U0265 alone sets no MIL.
c: Windshield camera resets or drops off the bus because of its software
Camera hardware fault when the loss recurs often and is easy to repeat
Connector or supply at the camera mount disturbed, e.g. after windshield work
Fault on the shared bus that silences several sensors at once
s: Service Driver Assist or front camera message, lane and collision functions unavailable
Steering assist reduced message on some models
Emergency braking lamp briefly amber, then normal again

U0266.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor B
U0266.d: Image processing sensor B has a documented owner at FCA, which reads U0266-00 as lost communication with the left camera of its 360-degree surround view. The central vision processing module (CVPM) takes each camera on its own colour-coded coaxial plug. On a 2022 Ram 1500 the driver mirror image stayed dark while every other camera worked, along with B23C6-92 and B23C6-1C; the guide plugs the tan driver lead into the brown passenger socket of the CVPM to separate camera from wiring, and the culprit was the door harness (S2208000115). On a 2019 Ram 1500 the left part of the top view dropped out now and then after a door repair; connector i6624C behind the door trim or XY451A at the kick panel had to be secured (S2108000266). Only the left image is missing, no MIL.
c: Coaxial camera lead in the driver door harness damaged or unplugged
Door or kick panel connector not secured after door repair
Camera plug loose at the central vision processing module
s: Left side of the surround or top view black, other views normal
Fault appears intermittently, often after door work
Left camera performance code stored as well

U0267.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor C
U0267.d: No vehicle maker documents U0267 in public service material, so the camera behind letter C remains unknown, and letters are assigned differently from brand to brand. What can break is clear from the hardware. Cameras usually send their data over a coaxial or twisted-pair serial link, and the receiving deserializer reports a lock status for each port; Texas Instruments' DS90UB954 even allows configuration of a camera only while its link is locked. A Chalmers thesis built on a parking camera rig ranks a cut or shorted cable and the loss of link lock after too many bit errors as the critical faults. Either one leaves sensor C silent for the module that polls it. The function fed by sensor C stops; the MIL stays off.
c: Camera link cable open or shorted, connector corroded
Link loses lock due to bit errors from a degraded cable or interference
Sensor C without supply, for example power over the coaxial line missing
s: One camera view or camera-based assistant unavailable
Service message for the camera or driver assistance

U0268.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor D
U0268.d: GM files U0268 among the codes of its object detection bus, a separate network that links the active safety module with the radars and the front camera on Cadillac Escalades of model years 2015–2020 equipped with driver assistance. Which sensor letter D denotes is not stated in the bulletins. The best documented cause is mechanical: the front fascia harness can rub through where the right side of the bumper bar ends and blow fuses F10DL, F19DR, F43UA or F46DR, so front parking, turn, daytime and cornering lamps fail while U0268 is stored along with U0265, U0269, U026A–U026C and U0075. GM has the fascia removed, the wiring repaired, and the harness rerouted behind the bar and tied to the fascia (PIT5487B, PIT5487E). Surround view, park assist and adaptive cruise report service messages; no MIL.
c: Front fascia harness chafed at the right bumper bar, fuses blown
Connector of sensor D loose or damaged after front-end repairs
Short or open on the object detection bus
s: Service messages for surround camera, park assist and adaptive cruise
Front parking, turn, daytime or cornering lamps dead, turn signal flashes fast
Several radar and camera U-codes stored at once

U0269.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor E
U0269.d: U0269 is a further member of GM's object detection group, kept by the active safety module first on 2015 Escalades with the Y66 driver assist package and, after a 2017 update, on many 2013–2018 Buick, Cadillac and Chevrolet models; GM does not publish which sensor letter E names. Its known trap is in the workshop: that bus uses its own circuits 3813 and 3811, which run to terminal 3 and terminal 11 of the DLC, which older scan tools seldom used. A worn MDI interface or cable on those pins can therefore produce a false U0269 and block any contact with the radars and front camera. GM's check is to try the same tool on a fault-free Y66 Escalade or with the EL-47955-1 loopback adapter before suspecting the sensor, (PIT5441B, PIT5441C). A genuine loss switches off the assistant that relies on sensor E.
c: Defective scan tool interface or cable on the object detection pins, false code
Object detection bus wiring damaged, for example in the front fascia
Sensor E without power or ground
s: Scan tool cannot reach radars or front camera, several U-codes at once
Service Active Safety, Service Driver Assist or lane departure message
Code present only while a particular tester is connected

U026A.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor F
U026A.d: At GM letter F belongs to the frontview camera module (K109, later B174W) on the windshield, which serves forward collision alert, IntelliBeam and the lane departure and lane keeping functions. On 2016–2017 Chevrolet, GMC and Cadillac models such as Malibu, Silverado, Tahoe and Escalade, early camera software made the cluster or body module store a history U026A or U023A while the Service Front Camera message came and went; later software could hang the camera at power-down, keep it warm and drain the battery within 30 days. GM prescribes reprogramming and no new part (16-NA-389, PIT5482A). On 2022–2023 XT5, XT6, Equinox, Acadia and Terrain, camera pins that are pushed back or absent can set U026A, and then the camera is replaced (PIT6046). Lane and collision warnings drop out; no MIL.
c: Camera software sets false history codes or locks up, cured by reprogramming
Pushed-in or missing terminals in the camera connector
Supply or bus wiring to the windshield camera interrupted
s: Intermittent Service Front Camera message
Lane departure warning, lane keep assist, collision alert or automatic high beam inoperative
Weak battery after standing for days, camera warm with ignition off

U026B.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor G
U026B.d: Letter G, too, is visible only through GM: U026B appears in the active safety controller of Escalades from 2015 fitted with the Y66 assistance package, always grouped with U0265, U0268, U0269, U026A, U026C and U0075, and GM does not say which radar or camera G is. The grouping is itself the diagnostic hint. U0075 means that an entire communication bus has gone off, so if it shows up with several sensor codes, a shared cause such as supply, a short on the bus or harness damage is far more likely than a faulty sensor G. A lone U026B without its neighbours instead points to that module, its plug or its own feed. The earliest bulletins of 2015 and 2016 already list exactly this set (PIT5441, PIT5487A). The assistant using sensor G stays off; no MIL.
c: Common cause on the object detection bus or its supply when several codes appear
Plug or fuse of sensor G when the code appears alone
Faulty scan tool cable producing false codes
s: Driver assistance or object detection service message
Code alone or together with U0075 and other sensor codes

U026C.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor H
U026C.d: U026C rounds off the GM object detection group reported by the Escalade's active safety module; GM leaves open which sensor letter H stands for. The PIT5487 series, revised from 2016 up to version F in 2020 for model years 2015–2020, shows how the code turns up next to lighting faults. Apart from camera, park assist, adaptive cruise and driver assist messages, the turn signals may flash fast and lamp body codes such as B2575 or B2605 can join, because one chafed bumper harness feeds both lamps and sensors. Such a mix of lighting and sensor faults at the front corner is the cue to inspect that harness before replacing any module. Assistance that uses sensor H stays unavailable until communication returns; no MIL.
c: Chafed bumper harness supplying both lamps and sensors
Shared fuse blown by a short in the front wiring
Connector of sensor H loose or corroded
s: Turn signal flashes fast, front lamps partly dead
Lamp body codes stored together with sensor U-codes
Service Driver Assist or surround camera message

U026D.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor I
U026D.d: No manufacturer documents U026D publicly, and the camera filed under letter I is unknown. Among the image sensors that now sit on the bus as modules of their own is the driver-facing camera: Ford runs a driver status monitor camera module (CMR) on the 2021 Mustang Mach-E and later on F-150, Expedition, Navigator and Corsair. Ford's notes show that such a module reports a blocked view itself, with B115E:97, B15E1:97 or B15E2:97 when the steering wheel, add-on devices or dust hide the lens; centring the wheel, clearing and running the CMR self-test settles it (SSM 50385, SSM 51776). A blocked lens is therefore not a lost connection. For any camera, the vehicle's own service data tell whether it uses U026D; the dependent function goes offline, no MIL.
c: Wiring or connector to sensor I interrupted
Sensor I without supply or ground
Sensor I not responding because of software or configuration
s: Camera-based function unavailable with a service message
Sensor not reachable in the module scan

U026E.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor J
U026E.d: U026E is not documented publicly by any manufacturer, so it is not known which camera letter J denotes. Exposed outside cameras show where such links are vulnerable. Prevost fits a side camera rear view system, eMirror, to H3-45 coaches from model year 2019 and to its X3 series. Its instructions for re-aiming these mirror-replacing cameras call for new single-use rubber washers on reassembly so the cover mount stays watertight (MI20-13, MI20-13A). Water in an exposed camera housing or its plug is a typical start of corrosion, intermittent contact and finally a silent sensor. Wherever sensor J sits, its loss blanks only the view or function it serves; the engine and its emissions are not involved, and no MIL is expected.
c: Water in an exposed camera housing or plug, corroded contacts
Camera lead damaged at a hinge, mirror arm or body passage
s: One camera image black or frozen
Fault more frequent in rain or after washing

U026F.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor K
U026F.d: Neither U026F nor the meaning of letter K appears in published manufacturer material. Some image sources are optional or arrive with towing equipment, and that matters before diagnosing a silent camera. GM ties the turn signal activated camera view of 2025–2026 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon, Silverado EV and Sierra EV to option code TRG, the trailer camera provisions. Without that option the feature does not exist at all; with it, a view that failed to appear without a trailer attached was put right by radio software (PIT6366, PIT6366A). So confirm first that the vehicle is built and configured for an extra camera. A genuine loss of sensor K removes only its view or assistant; there is no MIL and no effect on emissions.
c: Camera function expected although the vehicle lacks the option or configuration
Plug connection of an add-on or trailer camera open or corroded
Display or radio software not handling the camera input
s: Extra camera view missing or greyed out
View works only with or only without a trailer connected

U0270.t: Lost Communication With Image Processing Sensor L
U0270.d: U0270 ends the image sensor series, and no vehicle maker documents it publicly, so the camera behind letter L is unknown. Twelve letters reflect how many image sensors a vehicle can carry, and they compete for a limited number of receiver inputs: Texas Instruments' DS90UB954 hub, for example, combines one or two camera or radar links. Freightliner ran into such a limit on trucks with Detroit Assurance 5.0, where a retrofitted Bendix forward camera for better video capture needed a port that the factory driver-facing camera already used, so the two could not be combined (dealer letter, February 2020). A sensor that is wired but not configured, or the reverse, is worth ruling out before blaming the link. Losing sensor L disables only its own function; no MIL.
c: Sensor fitted or retrofitted without matching configuration, or configured but absent
Link cable or connector to sensor L interrupted
s: Function of sensor L unavailable with a service message
Fault right after retrofitting or replacing a camera

U0271.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Switch Module C
U0271.d: Seat control switch module C is a third switch unit with its own electronics that reports key presses to a seat module instead of carrying motor current. No manufacturer documents U0271 publicly, and which seat C serves is unpublished. The link is short but sensitive: on 2022 Ford Edge and Lincoln Nautilus built up to 14 March 2022 a driver seat switch stopped working because four terminals (1, 2, 5, 6) in connector C341F had opened up, and the driver seat module stored B14CE and B14D0 (SSM 50621). A patent on climate-controlled seats describes layouts where the memory seat module acts as LIN master while memory switches in the door report over CAN (US10414302B2). When switch C goes silent, its seat ignores those keys; driving is unaffected.
c: Spread or loose terminals in the switch connector
Signal wire between switch and seat module chafed under the seat or in the door
Switch module C without supply or ground
s: Seat does not move from this switch, other controls normal
Memory or comfort keys of this seat without function

U0272.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Switch Module D
U0272.d: Seat control switch module D is the fourth switch unit in this series; no manufacturer documents U0272 publicly or says which seat it belongs to. Such switches need not sit on the seat at all. On 2021–2023 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban and Yukon with the power-folding third-row bench (RPO AS8) the folding switches are in the overhead console and command the K169 folding third-row seat module; GM later dropped their red latch indicators (PIT6041). Jeep has technicians let a Grand Wagoneer third-row seat relearn its end stops by pressing its switch twice after the vehicle has been off for two minutes (9100364). So check the seat module and its learned state as well as the switch. If switch D falls silent, the seat it serves can no longer be moved from there.
c: Wiring to a switch mounted away from the seat (console, roof, trim) interrupted
Seat module lost its learned positions or needs new calibration
Switch module D without supply or ground
s: Rear or folding seat does not respond to its switch
Seat stops short of its end position

U0273.t: Lost Communication With Lighting Driver Control Module A
U0273.d: A lighting driver control module sits in or on a headlamp and powers its LED groups on command from a higher-level lamp or body controller. U0273 means that controller hears nothing from driver module A within its timeout. Lincoln's 2025 Navigator is a documented case: its headlamps use four lighting driver control modules, LDCMA to LDCMD, and module A received over-the-air release LDCMA-25.10.08 to correct colour and brightness at switch-on. GM's 2021 Tahoe and Suburban show that such drivers are separate parts, replaced left and right to fix a bluish daytime light. No maker publishes U0273 itself or which lamp letter A serves. The lamp may keep a basic beam while adaptive or animated functions stop.
c: Moisture or corrosion at the headlamp connector of driver module A
Driver module A without supply or ground (fuse, splice)
Module software outdated or update interrupted
Driver module A internally faulty (often only with complete headlamp)
s: Lighting warning in the instrument cluster
Adaptive high beam, cornering light or light animation unavailable
LED segments on one headlamp dark or in a default setting

U0274.t: Lost Communication With Lighting Driver Control Module B
U0274.d: U0274 is stored when the second lighting driver control module stops answering on its network. Lincoln documents a B unit on the 2025 Navigator, listed as LDCMB and updated with the same release 25.10.08 as its three siblings, but gives no position for it. What a silent driver does on its own is shown by TI's TPS92520-Q1 LED driver: a communication watchdog, set to about 1.67 s by default, switches the chip to limp-home current from preset registers when commands stop arriving. The lamp therefore often stays lit at a fixed level although the controller has lost the module. No manufacturer documents U0274 publicly. U0575 covers implausible data from the same unit.
c: Bus wire or connector to driver module B open or corroded
Supply or ground of driver module B missing
Driver module B software not current after an update
s: Lamp stays at one fixed brightness and ignores dimming
Lighting fault message
Adaptive light functions switched off

U0275.t: Lost Communication With Lighting Driver Control Module C
U0275.d: Driver module C is the third LED driver unit a lamp controller can address. Three or more of them appear where each headlamp has several separately driven zones, as on the 2025 Lincoln Navigator, whose release notes name LDCMC alongside A, B and D. U0275 means the controller no longer receives C's messages; the reason may be the bus, the supply or the module. Driver controllers such as TI's TPS92682-Q1 have a limp-home pin that, when raised, makes them run on a separate set of preset values, so a lamp section can keep working without network commands. Neither U0275 nor the lamp section behind letter C is described in any public service text. Expect a lighting warning and lost adaptive features.
c: Lamp harness or connector to module C damaged (e.g. after front-end repair)
Power or ground of module C interrupted
Module C internally faulty or overheated
s: Part of the headlamp light pattern missing or static
Warning for lighting system

U0276.t: Lost Communication With Lighting Driver Control Module D
U0276.d: U0276 closes the four-letter block: the controlling module has lost contact with lighting driver control module D. Lincoln names an LDCMD on the 2025 Navigator and updated it in the same over-the-air package as A to C; nothing more about its location is public, and no manufacturer documents U0276. Why a silent driver must not leave the driver in the dark follows from the US lighting standard FMVSS 108: a failure of automatic beam control may not take away manual low and high beam, and an adaptive driving beam must detect its own malfunctions and fall back to manual operation. A fault in module D should therefore cost comfort functions, not basic headlamp light. No MIL.
c: Connector of module D loose, wet or corroded
Bus line to module D chafed or open
s: Automatic or adaptive high beam deactivated, manual switching still works
Lighting warning in the cluster

U0277.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module K
U0277.d: Ford uses seat control module K for a second-row seat: on the 2025 Lincoln Navigator, SCMK drives the power seat behind the driver, in SSM 54226 called the rear left-hand power seat module. Its update SCMK-25.5.5.3 was meant to make that seat store its memory positions reliably, and SSM 54226 deals with second-row seats stuck in their longitudinal position, B167F:11 stored in SCMK or SCML, which moved again only after the configuration apps of both modules had been run in FDRS. U0277 itself, the lost-communication code for SCMK, appears in no public bulletin. If set, the left second-row seat cannot be adjusted electrically or recall memory positions; seats in front are unaffected. U0278 is the right-hand module, U0578 invalid data from SCMK.
c: Seat harness or connector under the second-row seat strained or unplugged
SCMK not configured or software update incomplete
Seat module fuse or supply open
Seat control module K internally faulty
s: Left second-row power seat does not move
Memory positions of that seat not stored or recalled

U0278.t: Lost Communication With Seat Control Module L
U0278.d: Seat control module L is the right-hand partner of K. On the 2025 Lincoln Navigator, Ford's SCML runs the second-row power seat on the passenger side; release SCML-25.5.5.3 targeted its memory function, and SSM 54226 lists it as the rear right-hand power seat module, with its own configuration app that must be run after a module change, for example when the seat ignores its fore-aft switch. U0278 signals that SCML has dropped off the network entirely, which no public bulletin covers for this code. Under-seat harnesses on sliding second-row seats are flexed with every adjustment, so connectors and wiring there deserve the first look. Only the right second-row seat loses its electrical functions.
c: Harness under the sliding seat damaged by seat movement
SCML configuration missing after replacement or update
Power or ground to SCML interrupted
Seat control module L internally faulty
s: Right second-row power seat inoperative
Seat memory on that seat not working

U0279.t: Lost Communication With Haptic Control Module
U0279.d: A haptic control module produces vibrations or pulses that the occupants feel, for example in the steering wheel, a seat or the floor. Where it sits varies: the 2026 Range Rover has separate haptic floor modules under the carpet, while on the 2019–2022 Hyundai Palisade the haptic steering wheel motor is driven by the integrated central control unit, so there is no separate network node. Care is needed with Maserati, whose HALF (haptic lane feedback) unit is really the forward-looking camera. U0279 means the module expected for this function has gone silent on the bus. No manufacturer publishes the code. Driving is unaffected; only tactile warnings or comfort effects stop, while visual and audible warnings remain.
c: Connector of the haptic module loose, e.g. after seat or carpet removal
Supply or ground of the haptic module interrupted
Vehicle configured for a haptic option the module does not match
s: No vibration warning in steering wheel, seat or floor
Message about haptic or warning system in the cluster

U027A.t: Lost Communication With Battery Charger Control Module C
U027A.d: Module C is a third on-board charger in the same vehicle; A and B have U019B and U01BB. Several chargers on one bus need clearly separated roles, and a Lear patent shows one way: each unit reads a coded input at start-up, then joins the vehicle bus either as master with the master message set or as slave with the slave set. A slave whose input or wiring is wrong can thus vanish from the network. U027A is stored when the supervising controller stops hearing charger C. No manufacturer documents the code publicly or names a third charger. For plug-in hybrids CARB only asks for detection of charger faults that stop charging or reduce the charging rate. AC charging then usually runs slower; driving and emissions are not affected.
c: 12 V supply or wake-up line of charger C missing
Bus connector at charger C corroded or not latched
Charger C coded or addressed wrongly after replacement
s: Reduced AC charging power or longer charging time
Charging fault message

U027B.t: Lost Communication With Battery Charger Control Module D
U027B.d: U027B refers to a fourth charger unit. In multi-charger designs the units also split the control task; in a dual charger system patented by Lear, two chargers feed the battery in parallel, one regulating voltage and the other regulating current. If one partner falls silent, the remaining unit has to carry the job alone or charging is stopped. U027B is set when the supervising controller loses all messages from charger D, whereas U057C stands for messages from D that arrive but fail checks. No manufacturer documents U027B or a fourth on-board charger publicly. The CARB rule for plug-in hybrids exempts charging faults that cannot be told apart from a supply problem outside the car. Expect slower or interrupted charging.
c: Low-voltage supply, fuse or wake-up of charger D missing
Bus wiring to charger D damaged or connector wet
s: Charging power lower than usual
Charging session aborted with a warning

U027C.t: Lost Communication With Off-Board Charger Control Module
U027C.d: DC fast charging uses a charger outside the car, so the vehicle needs a controller that negotiates with the station. Ford has a module with almost this name in its battery-electric vehicles: the off-board charger controller (OBCC) of the Mustang Mach-E, E-Transit and F-150 Lightning. Ford reprogrammed it in program 22B48 and SSM 50923 because some stations aborted DC charging, and SSM 52130 tells technicians to disregard P1A3C in the OBCC after an interrupted fast-charge session. Whether Ford stores U027C when the OBCC goes silent is not published, and no other maker documents the code. Without this module DC fast charging is not possible, while AC charging through the on-board charger normally still works. Driving is unaffected.
c: Supply or wake-up of the fast-charge controller missing
Controller software outdated or update failed
Bus wiring or connector to the controller faulty
s: DC fast charging fails or does not start
Charge failure notification on screen or in the app
AC charging still possible

U0284.t: Lost Communication With Active Grille Air Shutter Module A
U0284.d: The grille shutter actuator is a LIN node of the engine controller. GM's 2018 ECM tables set U0284 when the ECM loses the LIN link to shutter 1 for 3 counts in Run with at least 11 V; it is Type B, MIL after two trips. Ford's 2024 OBD summary lists it as a continuous monitor: entry 5 s after start at 11–16 V, fault when the AGS signal is missing over 10 s. A 2020 Volkswagen analysis list treats a lit MIL with U0284 in the ECM as its own case. Water is the common cause: Subaru 07-140-18 (2017–2019 Impreza, connector B63), Ford SSM 46857 (C-Max, C1651), Hyundai 23-01-075H (Ioniq 5 actuator). Several Ford SSMs pair U0284 with generator codes U012D/U042E. Shutters stop moving; engine warm-up and drag suffer.
c: Water intrusion and corrosion at the shutter actuator connector or its harness
Fault on a shared connection, e.g. with the generator (check U012D/U042E)
Unstable power supply to the actuator
Shutter actuator A internally faulty or damaged by impact
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Grille shutter warning, shutters do not open or close
Check charging system message when a shared connection is affected

U0285.t: Lost Communication With Active Grille Air Shutter Module B
U0285.d: Module B is the second shutter unit, typically the one behind the lower bumper opening. GM's 2018 ECM tables treat it as LIN device 1 (shutter 2): the ECM sets U0285 after 3 missed counts once the check has been enabled for 400 ms in Run at 11 V or more, Type B with MIL after two trips. Ford monitors it together with A in its OBD summary (signal missing over 10 s). Being low at the front, B collects water and road salt: Stellantis case S2523000095 for the 2025–2026 Ram 1500 reports a lit MIL with U0285 and P05AE and checks the lower shutter harness for corrosion first, and Hyundai's campaign 26-01-026H for the 2026 Palisade replaces corroded lower flap wiring, actuators or sensors. The lower shutters then stay put.
c: Corrosion in the lower shutter harness or connector from water and salt
Lower shutter or its wiring damaged by impact or debris
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on, often with P05AE
Lower grille shutters do not move
Active air flap warning message

U0286.t: Lost Communication With Radiator Anti-Tamper Device
U0286.d: Some low-emission vehicles carry a catalytic radiator coating that breaks down ground-level ozone; BASF sells it as PremAir, and EPA and CARB grant 5 mg/mi credit for it. CARB requires the OBD system to watch such a direct ozone reduction system. A Ford patent shows how: a unit whose pins are pushed between the radiator fins sends the ECU a temperature value, relevant because the coating only works from roughly 60 °C, together with an encrypted identity, and a breakable pin stops it being moved to a cheaper uncoated radiator. U0286 means the engine controller no longer hears this device, so it can neither confirm the coated radiator nor track its temperature. No manufacturer documents U0286 in a publicly accessible service text. Cooling itself is unaffected; the MIL can light.
c: Connector or wiring of the device at the radiator corroded or damaged
Radiator replaced and device missing or broken off
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Further codes for the ozone reduction system or radiator temperature

U0287.t: Lost Communication With Transmission Fluid Pump Module A
U0287.d: An electric transmission fluid pump with its own control electronics keeps hydraulic pressure available whenever the engine stands still, in auto stop or electric driving. Stellantis calls it transmission fluid pump module 1; the TCM sets U0287 when it stops responding. On 2021–2025 Jeep Wrangler and Grand Cherokee 4xe, TSB 21-041-26 links the code with MIL and limp mode to a failed in-pan pump, and 08-082-25 traces cases to a damaged high-voltage cable whose noise reaches the pump circuit. The 2026 Compass with 8F30 gets a new pump and TCM software (21-058-26), with stop-start off and a service transmission message. Hyundai sets U028700 in the pump itself on the 2.5 Santa Fe and Tucson with eight-speed automatic, disabling Idle Stop and Go (26-AT-002H).
c: Electric fluid pump or its integrated electronics failed
Damaged high-voltage cable inducing interference on the pump circuit (hybrids)
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and service transmission or hybrid message
Engine stop-start disabled
Limp mode on plug-in hybrids

U0288.t: Lost Communication With DC/AC Converter Control Module A
U0288.d: A DC/AC converter, usually called a power inverter, turns the vehicle's direct current into 120 V or 230 V alternating current for sockets in the cabin or the load bed. U0288 is logged when the module supervising those sockets stops receiving the cyclic frames of converter A. GM names the body control module as listener: preliminary information PIT6527 for the 2026 Colorado and Canyon reports U0288 appearing after BCM programming on trucks built without the KI6 outlet behind the centre console, where it affects nothing and may be ignored. On the 2021 F-150 with the 3.5 PowerBoost hybrid, Ford stores the code in secondary OBD module C, also called the inverter system controller, and cures it with new software (21-2128, index entry). Usually only the outlets go dead.
c: Body or gateway module configured for an outlet the vehicle does not have (false entry)
Outdated software in the converter or inverter system controller
Blown fuse, supply or bus wiring fault at converter A
s: 120 V or 230 V outlets without power
Outlet or power supply warning in the instrument cluster
Code stored without any noticeable symptom

U0289.t: Lost Communication With DC/AC Converter Control Module B
U0289.d: U0289 belongs to a second DC/AC converter, unit B, in vehicles that generate mains-voltage alternating current at two points, for example a small inverter for a console socket and a stronger one for the bed, or one converter per group of outlets. No manufacturer documents U0289 or describes a converter B in public material. Unit A shows how such a check behaves: GM's body control module on the 2026 Colorado and Canyon flags lost contact as U0288, falsely even on trucks without the outlet. GM's 2023 Silverado and Sierra programme, which later activated the inverter for dashboard and bed outlets by adding a power control module and reprogramming the BCM, shows that option coding decides which converters the network expects. Only the sockets fed by B should fail.
c: Network configured for a second converter that is missing or not activated
No supply or ground at converter B (fuse, connector)
Bus wiring or connector to converter B damaged
s: Some outlets dead while others still work
Power outlet warning message

U028A.t: Lost Communication With Transmission Fluid Pump Module B
U028A.d: An electric transmission fluid pump with built-in electronics holds clutch pressure and lubrication whenever the engine is stopped, in auto stop or electric driving. Module B is a second pump of this kind; U028A means the transmission or hybrid controller no longer hears its status frames. No manufacturer documents U028A or names a pump B publicly, so the reaction must be inferred from pump A. Stellantis calls that unit transmission fluid pump module 1 and ties U0287 on the Wrangler and Grand Cherokee 4xe to a failed in-pan pump with MIL and limp mode (21-041-26). Hyundai stores U028700 in the transmission unit of the Santa Fe and Tucson without any warning lamp and merely blocks Idle Stop and Go (26-AT-002H). For B, expect stop-start or electric drive to be withdrawn.
c: Electric pump B or its integrated electronics failed
Corroded or loose pump connector, oil wicking into the connector
Supply, ground or bus line to pump B interrupted
s: Start-stop function no longer active
Electric driving blocked or engine keeps running
Transmission warning, harsh engagement after an engine stop

U028B.t: Lost Communication With Active Grille Air Shutter Module C
U028B.d: Shutter module C is a third, separately addressed flap actuator behind the grille or bumper, used where a front end divides its cooling air openings into several sections. Hyundai documents the code: its 2026 Palisade and Palisade Hybrid have left and right actuators for the lower active air flaps, and campaign 26-01-026H lists U028B together with U0285 and flap position codes when water enters the bumper connectors and corrodes them. Owners then see an air flap warning, the check engine lamp and sometimes a low oil message; the remedy is to inspect pins and replace harness, actuators or sensors. How the engine controller decides on lost contact is visible at GM, which sets the code for shutters on the LIN bus after three missed responses as a two-trip fault.
c: Water ingress and corrosion at the bumper connector of shutter C
Front harness damaged by impact, stone chips or poor routing
Fault in the controlling engine module or its LIN output
s: Check engine lamp on
Active air flap warning in the cluster
Lower flaps no longer move

U028C.t: Lost Communication With Active Grille Air Shutter Module D
U028C.d: Module D is the fourth grille shutter address in the code list and only matters on fronts with four independently driven flap units, for instance upper and lower flaps on each side. No manufacturer documents U028C or says where unit D sits, so its position is maker-specific. The surrounding evidence is consistent: Hyundai's 2026 Palisade already splits its lower flaps into left and right actuators and stores U0285 and U028B, with the engine lamp, after water corrodes their plugs (26-01-026H). GM's 2018 engine controller counts a shutter that misses three LIN responses in Run at 11 V or more as a two-trip MIL fault. Under CARB rules, grille shutters belong to the active off-cycle features whose operating time is recorded. A silent unit D leaves its flaps frozen.
c: Moisture or corrosion at the connector of shutter D
LIN or supply wire to unit D damaged in the front end
Actuator D failed, for example after ice or impact
Wrong actuator variant or configuration after a repair
s: Check engine lamp on
Part of the shutters stays open or closed
Slightly longer warm-up or higher consumption

U028D.t: Lost Communication With Active Aerodynamic Feature Control Module A
U028D.d: Active aerodynamic features change the airflow around the body while driving, for example an extending front air dam, a movable wing or ride height that drops at speed. CARB defines them as active off-cycle technologies, cites grill shutters and speed-dependent ride height as examples and requires counters that record how long they are deployed. U028D is set when the first control module of such a feature stops sending on the network. No manufacturer documents U028D publicly.
