The front air dam has its own code: Ram 1500 owners see the check engine lamp with U0645 for lost contact and C0604 for poor function, and FCA's procedure starts with a check for impact damage before cycling the dam with the scan tool. Without the module, the element stays in its last position.
c: Element or its wiring damaged by kerbs, snow or debris
Water or corrosion at the module connector
Fuse, supply or ground of module A faulty
s: Active aero warning message in the cluster
Element does not deploy or retract
Slightly higher consumption at highway speed

U028E.t: Lost Communication With Active Aerodynamic Feature Control Module B
U028E.d: U028E concerns a second aerodynamic control module, B, on vehicles that drive more than one active element or split one element into separately controlled halves. Ford's F-150 is a practical example of the latter: its active air dam has a left and a right actuator whose firmware Ford blamed for C0604 logged by the PCM (SSM 51718), and bulletin 24-2404 and its successors cure the warning Active Air Dam System Fault See Manual and code C0604 with coordinated software updates. Neither Ford nor any other maker publishes U028E or assigns letter B to a specific part. If B drops off the bus while A still works, the elements can end up in unequal positions, and the system usually parks both and shows a warning. CARB treats such features as active off-cycle technology with tracked usage.
c: Wiring or connector of module B damaged near the moving element
Outdated software in module B or the commanding controller
Supply or ground of module B interrupted
s: Active aero or air dam warning in the cluster
One side of an element stuck or misaligned

U028F.t: Lost Communication With Active Aerodynamic Feature Control Module C
U028F.d: A third aerodynamic control module, C, is found on vehicles that combine front elements with rear ones such as a deployable spoiler or an adjustable wing. Sports cars show what these rear parts do: the 2017–2019 Ford GT raises and lowers an active aero wing, and Ford's bulletin 20-2353 deals with that wing touching the body after long storage in its lowered position. U028F is stored when the network loses module C altogether, so the element neither reports its position nor accepts commands. No manufacturer documents U028F or links letter C to a particular element. A wing that stays down reduces downforce at speed, one that stays up adds drag. CARB counts movable aero parts among the off-cycle technologies with logged operating time.
c: Wiring chafed or broken at the moving rear element
Moisture in the connector of module C
Fuse, supply or ground of module C faulty
s: Spoiler or wing no longer moves
Active aero fault message, sometimes a speed limitation

U0290.t: Lost Communication With Active Aerodynamic Feature Control Module D
U0290.d: Module D is the last of four aerodynamic control addresses and fits vehicles in which aerodynamics are integrated with chassis functions. Ford's Mustang GTD is such a case: its hydraulic system serves both the suspension and the active aero elements, and service message SSM 55237 lists the warning Active Aero Fault together with suspension and front lift messages, caused by vehicle dynamics module software that reports faults wrongly and fixed by reprogramming. U0290 means that controller has lost the fourth aero module entirely. No manufacturer documents U0290 publicly or says which element module D drives. Depending on the design, a failure can freeze one element or cause the vehicle to restrict modes and top speed. For CARB, such parts are active off-cycle technology.
c: Software of module D or the vehicle dynamics controller
Bus or supply wiring to module D damaged
Moisture or corrosion at the connector of module D
s: Active aero fault message
Drive modes or top speed restricted
Aero element stuck in one position

U0291.t: Lost Communication With Gear Shift Control Module B
U0291.d: With shift-by-wire, the driver's lever, buttons or dial is an electronic module that sends the selected range to the transmission over the network. Gear shift control module B is a second unit of this kind; U0291 means the transmission controller has stopped receiving its messages. Allison documents the pair for its sixth-generation controls of the 1000 to 4000 series, released in 2021: U0103 covers gear shift module 1, U0291 module 2, with separate codes for incompatibility (U0333) and invalid data (U0592) of the second selector. Mercedes-Benz uses U029100 on the 8-speed dual-clutch transmission 724.1 for a communication fault with the electronic selector lever module. Range changes requested at that selector are then ignored; the transmission typically stays in or returns to a safe range.
c: Loose or corroded connector at the second selector
Bus line to selector B chafed or interrupted
Selector variant or software not matching the transmission calibration
s: Gear selection at the selector has no effect
Transmission warning or flashing range display
Vehicle cannot be shifted out of Park or Neutral

U0292.t: Lost Communication With Drive Motor Control Module B
U0292.d: Electric and hybrid vehicles with a motor on each axle usually give the inverter of the second motor the address drive motor control module B. U0292 means the coordinating controller no longer receives its messages. Audi documents this for the 2019 e-tron quattro: bulletin 2055804 finds U029200 in the electric drive control unit J841 or the engine control unit J623, while the car refuses to become ready, limits the selectable positions and shows various warnings; the low-voltage harness of the rear motor chafes because of its routing, sometimes blowing fuses SJ7 or SD5. Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV lists U0292-00 as lost communication with power drive unit B, the rear unit. Expect warnings, loss of drive on that axle or no ready state.
c: Low-voltage harness of the second drive unit chafed
Blown supply fuse of module B
Connector at the inverter of module B loose or corroded
Inverter or control module B internally failed
s: Vehicle does not become ready to drive
Drive system warnings, restricted gear selection
Only one axle driven, reduced power

U0293.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Powertrain Control Module
U0293.d: The hybrid or EV powertrain control module coordinates engine, motors and high-voltage battery, so many controllers depend on its frames. Ford's 2019 hybrid OBD summary has the battery module set U0293 when HPCM messages are missing for 1 or 5 s, and the brake module set it because wheel torque data are lost; the 2014 list marks it with MIL. GM uses it in several units: the 2016 Volt VICM reacts after 500 ms as Type B, the 2018 L8B engine module after 0.5 s as Type A. Jeep cured it on the 2021 Wrangler 4xe with a TCM flash, Toyota found U029387 on the 2019–2020 RAV4 Hybrid in frost because the IGCT relay failed to power the HV ECU. Ford SSMs name connector grease and gateway software. Often the car will not start or drive.
c: Supply relay or fuse of the hybrid powertrain module (e.g. IGCT relay in frost)
Software in the hybrid module, gateway or receiving module
Connector fault, including grease applied to module connectors
CAN wiring to the hybrid module damaged
Hybrid/EV powertrain control module internally failed
s: Check engine lamp or hybrid system warning
Vehicle does not become ready or will not start
Stop safely now message, loss of power

U0294.t: Lost Communication With Powertrain Control Monitor Module
U0294.d: A powertrain control monitor module is a separate supervisor that recalculates torque, speed or driver demand and checks whether the main controller's commands stay within safe limits. U0294 is stored when that supervisor stops communicating, so the plausibility layer is missing. Ford's 2014 code list includes it lighting only the wrench symbol, never the MIL. Within one controller the same idea appears in Ford's 2024 throttle monitor, which compares main and monitoring processor and lights wrench lamp and MIL on faults. Audi's bulletin index lists U029400 for the 2025 Q6 and SQ6 e-tron, where no gear can be selected in cold weather together with U3035 and U0129, and for 3.0 V6 TFSI models with a drive system fault; the module meaning is not public. Expect reduced power or limp home.
c: Software of the monitoring or main controller (incl. cold-start behaviour)
Supply, ground or wake-up of the monitoring module faulty
Bus wiring or connector to the monitoring module damaged
s: Wrench or drive system warning lamp
Reduced power or limp home
Gear selection refused, especially in cold weather

U0295.t: Lost Communication With AC/AC Converter Control Module
U0295.d: An AC/AC converter takes in alternating current and delivers alternating current at a different voltage or frequency, with no DC storage in between. In electric vehicles such a stage can be part of a charger: in patent US9973107B2 a matrix stage converts the three mains phases directly to a high-frequency waveform, which an isolating transformer passes on before rectification for the battery. Other uses are possible, for example adapting power for on-board outlets. U0295 means the module controlling that converter has fallen silent on the network. No manufacturer documents U0295, and public service literature contains no module of this name; what it does is up to the vehicle design. If it sits in the charging path, CARB requires plug-in hybrids to detect faults that stop or slow charging.
c: Low-voltage supply or wake-up of the converter module missing
Bus wiring or connector to the converter damaged
Converter shut down after overheating or a coolant fault
s: AC charging not possible or interrupted
Charging or power supply warning

U0296.t: Lost Communication With AC/DC Converter Control Module A
U0296.d: An AC/DC converter rectifies alternating current; in plug-in vehicles the best known example is the on-board charger, which also runs in the opposite direction of an inverter feeding a motor. U0296 means converter module A no longer reports on the bus. CARB obliges plug-in hybrids to detect charger malfunctions that prevent full charging or limit the charge rate. Volvo is the maker that names the code: on plug-in XC60 and XC90 models from 2022, brake control module 2 logs BCM2-U029600, the ESC lamp comes on and Pure mode is locked out whenever a third-party device or Y-splitter loads the diagnostic socket (TJ 36559). On 2016–2018 T8 models the code appeared intermittently next to rear-axle inverter faults and cleared with inverter software (TJ 33723).
c: Aftermarket device or Y-splitter on the diagnostic connector disturbing the bus
Outdated software in the converter or inverter module
Supply, ground or bus wiring of converter A faulty
s: ESC or hybrid system warning in the cluster
Pure electric driving not available
Charging from the grid not possible

U0297.t: Lost Communication With AC/DC Converter Control Module B
U0297.d: Converter B is a second AC/DC unit, typically an additional on-board charger that raises AC charging power when combined with the first. Patents show how such pairs are coordinated: in Porsche's US10029578B2 one charger leads and the other follows commands received over a communication link, while Hyundai's US10270273B2 has a master controller steering slave controllers for several power modules. U0297 is stored when the controlling module no longer hears unit B. The vehicle usually continues to charge with converter A alone, but at a lower rate. Because CARB wants plug-in hybrid OBD to catch charger problems that reduce charging speed, a silent B is relevant there too. No manufacturer documents U0297 publicly; Volvo's use of U0296 concerns unit A.
c: Low-voltage supply or wake-up line of charger B missing
Communication line between the converters interrupted
Software or configuration does not match the fitted charger variant
s: AC charging noticeably slower than usual
Charging system warning

U0298.t: Lost Communication With DC/DC Converter Control Module A
U0298.d: A DC/DC converter adapts one direct voltage to another. Hybrids and EVs use it to charge the 12 V system from the traction battery, while some start-stop cars use it to keep the voltage steady for sensitive electronics during an engine restart. U0298 means converter module A no longer answers on the bus. Ford's 2014 OBD code list contains U0298 without the MIL. How this converter is supervised on start-stop vehicles is visible in its invalid-data partner: GM explains in 20-NA-191, covering CT4 and CT5 of model year 2020, that the ECM switches off auto stop at the first fault and lights the MIL at the second, and FCA lists DC/DC converter A data codes for the 2019 Cherokee V6. Expect start-stop to be withdrawn; on electrified cars the 12 V battery may run flat.
c: Converter connector corroded, often from water in the battery area
Blown fuse or missing supply at converter A
Bus wiring to converter A damaged
s: Start-stop no longer active
12 V battery discharging, charge warning
Electronics resetting during engine restarts

U0299.t: Lost Communication With DC/DC Converter Control Module B
U0299.d: A second DC/DC converter, B, appears where a single support stage cannot serve every consumer or where two networks are fed separately. FCA documents the code: in PCM reflash bulletins 18-023-19 Rev. B and 18-020-21, covering 2019 Cherokee models with the 3.2 V6 and stop-start, U0299 is named as loss of contact to DC-DC converter 2. Next to it stand performance and over-temperature codes for converter 2 (P0EA5, P0EA6) and invalid data from converters A and B. Customers report a lit MIL and an engine that does not always restart after an auto stop; the remedy is new PCM software, not a new converter. With B missing, start-stop is typically withdrawn and voltage-sensitive electronics may reset during restarts.
c: Supply, fuse or ground of converter B faulty
Bus wiring or connector to converter B damaged
Converter B internally failed, e.g. after overheating
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine does not always restart after auto stop
Start-stop function disabled

U029A.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Sensor Module
U029A.d: The battery pack sensor module is the electronics inside the high-voltage battery that reports pack current and voltage; many designs house it together with the main contactors. U029A means the battery or vehicle controller no longer hears from it. Stellantis documents the code in the battery pack control module of the 2024 Dodge Charger with 400 V electric drive: bulletins 08-026-25 Rev. B and 08-126-25 Rev. B reflash several modules and, if U029A stays, call for a six-minute sleep with the scan tool unplugged before a BPCM soft reset. Audi files U029A00 under address 8C for the 2025 Q5 e and the 2024 Q8 Sportback e-tron. Ford's 2014 code list shows it without the lamp flag. Lacking these values, the car may refuse to drive or charge.
c: Outdated software in the battery control module or sensor module
Code latched after programming because the network never went to sleep
Moisture or poor contact at the battery low-voltage connector or bus wiring
Battery pack sensor module internally failed
s: Wrench or turtle symbol, reduced power
Vehicle does not enable drive or stops charging
High-voltage system warning in the cluster

U029B.t: Lost Communication With Drive Motor Control Module C
U029B.d: Drive motor control module C is the inverter and controller of a third traction motor, so it only occurs on vehicles with three or four drive motors. Production examples are the tri-motor version of the GMC Hummer EV, which drives its rear axle with two motors, and Rivian's quad-motor R1T and R1S with one motor per wheel. U029B is stored when the propulsion or vehicle controller stops receiving any periodic messages from module C. Frames that still come but carry unusable values are U059C; U0292 and U029C cover the second and fourth motor controllers. Which motor gets letter C is the maker's decision, and no manufacturer documents U029B publicly. For hybrids, CARB 1968.2 demands that missing communication from digital inputs be detected. Expect that motor to be shut off and reduced power and traction.
c: Fuse, low-voltage supply or ground of module C faulty
Damaged or corroded bus wiring or connector at the drive unit
Software fault or interrupted programming of module C
Drive motor control module C internally failed
s: Reduced power warning, one motor disabled
Torque vectoring or all-wheel-drive functions unavailable
Drive system warning in the cluster

U029C.t: Lost Communication With Drive Motor Control Module D
U029C.d: Letter D refers to the controller of a fourth drive motor, which presupposes individual-wheel drive. Rivian's quad-motor R1S is the familiar production case: each wheel gets its own frame-mounted Bosch motor, so torque can be split freely between all four corners at any time. U029C says module D has gone silent on the network. If it still sent frames with bad content, U059D would be stored instead; a silent third motor is U029B. No manufacturer documents U029C publicly, so which wheel letter D belongs to and how the car reacts are vehicle-specific. CARB 1968.2 obliges hybrid OBD systems to notice when a digital input stops communicating. A plausible response is to drop the silent motor, cap the torque on the other side so the car still runs straight, and warn of reduced power.
c: Fuse, low-voltage supply or ground of module D faulty
Bus wiring near the wheel drive unit chafed or wet
Software fault or failed update of module D
Drive motor control module D internally failed
s: Reduced power and loss of torque vectoring
Drive system warning in the cluster
Uneven traction when accelerating

U029D.t: Lost Communication With NOx Sensor A
U029D.d: NOx sensor A is normally the engine-out or SCR inlet sensor; its control unit puts NOx and oxygen values on CAN. U029D means these frames have stopped. GM treats it as Type A: its 2016 diesel tables wait 10 s, the 2025 tables (25OBDG04A/B) about 1 s for most frames, at 11 to 18 V with the bus otherwise healthy; on the 2014 6.6 L LML the code also counted checksum errors. Ford's 2023 diesel summary allows just over 1 s. Ford found water in the sensor module plug of 6.7 L F-Super Duty trucks from 2017-2019 and replaced module and harness 14406 (TSB 18-2365). Volvo and Mack name fuses, supply, J1939 wiring and terminating resistors, and on 2023 trucks a start-up timing bug. Deutz uses U029D for the upstream SCR sensor. MIL, open SCR checks and derate are possible.
c: Water or corrosion in the NOx sensor module connector or harness
Blown fuse, open supply or ground of the sensor module
Sensor CAN wiring damaged or terminating resistor faulty
Engine control software with start-up timing fault
NOx sensor control unit internally failed
s: MIL on
SCR or NOx monitor not completed
Engine derate on some trucks

U029E.t: Lost Communication With NOx Sensor B
U029E.d: Sensor B usually measures NOx at the outlet, behind the SCR catalyst, so the SCR efficiency verdict depends on it. U029E is logged once its CAN messages fail to reach the engine controller. GM monitors the post-catalyst frames the same way as for sensor A and also treats a loss as Type A; Ford's 2023 diesel summary reacts after more than 1 s, and Ford's 2014 code list shows it with MIL. Typical causes are installation errors: Volkswagen's tech tip 01-18-09TT for the 2015 Golf, Jetta, Passat and Beetle 2.0 TDI tells technicians who see U029E after campaign 23Y8 to look for swapped plugs at the front sensor and its adapter and an unseated rear sensor plug. Ford's SSM 50455 ties it on 2021 F-Super Duty 6.7 L to an incomplete PCM reprogramming. The tailpipe check stays open.
c: Sensor plugs swapped or not fully seated after service work
Water or corrosion in the NOx sensor connectors
Incomplete or wrong engine control module programming
NOx sensor B control unit internally failed
s: MIL on
SCR efficiency monitor not completed
Engine derate on some heavy trucks

U029F.t: Lost Communication With Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Control Module
U029F.d: Some evaporative systems run the leak test through a separate module that holds its own valve, pressure switch or sensor and reports results to the engine controller. U029F is stored when those reports no longer arrive. Kia documents it for the Niro hybrid of 2017 to 2019: bulletin PS593 describes a MIL with U029F00 and, on cars built before October 2018, asks for a resistance check of the yellow signal wire between pin 12 of joint connector EF11 and pin 2 of the natural vacuum leak detection plug F56, since damaged insulation or corroded strands near F56 cause an open circuit. Ford's 2014 code list marks the code as a MIL code. CARB 1968.2 requires gasoline vehicles to find leaks as small as 0.020 inch, so the EVAP monitor cannot run. Driving is not affected.
c: Damaged insulation or corroded strands in the module signal wire
Corrosion or water at the leak detection module connector
Supply or ground of the leak detection module interrupted
s: MIL on
EVAP readiness not set
No noticeable change in driving

U02A0.t: Invalid Data Received From Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module D
U02A0.d: Although it sits among lost-communication codes, U02A0 is a data error code. The expected slot in the invalid-data series, U04A4, had already gone to particulate matter sensor A, as Ford's 2014 code list and Volkswagen's 2014 Touareg data show, so module D's data fault landed here. Interface modules are the boards in the high-voltage pack that read cell voltages and temperatures and switch cell balancing for the battery controller; GM's 2016 hybrid tables show eight of them, A to H, on a daisy-chained serial link, with a processor test and a balancing test for each board (P1EA0 and P1EA4 for D). U02A0 means module D still answers, but its data fail integrity or plausibility checks. No manufacturer documents U02A0 publicly. A silent D is U01A3. Expect a power limit.
c: Interface board D delivering corrupted or implausible data
Poor contact in the internal communication chain of the pack
Mismatched software between battery controller and interface modules
Damaged cell sense lead at module D
s: Hybrid or electric system warning
Reduced power or no charging
Engine runs more often on hybrids

U02A1.t: Lost Communication With NOx Sensor C
U02A1.d: A third NOx sensor, C, is fitted where the aftertreatment needs one more measuring point, typically behind a second SCR stage. U02A1 is set when its CAN messages no longer reach the engine controller. GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG04B) wait longer than 10 s without any of its five messages, with 11 to 18 V and the bus up, and rate it Type B, so the MIL comes on after the second failed trip; the sibling codes for sensors A and B are Type A there. GM also lists U02A1 in bulletin 21-NA-149 among codes caused by chafed engine harnesses on 3.0 L LM2 diesel trucks and SUVs. Ford's SSM 51750 links it on 2023 F-Super Duty 6.7 L to a harness 14406 rubbing on the EGR cooler near C146; first check 20 A fuse F18. The second SCR stage then goes unchecked.
c: Engine harness chafed on a hot component such as the EGR cooler
Blown fuse feeding the NOx sensor modules
Water or corrosion at the sensor C connector
NOx sensor C control unit internally failed
s: MIL on after two drives
Further NOx or PM sensor codes stored at the same time
SCR monitor for the second stage incomplete

U02A2.t: Lost Communication With Reductant Quality Module
U02A2.d: The reductant quality module tells the engine or dosing controller whether the tank holds proper diesel exhaust fluid; in many trucks it is one tank sensor unit with level and temperature. U02A2 means its messages have stopped. Ford's 2023 diesel summary allows 5 s without them. In TSB 19-2315 Ford blames water in connectors C3613 and C4851 of the reductant harness on the 6.7 L F-Super Duty of model years 2017-2019 and replaces harness, pump and heater assembly or tank. Hino's SB-15-030 for 2014 and 2015 trucks points to a faulty DEF tank sensor assembly and supplies a more robust one. Mack lists software faults, missing supply and the connector. CARB 1968.2 requires every input of the inducement strategy to be monitored, so the warning sequence that leads to a speed limit may begin.
c: Water in the reductant harness connectors at tank or pump
Defective DEF tank sensor unit with quality sensor
Missing supply voltage or wrong software version of the module
Damaged CAN wiring between tank sensor and controller
s: MIL and DEF system warning
Countdown to speed or restart limitation
DEF quality and level readings missing

U02A3.t: Lost Communication With Particulate Matter Sensor
U02A3.d: The particulate matter sensor behind the diesel particulate filter collects soot on a heated element; its own control unit reports the result over CAN, and the engine controller uses it to judge the filter. U02A3 means those frames have stopped. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets it after 7 s at 11 to 16 V. GM waits 10 s and rates it Type B. Ford's 2014 code list and FCA's Ram 2500 and 3500 bulletin 18-052-19 show it with MIL. FCA STAR case S2218000023 for the 2019 Jeep Compass explains U02A3 right after a sensor replacement by a wrong sensor variant, so compare the stamped part number. On 2023 Volvo and Mack trucks it set when the engine was cranked immediately after key on; new software followed. The filter check stays incomplete, and on trucks a derate is possible.
c: Wrong particulate sensor variant fitted during repair
Chafed harness, blown fuse or corroded connector at the sensor unit
Engine control software with start-up timing fault
Particulate sensor control unit internally failed
s: MIL on
Particulate filter monitor not completed
Derate or inducement warning on some trucks

U02A4.d: An NH3 sensor reports ammonia downstream of the SCR catalyst, showing whether more reductant is dosed than the catalyst can use. Like a NOx sensor it has its own control unit on CAN; Bosch even sells a NOx sensor that delivers a selective ammonia signal alongside NOx and oxygen. U02A4 is set when the engine or dosing controller no longer receives any ammonia messages. No manufacturer documents U02A4 publicly. FCA used a code of its own instead: bulletin 18-028-16, covering Cummins 6.7 L Ram chassis cabs (3500, 4500, 5500) of 2014, names U12A4 for lost contact with the ammonia sensor and offers separate calibrations for trucks with and without it. CARB 1968.2 requires inputs from smart devices that affect emissions to be monitored. Without the signal, dosing runs without slip feedback.
c: Engine calibration expects an ammonia sensor that is missing or different
Heat damage, water or corrosion at the sensor connector
Fuse, supply or ground of the sensor control unit faulty
NH3 sensor control unit internally failed
s: MIL on
SCR system warning
Higher reductant consumption possible

U02A5.t: Lost Communication With Reductant Heater Control Module
U02A5.d: At roughly -11 °C diesel exhaust fluid turns solid, while EU type approval asked for usable fluid within 20 minutes of a start at -15 °C, so tank, pump and lines carry heaters. Some systems leave their switching to a separate heater control module that reports state and temperatures to the engine or dosing controller. U02A5 is set when this module goes silent. No manufacturer documents U02A5 publicly. Many engines do without such a module: Ford's 2023 diesel summary drives the heaters straight from the engine controller and checks them with output codes such as P20BB, P20BC and P21DD. CARB 1968.2 requires every input to the inducement strategy to be monitored, and thaw control feeds it. In frost, dosing may start late, with a DEF warning and later inducement.
c: Fuse, relay or supply of the heater module faulty
Water or salt corrosion at the module connector near the tank
Shared bus disturbed by another faulty module
s: MIL and DEF system warning
Dosing delayed in cold weather
Inducement countdown if it persists

U02A6.t: Lost Communication With Safety Integration Control Module
U02A6.d: The Safety Integration Control Module is a name from the SAE code catalogue for which no carmaker publishes a role or a fitted model; the term points to a unit that bundles several safety functions, for instance restraint, braking and driver assistance data. U02A6 means another controller expects its cyclic messages and they no longer come. For safety signals that check is normally formalised: the AUTOSAR end-to-end protocol has the receiver watch the arrival of fresh data and declare a timeout once too many cycles pass without a valid new frame, alongside CRC and counter checks. ISO 26262 then requires a safe state for such faults. No manufacturer documents U02A6 or its partner U05A7 publicly. Typical results are warnings and switched-off assistance features, without an emissions link.
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the module faulty
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged
Software or configuration fault after programming
s: Several safety or assistance warnings at once
Driver assistance functions unavailable

U02A7.t: Lost Communication With Engine Sound Control 1
U02A7.d: Engine sound control means active sound design: a controller composes or amplifies engine sound from live data such as engine speed and torque and plays it through speakers or a structure-borne actuator, the way Volkswagen's Soundaktor or Kia's Active Sound System do. Where this runs in a separate unit, U02A7 records that unit 1 has stopped sending its network messages. Many makers integrate the function elsewhere: Ford's 2021 programme 21U04 for the Explorer ST and Lincoln Aviator had dealers activate active noise control and engine sound enhancement within the audio controller using the FDRS tool, because the plant had left them off. No manufacturer documents U02A7 publicly. Consequences are acoustic only: the synthetic sound is missing, the cabin may sound plainer.
c: Fuse, supply or ground of sound unit 1 faulty
Unit or function not enabled or wrongly configured
Bus wiring or connector to the unit damaged
s: Synthetic engine sound missing in the cabin
More audible drivetrain or road noise

U02A8.t: Lost Communication With Engine Sound Control 2
U02A8.d: A second engine sound control exists where one unit is not enough, for example when interior speakers and an exterior sound source are handled separately or two actuators sit at different points of the body. Active sound design covers both directions: inside it shapes what occupants hear, outside it can give a car a recognisable voice. U02A8 is stored when unit 2 drops off the network while unit 1 may still work. Keep it apart from pedestrian warning sound, which on electric cars has its own legal basis and module. No manufacturer documents U02A8 publicly; Ford, for one, runs its engine sound enhancement inside the audio control module, enabled by software. The fault does not affect driving, emissions or engine control, only the sound picture.
c: Fuse, supply or ground of sound unit 2 faulty
Water or corrosion at a connector in an exposed mounting point
Unit 2 coded as fitted but missing or disabled
s: Part of the engine sound effect missing
Code stored without other noticeable effect

U02A9.t: Lost Communication With Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A
U02A9.d: Water-cooled charge air coolers need an electric pump in the low-temperature circuit, normally run by the engine controller as a LIN node. U02A9 means the pump has stopped answering. GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG04B) declare it after 2.5 s without a response while the pump is enabled and the supply is 11 to 18 V, and rate it Type A. GM bulletin 23-NA-102 for 2022 to 2025 Silverado, Sierra, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and Escalade with the 3.0 L diesel traces it to water entering the M10 pump connector, with or without LIN code U1345. FCA's Ram 1500 case shows pushed-out terminals at connector D2476A; on 2019 Jeep Renegades without grille shutters, an exposed inline connector corrodes. Mercedes reflashes the PTCU on the GLC. CARB requires charge air cooling to be monitored. Expect a MIL and less boost.
c: Water or corrosion in the pump connector or an open inline connector
Terminals pushed out of the pump connector
Software of the LIN master controller needs an update
Charge air cooler pump electronics failed
s: MIL on
Reduced boost or hesitation at high load
Coolant warning or fan running at full speed on some models

U02AA.t: Lost Communication With Engine Disconnect Clutch
U02AA.d: In a parallel hybrid the engine disconnect clutch sits between crankshaft and motor-generator. Ford's patent US9296380B2 shows the layout: with the clutch open, the electric machine drives alone; closed, it lets the engine add torque or be started, and the controller exchanges signals with the clutch. Honda's two-motor hybrid uses a lockup clutch that couples the engine directly at higher speeds. U02AA concerns designs in which a smart actuator or sensor of the clutch sits on the network, and it is set once that device stops reporting. No manufacturer documents U02AA publicly. CARB 1968.2 treats hybrid components that affect emissions or engine operation as monitored inputs. Without clutch status the hybrid controller cannot coordinate engine starts, so electric-only driving or engine assist is usually blocked.
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the clutch actuator faulty
Harness or connector at the transmission or hybrid module damaged
Software fault in actuator or hybrid controller
s: Hybrid system warning, MIL possible
No electric-only driving or engine runs continuously
Rough or delayed engine starts while driving

U02AB.t: Lost Communication With Vehicle Thermal Management Control Module
U02AB.d: A vehicle thermal management controller coordinates pumps, valves, fans and the refrigerant circuit that keep cabin, battery and drive electronics at temperature; Marelli markets such an integrated module for electric cars, ready for fast-charge preconditioning and OBD compliance. U02AB means this controller has stopped talking to the rest of the vehicle. Audi lists it for the 2025 A5 and Q5 and the 2026 S5: various cluster messages, control unit 00C5 not reachable, U02AB00 with U042200, cured by a software update. For hybrids, CARB 1968.2 requires the electronic parts of battery and inverter thermal management to be monitored. Expect warnings, limited climate control and, on electrified cars, reduced charging or power.
c: Thermal management control module software needs an update
Fuse, supply or ground of the module faulty
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged
Thermal management control module internally failed
s: Several warning messages in the instrument cluster
Climate control or battery conditioning limited
Reduced charging or drive power on electrified models

U02AC.t: Lost Communication With Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A
U02AC.d: Boost control A is the actuator that sets boost, usually a vane or wastegate drive with its own electronics that receives targets and reports status over a data link. U02AC means the engine controller has stopped hearing from it. No manufacturer documents U02AC publicly. GM files the same situation under U010C: its 2025 tables flag the Turbocharger Boost Control Module when frame $099 is missing for over 10 s or $499 for over 9.2 s, with battery above 11 V and the bus itself healthy, and rate it Type B (lamp after two trips). CARB requires boost actuators to be monitored and a lost digital link to carry its own code. Ford's patent on an electric wastegate shows the fallback: a spring keeps the valve closed. Expect a warning lamp and reduced power.
c: Corroded or loose actuator connector, chafed bus wires near the hot turbocharger
Actuator loses its supply or ground (fuse, relay, ground point)
Electronics inside the boost actuator failed, often from heat
Weak 12 V battery causing modules to drop off during cranking
s: Check engine lamp
Noticeably less boost and power, engine in reduced-power mode
Boost actuator values missing or frozen in the scan tool

U02AD.t: Lost Communication With Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B
U02AD.d: A second boost actuator appears on engines with two chargers, either one per cylinder bank or in a staged layout where a high-pressure and a low-pressure stage share the work. BorgWarner's two-stage patent describes a valve that shifts exhaust gradually from the small to the large turbine; its setting decides which stage does the work. U02AD is stored when this B actuator falls silent on the bus while A may still respond. No manufacturer documents U02AD publicly. A Ford two-stage patent shows a typical failsafe: bypass valve fully open, wastegate shut and torque capped so the low-pressure charger cannot overspeed or surge, chiefly at altitude. CARB treats such actuators as monitored boost components. Expect a MIL and limited power.
c: Damaged plug or harness at actuator B, heat-aged insulation
Supply or ground of actuator B interrupted
Replacement actuator not matched or not set up for position B
s: Check engine lamp
Weak pull in the speed range where the second stage normally takes over
Engine power limited

U02AE.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Coolant Pump
U02AE.d: The battery coolant pump circulates coolant through the high-voltage pack. Electrically commutated pumps like Bosch's PAD2 carry their own electronics, take a speed request by PWM or LIN and report back. U02AE applies when such a pump is a bus node and stops answering the controller that runs battery thermal management. No manufacturer documents U02AE publicly. Pumps driven over a plain control line report P0C47 and its siblings instead: GM's 2019 hybrid table checks the HV battery pump line for under 200 mA or over 3 A while on, Type B. Under CARB 1968.2, every electronic input and output used to heat or cool the high-voltage battery must be monitored. Without the pump the pack warms faster, so charge and drive power may be limited. U0694 and U0695 name pumps A and B.
c: Moisture or corrosion in the pump connector, pushed-out terminal
Pump electronics failed (seized rotor, internal fault)
LIN/bus wire, supply fuse or ground of the pump interrupted
Software fault in the battery or thermal management controller
s: Hybrid or battery warning, possibly with the MIL
Reduced charging rate or electric drive power, especially when hot
Battery temperature rises faster than usual

U02AF.t: Lost Communication With Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Position Sensor
U02AF.d: In staged turbocharging a valve in the exhaust path decides how much gas passes through the small high-pressure stage and how much goes around it. GM's patent keeps this valve closed in one load and speed region, modulates it in a transition region and coordinates it with the variable vanes; Ford's two-stage patent opens the bypass fully and cuts torque when valve control is lost. Both depend on knowing the actual valve position. U02AF concerns a position sensor that sends that value digitally, for example as SENT frames, and has stopped doing so. No manufacturer documents U02AF publicly. An analog sensor would report P22D4 to P22D8 instead. CARB expects lost communication of digital inputs to set its own code. The engine typically limits boost and lights the MIL.
c: Heat-damaged connector or wiring at the sensor near the exhaust
Fault at the engine controller input
s: Check engine lamp
Boost limited, sluggish response at low and medium engine speed
Engine in reduced-power mode

U02B0.t: Lost Communication With Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Position Sensor
U02B0.d: This code covers the digital position feedback of the second boost actuator. Its A counterpart, U0656, appears in GM's 2025 engine tables: the ECM reads the vane position as SENT frames and fails the link when frames stop updating for more than 6.25 ms while the line sits steadily low or high, or when message errors pile up, 480 failures in 600 samples, rated Type A (lamp on the first trip). No manufacturer documents U02B0 publicly; it applies wherever actuator B, for example on a second stage or bank, has its own sensor of this kind. Without feedback the controller can no longer hold that actuator in closed loop and falls back to a safe setting. Analog sensors use P2586 to P2590. Expect the MIL and less power.
c: Signal line or connector of the B position sensor damaged or corroded
Position sensor of actuator B failed (often integrated in the actuator)
5 V reference or ground of the sensor missing
s: Check engine lamp on the first trip
Reduced power, boost no longer regulated by actuator B
Higher smoke or emissions on diesel engines

U02B1.t: Lost Communication With Comfort and Convenience Display A
U02B1.d: Comfort and convenience displays are touch screens for climate, seats and similar settings, separate from the main infotainment screen. Stellantis calls them CCDM; on the Jeep Grand Wagoneer a front unit (CCDMF) is joined by a rear unit (CCDMR) for the second row, and the front one can lock out the rear. Which of them counts as A is not published. U02B1 is set when display A no longer answers the module that polls it, so its touch inputs and status vanish from the network. No manufacturer documents U02B1 itself. Field cases of these screens concern firmware: phantom touches cured by newer parts (STAR S228A000013) and wrong massage graphics fixed by a newer part and proxi alignment (S2508000061). Driving is unaffected.
c: Loose or damaged connector behind the display, often after dash work
Fuse, supply or ground of the display interrupted
Display module or its firmware failed
s: Comfort display stays dark or does not react
Climate or seat settings cannot be changed from that screen

U02B2.t: Lost Communication With Comfort and Convenience Display B
U02B2.d: Where a vehicle carries two comfort screens, display B is normally the second one, the rear panel from which back-seat passengers set climate and seats. U02B2 means that unit has dropped off the bus while display A may keep working. No manufacturer documents U02B2 or says which screen carries the letter B. The Jeep Grand Wagoneer shows the layout: a rear display (CCDMR, two part numbers) next to the front one, with a lockout of the rear unit selectable from the front. Stellantis uses that lockout to find which screen issues phantom fan changes and replaces the culprit with a newer firmware part (S228A000013, Rev. A, 2023). Rear wiring runs through the console and seat area, where it can be pinched. Rear occupants lose their own climate and seat controls.
c: Harness to the rear display pinched or unplugged in the console or seat area
Fuse or ground of the rear display interrupted
s: Rear comfort display blank or frozen
Rear climate or seat functions only adjustable from the front, or not at all

U02B3.t: Lost Communication With Driver Monitoring System Module
U02B3.d: The driver monitoring module evaluates an interior camera that follows where the driver looks, how open the eyes are and how the body is held, to judge distraction and drowsiness; the EU's General Safety Regulation makes distraction warning mandatory on all new vehicles from July 2026. U02B3 is logged when this module stops talking to the network. No manufacturer documents U02B3 publicly. Subaru runs a separate DMS control unit on the 2019-2020 Forester and 2020 Legacy and Outback that also stores up to five driver profiles, which technicians back up with SSM4 before service (bulletin 07-175-20). Stellantis names a DMSM among the ADAS modules of the 2022-2025 Grand Cherokee and asks for 90 % battery charge and a 10-minute bus sleep after a deep discharge. Attention warnings and hands-off functions are then lost.
c: Deep battery discharge or replacement left the module offline
Connector at the camera or module loose, e.g. after steering column or dash work
Driver monitoring module or camera failed
s: Driver attention or drowsiness warning unavailable
Hands-free or lane assistance switched off with a service message
Stored driver profiles not recognised

U02B4.t: Lost Communication With Front Radar Module A
U02B4.d: At the front, radar modules measure range and speed of the traffic ahead, which adaptive cruise and automatic braking rely on; corner units also watch crossing traffic. U02B4 means module A no longer answers the assistance controller. No manufacturer documents U02B4 publicly, and letters differ by brand: on the 2026 Mercedes-Benz CLA electric (series 174) the invalid-data partner U05B555 shows that front radar A is the outer left unit, read by controller N62/5. GM uses its own code instead: its 2025 tables report a silent long-range radar as U0235 after 0.25 s, classed as emission-neutral Special Type C without lamp, and switch off adaptive cruise. U02B4 should behave alike: assistance messages, no MIL, normal engine operation. After a bumper repair or radar swap, calibration is often required.
c: Radar connector behind the bumper not latched, corroded or damaged after a collision
Supply, ground or fuse of the radar interrupted
s: Adaptive cruise and collision warning unavailable
Driver assistance message in the cluster

U02B5.t: Lost Communication With Front Radar Module B
U02B5.d: U02B5 is set when front radar B stops answering on the network. It is one of the few codes in this group with a public manufacturer case: on the 2022 Jeep Grand Wagoneer, Stellantis STAR case S2208000105 reports Active Driving Assist as not ready while the central ADAS module (CADM) holds U02B5, because connector D1082A of the front long-range radar (LRRF), mounted behind the bumper, was not fully latched; reseating and locking it cured the fault. At Stellantis, B therefore points to the long-range radar. Mercedes-Benz gives letter B to the right-hand outer radar at the front of the 2026 CLA electric, seen in its invalid-data partner U05B655. Adaptive cruise and the driving assistant stay off until the link returns; the engine is unaffected.
c: Radar connector not fully latched (Stellantis LRRF connector D1082A)
Wiring or radar damaged by a front impact or bumper work
s: Driving assistant reported as not ready
Adaptive cruise and forward collision warning off

U02B6.t: Lost Communication With Rear Radar Module A
U02B6.d: Rear radar modules are hidden behind the bumper corners at the back and supply blind spot detection, which in its advanced form uses one sensor on each side, and rear cross traffic alert. U02B6 means rear radar A has stopped communicating. Stellantis cites the pair U02B6/U02B7 for the rear corner radars of the 2022-2023 Jeep Grand Cherokee, Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer (GPOP 9100222, part 68629572): run the DTC test, then pin-unlock and swap the left and right radars and drive the car to calibrate them; if the fault stays on the same side after the swap, the wiring there is to blame. Which side is A is not stated there; on the 2026 Mercedes-Benz CLA electric, rear radar A is the outer left one. Blind spot warning on that side drops out.
c: Wiring or connector in the rear bumper damaged, e.g. after a parking knock or bumper repair
Rear radar A failed (confirmed when the fault follows a left/right swap)
Water or corrosion in the radar connector
s: Blind spot warning unavailable on one side
Rear cross traffic alert off, assistance message

U02B7.t: Lost Communication With Rear Radar Module B
U02B7.d: U02B7 reports that rear radar B, the second corner unit at the back, has gone silent. Stellantis lists it together with U02B6 for the 2022-2023 Grand Cherokee and Wagoneer models in GPOP review 9100222 and relies on a side-to-side comparison: after a pin unlock the two rear corner radars are exchanged, so the fault either follows the sensor or stays on the harness side. A swapped or new radar must then be calibrated on a drive. Mercedes-Benz assigns rear radar B to the outer right position on the 2026 CLA electric, as its invalid-data code U05B855 shows. Since blind spot and cross traffic systems need both rear corners, a fault on one side usually disables the warning for that side, and some systems shut the whole function off.
c: Harness or connector on the side of radar B damaged or loose
Radar replaced or swapped without completing the calibration drive
s: Blind spot lamp on one side stays off or shows a fault
Rear cross traffic alert unavailable

U02B8.t: Lost Communication With Rear Radar Module C
U02B8.d: A third rear radar is only fitted where the usual left and right corner pair is extended, for instance by a sensor watching straight back or along a long body. No manufacturer documents U02B8 publicly or states where module C sits, and its invalid-data partner U05B9 is equally unpublished. The documented rear letters belong to the corner pair: Mercedes-Benz gives A to the left and B to the right outer sensor at the back of its 2026 CLA electric. U02B8 means module C has dropped off the bus, so functions that rely on its field of view, typically cross traffic or exit warnings, lose part of their coverage while the corner units may keep working. Check its connector and supply first, then the module; after replacement the radar usually needs calibration.
c: Connector or wiring of radar C damaged or unplugged
Supply or ground of radar C missing
s: Rear assistance functions partly unavailable, assistance message
Cross traffic or exit warning restricted

U02B9.t: Lost Communication With Rear Radar Module D
U02B9.d: Rear radar module D completes a set of four rear sensors, a layout that only a few vehicles with extended rear sensing use. No manufacturer documents U02B9 publicly; there is no published fitting position, timeout or lamp rating. The code states that module D no longer responds on the bus. As with its siblings, the cause lies in wiring, connector or supply more often than in the radar itself, and Bosch radar systems show why one silent unit rarely blinds the car completely: rear warnings such as cross traffic alert draw on several sensors, so the assistance controller withdraws only the affected functions or reports limited availability. The engine lamp stays off, and driving itself is unaffected.
c: Wiring or connector of radar D damaged
Fuse, supply or ground of radar D interrupted
s: Some rear assistance functions unavailable
Message about limited driver assistance

U02BA.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Electronics Coolant Pump B
U02BA.d: Hybrid and electric cars cool their power electronics, such as inverter, DC/DC converter and on-board charger, with electric pumps that hang on a LIN line and report their state to a thermal or vehicle controller. U02BA means pump B of that loop no longer answers. No manufacturer documents U02BA publicly or says which pump bears the letter B. Stellantis shows the layout on the 2024-2025 Dodge Charger and Jeep Wagoneer S: three identical pumps, each with its own software and its own LIN bus to the EVCU; without a master message a pump falls into an emergency mode at full speed and can drain the 12 V battery (STAR S2508000056). GM's 2011 Volt wired pump A directly and rated its circuit fault P0CE9 as Type B. With pump B silent the electronics run hotter and drive power may be cut.
c: Loose or corroded pump connector, open or shorted LIN wire
Pump power supply or ground missing (fuse, relay, ground point)
Pump electronics failed or pump seized
Pump of another position fitted or controller software outdated
s: Warning for the hybrid/electric drive system, MIL possible
Reduced drive or charging power when the electronics warm up
Pump running constantly or not at all, 12 V battery drained

U02BB.t: Lost Communication With EVAP System Purge Pump
U02BB.d: The purge pump actively pushes fuel vapour from the charcoal canister into the intake, which turbocharged engines need because they often lack intake vacuum. GM fits it to models such as Blazer, Encore GX, XT4 and Silverado 1500 as a separate unit with its own electronics, linked to the ECM by LIN. GM's 2025 engine tables describe U02BB directly: the ECM marks the pump as lost when its response frame has been absent for at least 250 ms, checked once the LIN channel has been active for 3 s at 11 to 18 V; GM rates it Type B, meaning the lamp waits for a second failing trip. Pump failures were common enough that GM extended coverage to 15 years/150,000 miles (N242484740), there with the P146x pump codes. While the pump is mute the canister is not purged and evaporative tests are suspended.
c: Purge pump electronics failed (known GM failure, extended coverage)
LIN wire or pump connector damaged, corroded or unplugged
No supply from the actuator or powertrain relay, poor ground
s: Check engine light after two drives
Further EVAP or purge pump codes stored
Possible fuel smell; driving itself usually normal

U02BC.t: Lost Communication With Localization and Mapping Module
U02BC.d: The localization and mapping module merges satellite positioning, correction data and vehicle motion signals with a detailed map, so that hands-free or automated driving knows its lane and the road ahead; Bosch offers such a GNSS-based unit for driver assistance and automation. U02BC means this module has stopped communicating. Stellantis documents it for the 2024-2026 Jeep Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer (STAR S2508000095): U02BC-00 appears for the GNMM together with Ethernet time-sync and link-status faults toward the central ADAS module, blind spot alerts and other assistance functions shut off, and modules replaced for it proved healthy. The cause was an Ethernet harness routed too tight, straining its connectors; the fix is correct routing or a new harness, never a repaired cable. No MIL.
c: Ethernet harness routed too tight, connector strained or not latched
Bent or damaged Ethernet connector pins
Module supply missing or module internally faulty
s: Blind spot alert unavailable, service message in the cluster
Hands-free or advanced driver assistance disabled
Several ADAS and Ethernet codes stored at once

U02BD.t: Lost Communication With Night Vision Control Module
U02BD.d: The night vision control module evaluates an infrared camera, either a passive thermal unit that sees body heat or an active near-infrared system, picks out pedestrians and animals and passes image and warnings to the cluster or head-up display. U02BD is stored when a listening module, usually the body controller, hears nothing more from it. Jeep documents the case for the 2021-2023 Grand Cherokee including the 4xe (STAR S2208000163): the BCM holds U02BD-00, the cluster logs B0125-02 for the night vision module, and the system stays dark. Causes were female terminals in harness connector D3944A that were misaligned or held back by a solder spot, so the module's pins bent or never made contact. Realigning terminals or a connector kit cures it; the module is replaced only for lasting pin damage. Driving is unaffected.
c: Misaligned or not fully seated terminals in the module connector
Bent pins on the night vision module
Module supply missing or module internally faulty
s: Night vision display stays dark or the function is unavailable
Pedestrian or animal warnings at night are missing
Matching night vision code stored in the instrument cluster

U02BE.t: Lost Communication With Trailer Backup Assist Control Module
U02BE.d: The trailer backup assist module steers the tow vehicle in reverse so the trailer follows a curve the driver chooses with a knob; with Ford's Pro Trailer Backup Assist the hitch angle comes from a target sticker filmed by the backup camera or from a trailer-mounted sensor. Ram names its unit TRSCM. For the 2021 Ram 1500, STAR case S2108000067 shows U02BE active in the ABS, power steering and engine controllers while the TRSCM is absent from the CAN C bus; the driver gets a throttle-control service warning, the MIL and at times Rear Park Assist unavailable. The trigger was module software: cutting its power via fuse 53 or the connector restarts it, an update was planned, and a new module does not help. Otherwise only the assist is lost.
c: Module software hangs and the unit drops off the bus (Ram 1500, 2021)
Fuse, supply or connector of the module faulty
CAN wiring to the module damaged
s: Trailer backup assist unavailable
Ram: throttle control message, MIL and rear park assist unavailable
Code stored in several modules at once

U02BF.t: Lost Communication With Interior Lighting Control Module B
U02BF.d: Many cars spread cabin lighting over several controllers; module B is a second unit beside module A (U024A), for example for ambient strips or a rear zone. Such nodes are usually LIN slaves of the body computer, a single-wire bus of up to about 19.2 kbit/s in which the master can detect nodes that fail. U02BF means module B no longer replies. No manufacturer documents U02BF publicly or says which unit carries the letter B. Stellantis illustrates how a separate lighting unit is serviced: on 2023-2026 Wagoneer models and the 2023-2027 Grand Cherokee the auxiliary/ambient lighting module must match the vehicle configuration with two or three seat rows; if PROXI is wrong, it is recoded and hard-reset instead of replaced (GPOP 9100834). Expect dark or fixed-colour zones; driving is not affected.
c: LIN wire or connector of module B loose, damaged or corroded
Vehicle configuration does not match the module, module not reset after coding
Lighting module internally faulty or without supply
s: Some cabin or ambient lights stay dark
Colour or brightness of a light zone can no longer be changed

U02C0.t: Lost Communication With Active Radiator Air Flow Control Module A
U02C0.d: J2012 gives the active radiator air flow module its own codes, separate from the active grille shutter modules U0284 and U0285. A Hyundai patent shows the kind of hardware meant: a pair of flaps between bumper intake and radiator, fed by an air guide, whose opening meters the cooling air. U02C0 means module A of such a system has stopped answering the engine or thermal controller. No manufacturer documents U02C0 publicly. Closely related shutter cases show how makers treat the loss: the 2026 Ram 1500 lights the MIL with U0285 for its lower shutter (STAR S2523000095), and Subaru traced U0284 on the 2017-2019 Impreza to water and corrosion at connector B63 (bulletin 07-140-18). Expect a warning lamp and flaps held in a safe position.
c: Water ingress and corrosion at the front-end connector or harness
Flap unit or wiring damaged by stones or a minor collision
Actuator electronics of module A failed
s: Check engine light or warning lamp
Cooling flaps no longer move, slightly higher consumption

U02C1.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Electronics Coolant Pump C
U02C1.d: U02C1 concerns the third networked pump of the electronics cooling loop, pump C, which has gone quiet on its data line. Vehicles with three such pumps assign them to different branches, and which branch pump C serves is the maker's choice; no manufacturer documents U02C1 publicly. Stellantis' 2024-2025 EV platform shows why the pumps must be kept apart: the units look and fit alike, yet each carries its own part number and software so the EVCU can address it on its own LIN bus, and only the position on the bracket and a symbol tell them apart (STAR S2508000056). Bosch markets electric pumps of this class for cooling power electronics in hybrid and electric cars. Under CARB 1968.2 a mute digital input needs its own fault code. If its branch overheats, power is reduced.
c: Pump connector or LIN wire faulty
Look-alike pumps swapped between positions during service
s: Warning for the electric drive or charging system
Reduced power or charging rate under load or heat
Cooling fans running hard

U0300.d: U0300 is the general entry of the U03xx group: the module storing it finds that its own software, calibration or configuration does not fit, or that the modules around it run versions that do not belong together. It typically follows a module swap or flash. Ford's 2012 OBD summary uses it for a software version mismatch between electronic throttle processors, without MIL on Gen2 and with MIL on Gen3/Gen4. Volkswagen names it beside U0301/U0302 after ECM replacement on 2013-2018 gasoline cars (tip 01-18-10TT), Nissan in the TCM of the 2021-2023 Rogue after TCM or CVT replacement (NTB23-085), Mazda as U0300:57 in the BCM after a software update (SA-003/22), Jeep in the air suspension module with MIL (08-159-23). Effects range from a lamp to no start.
c: Module replaced without loading the latest software and configuration
Partner module left on an older software level after an update
Wrong module or part number fitted (e.g. with a replacement gearbox)
Programming aborted due to low voltage
s: Warning lamp or MIL, depending on the module
Function of the affected module limited, e.g. suspension levelling or throttle
Code appears right after module replacement or software update

U0301.d: U0301 means a module has found that the engine or powertrain controller carries software or a calibration it cannot work with, most often after the ECM was replaced, flashed or coded for another variant. GM's 2011 Saab 9-5 manual lists U0301 as a setup fault: tested between 9 and 16 V while the data link works, triggered by a module left unconfigured after fitting, repaired by programming rather than wiring work. Volkswagen names U0301 on 2013-2018 gasoline models after ECM replacement: both ECM and TCM must be on the latest software, then configured (tip 01-18-10TT). Volvo reports CEM-U030141 after service software downloads on 2015-2019 cars and calls it harmless. As CARB demands a unique CAL ID per emission calibration, the mismatch is emission-relevant; MIL and drivability limits are possible.
c: ECM/PCM replaced or flashed without configuration
ECM and TCM on different software levels after an update
ECM coded for the wrong variant or modified by tuning
Volvo: entry left behind by a service software download
s: Check engine light or other warning lamps
Gearbox or other systems in a restricted mode
Code stored in several modules after ECM work

U0302.t: Software Incompatibility With Transmission Control Module
U0302.d: U0302 points to a software or calibration conflict between the transmission controller and its partners. Volkswagen's 2014 Touareg and CC emission specification books show a typical trigger: the engine controller sets U0302 when it is coded for the wrong gearbox type, for instance it receives automatic transmission frames while coded for a manual, or is coded automatic in a manual car. CARB 1968.2 names this very design, a control unit holding manual and automatic variants that lights the MIL when the wrong one is active. GM's 2011 Saab 9-5 treats U0302 as a configuration fault checked at 9-16 V without wiring tests, and the Volkswagen tip 01-18-10TT names it among codes after an engine controller swap. U0101 stands for lost contact, U0402 for invalid data. Expect a MIL and possibly gearbox limp mode.
c: Engine controller coded for the wrong transmission type
TCM or ECM replaced or updated without matching the partner
s: Check engine light on
Harsh or missing shifts, transmission in limp mode
Code appears after engine or transmission controller work

U0303.t: Software Incompatibility With Transfer Case Control Module
U0303.d: U0303 reports that the transfer case control module, which engages 4WD and selects the low range, runs software or a calibration another module rejects. No manufacturer documents U0303 publicly. The mechanism is explained in GM's Saab 9-5 manual of 2011: certain units need software, serial numbers or option data loaded, and if that step is skipped after fitting, the matching U code follows, with the test enabled between 9 and 16 V and no circuit check involved. When the same module goes missing on the bus, GM's 2025 tables rate the result, U0102, as Type C, emission-neutral and without MIL, which suggests a similar rating here. Expect a 4WD warning and refused range changes until the module is programmed. U0403 covers invalid data.
c: Transfer case module replaced without programming or setup
Software variant does not match the transfer case or drivetrain
Engine, transmission or body controller updated, transfer case module not
s: 4WD or service 4WD warning
Shifting between 2WD, 4WD or low range refused
Code appears after transfer case module work

U0304.t: Software Incompatibility With Gear Shift Control Module
U0304.d: U0304 is stored when a control unit, usually the transmission controller, finds that the software or calibration identity of the gear shift control module does not match what it expects. GM's generic U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) treats such codes as configuration faults: checked at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, no circuit test, cured by setup or programming. Allison uses U0304 for its 6th-generation controls as Gear Shift Module 1 Incompatible: a 6th-generation push-button selector does not work with a 5th-generation TCM, and the selector must match the TCM calibration; U0333 covers selector 2. U0103 means lost contact, U0404 invalid data from the same module. The driver may be unable to select a range.
c: Shift selector generation or type does not match the TCM calibration (e.g. after replacement)
Shift module or TCM replaced or flashed without setup
Software update aborted, wrong file loaded
s: Gear ranges cannot be selected or the selector does not respond
Transmission warning or code shown on the selector display
Code appears right after a selector or TCM was replaced

U0305.t: Software Incompatibility With Cruise Control Module
U0305.d: On current cars the cruise control module is mostly the radar unit of adaptive cruise control, which asks engine and brakes for speed changes to hold a chosen gap. U0305 is stored when another controller finds that this unit carries software or a calibration that does not belong to the vehicle, typically after a radar swap or a partial update. No manufacturer documents U0305 publicly. Land Rover shows the underlying problem: on 2019 Range Rover Sport mild hybrids with the 3.0 L Ingenium six, the CCM could leave the plant with a wrong calibration and had to be reflashed before handover (N343NAS1). CARB names cruise control that switches itself off after a fault as a case of an emissions-neutral reaction, so no MIL is expected. U0104 means lost contact, U0405 invalid data. Cruise and distance functions stay unavailable.
c: Radar/cruise module replaced or swapped from another car without programming
Wrong calibration from the factory or after an incomplete software update
Engine, brake or gateway module updated without the cruise module
s: Cruise control and adaptive distance control cannot be switched on
Driver assistance warning in the cluster, often also collision warning off
Code appears right after radar replacement, windscreen or bumper work

U0306.t: Software Incompatibility With Fuel Injector Control Module
U0306.d: Some diesels fire their injectors through a separate fuel injector control module that raises the voltage and opens each injector when the engine controller commands it; Ford's 6.0 L Power Stroke used such a FICM at about 48 V, and GM's 2005 Duramax table watches its injector driver by a CAN status bit that must toggle every 20 ms. U0306 means the controllers judge the module's software or calibration as not matching, for example after a used or remanufactured FICM was fitted. Ford's 2014 OBD-II code interpretation carries U0306 without its MIL marker; other makers may rate it differently, because injection timing and quantity decide emissions. U0105 stands for lost contact, U0406 for invalid data. Depending on the strategy the engine runs roughly, drops into reduced power or will not start.
c: Used, remanufactured or wrong-variant injector module fitted without programming
Engine controller reflashed or replaced while the injector module kept old software
Programming of the injector module interrupted, e.g. by low battery voltage
s: Hard start or no start, engine may crank without firing
Rough running, misfire or reduced power
Further injector or injector module codes stored

U0307.t: Software Incompatibility With Glow Plug Control Module 1
U0307.d: Glow plug control module 1 switches the glow plugs of a diesel and exchanges data with the engine controller, usually over LIN. U0307 means that the controller does not accept the module's software. Volkswagen's 2014 Touareg TDI specification book sets it when the software check carried out over the LIN message fails. Ford's diesel OBD summaries of 2015 and 2023 list U0307 among the network faults and trip it when the glow module reports that it has fallen back to a safe glow mode; Ford's 2014 code interpretation marks it as a MIL code. GM tells technicians to check and update the module software on 2017 6.6 L L5P trucks after any glow plug replacement (PIP5524). CARB requires glow plug function to be monitored. Expect hard cold starts, white smoke and a lit MIL. U0106 means lost contact, U0407 invalid data.
c: Glow plug module software outdated or not matching the engine controller
Replacement glow module of another part number or engine variant fitted
Engine controller updated or replaced without updating the glow module
Disturbed LIN line corrupting the software check
s: Long cranking or no start in cold weather
White smoke and rough idle after a cold start
MIL and glow plug warning lamp on

U0308.t: Software Incompatibility With Throttle Actuator Control Module
U0308.d: U0308 flags that the throttle actuator control module carries software or a calibration that the engine controller does not accept. In most current cars throttle control lives inside the ECM/PCM, so a separate TAC module and this code are rare; no manufacturer documents U0308 publicly. Ford shows how such a mismatch is handled when the logic is integrated: its 2012 OBD summary files a software version mismatch between the electronic-throttle processors under U0300, non-MIL on Gen2 and MIL on Gen3/Gen4 throttle systems. GM's U03xx procedure links these codes to a module that was not configured after installation. Throttle control affects emissions, so CARB demands monitoring and a MIL is likely. U0107 means lost contact, U0408 invalid data.
c: Throttle or engine control module replaced or flashed without matching software
Wrong or outdated calibration loaded, e.g. by an engine tune
Programming aborted due to low voltage
s: Check engine light on
Reduced power or limp mode with limited throttle opening
Code appears after module replacement or programming

U0309.t: Software Incompatibility With Alternative Fuel Control Module
U0309.d: An alternative fuel control module runs the gaseous fuel side of a bi-fuel or dedicated LPG or CNG engine and works alongside the gasoline or diesel controller. CARB counts such engines as alternate-fueled vehicles that fall under OBD II. U0309 is set when the partners find the module's software or calibration does not match theirs, for example after a conversion system or one of the controllers was updated on its own. Ford's 2014 code interpretation lists U0309 with the MIL marker. Roush CleanTech's propane systems for Ford E- and F-Series trucks show the arrangement: a smart relay module of the propane side talks to the Ford PCM and keeps its own fault list, including an internal software incompatibility code. U0108 means lost contact, U0409 invalid data. Expect a MIL and a fallback to the base fuel or rough running on gas.
c: Gas system module software not released for the current engine controller calibration
PCM/ECM reflashed by a dealer without updating the gas system module
Gas system module replaced with a unit of another variant
s: Engine stays on or switches back to gasoline/diesel
MIL and gas system warning on
Rough running or hesitation in gas mode

U030A.t: Software Incompatibility With Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Control Module
U030A.d: In some evaporative systems a dedicated module with its own pump or valve, pressure switch and electronics runs the leak test. U030A means that controller has found the module's software or calibration not to fit. No manufacturer documents U030A publicly. Kia's 2017-2019 Niro hybrid uses such a natural vacuum leak detection unit: its lost-communication code U029F00 lit the MIL, and bulletin PS593 traced it to a damaged signal wire at the NVLD connector. Ford's 2014 code interpretation gives U029F the MIL marker as well. CARB demands the leak monitor, so a mismatch that blocks or falsifies it is emission-relevant and a MIL is probable. The car drives normally; the EVAP readiness flag may remain incomplete, which can fail an inspection. U029F is the lost-contact code.
c: Leak detection module replaced with a unit of another part number
Engine controller reprogrammed with a calibration that expects other module software
Damaged signal wire corrupting the identification exchange
s: MIL on, usually without any drivability change
EVAP readiness monitor not completed
Further EVAP leak test codes may follow

U030B.t: Software Incompatibility With Glow Plug Control Module 2
U030B.d: U030B is the counterpart of U0307 for a second glow plug control module, used where an engine splits its glow plugs between two drivers, say one per bank. It is stored when the engine controller rejects the software or calibration identity of module 2, typically after only one of the two units was replaced or flashed. No manufacturer documents U030B publicly. A GM patent explains the dialogue behind it: glow plug faults are judged from several messages passed between engine and glow controller, with a strategy that changes with how long the plugs have been on in a drive cycle. GM also asks for the glow module software to be brought up to date after glow plug work (PIP5524). CARB requires glow plugs to be checked for proper response. U019C stands for lost contact, U049D for invalid data. Cold starts suffer; a MIL is likely.
c: Only glow module 2 (or only module 1) replaced, software levels now differ
Module of another part number or engine variant installed in position 2
Engine controller updated without the second glow module
s: Hard cold start, uneven running until warm
White smoke after starting in the cold
MIL and glow plug warning on

U030C.t: Software Incompatibility With Reductant Quality Module
U030C.d: The reductant quality module tells the SCR system whether the tank holds proper urea solution (DEF/AdBlue); in many trucks it sits in the tank unit together with level and temperature sensing. U030C means the engine or dosing controller has rejected its software or calibration, as after a tank or sensor replacement with the wrong part number. Ford's 2014 code interpretation flags U030C as a MIL code; Ford's 2023 diesel summary calls the module RDQM and treats 5 s without its frames as lost communication (U02A2). CARB lets makers skip a direct reductant quality monitor only if an inducement strategy prevents long operation on poor fluid and its inputs, such as this sensor, are monitored themselves. Hence a MIL, DEF warnings and, if left unresolved, speed limits. U05A3 covers invalid data.
c: DEF tank unit or quality sensor of a different part number installed
Engine or dosing controller updated, quality module left on old software
Programming interrupted or wrong file loaded
s: MIL and DEF/AdBlue system warning
Countdown to speed limitation or no-restart shown
Code appears after tank, heater or sensor replacement

U030D.t: Software Incompatibility With NOx Sensor A
U030D.d: NOx sensor A is in most layouts the upstream sensor ahead of the SCR catalyst; its own control unit measures NOx and oxygen and sends both on CAN. U030D shows that the engine controller does not accept the software or calibration of this smart sensor, a frequent result of fitting a sensor meant for another engine or model year. Ford's 2014 code interpretation lists U030D with the MIL marker. Ford's 2023 diesel summary also shows how closely these sensors are checked: missing frames from sensor A count after 1 s, and U059E is set when the sensor's calibration verification number does not reach the ECU. CARB requires such a CVN to prove that emission software is valid for the vehicle. SCR dosing and catalyst monitoring depend on this signal, so a MIL is expected. U029D means lost contact, U030E covers sensor B.
c: Replacement NOx sensor of another part number or software level fitted
Aftermarket sensor whose identification the controller rejects
Engine controller updated to a calibration that expects a newer sensor
s: MIL on, SCR or emission system warning
NOx and SCR readiness monitors incomplete
Possible DEF countdown or reduced power on some trucks

U030E.t: Software Incompatibility With NOx Sensor B
U030E.d: NOx sensor B is usually the downstream sensor after the SCR catalyst, the one whose reading reveals how well the catalyst converts and guides the correction of urea dosing. U030E is stored when its software or calibration identity does not match what the engine controller expects, for instance after a replacement sensor with another part number or a controller update the sensor does not support. Ford's 2014 code interpretation gives U030E the MIL marker, just as for sensor A (U030D). In Ford's 2023 diesel summary sensor B is regarded as lost after about 1 s without frames (U029E), and the 2015 summary also lists invalid data from it (U059F). Without a trusted downstream value the SCR efficiency test cannot run, so readiness stays open; a MIL and, depending on the market, DEF-related warnings follow.
c: Downstream NOx sensor replaced with a part of another number or software level
Upstream and downstream sensors swapped or coded to the wrong position
Engine controller update requiring a newer sensor version
s: MIL and SCR/emission warning
SCR efficiency monitor never completes
Possible DEF countdown on some trucks

U030F.t: Software Incompatibility With Reductant Control Module
U030F.d: The reductant control module runs the urea side of an SCR system: pump, dosing valve, line heaters and level reading. U030F means the engine controller has found that this module's software or calibration does not belong with its own, for example after either unit was swapped or reflashed. No manufacturer documents U030F publicly, but how software-dependent the module is can be seen in bulletins. GM's 2018 Cruze diesel needed a reflash of the K115 reductant control module because the DEF level shown did not update after refilling (18-NA-058), and FCA reprogrammed the dosing control unit of 2016 Ram 2500/3500 Cummins trucks, replacing it where necessary (25-003-17). Because SCR controls NOx, a MIL and, under CARB inducement rules, power or speed limits are possible. U010E is lost contact, U040F invalid data.
c: Dosing/reductant control unit software outdated or not released for the engine calibration
Dosing unit or DEF tank assembly with integrated controller replaced by another variant
Engine controller reprogrammed without the reductant control module
s: MIL and DEF/SCR warning in the cluster
Wrong or frozen DEF level display
Countdown to speed limit or reduced power

U0310.t: Software Incompatibility With Fuel Pump Control Module
U0310.d: A fuel pump control module drives the in-tank pump at variable speed so that the pressure requested by the engine controller is reached. U0310 is set when the two controllers do not accept each other's software or calibration. No manufacturer documents U0310 publicly. GM's 2013 Cadillac ATS 2.5 L shows how tightly the pair belongs together: against a rough idle GM released matching software for the ECM and the FPCM and had both reprogrammed, each in its own session (PI1092B).
