Ford's 2014 code interpretation already gives the lost-contact code U0109 the MIL marker, and Roush CleanTech's propane trucks use two pump modules, A and B, so the letter in related codes matters. A mismatched pump module can deliver the wrong pressure, causing lean running, misfires or a no-start; a MIL is likely. U0410 covers invalid data.
c: Replacement or aftermarket pump module with software for another application
Engine controller reprogrammed, matching FPCM calibration not loaded
Interrupted programming of the pump module
s: Hard start or no start, stalling
Hesitation, lean running or misfire under load
MIL and fuel pressure codes

U0311.t: Software Incompatibility With Drive Motor Control Module
U0311.d: The drive motor control module, often built into the inverter, turns battery power into phase currents for an electric traction motor and reports torque and speed. U0311 means a partner, typically the hybrid or vehicle controller, rejects the module's software or calibration. No manufacturer documents U0311 publicly. GM's Ultium cars show how version-sensitive these units are: for the 2023-2024 Lyriq and 2024 Blazer EV and Equinox EV, PIP6041 cures hesitation, a false MIL with a fluid temperature code and other faults by reprogramming the K107 drive motor control modules, which update in sequence when both need it; PIP6022 blames older K107 software on the 2025 Silverado EV and Sierra EV for a spurious U11FD. CARB covers hybrid drive components in OBD. Expect reduced or no propulsion. U0110 means lost contact, U0411 invalid data.
c: Drive motor control module software behind the level the vehicle controller expects
Only one of two drive motor modules (front/rear) updated or replaced
Inverter or drive unit replaced without programming and setup
s: Reduced propulsion power or vehicle will not drive
Hybrid/EV system warning and MIL
Jerky acceleration or one-pedal driving switched off

U0312.t: Software Incompatibility With Battery Energy Control Module A
U0312.d: Battery energy control module A supervises the high-voltage or 48 V battery: cell voltages, temperatures, current, state of charge and contactors. U0312 is stored when a partner, usually the hybrid or vehicle controller, refuses the BECM's software or calibration, for example after a pack or module replacement. Ford's 2014 code interpretation marks U0312 as a MIL code. For the lost-contact code GM shows that software alone can cure it: on the 2011-2013 Volt, U0111 should be fixed by loading the latest BECM calibration rather than swapping the module (PIC5829). Without accepted battery data the drive system restricts charging and discharging; CARB includes hybrid components in OBD monitoring. Expect a hybrid warning, MIL and less electric operation. U0111 means lost contact, U0412 invalid data, U0313 covers module B.
c: BECM calibration outdated or not matching the hybrid controller software
Battery pack or BECM replaced without programming
Hybrid or vehicle controller updated without the BECM
s: Hybrid/EV system warning and MIL
Electric driving or charging limited or unavailable
Engine runs more often in hybrids

U0313.t: Software Incompatibility With Battery Energy Control Module B
U0313.d: Battery energy control module B is a second battery controller, for instance a sub-unit inside the pack that measures part of the cells for the main battery management. U0313 means the network does not accept its software or calibration. No manufacturer documents U0313 publicly. Mitsubishi's 2018 Outlander PHEV has such a pair: the main BMU expects frames from a sub-BMU and records U0112 after 0.3 s without them. Bulletin TSB-18-54-005 shows that the sub-unit's software matters on its own: a wrongly programmed sub-BMU took electrical noise for a fault in the leak detection circuit, lit several warning lamps and held the car to 60 km/h until it was reflashed. A mismatch flagged by U0313 can have similar effects: hybrid warning, MIL and limited power. U0312 covers module A, U0413 invalid data from module B.
c: Sub-module software outdated or faulty, newer level required
Module B or battery section replaced with a different variant
Main battery management updated without module B
s: Several warning lamps including MIL and hybrid system warning
Power or speed limited until the next restart
Electric operation or charging restricted

U0314.t: Software Incompatibility With Four-Wheel Drive Clutch Control Module
U0314.d: The four-wheel-drive clutch control module decides how much torque an on-demand coupling, such as a Haldex-type multi-plate clutch, passes to the secondary axle, using wheel speed, torque and brake data from other units. U0314 is stored when one of those partners rejects the module's software or calibration, for instance after the coupling, its controller or the engine controller was replaced or updated separately. No manufacturer documents U0314 publicly. Kia shows that the coupling logic lives in software: on 2024-2025 Seltos AWD it updates the 4WD software because drive to the rear wheels could drop out, with a Check AWD warning, the MIL and codes P1958 and P1960 (bulletin ELE374, SA605). With U0314 the car usually falls back to front- or rear-wheel drive and shows a warning. U0114 means lost contact, U0414 invalid data.
c: Coupling or its controller replaced without programming or coding
AWD software level not matching engine, transmission or ABS software
Used module from a vehicle with another drivetrain variant
s: AWD/4WD warning, drive only on one axle
Reduced traction on slippery roads or when pulling away
Code appears after coupling or controller work

U0315.t: Software Incompatibility With Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module
U0315.d: U0315 concerns the ABS control module, which on most cars also hosts traction and stability control. A partner module stores the code when the brake controller's software, calibration or option configuration does not fit, typically after a module was replaced without setup. GM documents it under its own name: the 2011 Saab 9-5 and 9-4X code lists give U0315 to the electronic brake control module, and the procedure runs whenever supply voltage lies within 9-16 V and the bus is operating; there is no circuit test, the fix is configuration or programming. On the 2016-2017 Cadillac CT6 a new EBCM calibration stopped false U0435 entries against the rear steering (17-NA-130). ABS, traction and stability warnings may light while basic braking remains; the MIL is normally off. U0121 means lost contact, U0415 invalid data.
c: ABS/EBCM replaced and not configured or programmed for the vehicle
Used unit from a vehicle with different equipment or drivetrain
Engine, steering or chassis module updated to a level the ABS unit does not support
s: ABS, traction control and stability warning lamps on
Stability and assistance functions switched off
Code present right after brake module replacement

U0316.t: Software Incompatibility With Vehicle Dynamics Control Module
U0316.d: U0316 means the vehicle dynamics control module, the electronic stability control unit, reports a software or calibration identity another module does not accept, typically after it was replaced or reflashed without setup. GM's U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) runs at 9-16 V and sets such codes when a module is not configured properly; GM itself uses U0315 for its electronic brake module. Mazda uses U0316 differently: in 2014-2015 Mazda3, Mazda6 and CX-5 bulletins U0316:09 sits in a receiving module and stands for an error signal received from the DSC unit, there caused by a failed SAS module. So on a Mazda it is a follow-up code, not a software issue. U0122 means lost contact, U0416 invalid data. Stability control may switch off; MIL normally off.
c: Stability control module replaced or flashed without setup/coding
Software variant does not match vehicle equipment
Mazda: fault in DSC or SAS module reported to other units (U0316:09)
s: Stability or traction control warning light on
Driver assistance functions unavailable
Code stored in several modules at once

U0317.t: Software Incompatibility With Park Brake Control Module
U0317.d: U0317 tells that the park brake control module of an electric parking brake runs software or a calibration another module does not accept. Following GM's generic U03xx logic it is checked at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, sets when a module is not configured properly and needs no wiring test; the cure is setup or programming. No manufacturer documents this J2012 meaning publicly. Mitsubishi reassigns the number: for the 2017 Outlander (TSB-17-23-001) U0317 stands for a CAN time-out with the EPB ECU, which a wrongly programmed TCM stored as P0317 instead; a TCM reflash corrects it. On such vehicles read U0317 as a communication fault. U0128 means lost contact, U0417 invalid data. Park brake warnings or disabled auto functions are possible; no MIL.
c: Park brake module replaced or flashed without setup
Mitsubishi: CAN time-out to the EPB ECU, e.g. connector unplugged
Software level of park brake module and partner module do not match
s: Park brake warning light or message
Automatic release or hill hold not working
Code appears after park brake module work

U0318.t: Software Incompatibility With Brake System Control Module
U0318.d: U0318 indicates a software or calibration mismatch with the brake system control module, a unit J2012 separates from the ABS module (U0315) and the vehicle dynamics module (U0316). Which box that is depends on the maker; on brake-by-wire systems or electromechanical boosters it is often the controller that builds brake pressure. GM's U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) describes the trigger: a module not configured properly, checked at 9-16 V, no external circuit involved. No manufacturer documents U0318 publicly, so the exact owner of the code must come from the vehicle's own manual. It mostly appears after a module swap or a broken flash. U0129 means lost contact, U0418 invalid data. Brake warnings and reduced assist functions are possible; MIL usually off.
c: Brake system module replaced or flashed without setup
Software level does not match the ABS/ESC or engine controller
Programming aborted due to low battery voltage
s: Brake system warning light or message
Brake assist or regenerative braking functions unavailable
Code appears after brake module service

U0319.t: Software Incompatibility With Steering Effort Control Module
U0319.d: U0319 is set when the steering effort control module, the unit that varies steering assist, for example with road speed, reports a software or calibration identity the network does not accept. J2012 keeps it apart from the power steering control module, which has its own code U0320. GM's generic U03xx description fits: the check runs at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, and a module that was not configured after installation sets the code; the repair is programming, not wiring. No manufacturer documents U0319 publicly, so which steering unit carries the code is maker-specific. U0130 means lost contact, U0419 invalid data from the same module. Steering may feel heavier or less speed-dependent, a steering warning may light, the MIL normally stays off.
c: Steering module replaced or flashed without setup
Software variant does not match vehicle configuration
Programming aborted or wrong file loaded
s: Steering heavier or assist no longer speed-dependent
Steering warning light or message
Code appears after steering module work

U031A.t: Software Incompatibility With Transmission Range Control Module
U031A.d: In shift-by-wire drivelines the transmission range control module carries out the driver's range request by mechanically engaging park, reverse, neutral or drive. U031A means a partner, such as the transmission or shifter controller, rejects its software or calibration. Ford's 2014 code interpretation lists U031A without the MIL marker. On the 2017 Buick LaCrosse and Cadillac XT5, GM bulletin 16-NA-373 traced a MIL with a Service Transmission message and P17xx codes to a calibration anomaly in the TRCM and cured it by reprogramming; separately, program 17075 replaced units whose actuator gear broke and left the car stuck in Park. A mismatched TRCM can likewise refuse range changes or default to Park. U019E means lost contact, U049F invalid data, U0304 a software mismatch with the shifter itself.
c: TRCM calibration outdated or faulty, newer release available
TRCM/range actuator replaced without programming and learn procedure
Transmission or shifter controller updated without the TRCM
s: Service transmission or shift system warning
Range changes refused, car stays in Park
Wrong range shown in the display

U031B.t: Software Incompatibility With DC/DC Converter Control Module A
U031B.d: DC/DC converter module A moves energy between two voltage levels, in hybrids and mild hybrids typically from the high-voltage or 48 V battery to the 12 V system. U031B means another module does not accept the converter's software. Audi documents it for the 2022-2023 A3, S3 and RS 3 with 48 V mild hybrid: after a 48 V battery replacement, battery management 2 (J1120) may store U031B00, because the updated battery (5WA.915.107.B) runs a validation check of voltage converter A7 that converter software 5WA.959.663 does not answer. With exactly these two part numbers Audi says the code can be ignored (TSB 2068368/1). On other combinations a genuine mismatch can stop the 12 V supply from being charged, so watch for battery or charging warnings. U0298 means lost contact. The MIL normally stays off.
c: 48 V/HV battery or its management replaced by a newer version the converter software does not support
DC/DC converter replaced without programming or coding
Converter software behind the level of the other powertrain modules
s: Often no symptom, code found during service
12 V battery or charging warning possible
Mild hybrid functions such as start-stop or recuperation limited

U031C.t: Software Incompatibility With Brake System Control Module B
U031C.d: In GM's hybrid OBD tables brake system control module B is the electromechanical brake booster (Bosch iBooster), which builds brake pressure without engine vacuum and works hand in hand with the stability control unit. The 2016 to 2019 tables describe the check behind U031C: the stability module receives a compatibility index from the booster over CAN and compares it with its own configuration. If the index stays incompatible for 0.1 s, the code is stored, provided supply voltage is between 7.5 and 16 V, the bus is active and 5 s have passed after a power mode change. GM classes it as Type A: the warning lamp comes on during the very first drive with the fault. U01B4 is lost contact, U04B5 invalid data from module B, U0318 concerns the main brake module. Expect brake warnings and possibly reduced electric boost.
c: Brake booster unit replaced or swapped without programming to the vehicle
Stability control module updated or configured for another booster variant
Programming interrupted, for example by low battery voltage
s: MIL on and brake or stability warning in the cluster
Changed pedal feel or reduced electric brake boost
Code appears right after brake booster or ESP module work

U031D.t: Software Incompatibility With Parking Assist Control Module A
U031D.d: Parking assist control module A evaluates the ultrasonic bumper sensors for park distance warnings and, on newer vehicles, supports low-speed helpers such as automated parking. U031D tells that another controller considers the software or configuration of this module wrong for the vehicle. Ford describes a case on 2021–2022 F-150 trucks without electric drive (SSM 52371): the PCM stored U031D, lit the wrench lamp and showed Service Vehicle Soon while the truck drove normally. Ford traces it to the PCM configuration and clears it with the FDRS routine that disables Pro Trailer Hitch Assist in the PCM. So the code can sit in the engine controller and still concern a parking function. U0159 means lost contact, U045A invalid data, U031E concerns module B. Park distance or trailer helpers may be unavailable.
c: Vehicle or PCM configuration lists a parking or trailer feature that does not match the fitted module
Parking assist module replaced or swapped without programming
Only some modules updated, leaving the parking module on an older level
s: Wrench lamp or service message without any drivability complaint
Park distance warning or trailer hitch assist not available
Code returns after clearing until the configuration is corrected

U031E.t: Software Incompatibility With Parking Assist Control Module B
U031E.d: Parking assist control module B is a second park aid unit, found where front and rear sensors are split between controllers or an automatic parking controller sits beside the distance warning; which unit gets the letter B is decided by each maker. U031E is set when a partner module rejects the software or setup of module B, mostly after a replacement or an incomplete update. No manufacturer documents U031E publicly. FCA illustrates how such units react to bad calibration data: on 2015–2016 Jeep Renegade with ParkSense or parallel and perpendicular park assist, the park assist module stored B1000-46, the cluster announced that ParkSense was not available, and only a reflash at stable voltage helped (08-078-16). U0243 is lost contact, U0544 invalid data, U031D covers module A. Distance warnings or self-parking stay off.
c: Second parking module replaced or taken from another car without programming
Module variant does not match the fitted sensor set or parking option
Software update of the parking module interrupted or incomplete
s: Park assist unavailable message in the cluster
No warning tones from front or rear sensors
Automatic parking function cannot be started

U031F.t: Software Incompatibility With Accessory Protocol Interface Module
U031F.d: The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) is the SYNC computer, as Ford calls it, behind the centre screen, which handles audio sources, phone, voice control and navigation. U031F tells that a connected unit finds the APIM software unsuitable. Ford shows the underlying problem on 2018–2019 Lincoln Navigator (SSM 51464): after a 10-inch centre display was renewed, the screen could fail to power up because displays from part number JL7T-18B955-UG onward need a newer SYNC software level; the remedy is an APIM software update with FDRS. Ford does not name U031F in that bulletin. The APIM is not part of engine control, so no MIL is expected. U0253 means lost contact, U0554 invalid data. Typical signs are a dark or restarting screen and missing phone, audio or navigation.
c: Replacement display or other unit needs a newer SYNC software level than installed
APIM replaced or swapped without module installation and configuration
SYNC update interrupted or installed only partly
s: Centre screen stays dark or keeps rebooting
No radio, phone or navigation functions
Rear camera picture or touch controls missing on the screen

U0320.t: Software Incompatibility With Power Steering Control Module
U0320.d: The power steering control module drives the electric assist motor and needs calibration data that suit the steering gear and the vehicle. U0320 is logged when another module refuses to work with its software. No manufacturer documents U0320 publicly, but GM and Volkswagen show the background. GM preliminary information PIC5771 for the 2013 Buick LaCrosse with NJ2 steering reports that after a gear replacement the module often refused programming and set C056E symptom 42, calibration not programmed, so Techline had to supply the data. Volkswagen cured weak assist on 2010–2013 Golf, Jetta, Passat and Beetle by new J500 software, followed by basic settings of steering and angle sensor. U0131 is lost contact, U0420 invalid data, U0319 concerns the steering effort module. Steering may turn heavy with a warning lamp.
c: Steering gear or steering module replaced without loading matching calibration
Steering module software older than required by the other modules
Basic setting or adaptation after programming not carried out
s: Steering heavy or assist only partly available
Power steering warning lamp or message
Lane keeping or park steering functions switched off

U0321.t: Software Incompatibility With Suspension Control Module A
U0321.d: Suspension control module A manages adjustable dampers, air springs or ride height, and on some cars it also leads active roll control; some code lists call it the ride level module. U0321 tells that a partner controller considers its software unfit. No manufacturer documents U0321 publicly. Bentley describes the typical situation on 2017–2021 Bentayga with active anti-roll bars (technical product information 2055643/2): after software or hardware of the adaptive suspension unit J775 or of the roll stabiliser units J924 and J1096 was replaced, the versions could stop matching, and the workshop must compare and align them. Jeep, in contrast, flags a fresh air suspension module on 2021–2022 Grand Cherokee with U0300 until it is flashed (08-109-22). U0132 is lost contact, U0421 invalid data. Ride height or damping may stay fixed.
c: Replacement suspension or roll control unit carries a software level the partners do not accept
Only one of the linked chassis modules updated
Suspension module coded for another equipment level
s: Suspension warning in the cluster
Ride height cannot be adjusted or vehicle sits at one level
Firm or uneven damping, more body roll

U0322.t: Software Incompatibility With Body Control Module
U0322.d: The body control module switches lighting, locks, wipers and many comfort functions and often holds configuration data used by other units. U0322 tells that a controller has found the BCM software or setup unfit for the vehicle. The code without a letter is meant for cars with one body controller; where two are fitted, U0331 names body control module A and U0339 module B. No manufacturer documents U0322 publicly. Ford shows the kind of mismatch on 2022 F-150 trucks (SSM 51591): following a software update of the BCM one or both headlamps could stay dark, sometimes with B14E5:08 or B14E7:08, because the LED headlamp module did not work with the new BCM software; Ford brings the BCM to the latest level and replaces the LED module. U0140 is lost contact, U0422 invalid data. Body functions fail, no MIL.
c: BCM replaced or swapped without loading vehicle configuration
BCM updated while a connected unit such as a headlamp module kept old software
BCM programming interrupted by low voltage or lost connection
s: Headlamps, interior lights or wipers work wrongly or not at all
Central locking or remote key functions unreliable
Several body codes stored at the same time

U0323.t: Software Incompatibility With Instrument Panel Control Module
U0323.d: The instrument panel control module is the cluster with gauges, warning lamps and messages; it also passes data such as units or outside temperature to other modules. U0323 means the engine controller or another unit rejects its software or coding. Mazda (MT-010/18, 2014–2019 models with Mazda Connect) and Toyota for the Scion iA (S-SB-0018-17) list U0323 in the PCM together with U0423 in the ABS and U3000 in the cluster: if the ignition is switched off within 20 s of switching on while the ROOM fuse or the infotainment unit is missing, the codes stick and TPMS and DSC lamps light. Volkswagen's 2014 Golf specification book sets U0323 when the cluster lacks coding for the ambient temperature sensor. Ducati saw U0323 with a lit MIL on Scrambler 800 MY21 after an accessory alarm kit. U0155 is lost contact.
c: Cluster not coded for the fitted equipment, for example the ambient temperature sensor
Start-up exchange interrupted by a missing fuse, disconnected infotainment unit or quick ignition off
Cluster replaced or updated without matching configuration
Retrofitted accessory such as an alarm kit disturbing the cluster data
s: MIL or several warning lamps such as TPMS and stability control on
Codes in engine, ABS and cluster that cannot be cleared
Outside temperature or other displays missing

U0324.t: Software Incompatibility With HVAC Control Module
U0324.d: The HVAC control module reads cabin and outside temperatures and drives blend doors, blower, defrosting and the request for the A/C compressor. U0324 means another controller has found its software or calibration unfit for the vehicle. No manufacturer documents U0324 publicly; GM bulletins show how tightly the HVAC calibration is tied to other parts. On 2018 Chevrolet Equinox and GMC Terrain the climate system stayed off during remote start below 6 °C because of a calibration issue in the HVAC module, cured by reprogramming (17-NA-388). On 2013–2016 Cadillac ATS automatic rear window and mirror defogging failed after a recall; Techline supplies HVAC software that matches a new radio antenna coil (16-NA-008). U0164 is lost contact, U0424 invalid data, U032A concerns the compressor module. Climate functions are limited, no MIL.
c: HVAC module calibration outdated or not matching the vehicle options
Connected part replaced, such as antenna, display or compressor, without matching HVAC software
HVAC module replaced or taken from another car without setup
s: Heating, cooling or defrosting works only in part
Climate settings reset or remote start climate stays off
A/C compressor not requested

U0325.t: Software Incompatibility With Auxiliary Heater Control Module
U0325.d: The auxiliary heater control module runs an extra heat source: a fuel-burning or electric coolant heater, or on electrified cars a high-voltage heater that warms the cabin while the engine is off. U0325 means a connected module rejects this unit's software. No manufacturer documents U0325 publicly. GM's 2013–2014 Volt shows the role: its coolant heater control module provides cabin heat in electric mode, and without it heat only comes once the engine runs (PIC5943). BMW shows that heater software can reach into OBD: on i3 and i8 the MIL came on with fault 8013A3, a low reading of the high-voltage heater's OBD coolant temperature sensor, although heating worked; BMW blamed the climate control software and reprogrammed the car (SI B12 21 16). U0166 is lost contact, U0425 invalid data. Expect missing heat.
c: Heater unit or its controller replaced without programming or coding
Climate or vehicle software level does not match the heater variant
Retrofitted parking heater not coded into the vehicle network
s: No auxiliary or parking heat, cabin warms only with the engine running
Heater warning or service message
On plug-in hybrids the engine starts more often for heat

U0326.t: Software Incompatibility With Vehicle Immobilizer Control Module
U0326.d: The vehicle immobilizer control module checks the transponder or smart key and releases the engine controller only after a coded exchange. U0326 means that a controller, usually the engine controller, does not accept the immobilizer's software or stored codes, mostly once either unit has been renewed or reprogrammed. No manufacturer documents U0326 publicly. Subaru uses its own code for this mismatch on 2016-and-later models: B1571, reference code incompatibility between immobilizer and ECM, found by the keyless access module (18-230-26). Chrysler reprogrammed PCMs of 2012–2013 Grand Voyager diesels because handshake failures with the wireless control module were stored as the wrong codes (18-023-13). U0167 is lost contact, U0426 invalid data, U0327 concerns the security module. The engine may crank but not start.
c: Engine controller or immobilizer unit replaced without pairing the security codes
Used module from another vehicle fitted, carrying foreign codes
Software of engine controller and immobilizer on incompatible levels after an update
s: Engine cranks but does not start, or starts and stalls at once
Security or key lamp flashes in the cluster
Keys are not recognised after module work

U0327.t: Software Incompatibility With Vehicle Security Control Module
U0327.d: The vehicle security control module handles theft protection: alarm, monitoring of doors, bonnet and tailgate and, at some makers, the key check that unlocks the engine. Chrysler, for example, gives this job to its wireless control module, and its lost-contact code U0168 calls that unit the vehicle security control module (18-023-13). U0327 means another controller finds the software of this module unsuitable, typically after a replacement, a used part or an update of only one side. No manufacturer documents U0327 publicly. Where the security module also performs the key check, the engine controller withholds release and the car will not start; elsewhere the alarm, remote locking or panic function misbehaves. U0326 covers a separate immobilizer module, U0168 lost contact and U0427 invalid data. No MIL is expected.
c: Security or wireless control module replaced without programming and key learning
Engine or body controller updated while the security module kept old software
Aftermarket alarm or remote start interfering with the security data
s: No start or start refused although the key is accepted at the door
Alarm triggers without reason or cannot be armed
Security lamp flashing, remote locking unreliable

U0328.t: Software Incompatibility With Steering Angle Sensor Module
U0328.d: The steering angle sensor module reports wheel angle and turning speed over CAN, mainly to stability control and electric power steering. U0328 means a receiving module rejects the software or variant of this sensor. No manufacturer documents U0328 publicly. GM shows how tight the pairing is: on 2012–2013 cars with NJ1 steering, among them Volt, Malibu and Equinox, a wrongly performed sensor alignment set C0544 and U0415 that would not clear, lit the MIL and cut assist; only flashing the steering module with different software removed it (PI0800A). Audi fixed an intermittent low-voltage code B116816 for the angle sensor in the ABS unit of the 2015 A3 with new J500 software and a fresh sensor calibration (2040449). U0126 is lost contact, U0428 invalid data, U0320 concerns the steering module. ESC and lane assist may switch off.
c: Steering angle sensor or column part replaced without calibration or setup
Sensor of another part number or software variant fitted
Brake or steering module software does not support the fitted sensor
s: ESC, traction control or lane assist warning lamps on
Steering assist uneven or the car pulls after alignment work
Code appears after wheel alignment or steering column repair

U0329.t: Software Incompatibility With Steering Column Control Module
U0329.d: The steering column control module gathers the stalks and wheel buttons for indicators, wipers, horn and cruise control, and on newer cars it may also handle the heated wheel or pass on the steering angle. U0329 means a partner module rejects the software of this unit. No manufacturer documents U0329 publicly. Ford shows a typical trap on the 2023 Bronco Sport: programming a replacement SCCM in FDRS can abort with a download error when a wrong part variant was fitted, and Ford lists which service part belongs to which engineering assembly number (SSM 52486). FCA updated SCCM software on 2011–2013 Dodge and Ram models because the cruise control reacted slowly or not at all to its switches (08-010-14). U0212 is lost contact, U0429 invalid data, U0328 concerns the angle sensor. Stalk or wheel functions may fail.
c: Replacement steering column module of the wrong variant fitted
Module installation or programming after replacement not completed
Steering column module software older than the connected modules expect
s: Indicators, wipers or horn work only partly
Cruise control or wheel buttons without reaction
Assistance functions using steering column signals unavailable

U032A.t: Software Incompatibility With A/C Compressor Control Module
U032A.d: The A/C compressor control module drives an electric refrigerant compressor, as used in hybrid and electric cars, and reports speed and status to the climate controller. U032A means that controller considers the compressor module's software or learned data invalid. Volkswagen and Audi document the code: in the 2021 ID.4 a dead A/C with U032A00 first calls for checking a pending software campaign, not for a new compressor (tech tip 87-23-02TT). On 2022–2023 Audi Q4 e-tron the HVAC electronics J979 store U032A00 when the compressor module J842 has lost its adaptation; running the compressor calibration in the guided test restores cooling (2071838), and a later bulletin names the ME 3.5 update package as the production fix (2074321). U016B is lost contact, U046C invalid data, U0324 concerns the HVAC module. The cabin is not cooled.
c: Compressor module lost its adaptation and needs the calibration routine
Climate or compressor software below the level of an open update campaign
Electric compressor replaced without programming and calibration
s: Air conditioning blows warm, compressor does not run
Fault returns after a while even when cooling was restored
On electric cars battery cooling or preconditioning may be limited

U0330.t: Software Incompatibility With Tire Pressure Monitor Module
U0330.d: The tyre pressure monitor module receives the radio messages of the wheel sensors, evaluates the pressures and, on many systems, works out which sensor sits on which wheel; from this it drives the warning lamp and cluster messages. U0330 is set when a partner controller finds the software or variant of this module unsuitable, usually after a replacement or a partial update. No manufacturer documents U0330 publicly. Porsche shows how much depends on that software: on Panamera and Cayenne from 2017, version 0630 could raise a TPM fault message for no reason, and the unit had to be reprogrammed and coded (90/18). FCA reflashed the TPM software of 2014–2015 Journey, Durango, Charger and Grand Cherokee when sensor location codes C151D and C1581 appeared (08-024-15). U0127 is lost contact. Only the tyre warning is affected.
c: TPMS module replaced or taken from another vehicle without programming and coding
Module still on a software level that the partner controllers no longer accept
Module configured for another wheel, tyre or sensor variant
s: Tyre pressure warning lamp or TPMS fault message in the cluster
Tyre pressures not shown or shown on the wrong wheel
Code appears after work on the TPMS module or a software update

U0331.t: Software Incompatibility With Body Control Module A
U0331.d: Body control module A is the first of several body controllers on vehicles that spread lighting, locking, wipers and power distribution over more than one unit. With a single body controller the same mismatch is reported as U0322; U0339 covers unit B. U0331 means a partner module finds the software or configuration of unit A unfit. No manufacturer documents U0331 publicly, and none reveals which controller is labelled A. Jaguar calls its auxiliary junction box body control module B (recall J017), leaving the central junction box as the leading body unit; on 2016–2017 XF models that would not start with both smart keys inside, Jaguar reconfigured that box to the latest level (K424). Ford cured failed BCM installations on many 2016–2017 models with a newer IDS release (SSM 50097). Body functions may fail; no MIL.
c: Body control module A replaced without loading the vehicle configuration
Programming aborted or corrupted by an outdated diagnostic tool release
Other body modules updated while unit A stayed on its old level
s: Lighting, locking or wiper functions fail or behave oddly
Keyless start or remote locking may not work
Several modules store network codes after body module work

U0332.t: Software Incompatibility With Multi-axis Acceleration Sensor Module A
U0332.d: Multi-axis acceleration sensor module A measures yaw rate plus lateral and longitudinal acceleration for stability control and driver assistance; it can be a separate box or part of another controller. U0332 means a receiving controller rejects its software or variant. No manufacturer documents U0332 publicly. GM treats the unit as a programmable module in its own right: the warranty labour list has a separate operation for reprogramming it with SPS (06-08-47-001N), and after the brake controller of the 2014 Cadillac ELR was recalibrated, the yaw rate sensor learn is run in this module (recall 14087). Audi removed sporadic C051F00, a correlation fault of sensor module A on e-tron models, with new software for ABS unit J104 and suspension unit J775 (2061908). U0125 is lost contact. Stability control may switch off.
c: Sensor module replaced by a part with another software or variant
Brake or suspension controller updated without matching the sensor module
Yaw rate sensor learn skipped after programming
s: Stability control or traction control warning lamp on
Driver assistance functions unavailable
Code follows module replacement or software update

U0333.t: Software Incompatibility With Gear Shift Control Module B
U0333.d: With shift-by-wire, both the driver's selector and the unit that actually moves the range are electronic modules; module B denotes a second such unit, either a further selector or the shift actuator. U0333 means its software or calibration does not fit the partner controller. Allison lists it for the sixth-generation controls of its 3000 and 4000 series, released in 2021, as Gear Shift Module 2 Incompatible, next to U0304 for module 1; the same bulletin warns that new push-button selectors do not work with fifth-generation TCMs and that the fitted selector must match the TCM calibration (SIL 14-TR-21). Lexus labels the shift actuator ECU of the 2022 NX 350 and NX 250 with B and reflashed its main and sub calibration in campaign 22LC03. U0291 is lost contact, U0592 invalid data.
c: Selector or actuator of another generation or part number fitted
Transmission calibration specifies a different selector than the one fitted
Shift actuator ECU still on an outdated calibration
s: Range changes requested at this unit are ignored
Transmission warning or shift indicator fault
Vehicle stays in or returns to neutral or park

U0334.d: On current vehicles the radio is the infotainment head unit: besides audio it runs navigation, voice control, phone connection and the setting menus for other systems such as seat heating. U0334 is stored when a controller relying on these services rejects the radio's software. No manufacturer documents U0334 publicly. FCA illustrates how tightly radio software levels build on each other: Uconnect 8.4 radios in European Jeep Cherokee 2019–2020 needed up to three USB stages to reach level 39.5, and skipping a stage could damage the unit so badly that it had to be replaced (08-033-21). On the Jeep Compass, an earlier update to 28.31 could leave the radio silent and grey out the heated seat and steering wheel buttons until 39.2 was installed (08-068-20). U0184 is lost contact, U0485 invalid data. No MIL.
c: Radio update done out of sequence or with a skipped intermediate level
Head unit replaced by a variant for another market or equipment
Other modules updated while the radio stayed on an old level
s: No sound or missing functions on the head unit
Comfort settings shown greyed out in the radio menus
Code appears after a radio update or replacement

U0335.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Sensor Module
U0335.d: The battery pack sensor module is housed in the traction battery, where it measures pack current and voltage for the battery controller. U0335 records that this controller or another partner rejects the module's software. Ford's 2014 code interpretation lists U0335 for the hybrid battery pack sensor module without a MIL marker. GM runs a comparable check in the Volt battery: its VITM compares the software versions of all slave modules 200 ms after power-up at 9 V or more and stores the maker-specific P1EB1 as Type A. Stellantis reprograms the battery pack control module and other units of the 2025 electric Dodge Charger and, if U029A for the sensor module remains, lets the car sleep for six minutes (08-028-25). U059B is invalid data. Lacking trustworthy readings, the vehicle can block driving or charging.
c: Battery controller updated without matching the sensor module, or the reverse
Sensor module or contactor box replaced with a part on another software level
Programming of the battery modules interrupted
s: Vehicle will not enter ready mode or drives with reduced power
Charging does not start or stops early
Range and state of charge shown incorrectly

U0336.t: Software Incompatibility With Restraints Control Module
U0336.d: The restraints control module reads the crash sensors and triggers airbags and belt tensioners according to a calibration written for one body style and equipment level. U0336 means a connected unit rejects the software or configuration of this module. Ford's 2014 code interpretation lists U0336 without the MIL marker. Jaguar Land Rover shows why the software level matters: replacement RCMs for the Range Rover Evoque came with software older than the factory level, the tester picked its update from the module content instead of the as-built data, and the unit stored B0002-13 until a manual patch fixed the choice (SSM74259). On 2013 Jaguar XJ AWD cars a generic RCM calibration failed FMVSS 208, leading to recall J040. U0151 is lost contact, U0452 invalid data. The airbag lamp stays on.
c: Replacement airbag module delivered with an older software level and not brought up to the vehicle level
Calibration for another body style, drive or equipment loaded
Used module from another vehicle installed
s: Airbag warning lamp stays on
Further restraint codes such as airbag circuit faults stored
Code appears right after airbag module replacement

U0337.t: Software Incompatibility With Battery Charger Control Module A
U0337.d: Battery charger control module A is the charger built into a plug-in car: it turns mains AC into DC for the traction battery and coordinates with the charging station and the battery controller. U0337 appears when a partner module refuses the charger's software or calibration. No manufacturer documents U0337 publicly. Maserati updates the OBCM software on 2025 GranTurismo and Grecale electric models because a charging fault could only be cleared by unplugging and reconnecting (Rapid Update 751). FCA's bulletin 08-048-14 for the 2013–2014 Fiat 500e updated charger, vehicle control unit, inverter and battery controller together, partly to cut 12 V drain on incompatible charging stations. CARB expects plug-in hybrids to monitor charging performance. U019B is lost contact, U049C invalid data. Charging may stop.
c: On-board charger left on an older software level after other modules were updated
Charger replaced without programming to the vehicle
Charger update interrupted, for example by low 12 V supply
s: Charging does not start or stops after a short time
Charging fault message that clears only after replugging
12 V battery drained after charging sessions

U0338.t: Software Incompatibility With Remote Function Actuation Module
U0338.d: The remote function actuation module receives key fob, passive entry and, on newer cars, phone key signals and passes lock, unlock or start requests to the body controller. U0338 means a partner rejects its software. No manufacturer documents U0338 publicly. Jaguar Land Rover shows the typical trap: RFA service parts FK72-19H440 for several Jaguar models from model year 2015 came loaded with software intended for dual-CAN cars, so in these multi-CAN cars the new module stayed silent towards the tester until its fuse was pulled and refitted and the module configured (SSM72557). For Land Rover models from 2010, JLR traces failed RFA downloads to low battery voltage, an interrupted diagnostic link or a corrupted file (SSM71856). U0214 is lost contact, U0515 invalid data. Keyless entry or start may fail.
c: Replacement module shipped with software for another network layout
Software download aborted by low voltage, a lost link or a corrupted file
Module fitted but not configured or keys not programmed
s: Remote or keyless locking does not respond
Keyless start refused or key not detected
Module not reachable by the diagnostic tool after replacement

U0339.t: Software Incompatibility With Body Control Module B
U0339.d: Body control module B is a second body controller that takes over part of the switching, for example in a rear or auxiliary junction box. U0339 means a partner module rejects its software or setup; U0331 covers unit A, U0322 vehicles with a single body controller. Jaguar uses exactly this name: on the 2010 XF 5.0 V8 and the 2010–2011 XK, the auxiliary junction box, listed as body control module B, could drop the fuel pump relay after start, so the engine stalled once the high-pressure pump ran short; recall J017 loaded revised software and reconfigured that box. Ford has a BCM-B on 2022–2023 Mustang Stealth models, where a wrong configuration left the sill plates dark until program 23B60 reconfigured it with FDRS. U0142 is lost contact, U0443 invalid data. Usually no MIL.
c: Body control module B carries a configuration that does not match the vehicle
Unit B left on an older software level after an update campaign
Auxiliary junction box replaced without programming
s: Functions switched by the second body module fail, such as lights or sill plate illumination
Depending on its tasks, engine may stall or not start
Network codes in several modules after body module work

U033A.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module A
U033A.d: U033A is the one code of this row that a manufacturer names in public. Volvo's bulletins for the battery-electric VNR Electric truck (KC-2288 of 2023, CBR-2288 of June 2024, the latter also valid for the Mack LRe) list it among faults that turn active right after the ESCM has been reprogrammed, together with missing-message codes for interface modules A to D. The cure is not a part but a second programming run, the routine that flashes the battery management unit. Module A is the first of the boards that report cell voltages and temperatures from inside the pack. Silence from A is U01A0, bad data U04A1. Volvo gives no MIL rating.
c: Battery management unit left on its old software after another controller was reprogrammed
Programming session ended before all battery-related units were flashed
Interface module A replaced and not brought to the matching level
s: Code turns active directly after a module programming session
Missing-message codes for interface modules A to D stored at the same time
High-voltage battery warning until the battery unit is reprogrammed

U033B.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module B
U033B.d: Module B is the second interface board, and on GM's eAssist mild hybrids it is also the last: bulletin PIT5513D lists exactly two, K112A and K112B, for 2016–2018 Silverado and Sierra and the 2018 LaCrosse, both under the same part number 24282084. Since one spare fits either slot, the part number alone does not tell which position a board serves. FCA's 2017–2018 Pacifica Hybrid shows a related split with maker-specific codes P1A29 and P1A2A for cell supervisory circuits A and B; bulletin 08-047-20 clears them by reflashing the battery pack control module. Neither maker documents U033B itself. U01A1 means B is silent, U04A2 that its data are invalid.
c: Board B replaced with a spare carrying another software level
Battery controller software older than the board it has to accept
Identical boards A and B swapped during pack repair
s: Hybrid system or battery warning, often with the check engine lamp on PHEVs
Electric assist or electric driving reduced
Fault follows work on the battery pack

U033C.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module C
U033C.d: U033C names the third interface board. GM's closest published check is its own code P1EB1 in the VITM of the Volt: at power-up the controller compares its own software version with that of all slave boards and logs P1EB1 if any one does not fit, within 200 ms, with at least 9 V and no slave lost-communication fault active. The 2015 table enters it as one trip, the 2018 table as Type A, meaning a MIL after one failed drive. GM thus reports one summary code rather than one per board, and a letter code like U033C does not appear there. Where a maker does use the letter codes, C stands for the third board only; U01A2 covers lost contact with it, U04A3 invalid data.
c: Board C carries a software version the battery controller does not list as compatible
Battery controller updated while the boards stayed on the old level
Unstable low-voltage supply at power-up corrupts the version exchange
s: MIL possible on hybrids, as GM rates its comparable check Type A
Hybrid or high-voltage battery warning after switching on
Electric driving or charging restricted

U033D.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module D
U033D.d: On the first-generation Chevrolet Volt the monitoring electronics end at the fourth board. GM's 2012 Volt table refers to four slave units through its own codes: P1EB2 to P1EB5 report a slave that answered wrongly or not at all when a programming session ended, and U2603 to U2606, listed in GM's U-code catalogue for the 2011 Saab 9-4X as loss of hybrid battery interface control modules 1 to 4, block the software comparison while a slave is silent. A fourth slot exists there, but GM uses its own numbers instead of U033D; in the 2018 table P1EB5 is labelled module D not programmed. A failed flash of that board thus shows up as P1EB5. U01A3 and U02A0 are the generic lost-contact and invalid-data codes for D.
c: Programming of the fourth board aborted or answered with an error
Replacement board D still on a superseded software version
Interrupted link to board D masks or disturbs the version check
s: Code appears after programming or replacing a battery section
Hybrid warning, MIL possible on plug-in hybrids
Reduced propulsion until all boards match

U033E.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module E
U033E.d: A fifth interface board exists, for example, in BMW's 330e plug-in hybrid of the F30 series: bulletin SI B61 25 17 lists voltage-measurement codes for cell supervision circuits 1 to 5 in the battery electronics SME, under BMW's own numbers 21F0C2 to 21F0C6. BMW replaces a CSC only if the fault is active, has been logged five times, or twice with the MIL lit, and once harness and cell voltages have been checked. Kia shows why software has to follow such parts: on the 2015–2017 Soul EV, a replaced battery pack or BMS may need a BMS update chosen by the installed part numbers and confirmed by ROM ID (TSB ELE 155). U033E would flag a fifth board whose software the master rejects; U01A4 and U04A5 cover silence and bad data.
c: Fifth supervision board replaced without matching the controller software
Battery controller not updated to the part numbers now installed
Boards of different production levels combined in one pack
s: Powertrain or hybrid warning, MIL possible on plug-in hybrids
Fault stored after a battery or BMS repair
Electric range or power temporarily limited

U033F.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module F
U033F.d: Public documents name no vehicle that uses U033F, nor a pack with exactly six interface boards; F is simply the sixth address in the row. What is documented is how strictly battery software must follow the hardware. Hyundai's bulletin 18-HC-003 requires a BMS parameter update whenever a replacement lithium battery is installed in a 2011–2015 Sonata Hybrid or a 2015–2017 Tucson Fuel Cell. FCA cured P1A29, a failure of cell supervisory circuit A on the 2026 RAM 1500 eTorque, with new battery pack control module software (08-282-26); owners had noticed limp-home mode and a disabled stop/start. CARB 1968.2 counts cell voltage sensing among the hybrid inputs OBD must watch. U01A5 and U04A6 are F's partners.
c: Battery parameters not updated after a pack or module replacement
Board F taken from another pack with a different software level
Battery controller on an outdated calibration
s: Limp-home mode or reduced electric power
Stop/start or electric assist disabled
Battery or hybrid warning after battery service

U0340.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module G
U0340.d: G is the seventh board, a position GM's 2016–2019 plug-in hybrids really have: table 16OBDG02 describes eight interface modules on a UART daisy chain to the battery system module. That table publishes lost-contact and processor tests for every board, yet it holds no counterpart to the P1EB1 version check of the older VITM design and no U0340. For G, GM thus documents silence (U01A6), not a software conflict. The older four-board design is stricter: P1F06 to P1F09 make each slave return a key value computed by a seed-and-key algorithm and fail it when wrong values persist for 1 s within a 1.4 s window, Type B in the 2015 table. U04A7 is the invalid-data code for G.
c: Seventh board replaced by a unit with another software level
Battery system module reflashed without the boards being brought along
Disturbed daisy-chain link garbles the version data of board G
s: Hybrid warning, MIL possible depending on the maker
Electric mode limited or unavailable
Other battery diagnostics paused while the code is active

U0341.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module H
U0341.d: Packs with eight boards end at H. Besides GM's 2016–2019 plug-ins, BMW's i3 is one: bulletin SI B61 02 16 lists eight cell supervision circuits for the i3 battery and, for boards built between December 2013 and September 2014, orders all of them renewed together once diagnosis calls for a CSC. When only one section of a pack is changed, GM adds a step for Volt and ELR: per PIC6097A the new section must be balanced to the rest with the EL 50332 service tool, using interface VIM-1 for the 2011–2015 Volt and 2014–2016 ELR and VIM-2 for the 2016–2019 Volt, with the tool itself updated first. Matching generations matter at every step. U01A7 and U04A8 are H's lost-contact and invalid-data codes.
c: Software of the last board does not match after a section replacement
Only some boards renewed where the maker requires a complete set
Service tool, adapter or tool software of the wrong generation used
s: Car cannot be made ready to drive
Code set after battery section work
Drive power reduced

U0342.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module I
U0342.d: Mitsubishi shows that a replaced monitoring board must first be given its place in the pack. On the 2022 Outlander plug-in hybrid, numbering of the cell monitoring units (CMU) is done at the factory; after a CMU or battery module has been replaced, the workshop runs CMU ID numbering from the battery management unit with the M.U.T.-III tester, never while the battery is charging, and checks that every ID data item reads complete, repeating the routine otherwise. The same manual names the CMU among probable causes of cell temperature faults. Mitsubishi uses no letter codes here, and the ninth position I presupposes a pack with nine boards. U01A8 is I's lost-contact code, U04A9 invalid data.
c: Replaced board not numbered or registered in the battery controller
ID numbering run while charging or aborted before completion
Board of another battery variant fitted at position I
s: Battery warning after a module or CMU replacement
EV mode or charging restricted
MIL possible on plug-in hybrids

U0343.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module J
U0343.d: J, the tenth board, only appears on larger packs. BMW's i8 is a documented example with more than ten: the parts list in bulletin SI B61 02 16 counts twelve cell monitoring circuits, and the battery electronics SME carries a voltage plausibility code for each of them, numbered 1 to 12 (21F0F3 to 21F0FE). The bulletin's cause is a failed CAN link between one or more CSCs and the SME, after which the contactor in the battery opens and the car cannot be made ready. BMW numbers the boards itself and does not use U0343; whether any maker maps J onto a tenth board in this way is not published. CARB asks for codes down to the smallest unit replaceable in service. U01A9 and U04AA are J's partners.
c: Tenth board carries software the battery controller does not accept
Replacement boards from different production batches combined
Internal battery bus disturbs the identification of board J
s: Car will not become ready to drive
High-voltage system switches off, contactor opens
Drivetrain malfunction message

U0344.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module K
U0344.d: Eleven boards or more are found in GM's Ultium packs: according to Wikipedia the Cadillac Lyriq carries twelve modules and the Hummer EV two layers of twelve, and the battery management works wirelessly. GM's service update N232401570 of October 2025 shows that master software decides whether such a unit is accepted: on 2023–2024 Lyriq and BrightDrop, 2024 Blazer EV and Silverado EV and 2022–2024 Hummer EV, the battery energy control module could stay stuck in its start-up commissioning because one cell monitoring unit was offline. The fix is a reprogrammed control module, by the dealer or over the air, without parts. GM does not say which codes appear. U01AA and U04AB cover K's silence and bad data.
c: Battery controller software does not accept the monitoring unit
Released software update for the battery controller not yet installed
Monitoring unit K replaced and not registered
s: Vehicle does not become ready after switching on
Battery or propulsion warning
Charging may be refused

U0345.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module L
U0345.d: L is the twelfth letter and thus the last board on packs with twelve, such as the twelve CSCs of BMW's i8, provided a maker counted them this way. The mismatch behind U0345 is easy to create during battery repair. Kia's bulletin ELE 151 for the 2011–2016 Optima Hybrid allows a BMS update only when the traction battery is swapped for a part number of the new generation, so that the controller logic matches the new pack; the right flash is confirmed by pack number and ROM ID, and the upgrade must run in manual mode, since auto mode is ruled out. Old pack, new logic or the reverse is exactly the pairing to avoid. U01AB is the code for a silent L, U04AC for implausible data from it.
c: Battery controller logic and pack generation do not match
Update for new-generation packs applied to an old-generation pack
Twelfth board replaced with a unit of another software level
s: Hybrid warning after high-voltage battery replacement
Electric assist reduced
MIL possible on hybrids

U0346.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module M
U0346.d: With M the row passes the common twelve-board size. GM's 2018 hybrid table 18OBDG02 includes lost-contact codes for interface modules up to M (U01AC) in its bundle BICM Loss of Comm and adds that GM shares software across programs, so a code counts only where the program in question uses it. A matching bundle for software codes such as U0346 is not listed. The one GM pack plainly beyond twelve modules is the Hummer EV, whose Ultium battery Wikipedia describes as two layers of twelve modules each, wired in parallel at 400 V. How GM addresses the monitoring units in that pack is not published, so no vehicle is known to set U0346. U04AD is M's invalid-data code.
c: Thirteenth board on a software level the controller rejects
Controller software variant for another pack configuration
Board installed in the wrong layer or position of a multi-layer pack
s: Battery or propulsion warning
Power or charging limited
Code seen only on very large packs

U0347.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module N
U0347.d: N, the fourteenth slot, is not tied to any vehicle in public sources. What can be shown is how false mismatch codes arise in the workshop. Volvo notes for its electric VNR that many apparent data mismatches come from TEA2+ control units not reporting to the tester; switching the truck on and letting it power up, then starting and logging into the tool, and only then plugging in the interface avoids them. Ford reports for 2012–2018 Focus Electric that U0130 can follow a battery pack replacement unless the programmable module installation is run, which flashes PCM and TCM for battery compatibility, and that reusing an old tester session can add U1030. A code for N is best judged after a clean session. U01AD and U04AE are its neighbours.
c: Stale or incorrectly started tester session reports a false mismatch
Programmable module installation skipped after a battery replacement
Board N really carries incompatible software
s: Code appears during or right after a tester session
Further network codes in the battery controller
Often no change in driving once programming is completed

U0348.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module O
U0348.d: O stands for a fifteenth board; no public document links U0348 to a vehicle. That the software inside a cell monitoring unit can itself be the problem is shown by Honda's recall 15V602 of October 2015: in 6,786 Accord Hybrids of 2014–2015 the cell voltage sensor (CVS) could misread electrical noise from inverter and motor circuits, a side effect of a change made for digital TV reception in Japan, and switch the car into a fail-safe EV mode limited to about 40 mph, with the engine off. Dealers installed new hybrid system software, which Honda says does not affect emissions or fuel economy. Honda uses no letter codes for the CVS. U01AE flags a silent O, U04AF corrupted data.
c: Firmware of the monitoring unit itself faulty and superseded
Board O missed a released software update
Pack boards on different update levels after a partial repair
s: Fail-safe mode with reduced speed and power
Engine switched off, electric drive only until the battery is drained
Hybrid warning with audible alert

U0349.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module P
U0349.d: P is the sixteenth and final letter; the following number, U034A, already names an engine disconnect clutch, so a pack with more than sixteen boards would need maker codes. No vehicle is publicly linked to U0349. A real case of out-of-date battery firmware comes from Rivian: in 2022 R1T trucks built from October 2021 to June 2022, an old BMS firmware version could block over-the-air updates, so campaign RCA-30-23-001 had technicians remove an underbody panel, read a serial label and escalate for a manual update. A version gap can thus stop the update path itself, which is why a mismatch needs the maker's flashing tool. CARB's hybrid rules cover cell sensing; battery-only vehicles fall outside OBD II. U01AF and U04B0 are P's partners.
c: Battery firmware so old that over-the-air updates cannot be applied
Sixteenth board replaced without matching software
Code confused with U034A, which belongs to another component
s: Software updates fail or are not offered
Battery warning after battery service
Charging or power limited in severe cases

U034A.t: Software Incompatibility With Engine Disconnect Clutch
U034A.d: Parallel hybrids place a disconnect clutch between combustion engine and electric drive; it couples the engine in or separates it for electric driving. Where the clutch has its own actuator controller, U034A means the hybrid or transmission controller rejects that unit's software. No manufacturer documents U034A publicly. Stellantis shows how closely clutch control depends on matching software in several modules: on the 2024 Jeep Wrangler 4xe, a lit MIL with P2885, a failure of the clutch to engage, and P0810 was cured by reprogramming PCM, TCM and the auxiliary hybrid controller (08-051-24 Rev. A); a later bulletin adds loss of propulsion and a Shift To Park warning (21-017-24 Rev. C). CARB requires hybrids to monitor parts that affect engine operation. U02AA is lost contact, U05AB invalid data.
c: Hybrid, engine and transmission controllers on software levels that do not belong together
Clutch actuator or transmission unit replaced without programming
Programming of a powertrain module interrupted
s: Engine warning lamp or transmission warning on
Electric driving or engine start-stop unavailable
Harsh engagement or loss of drive until the next key cycle

U034B.t: Software Incompatibility With Brake Booster Control
U034B.d: Brake booster control is the electromechanical brake servo that replaces the vacuum booster and lets regenerative braking be blended in; in the VW group it is unit J539, which holds the pedal travel sensor and the motor position sensor (self-study 861213). Audi documents U034B00 on the 2025 A3 and S3: with servo software 0562 the unit logs U034B00 with symptom 500032 during the start phase, the engine controller adds P162400, a request to switch on the warning lamp, and the check engine light stays on. Audi blames the servo software, rules out part replacement and gives clearing the codes as the interim workaround (2076568/1); the booster keeps working. U025E is lost contact, U055F invalid data, and U031C names brake system control module B. Braking itself is unaffected.
c: Faulty software level in the electromechanical brake booster
Brake booster unit replaced without programming or coding
Brake or engine controller updated without matching the booster
s: Engine warning lamp stays on after starting
Request-MIL code stored in the engine controller
Code returns after clearing until new booster software is installed

U034C.t: Software Incompatibility With Battery Energy Control Module C
U034C.d: Battery energy control module C is a third battery controller, found where a high-voltage battery is split into sections with their own management electronics. U034C means the leading controller or another partner rejects its software. No manufacturer documents U034C publicly or names a unit C. The risk of mismatched battery software is well documented: on the 2013–2015 Fiat 500e, a battery pack control module update added a limp home mode that the vehicle control unit did not recognise, which led to electrical shutdowns and recall 15V-179. GM's Volt battery compares the software versions of its slave modules 200 ms after power-up and treats a mismatch as Type A (P1EB1). CARB requires hybrids to monitor the energy storage system. U0312 and U0313 cover modules A and B, U014A lost contact. Power or charging may be limited.
c: Battery controllers on software levels that do not match each other or the vehicle controller
Battery section or its controller replaced without programming
Battery software update aborted or only partly applied
s: Reduced drive power or no ready mode
Charging refused or slower than usual
High-voltage system warning in the cluster

U034D.t: Software Incompatibility With Vehicle Thermal Management Control Module
U034D.d: The vehicle thermal management control module commands pumps, valves and fans that keep battery, drive electronics and cabin at their target temperatures. U034D means a partner controller rejects its software or calibration. No manufacturer documents U034D publicly. Audi shows that the software of this unit counts for OBD: on the 2020 Q5 hybrid, thermal management control module 00C5 judged normal temperature differences as faults, stored P0C4300 and P0CE100 and lit the MIL until campaign 80C9 updated it. Porsche reprograms the thermal management unit TME of the Taycan from 2020 together with the high-voltage heater to make cabin heating more robust (WPS9). CARB wants the electronic components that cool or heat hybrid battery and inverter monitored. U02AB is lost contact, U05AC invalid data. Heating, charging or power may be limited.
c: Thermal management controller on an outdated software level
Thermal management module replaced without programming
High-voltage heater or another partner updated without matching the thermal controller
s: Weak cabin heating or cooling
Charging or drive power limited to protect the battery
Warning lamp with thermal or coolant codes stored

U034E.t: Software Incompatibility With Active Grille Air Shutter Module A
U034E.d: Active grille air shutter modules are small actuator controllers, usually LIN slaves of the engine controller, that open and close flaps in the front end to speed up warm-up and cut drag. U034E means the engine controller refuses the software of shutter module A. No manufacturer documents U034E publicly. GM's 2024 Traverse and Acadia show that shutter firmware matters: units built before December 2023 could falsely set U0585 for the upper shutter (A) and U0586 for the lower one (B) with the check engine lamp, and GM fits a shutter with newer firmware instead of reflashing (PIT6133). Ford's 2023 diesel summary has the 3.0 L engine learn the end stops of shutters A and B by self-calibration. CARB counts grille shutters as active off-cycle technology. U0284 is lost contact, U0585 invalid data. The flaps stop moving.
c: Shutter actuator with an unsuitable firmware level fitted
Shutter assembly for another engine or model year installed
Engine controller updated to a level that expects a different shutter
s: Check engine lamp may light depending on the maker
Upper grille flaps stay open or closed
Slower engine warm-up in cold weather

U034F.t: Software Incompatibility With Active Grille Air Shutter Module B
U034F.d: Shutter module B is the second flap actuator; at GM it drives the lower shutter. U034F tells that its software or variant differs from what the engine controller has stored as valid, typically after a shutter with another part number or firmware was fitted. No manufacturer documents U034F publicly. In bulletin PIT6133 GM assigns U0586 on 2024 Traverse and Acadia models to the lower shutter, names early firmware as the cause and supplies a new assembly instead of a reflash. Ford checks shutters A and B of the 3.0 L diesel separately and flags an end-stop fault when self-calibration misses the closed position by more than 40 degrees. Because unit B sits low in the bumper, water and corrosion are worth ruling out before blaming software. U0285 is lost contact, U0586 invalid data. The lower flaps stop moving.
c: Lower shutter actuator with early or unsuitable firmware
Lower shutter replaced by a part with another part number
Water in the lower connector disturbing the module and misread as a software fault
s: Lower grille flaps no longer move
Check engine lamp may light depending on the maker
Code appears after a lower shutter was replaced

U0350.t: Software Incompatibility With Active Grille Air Shutter Module C
U0350.d: Module C denotes one more flap actuator with its own bus address, needed where the front end splits its air openings into more sections, for example left and right lower flaps. U0350 indicates that the engine controller does not accept this unit's software. No manufacturer documents U0350 publicly. Hyundai's 2026 Palisade shows that a module C exists in practice: it drives the lower air flaps with one actuator per side, and its campaign 26-01-026H names U028B, loss of shutter module C, beside U0285 when water corrodes their connectors; which side carries the letter is not stated. GM's 2024 Traverse case shows that a shutter misreporting because of its firmware is replaced rather than reprogrammed (PIT6133). CARB treats grille shutters as active off-cycle technology. U058C is invalid data. The affected flaps stay fixed.
c: Side or lower flap actuator with another part number or firmware fitted
Left and right actuators swapped or mixed between model versions
Engine controller software expects a different shutter configuration
s: Air flap warning message in the cluster
One group of flaps remains in its last position
Check engine lamp may light depending on the maker

U0351.t: Software Incompatibility With Active Grille Air Shutter Module D
U0351.d: Shutter module D is the fourth address the code list reserves for grille flap actuators and is relevant only where a front end has four independently driven flap groups. U0351 signals that the engine controller will not accept the software of that unit. No manufacturer documents U0351 or says where a unit D would sit, so the position is maker-specific. What is documented around it: Hyundai already splits the lower flaps of the 2026 Palisade into left and right actuators and stores codes for modules B and C when water reaches their plugs (26-01-026H), GM swaps shutters whose firmware misreports instead of reflashing them (PIT6133), and CARB requires the active time of such off-cycle features to be logged. Part number and software level of the fitted actuator should be checked first. U028C is lost contact, U058D invalid data.
c: Flap actuator of group D with another part number or firmware fitted
Front end or bumper from another version fitted with different shutter equipment
Engine controller calibration expects a different number of shutter modules
s: One flap group no longer opens or closes
Air flap warning or check engine lamp depending on the maker
No noticeable change in driving

U0352.t: Software Incompatibility With NOx Sensor C
U0352.d: NOx sensor C is a third smart NOx sensor with its own electronics, fitted on exhaust systems with a second SCR stage, where it watches the gas behind the last catalyst. U0352 means the engine controller declines the software or calibration of this sensor, for example after a part meant for another engine or model year was fitted. No manufacturer documents U0352 publicly. GM's 2025 engine tables show that sensor C is real: the ECM expects five of its messages, logs U02A1 as Type B after more than 10 s without them and checks counter and checksum of its data (U05A8). CARB requires each emission-critical control unit to report a calibration ID and a verification number for its software. While sensor C is not accepted, the second SCR stage cannot be judged and readiness stays open. U030D and U030E cover sensors A and B.
c: NOx sensor for another engine, model year or position fitted
Engine controller updated to a level that expects another sensor software
Sensor C swapped with the sensor of another position
s: Check engine lamp possible, depending on the maker's rating
SCR or catalyst readiness does not complete
Code appears right after a NOx sensor replacement

U0353.t: Software Incompatibility With Ion Sense Module
U0353.d: An ion sense module places a small voltage across the plug gap after each spark and turns the resulting ion current into combustion, knock and misfire information for the engine controller; Ford's patent US20170030322A1 shows such a unit inside the ignition system. U0353 says the engine controller has found software or a calibration in this module that does not match its own, typically after a module swap or a one-sided update. No manufacturer documents U0353 publicly. Stellantis' 3.0 L Hurricane six shows how tightly the parts depend on software: bulletin 18-004-24 cures P2F64 (ion sense feedback circuit A) with PCM software, and 08-205-24 reflashes ignition module and PCM together. CARB demands a calibration ID for each emission-related unit; without accepted ion data misfire detection loses its basis, so a MIL is likely.
c: Engine controller or ion sense module updated without the matching partner software
Replacement ion sense module with another part number or calibration
Programming of one of the two units interrupted or incomplete
s: Check engine light
Misfire or knock codes stored at the same time
Code appears right after a module replacement or reflash

U0354.t: Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Inductive Charger Control Module
U0354.d: The inductive charger control module is the on-board part of a wireless charging system: a receiving coil under the floor picks up energy from a ground pad, and the module rectifies it and coordinates the process with battery management and charge controller. U0354 is stored when one of those partners finds that the module runs software or a calibration it does not accept, say after an exchange or a partial update. No maker documents U0354 publicly; wireless charging is rare in series cars. BMW ran such a system as a pilot on 200 California 530e cars (option SA 4VC) and, in SIB 61 23 19, limited diagnosis to dealers that own a ground pad module. Until the software matches, wireless charging stays unavailable; charging by cable and driving are unaffected. U014B means lost contact, U044C invalid data.
c: Inductive charger module replaced but not programmed or configured
Battery or charge controller updated to a level that expects other charger software
Software update of the charger module aborted
s: Wireless charging does not start
Charging warning in the display while cable charging still works

U0400.d: U0400 is the unspecific entry of the invalid-data block. It says that a module receives messages from another node on time but rejects their content, without naming the sender; the codes from U0401 upward name the partner. GM's 2011 Saab 9-5 manual handles U0400 to U05FF in one procedure: the receiver doubts the integrity of incoming data, the test runs between 9 and 16 V while the network works, no circuit check is involved, and if the code stands alone the named module is reprogrammed, then replaced. Harley-Davidson shows the usual trigger in bulletin M1720: on 2021-2024 Pan America models, updating only the ECM leaves a U040000 that cannot be cleared, so the BCM must be flashed first. Lost contact is the U01xx block, software conflicts are U03xx. Effects depend on the module that stores it.
c: Modules on different software levels after a partial update
Replaced module not programmed or configured
Disturbed bus signal from poor connections or low supply voltage
s: Code cannot be cleared or returns at once
Functions of the storing module limited or warning lamp on, depending on the vehicle

U0401.t: Invalid Data Received From ECM/PCM A
U0401.d: U0401 is stored by a module that keeps receiving the engine or powertrain controller's messages but finds their content faulty. Most often the transmission controller logs it; Ford's 2012 OBD summary names engine torque and pedal position as the data concerned. In GM's 2025 tables the TCM checks rolling counter, protection value and checksum of several ECM frames, treats 8 bad results within 18 checks as a failure and classes the code Type A (MIL at once); GM's driver-assist module sets it as Type C and only switches off adaptive cruise. Saab's 2011 code list adds sub-codes 72 (counter) and 74 (checksum). Bentley's Continental GT gearbox stores U040100 when brake pressure decays too fast in ACC stops; a passive entry can stay. Ford's 2020 Escape and GM's 2024 Corvette needed new software. U0100 means lost contact.
c: Software of the ECM/PCM or of the receiving module (update available)
ECM sends a signal flagged invalid, for example after its own sensor fault
Disturbed CAN traffic from connectors, wiring or low battery voltage
s: Check engine light, often stored in the transmission controller
Harsh shifts or transmission limp-home mode
Adaptive cruise control switched off

U0402.d: U0402 is the reverse case of U0401: the engine controller or another listener receives the transmission controller's frames but rejects their content.
