GM's 2025 ECM checks counter, protection value and checksum of the estimated-gear and general transmission information signals, flags a fault at 8 errors among 18 checks, Type A after one trip; the body controller uses 15 of 16 and Type B. Saab's 2011 list names sub-codes 72 (counter), 73 (parity) and 74 (checksum). On the 2022 Ram 1500 5.7 L eTorque the PCM, once U0402 is set, refuses torque requests from the TCM, the gearbox falls into a fixed limp gear and the MIL lights; PCM software (18-001-23) cures it. On 2014-2015 Cherokee and 200 nine-speeds FCA traced U0402 and a rough 5-4 downshift to the C-clutch snap ring (21-008-15). U0101 is lost contact.
c: Software of PCM or TCM (update available)
Internal transmission fault making the TCM send implausible values
Disturbed CAN traffic from connectors, wiring or low voltage
s: Check engine light
Transmission stuck in a fixed gear (limp mode)
Harsh or delayed shifts

U0403.t: Invalid Data Received From Transfer Case Control Module
U0403.d: U0403 points to data from the transfer case control module, the unit that engages four-wheel drive and selects the range: its frames keep coming, yet the listener rejects what they carry. In GM's 2025 tables the ECM watches the secondary-axle signals from this module for faulty rolling counter, protection value or checksum, needs 8 bad results out of 18 to fail and assigns Type B (MIL on the second trip), whereas the lost-contact code U0102 there is Type C. On 2014-2016 Silverado, Sierra, Tahoe and Escalade GM saw U0403 with a Service 4WD message when ignition 1 voltage dropped out at fuse block terminals (PIT5391A). On 2019-2020 Ram 1500 with electronic transfer cases, U0403 and U1440 with traction lamp, driveline bumps and motor clicking were fixed by new drivetrain module software (08-083-20). U0303 is a software conflict.
c: Software of the transfer case or drivetrain control module (update available)
Ignition voltage dropping out at fuse block terminals or relays
Faulty range position sensor making the module send implausible values
Transfer case control module internally faulty
s: Service 4WD message
Traction control or check engine light on
Driveline bumps or clicking from the transfer case motor

U0404.t: Invalid Data Received From Gear Shift Control Module A
U0404.d: Gear shift control module A is the electronic selector of shift-by-wire cars: lever, dial or buttons that report the chosen range as data. U0404 means its messages still arrive but the receiver, usually the transmission controller, rejects them. GM's 2025 ECM checks counter and protection fields of the selector's position-sensor and self-check signals, fails a signal after 4 errors in 10 or 8 in 18 checks; the code is Type B with two trips. FCA stored U0404 in the TCM of 2016 Durango and Grand Cherokee eight-speeds with MIL and a blinking M on shifter and cluster, cured by TCM software (21-011-16 Rev. A). Audi found U040400 in the gearbox unit of 2021 A6/A7 models with an intermittent selector lever fault message and no range selectable; the gateway J533 needed new software. U0103 means lost contact, U0304 a software conflict.
c: Software of TCM or gateway (update available)
Position sensor or electronics in the selector delivering implausible values
Connector or bus line at the selector loose or corroded
s: Selector fault message or flashing range indicator
Range cannot be selected or vehicle stays in Park
Check engine light

U0405.t: Invalid Data Received From Cruise Control Module
U0405.d: Today the module behind this code is usually the distance radar of adaptive cruise, the unit that asks the engine controller for speed and torque changes. U0405 is set when those requests arrive but fail the receiver's integrity checks. Saab's 2011 code list breaks it down into sub-codes 71 (invalid data), 72 (message counter) and 74 (checksum). Stellantis documents it on the 3.0 L Hurricane six: 2025 Ram 1500 (TSB 18-071-24) and 2023 Wagoneer/Grand Wagoneer (18-076-25) store U0405 together with U0104 as permanent codes with MIL, and the bulletins call the detection false; new PCM software lets the codes clear on their own, which matters where emissions inspections read the MIL. Expect adaptive cruise to drop out while driving is otherwise normal. U0104 is lost contact, U0305 a software conflict.
c: Engine controller software detecting the fault falsely (update available)
Radar or cruise module sending implausible requests, for example after misalignment or damage
Disturbed CAN traffic from connectors or wiring
s: Adaptive cruise control unavailable
Check engine light that does not go out after clearing

U0406.t: Invalid Data Received From Fuel Injector Control Module
U0406.d: U0406 means a receiving controller, normally the ECM/PCM, gets messages from the fuel injector control module that arrive but fail its checks: wrong counter, checksum, range or a signal marked invalid. Ford's 2012 OBD summary shows the U04xx principle with U0401: the TCM stores it when the ECM sends invalid or faulted torque or pedal data. A separate injector module exists only on some designs; GM's 2013 bi-fuel CNG Silverado/Sierra uses an FICM that switches the injectors and passes rail pressure and temperature to the ECM over serial data. No manufacturer documents U0406 publicly. As fuel delivery affects emissions, CARB requires such inputs to be monitored and a MIL is likely. U0105 means lost contact, U0306 a software mismatch.
c: Corroded or loose connector, damaged bus wire to the injector module
Low supply voltage at the injector module
Software levels of injector module and ECM do not match
s: Check engine light on
Rough running, misfire or hard start
Reduced power

U0407.t: Invalid Data Received From Glow Plug Control Module
U0407.d: U0407 is stored when the engine controller receives data from the glow plug control module that it rejects as implausible. Volkswagen lists the code in the 2014 Touareg diesel OBD chart as Invalid Data Received From Glow Plug Control Module 1, criterion implausible messages received. On that engine the glow unit talks to the ECM over LIN; VW uses U0106 for a missing LIN message and U0307 for a failed software check, which separates the three siblings clearly. Ford's 2012 OBD summary shows the same U04xx idea for other modules: data arrive but are faulted. Because the glow module also reports plug faults, invalid data can hide real glow plug problems. Expect hard cold starts, white smoke and on a diesel usually the MIL.
c: LIN wire or connector between glow module and ECM corroded or loose
Glow plug control module internally faulty
Voltage dip during glow check or cranking
Glow module software does not match the ECM
s: Check engine or glow plug light on
Hard starting in cold weather
White smoke and rough idle after cold start

U0408.t: Invalid Data Received From Throttle Actuator Control Module
U0408.d: U0408 points to messages from the throttle actuator control module that the receiver, usually the ECM/PCM, judges invalid: implausible content, a failed checksum or counter, or a value outside its range. Most vehicles integrate throttle control in the engine controller, so a separate TAC module and therefore this code are uncommon; no manufacturer documents U0408 publicly. Ford's 2012 OBD summary illustrates the U04xx logic with U0401, which the TCM stores when ECM torque or pedal data are faulted. Because the throttle meters intake air, CARB's comprehensive component rules apply, and a MIL together with reduced power or a limp mode is likely. U0107 means lost contact, U0308 a software mismatch with the same module.
c: Damaged bus wire or poor connector contact at the throttle module
Throttle actuator control module internally faulty
Software of throttle module and ECM do not match
s: Check engine light on
Limp mode with reduced throttle response
Unstable idle or stalling

U0409.t: Invalid Data Received From Alternative Fuel Control Module
U0409.d: U0409 is logged when the engine controller receives data from the alternative fuel control module that fail its validity checks. Such a module runs the gas side of bi-fuel CNG or LPG vehicles. In Ford's 2000 bi-fuel OBD description the AFCM passes the requested mode (ALT or GAS) and supply status between the gas metering unit and the PCM, which then switches the petrol injectors on or off; GM's 2013 CNG Silverado/Sierra sends rail pressure and temperature from its injector module to the ECM over serial data. No manufacturer documents U0409 publicly. Corrupt data can make the engine fall back to petrol or misjudge gas pressure, so CARB monitoring applies and a MIL is likely. U0108 means lost contact, U0309 a software mismatch.
c: Corroded connector or damaged wiring of the retrofit or factory gas system
Faulty gas rail pressure/temperature sensor delivering implausible values
Alternative fuel control module faulty or wrongly configured
s: Check engine light on
Engine stays on or switches back to petrol
Gas gauge or fuel mode indicator incorrect

U040A.t: Invalid Data Received From Air Conditioning Control Module
U040A.d: J2012 separates the air conditioning control module, which governs the refrigerant side with compressor, pressures and, in electrified cars, an electric compressor drive, from the HVAC module that handles blower, flaps and set temperature (invalid data from that one is U0424). U040A is stored when frames from the A/C unit arrive but carry values the receiver cannot trust, such as a failed counter or checksum or a signal outside its range. No manufacturer documents U040A publicly. GM confirms the module itself: the 2011 Saab 9-5 code list carries U010F for lost contact with it, and GM's generic routine for U0400-U05FF reprograms the named module and replaces it only if the code returns. The compressor is likely held off, so cooling and demisting suffer; engine and emissions stay unaffected. U010F is lost contact.
c: Software of the A/C control module or of the receiver out of step
Faulty pressure or temperature input making the module send invalid values
Disturbed bus line, poor ground or low supply voltage at the module
s: Air conditioning blows warm, compressor stays off
Windows demist slowly

U040B.t: Invalid Data Received From Exhaust Gas Recirculation Control Module A
U040B.d: U040B refers to an exhaust gas recirculation system driven by its own electronics on the bus, for example a smart EGR valve actuator that receives position targets and returns its measured position. The code is set when that unit's replies reach the engine controller but fail plausibility or protection checks, so the controller can no longer verify how much exhaust gas flows back. U040B appears in no public manufacturer document and in none of the bulletins indexed by NHTSA. GM's 2025 tables show how such checks work on other emission-related modules: counter, protection value and checksum, a fail ratio such as 8 of 18 samples, then a MIL. CARB requires EGR flow to be monitored, so the code counts as emission-relevant; expect EGR to be switched off, higher NOx and possibly less power. U010A is lost contact, U040C module B.
c: Electronics or position sensor of the EGR actuator A delivering implausible values
Heat-damaged connector or bus line at the EGR unit
Software of engine controller and EGR module A out of step
EGR control module A internally faulty
s: Check engine light
Reduced power or rough idle
EGR flow codes stored alongside

U040C.t: Invalid Data Received From Exhaust Gas Recirculation Control Module B
U040C.d: U040C concerns a second, separately networked EGR control unit, B. Two units appear on engines with separate high- and low-pressure recirculation paths, common on modern diesels, or with one EGR valve per cylinder bank; which one counts as B is up to the maker. The engine controller logs U040C when module B keeps talking but its content fails validation, while module A may still deliver clean data, which narrows the search to B's branch. Public manufacturer material and the NHTSA bulletins are silent on U040C, so its limits are not known; checks of counter and checksum as in GM's 2025 tables are the common pattern. With one EGR path unverified the controller usually closes it, NOx rises, and the MIL is expected because CARB treats EGR as a monitored system. U010B is lost contact, U040B module A.
c: Electronics or position sensor of EGR actuator B delivering implausible values
Connector or bus line in the branch of module B damaged by heat or moisture
Module B with software that does not match the engine controller
s: Check engine light
Reduced power, more smoke or higher fuel consumption

U040D.t: Invalid Data Received From Turbocharger/Supercharger Control Module A
U040D.d: Turbocharger/supercharger control module A is in practice an electronic charger actuator that sets the vanes of a variable-geometry turbine or a wastegate on command and reports position and status back. U040D means those reports arrive but the engine controller judges them invalid. No manufacturer documents U040D publicly. The module is documented through its lost-contact code U010C: GM's 2017 small-diesel table expects its frames on a dedicated sensor bus, and FCA replaced the turbo actuator of 2015 Ram 2500/3500 trucks with the 6.7 L Cummins under a warranty extension when U010C came with boost codes (09-005-22). With invalid actuator data the boost loop cannot be closed with confidence, so the controller usually caps boost and torque; boost control is emission-relevant under CARB, so a MIL is likely. U040E is module B.
c: Electronics of the turbo actuator degraded by heat
Sticking vanes or linkage making the actuator report implausible positions
Connector or sensor bus line at the actuator damaged
s: Check engine light
Noticeably reduced power (limp mode)
Boost pressure codes stored alongside

U040E.t: Invalid Data Received From Turbocharger/Supercharger Control Module B
U040E.d: U040E is reserved for a second charger control module, B, on engines that run two separately actuated chargers: twin or sequential turbo layouts, or a turbocharger combined with an electrically driven or clutched supercharger. The engine controller sets it when module B's position or status messages keep coming but are judged invalid. No manufacturer documents U040E publicly, the NHTSA bulletin index has no entry, and thresholds are unknown. A useful check in the workshop is whether U040D is also stored: if only B is affected, its own actuator, connector and line are the first suspects, whereas both together point to the shared bus or the controller. With one charger unverified, boost and torque are usually limited and a MIL is likely, as CARB treats boost control as emission-relevant. U010D is lost contact, U040D module A.
c: Electronics or position feedback of charger actuator B faulty
Connector or bus line of module B damaged by heat
Module B with software that does not match the engine controller
s: Check engine light
Reduced power, especially at higher load

U040F.t: Invalid Data Received From Reductant Control Module
U040F.d: On a diesel with SCR, the reductant control module looks after the urea circuit, chiefly the pump, dosing and heater control, and reports pressure and status to the engine controller. U040F means its messages arrive but fail validation. GM's 2025 ECM tables check counter and checksum of the DEF information and dosing status frames, count 6 errors among 15 or 3 among 10 checks as a failure; the result is Type A with the MIL on trip one. Ford's 2023 diesel OBD summary groups U040F with the functional test of the reductant pump motor and sets it when the duty-cycle control signal of the pump motor controller leaves the 4 to 96 percent window, next to pump speed, voltage and temperature codes. Without trusted module data dosing is stopped, NOx rises and the inducement strategy may later limit speed. U010E is lost contact.
c: Pump motor controller in the reductant module reporting an invalid control signal
Corroded connector or damaged bus line at the tank-mounted module
Software of the reductant module or ECM out of step
s: Check engine light
DEF/AdBlue warning with countdown to a speed limit
Further SCR or reductant pump codes stored

U0410.t: Invalid Data Received From Fuel Pump Control Module
U0410.d: U0410 means the engine controller receives data from the fuel pump control module that it cannot trust, such as a bad checksum, counter or an out-of-range value. Many cars drive the in-tank pump through such a module to set the low-side pressure on demand. GM shows why the data matter for emissions: bulletin PIP5427 (2014-2016 trucks and SUVs) traces a lit service engine lamp and a fuel pressure deviation P2635 to communication faults between ECM and pump module, logged there as U0074 or GM's own U18A2. From 2014 GM renamed this unit chassis control module. No manufacturer documents U0410 publicly. Expect a MIL, hesitation or reduced power. U0109 means lost contact, U0310 a software mismatch.
c: Damaged bus wire or corroded connector to the fuel pump module (often near the tank)
Poor power or ground of the fuel pump module
Pump module and ECM software do not match after replacement
Fuel pump control module internally faulty
s: Check engine light on
Fuel pressure codes such as P2635 set together
Hesitation, stalling or reduced power

U0411.t: Invalid Data Received From Drive Motor Control Module
U0411.d: U0411 is stored when a controller, typically the engine or hybrid controller, receives messages from the drive motor control module (the inverter electronics of an electric traction motor) that it judges invalid. Volkswagen lists it in its 2014 hybrid OBD charts: for the Touareg Hybrid on implausible messages from the motor module, for the Jetta Hybrid on an incorrect CAN data length code. Bentley's Flying Spur Hybrid (2022-2023) stores U041100 in the engine control unit with a warning lamp, partly together with P0A2E for the motor temperature sensor circuit, and has the technician measure and inspect a harness connector. U0110 means lost contact, U0311 a software mismatch. Hybrid drive may be limited or switched off.
c: Damaged pins or poor contact in harness connectors near the drive motor (Bentley case)
Faulty motor temperature sensor circuit making the module send invalid data
Software of motor module and hybrid controller do not match
Drive motor control module internally faulty
s: Engine or drive system warning light on
Electric drive unavailable, engine runs constantly
Reduced power

U0412.t: Invalid Data Received From Battery Energy Control Module A
U0412.d: U0412 is stored when the hybrid or engine controller receives data from battery energy control module A, the management unit of the high-voltage battery, that it rejects as invalid. Volkswagen's 2014 Jetta Hybrid OBD chart sets it on implausible received data. FCA lists U0412-00 for the 2019 Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid (TSB 08-114-22) among codes that light the MIL and can remain as permanent codes, so the vehicle fails a state smog check; the fix is new software for the hybrid control processors, not a battery part. CARB requires emission-related control units to be monitored, which explains the MIL. U0111 means lost contact, U0413 covers module B, U0312 a software mismatch. Charging or electric driving may be limited.
c: Software error in hybrid controller or battery management (FCA: reflash HCP/AHCP)
Bus wiring or connector fault between battery module and hybrid controller
Weak 12 V battery disturbing module start-up
Battery energy control module internally faulty
s: Check engine light on, code may become permanent
Charging or electric driving limited
Hybrid system warning message

U0413.t: Invalid Data Received From Battery Energy Control Module B
U0413.d: U0413 is the counterpart of U0412 for battery energy control module B, used where the high-voltage battery has a second management unit or a split controller. Volkswagen's 2014 Jetta Hybrid chart sets it on implausible data, while the 2014 Touareg Hybrid chart uses U0413 for its single battery module, which shows that the A/B assignment is maker-specific. Audi stores U041300 in the engine and electric drive controllers of the Q5 and A7 plug-in hybrids (model years 2019-2022) together with a drive system warning; the cause was software in the battery management and its junction box, cured by an update. U0112 means lost contact, U0313 a software mismatch, U0412 covers module A. Electric driving may be restricted.
c: Software error in battery management or junction box (Audi: SVM update)
Bus wiring or connector fault at the battery module
Battery energy control module B internally faulty
s: Drive system or engine warning light on
Electric driving or charging restricted
Code stored in engine and electric drive controllers

U0414.t: Invalid Data Received From Four-Wheel Drive Clutch Control Module
U0414.d: U0414 is set when a listener, usually the engine controller, receives frames from the four-wheel-drive clutch control module but cannot trust what they carry. That module regulates an on-demand coupling feeding torque to the secondary axle and reports its state on the bus. GM's 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG03B) test the secondary-axle signal every 12.5 ms for faulty rolling counters, protection values or checksums; 8 errors among 18 checks, with at least 11 V and 5 s of stable operation, record a Type B fault, which lights the MIL on a second faulty trip. Ford's 2014 code interpretation also marks U0414 as a MIL code. Lost contact with the module is U0114, a software mismatch U0314. Expect an AWD warning and drive on the primary axle until the data are valid again.
c: Four-wheel-drive clutch module sends faulty values (internal fault, moisture)
Disturbed CAN traffic from connectors, wiring or low supply voltage
Clutch module and receiver on software levels that do not match
s: AWD or 4WD warning in the cluster
Drive on the primary axle only
Check engine light after two trips

U0415.t: Invalid Data Received From Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module
U0415.d: U0415 means a module accepts frames from the ABS control module only to find their content invalid, typically wheel speeds or brake status with a wrong counter, checksum or a value flagged as unavailable. GM's Saab 9-5 list (2011) splits it into sub-types 72 (message counter) and 74 (checksum) for the electronic brake module. Ford's 2014 code list gives it both MIL and wrench lamp. The storing module varies: Ford SSM 51489 says a 2023 F-Super Duty AWD module may log U0415 in self-test when no valid ABS signal arrives in time, harmless without MIL or other codes; FCA cures U0415-00 with MIL and a Service Transmission message on the 2025 Jeep Compass 2.0 L by TCM software (21-043-25). U0121 is lost contact, U0315 a software mismatch.
c: Software of the receiving module (TCM, AWD, steering) too strict or faulty; update available
ABS module passing on implausible values, for example from a faulty wheel speed sensor
Disturbed CAN traffic from water in connectors, wiring or low voltage
s: ABS, traction or stability warning lamps
Check engine light and Service Transmission message (model-specific)
AWD, steering or camera functions limited

U0416.t: Invalid Data Received From Vehicle Dynamics Control Module
U0416.d: U0416 points at the vehicle dynamics control module, the stability control unit that brakes single wheels and trims engine torque. A receiver logs the code when that unit's frames arrive but fail the plausibility check. GM's 2011 Saab 9-5 list adds sub-types 72 (counter wrong) and 74 (checksum error); Ford's 2014 code list carries U0416 without a lamp. Driver assistance suffers most: Honda bulletin 17-064 lists U0416-68 and U0416-92 on the 2017 CR-V after battery work, with adaptive cruise and brake warnings, and cures it with new radar software; Mercedes (LI54.71-P-078112) finds U0416FE in the Distronic unit of the G-Class, tied to weak battery health and gone after a key cycle. U0122 is lost contact, U0316 software. Assist systems switch off, the MIL normally stays dark.
c: Weak or recently disconnected 12 V battery disturbing the stability unit's data
Software of the receiving assistance module (radar, camera) needs an update
Steering angle or sensor calibration lost after battery work
Missing or damaged wire or connector in the bus branch
s: Adaptive cruise or emergency brake assist unavailable
Stability or brake warning in the cluster

U0417.t: Invalid Data Received From Park Brake Control Module
U0417.d: U0417 covers implausible data from the park brake control module, the controller of an electric parking brake that clamps the rear calipers by motor and reports apply state and faults on the bus. A receiver stores it when these frames arrive with a bad counter, checksum or an invalid value. No manufacturer explains U0417 in public documents. GM lists it only among history codes of the 2014 Cadillac ELR (PIC5988) that should not lead to replaced or reprogrammed parts unless they can be reproduced. GM's 2025 tables also show that the park brake apply status may be judged under U0418 instead: the front camera module counts it among brake signals whose protection may fail in 3 of 4 messages. U0128 is lost contact, U0317 software. Expect a park brake warning, disabled auto-apply or hill-hold functions and no MIL.
c: Low battery voltage or a voltage dip corrupting park brake messages
Park brake control module or its actuator feedback faulty
Connector or wiring fault in the park brake bus branch
s: Park brake warning lamp or message
Auto hold or hill start assist unavailable
Code only stored in history without current fault

U0418.t: Invalid Data Received From Brake System Control Module A
U0418.d: U0418 says a node rejects the content of frames from brake system control module A, on many cars the unit that combines ABS, stability control and brake boost. GM's 2025 tables are detailed: the engine controller tests brake status signals for bad counters, protection values or checksums, 8 faults in 18 checks give Type A with MIL after one trip; the TCM runs the same test as Type B, the BCM demands 15 bad of 16, and the front camera rates its check Special Type C and only disables adaptive cruise. Saab's 9-5 list adds sub-types 71, 72 and 74. FCA notes for the 2021 Jeep Cherokee 2.4 L that U0418 may set falsely below 10 V and reflashes the PCM (18-078-22); BrightDrop 24-NA-107 forbids repairs for it on the Zevo 600. U0129 is lost contact, U0318 software.
c: Low battery voltage (below about 10 V) during start or standstill
Engine or transmission controller software reacting too sensitively; update available
Loose connector or harness fault disturbing the chassis bus
Brake system control module internally faulty
s: Check engine light
Adaptive cruise, stop-start or driver assistance unavailable
Brake or stability warning in the cluster

U0419.t: Invalid Data Received From Steering Effort Control Module
U0419.d: U0419 concerns the steering effort control module, which varies the assistance or steering ratio the driver feels. Ford uses that name for the controller of its adaptive steering: bulletin 16-2066 on the 2016 Edge and MKX stores C1B00 in the steering effort control module (SECM) and replaces the steering wheel that houses the actuator. A receiver, such as the ABS or power steering unit, logs U0419 when SECM frames keep arriving but carry implausible values, a bad counter or checksum. No manufacturer documents U0419 publicly, so thresholds and the reacting module are not known. The power steering control module has its own code, U0420. U0130 is lost contact, U0319 software. Expect a steering warning and a fixed ratio or assistance; no MIL is expected.
c: Steering effort module or its actuator reporting implausible values
Clock spring, connector or bus wiring fault in the steering branch
Module not calibrated or configured after replacement
s: Steering system warning in the cluster
Steering ratio or assistance no longer speed-dependent

U041A.t: Invalid Data Received From Battery Isolation/Voltage Stabilization Control Module
U041A.d: U041A refers to the battery isolation or voltage stabilization module, which separates an auxiliary battery or sensitive loads from the starter circuit, so a restart after an automatic engine stop leaves the rest of the electrical system at stable voltage. GM's patent US 9,803,608 builds such an isolator from MOSFET switches. A receiver logs it once the module's status frames still arrive but are rejected as invalid. No manufacturer documents U041A publicly. Ford shows the module family on the 2021-2022 F-150 3.5 L PowerBoost, where lost contact (U061E) turns on the wrench lamp and a weak ground GD132 or a failed auxiliary battery isolator is blamed (SSM 50843); checking ground and auxiliary battery first makes sense for U041A as well. Expect stop-start to be disabled; a MIL is unlikely.
c: Poor ground connection of the isolation module
Weak auxiliary battery making the module report implausible values
Battery isolator or stabilizer internally faulty
s: Automatic stop-start not available
Battery or charging system message

U041B.t: Invalid Data Received From Exhaust Gas Sensor Module A
U041B.d: U041B names exhaust gas sensor module A, an electronic unit that heats and evaluates an exhaust probe, usually a wide-band oxygen sensor, and sends the result as bus data. The engine controller sets the code when the module still talks but its values fail plausibility, carry wrong counters or report the sensor as not ready. No manufacturer documents U041B publicly. Chrysler shows such a module on the Cummins 6.7 L in 2010-2012 Ram heavy-duty pickups: bulletin 25-002-14 lists its lost-communication code U011A among oxygen sensor faults and fits an overlay harness to the module before parts are replaced. CARB requires digital inputs of emission controls to be checked for out-of-range and rationality faults. Expect the MIL and closed-loop or aftertreatment functions held back. U046E is module B.
c: Heat-damaged sensor harness or connector at the sensor module
Aged or contaminated probe giving implausible readings
Exhaust gas sensor module internally faulty
s: Check engine light
Higher fuel use or regeneration problems on diesels

U041C.t: Invalid Data Received From Rocker Arm Control Module A
U041C.d: U041C relates to rocker arm control module A, the controller that switches oil-actuated rocker arms to change valve lift or shut cylinders down. The engine controller stores it when the module's lock-state or feedback frames arrive with implausible content, wrong counters or invalid values. No manufacturer documents U041C publicly, and it is open which engines use a separate module. CARB treats systems that vary valve lift or timing as monitored emission controls and asks for rationality checks of digital inputs, separate from lack-of-communication codes. Without trusted feedback the controller will usually keep all cylinders at normal lift and record the fault with the MIL; fuel use rises and running may be uneven. U011B is lost contact; module B has U041D.
c: Low oil pressure or sticking switching solenoid causing implausible lock-state feedback
Rocker arm control module A internally faulty
Connector or bus wiring fault at module A
s: Check engine light
Cylinder deactivation or valve lift switching locked out
Higher fuel consumption

U041D.t: Invalid Data Received From Rocker Arm Control Module B
U041D.d: U041D is the counterpart for rocker arm control module B, used where the switching of rocker arms is split, for instance by cylinder bank. The code tells that the engine controller still receives B's messages, but their lift or lock status cannot be trusted. Comparing with U041C helps: B alone points to that module, its harness branch or its solenoids, both together to the shared supply or the bus. No manufacturer documents U041D publicly and no thresholds are known. CARB requires monitoring of variable valve lift and plausibility checks of digital inputs. Likely effects: MIL, cylinders on the B side held in full-lift mode, higher fuel use and perhaps rough running. U011C is lost contact.
c: Switching solenoid or oil supply on the B side faulty
Rocker arm control module B internally faulty
Shared supply or bus fault (then usually with U041C)
s: Check engine light
Uneven running or higher fuel use

U041E.t: Invalid Data Received From All Wheel Drive Control Module
U041E.d: U041E concerns the all-wheel-drive control module, the unit that manages a complete AWD or transfer case system rather than a single clutch (U0414). A receiver logs it when that module's torque, mode or status frames arrive but are invalid. Stellantis documents it: on 2023 Ram 1500 (08-237-23) and Grand Wagoneer/Wagoneer built 16 to 24 June 2023 (08-122-24) a transfer case shift motor connector that was not fully seated caused U041E-00 along with U0403, U0418 and transfer case motor and sensor codes, a MIL and a 4WD service light. Ford's 2014 code list names U041E without a lamp. U011D is lost contact. Typical effects are an AWD or 4WD warning and a fixed drive mode or drive on one axle.
c: Transfer case shift motor or module connector not fully seated
Transfer case motor or position sensor faulty, making the module send invalid status
s: 4WD or AWD service light
Check engine light (model-specific)
Four-wheel-drive modes unavailable

U041F.t: Invalid Data Received From Throttle Actuator B Control Module
U041F.d: U041F addresses throttle actuator B control module, a separately housed driver for a second electronic throttle. Most engines use one throttle driven directly by the engine controller; a separate driver for the first throttle is covered by U0408. The engine controller sets U041F when B's position or status frames arrive but disagree with plausibility checks or carry bad counters. No manufacturer documents U041F publicly, and production engines with such a split are not known. CARB demands rationality monitoring of digital inputs used by emission controls. If throttle data cannot be trusted, the controller limits airflow, often to a fixed limp-home opening. Expect MIL and reduced power. U011E is lost contact, U0308 a software mismatch with a throttle controller.
c: Position feedback of throttle actuator B implausible (sensor or gearbox wear)
Throttle actuator B control module internally faulty
Connector or bus wiring fault at module B
s: Check engine light
Reduced power or limp-home mode

U0420.t: Invalid Data Received From Power Steering Control Module A
U0420.d: U0420 is stored when a listener gets frames from power steering control module A, the electric assist unit on rack or column, yet judges their content unusable. GM's 2025 tables name several listeners: the ECM tests the steering wheel information for bad counter, protection value or checksum and needs 8 failures within 18 samples for a Type C fault with no MIL; the EBCM runs similar Type C tests, and the EOCM3 assistance controller checks torque overlay and assist status (3 of 4 or 6 of 10 frames) and switches adaptive cruise off. Mazda bulletin 15-003/20 blames U0420:68 in the front camera on low voltage during cranking, which spoils the EPS centre learning; new EPS software helps. Jeep 08-094-25 (2025 Wagoneer) reflashes the EPS when U0420-00 comes with a MIL. U0131 is lost contact, U0320 software.
c: Low battery voltage during cranking corrupts steering module start-up data
Steering module or receiving module software needs an update
Corroded connector or poor ground at the steering module
s: Adaptive cruise, lane keeping or emergency braking unavailable
Stability control or steering warning in the cluster
Code returns after cold starts with a weak battery

U0421.t: Invalid Data Received From Suspension Control Module A
U0421.d: Suspension control module A runs air springs, ride height or adjustable dampers and broadcasts level and status data. U0421 tells that a receiving module gets these frames but finds them corrupt or implausible. GM spells out one receiver: in the 2025 tables the electronic brake module watches the vehicle level control frames for a frozen rolling counter or a wrong protection value, sets the fault at 8 errors in a window of 16 and does the same with 3 of 16 for the top speed limit sent by the automatic level control; all are Type C, so no MIL. FCA documents U0421 on 2019-2020 Ram 2500/3500 with air suspension: before an air suspension module is replaced, pull its 20 A fuse F50, clear U0132, U0421 and U0422 and road test, and replace only if they return. Ride height may stay fixed. U0132 is lost contact.
c: Suspension module software hang, cleared by a power reset
Low supply voltage or weak battery during start-up
Internal fault of the suspension control module
s: Service air suspension or leveling warning
Ride height no longer adjusts
Stability or brake system message alongside

U0422.t: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module
U0422.d: U0422 applies to cars with a single body controller; with several, U0431 names body control module A and U0443 to U0446 modules B to E. A receiver logs it when BCM frames arrive but carry unusable content. GM's 2025 ECM checks body information frames with 8 faults in 18 samples and serial data frames with 3 in 10, after 5 s at 11 V or more, as Type B, so the MIL follows a second faulty trip. Ford's 2012 OBD guide has the PCM set U0422 without MIL when VIN, tire, axle or vehicle configuration data from the BCM lie outside their valid range, or when the engine-off timer reads FFFFh after a battery disconnect. Volkswagen's 2014 Touareg book uses it for an ambient temperature of 00h. FCA links an active U0422 in the hybrid processor of the 2021 Pacifica to a check engine light. U0140 is lost contact.
c: Battery disconnect or low voltage leaves default values in BCM messages
Missing or wrong BCM configuration such as VIN, tire size or vehicle options
BCM or receiver software fault, cured by an update
s: Check engine light on some vehicles
Cruise control or driver assistance unavailable
Wrong outside temperature or A/C not working

U0423.t: Invalid Data Received From Instrument Panel Cluster Control Module
U0423.d: The instrument cluster does more than display: it sends outside temperature, display and chime status or confirmations from its menus to other units. U0423 marks cluster frames that arrive but fail the receiver's checks. In GM's 2025 driver assistance controller EOCM3, 8 of 10 bad frames on chime state, display status or speed limit confirmations set a Special Type C fault that turns adaptive cruise off. Volkswagen's 2014 Touareg book has the engine controller log U0423 when the cluster still reports the ambient temperature start value FEh. Toyota's T-SB-0270-17 for the 2017 iA lists U0423 in the ABS with U0323 and U3000 when battery or display was disconnected; TPMS and TCS/DSC lamps stay on. Honda saw U0423-68 with an auto high beam message on the 2017 CR-V. Ford's 2014 list marks it MIL. U0155 is lost contact.
c: Battery, fuse or display disconnected so the cluster sends start values
Software fault in cluster or receiving module
Another node on the same bus disturbing the cluster's messages
s: Stability, tire pressure or assistance warnings that cannot be cleared
Adaptive cruise or auto high beam unavailable
Check engine light on some makes

U0424.t: Invalid Data Received From HVAC Control Module
U0424.d: The HVAC control module reports climate requests and, on newer layouts, also the voltages of switches on the climate faceplate that it measures itself. U0424 says a receiver rejects these frames. GM documents the logic in the BCM of its 2025 vehicles: alive rolling counts, protection values, checksums or CRCs of the HVAC messages are checked every 10 ms, and 8 failures in 10 samples set a Type B fault once the BCM has been up for 5 s, the partial network has run for 3 s, power mode is Run and the battery has more than 11 V. As long as U0164 or U0424 is present the BCM suspends its faceplate switch tests (B2A01 and others), since their values come over CAN. GM's Saab 9-5 list (2011) contains U0424, and Ford marks it with the MIL in its 2014 code interpretation. U0164 is lost contact, U0324 software.
c: HVAC control module or faceplate electronics faulty
Low battery voltage or a reset of the HVAC module during start-up
HVAC or BCM software level that needs an update
s: Climate controls or buttons react incorrectly or not at all
A/C or defrost not available
Check engine light on some makes

U0425.t: Invalid Data Received From Auxiliary Heater Control Module
U0425.d: U0425 concerns the auxiliary heater control module, the controller of an extra heat source such as a fuel-fired coolant heater on a diesel. The HVAC or engine controller sets it when the heater's status frames arrive with implausible content. No manufacturer documents U0425 publicly; GM's 2013 bulletin PIP5094 merely includes it in a long list of codes for which terminal fit should be checked before circuit tests. Ford's patent US 10,124,649 shows how such a heater is tied into the network: it talks to the HVAC unit over the bus and to the engine controller through a bus interface, receives ambient temperature from it and runs its own fuel pump. GM's 6.6 L Duramax ECM (2014) watches messages from this module, stating lost contact as U0166, Special Type C. U0325 is software. The heater stays off; no MIL is expected.
c: Auxiliary heater control unit faulty or locked after an internal fault
Low supply voltage at the heater, for example from a weak battery
Loose terminals or corrosion in the heater's bus connector
s: Auxiliary or parking heater does not start
Slow warm-up and weak cabin heat in cold weather

U0426.t: Invalid Data Received From Vehicle Immobilizer Control Module
U0426.d: The vehicle immobilizer control module reads the transponder in the key and passes a coded release to the engine controller. U0426 is logged when that release or status message arrives but cannot be accepted, so the handshake fails even though the module is still talking. Stellantis documents a case on the 2015-2018 Ram ProMaster: the BCM holds U0426-31, labelled Minikrypt error, together with an intermittent no-start and a stuck key; the PCM did not power down at key off, and aftermarket equipment had disturbed the ignition feed circuits, so the voltages at each switch position must be checked (STAR case S2008000160). Ford's 2014 code list includes U0426 without a MIL flag. Lost contact is U0167, a software mismatch U0326; U0427 covers the security module. Typically the starter turns but the engine never fires.
c: Ignition feed voltages do not match the key position, often due to aftermarket equipment
Damaged key transponder or key not matched to the vehicle
s: Engine cranks but does not start, or no start at times
Security or key warning lamp flashing
Key hard to remove from the ignition

U0427.t: Invalid Data Received From Vehicle Security Control Module
U0427.d: The vehicle security control module looks after theft protection: alarm, door, bonnet and tailgate monitoring and, with some makers, the key authorisation for the engine. U0427 marks messages from this module that reach a partner but fail its checks. No manufacturer documents U0427 publicly; GM's 2013 bulletin PIP5094 only names it among many codes for which terminal fit comes before circuit tests. Chrysler shows how far the module may reach: bulletin 18-023-13 for the 2012-2013 Grand Voyager 2.8 L diesel names its wireless control module the vehicle security control module in U0168 and treats that code as a sign of a disturbed ignition handshake, cured by PCM software. If it joins the key check, the start may be refused; otherwise alarm or remote locking misbehave. U0168 is lost contact, U0327 software. No MIL is expected.
c: Security control module faulty or reset during start-up
Aftermarket alarm or remote start interfering with the module or its supply
Poor terminal fit or corrosion at the module connector
s: Alarm triggers falsely or cannot be armed
Remote locking or keyless functions unreliable
Engine start refused on vehicles where the module joins the key check

U0428.t: Invalid Data Received From Steering Angle Sensor Module
U0428.d: U0428 is for a separately networked steering angle sensor module, usually on the column, feeding angle and rate to stability control, assistance and stop-start. GM's 2025 brake module counts wrong checksums or counters in its frames (8 of a 16 window) and reacts at once to a cleared validity bit or a data mask stuck at zero, all Type C without MIL. Where the angle comes from the steering gear, GM files a similar data mask fault under U0420. Mitsubishi's 2019 Outlander PHEV sets U0428 in the PHEV-ECU on a failed sensor signal; after the CAN check and data item 333 it asks for calibration and a steering angle offset reset. Jeep cured U0428 with MIL and early engine stops in stop-start on the 2017 Cherokee 3.2 L by PCM software (18-013-17). Audi fixes U042800 on dynamic steering by software (2049656/1). U0126 is lost contact.
c: Steering angle sensor not calibrated after replacement or alignment work
Software in the engine, brake or steering controller misjudging the sensor data
s: Stability control or steering warning lamp
Stop-start stops the engine at the wrong moment or stays off
Check engine light on some vehicles

U0429.t: Invalid Data Received From Steering Column Control Module
U0429.d: U0429 covers the steering column control module (SCCM), which reads stalks and wheel buttons and on many cars also houses the steering angle sensor. A partner logs the code when SCCM frames are received but rejected. Ford's 2024 OBD summary lists U0429_48 in the supervision layer of the PCM's throttle monitor as a non-MIL fault. Stellantis calls the sender SCM: U0429 is among the codes a PCM flash removes on the 2021 Chrysler 300 3.6 L (18-013-22), and on a 2023 Jeep Compass with C221F and an EPS lamp, a vehicle configuration restore and PROXI alignment clear it, not a new EPS (STAR S2319000006). Mercedes notes U042986 in the power steering unit when the Kostal column module signal is wrong (LI82.90-P-080159). U0428 is a stand-alone angle sensor module; U0212 lost contact, U0329 software.
c: Vehicle configuration not restored or aligned after a module repair
Software fault in PCM, steering unit or column module
Steering column control module or its angle sensor faulty
s: Steering or power steering warning lamp
Cruise control or stalk functions unavailable
Driver assistance systems switched off

U042A.t: Invalid Data Received From V2X Module
U042A.d: The V2X module is the radio node for vehicle-to-everything messaging with other cars, roadside units and the network, via DSRC/ITS-G5 or cellular C-V2X. U042A tells that another module gets frames from it but cannot use their content. No manufacturer documents U042A publicly. Ford's patent US 9,769,762 shows the wiring that makes such a code possible: the V2X module sits on the CAN data bus with head unit, assistance unit and other controllers, adapts its transmit power to vehicle speed and message type, and broadcasts warnings such as hard braking on request of the assistance unit. Received alerts travel the other way to display and assistance functions, and that inbound path is what U042A guards. Nothing here affects emissions, so no MIL is expected; connected warnings simply drop out. U011F is lost contact.
c: V2X module or receiver software fault
V2X module faulty, for example after a supply interruption
Antenna or positioning input problem leading to invalid status data
s: Connected traffic or hazard warnings missing
Message about unavailable connected services

U042B.t: Invalid Data Received From Chassis Control Module A
U042B.d: Chassis control module A is a generic name for a controller that coordinates chassis functions, and the job behind the letter varies by brand. GM's documents give one concrete owner: the 2020 ten-speed transmission controller (20OBDG03A) treats the integrated chassis control module (ICCM) as chassis control module A and watches its frame $1F7; an L20 engine controller of 2016 also listens to this module. U042B is set when such frames keep arriving but fail content checks, as opposed to U012A, where they stop. No manufacturer documents U042B publicly, so thresholds and lamp behaviour remain open; GM rates the missing-frame case Type C on the transmission and Type B on the engine. Expect chassis or stability messages and a degraded function; a MIL depends on which controller stores it. U042C is module B.
c: Software fault in the chassis module or the receiving controller
Low voltage or reset of the chassis module during operation
s: Chassis, stability or suspension warning
Chassis functions such as damping or traction aids limited

U042C.t: Invalid Data Received From Chassis Control Module B
U042C.d: U042C refers to a second chassis controller, labelled B, where chassis tasks are split between two units. It is stored when that module's frames still arrive but carry a bad counter, checksum or implausible values. No manufacturer documents U042C or the B module publicly; the only public assignment found concerns module A, which GM's 2020 transmission tables equate with the integrated chassis control module. CARB asks emission-related controllers to flag faulty digital communication as well as its absence, which mirrors the pair U012B and U042C, although a chassis unit usually lies outside that rule. B alone points to that module or its harness, B with U042B to shared supply, gateway or bus wiring. A MIL is not expected; chassis messages are likely. U012B is lost contact.
c: Software fault in chassis module B or the receiver
Supply, ground or gateway problem affecting the module's messages
s: Chassis or suspension warning in the cluster
Chassis function handled by module B inactive

U042D.t: Invalid Data Received From Active Vibration Control Module
U042D.d: The active vibration control module drives active engine mounts or inertial actuators that push against engine vibration in counter-phase, useful with cylinder deactivation. It needs engine speed and other data from the bus and reports its own status back. U042D says a partner receives its frames but finds them invalid. No manufacturer documents U042D publicly. Honda's patent US 10,360,893 describes such a controller that adapts its cancelling output by adaptive filtering and also reads vehicle speed, blower air volume and window state. Bentley shows it is a separate box: fitting newer mounts on a 2017-2020 Bentayga calls for a new program or a new controller for the active mounts, since the old software does not suit them (2055760/1). U012C is lost contact. Expect more vibration; no MIL.
c: Control unit software not matching replaced mounts or actuators
Low supply voltage or poor connection at the module
s: Noticeable vibration or humming at idle
More body vibration when cylinders are deactivated

U042E.t: Invalid Data Received From Generator A Control Module
U042E.d: U042E points to the regulator of generator A, on many Ford models a smart alternator that the PCM commands over a LIN line and that answers with load, temperature and fault status. The PCM stores U042E when those answers come back distorted or implausible; if they stop altogether, U012D is set instead, and U0284 often joins because grille shutters may share the line. Ford's 2014 code list names the module generator control module and gives no MIL flag. Ford bulletins trace the trio of U012D, U0284 and U042E to wiring: water in connector C1050 on the 2022 Maverick 2.0 L, where the MIL comes from oxygen sensor codes P0036 and P0138 instead (SSM 50973), and LIN wire VE181 chafing to ground at a bracket of the left engine mount on the 2021-2022 F-150 2.7 L (SSM 50737). Expect a charging warning and a draining battery. U044D is generator B.
c: Chafed or shorted LIN wire between PCM and generator
Water intrusion or corrosion in a connector of the LIN circuit
Faulty voltage regulator of the generator
s: Check charging system message or battery lamp
Battery runs down, starting problems
Grille shutter codes stored at the same time

U042F.t: Invalid Data Received From Camshaft Position Control Module
U042F.d: U042F concerns a camshaft position control module, used where an electric motor with its own electronics moves the phaser instead of an oil valve. The engine controller commands a target angle and receives actual position and status; U042F means those replies arrive but fail plausibility or protection checks, while U012E is set when they stop. For the 2022 Outlander, Mitsubishi's TSB-23-11-003 lists U042F beside U012E, U0101, U0122, U0146 and U0155 among the engine controller's network codes, and its parts list for that engine includes an electric intake valve timing control module. No maker documents more. CARB requires variable valve timing to be monitored for target errors and slow response. Without trusted feedback the controller holds intake timing at a default; expect a MIL, less power and higher emissions.
c: Electric valve timing control module faulty
Supply, ground or connector fault at the module
Engine controller software misjudging the module data
s: Check engine light
Reduced power and rougher idle
Higher fuel consumption

U0430.t: Invalid Data Received From Tire Pressure Monitor Module
U0430.d: U0430 means that a receiver gets frames from the tire pressure monitor module but rejects what they contain, such as wheel pressures, sensor identifiers or a system status outside the permitted range, or a broken message counter. A stand-alone evaluation unit exists for example in the 2020 Jeep Gladiator Rubicon, whose TPM module FCA reflashed to add the selectable tire fill alert (bulletin 08-023-20). No manufacturer documents U0430 publicly with thresholds or a named receiver. FMVSS 138 obliges the TPMS malfunction telltale to light within 20 minutes of a fault that disturbs how the system creates or transmits its signals, so a lit warning lamp and missing pressure readings are the usual result. U0127 is lost contact, U0330 a software mismatch.
c: Outdated or unsuitable software in the tire pressure module
Wheel sensors not learned after tire or wheel change, module sends default values
Poor supply, ground or connector at the tire pressure module
s: TPMS malfunction lamp on or flashing
Tire pressures missing or shown as dashes in the cluster

U0431.t: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module A
U0431.d: U0431 points at body control module A on vehicles that split body functions over several controllers; with a single BCM the code is U0422, and units B to E have U0443 to U0446. Mitsubishi documents it in the all-wheel-drive ECU, which reads body data from the ETACS unit, among them the stop light switch, and sets U0431 when that signal is abnormal; CAN lines and ETACS codes are checked before the AWD unit is replaced. Its bulletin TSB-18-23-001 (2014-18 Outlander with AWC, built before 1 March 2018) reflashes the AWC ECU when the 4WD warning comes on with U0431. Audi finds U043100 in the gateway of 2023-24 e-tron and Q8 e-tron models with an ignition that refuses to switch on, and updates comfort central module J393. U0141 is lost contact, U0331 software.
c: Software of the receiving module (e.g. AWD unit) misreads body data, reflash needed
Body control module A software or coding faulty
Supply or ground problem at body control module A
s: All-wheel-drive or 4WD warning lamp on
Ignition or comfort functions do not switch on
Further body-related warnings in the cluster

U0432.t: Invalid Data Received From Multi-axis Acceleration Sensor Module A
U0432.d: Multi-axis acceleration sensor module A is the inertial unit that reports yaw rate plus lateral and longitudinal acceleration to stability control, airbag and assistance systems. U0432 is logged when its frames arrive but fail integrity tests. In GM's 2019 tables the XT4 brake module checks the IMU frames for a rolling count that stops changing and for a checksum mismatch; the failure counter must reach 10, rising by 2 per error, the test runs continuously and is Type C without MIL. Saab's 2011 9-5 list adds subtypes 72 (counter) and 74 (checksum). GM PIT5427 ties U0432 with ABS, AWD and suspension warnings on 2010-15 Equinox and Terrain to a corroded X411 connector; FCA lists it among faults addressed by a PCM flash for the 2017 Pacifica (18-002-19). U0125 is lost contact, U0332 software.
c: Corroded connector or terminals in the sensor module harness
Software in the receiving module (PCM, brake module) needs an update
Internal fault or loose mounting of the inertial sensor module
s: Stability control, ABS or AWD warnings
Start-stop or driver assistance functions unavailable
Several chassis codes stored at once

U0433.t: Invalid Data Received From Front Distance Range Sensor - Single Sensor or Center
U0433.d: U0433 concerns the forward distance sensor of adaptive cruise control when there is only one or when it sits in the middle, usually a long-range radar behind the grille. A receiver stores it when the radar's object frames fail their protection checks or carry implausible values. GM's 2025 tables describe the EOCM3 assistance controller testing six protected radar burst messages for wrong counter, checksum or authentication code; it reacts after errors in 3 of 4 messages, judged over about 0.03 s of a 0.04 s window and only at 9 to 16 V, and then switches adaptive cruise off as a special Type C fault without MIL. Ford's 2014 code list carries U0433 without lamp marking. For the driver, cruise and collision warning become unavailable. U0235 is lost contact; left and right sensors use U043B and U043C.
c: Radar misaligned after front-end work or impact, sending implausible objects
Radar or assistance controller software out of step
Low supply voltage or poor connector at the radar
s: Adaptive cruise control switched off
Forward collision warning or emergency braking unavailable

U0434.t: Invalid Data Received From Active Roll Control Module
U0434.d: The active roll control module drives actuators that twist the anti-roll bars on both axles against body lean, hydraulically in older designs and electrically in newer ones. U0434 tells that a receiver, for instance the chassis or brake controller, gets this module's status or torque frames but cannot trust their content. No manufacturer documents U0434 publicly. Land Rover shows how faults of such modules surface: notice N733 for the 2022-23 Range Rover and 2023 Range Rover Sport describes front and rear ARCMs that now and then fail to initialise at start, lighting an amber suspension warning, and updates their software. If roll data is invalid, the bars will typically be left passive, so the body leans more in corners and stability functions may be limited. U0133 is lost contact.
c: Roll control module software fails to initialise reliably
Weak supply to the roll control actuators or module
Internal fault of the roll control module or actuator
s: Suspension or chassis warning in the cluster
Noticeably more body roll in corners

U0435.t: Invalid Data Received From Power Steering Control Module - Rear
U0435.d: U0435 refers to the rear power steering module, the controller of active rear-wheel steering. A receiver sets it when the module's status or angle frames arrive but are unusable. GM bulletin 17-NA-130 explains one case on the 2016-17 Cadillac CT6: during a remote start the rear steer module had not yet initialised while the brake module already expected its data, so the EBCM stored U0435 and showed a Service Soon message; new EBCM software is the fix. Porsche's workshop campaign WE14 for the 2014 911 Turbo reflashes both rear-axle steering units after a software error; with the fault active the actuators lock in the straight position and the car behaves like one with fixed rear links until the next ignition cycle. U0134 is lost contact; U0420 covers power steering module A.
c: Rear steering module not yet ready when receivers expect data, e.g. at remote start
Software error in rear steering or brake module
Low voltage or poor connector at the rear steering unit
s: Service Soon or rear steering fault message
Larger turning circle, rear wheels held straight

U0436.t: Invalid Data Received From Differential Control Module - Front
U0436.d: U0436 concerns the front differential control module, a controller that locks or meters the front axle differential, for example the electric locker of an off-road vehicle. A receiver records the code when lock status, clutch torque or diagnostic frames from this module look implausible. No manufacturer documents U0436 publicly. Why trustworthy lock data matters is shown by Mercedes-Benz recall 20V-090 on 2019-20 G-Class: a resistor in the locking module's control unit could be degraded by sulfur from the axle oil, the measured current came out too high and the lock state could not be determined with certainty, so ABS and ESP were deactivated. Expect the front locker or torque split to be disabled and a warning in the cluster. U0135 is lost contact; the rear unit has U0437.
c: Fault in the locking module electronics, e.g. degraded measuring resistor
Corroded or damaged harness and connector near the front axle
s: Front locker or 4WD function unavailable
ABS, stability or drivetrain warning

U0437.t: Invalid Data Received From Differential Control Module - Rear
U0437.d: The rear differential control module runs an electronic limited-slip differential or the rear clutch of an on-demand all-wheel drive. U0437 is set when a receiver gets its frames but finds torque, clutch state or counter values invalid. No manufacturer documents U0437 publicly with thresholds. GM bulletins show how the module is organised: PI1074B links a Service All Wheel Drive message with U0136 in the brake module of 2014 Enclave, Traverse and Acadia AWD to the software of the K47 rear differential module, whereas on 2020 CT5 and Corvette the eLSD logic runs inside the brake controller (20-NA-217) and no separate module exists. Jeep's 2013-14 Grand Cherokee has its own ELSD module (21-001-14). Typical result: AWD or eLSD switched off and a service message. U0136 is lost contact.
c: Rear differential module software needs reprogramming
Corrosion at the module mounted on or near the rear axle
Faulty clutch actuator or motor feeding implausible status
s: Service AWD or rear axle message
All-wheel drive or limited-slip function inactive

U0438.t: Invalid Data Received From Trailer Brake Control Module
U0438.d: U0438 names the trailer brake control module, which applies the electric brakes of a towed trailer in step with the vehicle's braking; park brake data has a code of its own, U0417. Ford uses U0438 explicitly: SSM 52184 connects U0438:82 stored by the cluster of some 2023 F-150 PowerBoost hybrids, built from 24 to 26 October 2022, with a Trailer Brake System Fault message caused by the cluster configuration, which is re-run with the dealer tool. SSM 53980 for 2023-25 Super Duty blames U0438 together with other network codes on an incorrectly tightened ground G201 (8 ± 1.2 Nm). Saab's 2011 9-5 list knows subtype 71. The driver sees a trailer brake warning and gain control may not work. U0137 is lost contact.
c: Loose or wrongly tightened body ground
Internal fault of the trailer brake control module
s: Trailer brake system fault message
Trailer brake gain cannot be set or trailer brakes inactive
Further network warnings in the cluster

U0439.t: Invalid Data Received From All Terrain Control Module
U0439.d: U0439 relates to the all terrain control module, which manages drive modes for snow, sand, mud or rock and passes the chosen setting to powertrain, brake and suspension controllers. A receiver sets it when mode request, switch state or status frames from this module look invalid. No manufacturer documents U0439 publicly. Ford and Land Rover both call such a unit ATCM: Ford's SSM 54656 for 2025-26 F-150 finds a 4L switch held down by trim, logged in the ATCM, and Land Rover's SSM73849 covers ATCM variants the Pathfinder tester could not recognise, which shows the module also handles off-road switch inputs. If terrain data is invalid, receivers will typically fall back to the normal road setting, so off-road modes or low range may be unavailable. U0138 is lost contact.
c: Terrain or 4WD mode switch stuck or obstructed by trim
All terrain module software or variant coding wrong
Poor supply, ground or connector at the module
s: Check 4x4 or terrain system message
Drive mode selection does not respond

U043A.t: Invalid Data Received From Suspension Control Module B
U043A.d: Suspension control module B is a second chassis controller, often the one that runs adjustable dampers while module A handles levelling. U043A is logged when its frames reach a receiver but fail integrity checks. GM's 2025 tables give the example of the electronic brake module reading the damper control information: a rolling count equal to the previous one or a protection value that does not add up counts as an error, and 8 errors in a sliding window of 16 set the fault. The check runs only between 9 and 16 V, not during engine start and not within 5 s after a power mode change or reset; it is Type C, so no MIL. Ride control may drop to a fixed default and stability functions may be restricted. U0139 is lost contact, U0421 refers to module A.
c: Damper module resets or hangs, sending frozen counters
Low supply voltage at the suspension module
Software of suspension and brake modules not matched
s: Service suspension or ride control warning
Ride noticeably firmer or softer than usual

U043B.t: Invalid Data Received From Front Distance Range Sensor - Left
U043B.d: U043B covers the left front distance sensor, usually a short-range corner radar that widens the view of adaptive cruise and collision assistance beyond the central long-range unit; that one has U0433, the right corner U043C. A receiver sets U043B when the left sensor's object or status frames arrive but fail plausibility or protection checks. No manufacturer documents U043B publicly. GM's 2025 EOCM3 tables list only the lost-contact partner U023D for the left front short-range radar: frames absent longer than 0.2 s end adaptive cruise (special Type C), which indicates how the assistance controller is likely to react to corrupted data as well. Expect assistance features reduced or switched off and a prompt to clean or check the sensor area.
c: Left corner radar misaligned or damaged after a bumper impact
Corner radar software not matching the assistance controller
Moisture or corrosion in the left sensor connector
s: Adaptive cruise or lane change assistance unavailable
Message to clean or check front sensors

U043C.t: Invalid Data Received From Front Distance Range Sensor - Right
U043C.d: U043C is the right-hand counterpart: invalid frames from the right front distance sensor, a corner radar on cars that pair one long-range radar with two short-range units. Finding only U043C points at that sensor, its plug or its mounting area, for example after a light knock on the right bumper corner; U043B and U043C together suggest a shared supply, bus segment or a software issue in the receiver. There is no public manufacturer documentation of U043C and no known threshold. In GM's 2025 EOCM3 tables the right front short-range radar is checked only for message loss, under U023E: more than 0.2 s without frames ends adaptive cruise, special Type C. Functions relying on the right corner view are reduced, others may stay available. U023E is lost contact.
c: Right corner radar knocked out of alignment or damaged
Shared supply or bus segment fault when both corner codes appear
Moisture or corrosion in the right sensor connector
s: Assistance functions using the right front view switched off
Sensor blocked or check sensor message

U043D.t: Invalid Data Received From Accelerator Pedal Module
U043D.d: U043D applies where the accelerator pedal is a networked module that sends pedal position as messages instead of two analogue voltages. The engine or vehicle controller stores it when those messages carry an implausible position, redundant values that disagree or a broken counter. No manufacturer documents U043D publicly; in the systems that are documented the pedal stays hard-wired, for instance in the BMW i4, whose bulletin B610625 blames implausible pedal sensor signals on poor pins at the CCU connector and logs them under a BMW-specific code. CARB requires rationality checks of inputs used by emission-related controls, and electronic throttle systems drop to idle or limited torque when the driver demand cannot be trusted. Expect reduced power and a warning lamp. U013C is lost contact.
c: Poor pin contact at the pedal module or its receiver connector
Internal fault of the accelerator pedal module
Pedal module and engine controller software not matched
s: Reduced power or limp-home mode
Engine or drivetrain warning lamp on
Pedal response delayed or ignored

U043E.t: Invalid Data Received From Vacuum Sensor A
U043E.d: Vacuum sensor A reports the vacuum in a brake booster or vacuum reservoir; U043E is meant for designs in which this sensor sends digital messages and a receiver judges them invalid. No manufacturer documents U043E publicly. GM's usual layout uses an analogue booster vacuum sensor with P-codes: bulletin 17-NA-314 for 2018 Enclave and Traverse traces a Service Power Brake Assist message and brake shudder to wrong readings from a faulty sensor circuit board, setting P0557 and C025E, and 16-NA-366 for 2014-16 Encore links a hard pedal and a constantly running vacuum pump to contamination in sensor, check valve and hose. Comparable effects are plausible with U043E: brake assist warnings, a longer running vacuum pump or start-stop held off. U013D is lost contact; sensor B has U043F.
c: Faulty sensor electronics giving wrong vacuum values
Oil or dirt in the sensor, check valve or vacuum hose
Poor terminal tension at the sensor connector
s: Brake assist warning message
Hard brake pedal or vacuum pump running often

U043F.t: Invalid Data Received From Vacuum Sensor B
U043F.d: U043F is the counterpart for vacuum sensor B, used where a second vacuum signal exists, for example a redundant booster sensor or one watching a separate reservoir. A receiver records it when B's digital vacuum value arrives invalid. Comparing with U043E narrows the search: B alone points at that sensor or its wiring branch, both together at a shared supply, the bus or a genuine vacuum shortage. No manufacturer documents U043F publicly and no thresholds are known; in GM's analogue designs a booster sensor fault shows up as a P-code such as P0557 instead. Without a trustworthy second value the receiver loses its cross-check between the two sensors, so a brake assist warning and disabled vacuum-dependent functions are the likely consequence. U013E is lost contact.
c: Faulty vacuum sensor B or its electronics
Damaged wiring branch or connector to sensor B
Actual vacuum leak making both sensors disagree
s: Brake assist or vacuum system warning
Start-stop or other vacuum-dependent functions inactive

U0440.t: Invalid Data Received From Pedestrian Alert Control Module
U0440.d: U0440 points at the pedestrian alert control module, which drives the external speaker of electric and hybrid vehicles. FMVSS 141 in the US demands an audible signal while the vehicle stands with its propulsion active and at speeds below 30 km/h, so the module needs speed, gear and propulsion state and reports its own status back. A receiver sets U0440 when the module's frames arrive with invalid content. No manufacturer documents U0440 publicly; Ford names the part PACM, for instance in bulletin 21-2271 about a rattle from its connector in the 2020-21 Escape Hybrid. The likely result is a warning about the pedestrian alert system: the car stays drivable, but may be quieter than the rule allows at low speed. U013F is lost contact.
c: Loose or vibrating connector at the alert module
Alert module software not matched to the vehicle
Internal fault of the pedestrian alert module
s: Pedestrian alert system warning in the cluster
No external sound at low speed

U0441.t: Invalid Data Received From Emissions Critical Control Information
U0441.d: U0441 does not name one controller: the title refers to emissions-critical control information, the data powertrain units exchange for emission-relevant functions. A receiver logs it when such a message arrives but fails plausibility, counter or checksum tests; if the information stops altogether, U0113 applies. Ford's 2014 OBD-II code list marks U0441 for the MIL, whereas U0113 carries no lamp flag there. California's OBD regulation explains the background: data from emission critical powertrain units must be dependable, and a communication fault that keeps a default action from working has to light the MIL. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for U0441. Expect the check engine light, further powertrain codes in the sending unit and a failed emissions inspection until the cause is cleared.
c: Software of the powertrain unit sending the emission data is outdated or mismatched
Fault in the powertrain CAN wiring or connectors corrupting messages
Low or unstable supply voltage at the sending or receiving unit
s: Check engine light on
Additional powertrain or network codes stored
Emissions inspection not passed while the code is present

U0442.t: Invalid Data Received From ECM/PCM B
U0442.d: ECM/PCM B stands for a second engine or powertrain controller where a car carries more than one such unit; U0442 means its frames reach a receiver with invalid content, while U0115 means they stop arriving. Mazda applies the code in its own way: bulletin 01-015/18 for the 2018 Mazda6 and CX-5 and the 2019 CX-3 and MX-5 describes the TCM of automatic models flagging invalid PCM data, together with P061B and U0401, when the driver lets go of the brake during cranking. The PCM then enters a fail-safe mode with limited engine speed, and new PCM software cures the false detection. Mercedes-Benz lists U044287 with U014687 when a software conflict in the 48 V battery switches on the check engine light (LI54.21-P-078926). Expect the MIL and, depending on design, reduced power.
c: Control logic in the engine or powertrain software too sensitive, update available
Software levels of sending and receiving units do not match after an update
Bus wiring, connector or supply fault at the second powertrain controller
s: Check engine light on
Fail-safe mode with limited engine speed or lack of power
Transmission codes stored alongside engine codes

U0443.t: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module B
U0443.d: U0443 is set when a receiver gets frames from body control module B but rejects their content. The letters B to E come into play when a vehicle spreads body electronics such as lighting, locks, wipers or power distribution over several controllers; module A has U0431, a single BCM U0422, and lost contact with B is U0142. No car maker explains publicly which unit carries the letter B. Harley-Davidson uses the code on motorcycles: bulletin M1619 reports U04438F (failure type 8F, erratic) stored by the left hand control module shortly after start-up, alongside U04318F in the right hand module. As history entries they need no repair and await new software; if they are current, normal diagnosis applies. In cars, invalid data from module B tends to disable single comfort functions or trigger warnings.
c: Software of module B or of the receiver sets the code without a real fault
Loose connector or damaged network wiring at body control module B
Supply or ground problem at body control module B
s: Single comfort or lighting functions unavailable
Code stored as history right after start-up without complaint

U0444.t: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module C
U0444.d: Body control module C is the third body controller in vehicles with distributed body electronics; U0444 records invalid content in its frames, U0143 lost contact. Ford documents the code: TSB 24-2116 covers 2023 F-150 trucks with the 3.5L PowerBoost hybrid that warn of a trailer brake fault even with no trailer hitched, while the trailer module stores U0444:82, possibly next to U0140:87 and U0143:87. Failure type 82 stands for a message counter that is wrong or not updated, 87 for a message that is missing. Ford blames the software of gateway module A, not body module C itself. The case shows that a code naming a body module can point at the network path in between, so gateway and receiver software are checked before module C is replaced.
c: Gateway module software level corrupts or delays forwarded messages
Software of the receiving module (e.g. trailer module) misjudges the data
Supply, ground or connector fault at body control module C
s: Trailer brake fault message although no trailer is connected
Lost-communication codes for the BCMs stored together with U0444

U0445.t: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module D
U0445.d: U0445 belongs to body control module D, a fourth controller for body functions that only vehicles with heavily distributed body electronics need. A receiver sets it when D's frames arrive but their content fails range, counter or checksum tests; complete silence from D is U0144. No manufacturer documents U0445 publicly, and no maker states what D controls. That several body units can coexist in one vehicle is shown by Ford, whose 2023 F-150 trailer module monitors both the main BCM and module C (TSB 24-2116). Because the role of a D unit differs by design, the symptom depends on what it handles, from one inoperative light or lock to warnings in the cluster. Diagnosis starts with the freeze frame in the reporting module and the supply and bus wiring of module D.
c: Software of module D or of the receiver not matching after an update
Damaged bus wiring or corroded connector on the branch to module D
Internal fault or poor supply at body control module D
s: A body function handled by module D works erratically or not at all
Warning messages in the instrument cluster

U0446.t: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module E
U0446.d: U0446 refers to body control module E, the last letter in the series that starts with U0431 for module A. It is logged by a receiving controller when module E is present on the bus but delivers values or protection fields that cannot be trusted; if E stops sending, U0145 is stored instead. No manufacturer documents U0446 publicly. A body control module in general reads switches and drives comfort and lighting loads, so a fifth unit would handle only a narrow share of these. Before replacing any part, check whether other modules report E as well, compare software levels and inspect power, ground and the network branch leading to it. If only a single receiver complains, its own software is the more likely culprit, as Ford found for body module C on the 2023 F-150 (TSB 24-2116).
c: Software of the single reporting module misreads the data of module E
Fault in the network branch or connector leading to module E
Low supply voltage or poor ground at body control module E
s: Individual body or comfort functions inoperative
Code present in one or several receiving modules

U0447.t: Invalid Data Received From Serial Data Gateway Module A
U0447.d: As the central gateway, serial data gateway module A links the vehicle networks and forwards messages between them. U0447 means a receiver gets gateway frames with failed protection; for lost contact the code is U0146. In GM's 2025 tables, many receiving modules run this test: the ECM checks rolling count, protection value and checksum of backup power mode signals, a Type B code (two trips) follows after 3 bad samples out of 10, the TCM uses Type A; camera and radar modules allow 0.625 s, stay non-MIL and drop adaptive cruise.
