GM bulletin 23-NA-206 lists U0447 among history codes to ignore. Audi bulletin 2069299 for 2022-24 Q4 e-tron finds U044700 in both brake modules while the engine module reports U014600, and replaces gateway J533. VW reports it in the ECM of 2013-19 Golf models.
c: Gateway hardware or software fault, update or replacement of the gateway
Receiver software logs the code without a real fault (history entry)
Low battery voltage or poor ground at the gateway during wake-up or power mode changes
s: Several warning messages in the instrument cluster at once
Adaptive cruise or camera-based assistance unavailable
Check engine light on in vehicles that rate the fault as MIL-relevant

U0448.t: Invalid Data Received From Serial Data Gateway Module B
U0448.d: U0448 concerns serial data gateway module B, a second gateway that some architectures add next to the central unit to bridge further networks; U0147 is lost contact with it. A receiver stores U0448 when B's frames arrive but alive counter, checksum or message authentication do not match. No manufacturer documents U0448 publicly. For gateway A, GM's 2025 tables show what such checks look like: a few failed samples within a short window, MIL treatment that varies by receiver, and assistance functions such as adaptive cruise switched off as a fallback. Audi's Q4 e-tron bulletin shows a faulty gateway leaving several modules reporting it at the same time. Because every message routed through B is affected, symptoms tend to appear on several systems together; software level and supply of module B come first in diagnosis.
c: Software level of gateway B not matching the other modules
Supply or ground fault at gateway B
Internal fault in gateway module B
s: Warnings from several systems at the same time
Assistance or comfort functions on the networks behind gateway B unavailable

U0449.t: Invalid Data Received From Serial Data Gateway Module C
U0449.d: U0449 points at serial data gateway module C; its lost-contact partner is U0148. The receiver logs it when C keeps transmitting, yet the content breaks the rules agreed for that message, for instance a wrong length, a frozen counter or a bad checksum. No manufacturer documents U0449 publicly. How strictly receivers police gateway traffic is visible at GM: in one 2024 table the ECM checks the data length code of several frames that the gateway forwards from two CAN buses, and a wrong length lasting 10 s sets the gateway A code as a two-trip fault, while a missing frame sets a separate maker-specific code. A third gateway mostly appears in vehicles with many separate networks. Symptoms depend on which networks C joins; several unrelated warnings at once are typical.
c: Gateway C software sends frames in a layout the receiver does not expect
Wiring, termination or connector fault on a network served by gateway C
Low voltage or poor ground at gateway C
s: Several unrelated warnings in the cluster
Functions on one network segment unavailable

U044A.t: Invalid Data Received From Serial Data Gateway Module D
U044A.d: U044A covers serial data gateway module D. A receiver records it when D's frames carry implausible values or violate their counter or checksum; if they stop, U0149 is the matching code. No manufacturer explains U044A publicly, but Stellantis shows which unit can hold the letter D: for the 2021 Jeep Grand Cherokee, case S2108000139 describes the driver assistance module logging U0149-00, which Stellantis words as lost contact to the security gateway, together with a brief Traffic Sign Assist message at start-up; no repair is needed and a camera module software update was announced. On such vehicles invalid data from the security gateway would therefore mainly affect assistance and display functions. As with the other gateway codes, software levels and supply are checked before hardware is replaced.
c: Receiver software (e.g. camera or assistance module) misjudges gateway data at start-up
Software or configuration of gateway D not matching the vehicle
Supply, ground or bus wiring fault at gateway D
s: Brief assistance unavailable message at start-up
Driver assistance or display functions limited

U044B.t: Invalid Data Received From Battery Energy Control Module C
U044B.d: A third battery controller, module C, appears where a pack is divided into separately managed sections or a vehicle has more than one battery system. A receiver, typically the hybrid or vehicle controller, sets U044B when C's frames on cell voltages, temperatures, state of charge or contactor status fail validity checks; U014A is lost contact, U0412 and U0413 cover modules A and B. No manufacturer documents U044B publicly. Volkswagen group documents number such controllers: Bentley bulletin 2051553/2 for the 2017-18 Bentayga logs battery and sensor faults under battery management 2, the unit serving the dynamic ride roll control. Expect reduced electric power or a hybrid system warning, since the receiver cannot rely on the pack data.
c: Software of battery module C not matching the vehicle controller
Faulty cell or temperature sensing inside the pack section managed by C
Bus wiring, connector or 12 V supply fault at module C
s: Hybrid or battery system warning
Reduced electric power or range
Functions supplied by the affected battery switched off

U044C.t: Invalid Data Received From Hybrid/EV Battery Inductive Charging Module
U044C.d: U044C covers the module that controls inductive charging of the high-voltage battery: a receiver coil and electronics on the vehicle take energy from a ground pad without a cable and must agree with the charger on alignment, power and battery limits. A receiver such as the battery or vehicle controller stores U044C when the module's frames arrive but hold invalid status or power values; U014B is lost contact. No manufacturer documents U044C publicly. BMW ran such a system as a field test with 200 530e iPerformance cars in California (SIB 61 23 19), with a ground pad module paired over WLAN, and only a few dealers equipped to diagnose it. The likely result is an interrupted or refused wireless charge, while charging by cable and driving normally remain possible.
c: Poor alignment or disturbed link between vehicle unit and ground pad
Software of the inductive charging module not matching the battery controller
Internal fault or overheating of the inductive charging module
s: Wireless charging does not start or stops early
Charging system message in the display

U044D.t: Invalid Data Received From Generator B Control Module
U044D.d: U044D names the generator B control module. Ford uses the A version for its LIN-controlled alternator: in SSM 50737, 2021-22 F-150 trucks with the 2.7L EcoBoost warn about the charging system and store U012D and U042E in the PCM because a LIN wire rubs through to ground close to the engine mount on the left. A B unit would then be the regulator of a second alternator, as found on trucks with dual generators; Ford's 2014 code list already contains circuit codes for generator 2. U044D is set when that regulator answers but its status, load or fault data are invalid; U012F is lost contact. No manufacturer documents U044D publicly. The engine computer then cannot steer the second alternator reliably, so charging capacity may drop and a battery or charging warning may appear.
c: Chafed or shorted LIN wire to the second alternator
Faulty voltage regulator of alternator B
Second alternator not configured correctly in the engine computer
s: Battery or charging system warning
Low charging voltage under high electrical load

U044F.t: Invalid Data Received From Mirror Control Module B
U044F.d: U044F is stored when a controller receives data from mirror control module B that it cannot use; U014D is lost contact, U0514 covers module A. Depending on design, mirror modules adjust, fold and heat the exterior mirrors, store memory positions or run an interior mirror with camera display. Stellantis shows how the letters are assigned: case S2108000013 for the 2021 Jeep Grand Cherokee names module A as the combined rear view mirror module inside the cabin, whose lost-contact code U0213 sets in the BCM after a configuration restore wrongly enables a mirror that is not fitted. No manufacturer documents U044F publicly. FMVSS 111 sets the rear visibility rules such mirrors serve. Expect memory, folding, dimming or display functions handled by module B to stop working.
c: Vehicle configuration does not match the fitted mirror modules
Damaged wiring in the door hinge area or loose mirror connector
Internal fault of mirror control module B, often after water entry
s: Mirror adjustment, folding or memory function inoperative
Camera mirror display or automatic dimming unavailable

U0451.t: Invalid Data Received From Serial Data Gateway Module E
U0451.d: U0451 is the code for serial data gateway module E, the fifth gateway letter; lost communication with it is U0150. It is logged by a receiver that still hears E but finds its data implausible or its protection fields wrong. No manufacturer documents U0451 publicly, and five gateways in one vehicle are rare. Experience with gateway A helps in judging such entries: Volkswagen's bulletin 01-24-02 for the 2024 ID.4 lists U044700 among codes that various control units store statically or sporadically without a real fault, and GM's 2025 tables give camera and radar receivers a 0.625 s window and no MIL for gateway data. A stored U0451 without symptoms therefore deserves a software check before parts are replaced; an active one with warnings calls for checking bus and supply of module E.
c: Receiver software stores the code sporadically without a real fault
Software level of gateway E not matching after an update
Bus wiring, supply or ground fault at gateway E
s: Code stored without noticeable fault
Warnings from systems on the networks behind gateway E

U0452.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints Control Module
U0452.d: The restraints control module decides on airbag and belt tensioner deployment; in many GM vehicles it also sends yaw rate, lateral and longitudinal acceleration and post-crash data to other units. U0452 means a receiver rejects these frames; U0151 is lost contact. GM's 2025 tables show the checks: the ECM tests the alive counter and protection field, 8 failures in 18 samples or 4 in 10 set a Type C code without MIL; the EOCM3 needs 6 bad messages in 10 and turns off adaptive cruise. GM bulletin 23-NA-206 names U0452 in the brake module among history codes to ignore. Ford's SSM 46901 covers 2017-18 Fusion and MKZ with an airbag lamp or SYNC 911 Assist message and U0452 in the APIM; the RCM gets new software. SSM 46902 blames CAN overload in the F-150 FCIM.
c: Restraints control module software needs reprogramming
Receiver stores the code as history after start-up or network wake-up without a real fault
High CAN bus load, poor ground or connector fault on the restraints network branch
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Emergency call or crash notification message
Adaptive cruise or stability functions unavailable

U0453.t: Invalid Data Received From Side Restraints Control Module - Left
U0453.d: U0453 concerns a side restraints control module for the left side, used where side impact sensing or the firing of side and curtain airbags is handled by a separate unit next to the main restraints module. A receiver, usually the main restraints module, sets U0453 when the left unit's crash or status data are invalid; U0152 is lost contact, U0454 covers the right side. No manufacturer documents U0453 publicly. FMVSS 214 regulates side impact protection, and FMVSS 208 requires a readiness indicator, visible to the driver, that supervises deployable occupant protection, which is why an airbag warning lamp is the expected symptom; protection on the left side may be reduced until repair. For the main module (U0452), GM's tables use counter and protection checks without MIL.
c: Loose or corroded connector of the left side unit, for example under the seat or in the B-pillar
Software or configuration of the left unit not matching the main restraints module
Internal fault of the left side restraints unit, often after a side impact
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side or curtain airbag on the left possibly not available

U0454.t: Invalid Data Received From Side Restraints Control Module - Right
U0454.d: U0454 is the right-hand counterpart of U0453. Where a separate side restraints unit on the right evaluates side impact sensing or fires the right side and curtain airbags, a partner, normally the central airbag controller, stores U0454 when it judges that unit's messages corrupt or implausible. Contact itself still exists; a silent right unit would be U0153. No manufacturer documents U0454 publicly. Bosch describes airbag controllers with inputs for peripheral crash sensors that detect side impacts, and FMVSS 214 sets the side impact requirements such units serve. Because FMVSS 208 demands a readiness indicator for deployable protection, the airbag lamp is the expected reaction, and protection on the right may be missing until repair. No MIL is involved.
c: Loose or corroded plug of the right side unit, for example under the right seat or in the B-pillar
Software or configuration of the right unit not matching the central airbag controller, often after a module swap
Internal fault of the right side restraints unit, for instance after a side impact on the right
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side or curtain airbag on the right possibly unavailable

U0455.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints Occupant Classification System Module
U0455.d: The occupant classification module reads sensors in the front passenger seat and reports to the restraints controller if the seat is vacant, occupied by a child seat or by an adult; FMVSS 208 lets carmakers switch the passenger airbag off automatically on that basis. U0455 means the restraints controller still receives this classification but finds it invalid, whereas U0154 is total loss of contact. Ford uses the code in the RCM: SSM 46109 and SSM 46901 concern Fusion and MKZ of model years 2017-18 showing an airbag lamp or a SYNC 911 Assist warning, list U0455 among other RCM codes and have the RCM reprogrammed and its as-built data loaded again. Chrysler's restraint fault list in NHTSA file PE11-019 keeps a separate code for an undetermined classification. Expect the airbag lamp and doubtful passenger airbag status; no MIL.
c: Restraints controller software needing an update and as-built configuration
Damaged or unplugged seat harness of the passenger seat, for example after seat removal or adjustment
Faulty occupant classification module or seat sensor mat
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag on/off indicator wrong or flashing
Emergency call function reported as unavailable

U0456.t: Invalid Data Received From Coolant Temperature Control Module
U0456.d: U0456 means a module receives messages from the coolant temperature control module but rejects them as invalid; U0116 is the lost-contact twin. Such a controller runs electronically managed cooling, for example an electric coolant pump whose built-in electronics, as Bosch describes for its PAD2 pump, take speed commands over PWM or LIN and report back. Kia documents the code: Pitstop PS647 for the 2017-2020 Niro hybrid and plug-in hybrid links U045600 to the engine's electric water pump, whose plug and pigtail behind the coolant temperature sensor can be soaked with coolant; fuses for module 8 and the pump may blow, and the pump is replaced with its short harness. CARB requires communication errors of digitally controlled components to be detected. A temperature warning and reduced power are possible.
c: Coolant in the plug or pigtail of the electric water pump
Blown fuse or weak supply of the pump or cooling control module
Faulty electronics of the electric coolant pump or cooling module
s: Engine or coolant temperature warning
Reduced engine power as protection
Check engine lamp on some models

U0457.t: Invalid Data Received From Information Center A
U0457.d: Information center A is the first of two driver information displays defined alongside the instrument cluster, in practice often the central screen or head unit of the infotainment system. U0457 is stored when a listener still hears this display but rejects what it sends, for example because a message counter or checksum fails, the kind of protection AUTOSAR specifies for safety-related frames; a silent display gives U0156 instead. No manufacturer documents U0457 publicly. For the partner itself, Mazda treats information center A as its connectivity master unit (SA-029/20, Mazda3 and CX-30), and Volvo's central electronic module logs U015600 when the Sensus screen stays black (TJ 25872). Settings, messages or audio shown on that screen may be wrong or missing, while driving stays normal and no MIL lights. U0458 is center B.
c: Software fault or version mismatch in the display or head unit
Poorly seated fuse or weak supply of the display unit
Connector or bus wiring fault at the display
s: Central display showing wrong, frozen or no content
Network malfunction message in the cluster

U0458.t: Invalid Data Received From Information Center B
U0458.d: U0458 covers the second driver information display, information center B, which J2012 keeps apart from center A, the instrument cluster and the head-up display; which physical screen a maker calls B, for example a passenger or rear-seat display, is its own decision. A receiving module logs the code when frames from B arrive but fail plausibility, such as a stuck alive counter or a wrong CRC as described in the AUTOSAR end-to-end protocol; if no frames come at all, U0157 is set instead. No manufacturer documents U0458 publicly, and none of the bulletins checked names its lost-contact twin U0157 either. Since such a display only presents information, the effect is normally limited to missing or frozen content on that one screen, with no MIL and no limp mode.
c: Software fault or unsuitable software level in display B
Loose connector or damaged bus wiring to display B
s: Second display blank, frozen or showing wrong values
Functions operated through that display unavailable

U0459.t: Invalid Data Received From Head Up Display
U0459.d: The head-up display shows speed, route arrows or warnings as a virtual image in the windscreen. It takes most content from other modules and reports its own state, such as brightness, image position, page or standby, back over the vehicle bus or a LIN link to the cluster. U0459 is set when a partner receives HUD data that fail its checks; U0158 means the HUD is not heard at all. No manufacturer documents U0459 publicly. GM shows how near the two faults lie: in bulletin 22-NA-113 for 2020-22 Cadillac CT4 and CT5 with option UV6, badly timed LIN messages while the HUD entered standby left it blank and stored U0158 in the cluster, cured by reprogramming the cluster and pulling the HUD fuse. The 2011 Saab 9-5 code table lists the HUD as a separate node. Symptom: blank or frozen projection; no MIL.
c: Software of the cluster or HUD handling messages badly, for example around standby
HUD shutting down or sending fault status because of heat
Connector or LIN/bus wiring fault at the HUD
s: Head-up display blank or frozen
Brightness, position or page settings have no effect

U045A.t: Invalid Data Received From Parking Assist Control Module A
U045A.d: Parking assist module A evaluates the ultrasonic sensors and in newer cars requests steering or braking for automated parking. U045A flags invalid data from it; U0159 is lost contact, U0544 covers module B. GM's brake module tables for the 2019 Cadillac XT4 (19OBDG03D) and 2020 (20OBDG03C) test counter and checksum of the parking brake request, a failure count rising by 2 per error and tripping at 3, within 0.2 s, Type C without MIL; the 2025 EBCM (25OBDG04B) wants 8 bad frames in 16. Ford's 2024 OBD summary rates U045A type 48 as non-MIL on cars with fully aided park assist. FCA TSB 08-011-15 (2014 Cherokee) fixes U045A-86 with new PAM software, Mercedes LI46.35-P-071804 lets E-Class steering units ignore U045A00, and Mazda's CX-5 camera logs U045A:68 after water entered sensor plugs. Park assist drops out.
c: Parking assist module software needing an update
Water or corrosion in ultrasonic sensor plugs or the bumper harness
Receiver storing the code as harmless history after a software change
s: Park assist or automatic parking unavailable
Parking sensor indicator flashing or false obstacle warnings
Emergency braking or collision warning message

U045B.t: Invalid Data Received From Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module B
U045B.d: ABS module B is a second brake controller, found where braking has to survive a single fault. Bosch pairs an electromechanical booster or its integrated power brake with ESP for that purpose and, for automated driving, adds a separate redundant brake unit; its 2018 show message was that automated driving needs redundancy. U045B is stored when the partner, often the main brake unit or the automated driving computer, receives status or wheel data from B but rejects them because counters, checksums or values do not fit; U015A means B is silent, U0415 concerns the main ABS module. No manufacturer documents U045B publicly. Normal braking usually remains through the other path, yet a brake warning may appear and anything that relies on redundancy, such as automated or hands-off driving, is blocked.
c: Software levels of brake module A and B or the automation computer not matching
Weak supply or ground of brake module B
Internal fault of brake module B
s: Brake system or ABS warning
Automated or hands-off driving functions unavailable

U045C.t: Invalid Data Received From Power Steering Control Module B
U045C.d: Power steering module B is the second controller of a redundant electric steering system. Bosch presented a fail-operational EPS for highly automated driving in 2017: if one path fails, the system can still steer the car to a safe stop or spare the driver a sudden rise in steering effort. U045C is set when the partner, typically steering module A or the automation computer, gets messages from B but finds them invalid, for instance a frozen counter or a mismatching CRC under AUTOSAR end-to-end protection; complete silence from B is U015B, and invalid data from module A is U0420. No manufacturer documents U045C publicly. Assisted steering usually continues on path A, but a steering warning and blocked automated steering are likely until the cause is found.
c: Software or calibration of steering module B not matching module A
Voltage dips or poor ground at the second steering path
Internal fault of steering module B
s: Steering system warning
Lane centring or automated steering unavailable
Steering assist reduced in some cases

U045D.t: Invalid Data Received From Automated Driving System Control Module A
U045D.d: Automated driving system control module A is a computer that merges radar and camera data and plans braking and steering for features such as adaptive cruise, lane centring and emergency braking. U045D means a partner hears it but gets implausible content; U015C is lost contact. Stellantis documents the code. Its TSBs 08-256-25 through 08-259-25 (Dodge Charger and Jeep Wagoneer S, model years 2024-25, Active Driving Assist) require a MIL together with U015C-00 or U045D-00, often with an emergency braking unavailable message; the fix is new software for the front long-range radar, rated at 0.2 h. STAR case S2508000095 for 2024-26 Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer shows the CADM2 storing U045D-00 with a freeze frame about an unexecuted brake jerk request, traced to strained Ethernet cables. Assistance features switch off until repair.
c: Outdated software in the front long-range radar or ADAS module
Strained or badly routed Ethernet cable with poor pin contact at the ADAS modules
Internal fault of the ADAS control module
s: Automatic emergency braking unavailable message
MIL on in affected Stellantis models
Adaptive cruise and lane centring disabled

U045E.t: Invalid Data Received From Automated Driving System Control Module B
U045E.d: Control module B is the second unit of a split automated driving computer, and the two halves check each other. Stellantis documents U045E in STAR case S2508000095 for 2024-26 Jeep Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer: the CADM and the global navigation and motion module store U045E-00 next to U015D-00, Ethernet link errors and time synchronisation faults, and the freeze-frame data name failed message checks on two internal processor paths. Replaced modules showed no defect; taut Ethernet cables had strained the plugs. Technicians inspect plugs and pins, replace the harness without splicing and set clip C121 to the specified distances. U015D would mean B is silent, U045D covers module A. Customers see a blind spot alert unavailable message, lit mirror warning lamps and switched-off assistance; this case names no MIL.
c: Ethernet cable routed too tight, straining plugs and pins at the ADAS modules
Harness clip at the ADAS decision module outside the specified distance
Internal fault of ADAS control module B
s: Blind spot alert unavailable message
Blind spot lamps in the mirrors stay lit
Driver assistance features disabled

U045F.t: Invalid Data Received From Automated Driving System Interface Module A
U045F.d: Interface module A sits between an automated driving computer and the base vehicle: it turns the computer's steering, braking and propulsion requests into commands the vehicle's own controllers accept and reports their state back. Bosch places this act layer at the end of its sense-think-act chain. U045F is set when the automation computer or an actuator controller receives frames from interface A that fail checks such as alive counter, CRC or timing, the mechanisms AUTOSAR standardises for end-to-end protection; U015E means interface A is no longer heard. No manufacturer documents U045F publicly. Since the computer can no longer trust what reaches the actuators, it must disengage or, at higher SAE J3016 levels, bring the car to a minimal-risk stop and hand back to the driver. Manual driving remains possible.
c: Software of interface module A not matching the automation computer or actuator controllers
Connector, bus wiring or supply fault at interface A
Internal fault of interface module A
s: Automated driving or advanced assistance refuses to engage
Takeover request or warning to the driver

U0460.t: Invalid Data Received From Automated Driving System Interface Module B
U0460.d: Interface module B is the second, redundant link between an automated driving computer and the brakes, steering and propulsion. Bosch says plainly that automated driving is impossible without redundancy, which is why it doubles brake and steering paths. U0460 applies when B still communicates but its data are corrupt or implausible, for example out-of-sequence counters or CRC errors; if B falls silent, U015F is set, and U045F covers interface A. No manufacturer documents U0460 publicly. With only one trustworthy path left, a system above SAE level 2, where the machine rather than the driver watches the road, will usually refuse to engage or request a takeover, while a lower-level assistant may keep working with reduced functions. Software mismatches after updates, loose plugs and supply dips are the usual suspects.
c: Software level of interface module B not matching after an update
Loose plug or supply dips at interface B
Internal fault of interface module B
s: Automated driving unavailable or takeover request
Assistance functions limited

U0461.t: Invalid Data Received From Audible Alert Control Module
U0461.d: The audible alert control module produces warning chimes, for an unfastened belt, an open door or lights left on; in GM's list of U codes for the 2011 Saab 9-5 the matching node is called chime alarm control module. U0461 is stored when a partner, often the body controller or instrument cluster that requests or confirms the tones, receives status frames from this module that fail plausibility; U0160 is complete silence. No manufacturer documents U0461 publicly. The function has a legal side: FMVSS 208 requires an audible belt reminder lasting between 4 and 8 seconds, so a disturbed chime unit can mean warnings that never sound or keep sounding. Because many current cars generate these tones in the cluster or radio, only some models have a dedicated unit. U0440 concerns the outside pedestrian sound, a different device. No MIL.
c: Software of the chime module or requesting unit not matching
Loose plug or weak supply of the chime module
Internal fault of the audible alert module
s: Warning chimes missing, wrong or sounding constantly
Belt reminder without sound

U0462.t: Invalid Data Received From Compass Module
U0462.d: The compass module measures the earth's magnetic field, usually with two perpendicular sensors in the interior mirror or overhead console, and sends the heading to a display or navigation unit. Gentex patented a mirror compass of this kind with automatic calibration, compensation for magnetic disturbances inside the car and a link to the vehicle bus. U0462 is set when the receiving unit, for instance the instrument cluster, still gets compass messages but rejects them, for example because a counter or checksum fails or a value lies outside the possible range; if the messages stop, U0161 applies. No manufacturer documents U0462 publicly. The heading may show dashes or jump about; recalibration after a magnetic disturbance or a battery change sometimes helps. Driving is not affected and no MIL lights.
c: Compass calibration lost or disturbed by magnetic influences, for example after a battery change or roof-mounted accessories
Loose plug at the interior mirror or overhead console
Internal fault of the compass module or mirror electronics
s: Compass display shows dashes or wrong heading
Heading jumps while driving

U0463.t: Invalid Data Received From Navigation Display Module
U0463.d: The navigation display module is the screen part of a navigation head unit that shows maps and route guidance. U0463 marks invalid data from it, while U0162 means it is silent and U0464 concerns the navigation control unit. Subaru documents the partner: in bulletin 07-205-22 the rear vehicle detection module of the 2021 Crosstrek and 2020-22 Forester stores U0162 and lights its warning until reprogramming makes its CAN exchange with the head unit more robust, and TechTIPS 10/2015 calls the unit audio visual navigation display. No maker documents U0463 in this sense. FCA, now Stellantis, uses the number differently: in PCM bulletin 18-090-19 for the 2019 RAM ProMaster, U0463 is a fuel level plausibility code that new software switches off in favour of P0463. Usually only map and screen are affected; no MIL.
c: Software fault or mismatch in the head unit or display
Fuse, relay or supply problem of the display unit
Connector or bus wiring fault at the display
s: Navigation map or screen blank or frozen
Warnings of systems that share data with the head unit

U0464.t: Invalid Data Received From Navigation Control Module
U0464.d: U0464 is stored when a module still hears the navigation control module but rejects its content: a frame whose checksum fails, a message counter that no longer advances, or position, heading and route values outside their defined range. Typical listeners are the instrument cluster or head-up display, which repeat turn arrows, and on some cars predictive cruise or shift logic that reads the map ahead. No manufacturer documents U0464 in an openly accessible source. The protection behind such checks, a CRC and a sequence counter per message, is laid down in the AUTOSAR end-to-end protocol. U0163 means the unit has gone silent, U0463 concerns the separate navigation display and U046B the GPS receiver. The consequences stay in guidance and comfort: missing arrows or a wrong map position, no MIL.
c: Navigation unit software or map update fault sending implausible values
Loose connector or damaged bus wiring at the navigation unit or head unit
Weak 12 V battery or voltage dips during start-up corrupting frames
Internal fault in the navigation control module
s: Turn arrows missing in the cluster or head-up display
Vehicle position on the map jumps or is wrong
Route guidance stops or restarts unexpectedly

U0465.t: Invalid Data Received From PTO Control Module
U0465.d: U0465 flags implausible data from the power take-off (PTO) controller. That unit switches in an engine-driven output for dump beds, aerial lifts or pumps and asks the engine for a working speed. The engine or body controller logs it when PTO state or speed requests arrive corrupted or contradictory. GM uses the code: Saab's U-code tables for the 2011 9-5 and 9-4X, which follow GM's global architecture, list U0465 00 for invalid data from the PTO module, without timing or lamp rules. CARB lets the engine controller suspend monitor counters while a PTO runs, so a trusted PTO status matters for OBD bookkeeping. Caution: a Ram 1500 STAR case (S1908000041) prints U0465 in its title, but its body names U0645, the active air dam. U0117 is lost contact, P064B a PTO module fault. PTO or set speed drops out; no MIL.
c: Damaged or corroded wiring and connectors of the body-mounted PTO module
Mismatched configuration after installing or changing the body equipment
Voltage drops while the PTO and hydraulic loads are running
Internal fault in the PTO control module
s: PTO cannot be engaged or disengages on its own
Working engine speed for the body equipment is not held
PTO warning or message in the cluster

U0466.t: Invalid Data Received From HVAC Control Module - Rear
U0466.d: U0466 concerns the rear HVAC control module, the second climate controller in vans, minivans and large SUVs that runs its own blower, blend flaps and often a separate control panel for the back rows. A receiver such as the front climate unit or the body controller sets the code when the rear module's frames carry bad checksums, stalled counters or settings it cannot accept. No manufacturer documents U0466 publicly. For the front unit GM describes the equivalent check in its 2025 body controller: counters, protection values and CRCs of the HVAC messages are tested every 10 ms, and 8 failures within 10 samples set U0424 as Type B. U0165 means the rear module is silent, U0424 covers bad data from the front unit. The rear zone then ignores its controls or holds a fixed setting, while engine and front climate stay normal; no MIL.
c: Loose or corroded connector at the rear HVAC module, often in the rear trim or headliner
Software mismatch after replacing or programming one of the climate modules
Weak battery or voltage dips at the module
Internal fault in the rear HVAC control module
s: Rear climate controls do not respond
Rear blower or temperature stuck at one setting
Climate warning or fault message in the display

U0467.t: Invalid Data Received From Fuel Additive Control Module
U0467.d: U0467 belongs to diesels that use a fuel-borne catalyst. A separate fuel additive control module meters a metal-based additive from its own reservoir into the fuel after refuelling, so that soot trapped in the particulate filter ignites at about 350-450 °C instead of above 600 °C. The engine controller sets U0467 when the module's reports, for example dosed quantity, reservoir level or fault status, arrive corrupt or contradict each other. No manufacturer documents U0467 publicly. A Ford patent (US 6,276,310) outlines how such a dosing processor works with the engine controller, which supplies fuel consumption so the additive ratio stays constant. CARB requires the particulate filter and its regeneration to be monitored, so the fault counts as emission-related and a MIL is likely. U0118 is lost contact. Unrepaired, the filter clogs.
c: Corroded connector or damaged wiring at the additive pump module near the tank
Faulty additive level sensor feeding implausible values into the module
Module not adapted after refilling the additive or replacing the particulate filter
Internal fault in the fuel additive control module
s: Check engine lamp or particulate filter warning
Regeneration becomes more frequent or incomplete
Reduced engine power once the filter loads up

U0468.t: Invalid Data Received From Fuel Cell Control Module
U0468.d: U0468 marks invalid data from the fuel cell control module, the master controller of a hydrogen car, managing air and hydrogen supply, heat and water in the stack and the split of electrical power between stack, buffer battery and drive. Partners such as the motor inverter, battery management or the hydrogen storage unit reject its frames when checksums, counters or power requests do not hold up. No manufacturer documents U0468 publicly. Hyundai's supplier Kefico ranks the unit highest among the controllers of a fuel cell vehicle, and Hyundai's Nexo campaign T5D (2019-2020) rewrote its MIL logic together with that of the hydrogen storage management unit, so a lamp is possible. U0119 is lost contact, U0293 the hybrid/EV powertrain controller. Expect a warning, battery-only limp running or no READY.
c: Fuel cell control unit software needing an update from the manufacturer
Weak 12 V battery or poor ground disturbing the controller
Connector or bus wiring fault between the fuel cell unit and its partners
Internal fault in the fuel cell control module
s: Fuel cell system warning in the cluster
Reduced power, driving on the buffer battery only
Vehicle does not reach READY

U0469.t: Invalid Data Received From Starter / Generator Control Module
U0469.d: U0469 means the engine controller or gateway receives data from the starter/generator control module but cannot trust it. On 48 V mild hybrids this electronics sits in the belt starter generator, which cranks the engine, recuperates and charges both networks. Audi documents the code for A6, A7, A8, Q7, Q8 and related 48 V models from 2018 on: bulletin 2058831 pairs it with P0CA700 in the 48 V battery and first cures it with generator software; later revisions read the stored generator mode and compare requested with delivered torque, which should agree within 5 Nm. Bulletin 2073284 adds that U0469 often follows other CAN faults (U0028/U0029), so a new generator does not help. Ford's 2014 code list carries U0469 without MIL. U0120 is lost contact. Typical signs: electrical system warning, battery symbol, no start-stop.
c: Outdated software in the starter/generator control module
Other CAN or sensor faults disturbing the hybrid bus, with the generator only reporting the effect
48 V battery or 12 V supply problem upsetting the generator electronics
Internal hardware fault in the belt starter generator
s: Electrical system fault message and yellow or red battery symbol
Start-stop and recuperation no longer work
12 V battery not charged while driving

U046A.t: Invalid Data Received From Sunroof Control Module
U046A.d: U046A is logged when a module, usually the body controller or the overhead console, gets data from the sunroof control module that fails its checks: position and motion reports that contradict each other, a counter that stops changing or a bad checksum. The sunroof module drives the glass panel and sun blind and tracks their end positions. US standard FMVSS 118 restricts when a power-operated roof panel may close and demands automatic reversal where it closes outside those conditions, so a receiver that cannot trust the module usually blocks convenience closing from the key fob or rain sensor. No manufacturer documents U046A publicly. U0169 means the module is silent, U0140 concerns the body control module. Besides connectors, water from blocked roof drains is a plausible cause. The roof may ignore its switch; no MIL.
c: Water in the roof module or its connector from blocked sunroof drains
Lost end-position learning after battery disconnection or panel work
Chafed wiring or loose connector in the headliner
Internal fault in the sunroof control module
s: Sunroof does not open or close with its switch
Convenience closing by key or rain sensor no longer works
Panel stops midway or reverses unexpectedly

U046B.t: Invalid Data Received From Global Positioning System Module
U046B.d: U046B indicates that position, speed or time data from the global positioning system module fail plausibility in a receiving unit: a corrupt frame, a counter that stalls, or coordinates that cannot match the movement the car measures through its wheel speeds. The receiver feeds navigation, telematics, emergency call and map-based assistance. At Ford the telematics control unit evidently plays this role: according to SSM 54351, Transit vans of model year 2026 that lack a TCU can store the lost-contact twin U016A in a secondary OBD module, with no repair needed. A similar note for U046B does not exist; no manufacturer documents U046B publicly. U0464 covers bad data from the navigation unit, U0198 lost contact with the telematics module. The map position drifts or freezes; driving is unaffected, no MIL.
c: Damaged GPS antenna, cable or connector giving poor or jumping fixes
Software fault in the GPS or telematics module
Low battery voltage or poor ground at the module
Internal fault in the GPS module
s: Vehicle position on the map is wrong, jumps or freezes
Connected services or emergency call show no location
Clock or time zone set incorrectly

U046C.t: Invalid Data Received From A/C Compressor Control Module
U046C.d: U046C means that the electric A/C compressor's controller, i.e. the inverter spinning the high-voltage compressor in hybrids and EVs, sends data a receiver refuses: speed, power draw or status with bad checksums, frozen counters or values outside their range. Receivers are the climate controller and the hybrid or engine controller, which also use the refrigerant circuit to cool the traction battery. No manufacturer documents U046C publicly. GM's 2016 Volt table shows how tightly the compressor is supervised: the engine controller expects its message $222 and sets the lost-contact code U016B after 10 s as Type B (lamp on the second trip). U032A is a software mismatch, U0424 bad data from the HVAC unit. With untrusted compressor data, cabin and battery cooling may be cut back and charging or drive power limited in heat.
c: Damaged or chafed low-voltage harness or connector at the electric compressor
Compressor inverter software fault or mismatch after service
Weak 12 V supply disturbing the compressor electronics
Internal fault in the compressor control electronics
s: Air conditioning blows warm or switches off intermittently
Battery cooling limited, slower DC charging in hot weather
Climate or hybrid system warning in the cluster

U046D.t: Invalid Data Received From Fuel Pump Control Module B
U046D.d: U046D is about module B, the second of two fuel pump drivers, used on vehicles with two in-tank pumps or a saddle tank; for module A the matching code is U0410. A receiver, normally the engine controller, logs it when the module's reports, such as delivered pump output or its own fault status, arrive corrupt or implausible. No manufacturer documents U046D publicly. Ford shows that the same exchange can be judged without a U-code: in its 2024 OBD summary the pump B driver answers the engine controller over a duty-cycle feedback line, where 20 % (±4 %) flags an invalid command (P027B), 30 % an internal driver error (P26EA) and 0 or 100 % missing feedback, U016C, judged over 2-5 s with an 11-16 V supply. CARB requires fuel system components to be monitored. Expect the MIL, hesitation under load, hard starting or reduced power.
c: Poor ground or corroded connector at the second fuel pump driver
Damaged feedback or bus wiring between pump module B and the engine controller
Worn pump B drawing excess current and upsetting the driver's reports
Internal fault in fuel pump control module B
s: Check engine lamp on
Hesitation or power loss under heavy load
Long cranking or stalling

U046E.t: Invalid Data Received From Exhaust Gas Sensor Module B
U046E.d: U046E points to the B unit among exhaust gas sensor modules, a second smart device that warms a probe in the exhaust, interprets its signal, typically from a wide-band oxygen or NOx sensor, and transmits readings and readiness as bus data. The engine or aftertreatment controller sets it when frames still arrive but fail checksum or counter tests, or values such as NOx level or the ready flag are not credible. Which probe is B is up to the maker, often the one behind the SCR catalyst. No manufacturer documents U046E publicly. Chrysler bulletin 25-002-14 shows such a module on Cummins 6.7 L Ram heavy-duty pickups, there with its lost-contact code U011A. CARB counts these sensors as emission monitors that must be checked for rationality. Expect the MIL and urea dosing or mixture control on defaults. U041B is module A, U016D lost contact.
c: Heat-damaged or corroded connector and harness at the sensor module
Aged or contaminated probe making the module report implausible values
Calibration mismatch after replacing the sensor module
Internal electronics fault in exhaust gas sensor module B
s: Check engine lamp on
Exhaust aftertreatment or emission warning
Higher fuel or urea consumption from substitute values

U0471.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor A
U0471.d: U0471 is logged when the airbag controller still receives telegrams from restraints sensor A but rejects their content, for example because of a parity error, a reading outside the sensor's range or values that contradict the other crash sensors. Lost contact would be U0170. In Chrysler's diagnostic lists for the 2008 Jeep Wrangler, Compass, Patriot and Liberty, filed with NHTSA in investigation PE11-019, letter A stands for the left-hand up-front satellite, an acceleration sensor, with B1B70 for its internal fault. GM uses the letter differently: Saab's 2011 9-5 code list names U0170 as the passenger presence detection module, so on GM-based cars sensor A may belong to occupant sensing. Acura reports a silent left front sensor under its own code B0090. Expect the airbag lamp and weaker frontal crash sensing; no MIL.
c: Water or corrosion at the connector of a front satellite sensor in the engine bay
Sensor or its bracket deformed by a minor frontal impact
Replacement sensor of the wrong part number or orientation fitted
s: Airbag warning lamp stays on
Fault code stored in the restraints control module, sometimes with an internal sensor code

U0472.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor B
U0472.d: U0472 points to restraints sensor B: the airbag controller hears it but discards the transmitted values as corrupt or implausible, whereas U0171 would mean silence. Chrysler's NHTSA filing PE11-019 lists sensor B as the right-hand up-front satellite measuring acceleration on its 2007-2008 Jeep models, paired with internal fault B1B71. Front satellites of this kind sit in the crumple zone, where they notice a frontal crash earlier than the central unit. How much depends on their mounting is shown by Land Rover recall N685 for the 2022 Range Rover: front crash sensors fastened below the specified torque could work loose, feed the restraints system wrong information and even cause an unwanted frontal airbag deployment. Expect the airbag warning lamp; no MIL.
c: Front sensor not tightened to specification or loosened after body repair
Chafed or corroded harness between front sensor and airbag controller
Measuring element of the right front satellite defective
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal crash detection possibly degraded until repair

U0473.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor C
U0473.d: U0473 means the restraints controller receives sensor C but cannot use what it sends. In Chrysler's lists from investigation PE11-019, C is the first left-side satellite acceleration sensor, present already on the four-sensor Wrangler JK; its internal fault is B1B72, while U0172 covers lost contact. On later Jeeps such a side sensor sits in the B-pillar: FCA's STAR case S2108000269 for the 2022 Wrangler answers a B-pillar side impact sensor short (B2761-11) with a check for pinched wiring at the seat belt retractor bracket. Ford's program 22H05 had 2021 Bronco side sensors checked for a missing retaining stud on the B-pillar. A side sensor that delivers bad data can delay the left seat and curtain airbags. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Sensor wire pinched or chafed under the B-pillar or sill trim
Side sensor loose because a stud, nut or screw is missing
Sensor damaged by a previous side impact
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side and curtain airbag readiness uncertain

U0474.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor D
U0474.d: U0474 flags unusable data from restraints sensor D. Chrysler's lists in NHTSA file PE11-019 assign D to the second left-side satellite acceleration sensor (internal fault B1B73, lost contact U0173). It appears only for the 2007-2008 Compass and Patriot, which carry six satellites, and is absent from the four-sensor Wrangler list. A later FCA layout with two side sensors per flank is the 2019 Cherokee: recall 19V-449 replaced two front sensors in the engine bay and four side sensors in B- and C-pillars, because faulty solder joints could cut them off from the occupant restraint controller and make airbags fire late or not at all. That recall names no letters, so the pillar behind D stays unconfirmed. Airbag lamp on; no MIL.
c: Cracked solder joint inside the satellite sensor
Connector or wiring fault at the rear side sensor behind the pillar trim
Restraints controller configured for a different sensor layout
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side impact sensing on the left reduced

U0475.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor E
U0475.d: U0475 reports corrupt or implausible data from restraints sensor E; U0174 would be the lost-contact code. No manufacturer publicly ties letter E to a mounting point. Chrysler's restraint fault lists in NHTSA file PE11-019 even skip it, jumping from the second left-side sensor D to the first right-side sensor F. A system that uses E needs at least five peripheral crash sensors, and Bosch's compact AB light controller offers no more than six such inputs. The sensors talk over PSI5, a two-wire interface that grew out of airbag satellite links. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Damaged two-wire sensor line or connector
Internal fault in the satellite sensor itself
Restraints controller coding does not match the installed sensors
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller only

U0476.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor F
U0476.d: U0476 is stored when restraints sensor F still reports but its values fail the receiver's checks. Chrysler's lists in NHTSA investigation PE11-019 make F the first right-side satellite acceleration sensor, fitted even to the four-sensor Wrangler JK; internal fault B1B75, lost contact U0175. The side has little crush space, so this sensor must deliver usable data within milliseconds. FMVSS 214 sets the side impact tests such sensors help pass, a moving deformable barrier and a pole impact. When the right sensor sends garbage, deployment of the right seat and curtain airbags is no longer assured. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Wiring or connector fault at the right side sensor under the pillar or sill trim
Right side sensor damaged or misaligned after a side impact or body repair
Internal fault in the satellite sensor
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side and curtain airbag readiness uncertain

U0477.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor G
U0477.d: U0477 concerns restraints sensor G, whose messages arrive but are judged invalid; U0176 is lost contact. In Chrysler's lists from NHTSA investigation PE11-019, G names the second satellite on the right flank, an acceleration sensor with internal fault B1B76, and appears only on the six-sensor Compass and Patriot. What invalid data look like in practice is spelled out in Aston Martin's restraint control module manual: for the right C-pillar sensor of the Rapide it separates a dead line, Manchester or parity errors, readings outside the measuring range and plausibility faults, and often suspects a sensor with the wrong part number. Manchester bit coding with a parity bit is the PSI5 frame format. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Sensor of an unsuitable part number installed
Trapped or chafed sensor line causing corrupted telegrams
Sensor reporting values outside its measuring range
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear side impact sensing reduced

U0478.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor H
U0478.d: U0478 flags invalid data from restraints sensor H, the counterpart of lost-contact code U0177. No manufacturer publishes which sensor carries the letter H; the Chrysler fault tables filed with NHTSA under PE11-019 stop at G. An H implies at least eight satellites. Bosch's arithmetic allows that: besides acceleration satellites it wires two or four pressure sensors inside the door cavities, so four door sensors plus two side and two front acceleration sensors already add up to eight. Bosch's small AB light unit, with six sensor inputs at most, could not serve such a layout. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Moisture or a damaged seal affecting a door-mounted pressure sensor
Sensor line damaged, for example in a door hinge harness
Restraints controller coded for a sensor set that is not fitted
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code present only in the restraints controller

U0479.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor I
U0479.d: U0479 records that restraints sensor I sends data the airbag controller refuses; U0178 would be silence. No public source assigns the letter I to a mounting point, and a ninth peripheral sensor is rarely documented. Rear impact sensors are one way to reach such counts: Bosch offers its peripheral acceleration sensor for installation at the back of the vehicle, and on MCI coaches service instruction ITS-60877 had a rear impact accelerometer in baggage bay three moved because luggage could trigger it. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Damaged line or connector to the sensor
Sensor disturbed by loose cargo or a poor mounting location
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller

U047A.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor J
U047A.d: U047A means the airbag controller receives restraints sensor J but its content fails validation; lost contact is U0179. Which component carries the letter J is not published anywhere. Pedestrian protection is one source of extra inputs: Bosch fits either acceleration sensors or an air-filled tube with a pressure sensor at each end into the front bumper, lets the airbag controller evaluate them and can raise the hood within 10 to 15 ms. Corrupt data from such a sensor would put that function in doubt as well. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Bumper-mounted sensor damaged by a parking knock or bumper repair
Line or connector fault on the sensor circuit
Controller coding does not match the fitted sensors
s: Airbag or pedestrian protection warning shown
Code stored in the restraints controller

U047B.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor K
U047B.d: U047B: restraints sensor K is heard but its values are rejected; U017A covers lost contact. No manufacturer documents the letter K publicly, so its position stays open. Eleven satellites point to a large system, yet not every function needs one of its own: Bosch's AB premium controller can house rollover and inertial sensing internally and accepts as many as 18 PSI5 sensors. Where curtains also deploy in a rollover, FMVSS 226 requires a readiness indicator and lets NHTSA ask the carmaker to describe the deploying sensor system. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Corroded or loose connector in the sensor line
Restraints controller software evaluating the sensor incorrectly
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller

U047C.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor L
U047C.d: U047C sets when restraints sensor L still communicates but delivers unusable data; U017B is the lost-contact partner. L is the twelfth sensor letter, and twelve is exactly the number of PSI5 sensor interfaces Bosch quotes for its standard airbag control unit; more requires the premium version. No carmaker publishes what sits behind L. PSI5 frames carry a parity bit or a short CRC, so a corrupted telegram is caught before its value reaches the crash algorithm. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Damaged shielding or twisted pair causing checksum errors
Controller coding not matching the sensor equipment
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller

U047D.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor M
U047D.d: U047D reports invalid data from restraints sensor M; U017C is lost contact. A thirteenth satellite exceeds the twelve sensor interfaces of Bosch's standard airbag control unit, so a system using M needs a larger controller such as Bosch's AB premium with up to 18. No manufacturer discloses which component is M. The fault lies in content, not in the link: a wrong sensor variant, a damaged sensor or controller software that misreads the data are typical suspects. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Sensor variant not matching the vehicle configuration
Restraints controller software misinterpreting the sensor data
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller

U047E.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints System Sensor N
U047E.d: U047E closes the sensor series: restraints sensor N still sends, but its data are rejected; U017D is lost contact, and the following codes U047F and U0480 move on to belt pretensioner modules. Fourteen external sensors is precisely the maximum Bosch states for its airbag control unit for commercial vehicles. Trucks use such satellites too: Freightliner's campaign SF682 for early 2023-2024 eCascadia replaced AB12 modules because the forward crash sensors had been left unengaged. Which sensor any maker calls N is not published. Airbag lamp on, no MIL.
c: Corroded connector or damaged line to the sensor
Outdated restraints controller software or wrong sensor configuration
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code stored in the restraints controller

U047F.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Belt Pretensioner Module A
U047F.d: U047F concerns seat belt pretensioner module A, a belt retractor with its own motor and electronics rather than a purely pyrotechnic tensioner fired by the airbag unit. Such reversible retractors take up slack before a possible crash, during emergency braking or evasive steering, and can warn by pulsing the strap, as ZF LIFETEC describes for its ACR8. A receiver stores U047F when this module's messages are corrupt or implausible; U017E is lost contact. On 2025-2026 Audi Q5, Q6 e-tron, A5 and A6 models, bulletin 2081251 shows the partner code together with U017F and a proactive occupant protection fault. FCA calls U017E seatbelt sensor 1 in bulletin 18-013-22. Pre-crash belt tensioning may be unavailable; no MIL.
c: Software fault in the belt pretensioner module or its bus partner
Supply or bus wiring fault at the retractor in the B-pillar or seat
Internal fault in the motorised retractor module
s: Warning that proactive occupant protection is faulty
No belt pre-tensioning during hard braking
Airbag or restraint warning possible

U0480.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Belt Pretensioner Module B
U0480.d: U0480 mirrors U047F for seat belt pretensioner module B: the receiver gets its messages but finds them invalid, whereas U017F would mean silence. Honda's patent US 7,686,118 shows how such a unit is tied in: a dedicated electric belt controller drives the retractor motor, sits on the vehicle LAN, takes collision warnings from the brake control unit and receives the buckle signal routed through the airbag controller. With that many partners, bad data can come from the module itself or from inputs it relays. Autoliv's patent US 7,140,571 describes motor-driven reversible pre-crash tensioning. On 2025-2026 Audi models bulletin 2081251 records U017F00 beside U017E00. Comfort and pre-crash belt functions may switch off; no MIL.
c: Software fault in pretensioner module B or the unit sending it data
Faulty input relayed through the module, such as the buckle signal
Internal fault in the motorised retractor
s: Belt pre-tensioning or haptic belt warning unavailable
Restraint system warning message

U0481.t: Invalid Data Received From Automatic Lighting Control Module
U0481.d: U0481 means a module still receives frames from the automatic lighting control module but refuses their content, for instance an ambient-light value outside its range, a frozen message counter or a failed checksum; silence from that unit would be U0180. The unit decides from a light sensor, often housed with the rain sensor behind the windscreen, when the headlamps come on. No manufacturer documents U0481 publicly. Mazda shows how such a sensor flags its own trouble: on the 2019 Mazda3 (SA-035/19) heat drives the rain and light sensor beyond its operating range, the auto-light function pauses with B10AD:09 and resumes once the cabin cools. For automatic beam switching FMVSS 108 asks for an indicator telling the driver when the system is in control. Lights must be switched by hand; no MIL.
c: Light or rain/light sensor delivering values outside its range, e.g. after heat soak or windscreen replacement
Software or configuration of the lighting module not matching the receiving module
Corroded or loose connector on the bus line to the module
s: Automatic headlamp function unavailable, lights must be switched manually
Exterior lighting warning or message in the cluster

U0482.t: Invalid Data Received From Headlamp Leveling Control Module A
U0482.d: U0482 is stored when messages from headlamp leveling control module A arrive but fail the receiver's integrity or plausibility checks; complete loss of contact is U0181, and U048B covers a second leveling unit. Such a module takes axle ride-height signals and moves the beam actuators so that a loaded boot or hard braking does not lift the cut-off line, as Hella explains; dynamic versions also react to acceleration. The module may publish values for others: Subaru bulletin 07-232-26 for the 2024 WRX with manual gearbox describes leveler modules whose computed vehicle inclination always read 0 degrees on the centre display, cured by a unit with revised logic. GM's Saab list names the partner U0181 without a letter. No manufacturer documents U0482 itself. Beam height may freeze; lighting warning, no MIL.
c: Bent or faulty axle ride-height sensor feeding implausible values into the module
Leveling module software computing or transmitting wrong values
Basic setting of the leveling system not performed after repair or replacement
s: Headlamp leveling warning in the cluster
Beam height no longer adapts to load and may dazzle or fall short
Inclination display or related functions show fixed values

U0483.t: Invalid Data Received From Lighting Control Module - Front
U0483.d: U0483 means the front lighting control module, which switches low and high beam, daytime running and turn lamps or drives the LED channels in the headlamps, is still on the bus but delivers data the receiver rejects. U0182 would be the silent module, U0484 the rear counterpart. GM's Saab list names the front lighting control module among its partners. GM's 2024 Silverado and Sierra HD show how supply voltage upsets such a unit: with a weak battery its own voltage check fails, it resets every 8-10 s, the headlamps flash and P0606 is stored (24-NA-005), and replacing it is not the fix. Hella describes LED headlamp control units that report to the body control module over CAN and carry their own error monitoring. No manufacturer documents U0483 itself. Front lamps may revert to defaults; no MIL.
c: Weak battery or voltage dips during cranking upsetting the lighting module
Lighting module software or calibration fault
Moisture or corrosion at the module or headlamp connector
s: Headlamps or daytime running lamps flicker or flash
Exterior lighting warning in the cluster
Front lamps stay in a fixed default state

U0484.t: Invalid Data Received From Lighting Control Module - Rear A
U0484.d: U0484 is set when frames from rear lighting control module A are received but carry values the listener cannot accept; U0183 stands for lost contact, while rear module B has U0252 and U0553. Such modules drive tail, stop and turn lamps or LED segments at the back and report their status. BMW's 2022 iX shows the layout: four rear light modules, two in the side panels and two in the tailgate, share Body_CAN, and a software error in them produced communication and time-out entries with rear light warnings although the lamps worked (SIB 63 06 22). GM updated the exterior lighting module of 2024 Corvettes that failed to tell the driver about a failed rear turn signal, an indication FMVSS 108 requires. No maker documents U0484 itself. Lamp warnings, possible default lighting; no MIL.
c: Software error in the rear lighting module or a module not updated to the current level
Chafed or broken wires in the tailgate or boot lid harness
Water ingress at a rear lamp connector
s: Rear light system warning although the lamps may still work
Turn, stop or tail lamp failures not reported or lamps in default mode

U0485.d: U0485 means the radio or centre stack still transmits but a receiving module rejects its frames. GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG03B, 25OBDG04B) describe the body control module checking alive rolling counters, protection values, checksums and CRCs of centre-stack signals, among them HVAC control requests: 8 failures in 10 samples, for some signals 14 in 18 or 15 in 16, set it at least 5 s after power-up, with the partial network active for 3 s, power mode Run and over 11 V; Type B. GM PIE0807A covers a MIL with U0485 and U1962 on the 2024 Traverse and Acadia 2.5 L. Stellantis lists it in 08-046-23, 08-014-24 and 08-101-25 (Grand Cherokee, Wagoneer, Pacifica), stored by the amplifier or with a MIL; radio software cures it. U0184 is lost contact.
c: Radio or infotainment software level with known message errors, fixed by an update
Radio resetting or waking late so that counters and checksums no longer match
Low supply voltage or a disturbed bus connection to the centre stack
s: Radio resets, black screen or audio sources inoperative
Climate controls on the screen do not respond
MIL on some vehicles

U0486.t: Invalid Data Received From Antenna Control Module
U0486.d: U0486 points to the antenna control module: its frames still arrive, yet the receiver, typically the radio or a keyless-entry controller, discards them as corrupt or implausible. U0185 would mean silence. Such modules sit in the roof fin, rear screen or bumper and amplify, combine or switch signals for radio, satellite, navigation, phone or remote key, and some raise a powered mast. Mercedes shows how water affects them: on the G-Class from model year 2019 without sunroof, a crack near the left rear roof rail pan lets water in, the keyless-go controller stores antenna module faults and the key may no longer unlock the car (LI65.10-P-074539); sealing the crack is the repair. No manufacturer documents U0486 itself. Expect weak reception or reduced key range, with no MIL.
c: Water reaching the antenna module through a roof leak or failed fin seal
Internal fault of the antenna amplifier or module
Damaged coaxial or bus connector between antenna module and receiver
s: Poor or no radio, satellite or navigation reception
Remote key does not unlock or works only at short range

U0487.t: Invalid Data Received From Audio Amplifier A
U0487.d: U0487 means the external audio amplifier A keeps sending frames, but the radio or gateway finds their content invalid; once the amplifier vanishes from the bus, U0186 applies, and amplifier B has U0262 and U0563. Amplifiers return status such as mute state, sound settings and diagnostic results to the head unit. No manufacturer documents U0487 publicly. Mazda files faulty amplifier messages under U0186 with failure type 08 instead: on the 2019-2023 Mazda3 and CX-30 (SA-070-22) a backed-out pin in the MOST connector of the connectivity master unit caused it, together with static. Chrysler 08-020-14 reflashed amplifiers on 2013-2014 Ram, Durango and Grand Cherokee when the radio was muted because the amplifier went quiet. GM's Saab list calls the unit speaker amplifier module. Sound may mute or crackle; no MIL.
c: Backed-out or spread pin in the amplifier or MOST connector
Amplifier software level not matching the head unit
Poor supply or ground at the amplifier
s: No sound or radio muted
Static or crackling from the speakers, sometimes when tapping the dash

U0488.t: Invalid Data Received From Digital Disc Player/Changer Module A
U0488.d: U0488 is logged when the first networked disc drive, module A, still reports on the bus but its data fail the receiver's checks; U0187 would mean the drive is silent, while U0489, U048A and U0491 cover drives B to D. Many GM vehicles of 2013-2015 carried such a separate media disc player with its own fuse: bulletin PIT5344B (ATS, Escalade, Silverado, Tahoe and others) told technicians to cycle that fuse when CD playback stopped and to replace the player only if power and ground tested fine. In optical MOST networks a drive of this kind is a ring member that streams its audio to the head unit. No manufacturer documents U0488 itself. The radio then refuses disc playback while other sources keep working; no MIL.
c: Disc player hung internally, cleared by a power cycle
Poor supply or ground at the disc player
s: CD or DVD playback unavailable
Other audio sources keep working

U0489.t: Invalid Data Received From Digital Disc Player/Changer Module B
U0489.d: U0489 refers to disc player/changer module B, a second drive in the same network, such as a changer added to a radio that already plays CDs or a DVD unit for the rear seats. The receiver still hears it but rejects the content, whereas loss of contact is U0188; drive A has U0488. Two-drive layouts did exist at GM: the 2004-2009 Cadillac XLR paired its navigation radio with a separate CD changer, and GM PIC4858A notes that a replacement changer installed with its shipping pin still in place refuses discs and shows a CD error. No maker states which drive counts as B, and none documents U0489. Discs in that unit cannot be played, while radio and other sources work; no MIL.
c: Replacement changer fitted without removing the transport lock
Mechanical or internal fault in the changer
Vehicle coded for a second drive that is missing or of another type
s: Second disc drive does not accept or play discs
Disc error message on the display

U048A.t: Invalid Data Received From Digital Disc Player/Changer Module C
U048A.d: U048A stands for a third disc player or changer, module C. It is set when that unit's frames reach the receiver but fail its checks; silence would be U0189. Three networked drives in one vehicle are rare. Luxury cars with a DVD changer in addition to the head unit come closest: Audi's update 72K1 for the 2019 A8 replaced the changer mounting because its trim cover could come loose. No manufacturer assigns the letter C publicly or documents U048A, so the code works mainly as a reserve slot in the J2012 list. If it does appear, first check whether the vehicle actually has such a unit or carries a coding error after a retrofit, then power, ground and the bus link to the drive. No MIL; driving is unaffected.
c: Wrong vehicle coding after a retrofit or removal of a disc unit
Supply, ground or bus connection fault at the third drive
Internal fault of the disc unit
s: Disc playback from that unit unavailable
Code present without any noticeable fault on cars without such a unit

U048B.t: Invalid Data Received From Headlamp Leveling Control Module B
U048B.d: U048B concerns the second headlamp leveling control module, B, whose messages reach the receiver but are discarded as corrupt or implausible; if B fell silent, U018A would be logged, while module A has U0482 and U0181. A second address is needed where each headlamp carries its own electronics or a central unit works with lamp-side controllers. No maker assigns the letter publicly or documents U048B. Comparable lamp-side faults appear under brand codes: Mazda's AFS control module on the 2024 CX-90 falsely flagged B10A3:86, an error signal from the left swivel actuator, until new software arrived (09-039-24), and GM had the headlamp control module of the 2016 Buick Cascada set up again to clear B101E and a leveling warning (16-NA-044). Expect a lighting warning; no MIL.
c: Software of the lamp-side or leveling module misjudging actuator feedback
Setup or configuration of the headlamp module not completed after assembly or replacement
Moisture or poor contact at the connector of the second headlamp
s: Headlamp leveling or adaptive lighting warning
Beam height on one side no longer adjusted

U0491.t: Invalid Data Received From Digital Disc Player/Changer Module D
U0491.d: U0491 belongs to a fourth networked disc player or changer, module D: frames from that drive still arrive, yet the radio or gateway rejects their content. Its lost-contact partner is U0190; drives A to C have U0488, U0489 and U048A. Separate disc drives did exist, for example the media disc player in GM's 2017 Silverado, Sierra, Suburban, Tahoe and Yukon with entertainment package, which bulletin 17-NA-378 replaced when film sound drifted out of sync with the picture. A fourth unit of this kind is practically unknown, and no manufacturer documents U0491 or publicly assigns the letter D. On a car without such a drive the code hints at coding or software rather than hardware. No MIL; at most disc playback is lost.
c: Vehicle coding or head-unit software expecting a fourth disc drive that is absent or different
Disc drive D hung up or internally faulty
Poor supply, ground or bus link at the drive
s: Discs in that drive cannot be played
Code stored without noticeable fault on cars lacking such a drive

U0492.d: U0492 is set when a television tuner keeps transmitting but the module listening to it, usually the head unit or a display controller, cannot use what arrives, for instance because values lie outside their defined range, a message counter stalls or a checksum is wrong. GM's 2011 code lists for the Saab 9-5 and 9-4X simply call the matching lost-contact code U0191 Television, meaning a separate TV receiver on the bus. Elsewhere the tuner lives inside the radio: for Japanese-market Jeep Grand Cherokee and Cherokee of 2014, bulletin 08-067-15 updated the radio software, which among other things cured a blurry digital TV picture. No manufacturer documents U0492 itself. Expect a missing or frozen TV image while radio and other sources carry on; driving is unaffected, no MIL.
c: Tuner or head-unit software with faulty TV data, cured by an update
Internal fault of the TV tuner
Supply, ground or bus connection fault at the tuner
s: No TV picture or a frozen, blurred image
Radio and other media sources keep working

U0493.t: Invalid Data Received From Personal Computer
U0493.d: U0493 covers a personal computer sharing the vehicle network, a slot in the J2012 list that hardly any production car fills. The nearest real case is a fleet or police vehicle with a laptop or mobile data terminal wired into the car: Ford's 2027 Police Interceptor Utility offers an Integrated Computer Screen that mirrors a laptop stowed in the cargo bay, and a Vehicle Integration System that lets upfitters read the J1939 CAN signals. The code is logged when such a computer sends frames whose content a receiving module refuses; total silence would be U0192. No manufacturer documents U0493 publicly, so an aftermarket installation, its interface box or its software is the first suspect. Driving is unaffected and no MIL lights.
c: Aftermarket computer installation or interface box sending non-conforming frames
Software or configuration of the connected computer
Wiring or connector fault at the vehicle interface
s: Functions of the connected computer that rely on vehicle data fail
Often no noticeable fault in the vehicle itself

U0494.t: Invalid Data Received From Digital Audio Control Module A
U0494.d: U0494 is stored when digital audio control module A still communicates but supplies data the receiver will not accept. In GM's 2011 Saab 9-5 and 9-4X lists the matching lost-contact code U0193 belongs to the digital radio receiver, at that time the separate XM satellite tuner. GM bulletin PIT5413 (2015 Enclave, Traverse, Acadia) shows such a receiver as a module of its own with a 16-pin power and GMLAN connector, which must be checked for supply, ground and bus before a replacement is authorised. Other makers may fill slot A with a different device, and none documents U0494 itself. Typical result: satellite or digital channels drop out or show errors while FM keeps playing. No MIL; U0495 is module B.
c: Receiver software or activation state producing unexpected values
Supply, ground or bus fault at the receiver's connector
s: Satellite or digital radio channels missing or showing errors
Analogue radio and other sources unaffected

U0495.t: Invalid Data Received From Digital Audio Control Module B
U0495.d: U0495 is the invalid-data code for a second digital audio unit, module B. Where slot A is used at all, it tends to be the digital or satellite radio receiver, as in GM's Saab lists; for B no public code list or bulletin names a concrete device, and no maker documents U0495. The partner U0194 does appear in GM bulletin 15-NA-004 (2013-2016 Acadia), but only as one of eleven lost-contact codes traced to a low-speed LAN lead crushed by the rear climate duct in the headliner, which reveals nothing about module B itself. A stored U0495 should therefore first be checked against the vehicle's own module list, then software levels and the bus link. At worst one digital audio source is missing; no MIL.
c: Coding or software mismatch about which device occupies slot B
Damaged or pinched bus wiring disturbing several modules
Internal fault of digital audio module B
s: One digital audio source unavailable
Often stored together with other network codes

U0496.t: Invalid Data Received From Subscription Entertainment Receiver Module
U0496.d: U0496 points to the subscription entertainment receiver: a tuner whose programmes, typically SiriusXM satellite radio in North America, play only with a paid, activated account. Its frames still reach the radio, but their content fails the checks; complete silence would be U0195. Such receivers report more than audio: GM bulletin PIC5088E (2002-2015 cars and trucks with XM) has technicians read the receiver status, which shows whether the unit is bound and activated or has a binding failure, the latter meaning replacement. GM files its XM tuner as the digital radio receiver, so its own lists use U0193 rather than this slot, and no maker documents U0496 publicly. Symptoms: satellite channels missing or limited to the preview channels, other sources fine; no MIL.
c: Subscription or activation state not refreshed, receiver reports unexpected status
Internal binding failure of the receiver
Supply, ground or bus fault at the receiver
s: Only preview channels or no satellite channels at all
Terrestrial radio and media work normally

U0497.t: Invalid Data Received From Entertainment Control Module - Rear A
U0497.d: U0497 concerns rear entertainment control module A, which lets people in the back choose media, listen on headphones and watch their own screens independently of the front.
