Automatic functions of that window disabled

U052A.t: Invalid Data Received From Heated Steering Wheel Module
U052A.d: The heated steering wheel module powers the heating mat in the rim and reports its state, such as heater on or off, the requested level and the rim temperature read by an embedded thermistor, to the body or climate network. A receiver that gets these frames but finds the content implausible (temperature out of range, bad checksum or counter, wrong length) logs U052A; if the frames stop entirely, U0229 is set instead. Ford shows that the hardware depends on the option: if adaptive steering is fitted, heating is a job of Ford's SECM, the steering effort controller inside the wheel, otherwise of a separate HSWM (SSM 47850). No bulletin names U052A itself. For the driver the rim may stay cold, switch off early or show no status; steering is unaffected.
c: Rim temperature sensor drifting or open, giving implausible values
Worn clock spring or steering wheel wiring to the heater circuit
Heated steering wheel module internally faulty
Module software or configuration not matching after programming
s: Heated steering wheel stays cold or switches off early
Heater indicator or menu shows no or wrong status

U052F.t: Invalid Data Received From Object Detection Maintenance Control Module A
U052F.d: Object detection maintenance control modules appear in the generic code list, but no manufacturer has published what they do or when this fault sets. The name points to a unit that keeps cameras, radar or lidar used for object detection usable, for example by running washers, air jets or heaters. Ford's patent US10569746 describes such logic for a roof-mounted lidar: a contactless cleaner runs first, and a wiping cleaner follows only if the window is still too opaque. U052F means a receiver, most likely the driver-assist controller, gets messages from maintenance module A that are corrupt or implausible, so it cannot rely on the reported cleaning or blockage status. Assistance features may report a blocked sensor or switch off. Loss of the module is U022E; module B is U0530.
c: Software or configuration mismatch of maintenance module A
Internal fault of the maintenance module (e.g. moisture ingress)
Wiring or connector fault on the module's data line
s: Sensor blocked or sensor cleaning message
Driver assistance features temporarily unavailable
Sensor washing or heating not working

U0530.t: Invalid Data Received From Object Detection Maintenance Control Module B
U0530.d: Module B of this family is a second maintenance controller for object detection sensors, for instance one serving another sensor group or the other side of the vehicle. The generic definition offers no public explanation, and no manufacturer document names U0530. Denso's patent US11451765 illustrates the kind of decision such a unit supports: two sensors sharing a field of view are compared, and when they disagree about the objects they see, one of them is judged dirty and marked for cleaning. U0530 is stored when a receiving module gets frames from module B that fail checks such as range, counter or checksum. The outcome is usually a message that a sensor or assistance feature is unavailable, not any effect on drivability. Total loss of B is U022F; the A unit is U052F.
c: Software level of module B not matching the receiving controller
Module B internal fault, e.g. after water or road salt exposure
Intermittent contact in the data line or connector to module B
s: Message that a sensor or assistance function is unavailable
Automatic sensor cleaning on one side or sensor group not working

U0531.t: Invalid Data Received From Rear Gate Module
U0531.d: The rear gate module runs a powered liftgate or tailgate: motor drive, latch, pinch sensing and the requests from switches or key fob. U0531 is stored when its messages reach other controllers with content they refuse. No manufacturer documents U0531 itself, but its lost-communication partner U0230 appears in several bulletins. GM's Saab 9-5 code list calls the unit liftgate control module; GM PIT5422 traced U0230 on 2010–2015 Equinox and Terrain to water or corrosion in connector X901 in the upper liftgate area on the low-speed LAN; Toyota T-SB-0038-15 lists U0230 with B2222 on 2008–2013 Highlander whose power back door reversed instead of latching. FCA's WL Grand Cherokee shows signal-invalid codes inside the liftgate module. Driving is unaffected.
c: Water ingress or corrosion in connectors at the liftgate
Liftgate module software fault (update available on some models)
Broken wires in the harness passing through the liftgate hinge area
Hinge or drive damage after repeated obstruction while closing
s: Power liftgate does not open or close electrically
Liftgate reverses at the fully closed position
Interior lamps or other body functions fail at the same time (shared LAN)

U0532.t: Invalid Data Received From Rain Sensing Module
U0532.d: The rain sensing module behind the windshield measures how much infrared light wet glass scatters and, in most designs, also reads ambient light for automatic headlamps. Melexis describes such a unit as an optical front end, a microcontroller and a LIN system basis chip linking it to the body controller. U0532 is logged when that controller or a gateway receives the module's frames but rejects them, for example an impossible rain intensity, a parity or checksum error or a response of the wrong length. Jeep shows the related loss case: on the 2021 Grand Cherokee (WL) the body controller could store U0231-00 for the LIN rain sensing module without a MIL, corrected by a BCM flash (08-050-22, with sister bulletins for Wagoneer and 4xe). With bad data, automatic wipers fall back to manual or run at odd intervals.
c: Rain and light sensor electronics faulty
Sensor badly coupled to the glass or wrong variant after windshield replacement
Corroded connector or chafed LIN wire at the windshield headliner
Body controller software evaluating the sensor frames incorrectly
s: Automatic wipers do not react to rain or wipe on a dry screen
Automatic headlamps switch late, early or not at all

U0533.t: Invalid Data Received From Side Obstacle Detection Control Module A
U0533.d: Side obstacle detection modules are the corner radars behind the rear bumper that watch blind spots and crossing traffic. GM and Ford give letter A to the left unit: the 2011 Saab 9-5 code list names U0232 for the left side-object module, and Ford bulletin 24-2180 (Expedition/Navigator 2022-2024) logs U0232 in Ford's IPMA camera module together with faults of the left radar. Toyota instead labels U0232 as the slave sensor on the Tacoma. U0533 itself appears in no published manufacturer text; it would be set when the left module's frames reach the receiver but carry invalid content. The Ford case shows that mud, ice or corrosion at the sensor trigger false Blind Spot Not Available warnings. Blind spot and cross traffic alerts then switch off. U0232 is total loss, U0534 the right unit.
c: Mud, ice or damage at the left rear radar, bracket or bumper cover
Water or corrosion in the radar connector or harness
Radar module software or configuration fault
s: Blind spot monitoring unavailable message
Left mirror warning indicator inoperative
Rear cross traffic alert switched off

U0534.t: Invalid Data Received From Side Obstacle Detection Control Module B
U0534.d: Module B is the right-hand rear corner radar in GM and Ford numbering: Saab's 2011 list calls U0233 the right side-object module, and Ford's Expedition/Navigator bulletin 24-2180 pairs U0233 with the right sensor. Toyota uses U0233 for the master sensor of the Tacoma blind spot system, where bulletin T-SB-0063-19 had both sensors replaced and re-aimed with a reflector tool. No manufacturer document cites U0534, so its setting criteria are not public. The code stands for traffic from the right unit that arrives normally but whose payload the receiving module rejects. Typical outcome: the right blind spot indicator stays dark, cross traffic alert is unavailable and a service message appears. A wet or damaged plug at the bumper is a frequent trigger. U0233 means the module is silent; the left unit is U0533.
c: Moisture or corrosion at the right radar connector
Right radar damaged or misaligned after a bumper impact
Internal fault or outdated software in the right radar module
s: Right mirror blind spot indicator not working
Cross traffic alert unavailable
Service message for the blind spot system

U0535.t: Invalid Data Received From Convenience Recall Module
U0535.d: A convenience recall module keeps driver profiles and moves seat, mirrors, adjustable pedals or steering column back to stored positions, typically on a memory button or when the key fob linked to a profile unlocks the car. Ford's patent filing lists profiles covering seat, mirror, pedal and steering adjustment, and a Lear/Ford patent places a memory seat module with position sensors on the seat frame; Ram's owner's manual ties two memory profiles to two fobs. U0535 is set when profile or position data from this module arrive but fail validation. No manufacturer documents this code or the module name publicly, so which unit carries it varies; on many cars the driver's seat electronics handle memory recall (see U0509). Effect: positions are not recalled or recalled wrongly; driving is unaffected.
c: Seat, mirror or pedal position sensor reporting implausible values
Memory module internally faulty or stored profiles corrupted
Pinched or corroded wiring under the seat or in the door
Module not configured or positions not relearned after replacement
s: Memory buttons or key-linked profiles do not restore positions
Seat or mirrors move to wrong positions or stop part-way

U0536.t: Invalid Data Received From Lateral Acceleration Sensor Module
U0536.d: Lateral acceleration tells the stability system how hard the car is being pushed sideways in a bend; set against yaw rate and steering input it reveals whether the vehicle still follows the driver. U0536 is logged by a receiving module, usually the brake or ESC controller, when frames from a stand-alone lateral acceleration sensor module are present but unusable, for instance a reading beyond physical limits, an invalid flag or a broken message counter. Public manufacturer documents do not describe this code. Many designs have no separate lateral sensor any more: the 2011 Saab 9-5 bundles it in a multi-axis unit and reports bad data as U0125 with a failure type. With U0536 active, ESC and traction control are normally disabled and their lamps stay on, while ordinary braking works. U0124 covers a missing sensor.
c: Acceleration sensor element faulty or out of calibration
Module mounted loosely or in the wrong orientation after repair work
Corrosion or moisture at the module connector (often under seats or console)
Software or coding mismatch between sensor module and receiver
s: ESC and traction control lamps lit
No stability or traction intervention when cornering
Hill hold or adaptive cruise may be unavailable

U0537.t: Invalid Data Received From Column Lock Module
U0537.d: The column lock module drives the electric bolt that blocks the steering shaft when the car is parked and frees it before the engine may start. U0537 records that a partner module, such as the body controller or keyless start unit, received lock status messages it cannot trust. No manufacturer explains this exact code publicly. Related bulletins show how tightly the lock depends on timing and authentication: GM bulletin 16-NA-091 (ATS, CTS, XTS) reprogrammed the module after a Service Column Lock message with B2897, caused by door and power-mode changes within 100 to 300 ms, and Stellantis case S2408000110 (Wrangler 2024) lists implausible ignition, speed and coded BCM messages seen by the lock itself, with 10 to 16 V required. Possible effects: no start, column stays locked or a warning. U0236 is the lost-communication code.
c: Column lock module software or calibration fault (reprogramming)
Weak 12 V battery or voltage drops during start
Lock module not paired/learned to the body or immobilizer module after replacement
Mechanical or internal fault of the lock actuator
s: Engine does not start or start is refused
Steering wheel remains locked
Steering column lock service message

U0538.t: Invalid Data Received From Digital Audio Control Module C
U0538.d: Digital audio control modules are the networked parts of a sound system such as amplifiers, signal processors or media interfaces; the letters A to D merely count them. Ford groups U0237 and U0238, the lost-communication codes for modules C and D, with DSP trouble: 2020–2021 Escape, 2021 F-150, Mach-E, Expedition, Explorer and 2020–2022 Edge could lose all sound while chimes moved to the cluster, cured by a battery-disconnect reset and DSP reprogramming (SSM 49737, 50739, 51778). GM's Saab 9-5 list gives the C partner slot to the multimedia player interface module instead. U0538 itself appears in no bulletin; it means module C still communicates but its audio status or configuration content is rejected, which can mute zones or drop sources.
c: Audio module software fault, as in Ford's DSP cases
Poor fuse contact or low supply voltage at the module
s: No sound or missing speaker channels
Warning chimes only from the instrument cluster

U0539.t: Invalid Data Received From Digital Audio Control Module D
U0539.d: Ford assigns the D slot fairly clearly: on 2024–2026 Nautilus, 2025–2026 Aviator with the 28-speaker system and 2025–2026 Navigator, the audio control module stores U0238 when it cannot reach the digital signal processor (SSM 54751, 54752). The first check there is pulling the DSP fuse for one minute; only when contact returns are a fuse fault or a new DSP the answer, and on Nautilus and Navigator a software fix was still pending. U0539 is the step before total loss: the DSP's frames do reach the ACM, yet its status, volume or equalizer content fails the plausibility checks. Ford publishes no case for U0539 itself. Typical results are silence or missing channels while the radio display keeps working; the vehicle drives normally.
c: Poor blade contact at the DSP fuse or supply interruption
DSP or audio control module software fault
s: No audio from the speakers although the radio display works
Sound drops out intermittently or some channels are missing

U053A.t: Invalid Data Received From Entrapment Control Module A
U053A.d: Entrapment control modules handle pinch protection for powered closures where it is not built into the drive, typically sliding doors, liftgates or roofs with sensing edges. For windows, roof panels and partitions FMVSS 118 sets the goal: stop and reverse before 100 N act on the test rod. Chinese patent CN102923068B shows a dedicated anti-pinch module for a back door that drives the motor, reads a Hall sensor and exchanges commands and diagnostic messages with the body controller over CAN. U053A means such a module A is transmitting, but its data are rejected. No manufacturer documents the code or what module A protects. Expect the affected closure to refuse automatic closing or to reverse unexpectedly; U0239 is the lost-communication counterpart.
c: Entrapment control module A internally faulty or with wrong software
Damaged pinch sensor edge feeding implausible values into the module
Bus wiring to the module damaged, e.g. in a liftgate or door hinge
s: Power closure will not close automatically
Closure reverses without an obstacle

U053B.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Module A
U053B.d: Image processing modules evaluate camera data for assistance functions, and module A is the one most often named in service literature. GM's 2025 brake controller tables (25OBDG04A) check protection values and rolling counters in messages from the object fusion controller (EOCM); 3 errors in a window of 16 frames set U053B as Type C without MIL, and the test pauses outside 9 to 16 V. Ford's OBD summaries let the PCM store it, non-MIL, on Remote Park Assist and Auto Hitch programs. On the 2025 Maverick, IPMA software caused U053B:56 in the cluster (SSM 53385, update per SSM 54423). The 2025 Jeep Compass logs U053B 81 after a 12 V disconnect until the steering angle is relearned. GM's Lyriq bulletin PIC6500A lists it among codes held by the Lyriq camera processor. Lost communication is U023A.
c: Software in image processing module A (update available, e.g. Ford Maverick)
Steering angle not relearned after battery disconnect or transport mode (Jeep Compass)
Front camera not calibrated after windshield or module replacement
Supply voltage outside the valid window during start-up
s: Lane keeping or adaptive cruise unavailable message
Remote park assist or automatic hitch function refused
Code stored without noticeable symptoms

U053C.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Module B
U053C.d: U053C is documented by GM on cars with Super Cruise. On the 2023 Cadillac Lyriq it could set at start-up and remain current for as long as half an hour, keeping Super Cruise unavailable; an ignition cycle cleared it in some cases only (PIC6500). Revision PIC6500A widened the list of codes stored by that module and told technicians not to replace the controller, and PIC6500B closed the case in 2024. For the 2026 range from Escalade and Tahoe to Lyriq, Vistiq and Sierra EV, PIC6607 through PIC6607B again state that a history U053C is unrelated to the real Super Cruise fault and must not lead to module replacement. Elsewhere module B is often a surround-view unit, as Ford's IPMB on Explorer and Aviator. Lost communication is U023B.
c: Software behaviour at start-up between the image processing modules (GM Super Cruise)
Stored history code unrelated to the actual fault (GM PIC6607)
Fault in module B or its network connection
s: Super Cruise Unavailable message
Adaptive cruise or Service Driver Assist message
Surround view camera display faulty (other makes)

U053D.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Module C
U053D.d: No manufacturer text cites U053D. GM does show which unit occupies slot C: bulletin 21-NA-209 for the 2021 Escalade identifies U023C as the code for a silent K157 video processing module, where a software fault left the radio screen black with a crossed-out camera symbol until a fuse reset and reprogramming. The Lyriq bulletin PIC6500A also lists U023C among codes held by its camera processing unit. U053D is the counterpart for content errors: the video processing module keeps talking, but a receiver such as the camera controller or the display rejects its messages. Likely effects are camera views missing from the screen or assistance functions that depend on processed images becoming unavailable. Software updates are the usual first remedy, before hardware. A and B are U053B and U053C.
c: Software anomaly in the video/image processing module C
Module locked up, cleared by power reset (fuse) and reprogramming
Damaged video or network cable to module C
s: Black or missing camera image on the central display
Camera-based assistance functions unavailable

U0541.t: Invalid Data Received From Entrapment Control Module B
U0541.d: Entrapment control module B is the second slot for a separate pinch-protection unit. Some designs detect a person before contact: a capacitive strip changes its electric field as a hand approaches, and the attached electronics pass the result to the closure controller either as a switched output or as LIN or SAE J2602 data, as a review of tailgate anti-pinch approaches explains; patent US20030151382 likewise combines a capacitive field with a position sensor. U0541 is stored when frames from such a unit B are malformed or implausible. No manufacturer publishes the code. FCA's case S2208000106 shows how confusing two-sided sensing can be: its left and right liftgate pinch sensor codes may point to the wrong side, so check both connectors. U0240 covers complete loss of module B.
c: Capacitive sensor strip or its electronics delivering implausible values
Sensor connector not fully seated or corroded
Software or calibration of module B not matching after replacement
s: Power liftgate or sliding door stops or reverses without contact
Automatic closing refused with a warning

U0542.t: Invalid Data Received From Headlamp Control Module A
U0542.d: Headlamp control modules run adaptive lighting such as swivelling, levelling, matrix segments and LED daytime lights, frequently with one module per headlamp. U0542 means a receiver, for example the body or lighting master module, gets messages from module A that fail its checks. No manufacturer publishes text for U0542. Jaguar documents the units by letter: on the 2020 XE, headlamp control modules A and B stored false low-voltage faults for position and daytime lights because current and board voltage were sampled out of phase (SSM74402), and new software with a revised threshold was announced. Bentley's Continental GT treats the left and right light controllers as separate addresses for reprogramming. Expect a headlamp warning and adaptive features held in a default position. U0241 is lost communication.
c: Headlamp or module replaced without coding/configuration
Moisture or corrosion at the headlamp connector
s: Check headlamp or lighting system warning
Adaptive or cornering light not working on one side
Daytime running light or position light affected

U0543.t: Invalid Data Received From Headlamp Control Module B
U0543.d: Headlamp control module B is the second light controller, usually serving the headlamp opposite module A. Bentley's 2019-2020 Continental GT campaign (2056293/1) handles the two as light control left and right, at diagnostic addresses 29 and 39, and both needed new software when the outer daytime running lights failed. Jaguar's 2020 XE likewise names HCMA and HCMB (SSM74402). Which side B covers remains vehicle-specific. No public manufacturer text uses U0543; it marks data from B reaching the network in a form the receiver cannot accept. Matrix or bending light then normally falls back to a fixed low beam on the affected side, and a lighting warning appears. Swapping a headlamp without coding or running mismatched software levels left and right are typical triggers. U0242 means B is silent; A is U0542.
c: Different or outdated software in headlamp module B compared with A
Internal fault in headlamp module B
s: Lighting system warning in the cluster
Matrix or bending light on one side fixed to low beam
Daytime running light on one side out

U0544.t: Invalid Data Received From Parking Assist Control Module B
U0544.d: Parking assist control modules evaluate the ultrasonic sensors in the bumpers and work out distances or steering paths. Mercedes-Benz lists U0544 in its Intelligent Predictive Repair guide for its eight-gear DCT (models 118, 177, 247; document LI27.00-P-077141): the transmission controller stores U054487 when data from the PARKTRONIC unit are implausible, and failure type 87 points to a missing message. Ford's 2024 OBD summary treats the A unit through U045A, monitored non-MIL inside the PCM on vehicles with Fully Aided Park Assist, which shows that powertrain controllers also check parking data. With U0544 present, expect parking sensors or automatic parking to be switched off and a warning; normal driving is not restricted. Lost communication with module B is U0243.
c: Internal or software fault in parking assist module B
Messages from module B missing or delayed (bus fault, module reset)
Damaged bumper harness or sensors causing module B to send invalid data
s: Parking sensors or park assist switched off with warning
Automatic parking manoeuvre not available
Transmission control unit stores the code (Mercedes DCT)

U0545.t: Invalid Data Received From Running Board Control Module A
U0545.d: Power running boards deploy when a door opens and retract when it closes or the vehicle moves; a running board control module (Ford: RBM) drives the motors and reports position and faults. U0545 means its data reach other modules but are rejected. Ford shows how closely the function is tied to other electronics: on the 2027 Expedition and Navigator the boards stopped and the cluster warned of a running board fault while the driver seat module held C1008:15/C1009:15 and other modules stored U0208 and U0244, traced to DSM software (SSM 55168). Earlier F-150, Super Duty and Expedition RBMs switched from Auto to Off after low battery voltage with U3003:16 (SSM 50154) or due to software (SSM 52411). No bulletin names U0545. Boards may stay extended or retracted.
c: Software fault in the running board or hosting seat module
Low battery voltage event corrupting module data
Implausible motor position feedback from dirt, ice or corrosion at the board
s: Running boards do not deploy or retract, fault message in the cluster
Running board setting changes from Auto to Off by itself

U0546.t: Invalid Data Received From Entertainment Control Module — Front
U0546.d: The front entertainment control module is the media unit for the front row, usually the head unit or a separate media controller that also supplies rear systems. Visteon's patent describes this layout: a main unit for the front seats and an entertainment module for rear passengers, each with its own microcontroller, trade commands and status as multiplex messages, with the front unit steering sources for the rear. When frames from the front unit reach the network but fail checks for range, counter or length, a receiver such as the rear unit, the cluster or a gateway stores U0546; a silent front unit gives U0245. No manufacturer documents U0546 publicly. Rear screens may lose their source, displays may show wrong media data and audio controls may stop responding.
c: Head unit or media controller software fault
Damaged media bus wiring or connector behind the dash
s: Rear entertainment loses its source or control from the front
Wrong or frozen media information on displays

U0547.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Control Module E
U0547.d: Seat control module E belongs to the higher letters used once a car has more seat electronics than a driver and a passenger unit. Ford uses the E slot for a climate seat controller on the 2016 Lincoln MKX, where weak seat cooling was fixed by updating the as-built configuration of the SCME (SSM 46279). Climate seat patents explain what such a module handles: it reads the occupant's setting and a temperature sensor and drives the blower and the thermoelectric element, often only with the engine running. U0547 is logged when its frames arrive but carry implausible values; if they are missing, U0246 applies. No bulletin names U0547. Expect heated or ventilated seat functions to switch off or ignore the chosen level.
c: Wrong as-built configuration or software in the seat module
Seat temperature sensor or thermoelectric element giving implausible values
Loose or corroded connector under the seat
s: Seat heating or ventilation switches off or stays at one level
Seat climate setting on the screen does not match the seat

U0548.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Control Module F
U0548.d: For seat control module F no manufacturer publishes an official assignment, and U0548 appears in no bulletin. Ford's naming shows how far seat letters reach: B for the front passenger, G and H for multi-contour units, J for third-row power folding and K/L for the second-row power seats of the 2025 Navigator (SSM 54226), so F is one more seat node, possibly in a rear row. A Gentherm-family patent describes a common split in which a backrest module takes commands from the main seat module over a dedicated line, a layout in which bad data from a secondary unit is entirely possible. U0548 means unit F still answers but its content fails the checks; U0247 stands for lost contact. Heating, folding or adjustment of that seat may then be blocked.
c: Harness pinched in seat rails or folding mechanism
Module not configured to the vehicle after replacement
s: Functions of one particular seat unavailable
Seat switch or screen control for that seat does not react

U0549.t: Invalid Data Received From Remote Accessory Module
U0549.d: No manufacturer explains in public what the remote accessory module is; the term shows up only in code lists, together with its lost-communication partner U0248. Going by the name, it is a body-side unit controlling accessories away from the main controllers, and it is distinct from the accessory protocol interface module covered by U0554. GM's Saab 9-5 documentation describes the supervision behind such codes: receivers watch for expected signals, substitute defaults when a signal is not valid and set a code against the sender, and its code list splits invalid data into subtypes such as wrong message counter, checksum error or implausible value. U0549 follows that scheme for this module. What stops working depends on the vehicle; driving is not affected.
c: Retrofitted or upfitter equipment disturbing the module's data
Low battery voltage or power interruption while the module was active
s: An accessory function controlled by this module does not work
Code stored without noticeable effect

U054A.t: Invalid Data Received From Entertainment Control Module — Rear B
U054A.d: Some vehicles carry two rear entertainment units, for instance one screen per front headrest or separate units for second and third rows, which J2012 numbers Rear A and Rear B. GM's Saab 9-5 code list shows such a split: U0196 for the rear audio control module and U0249, the lost-communication partner of U054A, for a rear radio audio control module. A GM patent on reprogramming modules notes that rear-seat entertainment often sits on a fast MOST entertainment bus rather than on CAN. U054A means unit B still sends, but its status or control data are rejected; for unit A the code would be U0497. No public bulletin names U054A. Usually only the second rear screen, its headphone channel or its remote control stops working.
c: Rear entertainment unit B internally faulty
Strained wiring through seat, headrest or headliner to unit B
Software level of unit B not matching the front unit
s: Second rear screen shows no picture or wrong source
Headphones or remote of that screen do not respond

U054B.t: Invalid Data Received From Interior Lighting Control Module A
U054B.d: Interior lighting control module A runs cabin illumination such as dome, footwell and ambient light strips, in newer cars often RGB LED nodes on a LIN line below the body controller. Microchip's reference ambient lighting module shows the data involved: the master sends a command frame with zone, colour shares and intensity and asks for a status frame in return, each protected by a LIN checksum at 10.4 kbit/s. When status content from module A arrives but is implausible or corrupted, the receiver stores U054B; if the module stays silent, U024A applies, and module B has U05C0. No manufacturer documents U054B. Courtesy lights may then stay off, colour or brightness may change unexpectedly, or entry lighting may fail.
c: LED driver node or lighting module internally faulty
Chafed LIN line or loose connector in trim or headliner
Wrong vehicle configuration for the lighting variant
s: Interior or ambient lights stay off or flicker
Ambient colour or brightness differs from the setting

U054C.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Control Module G
U054C.d: Ford gives seat control module G a fixed meaning: SCMG is the driver's multi-contour seat module with massage and lumbar functions. Ford's TSB 19-2293 covers vehicles from the 2013 MKZ to the 2019 F-150 and Navigator with intermittent massage and lumbar operation, B1471 and U024B/U024C, caused by fretting terminals at the SCMG and SCMH connectors and fixed with new pigtails and a rerouted harness. On 2020–2021 F-Super Duty a misconfigured SCMG after a software update made the APIM store U024B, cured by the configuration app (SSM 53226). U054C stands for data that arrive but are rejected; Ford documents no case for it. Massage, lumbar or contour settings of the driver seat may then stop or be unavailable from the touchscreen.
c: Fretting corrosion at the multi-contour seat module connector
Seat module misconfigured after a software update
s: Driver seat massage or lumbar adjustment works only intermittently
Seat contour settings cannot be operated from the touchscreen

U054D.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Control Module H
U054D.d: Seat control module H is Ford's multi-contour module for the passenger seat (SCMH), the counterpart of SCMG. On 2022 Explorer and Aviator an intermittent passenger massage function without any stored code was traced to the configuration of both modules; first no fix was available, later reprogramming plus the configuration apps solved it (SSM 50591, 51927). The F-Super Duty case SSM 53226 shows where bad seat data is noticed: the APIM, which operates the seats from the SYNC screen, stored U024C. U054D is the code for an SCMH that still transmits but sends content failing validation, for instance after a wrong configuration or with fretting contacts at its plug. Passenger massage or lumbar adjustment then works only now and then.
c: Passenger seat module configuration not matching the vehicle
Fretting corrosion at the passenger seat module connector
Passenger multi-contour seat module internally faulty
s: Passenger seat massage starts and stops on its own
Passenger lumbar or contour adjustment does not respond

U054E.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Control Module J
U054E.d: Ford calls the module that folds the third-row seats electrically both PFSM and seat control module J (SCMJ). On 2025–2026 Expedition and Navigator its software left the seats unwilling to fold when 3L, Both or 3R was pressed, restored by a relearn in which Both is held for one minute and then five seconds more (SSM 53681), and caused misaligned upright seats after an obstruction reset (SSM 54613). Since the module halts motion on an obstruction and reports seat position, wrong data from it can confuse switch and liftgate-area logic. U054E means its frames arrive but are rejected, while U024D marks missing frames; no bulletin cites U054E itself. Expect third-row folding to stop, to move only partly or to need another relearn.
c: Power fold seat module software fault
Seat end positions lost after an obstruction event or power loss
Harness to the third-row seats damaged in the cargo area
s: Third-row seats do not fold or unfold electrically
Seats stop part-way or end up misaligned

U054F.t: Invalid Data Received From Side Obstacle Detection Control Module C
U054F.d: Some vehicles carry more than two side obstacle radars, adding units for wider coverage of lane changes and crossing traffic. Ford names them side obstacle detection control modules C and D (SODCMC, SODCMD) next to the left and right units SODL and SODR. Its bulletin SSM 51903 covers Ford and Lincoln models of 2021 to 2023 that log U2100 or U3002 in these modules after replacement, when configuration or VIN had not been written. No public manufacturer text uses U054F itself. It signals that module C is transmitting, yet the receiver refuses the content. A newly fitted module whose configuration does not match the car is the most plausible source, ahead of wiring or connector faults. Drivers see side assistance messages, while driving behaviour is unaffected. U024E is lost communication with C; D is U0550.
c: Module C not configured or VIN not written after replacement
Software level of module C outdated or incompatible
Harness or connector fault at module C
s: Side assistance or blind spot warning message
Lane change or cross traffic warnings partly unavailable

U0550.t: Invalid Data Received From Side Obstacle Detection Control Module D
U0550.d: Module D is the fourth radar of a side obstacle system, in Ford terms SODCMD alongside SODL, SODR and SODCMC. Which corner it serves depends on the vehicle and is not stated in the public Ford bulletins. U0550 has no published manufacturer description; a module receiving data from unit D sets it when that data proves invalid, for example a signal outside its range or a sequence error. Because these radars sit in bumper corners, impact damage, a bent bracket or water in the plug often come before network faults, and after a bumper repair the replacement module must be given the vehicle's configuration (Ford SSM 51903). The driver notices side assistance or cross traffic alerts disabled, not a drivability problem. U024F is total loss; module C is U054F.
c: Radar D or its bracket damaged by a bumper impact
Water ingress or corrosion at the module D connector
Replacement module D without vehicle configuration
s: Side assistance or cross traffic alert switched off
Warning message about a blocked or faulty sensor

U0551.t: Invalid Data Received From Impact Classification System Module
U0551.d: An impact classification system module helps the restraint system judge what kind of collision is under way, for example frontal, side or angled, and how severe it is, so that the right airbags and pretensioners fire at the right stage. U0551 means another module, typically the airbag or restraint controller, receives messages from this unit whose content fails its plausibility or integrity checks. No manufacturer has published a description or setting criteria for this code. Patents on bus-connected crash sensing such as US7832762 show why such traffic is protected: deployment decisions travel over the network to the protection devices. With the classification input in doubt, the airbag warning lamp comes on and the system cannot rely on that information. Treat it as a safety fault; a silent module gives U0250.
c: Internal fault in the impact classification module
Module or restraint controller not configured/programmed after replacement or crash repair
Damaged wiring or connector after collision or interior work
s: Airbag/SRS warning lamp on
Restraint system message in the instrument cluster
Passenger airbag status indicator behaving abnormally

U0552.t: Invalid Data Received From Running Board Control Module B
U0552.d: A second running board controller only makes sense where each side of the vehicle has its own electronics. A 2004 Ford patent for powered boards has one central module drive the left and right boards separately, so a design with one node per side is plausible, but no manufacturer publishes which side B would be. Ford, the best documented user of power running boards, fits a single RBM in the F-150, Super Duty and Expedition/Navigator; it drops from Auto to Off after a battery undervoltage event with U3003:16 (SSM 50154). U0552 means messages from module B arrive but fail plausibility; U0251 would mean they are missing. No manufacturer documents U0552 publicly. Typically one board stops deploying or the feature switches itself off.
c: Battery undervoltage or discharged battery disturbing the running board electronics
Running board module software fault (Ford fixes comparable faults by reprogramming)
Corroded connector or chafed wiring at the board motor under the body
Running board control module B internally faulty
s: Running board on one side no longer deploys or retracts
Running board setting changes from Auto to Off without driver input

U0553.t: Invalid Data Received From Lighting Control Module — Rear B
U0553.d: Rear lighting control module B is a second controller for the rear lamps. U0553 is set when its messages are received but their content is implausible. No manufacturer documents U0553 publicly, yet the partner code U0252 hints at what the module often is: GM's list for the Saab 9-5 calls U0252 the trailer interface control module, and Ford links U0252 and U0137 on 2021–2024 F-150, Expedition, Navigator and the 2024 Ranger to a trailer module that dropped off the CAN bus, fixed by disconnecting and reprogramming it. On 2023–2025 Super Duty trucks, a badly tightened ground G201 set U0252 among other codes. U0484 is the same fault for rear module A. Trailer or rear lamp functions may fail; no MIL.
c: Trailer or rear lighting module software hung or outdated (Ford remedy is reprogramming)
Loose or badly tightened ground connection
Corrosion or short at the trailer socket feeding back into the module
Rear lighting control module B internally faulty
s: Trailer lamps or trailer brake function reported as faulty
Individual rear lamps not working
Several warning messages after battery or ground work

U0554.t: Invalid Data Received From Accessory Protocol Interface Module
U0554.d: Accessory protocol interface module is Ford's name for the SYNC computer (APIM), which, at least in the first SYNC generation, sits apart from the audio control module and talks to the high- and medium-speed CAN buses. Because the touchscreen sends drive mode, settings and configuration through it, wrong APIM data reach far: on the 2021–2023 Mustang Mach-E, APIM software let the drive mode fall back to normal with Drive Mode Not Available, partly with U0253 in the ABS (TSB 24-2012); on the 2020 Aviator a misconfigured APIM made the display show a wrong number of radio presets (SSM 49092). U0554 stands for APIM frames that arrive but are rejected; U0253 marks missing frames and U031F a software mismatch. No bulletin cites U0554 itself. Settings made on the screen may not take effect.
c: Outdated or faulty SYNC/APIM software (often fixed by an over-the-air or dealer update)
APIM configuration not matching the vehicle equipment after replacement or update
Receiving module (e.g. ABS) evaluating APIM data with outdated software
s: Drive mode or vehicle settings chosen on the touchscreen are not applied or fall back
Wrong or incomplete information on the center display
Code stored in another module without noticeable fault

U0555.t: Invalid Data Received From Remote Start Module
U0555.d: A remote start module lets the engine run from a key fob or app for heating or cooling and must work around the immobilizer while doing so; it may be a factory part, a dealer accessory or an aftermarket box tied into the CAN network. GM lists the remote start module as its own node (Saab 9-5 2011: U0254). Subaru shows how a mismatch in the interface between gateway and its accessory Remote Engine Starter set U0254 on the 2020 Legacy/Outback without any effect on function, cured by revised modules (15-258-19R). Mercedes warns that aftermarket remote start and other CAN devices on Sprinter and Metris can cause communication faults and failed programming. U0555 means frames come in but are invalid; U0254 means none arrive. No bulletin names U0555. Remote start may fail or nothing is noticeable.
c: Aftermarket remote starter or other add-on device on the CAN bus sending non-conforming messages
Software of the remote start module not matching the vehicle gateway
Poor splices or connectors from the remote starter installation
s: Engine does not start or shuts down again when started remotely
Code found during an all-systems scan with no noticeable fault
Module programming at the workshop does not complete

U0556.t: Invalid Data Received From Front Display Interface Module
U0556.d: The front display interface module is the screen unit in the center of the dash; GM calls the matching node info display module (Saab 9-5 2011, U0255), Ford uses FDIM. The display mostly shows what other modules feed it. Ford examples: on the Escape (2016–2019) and Focus/C-Max (2016–2018) the FDIM ramps its backlight up and down in auto-dim mode, which looks like flicker but is normal (SSM 47748); on the 2020 Aviator the APIM configuration made the FDIM show the wrong number of radio presets (SSM 49092). U0556 is set by a receiver that gets FDIM frames, e.g. touch inputs or status, with implausible content; U0255 covers silence, U0558 the combined controls/display unit. No manufacturer documents U0556. Touch inputs may be ignored or the screen may act oddly.
c: Display module software fault or level not matching the infotainment unit
Wrong configuration of display or infotainment module after replacement or update
Front display module internally faulty (touch sensor or electronics)
s: Touchscreen does not respond or reacts to inputs that were not made
Wrong or incomplete content shown on the center display

U0557.t: Invalid Data Received From Front Controls Interface Module A
U0557.d: Front controls interface module A is the button panel in the center stack that reads keys and knobs for audio and climate and passes them on as bus messages; Ford calls it FCIM, GM the infotainment faceplate control module (Saab 9-5 2011, U0256). Ford shows how much depends on it: on 2015–2017 F-150 trucks heavy CAN traffic could freeze the FCIM, so A/C, radio and even window switch control failed intermittently with U0140, U0155, U0253, U0401 or U0452 in the FCIM; a battery reset and FCIM self-test came before any replacement (SSM 46902). U0557 stands for panel frames that arrive with invalid content, U0256 for absent ones, U055E for the second panel B. No bulletin cites U0557. Button presses may be ignored or trigger the wrong function.
c: Control panel electronics locking up under high bus load
Control panel software fault or mismatch with the infotainment unit
Stuck button or liquid spilled into the panel producing invalid key states
Front controls interface module A internally faulty
s: Radio or climate buttons work only intermittently or not at all
Several warning lamps or messages appear together with the button failure

U0558.t: Invalid Data Received From Front Controls/Display Interface Module
U0558.d: Simpler infotainment systems put buttons and a small screen into one unit, the front controls/display interface module. Ford calls it FCDIM, used for example with the 4-inch audio display, and the GM-built 2011 Saab 9-5 lists U0257 for its info display module/infotainment faceplate control module. Ford bulletins show its typical weak spot, the software: on the Escape from 2013 to 2016 and on 2016 Focus, Transit Connect and Transit vans, AM/FM presets could not be stored or recalled and the preset keys acted erratically until the FCDIM was reprogrammed (SSM 46891, 47234). U0558 means the combined unit sends frames that receivers reject; U0257 stands for lost contact, while U0556 and U0557 cover separate display and button modules. No bulletin cites U0558. Radio keys or the small display may misbehave.
c: Software fault in the combined controls/display unit (Ford remedy is reprogramming)
Unit programmed with a calibration for a different equipment level
Front controls/display interface module internally faulty
s: Radio presets cannot be stored or recalled, preset keys act erratically
Small audio display blank or showing wrong settings

U0559.t: Invalid Data Received From Radio Transceiver
U0559.d: Despite the name, the radio transceiver is not the audio tuner but the module that exchanges radio signals with keys and wireless accessories. Ford's name is RTM: on 2021–2022 Bronco Sport, jammed passive-key frequencies or a weak key battery could trigger No Key Detected, solved by placing the key in the console backup spot close to the RTM (SSM 50341); on recent F-150 and Super Duty trucks the RTM uses a new frequency, so only one specific accessory keypad pairs (SSM 54546). Keyless systems commonly work at 315 or 433.92 MHz. U0559 means the RTM's messages arrive but are invalid; U0258 means none arrive. No bulletin names U0559. Keyless entry, remote functions or key detection may fail.
c: Radio interference or weak key battery producing implausible receiver data
Accessory keypad or remote on a frequency the transceiver does not support
s: No Key Detected or similar key message in the cluster
Keyless entry or remote functions work poorly or not at all
Wireless keypad cannot be paired

U055A.t: Invalid Data Received From Special Purpose Vehicle Control Module A
U055A.d: Special purpose vehicle control modules are add-on controllers that body builders and upfitters fit to police cars, ambulances, utility trucks and similar conversions. U055A means frames from module A arrive but their content fails the receiver's checks. Ford lists the code in its 2024 OBD operations summary among the powertrain controller's internal plausibility tests and marks it non-MIL for programs carrying a special upfitter module. Ford's 2023 Super Duty shows how such equipment is attached: the factory upfitter integration system passes J1939 signals one way to the body equipment, while the vehicle network itself is encrypted. U0259 is the matching lost-communication code. Expect the upfitter function to misbehave; driving is normally unaffected.
c: Upfitter module programmed or configured for a different vehicle software level
Vehicle modules updated without matching the upfitter module
Poorly made bus connection or splice in the body builder's wiring
Special purpose module A internally faulty
s: Upfitter equipment (lights, outputs, interlocks) works erratically or not at all
Code stored without warning lamp

U055B.t: Invalid Data Received From Special Purpose Vehicle Control Module B
U055B.d: U055B concerns the second slot reserved for special purpose controllers. A receiving module gets frames from controller B, but a signal lies outside its permitted span, a counter or checksum is wrong, or the frame length does not match. No manufacturer documents U055B publicly. How freely these slots are filled shows in Deutz's engine controller for off-highway machines, which reports a timeout of its tractor-trailer bridge under U0259, the lost-communication code of slot A. On road vehicles slot B mainly matters when a conversion carries more than one add-on controller, for example separate units for warning lights and for body hydraulics. U025A is the lost-communication counterpart. Only the conversion equipment is normally affected.
c: Second add-on controller set up with wrong address or message set
Software of add-on controller B and vehicle modules not matched
Unstable supply or ground at controller B, e.g. on a shared accessory feed
s: One group of conversion functions fails while others still work
Fault entry in the receiving module, usually without warning lamp

U055C.t: Invalid Data Received From Special Purpose Vehicle Control Module C
U055C.d: With U055C a module rejects the content of messages sent by special purpose controller C, the third of four slots for conversion electronics. No maker publishes a code-specific description. Ford's body builder bulletin for the 2023 Super Duty points to a typical pitfall: the factory interface module, the infotainment unit and the body control module all need matching software before the upfitter tool can talk to them, and trucks built before a June 2023 cut-off require a reflash. Out-of-step software on either side therefore produces data the receiver cannot accept. Diagnosis starts with the conversion paperwork and software levels rather than with the vehicle's own modules. U025B covers total silence of controller C.
c: Software levels of conversion controller and vehicle modules out of step
Conversion equipment added or changed without updating controller C
Damaged bus wiring in the conversion harness
s: Functions controlled by the conversion do not respond as configured
Code appears after a software update or conversion work

U055D.t: Invalid Data Received From Special Purpose Vehicle Control Module D
U055D.d: U055D is the last of the four special purpose controller codes. It is stored when frames from controller D reach the network but carry values the receiver rejects. No manufacturer documents it; even Ford, which names slot A in its 2024 summary as a non-MIL check, says nothing about B to D. In practice the code is most likely on heavily converted vehicles with several add-on units, where one controller may feed implausible values after a voltage dip, a partial software update or a wiring change. Unlike U025C, the lost-communication code, the controller is still transmitting, so power and ground are usually present and the content of the data is what needs checking. Driving is not normally restricted.
c: Incomplete or interrupted software update of controller D
Voltage dip from heavy conversion loads corrupting controller D's output
s: Individual conversion functions fail intermittently
Fault entry without effect on engine or brakes

U055E.t: Invalid Data Received From Front Controls Interface Module B
U055E.d: Where the front switches are split over two panels, the second one is front controls interface module B. Ford uses exactly this name (FCIMB): on 2023 Transit vans with SYNC 3 Lite, rear-only parking aid and no front sensors, the parking aid disable switch sits in the FCIMB; for vehicles built between mid-March and early June 2023 it did nothing because the park aid module was misconfigured, fixed with the PAM configuration app (SSM 51837). That case shows that a fault visible at panel B can lie with the receiver. U055E covers B-panel frames that arrive with implausible content; U025D marks lost contact and U0557 the main panel A, which on the F-150 could freeze under heavy CAN load (SSM 46902). No bulletin cites U055E. Switches on the second panel may not work.
c: Receiving module configured for different equipment and misreading the panel B data
Software fault in the second control panel
Loose connector or damaged wiring behind the second panel
s: Switches on the second front panel have no effect
Indicator lamps in the switches do not match the actual function state

U055F.t: Invalid Data Received From Electronic Brake Booster Control Module A
U055F.d: An electronic brake booster replaces the vacuum servo: a travel sensor reads the pedal and an electric motor supplies the assist, as in Bosch's iBooster, which also lets the brake system blend in regenerative braking and back up the stability control unit. U055F is set when booster A transmits but its data, such as pedal travel, assist status or pressure request, fail the receiver's checks. No manufacturer documents U055F publicly. Ford fits such a booster (EBB) to the 2020-2021 Escape, Bronco Sport, Explorer, Corsair and Aviator; an interrupted supply to the EBB there left a network code in the ABS module and lit the ABS and stability lamps. Lost communication is U025E. Expect warning lamps and possibly reduced assist.
c: Booster control unit or its pedal travel sensor faulty
Supply interrupted or weak battery during start or service work
Booster and ABS/ESC software not matched
Bus wiring or connector at the booster damaged
s: ABS, brake or stability warning lamps on
Harder pedal or changed pedal feel
Regenerative braking or driver assistance functions limited

U0560.t: Invalid Data Received From Electronic Brake Booster Control Module B
U0560.d: A second brake booster unit mainly appears in architectures built for automated driving, where a single electronic brake must not be a single point of failure. Bosch, for example, pairs its integrated power brake with a separate redundant brake unit that can stop the car if the primary unit fails. U0560 reports that the module labelled B sends data the receiver cannot use, for instance a status that contradicts the A unit or a frame with a wrong counter or checksum. No manufacturer documents U0560 publicly, and which physical unit carries the B label depends on the maker. U025F is the lost-communication counterpart. Losing redundancy usually triggers a warning and can disable assisted or automated driving functions.
c: Secondary brake unit B internally faulty
Software of the two brake units not matched after update or replacement
Separate supply or ground of unit B faulty
s: Brake system warning lamp or message on
Driver assistance or automated functions unavailable

U0561.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Control Switch Module A
U0561.d: Modern power seat switches are often small control units of their own: they read the keys and send the result to the seat module over LIN instead of switching motor current directly. A Lear patent describes a seat electronics unit with a LIN driver that acts on commands from such an external switch. Mercedes documents a case for 2026 models: the seat adjustment switch group in the door (front left, SSE-VL) could stay in sleep mode, so the seat no longer moved; unplugging the switch resets it and new switch software prevents a repeat. Lincoln traced missing lumbar settings on the 2022 Aviator partly to the seat switch part level (SSM 51056). U0561 is set when frames from switch module A are implausible; U0260 is the lost-contact code. No bulletin names U0561.
c: Seat switch module software fault (e.g. switch stays in sleep mode)
Switch part or software level not matching the seat module
Loose or corroded connector at the seat or door switch
Seat control switch module A internally faulty
s: Seat cannot be adjusted with the switch
Seat settings such as lumbar not shown or not selectable on the screen

U0562.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Control Switch Module B
U0562.d: Switch module B is a second, separate seat switch unit, for the passenger side or another seat row; which position B denotes is not published by any manufacturer. Mercedes counts its seat switch groups by position, front left being SSE-VL, which points to one unit per seat. Lincoln shows the 2nd-row case: on 2025 Navigators with power second-row seats the switch would not move the seat fore and aft, with B167F:11 in the rear seat modules SCMK/SCML; running their configuration apps cured it (SSM 54226). So a switch fault may really be a seat module setup issue. U0562 means module B frames reach the bus but fail checks; U0261 means they stop, U0561 concerns switch A. No bulletin names U0562. The affected seat may not respond to its switch.
c: Receiving seat module not configured for the installed switch and seat equipment
Software fault in the second seat switch module
Connector or harness under a movable seat damaged by seat travel or objects
s: Passenger or rear seat does not move when its switch is pressed
Seat moves only in some directions

U0563.t: Invalid Data Received From Audio Amplifier B
U0563.d: Premium sound systems often use an external amplifier away from the head unit, and large installations can need a second one, audio amplifier B. Such amplifiers are network nodes: the head unit sends volume and other commands over CAN instead of an analog level, and the amplifier reports its status back, as a patent on modular vehicle amplifiers explains. Jeep shows the reverse direction on the 2023 Grand Cherokee and Wagoneer: the amplifier module logged U0485 for implausible data from the Uconnect 5 radio, cleared by radio software T25L (08-046-23). U0563 is the same kind of fault with amplifier B as sender; U0262 means it went silent and U0487 concerns amplifier A. No manufacturer documents U0563. Some speakers may drop out or volume may jump.
c: Amplifier B software not matching the head unit software level
Aftermarket amplifier or audio interface on the vehicle bus sending non-conforming data
Audio amplifier B internally faulty or overheated
s: Some speakers or the subwoofer silent while others play
Volume or sound settings react incorrectly

U0564.t: Invalid Data Received From Speech Recognition Module
U0564.d: In-car voice control lets the driver place calls, pick stations or play music by spoken command, in newer systems even in natural sentences. Some makers house it in a module of its own: FCA put Uconnect voice recognition into a hands-free module (HFM) on 2012–2017 Journey, Charger and 300; with old software it could hang while loading, ignore the steering-wheel voice key or pick up background noise, and a reflash fixed it (08-055-17 REV. A, where a silent HFM sets U0197). Ford runs voice commands on the SYNC computer (APIM). U0564 is set when a dedicated speech recognition module sends data that fail checks; U0263 covers lost contact. No manufacturer documents U0564 publicly. Voice commands may be ignored, misread or cause wrong actions.
c: Speech recognition software outdated or faulty (fixed by reflashing)
Unsupported language selection or mismatch between module and head unit settings
s: Voice control does not respond to the steering-wheel button
Voice commands misrecognized or system stuck while loading

U0565.t: Invalid Data Received From Camera Module — Rear
U0565.d: The rear camera module delivers the reversing picture and, on some vehicles, data that other controllers reuse. U0565 is logged by a receiver that gets its frames but judges the content implausible. Ford documents a clear case: on the Mustang Mach-E and F-150 from model year 2021, the Lightning, Expedition and Navigator from 2022 and the Corsair from 2023 (each up to 2024), image processing module A stores U0565:86 while the rear camera holds U2018:51, and BlueCruise plus lane centering go dead; reprogramming the rear camera cures it (TSB 24-2251, 25-2512). A 2024 Jeep Gladiator with only the basic reversing camera may set U0565-00 in the radio without any visible fault, and a new camera does not stop it. U0264 is the lost-communication partner. No MIL.
c: Rear camera module software level not matching the receiving module (Ford remedy is reprogramming)
Receiver flags the camera data too strictly although the picture is fine (Jeep Gladiator 2024 radio)
Water or corrosion in the camera plug or tailgate harness
s: Hands-free driving or lane centering unavailable (Ford BlueCruise vehicles)
Reversing picture missing, frozen or without guide lines
Code stored in radio or driver-assist module without noticeable fault

U0566.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor A
U0566.d: At GM, image processing sensor A is the front camera behind the windshield; its partner U0265 is called Front View Camera – Windshield in GM bulletins. GM's 2025 OBD tables show how U0566 is detected: the brake module and the EOCM3 driver-assist controller check rolling counters, checksums and message authentication on the camera's frames. EOCM3 sets it when 3 of 4 messages fail within about 3 seconds, the brake module after 3 counter errors in a window of 16, both only at 9–16 V and as Type C without MIL; adaptive cruise is switched off. On 2020 Cadillac CT4 and CT5 a resetting camera set U0566 with U0265 and P25A2, cut driver and steering assist, and P25A2 could light the MIL. Reprogramming the camera came first.
c: Windshield camera software resets or sends faulty protection values (GM remedy is reprogramming)
Front camera internally faulty when the fault recurs often (GM then replaces it)
Supply voltage dips or bus disturbances during start
s: Service Driver Assist or Steering Assist Reduced message
Adaptive cruise and automatic braking functions unavailable
MIL possible only through accompanying brake-module code P25A2

U0567.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor B
U0567.d: Image processing sensors are cameras that interpret their own picture and send results, not raw video, onto the bus. U0567 is set when frames from sensor B arrive but fail the receiver's checks, for instance a wrong CRC or a counter that jumps or repeats. No public manufacturer text names U0567 itself, but its lost-communication partner U0266 appears in a Stellantis case: on a 2022 Ram 1500 it stood for the left camera of the surround view, so there sensor B is the driver-side mirror camera; other brands may assign B differently. Some cars also carry an infrared night-vision camera that sees warm objects beyond headlamp range. Typically only the function fed by sensor B is disabled with a message, while the car drives normally. A MIL is not expected.
c: Sensor B software not matching the receiver after an update or replacement
Loose connector or damaged wiring causing corrupted frames
Image processing sensor B internally faulty
s: Assistance or night-view function served by sensor B switched off
Camera-related service message in the instrument cluster

U0568.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor C
U0568.d: U0568 means a receiver gets messages from image processing sensor C whose content it cannot trust. SAE only numbers these sensors; no manufacturer publishes which physical camera is C, and the partner U0267 appears in no public bulletin either. Typical consumers of a camera's object list are lane departure warning, traffic sign recognition and glare-free high beam. For the latter, the US lighting standard FMVSS 108 demands that the system detect malfunctions, including a blocked sensor, then revert to manual beam switching and warn the driver, so a lamp system fed with unusable camera data has to fall back to plain low and high beam. Expect such features to be greyed out; driving and emissions are unaffected.
c: Software mismatch between sensor C and the receiving controller
Intermittent contact in the sensor connector or bus wiring
Image processing sensor C internally faulty
s: Lane departure warning or traffic sign display unavailable
Automatic high beam falls back to manual switching with a warning

U0569.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor D
U0569.d: Sensor D's frames reach the receiver, but their content fails its plausibility or protection checks. Which camera carries letter D is not published, and U0569 itself appears in no bulletin. GM ties the partner code U0268 to its active-safety network: on 2015–2020 Cadillac Escalade models, a front fascia harness chafed at the right end of the bumper bar could blow fuses and set U0268 together with U0265, U0269 and U026A–U026C, with surround-vision, park-assist and adaptive-cruise messages; the harness had to be repaired and rerouted. Near-range cameras for surround systems use very wide lenses of about 137 to 192 degrees and sit exposed in the body. If front lamps fail at the same time, check the fascia wiring first. No MIL.
c: Front fascia or bumper harness chafed through (GM Escalade 2015–2020 pattern)
Blown fuse leaving the sensor with unstable supply
Image processing sensor D internally faulty or damaged in a collision
s: Surround-view, park-assist or adaptive-cruise service messages
Front park, turn, daytime or cornering lamps out at the same time
Several camera and radar codes stored together

U056A.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor E
U056A.d: U056A is the invalid-data code for image processing sensor E: the module still talks, but the receiver rejects what it says. No brand documents U056A itself. GM lists the partner U0269 among codes held by the active safety controller of many 2013–2018 models with driver-assist packages, among them Escalade, ATS, CT6, Malibu, Volt and Acadia. These sensors share a separate object detection bus, wired to pins 3 and 11 of the diagnostic connector. GM warned that a worn scan-tool interface or cable on exactly those pins produces false U-codes and blocks contact with the radars and front camera; a loopback adapter or a known-good vehicle proves the tool. Rule out the tester before chasing sensor E. No MIL.
c: Faulty diagnostic interface or cable on the object detection bus pins (false codes)
Fault on the dedicated object detection bus wiring
Sensor E software fault or internal defect
s: Object detection or Service Active Safety message
Scan tool cannot reach radars and front camera
Code returns only when one particular tester is connected

U056B.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor F
U056B.d: At GM, the partner of U056B – U026A – belongs to the front camera module B174W. A 2023 GM note for 2022–2023 Cadillac XT5 and XT6, Chevrolet Equinox and GMC Acadia and Terrain blames U026A plus the front-camera warning on terminals in that camera that were pushed back or absent, which then has to be replaced. On 2016 Escalade, Malibu, Silverado, Suburban, Tahoe, Sierra and Yukon, U026A could appear in the cluster or body module because of camera software, and GM advised against replacing parts. Sensor F is thus a forward camera on these GM platforms, whereas the 2020 CT4 and CT5 file their windshield camera under letter A. U056B itself is in no public bulletin; lane and collision functions are likely off while it is set. No MIL.
c: Pushed-in or missing terminals in the front camera connector (GM 2022–2023)
Front camera software fault, fixed by reprogramming
s: Service Front Camera message
Lane keeping, lane departure or forward collision alert unavailable

U056C.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor G
U056C.d: Image processing sensor G is sending frames that the receiving module refuses. Neither U056C nor a camera position for G is documented by a manufacturer. Its partner U026B, however, is on GM's list for 2015–2020 Escalades whose front fascia harness rubbed through at the right bumper bar: blown fuses F10DL, F19DR, F43UA or F46DR, dead front park, turn, daytime and cornering lamps, and messages for surround vision, park assist and adaptive cruise. Surround-view systems, pioneered by Infiniti with the EX35 of model year 2008 and sold by Chevrolet as Surround Vision, combine cameras at the front, rear and sides into a top-down picture. A sensor delivering bad data leaves a gap in that view or disables it. No MIL.
c: Bumper or fascia harness rubbed through, shorting circuits and fuses
Camera connector disturbed or misassembled after body repair
Image processing sensor G internally faulty
s: Surround view shows a black segment or is unavailable
Blown fuses and front lamps out at the same time

U056D.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor H
U056D.d: U056D is reported when sensor H's messages carry data that fail checks such as a CRC, an alive counter or an authentication value. AUTOSAR's end-to-end protection names the fault types behind this: repeated, lost, delayed, corrupted or masqueraded frames. GM uses the partner U026C on its object detection bus and lists it next to U0075, a bus-off code for a whole network. That split helps diagnosis: if the bus fails, a bus-off code and several lost-communication codes appear together; a lone U056D points to sensor H, its software or its own connector. Which camera is H is not public, and no brand documents U056D. Assistance that relies on it shuts off; no MIL.
c: Sensor H software computing counters or checksums incorrectly
Poor contact at sensor H connector while the rest of the bus is fine
Image processing sensor H internally faulty
s: Single assistance function unavailable while others work
U056D stored without bus-off or other lost-communication codes

U056E.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor I
U056E.d: The higher letters of the image-sensor series cover the further cameras that newer vehicles add. One growing group looks into the cabin: driver monitoring cameras check whether the driver is watching the road, as Super Cruise does at Cadillac, starting with the 2017 CT6, or Ford's BlueCruise, which uses a module on the steering column of the 2021 Mustang Mach-E and F-150; in the EU such warning systems fall under regulation 2019/2144. Ford's driver monitoring camera module on the 2021–2023 Mustang Mach-E and F-150, the 2022–2023 Expedition and Navigator and the 2023 Corsair reports its own faults as B-codes (B115E, B15E1, B15E2), mostly a blocked view, and Ford's 2024 OBD description treats invalid data from an image processing module as a non-MIL fault (U053B). Whether any maker files such a camera under letter I is not documented, and neither U056E nor its partner U026D appears in public service material. If the receiver keeps rejecting sensor I's data, the dependent assistant becomes unavailable. No MIL.
c: Sensor I software level not matching the receiving controller
Connector disturbed behind trim, dash or steering column panels
Image processing sensor I internally faulty
s: Hands-free or attention-dependent assistance not offered
Driver attention warning inactive or showing a fault

U056F.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor J
U056F.d: U056F concerns image processing sensor J, whose messages arrive but are not plausible. No manufacturer publishes this code, its partner U026E, or which camera carries the letter J. Cameras increasingly replace glass: Lexus put cameras in place of door mirrors on the ES sold in Japan from October 2018, later joined by Hyundai's Ioniq 5 and Audi's Q8 e-tron. In the US, FMVSS 111 governs rear visibility and requires the reversing image within 2.0 seconds after backing starts, which shows how tightly such picture paths are timed. Where a camera feeds a display of this kind, invalid data mean a blank or frozen view rather than a drivability problem. There is no MIL, and nothing changes for emissions.
c: Software mismatch after an update of camera or display unit
Damaged wiring or connector at an exposed camera position (mirror housing, door)
Image processing sensor J internally faulty
s: Camera view black, frozen or replaced by a warning
Camera-related message in the instrument cluster

U0570.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor K
U0570.d: Sensor K's frames reach the bus but are discarded as invalid. U0570 and its partner U026F are not documented by any vehicle maker, so the camera behind letter K is unknown. One use for additional image sensors is towing: a Magna patent describes satellite cameras fitted to the trailer whose images are merged with the picture of the car's own reversing camera into a see-through trailer view while driving forward, with a switch to the backup image in reverse. Such cameras connect through extra plugs and cables at the hitch, which brings contact and software-matching risks of their own. A fault of this kind would remove that view only; the towing vehicle drives normally and no MIL is set.
c: Corroded or loose plug where an add-on or trailer camera connects
Additional camera not configured or software not matching the vehicle
Image processing sensor K internally faulty
s: Extra camera view (for example trailer view) missing or black
Code appears mainly with a trailer or accessory connected

U0571.t: Invalid Data Received From Image Processing Sensor L
U0571.d: U0571 closes the image-processing-sensor block; the next number, U0572, already belongs to a vehicle motion control module. An image processing sensor computes objects inside the camera itself, for instance with a system-on-chip as in Bosch's multi purpose camera or with Mobileye's EyeQ processors, the first generation of which launched in 2008. That differs from an image processing module (U053B–U053D), a separate controller that evaluates camera streams. U0571 means sensor L's results arrived but failed the receiver's checks. No manufacturer documents U0571 or partner U0270, and the position of L is unknown. Expect the dependent assistant to switch off; no MIL.
c: Processing software in sensor L faulty or not matching the receiver
Wiring or connector fault corrupting the sensor's messages
Image processing sensor L internally faulty
s: Assistance function using sensor L unavailable
Code stored without warning lamp

U0572.t: Invalid Data Received From Vehicle Motion Control Module A
U0572.d: A vehicle motion control module sits above the individual chassis controllers and coordinates steering, brakes, damping and drive torque. ZF's cubiX software works this way and went into production in the Lotus Eletre; Hitachi Astemo describes a central controller that sends time-referenced instructions to several actuator modules. U0572 means that one of these actuator controllers or the gateway receives such instructions or status data from module A but finds them invalid, for example out of range or with a broken counter or checksum. No manufacturer documents U0572 publicly, and there is no generic lost-communication code for this module. The receiving controllers then ignore the commands and fall back to their own functions.
c: Software of motion control module and chassis controllers not matched
Motion control module A internally faulty
Implausible sensor input to the module (yaw, steering angle) leading to invalid outputs
s: Chassis or stability warning message
Rear-axle steering, active roll control or drive modes switched off
Car drives with basic stability control only

U0573.t: Invalid Data Received From Vehicle Motion Control Module B
U0573.d: U0573 is the B variant: invalid data from a second vehicle motion control module. A second unit makes sense where coordination tasks are split, for example lateral and longitudinal motion, or where a backup must take over for automated driving. Hitachi Astemo's patent explains why timing matters in such systems: actuator modules receive their instructions over a shared network that also carries other traffic, so each instruction refers to a common time frame. Data from B that arrive outside that frame, with stale counters or with values contradicting module A are rejected and stored as U0573. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, and no lost-communication code exists for this module. Coordinated functions are then reduced.
c: Lost time synchronisation between module B and the actuator controllers
Modules A and B on different software levels
Motion control module B internally faulty
s: Warning about reduced chassis or assistance functions
Automated or semi-automated driving functions unavailable

U0574.t: Invalid Data Received From Lighting Driver Control Module A
U0574.d: Lighting driver control modules switch and dim individual LEDs or LED segments in modern headlamps. Lincoln's 2025 Navigator has four of them, labelled A to D, and an over-the-air release (25.10.08) for all four adjusted headlamp colour and brightness at start-up; NHTSA's summary adds an intermittent resistance fault that dropped the lamps to their lowest setting. U0574 is set when a receiver gets module A's frames but rejects the data. No maker publishes U0574 itself or partner U0273. LED matrix drivers such as TI's TPS92662 report open or shorted LEDs over a serial line, so a corrupt status message can stop adaptive light although the lamp still works. U0542 concerns headlamp control module A. No MIL.
c: Lighting driver module software needing an update (Lincoln remedy over the air)
Moisture or poor contact at the headlamp connector
Lighting driver control module A internally faulty (often only with the headlamp)
s: Adaptive or glare-free high beam unavailable
Headlamp colour or brightness wrong, lamps at reduced level

U0575.t: Invalid Data Received From Lighting Driver Control Module B
U0575.d: U0575 flags implausible data from lighting driver control module B. Matrix headlamps split the high beam into many LEDs that a control unit switches individually; Audi introduced the first such glare-free system on the 2013 A8 with 25 segments per lamp. With several driver modules on board, the controller in charge expects regular and consistent status from each of them. Lincoln's 2025 Navigator names four headlamp driver modules, lettered A to D, and updated them over the air in October 2025; where each letter sits is not stated. Neither U0575 nor partner U0274 is documented by a manufacturer. Glare-free high beam or light animations may be withdrawn, while basic low and high beam should remain. No MIL.
c: Software of driver module B outdated or inconsistent with the other modules
Defective LED segment producing fault reports the receiver cannot match
Lighting driver control module B internally faulty
s: Glare-free high beam switched off with a lighting message
Individual LED segments dark or flickering

U0576.t: Invalid Data Received From Lighting Driver Control Module C
U0576.d: Lighting driver control module C is sending data that the receiver discards. The US standard FMVSS 108 explains why this matters for an adaptive driving beam: the system must recognise malfunctions, including a blocked sensor, switch to manual beam control until the fault is gone and show the driver a warning.
