Driver chips like TI's TPS92664 keep failsafe default settings in internal memory, so a lamp still lights without fresh commands. Lincoln fits its 2025 Navigator headlamps with four such driver modules, lettered A to D. U0576 and partner U0275 appear in no public service text, and which lamp C serves is unknown. Expect a lighting warning and manual beam switching; no MIL.
c: Driver module C software fault, curable by an update
Unstable supply or ground at the headlamp
Lighting driver control module C internally faulty
s: Lighting system warning in the instrument cluster
Automatic high beam replaced by manual switching

U0577.t: Invalid Data Received From Lighting Driver Control Module D
U0577.d: U0577 is the code for invalid messages from lighting driver control module D, the last of the four-letter block; U0276 is its lost-communication partner. LED matrix drivers can be chained: TI's TPS92662 addresses up to 31 devices over one multi-drop UART line, can use CAN transceivers for a sturdier physical layer, and also drives sequential turn signals and animated daytime lights. Lincoln documents four driver modules, A to D, for the headlamps of the 2025 Navigator without saying where each one sits. No manufacturer publishes U0577. Corrupt status from module D may disable dynamic functions it handles, while the lamp can keep burning in its default mode. No MIL.
c: Driver module D software not at the level of the other lighting modules
Fault on the serial link between lighting controller and driver chips
Lighting driver control module D internally faulty
s: Sequential indicator or animated daytime light not working
Lamp lit only in a basic setting

U0578.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Module K
U0578.d: Ford assigns letter K to a defined seat: on the 2025 Lincoln Navigator, seat control module K (SCMK) is the rear left power seat module of the second row. Its software update SCMK-25.5.5.3 removed a short delay in seat operation and made the memory function of that seat store positions reliably. SSM 54226 adds a configuration case: second-row seats that would not slide fore and aft with B167F:11 in SCMK and/or SCML until both configuration apps were run. U0578 is set when SCMK frames arrive but contain implausible values such as seat position or switch status; U0277 is the lost-contact partner and U0579 the right-hand seat. No bulletin cites U0578. Expect a second-row seat that moves late, forgets memory positions or does not move at all.
c: Seat module K software fault (Ford remedy is a software update)
Seat module K not configured for the installed second-row seat equipment
Connector under the second-row seat loose or damaged
s: Left second-row power seat responds late or does not move fore and aft
Memory positions of that seat not saved

U0579.t: Invalid Data Received From Seat Module L
U0579.d: Seat control module L (SCML) is Ford's right-hand counterpart to SCMK: on the 2025 Lincoln Navigator it runs the passenger-side power seat of the second row. Ford pushed SCML-25.5.5.3 over the air so that this seat keeps its memory settings consistently; the release note page itself is headed with the PCM by mistake but names seat control module L in the text. In SSM 54226, B167F:11 could sit in SCML when the second-row switch failed to move the seat, and the SCML configuration app was the fix. U0579 means frames from SCML reach other modules with implausible content; U0278 stands for missing frames, U0578 for the left seat module. No bulletin cites U0579. The right second-row seat may stop moving or lose its stored positions.
c: Seat module L software fault (fixed by an over-the-air update)
Seat module L configuration missing or wrong for the seat equipment
s: Right second-row power seat does not move with its switch
Stored seat positions on the passenger side lost

U057B.t: Invalid Data Received From Battery Charger Control Module C
U057B.d: Charger C is the third on-board charger slot. Some vehicles split AC charging over several units: the extended-range Ford F-150 Lightning, for example, offers 19.2 kW through a dual on-board charger. A Porsche patent describes such a group, in which only one charger is wired to the inlet and acts as master while the others are linked to it only by a communication line. U057B means data from charger C reach the network but fail the checks, so the master or charging controller cannot share the load with it. No manufacturer documents U057B or names a third charger publicly. U027A is total loss of contact. The usual result is reduced AC charging power; driving is unaffected.
c: Charger C on a different software level than master or charging controller
Communication line between the chargers damaged
s: AC charging slower than expected
Charging fault message in the display or app

U057C.t: Invalid Data Received From Battery Charger Control Module D
U057C.d: U057C covers the fourth charger slot. Large chargers are often built from parallel power modules: Hyundai's patent for a vehicle-mounted charger gives each module its own slave controller that reports to a master, which can drop to a single module once the battery reaches the constant-voltage phase. If the reports from unit D are implausible, the master cannot decide how to share current and stores U057C; a missing unit gives U027B instead. No manufacturer documents U057C or a fourth charger publicly. For plug-in hybrids CARB requires the OBD system to detect charger faults that block charging or limit the rate, but whether a lamp comes on is up to the maker. Expect reduced or interrupted AC charging.
c: Power module or slave controller D faulty
Charger software not matched across units
Overheating of unit D due to coolant or fan problems, corrupting its status data
s: Charging power lower than usual or charging stops
Charging system warning

U057D.t: Invalid Data Received From Off-Board Charger Control Module
U057D.d: Despite its name, the off-board charger control module sits inside the vehicle: it conducts the dialogue with an external DC fast charger, which under CCS runs as power line communication on the control pilot contact (ISO 15118, DIN 70121) and under CHAdeMO over a CAN link in the connector. Ford calls this unit the off-board charger controller (OBCC) on the Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit; SSM 50923 had new OBCC software fix interrupted DC fast charging at some EVgo stations. U057D is stored when another module in the car receives frames from this controller but rejects them, for instance because of a wrong counter, a failed checksum or implausible values. No manufacturer documents U057D itself. DC fast charging is likely to stop or refuse to start, while AC charging normally still works.
c: Fault or outdated software in the charging station
Dirty or damaged communication contacts in plug or inlet
Vehicle charging controller software not compatible with the station
s: DC fast charging aborts or does not start
Charging works at other stations

U0580.t: Invalid Data Received From Haptic Control Module
U0580.d: A haptic control module produces vibrations the driver feels, in the steering wheel, seat or a touch surface, mainly as a warning. Hyundai and Genesis use a separate haptic steering controller: on the 2015–2016 Genesis and 2017–2018 G80, B247100 for a vibration motor fault brought on the warning lamp and the controller was replaced (19-BE-001, 19-BE-001-G). On the 2021 Sorento, Kia traces B247300 to a poor contact in the wiring to the vibration motor, drawn in the audio or navigation schematics (PS687). GM vibrates the seat in stage 2 of Lane Keep Assist, i.e. after crossing the line by about 40 cm (PIC6048H). The lost-communication partner is U0279, not U027F. U0580 means its data arrive implausible; no maker documents it. Warnings may then come only as chimes or not at all.
c: Poor contact in the vibration motor circuit making the module report implausible status
Haptic controller internally faulty or on an old software level
Alert type setting (chime or vibration) not matching between modules
s: Steering wheel or seat no longer vibrates during lane or other warnings
Haptic system warning lamp or message in the cluster

U0585.t: Invalid Data Received From Active Grille Air Shutter Module A
U0585.d: Active grille shutters close the front opening to cut drag and speed warm-up; CARB counts them as an off-cycle CO2 technology. The shutter actuator is usually a LIN slave of the engine controller. GM's 2025 ECM tables check the rolling counter, protection value and checksum of shutter module A's status frame and set U0585 after 3 bad frames in 10, with battery voltage of 11 V or more for 5 s; it is Type B, so the MIL lights after two trips, and the shutter performance test P059F waits while it is present. On the 2024 Traverse and Acadia, GM's PIT6133 traces U0585 on the upper shutter to firmware and replaces the shutter. Ford's 2014 list carries U0585 without MIL. U0284 is the lost-communication code.
c: Shutter actuator A with faulty firmware or internal fault (GM PIT6133)
LIN wiring or connector at the front end damaged or wet
Replacement actuator of the wrong variant
s: Check engine light on
Shutters stay in a fixed position
Slightly higher fuel consumption

U0586.t: Invalid Data Received From Active Grille Air Shutter Module B
U0586.d: Vehicles with two shutter assemblies, typically one in the upper grille and one in the lower bumper opening, report the second one as module B. U0586 means the engine controller gets status frames from that actuator but cannot trust them. GM documents it in its 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG04B) with the same counter, protection value and checksum test as for module A: 3 failures in 10 frames, at least 11 V for 5 s, Type B with MIL after two trips; the B shutter performance check P05AE pauses meanwhile. GM's PIT6133 for the 2024 Traverse and Acadia links U0586 to the lower shutter and false sets from early firmware. Ford's 2014 code list also contains U0586, without MIL. U0285 is total loss of contact.
c: Lower shutter actuator B with faulty firmware or internal fault
Wiring or connector in the lower bumper area damaged by road debris or water
Upper and lower actuator swapped or wrong part fitted
s: Check engine light on
Lower shutter does not move

U0587.t: Invalid Data Received From Radiator Anti-Tamper Device
U0587.d: Some low-emission vehicles have a radiator coated with a catalyst that converts ground-level ozone, known as direct ozone reduction (DOR) or by BASF's trade name PremAir; it earns an emissions credit, and CARB then requires the OBD system to monitor it. A Ford patent filed by Swedish inventors describes the matching sensor: it is pressed into the radiator fins, reports radiator temperature, since the coating works above roughly 60 °C, and sends an encrypted message so the engine controller knows the original part is fitted; a frangible pin stops it being moved to another radiator. U0587 means that message arrives but fails verification or plausibility. No manufacturer documents U0587 publicly. U0286 is the lost-communication code.
c: Radiator replaced with an uncoated part or sensor moved from another radiator
Corroded connector or wiring at the radiator
s: Check engine light on
No noticeable change in driving or cooling

U0588.t: Invalid Data Received From Transmission Fluid Pump Module A
U0588.d: An electric transmission fluid pump keeps clutch and line pressure up while the engine is stopped by start-stop or in electric hybrid driving. Many such pumps have their own electronics and report speed, current and faults to the transmission or hybrid controller. U0588 means those reports arrive but cannot be trusted. Ford's 2014 OBD code list includes U0588 as a continuously monitored code without MIL. The lost-communication partner U0287 is better documented: Jeep sets it with MIL and limp mode on Wrangler and Grand Cherokee 4xe and replaces the in-pan pump, Hyundai on the Santa Fe and Tucson 2.5 with 8-speed automatic, where Idle Stop and Go stops working. Invalid data usually leads to the same reactions.
c: Electric pump or its integrated controller faulty
Pump connector not fully latched or wet
Pump and transmission controller software not matched
s: Start-stop function disabled
Service transmission or hybrid system message
Limp mode with limited gears on some hybrids

U0589.t: Invalid Data Received From DC/AC Converter Control Module A
U0589.d: A DC/AC converter turns the vehicle's DC supply into household-style AC for power outlets in the cabin or truck bed. Ford calls the 7.2 kW Pro Power Onboard unit of the 2021 F-150 PowerBoost direct current/alternating converter module A (DCACA) and fixed a service message there by reprogramming the PCM and the DCACA. GM's PIT6527 for the 2026 Colorado and Canyon shows that the body control module watches the converter of the 120 V outlet at the rear of the centre console; there U0288, lost communication, was set falsely on trucks without that outlet. U0589 is the case where the converter does talk but its data, for example output status, load or temperature, are rejected as implausible. A maker's text for U0589 itself is not available. Outlets may switch off.
c: Converter or receiving module software out of date (Ford DCACA reprogramming)
Body control module configured for an outlet option the vehicle does or does not have
s: Power outlets dead or switching off under load
Message that the onboard power system needs service

U058A.t: Invalid Data Received From DC/AC Converter Control Module B
U058A.d: U058A refers to a second DC/AC converter. Two converters can make sense when outlets in the cab and in the cargo bed are fed separately or when a high-power unit is added to a small one. GM's 2023 Silverado and Sierra 1500 illustrate how optional such hardware is: because of the chip shortage, trucks built from September 2022 left the factory with the inverter for the 120 V instrument panel and bed outlets inactive and later received an accessory power control module plus a body control module reprogram. Mismatched configuration after such a retrofit is a plausible source of invalid data. No manufacturer documents U058A or names a converter B publicly. U0289 is the lost-communication code. Only the outlets are affected.
c: Configuration not updated after fitting or retrofitting converter B
Converter B internally faulty or overheated
Bus wiring to converter B damaged
s: One group of outlets dead while others work
Outlet warning or service message

U058B.t: Invalid Data Received From Transmission Fluid Pump Module B
U058B.d: Some transmissions carry a second electrically driven oil pump with its own electronics, labelled module B, alongside or instead of a first one. Its job is to hold clutch pressure and lubrication while the combustion engine is off, so the receiving transmission or hybrid controller depends on the speed, current and fault status the pump reports. U058B is logged when those reports arrive but fail plausibility, counter or checksum checks. No manufacturer documents U058B or a pump B publicly. For pump A, Jeep replaces the in-pan electric pump on Wrangler and Grand Cherokee 4xe when lost communication U0287 appears with the MIL and limp mode. Expect start-stop or electric driving to be inhibited until the fault clears; U028A is the lost-communication partner.
c: Integrated electronics of electric pump B faulty
Pump B connector or pass-through in the transmission case wet or loose
Pump firmware and transmission controller software not compatible
s: Start-stop or electric drive mode unavailable
Transmission warning message
Delayed engagement after an engine restart

U058C.t: Invalid Data Received From Active Grille Air Shutter Module C
U058C.d: A third grille shutter unit appears on vehicles that split the lower intake into several flaps. Hyundai is the clearest case: on the 2026 Palisade and Palisade Hybrid, the lower active air flaps use left and right actuators, and campaign 26-01-026H lists U028B, lost communication with shutter module C, among codes that light the engine lamp after water entered bumper connectors and corroded them. U058C covers the less drastic case where module C still sends status frames but the engine controller rejects their content. No maker publishes thresholds for U058C itself; GM's 2025 tables check counter, protection value and checksum on modules A and B (3 bad frames out of 10, Type B), a plausible pattern for C as well. With a stuck flap, warm-up and drag suffer slightly.
c: Water ingress and corrosion at the lower bumper connectors (Hyundai 26-01-026H)
Shutter actuator C with internal electronics fault
Actuator of wrong variant or position fitted after a bumper repair
s: Check engine light on
Active air flap warning message
Lower flaps stay in one position

U058D.t: Invalid Data Received From Active Grille Air Shutter Module D
U058D.d: Module D is the fourth shutter position the code list reserves; it only matters on front ends with four separately driven flap sets, for instance two upper and two lower ones. No manufacturer documents U058D or names a shutter D in public material, so its exact placement remains maker-specific. The code means that frames from that actuator reach the engine controller but are judged unusable, for example because the alive counter stalls or the checksum is wrong; GM's shutter B check in the 2025 tables (25OBDG04B) shows the usual form of such a test, with MIL after two trips. CARB lists grill shutters among active off-cycle technologies whose activity must be tracked. In practice the affected flaps freeze, which barely changes driving. U028C covers total loss of the module.
c: Shutter D wiring or LIN connector damaged by road debris or moisture
Engine controller configured for a shutter layout that does not match the vehicle
s: Check engine light on some vehicles
One flap set does not move

U0592.t: Invalid Data Received From Gear Shift Control Module B
U0592.d: Shift-by-wire cars turn the driver's lever, dial or buttons into network messages; where two such units exist, or the selector is split from a park-lock unit, the second one is module B. U0592 says its messages arrive but carry an implausible selector position, a frozen counter or a bad checksum, so the receiver cannot rely on the requested gear. Land Rover's bulletin LTB00677 for the 2014 Range Rover Sport (index entry only) lists U0592-00 in the engine module next to U0402 from the transmission control switch, with a car that would not leave Park; the cause was communication between junction box and TCM. Mercedes names the partner code U0291 as a fault with the electronic selector lever module on its 8-speed DCT. Ford's 2024 summary checks gear shift module data without MIL on park-by-wire cars.
c: Selector module B electronics or position sensing faulty
Bus wiring or gateway path between selector and transmission controller disturbed
Software of selector, gateway or TCM out of date
s: Vehicle will not shift out of Park
Transmission fault message in the cluster
Restricted gear selection

U0593.t: Invalid Data Received From Drive Motor Control Module B
U0593.d: Electric vehicles with one motor per axle typically report the second inverter and motor as drive motor module B; on the 2019 Audi e-tron that is the rear unit, whose loss Audi logs as U0292 when a chafed low-voltage harness cuts it off. U0593 is set when that module keeps transmitting but its torque or status data are untrustworthy. GM documents U0593 in its 2025 brake controller tables (25OBDG03B), where it is described as invalid data from the hybrid e-motor powertrain control module: the brake module expects the brake axle torque and estimated gear messages, flags a stuck alive counter or a wrong authentication code after 10 consecutive events within about 0.1 s, and treats it as Type B. Regenerative braking and torque blending on that axle may be cut back.
c: Low-voltage harness to the second drive unit chafed or connector loose
Drive motor B inverter or receiver software out of date
s: Drive system warning, reduced power
Reduced or no regenerative braking
Vehicle drives on one axle only

U0594.t: Invalid Data Received From Hybrid/EV Powertrain Control Module
U0594.d: The hybrid or EV powertrain controller coordinates engine, motors and battery, so many modules read its messages. Ford's hybrid OBD summary explains that the ABS module logs U0594 when wheel-torque or driver-demand signals from the HPCM are flagged invalid, unknown or faulted; Ford's 2014 list carries it with MIL and its 2024 summary sets U0594_48 for bad monitoring data with MIL and wrench lamp. GM's 2023 brake tables expect serial data 31 from the module and set U0594, Type B, after 20 consecutive wrong authentication codes or a frozen alive counter. FCA names it implausible data from the HCP: on the 2020–21 Ram 1500 eTorque a poorly seated motor-generator connector led to stalling and a new MGU. Ford also found harmless U0594 entries in the Escape cluster and Lightning heat pump valve module.
c: Fault inside the hybrid system makes the controller mark its signals invalid (e.g. MGU connector on Ram eTorque)
Software of the hybrid controller or the receiving module out of date
s: Check engine light and hybrid or electrical system warning
Reduced power or stalling on some hybrids
Stored code without symptoms (Ford Escape, F-150 Lightning)

U0595.t: Invalid Data Received From Powertrain Control Monitor Module
U0595.d: A powertrain control monitor module is an independent supervisor that recomputes torque, engine speed or pedal requests and compares them with what the main controller commands, so that unintended acceleration or deceleration can be caught. U0595 is stored when that supervisor's results arrive but cannot be trusted. Ford's 2014 code list contains the partner U0294, lost communication with the powertrain control monitor module, marked with the wrench lamp only, not the MIL. How such monitoring is reported is visible in Ford's 2024 summary: its electronic throttle monitor sets supervision and torque plausibility faults with the wrench lamp, some also with MIL. No manufacturer documents U0595 itself. Drivers should expect reduced power or a limp mode.
c: Software mismatch between monitor module and main powertrain controller
Supply voltage dips or bus disturbances corrupting messages
s: Wrench or powertrain warning lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode

U0596.t: Invalid Data Received From AC/AC Converter Control Module
U0596.d: An AC/AC converter changes alternating current of one voltage or frequency into another without handing it to the battery first. In vehicles, such a stage can sit in a charger, for example a matrix converter that turns three-phase grid power directly into high-frequency AC for an isolating transformer, as in patent US9973107B2, or it can adapt power for on-board outlets. U0596 means the converter's controller sends status, current or temperature data that the receiving module refuses as implausible. No manufacturer documents U0596, and none names an AC/AC converter module in public service material, so the actual function depends entirely on the vehicle. Charging or outlet power is the most likely casualty; driving should not be affected.
c: Converter control electronics faulty or overheated
Converter and receiving module software not matched
Bus wiring to the converter damaged
s: Charging or outlet power interrupted
Warning about the charging or power system

U0597.t: Invalid Data Received From AC/DC Converter Control Module A
U0597.d: In plug-in hybrids and electric cars the AC/DC converter is normally the on-board charger: it rectifies mains power and controls the current into the traction battery. CARB requires plug-in hybrids to detect charger faults that stop charging or reduce its rate. U0597 is logged when the charger's messages about state, voltage or current fail validation at the battery or vehicle controller. Public maker texts for U0597 are missing; the partner U0296 is documented by Volvo, whose 2022-on XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrids store BCM2-U029600 together with an ESC warning and a blocked pure electric mode when a third-party dongle or Y-splitter loads the diagnostic connector. Interference of that kind can just as well corrupt data, so check for such devices first.
c: Third-party dongle or Y-splitter on the diagnostic connector disturbing the bus (Volvo TJ 36559)
On-board charger electronics faulty or overheated
Charger or battery controller software out of date
s: AC charging stops or runs at reduced rate
Electric-only mode unavailable on plug-in hybrids
Warning lamps such as ESC or check engine

U0598.t: Invalid Data Received From AC/DC Converter Control Module B
U0598.d: A second AC/DC converter exists where makers raise AC charging power by fitting two charger units; the F-150 Lightning, for instance, can be ordered with two 40-amp charger units that together reach 19.2 kW. Patents show how the pair is run: Porsche's US10029578B2 has one charger lead and the other follow via a communication line only, and Hyundai's US10270273B2 uses a master controller with slave controllers per power module. U0598 means the second unit keeps reporting but its data are rejected, so the vehicle typically falls back to the first charger and charges more slowly. No manufacturer documents U0598 publicly. The lost-communication counterpart in current code lists is U0297.
c: Second charger unit faulty or overheated
Software of the charger pair not matched after a replacement
Communication line between the chargers damaged
s: AC charging only at roughly half power
Charging system warning

U0599.t: Invalid Data Received From DC/DC Converter Control Module A
U0599.d: On start-stop vehicles a DC/DC converter can hold the 12 V supply for sensitive electronics while the starter pulls the voltage down; on hybrids it feeds the 12 V network from the high-voltage battery. GM's 2025 engine tables check the converter's output voltage and crank-control messages for alive counter, protection value and checksum errors and set U0599, Type B, after 8 failures in 18 samples with at least 11 V for 5 s. GM bulletin 20-NA-191 for the 2020 Cadillac CT4 and CT5 with auto start/stop shows the code set falsely: the ECM miscalculated the protection value during cranking without boost, disabled start-stop on the first failure and lit the MIL on the second; an ECM reprogram fixed it. FCA lists U0599 for the 2019 Cherokee V6 ESS; Ford's 2014 list has it without MIL.
c: Engine controller software miscalculating the converter's protection value (GM 20-NA-191)
Weak 12 V battery causing deep voltage dips during cranking
s: Auto start/stop disabled
Check engine light after repeated failures

U059A.t: Invalid Data Received From DC/DC Converter Control Module B
U059A.d: Converter B is a second DC/DC unit, used when one voltage support stage is not enough or when separate networks need their own supply. FCA is the only maker that names it publicly: in powertrain module updates for the 2019 Jeep Cherokee with the 3.2-litre V6 and engine stop-start (18-023-19 and follow-ups such as 18-020-21), the PCM lists both U0599 and U059A for invalid data from DC-to-DC converters A and B, plus U0299 for lost contact with converter 2. The customer complaint in those bulletins is a MIL and an engine that sometimes fails to restart after a stop-start event, and the fix is new PCM software rather than a new converter. A failing second converter mostly shows up as start-stop being withdrawn or electronics resetting during restarts.
c: Powertrain controller software evaluating converter B data incorrectly (FCA 18-023-19)
Wiring or ground connection of converter B poor
s: Check engine light
Engine does not restart after a stop-start event
Stop-start function withdrawn

U059B.t: Invalid Data Received From Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Sensor Module
U059B.d: The battery pack sensor module measures pack voltage and current and often sits in the switch box that holds the main contactors, reporting to the battery management controller. Audi uses U059B00 for an implausible signal from the high-voltage battery switch box on the 2024 Q8 e-tron family: after a stop at an AC charging point the car refused to enable its drive and the cluster asked the driver to stop safely, with contactor control codes P0ADC00 and P0AE000 stored alongside. Audi traced it to over-sensitive diagnostic software, advised a 20-minute bus sleep before towing and ruled out replacing parts. The 2025 Q5 e-tron shows U059B00 together with lost contact U029A00 (index entry only). CARB requires battery system faults that stop the pack moving the vehicle to be detected.
c: Current or voltage sensing in the switch box faulty
Battery-internal communication line or connector disturbed
s: Drive system cannot be activated
Drive system and electrical system fault messages
Charging interrupted

U059C.t: Invalid Data Received From Drive Motor Control Module C
U059C.d: A third drive motor controller exists only on tri-motor or quad-motor vehicles, where one axle carries two motors for torque vectoring. Examples are GMC's Hummer EV in tri-motor form and Rivian's quad-motor R1T with a motor at each wheel. U059C is stored when module C still talks but sends torque, speed or status values the vehicle controller cannot accept. Which wheel or axle module C serves is left to the maker, and none documents U059C publicly. The sibling logic is the same as for module B, which Audi treats as the rear drive unit on the e-tron and GM monitors with counter and authentication checks; for C the vehicle usually disables the motor and continues with reduced power and without torque vectoring on that axle.
c: Inverter or controller of motor C faulty
Low-voltage harness or connector at drive unit C damaged
Software level of motor C not matching the vehicle controller
s: Propulsion system warning and reduced power
Torque vectoring or a drive mode unavailable

U059D.t: Invalid Data Received From Drive Motor Control Module D
U059D.d: Module D only exists where four drive motors are fitted, one per wheel. Rivian's R1T and R1S Quad-Motor are production examples: each wheel has its own motor, so a single faulty controller costs one corner of drive, not a whole axle. U059D records that the fourth controller keeps sending frames whose torque, speed or diagnostic content fails the receiving controller's checks. Ford's hybrid OBD description shows the usual check for electrified modules: a CAN message missing for 5 s sets the lost-communication code, a signal reporting invalid states for 5 s the invalid-data code (U0111 and U0412 for the battery energy control module). No manufacturer documents U059D publicly, so the corner it refers to and the reaction are maker-specific. A typical response is to switch off that motor, mirror the limit on the opposite wheel so the vehicle stays straight, and drop to a reduced power mode. Distinguish it from U029C, where the module is silent, and from codes B and C for the other motors.
c: Inverter or controller of the fourth motor faulty
Signal wiring at the wheel motor damaged by road debris or water
Motor controller software not updated together with the others
s: Reduced power warning
Off-road or performance modes locked

U059E.t: Invalid Data Received From NOx Sensor A
U059E.d: NOx sensor A usually sits upstream of the SCR catalyst. Its attached electronics turn the probe current into NOx and oxygen readings and broadcast them on CAN. Here those frames still arrive, yet the receiver rejects them. GM's 2025 diesel ECM tables (25OBDG04A/B) count wrong alive rolling counts, protection values or checksums: 8 bad out of 18 samples for most signals, 3 out of 10 for a few, with at least 11 V present for 5 s. It is Type B, so the MIL follows on the second trip. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets it when the sensor's calibration verification number never reaches the ECU. U029D stands for a silent sensor, U05A1 for the reverse path. Until valid readings return, NOx-based SCR checks and dosing feedback cannot run.
c: Sensor control unit of NOx sensor A faulty (heat, moisture, internal error)
Replacement sensor of a different part number or software level
Corroded connector or damaged CAN/supply wiring at the sensor
Engine controller software needing an update
s: Check engine light after the second faulty trip
SCR and NOx sensor monitors stay incomplete
Engine usually runs normally

U059F.t: Invalid Data Received From NOx Sensor B
U059F.d: Sensor B is normally the tailpipe NOx sensor behind the SCR catalyst, so its readings decide whether the catalyst efficiency test passes. The code means its CAN frames are present but unusable. GM's 2025 diesel tables run the same counter, protection value and checksum test as for sensor A, here on the post-catalyst signal set, and treat it as Type B. FCA lists it for Ram 3500 to 5500 Cab Chassis trucks with the 6.7 L Cummins: bulletin 18-012-13 (2012) and 18-042-20 (2014, calibration without ammonia delete) reflash the ECM because the light could come on with no hardware fault. U029E means the sensor is missing entirely, U05A2 that sensor B rejects engine data. A stored code blocks the SCR efficiency verdict, so check software before buying a sensor.
c: Engine controller calibration known to flag false faults (FCA reflash)
Control unit of the downstream NOx sensor damaged
Chafed wiring or water in the connector near the exhaust
s: Check engine light on
SCR efficiency monitor not completing
No noticeable change in power

U05A0.t: Invalid Data Received From Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Control Module
U05A0.d: Some fuel systems hand the tank leak test to a separate module with its own pump, valve, pressure sensor and processor. Stoneridge patent US11773809 describes such a unit: it wakes hours after shutdown while the engine controller sleeps, runs the test alone and later passes pressure results over CAN or LIN, from which the OBD system decides on a fault code. U05A0 is set when those reports arrive but cannot be trusted, for example wrong length, counter or values. Ford's 2014 OBD code list shows it with the lamp indicator. CARB 1968.2 requires leak detection down to 0.020 inch on gasoline vehicles, so a module whose data are rejected leaves the EVAP readiness open. U029F means no messages at all, U030A a software mismatch. Driving is unaffected.
c: Leak detection module electronics or its pressure sensor failing
Corrosion at the module connector near the tank or canister
Module and engine controller software levels do not match
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set, emissions inspection may fail

U05A1.t: NOx Sensor A Received Invalid Data From ECM/PCM
U05A1.d: Here the fault is judged inside NOx sensor A: its control unit relies on engine controller frames, for instance the release to heat the probe once condensation is no longer a risk, and it reports back when those inputs are missing or make no sense. Ford's 2023 diesel OBD summary groups U05A1 with P2200 under the upstream NOx module checks. Typical triggers are a dew point release received while the ignition is off, or no message for more than 1 s; 5 s of fault are needed to register it. Ford's 2014 code list flags it as a MIL code. CARB 1968.2 asks that digital outputs to a component be checked for communication errors. U059E is the opposite direction, U05A2 and U05A9 cover sensors B and C. The probe may stay cold, leaving NOx readings and SCR monitoring unavailable.
c: Engine controller software or configuration sending wrong values to the sensor
Intermittent CAN connection to the sensor causing timeouts
Sensor control unit misjudging correct data
s: Check engine light on
NOx reading for sensor A stays invalid on the scan tool
SCR monitors not completing

U05A2.t: NOx Sensor B Received Invalid Data From ECM/PCM
U05A2.d: This is the downstream counterpart of U05A1: the tailpipe NOx sensor B finds the frames it gets from the engine controller missing or implausible and reports it. Ford's 2023 diesel summary documents it for the 3.0 L and 6.7 L engines next to P229E in the tailpipe NOx controller checks, using the same criteria as for the front sensor, an erroneous signal such as a dew point release with ignition off, or more than 1 s without a message, confirmed after 5 s. Ford's 2014 list also shows it with MIL. Because sensor B measures what leaves the SCR catalyst, the efficiency monitor cannot finish while the code is active. U059F describes the reverse problem, U029E a sensor that has gone quiet. A software update or bus repair usually comes before replacing the sensor.
c: Damaged harness to the rear sensor, exposed to road spray and heat
Engine controller software sending implausible commands
Fault inside the sensor B control unit
s: Check engine light on
SCR efficiency monitor incomplete

U05A3.t: Invalid Data Received From Reductant Quality Module
U05A3.d: A reductant quality module checks that the tank holds proper diesel exhaust fluid, a 32.5 % urea solution. SSI's TULC sensor, for example, derives concentration from the speed of sound and reports it with level and temperature over J1939 CAN to the dosing control unit. This code means those reports arrive but are rejected. FCA documents it for the 2019 Jeep Cherokee 2.2 diesel (EMEA): bulletin 18-088-20 reprograms the dosing control unit when U05A3 appears with a MIL, often together with P20F4/P20F5 consumption faults. CARB 1968.2 demands that every input used by the low-quality inducement be monitored. Ford sets U02A2 when the module's messages are missing for 5 s. The driver may see a DEF warning, and inducement can follow if it persists.
c: Dosing control unit software misreading the module (FCA reflash)
Quality sensor fouled by crystals or contaminated fluid
Corroded connector at the DEF tank sender
s: Check engine light and DEF warning
Reductant consumption faults stored alongside
Possible speed or restart limitation if not fixed

U05A4.t: Particulate Matter Sensor Received Invalid Data From ECM/PCM
U05A4.d: A diesel particulate matter sensor has its own control unit, which needs engine controller data to run its measuring and burn-off cycles. U05A4 is reported when that unit cannot accept what the engine controller sends. FCA lists it in bulletins 18-008-23 (2019 Jeep Compass with 1.6 or 2.0 L diesel) and 18-010-23 (2020 Compass 1.6): with the MIL on, U05A4 may appear among many PM sensor P-codes and U02A3, and the cure is new PCM software; only P2002 calls for a new filter and sensor. CARB 1968.2 requires PM sensor faults to be caught before the sensor stops being usable for filter monitoring. U04A4 is the reverse direction, U02A3 total silence. Expect a MIL and an incomplete filter test, with normal driving.
c: Engine controller software issue (FCA PCM update)
Damaged CAN or supply wiring to the PM sensor unit
PM sensor control unit faulty or wrong variant
s: Check engine light on
Several particulate matter sensor codes stored at once
Particulate filter monitor not completing

U05A5.t: Invalid Data Received From NH3 Sensor
U05A5.d: An ammonia (NH3) sensor behind the SCR catalyst tells the controller whether too much urea is dosed and ammonia slips through. Like NOx sensors it carries its own electronics and talks over CAN; Bosch even offers NOx sensors that add a selective ammonia signal. U05A5 means the ammonia data come in but fail validation. FCA's bulletin 18-028-16 for 2014 Ram 3500 to 5500 Cab Chassis with the 6.7 L Cummins shows a special case: two ECM calibrations exist, with and without the ammonia sensor, and if U05A5 or U12A4 appears after the update, the wrong one was loaded. CARB 1968.2 requires a monitoring plan for such other exhaust gas sensors. U02A4 means the sensor is silent. Dosing control loses its slip feedback.
c: Engine calibration does not match the sensor fit (with or without NH3 sensor)
Damaged wiring or connector at the ammonia sensor
s: Check engine light on
Code appears right after an engine software update
SCR dosing runs without ammonia feedback

U05A6.t: Invalid Data Received From Reductant Heater Control Module
U05A6.d: Diesel exhaust fluid freezes at about -11 °C, and EU rules demanded that it be usable within 20 minutes after a start at -15 °C, so tanks, pumps and lines get electric heaters. Where these heaters are driven by a separate control module, it reports heater states, temperatures and faults to the engine or dosing controller over the bus. U05A6 is stored when those reports arrive but are inconsistent or corrupt. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. CARB 1968.2 requires every component that feeds the emission control or its inducement to be monitored, which covers thaw control. U02A5 means the module is silent, P20B9 points to a heater circuit itself. In cold weather, dosing may start late and warnings may appear.
c: Water or salt corrosion at module connector or bus wiring
Software levels of heater module and engine controller do not fit
s: Check engine light or DEF system warning
Delayed DEF dosing after cold starts

U05A7.t: Invalid Data Received From Safety Integration Control Module
U05A7.d: The Safety Integration Control Module appears in the SAE code catalogue, yet no carmaker explains in public what this unit does or which models carry it; the name suggests a controller that ties several safety functions together. U05A7 is stored by a receiving module that still gets the unit's frames but refuses what they contain. Safety-related signals are normally secured end to end: the AUTOSAR E2E protocol attaches a CRC to detect altered bits, a counter to spot repeated or reordered frames and a data ID so that a wrong sender is recognised. Failing one of these checks is the typical trigger. No manufacturer documents U05A7 or its partner U02A6, which stands for a module that has gone silent. Expect warnings and reduced assistance, not an emissions fault.
c: Software fault or outdated software in the safety integration module
Module replaced or reprogrammed without matching vehicle configuration
Corrupted frames from wiring, connector or termination faults on the bus
Low supply voltage during start or after battery discharge
s: Warning message about safety or assistance systems
Individual assistance functions unavailable
Further network codes stored in several modules

U05A8.t: Invalid Data Received From NOx Sensor C
U05A8.d: A third NOx sensor appears on exhaust systems with two SCR stages, where sensor C watches the gas after the second catalyst. GM's 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG04B) are the public example: the engine controller checks alive rolling count and checksum of the post-second-catalyst NOx signals, eight failures in 18 samples or three in ten depending on the signal, with battery voltage of at least 11 V for 5 s, and logs U05A8 as Type B. The companion 25OBDG04A set has no such entry. U02A1 covers loss of sensor C messages, U05A9 the case where sensor C refuses engine data, U059E and U059F the first two sensors. The second SCR stage cannot be judged while the code is present.
c: Control unit of NOx sensor C faulty
Harness or connector of the rearmost sensor damaged
Sensors swapped between positions during repair
s: Check engine light after two trips
SCR monitor for the second catalyst incomplete

U05A9.t: NOx Sensor C Received Invalid Data From ECM/PCM
U05A9.d: With this code the third NOx sensor, fitted after a second SCR stage, reports that it cannot use the frames the engine controller sends it, such as heater release or operating state. No manufacturer documents U05A9 publicly. The closest published logic is Ford's 2023 diesel summary for sensors A and B (U05A1, U05A2): bad input is flagged when a dew point release comes while the key is off or when frames pause longer than 1 s, and the fault is logged after 5 s. GM's 25OBDG04B shows that a sensor C exists, but only for the opposite direction (U05A8). CARB 1968.2 requires communication errors on digital outputs to be detected. If the sensor never gets its heating release, its readings and the second-stage SCR check stay unavailable.
c: Intermittent bus connection to sensor C
Engine controller not configured for the third sensor
Sensor C control unit rejecting valid data
s: Check engine light on
No NOx value from sensor C on the scan tool

U05AA.t: Invalid Data Received From Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump
U05AA.d: Engines with a water-cooled charge air cooler use an electric pump, often a LIN slave of the engine controller, to move coolant through the low-temperature circuit. CARB requires the charge air cooling to be checked for performance and its electronic parts to be monitored. U05AA is set when the pump reports speed, current or fault bits that do not make sense. Public maker documentation exists for the partner U02A9: GM's 2025 tables declare lost LIN contact after 2.5 s without a pump response, Type A; Ram 1500 owners see a check engine light with U02A9 and P023B from pushed-out terminals at the pump connector; Mercedes links U02A900 on GLC and GLE to the PTCU software or LIN wiring. None documents U05AA itself. Expect reduced boost if intake air runs hot.
c: Pushed-out or corroded terminals at the pump connector
Fault elsewhere on the shared LIN bus or in the master module software
s: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power in hot conditions
Coolant warning or radiator fan running at full speed

U05AB.t: Invalid Data Received From Engine Disconnect Clutch
U05AB.d: In parallel hybrids the engine disconnect clutch sits between engine crankshaft and electric machine; opened, it lets the car drive electrically with the engine off, closed, it starts the engine or adds its torque. Ford's patents describe the clutch being prestroked so it is filled with pressure before an engine start is requested, and being advanced before the hydraulic pump spins down. Where the clutch has its own smart actuator or position sensor on the network, U05AB records that its reports of position, pressure or state arrive but are implausible. No manufacturer documents U05AB or its partner U02AA publicly. Without trustworthy clutch data the hybrid controller can no longer blend engine starts safely, so electric driving, engine start-stop or hybrid assist are typically restricted.
c: Clutch actuator electronics or position sensor faulty
Actuator and hybrid controller software not matched or adaptation lost
Wiring or connector at the transmission bell housing damaged
s: Hybrid system warning and check engine light
Electric driving unavailable, engine runs continuously
Jerky engine starts

U05AC.t: Invalid Data Received From Vehicle Thermal Management Control Module
U05AC.d: Electrified cars increasingly run cabin, battery and drive-unit cooling from one thermal management controller that commands pumps, valves, fans and the refrigerant circuit; suppliers such as Hirain and Marelli sell such units, Marelli explicitly with OBD compliance. For hybrids, CARB requires the electronic parts used for battery and inverter cooling or heating to be monitored and, where feasible, the cooling performance itself. U05AC is stored when that controller's status or temperature messages reach another module with invalid content. Audi reports the partner U02AB, the thermal management unit 00C5 not reachable, on the 2025/26 A5, Q5 and S5 with a software fix (index entry only). No maker documents U05AC itself. Charging and drive power may be limited to protect the battery.
c: Thermal management controller software out of date
Faulty temperature or pressure sensor feeding the controller
s: Various warning messages in the cluster
Reduced charging or drive power
Climate control not working properly

U05B2.t: Invalid Data Received From Comfort and Convenience Display A
U05B2.d: Stellantis calls its touch screens for climate, seat and similar comfort settings Comfort and Convenience Display Modules (CCDM); the Jeep Grand Wagoneer has one up front and a second one for rear passengers. U05B2 is logged when a receiver gets traffic from display A whose content is implausible. Which of the screens carries letter A is not published. Two field cases show what typically goes wrong: phantom touches that alter fan speed on their own, cured by a front or rear display with newer firmware (STAR S228A000013 Rev. A), and, on the 2025 Wagoneer S, massage graphics offered for seats without massage, fixed with a later part number and a proxi alignment (S2508000061). No manufacturer cites U05B2 itself; U02B1 is the lost-communication partner.
c: Display firmware with known faults, newer part number available
Display configuration not matching vehicle equipment, proxi alignment missing
Touch panel or display electronics defective
Loose or corroded connector at the display
s: Climate or seat settings change without input
Display shows functions the vehicle does not have
Comfort controls on the screen respond late or not at all

U05B3.t: Invalid Data Received From Comfort and Convenience Display B
U05B3.d: Display B is the second comfort screen on vehicles fitted with more than one, typically a rear unit from which back-seat occupants adjust climate and seats. U05B3 is set when its frames arrive but do not pass the receiver's validity checks, whereas U02B2 would mean that display B has fallen silent. No carmaker publishes U05B3 or states which screen counts as B. On the Jeep Grand Wagoneer the front display can lock out the rear one, and Stellantis uses exactly this to find out which unit issues unwanted commands such as fan changes; the rear screen then gets a newer part number with revised firmware (STAR S228A000013 and Rev. A, 2022-2023). A configuration that no longer fits after a replacement is another likely trigger. Rear climate controls may act on their own or ignore input.
c: Rear comfort display with old firmware sending spurious commands
Replacement display not configured to the vehicle
Chafed or loose wiring to the rear console display
s: Rear climate settings change by themselves
Rear comfort screen does not accept inputs
Front display shows rear functions as unavailable

U05B4.t: Invalid Data Received From Driver Monitoring System Module
U05B4.d: A driver monitoring system films the driver's face with an infrared camera to judge attention and drowsiness. Toyota launched it in 2006, Cadillac relies on one to allow hands-free Super Cruise, and EU Regulation 2019/2144 covers it. Subaru stores up to five driver profiles in its DMS control unit and asks technicians to save them before service (bulletin 07-175-20); Stellantis lists a driver monitoring system module (DMSM) among the ADAS units of the 2025 Grand Cherokee that drop features after a deep battery discharge (STAR S2408000086, charge above 90 %, then ten minutes of bus sleep). U05B4 means its gaze or status messages reach the ADAS controller but are invalid. No manufacturer documents U05B4 publicly; hands-free and lane functions are then usually withdrawn. U02B3 covers a silent module.
c: Low 12 V state of charge or recent battery replacement
Camera or infrared emitters covered, dirty or misaligned
Module software or calibration not matching the ADAS controller
s: Hands-free or lane assistance not available
Driver attention warning inactive or triggered without reason
Service message for driver assistance in the cluster

U05B5.t: Invalid Data Received From Front Radar Module A
U05B5.d: Front radar modules measure distance and closing speed of objects ahead for adaptive cruise, emergency braking and lane change support. Mercedes-Benz documents this code on the 2026 CLA electric (series 174): the driver assistance controller N62/5 stores U05B555 when the front radar on the outer left delivers implausible data because it has not been configured. Bulletin LI54.71-P-080345 (versions of April and May 2026) ties it to a lasting warning that the assistance systems are unavailable, mainly on cars built before 5 September 2025, and calls for an N62/5 teach-in calibration or a calibration drive followed by at least seven minutes parked and locked. Other brands use letters differently, so A is not always a corner sensor. U02B4 means module A is silent; U05B6 is the right twin.
c: Radar sensor not configured or calibrated in the assistance controller (Mercedes N62/5)
Outdated software in the driver assistance controller
Radar knocked out of alignment after bumper damage or repair
Radar connector behind the bumper loose or wet
s: Driver assistance unavailable message that does not clear
Adaptive cruise and emergency braking switched off
Lane change or blind spot functions on the front left limited

U05B6.t: Invalid Data Received From Front Radar Module B
U05B6.d: Letter B on a front radar points to different hardware depending on the brand. At Mercedes-Benz, U05B655 on the 2026 CLA electric marks implausible data from the front radar on the outer right, again with sub-code 55 for a sensor that was never configured, and it shares the remedy of the left unit: calibrating control unit N62/5 per LI54.71-P-080345. Stellantis gives B to the long-range radar behind the front bumper: on the Grand Wagoneer, lost communication U02B5 in the central ADAS module came from connector D1082A not being latched (STAR S2208000105). U05B6 itself means that module B keeps talking while its object or status data are rejected. Adaptive cruise, collision warning and lane centring then go offline; the engine lamp stays dark.
c: Right front radar not configured after production or replacement (Mercedes)
Long-range radar connector not fully latched (Stellantis D1082A)
Radar cover dirty, iced or damaged
s: Adaptive cruise control not available
Forward collision warning switched off
Lane centring or active driving assist not ready

U05B7.t: Invalid Data Received From Rear Radar Module A
U05B7.d: Rear radar modules are hidden in the corners of the rear bumper and feed blind spot warning, rear cross traffic alert and the exit warning that watches for cyclists when a door opens. Mercedes-Benz stores U05B755 on the 2026 CLA electric when the rear radar on the outer left sends implausible data because it is not configured; the driver assistance controller N62/5 then keeps several functions offline. Bulletin LI54.71-P-080345 (versions 1 and 2) has the N62/5 calibrated by teach-in, or alternatively by the calibration drive used after a bumper has been replaced. U05B7 thus points to a sensor that answers but is not accepted, unlike U02B6, where it no longer answers at all. Drivers notice a missing blind spot lamp on the left and assistance messages; driveability is unchanged.
c: Left rear radar not configured in the assistance controller
Rear bumper repaired or repainted, sensor mount or cover altered
Moisture or corrosion at the rear radar connector
s: Blind spot indicator on the left stays off
Rear cross traffic and exit warnings unavailable
Assistance unavailable message in the instrument cluster

U05B8.t: Invalid Data Received From Rear Radar Module B
U05B8.d: Module B is the right-hand rear corner radar in the only public manufacturer use: Mercedes-Benz lists U05B855 for the outer right rear sensor of the 2026 CLA electric. The fault type 55 reads as not configured, so the content is rejected because the controller N62/5 has no valid setup for that sensor, not because the radar is broken. The May 2026 version of bulletin LI54.71-P-080345 narrows the case to cars built before 27 February 2026 with persistent warnings and drops the hardware reset step of version 1; afterwards the car must sleep for seven minutes, and full assistance returns after roughly ten more minutes of driving. Replacing the sensor is therefore rarely the first step. Right-side blind spot and cross traffic warnings fail. U02B7 means module B is silent.
c: Right rear radar not configured, calibration of the assistance controller missing
Initial calibration of the controller's acceleration sensor not completed
s: Blind spot indicator on the right stays off
Assistance warnings reappear on every start
Rear cross traffic alert missing on the right

U05B9.t: Invalid Data Received From Rear Radar Module C
U05B9.d: A third rear radar is only needed on vehicles whose rear coverage goes beyond the usual pair of corner sensors, for example to watch longer flanks or the area directly behind. No manufacturer publishes U05B9 or the position of a rear radar C, and its lost-communication partner U02B8 has no public bulletin either. Where letters are documented, they belong to the outer units: Mercedes-Benz uses rear modules A and B for the outer left and right sensors of the 2026 CLA electric and reports them, when unconfigured, with fault type 55. U05B9 would follow the same logic for a further sensor: frames arrive, the content is refused. Configuration, calibration after bumper work and the connector are the first checks. Blind spot or rear crossing alerts may be partly unavailable.
c: Rear radar C not configured or calibrated after replacement
Sensor position or cover changed by rear body repair
Wiring or connector fault at rear radar C
s: Rear assistance warnings partly unavailable
Service message for driver assistance

U05BA.t: Invalid Data Received From Rear Radar Module D
U05BA.d: Rear radar module D is the fourth unit in the rear numbering and is reserved for layouts with an unusually dense sensor set at the back. Neither U05BA nor the matching lost-communication code U02B9 is described by any manufacturer in public, so there are no published thresholds or fitting positions. The code says that module D transmits, but the receiving assistance controller treats its frames as invalid, for instance due to a failed checksum or counter, an implausible status or a sensor that was never coded. Because radar functions such as parking help, exit warning and lane change support can draw on several rear sensors, a single faulty unit usually degrades only part of them. Mercedes-Benz shows for rear modules A and B that calibration rather than replacement is often the cure.
c: Rear radar D not coded to the vehicle
Assistance controller software rejects data from module D
s: Individual rear warnings such as exit warning not available
Assistance message in the instrument cluster

U05BD.t: Invalid Data Received From Localization and Mapping Module
U05BD.d: Hands-free and highly automated driving needs to know the car's position to lane level and the road ahead from a detailed map. GM handles this in a separate map module (K179) for Super Cruise: it holds a LiDAR-surveyed map that decides where the system may be engaged and receives map and GPS correction data over the air while driving. Bulletin PIT6000 (2021-2023 Escalade, Tahoe, Silverado and others) traces a Service Driver Assist message with B2BA1 to a map that stayed outdated after mostly short trips; on the 2022 Bolt EUV map files were updated by USB (N222360520). Bosch combines satellite positioning with correction data, inertial and wheel-speed signals. No manufacturer documents U05BD; it would flag invalid position or map data, U02BC a missing module.
c: Map database outdated because over-the-air updates could not complete
Poor satellite reception or faulty GNSS antenna and cable
Module software not matching the assistance controller
Localization and mapping module internally defective
s: Hands-free driving not offered on mapped roads
Service driver assist message
Lane-level guidance or map-based speed adaptation missing

U05BE.t: Invalid Data Received From Night Vision Control Module
U05BE.d: Night vision systems show the road beyond the headlight beam, either passively with a thermal camera that picks up heat from people and animals or actively with near-infrared illumination. The control module processes the picture, detects pedestrians and sends image and warning data to the cluster or head-up display. U05BE means those messages arrive but are judged invalid. No maker documents U05BE itself. For the lost-communication partner, Jeep reports on the 2021-2023 Grand Cherokee that U02BD-00 in the body controller and B0125-02 in the cluster came from bent pins or terminals not fully seated at the processing module connector D3944A (STAR S2208000163). Contact problems of that kind can also corrupt data rather than cut it off. Only night vision is lost; driving is unaffected.
c: Bent pins or loose terminals at the night vision module connector
Infrared camera or its video link delivering faulty data
s: Night vision image missing or frozen
Pedestrian and animal warnings at night unavailable
Night vision fault message in the cluster

U05BF.t: Invalid Data Received From Trailer Backup Assist Control Module
U05BF.d: Trailer backup assist lets the driver reverse a trailer by turning a knob rather than the wheel; the vehicle measures the hitch angle and steers for the chosen path. Ford's Pro Trailer Backup Assist reads the angle from a target sticker via the rear camera or from a sensor on the trailer, and a Ford patent caps the steering command according to how fast the hitch angle changes, so the rig does not jackknife. Ram calls its version trailer reverse steering. On the 2021 Ram 1500 the lost-communication partner U02BE turned up in the ABS, steering and engine controllers with a throttle control message and the MIL, caused by internal module software; pulling fuse 53 restarted the module (STAR S2108000067). No maker documents U05BF; it means the module talks but sends invalid data, and the assist is then blocked.
c: Internal software fault in the trailer backup assist module
Implausible hitch angle input from trailer target, camera or trailer sensor
Trailer profile incomplete or measured dimensions wrong
Module supply interrupted or connector loose
s: Trailer backup assist cannot be activated or cancels
Rear park assist temporarily unavailable
Warning messages in other modules, on some trucks with MIL

U05C0.t: Invalid Data Received From Interior Lighting Control Module B
U05C0.d: Cars with extensive ambient and cabin lighting split it across several controllers; module B is the second of these, for instance for the rear cabin, the doors or a separate light strip, while A runs the main zone. These nodes usually hang on a LIN line below the body controller, which sends them colour and brightness commands and polls their status; Microchip's reference design runs this at about 10.4 kbit/s with a checksum on every frame. U05C0 is set when status replies from module B arrive but are corrupt or implausible, as opposed to U02BF, where B stops replying. No manufacturer documents U05C0 or the allocation of letter B. Expect zones that stay dark or show the wrong colour, while the main interior lights controlled by module A (U054B) keep working.
c: LED controller of lighting module B defective
LIN line or connector to module B damaged, for example in a door hinge area
Replacement module B not configured for its zone
s: Ambient light zone stays dark or flickers
Wrong colour or brightness in part of the cabin
Lighting settings in the menu not applied to all zones

U05C1.t: Invalid Data Received From Active Radiator Air Flow Control Module A
U05C1.d: Besides shutters in the visible grille, some cars meter cooling air with flaps placed directly in front of the radiator, behind the bumper intake. Hyundai's patent US11225900B2 describes such an arrangement with two adjacent flaps between bumper opening and radiator plus an air guide steering air towards them. The J2012 list gives this unit its own module family, separate from the grille shutters, and U05C1 means module A delivers position or status frames that the engine or thermal controller rejects. No manufacturer documents U05C1 or its partner U02C0 publicly, so the threshold and lamp strategy are unknown. Because CARB treats active aerodynamic and warm-up devices as off-cycle CO2 technologies, a maker may handle the fault like the shutter codes; in practice the flap is parked open for safe cooling.
c: Connector behind the bumper wet or corroded
Flap blocked by debris or ice so the actuator reports implausible positions
s: Warning lamp on some vehicles
Flap stays open, slightly higher consumption

U0600.t: Lost Communication With Engine Oil Pressure Sensor A
U0600.d: Newer engines often use a digital oil pressure sensor that sends its value over a SENT line (SAE J2716) instead of an analog voltage. SENT is a one-way link with a 5 V supply, a signal wire and ground; each frame carries a CRC and a status nibble. U0600 means the engine controller no longer receives valid frames from oil pressure sensor A. Ford's gasoline summaries for 2020 to 2023 and 2024 list it with P0520 under the SENT oil pressure check: continuous, battery above 11 V, 5 s to register. Ford's 2023 diesel summary uses it when the SENT sensor reports a communication error. CARB 1968.2 requires a separate code for lost communication on computer-coded inputs. Oil pressure control and the low-pressure warning lose their input.
c: Open, shorted or chafed SENT signal, supply or ground wire
Oil or corrosion in the sensor connector
s: Check engine light on
Oil pressure warning or no oil pressure reading

U0601.t: Lost Communication With Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A
U0601.d: Particulate filter pressure sensor A measures the pressure drop across a diesel or gasoline particulate filter, the basis for soot load estimates and filter monitoring. Digital versions report over SENT. GM's 2025 diesel tables (25OBDG04A/B) call it differential pressure sensor loss of communication: it sets when the sensor reports an internal fault that shuts its SENT output, when 158 of 200 checks fail, or when no fresh message has come for over 12.5 s; it is Type A, so the MIL comes on in the first trip. Ford's 2023 diesel summary flags a SENT driver error or a line stuck high or low, and Ford's 2024 gasoline summary uses it for the filter sensors with 5 s to register. U0602, U0696 and U0697 cover sensors B to D.
c: SENT line, 5 V supply or ground interrupted or shorted
Sensor internal fault switching off its output (heat, moisture)
s: Check engine light, on GM already in the first trip
Filter regeneration may run on a model only or be blocked
Reduced power on some diesels

U0602.t: Lost Communication With Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B
U0602.d: Pressure sensor B serves a second particulate filter or a second measuring point, for example on engines with one gasoline particulate filter per bank. The code means its digital SENT output has stopped delivering usable frames to the engine controller. Ford's 2024 gasoline OBD summary lists U0602 with P245E in the check for SENT-type filter pressure sensors A to D, running continuously and needing 5 s to register; analog versions of the same sensors use the circuit low/high codes instead. CARB 1968.2 requires lost communication on a coded digital input to get its own fault code, apart from circuit and range faults. U0601 refers to sensor A, U0696 and U0697 to C and D. Filter loading for that branch must then be estimated without measurement.
c: Damaged SENT, supply or ground wire to sensor B
Loose or corroded connector at sensor B
s: Check engine light on
Particulate filter monitor for the affected branch incomplete

U0603.t: Lost Communication With Fuel Pressure Sensor A
U0603.d: Fuel pressure sensor A reports fuel or rail pressure, which the controller needs for injection quantity and pump control. When the sensor is digital, it transmits over a point-to-point SENT line instead of an analog voltage, and U0603 means its frames no longer arrive in usable form: wire open or shorted, signal stuck high or low, CRC errors or an internal sensor fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Ford's 2023 diesel and 2024 gasoline summaries show the same pattern for other SENT sensors (U0600, U0601) with 5 s to register. CARB 1968.2 demands a dedicated code for lost communication on such inputs. P0190 covers circuit faults of an analog sensor, U0604 the second sensor. Expect a fallback pressure strategy, rough running or no start.
c: SENT signal, 5 V supply or ground wire faulty
s: Check engine light on
Reduced power or limp mode
Hard start, stalling or no start

U0604.t: Lost Communication With Fuel Pressure Sensor B
U0604.d: Sensor B is the second fuel pressure measuring point, for example a low-pressure sensor in the feed line of a direct injection engine or a second rail on V engines; which pressure it reads depends on the maker. U0604 flags that this digital sensor has stopped sending valid SENT frames to the engine controller. Nobody publishes a manufacturer description for this code. By analogy with Ford's SENT checks for oil and filter pressure sensors, the controller would look for driver errors, a line held high or low or missing frames and confirm after a few seconds. CARB 1968.2 requires separate lost-communication codes for coded digital inputs. P018A is the analog circuit code for sensor B, U0603 the counterpart for sensor A. Depending on the role, pump control or the second rail falls back to defaults.
c: Damaged signal, supply or ground wire to sensor B
Sensor A and B connectors swapped or loose
s: Check engine light on
Hesitation or reduced power under load

U0605.t: Lost Communication With A/C Refrigerant Sensor A
U0605.d: The air conditioning controller needs refrigerant pressure or temperature to run the compressor and protect the circuit. Where this information comes over a serial link such as LIN, a single master polls the slave and expects an answer in a fixed schedule; U0605 means refrigerant sensor A no longer answers properly. Mazda shows a broader use: for the 2025 CX-70 and CX-90 plug-in hybrids, bulletin 07-002-26b assigns U0605 in the PCM to a LIN communication error between the electric A/C compressor and the PCM, often with P0D6D after an internal compressor short has blown the high-voltage A/C fuse; the fix is an updated compressor. U0626 and U0627 name dedicated pressure and temperature sensors. Usually the A/C stops cooling.
c: Open or shorted LIN, supply or ground wire to the sensor
Electric compressor shorted internally, high-voltage A/C fuse open (Mazda PHEV)
s: A/C does not cool
Compressor switched off by the controller

U0606.t: Lost Communication With Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A
U0606.d: Many electronic throttle bodies now report the blade angle as digital SENT frames (SAE J2716) instead of two analog voltages. U0606 means the engine controller no longer receives valid frames from position sensor A. Ford's gasoline summaries for 2020 to 2024 use it on SENT throttle bodies: a wiring fault or a faulted SENT device lasting over 4 s lights the MIL and the wrench lamp, while a line shorted low or high gets separate codes and P0120 covers a sensor that still talks but flags itself faulty. GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG03A) name it throttle position sensor 1 and fail it as Type A for line levels under 0.5 V or over 4.1 V, wrong pulse timing, stale messages or CRC errors. Throttle authority is then cut back.
c: SENT signal, 5 V supply or ground wire to the throttle body open, shorted or chafed
Loose, corroded or water-soaked throttle body connector
Sensor electronics in the throttle body failed (replacement usually as a complete throttle body)
Engine controller SENT input or software fault
s: Check engine light, on Ford also the wrench lamp
Reduced power or limp mode with limited throttle response
Rough or unstable idle

U0607.t: Lost Communication With Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B
U0607.d: Position sensor B is the redundant second track of a throttle or pedal unit. On SENT throttle bodies both tracks often share one sensor chip and even one frame (the dual throttle format A.1 of J2716), so a broken line usually drops A and B together. U0607 alone points to a fault confined to the second channel or its decoding. GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG03A) assign it to throttle position sensor 2 with the same SENT checks as sensor 1, Type A. On a GM engine with one throttle per bank (documents 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07) it pairs with U0606 on bank 1 when the line stays silent or pulse or calibration lengths fall outside the window for 0.13 s. Ford's SENT summaries skip this code. With one track left, plausibility checks are gone, so power is limited.
c: Second sensor channel inside the throttle or pedal unit failed
Damaged SENT line, supply or ground (often sets U0606 as well)
Spread or corroded terminal at the sensor connector
Engine controller software decoding the second channel wrongly
s: Check engine light, on GM in the first trip
Limited power because the redundancy check is lost

U0608.t: Lost Communication With Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C
U0608.d: Sensor C usually belongs to a second throttle body, as on engines with one throttle per bank or two throttles in parallel. Ford's 2020 to 2024 gasoline summaries spell this out: on dual-throttle applications the SENT sensor of throttle body B reports as sensor C, and U0608 sets with MIL and wrench lamp when wiring or the SENT device has been faulty for more than 4 s. P0225 and P0229 cover a self-reported fault or a brief dropout of the same sensor; oddly, Ford labels the matching shorted-line codes as sensor B. GM's dual-throttle calibration of 2023 and 2024 assigns U0608 to sensor 1 of the bank 2 throttle, 0.13 s, one trip, while that unit's second track reports as U0688. Losing one throttle forces the controller to limit both banks.
c: Wiring fault on the SENT harness branch to the second throttle body
Position sensor electronics of the second throttle body failed
Corroded or loose connector at throttle body B
s: Check engine light and, on Ford, wrench lamp
Reduced power, uneven running between banks

U0609.t: Lost Communication With Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Sensor
U0609.d: A digital manifold pressure sensor sends pressure, often with an intake temperature value, as SENT frames; chips built for this, such as Infineon's KP276, add a status nibble with error flags and a CRC to every frame. U0609 is stored when those frames stop arriving or cannot be used. Ford's 2023 diesel summary defines it for the SENT MAP sensor: the SENT driver flags a communication fault, the data line hangs at low voltage, or the sensor flags an internal fault, checked continuously and registered after 5 s. P0105 is the separate code for a sensor whose status bit or reading is implausible. The NHTSA index lists a 2023 Audi RS 6 Avant bulletin covering U0609 with U060A. Load and boost then run on substitute values.
c: SENT line stuck low, open or chafed, or supply/ground missing
Sensor reports an internal fault (moisture, oil or soot ingress)
s: Check engine light
Reduced power or limited boost
Rough running or harder starting at altitude

U060A.t: Lost Communication With Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor B
U060A.d: MAP sensor B is a second manifold pressure sensor, found for example on V engines with a separate intake plenum per bank or on engines measuring before and after the throttle. U060A applies when this sensor is digitally connected and the controller stops receiving usable SENT frames from it, whether because of a dead line, a broken frame or the sensor's own error code; Melexis' MLX90818, made for manifold and turbo pressure, sends reserved fast-channel values to signal internal faults. No manufacturer publishes a readable description of this code. The NHTSA index lists it with U0609 in an Audi bulletin for the 2023 RS 6 Avant, but that file is not readable. CARB 1968.2 requires a stand-alone code for lost communication on a digital input. P2A0A to P2A0E are the analog codes.
c: Open, shorted or chafed wire to MAP sensor B
MAP sensor B electronics failed or reporting an internal error
Corroded or loose connector at sensor B
s: Check engine light
Reduced power on the affected bank or intake path

U060B.t: Lost Communication With Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A
U060B.d: Boost sensor A measures charge air pressure after the compressor and is often a SENT pressure sensor with built-in temperature measurement. U060B means the engine controller no longer hears from it. Audi documents the code for the 2022 to 2025 Q5 and SQ5 family (bulletin 2074392): the MIL comes on and the engine control unit stores U060B00 against G31, the boost pressure sender, either intermittent or static. Engine vibration can break the three wires right at the sender connector, which may only show once the terminals are unpinned or the tape is removed; the fix is a new pigtail with set lengths, and production changed from January 2025. P0235 to P0238 cover an analog sensor's circuit faults. Boost control falls back to a safe low level.
c: Wires broken by vibration right behind the sensor connector
Loose terminal or oil in the connector
s: Check engine light
Noticeably less power, boost held low
Fault may come and go with engine vibration

U060C.t: Lost Communication With Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B
U060C.d: Boost sensor B is needed where charge pressure is measured twice: on twin-turbo V engines with one charge path per bank, on two-stage systems between the stages, or after the charge air cooler in addition to sensor A. When it is a digital SENT device, its frames carry pressure, often a temperature value, a status nibble and a CRC. U060C sets when those frames from sensor B are missing, corrupt or flagged as invalid by the sensor itself. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the logic follows Audi's bulletin for U060B and the CARB 1968.2 rule that lost communication on a digital input needs its own code. P0239 to P0242 are the analog counterparts, and P023E compares sensor B with manifold pressure. The controller usually limits boost on that branch.
c: Damaged wiring to boost sensor B, often near hot turbo plumbing
Loose or oil-soaked connector at sensor B
s: Check engine light
Reduced power with boost limited

U060D.t: Lost Communication With Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C
U060D.d: A third boost sensor C appears only on complex charging layouts, for instance sequential or two-stage turbo systems with pressure taps between and after the stages, or engines that add an electric compressor. U060D reports that the controller has lost the digital link to this sensor: no SENT frame inside the expected time, a frame failing its check, or a sensor that transmits only its reserved error value, a feature found on pressure chips such as Melexis' MLX90818. No manufacturer documents U060D publicly, so its use rests on the CARB 1968.2 requirement and the pattern of U060B. Which physical sensor is called C is a manufacturer decision. P25F2 to P25F5 cover the analog circuit of the same sensor. Expect boost to be limited on the affected stage.
c: Open or shorted SENT, supply or ground wire to sensor C
Sensor C sending only its error value
s: Check engine light
Power loss when the affected stage would build boost

U060E.t: Lost Communication With Crankcase Pressure Sensor
U060E.d: A crankcase pressure sensor lets the engine controller check the positive crankcase ventilation for leaks or a disconnected hose, which CARB 1968.2 requires. Ford fits it in two versions. The analog one reports circuit low, high and range faults; the SENT one uses P051A and U060E. Ford's gasoline summaries for 2020 to 2023 and 2024 run this check continuously and record a fault after 5 s once the controller recognizes faulted signal patterns from the sensor; P051A then marks a sensor that reports itself defective, U060E a link that no longer delivers usable frames. Both block the ventilation disconnect test (P04DB, later P2C90), because that monitor needs a working sensor. Drivability is normally unaffected, but the MIL comes on.
c: Damaged SENT, supply or ground wire to the crankcase pressure sensor
Oil or moisture in the sensor connector
s: Check engine light
Crankcase ventilation monitor does not complete
